title: [fuzz-coverage] http/h2/frame.rs: missing standalone fuzz target for FrameHeader::parse
description:
src/http/h2/frame.rs:122 — FrameHeader::parse(src: &mut BytesMut) decodes the 9-byte HTTP/2 frame header (RFC 7540 §4.1) — stream id, type, flags, length. Existing fuzz targets (h2_connection_frame_decoder, h2_connection_io) drive whole-connection bytes; no target exercises the header parser ALONE with adversarial 9-byte inputs.

Attack surface: every byte of every H2 frame any peer sends. The header is the first 9 bytes — most attacker effort begins here.

Malformed shapes:
  - <9 input bytes (truncation behavior)
  - Length field > 16 MiB (SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE default + escape)
  - Reserved high bit on stream ID (must be ignored — but observed?)
  - Unknown frame types (must be ignored per RFC §4.1)
  - Unknown flag bits (must be ignored)
  - DATA on stream 0 (PROTOCOL_ERROR — but does the parser flag it?)

Proposed target: fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_h2_frame_header_parser.rs

Source: /testing-fuzzing on src/http/* (2026-04-26).

title: [bug-hunt] cx/macaroon.rs bind_for_request not idempotent; double-bind silently produces unverifiable token
description:
src/cx/macaroon.rs:599-608 bind_for_request takes &self and replaces the discharge's signature with HMAC(self.signature, discharge.signature). Calling it twice on the same discharge:
- first call: D1.sig = HMAC(auth.sig, D.sig)
- second call (with D1 as input): D2.sig = HMAC(auth.sig, D1.sig) = HMAC(auth.sig, HMAC(auth.sig, D.sig))
D2's signature does not match what the verifier computes (verifier expects single-bind: HMAC(auth.sig, D.unbound_sig)), so D2 silently fails verification with InvalidSignature.

A holder that accidentally double-binds (e.g. via a retry loop or in code that defensively re-binds) would get a token that LOOKS bound but doesn't verify. The error message at the verifier is generic InvalidSignature; the holder cannot distinguish double-bind from a real signature corruption.

Fix options: (a) make bind_for_request detect already-bound discharges and reject (requires marking bound discharges, which the current type doesn't); (b) make bind_for_request return a NewType BoundMacaroonToken so the type system prevents double-bind; (c) document the precondition explicitly and return Err on attempted re-bind. Option (b) is the structural fix; (c) is the safe inline fix.
close_reason: Fixed in 89336ef09: added in-memory 'bound: bool' flag (NOT serialized) and changed bind_for_request signature to Result<Self, BindError> with new BindError::AlreadyBound variant. All ~30 callers updated with .unwrap(). 4 regression tests: fresh-mint unbound, first-bind sets flag, double-bind Err, deserialized treated as unbound.

title: Spawn mailbox audit: a panicking capture in a denied spawn kills the worker and hangs its JoinHandle; spawn_local requests dropped unresolved at worker exit; close() never wakes after runtime drop
description:
Read-only audit of src/runtime/spawn_mailbox.rs (spawn gateway, admission, local spawn lane, region commands) at origin/main 49fec5364 (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-05).

Sound:
- No double admission, and no lost wakeup on enqueue.
- Pre-admission abort, denial attribution and credit order are correct.
- Local-lane !Send safety and nested drives are correct.
- Create vs parent close is ordered; teardown is correct apart from the items below.

## HIGH
H1. A panicking destructor or joiner waker in a denied spawn kills the worker, hangs the JoinHandle, and can leave the region Closing (spawn_mailbox.rs ~1304/~1327 and the local versions ~870/~892).
- Where: SpawnRequestParts::resolve_cancelled/resolve_failed drop the payload, then fire the completion slot, with no containment. Their callers in three_lane.rs, builder.rs teardown and the current-thread cleanup have none either.
- Trigger: the request captures a panic-on-drop value, such as an unconsumed ObligationToken, which panics in every build, and the target region is Closing, Closed or at its quota.
- Impact:
  - The completion slot never runs. It is the only thing that opens the retirement barrier, so join stays Pending forever and monitors/links retry forever.
  - advance_region_state is skipped, so a Closing region hangs.
  - The panic escapes next_task/run_loop and the worker thread dies.
- FIXED in stack P (P11): every payload drop and slot call is contained (catch_unwind, payload forgotten), and the credit is still released last.

## MEDIUM
M1. Unadmitted spawn_local requests are dropped unresolved when a native worker thread exits. run_loop_until breaks on shutdown with requests on the thread-local lane, and lane cleanup exists only for the browser pump. Handles hang, and captured destructors run during TLS teardown, where a panic aborts the process. Fix: cancel_local_spawns_for_mailbox in the worker epilogue.

M2. ChildRegion::close()/close_with_outcome() awaited outside a dying runtime never wake: retire_region_commands wakes only Create/Watch, and RegionQuiescence::poll has no liveness check. Fix: register the close waiter as a TeardownWake and return RuntimeUnavailable once liveness is gone.

## LOW
- L1. After a budget-cut drain, current-thread block_on fails this runtime's live lane requests with RuntimeUnavailable and never advances their region.
- L2. Provisional-id collisions are reachable after 2^31 reuses of a hot task slot: canonical ids then satisfy is_spawn_mailbox_id. Fix: retire task-arena generations at 2^31 or above.
- L3. A user EntropySource::fork runs under the state lock after add_task, with no containment.
- L4. The ordering docs do not hold on multi-worker runtimes (per-region FIFO pairing, cancel-then-close order).
close_reason: All items H1, M1, M2, L1, L2, L3, L4 completed and verified.

title: [FS] Fuzz fs/uring.rs user_data overflow & state corruption
description:
FOLLOW-UP AUDIT: Additional vulnerabilities in fs/uring.rs user_data system

**CONTEXT**: Previous work fixed test constant collision (0xDEAD_BEEF -> 0xFF00_0000_DEAD_BEEF).
Deeper audit reveals additional critical vulnerabilities in user_data allocation and completion tracking.

**NEWLY IDENTIFIED VULNERABILITIES**:

1. **Integer Overflow** (line 488):
   - `next_user_data.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)` wraps after 2^64 operations
   - No overflow detection or handling
   - Post-overflow allocations restart from sequence=0

2. **Collision via sequence.max(1)** (line 489):
   - When counter wraps to 0, `sequence.max(1)` makes it 1
   - Collides with second operation ever submitted (also sequence=1)
   - Same OpKind + same sequence = identical user_data

3. **Silent Completion Loss** (line 507):
   - `let _ = mark_tracked_op_complete(...)` ignores failures
   - OpKind::decode() failures discard completions
   - Invalid OpKind values (>5) lose completion events

4. **State Machine Corruption**:
   - No validation that operations are in Pending state before completion
   - Duplicate completions not prevented
   - Corrupted state transitions possible

**ATTACK SCENARIOS**:
- **DoS via overflow**: Force 2^64 operations to trigger collision
- **Completion hijacking**: Craft user_data to collide with pending operations
- **State corruption**: Complete non-pending operations to corrupt OpState
- **Resource exhaustion**: Lost completions cause operation leaks

**FUZZER IMPLEMENTATION**: fs_uring_user_data_overflow.rs
- Mock allocator testing overflow scenarios
- Boundary condition testing: near-overflow, post-overflow, zero-sequence
- OpKind encode/decode validation for all edge cases
- Completion tracking with duplicate detection
- Collision detection between wrapped values

**TEST SCENARIOS**:
- Normal allocation patterns
- Near-overflow (u64::MAX - 100) operations
- Post-overflow wrap-around behavior  
- Invalid OpKind values (>5) handling
- Zero sequence and maximum sequence boundaries
- Deliberately colliding user_data values
- Mixed allocation patterns

**IMPACT SEVERITY**: 
- HIGH: Integer overflow leads to predictable collisions
- HIGH: Silent completion loss causes operation hangs
- MEDIUM: State machine corruption from invalid transitions
- LOW: Practical exploitation requires 2^64 operations (18 quintillion)

**ORACLE STRATEGY**:
- Encode/decode consistency validation
- Completion processing success tracking
- Duplicate completion detection
- Collision identification in post-overflow scenarios
close_reason: COMPLETED: Critical user_data overflow & completion loss fuzzer implemented. Discovered 4 additional vulnerabilities beyond previous test collision fix: integer overflow, sequence collision, silent completion loss, state corruption. 346-line comprehensive fuzzer targets boundary conditions and overflow scenarios.

title: [fresh-eyes] grpc/server: CallContext::from_metadata_at hardcodes wall_clock_instant_now — replay-determinism contract violation
description:
src/grpc/server.rs:683-702 — CallContext::from_metadata_at accepts now: Instant explicitly so callers can pin the deadline computation to a deterministic clock sample. The doc comment at line 680-681 states: 'This is useful for deterministic tests and replay harnesses that need to avoid ambient wall-clock reads.' But line 700 hardcodes time_getter: wall_clock_instant_now in the returned CallContext.

Concrete defect: a replay harness that calls from_metadata_at(metadata, timeout, addr, recorded_now) gets a CallContext whose deadline IS computed from recorded_now (good), but whose time_getter still points at the ambient wall clock. Any subsequent call to is_expired() / remaining() / timeout_header_value() reads the real wall clock — producing different verdicts across replays of the same recorded scenario.

Fix direction (one of, in order of preference):
  1. Add a time_getter: fn() -> Instant parameter to from_metadata_at and store it in the returned CallContext. Most direct fix; preserves the const-fn shape.
  2. Make from_metadata_at deprecated in favor of from_metadata_with_time_getter (which is the correct shape).
  3. Add a debug_assert!(false, 'use from_metadata_with_time_getter for replay') that fires only when the caller is in a deterministic-mode build, leaving production unchanged.

Severity P2: real replay-determinism contract violation, but low blast radius (most production callers go through from_metadata_with_time_getter via the explicit interceptor chain; only direct callers of from_metadata_at hit the bug).

Source: fresh-eyes 24h-diff audit (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Fixed: docstring updated, .with_time_getter() chain requirement made explicit, 2 regression tests pin contract (commit b2fac8f97)

comments.text:
SapphireHill: read-only review of c9661199f (map-reduce keeps the initiating failure after sibling drain), verified on origin 17f130960. One medium gap remains in this bead's property.
A drained sibling with a lower index that turns its drain into an Err displaces the initiating error. In src/combinator/map_reduce.rs ~927-929, `Some(Outcome::Err(error)) => failures.error(slot.index, ..)` is recorded whatever `joined` was. Unlike the Cancelled arm (~930-934), it is recorded even when the join is `Err(JoinError::Cancelled(drain_reason))`, meaning the child was only reacting to our own drain. The final selection (~1157-1164: `errors.sort_by_key(index)` then `errors.remove(0)`) then picks the lowest index. The sibling's induced error becomes `outcome` and `failure_index`, and the real cause survives only in `stopped_by`.
Trigger: the e2e setup, with index 1 returning Err("trigger") and index 0 parked in `receiver.recv(&child)`, where index 0 maps `Err(RecvError::Cancelled)` into Outcome::Err (the common `?` pattern). Result: outcome = Err(sibling's error), failure_index = Some(0).
Fix direction: when a child's join equals Cancelled(slot.drain_reason), demote its non-panic logical outcome, or prefer the stopped_by index when choosing the reported failure.
Missing test: a lower-index drained sibling that returns Err. The e2e covers the Ok, echo, independent, stronger and panic returns, but not Err.
Also, the drain filter matches only a byte-identical reason. A sibling returning a drain-derived but non-identical reason (e.g. race_loser) counts as independent and outranks the initiating Err. The e2e "independent_cancel" case asserts that; it is a contract question.

title: runtime/current_thread: block_on caller stranded forever in CurrentThreadDriver::acquire after a refused handover races a second caller
description: src/runtime/current_thread.rs acquire (~L315-356): after the background thread refuses a handover (slot back to Background, notify_all), a second block_on caller R2 can set Requested and wait; the first waiter R1 then sees Requested/Loaned in its loop and keeps waiting. When R2 releases, the background thread recovers WorkerSlot::Returned with *slot = Background and NO notify_all (~L285-288), and R1 has no timeout, so R1's block_on hangs until an unrelated release/shutdown. Trigger: a handle-spawned task on the background thread that spawn_locals (can_offer false) plus two threads calling block_on. Fix: Requested carries the requester (ThreadId); in the wait loop any state other than Offered or Requested(me) returns None (fall back to direct polling); notify_all on the Returned recovery arm. Add a two-thread regression test. Found by fresh-eyes review 2026-09-09; verified by reading. Owner of the file: CopperOak (reserved).

title: [EPIC-PHASE] Phase 3 - Actors and Session Types
description:
## Overview
Phase 3 introduces the actor model with supervision trees, region-owned actors, and optional session types for protocol-safe communication.

## Goals
1. Long-lived actors owned by regions
2. Supervision policies (restart, escalate, ignore)
3. Cancel-correct actor shutdown
4. Optional session types for protocol verification

## Key Components

### 1. Actor Model
```rust
pub trait Actor: Send + 'static {
    type Message: Send;
    
    async fn handle(&mut self, cx: &mut Cx<'_>, msg: Self::Message);
    
    /// Called before first message
    async fn on_start(&mut self, cx: &mut Cx<'_>) {}
    
    /// Called on actor shutdown
    async fn on_stop(&mut self, cx: &mut Cx<'_>) {}
}
```

### 2. Actor Handle
```rust
pub struct ActorHandle<A: Actor> {
    tx: Sender<A::Message>,
    // Two-phase send via tx.reserve().send()
}

impl<A: Actor> ActorHandle<A> {
    pub async fn send(&self, cx: &mut Cx<'_>, msg: A::Message) -> Result<(), SendError>;
    pub async fn ask<R>(&self, cx: &mut Cx<'_>, f: impl FnOnce(oneshot::Sender<R>) -> A::Message) -> R;
}
```

### 3. Supervision
```rust
pub enum SupervisionPolicy {
    /// Restart actor on panic/error
    Restart { max_restarts: u32, within: Duration },
    /// Escalate failure to parent region
    Escalate,
    /// Ignore failure, actor stops
    Ignore,
    /// Stop entire region on failure
    StopAll,
}
```

### 4. Region-Owned Actors
- Actors are spawned into regions like tasks
- Region close shuts down all actors
- Actor shutdown respects cancellation protocol:
  1. Stop accepting new messages
  2. Drain mailbox with budget
  3. Run on_stop finalizer
  4. Complete

### 5. Session Types (Optional, Advanced)
```rust
// Example: ATM protocol
type AtmSession = Send<Card, Recv<Pin, Choose<
    Send<Amount, Recv<Cash, End>>,  // Withdraw
    Recv<Balance, End>              // Check balance
>>>;
```

Session types encode protocol states at compile time. Violations become type errors.

## Dependencies
- Requires Phase 0 complete (core runtime)
- Requires Phase 1 complete (parallel scheduler)
- Requires Phase 2 complete (I/O for network actors)
- Requires two-phase channels

## Actor Lifecycle
```
Created → Running → ShutdownRequested → Draining → Finalizing → Stopped
```

Mirrors task lifecycle but with message-based trigger.

## Testing Strategy
- Actor spawn and message handling
- Supervision restart policies
- Graceful shutdown under cancellation
- Session type protocol compliance (if implemented)

## References
- asupersync_plan_v4.md: §7 Phase 3 (Actors)
- Erlang/OTP supervision trees
- Actix (Rust actor framework)
- Session types (Gay & Hole, Honda et al.)

## Success Criteria
- Actors run as region-owned long-lived tasks; no detached-by-default behavior.
- Supervision policies are explicit, monotone, and trace-visible.
- Optional session types provide protocol conformance checks without changing runtime semantics.
- E2E tests cover actor lifecycle, supervision escalation, and structured shutdown/quiescence.

- Mailboxes use cancel-safe, obligation-aware protocols (no silent drops).
- Actor lifecycle (start/stop/restart if supervised) is trace-visible and deterministic in lab simulations.

  - drain or reject remaining messages deterministically

- No message is silently dropped.
- Mailbox state is fully observable via trace.

- Session type AST encoding (`Send`, `Recv`, `Choose`, `Offer`, `End`, etc.)
- Duality computation
- Typed endpoints integrated with two-phase channels
- Compile-time protocol compliance via typestate

- This is optional and may start as a separate crate/module.
- Must not compromise determinism.

- Provides a session type representation + duality and a way to enforce protocol conformance.
- Integrates session-typed endpoints with two-phase/obligation-aware primitives.
- Compile-time compliance tests (e.g., trybuild or equivalent) are deterministic and explain failures clearly.

title: Implement quorum combinator for consensus patterns
description:
## Purpose
The quorum combinator implements M-of-N completion semantics - wait for M out of N concurrent tasks to complete successfully before returning. This is essential for distributed consensus patterns, redundancy, and fault-tolerant operations.

## Mathematical Foundation
Quorum builds on the near-semiring concurrency algebra from the spec:
- `join (⊗)`: All must complete (N-of-N)
- `race (⊕)`: First wins (1-of-N)
- `quorum(M, N)`: M-of-N - generalization between join and race

The outcome aggregation follows the severity lattice: Ok < Err < Cancelled < Panicked
For quorum(M, N): return Ok if ≥M tasks return Ok; otherwise aggregate errors.

## Semantic Model

```rust
pub async fn quorum<T, E>(
    cx: &mut Cx<'_>,
    m: usize,  // Required successes
    tasks: Vec<impl Future<Output = Result<T, E>>>,
) -> Outcome<Vec<T>, E>
```

### Behavior
1. Spawn all N tasks as region children
2. Track completions as they arrive
3. On M successes: cancel remaining (N-M) losers, drain them, return Ok
4. On (N-M+1) failures: know quorum impossible, cancel all remaining, return aggregated error
5. Losers MUST be fully drained (non-negotiable invariant)

### Edge Cases
- `quorum(0, N)`: Return Ok([]) immediately, cancel all tasks
- `quorum(N, N)`: Equivalent to join (all must succeed)
- `quorum(1, N)`: Equivalent to race (first wins)
- `quorum(M, N) where M > N`: Type error or early failure

## Cancellation Handling
- When quorum achieved OR impossible: request_cancel(losers)
- Wait for all losers to complete (Running → CancelRequested → Cancelling → Finalizing → Completed)
- Honor loser cleanup budgets
- Propagate incoming cancellation to all children

## Invariant Support
- **Losers always drained**: Core non-negotiable - all N tasks eventually complete
- **No obligation leaks**: If a winning task holds obligations, they flow to caller
- **Region quiescence**: Quorum region only closes when ALL children (winners + losers) are done

## Testing Requirements
1. Basic M-of-N success scenarios
2. Early failure detection (quorum impossible)
3. Loser draining verification
4. Cancellation budget honoring
5. Mixed outcome aggregation
6. Lab runtime determinism

## Example Usage

```rust
// Wait for 2-of-3 replicas to acknowledge
let acks = scope.quorum(cx, 2, vec![
    write_replica_a(cx),
    write_replica_b(cx),
    write_replica_c(cx),
]).await?;
```

## References
- asupersync_plan_v4.md: §5.7 Derived Combinators, §3 Near-Semiring
- asupersync_v4_formal_semantics.md: §3.2 Concurrency Algebra

## Acceptance Criteria
- Quorum(k) returns when k branches satisfy the success predicate, while cancelling + draining remaining branches.
- Result aggregation is policy-aware and deterministic in lab runs.
- Handles partial failures and cancellation without leaking obligations.
- E2E tests cover quorum success, quorum failure, and cancellation mid-quorum.

title: GenServerHandle::call panics with ASUP-E103 for root-region callers outside test builds; cfg(test)/test-internals region-0 fallback makes every in-tree test blind to it (latent: native spawn entry needs &mut RuntimeState)
description:
GenServerHandle::call (and call_with_timeout) mint the reply permit's graded obligation token from the CALLER's region. For a caller whose task lives in the root region, ObligationToken::reserve asserts and the caller's task panics with "[ASUP-E103] Cannot create obligation token in root region". Every in-tree test is blind to this because the same helper routes region 0 to ObligationToken::reserve_test under cfg(test) or the test-internals feature, and Cx::for_testing() carries RegionId (0:1), which is not zero. Latent today (see reachability), but it is a public-API panic that the test suite structurally cannot observe.

Evidence (7fc9e53a4):
- src/gen_server.rs 947 (call) and 1372 (call_with_timeout): reply_tx.reserve(cx) where reply_tx is a session::TrackedOneshotSender.
- src/channel/session.rs 476-481: TrackedOneshotSender::reserve calls reserve_tracked_send_obligation_for_region("TrackedOneshotPermit", cx.region_id()).
- src/channel/session.rs 64-74: under cfg(any(test, feature = "test-internals")) a region with as_u64() == 0 takes ObligationToken::reserve_test; otherwise ObligationToken::reserve(description, region).
- src/obligation/graded.rs 894-911: reserve asserts region.as_u64() != 0 with the ASUP-E103 message. docs/error_codes/ASUP-E103.md documents the token-level rule ("move the runtime path into a non-root region") but nothing on GenServerHandle::call, cast, try_call or the module docs says the caller must not be a root-region task.
- Root region id is zero: src/util/arena.rs 178/183 start generations at 0 and the root region is the first insert (src/runtime/state.rs 3449-3468), which the session fixture itself relies on (assert_ne!(child.as_u64(), 0, "exercise the production graded-token path")). The native runtime admits block_on's root task and every RuntimeHandle::spawn task into that root region (src/runtime/builder.rs 5732, 5792).
- Test blindness: src/gen_server.rs tests use Cx::for_testing() (RegionId 0:1) or lab child regions; tests/gen_server_leak_test.rs and examples/spork_minimal_supervised_app.rs use Cx::for_testing() too; none calls from a region whose id encodes to zero without the test fallback.

Reachability: the only GenServer spawn entry is Scope::spawn_gen_server(&mut RuntimeState, ...) (src/gen_server.rs 1766), so a downstream program cannot start a GenServer on the native Runtime through the public API today, which keeps this latent for RuntimeHandle::spawn / block_on callers. It IS reachable for a downstream that drives GenServer through the public LabRuntime without test-internals: create_root_region, create_task(root, ...) that calls handle.call(&cx, ...) panics, while the identical program under the test-internals feature succeeds. If a native spawn entry (Cx::spawn_gen_server or similar) is added later, every root-task caller hits the panic immediately.

Suggested repair, in order of preference:
1. Document the requirement on GenServerHandle::call, call_with_timeout, cast (which also reserves through the session layer where applicable) and the module docs, and add a debug_assert-free early return: check cx.region_id().as_u64() == 0 before reserving and return CallError::ServerStopped-like typed error. CallError (src/gen_server.rs 819-827) is NOT non_exhaustive, so adding a variant would break the v0.4.3 compatibility gate; reuse CallError::Cancelled(CancelReason::user("[ASUP-E103] root-region caller")) and trace it.
2. Remove the cfg(test) masking asymmetry from reserve_tracked_send_obligation_for_region so a root-region caller behaves the same in tests and production (the helper could always mint through reserve and let tests create child regions), and add one gen_server test that calls from a real root-region task on a LabRuntime built without the fallback to pin the chosen behaviour.
3. Keep the token-level guard as is; it protects the no-obligation-leak invariant and is not the defect.

Found during the read-only fresh-eyes pass (asupersync-cqzuzt) while source is frozen; no edits made.
close_reason: Fixed in ad61680be: root-region callers get CallError::Cancelled carrying [ASUP-E103] instead of a token-layer panic; lab call tests moved to child regions. RED control (old code served Ok(5)) / GREEN 273/273 receipts in comments.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
Repair landed (SapphireHill), option 1 from the bead with the test blindness removed for the call path.

Why not the other options: `reserve_test` mints against `RegionId::new_ephemeral()`, which br-asupersync-u3gsst gates to tests because production region ids must come from the runtime arena (lock ordering, deterministic replay), so production cannot simply mirror the test fallback. Not tracking the reply permit at all for root callers (the database transaction precedent) would need a proof-less `TrackedOneshotPermit` and silently downgrade a dropped reply from an E101 leak panic to `NoReply`. The registry remediation for ASUP-E103 is "move the path into a non-root region; preserve the guard", so the call is refused with a typed error before any mailbox slot is taken.

Changes: `reject_root_region_caller` (cx.region_id().as_u64() == 0, traced as `gen_server::call_rejected_root_region`) wired into `GenServerHandle::call` and `GenServerRef::call` after the stopped check; `CallError::Cancelled(CancelReason::user("[ASUP-E103] ..."))`; module, `CallError` and `call` docs; registry row + runbook page list gen_server as an emitter. Test harness: `lab_client_region` allocates a child region of the lab root; `lab_spawn_cx` (seven tests) uses it, and the five tests that build their client task directly through `create_task_infrastructure` (the cancellation test, the two-client and three-client lifecycle tests, the conformance lifecycle test) now pass that child region too. Two of those failed outright under the rejection and three had been ignoring the call result, so all twelve lab call tests now exercise the production graded-token path instead of the region-0 fallback. In-crate callers audited: src/app.rs only spawns; gen_server_conformance_tests, tests/gen_server_leak_test.rs and examples/spork_minimal_supervised_app.rs call through `Cx::for_testing()` (region 0:1, non-root). The `cfg(test)` region-0 fallback in `channel::session::reserve_tracked_send_obligation_for_region` is left in place for the other tracked senders; their public `reserve` signatures have no variant to carry a root-region refusal (v0.4.3 compatibility), so that asymmetry remains a documented follow-up rather than part of this bead.

Receipts (RCH clean-overlay on base 71ba3edd3):
- RED (deliberate-failure control: src/gen_server.rs overlaid with the new test, docs and harness but without `reject_root_region_caller`, its constant and both call-site checks, i.e. the pre-repair `call` bodies byte-for-byte; md5 1943226e8fce2fcb6113f72c5e487071; worker ovh-a): `cargo test -j 8 --lib --features test-internals -- gen_server::tests::call_from_root_region_task_is_rejected_with_asup_e103 --exact` -> compiled and ran; panicked at src/gen_server.rs:2774 "a root-region caller must be refused with CallError::Cancelled, got Ok(5)" (the masked region-0 fallback let the call succeed); test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; exit 101. A first control attempt that also removed the call sites but kept the helper failed to compile under the crate's dead-code denial and was discarded as not a control. The fixed file (md5 ef3cfb03ca9e348efb807371e272fe03) was restored byte-exact before chain C was submitted.
- GREEN (final files overlaid, chain C; worker vmi1149989, 1177.5s): `cargo test -j 8 --lib --features tls,test-internals -- gen_server:: gen_server_conformance_tests:: channel::session:: http::h1::http_client::tests::` -> test result: ok. 273 passed; 0 failed; the reproducer, `gen_server_call_cancellation_is_deterministic` and `conformance_full_lifecycle_no_obligation_leaks` all `... ok`; exit 0. title: [http-deepest-10th] h2/connection.rs:884-927 decode_headers does not flag trailers — pseudo-headers in trailers pass validation
description:
src/http/h2/connection.rs:884-927 (decode_headers), specifically lines 917-918 — when a HEADERS frame carrying HTTP/2 trailers is decoded (a second HEADERS frame on an already-opened stream with END_STREAM set), validate_h2_pseudo_headers() is called with the SAME `is_request` flag as the initial headers. RFC 7540 §8.1.2.1 / RFC 9113 §8.1 explicitly forbid pseudo-headers in trailers ("Trailers MUST NOT include pseudo-header fields"), but this code path does not pass an `is_trailer` flag and the validator has no way to enforce the rule.

The state machine in src/http/h2/stream.rs (lines 409-435) correctly detects and rejects trailers without END_STREAM, but it does NOT validate that trailers lack pseudo-headers; it only validates the END_STREAM flag.

Repro:
  T0 — server receives request HEADERS with `:method POST`, `:path /api`, headers_complete = true.
  T1 — peer sends a SECOND HEADERS frame with END_STREAM set, containing `:method DELETE` and `x-trailer-token: abc`.
  T2 — decode_headers calls validate_h2_pseudo_headers with is_request=true (or whatever the original direction was). The `:method DELETE` pseudo-header passes validation as if it were a fresh request header.
  T3 — downstream filters that inspect only the FIRST `:method` see "POST" and route accordingly. Filters that aggregate all `:method` instances (defensive ones) see "POST, DELETE" — undefined behaviour. Filters that take the LAST instance see "DELETE".

Impact: request smuggling / auth bypass on filters that see the trailer pseudo-header; cache poisoning if intermediaries fold trailers into the request canonicalisation.

Fix direction:
  1. Pass an `is_trailer: bool` parameter into validate_h2_pseudo_headers, propagated from decode_headers based on whether the stream's headers_complete flag was already set when this HEADERS frame arrived.
  2. When `is_trailer == true`, reject ANY decoded header whose name starts with ':' — return a malformed-trailer error.
  3. Equivalently: at decode_headers entry, if the stream's headers_complete is true and END_STREAM is set, scan the decoded headers for pseudo-header names and reject before the regular validation runs.
  4. Regression test: build a trailer HEADERS frame containing `:method` and `x-trailer-foo`; assert decode_headers rejects with H2Error::ProtocolError.

Severity MEDIUM because (a) the smuggling vector requires a downstream filter that processes pseudo-headers across HEADERS-frame boundaries (uncommon but not unheard of), (b) the spec violation is unambiguous, and (c) the same pattern was just filed at the recv_headers layer (sibling bead) — fixing both sites consistently is the right shape.

Source: /multi-pass-bug-hunting on src/http/* DEEPEST 10th-pass (2026-04-26).
close_reason: decode_headers now threads is_trailers (computed from new Stream::initial_headers_decoded() + per-direction end_stream check) into validate_h2_pseudo_headers. Trailers path rejects ANY pseudo-header per RFC 9113 §8.1 with a stream-level PROTOCOL_ERROR; §8.2.1 lowercase rule and §8.2.2 connection-specific-header ban still apply. Client-side discriminates trailers (END_STREAM=true) from 1xx informational (END_STREAM=false). 2 new tests: trailers_must_not_contain_pseudo_headers + trailers_reject_connection_specific_headers. Commit 3d75e38c2.

title: Add synthetic E2E proof for swarm autopilot workflow
description:
Background: The proposed autopilot pieces need one mock-free enough integration proof that they cooperate: receipts classify proofs, work finder avoids reserved files, scanner findings become beads, and closeout verifier catches omissions.

Goal: Add an end-to-end logged test or script that runs on synthetic fixture state and proves the swarm-autopilot workflow without touching real reservations or live remote workers.

Implementation approach: Use fixture directories and captured logs rather than live Agent Mail mutation where possible. The proof should exercise schema validation, parser classification, dirty-tree/reservation input, scanner template output, and closeout checks.

Tests/logging: The E2E should produce deterministic logs with enough detail to diagnose which stage failed. Include at least one happy path and one blocked path.

Success criteria: A single narrow validation command proves the pieces fit together and can be cited by future closeouts.

Non-goals: Do not require network access, do not create real branches/worktrees, and do not mutate production .beads data during the proof.

title: [sync] src/sync/mutex_metamorphic.rs:397 poison thread delay allows multiple waiters to succeed before poisoning
description: mr4_concurrent_poison_consistency assumes at most one waiter can succeed before the poisoning thread runs, but the poison thread sleeps 5ms before acquiring the mutex. After the barrier releases, queued waiters race on an initially unlocked mutex and can serialize multiple successful acquisitions before poison starts, making the success_count <= 1 invariant flaky and invalid. Suggested fix: have the poisoning thread acquire the mutex first, then release waiters so they contend behind the poisoned acquisition, or otherwise gate waiter progress until the poison holder is queued/holding.
close_reason: done

title: [conformance] raptorq/systematic.rs: K=1, K=2, K=3 K' ladder lower-edge boundary not tested (sub-area #3 of lc0anl)
description:
src/raptorq/systematic.rs::SystematicParams::try_for_source_block partitions K against the K' ladder via partition_point. Existing tests cover K=4 (params_small), K=11→K'=12 (params_lookup_uses_smallest_k_prime_ge_k), and K=100. The smallest K values (K=1, K=2, K=3) are NOT explicitly tested and would all map to K'=10 (the smallest entry in SYSTEMATIC_INDEX_TABLE).

A regression that, e.g., changed partition_point's predicate from `row.0 < k as u32` to `row.0 <= k` (causing K=10 to skip to K'=12 instead of K'=10) would NOT be caught by the existing K=4 test (since K=4 still rounds up to 10 either way) but would silently break K=10 itself. Similarly, K=1 / K=2 / K=3 are the smallest valid inputs — if a future refactor accidentally rejected K<min_k_prime as out-of-range, no test would notice.

Add explicit lower-edge boundary test (K=1, 2, 3, 9, 10) so each value pins K'=10 with the full (k, k_prime, j, s, h, w, l) tuple. Sub-area #3 of br-asupersync-lc0anl.

title: Poll quotas after r017wv: the lab charges the cancellation cleanup phase and production does not (owner decision); gen_server phase quotas and block_on roots are not charged natively
description:
## Context
r017wv landed in e275cba8a: the production scheduler now spends Budget poll quotas before each poll, as the lab does. On the harness scenario region_poll_quota_stops_a_busy_task, lab and native agree: round 7, PollQuota. Two differences remain, deliberately.

## 1. Cleanup phase (OWNER DECISION)
- Production does not charge a task that is already cancelling (CancelRequested, Cancelling or Finalizing). Its cleanup budget, Budget::MINIMAL with 100 polls, stays advisory natively, as before.
- The lab charges it.
- If production charged it, every user- or deadline-cancelled task whose drain takes more than 100 polls would have its reason changed to PollQuota, because PollQuota's severity (2) outranks User (0) and Deadline (1). That is an observable change for existing users.
- A long drain can therefore end with reason User natively and PollQuota in the lab.

Options:
- (a) Keep production advisory and document that the lab is stricter. The differential harness then needs a scenario that pins the difference.
- (b) Enforce it natively and accept the reason change. That is a behavior change against v0.4.3 and needs explicit approval.
- (c) Make the lab match production.

## 2. Gaps not covered by e275cba8a
- gen_server's PhaseBudgetGuard narrows a task's CxInner budget without touching its TaskRecord, so polls_remaining never sees a phase-only poll quota. Natively such a quota stays unenforced. A fix would mirror the phase quota into the record, or have consume_budget_poll read CxInner whenever a phase guard is active.
- A root future polled directly by block_on is not charged.

## Evidence
The r017wv comment and e275cba8a's commit body: the control, lib, contract, differential and doctest receipts.

comments.text:
SapphireHill 2026-10-01: fresh-eyes read-only review of my own e275cba8a (r017wv) on origin 4a9b9f2d6. Accounting matches the lab (per-poll, no double charge, no-quota hot path is one u32 compare, cancellation protocol and terminal publication intact). Findings:
COMPAT (owner decision, high confidence that behavior changed): defaults are unaffected (Budget::new/Default/INFINITE use u32::MAX; root region and block_on request Cx are INFINITE), but every EXPLICIT quota is now live in production where v0.4.3 ignored it: with_poll_quota on scopes/regions, AppSpec budgets[].poll_quota on managed unit regions (app.rs ~237-241, a long-lived service unit can now be cancelled), and the v0.4.3 README request-budget example with_poll_quota(10_000) (a streaming handler copied from it is now cancelled after 10k polls). Finalizer tasks (finalizer_budget, 100 polls) end up with a PollQuota cancel request after 100 polls (mask keeps checkpoint working, but is_cancel_requested() is true and wakes go to the cancel lane). This moves production toward the documented semantics, but it is an observable change with no CHANGELOG entry and no opt-out; AGENTS.md requires the owner's explicit approval, a release note, and ideally a builder opt-out. Not yet in a release (e275cba8a is after v0.5.0).
F2 (medium, regression from e275cba8a): Cx::spawn passes the caller's live budget (cx.rs ~4540) and it becomes the child's quota (state.rs ~4785). After a task acknowledges cancellation its live budget is the cleanup budget (task.rs ~1289: 1000 polls User, 500 Deadline, 300 PollQuota, 50 Shutdown), so a child spawned during cleanup (a flush or drain helper) now gets PollQuota after 50-1000 polls and its value becomes JoinError::Cancelled. This contradicts the commit's own "cleanup budgets stay advisory" choice.
F3 (low-medium): the exemption checks the task record, not the Cx: TaskHandle::abort writes the cancel request into the Cx first (task_handle.rs ~518-529) and the record changes only when the runtime processes the abort command; in that window an exhausted task is charged and its User reason is upgraded to PollQuota (three_lane.rs ~1130). Same for Cx-only cancellations (cancel_with, cancel_fast).
F4 (low-medium, fairness): an exhausted task that never checkpoints stays Running with the cancel flag set, so every later wake goes to the cancel lane (priority 215, up to 16 dispatches per ready dispatch) and takes the Cx lock per poll.
F1 (tests): the native differential case stops via checkpoint() at poll 8 (quota 0), so the scheduler's request-cancel branch (three_lane.rs ~1127-1135) never runs natively; deleting it, or the local-task site (~7956) or legacy worker sites (worker.rs ~510/529), keeps every test green except the hand-built unit test.
F6 (design note, matches the lab): a task that never checks cancellation and finishes on poll N+1 has its value replaced by Cancelled(PollQuota).

title: [db-bug-hunt] database/{postgres,mysql}.rs: simple-query (query/execute taking &str) accepts unparameterized SQL — injection vector when callers concatenate user input
description: src/database/postgres.rs:2838 PgConnection::query and :2978 ::execute, plus src/database/mysql.rs:1634 query / :2371 execute, all take pub fn (&mut self, cx: &Cx, sql: &str) — raw SQL goes straight into the wire-protocol Query/COM_QUERY message. There is NO parameterization on this path; callers MUST use the *_params / *_prepared variants for user-supplied values. The doc comment on the parameterized variants (postgres.rs:3134) correctly says 'This prevents SQL injection' — but the simple-query variants have NO equivalent warning telling callers 'do not concatenate untrusted input here'. Real risk: a developer migrating from a high-level ORM sees pub async fn query(...) -> Vec<Row> and writes conn.query(cx, &format!('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = \'{}\'', user_input)).await — classic injection. The library cannot statically prevent this, but it can: (a) add a #[doc = '# Security ...'] block to query() and execute() warning that this path is for trusted/literal SQL ONLY and pointing to query_params; (b) consider renaming to query_unchecked / execute_unchecked to make the contract loud at the call site; (c) add a clippy lint or a #[deny] attribute that flags format!()-built strings passed to these functions. Severity HIGH if any caller has ever concatenated user input into the simple-query path.
close_reason: Fixed in 8eae20001: deprecated query/execute on PgConnection, PgTransaction, MySqlConnection, MySqlTransaction. New *_unchecked variants carry # Security rustdoc block. Internal callers (begin/commit/rollback/KILL QUERY) updated to use *_unchecked. Deprecated shims delegate; existing callers get migration warning, no compile break.

title: API request: expose request_cx_with_budget on RuntimeHandle (downstream: frankensqlite io_native_cx)
description: Runtime::request_cx_with_budget (builder.rs ~:3551, new in v0.4.0) is the ambient-free production entry point for minting a gateway-carrying Cx, but it lives on Runtime only. Downstream holders of a RuntimeHandle (frankensqlite's RuntimeContext, which captures Runtime::current_handle() and pins Arc<RuntimeContext> -> RuntimeHandle -> RuntimeInner for lifetime safety) cannot reach it because RuntimeHandle::try_inner is pub(crate). They currently mint request Cx via a try_spawn_with_cx + sync_channel + timeout MINT-AND-EXIT dance (frankensqlite fsqlite-core/src/connection.rs ~:2516-2530; see frankensqlite beads bd-q8501 / bd-01he5). Request: expose an equivalent (RuntimeHandle::request_cx_with_budget or a handle-scoped minting API) so handle holders can mint gateway-carrying request Cx directly, with the same budget/capability semantics. Acceptance: public API on RuntimeHandle documented + tested; frankensqlite can delete its MINT-AND-EXIT path.

title: [GATED, experiment] Benchmark SAFE mutex-backed queue vs crossbeam-queue; KEEP unless safe wins/ties (no new unsafe)
description:
Phase 8b EVIDENCE-GATED (program: asupersync-ir2uf0). A BENCHMARK EXPERIMENT, not a committed replacement.

TARGET: prototype a SAFE (mutex-backed, e.g. Mutex<VecDeque> or a sharded safe variant) replacement for crossbeam-queue's SegQueue (global injector, epoch GC) + ArrayQueue (channel/mpsc, otlp exporter) and benchmark it against the incumbent on the real workloads. Per the safety taxonomy, crossbeam-queue is KEEP by default (ALGORITHMIC-UNSAFE class); the incumbent leaves ONLY if the SAFE variant wins or ties on the §8b gate metrics. This bead produces EVIDENCE, not a cutover; a passing result unblocks a separate, owner-signed cutover bead.

WHY EVIDENCE-FIRST: the mpsc source itself comments on the safe-mutex-VecDeque tradeoff; the global injector is on the scheduler hot path where SegQueue's lock-freedom may or may not matter given our single-lock multi-lane dispatch design already minimizes contention. Measure, do not assume — and do NOT hand-roll a new unsafe segmented queue (that is exactly the ALGORITHMIC-UNSAFE the taxonomy prohibits; loom/Miri/soak are not proofs of liveness/linearizability/weak-memory).

GATE METRICS: same full axis set as the parking_lot bead (throughput, p50-p999, fairness, cancel latency, alloc/RSS, 1/8/32/64-core scaling) on the injector-heavy benches (spawn_throughput, scheduler_benchmark) + channel benches.

ACCEPTANCE: a benchmark report committed under artifacts/ (or the bead) with the full-axis comparison and a clear verdict: KEEP crossbeam-queue (expected default) or a filed cutover bead if the safe variant genuinely wins/ties. Either outcome is a success for this bead — the point is a decision backed by numbers.
acceptance_criteria:
- Safe prototypes and incumbent run the full real-workload/core-count metric matrix with hardware/provenance.
- KEEP/DEFER is expected and terminal unless safe code wins/ties all required axes or owner accepts each named regression.
- A passing experiment files a separate cutover bead; this bead never introduces algorithmic unsafe or removes crossbeam-queue itself.
close_reason: Terminal KEEP: corrected production-backed exporter benchmark found a non-overlapping safe-candidate regression at 64 producers; no cutover or dependency removal authorized.

title: [security-saas] web/response.rs: Redirect::to/permanent/temporary accept arbitrary URI strings — Open Redirect vulnerability for phishing campaigns
description: src/web/response.rs:386 Redirect::to(uri: impl Into<String>) and :395 ::permanent / :404 ::temporary all accept arbitrary URI strings without validation that the destination is same-origin, in an allowlist of safe hosts, or even a path-only URI. Calling Redirect::to(user_supplied_param) — a common pattern for post-login 'return to' or post-action 'continue to' flows — lets an attacker craft URLs like https://example.com/login?next=https://attacker.com/phish that the server obediently turns into a 302 to attacker.com. The browser follows the redirect with the example.com origin in the Referer, lending the attacker site legitimacy for credential phishing. Industry standard mitigations: (a) Redirect::to_safe(uri, allowed_hosts: &[&str]) that returns Result<Self, RedirectError> and rejects external hosts; (b) Redirect::to_relative(path) that asserts the URI starts with '/' and contains no '//' (protocol-relative attack vector); (c) at minimum, document the open-redirect risk loudly in the rustdoc. The library currently CRLF-strips the Location header (response.rs:417 sanitization comment) but does NOT validate the URI's host. Severity HIGH for any SaaS that takes redirect targets from user input.
close_reason: Fixed in 158f1517d. Three coordinated changes in src/web/response.rs: (1) Added pub enum RedirectError { EmptyUri, ProtocolRelative, BackslashInPath, SchemeNotAllowed{scheme}, HostNotAllowed{host} } with Display + Error impls — surfaces the open-redirect defense as an explicit error type. (2) Refactored Redirect::to / ::permanent / ::temporary to return Result<Self, RedirectError> with safe-by-default validation: rejects empty URIs, protocol-relative '//x' (defeats naive starts_with('/') checks), backslash paths '/\\x' (some intermediaries normalize to //), and any scheme other than http/https (rejects javascript:, data:, file:, ftp:). (3) Added two opt-in modes: Redirect::to_with_allowed_hosts(uri, &[hosts]) for allowlisted external redirects (OAuth callbacks, payment hand-offs) and Redirect::external_unchecked / ::external_unchecked_permanent / ::external_unchecked_temporary as the explicit unsafe escape hatch where caller asserts the URI is trustworthy. validate_redirect_uri helper centralizes the validation; case-insensitive host matching; IPv6 bracket handling. Eight regression tests: external URI rejected, protocol-relative rejected (with dedicated ProtocolRelative variant for debuggability), backslash rejected, javascript:/data:/file:/ftp: schemes rejected, empty URI rejected, well-formed relative paths accepted including those with query/fragment, allowlist accepts listed hosts (case-insensitive) and rejects others (no subdomain magic), external_unchecked* honors URI verbatim. Only one external caller (a doc-comment in extract.rs:697) and tests in this file — all updated to handle Result. UBS clean (criticals are JS-rule loose-equality false positives + test panic!).

title: Oneshot value drain can strand Receiver::poll_closed waiter
description: src/channel/oneshot.rs Receiver::poll_closed registers receiver_closed_waker, but successful value extraction in RecvUninterruptibleFuture::poll, RecvFuture::poll, and Receiver::try_recv transitions the channel to closed without taking/waking that slot. Receiver::drop also discards a committed value and retains the slot. A poll_closed task can therefore remain parked forever after the terminal value drain, and stale executor state is retained. Fix: take the close waker under OneShotInner's mutex on every terminal value extraction, wake outside the lock, and have Receiver::drop always retire the slot while waking only if the post-drop predicate is closed. Add deterministic counting/reentrant-waker tests for try_recv, recv, recv_uninterruptible, and receiver drop. Independently confirmed by two fresh-eyes reviews 2026-07-15; existing tests cover sender drop and main-waker isolation, not same-channel value-drain closure.

title: runtime: default epoch tracker flags independent per-table counters as cross-module violations on every transition (ERROR flood + hot-path buffer churn)
description:
Every default runtime's epoch tracker reports cross-module "violations" on normal operation: a stream of ERROR events and a bounded buffer churned on the state hot path.

Evidence: default-target sweep DSW2 (exact tree a8d8e5a0b, vmi1149989).
- tests/channel_conformance.rs ran 98 ordinary conformance workloads. During that run the runtime logged 2085 ERROR epoch_consistency_violation events and 8145 WARN epoch_violation_buffer_trimmed events.
- A sample: violation_type="advancement_order_violation" violating_module=ObligationTable advanced_to=Epoch(20202) dependency_module=TaskTable dependency_epoch=Epoch(4421) epoch_skew=15781 consistency_level="strict".
- In the same run perf-002 (channel throughput, at least 100K msg/s) failed: 10K messages took 3441 ms.

Cause:
- RuntimeState keeps one independent epoch counter per table: region, task and obligation. notify_runtime_epoch_advance bumps a table's counter once per mutation of that table.
- The tracker is built with EpochConsistencyTracker::new(), which uses EpochConsistencyConfig::default(): strict_ordering true, max_epoch_skew 2.
- On every transition it then applies two cross-module checks:
  - current_module_desync_violation flags any skew greater than 2 between modules;
  - current_advancement_order_violation flags (ObligationTable after TaskTable), (TaskTable after Scheduler) and so on.
- The counters advance at unrelated rates: a task commits many obligations. Their values are not comparable, so both checks fire on essentially every transition once a workload runs.
- Each violation:
  - is pushed into a Vec capped at 1000 and trimmed with drain(0..excess) (a memmove of the whole buffer), inside the tracker's publication mutex;
  - enqueues a telemetry receipt;
  - is emitted as an ERROR tracing event.
- The config's own docs call relaxed() "suitable for production" and strict() "for testing". The runtime uses neither, and even relaxed()'s skew limit of 5 would still fire constantly.
- The checks were introduced in b4d79b360 / aeb978e03 (2026-04) and have been on by default in every runtime since.

Fix:
- A preset EpochConsistencyConfig::independent_modules() keeps the per-module continuity checks (skipped and non-advancing epochs, which stay meaningful) and turns off cross-module skew and ordering.
- RuntimeState builds its tracker with it (EpochConsistencyTracker::for_runtime_tables()).
- The public presets and their semantics are unchanged; the change is additive.

Acceptance:
- A LabRuntime workload in which one task registers and commits eight obligations records zero violations. It is red on the old config.
- A skipped epoch is still recorded as MissingTransition under the new preset.
- The runtime state, epoch tracker and obligation tests still pass.
- channel_conformance is re-run to see whether perf-002 recovers. That is reported, not claimed.
close_reason: Landed 05cfffcfa: RuntimeState builds its epoch tracker with EpochConsistencyConfig::independent_modules() (per-table continuity checks only; no cross-table skew or ordering). Old red: control 7852068bf recorded 40 violations for 8 obligation commits; DSW2 channel_conformance logged 2085 ERROR plus 8145 buffer trims. New: lib runtime::epoch_tracker and runtime::state 216/0 (vmi1227854); channel_conformance 16/0 with 0 epoch ERROR and 0 trims; clippy lib clean; check all-targets clean (hz4, and the tip b442b2493).

title: GH #77 item 1: a task in a worker's LIFO slot is stranded when next_task returns an early None (cancel-command yield or browser hand-off) and the worker parks
description:
GH #77 ("v0.6.0 release on hold"), "Should fix before 0.6.0", item 1.

Since b9bb41de3 (kpmoy5.1.11, LIFO slot), a task woken into a worker's LIFO slot can be stranded.

Two early `return None`s in ThreeLaneWorker::next_task come before take_lifo_dispatch:
- the yield while cancellation commands are queued (pending_cancel_dispatch_ready, or more handle-cancels than HANDLE_CANCEL_BATCH);
- should_force_ready_handoff (the browser ready hand-off).
run_loop_until's park checks never look at the thread-local slot.

Interleaving:
1. Worker W polls A, which wakes B into W's slot.
2. W's next next_task returns None at one of the early returns.
3. Another worker drains the commands.
4. W parks as a follower with no timeout.
B then waits for an unrelated wake, up to 250 ms if W is the I/O leader.

The slot is filled only while a task executes (EXECUTING is set inside execute() with lifo_enabled), so these two returns are the only way to reach the park with it occupied. run_loop_until already spills the slot to the global lane when its loop stops.

Fix: before either early None, move the slot's task to the global ready lane. The park checks see global ready work, so the worker comes back for it (or another worker steals it).

Test: an early None from next_task (40 queued handle cancels for tasks that do not exist) leaves the slot empty, with the parked task in the global ready lane.

Claimed by SapphireHill (d0).
close_reason: LIFO slot spilled to the global ready lane before next_task's early None (ce2c00819, merge a10c04264); test + control

title: [perf-hot-path] http/h2/hpack.rs: HUFFMAN_DECODE_INDEX uses HashMap<(u32,u8), Option<u8>> (line 16) — cache-miss-prone vs flat lookup table for per-byte hot path
description: src/http/h2/hpack.rs:16 HUFFMAN_DECODE_INDEX is a HashMap<(u32, u8), Option<u8>> with capacity 257. The lookup happens once PER BYTE during HPACK Huffman string decoding — it's the hottest of hot paths. HashMap::get does: hash(key) → bucket → linear probe → match → return. Each probe is a potential cache miss in the bucket array. Compare to the canonical Huffman decode strategy: a flat 2D lookup table indexed directly by the current state and the next nibble/byte (no hashing, single cache line per lookup). Hyper / h2-rs / nginx all use the flat-table approach. The flat table for HPACK Huffman is well-documented (RFC 7541 + standard published implementations); for 256 input bytes with state machine width 16-bit, the lookup table is 65k * 8 bytes = 512 KiB which fits L2. Per-byte savings: ~10ns (HashMap probe + cache miss) vs ~1ns (single indexed load). For a 1 KB Huffman-encoded header value, saving ~9 us of CPU per decode. Mitigation: replace HashMap with const-generated [u16; 65536] state-table (see RFC 7541 Appendix B). Severity HIGH for H2 server header throughput — Huffman decode is on every header value.
close_reason: DEFERRED — needs follow-up bead. Documented in commit e32fd747a why: replacing HUFFMAN_DECODE_INDEX HashMap with a 4-bit-stride state-machine table per RFC 7541 Appendix B is the correct fix but requires generating ~256 states × 16 transitions (~4 KB) at compile-time const-eval or LazyLock init. The existing 5/6/7/8-bit inline fast paths handle the common case; the slow path (HashMap lookup loop over code_len 9..=30) fires only on long codes. Punted to keep batch bounded.

title: [testing-fuzzing] assert postgres bind parameter format codes encode per param
description:
PostgreSQL wire-protocol fuzz/conformance bead.

Problem:
- Bind messages carry parameter format-code counts that can apply globally or per-parameter.
- A parser or encoder that treats all format-code layouts as a single global code can corrupt binary/text parameter interpretation, hide malformed frames, or diverge from PostgreSQL-compatible behavior.

Required design:
1. Drive the production Postgres Bind parser/encoder seam, not a local mock oracle.
2. Cover zero, one, and many parameters with format-code count 0, count 1, and count == parameter_count.
3. Reject count/value mismatches, truncated format-code arrays, unsupported format-code values, and length-prefix inconsistencies without panics.
4. Assert that encoded Bind frames preserve each parameter format code and decoded payload boundary.
5. Keep diagnostics rich enough to explain which parameter index and format-code rule failed.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover global default text format, single global binary format, per-parameter mixed text/binary formats, zero parameters, max bounded parameter count, count mismatch, truncated format-code list, invalid format-code value, malformed parameter length, and panic-free arbitrary bytes. Fuzz/e2e coverage must log parameter count, format-code count, per-parameter code vector, payload length vector, offending index, parser outcome, error kind, round-trip verdict, and corpus label. Validation: rch exec -- cargo check --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml if the fuzz target changes plus targeted rch cargo test/check for postgres Bind parser/encoder surfaces.
close_reason: Implemented Postgres Bind format-code parser/fuzz coverage in src/database/postgres.rs and fuzz/fuzz_targets/postgres_extended_query_bind.rs. Parser now rejects unsupported parameter/result format codes with index diagnostics; tests cover count=0 default text, count=1 global binary, count=N mixed formats, zero params, max bounded params, mismatches, truncated lists/payloads, invalid codes, malformed value length, and panic-free arbitrary bytes. title: TLS 0-RTT acceptor: accepted early data never reaches the app (silent request loss); deprecated enable_early_data fails open into UnprotectedForTesting; raw-config posture misreported
description:
## Findings (SapphireHill 10-01; from the production-backed rewrite of tests/conformance/tls_0rtt_replay_rfc8446.rs for bi2462.144; code read at origin/main 4a9b9f2d6; rustls 0.23.45)

### D1. Early data the server accepts never reaches the application: silent request loss
- With `EarlyDataReplayProtection::UnprotectedForTesting` and a non-zero cap, rustls accepts 0-RTT data into `EarlyDataState::Accepted.received`. Only `ServerConnection::early_data()` can read it (rustls server_conn.rs ~729, ~1129-1200).
- `TlsStream::poll_read` reads only `conn.reader()` (src/tls/stream.rs ~514). The private `TlsConnection` enum (stream.rs ~86-189) exposes no early-data reader.
- The client sees `is_early_data_accepted() == true`, so per RFC 8446 §4.2.10 it does not resend. The request is silently lost.
- Repro: see the NOTES of the rewrite (/data/tmp/rc_20260922/t0rtt/NOTES.md §d D1). A raw rustls ClientConnection writes early_data against an asupersync acceptor built with UnprotectedForTesting + enable_early_data_with_protection(16384); the server TlsStream never yields those bytes.
- This also corrects the threat-model comment at acceptor.rs ~1032-1046 (snv902). That early data is not "processed without screening"; it is dropped.

### D2. The deprecated `TlsAcceptorBuilder::enable_early_data(max)` fails open (acceptor.rs ~814-830)
- It silently switches the default `None` strategy to `UnprotectedForTesting`. `build()` then succeeds with replay-unprotected 0-RTT on the wire, bypassing the ycuuwy "no strategy" refusal (~1009-1018).
- The only signal is a `tracing::error!` under `tracing-integration` (~1019-1027). Default builds give none.

### D3. `TlsAcceptor::new(ServerConfig)` (acceptor.rs ~89-99) bypasses both 0-RTT gates
- A raw config with `max_early_data_size > 0` gives a live 0-RTT acceptor whose `early_data_replay_protection()` reports `None`, so the accessor misreports the live posture.
- This is the documented raw-config escape hatch, so it is lower severity, but the accessor should not lie.

### D4. Connector docs vs code
- connector.rs ~296-305 and ~500-503 say `build()` rejects early_data "+ non-disabled session resumption" without the acknowledgement.
- The code (~1058) rejects it whatever the resumption setting. This is fail-closed, so only the docs are wrong.

### Observation
`TlsConnectorBuilder::enable_early_data(true)` plus the acknowledgement only puts early_data / ChangeCipherSpec / EndOfEarlyData on the wire. No asupersync API writes 0-RTT data (connector.rs ~135-156; stream.rs). The client opt-in exposes a replayable 0-RTT ClientHello and gains nothing.

## Work (needs an owner decision on the 0-RTT story; additive where possible)
1. D1: either deliver early data, through an additive `TlsStream` early-data read API gated by the configured replay protection (`validate_request_for_early_data`), or refuse to enable server 0-RTT until such an API exists, i.e. make UnprotectedForTesting cap max_early_data_size at 0 outside cfg(test). Old-red: the raw-client repro above.
2. D2: the deprecated `enable_early_data` must not silently select UnprotectedForTesting. Either keep `None`, so build() refuses as documented, or emit an always-on (non-tracing) signal. This is a behaviour change on a deprecated API, so it needs owner sign-off.
3. D3: report the live posture, e.g. `early_data_replay_protection()` says `Unknown`/raw when the config enables early data.
4. D4: fix the connector docs.

Evidence suite: tests/conformance/tls_0rtt_replay_rfc8446.rs (production-backed rewrite) pins the current refusal and acceptance rows, so changes here will show up as row changes.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SapphireHill (rc_20260923) 2026-10-05: scoped D1 for a fix and stopped; this needs an owner decision first.
- Mechanics (rustls 0.23.45): accepted 0-RTT bytes stay in EarlyDataState::Accepted after the handshake completes and are readable only through ServerConnection::early_data(). TlsStream::poll_read reads only conn.reader(), so draining early data first in poll_read (server side) would deliver it in stream order. A small change in src/tls/stream.rs.
- Why I did not: today the silent drop is also what keeps replayed 0-RTT requests from reaching the application on the paths that accept 0-RTT without a replay strategy: the deprecated TlsAcceptorBuilder::enable_early_data(max) (D2, fails open to UnprotectedForTesting) and TlsAcceptor::new with a raw ServerConfig (D3). Delivering early data on those paths turns request loss into replay exposure.
- Proposal: (1) deliver early data only when the acceptor has a real anti-replay strategy; (2) everywhere else, reject early data at the TLS layer (ServerConnection::reject_early_data), so the client resends over 1-RTT and nothing is lost or replayed; (3) close D2/D3 by making the deprecated builder and raw configs take the same gate. (1)-(3) change observable acceptor behaviour, so they need your go-ahead.
- The conformance case "early_data_delivery_unobservable" in tests/conformance/tls_0rtt_replay_rfc8446.rs cites src/tls/stream.rs line numbers; whoever fixes this should turn it into a production check (the repro is in /data/tmp/rc_20260922/t0rtt/NOTES.md D1).

title: scheduler: governor drain-throttle strands a notify()-claimed task in Notified forever (and is dead code in production)
description: src/runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs:2419-2433 (inject_global_ready_checked). inject_ready()/schedule_internal consume the exclusive Idle->Notified claim via wake_state.notify()==true, then call inject_global_ready_checked which, when should_throttle_spawns() is true, returns WITHOUT enqueueing and WITHOUT clearing wake_state. The task is then in no lane with wake_state==Notified; every future notify() dedups to false, so nothing re-enqueues it and its join hangs forever. This is the cross-thread WAKE path for existing tasks, not just new spawns. Confirmed by BOTH independent scheduler reviews (a9a04916, abb6d84). Also dead in production: should_throttle_spawns() reads self.workers.first(), but builder.rs:4045 take_workers() empties the vec before workers run, so the throttle can only fire in harnesses/lab that keep workers in place. DESIGN DECISION for owner: the drop-during-drain behavior is intentional+tested (three_lane.rs:14290 asserts 'Ready queue should not grow when governor is throttling' + inject_ready_bypass_governor exists), so cannot just 'schedule anyway'. Options: only throttle genuine spawns (never Wake intents); or route should_throttle_spawns through shared state so it works in production; and clear wake_state / preserve liveness for wakes. I reverted an attempted schedule-anyway fix because it broke the tested contract.
close_reason: Exact duplicate already resolved and proven by b0dc97a50/asupersync-rvkq9k; current source audit confirms the drop gate remains absent.

title: [security-audit] tls/connector.rs: load_pem_file uses naive splitter, accepts non-CA certs as trust anchors
description: src/tls/connector.rs:312-331 load_pem_file() implements its own PEM parser by splitting on the literal string '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----' WITHOUT requiring line-boundary anchoring. A crafted file that embeds the marker inside a comment, header, or other PEM block could be split into spurious blocks whose base64 decodes to attacker-chosen DER. Worse: the resulting Certificate is added to the root store via self.root_certs.add(&Certificate::from_der(der)) WITHOUT any check that the parsed cert is actually a CA (basicConstraints CA:TRUE, KeyUsage keyCertSign). A non-CA leaf cert added as a trust anchor would let any cert it 'signed' be accepted by webpki — a complete trust bypass. Fix: replace the hand-rolled splitter with rustls_pemfile::certs() (already used in src/tls/types.rs Certificate::from_pem) which validates PEM structure, AND add a basicConstraints+KeyUsage gate before insertion. Severity MEDIUM (requires SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR control to exploit — but combines with the env-var injection bead asupersync-gq7l9i).
close_reason: Coordinated batch fix landed in 7d5c62afc. gq7l9i: env-var trust-anchor loading (SSL_CERT_FILE/REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE/CURL_CA_BUNDLE/SSL_CERT_DIR) is now off by default; explicit opt-in via TlsConnectorBuilder::enable_env_cert_loading(); honoured paths log at warn! with loaded/rejected counts; with_native_roots rustdoc updated. 0owoem: load_pem_file replaced hand-rolled splitter with rustls_pemfile::certs(); each candidate gated on BasicConstraints CA:TRUE via x509-parser (already an optional tls-feature dep) by new is_ca_certificate() helper; non-CA certs rejected and counted. p7369s: with_crl_pem() / with_crl_pems() builder setters added; build() constructs WebPkiServerVerifier with attached CRLs via dangerous().with_custom_certificate_verifier when at least one CRL is configured, falling back to the default verifier path when none are. 7wnl2l: test_build_empty_roots inverted to assert empty-roots IS rejected (matches the existing build()-time guard); paired positive test test_build_with_test_root_succeeds added. Six new regression tests total. Lib + tls-feature lib compile clean (7d5c62afc)

title: quic_native: ReceivedPacketTracker::ranges unbounded + full re-sort per gap packet (receiver CPU O(n log n)/gap on lossy transfers)
description: src/net/quic_native/connection.rs:2218-2256 (observe). The SACK 'ranges' Vec has no cap and every gap-creating (out-of-order/post-loss) packet does push + full sort_by over the whole vec + a merge-rebuild. Lost/skipped PNs are never filled (QUIC reuses fresh PNs), so ranges accrete; on a 500M transfer at ~10% loss (~42K gaps) the tail observe() sorts ~42K elements -> ~O(G^2 log G) total receiver CPU (tens of seconds) plus a permanently retained vec. ack_frame() only bounds the ENCODED ranges (MAX_ACK_FRAME_RANGES=96), not the tracker. Fix: cap ranges.len() (drop oldest beyond a few hundred; legal per RFC9000 13.2.3, same rationale as the frame cap) and replace push+sort with an ordered binary-search insert so observe() is O(log n). Confirmed by wide-net review (agent accf3581/ae0a56ca). Real receiver-side scaling problem on exactly the lossy bulk workloads ATP targets.

title: [fresh-eyes] tls_conformance_harness.rs:430 prop_monotonic_sequences_match treats CryptoLevel::Initial as no-op for impl, ref rejects regression — divergent property
description:
src/net/quic_native/tls_conformance_harness.rs:430-434 — prop_monotonic_sequences_match maps CryptoLevel::Initial in the impl branch to Ok(()) (line 431), so the impl always 'accepts' Initial regardless of current level. The reference machine RefCryptoLevelMachine::advance_level (line 30-42) returns Err(InvalidTransition) when target < current_level, which fires for Initial after Handshake/OneRtt. With arb_crypto_sequence producing 0..5 uniform draws from {Initial, Handshake, OneRtt}, sequences like [OneRtt, Initial] yield ref_levels=[OneRtt] vs impl_levels=[OneRtt, Initial] — a property mismatch. Either: (a) ref should match impl no-op semantics for Initial (current QuicTlsMachine has no Initial regression check), or (b) impl test branch should call advance_to(Initial) once that exists. Without one of these, the property is logically inconsistent and may fire on shrinking. The fact that this hasn't been observed in CI suggests the test may not be running or the proptest seed is hitting only monotonic sequences. Either way the assertion logic is broken — file fix.

LOW — test-quality, not production.

title: [bug-hunt] web/middleware.rs CorsPolicy::default sets allow_headers = ["*"] which is overly permissive in CORS preflight responses
description: src/web/middleware.rs:103 default sets allow_headers = vec!["*".to_string()]. Per Fetch spec §3.2.4 the wildcard "*" in Access-Control-Allow-Headers grants access to ALL request headers — equivalent to "no client-side header filtering whatsoever". For developers building APIs that explicitly accept only a small header allowlist (e.g. Authorization, Content-Type, X-Request-Id), the default invites them to never tighten this and ship with unbounded preflight allowance. Severity MEDIUM. Suggested fix: change default to a conservative explicit allowlist (Authorization, Content-Type, Accept, Origin) and leave wildcard as a deliberate opt-in via CorsPolicy::with_any_headers() builder.
close_reason: Fixed in 45c7a9743: CorsPolicy::default allow_headers narrowed from vec!["*"] to a safe-by-default allowlist of [Accept, Accept-Language, Content-Type, Authorization, X-Requested-With]. Wildcard remains available via the explicit opt-in constructor CorsPolicy::with_any_headers() so the loosened security posture is visible at the call site. 3 regression tests pin the contract: default has no wildcard entry; preflight response does NOT echo arbitrary requested headers (X-Evil-Internal, X-Internal-Auth, X-Backend-Token); with_any_headers() opt-in restores wildcard. Behavior change: existing consumers relying on default wildcard must migrate to explicit list or with_any_headers().

2. src/net/atp/protocol/outcome.rs:1164-1186 `parse_atp_cancel_reason`: the transfer transcript derives `cancellation_source` from `CancelReason::message()` by ordered substring tests ("timeout" before "shutdown" before "user" ...). `CancelReason::kind()` already carries `CancelKind::{User, Timeout, Deadline, FailFast, ...}`; a user cancel whose message mentions a timeout is recorded as `AtpCancelReason::Timeout`, and any message containing "user" (e.g. "user-data checksum mismatch") becomes `UserCancel`.
