title: [mock-code-finder][trace] Remove trace golden broad clippy suppression
description:
## Context
The README promises deterministic trace replay, canonical trace fingerprints, divergence-report stability, and golden artifacts that downstream replay tooling can trust. `tests/trace_golden_artifacts.rs` is the focused integration-test contract for that surface, but it still has a crate-level `#![allow(clippy::all)]` suppression. That broad suppressor hides future lint regressions in the exact file that should be high-signal for stable trace artifacts.

## Scope
Touch only `tests/trace_golden_artifacts.rs` unless a local lint in that file proves a narrower, documented allow is required. Remove the broad top-level `#![allow(clippy::all)]`. Preserve all existing snapshot names, fixture semantics, deterministic IDs/timestamps, assertions, and comments unless a lint-driven edit is behavior-neutral and improves clarity. Do not delete files, snapshots, or artifacts. Do not update insta snapshots unless a test failure proves an intentional contract change; this bead is intended to be no-behavior-change cleanup.

## User-facing benefit
Trace replay and postmortem tooling are only useful if their golden contracts fail loudly when they drift. Removing the broad suppression makes this trace artifact lane easier for users and operators to trust because future clippy warnings in the golden test must be resolved deliberately instead of hidden.

## Implementation plan
1. Reserve the source file with Agent Mail before editing.
2. Run the focused baseline through `rch` and capture the pass/fail status before any edit.
3. Remove the broad suppressor and make only local, behavior-preserving lint fixes if `clippy -D warnings` requires them. Prefer code clarity over adding new narrow allows; add a narrow allow only if the lint conflicts with the purpose of deterministic golden diagnostics.
4. Re-run focused formatting, snapshot tests, and scoped clippy through `rch`.
5. Commit only the reserved source path plus this bead status change; do not stage peer-owned dirty files or smoke artifact directories.

## Required proof commands and logging
Baseline unit/integration proof with deterministic test output:
`timeout 900 rch exec -- env CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 RUSTFLAGS='-C debuginfo=0' CARGO_TARGET_DIR=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rch_target_trace_golden_baseline cargo test -p asupersync --test trace_golden_artifacts --features test-internals -- --nocapture`

Post-edit structural checks:
`rg -n '^#!\[allow\((warnings|clippy::all)\)\]' tests/trace_golden_artifacts.rs` must return no matches for `clippy::all`.
`git diff --check -- tests/trace_golden_artifacts.rs` must pass.
`timeout 300 rch exec -- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check tests/trace_golden_artifacts.rs` must pass.

Post-edit unit/integration proof with detailed logging:
`timeout 900 rch exec -- env CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 RUSTFLAGS='-C debuginfo=0' CARGO_TARGET_DIR=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rch_target_trace_golden_test cargo test -p asupersync --test trace_golden_artifacts --features test-internals -- --nocapture`

Post-edit lint proof:
`timeout 900 rch exec -- env CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 RUSTFLAGS='-C debuginfo=0' CARGO_TARGET_DIR=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rch_target_trace_golden_clippy cargo clippy -p asupersync --test trace_golden_artifacts --features test-internals -- -D warnings`

If any proof fails, record the exact command, exit status, first failing test or lint, and whether the failure is pre-existing, local to the touched file, or a shared-main external blocker.

## Acceptance criteria
- The broad `#![allow(clippy::all)]` suppression is gone from `tests/trace_golden_artifacts.rs`.
- The trace golden snapshots and deterministic fixtures are behaviorally unchanged.
- Focused baseline and post-edit `trace_golden_artifacts` tests pass through `rch` with `--nocapture` output.
- Scoped clippy for the test target either passes or fails only on an explicitly documented external shared-main blocker, with no diagnostics in the touched file.
- The closeout commit references `[br-asupersync-<id>]`, and the bead close notes summarize proof results and any residual risk.

## Review pass
This bead is intentionally narrow and optimal for the current no-ready-work state: it improves a user-visible reliability signal, avoids active peer-owned files, does not add new abstraction or feature scope, and keeps all validation focused on the trace artifact contract. It should not be expanded into trace algorithm changes, snapshot refreshes, or broad test-suite cleanup.

Verified current file has no broad clippy::all/warnings crate-level suppression. Mail thread records rch baseline 8/8 pass, post-edit rch test 8/8 pass, rustfmt check pass, git diff --check pass, and clippy limited to the touched-file cleanup with no diagnostics in tests/trace_golden_artifacts.rs.

title: Obligation/cancel audit: cancel-broadcast dedup is check-then-act (a message is forwarded twice per hop); cancel_with stamps a fake 1 s timestamp; panic token drops uncounted; LOWs
description:
Read-only audit of src/obligation/, src/cancel/, src/record/obligation.rs, the Cx cancellation API (src/cx/cx.rs) and src/types/cancel.rs at origin/main 2e816db92 (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-04; read from origin). No HIGH.

## MEDIUM
1. Cancel broadcast dedup is check-then-act (src/cancel/symbol_cancel.rs receive_message ~1221-1226, mark_seen ~1384-1407): is_seen (read lock) then mark_seen (write lock, silently returns when present). Two handle_message tasks receiving the same CancelMessage from two peers (the normal mesh case) both pass is_seen, both count received, cancel and return Some(forwarded): the relay is sent twice per hop (the amplification the dedup exists to stop); duplicates undercounts. Fix: mark_seen returns SeenSequences::insert's bool; drop the separate is_seen.

## LOW
2. retry_failed_broadcasts (~1343-1353) re-inserts a failed front message at original_queue_len, behind messages pushed during the in-flight retry, breaking the documented FIFO. Fix: push_front.
3. Cx::cancel_with (cx.rs ~3670) builds CancelReason::new(kind), whose timestamp is hard-coded to 1 s (types/cancel.rs ~596-601); strengthen breaks equal-severity ties by earlier timestamp, so a later cancel_with(Timeout) can replace a real-time Deadline reason (origin, task, message lost; is_budget_exceeded flips; uptime-dependent). Fix: with_origin(kind, region, current checkpoint time).with_task(task).
4. ObligationToken<K>::drop during a panic returns without PANIC_LEAK_TRACKER.record_panic_leak() (graded.rs ~994-996), unlike GradedObligation; panic_leak_count undercounts (session permits, NameLease, DB transaction tokens).
5. Static leak checker (leak_check.rs ~632-634, join ~72-74): commit/abort on MayHold goes to Resolved with no diagnostic, so a double resolve on one branch path is reported clean.

## Design note
ObligationLedger::mark_region_finalized accepts a region with pending obligations (module invariant 3 not enforced; tests assert this). Additive try_mark_region_finalized -> Result would keep compatibility.

## Checked and sound
ObligationRecord transitions, ledger validation/stats/generation, Cx::checkpoint/checkpoint_with mask semantics, masked depth accounting, cancel waker check-register-recheck and dispatch, strengthen monotonicity, CancelWitness, SymbolCancelToken publication order and listener catch-up, CleanupCoordinator lock order.
close_reason: done

description:
## Purpose
Implement a test oracle that verifies the "no obligation leaks" invariant: all obligations (SendPermit, Ack, Lease, IoOp) are either committed or aborted before their owning region closes.

## The Invariant
From asupersync_plan_v4.md:
> Permits/acks/leases must be committed or aborted; no silent drops

Formally: `∀o ∈ obligations: state(o) ∈ {Committed, Aborted}` at region close

## Obligation Lifecycle
```
Created → [Committed | Aborted]
```

An obligation leak occurs when an obligation exists in Created state when its region closes.

## Oracle Design

```rust
pub struct ObligationLeakOracle {
    // Tracks all obligation lifecycle events
    creates: Vec<(ObligationId, ObligationKind, RegionId, Time)>,
    resolutions: Vec<(ObligationId, ObligationState, Time)>,  // Committed or Aborted
    region_closes: Vec<(RegionId, Time)>,
}

impl ObligationLeakOracle {
    /// Called when reserve() creates obligation
    pub fn on_create(&mut self, id: ObligationId, kind: ObligationKind, region: RegionId, time: Time);
    
    /// Called when commit() or abort() resolves obligation
    pub fn on_resolve(&mut self, id: ObligationId, state: ObligationState, time: Time);
    
    /// Called when region closes
    pub fn on_region_close(&mut self, region: RegionId, time: Time);
    
    /// Verify invariant holds
    pub fn check(&self) -> Result<(), ObligationLeakViolation>;
}
```

## Violation Detection
```rust
pub struct ObligationLeakViolation {
    pub region: RegionId,
    pub leaked_obligations: Vec<ObligationId>,
    pub kinds: Vec<ObligationKind>,  // SendPermit, Ack, Lease, IoOp
    pub region_close_time: Time,
}
```

A violation occurs when:
1. Region R closes at time T
2. ∃ obligation O in R with state ∉ {Committed, Aborted} at time T

## Obligation Kinds and Their Semantics
| Kind | Created By | Committed By | Aborted By |
|------|-----------|--------------|------------|
| SendPermit | tx.reserve() | permit.send() | permit.abort() or Drop |
| Ack | receive message | ack.commit() | ack.nack() |
| Lease | acquire_lease() | lease.release() | lease.expire() |
| IoOp | io.start() | io.complete() | io.cancel() |

## Linear Type Enforcement
The oracle complements Rust's ownership model:
- In ideal code, obligations are `#[must_use]` and consumed exactly once
- Oracle catches runtime violations that slip through static checks
- Particularly important for dynamic scenarios (vec of obligations, etc.)

## Testing the Oracle
1. **Correct case**: All obligations resolved → check passes
2. **Leak cases by kind**: Each obligation type can leak → check catches
3. **Nested regions**: Inner region obligations must resolve before inner closes
4. **Cancellation**: Cancelled tasks must still resolve their obligations (via abort)

## References
- asupersync_plan_v4.md: §4.4 Obligation Registry, §6.5 Two-Phase Operations
- asupersync_v4_formal_semantics.md: Invariant I2 (obligation_resolved)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Oracle flags any leaked obligation (task completes with unresolved reserved obligations).
- Supports per-kind accounting (permits/acks/leases/ioops) and region-scoped checks.
- Diagnostics include obligation id, kind, holder task, and owning region.
- Deterministic; usable on both trace events and direct registry snapshots.
close_reason: Implemented oracle module with TaskLeakOracle, ObligationLeakOracle, QuiescenceOracle, LoserDrainOracle, FinalizerOracle. All tests passing, clippy clean.

title: main broken under --all-features: atp_native_sdk_transfer test won't compile (runtime cap-rejection test vs compile-time cap model)
description:
DEFECT: cargo check --all-targets --all-features --keep-going FAILS on hz3 (RCH remote, verified 2026-09-16): error[E0308] at tests/atp_native_sdk/uploads.rs:248 in test target atp_native_sdk_transfer. Default --all-targets is CLEAN; only --all-features exposes it (the src/net/atp/sdk/native module is feature-gated), so routine default checks silently skip it — the exact class AGENTS.md warns hides for weeks.

ROOT CAUSE: fresh peer work c4541a4bc (engine) + 5591fb7f7 (test), both 2026-09-15 ~22:18-22:26. The upload engine has a RUNTIME capability-rejection design: validate_upload (src/net/atp/sdk/native/upload.rs:236) does 'let caps = cx.capabilities(); if !caps.io || !caps.entropy || !caps.time { return Err(NativeUploadError::MissingCapability) }', and the test native_upload_missing_capability_never_polls_or_spools_input constructs a no-cap Cx (Cx::detached_cancel_context() = Cx<CapSet<false,false,false,false,false>>) to exercise that rejection without polling/spooling the input. BUT send_reader takes cx: &Cx (defaults to Cx<cap::All> = CapSet<true,true,true,true,true>), and upload_admitted calls cx.random_bytes() (needs entropy) + spool I/O (needs io) which require cap::All at COMPILE time. So: (1) you cannot pass a reduced-cap Cx to send_reader (compile error = the E0308); (2) the runtime validate_upload cap check is provably DEAD for a cap::All Cx; (3) the test asserts a compile-impossible scenario.

This is the ONLY runtime capability-rejection in all of src/net/; every other cap-requiring host API uses compile-time &Cx<cap::All> (e.g. src/net/atp/quic/packet_protection.rs). There is NO capability-elevation API (runtime-check -> Cx<cap::All>).

RESOLUTION OPTIONS:
(A) Accept compile-time enforcement (idiomatic, and a STRONGER guarantee than the test's runtime goal: you literally cannot call upload without caps). Retire the compile-impossible test and the dead validate_upload cap check. KEEP the pub NativeUploadError::MissingCapability variant (removing it is a 0.4.x backwards-compat break) as harmless defensive dead code, OR keep the runtime check as belt-and-suspenders and only fix the test. Simplest; makes main green.
(B) Make reduced-capability uploads a real feature: build a capability-elevation primitive (runtime cap check that yields a typed Cx<cap::All>), make the upload chain generic over the capset, validate_upload rejects before any I/O. Bigger; a new Cx primitive.

RECOMMENDATION: (A) with minimal footprint — the author's safety intent ('missing cap never touches input') is already achieved MORE strongly by the compile-time model. Needs the author's/owner's design confirmation since it retires their fresh test. Found by SapphireHill via RCH --all-features readiness check.
close_reason: RESOLVED by the author + MY DIAGNOSIS WAS PARTLY WRONG. The E0308 I caught was against the STALE pre-fix snapshot 5591fb7f7 (which used Cx::detached_cancel_context() = a compile-time no-cap Cx). The author fixed it in parallel: commit 7ba229f91 'test(atp-sdk): deny uploads under an ambient CapMask::none restriction' changed the test to Cx::push_restriction(CapMask::none()) + Cx::current(). RETRACTION: my claim that 'the runtime validate_upload capability check is dead code' and 'the test is compile-impossible' was WRONG. push_restriction narrows capabilities at RUNTIME while Cx::current() keeps the compile-time type Cx<cap::All>, so send_reader compiles AND validate_upload's runtime check meaningfully returns MissingCapability. The design is coherent (compile-time caps = ceiling, runtime restrictions attenuate). VERIFIED: cargo check --all-targets --all-features --keep-going on current HEAD = 0 errors, [RCH] remote hz3 (736s), Finished 11m55s. main is all-features-clean. No code change from me was needed. Author SapphireHill (the real finding: main was briefly broken by the pre-fix snapshot, now fixed).

description:
# Comprehensive Unit Test Suite

## Purpose
Provide thorough unit test coverage for all Phase 0 components with deterministic execution and high-quality diagnostics.

Core principle:
- **tests should be reproducible** (lab runtime seed/config)
- **failures should be explainable** (trace dump + invariant evidence)

## Logging / Diagnostics Strategy (No `tracing` dependency)
We avoid relying on global logging infrastructure in core tests.

Plan-of-record:
- Use the runtime’s own `TraceBuffer` + `TraceFormatter`.
- On assertion failure, dump:
  - formatted trace
  - invariant violation evidence
  - first divergence step for replay/determinism checks

This aligns with the “no stdout/stderr in core” rule while still allowing tests to print helpful debug output.

## Test Categories

### 1) Core Type Tests
- Outcome severity ordering and aggregation laws
- CancelReason ordering + strengthen laws
- Budget product semantics laws
- Identifier invariants
- Policy aggregation / fail-fast behavior

### 2) State Machine Tests
- TaskState valid/invalid transitions
- RegionState lifecycle rules
- ObligationState terminal absorption

### 3) Registry/Arena Tests
- Task/Region/Obligation arenas behave correctly
- ObligationRegistry leak detection and marking projection

### 4) Scheduler/Waker/Timer Tests
- Cancel lane priority
- Timer wake behavior
- Wake dedup invariants

### 5) Cancellation/Finalization Tests
- cancel propagation
- bounded masking
- finalizer LIFO ordering

### 6) Combinator Tests
- join/race/timeout semantics
- loser draining

### 7) Two-Phase Primitive Tests
- oneshot reserve/commit/abort
- MPSC reserve/commit + receiver ack/nack (if implemented)

## Property-Based Testing
Use `proptest` to test algebraic laws:
- Outcome lattice laws
- Budget meet laws
- CancelReason strengthen laws

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Deterministic: tests pass under fixed seeds.
2. Diagnostics: failures dump trace and evidence.
3. Coverage: all Phase 0 components have targeted unit tests.

DEPENDS ON

- Trace infrastructure

title: [AUDIT] Deep correctness audit: src/http/h2/frame.rs

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Deep Audit: src/http/h2/frame.rs (1948 lines)

**Verdict: 1 MEDIUM bug found**

### BUG: Unknown frame types rejected instead of ignored (MEDIUM)

**Location**: `parse_frame()` line 1058
**Impact**: RFC 7540 compliance violation; interop failure with HTTP/2 extensions

`parse_frame()` returns `H2Error::protocol("unknown frame type: ...")` for unrecognized frame type bytes. However, RFC 7540 §4.1 explicitly mandates:

> Implementations MUST ignore and discard any frame that has a type that is unknown.

This means any peer sending extension frames (which is permitted by the spec) will trigger a connection error and tear down the session. The function should return something like `Ok(None)` or a dedicated `Frame::Unknown` variant to let the caller skip the frame.

### Analysis

HTTP/2 binary frame parser implementing all 10 frame types from RFC 7540 §4-§6.

**FrameHeader parse/write (lines 122-157):**
- Correct 24-bit length, 8-bit type, 8-bit flags, 31-bit stream ID (reserved bit masked with & 0x7f) in both directions
- Roundtrip-tested with high-bit stream IDs

**Per-frame validation (all correct):**
- DATA: stream_id != 0, PADDED handling (pad_length byte + overflow check + strip) ✓
- HEADERS: stream_id != 0, padding → priority → strip order correct per §6.2, self-dependency rejection ✓
- PRIORITY: stream_id != 0, exact 5 bytes → stream-level FrameSizeError (correct per §6.3), self-dependency check ✓
- RST_STREAM: stream_id != 0, exact 4 bytes ✓
- SETTINGS: stream_id == 0, ACK+payload rejected, length%6 check, ENABLE_PUSH 0/1 validation ✓
- PUSH_PROMISE: stream_id != 0, PADDED handling, min 4 bytes for promised_stream_id ✓
- PING: stream_id == 0, exact 8 bytes ✓
- GOAWAY: stream_id == 0, min 8 bytes, debug_data as remainder ✓
- WINDOW_UPDATE: exact 4 bytes, zero increment → connection error on stream 0, stream error on stream != 0 (correctly differentiated per §6.9) ✓
- CONTINUATION: stream_id != 0 ✓

**Encoders:** All 10 encode methods correct. Reserved bits properly masked on stream_id, last_stream_id, promised_stream_id, and increment. Priority exclusive bit correctly OR'd into dependency field.

**Design note (not a bug):** SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE (must be <= 2^31-1, §6.5.2 FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR) and SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE (must be in [16384, 16777215], §6.5.2 PROTOCOL_ERROR) are not range-validated at parse time, while ENABLE_PUSH is. This validation may be deferred to the connection layer when applying settings, but the inconsistency is notable.

**Tests:** 47 tests covering roundtrips for all 10 types, invalid inputs (zero stream IDs, wrong sizes, bad padding, self-dependency), size limits, flag validation, setting variants. Good coverage.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
**CORRECTION**: The unknown frame type error in parse_frame (line 1058) is unreachable from production code. connection.rs line 105-107 already filters unknown frame types with FrameType::from_u8().is_none() + continue BEFORE calling parse_frame. The implementation IS RFC-compliant at the connection layer.

Downgrading to DESIGN NOTE: parse_frame's API is defensive-only here. The error path exists as a safety net for any direct callers but is never hit in production.

**Revised verdict: SOUND — no bugs.**

description:
# Admission Control / Backpressure (Per Region)

## Purpose
The design calls out admission control and backpressure as core scheduling features:
- throttle spawn/admission per region
- apply backpressure at reserve points (two-phase effects)
- integrate priority into scheduling/budget decisions

Even if Phase 0 is minimal, we must track this as part of the scheduler’s long-term contract.

## Requirements
- Define region-level limits:
  - max live children
  - max outstanding obligations
- Define backpressure signals surfaced to users:
  - reserve waits

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
Stale agent verification (ac74712 - sync/pool.rs):

**CONFIRMED BUG: total_acquisitions incorrectly decremented (line 1221)**

When an idle resource fails health check, the code decrements total_acquisitions:
```rust
// Line 1221
state.total_acquisitions = state.total_acquisitions.saturating_sub(1);
```

This is semantically wrong - total_acquisitions is documented as:
- 'Total acquisitions since pool creation' (line 337)
- 'Lifetime acquisition count' (line 180)

It should be monotonic. The active count decrement (line 1220) is correct since the resource isn't used, but the acquisition was still attempted. Decrementing total_acquisitions corrupts pool metrics.

**Fix:** Remove line 1221 entirely. Only decrement state.active, not total_acquisitions.

Other findings (double-count asymmetry) are MINOR/style - not correctness bugs.

comments.text:
## pool.rs Full Audit (2515 lines) - SapphireHill

### Finding 1: TOCTOU in can_create() - pool can exceed max_size (NEW BUG)
Severity: Medium | Lines 1128-1131, 1243-1257

can_create() checks total_count() < max_size under lock, releases lock, then create_resource().await runs without lock, then record_acquisition() re-acquires lock. Under concurrent load, N tasks can all pass the check simultaneously, all create resources, and all call record_acquisition(), causing active to exceed max_size.

Impact: Pool over-provisions beyond configured max_size. Self-correcting (subsequent can_create() calls see the inflated count), but violates the active + idle <= max_size invariant temporarily.

Fix: Speculatively increment active (or a creating counter) inside can_create() before releasing the lock. On factory failure, decrement. This is the standard async pool pattern.

### Finding 2: total_acquisitions decrement (KNOWN - previously reported)
Severity: Low | Line 1221

When health check fails on an idle resource, total_acquisitions is decremented via saturating_sub(1). The field is documented as Total acquisitions since pool creation (line 337) - a monotone counter. Decrementing breaks monotonicity for external observers doing periodic sampling.

### Finding 3: Redundant unsafe impl Send (STYLE)
Severity: None (correctness ok) | Lines 516-517

PooledResource has unsafe impl Send. All fields (Option R, ReturnObligation bool, mpsc Sender, Instant) auto-derive Send when R: Send. The manual impl is unnecessary but harmless.

### Finding 4: Crate uses deny not forbid
lib.rs line 50: deny(unsafe_code) - MEMORY.md previously stated forbid. The allow(unsafe_code) on pool.rs line 516 is valid because deny can be overridden by allow (forbid cannot).

### Verdict: 1 new bug (TOCTOU), 1 known issue, 2 informational. Tests (lines 1800-2515) are thorough.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
## notify.rs Audit (628 lines) - SapphireHill

### Finding 1: Lost wakeup race in notify_one / Notified::poll (BUG - HIGH SEVERITY)
Lines 146-167 (notify_one) + 244-291 (poll Init)

Race condition between notify_one storing a notification and Notified::poll registering as a waiter:

1. poll(Init): checks stored_notifications (lockless, line 247) -> sees 0
2. poll(Init): checks generation (lockless, line 270) -> same as initial
3. Thread B: notify_one() acquires lock, scans entries, finds no waiters, drops lock (line 165)
4. Thread B: increments stored_notifications (line 166) -> now 1
5. Thread A: acquires lock, registers waiter at index i, drops lock, returns Pending

Result: stored_notifications = 1, waiter registered but never woken. Future hangs permanently.

Root cause: stored_notifications is incremented OUTSIDE the lock in notify_one (line 165-166), but the check happens BEFORE the lock in poll (line 247). No serialization between the two paths.

Additionally, the Waiting state (lines 293-330) never re-checks stored_notifications, so even if the future were spuriously re-polled, it wouldn't find the stored notification.

Fix (two-part):
1. In notify_one: move stored_notifications.fetch_add inside the lock (before drop(waiters))
2. In poll Init: re-check stored_notifications AFTER acquiring the lock, before registering the waiter. If stored > 0, CAS decrement and return Ready.

This ensures: either notify_one sees our waiter (notifies directly) or we see its stored notification (consume it).

### WaiterSlab design: SOUND
- Slot reuse via free_slots prevents unbounded Vec growth
- Tail shrinking correctly preserves notified entries (notified=true prevents shrinking)
- Tests verify no-growth invariant under repeated cancel cycles

### notify_waiters: SOUND
- Generation-based approach avoids the stored_notifications race (generation is checked locklessly and is monotone)
- Wakers collected under lock, woken after lock release (correct)

### Verdict: 1 HIGH severity lost-wakeup bug. WaiterSlab design and notify_waiters are SOUND.

comments.text:
## semaphore.rs Audit (917 lines) - SapphireHill

### Finding 1: Missing cascading wakeup in OwnedAcquireFuture (BUG - MEDIUM)
Lines 488-495 vs 287-301

AcquireFuture::poll (lines 290-297) wakes the next waiter when permits > 0 after a successful acquire:
```
if state.permits > 0 {
    if let Some(next) = state.waiters.front() {
        next.waker.wake_by_ref();
    }
}
```

OwnedAcquireFuture::poll (lines 488-495) is missing this logic entirely.

Impact: When add_permits(N) satisfies multiple waiters and the front waiter uses OwnedAcquireFuture, subsequent waiters stay blocked until the front waiter drops its permit. Permits are available but not distributed.

Fix: Add the same cascading wakeup block to OwnedAcquireFuture::poll after the successful acquire path (line 490, before the return).

### Design: SOUND otherwise
- FIFO fairness: try_acquire rejects when queue non-empty (no queue jumping)
- Cancel/drop: front-waiter delegation (wakes next) prevents lost wakeups
- add_permits: correctly wakes front waiter only (chain propagates via acquire-success wakeup... except for the OwnedAcquireFuture path)
- OwnedSemaphorePermit::try_acquire: correctly uses mem::forget to prevent double-release

### Verdict: 1 MEDIUM bug (missing cascading wakeup in OwnedAcquireFuture). Otherwise SOUND.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
## rwlock.rs Audit (1,281 lines) - SapphireHill

### Verdict: SOUND - No bugs found

### Architecture
- Dual tracking: StdMutex<State> for async coordination, StdRwLock<T> for data access
- Writer-preference fairness: writer_waiters > 0 blocks new readers
- Arc<AtomicBool> waiter liveness tracking (same pattern as mutex.rs)

### Key Correctness Properties Verified

1. **Guard Drop ordering** (lines 662-673, 696-706): StdRwLock guard dropped BEFORE calling release_reader/release_writer. Otherwise woken writers/readers would block on the still-held std lock.

2. **Baton-passing** in ReadFuture::Drop (477-503): If dequeued by drain_reader_waiters but dropped without acquiring, wakes a writer if readers==0 && writer_waiters>0.

3. **Baton-passing** in WriteFuture::Drop (600-644): If dequeued by pop_writer_waiter but dropped without acquiring, wakes next writer. Also drains reader_waiters when writer_waiters reaches 0 (critical: unblocks readers when last pending writer cancels).

4. **writer_waiters counting**: Increment on first poll (counted=false→true), decrement on acquire (counted back to false) or drop (if counted). Never double-decremented.

5. **can_acquire logic** (line 536-537): `!writer_active && readers == 0 && (dequeued || writer_waiters == 1)`. FIFO among writers: only the dequeued waiter or the sole waiter can acquire.

6. **Owned variants** (OwnedRwLockReadGuard, OwnedRwLockWriteGuard): Don't hold StdRwLock guards; use with_read/with_write for ad-hoc access. State tracking (readers count / writer_active) prevents concurrent access. This is safe because all acquisition paths check the state before accessing the StdRwLock.

7. **Poisoning consistency**: Flag set during panic before StdRwLock guard drops, so by the time release_reader/release_writer runs, the flag is set.

### Test coverage: Good
- Multiple readers, write exclusion, writer-blocks-readers, cancellation during read/write wait, try_read/try_write, guard release on drop, get_mut, into_inner.

| Module | Lines | Verdict | Bugs |
|--------|-------|---------|------|
| pool.rs | 2,515 | 1 new bug | TOCTOU in can_create() (MEDIUM) |
| notify.rs | 628 | 1 bug | Lost wakeup race in notify_one/poll (HIGH) |

### Bug Details

**1. notify.rs: Lost wakeup race (HIGH)**
- notify_one() increments stored_notifications OUTSIDE lock (line 166)
- Notified::poll(Init) checks stored_notifications BEFORE lock (line 247)
- Race window: notification stored between lockless check and waiter registration
- Fix: move increment inside lock + re-check after registration

**2. semaphore.rs: Missing cascading wakeup in OwnedAcquireFuture (MEDIUM)**
- AcquireFuture::poll (lines 290-297) wakes next waiter when permits > 0 after acquire
- OwnedAcquireFuture::poll (lines 488-495) lacks this logic

**3. pool.rs: TOCTOU in can_create() (MEDIUM)**
- can_create() checks total_count() < max_size, releases lock, create_resource().await, re-acquires lock
- N concurrent tasks can all pass the check and exceed max_size
- Fix: speculative increment before factory call, decrement on failure

### Patterns Observed
- **Arc<AtomicBool> waiter dequeue**: Used in mutex.rs and rwlock.rs for tracking waiter liveness
- **WaiterSlab**: Used in notify.rs for slot reuse with tail shrinking
- **VecDeque+ID**: Used in semaphore.rs for FIFO fairness
- **Condvar polling**: Used in barrier.rs (10ms timeout for cancel checks)
- **AtomicU8 state machine**: Used in once_cell.rs (UNINIT→INITIALIZING→INITIALIZED)
- **Double-check-after-registration**: Correctly used in once_cell.rs, MISSING in notify.rs (root cause of the HIGH bug)

### Previously Known Issues (confirmed)
- pool.rs total_acquisitions decrement (LOW) - breaks monotone counter semantics
- pool.rs redundant unsafe impl Send (STYLE)

comments.text:
Fresh-eyes random audit pass #2 (sync pool + blocking pool) landed two concrete correctness fixes:

1) src/sync/pool.rs — max_size race during async create + cancellation leak of in-flight create slots.
- Root cause: acquire checked capacity via can_create() before awaiting create_resource(), without reserving a slot. Concurrent acquires could both pass check and exceed max_size.
- Additional risk: if acquire future was dropped/cancelled while create_resource().await was in progress, capacity accounting could leak because nothing decremented pending creation state.
- Fix: added creation-slot accounting (`creating`) and drop-safe `CreateSlotReservation` RAII guard.
  - Wait path now considers `active + idle + creating` when deciding readiness.
  - reserve/release/commit helpers enforce capacity at reservation time and release slot on cancellation/error via Drop.
  - removed old post-create `record_acquisition` path.
- Warmup fix in same file: cap warmup target by available capacity (`max_size - existing`) so warmup never exceeds configured max_size.

2) src/runtime/blocking_pool.rs — shutdown contract violation on spawn.
- Root cause: `spawn_with_priority` accepted/enqueued tasks even after `shutdown()`, despite docs claiming new tasks are rejected.
- Fix: in both `BlockingPool` and `BlockingPoolHandle` paths, if shutdown is set then return an immediate cancelled+done handle (never enqueue work).

Regression tests added:
- sync::pool::tests::create_slot_reservation_enforces_max_size_and_releases_on_drop
- sync::pool::tests::warmup_respects_max_size
- runtime::blocking_pool::tests::spawn_after_shutdown_is_rejected

comments.author: EmeraldLake
comments.text:
[2026-02-09] Fix: prevent pending-result registration leak on transport send failure.

Issue: spawn_remote called runtime.register_task(...) before runtime.send_message(...). If send_message returns Err, the runtime may retain a pending_results entry forever (task never resolves), violating no-task-leaks / no-obligation-leaks expectations for distributed handles.

Fix: extended RemoteRuntime with default no-op unregister_task(task_id). spawn_remote now unregisters the remote_task_id if send_message fails and returns the original error. VirtualNetworkRuntime implements unregister_task by removing from pending_results map.

Regression test: remote::tests::spawn_remote_send_failure_unregisters_pending_task (fails prior behavior in a runtime that tracks register/unregister).

Validation: cargo fmt --check; cargo check --all-targets; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test (all pass).

comments.author: OrangeGrove
comments.text:
Extreme-optimization loop update (single-lever patch):

Scope kept to scheduler work-stealing hot path files already reserved:
- `src/runtime/scheduler/intrusive.rs`
- `src/runtime/scheduler/local_queue.rs`

What changed in this pass:
- Implemented fused non-local transfer in `IntrusiveStack::steal_batch_into_non_local()`.
  - Direct detach-from-source + attach-to-dest in one loop.
  - Avoids per-item handoff through separate `steal_one_assume_non_local()` + `push_assume_non_local()` call chain.
- Added regression test:
  - `runtime::scheduler::intrusive::tests::stack_steal_batch_into_non_local_preserves_ordering`

Correctness checks (all via `rch`):
- `cargo test -p asupersync --lib intrusive::tests::stack_steal_batch_into_non_local_preserves_ordering -- --nocapture` ✅
- `cargo test -p asupersync --lib local_queue::tests:: -- --nocapture` ✅ (28 passed)
- `cargo check -p asupersync --lib` ✅

Benchmark samples (via `rch exec -- cargo bench --bench scheduler_benchmark -- scheduler/work_stealing --sample-size 20 --warm-up-time 0.1 --measurement-time 0.2`):
- Worker variance remains high.
- On `vmi1149989` (pre-change baseline in this cycle):
  - `steal_single`: [3.1627, 3.4398, 3.8658] µs
  - `steal_batch/256`: [12.358, 13.297, 13.978] µs
- Post-change samples landed on other workers (`vmi1153651`, `vmi1152480`) and showed wider spread; a representative post-change run on `vmi1152480`:
  - `steal_single`: [5.6420, 5.8608, 6.1569] µs
  - `steal_batch/256`: [11.406, 12.261, 13.306] µs

Interpretation:
- `steal_batch/256` is at least not obviously worse in absolute terms on the post-change `vmi1152480` run, but cross-worker noise prevents strict causal proof.
- Need controlled same-worker A/B (or worker pinning support) for definitive closure.

Workspace-wide gates (requested in AGENTS.md) were executed with `rch` and failed for pre-existing unrelated issues:
- `cargo fmt --check` ❌ unrelated existing formatting drift in multiple files outside this bead
- `cargo check --all-targets` ❌ existing compile errors in `tests/contention_e2e.rs` (`state.lock()` now returns `Result` callsites not updated)
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` ❌ existing warnings/errors outside this bead (`symbol_cancel.rs`, `bulkhead.rs`, `rate_limit.rs`, `net/dns/cache.rs`, `deadline_monitor.rs`)

Keeping bead in-progress pending stronger same-worker benchmark evidence.

comments.author: OrangeGrove
comments.text:
Single-steal recovery lever applied:

Code change:
- `src/runtime/scheduler/local_queue.rs`
  - `Stealer::steal` now always uses locality-aware scan (`steal_one_with_locality`) and no longer forces the `has_local_tasks()==false -> steal_one_assume_non_local` fast path.
  - Batch fast path (`steal_batch_locked` + `steal_batch_into_non_local`) remains intact.

Rationale:
- Prior controlled data showed batch/256 improvement but single-steal regression.
- This isolates single-steal path while preserving batch optimization.

Validation (`rch`):
- `cargo test -p asupersync --lib local_queue::tests:: -- --nocapture` ✅
- `cargo test -p asupersync --lib intrusive::tests::stack_steal_batch_into_non_local_preserves_ordering -- --nocapture` ✅
- `cargo check -p asupersync --lib` ✅

Benchmark comparison (same worker, same command):
- Worker: `vmi1152480`
- Command: `rch exec -- cargo bench --bench scheduler_benchmark -- scheduler/work_stealing --sample-size 20 --warm-up-time 0.1 --measurement-time 0.2`

Before this lever (with single-steal fast path still enabled):
- `steal_single`: [5.6420, 5.8608, 6.1569] µs
- `steal_batch/256`: [11.406, 12.261, 13.306] µs

After this lever:
- `steal_single`: [4.3511, 4.6630, 5.1012] µs
- `steal_batch/256`: [11.127, 11.615, 12.150] µs

Observed direction:
- `steal_single` improved.
- `steal_batch/256` did not regress (slight improvement).

Keeping bead in progress for another pass only if we need tighter p-values across repeated same-worker samples.

comments.author: HazyCrane
comments.text: 2026-03-20 HazyCrane peer-review slice on src/process.rs: found a live runtime-thread blocking regression in the recent kill_on_drop reap change. Root cause: should_background_reap_kill_on_drop() only checked Cx::current(), but runtime worker threads keep Runtime::current_handle() installed even when no task is actively being polled, so dropping Child on a worker outside task-poll context could still take the blocking wait path. Fixed by treating either an ambient Cx or an installed runtime handle as reason to offload the reap, and added a regression proving worker startup sees runtime handle without ambient Cx but still takes the background-reap branch. comments.text: 2026-03-20 HazyCrane follow-up audit on src/lab/explorer.rs: found a real priority regression in the recent pending-seed dedup change. Root cause: the new dedup treated already-pending seeds as fully settled, so DporExplorer could not promote a seed from the back of the queue to the front when a later unknown-prefix path discovered it, and TopologyExplorer could not upgrade a pending seed to a higher TopologicalScore when a later derivation assigned it more novel evidence. comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
[2026-02-17 WildValley] Audit/fix completed for global queue scheduling backoff path.

Findings:
- Worker backoff loop used queue emptiness snapshots (`local.is_empty()`/`global.is_empty()`) before parking. Under concurrency these are advisory snapshots, which can race with newly-queued work and cause avoidable park-latency before the next dequeue.

Fix:
- `src/runtime/scheduler/worker.rs`: replaced backoff emptiness-hint check with direct dequeue probe (`pop_backoff_work`) and immediate execution when work is available. This makes backoff decisions based on concrete dequeues rather than stale emptiness hints.
- `src/runtime/scheduler/global_queue.rs`: documented `len`/`is_empty` as best-effort snapshots under concurrent producers/consumers.

Regression coverage:
- Added `test_backoff_probe_pops_global_work` in `src/runtime/scheduler/worker.rs`.
- Verified worker + global queue test modules pass.

title: [ATP][cache][security] shared-cache 'requires encryption' gate is satisfied by forgeable self-attested evidence
description: src/atp/cache/trust.rs:102 check_storage enforces 'private content MUST be encrypted in a shared cache' via a content_encrypted: bool that the caller derives with derive_cache_entry_encryption_status (src/atp/cache/mod.rs:139) = key.declares_encrypted_content() || content_has_encrypted_envelope(content). BOTH disjuncts are attacker-forgeable by an authorized seeder (one who passes check_access): (1) scope_declares_encrypted_content (mod.rs:105) returns true if any '-'/alnum token of the grant-SCOPE STRING equals encrypted|ciphertext|e2e|end-to-end|sealed — a scope like 'team:encrypted' marks content encrypted with zero byte inspection; (2) content_has_encrypted_envelope (mod.rs:116) accepts any JSON with (ciphertext|encrypted_data)+(nonce|iv)+(tag|auth_tag)+an algorithm/cipher field whose value .contains('aes'|'chacha'|'gcm') (SUBSTRING, the recurring fail-open class) — satisfied by {"ciphertext":"<b64 plaintext>","nonce":"x","tag":"y","algorithm":"aes-gcm"}. Impact: an authorized-but-malicious/careless seeder stores PLAINTEXT private content on an encryption-required shared/relay/CDN cache, defeating require_encryption_for_shared and leaking data to parties outside the read-access boundary. MITIGATIONS: (a) drop the scope-name disjunct entirely (a scope string must never imply the bytes are encrypted); (b) exact-match the algorithm field against a known allowlist, not .contains(); (c) real fix (design): check_storage must receive an AUTHENTICATED encryption status cryptographically bound to the actual encryption op, not a heuristic over caller-supplied bytes/scope. Found via fresh-eyes fail-open/authorization review (SapphireHill). RELATED LATENT OBSERVATIONS from the same review (low, tracked here to avoid bead-spam): (i) trust.rs:79 check_access does no scope check when grant_scope is None (mitigated on shared caches by check_storage rejecting None-scoped storage; residual on local()/shared_with_public()); (ii) enforcement.rs:186 EnforcementMode::LogOnly/Disabled rewrite every Denied into a FULL admin grant (Read+Write over Any) — no prod caller today, default Enforce, but a deployment flipping to LogOnly 'to only log' would authorize everything; (iii) PolicyEnforcer.usage_counts is in-memory only, so a consumer using PolicyEnforcer directly (not via GrantManager storage-backed accounting) re-grants max_uses after each restart (replay); (iv) scope.rs ResourceScope::Cache with an empty object_types set matches ALL object types (object_types.is_empty() || contains) — footgun if a Cache scope is ever built with a default/empty set expecting deny-all.

title: [EPIC] Cancellation Injection Testing Framework
description:
# Overview

A testing framework that systematically injects CancelRequested at every await point
in async code, then verifies that all invariants hold: obligations committed or aborted,
no leaked tasks, finalizers run, resources released.

## Why This Is The #1 Priority

This directly validates asupersync's core promise of "cancel-correctness." Without 
systematic testing, that's just marketing. This framework makes it PROVABLE.

The project's formal semantics (asupersync_v4_formal_semantics.md) defines exactly what
invariants must hold. This framework tests those invariants exhaustively.

## How It Works

1. **First run**: Execute the test, recording all await points reached
2. **Subsequent runs**: For each await point N, inject cancellation at that point
3. **Verification**: After each injection, run all oracles to verify invariants

```rust
#[test]
fn test_http_request_cancel_correct() {
    Lab::new()
        .with_oracle(CancellationProtocolOracle)
        .with_oracle(ObligationLeakOracle)
        .with_oracle(TaskLeakOracle)
        .with_cancellation_injection(InjectionStrategy::AllPoints)
        .run(|cx| async {
            let client = HttpClient::new(cx);
            client.get("https://example.com").await
        });
    // Automatically runs N times, injecting at each await point
}
```

## Invariants Verified (from formal semantics)

1. **Task Leak**: All spawned tasks must complete before parent region closes
2. **Obligation Linearity**: All obligations must be Committed or Aborted, never Leaked
3. **Quiescence**: Region close implies no live children
4. **Loser Drain**: Race losers are fully drained before winner returns
5. **Cancellation Protocol**: State machine transitions are valid
6. **Finalizer Guarantee**: Finalizers run exactly once

## Implementation Approach

1. Create `InstrumentedFuture<F>` wrapper that tracks await points
2. On first poll, record await point ID (file:line or unique counter)
3. `InjectionStrategy` determines which points to test
4. For each point, re-run test with cancellation injected at that point
5. Run oracles after each injected run
6. Report: which points were tested, which failed, why

## User Value

- **Library authors**: "I can prove my async code is cancel-safe"
- **Application developers**: "My critical paths are verified"
- **Adopters**: "This runtime has rigor I can't get elsewhere"

## Implementation Estimate

- ~500-800 lines of new code
- Builds on existing LabReactor and Oracle infrastructure
- Touches: lab/, new test utilities

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Can specify injection strategy (all points, random sample, specific points)
- [ ] Captures all await points in a test
- [ ] Injects cancellation at each point reliably
- [ ] Runs all configured oracles after each injection
- [ ] Reports clear failure information
- [ ] Works with existing Lab infrastructure
- [ ] Documentation with examples

title: Implement test oracle: losers_always_drained invariant checker
description:
## Purpose
Implement a test oracle that verifies the "losers always drained" invariant: in any race/select operation, losing tasks are cancelled AND fully drained before the operation returns.

## The Invariant
From asupersync_plan_v4.md:
> Races must cancel and fully drain losers

This prevents resource leaks, ensures cleanup runs, and maintains predictable behavior.

## What "Drained" Means
A task is drained when it has:
1. Received cancel request (`CancelRequested` state)
2. Run to next checkpoint (`Cancelling` state)
3. Executed finalizers (`Finalizing` state)
4. Reached `Completed(Cancelled)` state

Simply requesting cancellation is NOT sufficient. The task must actually complete.

## Oracle Design

```rust
pub struct LoserDrainOracle {
    // Tracks race/select operations
    race_starts: Vec<RaceEvent>,
    race_completes: Vec<RaceCompletion>,
    task_drains: HashMap<TaskId, DrainRecord>,
}

pub struct RaceEvent {
    pub race_id: RaceId,
    pub participants: Vec<TaskId>,
    pub start_time: Time,
}

pub struct RaceCompletion {
    pub race_id: RaceId,
    pub winner: TaskId,
    pub losers: Vec<TaskId>,
    pub complete_time: Time,
}

pub struct DrainRecord {
    pub cancel_requested: Option<Time>,
    pub drain_started: Option<Time>,
    pub finalizers_complete: Option<Time>,
    pub fully_drained: Option<Time>,
}

impl LoserDrainOracle {
    /// Called when race/select starts
    pub fn on_race_start(&mut self, race_id: RaceId, participants: Vec<TaskId>, time: Time);
    
    /// Called when race determines winner
    pub fn on_race_complete(&mut self, race_id: RaceId, winner: TaskId, time: Time);
    
    /// Called when task fully drains
    pub fn on_task_drained(&mut self, task: TaskId, time: Time);
    
    /// Verify all losers are drained before race returns
    pub fn check(&self) -> Result<(), LoserDrainViolation>;
}
```

## Violation Detection
```rust
pub struct LoserDrainViolation {
    pub race_id: RaceId,
    pub winner: TaskId,
    pub undrained_losers: Vec<(TaskId, DrainRecord)>,
    pub race_return_time: Time,
}
```

A violation occurs when:
1. Race R completes at time T
2. ∃ loser L where `fully_drained` time > T or is None

## Operations That Must Drain Losers
| Operation | Winner | Losers |
|-----------|--------|--------|
| `race(a, b)` | First to complete | Other participants |
| `select\!{...}` | Selected branch | Unselected branches |
| `quorum(M, N)` | First M successes | Remaining N-M |
| `first_ok(...)` | First success | Operations after success |
| `timeout(op, d)` | Whichever wins | Timeout or op |

## Testing the Oracle
1. **Two-way race**: Winner and loser properly handled
2. **N-way race**: Multiple losers all drained
3. **Nested races**: Inner race losers drained before outer race proceeds
4. **Loser with finalizers**: Finalizers run during drain
5. **Loser with obligations**: Obligations resolved during drain
6. **Slow drain**: Loser takes time to reach checkpoint

## Drain Timing Verification
The oracle tracks timing to ensure:

title: Instrument task lifecycle with tracing spans
description:
# Task

Add tracing instrumentation to task lifecycle in runtime/scheduler.

## What to Instrument

1. **Task spawn**: When `scope.spawn()` is called
   - Fields: task_id, owning_region, name (if provided), initial_state
   
2. **Task poll**: Each time the task is polled
   - Fields: task_id, poll_number, budget_remaining
   - Keep as trace-level to avoid overhead
   
3. **Task wake**: When waker is invoked
   - Fields: task_id, wake_source (timer, io, explicit)
   
4. **Task state transitions**: Created → Running → CancelRequested → Cancelling → Finalizing → Completed
   - Fields: task_id, from_state, to_state, outcome (on completion)

5. **Task completion**: Final outcome
   - Fields: task_id, outcome_kind (Ok/Err/Cancelled/Panicked), duration, poll_count

## Implementation Notes

- Task span should be child of region span
- Use span.in_scope() for poll instrumentation
- Wake events use follows_from to link to waker source
- Completion closes the task span

## Causality Links

```
Region[1] ──creates──> Task[100]
Task[100] ──woken_by──> Timer[5] 
Task[100] ──woken_by──> IoEvent[fd=3]
Task[100] ──cancelled_by──> Region[1].close()
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Spawn creates task span as child of region
- [ ] Poll events recorded at trace level
- [ ] Wake events include source
- [ ] State transitions recorded
- [ ] Completion includes outcome and metrics
- [ ] Causality links correctly established

NOT CAUSED BY THE ADJACENT mly63p FIX. That change was a `.rs` extension predicate inside local_test_file() in src/bin/dependency_verification_matrix.rs and cannot affect bead-ID coverage. A blind regeneration would sweep in every other campaign's in-flight rows under my commit, and I would be asserting evidence I have not verified for beads I do not own.

STRUCTURAL PROBLEM, which is the real content of this bead: this artifact is derived from live tracker state in a repo where a dozen agents close beads continuously. It drifts on a timescale of MINUTES. Any agent who runs this gate mid-session sees red through no fault of their own, and any agent who regenerates it wins a race that is lost again almost immediately. A per-commit regeneration duty cannot hold under that write rate.

SUGGESTED FIXES, in preference order:
1. Make the contract tolerant in the safe direction: treat tracker-side CLOSURE of a listed non-epic bead as acceptable (or compare against a snapshot pinned by commit) so `extra=[...]` from closures is not fatal, while keeping `missing=[...]` fatal. Missing rows are a real evidence gap; recently-closed rows are not.
2. Failing that, regenerate as a scheduled/owner-driven step under upksjk.6.x rather than as an implicit obligation on whichever agent happens to run the suite.
3. At minimum, have the failure message say "artifact is stale relative to the tracker; regenerate with <exact command>" so the next agent does not have to reverse-engineer that the four IDs were closed today.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
SapphireHill 2026-07-25: ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED. My original comment on this bead was wrong about the mechanism, and the correction changes the fix.

WHAT I ORIGINALLY CLAIMED: "all four are type=task and were CLOSED today by peer agents ... continuous tracker drift" -- i.e. that any close drifts the artifact, so a per-commit regeneration duty cannot hold.

THAT IS NOT HOW THE CONTRACT WORKS. tracker_matrix_ids() KEEPS closed beads. It excludes a closed bead only when close_reason matches "superseded" or "duplicate". An ordinary close does not drift the artifact at all. The 4 extras had two different causes:

(a) THREE ARE CORRECT EXCLUSIONS. h3jspm.9/.10/.12 all close with "...plan superseded". The contract deliberately drops superseded rows; the artifact predates those closes and is stale by exactly 3 rows.

(b) ONE IS A PREDICATE BUG THAT FAILS OPEN. asupersync-ym2wtv.1 closed as a DEFER decision: "GB-03 duplicated-runtime finding is decisive; terminal outcome DEFER, incumbent stands". It is not a duplicate of anything. It was dropped because contains("duplicate") matched the substring inside "duplicATED".

WHY (b) IS THE REAL FINDING: the artifact's own coverage_scope says it excludes "only closed tracker duplicates explicitly superseded by a canonical successor". A naked substring match does not implement that sentence. Any dep-plan bead whose close reason merely contains the letters "duplicate" or "superseded" -- "duplicated", "deduplicate" -- silently falls out of REQUIRED verification coverage, with no red gate to notice. Coverage requirements deletable by prose is the wrong direction for an evidence-bearing contract. The generator (src/bin/dependency_verification_matrix.rs:109) and the test (tests/dependency_verification_matrix_contract.rs:122) each carried their own copy of the same buggy predicate.

FIX: both copies replaced with a whole-ASCII-word match (SUPERSEDED_DUPLICATE_TOKENS + contains_superseded_duplicate_token). Deliberately fail-closed -- "duplicates" and "superseding" no longer match either, so such a bead stays IN required coverage and produces a visible red gate rather than silently vanishing. Keeping a bead is the safe error; dropping it is not. Unit test superseded_duplicate_tokens_match_whole_words_only pins both directions with the live ym2wtv.1 string as the regression case.

VERIFIED BEFORE REGENERATING: under the new rule tracker=332; against the current artifact missing=[] extra=[the 3 genuinely superseded h3jspm rows]. missing=[] is what makes regeneration safe -- it can only DROP rows, so it cannot sweep in unverified rows for beads I do not own, which was my stated reason for not regenerating yesterday.

title: Implement region heap allocator + quiescent reclamation
description:
# Region Heap Allocator + Quiescent Reclamation

## Purpose
Enable safe parallel tasks by allocating captured data in a region-owned heap that is reclaimed only when the region closes to quiescence.

This is the memory backbone for the “task tier.”

## Requirements
- Region heap lifetime = region lifetime.
- Reclamation only after:
  - all child tasks terminal
  - all finalizers complete
  - all obligations resolved

## Design Notes
- Start with a simple allocator design:
  - bump allocator per region for fast-path
  - fallback to global allocator when necessary
- Determinism: allocation addresses must not be used as observable identifiers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Region heap allocations remain valid for all tasks owned by the region.
- Region heap is reclaimed on region close without leaks.

## Testing
- Allocate values in region heap, spawn tasks that read them, close region, ensure memory is reclaimed (via debug counters, not UB).

title: Cancel-Aware Sync Primitives Verification Suite (unit tests, E2E)
description:
# Cancel-Aware Sync Primitives Verification Suite

## Purpose
Comprehensive verification for cancel-aware synchronization primitives (q48) ensuring correctness under cancellation and two-phase permit semantics.

## Test Categories

### 1. Unit Tests
- Mutex: lock, try_lock, cancel-during-wait
- RwLock: read, write, upgrade, downgrade
- Semaphore: acquire, try_acquire, two-phase permits
- Barrier: wait, reset
- Notify: notify_one, notify_all, notify_waiters
- OnceCell: get_or_init, get_or_try_init

### 2. E2E Scenarios
| Scenario | Verifies |
|----------|----------|
| Mutex contention | Fair queuing, no starvation |
| RwLock readers | Concurrent read access |
| RwLock writer priority | Writer preference |
| Semaphore permits | Count accuracy |
| Semaphore two-phase | Reserve/commit/abort |
| Barrier sync | All tasks reach barrier |
| Notify wake ordering | FIFO wake semantics |
| OnceCell race | Single initialization |

### 3. Cancel-Safety Tests
- Cancel while waiting for mutex: no leak
- Cancel while holding permit: proper release
- Cancel during barrier wait: barrier reset
- Cancel during semaphore reserve: abort semantics

### 4. Stress Tests
- High contention scenarios
- Many waiters, few resources
- Rapid acquire/release cycles
- Mixed read/write patterns

### 5. Deadlock Detection Tests
- Cycle detection in lock graphs
- Priority inversion scenarios
- Lab runtime deadlock oracle

## Logging Requirements
- Lock events logged with task IDs
- On failure: dump waiter queues, lock state
- Contention metrics: wait times, queue lengths

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All primitives have unit tests
- [ ] Cancel-safety verified for all operations
- [ ] No deadlocks in stress tests
- [ ] Two-phase permits work correctly
- [ ] `cargo test sync` passes deterministically

## Verification Commands
```bash
cargo test --package asupersync --lib sync
cargo test --test sync_e2e
```

title: Wake notifier replacement drops captured user state under its slot lock
description: WorkerCoordinator::set_wake_notifier assigns a new Arc while holding wake_notifier.slot. Retiring the previous last Arc runs captured user destructors under that mutex; a destructor that wakes a task routes through notify_wake and recursively locks the slot, deadlocking. The public ThreeLaneWorker setter admits callback replacement. Move retirement outside the mutex while preserving callback publication and the cheap unarmed path. Add a deterministic regression through the public worker setter with a try_lock state witness before real reentrant wake, so old code fails rather than hangs.
acceptance_criteria: Old-code regression fails on the slot-lock witness; repaired code permits captured Drop to wake and invoke the newly published callback exactly once, then normal later wake still works. Retain RCH terminal regression and required scheduler/native-cancellation/compiler/lint/format/Phase 6 evidence before closure. No public API or baseline changes.

title: Phase 0: Verification (Oracles, Unit Tests, E2E, Benches)
description:
# Phase 0: Verification (Oracles, Unit Tests, E2E, Benches)

## Purpose
Asupersync's guarantees are only real if we can continuously *prove them operationally*.

This feature organizes the verification surface:
- invariants (tree structure, task ownership, quiescence, no leaks, loser draining, cancel propagation, no ambient authority, determinism)
- unit tests
- E2E scenario tests
- baseline benchmarks

## Required Oracles (Phase 0)
The spec's invariants from asupersync_v4_formal_semantics.md §5 require these trace- or state-checkable oracles:

| Invariant | Oracle |
|-----------|--------|
| INV-TREE | region_tree_valid |
| INV-TASK-OWNED | no_task_leaks |
| INV-QUIESCENCE | quiescence_on_close |
| INV-CANCEL-PROPAGATES | cancellation_protocol_valid |
| INV-OBLIGATION-BOUNDED | no_obligation_leaks |
| INV-OBLIGATION-LINEAR | no_obligation_leaks |
| INV-MASK-BOUNDED | cancellation_protocol_valid |
| INV-DEADLINE-MONOTONE | deadline_monotone |
| INV-LOSER-DRAINED | losers_always_drained |

Additionally:
- all_finalizers_ran: Verify LIFO finalizer execution
- no_ambient_authority: Verify effects only via Cx
- determinism: same seed/config => identical trace

## Algebraic Laws Testing
The algebraic laws from asupersync_v4_formal_semantics.md §7 require property-based tests:
- LAW-JOIN-ASSOC
- LAW-JOIN-COMM
- LAW-RACE-COMM
- LAW-TIMEOUT-MIN
- LAW-RACE-NEVER
- LAW-RACE-JOIN-DIST

## Acceptance Criteria
- `cargo test` covers the invariants above with deterministic lab runtime.
- E2E scenarios exist for:
  - nested regions
  - cancellation end-to-end
  - race draining
  - two-phase channels under cancellation
  - replay/determinism
- Benchmark suite exists to set Phase 0 baselines (spawn cost, cancel path, channel ops) without regressing determinism.

## Logging & Debuggability
- Tests must emit detailed, structured diagnostics on failure:
  - dump formatted trace
  - show first divergence step for replay
  - show invariant violation evidence

Core runtime still must not write to stdout/stderr; printing is confined to test harnesses.
close_reason: All verification criteria met: 9 test oracles (region_tree_valid, no_task_leaks, quiescence_on_close, cancellation_protocol_valid, no_obligation_leaks, deadline_monotone, losers_always_drained, all_finalizers_ran, no_ambient_authority, determinism). 23 E2E tests covering all 10 canonical scenarios. 2145+ lib tests. Benchmark suite in place.

title: Build lab-vs-live adversarial differential validation program
description: Create a rigorous verification program that generates adversarial scenarios, executes them in lab and live runtime paths, compares normalized semantic outcomes, and backs every claim with explicit unit suites, golden fixtures, reusable dual-run e2e scripts, and detailed structured diagnostics instead of vague confidence.
design:
Build this as a staged verification program, not as a one-off test. The goal is to turn the question "does the lab model runtime behavior accurately enough to trust it?" into repeatable, differential evidence.

The implementation track should reuse and connect existing assets rather than invent a parallel framework from scratch: `src/lab/mod.rs`, `src/lab/runtime.rs`, `src/lab/fuzz.rs`, `src/lab/explorer.rs`, `tests/semantic_witness_replay_e2e.rs`, `tests/adversarial_witness_corpus.rs`, `tests/raptorq_conformance.rs`, `tests/common/mod.rs`, and `docs/replay-debugging.md` are the main starting points already in the tree.

The comparison contract must operate on normalized semantic observables instead of brittle raw interleavings. The expected comparator surface includes final `Outcome`, cancellation/drain/finalize completion, loser-drain behavior after races, region-close-to-quiescence, obligation balance, and any trace or witness facts that can be normalized across deterministic and live execution.

Rollout order matters. Start where the lab is strongest and external nondeterminism is weakest: cancellation, combinators, channels, obligations, region close/quiescence, and related sync behavior. Only after that should the program widen to virtualized timers and virtualized transports. Raw kernel, browser, and real-network fidelity are explicitly not automatic claims of this program unless those effects are captured or virtualized.

Every divergence must end in one of three buckets: real runtime bug, lab-model bug, or unsupported/insufficiently-observed scenario. The framework should default toward preserving evidence and minimizing the reproducer instead of guessing.
acceptance_criteria:
A complete issue graph exists with phase-local reasoning, dependency structure, coverage matrices, and explicit verification/logging expectations so future implementers do not need the original planning conversation.

Implementation is considered complete only when the project has: a reusable dual-run scenario model; direct unit/contract suites for the shared harness and live normalization layers; golden fixtures for scenario, comparator, and report outputs; reusable differential e2e runner scripts with structured logs and human-readable summaries; adversarial and DPOR-fed scenario generation; live evidence capture and normalization; divergence classification plus crashpack/replay artifacts; negative-control or self-calibration suites that prove the validator fails correctly; pilot suites for core semantic surfaces backed by explicit unit/e2e coverage matrices; and CI/stress execution lanes with retention, seed rotation, replay guidance, and stable profile semantics.

Supported claims, non-goals, logging vocabulary, and operator workflow are explicit enough that contributors know what the system proves, what it does not prove, and how to diagnose failures quickly.
notes:
Background: the motivating question was whether the lab feature can be stress-tested by generating adversarial examples, simulating them, and then comparing against what actually happens in live code paths. The correct framing is yes for supported semantic surfaces, no for "everything" in the literal sense.

Foundation beads already landed and should be treated as prior art rather than duplicated effort: `asupersync-3cddg.12.6` (cross-artifact witness replay end-to-end), `asupersync-3cddg.12.13` (adversarial witness corpus and regression generator), and `asupersync-2oh2u.10.3` (differential behavior suite pattern). This new epic is the programmatic glue that turns those ingredients into a coherent trust-building workflow.

comments.author: TurquoiseHawk
comments.text: Operator note: do not over-claim what this program proves. The target is semantic parity for explicitly supported surfaces under normalized observation, not magical equivalence for raw OS, browser, or network behavior. When in doubt, add a better boundary bead or a better observable before adding a bolder claim.

title: Define supported claims, semantic contract, and comparator rules
description: Pin down exactly what the lab-vs-live program is allowed to claim, which semantic surfaces are in scope first, which observables count as semantically equivalent, and which mismatches should be treated as real bugs versus harness noise.
design:
This phase exists to prevent the rest of the project from building the wrong harness. Before any implementation-heavy work lands, define exactly which surfaces are first-class targets, which observables are compared, and how much mismatch tolerance is acceptable.

The output of this phase should answer questions that would otherwise produce endless ambiguity later: Is exact event ordering required? Which trace facts are semantically relevant versus incidental? What counts as the same outcome across lab and live when scheduler interleavings differ? When does a mismatch indicate a true invariant violation versus a harness visibility gap?

This phase should also publish the initial scope ladder. Phase 1 targets should be pure runtime semantics. Later phases may cover timers and virtualized transport. Anything involving raw external systems must remain explicitly outside the trust claim until the effect boundary is virtualized or captured.
acceptance_criteria:
There is a written, bead-local definition of supported semantic surfaces, explicit non-goals, comparator inputs, and divergence classes.

Future implementation beads can reference this phase and avoid reopening basic scope debates.

The resulting contract is precise enough that two different implementers would build materially compatible comparators and would agree on what constitutes a real failure.
notes: Reasoning: differential systems rot when they silently compare the wrong thing. A smaller, explicit semantic contract is better than a larger but fuzzy claim set.
