title: Catalog supported surfaces, non-goals, and rollout order
description: Document the exact semantic surfaces this program is allowed to validate first, later, or not at all, with enough reasoning that future contributors can extend the scope without guessing.
design:
Produce a scope matrix that names each candidate semantic surface, marks its rollout phase, and explains why it is in-scope, deferred, or explicitly out-of-scope. This should include at minimum: cancellation, combinators, channels, obligations, region close/quiescence, sync primitives, timers, virtualized transport, raw sockets, HTTP, browser-like environments, and any other obvious future extension points.

The matrix should not be a bland checklist. It should preserve the reasoning future maintainers need when deciding whether a new surface belongs in this program or needs additional virtualization first. For each surface, state what the lab is expected to model faithfully, what the live path will exercise, and what external effects remain outside the semantic trust claim.
acceptance_criteria:
A bead-local matrix exists listing supported-now, supported-later, and unsupported surfaces.

Each entry includes a short rationale tied to observability and controllability, not just a label.

The rollout order is explicit enough that future contributors can tell which surface to differentialize next without reopening the base scope argument.
notes: This task is intentionally policy-heavy. If it is vague, the rest of the program will quietly sprawl into claims the framework cannot defend.
close_reason: Completed

title: Define normalized observable schema for lab-vs-live comparison
description: Specify the shared semantic record that both runtimes must map into before any comparison happens, including what counts as meaningful evidence and what must be discarded as incidental noise.
design:
Define the canonical record that lab and live runs will both be normalized into before comparison. The schema should include final outcome, cancellation lifecycle facts, loser-drain completion, region quiescence, obligation balance, any resource accounting that matters to the selected surface, and the seed/replay metadata needed to rerun the scenario.

Be explicit about what is intentionally absent. Exact raw event ordering, internal pointer identity, and scheduler-specific incidental details should only appear if they are part of the semantic contract for the surface under test. The schema needs examples showing how superficially different traces collapse into the same semantic result.
acceptance_criteria:
There is one documented normalized observable schema for differential comparison.

Both lab and live sides have an intended mapping into that schema.

The schema is strict enough to catch real semantic divergence and loose enough to avoid false mismatches on incidental ordering noise.
notes: This task is the fulcrum for almost every later bead. If the normalized record is poorly chosen, the system will either miss bugs or cry wolf constantly.
close_reason: Completed

title: Define divergence taxonomy, rerun policy, and escalation rules
description: Create the classification and escalation scheme that tells the framework what to do with different kinds of lab-vs-live mismatches, including when to rerun, when to preserve artifacts, and when to mark a surface unsupported.
design:
Write the mismatch taxonomy and decision policy the framework will use once comparisons start failing. The taxonomy should at least cover: probable runtime bug, probable lab-model bug, unsupported surface, missing or insufficient observability, suspected scheduler noise, and irreproducible/flaky divergence.

Define what follow-up each class requires. Some failures should trigger automatic artifact preservation and regression promotion; others should prompt more instrumentation or should block the surface from making stronger claims until its observability improves. Also define rerun heuristics so the system does not overreact to one noisy live execution or, conversely, discard a real bug because it is hard to reproduce.
acceptance_criteria:
The project has a clear divergence taxonomy and escalation policy.

Future comparator and CI beads can point to this task instead of inventing their own failure-handling rules.

The policy distinguishes actionable semantic failures from harness limitations without sweeping either class under the rug.
notes: Without an explicit taxonomy, every mismatch becomes an argument. This task exists to make failures operationally useful.
close_reason: Completed

title: Define verification taxonomy, minimum unit/e2e coverage, and structured logging standard
description: Create the global test-and-logging contract for the differential program so every later bead has explicit requirements for unit tests, end-to-end scripts, and failure diagnostics.
design:
Define the non-negotiable verification taxonomy for the whole program before implementation drifts into inconsistent habits. Every later bead should be able to answer three questions from this contract alone: what unit/contract tests are required, what end-to-end differential scripts are required, and what structured logging/artifact fields are required when those tests run.

The taxonomy should distinguish at least: unit/contract tests for local semantics, golden fixture tests for normalized records and scenario contracts, dual-run e2e scripts for full path validation, and heavier stress/nightly runs for adversarial exploration. It should also define the minimum log vocabulary for any failure or interesting run: scenario identifier, seed lineage, surface, runtime mode, comparator record summary, divergence class, rerun count, and artifact/crashpack locations.

This task exists to prevent a common failure mode in large test programs: strong ideas in prose but inconsistent test depth and inconsistent diagnostics in practice.
acceptance_criteria:
There is a bead-local testing and logging standard that later beads can reference directly.

The standard makes explicit what counts as sufficient unit coverage, sufficient dual-run e2e coverage, sufficient negative-control or self-calibration coverage, and sufficient failure logging/artifact retention for this program.

Two different implementers using this contract would produce materially similar verification assets rather than improvising their own definition of "tested."
notes: Claimed by WhiteCrane after architecture pass; defining verification taxonomy, minimum coverage contract, and structured logging standard with contract test and downstream doc bindings.
close_reason: Closure-ready on current HEAD: verification taxonomy/logging contract is present in docs/lab_live_verification_taxonomy.md, bound from docs/lab_live_differential_scope_matrix.md, and freshly validated via rch cargo test --test lab_live_verification_taxonomy_contract --test lab_live_differential_scope_matrix -- --nocapture (15/15 + 11/11).

title: Create shared dual-run scenario and harness architecture
description: Introduce a common scenario model and reusable harness layer so the same adversarial case can be executed by the deterministic lab runtime and the live runtime without rewriting assertions for each surface, then verify that harness directly with contract tests, golden fixtures, and a smoke-level end-to-end path.
design:
This phase defines the shared execution vocabulary. The core deliverable is a reusable scenario abstraction and harness layer that can drive both deterministic lab execution and live execution from the same case description, inputs, seeds, and assertions.

The design should avoid per-surface ad hoc harnesses. Instead, scenarios should declare setup, perturbations, expected observables, and any replay material in a form that both runtimes can interpret. The harness should make it easy to bolt on new semantic surfaces without rebuilding the execution plumbing each time.

This phase is where future maintainers should look first when adding a new surface. If a new pilot requires bespoke harness logic, that is usually a sign this phase is underspecified.
acceptance_criteria:
A common scenario model exists and is reusable across multiple surface-specific differential suites.

Shared assertions, seeds, and result collection logic are factored so pilots do not each reinvent execution plumbing.

The harness itself has dedicated unit/contract tests, golden fixtures, and at least one smoke-level dual-run e2e script with rich diagnostics.

Adding a new pilot surface mostly means writing adapters and semantic assertions, not inventing a new mini-framework or bespoke logging path.
notes: Justification: the lab already has rich generation and replay machinery, and the live runtime already has test setup paths. The missing piece is the adapter contract that allows the same adversarial case to travel through both worlds.
close_reason: Completed: child beads 2.1-2.5 are closed; shared scenario contract/harness landed in src/lab/{dual_run,scenario_runner,spork_harness}. docs/tests confirm smoke+golden coverage; rch semantic_golden_fixture_validation passed including dual-run harness contract checks. Remaining contract-suite rerun is currently blocked by remote worker /tmp exhaustion, not a code failure.

title: Design ScenarioSpec and adapter contract for dual-run cases
description: Create the shared scenario abstraction that represents one adversarial case once and can then be executed through lab and live adapters without rewriting the meaning of the test.
design:
Design the reusable scenario description that can feed both lab and live execution. It should cover setup state, actor roles, perturbations, cancellation points, timing or schedule hints where appropriate, expected semantic assertions, and replay metadata.

The contract should make it cheap to add new semantic surfaces without rewriting the entire scenario model. Prefer a small number of orthogonal concepts over a large pile of per-surface knobs. The adapter boundary should also make it clear which parts are interpreted by the deterministic lab runtime, which parts are interpreted by the live runner, and which parts are pure shared test intent.
acceptance_criteria:
A scenario contract exists that can be consumed by both lab and live execution paths.

The contract is expressive enough for the first pilot surfaces without being specialized to only one of them.

Canonical valid and invalid example scenarios, along with expected normalized-record examples, make the contract concrete enough that future implementers do not guess at edge-shape behavior.
notes: This is the main antidote to duplicating each test twice. If it fails, the whole program becomes a pair of unrelated harnesses pretending to compare the same thing.
close_reason: Completed

title: Implement shared witness/assertion helpers for dual-run suites
description: Extract reusable helpers that evaluate normalized records, express invariant checks cleanly, and produce informative mismatch diagnostics across multiple differential suites.
design:
Factor common assertion and witness-building helpers out of individual pilots. These helpers should know how to inspect normalized records, assert the surface-specific invariants that matter, and emit useful mismatch context when comparison fails.

The point is not merely deduplication. Shared assertion helpers are how the project keeps surface semantics consistent across pilots. If one suite checks obligation leakage differently from another, the framework will train contributors into inconsistent interpretations of the same invariant.
acceptance_criteria:
There is a shared assertion/helper layer used by more than one differential suite.

Surface-specific suites primarily declare scenario intent and invariant expectations instead of hand-rolling comparison plumbing.

Helper behavior and mismatch messages are exercised directly enough that failure output quality is stable, readable, and not treated as an incidental side effect.
notes: Good helper design here reduces both duplication and semantic drift between suites.
close_reason: Implemented: NormalizedObservable, NormalizedSemantics, TerminalOutcome, CancellationRecord, LoserDrainRecord, RegionCloseRecord, ObligationBalanceRecord, ResourceSurfaceRecord types. ComparisonVerdict and compare_observables() for semantic comparison. check_core_invariants() and assert_semantics() helpers. 41 new tests all passing.

title: Plumb deterministic seeds, parameters, and replay metadata through lab and live harnesses
description: Make seeds and replay identifiers first-class across both execution paths so adversarial cases can be rerun, shrunk, and promoted into long-lived regressions.
design:
Plumb seeds, scenario parameters, and replay identifiers through both runtimes in a way that survives failure and can be reissued later. This includes deciding what must be deterministic, what may remain probabilistic but logged, and how seed material is combined with surface-specific parameters.

The design should preserve a clean separation between semantic scenario identity and incidental run metadata. Replays must be able to say both "this is the same adversarial case" and "this specific execution used these runtime-side conditions" without collapsing those ideas into an opaque blob.
acceptance_criteria:
Both lab and live harnesses can run from shared seeds and parameter sets.

Replay metadata captures stable scenario family identifiers, concrete execution-instance identifiers, and enough human-readable labeling to make later reports and artifacts understandable.

The project can distinguish a scenario family from a single concrete execution instance and carry that identity cleanly into reruns, shrink steps, and regression promotion.
notes: Implemented deterministic dual-run metadata plumbing across scenario_runner, spork_harness, test_logging, and shared test helpers. rch-backed cargo check passed; focused rch tests passed. Full clippy remains blocked by pre-existing warnings/errors in src/lab/dual_run.rs and src/stream/debounce.rs unrelated to this bead.
close_reason: Implemented: SeedPlan, SeedMode, ReplayPolicy, ScenarioFamilyId, ExecutionInstanceId, RuntimeKind, ReplayMetadata, SeedLineageRecord, DualRunScenarioIdentity, Phase types in src/lab/dual_run.rs with 21 tests all passing. Seeds plumbed through lab and live harnesses with deterministic derivation, entropy decoupling, sweep support, and full serde roundtrip.

title: Create reusable dual-run test harness entrypoints and macros
description: Provide the practical top-level API for writing differential tests so future pilot suites can focus on scenarios and invariants rather than harness ceremony.
design:
Build the ergonomic top-level harness entrypoints that pilot suites will actually call. These should hide the dual-run ceremony, make it obvious how to declare a scenario and its expectations, and consistently route failure information through the common artifact pipeline.

Decide whether helper macros, builders, or plain functions are the right fit based on how the existing test tree is structured. The key requirement is that future pilots are easy to read and hard to misuse. If adding a new differential suite feels like writing a tiny framework from scratch, this task is incomplete.
acceptance_criteria:
There is a reusable top-level harness API that pilot suites call directly.

The API makes scenario declaration and dual-run execution concise without hiding important semantics.

At least one focused unit-level consumer and one smoke-level e2e consumer use the same entrypoint shape, and the shared run metadata or logging surface is stable enough that operators can tell which scenario/profile/seed path actually ran.
notes: This is the task that turns framework internals into something contributors will actually use.
close_reason: Implemented DualRunHarness builder with phase1(), from_identity(), lab(), live(), with_seed_plan(), run() API. DualRunResult with passed(), summary(). assert_dual_run_passes() convenience. 8 new harness tests (total 70 dual_run tests). Ergonomic entrypoint hides seed/metadata ceremony — pilots write lab and live closures only.

title: Build harness contract unit suite, golden fixtures, and smoke e2e coverage
description: Make the shared dual-run harness itself a strongly tested surface with unit coverage, golden fixtures, and a small end-to-end smoke path before pilots build on it.
design:
Build the harness-side verification suite that proves the shared scenario contract, helper layer, and public harness entrypoints behave correctly before any surface-specific pilot depends on them. This should include invalid-shape tests, seed/replay round-trips, golden fixtures for normalized scenario material, and ergonomic failure messages that make harness misuse obvious.

The suite should be deliberately fine-grained: unit tests for parser/validation behavior, golden fixtures for record shapes, and at least one small end-to-end smoke path proving the shared harness can execute a tiny dual-run case and emit understandable logs on failure.
acceptance_criteria:
The shared harness surface has comprehensive unit/contract coverage and golden fixtures.

Harness failures produce readable, detail-rich diagnostics instead of opaque assertion diffs.

At least one reusable smoke-level e2e exercise proves the shared harness can run a minimal dual-run case end-to-end.
notes: This bead prevents the worst kind of debugging loop: not knowing whether a pilot failed because the runtime is wrong or because the common harness is quietly malformed.
close_reason: Strengthened harness diagnostics and fixture-backed smoke/golden coverage

title: Integrate adversarial generation, DPOR exploration, and seed corpus management
description: Turn existing fuzzing and schedule-exploration machinery into a source of replayable dual-run scenarios, with shrinkable seeds and corpus rules that make divergences cheap to reproduce and retain.
design:
This phase converts existing adversarial infrastructure into a durable source of dual-run test cases. The key idea is that fuzzing and DPOR should not stop at finding an interesting lab schedule; they should be able to emit replayable scenario descriptors, minimized seed material, and corpus entries that feed the differential comparator directly.

The generation path should preserve enough metadata to reproduce failures later, while remaining compact enough to keep and rotate in CI. The shrinker path should focus on semantic preservation: smaller scenarios that still trigger the same differential mismatch are more valuable than simply shorter traces.

This phase should also define seed and corpus lifecycle rules so divergence-causing cases graduate into permanent regression coverage rather than vanishing after one debug session.
acceptance_criteria:
Fuzzing and DPOR outputs can be promoted into replayable differential scenarios instead of staying lab-local curiosities.

The system can retain, shrink, and re-run mismatch-causing seeds deterministically enough to support debugging and regression prevention.

Promoted adversarial cases preserve enough lineage and labeling that later unit/e2e suites, reports, and artifact registries can explain where a scenario came from and why it matters.
notes: Existing assets here include `src/lab/fuzz.rs`, `src/lab/explorer.rs`, and `tests/adversarial_witness_corpus.rs`. This phase should reuse those ideas rather than create a second unrelated corpus story.
close_reason: Completed: child beads 3.1-3.3 are closed; fuzz/DPOR promotion and corpus lineage are implemented in src/lab/fuzz.rs and src/lab/dual_run.rs, with end-to-end and corpus coverage in tests/replay_e2e_suite.rs and tests/adversarial_witness_corpus.rs. The parent was stale-open rather than missing implementation.

title: Promote FuzzHarness outputs into replayable ScenarioSpec cases
description: Bridge lab fuzzing outputs into the shared scenario format so generated adversarial cases can graduate into deterministic dual-run regressions.
design:
Extend the existing fuzzing path so interesting outputs can be promoted into the shared scenario format instead of dying inside lab-local test code. That means preserving enough setup, perturbation, and seed information to reconstruct the case through the dual-run harness later.

The bridge should prefer semantically meaningful scenario material over raw internals. A replayable scenario is more valuable than a giant opaque dump. Future maintainers should be able to look at the promoted artifact and understand what adversarial shape it represents.
acceptance_criteria:
`FuzzHarness`-style generation can emit replayable scenario descriptors for the differential framework, and direct unit/contract coverage proves the promoted artifacts satisfy `ScenarioSpec` shape, seed serialization, and lineage rules.

Interesting lab-found cases are promotable into stable regression material instead of remaining transient fuzz outputs, with readable scenario identity plus structured provenance, artifact, and replay fields preserved.

At least one promoted fuzz case is exercised end-to-end through the shared replay/regression flow, and the resulting logs or summaries make it obvious how a fuzz discovery became durable differential coverage.
notes:
This task is about converting discovery into reusable evidence. If it only finds bugs once, it is not doing enough.

2026-03-19 ScarletBear progress: landed a bounded fuzz-side support slice in src/lab/fuzz.rs and tests/replay_e2e_suite.rs that promotes FuzzFinding/FuzzRegressionCorpus outputs into replayable dual-run scenarios and exercises one promoted case end-to-end through DualRunHarness. Validation so far: replay E2E passed, rustfmt on touched files passed, repo-wide cargo fmt --check passed through rch, repo-wide cargo check --all-targets is currently red on an unrelated integration-test import in tests/../src/messaging/subject.rs (crate::util vs asupersync::util), and a focused rch cargo test --lib promotes_ run is still active.
close_reason: Already implemented in current tree: fuzz-to-scenario promotion lives in src/lab/dual_run.rs and is exercised by current inline plus integration coverage; revalidated via rch cargo check and targeted replay/schedule promotion tests

title: Promote DPOR and schedule exploration outputs into minimized differential scenarios
description: Make explored schedules first-class differential inputs by preserving the schedule constraints that matter and minimizing them into durable reproducer material.
design:
Extend the DPOR and schedule-exploration path so explored interleavings can be represented as compact scenario/schedule material for the differential framework. The emphasis should be on preserving the semantic schedule constraints that matter, not encoding every incidental detail of one particular execution.

Minimization belongs here too. A good promoted schedule is small enough to reason about, still triggers the same mismatch, and can be fed back into debugging or CI without carrying a huge irrelevant trace burden.
acceptance_criteria:
DPOR or similar schedule exploration can produce replayable differential scenarios or schedule hints, and direct unit/contract coverage proves the promotion path preserves the schedule constraints that actually matter semantically.

The promoted artifacts are minimized enough to be useful in debugging and regression suites, with shrink lineage and retained evidence making clear what corner condition survived minimization.

At least one promoted schedule-derived case is shown end-to-end through the shared replay/report flow, with structured logs, artifact pointers, and reproduction instructions preserving both the original and minimized lineage.
notes: This task turns schedule exploration from a lab-only investigation tool into a source of durable cross-runtime test inputs.
close_reason: Implemented schedule exploration promotion into replayable differential scenarios with targeted unit and integration coverage

title: Define divergence corpus registry, shrinker rules, and retention metadata
description: Create the long-lived storage and lifecycle rules for mismatch-causing seeds so discoveries survive debugging and become durable regression coverage when appropriate.
design:
Define how mismatch-causing scenarios are named, stored, shrunk, and retained over time. This includes metadata such as originating surface, seed lineage, shrink status, first-seen context, and whether the case is now a permanent regression or still under investigation.

The retention rules should support both debugging and long-term project hygiene. The corpus should grow by admitting high-value seeds, not by hoarding opaque one-offs forever. Shrinking should preserve semantic mismatch class, not just reduce byte size or step count mechanically.
acceptance_criteria:
There is a documented registry format and lifecycle for divergence-causing seeds and scenarios.

Registry metadata records at least surface/profile context, divergence class, first-seen lineage, minimization lineage, artifact pointers, and regression-promotion state.

The registry rules are exercised by direct validation tests and by at least one end-to-end promotion path so future contributors can add new mismatch artifacts without improvising storage conventions or losing provenance needed for debugging, reporting, or replay.
notes: A corpus without lifecycle rules becomes a junk drawer. This task keeps the artifact story sustainable.
close_reason: Completed divergence corpus registry, retention metadata, lifecycle docs, and contract coverage

title: Capture live-runtime semantic evidence and normalize it for comparison
description: Build the live-side adapter, instrumentation, and normalization pipeline needed to compare real executions against lab expectations without depending on fragile raw event-order equality, and verify that translation layer directly with deterministic fixtures and mismatch diagnostics.
design:
This phase makes live execution observable enough to compare meaningfully. The requirement is not perfect raw trace identity; it is sufficient semantic evidence to answer the comparator questions defined in the contract phase.

Live-side collection should prefer stable semantic markers over brittle internal details. The runtime adapter should aim for execution paths that reduce gratuitous scheduler noise, such as current-thread setups where appropriate, while still exercising the actual live code paths under test.

Normalization is a first-class design concern here. The output should collapse lab and live evidence into the same semantic record type so the differential engine is comparing comparable facts instead of raw heterogeneous traces.
acceptance_criteria:
There is a live-runtime adapter that can execute differential scenarios and emit semantic evidence suitable for comparison.

Normalization rules exist for the main observables under test and avoid depending on unstable raw ordering where ordering is not part of the contract.

The live capture and normalization path has dedicated unit/fixture coverage, representative golden records, and field-level mismatch diagnostics rather than being tested only transitively through later pilots.
notes: This phase should reuse test setup and runtime-builder patterns already present in `tests/common/mod.rs` and related runtime tests. It is intentionally separate from the comparator phase because evidence collection and mismatch judgment are different responsibilities.
close_reason: Closure-ready on current HEAD: 2a6k9.1 is now closed, all child implementation beads under 2a6k9.4 are closed, and the live adapter/normalization surface freshly validates via rch cargo test --lib run_live_adapter -- --nocapture, rch cargo test --lib normalize_ -- --nocapture, and rch cargo test --lib mismatch_summary_with_manifests_includes_capture_sources -- --nocapture.

title: Build current-thread live runner adapter for differential scenarios
description: Create the live execution adapter that runs shared scenarios through real runtime code paths while minimizing gratuitous scheduling noise and preserving reproducibility.
design:
Build the live-side execution adapter that can take a shared scenario and drive the actual runtime paths under test with as little incidental nondeterminism as practical. Prefer current-thread or otherwise constrained runtime setups where that reduces scheduler noise without changing the semantics the surface is supposed to exercise.

The adapter should be explicit about what it controls and what it cannot control. It must not quietly turn live execution into another simulated path. The whole point is to run the real code paths while still making comparison practical.
acceptance_criteria:
A live-run adapter exists and can execute shared differential scenarios through real runtime code paths using a documented execution model rather than ad hoc per-suite setup.

Adapter bootstrapping, run lifecycle, and teardown behavior have direct unit or contract coverage plus at least one smoke-level e2e path using the same live-run surface the later pilots and scripts will use.

The adapter emits structured run metadata rich enough for later reports and replay guidance, including scenario identity, profile, seed lineage, runtime mode, and any known nondeterminism qualifiers.
notes: This task is about controlling noise, not about hiding the fact that the live path is live.
close_reason: Implemented LiveRunnerAdapter: LiveRunnerConfig, LiveExecutionProfile, LiveWitnessCollector, LiveRunMetadata, LiveRunResult, run_live_adapter(). 10 new tests (total 80). Current-thread adapter with explicit witness collection, structured metadata logging, nondeterminism qualifiers, and full integration with DualRunHarness.

title: Add live-side semantic capture hooks for comparison-relevant events
description: Expose the semantic facts from live executions that the comparator needs, focusing on stable hooks rather than brittle raw traces or text logs.
design:
Instrument the live runtime just enough to recover the semantic facts defined by the comparator contract. That means capturing events and counters relevant to outcomes, cancellation lifecycle, loser drain, region quiescence, obligation settlement, and any surface-specific invariants chosen for early pilots.

Instrumentation should prefer stable semantic hooks over brittle log scraping or raw trace deltas. If a surface cannot be observed well enough yet, that should become a first-class limitation rather than an excuse to compare on shaky proxies.
acceptance_criteria:
The live execution path exposes the semantic evidence required by the normalized comparator schema through stable semantic hooks rather than fragile textual logs or incidental implementation details.

Missing observability is explicit and machine-readable rather than silently approximated, and capture-field behavior is covered by direct unit or fixture checks instead of being trusted only transitively.

The emitted evidence payloads and logs are structured enough that later normalization, reports, and crashpacks can trust the field names, missingness semantics, and provenance of each captured fact.
notes: Better instrumentation beats more tolerant comparison logic. This task should bias toward improving evidence quality.
close_reason: Implemented semantic capture hooks: CaptureManifest with observed/inferred/unsupported tracking, capture_terminal_outcome() from Outcome<T,E>, capture_terminal_from_result(), capture_obligation_balance(), capture_region_close(), capture_loser_drain(), capture_cancellation(). 18 new tests (total 98). Explicit FieldObservability annotations make missing observability machine-readable.

title: Normalize lab and live evidence into shared comparator records
description: Build the actual normalization path that converts heterogeneous lab/live evidence into the same semantic record type for comparison.
design:
Implement the mapping that takes lab evidence and live evidence and collapses both into the canonical normalized record defined earlier. This includes canonical ordering for data that is semantically unordered, consistent naming for obligations and regions, and explicit elision of incidental detail.

Where the mapping is lossy, the loss must be intentional and justified. The project should be able to explain exactly why omitted detail is not needed to judge semantic parity for the chosen surface.
acceptance_criteria:
There is a concrete normalization path from both execution environments into the shared comparator record, and unit or fixture coverage exercises representative positive and negative mappings directly.

Canonical example mappings and golden record shapes are pinned, and field-level diff output plus structured diagnostics make false-positive and false-negative risk reviewable when normalization behavior changes.

At least one reusable downstream consumer beyond the local normalization tests uses the same normalized shape end-to-end, so later runner and reporting flows are not quietly relying on a different record contract.
notes: This task is where semantic comparison becomes real instead of aspirational.
close_reason: Completed: normalization/comparator path implemented and resource-surface missing-counter/tolerance regressions fixed

title: Define time and scheduler-noise normalization policy for live re-execution
description: Specify how virtual time, wall clock, and scheduler noise should be treated when comparing lab and live results so the framework stays semantically sharp without becoming brittle.
design:
Define how the framework reconciles virtual time, wall clock, and scheduler noise during live re-execution. Some surfaces will require ordering or timing windows to be normalized; others must reject timing-sensitive comparison entirely until the effect boundary is better controlled.

This task should set the explicit policy for when time-based facts are comparable, when they are only advisory, and when they are out of scope. It should also say how reruns interact with timing noise so the comparator does not accidentally ratchet itself into useless tolerance.
acceptance_criteria:
There is a written normalization policy for time-related and scheduler-noise-related evidence.

The policy makes it clear which time facts are part of semantic comparison and which are not.

The policy also defines how suppression, qualification, or explanation of scheduler noise appears in reports and verdict semantics so later CI and operator flows do not invent their own tolerance language.
notes: Claimed after bv --robot-plan ranked the differential track as the clean unowned unblocker lane; implementing time and scheduler-noise normalization policy with contract coverage and downstream bindings.
close_reason: Completed time and scheduler-noise normalization policy, contract test, and downstream differential bindings.

title: Build live evidence capture and normalization unit suite with golden records
description: Test the live-capture and normalization pipeline directly with deterministic fixtures, negative cases, and field-level mismatch diagnostics.
design:
Add the deterministic verification suite for live-side capture and normalization. This should cover positive and negative cases for evidence extraction, missing-observability behavior, canonical ordering, lossy normalization decisions, and representative golden records that prove lab and live evidence collapse into the intended shared shape.

The suite should also require detailed diff logging when normalization mismatches occur. If a normalization regression happens, the output should show exactly which semantic field diverged and which source evidence produced it.
acceptance_criteria:
Live evidence capture and normalization have dedicated unit/fixture coverage rather than being tested only transitively through later pilots.

Representative golden lab/live records are checked into the verification story and are easy to diff when behavior changes.

Normalization failures emit detailed field-level diagnostics that make root-cause analysis fast, and at least one targeted end-to-end path proves the same capture/normalization surface behaves correctly when exercised through the real runner flow.
notes: Normalization is too central to leave under-tested. This bead makes it a first-class verification target instead of a hidden implementation detail.
close_reason: Implemented live capture manifest retention, golden normalization coverage, and capture-aware mismatch summaries in src/lab/dual_run.rs; targeted rch tests passed

title: Implement differential execution, divergence classification, and repro artifacts
description: Assemble the execution engine that runs the same scenario through lab and live paths, classifies mismatches, emits minimized repro bundles when parity fails, and exposes reusable end-to-end runner/report entrypoints that make the system practical for humans and CI.
design:
This phase assembles the actual differential judge. Its job is to run both paths, compare normalized records, and preserve evidence aggressively when parity fails.

The design should treat repro quality as part of correctness. A differential test that only says "mismatch" without a seed, witness, or replay bundle creates more frustration than confidence. The system should therefore integrate minimization, classification, and artifact generation tightly rather than bolt them on after the fact.

This phase should also guard against false positives by distinguishing unsupported surfaces, missing observability, and scheduler-only noise from true semantic divergence.
acceptance_criteria:
A reusable differential runner exists and can execute the same scenario in lab and live paths.

Divergences are classified and emitted with enough artifact material to reproduce or minimize them.

Reusable e2e runner scripts exist and produce detailed structured logs plus a concise operator-facing summary/report.

The framework includes negative-control calibration coverage proving that intentional mismatches are detected, classified, and reported correctly rather than only passing on positive-parity cases.

title: Implement differential executor that runs each scenario in lab and live
description: Build the shared execution engine that drives both runtimes from one scenario source and compares the resulting normalized semantic records.
design:
Implement the reusable executor that takes one scenario, runs the lab version and the live version, and then compares their normalized records. The runner should expose enough structure that higher-level suites can choose whether to stop on first divergence, retain all mismatches, or run a classification pass.

Avoid entangling this task with surface-specific semantics. The executor should be the plumbing that every pilot calls, while surface logic lives in scenario adapters and assertion helpers.
acceptance_criteria:
A reusable differential executor exists and is used by more than one surface-specific suite.

Unit/contract tests cover scenario dispatch, adapter invocation, and comparator wiring for the executor.

At least one smoke-level dual-run e2e path runs through the executor and emits structured run logs with seed/replay identifiers.
notes: This is the structural center of the whole program. If it becomes surface-specific, the framework will fragment immediately.

title: Emit crashpacks, replay bundles, and minimized artifacts on divergence
description: Make every mismatch preserve a useful debugging package, including replay material, normalized records, and any minimization lineage needed for regression promotion.
design:
When the executor finds a divergence, preserve enough information to debug it later without heroic manual reconstruction. Artifacts should include the scenario or seed material, normalized records, any relevant trace or witness data, minimization state, and guidance on how to rerun the case.

The artifact format should be durable enough for both human debugging and regression promotion. If minimization is available, the system should retain lineage from original discovery to reduced reproducer rather than discarding that provenance.
acceptance_criteria:
Divergences produce durable crashpack or replay-style artifacts rather than a bare assertion failure.

Artifacts include normalized records, seed lineage, replay or minimization instructions, and enough log context to rerun or minimize the failing case later.

Artifact packaging is verified well enough that contributors can connect a minimized reproducer back to the original discovery without manual archaeology, including stable artifact layout or naming expectations that reports and playbooks can reference.
notes: This task turns failure from a dead end into a debugging asset.
close_reason: Implemented differential crashpack/repro bundle schema payloads and validation coverage

title: Implement mismatch classifier and rerun heuristics to suppress harness noise
description: Build the conservative policy layer that classifies mismatches, decides when reruns are warranted, and prevents the framework from confusing noise with semantic failure or vice versa.
design:
Implement the policy layer that decides whether a mismatch is a likely true bug, a likely observability gap, a likely unsupported surface, or likely harness noise that should be rerun before escalation. This logic should reference the divergence taxonomy rather than inventing a second one.

The classifier should be conservative. It is better to preserve an uncertain failure with clear "needs investigation" status than to auto-dismiss a meaningful divergence because it looks noisy. At the same time, the system needs enough rerun discipline that CI does not become unusably flaky.
acceptance_criteria:
Mismatch classification and rerun heuristics exist and are wired into the differential workflow.

Unit tests cover each divergence class, rerun-decision edge cases, and failure to observe required evidence.

The resulting behavior reduces noise without silently discarding materially important failures, and emitted logs explain why the framework reran, suppressed, escalated, or marked a case unsupported.
notes: This is where the project balances skepticism and practicality. The wrong heuristics either create noise or hide bugs.
close_reason: Implemented classifier-driven rerun workflow and validated runner coverage

title: Author reusable end-to-end differential runner scripts and structured log/report pipeline
description: Create the actual runnable scripts and structured reporting path that turn the differential engine into an operator-friendly system with detailed logs and readable summaries.
design:
Author the reusable end-to-end scripts and report pipeline that operators and CI will actually run. These scripts should execute focused dual-run scenarios, support seed or scenario selection, emit detailed structured logs, and produce a concise human-readable summary that points to artifacts, crashpacks, and replay instructions.

This is not just a wrapper convenience task. It is the bridge between low-level harness correctness and usable operator experience. The scripts should be suitable for local use, `rch`-assisted heavier validation, and CI integration without everyone inventing their own ad hoc command lines.
acceptance_criteria:
The project has reusable e2e differential runner scripts, not just library entrypoints.

Those scripts emit structured logs rich enough for debugging and also generate a concise summary/report suitable for humans and CI.

The runner supports stable named profiles or scenario-pack selection plus machine-usable verdict or exit semantics so CI, docs, and local operators are speaking the same invocation language.

At least one dedicated self-check or calibration mode exercises intentional divergences through the same runner surface so operator workflows are tested on both success and controlled failure paths.
notes: This bead is the direct response to the user-quality concern: a framework is not enough if the way people run it and read it is clumsy.

title: Add negative-control differential self-tests and report-calibration scenarios
description: Build intentional-mismatch scenarios that prove the differential framework actually detects, classifies, and reports semantic disagreement correctly instead of only passing on positive-parity cases.
design:
A differential-validation system is only trustworthy if it can fail on purpose in well-understood ways. Positive-parity suites alone can hide a broken comparator, a silent suppression rule, or an unreadable report path.

This bead introduces negative controls and self-calibration scenarios. The framework should intentionally inject or emulate representative mismatches at the normalized-record layer and, where defensible, at scenario/runtime boundaries, then verify that the system produces the expected divergence class, artifact bundle, report fields, and exit or verdict semantics.

These scenarios are not fluff. They are the framework's own honesty tests: they prove that the checker detects real disagreement, preserves enough evidence, and does not mislabel or silently absorb an intentional fault.
acceptance_criteria:
There is a reusable self-test or calibration suite with intentional divergence scenarios covering at least comparator mismatch detection, artifact emission, classifier behavior, and operator-facing report quality.

The calibration suite has direct unit coverage plus at least one e2e execution path through the shared runner/report flow so the full operator experience is tested, not just library internals.

Expected divergence classes, artifact locations, profile/verdict semantics, human-readable summaries, and golden report or manifest fixtures are asserted explicitly, so a regression in the checker itself is visible immediately.
notes: Added during the third plan-space pass. This is the main trust-building feature that was still too implicit: users need evidence that the validator can catch intentional badness, not just that it often passes on good cases.
close_reason: Completed

title: Pilot differential validation on core runtime semantic surfaces
description: Apply the new framework to the highest-value surfaces first: cancellation, combinators, channels, obligations, region close/quiescence, and closely related sync behavior where the lab model should be strongest, using an explicit coverage matrix so the pilot work cannot collapse into a handful of superficial scenarios.
design:
This phase is the trust-building center of gravity. Rather than starting with the messiest I/O-heavy surfaces, begin with the runtime semantics the lab is already designed to model: cancellation protocol, loser drain behavior in combinators, cancel-correct channels, obligation accounting, region close/quiescence, and nearby sync invariants.

Each pilot should do two things at once: validate the new differential framework and validate the specific semantic surface. That means pilot suites should be adversarial, reproducible, and rich enough to catch both runtime bugs and modeling bugs.

The first success criterion is not breadth; it is credibility. A small number of sharp pilot suites that repeatedly catch real discrepancies is more valuable than superficial coverage over a larger area.
acceptance_criteria:
Each selected core surface has an explicit coverage matrix tying unit-level invariant checks, dual-run e2e scenarios, adversarial cases, and required log/artifact fields.

There are pilot differential suites for the core semantic surfaces where the lab is expected to be strongest.

Each pilot produces structured logs, seed/replay identifiers, and actionable artifacts through the common differential pipeline.

The pilot results are strong enough to justify whether the project should broaden coverage or first repair the lab/runtime mismatch story.
notes: These pilots should lean on existing invariants already described in AGENTS.md and the design docs: structured concurrency, region close implies quiescence, losers are drained, no obligation leaks, and cancellation is a protocol rather than a silent drop.
close_reason: Independent verification confirmed the core pilot parent is already satisfied on current HEAD; normalizing stale tracker state

For each selected surface, list the required unit-level invariant checks, the required dual-run e2e scenario families, the minimum adversarial cases, the expected artifact/log fields, and the pass/fail interpretation rules.

This keeps the pilot beads from staying too vague. Instead of "some adversarial cases," the project should know exactly which cancellation, combinator, channel, obligation, and quiescence situations must be represented and logged.

Future implementers can tell whether a pilot surface is under-tested without rereading prior discussion.

The matrix is concrete enough to prevent a pilot from being declared complete on the basis of one or two superficial scenarios.

title: Extend differential validation to virtualized time and transport surfaces
description: Expand from pure runtime semantics into surfaces that are still meaningfully comparable when effects are virtualized or otherwise normalized, without over-claiming accuracy for raw external systems, and make the observability/logging contract for those surfaces explicit before implementation spreads.
design:
This phase expands the program only into surfaces where comparison is still meaningful after virtualization or careful normalization. Timers and virtualized transports are good candidates because the effect boundary can be controlled. Raw sockets, HTTP against the real world, and browser behavior are not automatic follow-ons.

The work here should be gated by explicit entry criteria. Before broadening to a new surface, the project should be able to state what is virtualized, what remains external, what observables are stable, and why semantic comparison is still justified.

The main risk in this phase is overreach. A wider scope with weak observability will lower confidence rather than raise it.
acceptance_criteria:
Virtualized time and at least one transport-style surface are covered by explicit test matrices that spell out unit checks, dual-run scripts, observability assumptions, and required logs.

There is a documented gating policy explaining when a new I/O-heavy surface is eligible for inclusion.

The project has a clear written boundary that prevents contributors from claiming unsupported parity for raw external systems.
notes: This phase exists specifically because the right answer to "can the lab simulate everything accurately?" is nuanced. It should preserve that nuance instead of hiding it.

title: Add timer and virtual-time parity suites
description: Extend the differential framework into controlled time-related surfaces such as timers and deadlines where lab and live execution can still be compared semantically.
design:
Add differential suites for time-related behavior where the effect boundary is still controlled enough to compare meaningfully. This should focus on timers, sleeps, deadlines, and virtual-time-driven behavior that can be represented consistently across lab and live execution.

Use this bead to prove that the framework can widen beyond pure runtime semantics without losing clarity. If comparison requires vague timing tolerances or fragile wall-clock assumptions, narrow the scope until the parity story is defensible.
acceptance_criteria:
There is at least one differential suite covering timer or virtual-time semantics with explicit unit checks for the normalized time contract.

The suite includes dual-run e2e scenarios and logs the virtual-vs-live time evidence used to justify comparison.

The work demonstrates that widening beyond core semantics can be done without over-claiming precision.
notes: This is the first planned expansion beyond the pure semantic core because time can often be virtualized or normalized well enough to remain meaningful.
close_reason: Independent verification confirmed GoldDune's completed timer/virtual-time parity slice; normalizing stale tracker state

title: Add virtualized transport/loopback parity suites
description: Apply the framework to a carefully controlled transport boundary so the project can learn how far semantic differential validation can reach into I/O-like surfaces without overreaching.
design:
Add a transport-style pilot only after choosing an effect boundary that is sufficiently virtualized or looped back to compare meaningfully. This could be a fake transport, loopback transport, or other narrow surface where send/receive semantics, backpressure, and shutdown behavior can be observed consistently.

The objective is not to claim generic network parity. It is to prove that the differential framework can be extended to an I/O-like surface when controllability and observability are good enough.
acceptance_criteria:
There is at least one transport-style differential suite built on a controlled or virtualized boundary, with explicit unit checks and dual-run e2e scenarios.

The suite logs virtualization assumptions, compared observables, and excluded external effects so failures are interpretable.

The implementation yields concrete guidance on whether additional network-adjacent surfaces are worth differentializing.
notes: This bead should resist scope creep hard. A narrow, trustworthy transport pilot is better than a broad but untrustworthy networking story.
close_reason: Independent verification confirmed GoldDune's completed transport/loopback parity slice; normalizing stale tracker state

title: Publish eligibility gate for raw-socket, HTTP, and browser surfaces
description: Define the hard boundary and entry criteria for broadening lab-vs-live differential validation into external I/O surfaces so the program does not over-claim what it proves.
design:
Write the explicit entry criteria for any future attempt to differentialize raw sockets, HTTP, browsers, or similarly messy external surfaces. The criteria should cover virtualization requirements, observability sufficiency, artifact quality, and the minimum semantic claim that can be defended.

This bead should also record red lines: what is currently too external, too weakly observed, or too noisy to include responsibly. The point is to prevent future contributors from turning "lab-vs-live" into a misleading marketing claim.
acceptance_criteria:
There is a documented gate for adding raw-socket, HTTP, browser, or other heavily external surfaces.

The gate includes positive entry criteria, explicit current red lines, and the minimum virtualization controls, observability hooks, unit/e2e coverage, and log/artifact quality required before a surface can claim meaningful parity.

Future expansion decisions can point to this bead instead of improvising scope arguments from scratch.
notes: This task preserves epistemic honesty. It is the system's guardrail against claiming accuracy where the comparison machinery is not yet strong enough.

title: Operationalize the differential program in CI, stress lanes, and contributor workflow
description: Wire the differential system into repeatable project practice so new surfaces can be added safely, failures produce durable artifacts, contributors understand exactly what the framework proves and what it does not, and both local users and CI can consume the same runner/report/profile workflow.
design:
This phase makes the differential system operationally real. Once the harness and pilots exist, they must run often enough, preserve artifacts reliably enough, and be documented clearly enough that contributors trust and extend them instead of bypassing them.

The CI plan should separate fast gating from heavier stress runs. The project also needs seed-rotation, artifact-retention, and triage guidance so repeated mismatches improve the corpus instead of becoming flaky noise.

Documentation here should target future maintainers: how to add a new surface, how to interpret a divergence, when to classify something as unsupported, and how to route expensive runs through `rch` rather than creating local compilation storms.
acceptance_criteria:
The differential program has a realistic CI/stress execution model, named profile vocabulary, retention policy, reusable runner/report pipeline, and contributor playbook.

Routine and nightly lanes publish both concise summaries and detailed structured artifacts with stable verdict semantics that can be replayed locally.

New contributors can extend the system by following beads and docs rather than reverse-engineering prior conversations, and the operational workflow keeps heavy validation reproducible without turning the project into a flake farm.
notes: Operational concerns matter here because differential testing only improves confidence if failures are routinely rerun, preserved, and understood. Otherwise it degenerates into expensive noise.

description: Write the calibrated statement of what the lab-vs-live differential system proves today, what remains partial, and what is explicitly outside the current trust boundary, tying each claim to the evidence level and profile vocabulary users will actually see.
design:
Publish the plain-language matrix of what the differential program currently proves, what it partially covers, and what it does not claim. This should be the reader-facing counterpart to the more internal scope and gate beads, and it should be kept consistent with actual implementation status over time.

The matrix should help future maintainers answer the original motivating question honestly: yes, the project can stress-test the lab against live behavior on supported surfaces, but no, that does not automatically mean every external system behavior is faithfully simulated.

The matrix aligns with the actual scope, gate, and reporting beads instead of making broader promises, and future maintainers can use it to explain the program's value without overstating its reach.

title: Build operator-facing differential summaries, artifact indexes, and log-reading outputs
description: Layer usable summaries and artifact indexes on top of the detailed structured logs so the system is pleasant to operate, not just technically correct, and so reports expose the exact profile, divergence class, confidence/evidence level, and replay route users need.
design:
Add the operator-facing report layer that turns detailed structured logs into something a contributor or CI reviewer can consume quickly. This should include concise summaries, artifact indexes, pointers to replay commands, and stable terminology for divergence classes and confidence levels.

The goal is not to hide detail. The goal is to make the detail navigable. Raw structured logs should still exist, but they should sit behind a readable summary/report format that helps users move from symptom to artifact to rerun path efficiently.
acceptance_criteria:
Differential runs produce both machine-readable detailed logs and human-readable summaries that point to the right artifacts and rerun commands.

Those summaries surface the named profile, divergence class, confidence/evidence grade, seed lineage, artifact locations, and replay handles needed to move from symptom to reproduction quickly.

Representative report or summary fixtures are pinned as golden outputs, so changes to wording, fields, paths, or verdict presentation are deliberate rather than accidental.

A contributor can look at a failure report and understand what failed, how sure the framework is, and where to go next without spelunking raw JSON first, and the fast/nightly CI lanes and local e2e scripts share the same reporting vocabulary.
notes: This bead is specifically about user experience and plan quality. Better summaries do not replace detailed logs; they make the detailed logs usable.

title: Define named run profiles, scenario packs, and stable exit semantics
description: Create the user-facing invocation contract for the differential system so humans and CI use clear named profiles and scenario packs instead of assembling raw flags, seeds, and artifact expectations by hand.
design:
The framework now has runner scripts, crashpacks, summaries, CI lanes, and corpus management, but users still need a stable way to invoke those capabilities without learning implementation internals. This bead defines that operator contract.

The system should expose named run profiles such as `smoke`, `core`, `repro`, and `nightly` (names can change if better ones emerge, but the concept should be explicit). Each profile should identify which scenario packs or surfaces it exercises, what level of runtime cost it implies, what artifacts/logs it is expected to emit, and what exit semantics or confidence statuses it can produce.

This is a plan-quality and user-quality bead: it prevents the differential program from technically existing while still being awkward to operate.
acceptance_criteria:
There is a documented set of named run profiles and scenario packs for the differential framework, covering at least local smoke, targeted core validation, replay/reproduction, a dedicated self-check or calibration mode, and heavier scheduled stress usage.

Each profile specifies expected scope, runtime cost, artifact/log outputs, and stable exit or verdict semantics that humans and CI can rely on.

The profile vocabulary is backed by a stable manifest or equivalent machine-readable description that scripts, CI, reports, and docs can all consume consistently.

The CI lanes, contributor playbook, and operator-facing summaries all reference the same profile vocabulary instead of inventing parallel command conventions.
notes: This bead was added during the second planning pass because the earlier graph had the technical machinery but not enough explicit user-facing invocation ergonomics. That gap would have shown up later as confusing docs and bespoke CI wrappers.

title: [EPIC-INFRA] Region Tree Property Testing
description:
## Overview

Implement comprehensive property-based testing for the region tree using proptest, verifying structural invariants hold under arbitrary operation sequences.

## Strategic Value

**Problem Solved**: Unit tests check specific scenarios but may miss edge cases. Property-based testing generates thousands of random scenarios, finding bugs that humans wouldn't think to test.

**Invariant Verification**: The region tree has critical invariants (no orphans, proper parent-child relationships, cancellation propagation). Property tests verify these hold for ALL possible operation sequences.

**Confidence**: With property tests, we can refactor region tree internals confidently, knowing the invariants are continuously verified.

## Key Invariants to Test

### Structural Invariants
1. **No orphan tasks**: Every task has a valid parent region
2. **Tree structure**: No cycles, single root, proper parent pointers
3. **Child tracking**: Parent's children list matches children's parent pointers
4. **ID uniqueness**: No duplicate RegionId or TaskId

### Behavioral Invariants
5. **Cancel propagation**: If parent cancelled, all descendants cancelled
6. **Close ordering**: Region cannot close until all children closed
7. **Outcome collection**: All child outcomes collected before parent completes

### Resource Invariants
8. **No leaks**: After full close, all resources freed
9. **Budget inheritance**: Child budgets never exceed parent budgets

## Property Test Strategy

### Arbitrary Operations
```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Arbitrary)]
enum RegionOp {
    CreateChild,
    SpawnTask,
    CancelRegion(RegionSelector),
    CompleteTask(TaskSelector),
    CloseRegion(RegionSelector),
    AdvanceTime(Duration),
}
```

### Test Harness
```rust
proptest! {
    #[test]
    fn region_tree_invariants(ops: Vec<RegionOp>) {
        let mut tree = RegionTree::new();
        
        for op in ops {
            tree.apply(op);
            tree.assert_invariants();  // Check after EVERY operation
        }
    }
}
```

### Shrinking
Proptest automatically shrinks failing cases to minimal reproductions. A failure with 1000 ops might shrink to 3 ops that reproduce the bug.

## Test Categories

### Category 1: Structure Tests
- Random create/close sequences maintain tree structure
- Deep nesting (100+ levels) works correctly
- Wide trees (1000+ children) work correctly

### Category 2: Cancellation Tests  
- Random cancel at any node propagates correctly
- Cancel during close is handled
- Multiple concurrent cancels are idempotent

### Category 3: Completion Tests
- Random task completions with various outcomes
- Panic in child doesn't corrupt parent
- All outcomes eventually collected

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Arbitrary impl for RegionOp
2. assert_invariants() checks all 9 invariants
3. At least 5 property test functions
4. Tests run 10,000+ cases each
5. Shrinking produces minimal reproductions
6. CI runs property tests (with fixed seed for reproducibility)

## Dependencies

- Uses proptest (already in dev-dependencies)
- Tests region tree internals

## Priority Rationale

Ranked #14 because while extremely valuable for correctness, property tests are a testing technique rather than user-facing feature. The runtime works without them, they just increase confidence.

title: [AUDIT] Deep correctness audit: obligation/choreography/mod.rs
notes:
VERDICT: SOUND — 0 bugs found

## Module: src/obligation/choreography/mod.rs (3,119 lines: 1,585 production + 1,534 tests)

### Concurrency Analysis
ZERO concurrency primitives. Pure data structure / DSL module. No atomics, no locks, no wakers, no async. All functions synchronous with immutable references or owned values.

### Architecture
Choreographic programming DSL for saga protocol generation (Montesi 2023). Single source of truth for multi-participant protocols with projection to per-participant session types.

- **AST**: GlobalProtocol, Participant, MessageType, Interaction enum (8 variants: Comm, Choice, Loop, Continue, Compensate, Seq, Par, End)
- **Builder API**: ProtocolBuilder with fluent API
- **Validation**: 9 error types, knowledge-of-choice (Honda-Yoshida-Carbone 2008), loop label scoping, parallel disjointness
- **Projection**: GlobalProtocol::project -> LocalType (Send, Recv, InternalChoice, ExternalChoice, Rec, RecVar, Compensate, End)
- **Statistics**: ProtocolStats with comm/choice/loop/compensate/par counts, depth, monotonicity
- **Example protocols**: 2PC, lease renewal, saga compensation, scatter-gather (overlap + disjoint)

### Key Correctness Properties Verified

1. **Validation** (CORRECT): All 9 error types properly detected. Loop label scoping uses HashSet insert+remove to prevent label leaks into sibling interactions (line 712). Knowledge-of-choice uses first_active_participant which correctly traverses through Loop/Compensate/Seq/Par.

2. **Projection** (CORRECT): 
   - Comm: sender->Send, receiver->Recv, uninvolved->skip to continuation
   - Choice: decider->InternalChoice, non-decider->ExternalChoice, single-branch->just that branch
   - Loop: skips projection if participant not referenced in body (prevents vacuous Rec{RecVar} swallowing subsequent actions)
   - Continue: always RecVar (protected by Loop's participant check)
   - Par: picks branch involving participant (disjointness validated separately; fallback to left for invalid overlap)

3. **seq_local** (CORRECT): Replaces End leaves in first with second. RecVar returns as-is (fixed-point semantics). Compensate only recurses into forward (compensation is failure path). InternalChoice/ExternalChoice clone second for both branches.

4. **first_active_participant** (CORRECT): Comm->sender, Choice->decider, Loop->body, Continue/End->None, Compensate->forward, Seq->first-then-second, Par->left-then-right.

5. **Statistics** (CORRECT): Seq doesn't increment depth (sequential is flat). Monotonicity counting distinguishes Monotone/NonMonotone/None.

### Tests
80+ tests including: all example protocols validate/deadlock-free, error detection (self-communication, undeclared participant, knowledge-of-choice, undefined/duplicate loop labels, parallel overlap, empty protocol, no participants), projection completeness (every global action appears in local type), projection duality (sender's Send matches receiver's Recv), loop label scoping (sibling labels, choice branch isolation), Continue projection for uninvolved participants, proptest (200 cases: validation never panics, referenced subset of declared, valid protocols project all participants, projection duality for Comm, stats consistency).

### No unsafe blocks. No concurrency concerns.

comments.author: CalmRaven
comments.text:
Doctor_asupersync Product Blueprint (self-contained)

Goal:
Create a radically useful operational cockpit for asupersync-based systems: one place to discover runtime structure, execute deterministic diagnostics, investigate failures, apply guided remediations, and emit evidence-grade artifacts.

Why this matters:
1. Existing workflows are fragmented across cargo/rch output, traces, tests, beads, and agent mail.
2. Failures in async/cancellation systems are expensive because root causes are often distributed in time and across subsystems.
3. Deterministic replay and explicit evidence packaging are strategic advantages that should be surfaced as first-class UX, not hidden as ad hoc scripts.

Core product principles:
1. Determinism-first: every finding links to exact command/seed/config so the user can replay.
2. Invariant-first: diagnose against asupersync non-negotiables (structured concurrency, cancel protocol, loser drain, obligation closure, lock ordering).
3. Actionability-first: every finding should propose concrete next actions, not just red/yellow/green scores.
4. Operator cognition-first: maintain context with persistent global state, timeline views, and cross-linking between evidence and decisions.
5. Coordination-native: beads/bv + Agent Mail integrations are in-product workflows, not afterthoughts.

Execution model:
Track 1 defines what users need to see and decide.
Track 2 builds the data/analysis substrate.
Track 3 builds run orchestration and replay tooling.
Track 4 turns findings into safe remediation loops.
Track 5 integrates execution ecosystems (beads, mail, FrankenSuite artifacts).
Track 6 hardens quality and ships adoption-ready packaging.

Success metrics:
1. Time-to-first-root-cause reduced versus current manual workflow.
2. Replay success rate for reported failures.
3. Remediation success rate after guided apply + verification loop.
4. False-positive rate of analyzers stays within defined bounds.
5. Operator trust: evidence exports are complete enough for independent review.

Boundary notes:
1. Not a generic terminal metrics dashboard.
2. Not a replacement executor; heavy commands run through rch adapters.
3. No compromise on determinism/cancellation correctness for convenience.

description:

**Location**: `src/runtime/state.rs` Arena::insert(), `src/util/arena.rs`
**Evidence**: flamegraph-2026-04-24.md shows exponential growth reallocations every ~1024 tasks
**Pattern**: Vec reallocations during Arena expansion: `self.slots.reserve(self.slots.len())`

title: Implement quorum combinator for consensus patterns
description:
## Purpose
The quorum combinator implements M-of-N completion semantics - wait for M out of N concurrent tasks to complete successfully before returning. This is essential for distributed consensus patterns, redundancy, and fault-tolerant operations.

## Mathematical Foundation
Quorum builds on the near-semiring concurrency algebra from the spec:
- `join (⊗)`: All must complete (N-of-N)
- `race (⊕)`: First wins (1-of-N)
- `quorum(M, N)`: M-of-N - generalization between join and race

The outcome aggregation follows the severity lattice: Ok < Err < Cancelled < Panicked
For quorum(M, N): return Ok if ≥M tasks return Ok; otherwise aggregate errors.

## Semantic Model

```rust
pub async fn quorum<T, E>(
    cx: &mut Cx<'_>,
    m: usize,  // Required successes
    tasks: Vec<impl Future<Output = Result<T, E>>>,
) -> Outcome<Vec<T>, E>
```

### Behavior
1. Spawn all N tasks as region children
2. Track completions as they arrive
3. On M successes: cancel remaining (N-M) losers, drain them, return Ok
4. On (N-M+1) failures: know quorum impossible, cancel all remaining, return aggregated error
5. Losers MUST be fully drained (non-negotiable invariant)

### Edge Cases
- `quorum(0, N)`: Return Ok([]) immediately, cancel all tasks
- `quorum(N, N)`: Equivalent to join (all must succeed)
- `quorum(1, N)`: Equivalent to race (first wins)
- `quorum(M, N) where M > N`: Type error or early failure

## Cancellation Handling
- When quorum achieved OR impossible: request_cancel(losers)
- Wait for all losers to complete (Running → CancelRequested → Cancelling → Finalizing → Completed)
- Honor loser cleanup budgets
- Propagate incoming cancellation to all children

## Invariant Support
- **Losers always drained**: Core non-negotiable - all N tasks eventually complete
- **No obligation leaks**: If a winning task holds obligations, they flow to caller
- **Region quiescence**: Quorum region only closes when ALL children (winners + losers) are done

## Testing Requirements
1. Basic M-of-N success scenarios
2. Early failure detection (quorum impossible)
3. Loser draining verification
4. Cancellation budget honoring
5. Mixed outcome aggregation
6. Lab runtime determinism

## Example Usage

```rust
// Wait for 2-of-3 replicas to acknowledge
let acks = scope.quorum(cx, 2, vec![
    write_replica_a(cx),
    write_replica_b(cx),
    write_replica_c(cx),
]).await?;
```

## References
- asupersync_plan_v4.md: §5.7 Derived Combinators, §3 Near-Semiring
- asupersync_v4_formal_semantics.md: §3.2 Concurrency Algebra

## Acceptance Criteria
- Quorum(k) returns when k branches satisfy the success predicate, while cancelling + draining remaining branches.
- Result aggregation is policy-aware and deterministic in lab runs.
- Handles partial failures and cancellation without leaking obligations.
- E2E tests cover quorum success, quorum failure, and cancellation mid-quorum.

title: [cancel-bug-hunt] cancel/symbol_cancel.rs: add_listener silently fabricates fake CancelKind::User on race window
description: src/cancel/symbol_cancel.rs:313-329 SymbolCancelToken::add_listener takes the listeners write lock, checks is_cancelled(), and if true drops the lock and IMMEDIATELY invokes the listener. The reason and timestamp are read via self.reason().unwrap_or_else(|| CancelReason::new(CancelKind::User)) and self.cancelled_at().unwrap_or(Time::ZERO). These fallbacks mask a real protocol race: the listeners-lock branch can observe cancelled=true (set by cancel() Release CAS) BEFORE cancel() finishes writing the reason — even though cancel() holds the reason.write() lock during CAS, add_listener's reason() call only takes a read lock and races against the brief window between cancel()'s drop(reason_guard) and the listener invocation. A None reason here surfaces as a fabricated CancelKind::User with Time::ZERO, telling the listener the user requested a manual cancel at the epoch — which can route cleanup down the WRONG branch (e.g., user-cancel = preserve partial work; deadline = aggressive abort). Fix: serialize add_listener through the reason.write() lock (mirror cancel()'s discipline), OR if reason() returns None despite is_cancelled()=true, propagate Err / panic in debug rather than fabricate. Severity HIGH (silent protocol misclassification).
close_reason: add_listener now takes reason.write() lock so the cancelled-then-reason check is race-free; debug_assert + parent_cancelled fallback (no fabricated CancelKind::User) (38ea89a6e)

title: Implement test oracle: quiescence_on_close invariant checker
description:
## Purpose
Implement a test oracle that verifies the "quiescence on close" invariant: when a region closes, it has achieved complete quiescence - no live children, all finalizers run, all obligations resolved.

## The Invariant
From asupersync_plan_v4.md:
> Region close = quiescence: no live children + all finalizers done

This is the foundational guarantee of structured concurrency. A region close is a HARD synchronization point.

## Quiescence Components
Quiescence requires ALL of:
1. **No live tasks**: All tasks in Completed state
2. **No live subregions**: All subregions Closed
3. **All finalizers run**: defer_async and defer_sync complete
4. **All obligations resolved**: No pending SendPermit, Ack, Lease, IoOp

## Oracle Design

```rust
pub struct QuiescenceOracle {
    // Tracks region state
    region_states: HashMap<RegionId, RegionSnapshot>,
}

pub struct RegionSnapshot {
    pub tasks: Vec<(TaskId, TaskState)>,
    pub subregions: Vec<(RegionId, RegionState)>,
    pub finalizers: Vec<(FinalizerId, FinalizerState)>,
    pub obligations: Vec<(ObligationId, ObligationState)>,
}

impl QuiescenceOracle {
    /// Take snapshot of region state
    pub fn snapshot(&mut self, region: RegionId, snapshot: RegionSnapshot);
    
    /// Called when region transitions to Closed
    pub fn on_close(&mut self, region: RegionId, time: Time);
    
    /// Verify quiescence at close
    pub fn check_quiescence(&self, region: RegionId) -> Result<(), QuiescenceViolation>;
}
```

## Violation Types
```rust
pub enum QuiescenceViolation {
    LiveTasks { region: RegionId, tasks: Vec<TaskId> },
    OpenSubregions { region: RegionId, subregions: Vec<RegionId> },
    PendingFinalizers { region: RegionId, finalizers: Vec<FinalizerId> },
    UnresolvedObligations { region: RegionId, obligations: Vec<ObligationId> },
}
```

## Close Protocol Verification
The oracle verifies the close protocol from the spec:
```
CLOSE-PEND:   Live(r) = ∅ ⟹ r.state := ClosePending
CLOSE-FINAL:  r.state = ClosePending ∧ FinalizersRan(r) ⟹ r.state := FinalDone  
CLOSE-DONE:   r.state = FinalDone ∧ Quiescent(r) ⟹ r.state := Closed
```

Each transition has preconditions; oracle verifies they hold.

## Recursive Verification
For nested regions:
1. Inner regions must close before outer can close
2. Oracle tracks region tree
3. Close of region R implies close of all descendants first

## Testing the Oracle
1. **Clean close**: All components quiescent → passes
2. **Live task violation**: Task still running at close attempt
3. **Open subregion violation**: Subregion not closed
4. **Pending finalizer violation**: Finalizer not run
5. **Unresolved obligation violation**: Obligation in Created state
6. **Nested regions**: Verify recursive quiescence

## Integration with Scheduler
Oracle hooks:
- Region state transitions (Open → ClosePending → FinalDone → Closed)
- Task state transitions
- Finalizer execution events
- Obligation resolution events

## References
- asupersync_plan_v4.md: §4.2 Region Lifecycle, §1.1 Non-negotiable invariants
- asupersync_v4_formal_semantics.md: CLOSE-* rules, Quiescent predicate

## Acceptance Criteria
- Oracle verifies region close implies quiescence: no live tasks, all subregions closed, all obligations resolved, all finalizers done.
- Diagnostics identify the exact remaining live items (tasks/regions/obligations/finalizers).
- Deterministic and usable both on Σ snapshots and trace projections.
