title: [reader-starvation] sync/rwlock.rs writer-preference design allows indefinite reader starvation under continuous write load
description:
src/sync/rwlock.rs:286-356 — the RwLock implements writer-preference fairness (correctly prevents writer starvation) but allows reader starvation under continuous write load. A reader's try_read fails whenever writer_waiters greater-than 0; under steady write traffic, new read requests are perpetually blocked.

Why this is filed even though it's documented (lines 15-28): the documentation acknowledges the trade-off but does not surface the failure mode in the API. A caller writing read-heavy code that occasionally fails under load may not realize the cause is reader starvation rather than transient contention. The 'no obligation leaks' invariant of the project means reader-blocked tasks should make progress; indefinite starvation is a violation in spirit.

Concrete failure modes:
  (a) Read-heavy services with periodic writes (config reload every minute, leadership churn, etc.) see read latency spike during the write window, recover after, but the cumulative tail-latency is poor.
  (b) Read tasks that don't have a timeout block forever during a write storm.
  (c) Workloads that mix reads + writes from the same task can self-deadlock (the task's own future read attempt blocks behind its own pending writer, if both are queued via the cancel scheduler).

Fix direction (NOT a fix recommendation, just options):
  1. Document explicitly that RwLock readers should always carry a timeout or be cancellable, and that pure reader-priority is not provided.
  2. Or: add an alt RwLock::FAIR mode that alternates between batches of readers and writers, mitigating both starvation directions.
  3. Or: add a 'reader_grace_period' config: if writer_waiters greater-than 0 BUT readers have been blocked for X duration, admit a single reader batch.

Severity MEDIUM (design limitation that can cause application hangs but is documented; promotion to HIGH if a real workload is found in the wild).

Source: /reality-check on src/sync/* deepest pass (2026-04-26).
close_reason: mitigated: bounded write-prefer with consecutive_writers_served counter (limit 16) forces a reader batch, preventing indefinite reader starvation under continuous write load

title: [gauntlet PERF-R3] apply_perf_ratchet.py quarantine is one-sided (candidate cv_pct only) - flaky committed baseline would produce phantom verdicts
description:
Gauntlet round-3 finding. scripts/apply_perf_ratchet.py:168-172 quarantines a benchmark only when the CANDIDATE's cv_pct exceeds the flake threshold; it never checks the BASELINE side's cv_pct. Consequence: if a contention-noisy run is ever committed to .bench-history as the baseline, every future stable candidate gets compared against noise-skewed medians, producing phantom Block verdicts (false regressions) or phantom improvements.

This was discovered when the round-3 full-mode official baseline attempt came back with 39/51 benches flaky (cv_pct up to 19.4%) due to shared-worker contention - committing it would have silently corrupted the gate.

Fix: in the comparison loop, also read base.get('cv_pct'); if the baseline entry is flaky, quarantine the bench (reason: 'baseline_flaky') instead of scoring it. Update the synthetic Allow/Block/Quarantine test fixtures to cover a flaky-baseline case. Also update capture_baseline.sh docs/bead zb2a7h to state that committed baselines must have an empty (or near-empty) flaky_benches list.

Evidence: asupersync__gauntlet_workspace/PERF_NEGATIVE_RESULTS.md entry 'full-mode-baseline-on-shared-rch-worker' + reports/round3/perf005_official_sweep.log

title: Implement test oracle: losers_always_drained invariant checker
description:
## Purpose
Implement a test oracle that verifies the "losers always drained" invariant: in any race/select operation, losing tasks are cancelled AND fully drained before the operation returns.

## The Invariant
From asupersync_plan_v4.md:
> Races must cancel and fully drain losers

This prevents resource leaks, ensures cleanup runs, and maintains predictable behavior.

## What "Drained" Means
A task is drained when it has:
1. Received cancel request (`CancelRequested` state)
2. Run to next checkpoint (`Cancelling` state)
3. Executed finalizers (`Finalizing` state)
4. Reached `Completed(Cancelled)` state

Simply requesting cancellation is NOT sufficient. The task must actually complete.

## Oracle Design

```rust
pub struct LoserDrainOracle {
    // Tracks race/select operations
    race_starts: Vec<RaceEvent>,
    race_completes: Vec<RaceCompletion>,
    task_drains: HashMap<TaskId, DrainRecord>,
}

pub struct RaceEvent {
    pub race_id: RaceId,
    pub participants: Vec<TaskId>,
    pub start_time: Time,
}

pub struct RaceCompletion {
    pub race_id: RaceId,
    pub winner: TaskId,
    pub losers: Vec<TaskId>,
    pub complete_time: Time,
}

pub struct DrainRecord {
    pub cancel_requested: Option<Time>,
    pub drain_started: Option<Time>,
    pub finalizers_complete: Option<Time>,
    pub fully_drained: Option<Time>,
}

impl LoserDrainOracle {
    /// Called when race/select starts
    pub fn on_race_start(&mut self, race_id: RaceId, participants: Vec<TaskId>, time: Time);
    
    /// Called when race determines winner
    pub fn on_race_complete(&mut self, race_id: RaceId, winner: TaskId, time: Time);
    
    /// Called when task fully drains
    pub fn on_task_drained(&mut self, task: TaskId, time: Time);
    
    /// Verify all losers are drained before race returns
    pub fn check(&self) -> Result<(), LoserDrainViolation>;
}
```

## Violation Detection
```rust
pub struct LoserDrainViolation {
    pub race_id: RaceId,
    pub winner: TaskId,
    pub undrained_losers: Vec<(TaskId, DrainRecord)>,
    pub race_return_time: Time,
}
```

A violation occurs when:
1. Race R completes at time T
2. ∃ loser L where `fully_drained` time > T or is None

## Operations That Must Drain Losers
| Operation | Winner | Losers |
|-----------|--------|--------|
| `race(a, b)` | First to complete | Other participants |
| `select\!{...}` | Selected branch | Unselected branches |
| `quorum(M, N)` | First M successes | Remaining N-M |
| `first_ok(...)` | First success | Operations after success |
| `timeout(op, d)` | Whichever wins | Timeout or op |

## Testing the Oracle
1. **Two-way race**: Winner and loser properly handled
2. **N-way race**: Multiple losers all drained
3. **Nested races**: Inner race losers drained before outer race proceeds
4. **Loser with finalizers**: Finalizers run during drain
5. **Loser with obligations**: Obligations resolved during drain
6. **Slow drain**: Loser takes time to reach checkpoint

## Drain Timing Verification
The oracle tracks timing to ensure:
- `race_return_time > max(loser_drain_times)`
- Race does NOT return until all losers fully drained

## References
- asupersync_plan_v4.md: §5.5 Race with Loser Draining, §1.1 Non-negotiable invariants
- asupersync_v4_formal_semantics.md: RACE-LOSER-DRAIN rule

## Acceptance Criteria
- Oracle identifies each race and validates that all losers reach terminal completion before the race returns.
- Also validates losers are cancelled (or otherwise transitioned out of running) promptly.
- Produces actionable diagnostics (winner/loser ids, missing completion event).
- Deterministic and runs on every E2E scenario trace.
close_reason: Implemented oracle module with TaskLeakOracle, ObligationLeakOracle, QuiescenceOracle, LoserDrainOracle, FinalizerOracle. All tests passing, clippy clean.

title: [WASM][Rust API] Public Rust-authored browser runtime path
description:
Turn the Rust-authored browser-runtime path from 'architecturally feasible' into a real public lane. README and docs currently say the semantic core is portable but the Rust-to-WASM path is not yet documented, tested, or exposed as a public API path.

This epic closes that gap so Rust users can author browser-facing Asupersync code directly, not only consume the JS/TS packages.
design: Define the supported Rust authoring model first, then build a canonical example and validation harnesses around it. The goal is not to promise full native API parity inside wasm; it is to expose a truthful browser-safe Rust path with explicit capability use and clear unsupported-surface boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: 1. There is a documented, public Rust-to-WASM Browser Edition path with explicit scope and limitations.\n2. Canonical examples compile and run against supported browser profiles.\n3. Unit/browser harness coverage proves that Rust-authored scopes, tasks, cancellation, and browser-safe capabilities behave correctly.
notes: The path defined here must stay aligned with the same support matrix used for JS/TS consumers. No secret extra parity promises for Rust consumers.

2. The defined surface aligns with the browser support matrix rather than implying extra native parity.

title: [WASM][Rust API] Replace std::thread startup assumptions with browser host services abstraction
description: Replace native-thread startup assumptions with an explicit browser host-services seam. The current runtime startup path still assumes std::thread-backed workers and deadline monitors, which blocks a truthful public Rust browser builder. This bead creates the architectural seam needed so browser execution can bootstrap through host-provided scheduling, timers, worker creation, and health services instead of smuggled native assumptions.
design:
Refactor runtime startup so browser-native lanes receive host services explicitly: timer/deadline driving, worker/bootstrap hooks, event-loop wakeups, and lane-health callbacks. The design must preserve the same structured-concurrency and cancellation guarantees while making it impossible for a public Rust builder to accidentally rely on unavailable native primitives.

3. Unsupported native-only startup behavior is impossible to reach accidentally from the browser path.
4. Unit and smoke-harness evidence prove the seam is usable and diagnosable rather than only theoretically correct.
notes: This is the real blocker-removal step for the Rust browser story. Without it, every public builder would still be a polite lie and future debugging would stay opaque.

title: Unbounded exponential backoff in PostgresSaga retry logic could overflow
description:
In real_database_postgres_obligation_saga_integration_e2e_tests.rs:440, the retry logic uses unbounded exponential backoff:

cx.sleep(Duration::from_millis(100 * (1 << attempt))).await;

If max_retry_attempts is set to a high value (e.g., 30), the expression (1 << attempt) will overflow, potentially causing panic or infinite delay.

Root cause: No bounds checking on exponential backoff calculation.

Fix: Add bounds checking, e.g.:
let delay_ms = 100 * (1u64 << attempt.min(10));  // Cap at ~100 seconds
or use a proper exponential backoff library with jitter.
close_reason: Fixed exponential backoff overflow by capping shift operation to max 10, limiting delay to ~100 seconds

description:
# Codec Framework

## Overview
Bidirectional encoding/decoding with framing support.

## Core Traits

### Decoder
```rust
pub trait Decoder {
    type Item;
    type Error;
    fn decode(&mut self, src: &mut BytesMut) -> Result<Option<Self::Item>, Self::Error>;
}
```

### Encoder
```rust
pub trait Encoder<Item> {
    type Error;
    fn encode(&mut self, item: Item, dst: &mut BytesMut) -> Result<(), Self::Error>;
}
```

## Standard Codecs

### 1. LinesCodec
- Newline-delimited text
- Configurable max line length

### 2. LengthDelimitedCodec
- Length-prefixed framing
- Configurable length field (u8, u16, u32, u64)
- Big/little endian

### 3. BytesCodec
- Raw bytes passthrough

### 4. AnyDelimiterCodec
- Custom delimiter support

## Framed Transport

### FramedRead<T, D>
- Combines AsyncRead + Decoder
- Implements Stream

### FramedWrite<T, E>
- Combines AsyncWrite + Encoder
- Implements Sink

### Framed<T, U>
- Full duplex codec transport
- Stream + Sink

## Cancel-Safety
- Decode: partial frame preserved in buffer
- Encode: atomic frame writes
- Framed: tracks partial state

## Bytes Integration
- bytes::Bytes and BytesMut
- Zero-copy where possible

# Time/Timers Verification Suite

## Purpose
Comprehensive verification for the time/timer infrastructure (mf6) ensuring virtual/wall time correctness, budget integration, and deterministic behavior.

### 1. Unit Tests

- sleep_until(instant): absolute time pause
- interval(period): repeating timer

- Production: wall time advances independently

### 4. Determinism Tests
- Same seed → identical timer ordering
- Replay tests: record and replay timer sequences

## Logging Requirements
- Timer events logged with virtual/wall timestamps

- [ ] All timer operations have unit tests

title: [security-audit] src/security/key.rs: AuthKey not zeroized on drop (Phase 0 limitation)
description:
AuthKey is #[derive(Clone, Copy, ...)] (line 19) and the struct comment explicitly notes 'Keys should be treated as sensitive material and zeroized when dropped (Phase 1+ requirement). For Phase 0, we focus on functional correctness.'

The Copy derive precludes a Drop impl. Once asupersync moves toward Phase 1+, AuthKey needs to: (1) drop the Copy derive, (2) impl Zeroize + ZeroizeOnDrop (the zeroize crate). Same for MacaroonSignature::bytes (src/cx/macaroon.rs:405) which holds 32-byte HMAC chain signatures derived from root keys. Note: callers currently rely on Copy semantics via .as_bytes() and explicit clones; lifting Copy is a trait-bound ripple touching ~50 sites.

Other security patterns audited and SOUND in this pass:
  - tag.rs verify(): mac.verify_slice() is constant-time (RustCrypto subtle).
  - tag.rs PartialEq: manual XOR-OR loop (lines 94-102), no early exit.
  - macaroon.rs constant_time_eq (line 411): correct XOR-OR loop, no early exit.
  - macaroon.rs verify_signature, verify_discharge_signature, verify_caveat_chain: all use constant_time_eq on the chain HMAC.
  - tag.rs domain separation: AUTH_TAG_DOMAIN prefix prevents cross-context replay.
  - tag.rs canonical binding: tag covers domain || object_id || sbn || esi || kind || len || payload — a captured tag cannot replay against a different symbol.
  - macaroon.rs from_bytes: try_into() bounds-checks before [..AUTH_KEY_SIZE] subarray (line 980).
  - key.rs derive_subkey: HMAC-SHA256(self, purpose) — domain-separated chain.
  - Debug impls on AuthKey + MacaroonSignature truncate to 2 bytes — no full key leakage in logs.
close_reason: AuthKey now zeroizes on Drop via ptr::write_volatile + SeqCst compiler_fence. Copy derive removed (mutually exclusive with Drop) — callers using key by value updated to .clone(). New drop_zeroises_key_bytes test uses ManuallyDrop + raw-pointer pre/post observation. Audit of other security types: AuthenticationTag is non-secret (no zeroize needed), SecurityContext + KeyRing get zeroize transitively via field drop. 87/87 security tests pass.

title: Implement test oracle: no_task_leaks invariant checker
description:
## Purpose
Implement a test oracle that verifies the "no task leaks" invariant: after any region closes, no tasks spawned within that region remain running. This is one of the 6 non-negotiable invariants.

## The Invariant
From asupersync_plan_v4.md:
> Every spawned task is owned by a region; region close waits for all children

Formally: `∀r ∈ closed_regions: tasks_in_region(r) = ∅`

After `scope.region(...).await` returns, the region's `TaskSet` must be empty (all tasks in Completed state).

## Oracle Design

```rust
pub struct TaskLeakOracle {
    // Tracks all task spawns and completions
    spawns: Vec<(TaskId, RegionId, Time)>,
    completions: Vec<(TaskId, Time)>,
    region_closes: Vec<(RegionId, Time)>,
}

impl TaskLeakOracle {
    /// Called by scheduler on each spawn
    pub fn on_spawn(&mut self, task: TaskId, region: RegionId, time: Time);
    
    /// Called when task reaches Completed
    pub fn on_complete(&mut self, task: TaskId, time: Time);
    
    /// Called when region reaches Closed
    pub fn on_region_close(&mut self, region: RegionId, time: Time);
    
    /// Verify invariant holds
    pub fn check(&self) -> Result<(), TaskLeakViolation>;
}
```

## Violation Detection
```rust
pub struct TaskLeakViolation {
    pub region: RegionId,
    pub leaked_tasks: Vec<TaskId>,
    pub region_close_time: Time,
}
```

A violation occurs when:
1. Region R closes at time T
2. ∃ task spawned in R with no completion record at time ≤ T

## Integration Points
The oracle hooks into:
1. `Cx::spawn()` - records spawn event
2. Task state transition to `Completed` - records completion
3. Region state transition to `Closed` - records close and triggers check

## Lab Runtime Integration
In lab runtime, oracle checks run automatically:
- After each region close
- At end of test execution
- Before schedule replay verification

## Invariant Mapping

| Invariant | Oracle |
|-----------|--------|
| 1. Structured concurrency | **no_task_leaks** |
| 2. Region close = quiescence | quiescence_on_close |
| 3. Cancellation is protocol | (verified by state machine tests) |
| 4. Losers are drained | losers_always_drained |
| 5. No obligation leaks | no_obligation_leaks |
| 6. No ambient authority | no_ambient_authority |

This oracle verifies invariant #1.

## Testing the Oracle Itself
1. **Correct case**: Region with tasks that all complete → check passes
2. **Leak case**: Deliberately break invariant → check catches it
3. **Nested regions**: Parent close requires all descendant tasks done
4. **Cancellation**: Cancelled tasks still count as completed

## Performance Considerations
- Oracle overhead acceptable in lab runtime
- Production runtime: oracle disabled or sampled
- Data structures: consider append-only log vs indexed sets

## References
- asupersync_plan_v4.md: §1.1 Non-negotiable invariants
- asupersync_v4_formal_semantics.md: Invariant I1 (task_leak_free)
- AGENTS.md: 6 non-negotiable invariants

## Acceptance Criteria
- Oracle verifies task ownership/leak invariant: every spawned task is eventually completed (no orphans) within a closed region.
- Diagnostics include the set of missing completions and their owning region(s).
- Deterministic and integrated into E2E harness.

title: [Scheduler] Starvation: SCC deadlock detection lacks early-exit and can starve worker threads on large wait-graphs
description: In `src/runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs`, the `has_trapped_scc` function implements Tarjan's SCC algorithm to detect deadlocks. However, when it finds a trapped SCC and sets `self.trapped = true`, the recursive `strongconnect` function does not early-exit. It continues to process the rest of the adjacency list and explore other nodes on the stack. In a large wait-graph with many tasks, finding a deadlock will still force the detector to do unnecessary O(V+E) work, starving the worker thread that called it. `strongconnect` should check `if self.trapped { return; }` at the start of its adjacency loop to short-circuit the DFS.

title: Implement global runtime state (Σ)
description:
# Global Runtime State (Σ)

## Purpose
The global machine state Σ is the runtime’s “single source of truth.” All operational semantics steps are transitions over Σ.

Formal shape:
- regions (R)
- tasks (T)
- obligations (O)
- time (now)

## Structure (Plan-of-Record)

```rust
pub struct RuntimeState {
    pub regions: RegionArena,
    pub tasks: TaskArena,
    pub obligations: ObligationRegistry,

    pub now: Time,
    pub root_region: RegionId,

    pub scheduler: SchedulerState,
    pub trace: TraceBuffer,
}
```

Notes:
- Deterministic PRNG state lives in the **lab runtime** driver, not in Σ, unless we decide schedule decisions must be part of Σ for replay. (If we do include it, use the internal `DetRng`, not `rand`.)

## Formal Correspondence

```
Σ = ⟨R, T, O, τ_now⟩

R: RegionId → RegionRecord
T: TaskId → TaskRecord
O: ObligationId → ObligationRecord
τ_now: Time
```

## Required Invariants (must hold for all reachable states)
- INV-TREE
- INV-TASK-OWNED
- INV-QUIESCENCE
- INV-CANCEL-PROPAGATES
- INV-OBLIGATION-BOUNDED
- INV-OBLIGATION-LINEAR
- INV-MASK-BOUNDED
- INV-DEADLINE-MONOTONE
- INV-LOSER-DRAINED (as a trace/state property)

## Initialization
- Create root region with:
  - infinite budget
  - default policy
  - Open state

## Acceptance Criteria
- Σ can represent every Phase 0 transition:
  - spawn/schedule/complete
  - cancel request/ack/drain/finalize
  - reserve/commit/abort/leak
  - join waiting
  - region close phases
  - tick/timeouts

## Testing Strategy
- Unit tests verify invariants on constructed Σ states.
- Lab runtime checks invariants after each step (configurable).
close_reason: Implementation verified complete: RuntimeState (Σ), 3-lane Scheduler, safe Waker with dedup, TimerHeap - all implemented in src/runtime/. Tests pass.

title: [lab-divergence] lab/chaos.rs: wakeup_storm injection unconditionally fires regardless of region close state — produces traces unreachable from production and masks real bugs
description:
src/lab/chaos.rs:558-565 — should_inject_wakeup_storm gates only on `should_inject(probability)` and the count range; it does NOT consult the runtime's current region/finalizer state before greenlighting an injection:

  pub fn should_inject_wakeup_storm(&mut self, config: &ChaosConfig) -> bool {
      if !wakeup_range_can_emit_positive(&config.wakeup_storm_count) { return false; }
      self.should_inject(config.wakeup_storm_probability)
  }

The structured-concurrency contract says no new obligations may be added against a region in Closing, and finalizer tasks specifically expect the runtime to keep them at the front of the schedule (no other tasks should be racing them). A wakeup storm fired during finalization injects spurious wakes that:
  (a) re-poll arbitrary tasks in regions that may have transitioned to Closing/Closed since the chaos plan was computed, and
  (b) compete with finalizer tasks for the scheduler's attention, distorting the timing of finalizer completion.

This produces lab traces that are not reproducible by any production workload (production has no chaos source that can re-poll a task in a closed region) — the resulting oracle violations are noise, and worse, real production bugs that manifest only in the same timing regime are masked because every run is already 'failing' with a chaos-induced violation.

Concrete trigger: chaos plan with cancel_storm_probability=0.5 and wakeup_storm_probability=1.0 on a scenario that exercises region close: the cancel cascades push regions to Closing, the wakeup storm fires anyway, finalizer ordering is randomised, oracles report violations that don't reflect production behaviour.

Fix direction: thread the current runtime state into ChaosController and add a guard that returns false when any region currently in `Closing`/`Closed` would be affected by the proposed wake set. Mirror the same guard in lab/runtime.rs:1917 / 2180 (see asupersync-7uu7sa).

Source: /multi-pass-bug-hunting on src/lab/* (2026-04-26).
close_reason: should_inject_wakeup_storm now requires has_open_region: bool; lab::runtime passes state.live_region_count() > 0; gate-on-at-least-one-open-region prevents fabricated post-quiescence wakeup traces; regression test added

title: [bug-hunt][P1] channel/oneshot.rs: Sender::reserve does not check cx.checkpoint() — silently accepts a cancelled Cx
description: src/channel/oneshot.rs:234-247. Sender::reserve(self, cx: &Cx) -> SendPermit<T> is a synchronous function that consumes self and never calls cx.checkpoint(). A caller whose Cx is already cancelled gets back a fully usable SendPermit; the subsequent permit.send(value) commits the value to the channel even though the caller wanted out. Pass-3 violation per the user's audit framing. Fix is non-trivial: oneshot::SendError has only Disconnected(T) — no Cancelled variant — and the current return type is SendPermit<T> not Result<SendPermit<T>, SendError<T>>, so adding cancel reporting requires an API break. Suggested: introduce try_reserve(cx) -> Result<SendPermit<T>, SendError<T>> as a sibling and add SendError::Cancelled(T); leave reserve() unchanged for non-cancellation callers but document that it ignores cancel. session::Sender::reserve (src/channel/session.rs:240) inherits this gap.
close_reason: Sender::reserve now returns Result<SendPermit<T>, SendError<()>> with cx.checkpoint() gating; convenience send returns SendError::Cancelled(value) on cancelled cx; gen_server CallError::Cancelled mapping (a3f64df10)

title: [bug-hunt] messaging/redis.rs: Transaction::cmd_bytes sets self.finished=true before await; write_command/read_response failure leaves transaction permanently unusable
description: src/messaging/redis.rs:2031-2062 Transaction::cmd_bytes sets self.finished = true at line 2038 BEFORE the await on write_command (line 2045) and read_response (line 2046). If either network op fails or the cx is cancelled, the function early-returns with self.finished still true and self.conn already taken (moved into DiscardOnDropGuard which discards). The caller cannot queue any subsequent command — finished=true blocks further cmd_bytes calls — and the connection is gone. The transaction object is permanently bricked from a single transient network blip; the caller has no way to detect this is a recoverable retry candidate vs a hard transaction-protocol violation. Fix: either set finished=true only after both await points return Ok, OR reset finished=false on every error path before returning, OR keep the connection in self.conn until success is confirmed (commit-or-rollback discipline). HIGH because the failure mode is silent — caller observes "transaction failed" with no signal that the object is now dead vs the wire-protocol still being recoverable.
close_reason: Transaction::cmd_bytes no longer sets self.finished=true before the write_command/read_response await points; the eager-set-then-reset pattern (line 2038 set, lines 2051/2057 reset on success/Redis-error) is replaced by deferred-set-only-on-protocol-violation. On a transient network failure or cancel mid-await, the connection is still discarded by DiscardOnDropGuard (correct wire-state hygiene — the byte stream is poisoned), but self.finished stays false; subsequent calls hit the take().ok_or_else path with 'transaction already finished' rather than the misleading 'after transaction completion'. The Redis -ERR response path (transient command-scoped rejection) keeps the transaction alive for retry as before. Existing test 'dropped_transaction_queue_future_fails_closed_and_discards_connection' updated to accept either error message during the transition. New regression test 'transaction_redis_error_response_keeps_transaction_alive_for_retry' pins the retry-after-Redis-error contract end-to-end via TCP mock (MULTI -> -ERR -> retry -> +QUEUED -> EXEC -> +OK array). Lib compiles clean (4f3347298)

title: Progress-certificate Freedman bound plugs realized variance in as predictable variation
description: src/cancel/progress_certificate.rs:657-686: Freedman uses V_t = t*delta_variance() where delta_variance is the realized, mean-centered, biased (/n) sample variance of the SAME deltas being bounded (mu = empirical mean_credit too) with no empirical-Bernstein correction. The exp(-lambda^2/(2(V+b*lambda/3))) transcription is correct but the plugged-in quantity makes freedman_bound (which confidence_bound prefers, 786-796) not a valid probability bound. E.g. one large early drop + long stall keeps mean credit and small variance -> 'bound' ~0 while the process has stopped. Needs a predictable (past-measurable) variance proxy or an empirical-Bernstein correction. Related: Azuma factor-4 already fixed. Fresh-eyes review SapphireHill 2026-07-12.

title: io/codec: LengthDelimitedCodec num_skip<header_len counts differently from tokio-util (owner decision); write_f32/f64 canonicalize -0.0 and NaN; LineReader example drops partial lines
description:
Read-only audit of src/io (ext helpers, copy, split, BufReader/BufWriter, lines) and src/codec (Framed*, LinesCodec, LengthDelimitedCodec, BytesCodec) at origin/main 731a0f5b1 (2026-10-03, SapphireHill subagent). SapphireHill checked items 1-3 against the tokio sources (tokio 1.53.1, tokio-util 0.7.x).

1. (medium-high, OWNER DECISION) LengthDelimitedCodec counts the length differently from tokio-util when num_skip < header_len (src/codec/length_delimited.rs ~338-379).
   - asupersync waits for max(header_len, num_skip) + adjusted_len bytes and returns everything after num_skip, so kept header bytes are added on top of the length.
   - tokio-util skips num_skip bytes and returns exactly adjusted_len bytes; the caller counts the header through length_adjustment.
   - tokio's own documented recipe .length_field_length(2).length_adjustment(2).num_skip(0) on "\x00\x0BHello world\x00\x05abcde" therefore returns a 15-byte first frame that includes the next frame's header, then reads "ab" as length 24930 and waits forever.
   - max_frame_length is checked after adjustment; tokio checks the raw field.
   - The current behaviour was introduced deliberately by 16euv (now a tombstone) and is pinned by builder_num_skip_zero_retains_entire_header_and_keeps_alignment and builder_partial_header_retention_returns_remaining_prefix_bytes.
   - docs/tokio_io_parity_audit.md lists this codec as "Complete" parity.
   - Either semantics breaks someone: existing users configured for 16euv, or users porting tokio code. The owner decides: switch to tokio semantics (re-pin both tests with length_adjustment(4) and (2)), or keep it and document the divergence in the builder docs and the parity audit.
2. (NOT A DEFECT vs tokio) read_to_string drops the bytes it has read when the reader returns an I/O error, including the runtime's Err(Interrupted, "cancelled") on Cx cancellation (src/io/ext/read_ext.rs ~417-421).
   - tokio 1.53.1 does the same: finish_string_read(.., truncate_on_io_error = true).
   - std keeps the valid UTF-8 prefix.
   - io/mod.rs says "bytes are preserved" only for a dropped future.
   - Recorded for the owner's tokio-vs-std choice; no change.
3. (medium) write_f32/write_f64 and their _le variants canonicalize -0.0 to +0.0 and every NaN to the canonical NaN, so bit-exact floats do not round-trip (src/io/ext/write_ext.rs ~25-45, ~235-291).
   - The canonicalization came from the ATP manifest-hashing fix (z7t91p, c4fd912d5) but sits in the general AsyncWriteExt.
   - tokio writes to_be_bytes()/to_le_bytes() unchanged. read_f32 decodes raw bits.
   - Nothing in-tree calls these writers, and src/atp/manifest.rs has its own canonical encoder.
   - Check for a test pinning the canonicalization before changing it.
4. (low, docs) The LineReader example creates its String inside the loop, contradicting the cancel-safety claim: the complete part of a line goes into the caller's String, so a cancelled read drops it (src/io/read_line.rs ~301, ~316-325). Move the String out of the loop and drop the "bit-exact resumption" wording.

The auditor found these sound:
- read_exact and the int/float read futures; read_to_end; Chain, Take, ReadBuf;
- write and write_all, including zero-write as WriteZero and rejection of over-reported counts;
- BufReader with seek fallback; BufWriter partial-flush tracking, ordering and flush before shutdown;
- copy, copy_buf, copy_bidirectional and the copy sessions;
- the RefCell split and split_owned;
- read_line, Lines, ReaderStream, StreamReader, WritePermit;
- FramedRead/Framed/FramedWrite;
- LinesCodec; the LengthDelimitedCodec encoder and its overflow paths; BytesCodec.

title: DNS protocol packet parsing fuzz target
description:
Create comprehensive fuzz target for DNS protocol packet parsing functions in src/net/dns/resolver.rs. These functions parse untrusted DNS response packets from network servers.

**Functions to fuzz:**
- decode_dns_name() / decode_dns_name_inner() - DNS name parsing with compression pointers
- parse_dns_answer() - DNS resource record parsing (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, etc.)
- parse_resolv_conf_nameservers() - /etc/resolv.conf parsing
- DNS packet header parsing and validation

**Test cases needed:**
- Valid DNS response packets for all record types (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, PTR, TXT)
- Malformed DNS packets with truncated headers/data
- DNS compression pointer loops and invalid pointers
- Oversized DNS names and labels (>63 chars per label, >253 chars total)
- Invalid DNS packet structure and malformed RRs
- DNS cache poisoning attack vectors
- Buffer overflow attempts in name parsing
- Invalid UTF-8 in DNS labels
- Recursive compression pointer chains (max depth testing)
- Zero-length and oversized RDATA sections
- DNS response size limit boundary testing

**Oracles:**
- Crash detector for memory safety
- DNS protocol compliance validation
- Compression pointer loop detection
- Name length limit enforcement
- Round-trip validation where applicable

This targets a critical attack vector - DNS responses are untrusted network data that can contain malicious payloads designed to exploit parsing vulnerabilities.
close_reason: Implemented comprehensive DNS protocol packet parsing fuzz target with attack vectors for compression pointers, oversized names, malformed packets, and resource record boundary violations

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
FOUND 2026-07-26 by SapphireHill while verifying br-asupersync-u05hk9 / br-asupersync-9mvlue.

THE FINDING: `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --keep-going -- -D warnings` fails with 28 errors IN THE LIB. Because the lib fails, every test target behind it is never linted at all. u05hk9's 5 test-target sites and 9mvlue's 2 test-file sites were NEVER REACHED by this gate. This is br-asupersync-c6ppu4's thesis one layer up, and the "clippy --all-targets is a CHAIN not a wall" lesson: fixing one site moves the failure rather than clearing it.

EVIDENCE: RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1, `--base HEAD --clean-overlay` overlaying only the 3 9mvlue files, worker hz2, exit=101 in 164809ms:
  error: could not compile `asupersync` (lib) due to 28 previous errors

WHY IT WAS NEVER SEEN: every implicated module is gated behind a feature no routine gate compiles. `src/lab/replay_minimization.rs` is `#[cfg(feature = "benchmark-adapters")]` (src/lab/mod.rs:81) — NOT feature-gated in the way a grep for the mod decl alone suggests, which is how I initially misread it. The default clippy lane never compiles these files, so they have accumulated pedantic/nursery lints since 2026-06-14 untouched.

THE 28 SITES BY FILE:
  src/atp/benchmark/adapters.rs        10  (unnecessary_literal_bound x3, needless_borrows_for_generic_args x4, unnecessary_filter_map, if_same_then_else x2)
  src/lab/replay_minimization.rs        7  (self_only_used_in_recursion, enum_glob_use x3, unnested_or_patterns x2, wildcard_imports)
  src/lab/benchmark_cartel.rs           4  (manual_midpoint, needless_borrows_for_generic_args, unnecessary_map_or, wildcard_imports)
  src/atp/benchmark/reports.rs          2  (ref_option, manual_midpoint)
  src/atp/benchmark/profiles.rs         2  (needless_borrows_for_generic_args, cast_possible_wrap u64->i64)
  src/atp/benchmark/suite.rs            1  (redundant_closure)
  src/messaging/nats.rs                 1  (needless_return)
  src/net/atp/transport_quic/native_link.rs:1054  1  (future_not_send)

NOT ALL COSMETIC — do not sweep these with #[allow]:
  - `manual_midpoint which can overflow` x2 (reports.rs:801, benchmark_cartel.rs:454) is an actual overflow class, not style. Use `u64::midpoint`/`usize::midpoint`.
  - `if_same_then_else` x2 (adapters.rs:329, adapters.rs:860) is the classic copy-paste fingerprint: two branches that are supposed to differ and do not. Read both before collapsing — collapsing a genuine copy-paste bug HIDES it.
  - `cast_possible_wrap` (profiles.rs:296, u64 -> i64) can wrap.
  - `future_not_send` on native_link.rs:1054 is a QUIC link future; decide deliberately whether it should be Send rather than allowing it.
  - `enum_glob_use` in replay_minimization.rs sits on an EXHAUSTIVE match over TraceEventKind. Preserve exhaustiveness — replacing the match with `matches!` would silently default new variants to false. Convert the glob to an explicit variant list (or a short alias) and keep the match arms.

SEPARATELY OBSERVED, NOT A VIOLATION: `benchmark-adapters` enables `dep:tokio` (Cargo.toml:283-289) and `src/lab/replay_minimization.rs:921` calls `tokio::fs::read_to_string`. This does NOT contradict the no-tokio guarantee, which AGENTS.md scopes to the default and `metrics` production graphs; `benchmark-adapters` is a bench-only feature. Recording it so the next reader does not re-litigate it as a regression.

VERIFY WITH:
  RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay -o <changed files> -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=... CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --keep-going -- -D warnings

BLOCKS: br-asupersync-u05hk9 cannot be verified through the --all-features lane until this clears (I verified it through a narrower `--features sqlite,kafka,test-internals` lane instead, which sidesteps benchmark-adapters).
RELATED: br-asupersync-c6ppu4 (a red gate and a skipped gate are indistinguishable), br-asupersync-evb4i9, br-asupersync-9fhmts.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
PROGRESS 2026-07-26 SapphireHill, 539f35bd5: 28 -> 22.

CLEARED (6): manual_midpoint x2 (reports.rs:801, benchmark_cartel.rs:454 -> f64::midpoint), if_same_then_else x2 (adapters.rs:329 collapsed with the co-located unnecessary_filter_map into one `filter`; adapters.rs:860 `if http3 {7} else {7}` -> `7`), unnecessary_filter_map x1, unnecessary_map_or x1 (benchmark_cartel.rs:591).

Neither if_same_then_else was a masked copy-paste bug -- I checked both before collapsing, which is the point of not sweeping these with #[allow]. adapters.rs:329's two arms really were equivalent given the preceding split. adapters.rs:860's two arms really are both 7. But adapters.rs:860 DID surface a doc/code mismatch: the comment says "7.50+ for HTTP/3", the code requires 7.66. Left at 7.66 and flagged inline; relaxing it to match the comment would be a behavior change, not a lint fix.

VERIFIED: --base HEAD --clean-overlay overlaying only the 3 files, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --keep-going -- -D warnings`. All four targeted lint classes now report ZERO; no new class appeared. Gate still red -- this is progress, not green.

REMAINING 22, and three of them are NOT mechanical -- read this before picking it up:
  - unnecessary_literal_bound x3 CANNOT be fixed in the impls. They are `fn tool_name(&self) -> &str { "scp" }` on `BaselineAdapter` impls; the TRAIT declaration must change to `&'static str` or the impl signature stops matching. That is a trait-surface change touching every adapter.
  - enum_glob_use x3 (replay_minimization.rs:429/542/611) sit on an EXHAUSTIVE match over TraceEventKind. Converting to `matches!` would compile and would silently default every FUTURE variant to false. Keep the match exhaustive; replace the glob with an explicit variant list or a short alias.
  - needless_return x1 (nats.rs:1561) is inside `#[cfg(feature = "tls-native-roots")]` / `#[cfg(all(not(...), ...))]` blocks. The `return` may be load-bearing depending on which block is the tail expression under each feature combination. Read the whole fn under each tls-* combo before editing.
  - future_not_send x1 (native_link.rs:1054) is a QUIC link future -- decide whether it SHOULD be Send rather than allowing it.
  - ref_option x1 (reports.rs:630) changes `&Option<T>` -> `Option<&T>`, so call sites move.
  Remainder: needless_borrows_for_generic_args x6, wildcard_imports x2, unnested_or_patterns x2, self_only_used_in_recursion x1, redundant_closure x1, cast_possible_wrap x1.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
DONE 2026-07-26 SapphireHill, commit a6df86353. 22 -> 0. The LIB is clean.

VERIFIED: RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1, --base HEAD(a82af3150) --clean-overlay
overlaying only the 8 changed files, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features
--keep-going -- -D warnings`. `could not compile asupersync (lib)` no longer
appears in the output at all. Baseline on the same pristine HEAD immediately
before the change: 22 lib errors. ubs on the same 8 files: critical 64 -> 64,
warning 1512 -> 1512 (both entirely pre-existing), info 536 -> 531.

HOW THE THREE "NOT MECHANICAL" ITEMS RESOLVED:
  - unnecessary_literal_bound x3: I called this a trait-surface change touching
    every adapter, and it is, but the blast radius was smaller than the note
    implied -- the trait and all four impls live in adapters.rs, and the only
    external use is `dyn BaselineAdapter` in suite.rs. `&str` -> `&'static str`
    is object-safe and every call site coerces, so no caller changed.
  - enum_glob_use x3: kept the exhaustive match, as the note demanded. Used a
    `Kind` alias plus explicit prefixes on all ~44 arms of is_target_event
    rather than an explicit 44-variant import list. `matches!` would have
    compiled and silently defaulted every future TraceEventKind to false.
  - needless_return (nats): the `return` was NOT load-bearing. The three
    cfg blocks are mutually exclusive by construction (blocks 2 and 3 both
    require `not(tls-native-roots)`), so exactly one is ever compiled and it is
    always the function's sole tail expression.
  - future_not_send: answered "should it be Send?" with YES. The only obstacle
    was `&T` needing `T: Sync`; every caller already passes a plain serde
    record, so a `Sync` bound makes it Send. No #[allow] was used anywhere.

ONE THING THE FIX ITSELF SURFACED: replacing `use super::*` in the *public*
`utils` module with explicit imports orphaned the parent's `use std::path::Path`
-- `Path` was reachable only through that glob. The first verification run
failed on exactly that one unused import, which is the useful kind of failure:
it proves the explicit imports are load-bearing rather than additive.

SCOPE NOTE, deliberately not overclaimed: this bead was "28 denied lints in the
LIB", and that is what is closed. The --all-features gate is still RED overall.
Clearing the lib made 13 targets reachable for the first time, carrying ~275
lints that no gate had ever compiled. Filed as br-asupersync-47ppcq with the
full per-target and per-file inventory. Folding them in here would have made a
finished bead look like an unfinished one and hidden a genuinely new surface.

UNRELATED SITE LEFT ALONE, recorded so it is not lost: nats.rs
build_default_nats_tls_connector's *second* cfg block (the tls-webpki-roots-only
path) has the identical needless_return shape. It is cfg'd out under
--all-features, so no lane I ran compiles it and I will not land an unverifiable
edit. It will surface if a webpki-only lint lane is ever added.

title: [compile-blocker][e2e] Decouple common conformance artifact helper from removed crate alias
description:
## Context
A read-only baseline for the next non-overlapping WebSocket E2E cleanup failed before the target test could run. The failure is a shared compile frontier in `tests/common/mod.rs`, not a WebSocket behavior failure.

Baseline command, run remotely through `rch`:
`timeout 900 rch exec -- env CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 RUSTFLAGS='-C debuginfo=0' CARGO_TARGET_DIR=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rch_target_ws_binary_stream_baseline cargo test -p asupersync --test e2e_websocket ws_integration_large_binary_roundtrip --features test-internals -- --nocapture`

Remote worker evidence:
- `rch` selected `vmi1293453` and executed the command remotely.
- Exit status: 101.
- First compile errors:
  - `tests/common/mod.rs:289:64`: unresolved module or unlinked crate `conformance` in `conformance::runner::SuiteResult`.
  - `tests/common/mod.rs:300:23`: unresolved `conformance::write_json_report`.
  - `tests/common/mod.rs:309:24`: unresolved `conformance::render_console_summary`.

The root `Cargo.toml` currently comments out the `conformance = { package = "asupersync-conformance", ... }` dependency in both normal and dev dependency sections with the note that it was removed to break a cyclic dependency. Re-adding that dependency is therefore not an acceptable quick fix unless a deeper design proves the cycle has been eliminated. The defect is that a common helper compiled into unrelated integration targets still names the removed crate alias.

## User-facing impact
This blocks focused E2E validation for WebSocket runtime-lane work and can also block unrelated tests that include `tests/common/mod.rs`. It undermines the README/TESTING promise that lane-specific E2E proof can be run with detailed logs, because a common conformance artifact helper prevents the test target from compiling before behavior is exercised.

## Scope
Primary file: `tests/common/mod.rs`.

Likely follow-up file if needed: `tests/channel_conformance.rs`, because it is the only current caller of `write_conformance_artifacts(...)` and already owns conformance-specific summary rendering in the test target.

Do not edit production runtime code unless the focused compile proof reveals a real production API mismatch. Do not re-add the commented conformance dependency just to satisfy the helper. Do not weaken or remove E2E tests. Do not delete files or artifacts.

## Implementation guidance
1. Reserve the exact files before editing.
2. Preserve the existing artifact directory behavior: honor `CONFORMANCE_ARTIFACTS_DIR`, use `target/conformance` under CI, and no-op outside those modes.
3. Remove direct `conformance::...` references from `tests/common/mod.rs` so non-conformance integration tests can compile without the crate alias.
4. Prefer a small generic helper over a new abstraction: for example, make the common artifact writer accept `Serialize` plus a caller-provided text rendering, or move conformance-specific text rendering to the conformance-owning test while leaving common responsible only for directory creation and file writing.
5. Keep error handling/logging structured with `tracing::warn!` / `tracing::info!`; do not introduce stdout/stderr output in library paths.
6. If `tests/channel_conformance.rs` still cannot compile because it directly imports `conformance`, record that as a separate conformance-crate ownership issue unless it is a tiny local caller adjustment required by the helper change.

## Required proof commands and detailed logging
Baseline evidence is the remote failure command above; include it in close notes.

Post-fix focused E2E compile/behavior proof:
`timeout 900 rch exec -- env CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 RUSTFLAGS='-C debuginfo=0' CARGO_TARGET_DIR=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rch_target_ws_binary_stream_post cargo test -p asupersync --test e2e_websocket ws_integration_large_binary_roundtrip --features test-internals -- --nocapture`

Post-fix formatting:
`timeout 300 rch exec -- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check tests/common/mod.rs tests/e2e_websocket.rs tests/e2e/websocket/integration/binary_stream.rs`

Post-fix lint frontier for the affected E2E target:
`timeout 900 rch exec -- env CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 RUSTFLAGS='-C debuginfo=0' CARGO_TARGET_DIR=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rch_target_ws_binary_stream_clippy cargo clippy -p asupersync --test e2e_websocket --features test-internals -- -D warnings`

Structural checks:
`rg -n 'conformance::runner::SuiteResult|conformance::write_json_report|conformance::render_console_summary' tests/common/mod.rs` must return no matches.
`git diff --check -- tests/common/mod.rs tests/e2e_websocket.rs tests/e2e/websocket/integration/binary_stream.rs` must pass.

If the post-fix E2E command compiles past `tests/common/mod.rs` but fails on a true WebSocket runtime behavior, close this bead only if the helper compile frontier is fixed and file a separate behavior bead with the exact first failing assertion/log line.

## Acceptance criteria
- Non-conformance integration tests that include `tests/common/mod.rs` no longer require the removed `conformance` crate alias.
- The WebSocket binary-stream focused E2E target compiles past `tests/common/mod.rs` and either passes or exposes a separately documented behavior failure.
- Common artifact logging still writes deterministic JSON/text artifacts when enabled and still no-ops outside CI or `CONFORMANCE_ARTIFACTS_DIR`.
- The fix avoids reintroducing the root `asupersync -> asupersync-conformance -> asupersync` cycle.
- Close notes include the baseline remote failure, exact changed files, post-fix rch command results, and any residual risk.
close_reason: Fixed common conformance artifact helper compile frontier. tests/common/mod.rs no longer names conformance::runner::SuiteResult, conformance::write_json_report, or conformance::render_console_summary; tests/channel_conformance.rs renders the conformance summary and passes it to the generic common writer. Proofs: rg stale common conformance references -> no matches; git diff --check; rch exec -- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check tests/common/mod.rs tests/channel_conformance.rs tests/e2e_websocket.rs tests/e2e/websocket/integration/binary_stream.rs; rch exec -- cargo test -p asupersync --test e2e_websocket ws_integration_large_binary_roundtrip --features test-internals -- --nocapture -> 1/1 passed; rch exec -- cargo clippy -p asupersync --test e2e_websocket --features test-internals -- -D warnings -> passed.

title: HIGH: TOCTOU race condition in epoll registration
description:
TOCTOU (Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use) race condition in src/runtime/reactor/epoll.rs registration process. The vulnerability is explicitly documented in comments at lines 327-330 but accepted for performance reasons.

## Impact
Attacker can exploit timing between fd validation and epoll registration:
- Close/reuse file descriptors to make epoll registration target different resource than intended
- Potential privilege escalation if timing allows fd reuse for privileged resources
- Undefined behavior if epoll targets invalid/closed descriptors

## Root Cause
Lines 327-330 comment states:
'Do not preflight the fd with fcntl(F_GETFD) here. A separate validity probe widens the close/reuse race window without making registration safer'

The code deliberately avoids validation to prevent widening race window, but this creates exploitable TOCTOU condition.

## Fix Required
1. Use atomic fd validation + registration where possible
2. Add proper synchronization to prevent close/reuse race
3. Consider using eventfd or similar for internal wakeup to avoid external fd risks
4. Implement fd lifetime tracking to detect reuse attempts

## References
- CVE examples of TOCTOU in fd handling
- Linux kernel best practices for atomic fd operations
close_reason: Fixed HIGH TOCTOU race condition in epoll registration by implementing fd identity tracking via FdIdentity struct (dev/ino/mode). Added pre/post epoll_ctl validation to detect fd close/reuse races and cleanup epoll registration if identity changes. This prevents attackers from timing fd reuse to cause epoll to monitor unintended resources. Commit 39baf15a8 shipped to main.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
FOUND BY (SapphireHill, 2026-09-04): the QUIC loopback e2e lane at HEAD `fdb676ef0` and again at `5b1f1d523` + local A4 hardening.

SYMPTOM. `cargo test -p asupersync --test atp_cli_quic_loopback --features atp-cli` →

    test atp_send_recv_quic_loopback_accepts_explicit_self_signed_leaf_pin ... FAILED
    panicked at tests/atp_cli_quic_loopback.rs:1580:9:
    atp quic sender failed; stdout: ; stderr: atp failed: native QUIC error:
      quic handshake: crypto provider failure: provider=rustls-quic-handshake, code=read_hs_fatal_alert

It fails in under a second (the whole target finishes in 0.78 s), so this is the handshake refusing the pin, not a timeout. The rest of the target is green: 8 passed, 1 failed, 2 ignored.

WHAT IT COVERS. The test starts `atp` as a QUIC receiver with `--server-cert <leaf>` and runs the sender against it with the same leaf pinned explicitly — the "operator pins a self-signed leaf instead of a CA" path that `d0c3011ad` (2026-06-21, br-asupersync-z0v7ri) added support for. A fatal alert during `read_hs` means one side rejected the other's certificate message outright.

NOT CAUSED BY THE A4 WINDOW WORK. The failure is at handshake time, before any source stream, bounded window or MAX_STREAM_DATA exists; the A4 changes only touch post-handshake flow control, the admission gate and the limiter report. It reproduces identically before and after that work, and the two OTHER failures in the same target (`atp_send_auto_falls_back_to_rq_after_quic_fails`, `..._to_tcp_after_quic_and_rq_fail`, both "did not exit within timeout") WERE mine and are fixed. An attribution run of just this test at `582195258` (the round-6 push, no A4 code) is queued as lane r10 stage PIN_BASELINE; the result will be appended here.

LIKELIEST SUSPECTS, in order: the 2026-09-02 TLS commits `1d25e7274` ("align ALPN negotiation failure error contract and test assertions") and `922e24bf8` ("ASUP-E505 streaming body refusal assertion and DER parser divergence") — a DER-parsing or ALPN change is exactly what turns an accepted pin into a fatal alert; then a rustls minor bump in `Cargo.lock`; then the leaf's own validity window if the fixture bakes in dates.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE. This target needs `--features atp-cli`, so neither the default nor the release feature lists compile it, and the all-features gates only *build* it. It runs only in a dedicated lane, and that lane had been refused by the fleet (`rc=103`) for most of the last two sessions.

NEXT STEP for whoever takes it: run the single test with `RUST_LOG=trace` on both ends and capture which side sends the alert and its description byte (`bad_certificate` vs `unknown_ca` vs `certificate_unknown` tells you whether the pin comparison or the chain build is at fault), then bisect across `1d25e7274` / `922e24bf8`.

title: ATP-A6: Implement ACK, RTT, loss detection, PTO, congestion, and anti-amplification integration
description: Harden QUIC recovery so ATP can push large object data without unbounded retransmit storms or unfair congestion behavior.
design: ATP scheduler needs observable signals: smoothed RTT, latest RTT, loss, PTO count, bytes in flight, cwnd, ack delay, path instability, and congestion-limited sends.
acceptance_criteria:
- Recovery behavior passes deterministic unit/property tests for ACK loss, reordered ACKs, packet loss, PTO, cwnd reduction, cwnd growth, ACK range gaps, ACK delay bounds, persistent congestion, and anti-amplification.

- Logs include RTT estimator state, ACK delay, bytes-in-flight, cwnd, PTO count, loss reason, anti-amplification state, path id, scheduler feedback, and exact skip/blocker reasons.

title: Stream audit: forward/send_all never observe cancellation while waiting for an item (a quiet source hangs region close; a cancelled ReceiverStream returns Ok(()) and drops queued items)
description:
Read-only audit of src/stream/** at ac4d94ee7 (SapphireHill audit agent round 7, 10-05). merge, buffered, try_buffered, for_each_concurrent, debounce and broadcast_stream were skipped as recently audited. The MEDIUM was confirmed by re-reading forward.rs ~66-87.

## MEDIUM (owner decision: API)
M1. forward (and SinkStream::send_all) never observes cancellation while it waits for the next item: `while let Some(item) = stream.next().await`. cx is checked only once an item has arrived. This is the same shape c80f912e2 fixed in for_each_concurrent.
- (A) A quiet source that does not watch cx: the cancelled task re-parks on the source on every poll and never acknowledges, so its region cannot close until the source yields.
- (B) A ReceiverStream/WatchStream bound to the same cx maps Cancelled to None, so forward returns Ok(()). It then drops the stream and the Receiver, and the Receiver's drop discards the items still queued. Success is reported while items are destroyed. This contradicts forward's own "Cancel semantics" rustdoc (cancellation is returned as Err(SendError::Cancelled(item))).
- Why it is not a quick fix: SendError::Cancelled(T) needs an item, and forward has none in hand while waiting. Options:
  - (a) a new error type, e.g. ForwardError<T> { Cancelled(Option<T>) | ... }: an API break;
  - (b) an additive forward_cancellable that returns the unconsumed stream on cancellation;
  - (c) keep forward and document both behaviours.
- Tests: (A) the lab source from tests/stream_for_each_concurrent_lab_proof.rs (one item, then pending forever), with the region cancelled after the first item; the task must finish within the step bound. (B) A prefilled rx and a cancelled Cx: forward must not return Ok(()).

## LOW
- L2. The receiver_stream.rs / watch_stream.rs docs say poll_next "blocks"; neither documents that cancellation ends the stream with None (pinned by receiver_stream_none_is_terminal_after_cancel). Consumers (collect/fold/count/forward) cannot tell cancellation from a close. Doc fix.
- L3. chunks/ready_chunks allocate the full capacity eagerly. chunks(usize::MAX) panics with "capacity overflow", and a huge cap aborts. No `# Panics` docs. Fix: lazy allocation plus docs.

Judged SOUND: throttle (Cx clock, saturating, batch drain), chain, zip, peekable, fuse, take, skip, scan, filter, map, then, enumerate, inspect, iter, next, fold, collect, count, any_all, for_each, try_stream, chunks logic, partition, stream.rs, mod.rs. src/stream has no timeout, interval, take_until or select combinators.

What remains needs live hooks, or reclassification by the owner.

Data the lab holds at report time:
- Obligation records are never removed (ObligationTable::remove has no caller in state).
- Task records survive completion.
- The trace ring buffer (default capacity 4096) drops the oldest events; the report detects truncation (runtime.rs ~3775).
- Emitted during lab runs: Spawn, Complete (no outcome), ObligationReserve/Commit/Abort/Leak (no channel id), CancelRequest, RegionCancelled, RegionCloseBegin (cancel path only), RegionCloseComplete, RegionCreated, UserTrace.
- Never emitted during lab runs: Wake, Poll, Schedule, Yield, CancelAck, Worker*, Monitor/Down/Link/Exit.

Verdicts:
- PARTLY FEEDABLE, from records:
  - cancel_correctness: StuckCancellation only. It needs TaskRecord::cancel_witness() plus the time of the first CancelRequest. It overlaps cancellation_protocol's CancelNotAcknowledged.
  - region_leak: structural checks only. Its default clock is Instant::now, so it needs with_time_source, and continuous_checking duplicates violations. Overlaps quiescence, task_leak and finalizer.
  - channel_atomicity: reservation leak only. Its clock is SystemTime and the default max age is 3600 s, so the check never fires. Duplicates obligation_leak.
- SEMANTICALLY MISMATCHED (feeding them would mislead):
  - cancel_debt: a pressure heuristic; production debt_monitor never calls complete_work.
  - cancel_signal_ordering: TaskRecord has no parent task, and cancelling only a child region is legal.
  - runtime_epoch: per-table epochs advance independently, so feeding it trips EpochSkew at once.
  - ambient_authority: capabilities are type-level and nothing records them.
  - down_order: the real contract sorts by (completion time, task id, monitor ref), and DownDelivered is never emitted.
- NEEDS A LIVE HOOK:
  - waker_dedup: mpsc RegisteredWaker.
  - rref_access: record/region.rs heap_alloc and rref_get.
  - actor_leak: spawn_actor and spawn_gen_server.
  - supervision: the restart policy is not traced.
  - mailbox: actor send and gen_server receive.
  - reply_linearity: Reply::new.
  - registry_lease: cx/registry.rs commit_permit, release and abort.
  - supervisor_quiescence.
  - fabric_*: as before.

Suggested next step: an owner decision per family. Either (a) wire live hooks under cfg(lab or test-internals) for the six actor/spork/channel-waker families, or (b) mark the five mismatched ones experimental, or not part of the default lab suite. If (b) changes OracleSuite membership, that changes the default report, so it needs sign-off. Item 1 (truth) is done; items 2-4 are not.

  - actor_leak and supervisor_quiescence: they repeat task_leak and quiescence unless a child runs outside its supervisor's region.
- Hot-path cost: waker_dedup and channel_atomicity's waker half need hooks in the channel waiter queues.

Small gap noted: down_order is not in lab/runtime.rs TEMPORAL_ORACLE_INVARIANTS, so a down_order failure gets no counterexample-prefix length. finalizer isn't in that list either. This is diagnostic only.

Plan: wire registry_lease, then cancel_correctness, then supervision, one oracle per commit. Each gets a planted-violation test proving the wired path can fail. title: [fuzz-gap] grpc/reflection.rs: no fuzz target for ReflectionDescribeServiceRequest / GetFileByFilename string-arg parsing
description:
src/grpc/reflection.rs (~28KB) implements the gRPC server-reflection RPCs: ListServices (no body), DescribeService (string symbol), and GetFileByFilename / GetFileContainingSymbol / GetExtensionsOfType (string args). Even with the asupersync-mi4hzh fail-closed default, the parser path runs whenever an authenticated reflection caller hits the endpoint. Existing fuzz coverage is nil.

Input space (fuzz harness should generate):
  1. Symbol-name string: arbitrary UTF-8 — empty, single dot, double dots ("foo..bar"), trailing dot ("foo."), Unicode punctuation that LOOKS like a dot, CR/LF embedded, NUL embedded, U+202E bidi-override, very long names (megabyte-scale).
  2. Filename string: same UTF-8 alphabet as above plus path-traversal shapes ("../etc/passwd", "/absolute/path", Windows "C:\\..."), null-prefixed, escaped slashes "%2F".
  3. ReflectionRequest envelope (the prost-decoded message wrapping these strings): malformed varint length prefixes, mid-message truncation, unknown field tags with lengths that overrun, recursive embedded messages.

Crash classes a fuzzer would catch:
  - DescribeService's service-name lookup uses `BTreeMap::get(&str)`; correctness is fine but the str must be valid UTF-8. The prost decoder normally enforces this, but a custom callsite (or a future protobuf-compat fast path) could pass raw bytes.
  - GetFileByFilename / GetFileContainingSymbol — if these ever reach a filesystem read, the path-traversal shape matters; even today's in-memory descriptor lookup must be tested against attacker-controlled filename strings.
  - The error message in line 253-style format!("service '{service}' not found") allocates proportional to the input; megabyte-scale names cause megabyte-scale error allocations per request.

Source: /testing-fuzzing src/grpc/* + src/messaging/* (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Fixed in HEAD: grpc_reflection_describe fuzz target drives ReflectionService::describe_service + list_services with adversarial UTF-8 (U+202E, NUL, path-traversal shapes, very-long names). Asserts no panic / bounded allocation. Regression guard against future filesystem-touching refactors.

title: [perf-hot-path] grpc/codec.rs: identity_frame_compress (line 228) does Bytes::copy_from_slice on the no-compression path — full memcpy per gRPC frame
description: src/grpc/codec.rs:228 fn identity_frame_compress(input: &[u8]) -> Result<Bytes, GrpcError> { Ok(Bytes::copy_from_slice(input)) } — the IDENTITY (no-compression) frame compressor. The function takes &[u8] and returns a Bytes via copy_from_slice — a full memcpy + heap alloc per gRPC frame even though we're not actually compressing. Identity is the DEFAULT codec (no opt-in needed); every gRPC message goes through this path unless gzip/deflate is explicitly enabled. The wasted memcpy is the entire payload size per frame — for a streaming RPC with thousands of small messages, this is the dominant cost. Same issue at line 232 identity_frame_decompress. Mitigation: change the FrameCompressor signature from fn(&[u8]) -> Result<Bytes, _> to fn(Bytes) -> Result<Bytes, _> so identity becomes Ok(input) — zero copies, zero allocs. Callers already have a Bytes upstream of this layer (it's passed in from BytesMut::freeze), so the change is a simple refactor of the function-pointer type. Severity HIGH for any gRPC server handling large message volume on the default codec.
close_reason: Changed FrameCompressor signature from fn(&[u8])→Result<Bytes> to fn(Bytes)→Result<Bytes>. identity_frame_compress + identity_frame_decompress now zero-copy (pure move). Both call sites in FramedCodec updated to pass Bytes by-value. 4 test functions refactored. Commit d3841aa5c.

title: [profiling-perf-hotpath] channel/broadcast.rs:497 b: Waker::clone under inner.lock per recv poll (2 sibling sites)
description:
CATALOGUE: 1st-pass hot-path audit. Two sibling sites in src/channel/broadcast.rs both call `current_waker.clone()` in poll_recv_with_waiter (a per-receiver-poll function) under the channel inner lock:

  - line 497 — new waiter insertion path
  - line 501 — waiter token lookup miss fallback

Concrete reasoning: Waker::clone is roughly equivalent to Arc::clone (~5ns + cacheline invalidation). Both sites execute under `self.channel.inner.lock()`, so the clone runs IN the lock-held critical section — increasing lock hold time and exacerbating contention on the channel mutex. Under a fan-out broadcast pattern (10 receivers × 1k msg/sec = 10k Waker clones/sec), the cumulative overhead becomes a measurable lock-contention amplifier.

Profile evidence or microbenchmark outline:
  - criterion bench in benches/channel.rs: broadcast::Receiver::recv() throughput with N receivers (N=1, 4, 16, 64). Compare baseline vs a stub that registers a `Weak<Waker>` outside the lock and revalidates inside. Expect 2-3% throughput improvement at low N, 5-10% at high N (where lock contention dominates).
  - lock-hold-time microbench: instrument inner.lock() with hdrhistogram p99/p99.9; eliminating the Waker clones should reduce p99 hold time by 2-5 us.

Class: (b) Arc::clone in hot path that could be borrowed.

Source: /profiling-software-performance 1st-pass hot-path audit on src/channel/* (2026-04-26).

title: [modes-of-reasoning] child() holds children lock while waiting for cancelled_at publication
description: src/cancel/symbol_cancel.rs: child() acquires the children write lock and then calls cancelled_at_snapshot_for_child(), which can sleep/retry while an in-flight cancel publishes cancelled_at. Under the correctness lens this widens contention in the reason->children handoff window; under the performance lens it serializes all late child creation behind a lock that does not protect timestamp publication; under the observability lens it makes late-child latency depend on lock hold time rather than only on the timestamp publication race. Fix by snapshotting cancelled state under the children lock, but performing the cancelled_at wait only after dropping that lock.

title: CancellationDebtMonitor is fed on every obligation abort and finalizer registration (2 format!, a mutex, a BTreeMap insert) but never completed or read
description:
## Finding (verified at 0677f436b)
`RuntimeState::debt_monitor` (CancellationDebtMonitor) is fed on three paths:
- every obligation abort (state.rs ~6356);
- every sync finalizer registration (~8694);
- every async finalizer registration (~8747).

Each `queue_work` costs:
- a `format!` entity id, plus `format!("{cancel_reason}")`;
- a system-time read;
- a mutex and a BTreeMap insert (cancellation_debt_monitor.rs ~399-440).

Nothing in the codebase ever calls `complete_work` for this monitor. `DebtRuntimeIntegration` (debt_runtime_integration.rs ~257) is never constructed, and the public `RuntimeState::debt_monitor()` accessor has no caller.

So:
- the feed is pure overhead on the abort and finalizer paths;
- anyone reading the monitor sees "pending cancellation debt" that never completes. It only grows to the per-type eviction cap, so the data is wrong, not just unused.

The obligation-abort entry is queued after the abort has already happened, so it describes no pending work at all.

## Options
1. Stop feeding it (delete the three `queue_work` calls). The accessor keeps returning a monitor, now empty. Cheapest, and it makes the data honest (no entries instead of never-completed entries).
2. Make it real: queue finalizer work at registration and `complete_work` when the finalizer runs. Drop the obligation-abort feed, since that work is already done when queued.

Recommendation: option 2 for finalizers only if someone has a consumer for pending-finalizer debt. Otherwise option 1.

Before either, measure:
- a probe variant that aborts N obligations, and one that registers N finalizers in a region and closes it, before and after;
- rows in the head-to-head bench or the standalone probe.

## Compat
`debt_monitor()` stays. Its contents become empty (option 1) or accurate (option 2). Neither is documented behavior; it currently reports never-resolving debt.

title: [reality-check-wave2][http3][qpack] Blocked-stream scheduler and Required Insert Count gates
description:
Parent: asupersync-fjkixh
Depends on: asupersync-zun5wj and asupersync-lhitlf

Goal:
Implement QPACK blocked-stream scheduling around Required Insert Count, Known Received Count, and SETTINGS_QPACK_BLOCKED_STREAMS without weakening the default StaticOnly policy.

Current reality to preserve:
- Dynamic field-section decoding currently fails closed when Required Insert Count exceeds current dynamic table state.
- H3Settings already parses SETTINGS_QPACK_BLOCKED_STREAMS, and StaticOnly rejects nonzero blocked-stream settings.
- No production blocked-stream scheduler is advertised in artifacts/http3_qpack_support_matrix_v1.json.

Implementation requirements:
- Add a scheduler/state machine that classifies field sections as ready, blocked on Required Insert Count, cancelled, or failed with explicit connection-level vs stream-level error mapping.

title: [SUB-EPIC-INFRA] Integration Testing and Validation
description:
# Sub-Epic: Integration Testing & Validation

## Purpose

Comprehensive testing and validation to ensure the Phase 2 reactor implementation is correct, performant, and maintains all of asupersync's design invariants.

## Background

### Testing Philosophy

asupersync is built on formal foundations:
- **Deterministic testing** via Lab runtime
- **Trace capture and replay** for debugging
- **Oracles** for invariant checking
- **DPOR** potential for exhaustive exploration

Phase 2 must preserve these properties while adding real I/O.

### Test Categories

1. **Unit tests**: Individual reactor/primitive components
2. **Integration tests**: Full stack with real I/O
3. **Determinism tests**: Lab reactor produces reproducible results
4. **Stress tests**: High connection counts, rapid connect/disconnect
5. **Cancellation tests**: Verify cancel-correctness with I/O
6. **Obligation tests**: Verify obligation tracking for I/O operations
7. **Cross-platform tests**: Same behavior on Linux/macOS/Windows

## Test Infrastructure

### Dual-Mode Test Harness

Tests should run with both real and simulated I/O:

```rust
#[test_case(RuntimeMode::Lab)]
#[test_case(RuntimeMode::Production)]
fn test_tcp_echo(mode: RuntimeMode) {
    let runtime = match mode {
        RuntimeMode::Lab => LabRuntime::new_with_seed(42),
        RuntimeMode::Production => Runtime::new(),
    };
    
    runtime.block_on(async {
        // Test code works with both
    });
}
```

### Test Oracles for I/O

New oracles for Phase 2:
- **Registration Oracle**: All I/O sources deregistered on close
- **No Busy-Loop Oracle**: No wake_by_ref() on WouldBlock
- **Cancel-Safety Oracle**: Cancelled I/O doesn't leave dangling state

## Benchmark Suite

Measure improvement over Phase 0:

1. **Connection throughput**: Connections/second
2. **Latency**: Round-trip time distribution
3. **CPU usage**: Cycles spent waiting (should drop dramatically)
4. **Memory**: Per-connection overhead
5. **Scalability**: Performance vs connection count

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All existing tests pass
- [ ] New tests for reactor functionality
- [ ] Lab runtime tests remain deterministic
- [ ] Benchmarks show improvement over Phase 0
- [ ] No regressions in cancellation behavior
- [ ] Cross-platform CI passing
- [ ] Documentation updated with examples

comments.text:
# Agent-First Ergonomics (Why this is explicitly separate)

Jose's claim about Elixir being great for AI is largely about *agent ergonomics*:

- low ambiguity operational model
- consistent conventions
- documentation that doesn't rot
- tooling that makes debugging cheap

Spork can beat that if we design the workflow around deterministic artifacts.

## Agent UX Requirements

A coding agent should be able to:

- run a scenario and get a single `report.json` with:
  - trace fingerprint
  - invariant/oracle outcomes
  - structured failure summary

- when failing, automatically get:
  - crashpack manifest
  - minimal divergent prefix
  - replay command
  - evidence ledger cards (why the supervisor restarted / why the oracle fired)

- search and diff these artifacts deterministically across runs

## No "LLM-specific magic"

This isn't about calling LLM APIs from the runtime.
It's about producing the *kind of deterministic, explainable state* that lets humans and agents collaborate.

## Dependencies

This epic intentionally layers atop:

- Crash artifacts (`bd-qbcnu`)
- Observability / evidence (`bd-iu07v`)
- Lab harness (`bd-1vk6c`)
- Docs + examples (`bd-2rm8l`)

title: [alien-graveyard] Replace per-call hash-ring rebuilds with weighted HRW selection
description:
Observed:
- src/transport/router.rs:608-645 rebuilds `HashRing::new(64, self.hash_ring_salt)` on every hash-based route selection, inserts every healthy endpoint as 64 virtual nodes, sorts the ring, then resolves the winner back through string keys.
- src/messaging/fabric.rs:3417-3444 rebuilds a fresh `HashRing` per steward-pool selection and then probes `salt = 0..` until it accumulates `required` unique candidates, paying duplicate lookups because ring selection is not naturally top-k unique.
- src/distributed/consistent_hash.rs:38-209 is a Karger-style vnode ring designed for persistent membership state, but these two callsites use it as an ephemeral scoring function in hot routing paths.

Alien algorithm:
- Highest Random Weight / Rendezvous Hashing (HRW), optionally weighted HRW for heterogeneous capacities (Thaler-Ravishankar rendezvous hashing; practical constrained-HRW scoring is also called out in alien_cs_graveyard.md:4965).
- Score each candidate with a salted hash of `(key, node_id, seed)` and pick the max for single-owner routing, or the top-k scores for steward pools. No virtual-node materialization or ring sort is required.

Invariants preserved:
- Deterministic stickiness for a fixed membership set and per-router/per-fabric salt.
- Minimal remap on membership churn: only keys whose newcomer outranks the incumbent move.
- Existing load-pinning hardening stays intact by mixing the secret salt into the HRW score domain.
- Fabric top-k selection becomes exact and duplicate-free without the current retry-by-salt loop.

Expected gain:
- Router hot path drops from per-call O(N * vnodes + V log V) ring build/sort plus key/string indirection to a single O(N) score scan with zero virtual-node allocations.
- Fabric steward-pool selection drops from ring build + repeated lookup/dedup probing to one O(N log k) top-k pass; better small-pool balance and lower heap churn.
- Should measurably reduce `select()` p50/p99 under small-to-medium healthy sets while tightening per-key balance versus low-vnode rings.

Acceptance sketch:
1. Add an HRW selector path for router/fabric candidate sets without deleting the persistent `HashRing` API yet.
2. Preserve current deterministic/golden assignment guarantees for fixed seed + membership, with remap-rate tests on add/remove.
3. Add comparative microbench or conformance assertions showing lower selection overhead and no regression in stickiness/minimal-remap behavior.
close_reason: Already implemented on main in 71f868f0a: HashBased select_n now uses HRW top-k and the focused benchmark landed

title: [tls-chain-validation] tls/acceptor.rs: with_single_cert accepts empty / self-signed-leaf certificate chains without validation
description:
src/tls/acceptor.rs:500-502 — `with_single_cert()` accepts a CertificateChain via rustls without validating that the chain is non-empty, the leaf is not self-signed without proper constraints, or the intermediates are present when required.

Threat: a self-signed leaf cert with no intermediates is cryptographically valid and rustls accepts it, but downstream certificate-pinning or path-validation logic that expects the full chain (leaf + intermediates) fails silently or behaves inconsistently. Specifically:
  (a) Pinning libraries that pin the leaf cert may fail to match if the server presents only a self-signed leaf without an issuer.
  (b) Application logic that walks the chain to extract issuer info gets incomplete data.
  (c) Downstream RFC-6125 hostname-validation code may produce different verdicts than rustls's own check.
  (d) Self-signed leaves bypass the project-wide intent (per security/key.rs and security/context.rs) of using a CA-rooted PKI.

Concrete failure modes:
  - A misconfiguration that ships only a leaf cert (no intermediates) compiles and runs, but client pinning tests pass in dev (where the dev CA is in the trust store) and fail in prod (where it isn't).
  - Self-signed leaf with KeyUsage missing 'digitalSignature' is accepted by rustls but rejected by browsers — feature divergence between server-issued and browser-validated handshakes.

Fix direction:
  1. Validate at build() time that the chain is non-empty.
  2. Reject self-signed leaf unless an explicit `accept_self_signed_leaf(true)` opt-in flag is set, and document the pinning implications.
  3. Verify the leaf includes the BasicConstraints CA:FALSE (server cert) and the appropriate KeyUsage bits.
  4. Regression test: pass a chain consisting of only a self-signed leaf; assert build() returns Err with a clear diagnostic.

Severity HIGH because (a) reachable from the public TlsAcceptor builder, (b) self-signed leaves are a frequent operator misconfiguration that the framework should fail-loudly on, and (c) the pinning-mismatch failure mode is silent in dev and disastrous in prod.

Source: /security-audit-for-saas on src/tls/* deepest refresh (2026-04-26).
close_reason: build() now rejects empty cert chains before with_single_cert. Added require_full_chain() builder rejecting single-cert chains in production. Tests: build_rejects_empty_cert_chain, build_with_require_full_chain_rejects_single_cert. Commit 1960e018a.
