description: Wire src/transport/aggregator MultipathAggregator (dedup by (sbn,esi) + reorder + path-select) into the receiver so multiple peers feed ONE per-block decoder; decode on the UNION reaching rank K regardless of which peer sent which symbol. Parent G2.

title: G2.2: multi-peer symbol scheduling (avoid redundancy, preserve fungibility)
description: Multi-peer symbol scheduling: bias which ESIs each peer favors to avoid redundant work while preserving fungibility (no peer on the critical path; any peer can drop out). Per-peer pacing (F5) + aggregate capacity-matched repair (F4). Parent G2.

description: TEST: multi-peer loopback (object decodes from union of two lossy peers when neither alone has K) + cross-machine pull from two fleet senders simultaneously, sha256+merkle match, throughput > single-peer, with per-peer contribution logging. Parent G2.

description:
# G3 — Observability: structured tracing + metrics for the whole redesign (you must be able to SEE it work)

## Why (explicit user requirement)
"great, detailed logging so we can be sure that everything is working perfectly." Every new
component must emit inspectable, structured signals so we can diagnose convergence, throughput, and
fallbacks in the field and in tests. Library stays SILENT to stdout/stderr — all via cx.trace_with_fields
(pattern at native_link.rs:1438). Relates to existing b0k8qo.9.1 (ATP_QUIC_TRACE).

## Change — emit structured trace fields + counters for:
- Decode: per-block rank progression, k, exact deficit (k-rank), block-complete timing, feedback round#.
- Pacer (F5): BtlBw estimate, min-RTT, send_rate, cwnd, inflight vs credit, cold-start engaged.
- Repair (F4): eps_hat, repair-per-round, total symbols sent vs K/(1-eps) bound, distrust-fallback engaged.
- Receiver (F1): datagrams_received, datagrams_dropped_on_receive (must be 0 lossless), pump park events,
  reorder-buffer occupancy.
- Encode pipeline (F2/F3): ring occupancy, blocks-in-flight, M (parallel degree), per-block encode us,
  inline-fallback engaged, SIMD-vs-scalar path.
- Fan-out (G1): per-connection goodput, chosen fan-out degree.
- Control (F6): round_seq, PTO fires, beacon sends, self-heal events.

## Change — surface to the operator
Add the key aggregate metrics (symbols sent/accepted, feedback rounds, peak/avg ring occupancy, chosen
fan-out, decode time, drop/park counts) to the atp CLI JSON report and the stderr progress line, so a
user running atp can SEE convergence + saturation without a debugger.

## Default-on / fallback
Tracing always compiled (zero-cost when the trace sink is off); metrics in the CLI report always on.

## Success criteria
A trace-completeness test asserts each component emits its declared fields on a representative transfer;
the CLI JSON report contains the new metrics; no field leaks into the committed manifest.

description:
# G4 — e2e test harness + scripts with detailed logging (prove it works end to end)

## Why (explicit user requirement)
"comprehensive ... e2e test scripts with great, detailed logging so we can be sure everything is
working perfectly after implementation." Per TESTING_FOR_AGENTS.md this is the scenario/e2e tier on
top of the per-bead unit + lab tests. Scripts live in scripts/ (alongside the existing
atp_quic_vs_rsync_benchmark.sh) and emit verbose, timestamped, structured logs + artifacts.

## Change — four scripted e2e suites, each logging EVERYTHING (G3 metrics piped through):
1. Loopback suite: every size (512K/1M/10M/100M/1G) + nested heterogeneous tree, BOTH transports
   (rq + quic), sha256 + merkle verify, with full per-block / per-round logs. The 5/5 floor.
2. Lossy-link suite: inject loss (debug_drop_one_in and/or tc netem) at eps in {0.5%,2%,5%,10%},
   assert convergence in <=2 feedback rounds and log the exact-deficit NeedMore + repair counts.
3. Cross-machine gauntlet: OVH(fmd)->Contabo(vmi1149989), atp --transport quic + rq, captured under
   /usr/bin/time -v (wall/RSS/CPU) + tcpdump (packet/byte/size histogram) + the G3 metrics, sha256
   bit-for-bit verify. This is the convergence + saturation proof on the real internet.
4. Benchmark gauntlet vs rsync: extend scripts/atp_quic_vs_rsync_benchmark.sh to include the QUIC
   transport + the new metrics; emit the comparison table + JSON to artifacts/.

## Logging standard
Every script: timestamped lines, per-stage banners, captured raw tool output to artifacts/, a final
PASS/FAIL summary + a machine-readable JSON result, and on failure it dumps the receiver/sender logs +
the G3 metric trail so a failure is self-diagnosing.

## Success criteria
All four suites runnable with one command each; loopback + lossy green in CI/rch; cross-machine +
benchmark green on the fleet; artifacts (logs, pcap summaries, JSON) saved for every run.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
DELIVERED: convergence-under-loss e2e instrument — scripts/atp_e2e_lossy.sh + scripts/lossy_udp_relay.py.

The harness runs a real QUIC send->recv through a userspace lossy UDP relay (lossy_udp_relay.py: drops
a controlled, seeded fraction of datagrams) at an epsilon sweep, then asserts the transfer still
converges bit-for-bit (sender exits 0, receiver commits, dst sha256 == src sha256) and records the
relay's forward/drop counts (repair-cost proxy) + wall time. Loss is DATA-direction only by default so
it isolates "does erasure coding repair DATA loss" from the F6 control-plane concern. The relay needs
no root, no src changes, and does NOT globally degrade `lo` (which `tc netem dev lo` would do, breaking
every other agent on the box) — it is the clean third option vs the bead's suggested debug_drop_one_in
or tc netem. Single-file payloads so it does not also trip the multi-entry proof bug (G9 .20).

FINDING (first run 2026-06-16, loopback, size=2M, ctrl_loss=0): the current QUIC data plane does NOT
repair loss at all.
  eps=0     -> PASS, converges ~9s (data_fwd=2057, 0 dropped, sha OK)
  eps=0.01  -> FAIL/timeout 60s: 26/2057 datagrams (1.3%) dropped, sender HANGS, receiver never commits
  eps=0.05 / 0.10 / 0.20 -> same: timeout, no convergence
RaptorQ is designed to repair far more than 1.3% erasure trivially; that it cannot, ON LOOPBACK, is the
F1 bug reproduced locally and deterministically (no cross-machine fleet needed): the 256 drop-oldest
inbound DATAGRAM queue (connection.rs:234/1229) discards symbols the decoder needs, and there is no
decode-on-arrival / working exact-deficit NeedMore repair loop, so any single lost symbol stalls the
transfer until idle-timeout. This is the SAME defect as the cross-machine non-convergence (K-explosion
+ queue overflow) — cross-machine just has higher loss/RTT amplifying it. This harness now gives F1 a
fast, local, deterministic repro AND the green/xfail regression instrument that proves when it is fixed.

Wired as the F1.4-style verification floor: the harness KNOWN_GAPS marks every non-zero eps as a
tracked XFAIL pointing at G4.2/F1, so it is GREEN today (PASS at eps=0, XFAIL for loss). When F1
(decode-on-arrival + drain-until-empty + mpsc reorder buffer replacing the 256 drop-oldest) lands,
remove those KNOWN_GAPS keys and the loss cases should flip XFAIL->PASS with no harness source change —
that flip is the F1 acceptance signal. G4.2 stays blocked-on-F1 (br refuses to claim it); this is the
instrument, committed ahead of the fix it verifies (additive, touches no data-plane source).

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
DELIVERED (slice 1 of 2): process-level peer-death / cancel e2e harness — scripts/atp_e2e_cancel.sh.

What it does: SIGKILLs one side of a live 50M transfer mid-flight (KILL_DELAY 1.5s) and asserts the SURVIVOR (1) exits within a bounded window (SURVIVOR_TIMEOUT 80s = idle_timeout 60s + margin), (2) when the survivor is the RECEIVER, cleans its staging dir (.atp-*-staging-*) rather than leaking it on abnormal peer death (the F-REG failure mode), (3) leaves no orphaned atp procs. Covers both transports (rq, quic) x both victims (sender, receiver). Timestamped logs + results.jsonl + summary.json artifacts. Hardened with: an EXIT/INT/TERM trap that kills ONLY the pids this script spawned (never a broad pkill -f atp that would hit other agents' concurrent atp runs), and a KNOWN_GAPS xfail mechanism mirroring scripts/atp_e2e_loopback.sh.

Run 2026-06-16 (loopback, 50M): PASS=3 XFAIL=1 FAIL=0 (exit 0, green floor):
  rq  /kill-sender   -> receiver exits 0s, staging clean   PASS
  rq  /kill-receiver -> sender   exits 1s, clean           PASS
  quic/kill-sender   -> receiver exits 61s, staging CLEANED PASS  (slow: only the 60s idle timeout notices, but it self-cleans)
  quic/kill-receiver -> sender   hangs past 80s            XFAIL [known-gap G9/F6: quic has no peer-liveness signal; sender sprays into the void]
Finding (cross-referenced onto F6 .7 and G9 .20): rq gets fast bidirectional peer-death detection for free from its TCP control channel; transport_quic over pure UDP does not, so peer death is only noticed via the 60s idle timeout (and on the sender, not even then while it is still spraying). The F6 KeepAlive beacon is the fix; when it lands, remove the KNOWN_GAPS key and quic:receiver should flip XFAIL->PASS with no harness source change.

REMAINING (slice 2 of 2, NOT yet doable): the in-process cancel-correctness ORACLE portion of this bead's body — every parallel encode BlockingTaskHandle cancelled+drained (pending_count->0), encode-ahead ring + mpsc permits release with no lost/duplicated symbol, pacer + fan-out connections close, the cancel-correctness oracle proving NO leaked tasks/obligations, and a typed Cancelled error. That is a LAB test (frankenlab / LabRuntime, in-process), and it requires the F-redesign components that DO NOT EXIST yet: F1 receiver decode-on-arrival (.2), F2 encode-ahead ring (.3), G1 multi-connection fan-out (.12), and the pacer. Adding deps on F1/F2/G1 so this bead correctly shows blocked until those components land; until then the process-level harness above is the cancel/peer-death coverage that exists.

title: G5: Wire-protocol versioning + capability negotiation + conformance goldens (safe evolution)
description:
# G5 — Wire-protocol versioning + conformance + back-compat (the redesign changes the wire format)

## Why
F0 (bounded-K, the mod.rs:2316 both-ends match), F4 (NeedMore gains loss estimate), F5 (NeedMore
gains delivery-rate + flow-control credit), F6 (round_seq + KeepAlive beacon) all CHANGE the on-wire
control protocol. Without explicit versioning, a mixed-version transfer fails the Hello check in a
confusing way (or, worse, mis-parses a NeedMore). This bead makes protocol evolution safe + tested.

## Change
1. Hello capability/version negotiation: the Hello carries a protocol version + a capability set
   (bounded-K, exact-deficit NeedMore, delivery-rate/credit fields, control ARQ + beacon). Peers
   negotiate the intersection; a feature absent on one side is automatically not used (ties into F7
   automatic fallbacks) instead of a hard Hello rejection where graceful degradation is possible.
2. Keep the bounded-K both-ends requirement explicit + documented (mod.rs:2316): if block size cannot
   be reconciled, fail closed with a CLEAR typed error naming the version mismatch.
3. Wire-format conformance: golden-frame round-trip tests for the new/extended frames (NeedMore with
   new fields, KeepAlive beacon, round_seq), extending the existing QUIC frame conformance suite.

## Default-on / fallback
Latest version negotiated by default; older-peer interop degrades automatically per negotiated caps.

## Success criteria
Conformance golden tests pass for all extended frames; a mixed-capability negotiation test shows
graceful degradation (or a clear typed error when degradation is impossible); no silent mis-parse.

title: G6 (DEFERRED, captured): Resumable transfers — advertise decoded blocks, resume from deficit
description:
# G6 — (CAPTURED IDEA, P3) Resumable / restartable transfers for very large objects

## Why (user-value idea; capture so we do not lose it)
rsync resumes partial files; atp commits per-object atomically (all-or-nothing). For multi-GB objects
over a flaky WAN, a mid-transfer failure today restarts from zero. Fungible symbols make resume
natural: a receiver that already decoded blocks 0..n can advertise that and the sender skips them.

## Change (if/when scheduled)
Persist per-block decode progress in the staging dir; on reconnect, the receiver's Hello/NeedMore
advertises already-decoded blocks; the sender resumes from the deficit. Reuses the exact-deficit
NeedMore (F1) + capacity-matched repair (F4) machinery.

## Status
DEFERRED P3 — not current functionality; do NOT build until the core redesign (F0-F8) lands and a
real need is demonstrated. Captured here so the idea is not lost. Relates to asupersync-mixdaw.

## Success criteria (if built)
Kill a 1G transfer at 60%, restart, and it completes by sending only the remaining ~40% of symbols,
sha256 + merkle match.

title: G7: Security & trust posture preservation — auth-before-decode, AEAD, multi-peer trust, anti-amplification (fail-closed)
description:
# G7 — Security & trust posture preservation (fail-closed; the redesign must NOT weaken auth)

## Why (DO-NOT-LOSE; security is not optional)
The transport has per-symbol HMAC authentication (SecurityContext) + QUIC TLS-1.3 AEAD on the data
plane. The redesign changes the symbol path (decode-on-arrival F1, multi-peer G2, fan-out G1) and MUST
keep the fail-closed posture. An off-path attacker can inject UDP datagrams; a malicious peer (multi-
peer) can send poison symbols. None may corrupt a decode, advance rank falsely, or cause a false
commit. This bead makes that an explicit, tested invariant of the new data plane.

## Invariants to enforce + test
1. Auth-before-decode: every symbol's HMAC is verified BEFORE it is fed to the decoder (the F1
   decode-on-arrival path). A forged/unauthenticated symbol is dropped + counted (G3 datagrams_dropped
   /auth_rejected), NEVER reaches feed_symbol or the rank monitor. Default posture stays fail-closed
   (auth required); trusted-unauthenticated only via the existing explicit loopback/lab opt-out.
2. AEAD preserved: QUIC 1-RTT AEAD still protects every symbol datagram; the new pump/drain/fan-out
   must not bypass packet protection.
3. Multi-peer trust (with G2): each peer's symbols are independently authenticated; ONE malicious peer
   cannot poison the union; a peer that fails auth is dropped and the transfer still converges from the
   honest peers.
4. Anti-amplification: the QUIC receiver/server must not be a reflection/amplification vector — bound
   bytes sent to an unvalidated peer address (RFC 9000 3x limit) during handshake. Relates to b0k8qo
   handshake anti-amplification work (harness #22).

## Default-on / fallback (user mandate)
Fail-closed auth ON by default; trusted-unauthenticated only via the explicit existing opt-out.

## Success criteria
Security e2e (G7.3) green: forged-symbol injection rejected (decode unaffected, drop counted); wrong-
key symbols fail closed; multi-peer with one malicious peer still commits correct bytes from honest
peers; anti-amplification bound holds against a spoofed Hello. No silent acceptance of unauthenticated
data anywhere on the new path.

title: F1 (Phase 1): Receiver decode-on-arrival + drain-until-empty + mpsc backpressure (replaces 256 drop-oldest) [HIGHEST EV]
description:
# F1 — Phase 1: Receiver decode-on-arrival + drain-until-empty + backpressure (HIGHEST EV, critical)

## Why (THE symptom fix; EV 16.7, Tier S)
Even with bounded-K, the QUIC receiver's 256 drop-oldest queue + 16-batch pump evicts survivors
before a block completes. Replace eviction with decode-on-arrival + backpressure. This is what flips
OVH->Contabo from 0 to success. See epic asupersync-atp-dataplane-redesign-317hxr. rq is ALREADY correct here (16MiB kernel buffer +
pump_until_control biased select) — reuse it as the QUIC scaffold.

## Change (verified code sites, src/net/atp/transport_quic/native_link.rs + quic_native/connection.rs)
1. Drain-until-empty pump: loop receive_batch; raise INBOUND_PUMP_BATCH (139/456) and endpoint
   max_batch_size off 16 (548) so the receiver drains the socket fully per pump.
2. Per-batch decode-on-arrival: feed each symbol straight to its per-block DecodingPipeline via
   drain_native_symbol_datagrams_with_blocks (mod.rs:3190) -> feed_symbol (decoding.rs:383);
   try_decode_block on rank==k (decoding.rs:646).
3. Replace the 256 drop-oldest inbound queue (connection.rs:234/1229) with an mpsc reserve/permit
   reorder buffer (~2*BDP symbols) that PARKS the pump on overflow and NEVER evicts.
4. Decode-matrix RANK monitor => exact-deficit NeedMore (k - rank), not a K*overhead estimate, so
   convergence is 1-2 rounds.

## asupersync invariants
mpsc reserve/SendPermit (mpsc.rs:495) for backpressure; cancel drains permits; no silent loss
(datagrams_dropped_on_receive must be 0 on lossless loopback; lossy drops are kernel-buffer only,
counted via cx.trace).

## Default-on / fallback
On by default. AUTOMATIC fallback: mpsc cap=1 + inline one-at-a-time feed (today's behavior) if a
parallel-decode determinism check fails — runtime trigger, not a user flag.

## Success criteria
datagrams_dropped_on_receive==0 on lossless loopback; OVH->Contabo QUIC convergence (with F0).

SapphireHill evidence-engine (2026-06-19, MATRIX-8): DEFINITIVE per-round root cause for THIS bead (the pacing-rate collapse), from an instrumented 50M/bad run (ATP_RQ_TRACE=1, run artifacts/atp_bench_matrix/20260619T233043Z/). Sender per-round log (mod.rs:3060), identical across 3 reps:
  round=1 pending=1 sent=43700 send_wall=3.3s rate=106M overhead=1.1773 loss_bar=0.0875 fec_fallback=true
  round=2 pending=1 sent=15992 send_wall=12.3s rate=58M
  round=3 pending=1 sent=15992 send_wall=13.3s rate=58M
  round=4 pending=1 sent=7800  send_wall=12.0s rate=17M
  round=5 pending=1 sent=7800  send_wall=13.8s rate=12M
  round=6 pending=1 sent=7800  send_wall=15.0s rate=8.6M

THE COLLAPSE MECHANISM (precise): the 50M file = 100 blocks (sbn 0-99, K~437). Exactly ONE block fails to reach decode rank, so pending=1 persists. In observe_need_more (mod.rs:745) the pending backlog feeds byte_pressure = pending_bytes/total_bytes (~1 block ~= 14%) -> pressure_loss = byte_pressure * RQ_PENDING_PRESSURE_LOSS_FLOOR -> loss_hat -> loss_ema/loss_bar. Result: loss_bar=0.0875 = 4x the REAL 2% wire loss. The congestion controller then HALVES the path rate every round (106M->58M->17M->12M->8.6M bps). control_wait_ms is only ~200ms, so the wall is NOT RTT — it's send_wall (12-15s/round) at a collapsing rate. Sum send_wall ~= 80s of the 108s total is purely self-inflicted.

FIX (this is the biggest + easiest 50M/bad win): DECOUPLE decode-pending pressure from the WIRE-loss/pacing estimate. Pace from measured wire loss (pacing_loss_ema / est.loss_p_hat ~= the regime's real 2%), NOT from pending-decode backlog. The byte_pressure->pressure_loss term in observe_need_more conflates "blocks still pending decode" with "symbols lost on the wire" — drop or heavily de-weight pressure_loss in the rate/loss path (keep it, if at all, only for repair-overhead sizing, never for the path-rate controller). Expected: rounds run at ~106M instead of 8.6M -> ~70s of the 108s evaporates even before the single-block convergence fix (separate, bead 317hxr.6.1.1 / InconsistentEquations).

NOTE this is NOT an FEC-overhead problem (overhead=1.1773 is adequate; MATRIX-7's overhead theory is REFUTED by this trace). Full writeup: docs/atp_rq_beat_rsync_ledger.md MATRIX-8. I am NOT editing mod.rs (BluePike owns it). Ping when a candidate lands; I re-bench 50M+500M -> MATRIX-9. PASS = path_rate stays ~= round-1 (no collapse) AND wall < 58.7s.

comments.text:
SapphireHill evidence-engine — FULL SPEC for the 50M/bad rate-collapse (ledger MATRIX-6..11). Diagnosis is COMPLETE; this is the implementation spec. I do not edit mod.rs (yours); I will benchmark + verify.

== CONFIRMED MECHANISM (pacing_rate_for trace, ATP_RQ_TRACE=1, run 20260620T051415Z) ==
50M file = 100 RaptorQ blocks. ONE block fails to decode (InconsistentEquations, see bead 6.1.1) so the ENTRY stays pending. `pending` is ENTRY-granular: pending_bytes (mod.rs:1016) sums whole entry.size, so byte_pressure≈1.0. Then:
  pressure_loss = byte_pressure*RQ_PENDING_PRESSURE_LOSS_FLOOR = 1.0*0.05 = 0.05 (mod.rs:768)
  -> loss_ema climbs past RQ_MILD_LOSS_PACING_MAX_LOSS(0.02)
  -> mild_loss_pacing_floor_applies() returns FALSE at ~round 4
  -> pacing_rate_for: network_bps = min(bw_median, bw_trough) (mod.rs:948) follows the ratcheting bw_trough DOWN
  -> offered_bps (= sent_payload_bytes/send_wall_s, mod.rs:785) underestimates on the stalled repair rounds -> bw_median/bw_trough decay -> spiral.
Per-round network_bps: 15.3M -> 8.39M(floored) -> 8.39M -> 2.5M(floor off) -> 1.7M -> 1.1M -> 0.9M, on a 50mbit(=6.25 MB/s) link. Wall = sum(send_wall @ collapsing rate) ~= 80s of the 108s.

== DO NOT just cap pressure_loss (I tried it; it REGRESSED) ==
Commit 1ad8fb319 capped pressure_loss at 0.01 -> REVERTED in 36e4573a8. Re-bench (run 20260620T053641Z): bad 108s/7r -> 188s/13r, broken 153s/9r -> 240s/16r (both WORSE; perfect/good fine). WHY it backfired: loss_bar is DUAL-ROLE — it (wrongly) disables the pacing floor AND (rightly) drives FEC repair_overhead via source_fec_fallback_tuning (mod.rs:720, overhead_for_target(k, loss_bar,...)). Capping it cut repair_overhead 1.1773->1.0426 -> per-round FEC under-provisioned -> rounds DOUBLED 7->13. And the floor STILL disabled. So you cannot fix this by lowering the decode-pending loss signal.

== REQUIRED DESIGN (separate the two signals) ==
1. KEEP the decode-pending/byte_pressure loss for FEC repair-overhead sizing (it correctly keeps overhead high -> fewer rounds). Do NOT lower it.
2. GATE the pacing floor + congestion RATE on a TRUE WIRE-LOSS signal — actual datagram loss/gaps, NOT decode-pending. The receiver knows real symbol-gap stats; report them (E-7.2 PathEstimate-from-live-feedback / WIRE-2). Today loss_detector.observe_datagram_loss_sample (mod.rs:817) is fed lost_symbols = sent*pacing_loss_hat where pacing_loss_hat is ENTRY-pending-based (~0) — so the real wire loss is never measured. Fix: feed real receiver-observed loss.
3. With a true wire-loss signal, mild_loss_pacing_floor_applies() stays TRUE for bad (real ~2%) and FALSE for broken (real ~10%) via a single threshold (raise RQ_MILD_LOSS_PACING_MAX_LOSS to ~0.03 on the TRUE signal). That keeps the floor on for bad (rate ~link) and lets broken pace slow legitimately.
4. ALSO de-poison the bandwidth estimator: offered_bps from a stalled repair round (small payload, send_wall dominated by the stuck-block wait) is not a link-bandwidth sample. Either skip bw_ema/bw_trough updates on stalled/small rounds, or estimate bandwidth from the receiver's actual delivery rate. Otherwise bw_median/bw_trough still decay below link even with the floor on.

== VALIDATION GATE (I run it centrally) ==
Re-bench 50M perfect,good,bad,broken nocrypto with ATP_RQ_TRACE=1. PASS = bad wall < 58.7s (win if < ~15s) AND the pacing_rate_for trace shows network_bps does NOT collapse (stays ~link) AND broken NOT worse than 153s AND perfect ~3.7s / good ~4s AND all sha_ok=true. Ping this bead when a candidate lands; I rebuild + bench + ledger MATRIX-12. Diagnostic rqtrace already in HEAD (5b1b84b51). The single-block trigger is bead 6.1.1 (BluePike) — fixing it would make the entry decode in ~2 rounds and the spiral never start; the two fixes are complementary.

SapphireHill evidence-engine — VERIFIED your wire-loss/repair-pressure split (97b15fc9c+7d83d3aeb+2100065f9). Benched 50M all-4-regime on a build @2100065f9 (ATP_RQ_TRACE=1, run artifacts/atp_bench_matrix/20260620T144025Z/, ledger MATRIX-12). TRACE (50M/bad): received_this_round=16707 / sent=43700 ⇒ ~62% REAL wire loss in round 0. The round-0 spray bursts 43700 symbols in 3.3s (~127 Mbps) at a 50mbit (6.25 MB/s) link → netem legitimately drops 62% (over-pacing, no rate-limit on the initial spray). The estimator then over-reacts: repair_loss_bar CLAMPS to 0.90, repair_overhead explodes to 10.68× (UNBOUNDED — no cap in mod.rs), pacing_rate_for divides rate by (1+9.44) → ~1.04 MB/s. 1. RATE-LIMIT the round-0 / initial spray to the estimated path bandwidth — don't burst 127 Mbps into a 50mbit link (E-7.3 rate-matched pacing). round-0 received should ≈ sent (no self-inflicted loss).
2. CAP repair_overhead to a sane max (≤ ~2-3×). 10.68× is pathological; size it to the TRUE wire loss measured AFTER the spray is paced, not to the over-pace-induced 90%.

PASS target (→ MATRIX-13): 50M/bad round-0 received≈sent (no over-pace loss) AND repair_overhead ≲ 1.3× AND wall < 58.7s (win if < ~15s vs rsync). (2) ROUND-0 OVER-PACE: cold_start() uses RQ_COLD_START_PACING_BPS = 16*1024*1024 = 16 MiB/s = 134 Mbit/s (mod.rs:186). comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SapphireHill — LEVER 1 spec (round-0 slow-start), now LOAD-BEARING. Evidence: my overhead cap (committed 9206290ba, MATRIX-13) fixed 50M/bad 108→51s and 500M RSS 7GB→23MB, BUT 500M/bad is CATASTROPHIC (~1100s / 17.5GB / 6-7 rounds, MATRIX-14) and 50M/bad still loses rsync (51s vs 15.6s). ROOT for both = round-0 over-pace.

MECHANISM (traced): round-0 sprays the WHOLE object paced at cold_start = RQ_COLD_START_PACING_BPS = 16 MiB/s = 134 Mbit (mod.rs:186; RqSprayPacing::cold_start mod.rs:426 → RqSprayPacer token bucket, before_send mod.rs:489). On the 50mbit 'bad' link that's 2.7× the link → netem drops ~62% of round-0 (received_this_round=16702/sent=43700). Round-1+ paces correctly (~98% delivered) because by then the CongestionController has a bandwidth estimate from round-0 feedback. So the system is already "probe(round-0)→pace(round-1+)", but round-0 PROBES WITH THE WHOLE OBJECT → wastes the whole file's bandwidth + 62% loss across all blocks (catastrophic at 500M's ~1000 blocks).

FIX (structural, fast-link-safe): make round-0 a SMALL PROBE, not the whole object.
  - Round-0: spray only ~1 BDP / a bounded probe (e.g. min(object, cold_start_rate × est_rtt, or a few hundred symbols)), then take the NeedMore/feedback.
  - The CongestionController already converts round-0 delivery (received_this_round) into a bandwidth estimate; round-1 onward then sprays the BULK at the measured link rate (this path already works → ~98% delivered).
  - Fast links (1gbit perfect/good): the probe is small and the controller ramps to high rate within ~1 RTT, so the cost is ≈ +1 RTT (a few ms) — must NOT regress perfect 3.7s / good ~4s.
  - Slow links (50mbit bad / 10mbit broken): the probe over-paces only a few hundred symbols (tiny loss), then the bulk paces at ~link → round-0-style 62% loss is gone → ~1-2 round convergence.
  Do NOT just lower RQ_COLD_START_PACING_BPS globally — that paces the whole round-0 slow on fast links (perfect 3.7→~13s regression). The win is bounding round-0 SIZE, not its rate.
  (Where: the round-0 spray is mod.rs:~3018 `round_tuning = adaptive.round_tuning(&config); spray_round(...)`; spray_round at ~3362. The probe-cap likely goes in how many symbols round-0 enqueues before yielding to feedback.)

VALIDATION (I bench centrally → MATRIX-15): PASS = round-0 received≈sent (no over-pace loss) AND 50M/bad < 15.6s (WIN vs rsync) AND 500M/bad << 1100s (no 17.5GB) AND perfect 3.7s / good ~4s NOT regressed AND all sha ok. This is the E-7.3 rate-matched-pacing lever. I'll rebuild + bench 50M+500M all regimes the moment a candidate lands. The overhead cap (RQ_MAX_ROUND_REPAIR_OVERHEAD) is already in main and complements this.

comments.text:
SapphireHill — IMPLEMENTED + BENCH-VERIFIED the sender-only round-0 bounded-probe (lever 1). RESULT: REGRESSION across ALL regimes → REVERTED (stashed). Precise diagnosis below; lever 1 needs a RECEIVER-side change, not just a sender probe.

WHAT I TRIED (stash@{0} "lever1-round0-probe-FAILED-needs-receiver-change"): const RQ_ROUND0_PROBE_SYMBOLS=1024 + spray_round gained `max_symbols_this_round: Option<u64>` cap (both parallel+sequential send paths); round-0 call passes Some(probe), repair calls None. Compiles clean. Built release + benched 50M all-4 nocrypto, ATP_RQ_TRACE=1 (run 20260621T024201Z).

NUMBERS (50M median, atp vs tuned rsyncd, ALL sha_ok=true):
- perfect: 75.92s vs 1.23s (was ~3.7s → 20x WORSE)
- good:    96.00s vs 3.93s (was ~4.1s → 23x WORSE)
- bad:     80.52s vs 14.24s (was 51s → worse)
- broken:  134.33s vs 102s (was 124s → worse)

WHY (from the trace — the probe itself WORKS, the downstream breaks):
- Round 0 sprayed only 1311 symbols (≈1 block); received_this_round=1311 on perfect (NO over-pace loss — the bounded probe did exactly what it should).
- Round 1: receiver requests source_requests=8192 (the un-sent source blocks). GOOD — it does re-request fully-missing blocks.
- Round 2: sender sprays the requested source (sent_this_round=15992) but **received_this_round=0** ON A PERFECT (0-loss) LINK. That zero-delivery round poisons the estimator: repair_loss_bar jumps 0.0875→0.9000, path_rate_bps collapses 68.9M→13.4M→9.3M, repair_overhead pins at 2.0. Net: the rest dribbles out at ~1 MB/s → 76s.

ROOT (for the implementer): after a partial round-0, the source-resend path (spray_source_requests, NeedMore.source_symbols) reports received_this_round=0 despite sending ~16k symbols on a lossless link — either spray_source_requests doesn't actually deliver/credit the re-sent SOURCE symbols for whole-missing blocks, or the receiver doesn't count them in round_symbols_observed. That transient 0 then trips the SAME rate-collapse pathology (loss_bar→0.9). So:
1. The round-0 over-pace fix (bounded probe) is SOUND in isolation (round-0 received≈sent).
2. But it's COUPLED to the receiver/feedback/estimator: (a) the source-resend round must actually deliver+credit the re-sent source (fix received_this_round accounting / spray_source_requests for whole-missing blocks), and (b) the estimator must not collapse on a transient received=0 round (the E-7.2/WIRE-2 true-wire-loss work).

So lever 1 is NOT a surgical sender edit — it needs the receiver/feedback path (E-7.2/WIRE-2 + source-resend accounting). My probe is stashed for when that lands. I keep benching centrally; ping when a candidate (sender probe + receiver source-resend/estimator fix together) is on main.

BUG 1 — source-resend UNDER-CREDITS received_this_round (the core issue). On a 0-loss perfect link, round-2 source-resend: sent_this_round=15992 received_this_round=1884 (only ~12% credited). The receiver tail-drain accepts/counts only a small fraction of the re-sent source IN THE ROUND it's sent; the rest is credited a round late (round-3 perfect: sent 44092 received 14108). On a lossless link received_this_round MUST be ~= sent. The tail-drain timing / accounting still doesn't credit re-sent source in the same NeedMore window.

BUG 2 — the zero-guard only catches EXACT 0, not tiny-nonzero. Perfect round-2 received=1884 (nonzero ~12%) was fed to the estimator as ~88% wire loss → repair_loss_bar 0.0875→0.8822, pacing_loss_bar→0.9000, path_rate collapse 112M→21M→14M → 56s. (50M/bad happened to hit exactly 0 so it dodged this; perfect hit 1884 and collapsed.)

BUG 3 — even when it doesn't collapse (bad), convergence takes 7 rounds of ~7800 symbols at the ~58M cap, ~11s send_wall each → 80s. Source-resend is delivered in many small per-round batches instead of one bulk round at the measured rate.

FIX DIRECTION (cleanest): source-resend rounds are NOT a wire-loss sample — they re-send specifically-requested SOURCE symbols, so their delivery ratio must NEVER feed the loss/pacing estimator (not just when it's exactly 0). Gate it on the round TYPE (source-resend) rather than on received==0. Then: (a) credit re-sent source in the SAME round (fix tail-drain so received_this_round≈sent on a clean link), and (b) deliver the requested source in one bulk round at the measured rate, not 7 small batches. PASS target (I re-bench): 50M perfect~3.7s + good~4s NOT regressed AND 50M/bad<15s AND all sha_ok AND the trace shows source-resend round received≈sent + no path_rate collapse. Repro: 50M/bad encrypted (netem 50mbit, 2% loss, 80±20ms).
- Sender sent 46000 round-0 symbols; receiver OBSERVED only 918–1998 → ~98% drop. That is a QUEUE tail-drop on netem's default 1000-pkt queue, NOT the 2% random loss.
- CRITICAL: receiver reports round_loss_fraction=0.0000 despite the ~98% drop — it counts loss only among ARRIVED symbols (structurally blind to dropped ones). So AIMD / loss_pacing_cap NEVER engages → no backoff → re-sprays repair (requested_repair grows 45082→115528) into the same overflowing queue → 240 NeedMore PTO retransmits → timeout, sha_ok=false.

Proven it is a congestion-ADAPTATION gap, not a pacing-constant:
- Capping the sender to 40 mbit via atp's own --bwlimit (under the 50 mbit link, also disables the clean ramp) did NOT fix it — loss is rate-INDEPENDENT (918 @5MB/s vs 1998 @24MiB/s).
- rsync succeeds on the IDENTICAL cell in 18.07s (TCP backs off to fit the finite queue).

Fix requirements this evidence implies:
1. Loss/delivery signal must be SENDER-SIDE (sent-vs-acked over time), not the receiver arrived-symbol ratio — otherwise AIMD can never see the drop and never backs off.
2. Apply on the QUIC path too: transport_quic QUIC_AIMD_*; the clean-ramp gate mod.rs:1497 keys on pacing.path_loss_rate which is never seeded from the --rq-round0-loss-pct hint, and run_matrix_cell.sh doesn't even pass --rq-round0-loss-pct for the quic transport (rq-only). EXACT PATH (read line-level on HEAD 35f69b018):
- Data plane gates every symbol send on the QUIC cwnd: native_link.rs:2025/2034 call conn.transport().can_send(QUIC_DATA_PLANE_CONGESTION_PACKET_BYTES).

So bytes_in_flight and the gate are both in virtual-16 units. NOT half-applied — fully applied and still insufficient.
- WHY it collapses: on_loss_congestion (transport.rs:419-431) halves cwnd once per recovery epoch and floors it at min_cwnd = max_datagram_size*2 = 2400 (lines 427-428). On the bad link's continuous ~2% loss, a halving fires ~every RTT while additive-increase recovers only ~1 MSS-equiv/RTT -> steady-state cwnd == the 2400 floor. 2400/16 = 150 packet-credits; at ~160ms RTT that caps the data plane at ~150 datagrams/RTT ~= 1.1 MB/s -- under HALF rsync's ~2.5 MB/s on the identical cell.

The sender is ACTIVELY congestion-limited 5087 times = it WANTS to send and the cwnd refuses = a THROTTLE, not an idle feedback deadlock. This is why --bwlimit across a 50x span (2.5->24 MiB/s) changed nothing (MATRIX-131 rate-independence): the cwnd gate sits BELOW every bwlimit.

COMPOUND (reconciles MATRIX-123/124): Phase 0 OVERSHOOT (round-0 clean-ramp floods while receiver round_loss_fraction reads 0.0000) THEN Phase 1+ UNDERSHOOT (cwnd over-corrects to the 2x MSS floor, can't push the repair backlog). Both must be fixed.

1) Replace the conn.transport().can_send(16) admission checks (native_link.rs:2025/2034) with an adaptive token-bucket pacer admission check — mirror the PROVEN transport_rq pattern: pacer.before_send() (transport_rq/mod.rs:908) over a CongestionController clamped by RQ_MIN/MAX_PACING_BPS (mod.rs:214/584).
2) Pacer congestion signal = delivery-rate / RTT-gradient / loss-BEYOND-the-FEC-repair-budget (BBR/Vegas-style), never raw datagram loss.
3) Keep cwnd loss/RTT stats feeding PathEstimate (E-7.2) so true congestion still backs off — just not via a hard 2x MSS floor.
INTERIM PROOF-OF-CAUSATION (not the ship fix): raise the data-plane min_cwnd from 2*max_datagram to a BDP-appropriate floor (~link_BDP/16 ~= 64 KiB credits on this cell). If 50M/bad then converges, the floor is confirmed as the strangler.

title: G9: transport_quic multi-entry proof-exchange unreliable — receiver commits but sender times out 60s [found by G4.1]
description:
# G9 — transport_quic multi-entry proof-exchange unreliable (receiver commits, SENDER times out 60s)

## How found
DISCOVERED by the G4.1 loopback e2e harness on 2026-06-16: a 35-entry tree (~4.9MB) over quic on
LOOPBACK. The RECEIVER decoded + committed ALL 35 files correctly (committed:true, bytes_received
4911081, every committed_path present, sha256 OK) — but the SENDER then timed out: "atp failed:
transport timeout during receive proof or fountain feedback after 60s" (wall ~85s). So the data
transfer SUCCEEDED but the final Proof/feedback acknowledgement from receiver back to sender did not
complete, and the sender reports FAILURE for a transfer that actually succeeded.

## Why it matters
- Correctness/UX bug: a successful transfer reports failure; a caller/CLI would retry or error.
- The existing tests/atp_quic_real_udp_transfer_e2e tree case (3 files) does NOT expose this — it
  takes many entries to trigger, so it slipped through. This is a latent multi-entry control-plane
  defect on the HAPPY path (loopback, no loss), distinct from the cross-machine convergence work.

## Likely cause + change
The final Proof exchange races the --once receiver's commit/exit, or the per-entry ObjectComplete /
Proof loop does not terminate correctly for many entries, or the Proof frame is sent after the
receiver has stopped pumping. Fix the multi-entry finalize handshake so the receiver sends Proof and
the sender reliably receives it before either side tears down. Relates to F6 (reliable self-resync
control: a lost/raced Proof must self-heal via PTO/beacon rather than a 60s hang) — G9 may be the
concrete first slice of F6, or a simpler finalize-ordering fix.

## Verification

title: E-9 FIX: bad-regime false-rejection — bytes_written double-count in mixed source+FEC completion
description:
CRITICAL bug, ROOT-CAUSED 2026-06-17 (ATP_RQ_TRACE, loss 10% / 5M / REPS=3). The #1 blocker to "beat
rsync over a BAD connection" and a hard dependency of ATP Channel Bonding C2 (multi-source amplifies
it). Full evidence in docs/atp_rq_beat_rsync_ledger.md E-9.

SYMPTOM: on a lossy link, transfers intermittently fail with
"integrity verification failed: per-entry SHA-256 mismatch" (RqError::Integrity), fail-CLOSED (never
commits bad data). Beyond-reproach matrix: bad regime (50mbit/80+-20ms/2%) MISSes; bisection shows it
is LOSS-triggered (jitter-only passes); ATP_RQ_TRACE shows MISS correlates with src-completes>0
(MIXED source+FEC completion); the all-FEC rep (src=0) COMMITS OK.

ROOT CAUSE: a block decoded via FEC calls persist_decoded_block (transport_rq/mod.rs:3636,
bytes_written += data.len()). The SAME block can LATER reach received_count==k from late source
retransmits via persist_source_symbol (mod.rs:3498, bytes_written += block.len) because
persist_decoded_block never sets source_blocks[sbn].complete. => bytes_written is DOUBLE-COUNTED for any
block completed by both paths -> verify_and_commit (mod.rs:3702) decoder.bytes_written != e.size ->
sha_ok=false -> returned as the MISLEADING reason "per-entry SHA-256 mismatch" (mod.rs:3769).

IMPORTANT: THE FILE CONTENT IS CORRECT (verify also hashes the file; the hash matches). This is a FALSE
REJECTION of GOOD data, not corruption — atp's fail-closed integrity is fully intact. It wrongly
rejects correct transfers under loss, which is why atp "fails" the bad regime.

FIX (targeted, low-risk):
1. Count each block's bytes EXACTLY ONCE across both completion paths — e.g. a per-block written flag
   (or reuse source_blocks[sbn].complete) set by whichever path lands first, with bytes_written and
   dec.complete derived from it; guard both persist paths against double-incrementing a counted block.
2. AND/OR drop the fragile bytes_written != e.size proxy in verify_and_commit and gate solely on the
   already-computed actual file size + per-entry SHA-256 (the correct content-addressed check).
3. Unify completion so dec.complete is set iff every block is complete via EITHER path (the two
   trackers — source_blocks[].complete and pipeline.is_complete — currently desync in the mixed case).

TESTS (must add — existing signed_source_streaming_seeds_fec_decoder_from_staged_sources covers ONLY
single-block all-FEC, which is why this shipped):
- Unit: multi-block MIXED completion (some blocks source-complete, some FEC, one via BOTH) -> complete,
  bytes_written == size, committed, byte-identical.
- Regression: loopback/netns lossy (50mbit/2% and loss-only 10%) -> converges, sha OK, >=10 reps
  (probabilistic bug).
- Trace assertions: blocks_via_memcpy + blocks_via_fec, no double-count.

ACCEPTANCE: the bad-regime AUTH matrix (perfect/good/bad x 5M/50M) commits byte-identical sha OK across
reps; loss-only 10% 5M passes >=10/10; multi-block mixed-completion unit test green. Converts the ledger
F-POS-3 "bad: MISS" rows into wins.
close_reason: E-9 FIXED + LANDED commit d82e23bc0 (count each decoded block once via source_blocks[sbn].complete; gate verify_and_commit on content SHA not bytes_written) + VALIDATED across the F-POS-4 beyond-reproach matrix (bad/broken regimes now converge byte-identical at 500K/5M/50M; ledger E-9 + F-POS-4). Bead was stale-open + a P0 blocker choking downstream (C2 bonding, F1).

title: E-11/B-1: eliminate per-symbol file-op dispatch (mmap staging) — bad-large RSS + perfect-link
description:
ROOT CAUSE (heaptrack + perf, committed in docs/atp_rq_beat_rsync_ledger.md E-10/E-11): the receiver
does a per-symbol file `seek` via `spawn_blocking_io` in `persist_source_symbol`, plus payload.to_vec
+ HMAC. Measured: ~32 allocs/symbol (1.14M for a 50M transfer), 218MB live heap (4.4×), RSS 9× (churn
glibc won't return), ~74 ctx-switches/symbol. This ONE root drives BOTH the bad-large memory blowup
(E-11: 500M/bad times out) AND the perfect-link diffuse-CPU loss (50M 3.7×→500M 7.0× vs rsync).

FIX (highest EV — helps both frontiers): B-1 mmap the receiver staging file (memmap2 or unsafe mmap +
unsafe-ledger entry per AGENTS.md), make persist_source_symbol + persist_decoded_block write via
memory stores (no spawn_blocking dispatch); msync + rename on commit. Isomorphic alt: per-block write
batching (accumulate a block, one dispatch/block). Also pool/reuse receiver payload buffers to kill
payload.to_vec(). REFUTED non-causes (do not rechase): parallel-decode (29% CPU), glibc-arena
(MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1 no change), large-K (K=512), seed-all-blocks, decode-clone-per-attempt (gated).
ACCEPTANCE: sha-isomorphic (rq+decoding lib tests byte-identical); re-heaptrack 50M/bad alloc count
↓↓ + RSS ↓; perfect-50M wall ↓ toward rsync; 500M/bad converges (no timeout). Idle bench worker
109.123.245.77 (heaptrack installed, atp_dbg unstripped).
close_reason: mmap-staging REFUTED by before/after measurement (dispatch eliminated 16509->6 lseeks but wall unchanged 3.48->3.42s + RSS regressed 8->60MB). Real perfect-link lever is batching the per-symbol recv pipeline + cutting reactor/timer wakeups, not the staging write mechanism. See ledger E-10.

comments.text: LEVER CONFIRMED by measurement (2026-06-18, idle-109 strace, sha=YES). 20MB perfect loopback receiver: 16509 lseeks (~1/source-symbol; ~15k symbols) => ~400k blocking-pool seek-dispatches for 500M = the E-10 perfect-link CPU wall + E-11 super-linear (blocking-pool contention). Arrival order: lseek offsets 89.6% fwd / 10.4% back = 8 interleaved monotonic substreams (one per --streams 8, each +8 symbols). REFUTES two cheaper alternatives: (a) contiguous write-combine buffer coalesces ~nothing (consecutive arrivals +8 symbols apart); (b) per-block Vec buffer holds ~whole file (all blocks fill in parallel) => regresses bad-large RSS. mmap uniquely wins BOTH frontiers. title: E-14: large-tree FD exhaustion — receiver holds an open staging FD per entry (>1000 files = EMFILE)
description:
REAL BUG (found 2026-06-18, ledger E-14): atp send of a 2000-file tree → receiver dies "Too many open
files (os error 24)". EntryDecoder.file holds an OPEN staging FD per entry; the sprayer feeds all
entries concurrently → 2000 simultaneous FDs > default ulimit -n 1024 → EMFILE; sender then
"Connection refused". rsync transfers 2000 files fine. ⇒ atp fails ANY single transfer with >~1000
files — a real "any-workload" blocker (deeply-nested power-law trees were explicitly requested).

FIX: bound concurrent open staging FDs — (a) open-write-close per entry, or (b) an LRU FD pool that
reopens on demand, or (c) process entries in a bounded in-flight window (composes with the E-11
windowing). Stopgap for benchmarks: raise RLIMIT_NOFILE (soft→hard) at recv startup (setrlimit; unsafe
+ ledger, or the `rlimit` crate) — handles trees up to the hard limit but the bounded pool is the real
fix for unbounded trees. ACCEPTANCE: 2000-file + 20000-file tree transfers complete sha-identical
under default ulimit; receiver open-FD count stays bounded (assert). NOTE: the matrix tree cells are
ALSO blocked by a separate harness verify bug (rsync sha_mismatch: manifest_tree_digest vs
tree_digest(DEST) use different relpath roots in run_matrix_cell.sh) — fix that to score trees.

title: E-12: >2GB single-file gap — RaptorQ 256-block × 8MiB max object; multi-object split
description:
REAL LIMIT (found 2026-06-18, ledger E-12): atp send of a 5GB file errors TooLarge at ~5.8s. RaptorQ
uses a u8 SBN ⇒ ≤256 source blocks; effective_max_block_size caps the block at configured_max (8 MiB
default) via .min(configured_max) ⇒ max object ≈ 256 × 8 MiB = 2 GB. 5 GB > 2 GB → rejected. (NOT a
--max-bytes issue: the matrix sets MAX_BYTES=6GB.) rsync transfers 5G fine ⇒ atp cannot transfer any
file >2 GB — a real "any-workload" blocker.

FIX: MULTI-OBJECT split — chunk a huge entry into ≤2 GB RaptorQ sub-objects (each ≤256 blocks at a
sane block size so K stays ~512 and the O(K²) decode matrix stays small), transfer + reassemble in
order, sha-verify the whole. (Naive alt — raise the per-block size above 8 MiB for big files — keeps
1 object but K balloons: 5G/256≈20 MB block → K≈14k → ~196 MB decode matrix/block; rejected.)
ACCEPTANCE: 5G (and 10G) single file transfers sha-identical across perfect/good/bad regimes, decode
memory bounded, wall competitive with rsync; re-run the 5G matrix column (currently recorded `error`,
excluded from headline).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: cc_1 LEVER-R2 ROOT CAUSE (cheaper than threading) — from MATRIX-23's feed_micros=99.999%. The 77µs/symbol clean-link wall is NOT GF math and does NOT need per-block feed threading. It is an O(k^2) per-symbol whole-block REBUILD: try_complete_source_block -> try_complete_from_source_symbols (decoding.rs:1048) is called on EVERY deferred source symbol (feed_with_retention_and_mode call site ~690) and each call does Vec::with_capacity(block_plan.len) (allocates the ENTIRE ~MB block) + loops esi 0..k copying every received symbol, then returns None via '?' on the first missing esi. So for in-order clean arrival, symbol i allocates a full block buffer + copies i symbols, then DISCARDS it -> sum = O(k^2 * symbol_size) alloc+copy per block. prepare_decode_job (decoding.rs:875) has the same shape (clones symbols_for_block per call to check len<k). FIX (cheap, byte-identical, no lossy regression): gate on the EXISTING O(1) per-block count before the rebuild. PipelineBlockCounts.source_symbols (decoding.rs:355) is maintained per block; in try_complete_source_block, early-return None if block_symbol_counts[sbn].source_symbols < block_plan.k, and likewise gate prepare_decode_job on counts.total() >= k. Then the whole-block rebuild runs ONCE at completion instead of per-symbol -> O(k^2)->O(k) -> feed_micros collapses -> intake >> 15.5MB/s -> beats rsync clean. This is in decoding.rs which BronzeTiger holds (active lossy-fix WIP); it's a DIFFERENT hunk (source-completeness fast path, not finish_decode_job_deferred). I can implement it the moment decoding.rs frees, or BronzeTiger/owner can apply this 2-spot gate now. SapphireHill: this should beat the R2 threading lever with far less risk.

title: F2 (Phase 2): On-demand block read + bounded RSS (drop whole-object Vec), M=1 inline ring
description:
# F2 — Phase 2: On-demand block read + bounded RSS (fix 224MB blowup), M=1 inline ring

## Why
rq materializes the whole object in a Vec (collect_entries, transport_rq/mod.rs:617-686/1132) =>
224MB RSS at 100M. Stream blocks on demand. See epic asupersync-atp-dataplane-redesign-317hxr.

## Change
Drop the full-object Vec: read each source block on demand from the source file as the encoder needs
it (mmap or buffered read via Cx fs). Introduce the encode-ahead ring at M=1 inline (serial, but
producer/consumer-shaped) so it is byte-identical to HEAD and trivially deterministic — this is the
scaffold F3 later parallelizes.

## Reasoning (queueing)
RSS = ring_slots * batch_bytes <= ring_bytes_budget (~32MiB) instead of object size. Most of the RSS
win is the on-demand read; the ring bounds the rest.

## Default-on / fallback
On by default; byte-identical at M=1 so zero behavioral risk.

## Success criteria
1G RSS plateau profile bounded (< 64MB); committed bytes byte-identical to HEAD; loopback 5/5.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text: F3 (.4) profile + plan posted there is also the F2 driver: the parallel per-block encode must run in BATCHES of B blocks (encode B ahead, spray, repeat) so peak symbol RAM is ~B blocks not the whole object — that batch depth IS this M-ring. Baseline (scripts/atp_rq_encode_baseline.sh): 50M single-threaded = 18.3s @ 98% one core, maxrss 112MB (whole-object Vec). On-demand block read + the B-ring drops both the RSS and (with F3) the wall.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text: MEASURED: F3's parallel encode is useless (even harmful) WITHOUT this ring. A naive parallel encode that batch-encodes then bursts the spray made 50M 5.4x SLOWER (18.3s->98.6s, symbols 51300->115300) — the burst overran the receiver -> feedback explosion (see F3 .4 comment). So this M-ring must drain at the receiver-sustainable rate while encode runs ahead in parallel; encode+spray must OVERLAP at a controlled rate. F3's speedup only materializes once it feeds this paced ring.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text: F3 attempt 2 (parallel encode + transfer-sized 82MB recv buffer) STILL regressed 50M (115300 symbols / 5 rounds) — buffering does NOT absorb the burst; the receiver processing-rate is the ceiling. This M-ring must be paired with a PACED/ack-clocked spray (see F3 .4). Reverted (4249015a6).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: SapphireHill (orchestrator benchmark finding, 2026-06-18): RATE-CAPPED links REQUIRE atp send-side pacing. On netem rate=1gbit delay=2ms LOSS=0% (a CLEAN rate-capped link), atp-rq-auth FAILED: 'no convergence after 17 rounds, 1 entry pending' — the unpaced 8-stream burst overruns the rate-cap qdisc buffer -> drops -> non-convergence. rsync's single-TCP congestion-control fills the buffer WITHOUT overflow. So the CongestionController/TokenBucket pacing (WIRE-2/E-7.3) is MANDATORY for realistic (bandwidth-limited) links. The earlier 'pacing negative' verdict (N-2/E-7.3) was measured on an UNREALISTIC uncapped loopback (infinite bw, no buffer to overflow) — RE-EVALUATE pacing on rate-capped netem (rate + realistic limit), where it should be POSITIVE. This is THE lever to beat rsync on 'perfect/good/bad' rate-capped regimes. Pair with the Finding-1 FEC fallback (6acf22391) + GSO (1be226210).

title: F3 (Phase 3): Parallel + SIMD per-block encode on blocking_pool (encode -> network-bound; default-on, inline-in-lab)
description:
# F3 — Phase 3: Parallel + SIMD per-block encode (rq throughput: encode becomes network-bound)

## Why (Problem 2 core)
rq's large-file bug is SERIAL super-linear GF(256) encode on one core (encoding_parallelism:1) =>
100M 164.75s @ 99% CPU. With rq's existing K~=512, blocks are independent => embarrassingly
parallel. The user wants symbols batch-computed ahead, buffered, then sent. See epic asupersync-atp-dataplane-redesign-317hxr.

## Change (verified code sites)
1. Enable SIMD by default for the atp binary: add the simd-intrinsics feature to atp-cli; flip the
   encoding_parallelism:1 literals (transport_rq/mod.rs:1486, 2506, 2791) to a profile-driven
   degree. RE-BENCHMARK 100M FIRST to get an honest scalar/SIMD/serial baseline (the 164.75s number
   was without SIMD in the bin).
2. M>1 encode-ahead ring: parallel per-(entry,SBN) encoders on crate::runtime::spawn_blocking ->
   region BlockingPool, feeding the bounded mpsc ring (from F2) consumed by the paced sender. Per-
   block encode hooks already exist: encode_single_block_with_repair / _repair_range
   (encoding.rs:232/243, ESI-monotone). Make repair_cursor PER-BLOCK (BTreeMap<u8,usize>) so source
   symbols mint exactly once and repair ESIs stay [already, already+count) under concurrency.
3. SIMD kernels already exist + ledgered (gf256.rs:2743/1933/2201, row unsafe-src-raptorq-gf256-rs);
   keep coefficient matrix Vec<u8> so systematic.rs:570-573 addmul-slice adds ZERO new unsafe.

## Reasoning (Amdahl)
S(p)=1/((1-p)+p/M); p~=0.95, M=8-16 => ~9x, multiplicative with SIMD's 1.5-2.5x on the hot loop =>
100M ~15-25s (network-bound), beating/ matching rsync 8.44s once encode overlaps send.

## asupersync invariants (critical)
spawn_blocking runs INLINE (M=1) when the Cx has no pool => lab is deterministic; M>1 only when pool
present. Cancel-correct (region-scoped handles, CancelOnDrop, drain on finalize). Bit-identical to
serial via (sbn,esi) min-heap emit order.

## Default-on / fallback (USER MANDATE)
Parallel + SIMD ON by default in production (pool present + CPU SIMD detected). AUTOMATIC fallback:
inline M=1 serial when no pool (lab) or bit-identity golden fails; scalar GF(256) when no AVX2/NEON.
Runtime triggers, NOT user flags.

## Success criteria
Golden bit-identical parallel/SIMD vs scalar-serial; ESI-monotonicity under concurrency; cancel-leak
clean; 100M ~15-25s, 1G < rsync 176.84s on the re-benchmark.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
PROFILE + IMPLEMENTATION-READY PLAN for F3 (parallel per-block encode). Extreme-optimization
discipline: baseline measured, hotspot located, isomorphism strategy proven, primitives confirmed.

BASELINE (post-F0 bounded-K, single-threaded, loopback rq, 64-core host; scripts/atp_rq_encode_baseline.sh):
  10M -> 3.54s wall, 98% CPU (ONE core), 10260 symbols, sha OK
  50M -> 18.34s wall, 98% CPU (ONE core), 51300 symbols, sha OK
  => extrapolates ~37s/100M, ~370s/1G. This single-core encode IS the large-file loss vs rsync
     (MILESTONE-5 benchmark). 98% of 1/64 cores => ~30x headroom from parallelizing across blocks.

HOTSPOT: src/net/atp/transport_rq/mod.rs::spray_round (line ~1435). Round 0 builds one
EncodingPipeline PER ENTRY with `encoding_parallelism: 1` HARDCODED (line ~1486, also ~2506/~2791),
then runs pipeline.encode_with_repair(...) as a SEQUENTIAL iterator, awaiting a UDP send between
symbols. The expensive part is the per-source-block RaptorQ solve (intermediate symbols), done one
block at a time on one core. Post-F0 a large object = MANY independent source blocks (bounded K), so
the solve is embarrassingly parallel across blocks.

GOTCHA (file a cleanup or fold into F3): `EncodingConfig.encoding_parallelism` is a DEAD knob — it is
set all over (config.rs defaults it to available_parallelism(); transport_rq hardcodes 1) but NOTHING
consumes it to spawn/parallelize. There is zero blocking_pool/spawn_blocking/thread usage in the whole
encode path. So flipping the field does nothing; F3 must wire real parallelism (and either honor the
field or remove it).

ISOMORPHISM (why this is safe on the WORKING rq path): RaptorQ repair-symbol payloads are deterministic
functions of (object_id, SBN, ESI); the receiver decode is order-independent and verifies sha256+merkle.
So parallel-vs-sequential encode produces the IDENTICAL symbol set; spray order may differ but the
received file is byte-identical. Isomorphism holds at the transfer level. Building block already exists:
EncodingPipeline::encode_single_block_with_repair(object_id, sbn, block_data, repair_count) +
encode_single_block_repair_range(...) (src/encoding.rs ~232/243) preserve the exact object/SBN/ESI
layout, so a per-block parallel path emits the same datagrams encode_with_repair would.

PRIMITIVE (confirmed): Cx::spawn_blocking<F,R>(f) -> TaskHandle<R> (src/cx/cx.rs:3948). Region-owned
(region close waits => cancel-correct by construction; cancelling the region cancels the wrapper task,
the closure's result is discarded), pool-dispatched when a pool handle is present, and INLINE under the
lab runtime (deterministic fallback — satisfies F3 "inline-in-lab"). send_path already has `cx`.

SHAPE:
  1. Enumerate an entry's source blocks: (sbn, byte_range, block_source_n, repair_count). Mirror the
     block partition the pipeline uses (max_block_source_symbol_count at ~1077 + symbol_size +
     max_block_size); or expose a small `plan_blocks` accessor from EncodingPipeline.
  2. For each block (or each batch of B blocks), cx.spawn_blocking(move |child| { build a 1-block
     EncodingPipeline; collect encode_single_block_with_repair(object_id, sbn, &block, repair) into an
     owned Vec<Symbol> }). Symbols own their payload (Send).
  3. Await the batch's handles, then spray the collected symbols (network-bound, stays serial/paced).
  4. BOUNDED MEMORY (this is F2's M-ring): process blocks in batches of B (not all at once) so peak
     symbol RAM is ~B blocks, not the whole object. B ties to F2's encode-ahead ring depth.
  5. SMALL-OBJECT FAST PATH (F3.4 .4.4): if an object is a single block (<= ~512K/1M), skip spawning
     and encode inline — the spawn/join overhead would erase atp's small-file latency win (baseline
     10M already 3.5s; sub-1M must stay sub-100ms). Gate parallelism on block_count > 1 (or a small
     threshold).
  6. DEFAULT-ON (user mandate): parallelism uses the runtime pool by default (no opt-in flag); degree
     bounded by available_parallelism and the batch depth.
  Feedback-round encode (encode_repair_range, the else branch) is small per round — leave sequential
  first; parallelize later if profiles warrant.

VERIFICATION GATE: re-run scripts/atp_rq_encode_baseline.sh before/after — wall must drop, cpu_pct must
exceed 100% (multi-core), sha_ok must stay true; plus the loopback floor (scripts/atp_e2e_loopback.sh)
and the cross-machine rq proof (10M OVH->Contabo, see F0 .1 comment) must stay green (no regression to
the one working cross-machine path). The same per-block parallel structure then transfers to
transport_quic once F1 lands.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
EMPIRICAL FINDING (2026-06-16): a naive parallel per-block encode REGRESSES throughput — F3 MUST be
coupled with F2's paced encode-ahead ring; it cannot be batch-encode-then-burst-spray.

I implemented the parallel path exactly as planned (block enumerate -> Cx::spawn_blocking per block
batch over encode_single_block_with_repair -> collect -> spray; single-block inline fast path), built
it (compiles clean, lib + release), and ran the before/after gate (scripts/atp_rq_encode_baseline.sh,
64-core host, loopback rq):

  size  BEFORE (sequential)        AFTER (naive parallel)            verdict
  10M   3.54s @ 98%, 10260 syms    2.60s @ 142%, 10260 syms, sha OK  modest win
  50M   18.34s @ 98%, 51300 syms   98.62s @ 110%, 115300 syms, sha OK  5.4x REGRESSION

sha stayed OK at both sizes (the per-block parallel encode is CORRECT — symbols are byte-identical, the
isomorphism holds). But 50M got 5.4x SLOWER and sent 2.25x more symbols (51300 -> 115300).

ROOT CAUSE: the sequential encoder's per-symbol CPU time implicitly PACES the UDP spray. Removing it
(encode a whole batch fast, then spray it) turns each batch into a BURST that overruns the receiver's
UDP socket buffer + the bounded inbound queue -> packet loss -> a NeedMore feedback-round explosion
(the 2.25x extra symbols) -> wall time dominated by feedback rounds, not encode. The encode got faster
(10M proves it: 142% CPU, quicker) but the transfer got slower because the receiver can't drain the
burst. On 10M (few blocks, ~1 batch) the burst is small enough to win modestly; on 50M (many blocks,
multiple full batches) the bursts overwhelm.

CONCLUSION (validates the F3 -> F2 dependency as LOAD-BEARING, not formal): parallel encode must feed a
PACED, rate-matched drain — F2's encode-ahead RING. The correct shape is: encode blocks ahead into a
bounded ring (depth B) on the blocking pool, and drain/spray from the ring at the receiver-sustainable
rate (the existing SPRAY_FLUSH pacing / fanout), so encode runs parallel-and-ahead while the spray
stays paced. Encode and spray must OVERLAP at a controlled rate, never "encode batch then dump batch".
Also worth pairing with adaptive pacing (raise the spray rate until loss appears) so the parallel
encode's headroom actually reaches the wire.

CODE: the correct parallel-encode structure (block enumerate + spawn_blocking + encode_single_block +
SBN-ordered collect, with the single-block inline fast path) is preserved in my local git stash
("F3 parallel-encode WIP ..."); reusable once it drains through F2's paced ring. NOT committed — never
land a measured regression (extreme-optimization discipline). Baseline gate to reuse:
scripts/atp_rq_encode_baseline.sh (committed). Acceptance for F3+F2: 50M wall well under 18s, cpu>>100%,
symbols_sent ~= sequential (no feedback explosion), sha unchanged, loopback floor + cross-machine rq green.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
DEFINITIVE FINDING after two empirical attempts — F3 parallel encode REGRESSES unless the spray is
PACED to the receiver; a bigger recv buffer is NOT enough. Both attempts reverted (commit 4249015a6
reverts 7fe329ac9; the reverted code is preserved in git history for the paced re-implementation).

Attempt 1 (naive parallel encode, batch-then-spray, 16MB recv buffer):
  50M 18.3s -> 98.6s; symbols_sent 51300 -> 115300; 5 feedback rounds. 5.4x REGRESSION (sha OK).
Attempt 2 (+ recv buffer sized to the transfer = ~82MB for 50M, + Hello.total_bytes, + size gate):
  50M STILL 115300 symbols / 5 rounds. The buffer did NOT absorb the burst.

WHY (the hard constraint): the sequential encoder's per-symbol CPU time implicitly paces the spray.
Parallelizing encode lets the sender spray far faster than the receiver's CPU-bound decode drains it,
so the receiver drops symbols -> NeedMore feedback explosion (2.25x symbols, 5 rounds). A larger recv
buffer only delays overflow; the receiver's PROCESSING-RATE-UNDER-BURST is the ceiling, not buffer size.
10M wins modestly (3.54->2.56s) only because it is small enough that the burst is absorbed.

ALSO FOUND (blocks real parallelism): the atp CLI runtime (src/bin/atp.rs build_runtime) builds
`RuntimeBuilder::multi_thread().worker_threads(n)` with NO `.blocking_threads(min,max)` — the blocking
pool defaults to (0,0), so `Cx::spawn_blocking` takes its inline-on-worker fallback. Parallelism is
therefore capped at `--workers` (4 in tests), NOT the 64-core pool. Any real parallel encode must add
`.blocking_threads(...)` to the CLI runtime.

INFRA HAZARD: the swarm auto-committed my UNVERIFIED working-tree change to main (7fe329ac9) WHILE I was
mid-test, shipping the regression before I could revert it. Re-implementation must keep risky WIP out of
the auto-committed tree until verified (or coordinate to pause auto-commit).

CORRECT DESIGN (paced, robust for all sizes — the re-implementation):
  1. Configure the CLI blocking pool: build_runtime -> .blocking_threads(workers.max(2), <=available).
  2. Parallel per-block encode-ahead into a BOUNDED ring (F2): encode blocks on the pool, buffer a few
     batches in RAM; backpressure when the ring is full (bounds memory for 1G).
  3. PACE the spray so the sender never outruns the receiver. Self-tuning option (preferred):
     ACK-CLOCK it by chunking round 0 through the EXISTING ObjectComplete->NeedMore feedback — spray a
     window (<= recv-buffer worth), wait for the receiver's reply (which means it has drained that
     window), spray the next + re-send anything NeedMore reports lost. In-flight <= window; the reply
     timing clocks the sender to the receiver's true rate; no magic rate constant. Alternative: AIMD
     token-bucket on per-round loss.
  4. To lift the ceiling above the single-threaded decode (needed to actually beat rsync on 100M/1G):
     parallelize the receiver DECODE per-block too (F6.3), symmetric to the encode. Then both CPUs
     scale and the ack-clock keeps them matched.
ACCEPTANCE GATE (scripts/atp_rq_encode_baseline.sh, committed): 50M wall well under 18s, cpu>>100%,
symbols_sent ~= sequential (NO feedback explosion), sha unchanged; loopback floor + cross-machine rq green.
Realistic win without parallel decode: ~1.5-1.8x (decode-bound). With parallel decode: much larger.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
F3 implementation guidance — now that F2's encode-ahead ring has LANDED (9cc0e5cb6 M=1 ring scaffold;
e389fe123 on-demand block reads / dropped whole-object Vec). F3 = build parallel + paced drain ON this
ring. Two prerequisites/findings + the design + the proven safety gate:

PREREQUISITE LANDED: the atp CLI runtime now configures a blocking pool
(src/bin/atp.rs build_runtime: `.blocking_threads(workers.max(2), <=available)`). Without it
`Cx::spawn_blocking` ran INLINE on a worker (parallelism capped at --workers, never the pool) — that is
why my earlier parallel-encode attempts barely used >1 core. spawn_blocking now dispatches to the pool.

WHY THE CURRENT M=1 RING IS SAFE: `EncodeAheadRing::CAPACITY = 1`; the drain is lockstep
(`ring.push(sym); let s = ring.pop(); send_symbol_datagram(s).await`) — encode one, spray one. The
encode time per symbol implicitly PACES the spray (= sequential behavior, non-regressing).

F3 DESIGN (raise M + parallel fill + PACED drain):
  1. Raise CAPACITY: `slot: Option<EncodeAheadSymbol>` -> a bounded `VecDeque<EncodeAheadSymbol>` of M
     symbols (M ~ a few blocks' worth). push errors / backpressures when full; pop_front to drain.
  2. PARALLEL FILL: encode blocks via `cx.spawn_blocking` (now pool-backed) over
     `EncodingPipeline::encode_single_block_with_repair` (byte-identical per SBN -> transfer-level
     isomorphism; decode is order-independent + sha/merkle-verified). Fill the ring up to M ahead of
     the drain; backpressure when full (bounds RAM — this is the M-ring's purpose).
  3. PACE THE DRAIN — THIS IS MANDATORY. Raising M + parallel fill WITHOUT pacing the drain reproduces
     the 5.4x regression I measured (50M 18.3s->98.6s, symbols 51300->115300, 5 rounds): the drain
     bursts faster than the receiver's CPU-bound decode -> drops -> NeedMore explosion. A bigger recv
     buffer alone does NOT fix it (measured: 82MB transfer-sized buffer still gave 115300 symbols/5
     rounds). The drain rate must be <= the receiver's processing rate. Options:
       (a) ACK-CLOCK (preferred, self-tuning, no magic constant): chunk the source spray through the
           existing ObjectComplete->NeedMore feedback so the receiver's reply clocks the next window;
           in-flight <= one window. NOTE the source-request path is gated on repair_overhead<=1.0
           (default 1.001 disables it) — enable/adjust it for windowed source delivery.
       (b) Token-bucket at a rate that AIMD-adapts on per-round loss; or moderate fixed pace + recv
           buffer sized to absorb the (pace - drain)*duration overshoot (works for sizes the buffer
           covers; gate very-large transfers to sequential).
  4. CEILING: the receiver decode is single-threaded (~the sequential encode rate). Sender-only F3 is
     capped ~1.5-1.8x by it (and ~0 on the lossy OVH<->Contabo WAN, which is network-bound). To beat
     rsync on 100M/1G, ALSO parallelize the receiver DECODE per-block (F6.3 .7.3), symmetric to F3.

ACCEPTANCE GATE (scripts/atp_rq_encode_baseline.sh, committed): 50M wall well under 18s, cpu>>100%,
symbols_sent ~= sequential (NO feedback explosion), sha unchanged; plus loopback floor + cross-machine
rq stay green. The reverted parallel-encode code (block-enumerate + spawn_blocking + single-block) is
in git history at 7fe329ac9 for reuse.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SapphireHill 2026-06-17: F3 parallel per-block encode RE-APPLIED on the now-fixed blocking pool (CLI blocking pool fixed in 599356511) and LANDED in 4c665fe6a (main+master, auto-committer bundled it with the peer's 'stream large receives' rq commit). Adapted to the current disk-streaming spray_round (read_source_range + encode_single_block_with_repair per block), NOT the old enc.bytes path. Byte-identical wire output verified (sha256 OK on loopback before/after + cross-machine 10M/100M). Hello.total_bytes + receiver UDP recv-buffer sizing (16MiB->total+32MiB clamped 120MiB) + PARALLEL_ENCODE_MAX_BYTES=112MiB cap. transport_rq tests 51/0.

MEASURED (cross-machine OVH 16-core -> Contabo, sha-verified): baseline(scalar,serial)=164.75s -> F3(parallel,scalar)=113.85s (1.45x, CPU 99%->125%). 

SIMD re-benchmark (the bead asked for this): F3+simd-intrinsics(AVX2 GF256, runtime-detected) = 133.57s cross-machine 100M, 170s loopback -> NO net benefit vs scalar (slower, within variance). The decode bottleneck is NOT GF256-vector-bound. => did NOT wire simd-intrinsics into atp-cli default. 

ROOT CAUSE of remaining slowness: single-core RaptorQ DECODE is the wall. Default max_block_size=8MiB => K=8192, only ~13 blocks for 100M (bead's 'K~512' is STALE). Parallel encode shifts the wall to the single-threaded receiver decode (~0.8MB/s); on fast/loopback paths the parallel burst also outruns the decoder -> recv-buffer overflow -> 5-6 feedback rounds (230600 symbols sent vs 102565 needed). DECISIVE next levers: F6.3 (.7.3 receiver parallel decode) + F2 (.3.x rate-paced encode-ahead to stop burst overrun); possibly smaller max_block_size (more, cheaper blocks => wider encode+decode parallelism). rsync still wins clean (8.44s) AND mild-loss (1.5%/25ms: rsync 10M 2.41s vs atp 10.77s) because ATP is CPU(decode)-bound, not loss-bound.

title: F4 (Phase 4): Capacity-matched repair — ceil(K*p/(1-p)+z*sqrt+2), online eps estimator (kills 99% re-spray)
description:
# F4 — Phase 4: Capacity-matched repair (kills the 99% re-spray)

## Why
The sender re-sprays repair forever (blind max(K/4,16)) => 99% CPU and congestion collapse. Send the
EXACT deficit. See epic asupersync-atp-dataplane-redesign-317hxr.

## Change (verified code sites)
Replace repair_batch_per_block max(K/4,16) (transport_rq/mod.rs:1399 and transport_quic/mod.rs:1287)
with the capacity-matched formula. Add an online erasure-rate estimator (EWMA of receiver-reported
loss in NeedMore) as a PURE value type taking cx.now()/micros (mirror RttEstimator transport.rs:94;
do NOT use CongestionController's Instant::now() body). Decode-safety certificate (adaptive.rs
245/269) bounds P_fail.

## Reasoning (concentration)
repair*(K) = ceil(K*p/(1-p) + z_alpha*sqrt(K*p/(1-p)) + 2); at K=512,p=0.08 => 68 repair/block (vs
blind 128), P_fail = Phi(-z) + (1/256)^ceil(eps*K) <= alpha. Sending the deficit converges in
bounded rounds instead of never.

## Default-on / fallback
On by default. AUTOMATIC fallback to fixed eps_floor when eps_hat missing / feedback_rounds >
max/2 (estimate distrusted); HARD CEILING never exceeds today's max(K/4,16). Runtime trigger.

## Success criteria
Decode-safety certificate test (K x p sweep, P_fail <= 1e-3); lossy-link test converges in <=2 rounds
with exact-deficit NeedMore; total symbols sent <= K/(1-eps)*(1+floor_overhead).

title: F5 (Phase 4): Delivery-rate pacing + flow control (BBR-lite token bucket, cold-start floor fallback)
description:
# F5 — Phase 4: Delivery-rate pacing + flow control (BBR-lite, closed loop)

## Why
Open-loop spray floods the receiver. Pace to the MEASURED delivered rate and cap inflight to the
receiver's flow-control credit. See epic asupersync-atp-dataplane-redesign-317hxr.

## Change
New SymbolPacer: token bucket at pacing_rate = gain*BtlBw, cwnd = BtlBw*minRTT, where BtlBw = max
over a sliding window of delivered_symbols/dt from receiver feedback (useful_count, micros). Add a
flow-control-credit field to NeedMore so inflight <= receiver free queue slots. PURE value type
taking cx.now() explicitly (mirror RttEstimator transport.rs:94). Gate emission at the F2/F3 ring
consumer; replace native_link.rs fixed SPRAY_FLUSH_THRESHOLD/PAUSE (139/145/149) and rq pacing.

## asupersync invariants
Pure rate math on cx.now() => replayable; sleep via crate::time::sleep(cx.now(), ...).

## Default-on / fallback
On by default. AUTOMATIC COLD_START fallback to fixed 1ms/symbol floor (the loopback-tested path)
when <2 delivery samples / no min-RTT / malformed report — fail-SAFE to the floor, NEVER fail-open
to flood. Runtime trigger, not a user flag.

## Success criteria
Unit: rate estimate deterministic + monotone window; inflight <= credit; cold-start uses floor.
Cross-machine: sender CPU returns to ~0 after K reached; link-rate utilization.

Instrumented 50M/bad (ATP_RQ_TRACE=1, runs 20260620T051415Z / 233043Z): 50M = 100 RaptorQ blocks (sbn 0-99, K~437). Exactly ONE block never reaches decode rank across all 7+ feedback rounds (pending=1 the entire transfer). The receiver caught it mid-spiral: "rank=365/494 rank_deficit=129 rank_blocks=1" and "entry 0 parallel decode rejected reason=InconsistentEquations decode_ms=0". The sender keeps spraying 7800-15992 symbols/round at that block (repair_overhead 1.1773, fec_fallback=true from round 1 — adequate FEC) but source_received plateaus at 28432/43700 from round 3 — new symbols stop advancing the one stuck block.

== WHY IT MATTERS ==
That one stuck block keeps the ENTRY pending, which (via entry-granular byte_pressure -> pressure_loss=0.05) disables the pacing floor and collapses the path rate (bead 2.5). If this block decoded in ~1-2 rounds like the other 99, the entry would complete fast, byte_pressure would never hit 1.0, and the rate-collapse spiral would never start. So fixing convergence here is the cleaner ROOT fix (removes the trigger), complementary to 2.5's pacing-signal redesign.

== INVESTIGATION ==
The InconsistentEquations decode rejection is a RaptorQ correctness red flag: the received symbols for that block produced an inconsistent linear system. Candidates to check: (a) symbol/labeling mixing under loss+reorder (a symbol attributed to the wrong sbn/esi); (b) repair symbols that don't add independent rank (rank stalls at 365/494 despite receiving 461+ symbols => ~21% redundant, far above RaptorQ's <1% — suggests duplicate/dependent repair ESIs being accepted for that block); (c) the parallel-decode path mishandling the block's symbol set vs the inline path. Reproduce with the e2e: sudo env BIN=<release atp> ATP_RQ_TRACE=1 ... 50M @ bad (2% loss/50mbit/80ms) and grep recv.time for 'rank_deficit' + 'InconsistentEquations'. PASS = no block stalls (pending->0 in <=2-3 rounds), no InconsistentEquations rejections, sha+merkle ok. Ping when a candidate lands; I bench + verify (the rate-collapse should also shrink dramatically once the entry stops staying pending).

title: transport_rq pacing is ALREADY wired — clean-1gbit non-convergence is NOT an unpaced-burst problem; re-diagnose (rate-cap 64MiB/s vs decode-bound receiver)
description:
cc cross-review (read-only) of the WIRE-2/E-7.3 PACING premise. FINDING: the CongestionController/TokenBucket from datagram/congestion.rs is ALREADY wired into the RQ spray. send_symbol_datagram (mod.rs:2543) and the new batched queue_symbol_datagram (mod.rs:2500, in the current uncommitted WIP) both take `pacer` and call pacer.before_send() (mod.rs:425) before EVERY send; before_send loops on controller.try_consume_send_budget()/time_until_send_budget() (TokenBucket). Both the parallel-encode path (mod.rs:2328) and the sequential M=1 path go through it. So 'wire congestion.rs into spray_round/send_symbol_datagram' is DONE.
WHY THE 'unpaced burst overruns the qdisc' PREMISE IS LIKELY WRONG: RqSprayPacing.from_rate (mod.rs:373) clamps the spray to RQ_MAX_PACING_BPS=64MiB/s (~512mbit) and bursts only RQ_COLD_START_BURST_SYMBOLS=16 / RQ_ADAPTIVE_BURST_SYMBOLS=32 symbols (~19-38KB). On a clean 1gbit link (125MB/s) atp paces to ~HALF the pipe with a ~38KB burst — that cannot overrun a 1gbit qdisc. So a clean-1gbit FAILURE is not a send-side burst overrun.
REAL CANDIDATE ROOT CAUSES (A/B in Phase-2, do NOT blindly raise the rate):
  1. RATE CAP TOO LOW: paced to <=64MiB/s regardless of path capacity. 'pace to PATH rate' = track measured bandwidth and lift the cap. But...
  2. DECODE-BOUND RECEIVER: single-core RaptorQ decode ~0.8MB/s (per ledger). Even at 64MiB/s the receiver can't drain -> recv-buf overflow -> feedback-round explosion -> NoConvergence within max_feedback_rounds=16. Raising the send rate (root cause 1) makes THIS worse. The lever is RECEIVER parallel decode + encode-ahead, not faster spray.
  3. TIME-BASE SPLIT: before_send uses Instant::now() (mod.rs:427) for the controller but crate::time::sleep(cx.now(),..) — harmless in real runs, but breaks pacing under virtual-time lab tests (relevant to F8.4 controller-interference test 317hxr.9.4).
RECOMMENDATION: do not re-wire pacing (already done); instead Phase-2 A/B the 64MiB/s cap and confirm whether clean-1gbit non-convergence is decode-bound (measure feedback_rounds + receiver recv-buf overflow). transport_rq/mod.rs is currently dirty/locked (batched-send WIP) so I did not edit it.
