title: F6 (Phase 4): Reliable self-resync control (round_seq + PTO resend + KeepAlive beacon)
description:
# F6 — Phase 4: Reliable self-resync control automaton (lost marker self-heals)

## Why
The control STREAM has no loss recovery over a real link (native_link comment: "assumes low-loss
loopback/LAN") => one lost NeedMore/ObjectComplete/Proof deadlocks the transfer. See epic asupersync-atp-dataplane-redesign-317hxr.
Relates to b0k8qo handshake ACK/PTO (harness tasks #21/#22).

## Change
Add round_seq numbering + a PTO resend timer + a KeepAlive beacon (REUSE the existing KeepAlive
frame) so the control plane self-resyncs: idempotent NeedMore, sequence-numbered ObjectComplete,
periodic beacon. Prefer reusing quic_native loss-detector/PTO/RttEstimator over new machinery.

## Reasoning (self-stabilization / ARQ)
An idempotent + timeout-driven protocol cannot deadlock on a single loss: worst case is one PTO of
delay. Provide safety (no double-commit) + liveness (progress under bounded loss) obligations.

## Default-on / fallback
On by default. AUTOMATIC fallback: seq=0 (serde default) => scheduler disabled, beacons ignored,
current 250ms quiet-window break (old-peer / disabled). Fail closed after max_feedback_rounds.

## Success criteria
Inject control-frame loss => transfer still commits (bounded extra rounds, <250ms self-heal); no
deadlock; no double-commit; PTO schedule deterministic in lab.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
EVIDENCE for the KeepAlive-beacon / peer-liveness half of F6 (from the G4.6 cancel/peer-death e2e, scripts/atp_e2e_cancel.sh, first full run 2026-06-16, loopback, 50M).

The cancel suite SIGKILLs one side of a live transfer mid-flight and measures how fast the survivor notices and recovers. It isolates exactly the gap F6's KeepAlive beacon + reliable control is meant to close:

  rq  /kill-sender   -> receiver exits 0s, staging clean   PASS  (TCP control channel EOF = instant peer-death detection)
  rq  /kill-receiver -> sender   exits 1s, clean           PASS  (TCP control channel EOF)
  quic/kill-sender   -> receiver exits 61s, staging CLEANED PASS  (no liveness signal; only the 60s idle timeout notices, but it DOES self-clean staging on timeout)
  quic/kill-receiver -> sender   keeps spraying/waiting, hangs past the 80s survivor bound   FAIL (tracked XFAIL)

Root cause: rq gets fast bidirectional peer-death detection for free from its TCP control channel; transport_quic over pure UDP has NO liveness signal. Two concrete consequences:
  (1) On receiver death, the quic sender has nothing to interrupt its paced spray loop — the 60s idle timeout only fires once the sender STOPS sending, so a sender mid-spray hangs for spray-duration + idle-timeout (observed: still spraying into the void past 80s). It also wastes CPU/bandwidth spraying to a dead peer.
  (2) On sender death, the quic receiver waits the full 60s idle timeout before giving up (vs rq's 0s).

This is the same liveness/control deficit as G9 (multi-entry proof-timeout) seen from the peer-death angle. The F6 KeepAlive beacon (periodic liveness ping both directions, with a short miss-budget that fails the transfer closed) would let either side detect peer death in O(beacon interval) instead of O(60s idle timeout or never-while-spraying), and round_seq + PTO resend covers the lost/raced Proof case in G9. Recommend the beacon interrupt the spray loop on the sender, not just the proof-wait.

Regression gate already wired: scripts/atp_e2e_cancel.sh KNOWN_GAPS marks quic:receiver as a tracked XFAIL pointing at G9/F6. When F6 lands, remove that key — the scenario should then exit bounded on its own (sender notices the dead receiver via missed beacons and fails fast) and flip XFAIL->PASS with no source change to the harness.

title: F6.3 [throughput]: receiver parallel decode (inline-in-lab) + dest-disk backpressure
description:
F6.3 [throughput] — Receiver parallel decode + dest-write backpressure (symmetry for saturation).
At line rate with many bounded-K blocks, single-threaded RaptorQ decode (Gaussian elimination, super-
linear per block) can become the RECEIVER bottleneck, mirroring the sender encode problem. Decode
independent blocks in parallel on the receiver BlockingPool (SAME inline-when-no-pool determinism +
cancel-correctness rules as F3). ALSO add dest-disk backpressure: if the destination disk is slower
than decode, the commit path bounds in-flight decoded blocks so receiver RSS stays bounded on a slow
disk instead of growing.
TEST: parallel decode bit-identical to serial (golden); cancel-leak; slow-dest-disk test keeps RSS
bounded; receiver throughput scales with cores on a fast link. Parent F6.

title: F7: Default-on integration — ALL optimizations on by default, automatic fallbacks only (USER MANDATE)
description:
# F7 — Default-on integration + automatic fallbacks (USER MANDATE — gates the epic's product shape)

## THE PRODUCT DIRECTIVE (user, 2026-06-16)
"the default atp cli tool MUST support by default ALL optimizations and features/functionality!"
This bead enforces default-on across the epic and forbids opt-in gating of optimizations.
See epic asupersync-atp-dataplane-redesign-317hxr.

## Change
1. RqConfig::default() and QuicConfig::default() enable EVERY optimization: bounded-K (F0, QUIC
   K~=512), decode-on-arrival/backpressure (F1), on-demand+ring (F2), parallel+SIMD encode (F3),
   capacity-matched repair (F4), delivery-rate pacing (F5), reliable control (F6).
2. The atp CLI ships with simd-intrinsics enabled and uses these defaults — NO "--enable-X" flags.
   Any existing flag that DISABLES an optimization is removed or demoted to a clearly-documented
   debug-only internal switch that defaults to the optimized path.
3. Conservative modes are AUTOMATIC runtime fallbacks keyed on conditions (no pool -> inline M=1;
   lab Cx -> deterministic; <2 samples -> pacing floor; eps_hat distrusted -> repair floor; no SIMD
   CPU -> scalar; old peer / seq=0 -> control disabled), NEVER user-selected.

## Reconciliation with lab determinism (key)
"Default-on" does not break replay because spawn_blocking is INLINE (M=1) when the Cx has no pool
(the lab runtime) and estimators are pure cx.now() value types. Production (pool present) runs the
full parallel/adaptive path. The determinism-replay HARD GATE (F8) must be green before the adaptive
controllers flip default; once green, the END STATE is default-on.

## Success criteria
Running "atp send" / "atp recv" with NO extra flags exercises every optimization; a test asserts the
default config has all enabled; degraded-condition tests prove each automatic fallback triggers
WITHOUT a flag and never makes a transfer fail or corrupt.

title: F8: Proof & verification program — golden encode, decode-iso, convergence, determinism-replay HARD GATE, cross-machine + benchmark gates
description:
# F8 — Proof & verification program (the epic's exit gates)

## Why
Per extreme-software-optimization + alien-artifact discipline: golden/behavior-preservation proof +
measured before/after + named baseline comparator for every change. See epic asupersync-atp-dataplane-redesign-317hxr.

## The gates
1. Golden bit-identical encode: for every (object_id, SBN, ESI), parallel/SIMD encode_single_block_*
   == scalar-serial encode_with_repair byte-for-byte (existing GF(256) golden vectors + property
   test K in [16,4096]); extend fuzz/fuzz_targets/raptorq_gf256_simd_scalar_parity.rs to cover the
   systematic.rs:570-573 addmul-slice path.
2. Decode-isomorphism: arbitrary-interleaved parallel-encoded symbols decode via the UNMODIFIED
   DecodingPipeline to identical bytes; verify_and_commit SHA-256 + flat_merkle_root match.
3. Decode-safety certificate: K in {256,512,1024,4096,8192} x p in {0.01,0.05,0.1,0.2} =>
   decode_fail_probability <= alpha=1e-3 (adaptive.rs:245/269).
4. Convergence at capacity-matched repair: deterministic lossy-link (debug_drop_one_in) multi-block
   object converges in <=2 feedback rounds with exact-deficit NeedMore.
5. ESI monotonicity under concurrency: per-block repair_cursor BTreeMap; source minted once/block;
   repair ESIs [already, already+count) (encoding.rs:243).
6. No-silent-loss: datagrams_dropped_on_receive==0 on lossless loopback; lossy drops kernel-only with
   a cx.trace park/overflow counter.
7. DETERMINISM REPLAY (HARD GATE): same observation stream + same DetRng seed => identical (K,eps,N)
   and identical wire bytes (M=1); pool-present committed bytes == pool-absent. Adaptive controllers
   (F4/F5) do NOT flip default until this is green.
8. Cross-machine acceptance: OVH(51.222.245.56)->Contabo(212.90.121.76) atp --transport quic of file
   + tree, sha256 match, sender CPU ~0 after K reached, no 60s timeout. (Validates convergence — not
   loopback.)
9. Benchmark re-run gates: scripts/atp_quic_vs_rsync_benchmark.sh OVH->Contabo at 512K/1M/10M/100M/1G
   with the SIMD-enabled bin; 100M <= ~25s (from 164.75s), 1G < rsync 176.84s, RSS < 64MB; small-file
   wins preserved. Baselines: current atp-rq, tuned rsync, loopback 5/5.

## Success criteria
All gates green. These operationalize the epic's success criteria as tests/scripts.

title: F8.1: golden bit-identical encode + decode-isomorphism + fuzz parity extension
description:
Golden bit-identical encode (every (object_id,SBN,ESI): parallel/SIMD encode_single_block_* ==
scalar-serial encode_with_repair byte-for-byte; GF(256) golden vectors + property test K in [16,4096])
PLUS decode-isomorphism (arbitrary-interleaved parallel-encoded symbols decode via the UNMODIFIED
DecodingPipeline to identical bytes; verify_and_commit SHA-256 + flat_merkle_root match). Parent F8 (asupersync-atp-dataplane-redesign-317hxr.9).

title: F8.2 [HARD GATE]: determinism replay (observation-stream + pool-present==pool-absent bytes)
description:
DETERMINISM REPLAY HARD GATE: same observation stream + same DetRng seed => identical (K,eps,N)
sequence and identical wire-byte capture (M=1); pool-present committed bytes == pool-absent. The
adaptive controllers (F4 repair, F5 pacing) do NOT flip default until this is GREEN. This is the gate
that reconciles default-on with lab determinism. Parent F8.

title: F8.3: cross-machine QUIC acceptance + OVH->Contabo benchmark gates (atp <= rsync 10M/100M/1G)
description:
F8.3 — Cross-machine acceptance + benchmark gates (the Problem-1 + Problem-2 exit gates).
ACCEPTANCE (Problem 1): OVH(51.222.245.56)->Contabo(212.90.121.76) atp --transport quic of a single
file + a tree: sha256 + merkle match, sender CPU returns to ~0 after K reached, NO 60s symbol-round
timeout. Validates convergence on the real internet (not loopback).
BENCHMARK (Problem 2) via scripts/atp_quic_vs_rsync_benchmark.sh OVH->Contabo at 512K/1M/10M/100M/1G,
SIMD-enabled bin, all sha256 OK. THE BAR IS THE EPIC'S: atp <= rsync at 10M/100M/1G AND small-file
wins preserved (512K/1M). Baselines: tuned rsync (100M 8.44s, 1G 176.84s), current atp-rq (100M
164.75s), loopback 5/5 floor.
TIERED so progress is measurable AND the gate is honest:
 - Checkpoint after F3 (parallel+SIMD encode, single flow / NO fan-out): encode is no longer the
   bottleneck; atp 100M becomes network-bound and roughly MATCHES rsync (target ~8-15s, down from
   164.75s). This is a milestone, NOT the final bar.
 - FINAL beat-gate (REQUIRES G1 multi-connection fan-out): atp 100M and 1G are STRICTLY LESS than
   rsync, because fan-out uses more of the pipe than rsync's single ssh stream. RSS < 64MB throughout.
SUPERSEDES earlier "<=~25s" wording — 25s would LOSE to rsync's 8.44s; the real bar is atp <= rsync,
achieved via F3 (encode) + G1 (fan-out). Parent F8.

title: ATP TCP transport DoS hardening: receive timeout, memory amplification, multi-entry manifest validation
description:
Fresh-eyes audit of src/net/atp/transport_tcp/mod.rs (peer-active, HEAD audited 2026-06-12). The HIGH path-traversal-via-root_name bug was FIXED in this session (safe_base_for_root_name) and the prior OOM-via-Vec::with_capacity was already fixed by a peer (declared-total check + capped initial capacity). Remaining findings:

1. (MEDIUM) No read/idle/accept timeout in receive_connection; serve() handles connections sequentially (one at a time, no spawn). An unauthenticated client that connects and stalls (or completes handshake but never sends ObjectComplete) blocks every subsequent transfer indefinitely (head-of-line DoS). cx.checkpoint() only fires on cancel, not a stalled peer. Fix: per-connection idle/total timeout; consider bounded-concurrency per-connection handlers.

2. (MEDIUM) ~3x receiver memory amplification: after buffering all entries (1x), build 'rebuilt' by cloning every buffer (2x), then build_flat_graph does Object::file(bytes.clone()) (3x). With DEFAULT_MAX_TRANSFER_BYTES=4GiB a legit near-ceiling transfer needs ~12GiB. Doc claims memory is 'bounded' to 1x. Fix: verify SHA in place against buffers (already done) and feed merkle rebuild references/slices, or stream entries to temp files.

3. (LOW) is_directory=false with multiple manifest entries collapses all to one path (base.clone(), last wins) while receipt reports files=entries.len() and committed_paths has duplicates. Duplicate rel_path in directory transfers same issue. Fix: reject is_directory==false && entries.len()!=1, and reject duplicate rel_path.

4. (LOW) Many-file directory transfers fail at the 1MiB single-frame manifest ceiling (~8k files) with opaque FrameTooLarge; document or chunk the manifest.
notes: Finding 1 (head-of-line DoS) now RUNTIME-PROVEN: tests/atp_tcp_stalled_peer_timeout_proof.rs (cargo test --test atp_tcp_stalled_peer_timeout_proof --features test-internals -> 1/1 PASS in 0.51s). A real loopback receive_once accepts a raw TCP client that completes the handshake but stays silent, and fails closed with TransportError::Timeout at the 500ms idle window instead of hanging — proving the per-connection idle timeout reaps stalled peers. Combined with: finding 1 code (with_transport_timeout on all receive reads 895/911/956/989/1213 + concurrent ReceiveTaskHandle tasks + MAX_TRANSFERS_PER_SERVE), finding 2 (borrowed flat_merkle_root_from_slices, no 3x clone), finding 3 (validate_manifest rejects single-file-multi-entry/dup-rel_path/nonsequential/unsafe path), finding 4 (json_frame oversized-manifest preflight). ALL 4 findings addressed + the key security property runtime-proven -> closing.

The P1 head-of-line DoS security property is now RUNTIME-PROVEN by tests/atp_tcp_stalled_peer_timeout_proof.rs (1/1, 0.51s: a stalled peer fails closed with TransportError::Timeout).

title: [deadlock-finder][scheduler] Bound cancellation observation within a real quantum
description:
Deadlock-finder audit over src/{channel,sync,runtime,obligation,cancel} found no fresh lock-order or channel waker-dedup defect in the recently repaired channel/sync paths, but did find a live scheduler cancellation/preemption latency hole.

Proof in source: src/runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs has audit_cancellation_propagation_latency_is_not_bounded_by_one_quantum at lines 14938-15006. It documents and asserts that default cancel_streak_limit=16 and poll_budget=128 permit max_cancellation_delay_polls=2048. That is dispatch-count bounded but not quantum/preemption bounded, so long-running cancel-lane tasks can delay cancellation observation for many poll cycles before ready/timed work is reconsidered.

Concrete interleaving:
1. Sixteen cancel-lane tasks are queued.
2. Each dispatched cancel task can consume the default 128-poll task budget before yielding.
3. A subsequent cancellation-sensitive task or timed/ready fairness candidate is not rechecked until the scheduler completes up to cancel_streak_limit dispatches.
4. Cancellation observation latency becomes 16 * 128 = 2048 poll cycles, violating the stated bounded-latency expectation near one quantum.

Focused reproduction command used by GoldChapel:
rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_GoldChapel cargo test -p asupersync --lib audit_cancellation_propagation_latency_is_not_bounded_by_one_quantum -- --nocapture

Expected fix shape: add/enforce an intra-task quantum or cancellation checkpoint boundary so cancellation and deadline preemption are reconsidered within the intended quantum, while preserving the existing dispatch-level fairness guards for cancel, timed, and stolen-work lanes.

Non-duplicates checked: open beads only showed asupersync-lhx6m4 proof-lane epic; in-progress showed asupersync-lhx6m4.147 proof-runner work. Closed history includes prior scheduler fairness-definition and RwLock/oneshot fixes, but no live bead for this intra-task cancellation/preemption latency hole.

description:
Fresh-eyes audit follow-ups (2026-06-12), each verified against source. Lower-blast-radius or test-only surfaces deferred from the fix pass:

1. (MEDIUM) src/cx/capacity_ticket.rs CapacityTicketId is (owner_region, owner_task, lineage_depth) — NOT unique: two split() of the same parent get identical IDs (parent.lineage+1, same owner); two root request_capacity_ticket() by same task also collide. Receipt consumers matching releases by ticket_id would mis-close siblings, masking leaks. Also CapacityTicket derives Clone + by-value release/revoke, so clone().release() + revoke() mints two terminal receipts both stamped obligation_leak_free=true; no Drop/registry means a ticket dropped on panic/cancel emits no receipt. Fix needs a unique child index/sequence (API may need &mut self) + drop-or-registry-based leak detection. Test-only surface today (tests/capacity_ticket_agent_admission_contract.rs).

2. (MEDIUM) src/lab/config.rs with_oracles/oracle_selection is a no-op: only read inside config.rs's own tests; LabRuntime never consults selected_oracles() (scenario filtering is separate, scenario_runner.rs:450). Builder advertises filtering it doesn't perform. Wire LabRuntime's oracle-report builder to filter via config.selected_oracles(), or delete the field. Also with_chaos clobbers the caller's ChaosConfig seed with seed^0xCAFEBABE (module docs imply independent control).

3. (MEDIUM) src/util/path_security.rs resolve_existing_ancestor appends the not-yet-existing suffix UN-canonicalized; for write paths an attacker with sandbox write can plant a symlink at a suffix component between validate and write (TOCTOU escape). Fix: resolve relative to a pinned dir fd (openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH/NO_SYMLINKS) or re-validate after create_dir_all. Also (LOW) absolute input accepted if lexically within base (doc says joined-with-base); validation is opt-in (AtpInstallConfig defaults base_dir=None, only warns).

4. (MEDIUM) src/net/atp/chunk/dedupe.rs ChunkReuseManager.transfer_chunks (BTreeMap<String,Vec<ChunkIdentity>>) and transfer_stats are never bounded/evicted (ChunkCache is LRU-capped but these aren't) — unbounded memory if transfer_id/registration counts are attacker-influenced. (LOW) LRU keyed on SystemTime::now() (non-monotonic, lab-nondeterministic).

5. (MEDIUM, test-quality) src/atp/timing_security.rs test_constant_time labels a statistically-significant data-dependent timing difference below min_suspicious_delta_ns (default 100ns) as detected=false 'Constant-time operation verified' — a sub-100ns leak is exploitable with enough samples; a conformance tool should not certify 'verified' under it. (The real constant_time_eq in tls/types.rs + grpc/interceptor.rs are SOUND.)

6. (LOW) src/types/slo_policy.rs: p999_latency_budget_ms doc says 'Tightest' but is computed with .max() (loosest); exceeds_thresholds compares work queue_depth against the timer_queue_depth threshold (dimension mismatch, conservative); proof-report staleness check is bypassable by omitting observed_profile_hash (runtime-application validator requires it — inconsistent); evaluate_admission Reject emits ApplicationInvalid issue-kind even when validate() passed.

7. (LOW) src/runtime/env_config.rs: TOML thread_name_prefix with interior NUL panics in std at thread spawn instead of returning ConfigError (config-file feature only; env vars can't carry NUL). Reject/strip NUL in RuntimeConfig::normalize().

title: nats_io arms no budget-deadline timer; UDP recv_error duplicate report on set_recverr sockets
description:
## Findings (read-only review of 077ff3473 and 8abfb9132, SapphireHill subagent, 2026-10-02, at origin 7cd2204f5; not yet verified by running)

### 1. nats_io arms no timer for the call's budget deadline (pre-existing, medium confidence)
src/messaging/nats.rs ~1681. nats_io uses the same owner-plus-driver cancel-waker pattern as redis_io, but unlike redis_io (fixed in 077ff3473) it arms no timer for either budget deadline. A read_more parked on a silent server (for example through next_message) is not woken at the Cx budget deadline. The reviewer did not rule out every runtime-level wake source. A native test with a silent TCP peer and a short budget would settle it.

### 2. UDP recv_error can report one ICMP error twice on set_recverr sockets (low; based on Linux kernel behavior, not verified)
src/net/udp/txtime.rs ~599, a dequeue race the 8abfb9132 message itself names:
1. the kernel queues the report;
2. recvmsg(MSG_ERRQUEUE) dequeues it and clears sk_err;
3. __udp4_lib_err sets sk_err again.

The caller already got that ICMP as Ok(report), and the next recv_error returns it again as Err(ConnectionRefused). A caller looping on `recv_error(..).await?` exits its loop. That is better than the old spin, but on set_recverr sockets, clearing the pending error and re-arming would avoid the duplicate.

## Finding (SapphireHill 2026-10-03, kpmoy5.3.5 lanes)
scripts/run_stable_lane_e2e.sh's stable-clippy stage could never run on the RCH workers: their floating `stable` is rustc 1.93.1, below sysinfo 0.39's 1.95 floor. kpmoy5.3.5 pins the lane to 1.95.0. The pinned nightly's clippy does not report them.
- clippy::collapsible_match ("this `if` can be collapsed into the outer `match`"):
  - src/combinator/map_reduce.rs:933:21
  - src/http/h2/client.rs:789:29, 798:29, 813:29

title: [security] types/wasm_abi.rs: WasmHandleTable handle resolution validates only (kind, slot, generation) — no ownership check, JS can forge a handle by replaying any observed (slot, generation) pair
description:
src/types/wasm_abi.rs:962-998 — `WasmHandleTable::allocate(kind: WasmHandleKind) -> WasmHandleRef` returns a `WasmHandleRef { kind, slot, generation }` to the JS caller with NO check that the JS caller is authorised to allocate that handle kind. The only validation on subsequent `get(handle)` is the generation check (line 1045-1071), which only catches stale handles — not forged ones.

Concrete attack:
  1. JS caller observes a legitimate `WasmHandleRef { kind: Runtime, slot: 1, generation: 0 }` returned by `runtime_create()`.
  2. JS caller crafts a synthetic `WasmHandleRef { kind: Region, slot: <observed_runtime_slot>, generation: 0 }` and passes it to `scope_enter()` claiming it's the parent runtime handle.
  3. The handle-table's get() validates: kind matches (Region OR Runtime depending on scope_enter's expected kind), slot exists, generation matches. BUT there is no "did THIS caller allocate THIS handle" check.
  4. Attacker's scope is now a child of someone else's runtime, with cross-runtime capability flow.

Same architectural smell as asupersync-3zljmn (ArenaIndex::new), asupersync-plm0gr (LabIoCap::new), asupersync-zdfgjo (BrowserReadableStream::from_*) — a public token constructor that mints values whose downstream validation is "shape" rather than "ownership".

Fix direction:
  1. Embed an unforgeable allocator-side nonce in WasmHandleRef (not transmitted to JS) and verify it on get(). The JS-visible representation is just (kind, slot, generation); the runtime keeps a parallel nonce table indexed by slot and rejects any get() whose runtime-side nonce doesn't match.
  2. Or: per-runtime capability list. allocate() records `runtime_id -> Set<slot>` and get() checks the calling runtime's set. JS cannot forge a runtime_id because it is determined Rust-side at allocate time.
  3. Pair with asupersync-zdfgjo: the BrowserReadableStream constructors fix (cap parameter required) is the same shape.

Source: /multi-pass-bug-hunting src/types/* + src/record/* (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Fixed: WasmHandleTable mints SplitMix64 owner_token bound to issuing context, validated on get/get_mut (commit 42c0052fc)

title: [STUB][Z0] Freeze shared validation schema, artifact contract, and rch execution policy
description:
## Background
Cross-track validation requirements were previously scattered across implementation beads, which makes it too easy for different tracks to invent different logging formats, artifact naming, and command conventions. Before the final test suite and E2E runner are built, the epic needs one authoritative validation contract.

## Technical approach
- Freeze the shared validation log schema for unit, integration, E2E, and scan artifacts.
- Define the artifact naming and storage contract so failures are reproducible and easy to inspect.
- Define the `rch` execution policy for cargo-heavy validation, including stable `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` isolation and when a local fallback must be called out explicitly.
- Map each terminal implementation bead in Tracks B-I to the evidence it must contribute: unit coverage, deterministic integration/E2E coverage, scan/policy evidence, and audit/doc updates.
- Distinguish which checks should be source-structure scans, compile/build matrix checks, deterministic runtime tests, or user-facing E2E flows.

## Deliverables
- A single shared validation contract that downstream beads can implement against without inventing new conventions.
- A mapping from each terminal track bead to required validation surfaces and artifact ids.
- The command contract that Z0a, Z0b, Z1, and Z2 will follow for `rch`-backed verification.

## Test / validation plan
- Review against AGENTS `rch` rules and the Track A disposition matrix.
- Dry-run the contract against representative tracks to ensure there is no ambiguity about what evidence must exist.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Required structured log fields, artifact naming rules, and evidence ownership are frozen in one canonical contract.
2. Cargo-heavy validation commands are explicitly required to run via `rch exec --` with isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` handling and documented fallback expectations.
3. Each terminal bead in Tracks B-I has an explicit mapping to unit, integration/E2E, scan, and audit evidence.
4. Z0a, Z0b, Z1, and Z2 can implement against this contract without inventing additional conventions.
notes: This bead is a validation architecture decision, not the implementation of the tests themselves. Its job is to make the downstream validation work uniform, reproducible, and operator-friendly.

title: [PERF] three_lane cancel-injection is O(n^2): linear scan + VecDeque::remove of local ready queue
description:
Hotspot found in the Phase-C profiling pass of the scheduler cancel path (next_task() dispatch itself is already tight: governor-driven streak fairness + O(log n) lane pops).

FILE: src/runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs
FUNCTIONS:
  - move_local_ready_task_to_cancel_lane() (~line 1219)
  - schedule_cancel_on_current_local() (~line 1234)

WHAT IS SLOW: both move a task from the local ready queue (LocalReadyQueue = Mutex<VecDeque<TaskId>>) into the cancel lane by:
    if let Some(pos) = local_ready_guard.iter().position(|t| *t == task) { local_ready_guard.remove(pos); }
That is O(n) for the iter().position() linear scan PLUS O(n) for VecDeque::remove(pos) (mid-vector shift). Per single cancel = O(n) in the local ready queue length.

WHY IT MATTERS: cancelling K tasks that are sitting in a worker's local ready queue is O(K*n) ~ O(n^2). The structured-concurrency mass-cancel cases hit exactly this: region close cancelling all live children, FailFast cancelling all siblings, runtime shutdown. A worker under load can hold hundreds-to-thousands of ready TaskIds, so mass cancellation degrades quadratically. This pressures the 'region close = quiescence, bounded cleanup' invariant (cleanup latency should be bounded, not quadratic in queue depth).

NOT A CORRECTNESS BUG: behaviour is correct; this is a complexity/latency optimization (algorithmic fact, not a measured regression).

PROPOSED FIX (needs design): the position scan exists because VecDeque::remove needs an index. Options:
  1. Lazy tombstone: mark the task cancelled in a membership set and skip/drop it when next_task() pops it from the ready VecDeque (O(1) cancel, O(1) amortized skip-on-pop). Requires next_task ready-pop to consult the cancelled set.
  2. Maintain a HashMap<TaskId, ()> membership set so a not-present task short-circuits the scan (O(1) for the common 'task not in this lane' case), and only scan when membership is confirmed. Does not fix the remove() shift but removes the scan for absent tasks.
  3. Replace the local ready VecDeque with a structure supporting O(1)/O(log n) removal by key (e.g. an indexed slab + free list, or a BTreeMap keyed by insertion order).

MEASUREMENT: there is no existing cancel-storm bench. To get a real before/after, add a criterion bench (benches/) that builds a worker with N ready tasks (N in {64,512,4096}) and cancels all of them, measuring total cancel time; expect superlinear growth pre-fix. Run via rch with --features test-internals,criterion-benches. (Deferred: shared rch fleet is noisy for micro-benchmarks; a large-N cancel-storm should still show the superlinear trend robustly.)
close_reason: Closed by 4c836e468: HEAD already contained the lazy-tombstone local-ready cancel implementation and cancel-storm bench; added a scheduler regression test proving tombstoned entries skip cancelled tasks while preserving live FIFO order. Required RCH cargo check passed: RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_ayg4ot_check_final CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 RUSTFLAGS='-D warnings -C debuginfo=0' cargo check -p asupersync. Optional focused test local_ready_tombstones_skip_cancelled_entries_in_fifo_order was admitted on ovh-a but RCH reported progress-stale with fresh heartbeat and recommended cancellation; cancelled build 29894407268335633. rustfmt and git diff --check passed for src/runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs.

comments.text: 2026-06-14 (SnowyFortress): Surveyed; releasing for a focused session (not a safe session-tail rush). Confirmed the O(n^2): move_local_ready_task_to_cancel_lane / schedule_cancel_on_current_local do iter().position() (O(n)) + VecDeque::remove(pos) (O(n) shift) per cancel on LocalReadyQueue. Recommended fix = option 1 (lazy tombstone), with the CORRECTNESS subtlety the bead glosses: a cancelled task must still go through the cancel lane's drain/finalize (the cancel protocol), NOT be silently dropped. So: (1) cancel = O(1) insert into a per-worker cancelled_local set + push to the cancel lane (do not scan/remove local_ready); (2) next_task's local_ready pop consults cancelled_local: if the popped TaskId is tombstoned, DROP the stale local_ready entry (the task is already queued in the cancel lane) and remove it from the set (bounding set size), then continue popping. This keeps each task processed exactly once (cancel lane authoritative) with O(1) cancel + O(1) amortized skip-on-pop. Verify with the full scheduler cancel suite (no double-process, no drop of non-cancelled, region-close quiescence) + a new benches/ cancel-storm bench (N in {64,512,4096}) to show the superlinear->linear change. Option 2 (HashMap short-circuit) only helps the absent-task case and does NOT fix the present-task remove() shift, so it does not address the mass-cancel O(n^2). Releasing to open; this is hot-path + cancellation-invariant code that needs careful verification, not a churn-window rush.

title: Write macro DSL documentation and examples
description:
# Task

Write comprehensive documentation for the structured concurrency macro DSL.

## Documentation Structure

1. **Overview**: Why macros, what they provide
   - Reduce boilerplate
   - Enforce correct patterns
   - Better error messages
   
2. **Quick Start**: Get running in 2 minutes
   ```rust
   use asupersync::prelude::*;
   
   async fn main() {
       Runtime::new().block_on(|cx| async {
           scope!(cx, {
               let h1 = spawn!(scope, fetch_data());
               let h2 = spawn!(scope, process_data());
               let (data, processed) = join!(h1, h2);
           });
       });
   }
   ```

3. **Macro Reference**: Each macro in detail
   - Syntax variations
   - Expansion (what it generates)
   - When to use
   - Common mistakes

4. **Patterns**: Common usage patterns
   - Fan-out/fan-in
   - Timeout wrapper
   - Retry with race
   - Resource cleanup

5. **Migration Guide**: From manual API to macros
   - Side-by-side comparisons
   - When to use macros vs manual API

## Examples

```
examples/
  macros_basic.rs         # Simple scope/spawn/join
  macros_race.rs          # Racing with timeouts
  macros_nested.rs        # Nested scopes
  macros_error_handling.rs # Error propagation
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Overview explains value proposition
- [ ] Quick start is copy-paste runnable
- [ ] Each macro fully documented
- [ ] Patterns section with real examples
- [ ] Migration guide from manual API
- [ ] All examples compile and pass
- [ ] Doc tests pass

title: [SECURITY] DecodingConfig::default() verify_auth=false is a fail-open default (f4mdcr item 3 unaddressed): RaptorQ decode accepts unauthenticated symbols out of the box
description: Phase-C security hunt finding. SITE: src/decoding.rs:160 — impl Default for DecodingConfig sets verify_auth: false. EFFECT: DecodingPipeline::feed() (src/decoding.rs:325) only calls auth_context.verify_authenticated_symbol() when config.verify_auth is true; when false (the DEFAULT) it skips verification entirely and accepts the AuthenticatedSymbol as-is (decoding.rs:366 into_symbol() with no verify). So a DecodingPipeline built from DecodingConfig::default() authenticates NOTHING — forged/unauthenticated symbols are accepted (decode-matrix poisoning, same class as the repair_scheduler F4 hijack I fixed in yms9p9). The type name AuthenticatedSymbol implies auth occurred; with the default config it did not. RELATION: this is the UNADDRESSED item 3 of CLOSED bead asupersync-f4mdcr ('[security] DecodingPipeline silently skips auth when verify_auth=false'). f4mdcr implemented items 1+2 only (one-time WARN + skipped_verifications() counter, commit f1f086db6) — OBSERVABILITY. Item 3 ('add a must_verify_auth production-mode flag: panic on construction if verify_auth=false in a release build / under a production feature') was NOT done, so the fail-open DEFAULT remains. FIX OPTIONS (maintainer's call): (a) flip the default to verify_auth=true so default-config decode fails closed (rejects symbols without an auth_context, decoding.rs:338-344 already fails closed when context is None), with explicit opt-out for the legitimate no-auth/erasure-only paths (tests already set verify_auth:false explicitly so they are unaffected by the default flip; risk = default-config callers that feed symbols without configuring an auth_context would now reject — needs an audit of DecodingConfig::default() call sites that lack an auth_context); OR (b) implement f4mdcr item 3: a production-mode construction guard that refuses verify_auth=false unless an explicit insecure acknowledgment is set. KEY QUESTION for the maintainer: is decoding.rs the PRIMARY symbol-auth point, or is authentication layered upstream (ATP verifier / repair_scheduler peer-binding) so the inner check is intentionally optional? If upstream always authenticates before decode, default-false is mitigated; if decode can be reached with unauthenticated symbols, default-false is an exploitable fail-open. Filed by SapphireHill 2026-06-14 Phase-C security hunt.
close_reason: Fixed (option a) in f5ff623f0. DecodingConfig::default() now verify_auth=TRUE (fail-closed); a default-config DecodingPipeline rejects unauthenticated symbols (feed() already fails closed with verify_auth=true + no auth_context). Added pub DecodingConfig::without_auth() = explicit documented INSECURE opt-out (== old default); legitimate no-auth paths opt out by name. Repointed erasure-only TypedDecoder::new() + symbol_id fuzz target + 15 behavior-preserving in-lib test spread bases to without_auth(). NEW tests: tests/decoding_secure_default.rs (public-API integration proof, 3/3 PASS via rch) + in-lib default_config_is_fail_closed / default_config_pipeline_rejects_unauthenticated_symbol. On 'test-gated': the no-auth opt-out CANNOT be cfg(test)-restricted (production transport_rq integrity-only / fabric self-verify / TypedDecoder erasure decode legitimately need it — gating breaks the build); the secure default is instead locked by tests + the opt-out is explicit/greppable. Blast-radius safe: recovery.rs uses a full explicit DecodingConfig literal, fabric.rs sets verify_auth:false explicitly, RecoveryDecodingConfig is a distinct type. Gates: rustfmt --check OK; integration proof 3/3 green (lib compiled clean); clippy/errors ZERO in changed files. The lib-unittest + clippy -D warnings targets are red ONLY from a peer's UNCOMMITTED three_lane.rs LocalReadyQueue refactor (LocalReadyQueueInner absent on HEAD), so committed main with only my files stays clean. Pushed main+master.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
2026-06-14 (SapphireHill) Phase-C audit — blast-radius + decision aid.

DECISION INPUT for option (a) 'flip verify_auth default to true':
- The default is NOT only hit by ATP transport. DecodingConfig::default() also flows through src/types/typed_symbol.rs:676 (TypedDecoder => with_config(DecodingConfig::default(), format)) and inner_config() at typed_symbol.rs:886 derives inner pipelines from it. A blind flip makes DEFAULT-CONFIG TypedSymbol/erasure decoding fail closed (reject every symbol) UNLESS a caller attaches an auth_context, because feed() fails closed when verify_auth=true && auth_context==None (decoding.rs:338-345). Broad, possibly-breaking change for legitimate erasure-only callers. ~61 verify_auth refs across src/.
- SIBLING DEFAULT: src/distributed/recovery.rs:468-479 RecoveryDecodingConfig::default() sets verify_integrity=false for the same reason (comment: 'Default off until recovery is plumbed with a SecurityContext'). StateDecoder::decode() maps verify_auth = verify_integrity (recovery.rs:587), so recovery decode is the same fail-open-by-default family. A fix should cover both siblings.

RED HERRING (so reviewers do not chase it): recovery.rs:826-832 'trust_verified_flag' wraps a CollectedSymbol carrying verified=true as AuthenticatedSymbol::new_verified when verify_integrity=false. It LOOKS like trusting an untrusted bit but is INERT for security: (1) add_symbol (525-539) never reads is_verified(); (2) decode() rebuilds a fresh pipeline keyed only on verify_integrity and re-feeds self.symbols, so feed() ignores the carried bit when false and re-verifies vs context when true; (3) RecoveryResult.verified (871) is set from config.verify_integrity, not the carried bit. Changes no outcome today, but it is a latent footgun if a refactor ever makes is_verified() authoritative — recommend always using from_parts there (recover_from_symbols is a documented test path, low urgency).

RECOMMENDATION: prefer option (b) (a production/insecure-acknowledgment construction guard mirroring in-repo patterns CorsPolicy::with_any_headers / TlsConnector::acknowledge_zero_rtt_replay_risk) over a blind default flip, OR scope a flip with an explicit audit+migration of the typed_symbol/erasure default-config call sites. Treat RecoveryDecodingConfig::verify_integrity=false as the same decision. Filed config-layer twin: asupersync-securityconfig-unwired-phantom-controls-x7ad3b.

title: Actor audit: abort() during a graceful drain still runs every buffered message; stop() during a supervised restart backoff waits out the timer and drops the buffered message; capacity 0 panics
description:
Read-only audit of src/channel/oneshot.rs and src/actor.rs at origin/main 6ad7540cd (SapphireHill audit agent S3, 10-05). Each finding was confirmed by re-reading the code.

No HIGH. oneshot loses no value or obligation on any path, and no receiver can hang. In actor.rs no reply caller hangs: queued messages are always handled or dropped, so their reply channels close.

## MEDIUM
M1. abort() or a region cancel during a graceful drain is ignored (actor.rs ~965, ~978-1004).
- is_aborted is computed once, before the drain. The drain loop never checks cancellation again, so a cancel that arrives after the drain started still runs the handler for every remaining buffered message (default capacity 64) under a cancelled Cx.
- This contradicts the abort() doc ("exit at the next cancellation check point") and the drain comment ("If aborted, we just empty the mailbox").
- Fix (taken by SapphireHill): check cancellation at the top of each drain iteration. On cancel, drop the pending message, empty the mailbox and go to on_stop.
- Test: actor::tests::abort_during_a_graceful_drain_drops_the_rest_of_the_tail. With messages 0..=3 queued and stop() called, handler 0 parks until cancelled. abort() is then called, and the expected events are [start, handle-0, stop].

M2. stop() during a supervised restart backoff is not seen until the backoff timer fires, and a message buffered meanwhile is dropped unhandled (actor.rs ~1086-1093, ~1599-1622, ~295-298).
- wait_supervised_restart_delay checks only cx.checkpoint().
- stop() stores Stopping and calls close_receiver(). That wakes only a registered mailbox receive waker, and none is registered during the backoff.
- So join stays Pending for the remaining backoff (Fixed can be any length; the exponential cap is 10 s). The restart is then suppressed and the buffered message is dropped, contradicting stop()'s "will continue processing any currently buffered messages".
- supervised_actor_stop_during_restart_backoff_prevents_new_instance hides the delay because it uses run_with_auto_advance.
- Fix:
  - pass the state cell into the wait, and return when the state is Stopping;
  - register the task waker as the mailbox receive waker during the backoff, so close_receiver() wakes the task;
  - the owner decides whether buffered messages are then drained by a fresh instance, or the drop is documented.

## LOW
- L1. mailbox_capacity == 0 panics in Scope/Cx::spawn_actor and spawn_supervised_actor, through assert!(capacity > 0) in mpsc. They return Result<_, SpawnError> and have no # Panics doc. Fix: return an error or document the panic.
- L2. ActorHandle::send docs say it errors when the mailbox is full, but it waits for capacity. The module calls the mailbox "cancel-safe", but a dropped send future drops its message (mpsc.rs ~665-673).
- L3. The handle doc says dropping the handle makes the actor exit after the remaining messages. That only happens once every ActorRef clone and every live ActorJoinFuture is gone too. join() without stop(), abort() or cancellation never finishes.
- L4. oneshot doc errors:
  - SendError::Cancelled "carries ()" (it carries T);
  - reserve "if dropped before returning" (it is synchronous);
  - Receiver "is consumed" (recv borrows it);
  - is_closed is also true after the value was received;
  - poll_closed stays Pending after a successful send until the value is drained.
- L5 (unverified): a panic-on-drop message dropped on abort turns the join result into Panicked.
close_reason: done

title: [perf-audit] src/runtime/reactor/io_uring.rs:611-647 batch CQE bookkeeping under one state lock
description: IoUringReactor::poll() copies CQEs into a SmallVec, then reacquires self.state.lock() once per completion at src/runtime/reactor/io_uring.rs:611-647 to touch poll_ops/registrations and decide whether to emit an Event. Under readiness bursts this turns reactor dispatch into one mutex round-trip per CQE and contends directly with register/modify/deregister. Improvement direction: process the completion batch under a single state lock (or one lock per chunk), accumulate emitted events and deferred poll_remove actions, then drop the lock before submit_poll_remove()/events.push(). That keeps event dispatch amortized over the batch instead of serializing every CQE on the shared state mutex.

title: [reality-check-wave2][browser-io] Promote browser-native messaging and WHATWG stream APIs
description:
Promote browser-native messaging and WHATWG stream bridges from internal substrate to documented public SDK contracts.

Background and evidence:
src/io/browser_stream.rs already contains browser ReadableStream/WritableStream bridges, BrowserMessageChannelPair, BrowserBroadcastChannel, capability checks, in-memory/native host backends, and tests. src/runtime/reactor/browser.rs wires MessagePort and BroadcastChannel listener bindings. src/io/cap.rs models HostApiSurface::MessageChannel and HostApiSurface::BroadcastChannel. docs/integration.md still says public messaging-surface APIs are direct-runtime feasible but not yet promoted public Browser Edition contracts.

Scope:
- Design and export stable JS/TS and Rust-facing APIs for MessageChannel, MessagePort, BroadcastChannel, ReadableStream, and WritableStream bridges where the substrate is ready.
- Preserve explicit HostApiAuthority capability checks and degraded-mode behavior; users must receive deterministic errors rather than ambient browser access.
- Define public cancellation and close semantics for stream bridges: reader cancel, writer abort/close, lock release, backpressure, pending write cancellation, and message-port detach.
- Update docs/WASM.md, docs/integration.md, and package docs only after contract tests prove the API.

Unit tests required:
- Rust unit tests for stream read/write/cancel/shutdown/lock-release state machines and capability-denied paths.
- JS/TS package tests for exported API names, type-level signatures, error/reason codes, fallback behavior, and backward-compatible package entrypoints.
- Reactor tests for MessagePort/BroadcastChannel event listener attach/detach and duplicate registration failure.

E2E/script proof required:
Add a browser fixture that sends messages through MessageChannel and BroadcastChannel and pipes bytes through ReadableStream/WritableStream bridges. Logs must include bead_id, scenario_id, host_context, api_surface, capability_granted, degraded_mode, bytes_sent, bytes_received, messages_sent, messages_received, close_kind, expected_error, actual_error, verdict, and first_failure.

Validation:
Use rch exec for Rust tests/checks. Package/browser validation must be deterministic and record exact command, fixture path, browser version, and artifact path.

Non-goals:
Do not expose raw TCP/UDP/filesystem/process APIs in Browser Edition. Do not bypass capability checks for convenience. Do not break existing internal substrate tests.

Goal:
Promote browser-native MessageChannel, MessagePort, and BroadcastChannel from Rust substrate to a deliberate public Browser Edition SDK contract without bypassing capability authority or pretending these are asupersync channels. This bead covers the public JS/TS package contract and the Rust/package boundary for messaging only.

Current reality to preserve:
- Rust substrate already exists in src/io/browser_stream.rs: BrowserMessagePayload, BrowserMessageState, BrowserMessageError, BrowserMessagePort, BrowserMessageChannelPair / BrowserMessageChannel, and BrowserBroadcastChannel.
- src/io/cap.rs models HostApiSurface::{MessageChannel, MessagePort, BroadcastChannel}, HostApiAuthority::grant_messaging(), degraded-mode checks, and default-deny behavior.
- src/runtime/reactor/browser.rs attaches real wasm32 MessagePort and BroadcastChannel listeners and validates readable/error-only interest.
- packages/browser/src/index.ts does not currently export a public Browser Edition messaging API, support diagnostics, stable error codes, or type-level contract for these surfaces.

Implementation requirements:
- Design user-facing @asupersync/browser exports for MessageChannel, transferred MessagePort, and BroadcastChannel helpers. Names must be stable, typed, and documented in package source.
- Provide deterministic support diagnostics before construction: surface name, runtime context, capability_granted, degraded_mode, support_class, reason_code, message, guidance, and redaction policy.
- Preserve explicit authority: no helper may reach ambient MessageChannel/BroadcastChannel without an explicit capability/options object or support assertion.
- Define close/abort/detach semantics: close is idempotent; abort is sticky; messageerror transitions to a deterministic errored state; sends after close/abort fail with stable reasons.
- Keep MessageChannel/BroadcastChannel at the browser application boundary. Do not claim raw TCP/UDP, filesystem, process, server, or cross-origin transport support.
- Do not break existing service-worker broker or shared-worker coordinator helpers that also use MessagePort.

Unit tests required:
- Package type/build tests proving all public exports exist in packages/browser/src/index.ts and packages/browser/dist/index.d.ts after build.
- JS/TS behavior tests for support diagnostics, denied capability, degraded-mode denial, message send/receive, close, abort, duplicate close, messageerror mapping, and BroadcastChannel self-exclusion.
- Rust contract test that src/io/mod.rs continues to export the Rust messaging substrate and that src/io/cap.rs remains default-deny.

Proof / logging requirements:
This bead should emit or feed an evidence runner row with: bead_id, scenario_id, host_context, api_surface, capability_granted, degraded_mode, messages_sent, messages_received, close_kind, expected_error, actual_error, verdict, first_failure.

Acceptance:
- @asupersync/browser has stable public messaging exports and support diagnostics.
- All package/Rust contract tests pass through deterministic commands.
- Docs still clearly distinguish browser-native messaging wrappers from asupersync structured channels and from raw transport parity.

title: Notify::drop wake fanout has the same strand-peers bug as notify_waiters
description: src/sync/notify.rs Drop for Notify (around line 544) detaches every pending waiter (takes wakers, clears entries) under the mutex, then wakes them in a plain sequential loop. Same class as notify_waiters (br-asupersync-cnl0jn, fixed fbe222364): a first safe Waker panic aborts the loop, stranding the later detached waiters. Distinct from cnl0jn in TWO ways: (1) a Drop must NOT resume_unwind (a panic escaping Drop during an existing unwind aborts) — the correct handling is catch_unwind per wake + SUPPRESS (fail-closed), not resume; (2) reachability is uncertain/hard-to-test: Notified futures borrow &Notify, so parking a waiter and then dropping the Notify with that waiter still registered is difficult in safe code (a live Notified holds a shared borrow; a dropped Notified removes its own waker). Fix: isolate each wake in catch_unwind so a panicking Waker cannot strand later waiters or abort during teardown; suppress rather than resume. Add a regression only if a reachable populate-slab-then-drop path can be constructed (e.g. via an owned/Arc Notified variant); otherwise document the hardening. Found 2026-07-22 by SapphireHill while fixing cnl0jn.
close_reason: Fixed a9ce69798: per-wake catch_unwind with suppressed payload in Notify::drop; reachable safe-code regression test (mem::forget leak path) red pre-fix, green post-fix; full notify module green; clippy/check --all-targets green

title: src/bytes audit: BytesMut front compaction not amortized (quadratic write-buffer drain), safe set_len zero-fills, BufMut direct-window semantics, and LOWs
description:
Read-only audit of src/bytes (Bytes, BytesMut, buf/ traits, cursors, chains, limits) at origin/main c06414315 (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-03). No HIGH and no memory-safety issue: the module has no unsafe code (crate-level deny(unsafe_code), no allow), Send/Sync are auto-derived, aliasing is impossible by construction (BytesMut owns a unique Vec; split_to copies the head; split_off gives the tail its own Vec; freeze moves the Vec into an Arc that is never mutated).

## MEDIUM
1. FIXED in this session's next stack: BytesMut front compaction had no amortization guard (bytes_mut.rs compact_front_for_additional 115-134). With a full buffer consumed and refilled in small steps (FramedWrite advance after a partial write, then the next encode appends), every append moved the whole live region and capacity never grew: about B bytes copied per n-byte step.

## LOW
2. BytesMut::set_len is safe and zero-fills (491-498), so the spare_capacity_mut + set_len idiom ported from the bytes crate silently writes zeros. No in-tree caller. Pinned by set_len_overwrites_spare_capacity_writes and set_len_zeros_new_bytes. Options: make set_len shrink-only (panic on growth pointing to resize) or remove the pair (owner: public API).
3. The BufMut impls for BytesMut and Vec<u8> report remaining_mut() == usize::MAX - len while chunk_mut() is empty and advance_mut(n > 0) panics (bytes_mut.rs 617-642, buf_mut_trait.rs 325-352); a generic read(chunk_mut()) / advance_mut loop written for the bytes crate reads 0 bytes (silent EOF) or spins. Documented via direct_remaining_mut; pinned by logical_append_capacity_is_distinct_from_direct_window and two siblings. Options: a prominent doc warning, or a safe put_with(n, |buf| -> usize) helper.
4. BytesMut::split_off copies the tail and freeze/into_vec memmove when start > 0 (O(n) where the bytes crate is O(1)); no looping caller found. Document the complexity.
5. Take and Chain do not override copy_to_bytes (take.rs 75-99, chain.rs 71-103), so wrapping a BytesCursor loses its zero-copy path.
Doc slip: bytes/mod.rs:19 says forbid(unsafe_code); it is deny.

## Checked and sound
Bytes slice/split_to/split_off bounds and checked arithmetic; Eq/Hash consistency; BytesMut start <= data.len() invariant across every mutator; reserve capacity guarantee; Buf get_* endianness and underflow panics before any advance; io::Cursor clamping; BytesCursor; Chain/Take/Limit remaining-vs-chunk sums; no unbounded growth.
close_reason: Completed: MEDIUM 1 (amortized BytesMut front compaction) landed in c94f72038, LOWs resolved in 314a44422 (documented O(n) split_off tail complexity, Take/Chain copy_to_bytes, corrected unsafe doc slip), all 156 bytes unit tests pass.

title: [swarm-perf] Add controller interference matrix and timescale-separation proof harness
description:
Background:
- The swarm-perf graph now includes multiple adaptive or semi-adaptive control surfaces for large hosts: scheduler evidence and offline tuning, tail-risk admission, overload brownout, OTLP shedding integration, explainable host profiles, and governor-oriented state readers.
- Canonical graveyard guidance says multiple adaptive controllers sharing telemetry are a high-risk oscillation source and require explicit timescale separation proof plus an interference microbench before rollout.
- Right now the graph has good single-controller beads, but no first-class foundation bead that proves those controllers compose safely on 64+ core / 256GiB swarm hosts.

Candidate surfaces:
- artifacts/
- scripts/
- tests/
- src/runtime/config.rs
- src/runtime/builder.rs
- src/observability/ and runtime policy/evidence consumers

Required design:
1. Define a controller catalog for swarm-perf with explicit inputs, outputs, fallback mode, and update cadence for each controller that reads or writes shared runtime pressure signals.
2. Add a versioned interference-matrix artifact covering shared telemetry fields, shared knob surfaces, safe-mode precedence, forbidden pairings, and a timescale-separation statement for every composed controller pair.
3. Provide a deterministic proof harness or smoke bundle that replays fixed evidence through multi-controller scenarios and flags oscillation, thrash, fallback churn, or contradictory actions.
4. Require an operator-grade bundle with env fingerprint, selected controller set, fallback activation counts, decision traces, and an explicit "do not compose" verdict when the matrix says a pair is unsafe.
5. Keep the conservative baseline exact: if the composition layer is disabled or evidence is missing, the runtime must fall back to today’s per-controller conservative behavior.

Proof / validation:
- Snapshot or golden coverage for the controller catalog and interference-matrix schema.
- At least one deterministic scenario showing stable composition between two controllers over a fixed evidence stream.
- An interference microbench with detailed logs for oscillation detection, fallback churn, and decision-rate mismatch.
- Clear evidence that downstream controller beads can depend on this harness instead of inventing private compatibility notes.

Success criteria:
- No new swarm-perf controller bead merges without a composition contract, interference artifact, and deterministic proof path.
- Operators can inspect one bundle and understand which controllers were active, why they did not fight each other, and which fallback path would win under uncertainty.

Notes:
- This bead should block controller-composition-sensitive work such as tail-risk admission, brownout policy, OTLP shedding integration, and explainable host profile planning.
- Math families intentionally in scope: queueing/tail decomposition for shared observables, control-theoretic timescale separation, and expected-loss decision/fallback accounting.
design: Make controller composition a first-class artifact before additional adaptive policies land. The design surface is a catalog plus interference matrix that records every controller's inputs, outputs, update cadence, fallback mode, shared telemetry reads, knob writes, and precedence rules, then feeds a deterministic replay harness that proves controller pairs do not oscillate or issue contradictory actions under fixed evidence streams.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests must cover controller-catalog parsing, matrix validation, forbidden-pair detection, precedence resolution, missing-evidence fallback, and timescale-separation rule checks. E2E/script coverage must replay at least one stable two-controller composition and one intentionally unsafe/oscillating composition with detailed logs for evidence ticks, controller decisions, decision-rate mismatch, fallback churn, rejected pairings, and final do-not-compose verdicts. Artifact output must include env fingerprint, active controller set, shared telemetry fields, knob writes, fallback activation counts, decision trace, and an operator-readable explanation of why the composition is safe or unsafe.

Keep the proof adversarial: at least one stable composition and one unsafe/oscillating composition must be represented, with detailed logs for evidence ticks, decision cadence, knob writes, fallback churn, rejected pairings, and final compose/do-not-compose verdict. Unit tests must exercise parser/schema validation, missing-field rejection, forbidden-pair detection, precedence resolution, stale evidence fallback, and timescale-separation rules.

title: [observability-ambient-time] observability/debt_runtime_integration.rs: thread::sleep blocks wall-clock in monitoring loop
description:
debt_runtime_integration.rs:310: The monitoring_loop() spawns a real OS thread that calls thread::sleep(check_interval) with wall-clock duration. When tests use lab-runtime's virtual time, this thread blocks on real wall-clock instead of advancing with virtual time, breaking replay determinism and potentially causing test timeouts.

The loop correctly uses replayable_system_time() for elapsed-time calculations (line 289), but then sleeps on wall-clock, creating a mismatch where virtual time advances but the background thread is blocked in real time. Under lab-time fast-forward, this breaks observability record determinism and can cause race conditions between wall-time blockage and virtual-time advancement.

Fix: Replace thread::sleep() with lab-runtime's virtual-time-aware sleep primitive, or gate start_monitoring() to require an active Cx with a virtual timer driver.

Default constructor wires Arc::new(std::thread::sleep) (production unchanged). New with_sleeper builder lets LabRuntime tests inject a virtual-time sleeper for deterministic replayable monitoring. 3 unit tests including direct virtual-time loop drive. title: Setup project structure (Cargo.toml, modules, lib.rs)
description:
# Setup Project Structure (Cargo.toml, modules, lib.rs)

## Purpose
Create the initial Cargo crate and a *minimal, Phase-0-aligned* module layout that supports deterministic implementation and testing.

This task must respect the repo’s constraints:
- **No unsafe code** (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`)
- **Cargo only** (no other package managers)
- **Minimal dependencies** (avoid rand/tracing/etc. unless justified)
- **No file proliferation**: create files when they carry real functionality, not just placeholders

## Recommended Phase 0 Layout (minimal but extensible)

```
asupersync/
├── Cargo.toml
├── rust-toolchain.toml              # if we choose to pin toolchain
├── src/
│   ├── lib.rs
│   ├── error.rs
│   ├── util/
│   │   ├── mod.rs
│   │   ├── det_rng.rs               # deterministic PRNG (no rand)
│   │   └── arena.rs                 # internal Arena<T> for records
│   ├── types/
│   │   ├── mod.rs
│   │   ├── id.rs                    # RegionId, TaskId, ObligationId, Time
│   │   ├── outcome.rs               # Outcome severity lattice
│   │   ├── cancel.rs                # CancelReason/CancelKind (+ strengthen)
│   │   ├── budget.rs                # Budget product semantics
│   │   └── policy.rs                # Policy (aggregation/escalation)
│   ├── record/
│   │   ├── mod.rs
│   │   ├── task.rs                  # TaskRecord
│   │   ├── region.rs                # RegionRecord
│   │   └── obligation.rs            # ObligationRecord + registry
│   ├── trace/
│   │   ├── mod.rs
│   │   ├── event.rs                 # TraceEvent / TraceData
│   │   ├── buffer.rs                # TraceBuffer (ring)
│   │   └── format.rs                # formatting for tests/debug
│   ├── runtime/
│   │   ├── mod.rs
│   │   ├── state.rs                 # Σ = {regions,tasks,obligations,now}
│   │   ├── scheduler.rs             # 3-lane scheduler
│   │   ├── waker.rs                 # Waker (std::task::Wake) + wake dedup (no unsafe)
│   │   └── timer.rs                 # timer heap
│   ├── cx/
│   │   ├── mod.rs
│   │   ├── cx.rs                    # Cx trait + impls
│   │   └── scope.rs                 # Scope API
│   ├── combinator/
│   │   ├── mod.rs
│   │   ├── join.rs
│   │   ├── race.rs
│   │   └── timeout.rs
│   └── lab/
│       ├── mod.rs
│       ├── config.rs                # LabConfig
│       ├── runtime.rs               # LabRuntime loop
│       └── replay.rs                # replay/diff helpers
└── tests/
    ├── unit/                        # module-level unit tests
    └── e2e/                         # scenario tests (deterministic)
```

Notes:
- We **do not** pre-create Phase 2–5 modules here. Those should be added when their beads are started.
- The `util/` modules are intentionally explicit so we do not “accidentally” introduce heavy dependencies.

## Cargo.toml (Phase 0 defaults)

Goals:
- keep dependencies minimal
- keep determinism
- keep lints strict

Suggested starting point:

```toml
[package]
name = "asupersync"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
license = "MIT"

[lib]
path = "src/lib.rs"

[dependencies]
# Phase 0: prefer std/core; avoid bringing in executors/runtimes.

[dev-dependencies]
proptest = "1.4"

[lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "forbid"
missing_docs = "warn"
unused = "warn"

[lints.clippy]
pedantic = "warn"
nursery = "warn"
module_name_repetitions = "allow"
must_use_candidate = "allow"
```

If we later want compile-fail tests (session types), add `trybuild` as a dev-dependency in the Phase 3 bead.

## lib.rs

```rust
#![forbid(unsafe_code)]
#![warn(missing_docs)]
#![warn(clippy::pedantic)]
#![warn(clippy::nursery)]

pub mod error;

pub mod util;
pub mod types;
pub mod record;
pub mod trace;
pub mod runtime;
pub mod cx;
pub mod combinator;
pub mod lab;

pub use types::{Budget, CancelKind, CancelReason, Outcome, Policy, RegionId, TaskId, ObligationId, Time};
pub use cx::{Cx, Scope};
pub use lab::{LabConfig, LabRuntime};
```

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo check --all-targets` passes.
2. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
3. `cargo fmt --check` passes.
4. `cargo test` runs (even if empty initially).

## Why This Is User-Friendly
- The module structure mirrors the runtime’s mental model (types → records → runtime → user API → lab).
- Determinism utilities are explicit and dependency-free.
- Tests have a clear home and are expected from day 1.
close_reason: Completed: Project structure set up with all modules, Cargo.toml configured, all quality gates pass (check, clippy, fmt, test)

title: write_atomic commits (rename + parent fsync) synchronously on the async worker; offloading needs an additive API (split from bi2462.118)
description:
## Split from bi2462.118 (SapphireHill, 2026-09-28; origin 97bbe192a)
bi2462.118's Fix listed "offload write_atomic's rename and fsync". 830071203 fixed the other part (restricted-authority Cx keeps blocking-pool placement for file I/O), but src/fs/path_ops.rs still runs StagedAtomicWrite::commit synchronously on the async worker: std::fs::rename plus a parent-directory sync_all, via write_atomic -> stage_write_atomic(..).await?.commit(). On a slow disk those two syscalls block the worker.
Why it was not changed in place: the docs promise that commit "performs a synchronous rename with no cancellation point", that "once this method begins, async cancellation cannot interleave with the target mutation", and that "If this future is dropped during staging, the target path remains unchanged; the target rename occurs synchronously only after staging returns". Moving the rename to the blocking pool inside write_atomic would let a caller drop the future while the rename still happens in the background. That changes documented, observable cancellation behavior (the v0.4.3 compatibility gate).
## Options (owner decision)
(a) Additive API: StagedAtomicWrite::commit_async(self) / write_atomic_offloaded(..). It runs rename + parent fsync on the blocking pool with "completes once started" semantics, documented explicitly (dropping the future does not undo or stop the rename). Keep write_atomic unchanged.
(b) Keep the synchronous commit and document the worker-blocking cost next to it.
Current in-repo callers: the trace journal only; grep write_atomic/stage_write_atomic before choosing.
## Tests for (a)
A slow-commit probe (FilesystemOperationProbe hooks exist under test-internals): while commit_async's rename is parked, another task on the same single worker makes progress. Dropping the future after the rename starts leaves the target replaced, with no temp-file leak. Dropping before it starts leaves the target unchanged.
close_reason: Implemented Option (a) additive API: StagedAtomicWrite::commit_async and write_atomic_offloaded run rename + parent fsync on the blocking pool with explicit completes-once-started cancellation semantics. Documented worker-blocking cost on synchronous commit/write_atomic. Added test-internals probe hooks and regression tests verifying that while commit_async's rename is parked on a single-worker runtime, other tasks make progress, dropping the future after rename starts completes replacement without temp-file leaks, and dropping before leaves target unchanged. Updated unsafe boundary ledger.

description:
Lib test combinator::stream_collect::scoped_tests::scoped_descendant_panic_is_not_hidden_by_successful_item is RED on main. It was added in 3a496f4ca (feat(stream): scoped terminals with complete subtree drain, no bead cited), and stream_collect.rs is unchanged since fa1a7fe1c.

Evidence (SapphireHill d0, 2026-10-07): an RCH A/B on ovh-a with -j 1 and --features test-internals --lib fails identically on origin fa1a7fe1c (lane LSabBase) and on the unrelated SV candidate ed3a89360 (LSabSv). It fails at src/combinator/stream_collect.rs:654:

The lab_test wrapper reports seed 376849. In the trace, the grandchild descendant (TaskId 3, RegionId 2) panics after its cleanup and completes Panicked. The nested region and the item's region close, but the scoped terminal's result is not that panic.

The commit cites no bead and landed without a compile path, so under land-then-heal the watchdog operator (SapphireHill d0) owns the heal. It is claimed here, and the fix repairs forward.
close_reason: Healed in 84d9c9f1b: nested-region panics reach the scoped terminal; the test passes on the gated tree (full lib 24630/0) and on the merged tip (122/0).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Healed in 84d9c9f1b (merge of the gated commit onto origin f1eeeca53; exact gated tree 902454f41 on d4291d488).

Root cause: the test had never passed (3a496f4ca was not compiled). A task's panic in a NESTED region was folded only into that region's own close outcome. Region close passed only finalizer cleanup outcomes to the parent, so the scoped terminal's receipt held Ok.

title: Epic: Scheduler Performance & Fairness Improvements
description:
# Epic: Scheduler Performance & Fairness Improvements

## Overview

Beyond critical bugs, the scheduler has several performance and fairness 
issues that impact throughput, latency, and predictability under load.

## Background & Context

The scheduler's performance characteristics directly impact:
- **Throughput**: Tasks processed per second
- **Latency**: Time from task ready to execution
- **Fairness**: Equal treatment of equal-priority tasks
- **Efficiency**: CPU cycles per task

## Performance Issues

1. **PriorityScheduler O(n) insert** (`priority.rs:27-43`)
   - Linear scan for insertion position
   - Degrades with large queues

2. **Imprecise wakeup strategy** (`three_lane.rs:127-134`)
   - Always wakes first parker
   - No load balancing consideration

3. **Try-lock contention in stealing** (`three_lane.rs:367`)
   - Multiple stealers contend on same lock
   - Wasted CPU cycles

## Fairness Issues

4. **RNG tie-breaking bias** (`priority.rs:27-70`)
   - Single RNG hint used for all decisions
   - Predictable, non-random selection

5. **Duplicate scheduling across queues** (`priority.rs:131-135`)
   - Task can be in both local and global queue
   - Potential double execution

6. **Only stealing from ready lane** (`three_lane.rs:354-387`)
   - Cancel/timed work not stolen
   - Uneven work distribution

## Performance Goals

- O(1) or O(log n) operations on hot path
- Minimal lock contention
- Efficient work distribution
- Predictable latency

## Success Criteria

- Benchmark suite for scheduler operations
- Throughput improvement measurable
- Latency distribution documented
- Fairness verified statistically
