title: [testing-fuzz] HTTP/3 QPACK cross-component integration edge cases
description:
**Target function**: src/http/h3_native.rs QPACK decoding integrated with QUIC stream management and HTTP/3 frame processing

**Problem**: Individual components (QPACK decoder, QUIC streams, HTTP/3 framing) are well-fuzzed in isolation, but their integration creates complex interaction bugs. HTTP/3 QPACK decoding depends on multiple QUIC streams with ordering dependencies that can trigger race conditions or state inconsistencies when streams arrive out-of-order or with malformed interactions.

**Input shape**: Multi-stream HTTP/3 message sequences with:
- QPACK decoder stream with dynamic table updates out-of-order with header blocks
- HTTP/3 request streams with QPACK-compressed headers referencing not-yet-inserted dynamic entries
- QUIC stream flow control edge cases affecting QPACK stream processing
- HTTP/3 frame boundaries that split QPACK header blocks across frames
- Concurrent QPACK encoder/decoder stream updates with conflicting table modifications
- HTTP/3 goaway/reset interactions with pending QPACK decoder state

**Bugs to look for**:
- QPACK decoder state corruption from out-of-order stream delivery
- Use-after-free in QPACK dynamic table during concurrent stream processing
- HTTP/3 frame parser state confusion when QPACK decoding fails mid-stream
- Deadlock in QPACK stream dependencies under flow control backpressure
- Memory exhaustion from unbounded QPACK decoder state accumulation
- Header injection via QPACK decoder stream manipulation

**Implementation**: Multi-stream stateful fuzzer that coordinates QUIC stream delivery timing, HTTP/3 frame boundaries, and QPACK stream interactions to exercise cross-component edge cases that individual fuzzers miss.

**Success criteria**: Find integration bugs, state corruption, or security issues arising from complex interactions between HTTP/3, QUIC, and QPACK components under adversarial stream ordering and timing.
close_reason: done

title: Add conformance/src/tests/obligation_no_leak.rs for cancelled permit reclamation
description:
## Problem
The reusable `conformance/` crate only has proxy obligation checks in `conformance/src/tests/outcome.rs` that assert channel close or oneshot failure. It does not prove the no-leak invariant for cancelled blocked operations, so a runtime could leak channel permits or phantom capacity and still pass.

## Proposed Test File
- `conformance/src/tests/obligation_no_leak.rs`

## Expected Assertions
- Cancelling a blocked bounded-channel send does not consume capacity permanently.
- After the cancellation path drains, a later send can reuse the reclaimed permit and deliver exactly once.
- Cancelled senders do not create phantom messages or duplicate delivery.
- Receiver-side abort/close paths leave the channel in a reusable or cleanly closed state with no stuck waiters.

## Notes
This suite should be implementable against the current `RuntimeInterface` using bounded MPSC channels, timeout, and observable follow-on sends.
close_reason: Added conformance/src/tests/obligation_no_leak.rs and registered suite

title: Phase 0: Scaffolding & Core Utilities
description:
# Phase 0: Scaffolding & Core Utilities

## Purpose
Establish the *non-negotiable* foundations that every other Phase 0 component will build on:

- A clean crate/module layout and lint configuration
- Deterministic, dependency-minimal utilities that preserve the lab runtime’s determinism
- Internal data-structure utilities (arenas/queues/small collections) needed to implement the kernel without pulling in large crates or ambient globals

This feature exists to keep the core runtime implementation **small, deterministic, and dependency-disciplined**.

## Why This Needs Its Own Feature
The design documents repeatedly demand:
- **Determinism** (lab runtime, replay)
- **No ambient authority** (no hidden globals)
- **Minimal dependencies** (avoid pulling in large ecosystems)
- **Hot-path performance** (avoid unnecessary allocations)

These are easiest to satisfy when we explicitly plan and implement “supporting utilities” *before* we write the scheduler and state machine.

## Scope (What This Feature Covers)
### 1) Crate scaffolding
- Cargo workspace + `src/` module layout that mirrors runtime concepts (ids, outcomes, budgets, records, scheduler, trace, lab)
- Strict lints: `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, clippy pedantic/nursery as configured by project policy
- A project structure that makes it hard to accidentally introduce ambient globals or side-effectful logging

### 2) Deterministic PRNG (lab-only)
We need deterministic tie-breaking (e.g., choosing among runnable tasks) and deterministic jitter (e.g., backoff). We **must not** rely on OS entropy or global RNG.

Plan-of-record:
- Implement a tiny internal PRNG (e.g., `SplitMix64`/`XorShift`-class) with:
  - explicit seed in `LabConfig`
  - reproducible `next_u64()` and `gen_range(n)`
  - no external dependencies

### 3) Internal arenas / IDs / small collections helpers
The kernel needs “arenas” for `RegionRecord`, `TaskRecord`, `ObligationRecord` and stable IDs.

Plan-of-record:
- Implement an internal `Arena<T>` backed by `Vec<Option<T>>` (or equivalent) that provides:
  - `insert -> Id`
  - `get/get_mut`
  - `remove` (only when safe; e.g., after close/quiescence or for tests)
  - deterministic iteration order when needed (or explicit “order is unspecified”)
- Avoid pulling `slab`/`slotmap` unless we can justify it under the dependency policy.

### 4) Test-only helpers
- Minimal helpers to run deterministic tests and print/format traces **only inside tests**.

## Non-Goals
- Implementing the runtime itself (scheduler, cancellation, region close) — those are separate features.
- Adding any new executor runtime dependency (tokio/async-std/etc.)

## Acceptance Criteria
- We can build an empty crate and pass the quality gates:
  - `cargo check --all-targets`
  - `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo fmt --check`
- Deterministic PRNG utility exists and is used anywhere “randomness” is required.
- Arena utility exists and is used for runtime records (no ad-hoc `Vec` indexing scattered everywhere).
- No external dependency is introduced without explicit justification.

## Testing Strategy
- Unit tests for PRNG determinism: same seed => identical sequence.
- Unit tests for arena safety: insert/get/remove invariants, ID reuse policy documented and tested.
close_reason: All acceptance criteria met: quality gates pass, deterministic PRNG (det_rng.rs) and Arena utilities (arena.rs) implemented with tests, no external dependencies added.

title: [swarm-perf][topology] Add stable topology fixture and replay-hash helper
description:
Background:
- asupersync-wk0ciq is currently too broad for a single <60m ship slice even though the topology replay lane is clearly high-EV for NUMA/locality work.
- The existing scheduler evidence artifact already defines a compact topology descriptor (`SchedulerTopologyDescriptor`), so the first slice should reuse that instead of inventing another parallel schema.
- We need a deterministic, test-only helper that can build topology fixtures, replay steal-heavy traces, and emit a stable hash before locality-aware scheduler behavior beads land.

Candidate surfaces:
- src/runtime/scheduler/mod.rs
- src/runtime/scheduler/ test-only topology helper module
- one focused scheduler topology replay test

Required design:
1. Reuse `SchedulerTopologyDescriptor` as the canonical host/cohort shape for the helper API.
2. Add a test-only topology fixture builder for worker->cohort placement and deterministic task seeding.
3. Add a stable replay-hash output so repeated runs of the same fixture prove determinism.
4. Keep the helper scheduler-focused but generic enough for later blocking-pool topology tests to consume.

Proof / validation:
- Unit/integration coverage for fixture building and stable replay hash across reruns.
- At least one explicit assertion over locality/spill labeling in the replay trace.

Success criteria:
- Follow-on topology beads can depend on one reusable deterministic fixture/replay helper instead of inventing ad hoc host-shape scaffolding.
design: Use the existing SchedulerTopologyDescriptor as the canonical topology shape and keep this bead to the first deterministic helper slice only: fixture construction, stable replay hashing, local/remote spill labeling, and reusable support code that later scheduler and blocking-pool topology beads can consume. Do not broaden this into NUMA scheduling policy or blocking-pool affinity behavior; those remain downstream beads.
acceptance_criteria: Unit coverage must verify fixture construction, worker-to-cohort placement, stable hash determinism across reruns, and edge cases such as empty cohorts, single-worker cohorts, repeated task seeds, and remote-spill classification. The e2e/integration proof must run the scheduler_topology_replay test or equivalent script with detailed --nocapture/log output showing the fixture inputs, replay hash, locality labels, local steals, remote steals, and spill counts. Completion requires safe ownership/adoption of the current helper artifacts, a green rustfmt check, a green cargo check for the integration test target, and an actual runtime test proof once asupersync-wfbfg3 clears the shared lib-test blockers.

title: [idea-wizard][proof-citation] Hard proof-citation ledger for shared-main swarms
description:
Idea-wizard Phase 5 operationalization.

Background:
Asupersync now has proof-lane planner contracts and proof-artifact freshness receipts, but shared-main swarm closeouts still depend on operators manually interpreting green logs. The next sophistication step is a hard proof-citation layer: every closeout-ready green claim should be machine-checkable for current HEAD, main branch, touched surface, command provenance, proof status, RCH routing, target-dir/source freshness where relevant, and dirty-peer overlap. This makes large multi-agent swarms faster and safer because agents can cite proof artifacts without re-litigating whether the evidence is stale, local-only, failed, or accidentally unrelated.

Goals:
- Convert common proof-citation false positives into deterministic classifier failures.
- Keep each rule narrow, explainable, and backed by fixtures/contracts.
- Preserve existing focused proof lanes; do not make broad release claims from narrow tests.
- Make future Agent Mail closeouts cite a receipt classification instead of prose-only judgment.

Non-goals:
- Do not replace the existing proof-lane planner or manifest artifacts.
- Do not touch active fuzz gate work owned by asupersync-z4nu2u.
- Do not require live network services or ambient global state.

Completion shape:
This epic is complete when the child beads pin the most important proof-citation false positives and the helper has deterministic fixtures/tests for each rule.

title: Barrier detached cancellation does not wake parked waiter
description: src/sync/barrier.rs BarrierWaitFuture checks Cx::checkpoint() only when polled and stores the task Waker solely in barrier.state.waiters; it never registers with Cx::register_cancel_waker. Cx::detached_cancel_context() starts with cancel_waker=None, while cancel_fast/cancel_with/set_cancel_requested wake only the optional Cx cancellation slot. Therefore a waiter on Barrier::new(2) can poll Pending, have its detached/custom-executor Cx cancelled, and remain parked indefinitely until another party trips the barrier or an unrelated wake repolls it. Managed runtime tasks often mask this with a scheduler-installed baseline cancellation Waker, but detached_cancel_context is an explicitly documented supported adapter/CLI surface. Fix with one balanced per-future cancellation-Waker registration that updates only when the task Waker changes, clears on every Ready/Drop/replacement path, and performs a post-registration cancellation recheck to close the checkpoint-to-registration lost-wake window without disturbing trip-vs-cancel precedence or generation/accounting. Deterministic acceptance: poll Barrier(2) once with detached_cancel_context and a counting Waker, call cancel_fast(User), require an immediate wake and then Cancelled on repoll with exact arrived/waiter/cancellation cleanup; cover cancellation during initial registration, changed task Waker balance, normal trip cleanup, and future Drop cleanup. Async conversion commit 1079a501f removed the prior timed Condvar repoll; git history has never registered a cancel Waker in barrier.rs. Independently confirmed by two source reviews on 2026-07-15; no matching tracker bead exists, and trip/cancel precedence plus waiter-removal beads are distinct.

title: Barrier trip can strand peers when one waker panics
description: src/sync/barrier.rs commits a generation and drains all waiters, then calls each Waker::wake before marking the leader future Done. A safe Wake implementation may panic: the loop aborts, remaining waiters are dropped without notification and can remain parked forever despite generation advancement, while a caught-and-repolled leader is still Init and can incorrectly enter the next generation. After detaching under lock, mark the leader Done before callbacks; contain each wake panic long enough to notify every detached waiter, then resume the first panic. Deterministic regression: register a first panicking waker and second counting waker, trip with a third arrival under catch_unwind, require the counter wake, committed generation, and PolledAfterCompletion on leader repoll. Confirmed during two read-only reviews of asupersync-barrier-waker-drop-under-lock-mk1s3g on 2026-07-15; the current trip path only solved wake-under-lock and no matching bead exists.
close_reason: Fixed in a7bea22af: trip wake loop contains each Waker::wake panic (catch_unwind), notifies every detached peer, resumes the first panic after all are woken. Leader already Done pre-loop (PolledAfterCompletion on repoll). Regression trip_notifies_all_peers_despite_wake_panic_then_resumes. sync::barrier 50/50 pass.

title: Barrier destroys stored wakers while holding state mutex
description: src/sync/barrier.rs cancellation removal, future-drop swap_remove, and changed-waker clone_from can destroy the last stored Waker while BarrierState parking_lot mutex is held. A safe Waker::from(Arc<impl Wake>) payload Drop can re-enter a public barrier method and self-deadlock; clone_from also clones/replaces under the guard. Trip correctly drains and wakes outside. Move removed/replaced wakers out under lock, commit cancellation completion, unlock, then drop them; clone incoming wakers before acquiring the barrier mutex so allocation/unwind cannot drop user wakers under lock. Add deterministic DropProbe tests for pending-future drop, cancellation re-poll, and changed-waker re-poll that assert barrier.state.try_lock succeeds during payload destruction and state accounting remains exact. Independently confirmed by two read-only fresh-eye reviews 2026-07-15; prior 5cb48b40c moved only trip wake calls outside lock and existing tests use inert wakers.

title: Implement first_ok combinator for fallback chains
description:
## Purpose
The first_ok combinator tries a sequence of operations, returning the first Ok result. If all operations fail, returns an aggregated error. This is essential for fallback chains, service discovery, and graceful degradation.

## Distinction from race
- **race**: Run all concurrently, first to complete wins (regardless of success/failure)
- **first_ok**: Run sequentially or with controlled concurrency, first SUCCESS wins

For Phase 0 (single-threaded), implement sequential first_ok. Concurrent variants in Phase 1.

## Semantic Model

```rust
pub async fn first_ok<T, E>(
    cx: &mut Cx<'_>,
    operations: Vec<impl Fn(&mut Cx<'_>) -> impl Future<Output = Result<T, E>>>,
) -> Outcome<T, Vec<E>>  // Returns first Ok or all errors
```

### Behavior (Sequential)
1. For each operation in order:
   a. Execute operation
   b. If Ok: return immediately (short-circuit)
   c. If Err: collect error, continue to next
2. If all fail: return Err(collected_errors)
3. If cancelled at any point: return Cancelled

### Behavior (Concurrent - Phase 1)
1. Spawn all operations
2. As results arrive:
   a. If Ok: cancel remaining, drain them, return Ok
   b. If Err: collect, continue waiting
3. If all complete with Err: return aggregated errors

## Error Aggregation
Two options for error return:
1. `Vec<E>`: All errors in attempt order
2. `FirstOkError<E> { errors: Vec<E>, attempted: usize }`: With metadata

The simple `Vec<E>` is preferred for Phase 0.

## Cancellation Handling
- Check cancellation before each attempt
- If cancelled: return Cancelled with errors collected so far
- Do not start new attempts after cancellation

## Use Cases
1. **Service fallback**: Primary → Secondary → Tertiary endpoint
2. **Configuration sources**: File → Environment → Defaults
3. **Parser fallback**: Try parsers in preference order
4. **Cache hierarchy**: L1 → L2 → L3 → Origin

## Invariant Support
- **Short-circuit**: First success returns immediately
- **Complete error context**: All failures preserved for debugging
- **Cancel-correctness**: Respects cancellation between attempts

## Testing Requirements
1. First operation succeeds (no fallback needed)
2. Middle operation succeeds (some fallbacks tried)
3. All operations fail (error aggregation)
4. Cancellation at various points
5. Empty operations list (edge case)
6. Single operation (degenerate case)

## Example Usage

```rust
// Try multiple DNS resolvers
let addr = scope.first_ok(cx, vec\![
    |cx| async move { resolve_dns(cx, "8.8.8.8", domain).await },
    |cx| async move { resolve_dns(cx, "1.1.1.1", domain).await },
    |cx| async move { resolve_dns(cx, "9.9.9.9", domain).await },
]).await?;

// Try config sources
let config = scope.first_ok(cx, vec\![
    |cx| async move { load_config_file(cx, "/etc/app/config.toml").await },
    |cx| async move { load_config_env(cx).await },
    |cx| async move { Ok(Config::default()) },  // Always succeeds as final fallback
]).await?;
```

## References
- asupersync_plan_v4.md: §5.7 Derived Combinators
- Railway-oriented programming
- Option::or_else chains in Rust
- asupersync_v4_formal_semantics.md: §3.2 Error handling

## Acceptance Criteria
- Returns the first `Ok` result if any branch succeeds; otherwise returns aggregated failure information.
- All losing/failed branches are cancelled and drained before returning.
- Deterministic behavior in lab runs with explicit tie-breaking.
- E2E tests cover cancellation + loser draining and interaction with policies.
close_reason: first_ok combinator implemented with sequential fallback semantics, error collection, cancellation handling, and comprehensive tests. All tests pass.

title: Design structured concurrency span model
description:
Design OpenTelemetry span creation and context propagation for structured concurrency.

## Requirements
- Span creation at region boundaries (create/close/cancel)
- Task span creation with proper parent/child relationships  
- Context propagation through structured concurrency scopes
- Efficient span storage without affecting runtime performance
- Integration with existing Cx (context) infrastructure

## Span Types to Define
- Region spans: lifecycle from creation to quiescence
- Task spans: execution from spawn to completion/cancellation
- Operation spans: IO/timer/channel operations with cancel semantics
- Cancel spans: cancellation propagation events and drain operations

## Context Propagation Strategy  
- Leverage existing Cx context passing for span context
- Automatic span parent/child relationships through region hierarchy
- Span correlation across async boundaries
- Proper span closing on cancellation vs normal completion

## Performance Considerations
- Lazy span creation to minimize overhead
- Configurable sampling rates for different span types
- Efficient span storage during async operation execution
- Minimal allocation overhead in span creation paths

## Integration Design
- Hook into existing region creation/destruction
- Integrate with task spawn/completion infrastructure
- Add span context to Cx capabilities
- Leverage existing structured concurrency guarantees
close_reason: Designed comprehensive structured concurrency span model with automatic span creation at region/task/operation boundaries, perfect hierarchical relationships, context propagation through Cx, lazy materialization for performance, and rich structured concurrency semantics. Created detailed design document at docs/structured_concurrency_span_model.md covering span types, lifecycle management, context inheritance, and runtime integration.

title: Design Contract: Advanced Mathematical Lenses (tracking)
description:
# Design Contract: Advanced Mathematical Lenses (Tracking)

## Purpose
The design documents include several advanced mathematical lenses that are part of the long-term contract. Phase 0 does not need to implement them explicitly, but **must not preclude them**.

This feature tracks those lenses as explicit “don’t break this later” constraints and, where useful, as concrete experiments.

## Lenses to Track
- Event structures / HDA / directed topology (tracked separately in Phase 5+)
- Quantitative/graded types (tracked separately in Phase 5+)
- Polynomial functors for compositional dynamics
- Dialectica view of two-phase effects (forward value + backward obligation)
- Guarded recursion for actors/leases
- Cancellation as a quantitative game (already partially encoded via bounded mask/checkpoint budgets)
- Lyapunov-guided scheduling governor (optional)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each lens has:
  - a concise statement of “what it would buy us”
  - a concrete preservation constraint on the runtime semantics
  - a test/tooling hook where applicable

title: Phase 1: Work-Stealing Scheduler
description:
# Phase 1: Work-Stealing Scheduler

## Purpose
Extend Phase 0’s single-thread scheduler to a parallel work-stealing scheduler while preserving all invariants and retaining deterministic lab behavior.

## Core Requirements
- Per-worker local queues (fast path)
- Steal protocol for load balancing
- Global injection queue for external wakes/spawns
- Wake dedup across threads
- Cancel lane priority must remain semantically dominant

## Determinism Constraint
Even if production scheduling is nondeterministic, the lab runtime must be able to:
- simulate multi-worker scheduling deterministically
- replay schedules

This implies the scheduler must expose a “virtual schedule” control surface in lab mode.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Parallel execution preserves:
  - region close ⇒ quiescence
  - cancellation protocol drains
  - losers drained
  - no obligation leaks
- No task can be orphaned due to migration.

## Testing
- Parallel stress tests with deterministic seed.
- Schedule replay tests.
- Work-stealing invariants tests (no lost tasks, no duplicate polls, no starvation).

title: [bug-hunt][P1] channel/broadcast.rs: Sender::reserve checks cx.checkpoint() but only TRACES the cancel — returns Ok permit when cx is cancelled (Pass 3 violation)
description:
src/channel/broadcast.rs:190-200. reserve() body:

  if cx.checkpoint().is_err() { cx.trace(...) }   // observed but ignored
  if receiver_count == 0 { return Err(Closed) }
  Ok(SendPermit { sender: self })

The cancel-mid-reserve invariant the user explicitly listed in Pass 3 is violated — caller gets a usable SendPermit even when their Cx is cancelled, and the subsequent permit.send() will succeed silently, delivering messages that the caller wanted aborted. Compare partition.rs:339 where the same checkpoint pattern returns SendError::Cancelled(value) — broadcast should follow the same convention. Fix is non-trivial because broadcast::SendError has only Closed(T) — no Cancelled variant — so a proper fix needs either: (a) add SendError::Cancelled(T) and audit all match arms (breaking change for callers that match exhaustively), or (b) reuse Closed (semantically wrong — Closed means 'no receivers'). Suggested: option (a) with a non-exhaustive enum + clippy::manual_non_exhaustive guidance for callers.
close_reason: Sender::reserve now returns SendError::Cancelled when cx.checkpoint() detects cancellation (was: trace-and-fall-through to grant permit anyway). Sender::send propagates the new variant. 2 regression tests cover API contract + receiver-sees-no-message invariant.

title: Property-fuzz for trace file parsing edge cases: truncation, version mismatch, magic-prefix mutations
description: fuzz/fuzz_targets/trace_file_parsing.rs is a random-bytes fuzz that mostly hits early-rejection paths (wrong magic, too-short input). It does NOT systematically cover: (1) valid header followed by truncation at every byte offset, (2) header with version != TRACE_FILE_VERSION (currently 2) — every other version code from 0..u16::MAX, (3) header with valid magic + invalid flag bits, (4) valid metadata length but truncated metadata bytes, (5) valid event count but truncated event payload. Add tests/trace_file_parsing_property_fuzz.rs that proptest-generates a known-good trace prefix (magic + version + flags) then applies one of {truncate-at-offset-N, flip-version-to-X, mutate-flag-byte} and asserts (a) the parser either Ok(reader) or Err(io::Error) — never panics, never hangs, never returns Ok with a corrupted state, (b) version-mismatch always Err, (c) truncation at any offset before HEADER_SIZE always Err.
close_reason: Trace file parser property-fuzz landed in fade11bc7 (other agent's commit swept up my tests/trace_file_parsing_property_fuzz.rs from working tree). Four proptests complement fuzz/fuzz_targets/trace_file_parsing.rs by feeding valid header prefixes + targeted mutations: truncation_below_header_size_always_errors (every offset 0..HEADER_SIZE rejects), future_version_always_errors ((TRACE_FILE_VERSION+1)..u16::MAX → Err::UnsupportedVersion), corrupted_magic_always_errors (every magic bit-flip → Err::InvalidMagic), random_flag_bits_never_panic (panic-freedom only — unknown flags may be forward-compat). 64 cases × 4 properties ≈ 256 mutated headers per run. cargo check --test trace_file_parsing_property_fuzz clean. Uses tempfile + TraceReader::open since TraceReader has no from_reader constructor (the existing libfuzzer target's reference to from_reader is broken — separate bug worth filing if not already known).

title: [AUDIT] Deep correctness audit: cx/registry.rs
notes:

Module: src/cx/registry.rs (3,414 lines: 1,195 production + 2,219 tests)

title: ATP-C: Model verified object graphs, manifests, Merkle roots, chunking, and proof bundles
description: The core abstraction is not a file. ATP moves verified object graphs: files, directories, streams, snapshots, datasets, sparse images, CI artifacts, container layers, model bundles, and application-defined objects. This workstream defines the content-addressed graph and proof model that makes the rest of ATP reusable.
design: A manifest must describe object identity, metadata, chunk plan, hash algorithms, optional compression/encryption policy, RaptorQ repair groups, and final commit semantics. Canonical encoding matters because TransferId, proof bundles, dedupe, resume, and cross-peer verification depend on stable bytes.
acceptance_criteria:
- ObjectGraph supports FileObject, DirectoryObject, StreamObject, SnapshotObject, DatasetObject, ArtifactBundle, SparseImage, ContainerLayer, and application-defined extensions.
- Manifest encoding is canonical and versioned.
- Merkle roots prove object and graph completion.
- Chunking profiles include bulk fixed-size and sync-friendly content-defined modes.
- Proof bundles record manifest root, object roots, chunk bitmap, repair groups, final commit, peer identity, path summary, journal digest, and replay pointers.
notes: This workstream should produce reusable data structures for backups, artifacts, distributed snapshots, and future Asupersync logistics.

title: [idea-wizard-wave4] SLO to Budget policy compiler and proof loop
description:
Background:
The incident replay refinery closed the operator-facing path from field artifact to proof report. The next highest-leverage gap is turning operator service goals into deterministic runtime policy: latency/error/resource SLOs should compile into Budget values, cleanup deadlines, admission and brownout decisions, fallback/no-win receipts, and exact rch-verifiable evidence. Existing code has Budget types, capacity planners, admission/brownout proof runners, and no-win diagnostics, but they remain hand-assembled proof lanes rather than one stable operator contract.

Idea-wizard rationale:
- Phase 2 top idea after incident refinery: SLO to Budget policy compiler.
- Phase 3 complement: operator no-win decision atlas and proof-lane command routing.
- Why this is accretive: users running massive agent swarms need a concrete way to say "p99 queue wait <= X", "cleanup within Y", "brown out optional work before violating Z", and get deterministic asupersync policy plus proof artifacts instead of bespoke scripts.

Non-goals:
- Do not add a new runtime, scheduler, or host-global stress harness.
- Do not replace existing Budget/admission/capacity artifacts; compile into them and reuse their proof vocabulary.
- Do not make broad README claims until executable or dry-run proof artifacts exist.

Implementation expectations:
- Include latency objectives (p50/p95/p99/p999), cleanup deadlines, max queue wait, memory/FD/timer pressure thresholds, optional work classes, brownout priorities, and no-win fallback declarations.

- Preserve provenance: profile id, workload class, target commit, feature flags, and related bead.
- Keep the artifact deterministic and JSON/JSONL friendly.

Required tests and proof:

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
SapphireHill 2026-09-02 17:0x ET — INFRA HAZARD that affects every lane cited on this epic (and on rounds 1-5): the rch worker checkout (/data/projects/asupersync on hz3/hz4/ovh-a) is one directory shared by all agents and is a plain rsync target (not a git repo); the sync does not replace a worker file whose mtime is newer than the local copy. Concretely, tests/e2e_web.rs on hz3 lacked my 12:29 fix, carried a peer's 15:05 mtime, and my 16:39 sync left it in place, so the E1 lane re-reported eight lints that were fixed and committed at 13:50. The same mechanism explains today's "stale" K=10000 binary and the ambient snapshot that would not update.

Rule for every lane from now on (added to the epic description's RULES): before launching, `git diff --name-only <base>..HEAD | xargs touch; git status --short | awk '{print $2}' | xargs touch`, then probe the worker (`ssh <worker> 'bash -s' < probe.sh` grepping for a marker of your change) before trusting a result. E1 was cancelled and relaunched on the bumped tree; the G1/I2/B1 lanes touch only files edited in the last hour (mtimes newer than any peer sync seen), so their results stand, but their receipts will name the probe.

The proper fix belongs to the rch project (per-agent worker checkouts, or a sync that compares content instead of mtime); filed as a note here because this repo cannot change it.

title: QUIC WAN A1: reproduce the high-RTT window limit in a netem 'wan' regime (90 ms, 0 % loss, 300 Mbit)
description:
WHY: On 2026-09-02 the first cross-machine ATP-over-QUIC/TLS1.3 receipt (artifacts/atp_bench_matrix/wan_quic_receipt_2026-09-02.md) moved 256 MiB Hetzner Ashburn -> Contabo France (96 ms RTT) in 42.90 s = 6.26 MB/s, and Contabo NY -> France (88 ms) in 100.86 s = 2.66 MB/s, while the same binary over plain TCP did 19.9-22.9 MB/s on the same paths. bytes_in_flight ~= throughput x RTT ~= 0.25-0.6 MB, i.e. the sender is window-limited on high-RTT paths. The netem matrix (2 ms "perfect", 80 ms +-20 ms 2 % loss 50 Mbit "bad") cannot show this: at 2 ms the window is irrelevant and at 50 Mbit the link caps first (50M/bad: atp 13.96 s vs rsync 17.35 s, both link-bound). The README's ATP promise ("beats rsync") is only true on lossy links today; this is the biggest remaining gap in the encrypted tier.

WHAT: add a `wan` regime to scripts/atp_bench/matrix_bench.sh / run_matrix_cell.sh: delay 45 ms +-2 ms each way (90 ms RTT), 0 % loss, rate 300 Mbit, netem limit sized for the BDP (>= 90 ms x 300 Mbit / 1200 B ~= 28k packets; see the existing "BDP ~33k pkts" comment in run_matrix_cell.sh ~441). Run the encrypted 50M and 500M cells with reps 3 on ovh-a (idle, sudo, OpenSSL 3.5 -> the CA:FALSE certificate fix from 5f03c9f9e is required) and record: atp-quic-tls13 vs rsync-ssh-aes128gcm vs (new, non-scored) atp-tcp so the limiter is isolated from the path.

HOW: `sudo env BIN=/tmp/atp_bench/atp ATP_MATRIX_TIMEOUT=300 bash scripts/atp_bench/matrix_bench.sh --execute --generate-workloads --out /tmp/atp_bench/<run> --workloads 50M,500M --regimes wan --tiers encrypted --reps 3 --run-cell-command 'bash scripts/atp_bench/run_matrix_cell.sh'`; then score_matrix.py. Memory rules: never two cells at once on one host (same netns IPs), clear-check pgrep/netns first, delete only atp netns on cleanup. Keep --out outside the checkout (rch sync deletes untracked files).

title: Distributed C1: bounded Cx-aware authenticated snapshot transfer and two-process recovery
description:
CURRENT GOVERNING SCOPE — 2026-09-04. distribution.rs:193-254 serially awaits replicas and ignores ack_timeout/max_concurrent/hedge controls; its send-only transport trait lacks Cx and only test-double implementation exists. Adding SnapshotSymbols to strict V3 is NOT authorized. Preserve V1-V3 enum/public/wire bytes, unknown-field rejection and consumer traits. Use an additive bounded Cx-aware interface and a versioned registered computation inside the existing native mTLS boundary; if inadequate, design a deliberately negotiated new protocol while retaining old peers. Do not silently add required trait methods or wire fields.

Implement actual remote symbols/metadata, authenticated correlation of object digest, replica, transfer attempt and decode/recovery acknowledgement. Distinguish queued bytes, accepted symbols and independently verified recovered snapshot. Honor deadlines, byte/symbol limits, total concurrent attempts and hedging; cancel/drain losers and parent-owned work after quorum/error/cancel. An accepted connection withholding ack must not indefinitely block healthy replicas.

Native two-process acceptance: recover a real 4MiB snapshot byte-for-byte over TCP+mTLS after a specified recoverable symbol loss; derive source/repair counts so the pattern is actually decodable. Wrong certificate/grant/object/digest/attempt, corrupt symbols, stale/duplicate ack and withheld ack cannot satisfy quorum. Cancel after observed in-flight state, then prove deadline/cleanup and a subsequent healthy transfer. With three controlled slow peers and cap=2, instrument peak active attempts <=2; hedge includes its attempts in that cap and drains its loser. Source/public-trait fixtures and unchanged V1-V3 goldens plus terminal native RCH evidence are required. No consensus, remote exactly-once, arbitrary closure, durability or WAN-performance claim. C3 waits for this proof. This governs over conflicting protocol or serial-control assumptions in the retained original context.

HISTORICAL ORIGINAL CONTEXT (preserved for provenance; the current governing scope above supersedes conflicting instructions):

WHY: src/distributed/distribution.rs `SymbolDistributor::distribute` calls `DistributorTransport::send_symbols`, whose only implementation is the `#[cfg(test)]` `MockSuccessTransport`; nothing in the crate can move RaptorQ snapshot symbols between two processes, although the README (until 2026-09-01) advertised RaptorQ snapshot distribution. The V3 remote transport (src/remote.rs: RemoteTransport over TCP + mTLS, MessageEnvelope, RemotePeerHello, admission policy, proven by tests/remote_transport_lifecycle_contract.rs) is the natural carrier: authenticated, framed, already region-aware.

WHAT: `RemoteDistributorTransport` in src/distributed/distribution.rs implementing `DistributorTransport` over `RemoteTransport`: a new `RemoteMessage::SnapshotSymbols { snapshot_id, sbn, esi_range, payload }` variant (additive; unknown-variant rejection tests in remote.rs must be extended — grep `assert_remote_unknown_field_rejected`), bounded in-flight bytes per peer (backpressure through the existing envelope credit or an explicit window), per-peer delivery receipts feeding `SymbolDistributor`'s existing success/failure accounting, and cancellation through the calling `Cx` (no orphaned sends). Receiver side: a `SnapshotSymbolSink` registered on the RemoteRuntime that hands symbols to the RaptorQ decoder (src/raptorq/decoder.rs InactivationDecoder via the pipeline) and reports decode completion.

TESTS: unit tests with an in-memory RemoteTransport pair (already used in remote.rs tests) for framing, backpressure, cancellation mid-transfer (no leak: obligations resolved, region quiescent); a TWO-PROCESS e2e (tests/distributed_snapshot_two_process_e2e.rs) that spawns a child process running the receiver over loopback TCP+mTLS with test certs, distributes a 4 MiB snapshot with 20 % of symbols dropped by a fault-injecting transport wrapper, and asserts the child decodes the exact bytes (SHA-256 in the child's stdout receipt). Planted negative: corrupt one symbol -> decode fails or mismatched digest.

ACCEPTANCE: two-process e2e green through rch; unit tests green; no tokio; public API additive; PBFT untouched (already deprecated in round 3).

NO-CLAIM: no multi-donor bonding here (atp bond-pull exists separately); no SWIM (C2).
acceptance_criteria: Actual authenticated two-process transfer recovers the exact 4MiB snapshot under a declared recoverable loss pattern with explicit source/repair counts. Independently reject wrong identity/grant/object/digest/attempt, corrupt symbols and stale acknowledgements. A withheld acknowledgement obeys the configured deadline; actual concurrent attempts and hedge losers remain within the shared cap and are canceled/drained. Cancellation starts after an in-flight witness, leaves exact task/byte/lease accounting and permits healthy recovery. Unit and native process suites have terminal strict-remote nonzero positive counts. Preserve existing public traits and strict V1-V3 goldens; no new required trait method or wire variant, Tokio edge, consensus or WAN-performance claim. C3 follows this evidence; no gap-parent closure is a prerequisite for this child.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
C1 DESIGN NOTE (SapphireHill, 2026-09-02) — grounded in the code as it is today, so the implementer does not re-derive it.

Carrier facts:
- The "V3 TCP+mTLS remote transport" is a typed request/response RPC, not a stream: `RemoteComputationRegistry::register::<I, O, _, _>(name, |cx, invocation| async {...})` (remote.rs:2770; I/O must implement `HasSchema`), served by `RemoteComputationService::bind(addr, TlsAcceptor, RemotePeerAdmissionPolicy, registry, RemoteComputationServiceConfig)` (remote.rs:8947, feature `remote-service` + `tls`, unix), called by `RemoteComputationClient::call(cx, &RemoteServiceWireRequest)` (remote.rs:6168) with retries, cancellation through `Cx`, idempotency keys and `wire_limits.max_frame_bytes()` = 64 KiB by default (DEFAULT_REMOTE_SERVICE_MAX_FRAME_BYTES, remote.rs:2840; configurable).
- `DistributorTransport::send_symbols(&self, replica_id, Vec<AuthenticatedSymbol>) -> Future<Result<ReplicaAck, ReplicaFailure>>` (distribution.rs:25) is the only seam `SymbolDistributor::distribute` uses; the only impl is the `#[cfg(test)]` MockSuccessTransport (distribution.rs:500). `AuthenticatedSymbol { symbol: Symbol, tag: AuthenticationTag, verified }` (security/authenticated.rs:16) is NOT serde-serializable; a wire form is needed.
- Test material already exists: `remote_client_test_mtls_pair() -> (TlsAcceptor, TlsConnector)` and the cross-process template `remote_service_cli_hosts_mtls_v3_and_drains_cross_process` (tests/remote_transport_lifecycle_contract.rs:4610 / :3499), plus `tests/tls_conformance.rs generated_mtls_material()`.

Design (additive, no tokio, no PBFT):
1. Wire types in src/distributed/distribution.rs (serde + HasSchema): `SnapshotSymbolBatch { snapshot_id: [u8;32] hex, sbn: u8, symbols: Vec<WireSymbol { esi: u32, data: Bytes-as-base64-or-raw-vec, tag: [u8;32] }>, batch_index: u32, batches_total: u32 }` and `SnapshotSymbolReceipt { accepted: u32, rejected_tag: u32, decode_complete: bool, digest_sha256: Option<hex> }`. Keep each batch under `max_frame_bytes` minus envelope overhead (a `frame_budget` computed from the client's wire limits); a 4 MiB snapshot at 1400-byte symbols is ~3000 symbols = ~75 batches at the 64 KiB default (raise the limit in the e2e config to 1 MiB to keep the round-trips sane, and test the budget arithmetic at the default).
2. `RemoteDistributorTransport` (client side) holds a `RemoteComputationClient` per replica (replica_id -> client) and implements `DistributorTransport`: split -> serialize -> `call` per batch with the caller's `Cx` (cancellation propagates through `call`), bounded concurrency `max_in_flight_batches` per replica (backpressure), receipts folded into `ReplicaAck { symbols_received = sum(accepted), ack_time = cx clock }`; any transport error becomes `ReplicaFailure { error_kind }` after the client's own retries. No orphaned sends: batches are awaited inside the call; a cancelled `Cx` returns `Cancelled` and the receiver's decoder simply never completes (the receiver has an idle timeout per snapshot_id).
3. Receiver side: `SnapshotSymbolSink::register(registry, sink_config)` registers the `distributed.snapshot_symbols` computation whose handler verifies each symbol tag against the configured `SecurityContext`, feeds the symbol into an `InactivationDecoder` kept per snapshot_id behind an `Arc<Mutex<BTreeMap<snapshot_id, DecoderState>>>` captured by the closure, and answers with the receipt; when the decoder completes it stores the bytes + SHA-256 and reports `decode_complete = true` on that and every later receipt. A bounded LRU of snapshot states plus an idle timeout keeps memory bounded.
4. Two-process e2e (tests/distributed_snapshot_two_process_e2e.rs): the parent spawns the test binary itself with an env marker as the child (same pattern as the CLI cross-process test), the child binds the service on 127.0.0.1:0 with the mTLS acceptor from `remote_client_test_mtls_pair`, prints its port, and on completion prints a JSON receipt line with the SHA-256 of the decoded bytes; the parent encodes a 4 MiB pseudo-random snapshot, wraps the transport in a fault-injecting `DistributorTransport` decorator that drops 20 % of symbols deterministically (seeded), distributes with `ConsistencyLevel::All`, and asserts the child's digest equals its own. Planted negative: flip one byte of one symbol's data after signing -> the receipt shows `rejected_tag >= 1`, and with too few surviving symbols the decode never completes (assert `decode_complete == false` and no digest). Unit tests (single process, in-memory `RemoteComputationClient` over loopback mTLS): batch budget arithmetic at the 64 KiB default, backpressure cap honoured, cancellation mid-transfer leaves the region quiescent.
5. Docs: README distributed section states exactly this (snapshot symbols over the V3 mTLS RPC; no SWIM until C2; no multi-donor bonding).

Estimate: 1.5-2 days of focused work; unblocked; nothing else in round 6 depends on it except C3.

comments.text:
SapphireHill: read-only review of 56e34d99d, 534a6cb7f, 93c71a14e, 76dab53d0 and 5d91be26c (authenticated erasure-striped checkpoints, recovery, chunked transfer) on origin 17f130960. No authentication, integrity or memory-bound defect: digests are checked before decode and tags on every symbol; the manifest MAC binds identity and peer; recovery requires exact region, origin, epoch and sequence; every length is checked before reserving; per-peer and global staging bounds hold; ranges append only at the exact offset. Availability findings:
1. Medium (verified): publication does not cap its fanout at the transport's in-flight limit. native/checkpoint/workflow.rs ~276 checks only `self.max_in_flight() == 0`, and prepare ~377 only `policy.max_concurrent == 0`, so the fanout fills max_concurrent slots. native/admission.rs Admission::acquire refuses (`if active >= self.limit { return Err(Admission) }`) instead of queuing, so excess sends fail immediately and count as replica failures. Trigger: new_bounded(.., 2) with max_concurrent 4, consistency All and 4 healthy replicas gives CheckpointError::Quorum. A concurrent recovery on a shared transport clone has the same effect. Every fixture uses equal limits (2/2, 4/4).
2. Low-Medium: the client never sends ABORT (0 uses under native/), so cancelled, expired or quorum-retired uploads keep their staging reservation until expiry. With max_uploads_per_peer=1 the next checkpoint to that replica fails with Limit("peer staged uploads") for the whole window. Upload ids come from the process-local RemoteTaskId::next(), so a restarted publisher can collide with its predecessor's stale stage (Conflict). tests/symbol_service_native.rs ~356 hides this by reaping by hand.
3. Low, design: quorum-first striped publication seals only the first decodable set, giving zero replica-loss tolerance (asserted at tests/symbol_checkpoint_striped_native.rs ~427).
4. Low, behaviour versus v0.4.3: encode now honours repair_overhead and rejects values below 1.0; v0.4.3 accepted 0.0. No in-tree caller is affected.
Test notes: all three integration suites and the native unit tests need tls,test-internals, so plain `cargo test` runs zero of them. There is no two-process test and no peak-concurrency <= 2 check with slow peers, both of which this bead's acceptance requires.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SapphireHill 2026-10-01: read-only review of 56e34d99d / 534a6cb7f / 93c71a14e on origin 232317201 (51a7c3ee6 the only later fix). NO authentication, integrity, quorum-arithmetic or memory-bound defect found (quorum counting, coverage decision, content-addressed keys and replay, chunk framing bounds and reservations, cancellation, API additivity all checked). F3 (abandoned uploads hold staging quota until TTL; attempt ids restart at 1) and F4 (on-quorum mode seals the first decodable set, so zero replica-loss tolerance) from 09-28 remain open. NEW:
F1 (medium, availability): stripes are placed round-robin in the caller's replica order (assignment.rs ~153) and the store keeps exactly one batch per (origin, object_id), rejecting different bytes (symbol_service.rs ~105-112). Retrying a failed striped publication of the same EncodedState over a changed replica list ([a,b,c] -> [a,b,c,d] or [a,b]) changes every replica's stripe: replicas that stored a stripe refuse with Conflict forever for that ObjectId. The caller sees Refused mapped to AdmissionDenied (native.rs ~216), not Conflict; over the chunked path BEGIN reserves and transfers the whole stripe before COMMIT fails (service/chunked.rs ~168/219); re-encoding with the same id or seed hits the same wall. Fix: surface Conflict as its own non-retryable failure, refuse at BEGIN when the origin's slot holds a different digest, and document or enforce a fresh ObjectId for a changed replica list.
F2 (low, verified by reading): COMMIT runs store.put (full digest and every symbol's tag check, up to max_encoded_bytes) while holding the global staging mutex (service/chunked.rs ~205-230; deliberate, to keep the reservation). Every BEGIN/CHUNK/READ from every origin takes that lock first, so one origin's commit stalls all other transfers and recovery reads, parking runtime workers on a parking_lot mutex; this contradicts store.put's own verify-outside-the-mutex rule. Fix: move the stage out of the map with its total still charged in reserved, drop the lock, verify and put, then re-lock to release the reservation.
Residual of 51a7c3ee6 (low): in-flight admission is shared with clones and refuses rather than queues (admission.rs ~21-24), so a concurrent recovery on a clone still turns a publication send into a replica failure.

title: ManagedSupervisor supports registered (named) children
description:
## Context
The managed supervisor refuses any child with a registration policy (src/supervision.rs ~2099-2103, `UnsupportedRegistration`). Named children therefore cannot be live-supervised. README's Spork table says "Registry: names as lease obligations: reserve/commit or abort (no stale names)". `NameLease` is a standalone `ObligationToken` drop-bomb (cx/registry.rs ~148), not a runtime-table obligation. `NameRegistry::cleanup_region` (~1438) has no runtime caller, so region close does not reap names.

## Work
Bind the registry into ManagedSupervisor generations: a restart releases the old name lease and re-registers under the new generation, and region close reaps names. Keep the existing registry API compatible.

## Acceptance
Lab and native tests: a named child restarts, lookups resolve to the new generation, there are no stale names after restart or close, and a `mem::forget` of a lease is detected by the runtime oracle (or the gap is documented).

---
**Provenance and binding rules.** Created by the 2026-09-22 reality check (SapphireHill); see the "September 22 assessment" section of `ASUPERSYNC_BRIDGE_PLAN_2026-09-01.md`. Evidence base: main at `8525d70554dd7cb7ab02ea16b461c5a6767e9e01` unless another SHA is named. Line numbers are approximate (`~`) and will drift, so re-locate by symbol before editing.

AGENTS.md rules that bind this work:
- Work on `main` only; no branches or worktrees.
- No file deletion without explicit written owner permission.
- No scripted code edits.
- Preserve public API and documented behavior (v0.4.3 floor for 0.4.x; the 0.5/0.6 policy is pending the owner, see R35b). Prefer additive APIs; any break needs explicit owner approval.
- Execute proof only through the owner-authorized validation path (see G1). The default is `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec --base <sha> --clean-overlay --no-overlay -- cargo ... -j 8` with an isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. Never use local fallback unless G1 authorizes it.

**Closure requires a receipt:** commit SHA, exact command, worker, and per-target running/passed/failed/ignored/filtered counts. Running must be greater than 0, and named tests must be neither ignored nor filtered. A bug fix also needs an old-red receipt taken at a pre-fix commit. Tests must log structured detail (ids, states, timings) so that a failure can be diagnosed from the log alone. Self-waking mocks cannot prove cancel-waker paths; use never-waking parked futures.

    Retained::drop never ran (no "retained drop" line).

Reading of the evidence:
1. The drop is not asynchronous. RuntimeInner is gone when the assertion runs, and teardown's retire_region_commands ran synchronously, but it found an empty queue.
2. The test's premise ("No current-thread pump is running") is false. RuntimeBuilder::current_thread() runs a background worker (CurrentThreadDriver::run_background) whenever no block_on caller holds the worker. Its dispatch loop calls next_task, whose PHASE 0.7 drain_region_commands applies RegisterFinalizer through RegisterRegionFinalizer::apply, which calls state.register_sync_finalizer. The child region is still open, so the admission succeeds. The two commands were queued when the probe ran and had been applied by the time teardown ran.
3. Once a Retained is applied, it lives in the region record's FinalizerStack inside RuntimeState, and each Retained holds Arc<ContendedMutex<RuntimeState>>. That is a reference cycle. Teardown takes state.tasks but not region finalizers, so nothing ever drops them: dropped stays 0 for good, not merely "not yet".
4. The outcome depends on whether the background pump applies the commands before teardown. That fits "fails under the full suite, passes filtered with --test-threads=1" at 7454f3897.

Implication: this is a real leak, not only a test artifact. Any finalizer admitted into a region that never closes before runtime drop, and that captures anything which keeps RuntimeState alive, survives the runtime. Cx and retained registrations are examples (supervision.rs:2506 retains the registration this way). Two fix directions, both runtime-side:
  (a) In RuntimeInner::drop teardown, after the worker joins, take every pending FinalizerStack out of the region records under the state lock (embedded and sharded tables). Then drop each Finalizer outside the lock, inside catch_unwind, the same way retire_region_commands already treats queued commands.
  (b) Only make the test deterministic, for example by asserting on a runtime whose commands provably stay queued. That hides (3), so I recommend (a) plus the existing test, with a second case that waits for the acknowledgment first, which forces the applied path.
Log: /data/tmp/rc_20260922/lanes/diag100b_dddc0b848.log

title: Lab and native disagree on panic-path loser drain in Scope::race/race_all/hedge (lab records a drain that did not happen)
description:
## Context (combinator audit, verified by reading)
`Scope::race` (scope.rs ~1003-1015, ~1029-1037), `race_all` (~1315-1327) and `hedge` (~1165-1186) treat "a panicking winner off a three-lane worker" as a direct block_on test with no scheduler: they poll each loser once with a noop waker, call `record_loser_drain_complete`, and return. The guard is `current_worker_id().is_none()`, and LabRuntime never sets `CURRENT_WORKER_ID` (only three_lane.rs ~5025/~7161 and current_thread.rs ~571 do). Under the deterministic lab, a panicking winner therefore returns WITHOUT draining losers while the drain is recorded as complete. Lab runs cannot prove the native panic-path drain, and the oracle is fed a false "drained" event.

## Fix
Give the lab a worker identity (or a dedicated "driven by a scheduler" predicate) so the lab drains exactly as native does, and never record a drain completion that did not happen.

## Tests
LabRuntime: `race_drained` with a panicking winner and a parked, cancel-aware loser that sets a flag on cancellation; assert the flag is set before return (it is false today). The same on native current-thread. Old-red at 8525d7055.

## Acceptance
Lab/native parity test green with counts plus old-red.

title: HTTP/2 listener: unbounded preface read and pump_writes, handlers orphaned on RST (Rapid-Reset amplification), unbounded shutdown join
description:
## Defects (network audit, verified by reading at 8525d7055)
- N1: `stream.read_exact(&mut preface).await?` (src/http/h2/listener.rs ~2614-2615) runs before any idle/deadline logic. The connection task is a root `runtime.try_spawn` (~3903-3934). A client that sends fewer than 24 bytes holds a slot forever. `run()` then awaits every connection task with no bound (~4046-4056), so graceful and forced shutdown never return.
- N2: `pump_writes` awaits `framed.poll_ready`/`poll_flush` with no timeout and no ForceClosing race (~2008-2027). It is called at the top of every loop turn (~2665) and on teardown paths. A peer that requests a large response or floods PINGs and never reads pins the slot forever, and shutdown hangs.
- N3: handlers are detached root tasks (`runtime.try_spawn`, ~2246). A peer RST only marks the stream (~1516-1526, ~3091-3115); the handler is never cancelled. `request_timeout: None` is the default (~3499). There is no global in-flight admission cap (`in_flight_requests` is only a counter, ~2241, ~3751). The RST limiter counts only peer-sent RST_STREAM (connection.rs ~1576-1596), not server-generated stream errors such as the stream-scoped zero-increment WINDOW_UPDATE (connection.rs ~1824-1832). HEADERS+END_STREAM followed by an immediate RST (or a WINDOW_UPDATE(0)) frees the MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS slot while the handler keeps running: up to 1000 handlers per connection (`max_requests_per_connection`), multiplied by reconnects. This is CVE-2023-44487 (Rapid Reset) and "MadeYouReset" class amplification.
- Known and still present: `stream_idle_timeout: None` by default lets one open stream disable the connection idle timeout (~2715-2727, ~3504; hw83se).

## Fix
Preface deadline (configurable, default e.g. 10 s). Bounded `pump_writes` raced against force-close and a write-progress deadline. Handlers become region-owned children of the connection, cancelled on RST/GOAWAY/connection close. Global plus per-connection in-flight caps. Count server-generated stream resets toward the reset limiter. Bound the shutdown join with force-close escalation. Keep public config types compatible (additive fields with defaults).

## Tests (real sockets, native runtime)
Partial-preface client (slot freed at deadline; shutdown returns). Non-reading client with a large response (slot freed; shutdown returns). Rapid-reset loop (in-flight handlers stay at or below the cap; cancelled handlers observed Cancelled). A shutdown under each stall completes within its bound. h2spec rerun stays 147/147 (G2.4). Log per-connection state transitions.

## Acceptance
All tests green with counts. h2spec receipt. Old-red for at least the rapid-reset and partial-preface tests.

title: HTTP/1 streaming responses and buffered error-path flushes have no write timeout (slot pinned, shutdown join hangs)
description:
## Defects (network audit, verified)
- N4: `write_streaming_response` has only a pre-write `checkpoint()`, then `write_all`/`flush` with no idle_timeout or force-close race (src/http/h1/server.rs ~2656-2676). It is used for the main response of streaming `serve` (~1431/~1661) and 16 other sites. A client that requests a large response and stops reading pins the connection forever, and `run_streaming()` join hangs (h1/listener.rs ~984). This contradicts the closed hw83se "FIXED" note.
- N5: buffered-H1 error-path flushes (431/400 reject, 421, 417, 100-continue) use `poll_fn(framed.poll_flush)` with only a checkpoint (server.rs ~1016-1025, ~1081-1090, ~1102-1111, ~1127-1136). The normal flush (~1289-1308) is bounded. Pipeline requests to fill the send buffer, then send a malformed head, and never read.

## Fix
Apply the same bounded-write discipline (idle/write-progress deadline raced with force-close) to every write site. Add a census test that fails if a new write site bypasses the bounded helper.

## Tests
Non-reading client against streaming and error-path responses: the slot is freed within the bound and shutdown completes. Old-red at 8525d7055.

title: Native gRPC streaming connect_tcp/connect_tls always refuse on the native runtime (wrong capability predicate cx.has_io())
description:
## Defect (source-verified at 8525d7055; confirmed by the root's lib run)
`NativeStreamEndpoint::admit` (src/grpc/native_stream/connect.rs ~219-221) refuses with `Status::failed_precondition("native streaming connect requires explicit I/O authority")` unless `cx.has_io() && cx.io_driver_handle().is_some()`. `Cx::has_io()` returns `self.handles.io_cap.is_some()` (src/cx/cx.rs ~2037-2042), an OPTIONAL VIRTUAL `IoCap` implemented only by Lab and Browser (src/io/cap.rs). The native runtime builds every task `Cx` with `io_cap = None` (src/runtime/state.rs ~3874-3883, ~4251-4260). So every native plaintext and TLS gRPC streaming dial fails before any I/O. The root's lib run at 8525d7055 showed three failures consistent with this: `native_endpoint_dials_health_watch_and_closes_its_owned_connection` (unwrap at tests.rs:240), `native_setup_timeout_closes_stalled_header_wait_without_cancelling_parent` ("preface not sent"), `native_cancel_and_dropped_setup_retire_a_witnessed_pending_header_wait`. The code came in with f16eeae89 ("rch not found", never run) and was inherited by bfcf44a0a `connect_tls`.
The same predicate class gates relay/IPv6 in src/net/atp/rendezvous/mod.rs (~223, ~246, ~340, ~352). SUSPECTED: always Denied on native.
Also in the same test module: `admitted_call_keeps_original_deadline_and_forwards_only_remaining_time` expects "6000000u", but `format_grpc_timeout` (src/grpc/server.rs ~2265-2297) has emitted the largest lossless unit ("6S") since March. That is a TEST bug; fix the test.

## Fix
Gate on the real native I/O capability (I/O driver handle present and the runtime capability mask permitting I/O), not the virtual `IoCap`. Audit every `has_io()` call site for the same confusion and record a census. Fix the timeout-unit test.

## Tests
The four lib tests green; native TLS dial tests green (with `tls`); a census test listing `has_io()` call sites with their intended semantics. Old-red receipt = the 8525d7055 lib run already recorded (/data/tmp/rc_20260922/lanes/lib_tests.log).

## Acceptance
Green receipts with counts; census recorded; ATP rendezvous verdict recorded (fixed or proven intended).

The H2 listener's produced-body poll (poll_one -> OutgoingBody::poll_frame) receives with the PRODUCER's request Cx. mpsc::Receiver::poll_recv checks cx.checkpoint() BEFORE popping the queue (src/channel/mpsc.rs ~1646), so with the request Cx cancelled it returns RecvError::Cancelled. title: grpc::Server::serve is a legacy probe that binds and returns Ok without serving; make the real serving entry point unmistakable
description:
## Context (source-verified)
`Server::serve(self, addr)` (src/grpc/server.rs ~2186-2212) binds a `std::net::TcpListener`, sets nonblocking and returns `Ok(())`. Its rustdoc says it "remains functional for v0.4.3 compatibility but does not accept or dispatch requests". With a tonic-like name, users will assume it serves. `u0j91o` was closed without addressing this.

## Work
Keep the method (compatibility) but mark it `#[deprecated(note = "...use <real API>...")]` if the owner approves deprecation (deprecation is allowed under AGENTS; removal is not). Point README/docs to the real serving API with a compiled example.

## Acceptance
The doc example compiles and serves one real request in a test.

---
**Provenance and binding rules.** Created by the 2026-09-22 reality check (SapphireHill); see the "September 22 assessment" section of `ASUPERSYNC_BRIDGE_PLAN_2026-09-01.md`. Evidence base: main at `8525d70554dd7cb7ab02ea16b461c5a6767e9e01` unless another SHA is named. Line numbers are approximate (`~`) and will drift, so re-locate by symbol before editing.

AGENTS.md rules that bind this work:
- Work on `main` only; no branches or worktrees.
- No file deletion without explicit written owner permission.
- No scripted code edits.
- Preserve public API and documented behavior (v0.4.3 floor for 0.4.x; the 0.5/0.6 policy is pending the owner, see R35b). Prefer additive APIs; any break needs explicit owner approval.
- Execute proof only through the owner-authorized validation path (see G1). The default is `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec --base <sha> --clean-overlay --no-overlay -- cargo ... -j 8` with an isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. Never use local fallback unless G1 authorizes it.

Running must be greater than 0, and named tests must be neither ignored nor filtered. A bug fix also needs an old-red receipt taken at a pre-fix commit. Tests must log structured detail (ids, states, timings) so that a failure can be diagnosed from the log alone. Self-waking mocks cannot prove cancel-waker paths; use never-waking parked futures.

title: QUIC/H3 remote resource exhaustion: no Retry/address validation, uncapped PATH_CHALLENGE queue, un-negotiated DATAGRAM frames queued
description:
## Defects (network audit, verified by reading)
- N6: NativeH3Listener handshake slots can be exhausted with spoofed Initials. Each admission lives until `now + ACCEPT_PTO*64` = 96 s (managed_endpoint.rs ~1042-1044). Once the capped anti-amplification flight is outstanding, the flight counter never advances (~1379-1394). When `pending >= limit`, new Initials are silently dropped (~1146-1149). The default `max_pending_handshakes` is 16 (h3_listener.rs ~86, ~256-260). There is no Retry or address validation. 16 spoofed 1200-byte Initials every 96 s (~200 B/s) deny all new H3 clients.
- N10: every PATH_CHALLENGE is pushed onto `pending_control_frames` with no cap (src/net/quic_native/connection.rs ~2525-2528). A handshaked peer that never ACKs (cwnd-limited) can stream challenges without bound while inbound packets keep refreshing the idle timer. Also PATH_RESPONSE sets `peer_address_validated = true` without matching a sent challenge (~2530-2533).
- N11: `QuicFrame::Datagram` frames are queued (up to `MAX_INBOUND_DATAGRAMS = 65_536` per connection, ~2562-2565, ~2600-2615, ~389) even if we never advertised `max_datagram_frame_size`; RFC 9221 requires PROTOCOL_VIOLATION. H3 never calls `recv_datagram`. That is ~78 MB per connection, ~5 GB at the 64-connection default.

## Fix
Stateless Retry with address-validation tokens for the managed endpoint (configurable; on by default when the pending-handshake budget is under pressure). title: QUIC protocol correctness gaps: managed key update/AES-GCM limit, MAX_STREAMS ignored, UDP-driver idle timeout, client Retry handling, parameter validation symmetry
description:
## Defects (network audit)
- N12: the managed/H3 endpoint never initiates a key update and never checks `confidentiality_limit_reached`. The only initiation site is udp_connection.rs ~839. RFC 9001 §6.6 is violated after ~8.4M packets under one key.
- N13: received MAX_STREAMS is ignored (connection.rs ~2588-2590). A client can never exceed the peer's initial stream limit; H3 works around this by retiring connections after 128 requests.
- N14: the standalone UDP driver stores the idle timeout (udp_connection.rs ~590) but only the router reads it (connection_manager.rs ~1430). With no stateless reset, a dead peer leaves the driver PTO-probing forever.
- N15: the QUIC client aborts on any Retry, or on a malformed long header from the server address (handshake_driver.rs ~869-870, ~1435-1443). An off-path spoofer can kill handshakes, and Retry-using servers cannot interoperate.
- N16 (SUSPECTED): CRYPTO reassembly copy cost is quadratic before authentication (handshake_driver.rs ~494-517, ~948-953).
- N23: `TransportParameters::encode` does not validate (quic_core/mod.rs ~538-539), while decode rejects max_ack_delay ≥ 2^14 and ack_delay_exponent > 20. Decode misses the RFC 9000 §4.6 check that `initial_max_streams_*` must not exceed 2^60 (~593-598). The lib test `net::quic_native::transport_conformance_tests::comprehensive_tests::all_parameters_maximum_values` fails at 8525d7055 because it round-trips max_ack_delay = 2^62-1. It is a stale test, but fixing only it would hide N23.

## Work
Fix each, keeping public APIs compatible. The encoder validates with the same predicates as the decoder (shared function). Update the stale test to assert that the encoder rejects out-of-range values.

## Acceptance
Unit tests per defect; the `all_parameters_maximum_values` lib test green for the right reason; an interop note if an external QUIC peer is available.

title: One request's finalizer/cleanup failure stops the whole NativeH3Listener for every peer
description:
## Defect (network audit, verified)
A request region whose finalizer outcome is not `Ok` returns `Err(CleanupFailed)` (src/web/router/h3_listener.rs ~816-817; the ownership errors at ~791-797 and ~822-823 behave the same). The error is stored in `self.failure` (~1235), `poll` returns Ready (~1273-1275), and `serve_with_shutdown` returns Err for ALL peers (~314-320). A single handler whose finalizer panics tears down every connection. Also: the buffered-response cap is checked after the handler materialized the body, with no aggregate cap (128 × 16 MiB worst case, ~1824).

## Fix
Contain request-scoped cleanup failure to that request/stream (reset the stream and record diagnostics). Reserve listener-fatal errors for listener-level invariants. Add an aggregate buffered-response budget.

## Acceptance
Live UDP test: one request's panicking finalizer does not affect a concurrent request on another connection; the listener keeps serving. Counts recorded.

title: Distributed C2: authenticated membership generations, discovery and live lease revocation
description:
CURRENT GOVERNING SCOPE — 2026-09-04. MembershipLeaseManager::sync already invokes the reactor (remote.rs:1513-1529) and returns obligations for the caller to abort. The missing seam is production orchestration, not that call. lease_reactor.rs:85-86 and swim.rs:481-489 make revoked/dead identity terminal; naive higher-incarnation same-identity rejoin contradicts that policy.

Create a region-owned bounded SWIM/discovery/lease orchestrator. Bind admission to authenticated node generation/TLS identity and explicit grants. Gossip is liveness evidence, never authority to replace pins or issue capabilities. Suspect pauses grants under declared policy; confirmed death terminalizes old-generation leases and actually aborts/compensates their runtime obligations once. Rejoin authenticates a fresh generation without reviving old authority. Preserve existing terminal NodeId APIs through additive identity mechanisms. Reconcile lagging event cursors after membership log compaction so a missed death cannot preserve a lease.

Real two-process tests: join, authorized computation, suspect/recover, kill after lease admission, route removal plus actual obligation abort, authenticated new-generation rejoin and old-packet replay refusal. Spoofed/wrong-identity announcements and a seed that never responds cannot authorize a route. Exercise compaction past a delayed consumer and duplicate/reordered death observations. Derive timing from configured probe/indirect/suspicion/dissemination bounds; do not assume every peer becomes visible in two probes. Log generation, authority, route, lease/obligation and cleanup transitions with redaction. C3 integrates only after terminal native proof. No universal failure-detector accuracy, consensus or cross-node exactly-once claim. Earlier contrary assumptions below are historical.

HISTORICAL ORIGINAL CONTEXT (preserved for provenance; the current governing scope above supersedes conflicting instructions):

WHY: src/distributed/membership/swim.rs implements SWIM over real UDP (probe, indirect probe, suspicion, dissemination) with its own tests, but no runtime consumer exists: `MembershipLeaseReactor` is imported by src/remote.rs:55 and never called, and `NativeRemoteDiscoveryDriver` (the remote runtime's peer discovery) is fed by static configuration only. "Distributed" in the README therefore means "two hand-configured peers".

WHAT: `SwimDiscoverySource` adapter: subscribes to SWIM membership events (alive/suspect/confirmed-dead with incarnation numbers) and drives `NativeRemoteDiscoveryDriver` peer add/remove/quarantine; suspect peers are kept but deprioritized, dead peers removed after the dissemination period; a peer that rejoins with a higher incarnation is re-added. The SWIM node itself is started by the same builder hook (bind address, seed list, probe interval, suspicion multiplier) and stopped on runtime close (region-owned task; quiescence waits for it). Metrics: current membership size, suspicions/min, false-positive rate (a peer marked suspect that answers the next probe).

TESTS: unit tests with a scripted SWIM event stream (add/suspect/dead/rejoin ordering, incarnation tie-breaks); a TWO-PROCESS e2e (tests/distributed_swim_discovery_two_process_e2e.rs): parent starts SWIM + driver; child process joins over loopback UDP; the parent's driver lists the child within 2 probe intervals; child is killed (SIGKILL) and the driver removes it within suspicion_timeout + dissemination; planted negative: a child that never answers probes is never listed as alive.

ACCEPTANCE: both test files green via rch; SWIM task is region-owned (runtime close proves quiescence); no ambient-authority additions beyond the existing UDP socket (inventory reviewed if the count moves).

NO-CLAIM: no gossip of application state; no consensus.
acceptance_criteria: A region-owned production orchestrator binds authenticated node generations to discovery grants, route policy and live lease/obligation revocation. Real process join/suspect/recover/death/rejoin tests derive deadlines from configured probe, indirect-probe, suspicion and dissemination bounds; there is no universal two-probe visibility bound. Confirmed death terminates old-generation grants and actually aborts/compensates the corresponding runtime obligations once. Fresh-generation rejoin cannot resurrect old authority. Wrong identity, nonresponding seed, stale packets and delayed cursors past event compaction cannot authorize or preserve a route/lease incorrectly. Required unit/native process and parked-cancellation tests have terminal strict-remote nonzero positive counts and exact cleanup. Preserve terminal NodeId behavior through additive mechanisms; no gossip-derived authority, universal detector-accuracy or consensus claim.

title: PostgreSQL: cancelling a query parked on the socket never sends CancelRequest (server keeps executing and holding locks)
description:
## Defect (data audit, verified by reading at 8525d7055)
When a query waiting on the socket is cancelled, the read returns Cancelled and the loop only shuts the socket down (src/database/postgres.rs ~3268-3294, ~3654-3657, ~3549-3552). `cancel_in_flight`, the only code that sends the server's CancelRequest (~3916-3935), runs only if the check at the top of the loop sees the cancellation first. So a cancelled `SELECT pg_sleep(30)` or long UPDATE keeps running server-side and holds its locks until it finishes. The doc comment at ~3235-3236 claims the opposite. MySQL's cancel wrapper does this correctly (mysql.rs ~3157-3163). Beads `gvkj1r`/`xgkg5w` were closed, but their real-server test measures only how long the client waited, so it cannot see the CancelRequest.

## Fix
On cancellation of an in-flight query from any await point, send CancelRequest on a side connection (bounded by a timeout), then drain or close the main connection per protocol. Keep the public API unchanged.

## Tests (real PostgreSQL 16 via the G1-authorized path)
Start `SELECT pg_sleep(30)` on connection A; cancel the task while it is parked on the socket (prove it is parked first); then from connection B query `pg_stat_activity` and assert the backend's query is no longer active within 2 s. Also check a lock held by an UPDATE is released. Old-red at 8525d7055. Log backend pids and states.

## Acceptance
Real-server receipt with counts plus old-red. `gvkj1r`/`xgkg5w` follow-up recorded.

title: PostgreSQL TLS trust options (sslrootcert, verify-ca/verify-full) and a TLS handshake timeout
description:
## Context (data audit)
PG TLS trusts only webpki roots, which is a no-op without the `tls-webpki-roots` feature (tls/types.rs ~386-390), plus an implicit `SSL_CERT_FILE` (postgres.rs ~4200-4217). title: MySQL: TLS, caching_sha2 full authentication (cold MySQL 8 login), working KILL-on-drop, less brittle SQL heuristics
description:
## Context (data audit, verified)
- No TLS at all: both Preferred and Required fail closed (src/database/mysql.rs ~2766-2776).
- caching_sha2 full authentication (RSA or TLS path) is not implemented (~2921-2925), so the client cannot log in to a freshly restarted MySQL 8 server. The old CI worked around this by warming the server over TLS first (ci.yml ~1957-1970). README's MySQL row states "caching_sha2 by default" with no caveat. Beads `2s7d3`, `j1x8k`, `wy4zkq` were closed without this.
- KILL QUERY on dropping a connection mid-query can never run: its predicate requires `closed == false`, but every exchange sets it to true first (~1831-1841 vs ~3196-3200). The unbounded `runtime.block_on(join)` (~1878) would leak a thread if it ran (`22i5tn` closed without this).
- `validate_sql_security` is a denylist heuristic that rejects valid SQL (`INSERT INTO t VALUES (1)`) and is bypassed by `set `/`show ` prefixes (~2969-3015).

## Work
TLS via rustls behind the existing `tls` feature; caching_sha2 full auth over TLS and the RSA public-key exchange; fix and bound KILL-on-drop; replace the heuristic with an opt-in policy or document it precisely (compatibility: do not start rejecting SQL that is currently accepted without owner approval).

## Acceptance
Real MySQL 8 tests: cold-server login over TLS and over RSA; KILL observed in `information_schema.processlist` after a mid-query drop; heuristic regression tests.

title: First ctrl_c()/signal() call installs handlers for all ten signals, disabling default termination process-wide (SIGTERM ignored)
description:
## Defect (source-verified at 8525d7055)
`SignalDispatcher::start` (src/signal/signal.rs ~207-240) registers `signal_hook::iterator::Signals` for `all_signal_kinds()` at once the first time any signal API is used (`signal()`, `ctrl_c()`, even `ctrl_c::is_available()`; ctrl_c.rs ~86-95; signal.rs ~419-432). A handler replaces the default disposition, so from then on SIGTERM, SIGHUP, SIGQUIT, SIGUSR1/2 and SIGALRM no longer terminate the process. A service that only waits on `ctrl_c()` ignores `docker stop` / systemd SIGTERM until it gets SIGKILL after the grace period. `ShutdownController` listeners are one-shot (shutdown.rs ~488-507), so a second Ctrl-C or SIGTERM cannot force exit. Tokio registers only the signals actually requested.

## Fix
Register lazily, per requested kind. Preserve default dispositions for kinds nobody asked for. Document the semantics for a kind that was requested and then all its listeners dropped (tokio keeps the handler installed; state what asupersync does).

## Tests (subprocess, unix)
A child process that awaits only `ctrl_c()`; the parent sends SIGTERM and asserts the child exits with SIGTERM's default status within 1 s (old code: it keeps running; old-red). A second test requests SIGTERM explicitly and asserts it is delivered to the listener. Log exit statuses.

## Acceptance
Subprocess tests green on Linux (and macOS if a host is available) with counts plus old-red.

title: Dropped still-running child processes without kill_on_drop become unreaped zombies; wait_async cancel path untested
description:
## Context (data audit)
A child still running when its handle is dropped without `kill_on_drop` becomes a zombie that nothing reaps (src/process.rs ~3100-3121). Long-lived servers accumulate zombies, exactly the `bn2iln` scenario (closed). `wait_async` polls every 1-50 ms, and both tests named `pc_03_wait_async_cancel_safe` never cancel anything.

## Work
A background reaper (orphan-reaping registry, as tokio does) or documented detach semantics with reaping. Real cancel tests for `wait_async`.

## Acceptance
Test: spawn and drop 100 still-running children, let them exit, and assert there are no zombies in /proc for our pid. Cancel `wait_async` mid-wait and assert the child is still reaped later.

title: Kafka consumer teardown hangs in about half of CI runs after the test body passes
description:
## Context (data audit; symptom verified in CI logs 09-03..09-07)
Kafka finished in only 8 of 19 CI runs; 9 hung until the 3600 s job timeout AFTER the test body had logged a pass, i.e. during consumer teardown. Suspected cause: `leave_group_bounded` returns early (src/messaging/kafka_consumer.rs ~690-708), and `Drop` does up to ~5 s of blocking polls on the dropping, possibly async, thread (~711-723). There is no native Kafka wire code; rdkafka only. ADR-009 says keep rdkafka.

## Work
Reproduce with 10+ consecutive runs against redpanda on an authorized host (G2.7), root-cause, and fix without blocking an async worker in Drop (move teardown to the blocking pool with a bound). Add a teardown-duration assertion.

## Acceptance
20 consecutive green runs, teardown under a stated bound, old-red hang reproduction recorded.
