title: Observability truth: production poll counts always 0; find_leaked_obligations reports healthy obligations and ignores Leaked records; blocked explanation hardcoded
description:
## Context (data audit, verified)
`increment_polls` is called only from tests (record/task.rs ~587), so TaskInspector `poll_count` is always 0 for production tasks (runtime_inspector_e2e.rs ~17-19 admits it). As a result `is_potentially_stuck` flags healthy parked tasks (task_inspector.rs ~320-323, ~700). `TaskBlockedExplanation` returns a hardcoded "unknown await point" (diagnostics.rs ~472-483). `find_leaked_obligations` reports live Reserved obligations and ignores records the runtime marked `Leaked` (~598-625). README's "Task Inspector and Diagnostics" section presents these as working.

## Work
Count polls on the production dispatch path (a relaxed atomic; verify with the Phase-6 benchmark gate that the hot path is not regressed). Fix leak detection semantics. Make the blocked explanation truthful (the last recorded checkpoint message, or explicitly "unknown").

## Acceptance
Native test: a task polled N times reports N. A leaked obligation is reported and a healthy one is not. Baseline benchmark receipt.

---

title: OTLP exporters cannot compose in MultiExporter (export always errors); MultiExporter has no production caller
description:
## Context (data audit, verified)
`OtlpHttpExporter::export` always returns an error (src/observability/otel.rs ~7328-7332), and so does the logs exporter (~5390). title: File poll traits and write_atomic block an async worker when the Cx lacks SPAWN or no blocking pool exists
description:
## Context (data audit, verified)
Each read/write/seek is offloaded in 128 KiB chunks when a blocking pool exists (file.rs ~631-641). It runs inline on the async worker when (a) the runtime was built with a bare `RuntimeBuilder` (no pool by default), or (b) the task's Cx lacks SPAWN, because file.rs ~637 and process.rs ~2950 use the SPAWN-gated pool getter (the sibling fix 1385ef2d5 covered only `spawn_blocking`). Separately, `write_atomic` does the rename and parent-dir fsync synchronously on the worker (path_ops.rs ~515-520, ~580-582).

Use the capability-appropriate pool accessor. Offload `write_atomic`'s rename and fsync. Document the no-pool behavior (inline is intentional there), per README.

## Acceptance
Native test with a SPAWN-restricted Cx: a slow-disk-simulated read does not block other tasks on the worker (use a FIFO or a sleep in a FUSE-less fake file) and progress is measured.

title: DNS in connect is uncancellable and untimed; connect_timeout spends its whole budget on the first address
description:
## Context (network audit, verified)
`lookup_all` uses `spawn_blocking` getaddrinfo (src/net/resolve.rs ~56-99), and the receiver is not cancel-aware. `connect_timeout` resolves before its deadline starts. Its per-address loop gives the full `remaining` budget to the first address and breaks on timeout (src/net/tcp/stream.rs ~835-850). A black-holed IPv6-first address exhausts the timeout and the working IPv4 address is never tried.

## Fix
Cancel-aware resolution bounded by the connect deadline. Happy-eyeballs-style or per-address budget splitting (RFC 8305 spirit), additive and configurable.

## Acceptance
Test with a black-holed first address and a working second address: connects within the budget. Cancellation during resolution returns promptly.

title: Distributed C3: compose snapshot, membership and region-owned remote lifecycle through public APIs
description:
CURRENT GOVERNING SCOPE — 2026-09-04. Preserve all original public builder/integration goals. Compose bounded snapshot transport (bi2462.10), authenticated generation-aware discovery/lease orchestration (.11), and remote region-owned lease/drain (.16) only after their native proofs. An additive builder/handle must preserve 0.4.x exhaustive struct/trait behavior and strict V1-V3 bytes. Validate actual socket/protocol constraints: allow explicit singleton/bootstrap mode; do not universally require seeds or distinct numerical TCP/UDP ports.

Public two-/multi-process journey: configure authority and capacities, start services, join, spawn a named remote computation, distribute/recover a snapshot, kill/partition a peer with real in-flight lease, observe local cancellation/compensation, rejoin a freshly authenticated generation, repeat successful work and close the owning region. Assert exact object/result identity, no unauthorized grants, bounded active attempts/bytes, no stale-generation resurrection and task/obligation/finalizer cleanup. Inject wrong identity, unavailable seed, withheld ack, stale death/ack and invalid configuration before publication. Test partial startup rollback and owner cancellation at each phase. Logs carry source/config/peer/generation/object/attempt/lease identity and terminal counts; no fixture-only success. Preserve PBFT's explicit scaffold/unavailable boundary; two-process recovery is not consensus, durable database replication, arbitrary closure migration, or a WAN throughput result. Parent e6drlx closes only for its actually proved acceptance, not builder field presence.

HISTORICAL ORIGINAL CONTEXT (preserved for provenance; the current governing scope above supersedes conflicting instructions):

WHY: C1 and C2 each work in isolation; the runtime still needs one opt-in entry point so a user can enable snapshot distribution and SWIM discovery without assembling five types by hand, and the docs must say exactly what is and is not provided.

WHAT: `RuntimeBuilder::distributed(DistributedConfig)` (additive) with `DistributedConfig { swim: Option<SwimConfig>, snapshot_transport: Option<RemoteTransportConfig>, discovery_seeds: Vec<SocketAddr> }`; starting it creates the region-owned SWIM node (C2), the RemoteRuntime listener with the snapshot sink (C1), and exposes `RuntimeHandle::distributed() -> Option<DistributedHandle>` (membership snapshot, distribute(snapshot) future, metrics). Runtime close drains everything (tests assert quiescence and no obligation leaks). Docs: README "Distributed" section rewritten to the truthful scope with a 20-line example; docs/distributed.md (or the existing plan section) updated; CHANGELOG. Close asupersync-gap-snapshot-transport-swim-pbft-e6drlx with the C1/C2 receipts.

TESTS: builder-level test (config validation: seeds required when swim is set; ports must differ), an e2e that starts two runtimes in one process on loopback with SWIM + distributor and moves a snapshot through the public API only.

ACCEPTANCE: public-API e2e green; docs match code; e6drlx closed; no default-on behaviour change (opt-in).
acceptance_criteria: After .10/.11/.16 have their required native evidence, the opt-in public builder journey starts services, authenticates peers, runs a named remote computation, distributes/recovers a snapshot, loses a peer with an admitted lease, reauthenticates a fresh generation, performs healthy follow-up work and closes the owning region. Wrong identity, unavailable seed, stale ack/death, invalid config and partial startup exercise exact refusals/rollback. Prove bounded attempts/bytes and task/obligation/finalizer cleanup with terminal strict-remote nonzero positive counts. Permit supported singleton/bootstrap and protocol-valid port configurations. Preserve 0.4.x exhaustive public types and V1-V3 bytes; PBFT remains explicitly unavailable. Documentation matches this actual scope. Close this child on its own acceptance, then evaluate e6drlx with all remaining scope; e6drlx is not required to close first.

title: WebSocket ping_interval is dead config (30 s default never read); client handshake response read has no timeout; unimplementable extension echoed
description:
## Context (network audit, verified)
`ping_interval` is stored (client.rs ~245/~289, server.rs ~127/~278) but never read, so users believe keepalive is on while half-open peers pin `recv()` forever. The client handshake response read has no timeout or cancel waker (client.rs ~1192-1242); `connect_timeout` wraps only the TCP connect (~1105). The low-level `WebSocketAcceptor::extension()` echoes an offered extension (handshake.rs ~751-777) while the codec always rejects RSV bits (server.rs ~302, frame.rs ~593), so configuring permessage-deflate makes every compressed browser frame fail. Also: `EarlyDataReplayProtection::UnprotectedForTesting` is a public non-test variant enabling wire 0-RTT with only a tracing-gated warning (tls acceptor.rs ~414, ~1019-1030).

## Fix
Implement ping/pong keepalive per `ping_interval` with a pong deadline. Bound the handshake read. Refuse to negotiate extensions the codec cannot implement. Gate or rename the testing-only replay variant (compatibly: deprecate and warn).

## Acceptance
Tests: a half-open peer is detected within interval+deadline; a stalled handshake times out; an extension offer is refused.

---

Evidence base: main at `8525d70554dd7cb7ab02ea16b461c5a6767e9e01` unless another SHA is named. Line numbers are approximate (`~`) and will drift, so re-locate by symbol before editing.

AGENTS.md rules that bind this work:
- Work on `main` only; no branches or worktrees.
- No file deletion without explicit written owner permission.
- No scripted code edits.
- Preserve public API and documented behavior (v0.4.3 floor for 0.4.x; the 0.5/0.6 policy is pending the owner, see R35b). Prefer additive APIs; any break needs explicit owner approval.
- Execute proof only through the owner-authorized validation path (see G1). The default is `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec --base <sha> --clean-overlay --no-overlay -- cargo ... -j 8` with an isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. Never use local fallback unless G1 authorizes it.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SapphireHill: item 2 LANDED in 7454f3897 (main/master). The client upgrade exchange (write request, read the 101 head) now runs under its own connect_timeout bound and the caller's cancellation, through bounded_upgrade_exchange (Sleep::poll_deadline plus WsCancelWakerGuard). A silent server can no longer park connect forever, and a cancelled caller gets WsConnectError::Cancelled.
Tests: upgrade_exchange_times_out_when_the_peer_never_answers, cancelling_a_parked_upgrade_exchange_returns_cancelled, connect_times_out_when_a_tcp_server_never_answers_the_upgrade (native runtime, real TCP). All pass in lane cn_lib on hz4.
Old-red control ebe3cef78 (the e2e test on the pre-fix client): hangs, 'connect must not hang ... Timeout' at the 10 s bound. The native cancellation contract is 42/42 on the same src.
Remaining items need an OWNER decision, so they are not done here:
(1) ping_interval keepalive. The default is Some(30 s). Making it live changes behaviour for every default connection: pings are sent, and non-responding peers are disconnected. The choice is between default-on keepalive and the dead config being documented or removed.
(3) Extension refusal. Both WebSocketAcceptor::extension and web::websocket's .extensions() negotiate extensions that FrameCodec (which rejects every RSV bit) cannot honour, so a negotiated permessage-deflate breaks every compressed frame. Declining would change the observable negotiation of two public APIs. The low-level ServerHandshake is conformance-tested (tests/conformance_websocket.rs) and should stay as it is.
(4) EarlyDataReplayProtection::UnprotectedForTesting: recommend no change. The name and docs state that it is dangerous, the other strategies fail closed, and deprecating it would contradict the fail-closed error message, which points testers to it.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SapphireHill source review of 1d9799819 (WSS client, read-only at 534a6cb7f); no defect found in the security-critical path:
- connect_tls refuses non-wss:// URLs, so there is no plaintext fallback.
- TlsConnector::validate_domain runs on the URL host, and connector.connect(&parsed.host, ..) uses the URL host/IP as the certificate identity. Trust comes only from the caller's connector, never an implicit root. SNI is required for DNS names.
- A negotiated ALPN other than http/1.1 is refused before any HTTP bytes are sent.
- The shared perform_client_handshake builds a wss:// handshake URL from host_header().
- ClientHandshake::validate_response (handshake.rs ~558) enforces status 101, Upgrade/Connection tokens, the exact Sec-WebSocket-Accept (compute_accept_key), a subprotocol that was offered, and extensions that were offered (RFC 6455 §4.1).
- The upgrade read stays bounded (bounded_upgrade_exchange). One WsTlsSetup deadline spans DNS/TCP/TLS/HTTP, tightened by both the caller's and the ambient budget, with cancel wakers on both contexts.
Execution: the peer's e63879feb receipt ran websocket_tls_native 5/0 (--features tls,test-internals). This note does not cover the ping_interval item.

title: Reactor fail-open: DesktopRuntimeProfile installs BrowserReactor on native (sockets park forever); reactor poll errors silently swallowed
description:
## Context (network audit, verified)
`DesktopRuntimeProfile` installs `BrowserReactor` on native targets (src/runtime/desktop_profile.rs ~161). `BrowserReactor::register` ignores the source and returns Ok (reactor/browser.rs ~719-724), so any TcpStream/UdpSocket/UnixStream under that runtime parks forever with no error. Separately, reactor poll errors are swallowed: three_lane.rs ~4957 maps `Err(_)` to Follower and worker.rs ~321 keeps only `Ok(Some(_))`. A persistently failing reactor looks like an idle runtime.

## Fix
The desktop profile uses the platform reactor on native, or registration refuses with `Unsupported`. Reactor errors are counted, traced, and escalated after a threshold.

## Acceptance
Test: a TCP connect under the desktop profile either works or fails fast with Unsupported. A fault-injected reactor error increments a metric and surfaces a diagnostic.

title: Remote: a silent peer after Accepted hangs region close (no deadline/keepalive; uninterruptible RemoteHandle close)
description:
## Defect (source-verified at 8525d7055)
After the remote accepts, the native origin driver waits with no deadline and no keepalive: `session.exchange_event::<RemoteServiceSessionCommand>(cx, None)` (src/remote.rs ~7428) raced only against the control channel, with `read_remote_service_frame` having no timeout (~3772-3786). `RemoteHandle::close` requests cancel and then waits with `self.receiver.recv_uninterruptible().await` (~918-930). A peer that goes silent after `Accepted` (partition without RST, SIGSTOP, a wedged host) therefore hangs the `distributed::remote_owned::run_remote` child region, its admission credit, and the PARENT region's close. It stays stuck until someone calls `NativeRemoteRuntime::close/force_close`, or until kernel TCP retransmission fails the written Cancel (~15 min on Linux defaults; forever if the peer ACKs but never answers). The lease never bounds the origin. This contradicts `bi2462.16`/`udjmtx` ("a never-answering remote is reported lease-expired at the bound") and plan v4 §8.4 ("lease bounds orphan work").

## Fix
Bound the origin wait by the lease (plus renewal) and a drain budget. Add application-level keepalive/lease-renewal traffic. `close` becomes interruptible after the drain budget and yields a deterministic `LeaseExpired`/`Cancelled` outcome that is recorded as delivery-ambiguous (never retried automatically). Preserve V1-V3 wire goldens: any new message needs a new protocol version per v4 §8.4.1.

## Tests
A TLS listener that returns V3 `Accepted` and then neither reads nor replies; `run_remote` with a 1 s budget inside a parent region that then closes. Assert the parent close completes within lease+drain, with the documented outcome. Old-red at 8525d7055 (hang, detected by a wall-clock bound). Log the session state transitions.

## Acceptance
Test green with counts plus old-red; wire goldens unchanged, or a new protocol version with negotiation tests.

title: Remote origins never renew leases; any native remote computation over 30 s ends LeaseExpired
description:
## Defect (distributed audit, verified by reading)
The origin driver renews only on a user-sent `LeaseRenewal` (src/remote.rs ~7466, ~7949). `RemoteHandle` has no renew API, and the default lease is 30 s (~441). So any `NativeRemoteRuntime` computation longer than the default lease is cancelled server-side and surfaces as `LeaseExpired`, including under `run_remote`, which has no lease setting. A related LOW defect (R27c) is folded in here: the server clamps the enforced lease to 24 h but echoes the UNclamped requested lease in Accepted/LeaseRenewed (~5461-5480, since 2ab2f1fbf), so the acknowledgement overstates what is enforced.

## Fix
Automatic origin-side renewal at a safe fraction of the granted lease while the handle is live and the owning region is open; a `run_remote` lease option; the server echoes the clamped value. Wire compatibility per v4 §8.4.1.

## Tests
A 45 s (or time-scaled) remote computation completes Ok with renewals observed. Renewal stops when the owning region is cancelled and the computation is cancelled at lease expiry. A clamp echo test.

## Acceptance
Native two-process test green with counts plus old-red.

title: ATP: decide and implement secure defaults (atp send defaults to plaintext unauthenticated TCP)
description:
## Context (source-verified at 8525d7055)
`src/bin/atp.rs` (~312-313): `#[arg(long, value_enum, default_value_t = Transport::Tcp)] transport`. `transport_tcp` has no TLS or HMAC code (`rg -i 'tls|hmac|authenticat' src/net/atp/transport_tcp/mod.rs` has 0 hits), so integrity is checked only against an unauthenticated manifest and a MITM can substitute manifest and bytes. The `auto` transport refuses plaintext fallback unless `--allow-plaintext-fallback` is given (~217), but `auto` is not the default. In the RQ transport the control transcript is unauthenticated, and even in the authenticated delta mode the NeedMore feedback frames are never MACed (transport_rq/mod.rs ~8950 parse, ~11798-11808 emit). `e880xo` (P0) owns control-transcript authentication, but has had no implementation since 06-15 and its owner has been idle since June. Also `asupersync atp serve` is a plaintext TCP listener (src/bin/asupersync.rs ~5760).

## Decision for the owner (CLI default is documented behavior; changing it is a compatibility event)
(a) Make the default an authenticated transport (QUIC/TLS) with plaintext only via an explicit flag. (b) Keep TCP as the default, but refuse non-loopback plaintext without `--allow-plaintext`. (c) Keep as is and document prominently.

## Work after the decision
Implement it with tests: default invocation to a non-loopback target behaves per the decision, and a MITM test (a proxy that rewrites the manifest) is detected under the authenticated default. Add NeedMore MAC coverage to `e880xo`'s scope (comment there).

title: ATP legacy SDK surfaces fake success and give false integrity verdicts (send_object no I/O, verify_object tautological or failing every tar)
description:
## Defects (ATP audit, verified by reading)
Two public legacy session types exist:
1. `crate::atp::sdk::AtpSession` (src/atp/sdk.rs): `send_object` builds a local `TransferActor` and returns `Ok(TransferHandle)` with NO network I/O (~327-403). `stream_large_buffer` returns `Ok(StreamHandle{bytes_sent:0})` (~465-543). `cancel_transfer` returns `Ok(())` for an unknown id (~624-636). `verify_object` computes `let computed_hash = *object_id.hash_bytes();` and never reads content (~554), yet its doc says "Verify an object's integrity and authenticity". `path_diagnose` always returns NoAvailablePaths (~639-647).
2. `crate::net::atp::sdk` session (src/net/atp/sdk/transfer.rs): send/receive/sync/stream/resume/cancel return `NotImplemented` (~461, ~497, ~618, ~630); daemon paths refuse (~665, ~691, ~709). Its `verify_object` marks any file over 100 bytes whose last 10 bytes are zero and whose length is a multiple of 512 as `integrity_check_passed=false`. That covers every POSIX tar archive and many disk images, even when the SHA matches (~549-554). Empty files fail unless the PATH STRING contains "empty" (~544-545). It reads the whole object into memory although policy allows up to 10 GB (~519). Every method maps `cx.checkpoint()` Err to `AtpError::Platform(OperatingSystemError)` instead of Cancelled (~449-450, ~474-475, ~578-579, ~627-628, ~657-658, ~683-684, ~699-700).
This is the same fake-success class that qk02uw/4hifsd/tgx695 removed from the CLI.

## Fix (compatibility: signatures stay; behavior becomes truthful)
Fake successes become typed refusals (like the net SDK's NotImplemented), or delegate to the real native engine (`AtpSdk::native_transfers`). `verify_object` actually hashes content in bounded streaming reads and never uses content heuristics. Cancellation maps to Cancelled. Record which public surface is canonical (see R31).

## Tests
A tar file with a correct SHA verifies OK. A tampered file fails. `send_object` to an absent peer does not return Ok. Cancel on an unknown id returns an error. Cancellation surfaces as Cancelled. Old-red at 8525d7055.

title: Obligation seam D1: private Cx::try_register_obligation gateway (zero-alloc, no-state Cx passthrough, leak visible to the oracle)
description:
WHY: The plan (asupersync_plan_v4.md, obligations) says every reserved permit is a tracked obligation so region close can prove "no leaked permits" and the lab's futurelock/obligation-leak oracles can see them. In code only session-tracked permits (src/channel/session.rs) and IoOp register an ObligationKind; stock mpsc/oneshot/broadcast SendPermit and SemaphorePermit register nothing (zero ObligationKind refs in src/channel/mpsc.rs, oneshot.rs, broadcast.rs, src/sync/semaphore.rs). Both asupersync-gap-permits-as-obligations-cv5sqe and asupersync-gap-remote-handles-region-owned-udjmtx are blocked on the same missing seam: a way for a primitive holding only a `&Cx` to mint and resolve an obligation record in the runtime state WITHOUT allocating on the fast path and WITHOUT changing public signatures.

WHAT: private, crate-internal gateway on Cx: `Cx::try_register_obligation(&self, kind: ObligationKind, holder: TaskId) -> Option<ObligationToken>` returning None when the Cx carries no runtime state (LabRuntime and production both carry it; hand-built `Cx::new()` in tests does not -> today's untracked behaviour is preserved), `ObligationToken::commit(self, &Cx)`, `abort(self, &Cx)`, and a Drop that records a leak (never panics; leak surfaces through the existing obligation oracle and `Runtime::is_quiescent` accounting). Ids come from the existing obligation arena (src/record/obligation.rs, RuntimeState) — no Box, no Arc; token is Copy-sized (id + generation). Region close accounting counts these like every other obligation (pending_obligations already gates drain: see runtime/builder.rs work_is_drained). Document the seam in docs (obligations section) and in TESTING_FOR_AGENTS.md (how to assert no-leak in a test).

TESTS: register/commit, register/abort, register/drop-leak (oracle reports it; region close waits or reports per policy — match the existing IoOp semantics), no-state Cx returns None, 1M register/commit in a loop allocates zero (count allocations with the existing test allocator hook if present, else assert no heap growth via the arena len), LabRuntime obligation-leak oracle catches a leaked token.

ACCEPTANCE: seam merged with the tests green under test-internals + lab features; no public API change; zero-alloc proof cited; D2/D3/D4 unblocked.

NO-CLAIM: no primitive uses it yet.
acceptance_criteria: gateway + tests green (register/commit/abort/leak, no-state None, zero-alloc proof, lab oracle catches leak); no public API change

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
D1 DESIGN NOTE (SapphireHill, 2026-09-02) — read before implementing; the bead's "synchronous arena id from a bare &Cx" is not reachable as written.

Facts from the code:
- Unified (default) mode keeps the obligation table EMBEDDED: `RuntimeState.obligations: ObligationTable` (runtime/state.rs:1732); only opt-in sharded mode puts it behind `ShardedState.obligations: Arc<ContendedMutex<ObligationTable>>` (sharded_state.rs:176). Production tasks reach the state only through `RuntimeInner.state: Arc<Mutex<RuntimeState>>`; the LabRuntime owns `state: RuntimeState` by value and polls task futures from inside its own step, so a future polled by the lab has no path to `&mut RuntimeState` at all (the spawn path solves exactly this with the SpawnGateway MAILBOX, drained at step start).
- `Cx` carries `CxHandles` (private struct): `spawn_gateway: Option<Arc<SpawnGateway>>`, `pending_spawns: Option<Arc<PendingSpawnCounter>>` (a region-owned atomic counter shared into the Cx). `RuntimeState` builds every task Cx itself (`.with_spawn_gateway(self.spawn_gateway.clone())` at state.rs:3758/4105/4208), so a new handle can be attached at the same sites without any public signature change.
- All obligation mutation is already funnelled through `RuntimeState::create_obligation / commit_obligation / abort_obligation` (state.rs:4882/5326/5498) which do the holder/region checks, region `pending_obligations` accounting, trace events and leak escalation. The seam must route through these (one authoritative implementation), not around them.

Decision: DEFERRED-EXACT registration through an obligation mailbox, mirroring the spawn gateway.
1. `ObligationGateway` (crate-private, in runtime/obligation_mailbox.rs or next to spawn_mailbox.rs): a bounded, lock-free ring of Copy messages `{ op: Reserve|Commit|Abort|Leak, kind, holder: TaskId, region: RegionId, ticket: u64 }` plus the same `notify` hook the spawn gateway uses. Zero allocation after construction (fixed capacity; a full ring falls back to a Mutex<Vec> slow path counted in metrics, never dropped silently).
2. `Cx::try_register_obligation(&self, kind, holder) -> Option<ObligationToken>` (pub(crate)): returns None when the Cx has no gateway (hand-built `Cx::new()` in tests, today's behaviour preserved). Otherwise mints a `ticket` from a per-gateway AtomicU64, bumps the region's pending counter (an `Arc<PendingObligationCounter>` attached like `pending_spawns`, so region close / `is_quiescent` see the reservation IMMEDIATELY, before drain), posts Reserve, and returns `ObligationToken { ticket, kind, holder, region }` (Copy-sized, no Box/Arc).
3. `ObligationToken::commit(self, &Cx)` / `abort(self, &Cx)` post Commit/Abort; `Drop` of an unresolved token posts Leak (never panics). All three decrement the pending counter when the runtime applies them, not at post time, so a token that is posted-but-undrained still counts as pending.
4. The runtime drains the mailbox where it drains spawn admissions (LabRuntime::drain_spawn_admissions site; production scheduler's admission drain): Reserve -> `state.create_obligation(kind, holder, region, None)` and records ticket->ObligationId in a small table; Commit/Abort -> `commit_obligation`/`abort_obligation`; Leak -> `mark_leaked` + the existing ObligationLeakResponse path (oracle sees it). Ordering is deterministic in the lab (drained at step start, ticket order).
5. Region close: `pending_obligations` accounting stays authoritative in RuntimeState; the counter only makes an in-flight reservation visible to `is_quiescent`/drain gating between post and drain (the same role `PendingSpawnCounter` plays for spawns: see runtime/builder.rs work_is_drained).

Tests to write (unchanged in spirit): register/commit, register/abort, register/drop-leak (lab oracle reports it), no-gateway Cx returns None, 1M register/commit in a loop with zero heap growth after warm-up (measure with the existing allocation counter if present, else assert ring capacity is never exceeded and the slow path counter stays 0), LabRuntime obligation-leak oracle catches a leaked token, region close waits for an undrained reservation.

Why not the synchronous variant: it needs either the embedded table behind its own lock in Unified mode (a runtime-core refactor that the 8fuxnt gate deliberately left opt-in) or an ambient/unsafe "current state" pointer during polls (forbidden by the capability model and the unsafe ledger). The mailbox keeps zero-alloc, keeps Cx signatures, keeps the lab deterministic, and keeps the lab oracle in the loop. Implementation follows once the round-6 verification batch (A2, G1, G2, I2, B1, B2) lands.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text: D1 FOLLOW-UP (SapphireHill, 2026-09-03): the macOS full-suite run of the round-6 tree (mac-mini-max, 22234 passed / 1 failed / 23 ignored) failed exactly one test, `runtime::obligation_mailbox::tests::dropping_an_unresolved_token_is_recorded_as_a_leak`, at the `leak_count() >= 1` assertion. Root cause (real gap, not a test bug): `apply_obligation_posts` routed `ObligationOp::Leak` to `RuntimeState::mark_obligation_leaked`, which resolves the record and emits the trace event but never reaches `handle_obligation_leaks` — no `leak_count` increment, no `LeakEscalation` threshold check, no `Recover` auto-abort. The completion-time sweep then found nothing pending (the record was already marked leaked), so a dropped token was invisible to the leak policy. Fix: `RuntimeState::report_obligation_leak(id)` (pub(crate)) snapshots the pending record and hands it to `handle_obligation_leaks` with the same sharded/embedded target shapes as `mark_obligation_leaked`; the mailbox `Leak` arm uses it. Tests: the existing test now asserts `leak_count() == 1` and exactly one `ObligationLeak` trace event; a new test with `LeakEscalation::new(1, Recover)` proves the dropped token is auto-aborted (one `ObligationAbort` event, no `ObligationLeak`, pending 0, quiescent). title: Browser WebTransport datagram inbox and pending-write queues are unbounded
description:
## Defect (browser audit, verified)
The read loop pushes every datagram into `state.inbox` with no cap (packages/browser-core/index.js ~707-714, ~825-850), and `webtransport_send` appends to `pendingWrites` with no cap (~1300). A fast server or a slow consumer causes unbounded memory growth. The stream side has a 64-stream limit and 1 MiB writes; datagrams do not.

## Fix
Bounded queues with an explicit overflow policy (drop-oldest with a counter, or backpressure/refusal with a typed error), documented. Node tests plus a browser test if available.

title: Release decision: publish a 0.5.1 carrying the remote defects fixed only on main (V3 reply decode, RemoteCap across child regions)
description:
## Context (distributed audit, verified by commit history)
Two production defects shipped in v0.5.0 (crates.io, 2026-09-12) and are fixed only on main:
- `RemoteComputationClient::call` with a V3 request delivered and executed the work, then failed to decode the V3 `Accepted` reply ("missing field response"), so the caller got an ambiguous exchange error after remote execution (fix 7883e09ee, 09-22). `call_once` at v0.5.0 has no V3 branch.
- `open_child_region` dropped the caller's `RemoteCap`, so `run_remote` never dispatched (`NoRemoteRuntime`) (fix 479d67ed6, 09-22).
Neither fix has a CHANGELOG entry. Main is 615+ commits past v0.5.0, with a 0.6.0 version bump and large unexecuted additions, so releasing main as-is is not a patch.

Cut 0.5.1 from v0.5.0 plus these fixes (cherry-pick onto a release commit on main's history, per the no-branch rule; the release mechanics must respect AGENTS RULE 2, e.g. DSR from a tagged commit), or accept that 0.5.x users stay broken until 0.6.0.

title: Escaped defect: identify the real 0.5.0 public-API/behavior break (CHANGELOG blames an unchanged Outcome Debug derive) and add a public-surface diff lane
description:
## Context (governance audit, verified by reading)
CHANGELOG's 0.6.0 section documents a "silent, source-breaking change" in 0.5.0 attributed to `Outcome<T, E>`'s conditional `Debug` derive, which broke a downstream consumer (mcp_agent_mail_rust per the audit). But the derive is identical at v0.4.3 (src/types/outcome.rs ~217). So the real cause of that downstream break is unknown, and an unapproved break of the v0.4.3 surface may be live in 0.5.0. AGENTS' escaped-defect protocol (reproduce through the same public API; parked-state witness where relevant; old-red/new-green; census; gap analysis; downstream canary) was not followed. There is no bead. The only API drift guard, `tests/api_surface_map_contract.rs::api_surface_map_tracks_root_public_exports`, lists root export names only and is predicted red at HEAD (`desktop_profile`/`desktop_samples` since 09-14, `pub mod future` 09-22 are missing from the artifact). There is no cargo-semver-checks or rustdoc-JSON diff.

## Work
1. Build rustdoc JSON for v0.4.3, v0.4.11, v0.5.0 and HEAD, and diff the public items and signatures.
2. Reproduce the downstream failure with a minimal consumer through the same public API; identify the breaking change; decide with the owner (restore compatibility in 0.5.1 vs approve).
3. Add a public-surface diff lane (rustdoc JSON or cargo-semver-checks) to the validation lanes, and repair `api_surface_map_contract`.
4. Write the escaped-defect gap analysis (why the suite missed it).

## Acceptance
Root cause identified with a reproducer receipt. Owner decision recorded. The diff lane runs and fails on a planted break (negative control).

---
**Provenance and binding rules.** Created by the 2026-09-22 reality check (SapphireHill); see the "September 22 assessment" section of `ASUPERSYNC_BRIDGE_PLAN_2026-09-01.md`. Evidence base: main at `8525d70554dd7cb7ab02ea16b461c5a6767e9e01` unless another SHA is named. Line numbers are approximate (`~`) and will drift, so re-locate by symbol before editing.

AGENTS.md rules that bind this work:
- Work on `main` only; no branches or worktrees.
- No file deletion without explicit written owner permission.
- No scripted code edits.
- Preserve public API and documented behavior (v0.4.3 floor for 0.4.x; the 0.5/0.6 policy is pending the owner, see R35b). Prefer additive APIs; any break needs explicit owner approval.
- Execute proof only through the owner-authorized validation path (see G1). The default is `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec --base <sha> --clean-overlay --no-overlay -- cargo ... -j 8` with an isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. Never use local fallback unless G1 authorizes it.

**Closure requires a receipt:** commit SHA, exact command, worker, and per-target running/passed/failed/ignored/filtered counts. Running must be greater than 0, and named tests must be neither ignored nor filtered. A bug fix also needs an old-red receipt taken at a pre-fix commit. Tests must log structured detail (ids, states, timings) so that a failure can be diagnosed from the log alone. Self-waking mocks cannot prove cancel-waker paths; use never-waking parked futures.

ROOT CAUSE of the 0.5.0 downstream break (SapphireHill, 2026-09-24, established from source and lockfiles; no build was needed):

**It is not an asupersync API change.** Evidence chain:
1. `Cx::for_request`, `Cx::for_request_with_budget` and `Cx::for_testing` carry `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-internals"))]` at v0.4.3 (src/cx/cx.rs 4769/4782/4657), v0.4.9, v0.4.11 and v0.5.0 alike. The gating is unchanged. `default` features never included test-internals (v0.4.0..v0.5.0 all `["proc-macros", "nightly-outcome-try"]`), and no feature newly stopped implying it.
2. The downstream says it itself: mcp_agent_mail_rust b00eaa9b reads "main stopped compiling without dev-dependencies at e6220b80: asupersync 0.5 gates Cx::for_request*/for_testing behind `test-internals` … `--all-targets` feature unification masked the break". About 52 server/CLI production sites called `Cx::for_request*` at e6220b80^ (e.g. crates/mcp-agent-mail-cli/src/legacy.rs:1177).

Those sites compiled at 0.4.9 because a NORMAL dependency enabled the feature: **sqlmodel 0.4.0** has `asupersync = { version = "0.4.9", default-features = false, features = ["test-internals"] }` in [workspace.dependencies], used under [dependencies] by sqlmodel-core/-pool/-query/-schema/-frankensqlite. The downstream lock at e6220b80^ holds sqlmodel 0.4.0 on the same asupersync 0.4.9.
4. The upgrade commit e6220b80 moved to sqlmodel 0.5.0 on asupersync 0.5.0. sqlmodel_rust 580e66e ("keep test internals out of published dependencies") had removed the leak, so production builds lost `test-internals` and the constructors with it.

- The CHANGELOG correction paragraph (still saying "unidentified") is updated with the cause and the production alternatives (`Cx::current()`, `Runtime::request_cx_with_budget`). Landing is in flight.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
Read-only narrowing (SapphireHill, 2026-09-25, no build; scripts in /data/tmp/rc_20260922/):

1. Root exports (`root_exports_diff.py`, the same `pub mod`/`pub use` extraction as api_surface_map_contract, plus the `#[cfg]` on each item): v0.4.3 has 315, v0.4.11 and v0.5.0 have 369, origin/main has 372. Nothing was removed and no cfg changed. The break is not at the crate root.
2. Nominal `Debug` loss (`debug_loss.py`): I compared every `pub struct`/`pub enum` in src/, excluding bins and tests, between v0.4.3 and v0.5.0. A type counts as having `Debug` when it has a `derive(..Debug..)` or any `impl .. Debug for Name`. No type lost `Debug`. Three names disappeared: `BackpressureTestConfig` (mpsc.rs:4392) and `ZeroRttConfig`/`ZeroRttState` (h3_native.rs ~10200). All three sit in test-module regions.
3. So the CHANGELOG's mechanism, "`{:?}` of a whole Outcome whose Ok type is not Debug", can only have become newly reachable in 0.5.0 in one of two ways:
   (a) a public fn/method changed its Ok type to a type without `Debug`, for example a pooled handle returned where a `Debug` value used to be;
   (b) a generic `Debug` impl gained a bound.
   Neither shows up in a name-level scan. Item 1 of this bead, the rustdoc-JSON signature diff, is required. Name lists cannot settle it.
4. Feasibility of the diff lane: `rch exec --job --result-dir <dir>` runs a non-compilation job and syncs the named directory back even on a nonzero exit. The pinned nightly (2026-08-31) emits rustdoc JSON (`-Zunstable-options --output-format json`). Build both sides with the same toolchain so the format_version matches. The crates.io 0.4.3 package can be documented as a dependency, which avoids needing v0.4.3 history on the worker.
5. Item 3's "repair api_surface_map_contract" is not a local fix. `python3 scripts/generate_api_surface_map.py --check` is red on origin/main (eddfdf39f). The artifact lacks three root exports, all deliberate and additive: `desktop_profile` and `desktop_samples` (0967799e0, 09-14, feature-gated) and `future` (ae86e6fbe, 09-22, a convenience re-export). Regenerating it is correct in substance, but the artifact's bytes are hash-pinned (sha256 3b63065b...) by 8 other inventories: hex, regex_privacy, scenario_yaml, signal_boundary, x509_validation_ownership, xattr_boundary, futures_lite and nkey_normative_spec. The capability registry also pins its semantic_sha256. Refreshing it breaks all of those pins, so the owners must re-pin in one coordinated change, or switch those pins to semantic ones. Owner decision needed. I did NOT regenerate it.
6. So the rustdoc diff should be a standalone lane with no artifact: extraction and diff only, exiting nonzero on removals or breaking additions, with a negative control on fixtures. Prototype: /data/tmp/rc_20260922/apidiff/surface.py.

## Rustdoc-JSON diff results (SapphireHill, 2026-09-25 ~19:45Z)
Method: rustdoc JSON (format_version 61, nightly-2026-08-31, DEFAULT features) built on RCH workers from the crates.io packages of 0.4.3 and 0.5.0 and from the codeload tarball of main eddfdf39f. Normalizer: /data/tmp/rc_20260922/apidiff/surface.py. It records every public path (pub mod + pub use), signature, public field, variant, trait item, inherent method and trait impl, auto traits included, with the impl's generics. The diff classifies facts as REMOVED (the identity is gone), BREAKING ADDITION (a new required trait item, a field on a constructible struct, a variant on an exhaustive enum) or CHANGED (same identity, different signature). Negative control: a fixture with a planted Debug loss, a new required trait fn and a changed return type gives exit 1 with all three flagged; a self-diff gives exit 0. Surfaces: v0.4.3 202,285 facts; v0.5.0 207,341; main 213,351.

Shipped in 0.5.0 (v0.4.3 -> v0.5.0):
- security::AuthKey lost StructuralPartialEq (PartialEq no longer derived), so AuthKey constants cannot be used as match patterns.
- time::TimerDriver<T> lost UnwindSafe; web::websocket::WebSocketUpgrade lost UnwindSafe and RefUnwindSafe.
- runtime::spawn_mailbox::LocalSpawnRequest.on_admission_error and .on_unadmitted_cancel changed type (AdmissionErrorFn -> LocalAdmissionErrorFn, UnadmittedCancelFn -> LocalUnadmittedCancelFn) on a constructible public struct.
- (harmless) http::h1::IncomingBodyWriter no longer implements Drop.
- 222 changed facts are signature-neutral: 92 are only the `impl<'scope, P>` headers of Scope methods, and the rest are relaxations. AsyncCxFnHandler1-8 moved to PhantomData<fn() -> T>, so Send/Sync no longer require the T's, and the Handler impls dropped `T: Sync`.

On main since 0.5.0 (unreleased, still fixable before 0.6.0):
- net::atp::protocol::QuicFrame, an exhaustive public enum at 2 paths, gained NewConnectionId, NewToken and RetireConnectionId. That breaks downstream exhaustive matches.
- net/web ServerWebSocket<IO> lost UnwindSafe and RefUnwindSafe; messaging::kafka::TransactionalProducer lost UnwindSafe.

The Outcome/Debug break is NOT in the default surface: no Debug impl disappeared and no Ok type changed. The consumer (mcp_agent_mail_rust e6220b80) moved 0.4.9 -> 0.5.0 with features tls-webpki-roots (implies tls) + test-internals. The same diff for that path and feature set is running (job_rustdoc_feat.sh). Also check sqlmodel 0.5.0, upgraded in the same commit, as the source of the non-Debug pooled handle.
- Downstream pieces ruled out (read-only): sqlmodel_rust Pool::acquire returns Outcome<PooledConnection<C>, Error> identically at v0.4.3 and HEAD 0.5.0, and `impl<C: Connection + Debug> Debug for PooledConnection<C>` exists in both. FrankenSQLite's `Connection` implements Debug at both v0.3.18 and v0.4.4. So none of the three upgraded crates removed a Debug that the CHANGELOG mechanism needs. Unless the feature-matched diff finds one, the CHANGELOG 0.6.0 note misattributes the E0277 to a 0.5.0 change. More likely the consumer's own non-Debug Ok type met a new or edited `{:?}` in its tests. The note's advice (match the variants) is still correct; its "landed in 0.5.0" claim is not supported.

## Root causes of the auto-trait losses (read-only; owner decides whether 0.6.0 restores them)
- `time::TimerDriverHandle` is `Arc<dyn NativeTimerDriverApi>`. It was `Arc<dyn TimerDriverApi>` at v0.4.3, so it has always been !UnwindSafe/!RefUnwindSafe, because the trait object carries no RefUnwindSafe bound. Every public type that newly holds a handle loses UnwindSafe. Since 0.5.0 that includes `ServerWebSocket<IO>`, through its new `heartbeat: Heartbeat { clock: Option<TimerDriverHandle> }` field (5cc3a89f1, .120).
- Candidate remedy, additive: `impl UnwindSafe for TimerDriverHandle {}` and `impl RefUnwindSafe for TimerDriverHandle {}`. The claim is honest for the current driver: `process_timers` collects expired wakers under the wheel lock, releases it, and then calls each waker inside `catch_unwind`, and deadline reactors are woken the same way. No user code runs inside a driver critical section, so a caught panic cannot leave the wheel half-updated. tokio makes the same assertion for its runtime `Handle`.
- The other losses have separate causes. Each needs its own look before any assertion: `WebSocketUpgrade` (candidates are the `origin_policy: OriginPolicy` or `http1_upgrade_slot: Option<Http1UpgradeSlot>` fields), grpc `Channel`/`ChannelBuilder` (tls), kafka `TransactionalProducer`, and `TimerDriver<T>`, which lost even its conditional impl in 0.5.0, probably through `deadline_reactors: Mutex<Vec<Arc<dyn ...>>>`.
- `QuicFrame` (net::atp::protocol) is a wire-protocol enum that grew 3 variants for connection migration. Marking it `#[non_exhaustive]` stops future additions from breaking anyone, but it is itself a one-time break for exhaustive matches. Owner call for 0.6.0.

## Reconciliation with the CHANGELOG's 2026-09-24 root cause
The CHANGELOG 0.6.0 note already records, as of 2026-09-24, that the consumer's break came from `sqlmodel` 0.4 leaking `asupersync/test-internals` into normal dependencies. Production code relied on the test-only `Cx::for_request*` / `Cx::for_testing` constructors, and sqlmodel 0.5 stopped leaking the feature (580e66e). The rustdoc diff corroborates this. On the consumer path (0.4.9 -> 0.5.0, features tls + test-internals) nothing about those constructors changed, and no Debug/Outcome fact changed. The E0277 therefore did not come from an asupersync API change.
What the diff adds is the REAL surface drift that no one had listed (sections above). AGENTS requires release-note coverage and an owner decision for each: restore before 0.6.0, or approve and document. Suggested order:
(1) the unreleased QuicFrame variants (decide #[non_exhaustive] now, before a second release freezes the exhaustive shape);
(2) the TimerDriverHandle UnwindSafe/RefUnwindSafe impls, an additive restore with the justification above;
(3) LocalSpawnRequest field types (probably an internal-only struct that is `pub` by accident: consider #[doc(hidden)] or pub(crate) via semver process);
(4) AuthKey StructuralPartialEq, which was probably deliberate (constant-time eq). If so, approve and document it.
Lane: scripts/public_api_diff.py + tests/public_api_diff_contract.rs (batch 4, landing).

title: Obligation seam D2: mpsc/oneshot/broadcast SendPermit reserve/send/abort register runtime obligations
description:
WHY: The two-phase channel contract (reserve -> send / abort) is the project's flagship cancel-correctness claim; a reserved SendPermit that is dropped without send is exactly the class of leak the obligation system exists to catch, yet stock mpsc/oneshot/broadcast permits are invisible to it (see D1 WHY). The onramp Level 3 example creates the obligation by hand, which is the documentation admitting the gap.

WHAT: in src/channel/mpsc.rs, oneshot.rs, broadcast.rs: `reserve(&cx)` (and `try_reserve`, `reserve_with_budget` variants) calls D1's `try_register_obligation(ObligationKind::SendPermit, task)`; `SendPermit::send` commits; `SendPermit::abort` / explicit drop-after-abort aborts; a permit dropped without send or abort leaks (recorded, not panicked; the oracle reports it; region close accounting follows the existing policy for leaked obligations). Permits obtained through a state-less Cx behave exactly as today. Public signatures unchanged (the token lives inside the permit struct; struct is not exhaustively constructible publicly — verify, else keep it behind a private field type that already exists).

title: Proof-status freshness time bomb: two fresh rows expire 2026-09-23 00:00 UTC; demotion trips hard-coded fresh-rch-pass assertions
description:

Do not fabricate a rerun or change clocks. Make contract tests take "now" from an explicit input in their assertions, so that a run is reproducible and the freshness check is a separate, explicit lane.

comments.text:
SapphireHill 10-01, status of each item at origin/main 5a081fb66:

1. scripts/run_raptorq_e2e.sh zero-test PASS.
   - CORRECTION to the 09-22 claim: today RQ-E2E-REPORT-DETERMINISM does select its test without extra features. The asupersync-conformance dev-dependency enables test-internals on asupersync through feature unification, so the gated pipeline_e2e module compiles in every test build.
   - Receipt RQnofeat (5a081fb66, vmi1227854): `cargo test --test raptorq_conformance e2e_pipeline_reports_are_deterministic` gives pipeline_e2e::e2e_pipeline_reports_are_deterministic ok, 1 passed, 73 filtered out.
   - The structural hole remains: the script marks a scenario PASS on rc=0 whatever it ran, so a renamed test or a lost feature turns that scenario into a silent 0-test PASS.
   - Fix (landing with this comment): a scenario whose libtest summary shows 0 passed FAILS ("zero tests ran for filter ..."), and the PASS line prints the summary count.
   - Control, local: a fake RCH_BIN replays libtest output (/data/tmp/rc_20260922/rqctl). With zero selection the old script gives 5/5 PASS, exit 0, and the new one 5/5 FAIL, exit 1. With real selection the new script passes.
2. tests/conformance/raptorq_differential: still self-comparing. our_implementation() returns fixture.reference_output.clone(). The crate also has no fixtures on disk and is not built by any target or lane. Its Cargo.toml says the asupersync path dependency is blocked by a lint mismatch (dagagh). A real fix needs libraptorq-generated fixtures plus the path dependency; until then it should not be cited as differential evidence. Not changed.
3. atp_cli_journey: still a simulation. scripts/atp_user_journey/push_artifact_cli_daemon.sh stages and "delivers" the payload with cp/mv (~274-275, ~360-365), and no binary runs. A real CLI journey now exists elsewhere: src/bin/asupersync.rs test atp_serve_and_send_move_a_file_over_loopback (c9b415207) runs `atp serve` and `atp send` and checks the received bytes. Replacing the script's cp/mv with those two commands is the remaining work. Until then, tests/atp_cli_journey.rs should not be cited as CLI-to-daemon evidence.
4. Conformance registry hollow modules.
   - websocket_rfc6455: FIXED (9b38fd3cd + 184373e2d, merged as 12f8943a8). Six of the eight live submodules were `timed_test(|| Ok(()))` stubs counted as MUST passes. Meanwhile ~35 real close/status-code/control tests sat in the legacy tests/conformance/websocket_rfc6455.rs, which no target compiles. Those tests are ported, plus real masking, fragmentation, control and extension tests: 59 against production code.
   - The suite's 95% MUST gate is now "every MUST passes, each failure named". The real tests found a production RFC 6455 §7.1.7 violation, 7w5t34, fixed in 9b38fd3cd: data was still delivered after an assembly failure had failed the connection.
   - Receipts: control 23887ceb6 red on exactly 7.1.7; candidate all 67 MUST pass; the 10 websocket targets 91/0; lib net::websocket 287/0; exact-tip 184373e2d websocket tests 377/0; check --all-targets green.
   - quic_retry_rfc9000 "integrity": the module only round-trips placeholder tags through the quic_core codec, which is a legitimate codec check. The real tag computation, handshake_driver::retry_integrity_tag (pub(crate)), is proven by the lib test retry_integrity_tag_matches_rfc_9001_appendix_a4. The module's IntegrityValidation label overstates what it checks; the proof exists elsewhere.
   - dns_message: confirmed hollow. 70 KB, no asupersync import; every test parses with local model helpers. Rewiring it to the production parser hooks (parse_dns_response_for_fuzz / decode_dns_name_for_fuzz, test-internals) is in progress.
   - tls_0rtt and kqueue_bsd_events: not examined in this pass.

comments.text:
SapphireHill 10-01: three test targets that the watchdog rotation at ec0d493d6 ran for the first time now test real behaviour. Landed in 29bc8fab8 (landed on main in 6c3f07b43) (merge over the peer's 8458bca00; disjoint files).

1. tls_conformance (adca80477): three stale tests fixed.
   - handshake_rejects_self_signed_without_root: the builder already refuses a client with no roots (TlsError::Certificate "no root certificates configured"); the test asserts that refusal.
   - acceptor_build_rejects_empty_certificate_chain: production says "certificate chain is empty".
   - alpn_required_mismatch_fails: with no protocol in common, the server aborts with no_application_protocol (RFC 7301), so the client sees TlsError::Handshake. The pinned unit test tls::acceptor::tests::test_alpn_required_client_errors_on_no_overlap requires that, so production stays as it is. The require_alpn doc now names both outcomes. A typed error for the no-overlap case would need an owner decision.
   - Receipts: old red 62/3 (watchdog, ovh-a); candidate 65/0 plus tls_pin_mismatch_e2e 2/0, lib tls:: 209/0, check --all-targets --features tls, clippy clean.
2. scheduler_lane_ordering_metamorphic::test_edf_ordering_basic (037e0174b): it compared dispatched tasks with the deadlines in injection order, so correct EDF dispatch failed it and a wrong order could pass. It now pairs each task id with its own deadline and requires all three to dispatch. Candidate 11/0 (hz4, test-internals+tls); mutation control (timed lane latest-deadline-first) red; clippy clean.
3. raptorq_decoder_metamorphic (37ba52791): every decode had failed with InsufficientSymbols because the suite never supplied the S + H constraint rows. MR2, MR5 and composite were red; MR1, MR3 and MR4 passed without decoding. The suite now prepends decoder.constraint_symbols(), fixes the MR5 underflow, and makes the MR1 and MR3 error branches assert. Candidate 20/0 (vmi1152480). Control (constraint rows mutated to zero): MR1, MR2, MR3, MR5 and composite red.
   - MR4 never ran at K = 1. That was fixed by v3 in the next landing (see the following comment).

Exact stack tip before the merge (tree 1cb71062a): cargo check --all-targets --keep-going, default features, ovh-a: green. The pre-push hook checked the merge tip.

Census note: kafka_record_batch_v2/mod.rs says it "ensures our producer batching and wire format handling conforms", but production uses librdkafka and has no RecordBatch codec. I did not relabel it: the Kafka provenance matrix (KAFKA-K0-4-PIN-015) hash-pins mod.rs and is currently fresh, and that matrix already classifies the module as RECORD-BATCH-LOCAL-MODEL. The header fix belongs to the matrix owner (sarszu.*) together with a re-pin.

comments.text:
SapphireHill 10-01, second landing (6c3f07b43, main = master):

1. raptorq_decoder_metamorphic v3 (b7312f375). Every relation ran at K = 1 (symbol_size 512 on 256..512-byte objects), and MR4 never ran: its K + 10 guard never held.
   - It now uses symbol_size 16, so K = 16..32, and MR4 decodes random (K + 2)-subsets, failing closed on its premises.
   - Control (constraint rows mutated to zero): all six relations red, MR4 included ("K = 16, 6 source symbols dropped").
   - A 4096-case probe ran 12,288 MR4 subset decodes with 0 failures.
2. Item 3, the atp_cli_journey simulation, FIXED (e7c585c5a).
   - The journey now runs the real `asupersync` binary: `atp serve` on 127.0.0.1:0, then `atp send` of a ~784 KB artifact. It checks the committed inbox bytes and SHA-256 against the source. With no binary it refuses (exit 2); there is no cp/mv fallback.
   - The target is registered with required-features = ["cli"].
   - Control (the receiver flips the first byte it writes): the new journey goes 3 red, while the binary itself reports committed, sha_ok and merkle_ok. The OLD journey on the same corrupted receiver stayed 3/0 green.
3. Found through item 3:
   - transport_tcp::serve reported finished transfers up to 60 s late, and reported its own stop as a failed transfer. Fixed in 481b6f8e6, with old-red/new-green test tests/atp_tcp_serve_prompt_report.rs (two controls, one per fix).
   - atp serve has no SIGTERM handling: filed ylvfod.
4. Census note on 52hxjz (oracle truth landed in 4de57ed1a): frankenlab and `asupersync lab run` now say how many checked oracles the lab runtime never feeds ("24/24 passed (16 not fed by the lab runtime)").

Still open on this bead:
- tls_0rtt: a production-backed rewrite is in lanes (31 RFC 8446 rows, 26 decided by asupersync::tls through real TLS 1.3 handshakes; defects filed as 0n1dvh).
- raptorq_differential: self-comparing; blocked on dagagh fixtures.
- kafka_record_batch_v2 header: owner re-pin.
- quic_retry label.

The test certificate time bombs found while doing this are kjyh84; the 2027-01-28 cert is fixed in 0c8ceb714.

title: Main watchdog: every new main commit gets an authorized-path check and targeted tests; red files a P0 naming commit and author identity
description:
## Why
GitHub Actions has been disabled at the repository level since ~2026-09-07 (`actions/permissions` → `enabled:false`; the `CI` workflow has zero successful runs in its history). The pre-push hook covers only local pushes. 209 of 471 non-merge commits since 09-15 came from the GitHub-API/web identity `35050222+Dicklesworthstone@users.noreply.github.com`, which bypasses local hooks. 157 of that identity's commits declare they were never compiled. Main was red several times in that window and was healed only when someone happened to notice (e.g. 234d0eee9, 37869620e, 73ee23325). Nothing watches main.

## What to build (an agent-run loop, e.g. /loop or a scheduled agent; no GitHub Actions needed)
For each new commit on `origin/main` since the last receipt:
1. `cargo check --all-targets --keep-going` (default) and `--all-features`, both via `rch exec --base <sha> --clean-overlay --no-overlay` (or the G1-authorized path).
2. The native cancellation contract `--test runtime_abort_vs_cancel_semantics_audit`.
3. Targeted tests for the touched area: map changed paths to test targets, including feature-gated ones via the G3 census mapping.
4. Post a receipt comment (SHA, commands, worker, counts) on the bead(s) the commit cites. If it cites none, record that in a daily summary.
5. On red: file a P0 bug bead titled with the commit, author identity, failing target and first error, and ping Agent Mail if reachable. Do not revert or edit others' code automatically.
6. Flag commits whose body says "not compiled/executed" (proof-class inflation) in the daily summary.
7. Maintain the refresh's exit metrics: % of commits green within 2 h, beadless code commits, orphan count, P0/P1 count, and stale in_progress count.
Batch commits when the fleet is busy (check the newest commit plus a bisect on red) to stay within RCH admission limits (one asupersync lane per worker; hz3/hz4 need `-j 8`/`-j 10`).

## Acceptance
It runs unattended for 72 h. Every main commit in that window is covered, directly or by a batch. A planted red commit on a test fixture (without pushing broken code to main, e.g. the watchdog's own dry-run mode against a synthetic SHA list) produces a P0 bead. A daily summary is recorded in this bead.

- Preserve public API and documented behavior (v0.4.3 floor for 0.4.x; the 0.5/0.6 policy is pending the owner, see R35b). Prefer additive APIs; any break needs explicit owner approval.
- Execute proof only through the owner-authorized validation path (see G1). The default is `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec --base <sha> --clean-overlay --no-overlay -- cargo ... -j 8` with an isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. Never use local fallback unless G1 authorizes it.

**Closure requires a receipt:** commit SHA, exact command, worker, and per-target running/passed/failed/ignored/filtered counts. Running must be greater than 0, and named tests must be neither ignored nor filtered. A bug fix also needs an old-red receipt taken at a pre-fix commit. Tests must log structured detail (ids, states, timings) so that a failure can be diagnosed from the log alone. Self-waking mocks cannot prove cancel-waker paths; use never-waking parked futures.

comments.text: 2026-10-09: the watchdog's tracker writes now use `br --no-db` (scripts/main_watchdog.py, the BR constant). In DB mode they had been landing only in this checkout's beads.db. Local agents write issues.jsonl with --no-db and never import, so the DB fell behind, and from early Oct 8 br refused every export ('Refusing to export stale database that would lose issues'). bi2462.147.103 through .122 and about 40 receipt comments sat DB-only for a day; they were published in 435d9811e after an import, flush and id-level audit. That import also showed br's import resolves a whole row by updated_at, so a newer local receipt had made stale DB rows win on 1sngsf and 5f1fcj; both were restored by union. Probe on a scratch copy: create (parent, labels, --json id continues the .N sequence), comments add -f and -m, and close --reason --actor all work with --no-db and write the JSONL directly.

title: Watchdog: stranded-work alarm, duplicate-fix detector, API-lane heal latency, first-run ledger, decision ledger
description:
## Why (reality check 2026-09-23, findings S8-S10)
The watchdog (bi2462.147) detects red commits. The September 23 assessment found three failure modes it does not yet
cover, each of which cost the swarm a day:
1. Stranded work: the shared tree's `main` was 4 commits ahead / 16 behind origin for 32 hours, holding RCH-receipted
   fixes for R16 (bi2462.91) that no one could see on origin (details in R61).
2. Duplicate fixes: R22a was fixed twice (409a695d8 vs local 4aab18400, identical predicate), the replay_connect_native
   compile break was fixed twice (a01270e7a vs local), and a second R26a patch is in flight locally beside e1df06645.
3. Unhealed API-lane code: every API commit since 09-22 carried no receipt; defects surfaced only when the reality check
   ran them (R56, R57, R58). New test targets had never run (56 targets added since 09-15).

## Work (extend scripts/main_watchdog.py once bi2462.147 lands; stdlib only; never reverts, edits or pushes code)
1. Stranded-work report: for the shared tree at /data/projects/asupersync, record `git rev-list --count
   origin/main..main` and `main..origin/main`, the age and bead citations of the oldest unpushed commit, and dirty paths
   by last-modified age. Alert (bead comment on the cited bead + Agent Mail when reachable) when unpushed work is older
   than 2 h or the tree is more than 5 commits behind origin.
2. Duplicate-fix detector: flag pairs of (commit on origin, commit or uncommitted diff locally) that cite the same bead
   id or modify overlapping hunks of the same file within the last 72 h.
3. API-lane heal latency: for every commit by the API identity, the time from landing to its first green receipt, and
   the list of such commits with no receipt after 2 h (P0 bead after 6 h, naming the commit).
4. First-run ledger: every `tests/*.rs` target added since a baseline SHA, with whether it has ever executed (selected
   > 0 tests) in a watchdog lane; include the count in the daily summary.
5. Decision ledger: beads whose comments record an owner decision with no implementation commit after 48 h.

## Acceptance
- `python3 scripts/main_watchdog.py evaluate` scenarios (the existing dry-run mode) cover: a 2-commit-ahead shared tree
  older than 2 h (alert), a duplicate fix citing the same bead (flag), an API commit with no receipt after 2 h (listed)
  and after 6 h (bead payload printed), a never-run new test target (listed). Each scenario has a negative twin that
  must stay silent.
- A contract test in tests/main_watchdog_contract.rs (or the bead-147 test file) pins those scenario outputs.
- One live `summary` run posted as a comment here with real numbers.
close_reason: items 1-5 landed (5ad0f40aa, cd1349c78 via de2230584); contract 18/0; live summary posted

Also flag API-lane Rust commits that cite no bead (the policy requires one). Between block_on calls the current-thread background pump drains region commands, so when it wins, the RegisterFinalizer requests are APPLIED rather than queued. comments.text: SapphireHill: lane tlib, the exact watchdog targeted-lib command on a764e10eb (RCH, --features mysql,tls): 1236 passed, 2 failed. Still red: redis_native_caller_and_driver_cancel_parked_transports and redis_native_dropped_pipeline_closes_partial_write_and_releases_pool_slot. Both panic at src/messaging/redis_tests.rs:361, closed.unwrap() on Err(Timeout): the controller's 4 s wait for the fake peer's close verdict expired. The first variant (CommandWrite, current_thread, caller cancel) already fails. Before that point, done, expected Cancelled, registrations retired, pool active/total/waiters 0 all passed. So the cancel is observed and the pool slot is released, but the peer does not finish its read loop within 4 s even though its reads time out after 3 s. That points to data still flowing after the cancel, or a late close. The test and fix came together in 359d60a91 (API lane, uncompiled, 09-26 05:36Z) and have never passed. Probe 960fc32de logs peer bytes and timing with a 20 s wait. I own the heal (bead assignee and watchdog operator).

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE (test harness, not the Redis fix). Probe 960fc32de (a764e10eb with peer timing logs and a 20 s wait), CommandWrite, current_thread, caller cancel: 'PROBE peer CommandWrite end=eof closed=true received=3866616 reads=123 elapsed=25.311004531s'. The cancelled write DOES close its transport (EOF), and only 3.87 MB of the 16 MiB command escaped, so 359d60a91's cancellation works. But the peer set a 16 KiB receive buffer to park the client's write and kept it for the verdict. Draining the ~3.9 MB the client had queued then crawled through zero-window probing (about 32 KB per ~200 ms, 25 s total), far past the controller's 4 s budget. Fix, series tip S4 c99d81275: once the verdict phase starts (release), the peer opens its receive buffer to 8 MiB, so the backlog drains at loopback speed before EOF. Both assertions keep their meaning: the transport must close before the owners drop, and the full command must not escape. Lane p4lib runs messaging::redis::tests::redis_ (including the TLS variants) with --features tls.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text: LOSS: raising the peer's SO_RCVBUF to 8 MiB for the verdict did not speed the drain. Lane p4lib (c99d81275, --features tls) still fails both tests at :368 with the same 25.27 s.    - Red: 89f584086 (vmi1227854), ed38df0fb (vmi1152480) and dba315307 (vmi1153651). ed38df0fb and dba315307 are both beads-only.

3. Two different signatures:

This is exactly r02ssd, which the peer filed with a root cause: the receiver commits, then gives up delivering its Proof after 4 silent PTO rounds (proof_wait_exhausted attempts=4).
   - (b) dba315307: both sides fail at exactly 20 s, sender Timeout "quic client handshake" and receiver Err(Timeout "quic server accept handshake"). The stall-PTO test printed total_packets=0, so no data phase started. The handshake packets themselves are protected: the proxy's first 64 packets pass with no loss and no delay.

The receiver's accept clock therefore starts while the sender is still preparing: the pass-1 checkpoint loop, then a spawn_blocking stat/xattr pass over 2000 members, then the read/hash/pack build pass. If sender prep exceeds 20 s on a loaded worker, the server's accept deadline expires first. The client's handshake then waits its own 20 s with no server, so both sides fail at exactly 20 s.

Not claiming: the peer owns r02ssd and is working in this exact test family (SC/SC2, nnm3gw). This P0 should close with the r02ssd fix plus a fix for signature (b), backed by a repeated green receipt of both tests.

comments.text:
SapphireHill, 2026-10-01: HEALED and landed in 04b6bc28f (main=master=f8e748293).

Root cause: the test's oracle raced with itself; the runtime was not at fault. BudgetedFinalizer::retire drops the user finalizer, together with its OwnedMutexGuard, before the finalizer task reports Ready. But the generation-2 factory checked `resources.iter().all(|r| r.try_lock_owned().is_ok())`, and that takes each lock. Concurrent replacements, under OneForAll and RestForOne on the 2 sharded workers, and the test thread's own post-close try_lock_owned probe made each other fail. That explains the flake on the beads-only commit 5ded50015 while its parent 83d467e31 was green.

The fix is in the test only: each held finalizer also owns a per-child Arc lease, and the factory asserts every lease's strong_count == 1, which takes no lock.

- Old oracle + the test-thread probe held for 200 ms (d4a2b2afa, ovh-a): RED, 6 passed and 2 failed. Both native_current_thread_ and native_sharded_managed_replacement_waits_for_registered_finalizers failed with the watchdog's exact signature (builder.rs:12484, then generation 3).

- Exact landed tree for the test file: stack tip 390c9389c (hz2), the watchdog's targeted-lib command (--features tls, the same module filters) plus sync::pool: 890 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored (the same 4 the watchdog ignores). Both replacement tests passed.

title: Lab/native differential harness for kernel semantics (same program, three runtimes, same outcome class)
description:
## Why (test-blindness class B2)
Several 09-22 defects exist only because a behavior was proven in LabRuntime and assumed on native. (1) The panic-path loser drain in `Scope::race`/`race_all`/`hedge`: the lab never sets `CURRENT_WORKER_ID`, so the lab takes a "no scheduler" branch that records a drain that never happened (R29c). (2) The default UCB1/Lyapunov reward reads `RuntimeState::now`, which only the lab advances (R18a). (3) Production schedule capture is not implemented while lab replay tests pass (R19a/b). LabScheduler is a separate single-threaded model, not the production three-lane scheduler (src/lab/runtime.rs ~5742), with a fixed cancel-streak limit of 16 while production defaults to the adaptive selector.

## Build
A scenario table (one Rust test module, default lab lane) in which each scenario is a function `fn(&Cx) -> Observation`. It runs on LabRuntime (N seeds), native current-thread, and native multi-worker (4 workers, repeated M times). `Observation` records terminal outcome kinds per task, cancellation reasons/attribution, finalizer run counts and order where specified, obligation conservation (reserved/committed/aborted/leaked), and region close outcome. Divergence between runtimes is a failure, except for explicitly declared schedule-dependent fields.
Scenarios (minimum): spawn/join; `race!` with a parked cancel-aware loser (closure form after R37) and with a panicking winner; quorum; `Scope::hedge`/Cx hedge; pipeline and map-reduce with an error in stage k; region close with a pending finalizer and a reserved permit; cancel before first poll; abort of a task parked on mutex/mpsc/semaphore; `#[main]`-style root drain.

## Acceptance
The harness is in the default test lane with counts recorded. It detects R29c at 8525d7055 (old-red: lab and native disagree), and scenario count ≥ 12. Logs show per-runtime observations side by side on failure.

---
**Provenance and binding rules.** Created by the 2026-09-22 reality check (SapphireHill); see the "September 22 assessment" section of `ASUPERSYNC_BRIDGE_PLAN_2026-09-01.md`. Evidence base: main at `8525d70554dd7cb7ab02ea16b461c5a6767e9e01` unless another SHA is named. Line numbers are approximate (`~`) and will drift, so re-locate by symbol before editing.

AGENTS.md rules that bind this work:
- Work on `main` only; no branches or worktrees.
- No file deletion without explicit written owner permission.
- No scripted code edits.
- Preserve public API and documented behavior (v0.4.3 floor for 0.4.x; the 0.5/0.6 policy is pending the owner, see R35b). Prefer additive APIs; any break needs explicit owner approval.
- Execute proof only through the owner-authorized validation path (see G1). The default is `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec --base <sha> --clean-overlay --no-overlay -- cargo ... -j 8` with an isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. Never use local fallback unless G1 authorizes it.

**Closure requires a receipt:** commit SHA, exact command, worker, and per-target running/passed/failed/ignored/filtered counts. Running must be greater than 0, and named tests must be neither ignored nor filtered. A bug fix also needs an old-red receipt taken at a pre-fix commit. Tests must log structured detail (ids, states, timings) so that a failure can be diagnosed from the log alone. Self-waking mocks cannot prove cancel-waker paths; use never-waking parked futures.

SapphireHill 2026-09-30: landed in 12ace79cb as tests/kernel_semantics_differential.rs, a default-feature integration target that the default test lane and the watchdog rotation run.

Each of 17 scenarios runs 12 times: LabRuntime under six seeds (check_invariants required clean), native current-thread ×3, and native four-worker ×3. All 12 observations must agree, except fields a scenario declares schedule-dependent. On a divergence, every run's observation is printed side by side.

Scenarios, against the Build list:
- spawn/join.
- race with a parked cancel-aware loser; race with a panicking winner (R29c).
- race_all; quorum 2-of-3.
- hedge via Cx::hedge_drained_with, with a winning backup and with a panicking backup.
- first_ok.
- map_reduce with a failing item; a two-stage pipeline whose second stage rejects input 3.
- scope join of an ok task and a panicking task.
- region close releasing a permit held inside it; region close waiting for a cancelled task's pending cleanup.
- abort right after spawn (cancel before first poll; whether the body ran is declared schedule-dependent).
- abort of a task parked on a mutex, on an mpsc recv and on a semaphore.

Deviations from the Build list, stated in the module doc:
- Scope::hedge and Scope::defer_* (region finalizers) take &mut RuntimeState, which only the lab exposes. They cannot run on both runtimes.
- #[main]'s drain_root_region has no lab counterpart.
- The Cx hedge and the pending-cleanup region-close scenario cover what those share with native.
- Observation records outcome kinds, cancellation kinds, drain-before-return and capacity/lock/permit recovery. Per-kind obligation counters are not compared, because the native side has no reserved/committed/aborted counts through a public API. Live and leaked obligations were proven separately on both runtimes (cv5sqe, 54cb51d08).

First finding: the pipeline scenario's outer outcome kind depends on the schedule. The typed error agreed in all 12 runs. The kind was err in 2 of 3 four-worker runs and cancelled in every other run (KDtest4 63f9644dd). PipelineExecutionReport documents this: draining a sibling cancelled mid-work strengthens Err into Cancelled, and error() keeps the typed error. So outcome_kind is declared schedule-dependent, while "err or cancelled" and the typed error stay compared. map_reduce's outcome is stable across all 12 runs. API users who branch on the pipeline's outcome kind rather than on error() get schedule-dependent behavior. That is by design, but it deserves a line in the pipeline's user docs if it surprises anyone.

Acceptance:
- In the default test lane, with counts: KDtest4 37d1813cf, 17 passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored / 0 filtered (hz4). Each of the 17 printed its agreed observation with runs=12.
- Detects R29c: the old-red comes from a reverted boundary, because RCH refuses a base as old as 8525d7055 (E413). Control C37d1813cf replaces the lab's ScopedSchedulerDriven guard around task polls with an immediately dropped one, which is the pre-bi2462.101 behavior. Result: 15 passed, 2 failed (hz4). The failures are exactly the two R29c-shaped scenarios, race_panicking_winner_still_drains_loser and hedge_panicking_backup_still_drains_the_primary. The hedge goes through Cx::hedge_drained_with, so the detector covers both combinators. In each side-by-side table, all six lab seeds report the loser drained=false and all six native runs report true.
- Scenario count ≥ 12: 17.
- Logs show per-runtime observations side by side on failure: yes (the control output above).

title: Mutation-backed proof for kernel hot spots (cargo-mutants restricted to named functions and their tests)
description:
## Why (test-blindness class B5)
Tests that cannot fail were a recurring 09-22 finding: the UCB1 "determinism golden" has no frozen expected values, and its cancel flood never affects the arm choice (a mutation control would have exposed it); the drain tests use self-waking losers; some Lean theorems are vacuous. A test should count as proof of a kernel property only if it kills the mutants that break that property.

## Work
Install `cargo-mutants` on an authorized worker (a dev tool, NOT a crate dependency; record the version). Run it restricted (`--file`/`--re`) to: `Cx::race_drained` and `Scope::race_all` (src/cx/cx.rs, scope.rs); the obligation mailbox admission path (src/runtime/obligation_mailbox.rs); the retirement barrier open/consume paths (task_handle.rs, three_lane.rs completion); the ManagedSupervisor restart loop (supervision.rs); the signal dispatcher registration (signal/signal.rs); the H2 RST/stream reset path. For each, name the tests intended to kill the mutants. Record the kill rate. File a gap bead for each surviving mutant that represents a real property.

## Acceptance
Per-target kill-rate table with the mutants-tool output retained. Surviving property-relevant mutants have beads. The run is repeatable via a documented command.

---
**Provenance and binding rules.** Created by the 2026-09-22 reality check (SapphireHill); see the "September 22 assessment" section of `ASUPERSYNC_BRIDGE_PLAN_2026-09-01.md`. Evidence base: main at `8525d70554dd7cb7ab02ea16b461c5a6767e9e01` unless another SHA is named. Line numbers are approximate (`~`) and will drift, so re-locate by symbol before editing.

- Preserve public API and documented behavior (v0.4.3 floor for 0.4.x; the 0.5/0.6 policy is pending the owner, see R35b). Prefer additive APIs; any break needs explicit owner approval.
