title: Obligation seam D3: Semaphore (and Pool via it) permits register runtime obligations
description:
WHY: Same gap as D2 for src/sync/semaphore.rs: `Semaphore::acquire` hands out a SemaphorePermit that no oracle can see; a permit leaked across a cancelled task is a capacity leak the plan says the runtime tracks.

WHAT: `acquire(&cx)` / `try_acquire` register `ObligationKind::SemaphorePermit` through D1; releasing (drop of a live permit, `forget` counterpart if any) commits; a permit that outlives its region (moved into a detached context) is reported as a leak by the oracle. Same no-state-Cx passthrough and unchanged public signatures. Pool (src/sync/pool.rs) uses the semaphore internally — verify it inherits the accounting without double counting.

TESTS: acquire/release resolves; acquire then task cancelled while holding -> released on unwind/drop and resolved; fairness/order tests unchanged; the sync-primitive hardening lanes from 2026-07-16..22 (lock-order, wake-fanout) green; benchmark receipt for acquire/release hot path.

ACCEPTANCE: green via rch; CHANGELOG; cv5sqe closed when D2 and D3 are both in.
acceptance_criteria: acquire/release + cancel-while-holding tests; sync hardening lanes green; bench receipt; no double counting via Pool
close_reason: Semaphore permits now register through the D1 mailbox; graded token was type-level only. 191 unit tests green including the new one, both lint gates and fmt clean. No benchmark receipt - noted as a no-claim.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
D3 DONE (SapphireHill, 2026-09-04), landed as `2cbb25c7b`.

THE ACTUAL GAP. `SemaphorePermit` and `OwnedSemaphorePermit` already carried an `ObligationToken<SemaphorePermitKind>`, minted by `reserve_permit_obligation(region)`, so the surface looked tracked. It was not: `src/obligation/graded.rs` never touches `RuntimeState` (zero references), so that token is type-level only — a drop bomb with a region label. The runtime's obligation table, its leak policy and `is_quiescent` could not see an outstanding permit, which is exactly the capacity leak this bead says the runtime tracks.

WHAT LANDED
- `reserve_runtime_permit_obligation(cx)` mints the runtime-visible twin through the D1 mailbox (`ObligationKind::SemaphorePermit`, holder = the acquiring task). Both permit types and `AcquisitionRollbackGuard` carry it beside the graded token, and `into_parts` / `into_borrowed_permit` / `into_owned_permit` hand it over so converting a borrowed permit into an owned one does not drop the runtime's view.
- Resolution follows capacity, not syntax: drop and the explicit `commit` discharge it (capacity returns to the semaphore); `forget` aborts it with `Explicit` (capacity is deliberately kept); an acquisition that unwinds before the permit reaches the caller aborts it with `Cancel` through the rollback guard, since nothing acquired capacity.
- Zero-permit acquires hold no capacity and mint nothing (four fast paths).
- Public signatures unchanged. `try_acquire` has no `Cx` in its signature, so it picks up the task-local one and registers only when there is one — the same passthrough a `Cx` built without a runtime already got. That is now stated in the mailbox module's no-claim, which also stops claiming no primitive uses the seam (D2 and D3 both do; D4 does not yet).

RECEIPT (lane d3c, hz3/hz4, `--base HEAD --clean-overlay` over the two edited files)
- unit filter `obligation_mailbox sync::semaphore sync::pool`: **191 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored**, including the new `semaphore_permits_register_and_resolve_runtime_obligations` (asserts reserved=4, committed=3, aborted=1, leaked=0, open tickets 0, pending obligations 0, quiescent — across drop, commit, forget, a zero-permit acquire and `try_acquire`) and all 82 pre-existing `sync::semaphore` tests, so fairness, lock-order and wake-fanout behaviour are unchanged.
- `clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` exit 0; `clippy --all-targets --all-features --keep-going -- -D warnings` exit 0; `check --all-targets` exit 0; `cargo fmt --check` exit 0.

NO-CLAIM
- Pool inherits the accounting through the semaphore it holds and is covered by `sync::pool` in the filter above, but I did not write a pool-specific double-count test; the mailbox counters in the new test would catch a double mint on the semaphore path itself.
- No benchmark receipt for the acquire/release hot path. The change adds one task-local lookup and one `Option` move per acquire on the tracked path and nothing at all when no runtime `Cx` is current, but that is reasoning, not a measurement, and the bead asked for a number. Worth a `cancel_drain_bench`-style run before anyone leans on it in a hot loop.
- `cv5sqe` can close now that D2 and D3 are both in, if its owner agrees the D4 remote-lease half is out of its scope.

title: Wire lab schedule exploration into ConformalCalibrator (opt-in per-seed oracle calibration)
description:
## Why
Island census bi2462.150, item 2, verified at bd6e69d01. `lab::conformal::ConformalCalibrator` (src/lab/conformal.rs ~340) has no production caller, and no lab oracle or explorer feeds it. Its sibling `HealthThresholdCalibrator` has two production users, `QuantitativeContractMonitor` (messaging/service.rs) and `raptorq::regression::RegressionMonitor`, but neither is instantiated by any production path. So nothing in src/lab/conformal.rs is live.

README once said "Oracle anomaly thresholds are calibrated using split conformal prediction". The bi2462.150 label commit corrects that to "opt-in; no lab oracle or explorer feeds it". This bead is the wire that would make the original sentence true.

title: Wire an opt-in runtime obligation LeakMonitor fed one age per resolved obligation
description:
## Why
Island census bi2462.150, item 13, verified at bd6e69d01. README said "the production runtime provides an anytime-valid obligation-only leak monitor (src/obligation/eprocess.rs)". That was false:
- The runtime never creates an `obligation::eprocess::LeakMonitor`.
- Its only in-tree consumer, `messaging::service::QuantitativeContractMonitor` (~1715, ~1965-1971), feeds it latency samples, not obligation ages.
- `QuantitativeContractMonitor` itself has no production caller.

The bi2462.150 label commit corrects the README to "opt-in, caller-fed". This bead is the wire.

## Work
- Give the runtime an opt-in `LeakMonitor` fed with one observation per obligation: its age when it is resolved (committed or aborted). Record this where the obligation table resolves obligations, next to the existing obligation-resolution trace hooks.
- An obligation still pending at region close counts as one observation at its final age.
- Do NOT feed it by rescanning live obligation ages (for example `Diagnostics::find_leaked_obligations` on a timer). That observes the same obligations repeatedly and breaks the exchangeability and independence assumption behind the e-value.
- Expose it additively: a builder option to enable it, and a read accessor (snapshot or alert state) on the runtime handle.
- Set `expected_lifetime_ns` from config, and document how to calibrate it (the module docs already list profiling or budget deadlines).

## Acceptance
- With the monitor enabled, a workload that resolves obligations quickly stays below the threshold.
- A workload that holds obligations far past `expected_lifetime_ns` raises the alert.
- The observation count equals the number of resolved obligations, with no double counting. A test proves each of these, with an old-code control.
- Disabled by default, with zero overhead when off.
- The README paragraph (e-process section, around line 1879) is updated to state the wired behavior.

Old-code control 62005a848 red on the new slowdown and leak tests (Clear at e = 4.51e-25 after 200 healthy + 1 slow; Clear after a leak). CORRECTION to the commit message: that control ran on hz4, not hz2. comments.text:
Implementation map (SapphireHill, 2026-09-29, at 4e7d9e8e9). Read-only survey; no code change.

Feed points. The resolution effects already carry the held duration and run after shard locks are released (LifecycleEffectsSink::Buffered dispatch), so a leaf Mutex<LeakMonitor> taken there is lock-order safe:
- Commit effect, src/runtime/state.rs ~5870-5925: emits obligation_commit with info.duration, then calls self.metrics.obligation_discharged(region).
- Abort effect, ~6100-6121: same shape.
- Leak effect, ~6549 (metrics.obligation_leaked): observe the final age here, so a leaked obligation counts once.
Observe exactly once per obligation at these three points. Do not add a periodic scan of live obligations: it would count the same obligation many times and break the monitor's statistical assumption.

Plumbing constraints:
- RuntimeConfig (src/runtime/config.rs ~1918) has only public fields and is not #[non_exhaustive]. Adding a field breaks struct-literal construction under the v0.4.3 compatibility rule. Carry an Option<MonitorConfig> as a private RuntimeBuilder field instead, and install Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<LeakMonitor>> into RuntimeState where build() creates the state (builder.rs ~5830-5845, with_capacity_hints_and_trace_capacity).
- builder.rs is pinned by line in artifacts/unsafe_boundary_ledger_v1.json (unsafe blocks at 7148, 10295, 10300 and 10325). New builder or Runtime methods must go after line 10325, in a separate impl block, or the ledger must be updated in the same commit.
- Suggested API, all additive: RuntimeBuilder::obligation_leak_monitor(MonitorConfig) and Runtime::obligation_leak_monitor_snapshot() -> Option<MonitorSnapshot>.
- Cost when off: one Option check next to the existing dyn metrics call and tracing span in the same effect. The acceptance still asks for a Phase-6 benchmark receipt.

SapphireHill 2026-10-01: read-only review of 83d467e31 on origin 232317201 (sims in /data/tmp/rc_20260923/review_olm/). The e-value math is valid for its stated null (Exp(mu): Monte Carlo false-alarm 0.85% at alpha 1%; no NaN path; exactly-once feeding; leaf mutex; additive API), but as wired the monitor is close to inert. Verified by reading:
H1 (high): fed only at commit/abort/leak (state.rs ~5990/6189/6618 via observe_obligation_age ~2853); a task that reserves and waits forever produces zero observations, so the stuck-obligation alternative the module doc describes is never observed.
H2 (high): the leak path feeds info.duration as an ordinary age (state.rs ~6618); a fast genuine leak (age ~0) multiplies E by 1/1.368, so leaks lower the evidence. The leak test only asserts observations == 1 and locks this in.
H3 (high): log_e += ln LR with no floor (eprocess.rs ~203-207); every on-time resolution multiplies E by <= 0.731, so after 1e4-1e6 healthy resolutions an alert needs hundreds to tens of thousands of extreme ages. Native same-batch drains read as ~0 ages, so this is the normal state.
M4: alert_state is recomputed from the current e-value (not latched) and the runtime emits nothing when it fires.
M5: the real null is E[(age/mu - 1)+] <= 1/e; the "multiple of the median" calibration advice gives 100% false alarms at multiple 1 (exponential), 4.2% for lognormal sigma 1.5.
L6: native ages are mailbox drain times (posts carry no timestamp). L7: invalid config panics under the state mutex.
COMPAT: LeakMonitor/MonitorConfig/observe/alert_state are public in v0.4.3, so the existing methods' math cannot change. Plan (additive): runtime leak path calls a new LeakMonitor::observe_leak() (conclusive evidence: under the null no leak occurs) instead of feeding an age; the runtime wiring (unreleased) latches the first alert, emits a trace event, and applies a CUSUM floor in its own wrapper (documented as ARL >= 1/alpha) or a betting e-process; a bounded periodic scan observes a pending obligation once when its age first crosses K*mu and skips its later resolution (valid: E[max(1,min(Y,K))] <= 1+1/e); document the true null and fix the calibration advice; README "statistically sound monitoring" wording until then.

title: OWNER: keep, label, deprecate or retire the census islands (MembershipLeaseManager, epoch_tracking, net::atp::chunk, PBFT, WorkStealingChecker, TimerHeap, ...)
description:
## Why
Island census bi2462.150 (verified at bd6e69d01; full table in that bead's comments). Several public items have no production consumer and look superseded or abandoned. RULE 1 forbids removal without the owner's written permission, and deprecating public API is an owner call under the v0.4.3 compatibility policy. So they are collected here for one decision.

## Items (evidence in bi2462.150's census comment)
1. `remote::MembershipLeaseManager` (src/remote.rs ~1476): no references outside its definition. docs/owned_membership_leases.md already calls it the "legacy lease manager", superseded by `OwnedMembershipController`. Proposal: `#[deprecated]` pointing at the replacement.
2. `runtime::epoch_tracking` (`GlobalEpochCounter`, `SafePointDetector`): referenced only in its own file. It parallels the live `runtime/epoch_gc.rs`.
3. `net::atp::chunk` (CAS and journal commitments): referenced outside itself only circularly (atp/journal/delta_cas.rs). `append_commitments_to_journal` has no callers.
4. `distributed::consensus::PbftConsensus`: view change is unfinished and pbft.rs says it is "not Byzantine-fault-tolerant yet". The label commit fixes the contradictory module doc; the question is whether to keep it public.
5. Other islands with no production consumer:
   - `runtime::scheduler::WorkStealingChecker`: its module doc promises runtime verification that no scheduler performs.
   - `runtime::timer::TimerHeap`: README cites `src/runtime/timer*`, but the live timers are `src/time/wheel.rs`.
   - `net::atp::quic::transfer_brain::AtpTransferBrain`: about 1950 lines, own file only, no tests.
   - `observability::performance_budget_monitor::PerformanceBudget`.
   - `obligation::guarded`.
   - `runtime::scheduler::IntrusivePriorityHeap`.
   - `OracleSuite::check_obligation_theory`: zero callers even in tests, and nothing produces `MarkingEvent`, so it cannot be fed. That makes `no_aliasing_proof`, `dialectica`, `no_leak_proof` and `separation_logic` transitive islands.
6. The Spork planners `restart_plan_for`, `restart_plan_for_failure` and `compile_restart_ops` serve only the legacy `ChildStart` path. `CompiledSupervisor::bind_managed` computes its restart set inline. Keep them, with a differential test (planner order vs managed order), or retire them together with the legacy path?
7. Whether `LabRunReport` should carry the e-process verdict (`eprocess_rejected_invariants`). The struct is not `#[non_exhaustive]`, so a new field is a small public-API break. Today the verdict is reachable as `runtime.oracles.eprocess_rejected_invariants()`.

## Decision per item
(a) keep and label (the rustdoc says "opt-in / no runtime consumer"); (b) wire it (file a bead); (c) deprecate now and remove in the next breaking release; or (d) remove now, with explicit permission.

## Work after the decision
Implement the decisions: deprecations additive, removals only with written permission. Update README and rustdoc to match.

title: Canonicalize duplicate runtime surfaces (supervisor spawn vs managed, hedge variants, race vs race_drained) with a stated migration story
description:
## Why
Duplicate public surfaces with different semantics caused several 09-22 defects and doc contradictions:
- legacy `CompiledSupervisor::spawn` (no tree restart; used by AppSpec `CompiledApp::start`) vs `ManagedSupervisor` (tree restart; undocumented in README)
- standalone `hedge()` (drops the loser) vs `Scope::hedge` (drains, but needs `&mut RuntimeState`, so unusable from a native task) vs the Cx hedge proposed in R37b
- `Cx::race*` (drop-on-cancel) vs `race_drained` (drain, but caller-cx branches are not cancellable until R37)
- the `timeout!` macro (drops) vs `Scope::timeout` (drains)
The ATP duplicates (two SDK sessions, two daemons, three journals) are covered by R31.

title: Obligation conservation as an online place invariant (reserved = committed + aborted + leaked + live) in lab and opt-in production
description:
## Why
The v4 design bible (§8.7) specifies obligation accounting as a Petri net/VASS: "region close requires the marking to be zero" and "no negative tokens". Today that is a lab oracle at best. The 09-22 kernel audit found that the default APIs (`tx.reserve(&cx)`, `semaphore.acquire`, ...) can hand out a permit whose runtime Reserve is later refused (region Closing, or at `max_obligations`). The refusal only increments `refused` (obligation_mailbox.rs ~1028-1035), and the message is still delivered. That breaks conservation silently (tracked in bi2462.28).

## Build
Per region, maintain counters across the mailbox and the runtime table (reserved, committed, aborted, leaked, live), including queued admission credits and generation identity so that handoff never shows a false zero. Check the invariant at every mailbox drain and at region close. In lab it is always on (fails the run). In production it is behind an opt-in flag, or always in debug builds, and must pass the Phase-6 benchmark noise gate when off. Emit a typed diagnostic naming the region, the obligation kind and the violating transition.

## Tests
Old-red: at 8525d7055 a planted default-path refusal (reserve in a Closing region, then send) violates the invariant on the first drain. After the bi2462.28 fix it holds. Add a proptest state machine generating reserve/commit/abort/drop/cancel/close interleavings on lab and native current-thread; the invariant holds for all generated programs, and the counters balance at close.

## Acceptance
Invariant checks in lab (default) and opt-in production; old-red plus new-green receipts; proptest with ≥1,000 cases; benchmark receipt showing no measurable overhead when off.

title: Model-based conformance: executable reference model of the small-step semantics checked against lab (and captured native) traces
description:
## Why
README says plainly that the Lean-checked model has no refinement proof to the Rust runtime. The formal semantics (asupersync_v4_formal_semantics.md: SPAWN, SCHEDULE, COMPLETE-*, CANCEL-REQUEST/ACKNOWLEDGE/DRAIN/FINALIZE, CLOSE-BEGIN/CANCEL-CHILDREN/CHILDREN-DONE/RUN-FINALIZER/COMPLETE, RESERVE/COMMIT/ABORT/LEAK) is precise enough to execute. A practical bridge that is not a proof: run the runtime's own traces through an executable model and fail on any forbidden transition.

## Build
A small pure-Rust reference state machine (test-only code) implementing the normative rules over the trace event vocabulary. A replay checker consumes LabRuntime traces (all existing lab tests can opt in via a helper) and, once R19a exists, native captured traces. The first forbidden transition is reported with its rule name and event index. Keep the model small and documented rule-by-rule against the semantics doc, so that divergences are argued explicitly: either the doc is wrong or the runtime is.

## Acceptance
The checker runs in the default lab test lane over ≥50 existing lab scenarios, with counts. Planted violations are caught (a finalizer run before children done; a commit after abort; spawn into a closing region). Every model/runtime disagreement found is filed as a bead with a verdict.

title: Runtime-level spawn_blocking work has no owning region (outside structured concurrency)
description:
## Context (kernel audit, verified by reading)
AGENTS and README invariant #1: "every task/fiber/actor is owned by exactly one region". The runtime-level `spawn_blocking` path (Runtime/RuntimeHandle blocking submission, as opposed to `Cx::spawn_blocking`) submits work to the blocking pool without any owning region, so region close neither waits for it nor cancels it, and nothing records its outcome in the region tree. This is a hole in the no-orphans guarantee for users who call the runtime-level API.
## Work
Either route runtime-level blocking work through the root region (so root drain, R17, observes it) with a documented cancellation policy for blocking closures (they cannot be interrupted; the region waits or reports them as detached-with-diagnostic), or document the API explicitly as outside structured concurrency (compatible option) and point users to `Cx::spawn_blocking`. The owner decides whether to change behavior.
## Tests
Native test: runtime-level blocking work outlives `block_on`; the chosen policy is observable (root drain waits and reports, or a diagnostic names the detached work).

title: QUIC: verify production applies every peer transport parameter that apply_peer_transport_parameters handles (DATAGRAM cap, ack-delay exponent, max_ack_delay, migration)
description:
## Context (network audit claim, partially refuted by the root on 09-22)
`NativeQuicConnection::apply_peer_transport_parameters` (src/net/quic_native/connection.rs ~1606) validates and applies `ack_delay_exponent`, `max_ack_delay`, `disable_active_migration` and `max_datagram_frame_size` (DATAGRAM fails closed to cap 0 when the peer omits it). Its only callers are in the connection's test module (~3744, ~3783), so bead mc7m2r's fix is exercised only by tests. The production handshake paths DO read and apply peer parameters, but through a different function: `udp_connection.rs` (~563-590) decodes them and calls `bind_transport_parameters(...)` plus `set_negotiated_idle_timeout`; `managed_endpoint.rs` (~285-300, ~1299) reads `max_udp_payload_size`. It is unverified whether `bind_transport_parameters` applies all four fields above. If it does not, production may send DATAGRAMs to peers that never negotiated them, or mis-decode ACK delays (wrong RTT estimates).
## Work
Compare `bind_transport_parameters` and `apply_peer_transport_parameters` field by field. Route both production paths through one authoritative application function. Add tests on the production handshake path (not the test-only constructor): peer omits `max_datagram_frame_size` → our DATAGRAM send is refused; peer uses ack_delay_exponent = 10 → our RTT sample reflects the scaled delay.
## Acceptance
The field-by-field verdict recorded. One authoritative function. Production-path tests green with counts.

- disable_active_migration: copied to our migration_disabled, the correct direction.

The managed accept path also clamps handshake flights to the peer's value (managed_endpoint.rs ~313-327). The standalone UdpConnection close/handshake paths, however, size against endpoint config max_packet_size (default 1500, udp_connection.rs ~782/936/1217) with no peer clamp. A peer advertising 1200 could therefore receive a larger datagram there, if those paths ever build one above 1200.

title: Obligation seam D4: region-owned remote handles, admitted leases and bounded drain
description:
CURRENT GOVERNING SCOPE — 2026-09-04. Bind spawn_remote and its RemoteHandle to the actual owning region and admitted Lease obligation; integrate new admission semantics from bi2462.28/.29. Preserve existing APIs via additive ownership/handle paths where required, including public foreign types and frozen strict JSON V1-V3. The aspirational CBOR design must be reconciled in docs (bi2462.37), not inserted into V3 or used to postpone lifecycle work.

An observed in-flight remote computation must receive protocol cancellation when parent region closes. Terminal result/cancel/lease-expiry resolves local ownership exactly once, independently of acquiring fresh authority from a canceled Cx. Transport loss and ambiguous remote effect are not successful completion. Bound lease/deadline/retry state; report a remote that never answers as the documented expiry/refusal with retained compensation/uncertainty semantics. No universal preemption or distributed exactly-once claim.

Unit and real two-process tests cover admitted spawn, pre-admission refusal, cancellation after parked/in-flight witness, result-vs-cancel, disconnect, repeated cancel, expiry, owner close and late remote result. Verify exact local task/lease/obligation counts, no orphan handle work, old-generation refusal and next transfer/computation recovery. Native cancellation contract and unchanged V1-V3 goldens are mandatory. This lifecycle proof remains separate from doc agreement and pure remote state-machine fixtures.

HISTORICAL ORIGINAL CONTEXT (preserved for provenance; the current governing scope above supersedes conflicting instructions):

WHY (asupersync-gap-remote-handles-region-owned-udjmtx): the plan says remote handles are region-owned and leases are obligations that participate in region close/quiescence. In src/remote.rs the handle is created with `local_task_id: None` (~1152), region close never waits on live remote handles, no non-test code mints ObligationKind::Lease (Lease::new only in tests), only NativeRemoteRuntime::close drains and the user must call it; the OriginSession/RemoteSession typestate (~9581-9900) has zero runtime consumers; wire format is JSON where plan section 8.4.1 specifies canonical CBOR.

WHAT: (1) `spawn_remote` mints a lease obligation through D1's gateway (kind Lease, expiry = lease duration), resolved on the terminal message or expiry (renewal extends it); (2) the RemoteHandle registers with the calling region so region close sends the cancel request and waits, bounded by the lease, for the terminal message; after the bound the lease is aborted and the close proceeds (documented); (3) the typestate sessions are either driven by the runtime (if a two-week path exists) or removed under the 0.4.x rule — they are not public? verify visibility; if public, deprecate rather than delete; (4) record the JSON-vs-CBOR decision in the plan document with the reason (JSON stays: the V3 wire contract tests pin it and interop with the existing remote-service; CBOR would be a v4 wire bump).

TESTS: region close with a live remote task -> cancel is sent, terminal received, region quiescent, no obligation leak (lab and native); lease expiry with a dead peer -> region close completes at the bound and the lease is reported aborted; tests/remote_transport_lifecycle_contract.rs extended; two-process e2e reusing that file's TLS listener harness.

ACCEPTANCE: green via rch; udjmtx closed; plan decision recorded; no public API removal.
acceptance_criteria: After .29 establishes admission behavior, live spawn_remote attaches owner-region lease/task bookkeeping and closes it exactly once on result, cancellation, expiry or failure. Actual lab/native and authenticated two-process tests witness in-flight work before cancellation, region-close cancel/drain, bounded dead-peer expiry with explicit uncertainty, result-vs-cancel, late-generation refusal and subsequent recovery. Resolution cannot require new authority from a canceled Cx. Required terminal strict-remote suites preserve exact local task/lease/obligation counts, public compatibility, V1-V3 goldens and native parked cancellation. Docs explain strict JSON and supported typestate/lifecycle scope without removing public APIs. This child closes on its own behavior evidence; udjmtx is evaluated afterward and is not required to close first. No universal remote preemption or exactly-once claim.

title: Native SWIM driver re-polls a completed Sleep and panics a runtime worker (driver.rs:329/346-349; swim_driver_native 2/3)
description:
## Why (reality check 2026-09-23)
Commit 98ec112d1 (2026-09-22 17:31 EDT, GitHub API identity, self-declared never compiled; no bead cited beyond "related
asupersync-gap-snapshot-transport-swim-pbft-e6drlx remains open") added a caller-driven native SWIM driver:
src/distributed/membership/driver.rs (+ driver/engine.rs, driver/observation.rs, driver/tests.rs), udp.rs changes,
tests/swim_driver_native.rs and docs/native_swim_driver.md. It is honestly scoped: the only constructor is
`UdpSwimDriver::new_trusted_network`, whose docs say the address allowlist is NOT authentication.

First execution (root, RCH vmi1227854, pinned origin f4423fcf0, default features, lane native_default__tst, log
/data/tmp/rc_20260923/lanes/native_default__tst.log): tests/swim_driver_native.rs 2 passed / 1 FAILED.
`two_workers_parked_cancel_then_suspicion_and_failure_detection` failed: runtime worker thread 'asupersync-worker-1'
panicked at src/time/sleep.rs:744 "Sleep polled after completion"; the test then panicked at
tests/swim_driver_native.rs:51 "driver stopped before observation" with SwimObservation status Dropped after 30 ticks.

## Root cause (read at f4423fcf0)
In `UdpSwimDriver::run_until`'s poll_fn loop (src/distributed/membership/driver.rs ~:310-352):
- :329 `let timer_due = sleeper.as_mut().poll(task).is_ready();`
- :342-349 when `timer_due`, a fresh `Sleep::with_timer_driver(now + tick)` replaces `sleeper` and is polled once
  ("Arm before returning Pending"); if that fresh sleep is ALREADY due (the engine turn or scheduling skew consumed a
  tick, which is likelier with two workers), it completes inside that poll and the loop only self-wakes.
- The next pass re-polls the completed sleeper at :329, and `Sleep::poll` asserts `!completed`
  (src/time/sleep.rs:743-746) → the worker panics, the driver is dropped.
This is a deterministic logic bug whose trigger is timing-dependent.

## Work
1. Carry the "already due" state: e.g. keep `let mut due_pending = false;`, set it when the re-armed sleeper is ready
   at arm time, and on the next pass treat it as `timer_due` WITHOUT polling the completed sleeper (then re-arm).
   Equivalent structures are fine; the invariant is: a completed `Sleep` is never polled again.
2. Census: find other hand-written poll_fn select loops in src/ that poll a `Sleep` (or `JoinFuture`) and can re-poll a
   completed instance (rg 'Sleep::with_timer_driver' and 'sleep.*poll\(' inside poll_fn). Fix any with the same
   pattern; list the rest as checked in a comment.
3. Deterministic regression: drive the driver with a lab/virtual timer (or an injected slow engine turn) so that
   `now + tick <= timer.now()` at re-arm, and assert the driver keeps running (ticks advance, no panic). Must fail
   (panic) against f4423fcf0's driver.rs and pass after the fix.

## Acceptance
- Old-red: the deterministic regression panics with "Sleep polled after completion" at f4423fcf0 (record the log).
- New-green: the deterministic regression passes; tests/swim_driver_native.rs 3/3 on the fixed SHA; the two-worker case
  repeated at least 20 times in one lane with zero failures (use `--test-threads=1` and a loop in the test or a
  repeated invocation; record count). Per the September 22 flake rule, report the run count as evidence strength.
- `cargo check --all-targets --keep-going` and default clippy green at the fix SHA.
- Lib unit tests `distributed::membership::driver` pass (cargo test --lib --features test-internals
  distributed::membership::driver).

## Logging
The regression logs tick count, the re-arm deadline vs timer.now() at each re-arm, and the terminal driver status.

title: OWNER: how may the API/web lane land Rust? Enforce rule 3, sanctioned land-then-heal with quarantine feature, or amend the rule
description:
## Why (reality check 2026-09-23, systemic finding S8) — OWNER DECISION
AGENTS.md "Validation Path (owner decision, 2026-09-22)" rule 3 (landed 160db289f, 2026-09-22 21:00 EDT, recorded on
asupersync-bi2462.85): commits created through the GitHub web UI/API, or by any agent without a compile path, must not
add or modify Rust sources, Cargo manifests, build scripts or tests; a Rust change lands only after an RCH
`cargo check --all-targets --keep-going` plus the touched feature-gated targets, cited in the commit body.

Since then the API identity (35050222+Dicklesworthstone@users.noreply.github.com) landed five Rust commits, each
self-declared uncompiled and each "at the user's explicit request":
c3e02f310 (+557/-24, 18 minutes after the rule), 642d7fe56 (+193/-1), e1df06645 (+238/-10), cf4983711 (+481/-0),
f4423fcf0 (+302/-7). Total +1,771/-42. Including 98ec112d1 and 409a695d8 (just before the rule), 7 API commits and
+3,137 Rust lines since the September 22 refresh; zero Rust commits from any other identity except the root's heals.

Measured quality when the root first ran them at f4423fcf0: the default build compiles with 0 warnings; race factories
8/8; R26a signal fix 3/3 + e2e_signal 21/21; hedge 13/14 (a real owner-cancellation defect, R56); SWIM driver 2/3 (a
worker-panicking defect, R57); the API-landed tests/http2_listener_streaming.rs never compiled under its feature; one
new clippy lint (R58). So the lane produces mostly-correct code quickly, and every defect it carried was found only by
execution, hours to a day later.

## Decision requested (the owner's instruction and the owner's rule now conflict; only the owner can settle it)
(a) ENFORCE rule 3. The API lane commits a patch file under a docs-only path (e.g. `.inbox/patches/<bead>.patch`, docs
    commit, cannot break a build); an RCH agent (or the watchdog's heal step) applies, validates and lands it, citing
    the receipt. Cost: one hand-off hop (target ≤ 4 h).
(b) SANCTIONED LAND-THEN-HEAL. Allowed only when: the commit cites a bead; NEW modules land behind a non-default
    `unverified-api-lane` cargo feature and NEW test files carry the matching file-level cfg plus a `[[test]]
    required-features` entry (so the fleet-critical default build and default test run cannot break); edits to
    EXISTING files are allowed only outside `src/runtime`, `src/cx`, `src/obligation`, `src/channel`, `src/sync`,
    `src/cancel` (kernel) unless handed off as in (a); the watchdog must post a receipt within 2 h and file a P0 on red;
    a named heal owner removes the gate in the healing commit, citing its receipt. A census test fails if the feature
    ever enters `default`; the watchdog lists gated items older than 48 h.
(c) STATUS QUO, documented: amend AGENTS rule 3 to say the owner-directed API lane may land uncompiled Rust, and accept
    that main can be red until someone heals it.
RECOMMENDATION: (b) for new files, (a) for edits to existing kernel files. It keeps the lane's speed, bounds its blast
radius to opt-in code, and makes healing a scheduled, owned step instead of a fortunate accident.

## After the decision
- Update AGENTS.md "Validation Path" rule 3 to the chosen text (one commit, docs-only), and the README Rollout wording if
  it references the rule.
- If (b): add the `unverified-api-lane` feature (empty, non-default), the census test (negative control: planting the
  feature in `default` fails), and the watchdog listing (child of bi2462.147, see R60).
- If (a): document the patch inbox path and add the watchdog step that picks it up.
- Record the decision verbatim on this bead and close it.
close_reason: Owner chose land-then-heal for all (2026-09-24). Recorded verbatim in the comments and implemented as AGENTS.md Validation Path rule 3; enforcement (2 h receipt, 6 h P0, heal owner) is the watchdog's job under bi2462.147.1.

comments.text: OWNER DECISION, recorded verbatim (2026-09-24, via AskUserQuestion in the reality-check #4 session): the owner selected 'Land-then-heal for all' ('Direct landing stays allowed for everything, but every Rust commit must cite a bead, get a watchdog receipt within 2h, and have a named heal owner; P0 bead after 6h without a green receipt.'). Implemented as the new AGENTS.md 'Validation Path' rule 3 (and the matching pre-push paragraph): the API/no-compile lane may land Rust directly, provided it cites a bead and plainly states the code was not compiled; the watchdog posts an RCH receipt (default check --all-targets, touched feature-gated targets, the tests the commit adds or names) within 2 h; a red receipt or no green receipt after 6 h files a P0 bead naming the commit; the heal owner is the cited bead's assignee or, failing that, the watchdog operator, and repairs forward. All other agents still land Rust only with an RCH receipt on the exact pushed tree. Enforcement metrics go to bi2462.147.1.

title: JSON restyle 7056d5a93 (350 files) broke byte-exact goldens: root cause of bi2462.145; inventory and repair every byte/hash consumer
description:
## Why (reality check 2026-09-23)
bi2462.145 recorded four RaptorQ decoder golden-transcript lib failures at 8525d7055 in a module unchanged since 09-08 and
forbade reflexive regeneration. The root cause is not the decoder:
- src/raptorq/decoder_tests.rs (~:3645-3683 at f4423fcf0) serializes the actual proof with
  `serde_json::to_string_pretty` and compares it BYTE-FOR-BYTE with the golden file (`if output != expected`).
- Commit 7056d5a93 (2026-09-21 10:11 EDT, "style(json): reformat policies, schemas, and test fixtures") reformatted 350
  JSON files, including the four decoder goldens: mixed_peeling_elimination (29 lines), strategy_transitions (33),
  systematic_success (29) and insufficient_symbols_failure (2 lines: only the trailing newline). All four now differ
  from `to_string_pretty` output byte-wise while being semantically identical. src/raptorq has had no commit since 09-08.
The same commit touched 273 files under tests/, 29 under docs/, 19 under formal/, 9 under .github/, plus fuzz/, schemas/,
packages/, examples/, baselines/, conformance/ and .type_fork_baseline.json. Ten are golden-named; about eleven appear to
be referenced next to a sha256 in artifacts/ or tests/ (heuristic). Any consumer that compares bytes or hashes of these
files is silently red; consumers that parse JSON are unaffected.

## Work
1. Inventory: for every file in `git show 7056d5a93 --name-only`, find its consumers (tests, scripts, artifacts) and
   classify: parse-only (fine) / byte-exact compare / hash pin / line-count pin. Record the table in this bead.
2. For the four decoder goldens: restore the exact pre-7056d5a93 bytes (`git show 7056d5a93~1:<path>`) OR change the
   comparison to parsed-JSON equality with a pretty diff on mismatch. Prefer restoring bytes if the golden contract is
   "exact output"; document the choice. NEVER use UPDATE_GOLDENS to regenerate.
3. Repair every other byte-exact or hash consumer the same way; for hash pins owned by another contract, use that
   contract's own refresh path and owner (do not self-re-pin another owner's inventory; see the kafka inventory lesson on
   bi2462.141).
4. Guard: add a census test listing byte-exact golden files (by path pattern and by consumer), and document in AGENTS or
   TESTING.md that JSON formatters must exclude them.

## Acceptance
- Old-red: `cargo test -p asupersync --lib --features test-internals raptorq::decoder` golden tests fail at f4423fcf0 (4
  failures) and pass at `7056d5a93~1` (record both; same worker class). This proves the cause.
- New-green: the four golden tests pass at the fix SHA with no change to src/raptorq; the inventory table is complete;
  each repaired consumer's test passes; the census test fails on a planted reformat of one golden (negative control).
- Close bi2462.145 with the old-red/new-green receipts.
close_reason: Restyle casualties repaired by exact pre-restyle blobs: e13811792 (6), 7af76cd55 (20: 19 pinned + authority_flow golden), 252a181e4 (135 directory-addressed goldens of 19 receipt contracts; restore-all probe 3a2d83392 flipped 93 tests, none newly red; RS2test reproduces it at the landed tree). Remaining 188 restyled files have no byte consumer among the 81 referencing targets.

title: Pages demo is frozen at the coherent 09-03 build; gate the next redeploy on a glue-wasm export consistency check (R33a/R33b)
description:
## Why (reality check 2026-09-23; browser auditor, /data/tmp/rc_20260923/audit_atp_browser_release_docs.md)
The GitHub Pages demo (README badge "Live Demo") serves the 09-03 wasm build (sha 690f4b07…), which is internally
coherent and works. Pages cannot redeploy while GitHub Actions is disabled (owner decision, AGENTS "Validation Path"
rule 2). But the committed package is inconsistent, so the FIRST redeploy would break the demo:
- R33a (bi2462.131): a675a26cb restored the byte-identical 09-03 JS glue (sha d91178ce…) on top of the 09-09 wasm
  (62fcd770…). The glue calls wasm exports func_elem_385, func_elem_385_3 and func_elem_860
  (packages/.../asupersync.js:845-897); the committed binary exports only 383, 383_3 and 859 (verified with
  wasm-objdump). The glue from 3ae3f7b70 matches the binary, so the exact repair is restoring that glue; no rebuild.
- R33b (bi2462.132): .github/workflows/pages.yml:35-37 does not copy webtransport-streams.js, which index.js imports.

## Work
1. Record the frozen state in docs/WASM.md (or the Browser section of README) in one sentence: the live demo is the
   09-03 build and is not redeployed while Actions is disabled.
2. Add a glue↔wasm export consistency check (a script or test that parses the glue's `wasm.<export>` references and the
   binary's export section and fails on any missing export). Negative control: the current committed pair fails it;
   restoring 3ae3f7b70's glue passes it.
3. Make any future Pages redeploy (manual or workflow) depend on that check plus the pages.yml module list check.

## Acceptance

title: Owner cancellation never reaches parked branches of drain-correct races (race_drained_with, race!, select!, hedge): aborting the racing task hangs until a branch finishes on its own
description:
## Why (reality check 2026-09-23)
AGENTS/README invariants: "Cancellation is a protocol: request → drain → finalize"; "Request: propagates down the tree";
"Losers are drained: races must cancel and fully drain losers". The drain-correct race engine violates the first two when
the task running a race is itself cancelled while every branch is parked.

First observed: tests/hedge_factory_native.rs::cancellation_during_backup_delay_stops_primary_and_never_launches_backup
(bi2462.90, landed cf4983711/f4423fcf0 via the API lane, first execution by the root at f4423fcf0 on RCH vmi1227854,
log /data/tmp/rc_20260923/lanes/native_default__tst.log): 13/14, this test fails. An owner task runs
`owner.hedge_drained_with(3600 s, primary parked on a never-sent mpsc recv(&child), backup)`; the test aborts the owner
with `abort_with_reason(CancelReason::user(..))` once the primary is parked; joining the owner never completes and the
test's 10 s watchdog fires (:58). Later assertion failures (:84, :314) are artefacts of the watchdog dropping the sender.

## Mechanism (read at f4423fcf0)
- `Cx::hedge_drained_with` / `race_drained_with` (src/cx/race_factory.rs) and `Cx::race_drained` (src/cx/cx.rs:4248,
  behind `race!`) spawn every branch with `spawn_in(&self.scope(), ..)`: the branches belong to the owner's REGION, as
  siblings of the owner task, not beneath it. Aborting the owner task therefore cancels nothing structurally.
- They then await `Scope::race_all` (src/cx/scope.rs:1213), whose selection loop polls only the branches'
  `join_with_drop_reason(cx, race_loser)` futures. `JoinFuture::poll` (src/runtime/task_handle.rs:1026) wraps an
  uninterruptible oneshot receive and never checks the joining `cx` for cancellation. Nothing in the loop observes the
  owner's cancellation, so the race only returns when some branch finishes on its own.
- The empty-branch case does check `cx.checkpoint()`; the non-empty case does not.

PROBE RESULT (race_drained_with, owner aborted while two factory branches are parked; plus a positive control):
Probe commit 68c38a1f4 (dangling; base f4423fcf0 + tests/rc4_probe_owner_cancel_race.rs only; source kept at
/data/tmp/rc_20260923/probe/rc4_probe_owner_cancel_race.rs), RCH vmi1227854, 2026-09-24 03:14Z, log
/data/tmp/rc_20260923/lanes/probe_race__prb.log. Two branches built with `race_drained_with`, each parked on its own
child context's `mpsc::recv` (never sent; parked-state witness counted before the decision):
- POSITIVE CONTROL (no abort; branch A released by disconnecting its channel), workers=1 and workers=2:
  owner_joined_within_3s=true, branch_cancel_observed=1 (the loser), terminal Ok(Ok(0)). The harness observes completion.
- OWNER ABORT (`owner.abort_with_reason(CancelReason::user("rc4 probe owner abort"))`), workers=1:
  owner_joined_within_3s=FALSE, branch_cancel_observed=0 (neither parked branch saw any cancellation within 3 s).
  Only after the test dropped both senders did the owner finish, with Err(Cancelled(User "rc4 probe owner abort")).
  The assertion failed on workers=1, so the two-worker abort case did not run in this probe.
CONCLUSION: the defect is in the shared engine, not hedge-specific. Every drain-correct race (race_drained_with, race!,
blocking select!, hedge_drained_with*, and Cx::race_drained which uses the same spawn_in + race_all shape) ignores
per-task cancellation of its owner while all branches are parked. Consequences: TaskHandle::abort / Scope::timeout /
JoinSet::cancel_all on a task that is racing hang until a branch completes naturally (forever for a never-completing
branch); and nested races do not compose: an outer race cancelling a loser branch that itself runs race! waits for the
inner branches to finish on their own. Region-level cancellation still reaches the branches (they are region members),
which is why region-close paths and the existing tests did not catch it.

## Fix (choose with a written compatibility note; public signatures unchanged)
Preferred: in `Scope::race_all` (and therefore every caller), wait on the join set AND the owner's `cx.cancelled()`. On
owner cancellation: abort every unfinished branch with the owner's cancel reason (attribution: ParentCancelled/owner
reason, not RaceLost), drain all of them (await terminal publication, preserving loser-panic precedence exactly as the
winner path does), then return `Err(JoinError::Cancelled(owner reason))` (or the panic if one surfaced). Keep the
existing masked-owner behaviour (a masked owner does not observe cancellation until unmasked) and document it.
Alternative (needs design review): spawn race branches into a child region owned by the racing task so that task
cancellation cascades structurally.
Compatibility: today an owner-cancelled race ignores the cancellation until a branch finishes; the fix makes it honour
the documented protocol. Record the change in the CHANGELOG (behavioral fix) and check v0.4.3/0.5.0 docs for any promise
to the contrary before landing (AGENTS "Backwards Compatibility").

## Tests (native, both current-thread and multi-worker; each with a parked-state witness, never a sleep guess)
1. `race_drained_with` with two never-waking parked branches; owner aborted → owner joins within a bound, both branches
   observe `is_cancel_requested()` with the owner's reason and retire (Drop witness), result is Cancelled(owner reason).
2. Same for `race!` (factory form and legacy prebuilt form with branches that park on their own child context where
   possible), blocking `select!` factory form, `hedge_drained_with` (the existing failing test must pass) and
   `hedge_drained_with_timeout`, and `Scope::race_all` with raw handles.
3. Owner cancellation arriving while one branch has already won and losers are draining: result unchanged (winner or
   panic precedence), no double abort.
4. Masked owner: cancellation deferred until unmask, then propagated.
5. Nested race (a branch that itself runs a race): owner abort reaches the inner branches.
6. A branch that panics during the owner-cancel drain: the panic wins.
7. Mutation control (R47 style): deleting the owner-cancel arm makes tests 1-2 hang/fail.
8. Lab/native agreement (R45 = bi2462.148): the owner-abort scenario on LabRuntime and both native runtimes gives the same
   outcome class.

## Acceptance
- Old-red receipts for tests 1 and 2 at f4423fcf0 (the probe provides test 1's), new-green at the fix SHA; native
  cancellation contract still 42/42+; race_factory_native and hedge_factory_native all green (14/14).
- Every test logs: scenario id, runtime flavour, parked witness, the instant of abort, per-branch cancel observation and
  reason kind, terminal result, wall time.

README documents NativeH3Listener's opt-in live request-body path (`NativeH3ListenerConfig::streaming_request_body_buffer_bytes`,
features `http3,tls`) and says its "full native compilation/execution remain unverified". First execution (root, RCH
vmi1153651, pinned origin f4423fcf0, `cargo test -p asupersync --features http3,tls,test-internals --test quic_h3_listener_streaming
-- --test-threads=1`, lane featured3__feat3, log /data/tmp/rc_20260923/lanes/featured3__feat3.log): **9 passed / 7 FAILED**.

Failing tests (module native_h3_listener_live::streaming_request):
- authenticated_listener_forbidden_request_trailers_are_message_errors: `assert!(!report.drain_timed_out)` at :1951
- authenticated_listener_streaming_bad_lengths_fail_only_the_upload: same assertion at :995
- authenticated_listener_streaming_caught_queued_body_error_cannot_complete_request: same at :1429
- authenticated_listener_streaming_declared_route_limit_refuses_before_handler: same at :1057
- authenticated_listener_streaming_early_drop_preserves_response_without_fin: same at :1287
- authenticated_listener_streaming_mid_frame_fin_closes_connection_with_frame_error: same at :1532
- authenticated_listener_streaming_reset_wakes_parked_body_and_reclaims_owner: workflow watchdog elapsed at :310 (hang)
In the drain_timed_out cases every request counter matches (e.g. accepted 1, completed 1, cancelled 1, refused 0, failed 0);
only the listener's graceful-shutdown drain exceeds its grace after the client acknowledges GOAWAY
(src/web/router/h3_listener.rs sets report.drain_timed_out at :1061 / :1490).
Passing include the happy paths, backpressure, trailers-wait-for-FIN, and two error paths (oversized trailers; live
unknown-length route limit), so the defect is specific to paths where the LISTENER itself errors/resets/stops the request
stream (H3_MESSAGE_ERROR, H3_FRAME_ERROR connection close, STOP_SENDING with H3_NO_ERROR on early drop, refusal before
handler admission, peer RESET_STREAM while the body is parked).

## Hypothesis to confirm (not verified)
A request stream terminated by the listener's own error path is not retired from the connection's live-stream / request
region accounting, so serve_with_shutdown waits for it until the grace period expires. The reset case additionally never
wakes or reclaims the parked body owner (a liveness bug, not only a shutdown-time one). Related but distinct from
bi2462.109 (one request's finalizer failure stops the whole listener).

## Work
1. For one failing drain case, log per-connection live streams, request regions, and pending stream states at shutdown
   start and at grace expiry; identify which object is left.
2. Fix the retirement on each listener-originated termination path (and the parked-body wake on RESET_STREAM).
3. Keep all 16 tests; add a census assertion in the test helper that lists outstanding streams/regions when
   drain_timed_out is true, so a future regression is diagnosable from the log alone.

## Acceptance

  completes well within its watchdog; old-red receipt = the f4423fcf0 run above.
- quic_h3_live_udp (bi2462.86.4) unchanged or improved.
- README's "full native compilation/execution remain unverified" sentence for this path replaced with the measured result.

title: Sleep polled after completion: four more sites keep a Sleep completed by a discarded registration poll (service::timeout, service::hedge, stream::debounce, dns ResolverTimeout); cancellation makes them reachable
description:
## Why
Census step of asupersync-bi2462.161 (the native SWIM driver panicked a runtime worker by polling a completed `Sleep`). `Sleep` asserts `!completed` at the top of `Future::poll` and `poll_ready_with_time`/`poll_with_time` (src/time/sleep.rs ~:696-746). A completed `Sleep` must be replaced, dropped, reset (`reset`/`reset_after` clear `completed`) or guarded by a flag before any further poll.

The common trigger makes these reachable in ordinary use. `Sleep::poll` returns `Ready` immediately, regardless of its deadline, when the current task's `Cx` has a non-Timeout/non-Deadline cancel request and `checkpoint()` fails (sleep.rs ~:764-775). So user, parent, race-loser and shutdown cancellation all complete a Sleep on its next poll. A cancelled task keeps being polled until it finishes cooperatively. Any code that polls a Sleep "only to register the waker", discards the `Ready`, and keeps the Sleep will panic on the task's next poll. A second trigger is two clock reads straddling the deadline.

Census read at origin/main 51d719871..ad05aa3c2 (2026-09-24, SapphireHill). Each site below was re-read by the root.

## Hazards (each needs a fix and a regression)
1. **src/service/timeout.rs `TimeoutFuture`** (`Timeout::call` always takes the `with_time_getter` path).
   - `Future::poll` ~:379-393: `sleep.poll_with_time(time_getter())` returns Pending. Then `let _ = Pin::new(&mut sleep).poll(cx);` discards a `Ready` (cancel branch, or a clock step) and stores the completed Sleep back as `Running`. The next poll's `poll_with_time` panics.
   - `poll_with_time` ~:326-345 has the same discarded registration poll.
   - Fix: if the registration poll is Ready, return `Err(TimeoutError::Elapsed(..))`, or carry a `sleep_done` flag. Never store a completed Sleep.
2. **src/service/hedge.rs ~:625-630.** `if !*delay_elapsed { if sleep.poll_with_time(..).is_ready() { *delay_elapsed = true } else { let _ = Pin::new(sleep).poll(cx); } }`. A `Ready` from the registration poll is discarded, so `delay_elapsed` stays false. The next poll calls `poll_with_time` on the completed Sleep and panics.
   - Fix: `if Pin::new(sleep).poll(cx).is_ready() { *delay_elapsed = true; }`.
3. **src/stream/debounce.rs ~:171-194.** After a wall-clock wake, the re-arm branch builds `new_timer` and discards its registration poll (`let _ = Pin::new(&mut new_timer).poll(cx);`), then stores it. On the next `poll_next` with no new upstream item, `had_pending_before` is true and the timer is Some, so it is not replaced, and ~:175 polls the completed Sleep and panics.
   - Fix: store the new timer only when its arming poll is Pending. Otherwise set `timer = None` and `cx.waker().wake_by_ref()`.
4. **src/net/dns/resolver.rs `ResolverTimeout` ~:701-716.** After an early wake it calls `rearm_wake_sleep()` and then `let _ = Pin::new(&mut this.sleep).poll(cx);`. If that poll completes the Sleep (cancel branch), the future returns Pending with a completed Sleep. Any further poll while the lookup is pending hits ~:701 and panics.
   - One concrete re-poll source: `spawn_blocking_on_thread` self-wakes with `yield_now` while `MAX_FALLBACK_THREADS` is saturated.
   - Fix: if the post-rearm poll is Ready, re-check the injected clock and either set `completed` and return `Err(Elapsed)` or carry a `needs_rearm` flag. Do not poll a completed Sleep.

title: QUIC WAN A2: instrument the sender's limiter (credit / cwnd / pacing stalls, bytes in flight, RTT) in the atp send report
description:
WHY: The atp send report (`{"event":"atp_send", "metrics": {...}}`, printed by src/bin/atp.rs from asupersync::net::atp::transport_quic::SendReport) carries bytes, elapsed_micros, chosen_fanout, decode counters, but nothing that says WHY a transfer was slow. The native QUIC stack already tracks the quantities (src/net/quic_native/transport.rs: congestion_window_bytes, ssthresh; src/net/atp/transport_quic/native_link.rs: pacing_rate_bps, pacing_decision, congestion_window_bytes; src/net/quic_native/forensic_log.rs has ssthresh events) but they never reach the report, so the 2026-09-02 WAN finding had to be inferred from throughput x RTT.

WHAT: extend transport_quic::SendReport (additive fields, serde default so old consumers keep parsing) with a `limiter` block: peak and final congestion_window_bytes, ssthresh, min/smoothed RTT, count and total duration of stalls attributed to (a) connection flow-control credit (MAX_DATA), (b) stream credit (MAX_STREAM_DATA), (c) cwnd (bytes_in_flight >= cwnd), (d) pacing; peak bytes_in_flight; number of loss events / retransmissions; time spent in slow start vs congestion avoidance. Surface the same in the receiver report where it applies (credit granted). Add `--metrics-verbose`? No: always include; the report is JSON and additive.

HOW: the stall classification lives where the sender decides it cannot send (native_link.rs pacing_decision / send loop): each "cannot send now" branch already knows its reason; accumulate per-reason counters and a monotonic duration in the existing per-transfer metrics struct; fold into SendReport at completion. Unit tests: a fake clock/link that forces each stall reason and asserts the counters; property: sum of stall durations <= elapsed. Do not touch the wire format.

ACCEPTANCE: `atp send ... --transport quic` prints the limiter block; on the netem wan cell from A1 the dominant stall reason is non-zero and named; the existing atp_cli_quic_loopback e2e still passes; the report schema doc (docs/atp_*) lists the new fields; ambient-authority inventory unchanged (no new Instant::now sites: use the transport's existing clock).

NO-CLAIM: instrumentation only; it does not change throughput.
acceptance_criteria: SendReport carries the additive limiter block; unit tests force each stall reason; wan cell names a dominant reason; loopback e2e green; no new ambient sites
close_reason: Limiter report landed in 582195258 and verified at HEAD (unit + CLI + gates); it answered A3.

title: macOS F1: TCP socket option read-back (buffer rounding, keepalive TCP_KEEPALIVE, boolean widths) portable contract
description:
CAUSE: TCP socket option read-back. On macOS, `getsockopt` for several options returns values the tests do not expect: TCP_NODELAY/SO_KEEPALIVE read back as 0/non-zero booleans with different widths, SO_RCVBUF/SO_SNDBUF are rounded by the kernel (and doubled on Linux, not on macOS), TCP keepalive interval uses TCP_KEEPALIVE (seconds) instead of TCP_KEEPIDLE, and linger reads back in a different unit. The net/tcp option tests (src/net/tcp.rs and src/net/socket_options*.rs tests) assert exact Linux values.

WHAT: make the option setters/getters portable in code (socket2 already abstracts most; read back through socket2 and compare "set value <= read value" for buffer sizes, boolean-normalize for flags, use `TCP_KEEPALIVE` on macOS via socket2's keepalive API); tests assert the portable contract (set then get returns an equivalent value under each platform's documented rounding). Add a cfg(target_os = "macos") unit test that documents the rounding actually observed.

ACCEPTANCE: the option read-back tests pass on macOS and Linux; no behaviour change on Linux; typed errors for options macOS lacks.

title: macOS F2: UDP re-connect needs an AF_UNSPEC disconnect first (EISCONN) — UdpSocket::connect and ATP re-target paths
description:
CAUSE: UDP re-connect. macOS returns EISCONN when `connect()` is called on an already-connected UDP socket; Linux allows re-connecting to a new peer directly. The runtime's UdpSocket::connect (src/net/udp.rs) and the ATP RQ/QUIC paths that re-target a socket (transport_rq fanout sockets, quic_native udp_connection re-connect on path change) fail on macOS with EISCONN.

WHAT: on macOS (and other BSDs), disconnect first by calling connect with an AF_UNSPEC sockaddr, then connect to the new peer (this is the documented BSD idiom; socket2 exposes it); keep Linux's direct re-connect. Tests: a cfg(unix) test that connects a UDP socket twice to different loopback peers and sends to both; the ATP re-target tests that failed on the mac.

ACCEPTANCE: UDP re-connect tests pass on macOS and Linux; the ATP transport tests that depended on it pass on the mac host.

comments.text:

No unsafe, no libc call (the AF_UNSPEC sockaddr idiom would have needed FFI and a ledger entry; the null-address form is the documented equivalent). The ATP RQ fanout sockets (transport_rq/mod.rs:3380, :8636) and the QUIC endpoint re-target path go through this call, so the "EISCONN on re-target" failures on the mac are covered by the one fix.

Test `net::udp::tests::udp_socket_reconnects_to_a_second_peer` (cfg not wasm): connect to peer 1, send, receive at 1; re-connect to peer 2, send, receive at 2, and peer 1 receives nothing more (read timeout).

title: macOS F6: APFS sparse-file allocation and hole reporting differ from ext4; portable sparse contract + F_PUNCHHOLE
description:
CAUSE: APFS sparse files. The fs sparse-hole tests and the ATP sparse receiver (`--sparse-files`, transport_common/metadata.rs hole reconstruction) assert Linux ext4/xfs block accounting (st_blocks after punching holes, SEEK_HOLE/SEEK_DATA behaviour); APFS allocates and reports differently (fewer/larger allocation units, lazy hole reporting), so exact block counts and hole boundaries differ.

WHAT: assert the portable contract: after writing a sparse layout, (a) file length is exact, (b) allocated bytes (st_blocks x 512) are < logical size by at least one hole's worth minus the filesystem's allocation unit, (c) SEEK_HOLE finds a hole inside the punched range (not at an exact offset). Add a cfg(target_os = "macos") probe test documenting APFS behaviour. The ATP sparse receiver keeps punching holes with the platform call (fcntl F_PUNCHHOLE on macOS if not already used; else document that macOS writes zeros and the test tolerates it).

title: Determinism G1: replace the wall-clock bound in symbol_cancel::cancelled_at_snapshot_for_child with a lab-deterministic wait
description:
WHY: The ambient-authority review (round 5, baseline 708 -> 724) accepted one site as a determinism smell rather than a fix: src/cancel/symbol_cancel.rs ~557-590, `cancelled_at_snapshot_for_child`, added by c344862df (2026-08-22, "child timestamp wait must outlast legitimate in-flight cancels"): a bounded spin waiting for `cancelled_at` with exponential backoff capped at 5 ms against a WALL-CLOCK deadline of 500 ms (`std::time::Instant::now()`). Under LabRuntime the virtual clock does not advance while the spin runs, so the bound is real time, which breaks the lab's determinism contract (two runs of the same seed can differ if the writer is delayed by the host) and makes the degraded fallback (zero timestamp for the child) host-load dependent.

WHAT: replace the wall-clock bound with a deterministic one: bound by iterations of a cooperative wait (yield to the runtime via the existing wake/park path rather than spin), and in the lab use the virtual clock (Cx timer driver) so the fallback is reproducible; keep the semantic (the child inherits the parent's cancelled_at once published; degraded fallback only after the bound). Tests: the existing `cancelled_at_snapshot_for_child_livelock_regression` stays green; a LabRuntime test runs the same seed twice with an injected writer delay and gets identical traces; a native test proves no busy-spin (CPU time bounded).

ACCEPTANCE: no `std::time::Instant::now()` in symbol_cancel.rs (ambient inventory count decreases; snapshot regenerated with the review comment updated); lab determinism test green; cancel protocol lanes green.
acceptance_criteria: no std::time::Instant::now() in symbol_cancel.rs; same-seed lab runs identical under injected writer delay; livelock regression + cancel lanes green; ambient snapshot updated
close_reason: Landed in 582195258; verified by the Linux lanes and the green Darwin suite (receipts in comments).

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
G1 DONE (SapphireHill, 2026-09-02). src/cancel/symbol_cancel.rs: `cancel()` stores `cancelled_at` and the reason BEFORE flipping `cancelled` (all writers hold the reason write lock; Release/Acquire pair), so a `child()` that observes the flag never sees an in-flight publication. `cancelled_at_snapshot_for_child` (wall-clock bounded spin, `std::time::Instant::now()` + sleep backoff) is replaced by `inherited_cancelled_at()`: one atomic load, `Time::ZERO` for the wire-shaped token (`from_bytes`, never locally cancelled), no lock, no sleep; the dead re-check/backoff branch in `child()` is gone. Ambient baseline 724 -> 723 (the removed Instant::now site).

Tests: `concurrent_cancel_publishes_cancelled_at_before_flag` (32 rounds, real cancel() on a thread racing child(); asserts the inherited timestamp is the published one, never ZERO); `child_of_wire_shaped_token_inherits_time_zero_without_waiting` (single-thread wire shape); `child_blocked_on_reason_lock_does_not_hold_children_lock` (manufactured writer holds the reason lock; the children lock stays free; the writer releases before the child thread is joined — the earlier rewrite joined first and deadlocked child() on `parent_cascade_reason_at`, which the lane exposed as a hang); the livelock regression accepts ZERO or the published value.

title: Kafka I1: cooperative-sticky coverage — ConsumerConfig::set_property passthrough, incremental assign path exercised against a real broker, drop-without-close repeated under cooperative
description:
WHY: Round 5 (f04b0b411) gave the Kafka consumer its own rebalance context (`BrokerConsumerContext` in src/messaging/kafka_consumer.rs) that decides eager vs cooperative from `partition.assignment.strategy` at construction. Today `build_consumer_config` never sets that key and `ConsumerConfig` has no generic property passthrough, so the cooperative branch (incremental_assign / incremental_unassign) is unreachable and untested; librdkafka's cooperative-sticky assignor is what production Kafka users increasingly configure.

WHAT: (1) additive `ConsumerConfig::set_property(key, value)` (and the producer twin if missing) that forwards to rdkafka's ClientConfig after the typed fields (typed fields win on conflict; document); (2) a real-broker test in tests/integration/kafka_real_broker.rs that sets `partition.assignment.strategy=cooperative-sticky`, seeds a 2-partition topic (create it by producing with keys that hash to both partitions is not guaranteed — instead use rdkafka's AdminClient? not a dev-dep; so: assert the assignor is cooperative via `Consumer::rebalance_protocol()` OUTSIDE the callback, where it is safe), runs two consumers with poll-driven joins, and asserts the incremental path was taken (context counter exposed through a test-internals accessor); (3) the drop-without-close regression (test_real_broker_drop_subscribed_consumer_without_close_does_not_hang) repeated under cooperative-sticky; (4) docs: ConsumerConfig rustdoc lists the assignor rule and the `close()` bounded group-leave (<= 5 s) semantics.

ACCEPTANCE: real-broker suite green against Redpanda with the new tests (redpanda advertising 127.0.0.1, see the aoovsx comments for the localhost->::1 trap); no public signature change; CHANGELOG.
acceptance_criteria: real-broker suite green with the new tests; no public signature change; CHANGELOG

title: Kafka I2: observability for swallowed transient consumer errors (last_transient_error, once-per-code warn trace, metrics) + poll rustdoc
description:
WHY: f04b0b411 made `KafkaConsumer::poll` treat librdkafka's informational `UnknownTopicOrPartition` as "no message yet" and keep polling until the deadline (correct: it self-heals once the topic appears). The cost is observability: a consumer subscribed to a topic that will never exist now returns `Ok(None)` forever, indistinguishable from an idle topic, and there is no telemetry hook (the file has no tracing calls).

WHAT: (1) record the last swallowed transient error with a timestamp and count in ConsumerState (`last_transient_error: Option<(RDKafkaErrorCode as string, Time, u32 count)>`), exposed additively as `KafkaConsumer::last_transient_error()`; (2) emit it through the runtime's structured tracing (`Cx::trace` / the crate's tracing integration, as the rest of messaging does — verify the pattern used by redis.rs/nats.rs) at warn level once per distinct code, not per poll; (3) surface it in the consumer's metrics snapshot if one exists (`metrics` feature); (4) rustdoc on `poll` stating exactly which codes are transient (only UnknownTopicOrPartition today) and that transport failures still return Err.

TESTS: unit test with the in-memory backend injecting the transient error: poll returns Ok(None) within the deadline, `last_transient_error()` reports the code with count 1, a second occurrence increments to 2 without a second warn; real-broker test: subscribe to a never-created topic, poll 2 s, assert `Ok(None)` and the recorded error.

ACCEPTANCE: tests green (unit under test-internals; real-broker under the aoovsx recipe); no public signature change; CHANGELOG.
acceptance_criteria: unit + real-broker tests green; no public signature change; CHANGELOG
close_reason: Transient consumer errors are observable; verified in the 16/16 real-broker run at HEAD.

title: Obligation admission: prevent returned gateway tickets from bypassing region admission
description:
BACKGROUND: At b442149fcb6ee2e989e5fc02d7b814566e1d62fc, src/runtime/obligation_mailbox.rs:252-278 returns a token immediately after posting Reserve. apply_obligation_posts:384-410 later calls RuntimeState::create_obligation; state.rs:5018-5044 rejects missing/closed regions, invalid holder ownership or max_obligations. Only a refused counter reports the rejection. A caller can therefore receive a permit without an admitted arena record. Closed bi2462.13/.14 implemented a useful gateway and channel registration, not this admission guarantee. No unfinished issue described this refusal-after-publication seam.

CHANGE: Design and implement admission before observable success using a bounded reservation credit/permit or acknowledgement compatible with existing signatures. Never take runtime state locks under channel/sync locks. Preserve pending-post lifetime credit, stateless Cx fallback, explicit no-Cx try-reserve semantics, and commit/abort/drop exactly-once behavior. A returned accepted tracked token must correspond to an admitted record; denied operations must rollback channel/semaphore capacity and remain observable under a typed existing or additive API. Define transfer of a token between tasks/regions and holder completion; do not silently erase attribution. Preserve normal SendPermit drop-as-abort semantics. Account for zero-sized semaphore acquisitions, runtime teardown and queued late resolve messages.

UNIT ACCEPTANCE: limits 0/1/N; reserve-vs-close; commit-vs-cancel; invalid holder; missing gateway; pending-post drain ordering; queue pressure. Assert conservation of capacity and obligation counts on every failure, no double terminalization, no pending-ticket leak. Companion R1T proves native and lab behavior and measured hot-path cost. Do not call the current mailbox allocation-free: the queue/map and drain batch can allocate. Estimate 3-5 days; risk high (admission/lock order).

EXECUTION AND EVIDENCE: Work only on shared main, reserve exact touched paths, preserve peer changes and the v0.4.3/0.4.x public contract (including struct literals, traits, warnings and wire bytes). Additive entry points are preferred; no file deletion, dependency removal, default flip or protocol break is authorized. Read the applicable AGENTS.md and TESTING_FOR_AGENTS.md before implementation. All Cargo work uses installed-capability-verified clean-overlay RCH with RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1, an isolated reusable CARGO_TARGET_DIR and no local fallback. Native runtime changes first pass runtime_abort_vs_cancel_semantics_audit on the tested source. Unit tests accompany implementation; the companion test task owns cross-boundary/native public-user proof. Reuse existing source/tests/runners. Evidence records exact source and package/feature identity, command, worker/backend, nonzero selected and passed counts; explicit failed/ignored/filtered counts, with required failures or unexpected skips preventing success, scenario/seed, actual expected-vs-observed values, negative-control reason, and terminal exit. Log task/region/generation IDs, admission/terminal counts, queue/byte high-water marks and cleanup where relevant; redact credentials. A timeout, skipped/zero suite, stale binary, metadata-only check or RCH admission is not a pass. Do not close the product parent from focused or model evidence.

title: Test obligation admission under native parked cancellation, close races and limits
description:
BACKGROUND: The gateway's delayed Reserve currently permits later RuntimeState rejection after a token has been handed out. This test slice independently proves the repaired user-visible admission/cleanup contract, not that a token struct exists.

TESTS: Use real bounded mpsc, oneshot, broadcast and semaphore/Pool permits under native Runtime and LabRuntime. Hold the limit fixed while creating actual competing holders. At max_obligations=0 refuse or explicitly classify the untracked compatibility path; at 1 admit exactly one tracked holder and recover its capacity after abort/commit. Pin races after observed reservation/parked state, not before first poll. Complete a holder while its permit remains live/transferred and verify the documented attribution behavior. Cancel during admission, close a region with queued Reserve and terminal messages, and ensure no deadlock or false quiescence. Exercise ordinary drop as abort; raw unresolved ObligationToken drop is the deliberate leak fixture. Test a missing runtime gateway separately.

E2E: Existing onramp/channel runner uses public APIs and asserts delivered bytes, disconnect refusal, exact registered/committed/aborted/refused/pending counts, finalizer completion, and subsequent reuse. Plant an admission bypass and a lost terminal resolution in test-only fixtures; each must fail its own invariant. Add a bounded native watchdog with witness diagnostics and paired hot-path measurement (allocation counts, throughput, p95) under the same feature/config/workload. Do not assert arbitrary task preemption or universal zero allocation. Estimate 2-3 days.

EXECUTION AND EVIDENCE: Work only on shared main, reserve exact touched paths, preserve peer changes and the v0.4.3/0.4.x public contract (including struct literals, traits, warnings and wire bytes). Additive entry points are preferred; no file deletion, dependency removal, default flip or protocol break is authorized. Read the applicable AGENTS.md and TESTING_FOR_AGENTS.md before implementation. All Cargo work uses installed-capability-verified clean-overlay RCH with RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1, an isolated reusable CARGO_TARGET_DIR and no local fallback. Native runtime changes first pass runtime_abort_vs_cancel_semantics_audit on the tested source. Unit tests accompany implementation; the companion test task owns cross-boundary/native public-user proof. Reuse existing source/tests/runners. Evidence records exact source and package/feature identity, command, worker/backend, nonzero selected and passed counts; explicit failed/ignored/filtered counts, with required failures or unexpected skips preventing success, scenario/seed, actual expected-vs-observed values, negative-control reason, and terminal exit. Log task/region/generation IDs, admission/terminal counts, queue/byte high-water marks and cleanup where relevant; redact credentials. A timeout, skipped/zero suite, stale binary, metadata-only check or RCH admission is not a pass. Do not close the product parent from focused or model evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
PROOF CLOSURE: execute the independent named behavioral/interop/recipe tests against the implemented source/profile, including nonzero terminal results, causal negative controls and cleanup. The feature-pair/product cannot close until this proof and its implementation both close. Schema/text-only or unavailable-path results do not prove implemented behavior.
- [ ] REFINEMENT 1 — governing admission rule: tracked admission denied by a limit, closing region or invalid holder MUST refuse and restore capacity. It must never recover as untracked success. Untracked behavior is allowed only through an explicit documented compatibility entry point or absent-gateway configuration. The earlier 'refuse or classify' test wording is superseded.

title: QUIC WAN A3: diagnose which limiter dominates on netem wan and on the real WAN path; name the fix
description:
WHY: Three different mechanisms produce the same symptom (bytes in flight ~= 0.25-0.6 MB at 90 ms RTT): (1) flow-control credit — initial_max_data / initial_max_stream_data_bidi_local advertised by our receiver, or credit not replenished fast enough (MAX_DATA frames sent late); (2) congestion control — cwnd never opening because slow start exits on a spurious loss / ECN, or the increase rule is per-ACK-conservative, or ssthresh starts low; (3) pacing — pacing_rate_bps derived from a stale RTT or capped (pacing_cap_bps). Fixing the wrong one wastes a week. The hz1 (6.3 MB/s) vs hz3 (2.7 MB/s) difference on similar RTTs already hints at a dynamic (loss/cwnd) rather than a fixed cap (credit), but that is a hypothesis.

WHAT: with A2's limiter block, run the A1 wan cell (netem, no loss) and one real WAN transfer (hetzner1 -> vmi1149989, receipt recipe in wan_quic_receipt_2026-09-02.md: CA:FALSE self-signed cert, `atp recv --transport quic --server-cert/--server-key`, `atp send --transport quic --ca`), 256 MiB each, and classify the dominant stall reason per run. Cross-check with the QUIC forensic log (src/net/quic_native/forensic_log.rs) if the report alone is ambiguous. Write the diagnosis as a dated ledger entry (docs/atp_rq_beat_rsync_ledger.md) with the numbers, and name the fix for A4 (which knob, which code path, expected effect: e.g. credit -> raise defaults to BDP for 200 ms x 1 Gbit = 25 MB per connection, 4 MB per stream, and send MAX_DATA at 50 % consumption; cwnd -> RFC 9002 slow start with HyStart++ and proper loss detection; pacing -> pace at 1.25 x cwnd/RTT).

ACCEPTANCE: ledger entry states the limiter with the counters that prove it and a countermetric (the other two reasons near zero); A4 is refined with the concrete change.

NO-CLAIM: no code change beyond instrumentation consumption.
acceptance_criteria: dated ledger entry with counters proving the limiter and a countermetric; A4 refined with the concrete change
close_reason: Diagnosis delivered: the WAN limiter is the fixed 2 MiB source-stream receive window; ledger entry 782b190a8 with five committed runs, static resize refuted both ways.
