comments.text:
A3 DIAGNOSIS (SapphireHill, 2026-09-03). Binary: release atp built on ovh-a from the round-6 tree (582195258 content; sha256 cce4148d…), bench host ovh-a, 500M, encrypted tier, reps 2, every row sha ok unless marked FAIL. rsync-ssh (aes128-gcm) walls for the same cells: wan 27.1 s, wanqueue 27.2 s, good 25.0 s, bad 129 s.

| regime | stream recv window | atp-quic wall | dominant stall (share) | retransmitted stream bytes | reading |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| wan (90 ms, 300 mbit, deep queue) | 2 MiB (default) | 25.9 s | stream_credit 90 % | 0 | the sender waits on the peer's per-stream flow-control credit; 2 MiB < BDP 3.4 MB, so the link runs at ~half rate |
| wan | 4 MiB | 15.66 s | unacked_guard 75 % | 0 | 255 mbit of 300; 1.73× faster than rsync-ssh; the BDP in-flight cap (gain 2 × BtlBw × RTprop) now binds |
| wan | 8 MiB | 15.66 s | unacked_guard 75 % | 0 | identical to 4 MiB; receiver RSS 43 MB vs 34 MB |
| wanqueue (limit 1000) | 2 MiB | 42.4 s | stream_credit 76 % | 1.9 MB (~290 batches) | shallow-queue loss + head-of-line; credit still dominates |
| wanqueue | 4 MiB | 38.6 / 48.4 s | — | — | NOISY at reps 2 (cv ≫ 5 %); needs reps ≥ 5 before any claim |
| wanqueue | 8 MiB | 42.0 s | unacked_guard 75 %, pacing 26 % | 1.1 MB | no gain: the queue-loss path, not the window, is the limiter here |
| good (shallow shaper ≈ 1.4 MB) | 2 MiB | 41–44 s | stream_credit 54–58 %, pacing ~32 % | 38–42 MB | the MATRIX-228 optimum |
| good | 8 MiB | 67–68 s | unacked_guard 66 %, pacing ~45 % | 305 MB (61 % of the file re-sent) | repair explosion, exactly the MATRIX-228 refutation |
| bad | 2 MiB | 133–134 s | stream_credit 60 %, pacing 32 % | 108 KB | parity with rsync (link-bound) |
| bad | 8 MiB | 363 s FAIL ×2 | (sender died) | — | receiver: "stream receive reassembly fragment limit exceeded" (4096 chunks/stream, no coalescing); sender: [ASUP-E804] admission timeout after 360 s |

Answer to A3: on the clean high-RTT path the QUIC sender is FLOW-CONTROL-BOUND by the fixed 2 MiB source-stream receive window (`QUIC_SOURCE_STREAM_RECV_WINDOW_BYTES`, env override `ATP_QUIC_STREAM_RECV_WINDOW`), not cwnd, not pacing, not PTO. On queue-limited or lossy paths the same window is the RIGHT size: a larger static window inflates repair volume (good) or kills the connection outright (bad). NewReno cwnd never bound anywhere (cwnd stall = 0 in every row); pacing is the secondary limiter on the shallow-queue regimes.

Report caveats found while reading the rows (fix in A4): `min_rtt_micros` / `smoothed_rtt_micros` / `pto_count` / `*_congestion_window_bytes` come from `transport.rtt()` and run on the link's synthetic event-count clock (`QuicLink.clock`, +1 ms per packet), so they are not time; the wall-clock RTprop lives in the stream delivery sampler (`rtprop_min_micros`). `transport_samples` is fine. `peak_bytes_in_flight` is 0 on this path (bulk data is transport-untracked); `stream_unacked_bytes` peak is what should be reported.

title: Reconcile current runtime contracts across plans, README and reachable recipes
description:
BACKGROUND: September 4 code outruns some docs and contradicts others. Channel permits now use Cx registration, while no-Cx try_reserve may be untracked; SendPermit::send returns an Outcome that can report disconnect. Explicit root drain differs from block_on/Runtime teardown. v4 plan and docs/integration.md still demand canonical CBOR/ignored unknown fields despite frozen strict JSON V1-V3. Formal semantics:1488-1515 assumes termination under fairness alone and :1648 says exact lab refinement; README correctly disclaims it. WASM guarantee tables overstate a handle ledger. Dependency plan removal paragraphs conflict with KEEP/additive Rev-5. TESTING.md has old counts and dormant supervision recipes.

CHANGE: Revise existing controlling docs in place, trace every change to code and actual evidence, distinguish current source, historical receipts, model laws and published package behavior. Keep unimplemented goals linked to their real implementation task rather than closing them by relabeling. Correct send examples to deliberately handle outcomes; do not add breaking must_use warnings under 0.4.x. Preserve strict wire, document future protocol decisions explicitly. State cooperation/progress/mask/finite-work assumptions for liveness. Preserve complete generic dependency/feature capability and current KEEP decisions. Fix recipe references/discovery, and coordinate actual supervision harness work with R5T; never wire Tokio scaffolding into core. Include ATP adaptive-regret theorem/units/horizon corrections and AppSpec/snapshot metadata-vs-execution scope.

ACCEPTANCE: source-referenced contradictions resolved, dated support/proof boundaries exact, no feature removed, and R9T proves executable examples/commands rather than only matching prose. No new dashboard or artificial test-LOC quota. Estimate 2-3 days.

EXECUTION AND EVIDENCE: Work only on shared main, reserve exact touched paths, preserve peer changes and the v0.4.3/0.4.x public contract (including struct literals, traits, warnings and wire bytes). Additive entry points are preferred; no file deletion, dependency removal, default flip or protocol break is authorized. Read the applicable AGENTS.md and TESTING_FOR_AGENTS.md before implementation. title: QUIC WAN A4: fix the limiter (BDP-sized credit / RFC 9002 slow start + HyStart++ / pacing) with lab-deterministic tests and the netem wan receipt
description:
WHY: See A1-A3. The encrypted ATP tier must not be 3-9x slower than plain TCP on a 90 ms path for the README's transfer promise to mean anything outside a LAN; QUIC with a correctly sized window and standard congestion control should match TCP on a clean path and beat it under loss (RaptorQ + no head-of-line blocking).

WHAT: implement the fix A3 named. Expected shapes (pick the one A3 proved): (a) flow control: raise the receiver's advertised initial_max_data / initial_max_stream_data_bidi_* defaults to BDP-sized values (targets: 25 MB connection, 4 MB stream at 200 ms x 1 Gbit) and replenish credit when 50 % is consumed rather than at exhaustion; make them configurable through the existing NativeQuicConnectionConfig (additive fields with defaults); (b) congestion control: RFC 9002 NewReno with slow start until the first loss or ECN-CE, HyStart++ exit, initial window 10 x max_datagram_size, persistent-congestion handling, and cwnd growth per acked bytes (not per ACK frame); (c) pacing: pacing_rate = 1.25 x cwnd / smoothed_rtt in slow start, 1.0 x afterwards, never below the link estimate. Whatever the shape, the sender must stay bounded-memory (the earlier RSS work MATRIX-213 brought the encrypted board from 882 MB to 12 MB — do not regress: the receiver's advertised credit is the bound; cap total buffered bytes explicitly).

TESTS (all deterministic, LabRuntime clock): unit tests for the CC/credit state machine (cwnd trajectory under a scripted ACK/loss sequence, credit replenishment timing, persistent congestion); a planted negative that a regression to the old window shape fails; the QUIC conformance tests in src/net/quic_native/transport_conformance_tests.rs extended for the new defaults; then the netem wan cell from A1 (QUIC >= 60 % of TCP on the same cell) and the perfect/good/bad encrypted cells unchanged or better (scorecard diff).

ACCEPTANCE: wan cell QUIC/TCP wall ratio <= 1.7 (from >= 3 today), no regression on the other regimes, sender peak RSS within 1.5x of today's, all QUIC unit/conformance lanes green, lab-deterministic tests cover the new state machine, public API additive only.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
A4 DESIGN (SapphireHill, 2026-09-03), from the A3 measurements: a static window change is OFF the table (8 MiB: wan 1.65× faster, good 1.6× slower with 61 % of the file re-sent, bad = hard failure). The fix is sender-gated receive-window growth so a clean high-RTT path grows past 2 MiB and a queue-limited or lossy path never does.

1. Receiver (src/net/quic_native/streams.rs + connection.rs): on `STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED{stream, limit}` for a bounded-window stream, if `limit >= recv_limit_advertised - window/16` (the peer really is at our edge) and the stream has consumed at least one full window since the last growth, double `recv_window_bytes` up to a cap; `advance_bounded_recv_windows` then advertises it. Today the receiver ignores the frame (`process_frame_at` => `Ok(())`).
2. Sender (src/net/atp/transport_quic/native_link.rs `wait_source_stream_send_admission`): the ATP link waits BEFORE writing, so `write_stream_bytes` never hits `FlowControlError::Exhausted` and no BLOCKED frame is emitted today. Add `pub(crate) NativeQuicConnection::request_stream_window(id)` (wraps `queue_stream_data_blocked`) and call it from the StreamCredit stall branch, at most once per advertised window, and ONLY while loss-clean: `retransmit_batches` unchanged since the last request, no ack-gap losses in the window, and not unacked_guard-bound. Lossy shallow-queue paths therefore never ask.
3. Growth cap: 4 MiB until reassembly chunks coalesce. `MAX_BUFFERED_STREAM_REASSEMBLY_FRAGMENTS = 4096` nodes per stream and `recv_chunks` never merges adjacent chunks, so behind one hole an 8 MiB window buffers ~7000 × ~1.2 KB chunks and trips the guard deterministically (the bad-regime failure). 4 MiB captured the entire wan win (15.66 s, same as 8 MiB) at lower RSS. Coalescing contiguous chunks on insert (node count = holes + 1; hostile non-adjacent fragmentation still counted; existing fragment-limit tests kept) is the enabler for 8–16 MiB later — file it as A4b if not done in the same change.
4. Backstop: when the fragment guard trips, stop advertising credit (backpressure) instead of failing the connection; a loss burst after growth must degrade, not kill.
5. Report fixes (same change): RTprop/BtlBw from the stream delivery sampler (wall clock) instead of `transport.rtt()` (synthetic event clock, documented in the report docs); add min live `unacked_admission_cap_bytes` sampled at each stall and peak `stream_unacked_bytes`.
6. Tests: streams/connection unit tests (growth on BLOCKED, hysteresis, cap, no growth without consumption, no growth without a BLOCKED); native_link lab test for the loss gate (loss-free path grows, a path with a retransmit batch does not); bench: wan ≈ 15.7 s, wanqueue unchanged (reps ≥ 5), good unchanged ≈ 43 s, bad unchanged ≈ 133 s, every row sha ok.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
A4 MEASURED — FIRST GATE WAS TOO WEAK, HARDENED (SapphireHill, 2026-09-04). Read this before trusting the growth path on main.

The sender-gated growth landed in fc892d50c (with 5061e609f / fdb676ef0 fixing two compile breaks). Bench on ovh-a with the HEAD binary (sha 88d90d23, no env override, WORK_DIR reuse), 500M encrypted, every row SHA-verified unless marked:

| regime | reps | atp-quic wall | rsync-ssh | vs the 2 MiB baseline | window requests | peak unacked | retransmitted |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| wan (90 ms, 300 mbit, deep queue) | 3 | 15.67 / 15.96 / 15.97 s | 27.1-27.7 s | 25.9 s → 15.7 s, **1.72× faster than rsync** | 242 | 4.19 MB | 0 |
| good (shallow shaper) | 3 | 44.6 / 55.5 / 56.1 s | 24.6-25.3 s | 42.4 s → 55.5 s, **REGRESSION** | 41-50 | 2.8-3.0 MB | 149-240 MB |
| wanqueue (limit 1000) | 2 | 51.7 / 43.7 s | — | 42.4 s → noisy/worse | 49-59 | 4.19 MB | 10-103 MB |
| bad | 2 | 363.6 / 365.7 s **FAIL, sha_ok=false** | 129 s | 133 s → hard failure | — | — | — |

The `wan` result is the intended win and proves the mechanism end to end: peak unacked 4.19 MB is above the 2 MiB HelloAck window, so the receiver really did grow it, with zero retransmits. But the gate let the window grow on the loss-prone paths too, and there the grown window is exactly the MATRIX-228 disaster: `good` re-sent 149-240 MB (vs 38-42 MB at 2 MiB), and `bad` died with the receiver reporting `stream receive reassembly fragment limit exceeded` and the sender timing out with `[ASUP-E804] transport timeout during source stream send admission after 360s`.

Root cause of the weak gate: it asked whenever no retransmit batch had happened *since the last decision*. Early in a transfer that is trivially true, so the first request always went out before any loss could be observed; and later, on a bursty-loss path, any single quiet window qualified. `good` has ~333 repair episodes over the transfer and still found 41-50 quiet windows.

Hardened (verification lane running):
- **Cumulative disqualification plus a warmup.** `source_stream_window_request_due` now asks only when the transfer has *never* retransmitted, and only after 8 windows of credit (16 MiB, ~3 % of a 500 MB WAN transfer) have gone by cleanly since the admission gate first ran; then at most once per window. One repair episode disqualifies growth for the rest of the transfer.
- **Receiver-side veto.** `allow_stream_recv_window_growth` now takes the reassembly-fragment budget, and `note_peer_stream_data_blocked` refuses to grow once a quarter of it is already buffered as out-of-order chunks. A holey stream can no longer walk itself into the fatal guard.
- **The ask is best-effort and adds no wait.** The frame is queued and rides the gate's existing flush (the flush condition now also fires on pending control frames); a failure to queue is ignored. The earlier version's extra `flush().await` inside the admission loop is what made `atp_cli_quic_loopback` time out in two fallback tests and pushed the auto-trait solver over its recursion limit (`overflow evaluating the requirement {async block@src/net/atp/sdk/bonded.rs:375}: Send`), which broke the release-blocking cancel-contract lane's compile.

KNOWN STATE OF main RIGHT NOW (5b1f1d523): the weak gate is still what is pushed. On a lossy path it can grow the window and fail the transfer (typed error, SHA-verified failure, no silent corruption). The fix above is written and in verification; it lands as soon as the lane is green. Do not run ATP over QUIC on lossy paths from this HEAD.

No-claim: the 4 MiB cap stays. Growth beyond it needs contiguous reassembly chunks to coalesce (node count = holes + 1) so a large window cannot approach the 4096-fragment guard; that is a follow-up, as is making the guard back-pressure instead of failing the connection. `wanqueue` remains too noisy at reps 2 (rsync itself moved 27 s → 45-49 s between runs) for any claim beyond "the window is not its limiter".

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
A4 ATTRIBUTION — the `Send` overflow is mine, and it broke a release-blocking lane (SapphireHill, 2026-09-04).

Symptom: the cancel-contract lane (`cargo test -p asupersync --locked --test runtime_abort_vs_cancel_semantics_audit` with `RUSTFLAGS='-D warnings'`) fails to COMPILE the lib:

    error: overflow evaluating the requirement `{async block@src/net/atp/sdk/bonded.rs:375:50: 375:60}: std::marker::Send`
      = note: which requires `{async fn body of BondedTransfer::run_receive}: Send`
      = note: which requires `{async fn body of transport_rq::bonded::receive_bonded}: Send`
      = note: which requires `{async fn body of transport_rq::bonded::receive_bonded_with_options}: Send`
      = note: which requires `{async fn body of transport_rq::bonded::receive_bonded_with_options_and_advertised_ips}: Send`
      = note: which requires `{async fn body of transport_rq::bonded::drain_bonded_round_tail}: Send`   (… truncated)

Bisect, same command, committed trees only (`--base <sha> --clean-overlay --no-overlay`, `cargo check -p asupersync --lib` with the same RUSTFLAGS), lane `lane_bisect`:

| base | what it is | result |
|---|---|---|
| `ef1867cff` | before the round-6 push | exit 0, overflow count 0 |
| `582195258` | the round-6 push (obligation mailbox, lab replay, limiter report) | exit 0, overflow count 0 |
| `5b1f1d523` | current HEAD, includes the A4 window growth | exit 101, overflow count 1 |

The toolchain pin (`340ce087b`, nightly-2026-08-31) is NOT the cause: it is a descendant of `fdb676ef0`, and `fdb676ef0` — A4 code on the OLD toolchain — already showed the same overflow in lane r6b. So the A4 change is what tipped it.

Cause and fix: `Cx::spawn` requires the whole coroutine witness of the bonded receive chain to be `Send`, and proving that walks one solver frame per `async fn` link. The chain was already close to the default depth of 128; A4's additions to the QUIC send path (new limiter fields carried across awaits, the probe state on `QuicLink`) pushed it over. The chain is deep, not recursive, so the depth is the thing to raise: `#![recursion_limit = "256"]` in `src/lib.rs`, with a comment naming the chain so the next person who adds an async link there knows what they are near. Removing the extra `flush().await` I had added did NOT fix it on its own (it did fix the two `atp_cli_quic_loopback` fallback timeouts), which is what sent me to the bisect.

Honest note on why this reached main at all: the lane that catches it is release-blocking, but it had been refused by the fleet (`rc=103`, wrong `-j` for the workers' 10 slots) for most of two sessions, so nothing red was visible when the sweeper pushed. Verification of the raised limit is lane r10 stage CANCEL_CONTRACT.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
A4 DONE (SapphireHill, 2026-09-04). Sender-gated receive-window growth for the ATP source stream, plus the report fixes A3 asked for.

WHAT LANDED
- Receiver (`quic_native`): `note_peer_stream_data_blocked` doubles a bounded window on STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED, but only when growth was enabled, the peer is within one window of our advertised edge, a full window has been consumed since the last growth, and fewer than a quarter of the reassembly budget is buffered as out-of-order chunks. `allow_stream_recv_window_growth(id, max_window, fragment_ceiling)`, `stream_recv_window_bytes`, `stream_send_limit`, `report_stream_data_blocked` and `has_pending_control_frames` are additive.
- Sender (`transport_quic`): `source_stream_window_request_due` asks once per window of credit, only on a transfer that has NEVER retransmitted, and only after 8 clean windows (16 MiB at the 2 MiB default). The frame is queued best-effort and rides the admission loop's existing flush — it adds no await.
- Cap: 4 MiB (`ATP_QUIC_STREAM_RECV_WINDOW_MAX`), clamped by `quic_source_stream_recv_window_growth_cap` so a window of minimum-size frames behind one hole stays under the 4096-node reassembly guard.
- Report: `path_rtprop_micros`, `path_bottleneck_bytes_per_s`, `min_unacked_admission_cap_bytes`, `peak_stream_unacked_bytes`, `stream_window_requests`, `peak_stream_send_window_bytes`; the transport's own RTT/PTO/cwnd fields are documented in the bench spec as synthetic event-clock units.

MEASURED (ovh-a, binary 2cc0fbf4, 50M encrypted, QUIC only, 3 reps, `artifacts/atp_bench_matrix/20260904T165946Z_hardened_gate_50m/`)
- `wan`: 2.453 / 2.454 / 2.448 s, 14-15 window requests, peak send window 4.19 MB, zero retransmits. The same cell at the fixed 2 MiB window was 3.154 s and rsync-over-ssh is 4.853 s, so 22 % faster than before and 1.98x rsync.
- `good`: 3.656 / 3.756 / 3.954 s, **0 requests**, window stays at 2 MiB.
- `bad`: 15.775 / 14.470 / 14.263 s, **0 requests**, window stays at 2 MiB, all three reps `sha_ok=true`.
Every row verified. The first version of this gate failed `bad` outright; see the two comments above for that measurement and its root cause.

VERIFIED AT HEAD (lane r17 stages against the committed tree, `--base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay`, hz3/hz4; the all-features lint gate from lane r18 at 276ed7e33)
- `clippy --all-targets --all-features --keep-going -- -D warnings` exit 0 in 1572 s, zero diagnostics
- `clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` exit 0; `check --all-targets --all-features --keep-going` exit 0; `cargo fmt --check` exit 0
- cancel contract 34 passed / 0 failed; A4+D1 unit filter 206 passed / 0 failed (Darwin: same filter 205/0, full lib suite 22236/0/23)
- QUIC loopback e2e 8 passed / 1 failed — the failure is `accepts_explicit_self_signed_leaf_pin`, filed as **asupersync-51qpby** and reproduced at `582195258`, before any A4 code

NO-CLAIM
- Measured at 50M, not 500M: ovh-a's root filesystem is full (1.9 GB free; the harness keeps every cell's received copy, so a 500M matrix needs ~5 GB). The 500M re-measurement is owed and is the number to quote for the headline; A5 is the natural home for it.
- `wanqueue` is excluded from every claim: at 2-3 reps it swings 38-52 s for ATP and 27-49 s for rsync on the same host.
- The 4 MiB cap cannot rise until contiguous reassembly chunks coalesce (node count = holes + 1), and the fragment guard should back-pressure instead of failing the connection. Both are follow-ups.
- This work also introduced, and then fixed, a `Send`-proof depth overflow that broke the release-blocking cancel-contract lane's COMPILE; the bisect and the fix are in the comment above. `recursion_limit` now has to be raised per crate (lib, 8 integration tests, the atp binary), which is fragile — boxing one future in the bonded receive chain would fix it structurally and is worth a follow-up.

title: Test: Canonical ATP extensions: stable encoding and duplicate-ID refusal
description:
INDEPENDENT BEHAVIORAL PROOF for Canonical ATP extensions: stable encoding and duplicate-ID refusal.

Construct semantically equal maps with every insertion-order permutation for a small set, repeated independent hash seeds, empty/single/multiple extensions and boundary IDs. Require exact bytes/transcript equality and round-trip values. Feed raw encoded duplicate IDs (same and conflicting payload), truncated extension fields and oversized lengths; require exact duplicate/bounds refusal without consuming a partial frame incorrectly. Verify historical valid unsorted frames still decode if the existing protocol permits them, and existing single-extension goldens stay compatible. Include real native transfer negotiation/transcript roundtrip on two processes. Plant unsorted emission/duplicate overwrite via test fixture and verify the oracle fails.

Use the real public entry point and actual implementation components. Cover deterministic unit/property boundary cases alongside native/process E2E. Each positive runs a meaningful workload; at least one planted violation must fail the named invariant, not an unrelated startup/import error. Preserve first failure, source/package/feature identity, scenario/seed, expected/observed output and terminal counts. For transfer work log session/attempt/peer identity, chosen transport, source/manifest/destination hash, staging/commit state, queue/byte high-water, checkpoint and cancellation/cleanup, with credentials and bearer tokens redacted. A path still returning its compatibility refusal remains an open feature, not completed by a refusal test. Estimate 1-3 days after implementation.

EXECUTION AND EVIDENCE: Work only on shared main, reserve exact touched paths, preserve peer changes and the v0.4.3/0.4.x public contract (including struct literals, traits, warnings and wire bytes). Additive entry points are preferred; no file deletion, dependency removal, default flip or protocol break is authorized. Read the applicable AGENTS.md and TESTING_FOR_AGENTS.md before implementation. All Cargo work uses installed-capability-verified clean-overlay RCH with RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1, an isolated reusable CARGO_TARGET_DIR and no local fallback. comments.text:
SapphireHill (watchdog operator, session 1ca3d7f1). This is about the runtime red that remains after the compile heal. The compile heal landed as 60d373655, by the other SapphireHill session. My identical annotation heal is dropped.

Once tests/appspec_v1_managed.rs compiles, 3 of its 7 tests fail. Evidence: RCH hz3 at 4515ba13f, and again at the verified series tip a35f6e9e8.
- managed_app_executes_routes_restarts_and_enforces_context_on_native_workers

appspec_v1_compiler (7/7) and appspec_v1_lab_replay (2/2) pass.

The first failing assertion is tests/appspec_v1_managed.rs:102. It expects `cx.capability_budget().io_bytes == Some(128)` inside the workload and gets `None`. The two native scenarios then hit their 10 s watchdog, and the lab run ends non-quiescent.

ROOT CAUSE: `RuntimeState::mint_child_region_parts` (src/runtime/state.rs) builds the child region's principal Cx with `Cx::new_with_drivers` and never applies the envelope the region record admitted. The record's envelope is the parent's met with `ChildRegionSpec::capability_budget`. The principal therefore reports `CapabilityBudget::UNSPECIFIED`, and every task spawned through it inherits that. Code under an enveloped parent can thus escape the envelope by opening a child region. AppSpec routes and workers run in exactly such child regions.

FIX (mine; I am the heal owner for this runtime red): after building `principal_cx`, apply `region.capability_budget()` with `apply_child_capability_budget(.., CapabilityBudgetRequirements::NONE)`. Native and lab region opening share this path. Regions under an unspecified parent with no requested budget are unchanged. A commit is built. Receipt lanes cover appspec_v1_* plus 10 more child-region and capability targets, the lib and clippy. They run after my current series lands. Please do not duplicate this fix. comments.text:
A5 PREREQUISITES AND EXACT RECIPE (SapphireHill, 2026-09-04). A4 closed with its measurement taken at 50M, not 500M, so the headline number is this bead's to produce. Everything needed is staged; only the host condition is missing.

WHAT IS OWED. The 500M encrypted matrix with the A4 growth gate live, against the pre-A4 baselines already in the ledger (`wan` 25.9 s at the fixed 2 MiB window, rsync-over-ssh 27.1 s). The 50M result was `wan` 3.154 s → 2.45 s with 14-15 window requests and a 4.19 MB peak send window, `good` and `bad` issuing zero requests, every row sha-verified.

HOST CONDITION (the blocker, checked 2026-09-04 19:5x ET). ovh-a now has 90 GB free — the disk pressure that forced the 50M fallback is gone — but its load average is 47 on 16 cores, with rustc and several multi-hour `bash` processes belonging to other work. A netem bench under that load measures the load, not the change. Wait for the host to be quiet (load < 2, no `rustc`, `ip netns list` empty) before running; do not run the matrix on hz3/hz4 instead, because they are the shared rch build workers and their own queue would both perturb the numbers and be perturbed by them.

RECIPE, all of it already on ovh-a under `/data/tmp/atp_bench_runs/`:
- Launcher `ovh_matrix_a4c.sh`, parameterised by `BIN`, `WORKLOADS`, `REPS`, `REGIMES`, `METHODS`, `WORK_DIR`, `MIN_FREE_GB`. It aborts if another `matrix_bench.sh` is running or if `ip netns list` is non-empty, and it deletes its own `atpc*/atprs*` namespaces at the end.
- Binary `bin/atp_hardened` (sha256 `2cc0fbf4…`), built from the A4-hardened tree. Rebuild from a current HEAD if the ATP path has moved since: `RCH_WORKER=hz3,hz4 rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/rch_target_orch_atpcli cargo build --release -j 4 --bin atp --features atp-cli`, then scp the artifact.
- Run both arms on the SAME host in the same sitting, which is better evidence than comparing against an older run: growth on (default), and growth disabled as the control by setting `ATP_QUIC_STREAM_RECV_WINDOW_MAX=2097152` — a cap at or below the 2 MiB starting window makes `quic_source_stream_recv_window_growth_cap` return `None`, so the receiver never enables growth and the sender's asks are ignored.
- `REPS=5` for anything involving `wanqueue`: at 2-3 reps it swung 38-52 s for ATP and 27-49 s for rsync on the same host, which is why A4 excluded it from every claim.
- Disk: the harness keeps every cell's received copy, so budget ~500 MB per cell. A 3-regime, 3-rep, both-arms run is ~9 GB. Pass `MIN_FREE_GB` and check `df` first; the 2026-09-02 outage started exactly this way.

Evidence already committed for comparison: `artifacts/atp_bench_matrix/20260903T000439Z_wan2mib`, `…T001018Z_wan8mib`, `…T004813Z_wan4mib`, `…T001555Z_goodbad8mib`, `…T003552Z_goodbad2mib`, `20260904T051031Z_growth_wan_good`, `20260904T052300Z_growth_bad_wanqueue`, `20260904T165946Z_hardened_gate_50m`.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
## SapphireHill (agent-mail id NavyFox this session) — observation scope fixed; verification requested

Independently verified the described bugs against HEAD before touching anything.

**The bugs this bead described are already refactored away.** `next_progress`,
`wait_for_completion`, and the event-consuming `is_complete` no longer exist
anywhere in `src/atp/`. `TransferHandle::progress()`/`state()` are now
non-destructive snapshot reads under the actor lock (idempotent, temporary
no-event is not success — `state()` returns the actor's real state, e.g.
`Offered` when not started, not a fabricated terminal), and
`transfer/mod.rs`'s pressure API fails **closed**. So there is no destructive
progress/completion helper left to make non-destructive. I did NOT fabricate
pending/running/terminal state machinery over an already-correct path
(that would be ceremony).

**One genuine residual fail-open bug found and fixed** (commit `da48fce40`):
`TransferHandle::progress()` computed
`bytes_transferred = max(committed, verified, offered)`. Because the actor
reports the documented invariant `offered >= verified >= committed`, that
always collapsed to `offered_bytes`, so every transfer reported **100%** the
instant it offered bytes — before a single byte was verified or committed.
Dormant today (send_object never drives the actor, so offered stays 0), but a
live wrong reading the moment workers are wired — exactly this bead's stated
concern ("dormant helpers become correctness bugs when workers are wired").

Fix: `total_bytes = offered_bytes`;
`bytes_transferred = verified.max(committed).min(offered)`
(verified = transferred; committed is a subset kept via max only for counter-
order robustness; min clamps the ratio <= 100%).

**Evidence (local, repo-pinned nightly; RCH fleet blocked by bi2462.81):**
- RED control: `transfer_handle_progress_measures_verified_against_offered`
  FAILED against the old code (returned 1000/offered, not 400/verified).
- After fix: full `atp::sdk` suite **86 passed / 0 failed** (incl. the 2 new
  tests). rustfmt clean; clippy `--lib` clean for sdk.rs (0 warnings).
- Companion test coverage (bi2462.54): 2 tests added — the 40%-verified case
  and the 100%-only-when-verified case.

**Not in this bead's scope (separate work):** the actor is still never driven
(`send_object` returns a handle over an undriven `TransferActor`), so state and
progress never advance in practice. That "completion waits for verified commit +
worker drain" behavior is gated on the send_object actor-driving / session work
(bi2462.51 and the SDK-execution program), not on observation non-destructiveness.

**Request:** the observation/terminal-query non-destructiveness this bead asked
for is now satisfied. Not self-certifying closure — CopperOak (or the verify
orchestrator), please confirm and close if you agree, or tell me what residual
you still want under this bead.

title: Lab replay B1: specify the production schedule projection and add trace::replay::ProductionSchedule
description:
WHY: The README promises "trace capture/replay: debug production issues locally". Round 2 delivered the first half (asupersync-gap-prod-trace-export-ro6zzy): `Runtime::trace_snapshot()` / `RuntimeHandle::trace_snapshot()` export the production ring buffer in the lab's TraceEvent schema, and tests/runtime_trace_export_e2e.rs proves the lab analysis tools (normalize_trace_default, HappensBeforeGraph, RaceDetector) accept it. The second half does not exist: nothing can RE-EXECUTE a production interleaving in the lab. The lab's ForcedSchedule (src/lab/runtime.rs ~168) is explicitly "not a production scheduler-control format" (config-hash bound to a fresh LabRuntime), and the three-lane production scheduler is not the LabScheduler. Before code, the projection has to be defined precisely or every later bead argues about semantics.

WHAT: write the spec and the type. Spec (docs/replay-debugging.md, new section "Production schedule projection"): which TraceEvent kinds define an interleaving (Spawn, Schedule, Poll, Wake, Complete, CancelRequest/Ack, RegionCreated/CloseBegin/CloseComplete; TimeAdvance/TimerFired as time hints; IoRequested/IoReady/IoResult as opaque outcomes that a replay may only re-inject, never re-perform); how production TaskIds map to lab TaskIds (by spawn order within a region, since ids are arena slots with generations and will differ); what "same interleaving" means (the sequence of (task, poll) pairs, not wall time); what is out of scope (worker identity, wake batching, I/O timing). Type: `asupersync::trace::replay::ProductionSchedule` built from `&[TraceEvent]` with `from_trace(&[TraceEvent]) -> Result<Self, ProjectionError>`, exposing `steps()` (ordered (spawn-ordinal, poll-ordinal) pairs), `task_map()`, and `summary()`; errors for traces that are truncated by the ring buffer (a Poll for a task whose Spawn is missing) — never silently drop.

TESTS: unit tests on hand-built traces (two tasks, interleaved polls; a truncated ring buffer; a trace with regions) and a property test that projecting the lab's own recorded trace round-trips (LabRuntime -> trace -> ProductionSchedule -> equal to the lab's step list).

ACCEPTANCE: doc section merged; ProductionSchedule with the tests above green under `--features test-internals`; no runtime behaviour change; API additive.

NO-CLAIM: no re-execution yet (B2).

title: Lab replay B2: LabConfig::replay_production_schedule drives LabScheduler choices with divergence reporting
description:
WHY: With B1's ProductionSchedule, the lab needs a scheduling oracle that prefers the recorded next task while it is runnable and reports the first divergence otherwise. The LabScheduler already supports seeded and DPOR-guided choice (src/lab/explorer.rs, src/lab/runtime.rs); the ForcedSchedule machinery (run_forced_schedule, ForcedScheduleCandidate) shows the shape of "external choice + revalidation" but is bound to a lab config hash. This bead adds the production-facing variant without touching the production scheduler.

WHAT: `LabConfig::replay_production_schedule(schedule: ProductionSchedule)` (additive; `replay_trace(path)` stays as the metadata string it is today). During execution the LabScheduler consults the schedule: if the recorded next (task, poll) is runnable it is chosen; if it is not runnable yet, the lab advances virtual time / drains wakes up to a bounded number of steps looking for it; if the recorded task no longer exists or the bound is exhausted, execution records a `ReplayDivergence { step, expected, actual, reason }` and either stops (default) or continues with the normal policy (`on_divergence: Stop | Continue`). title: Managed QUIC: drive receive, deadlines and cancellation from one runtime clock without fixed polling
description:
BACKGROUND: managed_endpoint.rs:254-290 serially awaits receive and timer handling, then uses SystemTime plus a fixed 1ms sleep. connection_manager.rs:1112-1140 reads Instant::now and passes remaining duration as Time to Sleep::new, although Sleep::new consumes an absolute deadline (time/sleep.rs:361-365); overdue scheduling returns without an explicit fired event. These are generic substrate gaps identified by RABS section44.5, not a request to build RABS. Existing b0k8qo is a transport campaign and 5u6vzr is Initial rerouting; neither owns this work.

IMPLEMENT: preserve existing public ManagedEndpointConfig, QuicTimerScheduler Instant-taking API, packet/config/error types and accepted wire behavior. Introduce private same-clock conversion or additive explicit-clock APIs, using a stable capability-bound monotonic/runtime origin and checked/saturating representable deadlines; no relative duration may be mistaken for an absolute Time. Existing public APIs may delegate to the private mapping. Drive socket readability, pending writable sends, the earliest live protocol deadline, and caller cancellation together so neither an idle socket nor a future timer prevents the other from making progress. Preserve packet ownership and partially sent batches when a branch yields/cancels, and do not assume any awaited receive/send is cancellation-safe without proving it. Bound per-turn packet/timer work to avoid starvation under continuous input. Recompute/cancel deadlines when connections close, handle overdue timers immediately, permit earlier reschedule without duplicate firing, and remove unconditional millisecond polling. Preserve the Initial-reroute fix, existing packet batching/metrics, connection limits and graceful shutdown. Do not replace the QUIC engine or enable adaptive batching as an unmeasured default.

UNIT/PROPERTY: nonzero virtual time epochs; future deadline initially pending and ready exactly after the controlled advance; overdue deadline fires once; earlier/later/repeated reschedule; no connections cancels obsolete timer; timestamp arithmetic boundaries; simultaneous readiness/cancel/timer; continuously ready input cannot starve due timers; no lost wake between interest registration and readiness. title: Test managed QUIC deadline, idle wake and saturated cancellation through real UDP
description:
Build independent causal regression proof for R14 using the real public managed endpoint and native runtime, not only ConnectionRouter helpers. Extend the maintained native QUIC E2E runner with two real processes and authenticated test identities where supported by the existing connection path. Prove that the intended managed endpoint actually drives the exchange; a separate NativeQuicConnection loop is not a substitute.

SCENARIOS: (1) park an established/armed endpoint with no incoming packet, witness its actual timer registration, and observe due protocol output or declared idle expiry; (2) arm a future deadline, inject a datagram before it, and observe prompt packet progress without waiting for that timer; (3) run repeated long-idle to burst transitions, simultaneous packet/deadline readiness, earlier/later timer replacement and connection removal; (4) saturate receive and constrain send until a real WouldBlock/readiness wait, then request cancellation only after the wait witness and prove owned buffers/connections/tasks/timers drain; (5) continuously ready traffic does not starve due timers/control or another connection; (6) restart a clean endpoint and complete a healthy exchange after each failure/cancel case.

Measure idle loop/poll/wake counts and CPU against the incumbent under identical workload/clock/platform; the correctness acceptance is absence of periodic polling and retained progress, while any performance claim uses raw distributions and predeclared thresholds. Use nonzero-epoch virtual unit/property cases from R14 plus native watchdogs as separate evidence. Plant relative-duration-as-absolute deadline, receive-first starvation, missing wake, or periodic-wake behavior in a test fixture/mutation seam and ensure the matching oracle fails after setup succeeded. Logs record source, peer/connection, clock domain/current/deadline, wake cause, processed packet/timer counts, queued bytes, cancellation witness and final cleanup; redact keys/tokens. Empty suite, mere bind, handshake-only success, test-internal connection creation, timeout and metadata logs cannot pass.

Use existing tests/runners and only br for tracker changes. Work on shared main with exact reservations; preserve peer changes, public 0.4.x source/foreign-trait/exhaustive-struct/behavior contracts, protocol V1-V3 bytes and accepted ATP behavior. No file deletion, dependency removal, default flip, arbitrary preemption or new external product scope. All Cargo through verified installed clean-overlay RCH, RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1, reusable isolated CARGO_TARGET_DIR, no local fallback. Native runtime-changing work first passes runtime_abort_vs_cancel_semantics_audit at the claimed source. Unit/property tests accompany implementation; companion owns causal native/process E2E via maintained scripts with bounded readiness/watchdogs and cleanup. Every required positive has nonzero terminal counts; planted negatives fail for the intended invariant. Preserve first failure, command, exact source/lock/package/features/toolchain/worker, seed/scenario, measured expected/observed values, terminal exit, redacted timing/queue/byte/task/region/connection/lease state. Missing/zero/skipped/timed-out/stale/admission-only evidence is non-green. Product parents wait for implementation and companion proof; no reciprocal prerequisite edges.

title: Remote runtime: add per-peer byte/message admission and protected lifecycle-control capacity
description:
BACKGROUND: NativeRemoteRuntime already caps global live sessions (remote.rs:6813-6846,7060+) and coalesces cancel/lease updates via a capacity-one wake (6928-6985). RemoteRuntime::send_message remains a public synchronous trait method (277-283). RABS section44.4 additionally requires per-peer byte/message limits, priority lanes, cancellation-aware reserve/commit and control capacity that bulk demand cannot exhaust. Existing bi2462.10 is snapshot-specific credits; .16 is region/lease ownership. Neither is generic admission ownership.

IMPLEMENT: add an opt-in, public-compatible NativeRemoteRuntime admission surface with immutable validated policy and an additive Cx-aware reservation API; do not add required trait methods or change synchronous send_message behavior/signatures. Existing callers retain documented behavior; the new admitted path must reach the real named-computation transport. Bound global and authenticated-peer active/queued message count, encoded/payload bytes and waiter metadata, including values owned by a pending future; account repeated cloning/retry materialization or establish a conservative fixed bound. Use checked size validation before cloning or encoding untrusted payloads. Define credit lifetime from reservation through transfer/publication/terminal release, exactly-once release on abort/cancel/error, fixed acquisition order across global/peer/session/byte limits, and identity-generation cleanup without stale credit reuse. A cancellation-aware waiter must remove itself and release all held partial credit; oversize requests fail immediately instead of waiting forever. Bound waiter counts/metadata and define FIFO within a class plus non-starvation across eligible peers.

Protect cancellation, lease renewal and drain capacity independently from queued user work; reuse the existing coalesced control semantics instead of replacing them with an unbounded priority queue. Caller-provided budget priority cannot impersonate authenticated lifecycle control. Preserve authentication/route/grant checks, peer isolation, max_in_flight limits, idempotency and strict JSON V1-V3 bytes; reserve/commit is LOCAL publication/ownership semantics, not remote exactly-once. Saturation returns a typed local refusal or a bounded caller-Cx wait under the new API, and records committed/aborted/live credit. Partial send cancellation cannot release accounting while buffers/task work remain owned. Transport failure is not success; retries remain within the same bounded envelope. No durable build IDs, RABS scheduler, new wire variant, new protocol version or bulk object protocol is required.

UNIT/MODEL: capacities 0/1/N, per-request oversize, sum/encoding overflow, multiple peers, ordering/starvation, canceled waiter, canceled reservation, reserve-vs-close, cancel-vs-commit, failed spawn rollback, retry and identity rotation, result-vs-cancel, control coalescing under full data quotas, and exact credit conservation. Preserve old public trait/object/struct consumers and existing V1-V3 goldens. R15T owns real process behavior and memory/control-latency proof.

Use existing tests/runners and only br for tracker changes. Work on shared main with exact reservations; preserve peer changes, public 0.4.x source/foreign-trait/exhaustive-struct/behavior contracts, protocol V1-V3 bytes and accepted ATP behavior. No file deletion, dependency removal, default flip, arbitrary preemption or new external product scope. All Cargo through verified installed clean-overlay RCH, RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1, reusable isolated CARGO_TARGET_DIR, no local fallback. Native runtime-changing work first passes runtime_abort_vs_cancel_semantics_audit at the claimed source. Unit/property tests accompany implementation; companion owns causal native/process E2E via maintained scripts with bounded readiness/watchdogs and cleanup. Every required positive has nonzero terminal counts; planted negatives fail for the intended invariant. Preserve first failure, command, exact source/lock/package/features/toolchain/worker, seed/scenario, measured expected/observed values, terminal exit, redacted timing/queue/byte/task/region/connection/lease state. Missing/zero/skipped/timed-out/stale/admission-only evidence is non-green. Product parents wait for implementation and companion proof; no reciprocal prerequisite edges.



REFINEMENT 4 — MIXED ENTRY-POINT ACCOUNTING: declare and enforce the accounting domain before implementation. Legacy synchronous calls that share an admitted transport/driver must consume its global/peer/message/byte/control envelope through a compatible internal path, or legacy work must use a genuinely separate bounded transport/driver/queue domain whose memory and claims are reported separately. Merely tagging legacy buffers as excluded inside the same unconstrained queue is not isolation. Preserve the shipped default synchronous behavior and signatures; do not impose new default refusals to make the opt-in numbers pass. Bound all shared transport memory/metadata and show which class owns every buffer. Unit and real process tests concurrently saturate legacy and admitted calls to the same and different peers, then cancel/renew/drain and run a healthy admitted request. Verify the declared total/domain high-water bounds, no bypass of advertised peer/control guarantees, exact release and old-call compatibility under mixed load. If compatible shared accounting cannot be established, select the separate opt-in domain and constrain the claim explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: IMPLEMENTATION CLOSURE: focused code and unit/compatibility proof; the product pair additionally requires its independent test companion. The opt-in admitted API drives actual native remote computations while every tracked global/peer/message/byte/waiter limit is enforced, all credits resolve exactly once, and data saturation cannot reject/starve authenticated cancel/renew/drain solely for lack of data credit. No cross-peer starvation or head-of-line deadlock under declared finite work assumptions. Pending/retry buffers are included in a stated bound. Old synchronous callers and V1-V3 wire stay compatible. Unit/model/property evidence and required native cancellation baseline pass; no distributed exactly-once or unbounded third-party-code preemption claim. Mixed legacy/admitted-call saturation proves the explicit shared or isolated accounting domain, preserves legacy defaults and cannot bypass the advertised memory, peer-isolation or control-capacity guarantee.

title: Lab replay B3: complete production capture, explicit prefix mode and native-to-lab outcome proof
description:
CURRENT GOVERNING SCOPE — 2026-09-04 reality check. Native trace_snapshot and ProductionSchedule/projection/driver now exist; preserve bi2462.6/.7 and complete ForcedSchedule behavior. Their lab-generated fixtures are not production capture. replay.rs:851-1022 lacks complete coverage checks and projects completion outcome to zero; lab/runtime.rs:1285-1288 falls back to ordinary scheduling at end of recorded choices. That may serve explicit legacy prefix replay, but cannot establish complete replay.

Implement an additive complete-capture mode/provenance or typed inability-to-prove-completeness refusal, preserving current 0.4.x prefix behavior. Capture from a real two-worker Runtime running 4-6 interacting yielding/channel tasks, then use identical workload factories and explicit inputs under LabRuntime. Prove birth-to-replay identity mapping, actual poll order, channel values, terminal Outcomes and quiescence. Complete mode never silently executes extra unrecorded work after exhaustion. Source/feature/config/capture identity must be retained.

Negative controls on copies of a real capture: missing prefix births, interior poll loss, suffix loss after all births, duplicate/reordered sequence, altered task generation, extra replay work and terminal outcome drift. Refuse each before incorrect work/effects where detectable; cases that cannot be validated must be unsupported, not successful complete replay. Cancellation-order acceptance requires projected and executed CancelRequest/Ack causality; retaining hints alone does not prove it. Timers/arbitrary IO/external state remain unclaimed. The integration target must be normally discovered with nonzero terminal RCH results. bi2462.9 and ro6zzy closure depend on this actual behavior. Preserve all original workload/failure goals below; conflicting source-absence and implicit-strict/default assumptions are superseded.

HISTORICAL ORIGINAL CONTEXT (preserved for provenance; the current governing scope above supersedes conflicting instructions):

WHY: B1+B2 are only real if a trace captured from a PRODUCTION runtime (three-lane scheduler, real threads) replays in the lab and reproduces the recorded poll order. This is the behavioural proof the README claim needs; unit tests on hand-built traces are not it.

WHAT: tests/runtime_trace_replay_e2e.rs: build a multi-worker production runtime (RuntimeBuilder, 2 workers) with trace capture on; spawn 4-6 tasks that yield a deterministic number of times and exchange messages over an mpsc so their poll order is data-dependent; export via `Runtime::trace_snapshot()`; project (B1); replay in a LabRuntime (B2) running the SAME task bodies; assert the lab's recorded (spawn-ordinal, poll-ordinal) sequence equals the production projection and the replay report has no divergence. Planted negative: perturb one step of the projection and assert divergence at that step. Second scenario: a trace truncated by a small ring buffer (`trace_buffer_capacity`) must produce a ProjectionError, not a silent partial replay. Third: a production trace containing cancellation (CancelRequest/Ack) replays with the same cancel ordering.

HOW: the task bodies must be runnable under both runtimes: write them against `Cx` + the sync primitives only (no I/O, no wall-clock). Use test-internals feature for lab hooks. Run through rch with RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 and keep it in the CI test job's feature set.

ACCEPTANCE: e2e green on Linux with the release feature list; the planted negative fails as designed; the truncated case errors; test listed in the CI feature set (not `#[ignore]`).

NO-CLAIM: does not replay I/O outcomes or timers (recorded as hints only); does not prove replay of arbitrary user code that touches ambient state.
acceptance_criteria: Complete-capture mode records a real two-worker native Runtime workload and replays the same workload inputs with exact birth/generation mapping, poll order, channel values, terminal Outcomes and quiescence. Complete replay cannot silently fall back to unrecorded scheduling. Missing prefix/interior/suffix, altered generation/order/outcome and extra-work controls fail for the intended reason; unsupported capture coverage is explicitly refused. Preserve legacy prefix behavior and restrict cancellation claims to executed request/ack causality. The normally discovered integration target and native cancellation baseline have terminal strict-remote results at the claimed source/profile, nonzero selected and passed counts and explicit failed/ignored/filtered counts. No arbitrary IO/timer replay claim. This child closes on its own evidence; .9 and ro6zzy follow afterward.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text: PREREQUISITE FOUND (SapphireHill, 2026-09-02, while implementing B2): the production runtime's trace buffer records TraceEventKind::Spawn (runtime/state.rs create/admit path) and Complete, but NO per-poll event: nothing in src/runtime/ (three-lane worker, scheduler) pushes a Poll or Schedule TraceEvent. Only the LabRuntime's replay recorder records TaskScheduled per step. Consequently ProductionSchedule::from_runtime_trace on a real production trace yields spawn order but zero steps (summary.steps == 0), and B3's "same poll order" e2e cannot be built until the three-lane worker emits a Poll (or Schedule) trace event at its poll site. B3 must add that emission (cheap, seq + task + region; consider gating behind the existing trace capacity/kind filters rather than a new feature flag), then project. B2 is built and tested against lab recordings: spawn order from the lab's TraceEvent buffer (state.rs Spawn events) + poll order from the replay recorder's TaskScheduled events, merged by LabRuntime::recorded_production_schedule().

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
B3 precise site (SapphireHill): src/runtime/scheduler/worker.rs `execute()`, after `region_id` and `poll_attempt` are computed (~line 585) and before `self.panic_isolator.isolate_task_execution(task_id, region_id, poll_attempt, || stored.poll(&mut cx))`, add `self.trace.record_event(|seq| TraceEvent::poll(seq, poll_start, task_id, region_id));` (optionally `TraceEvent::yield_task` on `Poll::Pending`). `record_event` hands out the seq from the buffer, the same pattern the worker already uses for `io_requested` / `io_ready` (worker.rs:310-315). With that, `ProductionSchedule::from_runtime_trace` projects the real poll order.

CAUTION before closing B3: every poll then pushes one trace event. Audit the native-runtime tests that fingerprint or count trace events (trace_fingerprint, crashpack goldens, replay-delta docs, any `trace().snapshot().len()` assertion) in the same change, and run the full lib + trace + lab test lanes in clean-overlay mode.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Progress (SapphireHill, 2026-09-30): landed 926d7deb6 (fix) and e629f47ae (test-only, tests/native_schedule_capture.rs).

0. REGRESSION FOUND AND FIXED (926d7deb6). Since d8e81f2cd (3dridc, 2026-09-25), block_on registers its caller's root future as a task. Every block_on call therefore added a Spawn and a Complete to the trace, and schedule capture projected those caller tasks as scheduled work that the Lab cannot recreate. Strict replay of any capture taken around block_on, including every #[main] program, expected extra spawns. The existing native_schedule_capture test had been red since then (spawned 4 vs 2), and nothing ran it; the last pass was at f4bd942d3.
   - The fix: CallerTaskRegistration notes the task with the capture. ScheduleCaptureSnapshot::caller_tasks() reports it (additive), and production_schedule() leaves caller observations out, so the harness plays the caller's part.
   - The old-code control (note disabled) fails the new witness, "one caller task per block_on".

1. native_ring_capture_replays_poll_order_and_channel_values: 4 interacting tasks on the production runtime (1 and 2 workers, with and without sharded state).
   - The tasks pass one token around a ring of capacity-1 asupersync mpsc channels, for 12 hops.
   - Every stage genuinely parks (a Pending witness) before an external oneshot kick. From then on only the token holder is runnable.
   - For each combination:
     - the capture is complete (4 spawns, at least 28 polls);
     - strict Lab replay of the same stage bodies returns Matched and passed(), with every recorded poll matched;
     - every Lab task finishes;
     - every stage received exactly the native tokens, which also equal a runtime-free model.

2. real_ring_capture_copies_with_defects_are_refused: negative controls on copies of one REAL 1-worker capture. The unmodified copy replays completely. Each damaged copy:
   - Missing birth (stage 0's Spawn removed): the projection returns MissingSpawn. Admitted as an orphan, the driver returns OrphanSpawns{1} before any work.
   - Altered task generation on one poll: MissingSpawn at that poll's seq.
   - Duplicated poll, or that poll swapped with the next event: SourceOrder, naming both sequences, before any work.
   - Interior poll loss: Diverged, TaskNotRunnable at ordinal 3. The driver stops at the first recorded choice it cannot honour and never polls the unrecorded work.
   - Suffix loss after all births: SourceExhausted, with exactly the retained polls matched and no divergence.
   - Extra Lab task: SpawnCountMismatch{4,5} after zero driver steps.
   - Terminal outcome drift: the projection carries no results (completions carry outcome 0). The same schedule drives a ring kicked with a different value to Matched with different tokens, so result equality is the harness's oracle (both tests compare values). This is documented as outside the strict receipt, not claimed.
   In every refused or stopped case no stage completes, and the helper then drains the retained work under ordinary scheduling.

Still open for this bead's acceptance:
- Cancellation-order replay. The projection skips CancelRequest and CancelAck; native capture records CancelAck (native_cancellation_capture_contains_ack_before_completion), but replay neither projects nor executes cancel causality.
- Workloads whose polls race on shared state across 2 workers. The capture records poll-entry order, and overlapping polls are outside what replay claims (see the src/trace/capture.rs docs).
- Timers, I/O and external state remain unclaimed, as the scope says.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SapphireHill, 2026-10-01, design note for the two remaining items (read-only, origin 3913fd642):
1. Terminal-outcome drift. The production trace's Complete event is TraceData::Task { task, region }, with no outcome. The projection therefore emits ReplayEvent::TaskCompleted { outcome: 0 } (src/trace/replay.rs ~983; ProjectionSummary::completed says so). TraceData, TraceEventKind and ReplayEvent are all exhaustive public enums, unchanged in shape since v0.4.3. Adding an outcome field or a variant would break downstream exhaustive matches.
   Additive route: the capture recorder (CaptureContext, the same hook as note_caller_task) records each task's terminal OutcomeKind (Ok/Err/Cancelled/Panicked) at completion, outside the trace. ScheduleCaptureSnapshot exposes it through a new accessor, for example terminal_outcomes() -> &[(TaskId, Severity)]. The replay harness or driver then compares Lab outcomes against it and refuses a mismatch. No trace or replay enum changes.
2. Cancel-order causality. CancelRequest/CancelAck are not projected; they are counted as unsupported. The same side-channel shape works: ordered (task, CancelRequested{reason kind}) and (task, CancelAcked) observations kept by the recorder. Replay must then inject the cancel at the recorded ordinal and check the ack order. Retaining hints alone does not prove causality, as the bead says.
Both are additive. They need a recorder hook at task completion and at cancel request/ack in the three-lane worker, so they touch scheduler hot paths. That needs the runtime_abort_vs_cancel_semantics_audit lane and an overhead check with capture off.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SapphireHill, 2026-10-01: terminal-outcome drift is now refused. LANDED as de7ef04ba (main=master).

What landed:
- A native capture keeps each task's terminal outcome beside its Complete event. This is the TraceBufferHandle outcome annex, enabled only when a capture is active; RuntimeState records it on every Complete.
- ScheduleCaptureSnapshot::terminal_outcomes() lists them. production_schedule() carries them into the projected TaskCompleted events and refuses a completion without one (new ScheduleCaptureError::MissingOutcome).
- ProductionSchedule::carries_outcomes() and captured_outcome() report them.
- run_production_schedule_strict compares each recorded task's Lab outcome by spawn ordinal. A run that would be Matched becomes OutcomeMismatch { ordinal, expected, observed }.
All of this is additive: the new enum variants are on #[non_exhaustive] enums, and no trace or replay event type changed.

Receipts:
- native_schedule_capture 7/0 (hz2). The new native_capture_outcomes_refuse_terminal_outcome_drift ends in OutcomeMismatch { 1, Ok, Some(Panicked) }; the parked-wakes and ring replays still end Matched with outcomes compared.
- runtime_abort_vs_cancel_semantics_audit 42/0.
- lib trace:: lab::runtime runtime::state 1506/0/1 (hz4).
- Control with the driver check disabled: red. Without the check the receipt was Matched, with 24/24 oracles passing, although the reconstructed task panicked.
- clippy clean.

Caveat, documented and filed as 6hewgp: an outcome is the runtime's record. RuntimeHandle::spawn records a panicking future as Ok and re-raises the panic on its JoinHandle; state tasks record Panicked. Reconstructions must end the same way.

Still open here: cancel-order causality (CancelRequest/Ack projection and injection), per the 10-01 design note.

title: Restore admissible remote validation without automatic deletion and run the native canary
description:
Reality-check prerequisite extracted from all-open-bug-fixes-eti0ty. Installed rch 2.0.0 commit 3289f5e4e977 still calls worker_cache_prune_rsync_path_prefix in /data/projects/remote_compilation_helper/rch/src/transfer.rs:247. That focused run is not an equivalent benchmark. Existing p26k3k owns compiler errors, .81 owns admissible retained-artifact RCH, and closed validation-frontier work defines contracts; none establishes a bounded, current, actually executed default user validation journey.

Implement in existing TESTING.md, applicable test runner(s), Cargo target organization/configuration only as measurement justifies. No new readiness dashboard. First measure an exact frozen revision, lock, toolchain, feature graph and worker: cold compile, link, test execution, peak RSS, retained disk, warm rerun. Do not delete caches to simulate cold: use an admitted empty target path, retain artifacts under .81. Record sample counts and pressure so noisy/failed runs cannot become performance wins.
Define a native-first default developer lane that completes WITH executed tests inside a declared 3600-second envelope on an explicitly named supported worker/profile; this is a proposed acceptance target, not a claim already achieved. Keep the unfiltered runtime_abort_vs_cancel_semantics_audit first, then representative core ownership/channel/lab journeys. Diagnose whether target fanout, linking, feature unification, or codegen dominates before changes.

Target consolidation is permissible only with exact test-identity coverage, cfg/feature/platform partitions, ignored-test inventory, and crate-isolation/global-state side effects reviewed. No dropping tests, adding ignores, narrowing existing release guarantees, blanket lint allowances, dependency removal, or local Cargo. Use existing runner infrastructure and compatible Cargo features. Do not add GitHub Actions. Measure both cold and warm costs; performance acceptance cannot be satisfied by moving costs outside the measured interval.
Companion independent verification must run the maintained command, count actual selected/executed tests, reject zero tests and early successful exits, preserve native negative controls, and demonstrate coverage conservation for the full schedule. Work can investigate statically before .81 is resolved, but no new build until its admission conditions hold. Shared main, exact reservations, no branches/worktrees/deletion, no public API or wire change. Complexity L; closes an execution-cost gap, not runtime correctness or release readiness.

title: Measure where validation time goes: --timings for check/test --no-run at a pinned SHA, cold/warm, per target class, plus capacity model
description:
## Why (reality check 2026-09-23, S7) — child of bi2462.82 (build budget), which this refresh raises to P0
Validation capacity is now the binding constraint on delivery. At origin f4423fcf0 the crate has 1,507 integration-test
targets (397 `*_contract.rs`; 553 never reference the `asupersync` crate; 110 with a file-level feature cfg but only 15
`[[test]]` entries), 84.4 MB of src .rs and 37.9 MB of tests .rs. GitHub issue #72: cold workspace clippy 48m12s; cold
`cargo test --workspace` killed at 3600 s still compiling, zero test binaries run, 120-150 GiB artifacts. Root lanes on
09-23 (-j 3, vmi workers): default all-targets check 24m40s; all-features check 33m; default clippy 19.4m; native tests
5m26s warm. RCH recorded 319 asupersync admission refusals in ~25 h. Nobody has measured WHERE the time goes.

## Work
Measure, at one pinned SHA on one named worker (hz4 preferred; record slots, RAM, disk free, other load):
1. `cargo check --all-targets --timings` and `cargo test --no-run --timings` (default features), cold (fresh admitted
   target path; do not delete caches to simulate cold) and warm (immediate rerun, and a rerun after touching one src file
   and one tests file). Keep the HTML/JSON timing reports as artifacts under the bead (not in git).
2. Split total time into: dependency build, asupersync lib (check / codegen), per-test-target compile, and link. Report
   the top 30 targets by time, and aggregate time for the 553 crate-independent targets, the 397 contracts and the rest.
3. Retained disk per target class (bytes of each test binary + deps), total target size, with and without
   CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0.
4. Compute the capacity model with the measured S: ρ = λ·S/(c·1440) for λ = 12 and 68 commits/day and c = 2, 3, and the
   S needed for ρ ≤ 0.5 at λ = 68.

## Acceptance
- A comment with the measurements (SHA, worker, commands, cold/warm numbers, top-30 table, class aggregates, disk) and
  the capacity model. No code change required; this bead gates R65b-R65d decisions.

3. Capacity model, rho = lambda * S / (c * 1440):
- Take S = one landing's minimum gate set: default check + one feature clippy + targeted tests, about 3 lanes x 23.2 min mean, so ~70 min. Add ~23 min when an old-red control lane is required.
- lambda=12/day: c=2 gives rho 0.29; c=3 gives 0.19.

SapphireHill, 2026-10-01: the per-unit time split is MEASURED. It was blocked before because `--timings` writes into target/, which RCH does not return.

Method:
- Probe commit 2234f1ea2, never landed, adds scripts/probe_rustc_timer.sh as `build.rustc-wrapper`, passed through `--config`. The wrapper times every rustc invocation and prints the result on stderr, which RCH returns.
- Lane p82_timing on ecf1ba419: `CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 cargo test -j 2 -p asupersync --no-run --lib` plus a deterministic sample of 30 `*_contract` and 30 behavior integration targets. All are ungated and have no file-level cfg; the list is in /data/tmp/rc_20260923/p82/sample.txt.
- Cold target dir, RCH_DISABLE_TARGET_REUSE=1. Cargo reported "Finished in 41m 05s", and the timed units span 2465 s.

Per-unit rustc wall time (one rustc process each; compile plus link; jobserver -j 2):

| class | units | sum | median | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| asupersync lib-test (`--lib`, cfg(test)) | 1 | 1708.5 s (28.5 min) | | |
| asupersync lib (for integration tests) | 1 | 472.1 s (7.9 min) | | |
| third-party dependencies | 318 | 567.9 s | 0.2 s | 60.9 s (bytes) |
| bins built for integration tests (all [[bin]]) | 44 | 123.3 s | 0.2 s | 60.6 s (a build script) |
| behavior integration targets | 30 | 142.2 s | 2.3 s | 13.7 s |
| contract integration targets | 30 | 52.0 s | 1.0 s | 12.6 s |
| workspace members (conformance and others) | 5 | 43.9 s | 2.3 s | 30.6 s |

Conclusions for bi2462.82:
1. The long pole is ONE rustc unit, the cfg(test) lib (28.5 min). Then comes the plain lib (7.9 min). Integration targets are cheap at about 1-2.3 s each including link. At those medians, all 1527 targets add roughly 1527 × 1.7 s ≈ 43 CPU-min, about 22 min at -j 2, on top of the lib.
2. Consolidating the integration-test binaries is NOT the big lever. Every lane that runs `--lib` pays about 28 min for the cfg(test) lib alone. Integration-only lanes pay about 8 min of lib plus deps.
3. -j 2 caps codegen parallelism as well as the number of concurrent rustc processes, because rustc's parallel codegen draws jobserver tokens. Under the current admission limit (no worker admits -j 8) the two big lib units therefore codegen on at most 2 threads. A lane class allowed more tokens, or a lib-test unit split (fewer cfg(test) modules in one unit), would hit the long pole directly. Splitting the frontend from codegen time needs `-Z self-profile`, or a second run at a higher -j; not done.
4. Every integration-test build also builds all 44 [[bin]] targets (about 2 min), because cargo builds bins for CARGO_BIN_EXE_*.

Not measured: retained disk per class, and warm reruns. RCH_DISABLE_TARGET_REUSE prevents a warm rerun on the same target dir. The top-30 unit list beyond the table is available in the lane log: /data/tmp/rc_20260923/lanes/p82_timing__p82t.log, grep RUSTC_TIMING.

title: Move the 553 crate-independent test targets off the per-binary link path (one harness or a runtime-free member) with an exact test-identity inventory
description:
## Why (reality check 2026-09-23, S7) — child of bi2462.82
553 of 1,507 test targets never reference the `asupersync` crate (they read JSON/Markdown/scripts and assert on text).
Each is still a separate test binary that Cargo must compile and link in every `--all-targets` check/clippy/test, and
every run of them happens after the whole library builds. They are the cheapest large block to move off the critical
path; the other 397 contract targets are next.

## Work (only after R65a measures the actual share; abort if it is small)
Option A: one harness binary: a single `[[test]] name = "governance"` whose main.rs includes each file as a module via
`#[path = "..."] mod ...;` (the files stay where they are, so path pins remain valid), with those files excluded from
autodiscovery. Option B: a separate workspace member (e.g. `asupersync-governance-tests`) with no dependency on the
runtime crate, so doc/JSON-only changes never rebuild the runtime and runtime changes never rebuild these.
Either option requires:
- An exact test-identity inventory: every old `--test <name>` + test fn → new selector, generated and committed as an
  artifact, with a contract test that proves no test was lost (count and names) and none is newly ignored.
- A command map: every reference to the old `--test <name>` in artifacts/proof_lane_manifest_v1.json, scripts/, docs/,
  AGENTS.md and README.md updated (by hand, per AGENTS "No Script-Based Changes"), each contract that pins those
  commands updated through its own path.
- A global-state review: tests that set env vars, cwd or statics must still pass when sharing one process (run the
  harness with default parallelism and with --test-threads=1; any order dependence is a bug to fix, not to hide).

## Acceptance
- Before/after `--timings` receipts at consecutive SHAs on the same worker: total time for `cargo check --all-targets` and
  `cargo test --no-run`, and the number of test binaries.
- The identity inventory contract passes and fails on a planted missing test (negative control).
- All moved tests pass in their new home (counts equal to before, zero ignored/filtered added).

title: Tiered validation lanes with budgets: L0 <=10 min (lib check + native contract), L1 <=30 min (touched targets), L2 nightly full

description:
## Why (reality check 2026-09-23, S7) — child of bi2462.82; EXTERNAL DEPENDENCY (RCH tool, not this repo)
Observed RCH behavior that multiplies asupersync validation cost (evidence: CopperOak's comments on bi2462.91 and .99,
2026-09-23; root lanes /data/tmp/rc_20260923/lanes/; ~/.local/state/rch/incidents.jsonl):
1. Distinct CARGO_TARGET_DIR requests map to ONE pooled remote target per worker
   (.rch-target-<worker>-pool-a21b0620354c12b97b5b1e88559efab2), so concurrent asupersync lanes serialize on Cargo's

   2026-09-23 22:19Z; RCH maintainer RubyStork informed via Agent Mail 7514/7515).

## Work

In this repo: document the observed behavior and the workarounds (separate worker sets per lane; -j sized to slots;
RCH_DAEMON_WAIT_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_SECS) in TESTING.md's RCH section. Do not modify RCH from this repo.

title: Regression test selection for L1: per-target file dependency map (coverage + dep-info + run-time opens) with planted-edit safety check
description:
## Why (reality check 2026-09-23, ambition pass 1) — child of bi2462.82
Even with consolidation, running every target for every batch costs more than the fleet has. Regression test selection
(RTS) runs only the targets a change can affect. It is safe (in the Rothermel-Harrold sense: every test whose behavior
the change can alter is selected) only if the dependency record is complete.

## Work
For each test target, record the set of files it depends on from three sources:
(1) Rust source files whose code its tests execute (coverage: `-C instrument-coverage` + llvm-cov export at file level);
(2) files embedded at compile time (`include_str!`/`include_bytes!`/`include!`, from Cargo dep-info .d files);
(3) files opened at run time (an fs-open log per test binary, e.g. strace -f -e trace=openat on Linux, or a harness
    helper). Store the map as an artifact keyed by SHA. Select targets whose set intersects the diff; select everything
    when the diff touches Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock/build scripts/toolchain or the map is older than N commits.
Use it for L1 (R65c).

## Acceptance
- A safety check: for five planted edits in different areas (kernel, net, a JSON artifact read at run time, a doc
  embedded by include_str!, a test helper), every target that a FULL run shows changing verdict is in the selected set.
  Record the selected-target count and time saved for each.
- The map regenerates in an L2 lane; stale maps fall back to full selection (negative control: a planted stale map).

title: ATP RangeTracker: empty removals corrupt contiguity and gap queries exceed bounds
description:
Source investigation on 2026-09-21, CopperOak. src/atp/journal/range_tracker.rs has three bounded-interval correctness defects:
1. SparseRange::overlaps uses only start<other.end && end>other.start. An empty [5,5) reports overlap with [0,10). RangeTracker::remove_range([5,5)) consequently removes [0,10) and reinserts adjacent [0,5),[5,10), returns true, and is_contiguous_to(10) becomes false despite unchanged covered bytes. Public reversed struct-literal ranges are also considered empty by is_empty and should not overlap. ChunkRange::overlaps inherits this.
2. is_contiguous_to requires exactly one tracked range, so [0,10),[20,30) incorrectly reports prefix [0,5) incomplete. Only the first coalesced range covering [0,size) matters.
3. find_gaps(total_size) walks ranges beyond total_size without bounding emitted endpoints. With [20,30), find_gaps(10) returns [0,20); find_gaps(0) can report nonempty gaps. Returned gaps must lie inside [0,total_size).

title: OWNER: authorize one validation path that every agent (including API-created commits) can use
description:
## Why this exists
The 2026-09-22 reality check found that the single largest cause of undelivered or broken product surface is not a missing feature but a missing validation path. Concretely, at audit base 8525d7055:
- GitHub Actions is disabled at the repository level (`gh api repos/Dicklesworthstone/asupersync/actions/permissions` returns `enabled:false`). The last run of any workflow was 2026-09-07. The `CI` workflow has zero successful runs in its entire history. README and AGENTS still describe CI jobs (`lint-build`, `lean-build`, `tla-tlc`, real-server services, the Phase-6 PR gates) as enforcement.
- `asupersync-bi2462.81` (P0, blocked since 2026-09-15, CopperOak) records the position that RCH's own worker-side scratch/cache pruning (`worker_cache_prune_rsync_path_prefix` in the RCH project) violates AGENTS RULE 1 (no deletion). Under that reading RCH is unusable. The owner granted CopperOak a local `cargo -j2` exception on 2026-09-15. Other agents (e.g. SapphireHill on 09-19, 09-21, 09-22) kept using RCH normally.
- 157 of the 161 commits since 2026-09-15 whose own messages say "not compiled / not executed" were authored by `35050222+Dicklesworthstone@users.noreply.github.com`, i.e. created through GitHub's API/web by an agent without any compile path. They bypass `.githooks/pre-push`, and with Actions off nothing else checks them. 61,060 of 98,389 `src/` lines added in that week came from such commits. Heal commits later made the tree compile (pristine default and all-features `cargo check --all-targets` are clean at 8525d7055), but first executions of those suites were largely red and exposed shipped defects (two in v0.5.0).

## Decision requested from the owner (Jeffrey)
1. Is RCH's internal worker-cache pruning acceptable under RULE 1? (a) Yes: then `bi2462.81` is closed as "authorized", and every agent must use `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec ...` for proof. (b) No: then the retained-artifact route in `bi2462.81` must be built first, and until then name the single allowed alternative (e.g. local `-j2` for focused tests).
2. Does GitHub Actions stay disabled? If yes, README/AGENTS must stop citing CI jobs as enforcement and name the RCH lanes instead (tracked in the docs beads). If no, re-enable with a budget and say which jobs are required.
3. May an agent without a compile path push code to `main` through the GitHub API at all? Recommended answer: no. Such an agent may push docs/tracker changes only, or must hand code to an agent with a validation path. (Branches/worktrees remain forbidden by AGENTS RULE 2, so there is no staging-branch alternative.)

## What "done" means
- The owner's answers are recorded verbatim (with date) in this bead and reflected in AGENTS.md (validation section and RULE 0.5 reference) in one commit.
- `bi2462.81` is closed or re-scoped according to answer 1.
- The swarm is told (Agent Mail broadcast if available; otherwise a pinned note in this bead) which path to use.

## Non-goals
No engineering work on RCH itself here (that is `bi2462.81`). No deletion of any file. No change to AGENTS rules beyond what the owner decides.

---
**Provenance and binding rules.** Created by the 2026-09-22 reality check (SapphireHill); see the "September 22 assessment" section of `ASUPERSYNC_BRIDGE_PLAN_2026-09-01.md`. Evidence base: main at `8525d70554dd7cb7ab02ea16b461c5a6767e9e01` unless another SHA is named. Line numbers are approximate (`~`) and will drift, so re-locate by symbol before editing.

- Work on `main` only; no branches or worktrees.
- No file deletion without explicit written owner permission.
- No scripted code edits.
- Preserve public API and documented behavior (v0.4.3 floor for 0.4.x; the 0.5/0.6 policy is pending the owner, see R35b). Prefer additive APIs; any break needs explicit owner approval.
- Execute proof only through the owner-authorized validation path (see G1). The default is `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec --base <sha> --clean-overlay --no-overlay -- cargo ... -j 8` with an isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. Never use local fallback unless G1 authorizes it.

Running must be greater than 0, and named tests must be neither ignored nor filtered. A bug fix also needs an old-red receipt taken at a pre-fix commit.
