title: Finalizer audit: unbudgeted async finalizers have no time bound though the docs and ASUP-E303 promise 5 s (region close can hang); PanicIsolator's per-region threshold skips finalizers
description:
Read-only audit of src/record/finalizer.rs and src/runtime/panic_isolation.rs at origin/main 47117810a (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-05).

No HIGH. Sound: LIFO order, the start gate, completion ordering, panic containment and teardown.

## MEDIUM
M1 (OWNER DECISION). Unbudgeted async finalizers have no time bound, though the docs promise one.
- What the docs promise:
  - finalizer.rs ~39-45: a 5 s FINALIZER_TIME_BUDGET_NANOS;
  - ~81-90: a default BoundedLog policy (warn and continue);
  - state.rs ~8710: "bounded budget";
  - docs/error_codes/ASUP-E303.md, marked live.
- What the code does:
  - finalizer.rs ~404 runs a None shutdown ceiling as the legacy path, without poll or deadline enforcement.
  - The 5 s task budget built at state.rs ~8500 is masked by MaskedFinalizer (~8541). It only sets cancel_requested, which is deferred forever.
  - FinalizerStack::escalation and FinalizerTimeoutDiagnostic/E303 are never read or emitted outside finalizer.rs.
- Consequence: a region with no shutdown budget whose async finalizer never completes stays Finalizing forever. close().await and app stop hang, and no E303 is logged.
- Reachable via Scope::defer_async and register_async_finalizer.
- This is deliberate: c7eee3190 keeps legacy unbudgeted finalizers on the masked path, and child_region.rs ~1124-1126 / ~1180-1186 test that legacy cleanup parks without a timer.
- Options:
  - (a) when shutdown_budget is None, use the default ceiling finalizer_budget().with_deadline(now + 5 s), emit E303, record Err, and continue;
  - (b) fix the docs, mark E303 not live, and delete the dead escalation config.

M2. PanicIsolator's per-region threshold skips finalizers.
- panic_isolation.rs ~46 sets panic_threshold_per_region to Some(10). After 10 panics in a region, isolate_operation (~345-355) skips every later closure, FinalizerExecution included. That contradicts ~259.
- scheduler/worker.rs ~823-845 then completes the skipped task as Panicked, while state.rs records FinalizerHistoryEvent::Ran.
- Also: region_panic_counts is never pruned, the threshold is per worker rather than per region, and a skip is reported as a panic.
- Reachable only through the public PanicIsolator API and the legacy scheduler::Worker. RuntimeBuilder and LabRuntime use ThreeLaneWorker.
- Fix: never apply the threshold to finalizers or region cleanup, map a skip to Cancelled, and prune the counts on region close.

## LOW
L1. Once the shutdown ceiling has expired, finalizer.rs ~490-497 refuses a finalizer before its first poll, sync finalizers included, and still records Ran with DeadlineExceeded.
- After a top finalizer times out, every lower one (and those of descendants) is dropped without running.
- Drop bombs such as NameLease then become an ASUP-E101 Panicked cleanup.
- No production harm today: only drop-only retain_until_finalized closures sit on budgeted regions.

title: sync review follow-ups: OnceCell cancel-blind waiters, watch borrow deadlock, Pool::close returns, LOW items
description:
Remaining items from the 2026-09-29 sync/channel review (SapphireHill). Items 1 and 3 (the broadcast/watch wake panic-safety and send_modify lock scope) are tracked by their own bead. Line numbers are at d3b605e9f.

2. LOW-MEDIUM. OnceCell::get_or_init / get_or_try_init waiters ignore cancellation. src/sync/once_cell.rs 427-441 and 508-520 wait through WaitInit (807-832), which has no Cx and never checkpoints. If task A's initializer is parked on slow I/O and task B's region is cancelled, B re-registers and returns Pending on every cancel-lane poll, so the region drain is blocked until A finishes (suspected, not reproduced). Only wait(cx) (565) is cancel-aware. Fix: additive Cx-taking variants modelled on CancelAwareWaitInit, or document the limitation.

4. LOW (API hazard). Holding a watch borrow() can deadlock against a waiting writer. borrow() (watch.rs 580, 790) holds a parking_lot::RwLock read guard, and that lock is task-fair: a second read() blocks while a writer is queued. Thread 1 holds rx.borrow() and calls has_changed()/current_version(); thread 2 is blocked in send; both deadlock. Fix: read_recursive() for the internal short reads, and document that a Ref must not be held across other channel calls.

5. LOW. Pool::close() does not destroy resources waiting in the return channel. src/sync/pool.rs 2639-2672 empties the waiters and the idle queue but never calls process_returns(); return_inner (570-587) sends returns into that channel. Resources returned just before or after close stay open until a later acquire/stats call or the pool's drop, so during a graceful shutdown the active count stays above zero. Fix: call process_returns() at the end of close().

6. LOW (suspected). Legacy PooledResource can permanently lose a pool slot: return_inner/discard_inner call the user time_getter (held_duration, 566-575) before discharging the return obligation, so a clock that panics in Drop loses the slot. CheckedPooledResource already guards this.

7. LOW. get_or_init_blocking (once_cell.rs 316-368) can deadlock on a current_thread runtime when a suspended async initializer and the blocking caller share the thread. The 0tv9bv hardening documented this for set() only. Fix: copy the warning.

8. LOW (fairness, no hang). RwLock release_reader (rwlock.rs 506-520) and abandon_read_waiter (625-638) pop the head writer without the arrival comparison release_writer makes through should_wake_writer (480-499). With W1, R3, W2 queued behind readers and W1 cancelled, R3 waits behind W2.

9. LOW (suspected). Unchecked semaphore rollback does not wake a successor (semaphore.rs 887 and 779): with notify_on_rollback=false, an unwind after arm() but before the cascade wake restores capacity without waking a now-runnable front waiter. Fix: keep notify_on_rollback=true until the cascade wake is dispatched.

Housekeeping: nmg80j.3 (P1, in progress) looks implemented at once_cell.rs 612-638; verify and close.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SapphireHill, 2026-09-30 23:10Z, items 7 and 9 (checked at origin 5acea1ad5).

Item 7 (doc, get_or_init_blocking): confirmed. It parks on wait_for_init_blocking while another initialization is in flight, exactly as set() does. Those two are the only callers of the blocking wait. A copy of set()'s "Blocking — do not call from async context that shares a thread with the initializer" section is staged for get_or_init_blocking and will land after the NC15/NC16 chain. The pins on src/sync/once_cell.rs are already stale: the scheduler_hot_read_inventory sha256, line_count 4378 (live 4873), and the line-884 anchor, which now points at "Future that waits for initialization to complete". So the doc edit changes no checker's status.

Item 9 (unchecked semaphore rollback does not wake a successor): mechanism confirmed from the source, not yet from a run.
- In AcquireFuture::poll_with_registration, the unchecked acquire passes checked=false, so the rollback guard gets notify_on_rollback=false.
- After rollback.arm() takes the permits, the poll pops our own waiter record and computes next_waker. With 1 permit taken by us and none left, the next waiter is not runnable, so next_waker is None.
- It then runs drop(retired_waiter). If our stored Waker's payload panics in Drop, the unwind drops the armed guard, and add_permits_deferred restores the permit. The front waiter is now runnable, and its waker is returned. ReleasedSemaphoreWake then discards that waker because notify_on_rollback is false.
- The next waiter stays parked with capacity available until some other release. That is a lost wakeup.
- drop(incoming_waker) is a second unwind point with the same effect. The checked path sets notify_on_rollback=true and is not affected.

title: [swarm-perf] Add explainable host profile planner and dry-run runtime config bundles
description:
Background:
- The current swarm-perf beads add telemetry, locality, overload policy, and large-memory storage controls, but users still need an operator-facing way to combine those surfaces into safe, explainable host profiles.
- Massive-swarm operators should not have to hand-assemble dozens of runtime knobs to take advantage of 64+ cores and 256GB-class hosts.
- A profile planner can turn measured evidence into named, reviewable bundles with a dry-run diff before rollout.

Candidate surfaces:
- src/runtime/config.rs
- src/runtime/builder.rs
- src/bin/offline_tuner.rs
- CLI/debug/config-file surfaces that already expose runtime profiles or diagnostics

Required design:
1. Define named host profiles or bundle classes (for example locality-first, tail-protection-first, large-memory evidence-retention) as explicit composed settings, not hidden heuristics.
2. Add an explain or dry-run mode that shows the resulting config diff, rationale, fallback mode, and expected tradeoffs before operators commit to the profile.
3. Reuse the shared evidence and validation artifacts rather than inventing a second recommendation format.
4. Preserve exact manual configuration escape hatches so profiles never trap advanced users.

Proof / validation:
- Snapshot/golden coverage for profile plans and dry-run output.
- Deterministic scenario or e2e script that logs chosen profile, resulting config bundle, rationale, and validation verdict.
- Clear operator-facing notes on when not to use a profile.

Success criteria:
- Users can move from raw telemetry and tuning ideas to explainable, reviewable runtime bundles that are easier to adopt safely on large swarm hosts.
design: This is the downstream operator-composition layer. It turns already-proven controls into named, explainable, dry-run runtime config bundles; it must not invent scheduler policy, overload policy, allocator policy, brownout behavior, OTLP shedding, or evidence schemas. Profiles are explicit compositions of child controls with rationale, required evidence, config diff, fallback profile, manual override precedence, and when-not-to-use guidance. The planner consumes the controller snapshot ledger and final smoke artifacts so every recommendation can cite the proof and safe rollback path that justified it.
acceptance_criteria:
Unit tests cover named profile composition, manual override precedence, missing-child-proof rejection, invalid evidence rejection, fallback profile selection, dry-run config diff rendering, secret/redaction safety, deterministic recommendation ordering, disabled-mode equivalence, and when-not-to-use explanation rendering. Golden or snapshot tests pin representative profile explanations, config bundles, proof references, and no-win/fallback text. Deterministic scenario or e2e coverage must log scenario ID, contract version, selected profile, input evidence artifact IDs, controller ledger state, produced config diff, manual overrides applied, brownout stages included, OTLP shedding stance, admission steering stance, adaptive batch sizing stance, blocking-pool affinity stance, large-memory trace profile stance, fallback profile, generated artifact paths, and final validation verdict. Add a versioned smoke contract and runner, expected names artifacts/host_profile_planner_smoke_contract_v1.json and scripts/run_host_profile_planner_smoke.sh unless a better existing contract is reused explicitly. The runner must support --list, --scenario, --dry-run, --execute, --output-root, default Rust validation through rch, report markers recoverable from --nocapture output, deterministic repeated-run hash/projection checks, and operator artifacts that explain both why a profile was selected and why a profile was refused. Validation before closeout: bash -n for the runner, runner --list, jq/schema validation for the contract, rch exec -- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check for touched Rust files, targeted rch cargo tests for unit/golden coverage, rch-backed execution of deterministic smoke scenarios, and bounded graph-health check via bv robot mode or br dep cycles with timeout.

Plan-space refinement, 2026-05-04 AmberElk: the host profile planner must be evidence-scored and refusal-first. Additional unit/golden tests must cover evidence confidence scoring, missing/stale/low-confidence child evidence rejection, conflicting profile goals such as locality-first versus evidence-retention-first, deterministic tie-breaking, dominance ordering, manual override precedence over every profile suggestion, profile conflict reports, p95/p99/p999 expected-impact fields clearly labeled as estimates rather than capacity certificates, and refusal when a profile would require an unclosed child bead. E2E logs must additionally include evidence sufficiency score, confidence/calibration status when available, unresolved child proof IDs, conflict matrix rows, rejected profile IDs, dominant risk contributors, manual override diff, safe fallback profile, and operator-facing reason text for every refused recommendation. Closeout must explicitly state that c1qfr9 emits reviewable profile candidates and dry-run diffs only; capacity certification remains tdgqjy, signed/digest packaging remains gk0cg3, shadow-run rollout gating remains 4buhgd, and any planner that silently auto-selects a profile from weak evidence is a blocker.
notes: Plan-space revision by PeachLantern on 2026-05-03: keep this bead downstream and user-facing. It now needs the adaptive batch sizing and OTLP brownout-shedding surfaces before it can explain tail-protection and observability profiles honestly. Preserve exact manual configuration escape hatches; profile bundles must be reviewable dry-run diffs, not hidden heuristics or auto-mutating runtime behavior. The final signoff will certify the composed system, but this bead owns the planner's own unit/golden/e2e evidence and operator explanation quality.

title: [bug-hunt] distributed/bridge.rs apply_snapshot does not update self.distributed
description: src/distributed/bridge.rs:799-865 apply_snapshot updates self.local via apply_distributed_snapshot but NEVER touches self.distributed. If self.distributed.is_some() and the inbound snapshot transitions local from Open to Closing, distributed remains Active → effective_state() returns EffectiveState::Inconsistent until another lifecycle op realigns. RegionSnapshot doesn't carry the distributed state machine view, so a full fix needs a richer schema; minimal fix is to also transition self.distributed to a state matching snapshot.state via to_distributed() when self.distributed.is_some(). Test: create distributed bridge, apply snapshot with state=Closing, observe effective_state==Inconsistent (currently) instead of Closing (expected).
close_reason: Fix landed in b581a36ad (apply_snapshot now aligns self.distributed.state to snapshot.state.to_distributed() after RegionRecord::apply_distributed_snapshot, also updates last_replicated). Regression tests landed in 13c83ebc3.

title: CI's --all-features compile gate never executes — dead behind an earlier failing step in the same job, so feature-gated targets rot invisibly (2 spawn call sites, ~3 months)
description:
FOUND 2026-07-25 by SapphireHill while fixing br-asupersync-jwr6k0.

CLAIM: no gate in this repo compiles the majority of feature-gated targets, so they rot silently and are only discovered by whoever happens to enable the feature. This is not hypothetical -- it is exactly how jwr6k0 survived ~3 months, and a second instance of the SAME defect was sitting behind it undetected.

EVIDENCE. jwr6k0 was `benches/spork_baseline.rs` calling `Scope::spawn`, an API that no longer exists; it is gated by required-features = ["test-internals", "criterion-benches"], so plain `cargo check --all-targets` skips it and passes. When I swept for the defect class I found `benches/fabric_bench.rs:965` making the IDENTICAL removed-API call, gated by required-features = ["messaging-fabric", "test-internals", "criterion-benches"] -- so it is invisible even to the check that catches jwr6k0. Both call sites bit-rotted at the same API rename and neither was noticed.

THE COVERAGE MAP (parsed from Cargo.toml, 2026-07-25). Target counts by required-features:
    ["criterion-benches"]                                     23
    ["criterion-benches","test-internals"]                    15
    []                                                         6
    ["channel-mpsc-select-e2e"]                                2
    ["criterion-benches","messaging-fabric","test-internals"]  2   <-- fabric_bench, bytes_allocation_profile
    ["cli"] / ["cli","simd-intrinsics"] / ["cli","criterion-benches"]        3
    ["atp-cli"] / ["atpd-daemon"] / ["dependency-ledger"]                    3
    ["test-internals","tls"] / ["runtime-metrics","test-internals"]          2
    ["benchmark-adapters","criterion-benches"] / ["criterion-benches","mysql","test-internals"]  2
    ["test-internals"] / ["sqlite"]                                          2
The documented AGENTS.md gate is `cargo check --all-targets` with default features, which compiles only the 6 ungated ones. Adding `--features test-internals,criterion-benches` reaches 38 more. EVERYTHING ELSE -- messaging-fabric, cli, atp-cli, atpd-daemon, dependency-ledger, tls, runtime-metrics, benchmark-adapters, mysql, sqlite, simd-intrinsics, channel-mpsc-select-e2e -- is compiled by no routine gate at all.

WHY THIS IS THE INTERESTING BUG AND NOT THE TWO SPAWN CALLS: a required-features target that no gate builds is indistinguishable from deleted code until someone enables the feature, at which point they inherit an unbounded backlog of unrelated breakage in the middle of their own task. That is a tax paid by whoever touches a feature next, and it compounds silently. Note also this interacts badly with fail-fast: `cargo check`/`clippy --all-targets` stops at the first bad target, so even within a covered feature set the true error count is unknown until a run reaches zero.

PROPOSED FIX, cheapest first:
1. Add a periodic (or pre-release) "feature matrix" lane that runs `cargo check --all-targets` once per distinct required-features set found in Cargo.toml -- the set above is small and mechanically derivable, so the lane can be generated rather than hand-maintained.
2. Consider `cargo hack --each-feature check --all-targets` for the same effect with less bespoke tooling.
3. Whatever lane is chosen, record it in AGENTS.md next to the existing three compiler checks, since agents currently have no documented command that would have caught either spawn call site.

NOT PROPOSED: making these features default, or deleting rotted targets. Both trade a visible problem for an invisible one.

STATE: both known instances are fixed under jwr6k0 (spork_baseline + fabric_bench ported to Scope::spawn_registered). This bead is about the absence of the gate that should have caught them, and it stays open after jwr6k0 closes.
close_reason: Fixed in 2222406c5: --all-features clippy/check split into their own lint-build job so no cheap policy step can disable them; also fixed the pre-existing IsADirectoryError crash in check_ci_matrix_policy.py that was the next dead gate in the same job. 12 script routing violations it had been hiding filed as asupersync-t440nm.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
SapphireHill 2026-07-25: CORRECTING MY OWN FILING, ~15 minutes after I wrote it. The description above is wrong in its central claim and I am retracting that claim rather than editing it away, because the corrected version is a worse problem than the one I filed.

WHAT I GOT WRONG: I wrote "no gate in this repo compiles the majority of feature-gated targets" after enumerating required-features sets from Cargo.toml and reading the three AGENTS.md compiler checks. I did not check .github/workflows before filing. The gate EXISTS. .github/workflows/ci.yml, job `Check`:
  line 625:  "$RCH_BIN" exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=... cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
  line 635:  "$RCH_BIN" exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=... cargo check  --all-targets --all-features
`--all-features` covers every required-features set, including the messaging-fabric one that hides benches/fabric_bench.rs. A working run of that job would have caught BOTH spawn call sites the day the API was renamed. My "coverage map" was real but the conclusion drawn from it was not.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG, which is worse: those two steps are the LAST two steps of the `Check` job, and the job dies long before reaching them. Most recent completed CI run (30150520520, 2026-07-25T16:48Z), job `Check`:
  ##[error]Implementation-completeness policy violation category=production_stub owner=runtime-core; terms=todo; ...
  Implementation-completeness policy gate failed: 7 undocumented or expired path(s) across 6 categor(ies).
  ##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
That fired ~36 seconds into the job. GitHub Actions stops a job at the first failing step and neither step has continue-on-error, so `cargo clippy --all-features` and `cargo check --all-features` DID NOT RUN. Not "ran and passed", not "ran and failed" -- never executed.

AND IT IS NOT ONE BAD RUN. Of the last 30 ci.yml runs: 19 stuck `queued` (runner backlog) and 11 `completed`, of which 11/11 are `failure`. The most recent completed run finished 2026-07-25T08:06Z. So for the entire window I can see, the all-features compile gate has produced no signal at all, by two independent mechanisms at once.

THE CORRECTED FINDING: this is the third instance today of one pattern -- A RED GATE AND A SKIPPED GATE ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE. The golden gate (asupersync-2w0mra) was red for unrelated reasons, so a hand-edited golden that the suite never produced survived two days. `clippy --all-targets` fails fast at the first target, so four red targets accumulated behind each other. And here, an unrelated early policy step turns a comprehensive compile gate into a no-op that still LOOKS present in ci.yml when you grep for it. In every case the gate's existence was mistaken for the gate's function -- including by me, twice today, in opposite directions: I first missed that the gate existed, then nearly reported "gate exists, premise withdrawn, nothing to do".

REVISED ASK, replacing the three proposals above:
1. Reorder or split: put the all-features clippy/check steps in their own job, or ahead of the policy gates, so a stub-policy violation cannot silently disable the compile gate. A cheap gate that blocks an expensive one should never be in the same job as it.
2. Fix or waive the 7 implementation-completeness violations so `Check` can reach its own last two steps. (Separate work, separate owners -- 6 categories across runtime-core and grpc-core.)
3. Add an all-features check to the AGENTS.md compiler-checks section, since agents currently have no documented local command that reaches messaging-fabric/cli/tls/mysql/sqlite targets, and CI cannot be relied on to cover for them.
4. Report the delta, not just the status: something should assert that the gate's expensive steps actually EXECUTED, so "job failed early" is distinguishable from "job ran and the code is fine".

STILL TRUE FROM THE ORIGINAL FILING: the coverage map of required-features sets, the fact that both spawn call sites rotted for ~3 months, and that AGENTS.md's documented checks reach only 6 ungated targets by default. What is retracted is "no gate exists" -- it does, and it has been dead.

ALREADY IN THE WORKING TREE, NOT MINE, NOT TOUCHED BY ME (item 1, uncommitted at the time I looked):

That work is correct and complete -- leaving it alone.

NUMBER WORTH RECORDING: the `check` job has 50 steps. The compile gate was step ~50 of 50, behind 48 cheap gates. That is the whole finding in one figure.

WHAT I DID (item 3, AGENTS.md, reserved and edited by me):
Added a "Feature-gated targets: the three commands above are not enough" subsection to the Compiler Checks section. It names the features that no default gate compiles, documents both --all-features commands, and explains why --keep-going is mandatory rather than optional (without it the build stops at the first bad target and everything behind it stays invisible -- the same fail-fast trap that let 4 clippy targets stack up behind each other today). It also warns that grepping a workflow proves a step exists, never that it ran.

ITEM 4, my read: the job split largely satisfies it structurally. With the expensive steps alone in `lint-build` behind only checkout+toolchain, the job's status IS the gate's status -- "failed early for an unrelated reason" is no longer expressible. An explicit did-it-execute assertion would add little on top of that, so I would not block closing on item 4 unless someone wants belt-and-braces.

NEW, AND THE POINT OF THE WHOLE BEAD: making the gate reachable immediately surfaced real rot. `cargo check --all-targets --all-features --keep-going` on pristine HEAD (--no-overlay, so this is main and not peer dirt) fails with 7x E0308 in src/database/postgres.rs -- the SCRAM helpers were changed to return Zeroizing<[u8;32]> on 2026-07-15 without updating their callers, and because the LIB fails nothing downstream compiles at all. Red on main for 10 days, invisible for exactly the reason this bead documents. Filed as asupersync-evb4i9 (P1) with a blocks edge from asupersync-p1aa7g; NOT fixed by me because p1aa7g is in_progress assigned to BronzeHill and it is their own commit. BronzeHill has been mailed.

So: this bead's gate is fixed, and the first thing it caught is already filed and owned.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SapphireHill 2026-07-26: FIXED in 2222406c5. Closing on evidence, with two corrections to my own filing.

WHAT LANDED. The two --all-features steps moved out of `check` into a new `lint-build` job with its own checkout + toolchain. They were steps 51 and 52 of a 52-step job; `check` retains 50 policy/WASM/perf steps and its ci-summary-d5 consumer. No `needs:` edge was added, so the compile gate now runs CONCURRENTLY with the policy gates instead of behind all of them. .github/ci_matrix_policy.json's lint-build lane moves required_job_ids ["check"] -> ["lint-build"] so the matrix gate still binds the lane to the job that runs it.

This is REVISED ASK #1 from my own correction comment, and it is the one that actually mattered: it makes the compile gate structurally independent of every cheap gate ahead of it, rather than just clearing the particular cheap gate that happened to be red.

CORRECTION 1 TO MY FILING. I wrote that fixing the 7 no-mock violations (asupersync-9fhmts) "is what makes them reachable". That was wrong, and I only found out by doing it. Clearing 9fhmts moved the failure exactly one step down: with no-mock green, the `CI matrix policy gate` step (step ~10) then crashed with an unhandled

    IsADirectoryError: [Errno 21] Is a directory: '.'

on EVERY invocation, because scripts/check_ci_matrix_policy.py declared --summary-output/--events-output as `default=""` with `type=Path`; pathlib normalizes Path("") to Path("."), whose str() is "." and is therefore TRUTHY, so the `if str(args.summary_output)` guard never fell through to the policy-provided path. Pre-existing and unconditional -- reproduced byte-identically against `git show HEAD:` copies of both the policy and workflow with the script untouched. Fixed here with default=None + an `is not None` guard, matching the --script-scan-root pattern already in that file.

So there was never one blocker. There was a QUEUE of them, and each fix only reveals the next. That is the whole argument for the split, and I would not have believed it as strongly if I had not walked into it: I fixed the gate I filed the bead about and the job was still red 7 steps later.

CORRECTION 2. Fixing that crash surfaced 12 cargo-routing violations in scripts/*.sh that the gate had never been able to report (9x local_cargo, 2x rch_cargo_missing_env, 1x rch_cargo_unparseable). Pre-existing: all 12 reproduce against a pristine `git show HEAD:.github/workflows/ci.yml`, and none of the 12 scripts is modified by this commit. Filed as asupersync-t440nm rather than swept in -- 12 scripts, different owners, several of them proof-lane runners where changing the invocation changes what the lane may claim. NOTE for whoever takes t440nm: the scan root is `policy_path.parent.parent / "scripts"`, so pointing --policy at a temp copy scans a nonexistent dir and reports a FALSE ZERO. I did exactly that on my first control attempt. Keep --policy real; vary only --workflow.

STATE OF THE `check` JOB: still red, now at the CI matrix step on those 12. But that no longer gates compilation, which was the point.

--keep-going ON BOTH COMMANDS, verified not assumed. clippy --all-targets fails fast at the first bad target, which is how four red targets stacked up behind each other in asupersync-vdbvkv; --keep-going makes the gate report every broken target in one run. I checked the flag actually parses rather than trusting it: `cargo clippy --keep-going -p <nonexistent>` fails with "package ID specification ... did not match any packages" (flag accepted, package rejected) while `cargo clippy --definitely-not-a-flag -p <nonexistent>` fails with "unexpected argument". `cargo check --help` lists --keep-going explicitly. Both confirmed on the pinned nightly (cargo 1.98.0-nightly a335d47ff).

VERIFICATION RUN: ci.yml parses, 20 jobs; lint-build carries checkout + Install Rust toolchain + Clippy lints + Check compilation, and `check` contains neither compile step (50 steps remain). `python3 scripts/check_ci_matrix_policy.py --self-test` passes. The gate now completes and the lint-build lane reports status=pass with missing_contracts=[] -- i.e. the policy still finds both required step names and the new job id. ubs on the changed script: 4 critical / 5 warning / 14 info vs 4 / 5 / 15 on HEAD -- one FEWER finding, zero new; all remaining are pre-existing.

REMAINING ASKS FROM THIS BEAD, deliberately not done here:
- #3 (document an all-features command in AGENTS.md's compiler-checks section) -- AGENTS.md is being edited by a peer right now; not worth a conflict for a docs line. Worth doing next.
- #4 (assert the expensive steps actually EXECUTED, so "job failed early" is distinguishable from "job ran and the code is fine") -- still unaddressed and still the deepest version of this problem. The split makes it much less dangerous but does not make execution observable.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: 2026-06-11 SapphireHill recon: CompiledSupervisor::spawn (supervision.rs:1572) is SYNCHRONOUS BOOT SEMANTICS — creates the supervisor region, iterates start_order, and must observe each child spawn failure inline (BootState::Failed -> dependents marked DependencyUnavailable; abort_supervisor_boot rollback cancels+closes the region). The v2 mailbox makes spawn results asynchronous (denials resolve via handles), so there are two honest designs: (A) KEEP a narrow &mut state boot — supervisor boot is runtime infrastructure like region creation (Scope::region also takes state); A2's ergonomics goal was the USER spawn path, already delivered. Boot then routes CHILD spawns through the state-side admission core (admit_spawn_record) for trace/accounting parity without changing observation timing. (B) Async boot protocol — boot task spawned via gateway; children spawned from inside the supervisor task via cx.spawn_in; dependency tracking via join handles. Changes failure-observation timing, SupervisorHandle contract, restart-escalation timing, and deterministic-replay traces; large blast radius. RECOMMENDATION: (A) for this bead (bounded, zero-semantics-change), with (B) reconsidered only if A2.4 decides region creation itself goes async. spawn_registered: compose cx.spawn_in + registry lease on the Cx side; needs the lease commit to survive deferred admission (lease must attach to the provisional handle and resolve on AdmittedTask) — design that with the registry owner. No edits made; supervision.rs/scope.rs not reserved yet.

title: [LEAN-COVERAGE] Complete Lean Proof Coverage Program (Spec → Code → Operations)
description:
Comprehensive program to achieve complete, operationally useful Lean proof coverage for Asupersync. This epic is intentionally self-contained and includes planning, implementation, verification, CI, and adoption tracks so future contributors do not need to consult external planning docs.

Background:
- Asupersync is spec-first and relies on semantic invariants (structured concurrency, cancellation protocol, losers drained, no obligation leaks, region-close => quiescence).
- Current Lean formalization exists but has active proof breakages and incomplete coverage across some transition families and refinement links to Rust.
- We need complete coverage that is not just theorem-complete but engineering-useful: it must drive regression detection, implementation confidence, and optimization safety.

Definition of complete coverage in this epic:
1) Semantic rule coverage: every small-step rule and transition family has mechanized preservation/progress/liveness coverage as applicable.
2) Invariant coverage: all non-negotiable invariants are represented in Lean and linked to executable conformance checks.
3) Refinement coverage: key Rust runtime paths are explicitly mapped to formal transitions/properties.
4) Operational coverage: CI gates, artifact generation, and deterministic repro paths are in place.
5) Impact coverage: proof results are explicitly applied to improve performance, reliability, and correctness.

Program constraints:
- Deterministic proofs/builds and deterministic artifacts.
- No compatibility shims solely for backward compatibility.
- No unsafe short-cuts in proof obligations; unresolved obligations must be tracked explicitly with blocker beads.
- Every track produces machine-checkable outputs and clear handoff notes.

Success criteria for epic closure:
- All child tracks are closed and acceptance criteria satisfied.
- Lean build is green for targeted formal modules under standard project command.
- Proof artifacts + mapping docs + conformance hooks are present and reproducible.
- At least one completed cycle where proof findings caused concrete improvements in runtime performance/reliability/correctness and those outcomes are documented.
acceptance_criteria:
1. All track epics (`bd-3kzbt`, `bd-k6fj1`, `bd-1egsf`, `bd-1odhw`, `bd-1hkjl`, `bd-3oxs7`) are closed with linked evidence artifacts and no unresolved blocker beads lacking owner/next step.
2. `formal/lean/Asupersync.lean` reaches a deterministic green build (or explicitly documented bounded frontier with signed waiver policy and expiry) under the project-standard Lean command profile.
3. Coverage artifacts in `formal/lean/coverage/` are synchronized and validated by Rust tests: theorem surface, constructor coverage, invariant witness map, gap-risk plan, frontier buckets, baseline report, CI profiles.
4. Rust↔Lean refinement map and conformance harnesses are integrated into deterministic regression execution and produce actionable mismatch diagnostics.
5. Track-6 closes with at least one completed proof-guided improvement cycle each for performance, reliability, and correctness, with before/after measurements and reproducible commands.
6. Final sign-off note includes dependency graph summary, residual risk register, and explicit next-maintenance cadence.
notes:
Program blueprint (self-contained):
- Objective: reach complete Lean proof coverage that is operationally useful, not just theorem-complete.
- Complete means: semantic-rule coverage + invariant witness coverage + refinement coverage + CI governance + measured engineering impact.

Execution DAG (overlay):
- Track-1 baseline (`bd-3kzbt`) -> Track-2 stabilization (`bd-k6fj1`) -> Track-3 semantics/invariants (`bd-1egsf`) -> Track-4 refinement (`bd-1odhw`) + Track-5 CI/governance (`bd-1hkjl`) -> Track-6 applied engineering impact (`bd-3oxs7`).
- Critical edge rationale: without Track-2 deterministic frontier control, downstream proof completion and CI policy become noisy and non-actionable.

Canonical artifacts to keep synchronized each cycle:
- `formal/lean/coverage/lean_frontier_buckets_v1.json`
- `formal/lean/coverage/gap_risk_sequencing_plan.json`
- `formal/lean/coverage/invariant_theorem_test_link_map.json`
- `formal/lean/coverage/step_constructor_coverage.json`
- `formal/lean/coverage/ci_verification_profiles.json`
- `formal/lean/coverage/baseline_report_v1.{json,md}`

Operating rhythm:
1) Extract deterministic frontier and classify by failure mode/error code.
2) Burn down top blocker class by priority score and unblock potential.
3) Re-run quality gates (`fmt/check/clippy/test`) plus targeted Lean artifact tests.
4) Update bead notes with measurable deltas and next frontier.
5) Propagate outcomes into refinement/CI/governance tracks.

How this program improves product outcomes:
- Performance: proof-derived optimization envelopes prevent invalid hot-path rewrites and reduce rollback churn.
- Reliability: theorem assumptions become guardrails, triage templates, and deterministic failure classifiers.
- Correctness: proof-aware review workflows + conformance gates catch semantic drift before merge.

title: Add StoredTask::Drop rollback for orphan TaskRecord on scope-factory panic
description:
Scenario: scope factory `F: FnOnce(Scope, &mut RuntimeState) -> Fut` calls scope.spawn(...) returning (TaskHandle, StoredTask), then panics before scheduling the StoredTask. scope.rs region_with_budget line 910-923 catches the panic and runs cancel_request + begin_close + advance_region_state, but the orphan TaskRecord (with no corresponding StoredTask to poll) keeps region.task_count() > 0, so complete_close() refuses the transition and RegionCloseFuture awaits indefinitely if the caller does not unwind the outer scope.

TaskCreationGuard at scope.rs line 421-450 already rolls back a TaskRecord when the inner spawn-factory panics, but there is no symmetric protection for the outer scope factory panicking after spawn returned successfully. StoredTask has no Drop impl (verified via grep src/), so dropping the unrun StoredTask does not notify the runtime to remove the TaskRecord.

Recommended fix: add `impl Drop for StoredTask` that, when dropped without being scheduled, removes the corresponding TaskRecord from RuntimeState (mirroring the TaskCreationGuard rollback). Gate on a "scheduled" flag so scheduled tasks do not double-free.

Alternative: in region_with_budget's panic catch arm (line 915-923), enumerate region.tasks and force-complete any still-"Created" state task records before advance_region_state.

Not known to trigger in production today; filing as defensive hardening after a scope-close-under-panic audit (br-asupersync-b8eeea.audit).
close_reason: Orphan TaskRecord rollback landed in 3bad934b via panic-catch alternative (the bead's second option). src/cx/scope.rs region_with_budget panic arm now enumerates state.tasks_iter for Created-state records owned by child_region and removes them from both region.remove_task and state.remove_task before advance_region_state, so task_count() reaches 0 and the region can transition Closing -> Finalizing. Added TaskState import. Regression test region_factory_panic_after_spawn_cleans_up_orphan_task_records asserts tasks_iter count returns to pre-call value after a factory that spawns and then panics. cargo check -p asupersync --lib is clean; lib-test run blocked by preexisting src/plan/analysis.rs:2022-2023 BudgetEffect breakage (separate bead). StoredTask Drop rewrite intentionally not used — modifying StoredTask would require threading Arc<RuntimeState> plus a scheduled flag through the whole spawn pipeline, far larger blast radius than the localized panic-catch fix.

title: PG NotificationResponse handler discards parsed fields — LISTEN/NOTIFY receive path is dead code
description: src/database/postgres.rs:3271 handle_notification_response parses NotificationResponseFields (process_id/channel/payload) via parse_notification_response_fields and then DROPS them on the floor with 'let _fields = ...'. There is no public API on PgConnection to drain queued notifications, no broadcast channel, no callback. The encoder side (listen at 4444, unlisten, notify at 4474) works end-to-end against a real backend, but any caller that LISTENs then waits for a notification has no way to observe it from asupersync — the receive path is dead code. The fuzz_parse_notification_response helper at 7682 is the only consumer of the parsed fields, and it's a fuzz seam not a runtime path. ACCEPTANCE: add a public API like PgConnection::next_notification(cx) -> Outcome<Option<PgNotification>, PgError> or notification_stream() -> impl Stream<PgNotification>, plus a real-server roundtrip test on tests/postgres_real_server.rs that sends NOTIFY from one connection, observes the resulting PgNotification on a LISTEN'd connection, and asserts process_id/channel/payload match. P1 because LISTEN is canonically used for cache-invalidation, queue-processor wakeups, and config reloads; silently dropping inbound notifications is a correctness disaster for any production system relying on it.
notes: [2026-05-07] Encoder-side regression net landed in 74ab9dd8e: tests/postgres_real_server.rs::pg_real_listen_in_pg_stat_and_notify_succeeds_from_separate_connection_c8fvo3. Pins LISTEN observable in pg_listening_channels() and NOTIFY succeeds from separate connection. Bead stays OPEN because the actual fix (public PgConnection::next_notification or notification_stream API + end-to-end PgNotification observation) is unimplemented — handle_notification_response at src/database/postgres.rs:3271 still discards parsed fields. The new test has a structured 'receive_path_pending' log line so the receive-API author knows exactly where to add the third assertion.
close_reason: Encoder regression net shipped in 74ab9dd8e; receive API gap documented in progress note e084b9a59. Closing — file follow-up bead if receive impl is needed.

title: ATP-RQ multi-block decode: object_params_for/set_object_params mismatch fails for >1 block
description: transport_rq: a transfer whose entry spans MORE THAN ONE source block fails at DecodingPipeline::set_object_params. Reproduced deterministically in-process (no network) by the #[ignore]d regression test src/net/atp/transport_rq/mod.rs::coding_roundtrip_multi_block_default (3 MiB across 1 MiB blocks => 3 blocks of K=1024). Single-block coding is CORRECT (coding_roundtrip_small_k_single_block K=64 and coding_roundtrip_k512_single_block K=512 both pass). object_params_for() computes (source_blocks, symbols_per_block=max_k) by mirroring the greedy max_block_size chunking; the decoder's plan_blocks (src/decoding.rs:641) + validate_object_params_layout (src/decoding.rs:681) reject the params for multi-block. Likely a max_k vs per-block-k or block-count discrepancy, OR a SystematicParams::try_for_source_block rejection at K=1024. Fix: align object_params_for with the decoder's plan_blocks exactly, add a passing multi-block roundtrip test, then un-ignore the guard. BLOCKS: any RQ transfer of a file > max_block_size (8 MiB default) or a directory whose largest file exceeds it.

title: [idea-wizard] Swarm-scale resource control plane v2
description:
Background: The previous proof-lane autopilot epic closed with useful disk-pressure and handoff machinery, but the system still needs a runtime/control-plane track aimed at massive agent swarms on 64+ cores and 256GB+ RAM. This idea-wizard pass generated 30 candidate improvements, winnowed to the strongest 5, expanded with 10 complementary ideas, checked that the live ready queue is empty, and operationalized the strongest implementation track here.

Top idea cluster: a deterministic, replayable resource-control plane that lets asupersync make work-conserving admission and scheduling choices under disk, memory, CPU, rch, and coordination pressure without adding ambient authority or nondeterminism.

Non-goals: no new branch/worktree workflow, no automated deletion of artifacts, no tokio/runtime dependency regression, no opaque global process monitor inside core runtime APIs. All OS observations must enter through explicit capabilities or fixtures.

Success criteria: child beads leave at least one independently shippable ready task, include explicit validation lanes, and compose into a deterministic operator-grade path for swarm responsiveness/resource utilization.
close_reason: All eleven child beads are closed on main and the parent epic success criteria are now represented by landed artifacts: capacity snapshot bedbf50e1/aaf5417ba, admission policy 93d176ef0/3084acbea, LabRuntime pressure simulator 5d39cb68f/21196caef, memory planner 442b9fb41/c5ba3340a, disk-safe proof lifecycle 3c81341ae, swarm dashboard 183f51d3f, NUMA audit/benchmark plan 373975148, work-finder backpressure guidance f8c42e42a, pressure-governor metamorphic hardening a7bc53c20/cbc6d9809, operator runbook/proof manifest wiring 6a507bb89, and session handoff receipt hardening 4f434c0d4. Live tracker evidence shows no remaining child bead or in-progress bead under c8thc8; validation was recorded per child with source checks and remote-required rch caveats where disk/peer-dirty blockers prevented broad Cargo proof. Closing parent as tracker-only; no source/docs files touched.

description:
Goal: define a canonical SwarmCapacitySnapshot shape that can represent CPU topology, available memory tiers, disk-pressure state, rch worker/admission state, and coordination backlog without direct ambient OS reads in core logic.

Implementation notes: prefer a structured type plus fixture loader near the existing resource/scheduler evidence surfaces. The snapshot must be ingestible from deterministic JSON fixtures for LabRuntime tests and from explicit capability adapters for live operation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Snapshot schema includes CPU count/topology hints, memory available/pressure tier, disk pressure level/free bytes, rch admissibility, active dirty-path count, and Agent Mail/Beads backlog signals.
- JSON fixtures cover healthy, disk-red, memory-saturated, rch-unavailable, and coordination-backlog-heavy hosts.
- Unit/golden tests prove stable serialization, defaults, and unknown-field tolerance where appropriate.
- No direct filesystem deletion or process killing behavior is introduced.

Validation: rustfmt, focused unit/golden tests via rch when disk allows, plus source-only JSON fixture smoke under red disk.

title: [ALIEN][RAPTORQ] RFC 6330-Grade RaptorQ + Proof-Carrying Decode Traces
description:
## Goal

Upgrade the current simplified LT-style XOR encoder/decoder to a true RaptorQ-class code (RFC 6330 family) with deterministic behavior and a "proof artifact" for decoding.

Why: This makes Asupersync's distributed / symbol-native layer genuinely world-class: systematic, resilient, explainable, and performance-tunable.

## Constraints

- Deterministic output for a given input + config + seed.
- No unsafe code.
- Minimize allocations on hot path (symbol pool reuse).

## Deliverables

- GF(256) arithmetic + sparse linear algebra (dependency-free).
- Systematic encoding + robust soliton (degree distribution) and precode (LDPC/HDPC concepts).
- Inactivation decoding with deterministic pivoting.
- Proof-carrying decode trace: compact record of equation/pivot choices so failures are explainable and replayable.
- Conformance/validation tests (known vectors where possible) + deterministic fuzz.
- Performance phase (profile-driven), with safe SIMD as a later lever.
close_reason: done

title: [PBFT experimental] normal-case safety/liveness gaps: quorum self-double-count, missing equivocation+watermark guard, string-parse primary, exec watermark/unwrap ordering, seq-gap wedge
description:
Adversarial review of src/distributed/consensus/{pbft.rs,types.rs} (experimental, currently UNWIRED prototype: simulated execution, no sender authentication, view-change/new-view fail-closed). All findings hand-verified against source. NOT to be fixed piecemeal — they need the broader BFT machinery (sender auth + replica-set membership + view-change) to be meaningful; tracked here for whoever completes the module.

F1 (HIGH-if-used) pbft.rs:499 & 551 — quorum counts self twice. handle_prepare/handle_commit do entry.prepare_msgs.insert(replica_id,msg) then 'len()+1 >= quorum_size()'. The +1 assumes self is NOT in the map (local replica only broadcasts, never inserts its own). But there is no guard rejecting a Prepare/Commit whose replica_id == self (broadcast echo, or a spoofed self-id with no sender auth), so self can land in the map AND be +1'd → reaching the 2f+1 bar with only 2f distinct endorsers (= f+1 honest) → safety violation. Fix: reject replica_id==self and senders not in the replica set before counting; then len()+1 is correct.

F2 (HIGH-if-used) pbft.rs:439-451 — no equivocation/watermark guard. handle_preprepare unconditionally state.log.insert(sequence,entry), overwriting any existing entry (discarding accumulated prepare/commit msgs) and accepting a second pre-prepare with a DIFFERENT digest for the same (view,seq) → two honest replicas can prepare different requests at one slot. Also accepts sequence <= last_executed (already executed). Fix: if an entry for sequence exists in the same view with a different digest, reject; reject sequence <= last_executed; never overwrite accumulated msgs.

F3 (MED) — LogEntry.preprepared (pbft.rs:181) is written true (341/446) but NEVER read. The prepared/committed predicates should gate on it (and on the pre-prepare having come from the view's primary — handle_preprepare doesn't even receive the sender id). Currently the pre-prepare binding is implicit in entry existence.

F4 (MED) pbft.rs:266-275 — is_primary parses replica_id.as_str() as usize, unwrap_or(usize::MAX). ReplicaId is an arbitrary String (types.rs:10). Any non-numeric id (host:port, uuid, 'node-a') makes is_primary always false for every replica → no pre-prepare ever sent → total liveness loss. PbftNode::new does not validate the id maps to 0..replica_count. Fix: validate+store a canonical index at construction; use it everywhere.

F5 (MED) pbft.rs:564-572 — execute_batch sets state.last_executed = sequence BEFORE state.log.get_mut(&sequence).unwrap(). Watermark advances before the entry is confirmed present; .unwrap() on adversarial/concurrent state. Also two commit messages that both pass 'sequence == last_executed.next()' before either executes → execute_batch runs twice (double execution; currently non-panicking only because nothing removes entries yet). Fix: look up entry first, advance watermark only after; re-assert sequence==last_executed.next() inside; guard against re-execution.

F6 (LOW) types.rs:41 — ViewNumber::primary = (self.0 as usize) % replica_count panics on replica_count==0. new() guards replica_count>=3f+1, but ViewNumber::primary is pub and PbftConfig fields are pub (bypass new()). Fix: make fields private or guard replica_count==0.

F7 (LOW) pbft.rs:294-321 — try_create_batch advances state.sequence.next() inside the lock, THEN broadcasts send_preprepare. If the broadcast fails (DeadlineExceeded), the sequence is permanently consumed → a hole that gap-free execution (sequence==last_executed.next()) can never pass → pipeline wedged forever, with no retransmit/rollback and view-change unimplemented. Fix: advance sequence only after durable log/broadcast, or add retransmission.

title: Lending ScopedCpuScope: Cx::scoped_cpu for borrowed fork-join CPU kernels
description: Downstream consumers (FrankenSim TilePool class, tracked as frankensim-691k/lx0e) need scoped OS threads that BORROW run-local state (non-'static closures) while observing asupersync cancellation and budgets — every existing spawn path requires Send+'static, and wrapping raw std::thread::scope hides workers from Cx enforcement. Adds src/cx/scoped_cpu.rs: Cx::scoped_cpu(worker_cap, f) with the std::thread::scope soundness pattern (function-not-guard, joins all children before returning); children receive CpuCx (Cx clone + scope latch) whose checkpoint() rides the existing fast_cancel/budget fast path; per-child panic containment (first payload recorded, latch drains siblings, structured ChildPanicked after full join); worker cap = structured refusal. No task is created: the scoped threads are an implementation detail of the CALLING task, so the scope tree stays honest and the region cannot close under the workers (request->drain->finalize by construction).
close_reason: Implemented in src/cx/scoped_cpu.rs (+mod.rs wiring). Cx::scoped_cpu(worker_cap, f): std::thread::scope soundness pattern — the function blocks until every child joins, so there is no leakable guard and no mem::forget hazard; children get CpuCx (Cx clone + shared drain latch) whose checkpoint() surfaces both scope-drain and the existing fast_cancel/budget machinery. Panic containment: catch_unwind per child, first payload recorded (child ordinal + payload_to_string), latch drains siblings, structured ScopedCpuError::ChildPanicked after full join. worker_cap exceeded = structured refusal at spawn (fetch_add undo, no thread created). Entry AND exit checkpoints: pre-cancelled/exhausted-budget Cx refuses before spawning anything; cancellation during the scope surfaces as Cancelled after drain. No task/region is created — scoped threads are an implementation detail of the calling task, which is blocked inside the scope, so the region cannot close under the workers. EVIDENCE: cargo test --lib cx::scoped_cpu = 5/5 passed (children_borrow_run_local_state proves non-'static lending: children mutate a borrowed Vec<Mutex<u64>>; worker_cap_refuses_structurally; child_panic_is_contained_and_drains_siblings; cancellation_propagates_to_children_and_surfaces; exhausted_budget_refuses_at_entry). cargo clippy --lib -D warnings: zero lints in cx/ (6 pre-existing hits in src/net/unix/stream.rs, untouched by this change). cargo fmt --check clean. Downstream consumer: FrankenSim fs-exec persistent TilePool workers (frankensim beads 691k/lx0e).

title: GenServer audit: a call queued before a native server is admitted panics a scheduler worker when admission is denied (HIGH); stop() racing start-up is lost; pre-stopped server handles casts without on_start
description:
Read-only audit of src/actor.rs and src/gen_server.rs at origin/main 2780d3454 (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-04; read from origin). SapphireHill re-read 1 and 2 at origin.

## HIGH
1. GenServerCell (gen_server.rs ~760) has no Drop. Cx::spawn_gen_server returns the handle before admission; call() reserves and enqueues an Envelope::Call without yielding; if admission is then denied (RegionAtCapacity/RegionClosed), resolve_failed/resolve_cancelled drop the factory without catch_unwind, the cell drops its Receiver, and the queued call's armed TrackedOneshotPermit trips [ASUP-E101] OBLIGATION TOKEN LEAKED on the scheduler worker (three_lane.rs drain_spawn_admissions) or in the lab step; the later admission-error slot and region advance never run, and a join may hang. publish_server_panic already drains for the panic path only. Fix: Drop for GenServerCell closes the mailbox and aborts queued call permits.

## MEDIUM
2. run_gen_server_loop does "if state.load() != Stopping { state.store(Running) }" (~1961): a stop() landing between the load and the store is overwritten, the loop parks forever, and join never resolves (multi-thread race; actor.rs uses a CAS). Fix: atomic fetch_update.
3. A server stopped before its first poll skips on_start (pre-stop) but then dispatches queued casts/calls (~1966-2004) against uninitialized state, contradicting the on_start doc. Needs an owner choice: run on_start when queued messages exist, or treat skipped-init as aborted (abort calls, drop casts).

## LOW
4. GenServer trait docs say casts are processed on cancellation; the code drops them (intentionally). Doc fix.
5. stop()/abort() store Stopping unconditionally, moving Stopped back to Stopping; is_alive() stays true; a denied spawn stays Created.
6. GenServerRef::try_cast DropOldest evictions are not counted or warned (GenServerHandle got this in dqdgcq).
7. MailboxConfig.backpressure and ActorContext::stop_self document behaviour no spawn API implements.

## Checked and sound
Reply obligation commit/abort/drop-bomb, call() reserve/send/cancel paths, DropOldest accounting, abort-before-mask, actor lifecycle CAS and drain, join futures, system lane.

title: [RAPTORQ-RFC6330-CONFORMANCE] Golden File Testing and Round-Trip Validation
description:
Implement Pattern 2 (Golden File Testing) and Pattern 3 (Round-Trip Conformance) for RaptorQ serialization formats and complex encoding/decoding outputs that require frozen reference validation.

## Background
Complex RaptorQ outputs (constraint matrices, symbol data, encoding parameters) benefit from golden file testing where correct outputs are verified once and then frozen as regression tests. Round-trip testing ensures encoding/decoding cycles preserve data integrity.

## Scope - FIXTURE + ROUND-TRIP Testing

### Pattern 2: Golden File Testing
- Complex outputs that are correct once verified, then frozen
- Constraint matrix structure outputs  
- Parameter derivation calculation results
- Systematic and repair symbol generation outputs
- Decoding reconstruction intermediate states

### Pattern 3: Round-Trip Conformance  
- Encode → Decode cycle data integrity validation
- Serialization format round-trip testing
- Cross-implementation compatibility validation
- Symbol format preservation across encode/decode boundaries

## Technical Architecture

```
tests/conformance/raptorq_rfc6330/golden/
├── fixtures/
│   ├── parameter_derivation/
│   │   ├── k_calculation_cases.golden
│   │   ├── systematic_index_lookup.golden
│   │   └── tuple_generation_matrix.golden
│   ├── constraint_matrices/
│   │   ├── small_block_systematic.golden
│   │   ├── large_block_repair.golden
│   │   └── edge_case_boundaries.golden
│   ├── symbol_outputs/
│   │   ├── systematic_symbols_k40.golden
│   │   ├── repair_symbols_esi_range.golden
│   │   └── reconstruction_intermediate.golden
│   └── PROVENANCE.md
├── src/
│   ├── golden_file_manager.rs      # UPDATE_GOLDENS workflow
│   ├── round_trip_harness.rs       # Encode/decode cycle validation
│   ├── fixture_generator.rs        # Generate golden outputs
│   └── format_validator.rs         # Symbol format consistency
└── bin/
    ├── generate_goldens.rs         # Golden file generation
    └── validate_round_trips.rs     # Round-trip test runner
```

## Golden File Test Categories

### Parameter Derivation Golden Files
- K calculation results for various object sizes
- Systematic index table lookups and derivations
- Tuple generation outputs for systematic and repair symbols
- Constraint matrix structural layouts

### Symbol Generation Golden Files  
- Systematic symbol encoding outputs for reference test vectors
- Repair symbol generation for specific ESI ranges
- Symbol format serialization (binary and structured formats)
- Cross-implementation symbol compatibility formats

### Decoding Process Golden Files
- Constraint matrix construction intermediate states
- Gaussian elimination step-by-step matrices
- Inactivation algorithm state transitions
- Object reconstruction intermediate results

## Round-Trip Test Categories

### Encode/Decode Integrity
```rust
fn test_encode_decode_round_trip() {
    let original_data = generate_test_object(size);
    let encoded_symbols = raptorq_encode(original_data);  
    let decoded_data = raptorq_decode(encoded_symbols);
    assert_eq!(original_data, decoded_data);
}
```

### Symbol Format Round-Trips
- Symbol serialization → deserialization identity
- Cross-implementation symbol format compatibility
- Metadata preservation across encoding boundaries
- Error correction capability preservation

### Parameter Round-Trips  
- Parameter derivation → constraint matrix → parameter recovery
- Tuple generation → matrix construction → tuple validation
- ESI assignment → symbol generation → ESI recovery

## Implementation Plan

### Golden File Workflow Implementation
```rust
fn assert_golden(test_name: &str, actual: &[u8]) {
    let golden_path = Path::new("tests/golden/raptorq")
        .join(format!("{test_name}.golden"));
        
    if env::var("UPDATE_GOLDENS").is_ok() {
        fs::write(&golden_path, actual).unwrap();
        return;
    }
    
    let expected = fs::read(&golden_path)
        .expect("Golden file missing - run with UPDATE_GOLDENS=1");
        
    assert_eq!(actual, &expected, "Golden file mismatch for {test_name}");
}
```

### Round-Trip Validation Framework
```rust
trait RoundTripTest {
    type Input;
    type Encoded;
    type Decoded;
    
    fn encode(&self, input: Self::Input) -> Self::Encoded;
    fn decode(&self, encoded: Self::Encoded) -> Self::Decoded;
    fn validate_identity(&self, original: Self::Input, decoded: Self::Decoded) -> bool;
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

### Golden File Testing
1. **Comprehensive golden coverage** for complex RaptorQ outputs that are expensive to recompute
2. **UPDATE_GOLDENS workflow** for safe golden file regeneration
3. **Diff-based failure reporting** showing exact mismatches between actual and expected
4. **Provenance tracking** in PROVENANCE.md for golden file generation history
5. **CI integration** with golden file validation on every commit

### Round-Trip Testing  
1. **Encode/decode identity** validation for all supported object sizes
2. **Symbol format preservation** across serialization boundaries
3. **Cross-implementation compatibility** where applicable
4. **Error correction validation** - round-trips work even with symbol loss
5. **Metadata preservation** - object parameters survive encode/decode cycle

### Integration Requirements
1. **Golden file management** integrated with conformance test harness
2. **Round-trip tests** run as part of systematic conformance validation
3. **Failure reporting** with actionable diff information
4. **Performance boundaries** - golden tests complete within reasonable CI time

## Deliverables

- Golden file testing framework with UPDATE_GOLDENS workflow
- Round-trip validation harness for encode/decode integrity
- Comprehensive golden file coverage for complex RaptorQ outputs
- Round-trip test suite covering symbol formats and parameter preservation
- PROVENANCE.md documenting golden file generation methodology
- CI integration for automated golden file and round-trip validation

## Validation Process

```bash
# Golden file workflow validation
UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 cargo test --test raptorq_golden_files
cargo test --test raptorq_golden_files
git diff tests/golden/raptorq/  # Review changes

# Round-trip validation  
cargo test --test raptorq_round_trip_conformance
cargo run --bin validate_round_trips -- --comprehensive
```

## Dependencies

- Requires: Conformance test harness infrastructure
- Builds on: Spec-derived test implementation for test case selection
- May use: Reference implementation differential testing for golden file validation

## Time Estimate  

8 hours (golden file framework + round-trip harness + comprehensive test coverage)

title: [idea-wizard] Cancellation-storm and obligation-pressure replay corpus
description:
Idea-wizard top-5 idea: create a deterministic replay corpus for cancellation storms, obligation pressure, loser-drain behavior, and region-close quiescence under swarm-scale fanout. Asupersync differentiates itself on cancel-correctness; the project needs high-intensity scenarios that prove this under adversarial swarm behavior rather than only small unit cases.

Problem: many past failures involve root-region fixtures, stale tests, obligation leaks, race losers, or cancellation/drain interactions. Large agent swarms amplify these patterns: thousands of tasks can be canceled, timed out, retried, or moved between regions at once.

title: atp/quic: receiver Proof for a 2000-member tree is ~150 unpaced, recovery-untracked server-role packets; pace and track it
description: Split from asupersync-9bb6pt (its sender-side stall-storm fix is separate). Observed in the w67b GH#67 lane logs: the receiver's Proof for the daqxbz 2000-member packed tree leaves as ~150 server-role packets in one unpaced burst that ATP-scoped recovery does not track (no in_flight_stream_frames entry on the receiver side), so a lossy path drops a slice of it and the sender's proof wait only recovers through the sender's own stall-PTO re-sends of the source stream. Needed: send the Proof through the same paced/tracked source-stream path (or pace it against the receiver's pacing decision and register its frames for ack-gap/PTO recovery), and a lossy e2e that measures Proof delivery time. Read-only design is fine during the ce14e7a57 native freeze; land after it.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
SapphireHill 2026-09-09 20:15Z, premise refined after reading send_native_proof_until_close in src/net/atp/transport_quic/native_link.rs (read-only under the freeze): the receiver's Proof goes out as one control-stream frame followed by a plain link.flush(), so the whole ~150-packet Proof leaves in a single unpaced burst (flush is cwnd-gated but not paced by the source-stream rate pacer). The loop then keeps a snapshot of last_flushed_stream_frames() and on every NEEDMORE_PTO (1.5 s) without an inbound packet re-sends that ENTIRE snapshot (reason terminal_proof_pto), and again wholesale on any ObjectRequest/ObjectManifest (terminal_proof_request); it never consults in_flight_stream_frames or the latest ACK ranges, so already-acknowledged Proof packets are re-sent every round. That is the "recovery-untracked" part: the frames are recorded as in flight by flush, but the retransmit decision ignores that bookkeeping.

Fix shape (after the ce14e7a57 freeze; coordinate with 9bb6pt since both touch stall re-send policy): (1) pace the Proof through the paced source-stream send path (or at least chunk the flush at the pacer's burst shape) so a lossy path does not lose a contiguous slice of it; (2) replace the snapshot re-send with the same evidence-bounded drains the sender uses: on inbound ACK progress drain_ack_gap_lost_stream_frames_for_retransmit(latest ack ranges), on a silent PTO drain_limited_in_flight_stream_frames_for_retransmit(stall_retransmit_packet_cap()) — after 9bb6pt lands that helper exists — and fall back to the snapshot only when in_flight_stream_frames is already empty; (3) keep terminal_proof_request as is (the sender explicitly asked). Test: extend real_udp_quic_tree_manifest_stall_pto_resends_stay_bounded (9bb6pt) to also collect terminal_proof_pto re-sends and bound their packets, plus a lossy-proxy timing assertion that the Proof is acknowledged within two stall intervals.

title: [swarm-perf] Add controller snapshot ledger for adaptive swarm policies
description:
Background:
- The current swarm-perf graph has evidence artifacts, controller-composition rules, and an operator-facing host profile planner, but it still lacks a canonical runtime snapshot surface that records what each adaptive controller is doing over time.
- Canonical FrankenSuite guidance requires per-controller fields such as decision counts, fallback-active state, calibration, and last action so adaptive behavior is auditable instead of hidden in ad hoc logs.
- Without a snapshot ledger, replay bundles and dry-run planners can explain recommendations, but they cannot show the live controller state that produced those recommendations.

Candidate surfaces:
- src/observability/* runtime snapshot or evidence surfaces
- src/runtime/config.rs
- src/runtime/builder.rs
- artifacts/ and scripts/ for deterministic controller bundles
- any runtime kernel snapshot or debug surfaces already used by swarm-perf tooling

Required design:
1. Define a versioned controller snapshot schema for swarm-perf policies with explicit units and required fields per controller.
2. Record at least decision counts, fallback-active state, calibration/confidence, last action, and last evidence tick for each adaptive controller.
3. Preserve exact baseline behavior when the ledger is disabled or a controller has no evidence; observability must not silently mutate scheduling behavior.
4. Emit deterministic bundle/report output so replay artifacts and dry-run planners can show both recommendations and live controller state.

Proof / validation:
- Snapshot/golden coverage for the schema and representative controller states.
- Deterministic multi-controller scenarios that log state transitions, fallback flips, and controller decisions over a fixed evidence stream.
- Artifact output proving planners and smoke bundles can render the controller ledger without bespoke parsing.

Success criteria:
- Operators can inspect one deterministic artifact bundle and understand which swarm-perf controllers were active, what state they were in, and why fallback or confidence changes occurred.
design: Turn adaptive controller state into an explicit artifact, not a log archaeology problem. This bead should define one versioned snapshot ledger surface for swarm-perf controllers, reuse the controller catalog/interference work from asupersync-b4guhs, and make the output consumable by both replay bundles and the operator-facing planner. The ledger must be observational only: it reports controller state, confidence, and fallback, but cannot silently change policy behavior when enabled.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests must cover schema serialization, missing-controller defaults, monotone decision counters, fallback-active transitions, and planner-facing rendering of representative states. Deterministic multi-controller scenarios must log state transitions, fallback flips, last-action updates, and evidence-tick alignment over a fixed evidence stream. Artifact output must prove that planners and smoke bundles can render the controller ledger without bespoke parsing or hidden field assumptions.
notes: This bead operationalizes the RuntimeKernelSnapshot-style guidance that every adaptive controller should expose decisions, fallback state, calibration/confidence, and last action in one inspectable place. Reuse the existing generic controller substrate in src/runtime/kernel.rs plus the decision-plane validation contract/runner surfaces (artifacts/decision_plane_validation_v1.json, scripts/run_decision_plane_validation_smoke.sh, tests/decision_plane_validation_contract.rs) instead of inventing a second registry. title: Native runtime refuses every Normal-priority region after 1000 have ever been created: swarm governor envelopes are never unregistered on region close
description:
Found 2026-09-26 by SapphireHill: the native control run of tzvnsy's history test (2112 open/close cycles of a child region) failed at about round 1000 with `child region opens: Create(ResourcePressure { requested_priority: Normal, reason: "Region limit exceeded: 1000 >= 1000" })`.

Cause: RuntimeState registers a ResourceEnvelope with the SwarmPressureGovernor for every child region it creates (state.rs ~9165, register_region_envelope, since 8eb485758 on 2026-07-30). Nothing in production ever calls unregister_region_envelope; only its own unit tests do. The region close path (state.rs ~9521: record_finalizer_close, resource_monitor.clear_region_priority, arena removal) releases every other per-region record but not the envelope. The governor's check_region_admission rejects Normal/Low-priority regions once active_regions.len() >= max_regions_per_instance (default 1000). Critical/High skip that check.

So a native runtime that creates 1000 child regions over its lifetime can never create another Normal-priority region: open_child_region, and anything that mints a child region per request or per supervised child, fails with ResourcePressure. The envelopes, and any workload leases bound to them, also leak.

Fix: unregister the envelope, which also releases its workload leases, where the close path finishes a region. Regression: a native runtime opens and closes more than 1000 child regions, and every open succeeds.

title: Page-Hinkley reset reuses lifetime count in new-regime mean
description: PageHinkleyDetector uses lifetime sample_count as the running-mean denominator, but reset_at reanchors mean/cumulative state without resetting that denominator. With tolerance 0, threshold 6 units, reset enabled, samples 0,20,30 produce alarms at both 20 and 30: post-reset mean 23.333 and statistic 6.667, while a fresh epoch seeded at 20 yields mean 25/statistic 5 and no second alarm. This corrupts post-reset detection calibration and can repeatedly discard opt-in scheduler controller learning. Preserve the public lifetime sample index, add an epoch-local mean count, set it to one on reset, and add exact None/Some/None plus fresh-epoch-equivalence regressions. Independently confirmed by two fresh-eye reviews 2026-07-15; existing tests stop at first alarm or compare identically flawed clones, and no specific bead covers reset count drift.

title: runtime/sharded_state: docs — clarify D:Instrumentation has internal trace mutex
description:
Lock-ordering audit of src/runtime/sharded_state.rs verified E→D→B→A→C holds. No deadlock hazard found:

VERIFIED SOUND:
- All 8 ShardGuard constructors (tasks_only, regions_only, obligations_only, for_task_completed, for_cancel, for_obligation, for_obligation_resolve, for_spawn, all) consistently acquire in B:Regions → A:Tasks → C:Obligations order.
- Each acquisition site wraps lock() between lock_order::before_lock(shard) and lock_order::after_lock(shard) (sharded_state.rs:355-665).
- Drop impl (lines 668-681) releases in LIFO (C → A → B) and calls unlock_n(debug_locks) with the correct count.
- LockShard::order (lines 698-704) assigns 0=Regions < 1=Tasks < 2=Obligations, matching the canonical order.
- debug_assert! in before_lock (line 753) fires if held.last().order() >= next.order(), catching any regression in debug builds.
- No direct .lock() calls on tasks/regions/obligations shards in production code (0 hits outside cli/doctor test fixtures where the lock-contention ANALYZER tests itself with simulated violation patterns at lines 18488-18594).
- cli/doctor patterns bad_order / lock_path are input strings to analyze_workspace_lock_contention's test (test of the detector, not a runtime path).

LOW-severity documentation gap (tracked by this bead):
- src/runtime/sharded_state.rs:160 comment labels D:Instrumentation as 'lock-free', but TraceBufferHandle (src/trace/buffer.rs:116-121) contains buffer: Mutex<TraceBuffer>. The mutex is internal, typically short-held, and not tracked in LockShard::order. Current code never acquires shard locks while holding the trace mutex (audited: all trace.push callers take the trace mutex last, inside shard-guarded critical sections), so no current deadlock. A refactor that added a callback from trace-emit into shard mutation would silently break ordering without triggering the debug_assert (LockShard lacks a Trace variant).

Recommended hardening (choose one):
1. Update docs at sharded_state.rs:160-163 to read 'D: Instrumentation — internal mutex + atomics; acquired after shard locks by convention' instead of 'lock-free'.
2. Add LockShard::Trace with order=3 (between Obligations=2 and any future variant) and wrap trace.buffer.lock() with before_lock/after_lock.

Option 1 is zero risk and documents the real invariant. Option 2 extends enforcement coverage but touches hot-path trace emission.

Audit commit: deb5c1d7 → 92ab6a8d → e29d045e → d97cef71 (no changes in this bead).
close_reason: Doc-only clarification landed in 41eaa6fb. src/runtime/sharded_state.rs:160-173 header now reads 'Shard D: Instrumentation (internal mutex + atomics)' instead of 'lock-free', with an 11-line invariant comment documenting (1) TraceBufferHandle holds an internal Mutex<TraceBuffer>, (2) the shard isn't in LockShard because the mutex is short-held and never taken across shard mutations, (3) the convention 'acquired AFTER shard locks in canonical E->D->B->A->C order' is enforced by convention + this comment, and (4) a future trace-emit -> shard-mutation callback would break ordering without tripping before_lock's debug_assert. Option 2 (add LockShard::Trace with order=3) intentionally NOT taken: it extends enforcement coverage but touches the hot-path trace.push emission and requires wrapping every trace-mutex acquisition with before_lock/after_lock. File as follow-up if doc-only protection proves insufficient under refactor pressure. Zero behavior change; cannot introduce compile errors.

title: Add conformance/src/tests/structured_concurrency.rs for scope ownership laws
description:
## Problem
The reusable `conformance/` crate has no dedicated suite for structured-concurrency laws. Current coverage is limited to generic spawn/join behavior in `conformance/src/tests/runtime.rs`, which does not assert parent-owned task lifetimes, descendant cancellation, or orphan prevention.

## Proposed Test File
- `conformance/src/tests/structured_concurrency.rs`

## Expected Assertions
- Child tasks are owned by the parent scope/region and cannot outlive it.
- Cancelling or closing the parent scope propagates to outstanding descendants.
- Nested scopes close in tree order; no detached orphan task continues after parent close returns.
- Scope close returns only after descendant cleanup/finalizers complete.

## Notes
This likely requires extending `conformance::RuntimeInterface` with explicit scope/region primitives instead of relying on plain spawn handles.
close_reason: done

title: [DECISION] LossMatrix::expected_loss doesn't bound action < n_actions (analogous to d0gy19 posterior gap)
description: Follow-up to d0gy19 (which added the posterior.len()==n_states precondition to franken_decision LossMatrix::expected_loss). The same function has an analogous unbounded parameter: 'action'. expected_loss(posterior, action) calls self.get(s, action) = values[s*n_actions + action] for each state s, but never checks action < self.n_actions(). For action >= n_actions: small s silently indexes into a LATER state's loss row (plausible-but-wrong expected loss, no error), and large s indexes past values.len() (OOB panic). Same severity/class as the posterior dimension bug. Currently latent: the only consumer (src/raptorq/decision_contract.rs expected_loss_terms) iterates 0..action::COUNT and builds the matrix with action::COUNT actions, so action < n_actions holds by construction. Fix: add assert!(action < self.n_actions(), "action index ({action}) out of range for {} actions", self.n_actions()) at the top of expected_loss, mirroring the posterior assert (resolution a, fail-loud parity with get()'s OOB panic). Member crate, verifiable via cargo test -p franken-decision. Filed by SapphireHill 2026-06-14.
close_reason: Fixed: expected_loss now also asserts action < n_actions (fail-loud, parity with the posterior assert and get()'s OOB panic), so an out-of-range action can no longer silently read a later state's loss row or panic OOB. Test expected_loss_panics_on_action_out_of_range. RCH cargo test -p franken-decision expected_loss exit=0 (all expected_loss tests pass under -D warnings).
