title: [security-audit-HIGH] raptorq/decoder.rs:2152 silent zero-fill substitute when prow >= n_rows masks rank-deficiency
description: src/raptorq/decoder.rs:2151-2156 (and the parallel site at 2451-2456 inside inactivate_and_solve_with_proof): after Gaussian elimination, the pivot_row[dense_col] lookup is guarded by 'if prow < n_rows' and the else branch silently fills the column with vec![0u8; symbol_size] rather than returning DecodeError::SingularMatrix. Attack: a crafted symbol stream where select_pivot_row fails to update pivot_row for certain dense columns (but elimination_error remains None) produces intermediate symbols that are entirely zero for those columns. Subsequent source extraction is silent data corruption — the decoder reports success while emitting attacker-influenced zero blocks. Suggested fix: replace the defensive zero-fill with an explicit DecodeError::SingularMatrix { row: col } on the else branch so an unexpected pivot table state surfaces as failure instead of malformed output. Source: /security-audit-for-saas src/raptorq/* (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Fixed in f84f365fd: inactivate_and_solve and inactivate_and_solve_with_proof return Err(DecodeError::SingularMatrix { row: dense_col }) instead of zero-filling state.solved when pivot_row[dense_col] >= n_rows. Crafted symbol streams can no longer disguise rank-deficient decode as success-with-zeros.

title: [security-saas-refresh] web/session.rs: CSRF defense relies SOLELY on X-CSRF-Token header — no Origin/Referer header verification as defense-in-depth layer
description: src/web/session.rs:544-567 CSRF check verifies ONLY the X-CSRF-Token request header against the session-stored token via constant-time comparison. There is NO complementary Origin or Referer header verification against the server's expected origin. OWASP CSRF Cheat Sheet recommends DEFENSE IN DEPTH using BOTH (a) synchronizer token (X-CSRF-Token check — implemented) AND (b) Origin/Referer header validation (NOT implemented). Why both: (a) protects against attackers who can guess/leak the token; (b) protects against header-stripping intermediaries that drop X-CSRF-Token but preserve Origin (forms posted from same site without JS). Modern browsers ALWAYS send Origin on state-changing requests (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) — checking it costs almost nothing and adds significant defense. Mitigation: in the CSRF middleware path, additionally extract the Origin header (fallback to Referer) and assert it matches the server's allowlisted origin (HostMiddleware allowed_hosts from bead t9yqht). If both Origin and Referer are missing AND the request is state-changing, reject 403. Severity HIGH for any SaaS that depends on CSRF protection (the existing single-layer defense is OWASP-non-compliant).
close_reason: Fixed in commit 5e1ebd1bf: SessionConfig.allowed_origins enables Origin/Referer allow-list as 2nd CSRF defense layer per OWASP CSRF Cheat Sheet.

title: [DECISION] LossMatrix::expected_loss doesn't check posterior.len()==n_states: shorter posterior silently miscomputes expected loss (longer panics OOB in get)
description: franken_decision LossMatrix::expected_loss(posterior, action) computes sum_s posterior(s)*get(s,action) by iterating posterior.probs() with s as the state index, but never checks posterior.probs().len() == self.n_states(). get(s,a) = values[s*n_actions + a]. If the posterior has MORE entries than n_states, get(s,a) indexes past values.len() and panics (OOB). If the posterior has FEWER entries than n_states, expected_loss silently sums only the leading states and returns a plausible-but-wrong expected loss with no error — and bayes_action/expected_losses propagate the wrong value. The math is correct for matching dimensions; this is a missing precondition on a public API. Resolutions (maintainer's call): (a) assert_eq!(posterior.probs().len(), self.n_states()) at the top of expected_loss — fail-loud, consistent with get()'s existing OOB panic, converts the silent-shorter case to a clear panic; (b) return Result/Option with a DimensionMismatch error (API change); (c) document the precondition explicitly. title: [bug-hunt] messaging/nats.rs: publish() runs handle_pending_messages AFTER setting connected=true — caller can see Err for a publish that already succeeded on the wire, leading to duplicates on retry
description: src/messaging/nats.rs:1019-1057. After publish() writes PUB+payload+CRLF and flushes, sets self.connected=true (line 1051), it then calls self.handle_pending_messages(cx).await? (line 1054). If handle_pending_messages returns an error (e.g., a server -ERR or a cx checkpoint that races with cancel), publish() returns Err to the caller. But the message was already serialized to the wire and flushed — the server has it and will dispatch it to subscribers. The caller sees an error and may retry, producing a duplicate. Compare publish_request (lines 1059-1095) which does NOT call handle_pending_messages — inconsistent. Severity MEDIUM. NATS core publish/subscribe is at-most-once by protocol so duplicates are technically allowed, but a publish that returns Err yet was wire-delivered violates the principle of least surprise. Suggested fix: drain pending server messages BEFORE the publish (so any pending PING+ERR are observed up-front), or move the handle_pending_messages call to a separate API the caller can run between publishes.
close_reason: Shipped in 22dc476a3: handle_pending_messages now runs BEFORE wire write; post-flush commits to Ok unconditionally — at-most-once contract restored

title: [bug-hunt][HIGH] web/middleware.rs CorsMiddleware: silently reflects ANY origin when allow_credentials=true — Fetch §3.2.5 violation, credential-reflection vulnerability
description: src/web/middleware.rs:141-154 CorsMiddleware::allowed_origin_value. When CorsPolicy.allow_origin = CorsAllowOrigin::Any AND allow_credentials = true, the function returns Some(origin.to_string()) — echoing the requesters Origin header. Per Fetch spec §3.2.5, the Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * + Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true combination is FORBIDDEN because it lets any origin read credentialed responses (canonical credential-reflection vuln). The current code silently downgrades Any to per-request Origin echo, which technically conforms to the spec letter (Allow-Origin is no longer *) but accomplishes the SAME exfiltration: any origin gets its own Origin echoed back, so any origin can read the credentialed response. Severity HIGH P1. Mitigation landed in 967c... (debug_assert in CorsMiddleware::new + tracing warn in release). Real fix: change allowed_origin_value to RETURN None when (Any, allow_credentials=true) so the response carries no Allow-Origin header and the browser blocks the response entirely; OR change CorsPolicy::default to use Exact(empty) so the unsafe combination is unconstructable by accident.
close_reason: CorsMiddleware fails closed under (Allow-Origin=Any, Allow-Credentials=true): allowed_origin_value now returns None instead of echoing the requester's Origin, the downstream call path emits NO Access-Control-Allow-Origin / Allow-Credentials headers, and the browser blocks the credentialed response per Fetch §3.2.5. Allowlist path (Exact + credentials) preserved verbatim. tracing::warn emits at the rejection site so SREs can spot the misconfig in logs. Existing test 'cors_with_credentials_echoes_origin' replaced with two new regression tests pinning the allowlisted-origin echo path and the non-allowlisted-origin fail-closed path; an additional release-only test pins the (Any, credentials) fail-closed path symmetrically (the debug_assert in new() handles debug-build rejection) (30fdd1b5c)

title: blocking_pool: shutdown_and_wait can return true (clean) while a replacement worker leaks its JoinHandle (race)
description: Found in deep review (SapphireHill 2026-06-29). src/runtime/blocking_pool.rs guard-drop (~1216) decrements active_threads to 0 BEFORE checking pending work + spawning a replacement. shutdown_and_wait (~753) can observe active_threads==0 in that window, drain+join the current handle snapshot, and return true. The replacement worker (spawned to drain a task that linearized just before shutdown) then runs with its JoinHandle pushed into the now-emptied vec, never joined -> function claims clean shutdown while a worker is still live + that handle is leaked (detached). No UAF (worker's Arc<Inner> keeps inner alive) and the task still runs; the issue is the false true + un-joined handle. FIX: in the guard, spawn/notify the replacement (or set a replacement-pending flag) BEFORE the fetch_sub; or re-check active_threads/thread_handles after draining in shutdown_and_wait and loop again if any handle remains.
close_reason: Fixed (SapphireHill, commit pending): blocking_pool replacement-handoff race. Added replacement_pending: AtomicUsize to BlockingPoolInner; the retiring worker's guard announces the hand-off (fetch_add) BEFORE decrementing active_threads and clears it (fetch_sub) only AFTER the replacement spawn attempt. shutdown_and_wait now gates its wait loop on (active_threads>0 || replacement_pending>0), closing the window where it observed active_threads==0 mid-handoff, returned a clean true, and leaked the replacement's never-joined handle. Deterministic regression test shutdown_and_wait_blocks_until_replacement_handoff_resolves (fails pre-fix, passes post-fix). clippy -D warnings clean; lib tests green.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: CORRECTION (SapphireHill, e200fd30e): the original fix (4b46b0e63) introduced a work-stranding race — checking pending work BEFORE the active_threads decrement let a task enqueued in that window be missed by the retiring worker while a concurrent enqueuer's maybe_spawn still saw active==1 and declined to spawn (spawn_with_affinity calls maybe_spawn after enqueue). FIX: made the replacement_pending announce UNCONDITIONAL before the decrement and moved the pending check back to AFTER the decrement (original race-free order) — keeps the shutdown-race closed AND restores no-stranding. Re-verified clippy + full blocking_pool tests green.

title: [swarm-v2] Autonomic live control loop and proof certificates
description:
## Background
The first massive-swarm program closed the smoke-runner/signoff graph for 64+ core and 256GB+ host optimization. It produced deterministic contracts for topology, batching, tail-risk admission, capacity hints, profile bundles, generated smoke artifacts, and coordination workload bridge signoff. The next useful step is not to duplicate that graph; it is to promote the strongest evidence lanes into an operator-safe live control loop with proof-carrying certificates, conservative fallbacks, and deterministic replay.

## Goals
- Turn redacted coordination, scheduler, capacity, and tail-latency evidence into live but fail-closed control inputs.
- Produce compositional certificates for latency budgets, capacity envelopes, and controller decisions.
- Keep every controller reversible, auditable, deterministic under replay, and safe to decline.
- Provide unit tests plus deterministic e2e or smoke runners with detailed logs for each slice.

## Non-goals
- No new executor/runtime dependency.
- No raw Agent Mail, Beads, rch, git, home-directory, secret, or host-identifying data inside the core runtime crate.
- No mandatory 64+ core host in ordinary CI; large-host proofs are template or fixture-backed unless explicitly enabled.

## Success Criteria
All child beads are closed with rch-backed validation, deterministic artifact paths, fallback/no-win behavior, explicit rollback semantics where configuration changes are proposed, and a final signoff row proving the v2 control loop does not rely on proxy green statuses.
notes: Coordination note: this parent epic is a planning container, not a direct implementation claim target. Claim child beads only; close the parent after asupersync-d87ytw.15 completes final signoff.
close_reason: All 15 child beads are closed, including asupersync-d87ytw.15 final control-loop signoff audit. Parent epic was a planning container; closeout follows the recorded instruction to close after .15 completed final signoff. Final signoff close reason records rch rustfmt, focused test 7/7, scoped clippy, and smoke runner proof with no proxy evidence.

## Why
The qn8i0p bridge proves fixture replay only. Operators running massive swarms need a safe live ingestion gate so real contention and proof pressure can become deterministic workload inputs.

## How
Keep the collector outside the core runtime crate. Reuse the v1 redaction taxonomy, add live-source adapters that fail closed on stale, unredacted, unsupported, nondeterministic, or duplicate input, and emit deterministic bundle hashes plus refusal rows.

## Tests and logging
Unit tests must cover required-field validation, redaction rejection, stable ordering, duplicate handling, stale-source refusal, and no core-runtime dependency keys. E2E/smoke runner must log source kind, pseudonymized agent, correlation id, workload family, refusal reason, source hash, output bundle path, and replay command.

## Success criteria
A focused rch-backed test and deterministic smoke runner prove accepted live-like fixtures and refused unsafe fixtures; ordinary CI uses fixtures, while real live ingestion is explicitly opt-in.

## Why
Certificates and controllers need live evidence. The current taxonomy defines the language; v2 needs carefully scoped producers that preserve determinism, overhead bounds, and unknown-bucket honesty.

## How
Start with compact core fields at stable producer seams: ready queue depth, poll count, I/O events, retry delay, lock wait, heap live/bytes-live, and explicit unknown residual. Extended direct durations can remain feature-gated or replay-only until proven.

## Tests and logging
Unit tests must cover schema-key stability, missing producer fallback to unknown, deterministic serialization, disabled equivalence, and low-overhead feature gating. E2E/smoke runner must log scenario id, event id, taxonomy version, all compact fields, residual unknown, overhead estimate, artifact path, and replay command.

## Success criteria
The runtime can emit certificate-ready compact tail rows without silently treating unmeasured terms as zero or introducing a new hot-path allocation/regression.

title: [swarm-v2] Controller interference digital twin
description:
## Phase
Idea-wizard next 10, rank 6.

## What
Build a deterministic digital-twin harness that replays interactions among admission, batching, brownout, topology, trace-retention, and capacity controllers before any combined policy is accepted.

## Why
Each controller can be locally reasonable and still produce oscillation, starvation, or contradictory fallback behavior when composed.

## How
Represent controller outputs as a bounded state vector, replay fixture and synthesized workload scenarios, and flag interference classes: oscillation, priority inversion, hidden overload transfer, conflicting no-win decisions, and stale evidence reuse.

## Tests and logging
Unit tests cover each interference class and deterministic ordering. E2E runner logs controller versions, input evidence hashes, state vectors, detected conflicts, fallback decision, artifact path, and replay command.

## Success criteria
Combined controller bundles cannot pass signoff without a deterministic interference report showing pass or explicit no-win/fallback.

title: [swarm-v2] Shadow promote and rollback receipts
description:
## Phase
Idea-wizard next 10, rank 7.

## What
Create a shadow-run promotion gate that compares candidate controller/profile bundles against the conservative baseline on the same evidence snapshot and emits promote, hold, rollback, or no-win receipts.

## Why
Operators need a deterministic answer to whether a profile should actually be enabled, not just that its schema is valid.

## How
Use paired baseline/candidate reports, regret margins, tail and capacity certificates, and explicit rollback receipts. Refuse promotion on stale evidence, missing certificates, unexplained dirty artifacts, weak sample size, or conflicting controller outputs.

## Tests and logging
Unit tests cover promote, hold/no-win, stale evidence, certificate mismatch, and rollback rendering. E2E runner logs baseline hash, candidate hash, regret margin, p99/p999 deltas, certificate ids, decision, receipt path, and replay command.

## Success criteria
Any v2 policy bundle has a deterministic shadow decision and rollback receipt before it can be recommended.

title: [swarm-v2] Unified admission and brownout contract
description:
## Phase
Idea-wizard next 10, rank 8.

## What
Unify tail-risk admission, cohort steering, and brownout shedding into one policy contract with precedence rules, critical-surface preservation, and reversible restoration semantics.

## Why
Separate controls can accidentally reject important work, shed evidence needed for diagnosis, or move pressure to another subsystem. Operators need one explainable ladder.

## How
Define policy states, allowed transitions, critical/non-critical surfaces, preserved telemetry minimums, fairness escape hatches, restoration conditions, and no-win fallback rules.

## Tests and logging
Unit tests cover precedence, restoration, critical-surface preservation, fairness escape, and disabled equivalence. E2E runner logs policy phase, reason code, admitted/refused counts, preserved telemetry, restoration trigger, fallback reason, and replay command.

## Success criteria
The control plane has a single deterministic contract for what gets admitted, deferred, shed, or restored under overload.

title: [swarm-v2] Self-tuning trace storage profiles
description:
## Phase
Idea-wizard next 10, rank 9.

## What
Make large-memory trace retention profiles self-tuning from capacity and tail evidence, while preserving deterministic retention decisions and low-memory fallbacks.

## Why
A 256GB host can keep more forensic evidence, but trace retention must not compete with hot runtime paths or hide dropped evidence.

## How
Use memory buckets, hot/cold artifact tiers, workload class, and certificate confidence to select retention windows and drop policies. Every drop must be accounted for and every large-memory choice must have a rollback-safe profile.

## Tests and logging
Unit tests cover memory bucket parsing, low-memory fallback, deterministic retention, drop accounting, and no hidden cold-path interference. E2E runner logs selected profile, memory bucket, retained/dropped counts, hot/cold bytes, confidence, fallback reason, and replay command.

## Success criteria
Trace retention adapts to large hosts without making high-memory behavior mandatory or interfering with scheduler hot paths.

STILL MISSING (this bead):
  1. The retry/dedup PROPERTY against the deterministic harness in the `not(kafka)` lane. The helper the deleted test used still exists, renamed: `deterministic_broker_end_offset` (src/messaging/kafka.rs:654, gated `cfg(all(not(feature = "kafka"), any(test, feature = "test-internals")))`).

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
DONE 2026-07-26 SapphireHill, commit 31b163e71.

ITEM 1 (the retry/dedup property) — DONE, but not where this bead proposed.

The bead suggested re-homing it "in the not(kafka) lane" of the integration file.
That is not possible, and finding out why is the useful part: integration tests
compile as downstream consumers, and there `send()` fails closed with
FeatureDisabled instead of reaching the deterministic broker. That is not an
accident to work around — it is br-asupersync-w2p2a0's deliberate boundary, and
it is exactly what the three surviving tests in that file assert. The property
has to run where the harness is actually reachable, i.e. in-crate, where
`deterministic_broker_allowed_for_testing()` returns true under cfg(test)
(kafka.rs:1397).

It now lives at
`messaging::kafka::tests::deterministic_broker_does_not_deduplicate_idempotent_retries`,
next to the other deterministic-broker tests. Written as a BOUNDARY test, not an
aspiration: enable_idempotence(true) configures the client, the harness does not
validate producer-id + sequence-number pairs, so a byte-identical retry appends
twice. Pinning that stops the flag from ever reading as exactly-once against the
harness and forces a deliberate rewrite if real dedup ever lands. Anchors on the
current end offset because the harness broker is process-global.

PROVEN TO HAVE TEETH: flipping the expected second offset to `before` (simulating
a broker that DID deduplicate) fails with `left: 1, right: 0`. So the assertion is
evaluated against real broker state, not passing vacuously. Restored byte-exact,
md5 verified. Verified green: 114 passed / 0 failed via
`cargo test -p asupersync --lib --features test-internals messaging::kafka`,
RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1, --base HEAD --clean-overlay overlaying only kafka.rs.

I also updated the stale comment at the head of the integration file, which still
said the property was "never re-homed". A note that outlives its truth is how
br-asupersync-z01bbr.8.5 sat unactionable for six weeks.

ITEM 3 (required-features) — MY OWN CLAIM WAS WRONG, and it is retracted.

I filed that this target "does not compile on a plain cargo test without
test-internals" and proposed adding `required-features`. I checked before editing:
`cargo check --test kafka_producer_idempotence_audit` on pristine HEAD with
DEFAULT features SUCCEEDS. The cause is feature unification through a
dev-dependency cycle — conformance/Cargo.toml:173 depends on asupersync with
["metrics", "test-internals", "tracing-integration", "fuzz"], and asupersync
dev-depends on conformance. So test-internals is always on for test builds.

No Cargo.toml change was made. Adding required-features would have "fixed" a
non-existent problem and masked the real one, which is far more interesting and is
filed as br-asupersync-z2kt29: NO integration test in this repo ever exercises the
default feature surface, and the fail-closed boundary tests are themselves
compiled with test-internals on.

ITEM 2 (what --features kafka coverage should look like) — NOT DONE, and I am not
closing it silently. With `--features kafka` this target still has zero producer
coverage; the real-broker assertions in tests/integration/kafka_real_broker.rs
remain env-gated behind REAL_KAFKA_TESTS and do not run in CI. Deciding that needs
a call on whether to stand up a broker in CI or accept the gap explicitly, which
is a scope/infra decision rather than a code fix. The gated imports in the audit
file still record the gap, which was the point of gating rather than deleting them.

title: rate_limit: try_acquire fast-path can barge a token past a FIFO-queued waiter (fairness)
description: Found by bug-hunt (SapphireHill 2026-06-29). src/combinator/rate_limit.rs RateLimiter::try_acquire reads pending_queue_count with Relaxed and NO wait_queue lock (~:395), then fast-path-consumes a token (~:404-414). enqueue holds wait_queue.write() and push_back's the waiter (~:642) BEFORE pending_queue_count.fetch_add (~:650), so a concurrent try_acquire can observe the entry pushed but count still 0 and barge the token past the FIFO-queued waiter. Consequence is FAIRNESS ONLY: token accounting stays correct under state.lock(), no leak/double-grant/hang, the queued waiter is served on the next refill. The sibling bulkhead.rs (~:296-303) deliberately closes the identical window by scanning queue contents under queue.read() before consuming — so this is an inconsistency/regression worth aligning, low severity.

Acquires wait_queue BEFORE state to match the enqueue/process_queue order (wait_queue->state; reset releases state before wait_queue so no inversion). Closes the barge window where enqueue pushed a waiter before bumping pending_queue_count. Deterministic test try_acquire_defers_to_queued_waiter_when_count_lags (queued entry + count==0 => defer). clippy -D warnings exit 0; tests green.

title: Instrument cancellation flow with tracing
description:
# Task

Add comprehensive tracing for cancellation propagation through the region tree.

## Why This Is Critical

Cancellation is THE core feature of asupersync. Understanding how cancellation flows
through a region tree is essential for debugging. Users need to see:
- Where cancellation originated
- How it propagated through regions
- Which tasks were affected
- How cleanup proceeded

## What to Instrument

1. **Cancel request**: Initial cancellation trigger
   - Fields: target (task_id or region_id), reason, source_task, budget_for_cleanup
   
2. **Cancel propagation**: As cancellation flows to children
   - Fields: from_region, to_region, to_task, propagation_depth
   - Use follows_from to link propagation chain
   
3. **Cancel observation**: When task observes via checkpoint()
   - Fields: task_id, reason, remaining_budget, mask_depth
   
4. **Drain phase**: Task draining to terminal state
   - Fields: task_id, drain_start, operations_pending
   
5. **Finalize phase**: Finalizer execution
   - Fields: task_id, finalizer_count, finalizer_budget

## Propagation Visualization

The tracing should enable reconstruction of:

```
cancel_request[target=Region(1), reason=Timeout]
  └─> propagate[to=Region(2)]
      ├─> propagate[to=Task(100)] 
      │   └─> observed[at=checkpoint, mask_depth=0]
      │       └─> draining[ops_pending=1]
      │           └─> finalizing[finalizers=2]
      └─> propagate[to=Task(101)]
          └─> observed[at=checkpoint, mask_depth=1] // masked!
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Cancel origin is always traceable
- [ ] Propagation path is fully recorded
- [ ] Observation points are recorded
- [ ] Drain and finalize phases are visible
- [ ] Masked cancellation is distinguishable
close_reason: Completed

title: [testing-fuzzing] grpc/codec LPM multi-frame stream boundary — preservation + no overflow on huge length
description:
gRPC codec length-prefixed-message boundary fuzz bead.

Problem:
- gRPC framed messages use a compression flag plus a 32-bit length prefix.
- Multi-frame streams and huge length prefixes are easy places to lose bytes, allocate too much, overflow length arithmetic, or accept malformed partial frames.
- The target must prove production ProstCodec/framing behavior, not just a byte-splitting mock.

Required design:
1. Exercise production encode/decode and stream-boundary handling for length-prefixed gRPC messages.
2. Preserve message ordering and exact payload bytes across arbitrary frame segmentation.
3. Reject huge or overflowing length prefixes before unbounded allocation.
4. Distinguish incomplete frame, malformed frame, unsupported compression flag, and valid multi-frame outcomes.
5. Keep cancellation/backpressure behavior observable where the codec participates in stream polling.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover empty payload, one-byte payload, multiple messages in one buffer, one message split across every possible byte boundary, many frames in sequence, compression flag preservation/rejection, length exactly at configured max, length over max, u32 max length, truncated header, truncated body, and panic-free malformed bytes. Fuzz/e2e script coverage must log frame count, split pattern, declared length, actual length, compression flag, decode state, allocation guard decision, error kind, output message ordering, and final preservation/no-overflow verdict. Validation: rch exec -- cargo check --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml if a fuzz target changes plus targeted rch cargo test/check for grpc codec/prost framing surfaces.

title: Database client audit: stale prepared handle after reconnect, streaming params never Describe, commit Ok on a rolled-back block, pool shrink livelock, client_encoding, statement_timeout cache, MySQL midnight DATETIME, and more
description:
A read-only audit of src/database (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, pool, transaction helpers) on origin/main 101f469e5 found the defects below. None was in an existing bead. Line numbers are from 101f469e5.

## Being fixed now (SapphireHill, round 5)

1. HIGH (postgres.rs reconnect_idle 4056-4113, query_prepared/execute_prepared 6937-6953 and 7032-7048): after a transparent reconnect an old prepared-statement handle can run a different statement. The fresh session restarted statement numbering at 0, and handles were re-prepared only when the reconnect happened inside the same call. Handles A (s0) and B (s1); the server drops the idle connection; query_prepared(B) reconnects and re-prepares B as s0; query_prepared(A) then binds s0 and runs B's SQL with A's parameters. Fix: carry next_stmt_id over the reconnect and stamp each PgStatement with a session generation; a handle from an earlier session is prepared again before use.
2. HIGH (postgres.rs query_stream_params 1340-1422, PgRowStream::next 1213-1219): the stream sent Parse/Bind/Execute/Sync with no Describe. Execute never sends RowDescription, so every row-returning streaming query failed with "DataRow before RowDescription". Its only test checked the frames written, not rows read. Also, an ErrorResponse returned without reading to ReadyForQuery, leaving the connection closed. Fix: Describe the portal; on ErrorResponse drain to ReadyForQuery before returning the error.
4. MEDIUM-HIGH (postgres.rs PgTransaction::commit 9201-9235): in a failed transaction block (status 'E') PostgreSQL answers COMMIT with the tag ROLLBACK and no error, so commit() returned Ok while nothing was saved (caller swallowed a unique violation, committed, got Ok). Only with_pg_transaction checked requires_rollback_before_commit. Fix: commit() refuses the same way (PgError::Protocol "transaction must roll back before commit", as src/database/transaction.rs:228 does); Drop rolls back. This changes a v0.4.3 observable result (Ok -> Err) only for a commit the server did not perform.
5. MEDIUM (pool.rs set_max_size 2077-2083, acquire loops 2386-2421 and the client loop, wait_for_async_pool_turn): a front waiter woken for capacity that a shrink then took stays ready; wait_for_async_pool_turn returns at once, the acquire loop chooses Wait again, and it spins without yielding or timing out (deadline recomputed each pass). Fix: when the caller holds the turn but no capacity is left, clear its ready flag so the wait parks; set_max_size wakes the front waiter so a raised cap is used at once.
6. MEDIUM (postgres.rs send_startup 4578-4604): the startup message never set client_encoding=UTF8 (tokio-postgres always does). Rows are decoded as UTF-8, so a LATIN1 database (or a role with client_encoding set) stored "cafe" with a mangled e-acute and failed to decode reads. Fix: send client_encoding=UTF8.
7. MEDIUM (postgres.rs apply_statement_timeout 5105-5145): a managed SET statement_timeout sent inside a transaction block is undone by ROLLBACK, but applied_statement_timeout_ms still said it was applied, so later queries sent no SET and ran with no server-side limit. Also, after a failed SET the cache was set to None, which also means "server default", so a following query that wanted the default sent nothing. Fix: a SET made inside a block marks the cache uncertain when the block ends (ReadyForQuery 'I'); a failed SET marks it uncertain; an uncertain cache always re-sends.
8. MEDIUM (mysql.rs parse_binary_datetime_value 4181-4223): the server sends a DATETIME/TIMESTAMP at 00:00:00 as 4 bytes; the len == 4 branch rendered a bare date ("2024-01-15"), unlike the text protocol. Fix: render "2024-01-15 00:00:00" for DATETIME/TIMESTAMP.
11. LOW (postgres.rs drain_to_ready 7998-8010): a NotificationResponse (or ParameterStatus/Notice) between an ErrorResponse and ReadyForQuery was skipped, contrary to the documented "notifications encountered during queries remain queued". Fix: route them through handle_async_backend_message.

## Not fixed yet

3. HIGH (postgres.rs 1807-1812, 4748-4786): SCRAM channel binding (tls-server-end-point) always hashes the server certificate with SHA-256. RFC 5929 section 4.1 and PostgreSQL's be_tls_get_certificate_hash use the certificate signature algorithm's hash (SHA-256 for MD5/SHA-1/SHA-256, else SHA-384/SHA-512). With a certificate signed ecdsa-with-SHA384 (Let's Encrypt E5-E9, RDS rds-ca-ecc384-g1) every TLS login that picks -PLUS fails with "channel binding check failed". Fix: pick the hash from the leaf's signatureAlgorithm OID. Test: an ecdsa-with-SHA384 fixture must give a 48-byte binding. tests/postgres_scram_channel_binding_audit.rs pins related behaviour; read it first.
9. MEDIUM (mysql.rs begin_with_isolation 4702 and 4772): both reads query @@SESSION.transaction_isolation, which raises ERR 1193 on MariaDB up to 11.0 and on MySQL before 5.7.20, although the rustdoc names MariaDB. Fix: on 1193 fall back to @@tx_isolation. Test: scripted server answers ERR 1193 to the first query.
10. LOW-MEDIUM (transaction.rs 242-286 and 758-801): the PostgreSQL and MySQL helpers never send ROLLBACK once the Cx is cancelled (rollback checks cancellation before writing), so on an unpooled long-lived connection the transaction and its locks stay open until the next operation. The SQLite helper already wraps its rollback in commit_section; do the same.
12. LOW, batched: an OID above 2^31 in text format fails i32 parsing and closes the connection (postgres.rs 7539); a MERGE n command tag reports 0 rows (6855-6875); CancelRequest re-resolves the host, so behind round-robin DNS it can reach another server (3093-3105, 3942; libpq reuses the connected address); DbPool::get_with_retry_for_client sleeps a blocking 100 ms before its first attempt (pool.rs 1251-1308); on MySQL an ERR packet mid result set discards a connection that is still in sync (mysql.rs 3791, 3855); a panicking disconnect leaks a pool slot.

## Checked and found sound
PostgreSQL framing/length caps, extended-query Sync/drain-on-error, fail-closed marking before each exchange, COPY IN/OUT state machines, stream ErrorResponse/ParameterStatus/Notice handling; SCRAM nonce/salt/iteration bounds, constant-time server signature check, AuthenticationOk-without-challenge refusal, MD5/cleartext refusal, NUL-poisoned builders; LISTEN quoting, savepoint names, pool release_check routing; MySQL packet split/reassembly, lenenc and NULL bitmap bounds, sequence ids; SQLite binding/decoding and rollback after a failed COMMIT.
close_reason: All ten audit items landed in 418335067 (74130ae52, 956b06afe, 55aa4cdbb, 60e38ca64); receipts on the LANDED comment. The with_pg/mysql_transaction body-signature note stays recorded above for the owner.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SapphireHill 10-03, new finding while fixing item 4 (not fixed; API decision):
- with_pg_transaction and with_mysql_transaction take `F: FnOnce(&mut PgTransaction<'_>, &Cx) -> Fut` with `Fut` a single type that does not depend on the borrow's lifetime. The body's future therefore cannot hold the `&mut` transaction across an await, so it cannot run a query on it. The helpers can only wrap bodies that ignore the transaction. The SQLite helper is shaped correctly: `for<'a> FnOnce(&'a SqliteTransaction<'_>, &'a Cx) -> SqliteTxFuture<'a, T>` (a boxed future carrying the lifetime).
- Fixing it changes a public signature (v0.4.3 gate). The additive route is a second, correctly shaped helper, for example `with_pg_transaction_boxed` with the SQLite bound, keeping the old one.
- Related: PgTransaction::requires_rollback_before_commit counts needs_discard, which every session-changing statement sets (SET LOCAL, ...). The helpers would therefore refuse a commit after such a statement. That is unreachable today, because of the signature above. The commit() fix in round 5 checks only needs_rollback || status 'E'.

title: ATP SSH bootstrap: keep generated RQ keys out of process arguments
description:
When SSH bootstrap auto-generates or forwards an RQ authentication key, the key is placed in local and remote process argument vectors. Other same-host users or process telemetry can expose it.

Replace argv transport with a protected stdin, inherited descriptor, or short-lived mode-0600 secret channel that is never logged. Zero or drop secret buffers promptly, define remote cleanup behavior, and add tests proving the key is absent from argv, command logs, and error output while bootstrap still succeeds.

title: DbPool sync Drop unhealthy path double-decrements client quota
description: src/database/pool.rs PooledConnection (sync) Drop (~1742-1798): decrements the per-client quota INLINE (:1749-1754), then on the !release_check (unhealthy) branch calls safe_discard_connection(conn, client_id) which ALSO decrements client_connections internally (:1612-1615). When a client holds >1 connection (entry not removed by the inline decrement to 0), the unhealthy-drop path decrements TWICE — over-counting the release, which can let the client exceed max_connections_per_client or prematurely drop the entry. The healthy path (return_connection) does not decrement, so it is correct (1 inline). The async Drop uses safe_disconnect (which does NOT decrement) so it is correct (1 inline). FIX: make the sync unhealthy branch not double-count — either have Drop NOT inline-decrement and rely solely on safe_discard_connection's decrement (matching how the now-fixed sync discard() calls safe_discard_connection directly = 1 decrement), or pass a flag so safe_discard_connection skips its decrement when the caller already did it. Found while fixing the return_to_pool/discard quota leak (committed); this is the inverse (over-decrement) error in the Drop-unhealthy path.

title: [qpack] src/http/h3_native.rs: dynamic decode ignores Required Insert Count/base semantics
description:
Review of commit b833b816 found a correctness bug in dynamic QPACK decoding. `qpack_decode_field_section()` now accepts dynamic references, but it only parses `required_insert_count` and `delta_base` for bounds checking and never uses them to resolve dynamic indices. The decoded `DynamicIndex(index)` / `DynamicNameLiteral { name_index, ... }` are later resolved by `qpack_dynamic_entry()` / `qpack_dynamic_name()` as if the wire index were a raw absolute index into the table. Under RFC 9204, dynamic references are relative to the field-section base / Required Insert Count, so the current code can silently resolve the wrong entry instead of enforcing blocked-stream availability or base-relative addressing.

Evidence:
- `qpack_decode_field_section()` parses `required_insert_count` and `delta_base` at src/http/h3_native.rs:889-922 but does not thread them into the emitted plan.
- Dynamic indexed/name-ref lines at src/http/h3_native.rs:947-982 emit only the raw wire index.
- `qpack_plan_to_header_fields()` resolves that raw number via `qpack_dynamic_entry()` / `qpack_dynamic_name()` at src/http/h3_native.rs:1046-1058, which operate on absolute table indices.

Fix direction:
- encode the effective base/relative addressing into the plan or resolve during decode with access to the current QPACK context
- reject references whose Required Insert Count exceeds available insertions rather than misresolving them
- add tests covering non-zero Required Insert Count and base-relative dynamic lookups
close_reason: QPACK base-relative indexing fixed - dynamic indices now correctly resolved per RFC 9204

title: Migration planner: derive Cx, region, and capability-flow plan
description:
## What
Layer a semantic migration planner on top of the inventory rows. It should identify async entry points, spawn sites, timer/sleep/retry loops, channel/sync primitives, request boundaries, and ambient authority patterns, then propose where `&Cx`, `Scope`, region ownership, cancellation checkpoints, and capability narrowing belong.

## Why
The biggest migration mistake is treating Asupersync as an executor swap. The value comes from explicit `Cx`, owned regions, cancel-correct effects, and capability security. The planner should steer users toward those semantics before code churn starts.

## Implementation guidance
- Consume the inventory schema from the first task rather than rescanning independently.
- Classify source patterns into `cx_threading_required`, `region_ownership_required`, `cancel_checkpoint_required`, `capability_narrowing_required`, `compat_boundary_ok`, and `manual_design_required`.
- Include rationale and confidence for each recommendation.

title: Deadline monitor can stall runtime drop for the full scan interval
description: RuntimeBuilder deadline monitoring accepts any check_interval, and the monitor thread uses uninterruptible std::thread::sleep(interval). RuntimeInner::drop sets only an atomic stop flag then joins the sleeping thread before scheduler/worker shutdown, so a 60-second interval can stall runtime destruction for almost 60 seconds and extreme durations effectively hang; Duration::ZERO creates a scan/lock busy loop. Replace the sleep/atomic pair with an interruptible Condvar wait_timeout or channel recv_timeout, notify before join, reject or normalize zero intervals, and add deterministic long-interval prompt-drop plus zero-boundary regressions.

title: Dep-plan Phase 1: Rev-5 foundations — safety, marginal ledger, oracle, capability, and verification gates
description:
PHASE 1 of the Dependency Sovereignty Program (parent asupersync-ir2uf0). REV-4 FOUNDATIONS. This phase blocks every later implementation and cutover.

WHY REV-4 EXPANDS THE FOUNDATION: the three implementation-unsafety classes remain useful, but they are not a complete risk model. A parser can be 100% safe Rust and still be security-critical; a DER parser is not BOUNDARY-UNSAFE merely because it parses hostile bytes. Likewise, a marginal package count is meaningless unless it is attached to a feature profile, target triple, host triple, dependency edge kind, and a reproducible counterfactual. Differential oracles also need policy: a pure-Rust dev oracle can be useful, while a native/C oracle can defeat the very C-eviction goal, and FrankenSQLite cannot be inserted as an asupersync dev-dependency because the downstream engine already depends on asupersync.

CHILD GATES:
1. Two-axis taxonomy: implementation-unsafety class plus orthogonal review-sensitivity tags, with a complete planned-replacement inventory.
2. Cargo-built Rust marginal-ledger generator: feature-profile × target/host measurements, explicit edge-removal counterfactuals, normalized upstream identities, and honest native-code evidence.
3. Differential-oracle policy: pure-Rust retention, native/C quarantine, reverse-dependency harness placement, expiry, and retirement.
4. Foundation signoff: cross-check the three artifacts, freeze the baseline, and publish the exact regeneration/retirement commands.

EXECUTION RULE: no Phase 2-9 implementation, migration, or dependency cutover may start before the Phase-1 signoff closes. Source investigations and owner ADRs may be read-only, but no implementation bead may claim readiness from an epic parent alone; the blocking edges are attached to executable leaves.

CONTEXT SNAPSHOT (historical baseline, to be regenerated rather than trusted): post-Phase-0 commit a86bfb3a6 reported 121 external names / 130 crate-versions in the default consumer and native C/asm through ring, bundled SQLite, bundled librdkafka, psm/stacker, and selected verification lanes. title: Two-axis dependency safety taxonomy + contract: implementation unsafety AND security/review sensitivity
description:
Part of Dependency Sovereignty Program asupersync-ir2uf0, Phase 1. Preserve GreenCove's live claim. Create the machine-readable taxonomy every replacement must cite.

CORE CORRECTION: implementation unsafety and review sensitivity are orthogonal axes. A strict safe-Rust DER/protobuf/DEFLATE parser is SAFE-OWN and may simultaneously be SECURITY-SENSITIVE-PARSER; it is not BOUNDARY-UNSAFE. BOUNDARY-UNSAFE is reserved for actual unsafe at OS/FFI or CPU-dispatch boundaries.

AXIS A — IMPLEMENTATION UNSAFETY:
1. SAFE-OWN: first-party code clean under #![forbid(unsafe_code)]. Default eligibility.
2. BOUNDARY-UNSAFE: narrow ledgered unsafe at OS/FFI/ABI or target-feature dispatch boundaries. Eligible only with the repository unsafe-ledger contract, narrowest allow scope, category evidence, proof note, and owner-approved justification.
3. ALGORITHMIC-UNSAFE: unsafe encoding ownership, initialization, pinning, weak-memory, parking, or liveness arguments. Prohibited by default. Exception requires a measured incumbent defect, a benchmarked safe alternative that failed the agreed gate, a concrete proof/audit plan, and verbatim owner signoff. Loom, Miri, and soak tests are useful evidence but do not prove liveness, linearizability, or weak-memory correctness.

AXIS B — REVIEW-SENSITIVITY TAGS, MULTI-VALUED:
ordinary; public-api-redesign; persistent-format; wire-format-parser; security-sensitive-parser; cryptographic-format; concurrency-liveness; platform-boundary; runtime-hot-path. The artifact must define required evidence for each tag. Examples: X.509 residue = SAFE-OWN + security-sensitive-parser + wire-format-parser; protobuf decoder = SAFE-OWN + wire-format-parser + security-sensitive-parser; nkey codec = SAFE-OWN + cryptographic-format + security-sensitive-parser; signal/xattr shims = BOUNDARY-UNSAFE + platform-boundary; safe mutex queue prototype = SAFE-OWN + concurrency-liveness + runtime-hot-path.

COMPLETE ROW INVENTORY: include every OWN or evidence-gated candidate in this program, not a hand-picked subset: time/chrono formatting, future adapters including panic catching and public Stream migration, visibility macro, slab, hex, base64 including padded URL_SAFE, ATP version scanner, NKey, protobuf, typed-symbol/snapshot/trace formats, JSON migrations, CLI parser, OTLP, redaction matcher, parking wrapper, safe queue prototype, signal/sysinfo/xattr, X.509 residue, LZ4, DEFLATE, CachePadded experiment, and polling/socket2 decision rows. KEEP rows may be present to explain why work is prohibited.

DELIVERABLES: artifacts/dependency_safety_taxonomy_v1.json; tests/dependency_safety_taxonomy_contract.rs; docs/dependency_safety_taxonomy.md. The contract fails if a planned OWN/evidence-gated bead lacks a row, if a parser is classified BOUNDARY-UNSAFE without actual unsafe, if an algorithmic-unsafe row is eligible without the complete exception receipt, or if required sensitivity evidence is absent.

NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY: this artifact classifies proposed replacements and review obligations. It does not prove implementation correctness, erase existing unsafe-ledger obligations, or authorize an evidence-gated candidate.

title: Cargo-built marginal ledger: feature-profile × target/host graph, explicit counterfactuals, active-native evidence
description:
Part of Dependency Sovereignty Program asupersync-ir2uf0, Phase 1. Build the program's reproducible marginal-cost ledger. This bead depends on the taxonomy because ledger rows cite both taxonomy axes.

NON-NEGOTIABLE IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINT: the repository is Cargo-only. The generator must be a Cargo-built Rust tool using std plus already-approved workspace dependencies; do not add a Python, pnpm, npm, shell, or other package-manager implementation. A small dedicated Rust binary is appropriate genuinely new tooling.

MEASUREMENT KEY: every result is keyed by (feature_profile, target_triple, host_triple, dependency_edge_kind, direct_root_edge). Platform-only rows are insufficient. Canonical profiles must include at least minimal/no-default, default, and each relevant production or quarantine profile that activates a direct dependency: tls, sqlite, kafka, metrics, cli, compression, trace-compression, io-uring, loom-tests, fuzz quarantine, and a full workspace/dev-build audit profile. The artifact records the exact feature vector, not a nickname alone.

GRAPH MODEL:
- Synthesize an out-of-workspace Cargo consumer for each profile.
- Traverse cargo metadata PACKAGE IDs, excluding only the synthetic root and explicitly identified first-party path packages.
- Distinguish target normal/build edges from host build-script/proc-macro edges; cross builds execute host code even when target cfg excludes runtime code.
- Report unique package names, package versions, source identities, build scripts, proc macros, unsafe class, and edge reachability.
- Record direct dependencies that are absent in a profile rather than silently omitting them.

COUNTERFACTUAL METHOD: marginal(root edge R) is computed by generating a second valid consumer/manifest configuration with exactly R's direct edge or activating feature atom removed, rerunning Cargo resolution, and diffing reachable package IDs. Never simulate a removal by deleting R from an already-resolved graph. Store the baseline manifest hash, counterfactual manifest hash, Cargo/rustc versions, target/host, and exact command.

UPSTREAM TRUST IDENTITY: normalize repository/source identity deterministically: canonicalize registry source/checksum, git URL+immutable rev, and package repository URL after scheme/.git/case normalization. Missing repository metadata must resolve to a fail-closed source-derived identity or explicit unknown:<package-id>; never merge unrelated missing repositories.

NATIVE EVIDENCE: Cargo.lock proves resolution, not native compilation. Each native_code row carries status active, declared-inactive, or unknown plus evidence sources: enabled feature path, build.rs inspection, target cfg, and where practical a captured build transcript or emitted-link evidence. Signal-hook's inactive cc declaration and rdkafka's active configure/make path are regression fixtures. Unknown is not reported as safe.

DELIVERABLES: Cargo-built Rust generator; artifacts/dependency_marginal_ledger_v1.json; tests/dependency_marginal_ledger_contract.rs; documented regeneration command. The artifact contains per-phase forecasts as generated data, never hand-entered targets.

ACCEPTANCE: all direct dependency edges appear for all applicable profiles; host/target and edge-kind fields are non-null; a deliberate feature-profile change alters only expected rows; known checks such as memchr default marginal 0 and prost/nkeys ranges are treated as drift-detection ranges, not eternal magic constants; no Python or non-Cargo generator is introduced.

title: Differential-oracle policy: pure-Rust retention, native/C quarantine, cycle-safe placement, expiry
description:
Part of Dependency Sovereignty Program asupersync-ir2uf0, Phase 1. Resolve the program-wide contradiction between differential testing and dependency sovereignty before any replacement lands.

POLICY CLASSES:
1. PURE_RUST_IN_WORKSPACE_ORACLE: may remain a dev-dependency only when it adds no prohibited runtime, native, or build surface; feature unification cannot contaminate production profiles; retention has an owner, introduction release, mandatory retirement release no later than two releases later, and a frozen fixture alternative.
2. NATIVE_OR_C_ORACLE: forbidden from the asupersync workspace release/dev/build graph after the production cutover unless the owner grants a narrow exception. Prefer immutable golden vectors, pre-cutover transcripts, or an explicitly quarantined external Cargo harness that is not built by normal check/test/release lanes. This applies to rdkafka/librdkafka and rusqlite/libsqlite3-sys; sqlparser's psm/stacker path is treated as native exposure too.
3. REVERSE_DEPENDENCY_ORACLE: must live in the downstream project or a neutral synthesized consumer. A project that already depends on asupersync cannot be added back as an asupersync dev-dependency; Cargo would form a package cycle. FrankenSQLite parity belongs in FrankenSQLite or a neutral consumer depending on both engines.
4. SECURITY_PROTOCOL_ORACLE: differential libraries may be used only in quarantined tests/fuzzing with explicit corpus provenance, strict secret redaction, and an expiry or permanent-KEEP justification.

REQUIRED REGISTRY FIELDS: replaced dependency/package IDs; oracle class; normal/dev/build/fuzz lane; native/unsafe status; allowed profiles; harness location; fixture source and license; introduction release; expiry release/date; retirement bead; owner; feature-unification check; no-claim boundary.

EXAMPLES THAT MUST BE ENCODED: nkeys, prost, bincode/rmp, regex, hex/base64, time/chrono are candidates for bounded pure-Rust oracle retention; rdkafka and rusqlite are native/C quarantine cases; FrankenSQLite is reverse-dependency placement; x509-parser is a security-parser oracle whose retention must not silently keep the entire production TLS graph.

DELIVERABLES: artifacts/dependency_oracle_policy_v1.json; tests/dependency_oracle_policy_contract.rs; short operator docs. The contract rejects an oracle without a retirement disposition, a native oracle in a normal workspace profile, a reverse-dependency cycle, and an expired oracle with no explicit extension signoff.

NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY: differential agreement is evidence, not proof that both implementations are correct. Native quarantine removes the oracle from ordinary build/release machines; it does not certify the external harness.
acceptance_criteria: Done only when: every replacement oracle has a class, graph lane, harness location, native status, owner, expiry, and retirement bead; native/C oracles are absent from ordinary workspace release/dev/build profiles; reverse-dependency placement is cycle-safe; expired oracles fail the contract; focused RCH tests pass with nonzero tests.
close_reason: Delivered governed oracle registry, operator policy, and 22-test fail-closed contract; focused RCH proof green.

title: Capability-preservation registry and no-loss cutover gate [P1]
description:
PHASE-1 CAPABILITY-PRESERVATION EPIC. Dependency removal is never allowed to make the system smaller by deleting, narrowing, hiding, relocating without an equivalent user path, or silently degrading a capability. This epic creates the authoritative inventory and gate for every current feature flag, public API family, CLI command and option, accepted config/scenario format, wire protocol, authentication mode, persistent artifact, platform behavior, operator diagnostic, and documented user workflow touched by this program.

Each capability receives a stable ID, current owner and source locations, supported profiles/platforms, observable behavior, error and resource contract, downstream consumers, baseline fixtures, and the exact replacement bead. A candidate may cut over only when every affected row is SAME or BETTER with evidence. If parity is unavailable, the incumbent dependency remains and the work closes with a KEEP receipt. API redesign is allowed only when the new path preserves capability and usability; permanent compatibility shims are not required, but versioned data readers or explicit reversible migrators are real product functionality and may be required.

The child DAG inventories capability and UX, captures baselines and downstream consumers, defines migration/rollback policy, then signs off the no-loss contract. This gate is additive to safety, marginal cost, and performance: a smaller graph does not compensate for lost behavior.

Every current feature, API, format, protocol, platform behavior, diagnostic, and user workflow is assigned a terminal SAME, BETTER, KEEP, or explicitly BLOCKED verdict with evidence. No capability-removal option remains in the dependency program. The Phase-1 aggregate signoff depends on this epic final signoff.

title: CAP A3: migration, rollback, coexistence, and KEEP policy for zero feature loss
description:
Define the universal cutover policy consumed by every dependency bead. A replacement must map all affected capability IDs; preserve or improve supported behavior, ergonomics, diagnostics, security, cancellation and resource bounds; provide reversible rollout or dual-read and shadow comparison where state or wire formats are involved; and retain the incumbent when evidence is incomplete. Dependency removal and capability removal are separate decisions, and only the first is in scope.

Specify valid terminal verdicts: REPLACE when every row is SAME or BETTER and all gates pass; KEEP when the dependency is the best safe way to preserve capability; DEFER when hardware, platform, upstream or owner evidence is missing, with no partial production switch; BLOCKED for an unresolved required choice. A downstream move such as FrankenSQLite counts only if an official, tested, documented and no-worse user path exists before the old path changes. Define versioned readers or migrators for persisted data without creating permanent deprecated API shims. Rollback must name revision boundaries, artifact compatibility, and how to restore the incumbent without data loss.
acceptance_criteria: Policy contract tests reject a cutover with an unmapped capability, worse or UNKNOWN row, missing downstream consumer proof, missing migration or rollback for stateful formats, silent unsupported platform, or unresolved regression. KEEP and DEFER are first-class successful outcomes with no partial production switch. User documentation, examples, errors, discoverability and operational recovery are explicit gates, not post-cutover cleanup.

title: ADR: preserve generic SerdeCodec JSON + MessagePack + Bincode while versioning owned artifacts

DECISION ONLY. The current public SerdeCodec is generic over arbitrary Serialize and DeserializeOwned values and SerializationFormat exposes MessagePack, Bincode, JSON and Custom. Decide how to version project-owned typed-symbol, snapshot and trace artifacts without narrowing the generic public formats. A format dependency may leave only after synthesized arbitrary-type consumers, persisted corpus, malformed corpus and migration readers all pass. KEEP is correct if the marginal benefit does not justify reimplementing a complete serializer/deserializer.

The ADR must freeze exact byte versus semantic compatibility, unknown-field/version behavior, canonicalization, bounds, data migration, public error types, custom codec extension, downstream consumer story, unit/property/fuzz matrix, E2E artifact replay and rollback.

title: ADR: preserve SQLite feature and one-stop user experience under cycle-safe FrankenSQLite integration

So replacing chrono is not a formatting change, it is a migration that must PARSE an existing on-disk corpus, and it is semver-breaking whenever cli or benchmark-adapters is enabled. TWO FINDINGS MAKE IT MORE TRACTABLE THAN IT LOOKS. First, the repository ALREADY OWNS two chrono-free RFC3339 formatters -- one at second precision built on a civil-from-days conversion in src/atp/logging/mod.rs, one at nanosecond precision with correct pre-epoch handling via euclidean division in src/messaging/jetstream.rs. They are duplicated logic in two unrelated modules and are the natural seed for the owned type; consolidating them is Phase-2-sized work that stands on its own. Second, the owned type is GENUINELY NEW, not a rename: types::Time is nanoseconds and serde-derived but its wall-clock accessor is PROCESS-EPOCH relative and it deliberately carries no calendar semantics because it exists for scheduling and virtual time; conflating it with a UNIX-epoch instant would either corrupt scheduling or produce wrong timestamps. What is owned today: monotone/virtual/logical time, the timer wheel, the injectable clock seam, RFC3339 EMISSION. What is not: calendar arithmetic, RFC3339 PARSING, and a serde-stable UTC instant type -- exactly what chrono supplies. Nine gaps TIM-GAP-01..09. Biggest: NO round-trip test for any chrono field and NO test at all for the three persisted index stores, while the registry promises round-trip compatible persisted values; and no byte-level golden for any chrono-serde document, with the CLI golden SCRUBBING timestamps so it is format-blind. Also recorded: chrono is a test-only differential oracle for PostgreSQL binary temporal decoding, so the dev-dependency must OUTLIVE the production one. Registry defect filed on asupersync-dvgpji: source_owners names src/time/mod.rs, and every file under src/time/ has ZERO chrono and ZERO time-crate references -- matched on the WORD 'time', the same failure mode as the encoding::/decoding:: selector. PLAN TENSION RESOLVED: three documents disagreed (time=REMOVE/Phase2, chrono=OWN/Phase5, and an audit line saying consolidate both in Phase 2); the registry binds both to one capability whose no-claim boundary says a nanos-to-RFC3339 helper cannot justify removing either. PROOF: 13/13 PASS on vmi1149989. BLOCKED: clippy per asupersync-yjwqba. No source under src/ changed.

title: ADR: preserve full user-supplied regex semantics and privacy guarantees; fixed scanners are only a fast path

Require adversarial privacy corpus, differential/property/fuzz evidence and downstream custom-pattern E2E with secret-redacted logs.

title: ADR: preserve arbitrary downstream Protobuf messages and ergonomic authoring; finite internal schemas are insufficient
description:
DECISION ONLY. ProstCodec<T,U> is a public generic codec for arbitrary downstream-defined prost::Message types. Replacing it with a finite hand-written message set would remove functionality and is forbidden. The ADR must preserve the ability to define new protobuf messages, encode and decode every currently supported scalar, repeated, packed, map, enum, oneof, nested and unknown-field behavior needed by public users, and use the generic codec in unary and streaming gRPC.

Choose among: KEEP prost as the public authoring and codec boundary while owning only finite internal OTLP messages; build an owned ProtoMessage trait plus production-quality derive or code-generation and migration tooling that is at least as usable; or a staged coexistence where prost remains until the full downstream surface passes. Manual trait implementation alone is not equivalent ergonomics unless the owner explicitly finds it better after consumer trials. Production prost exits only after arbitrary downstream consumer compile/runtime fixtures, cross-language Protobuf and gRPC interoperability, malformed/resource tests, fuzzing and rollback pass.
acceptance_criteria: ADR preserves arbitrary downstream message authoring and generic codec use, not only the in-repo message set. It inventories the accepted Protobuf language and prost attribute surface, public errors, unknown fields, deterministic encoding promises and size limits. KEEP is mandatory until a full ergonomic replacement and cross-language E2E prove SAME or BETTER capability. Phase-5 protobuf children and cutover are updated accordingly.

title: ADR: additive canonical JSON while preserving accepted TOML config and YAML scenarios
description:

comments.text: COMPLETED 2026-07-24 by SapphireHill. DEP-ADR-008 resolved: capability posture PRESERVE_AND_REPLACE_IF_PARITY / BLOCKED_PENDING_EVIDENCE for CAP-FUTURES-STREAMS; dependency_exit_allowed=false. THE CLASSIFICATION THE BEAD DEMANDED TURNS A SCARY NUMBER INTO A PRECISE ONE: of ~796 references across 148 files under src/, essentially all are inside cfg(test) modules. The PRODUCTION SET IS 6 SITES IN 5 FILES: src/net/atp/sdk/stream.rs (impl futures_lite::Stream for AtpWriter and AtpReader), src/web/middleware.rs and src/web/negotiate.rs (FutureExt::catch_unwind panic containment), src/web/router.rs (block_on inside the PUBLIC SYNCHRONOUS Router::handle), and src/signal/shutdown.rs (block_on x2 driving signal-listener threads outside any runtime), plus 2 doc-comment examples on public Notify. THE SHAPE DECIDES IT: exactly ONE is a public trait impl -- AtpWriter/AtpReader implement the FOREIGN futures_lite::Stream, publicly reachable with no feature gate, semver-relevant, and the ONLY impl of that trait anywhere in the crate. Everything else in net/io/stream uses asupersync's OWN Stream trait, a complete 33-file implementation with ~30 combinators and ZERO futures-lite dependency. The two traits are structurally identical and completely disjoint -- no adapter, no blanket impl, no conversion -- so the ATP SDK types are the sole outlier and the only reason futures-lite is in the public API at all. THE PLAN'S FRAMING DOES NOT SURVIVE: it lists futures-lite as a Phase-2 low-risk leaf removal over 'genuinely parallel, disjoint files' with a util/future.rs shim covering block_on/poll_fn/zip/race/yield_now. But the capability is public-api exposed, cutover is BLOCKED_PENDING_EVIDENCE, total churn is ~272 files incl. tests, and the shim list omits poll_once, join_all, pending, FutureExt::catch_unwind and Stream -- the last two are not free functions a helper module can supply. The bead's own description also misses router.rs and shutdown.rs, which are the highest-risk sites. Seven gaps FUT-GAP-01..07, notably: registry source_owners names src/stream/mod.rs (1 futures-lite ref, in a test module) and src/io/stream_adapters.rs (ZERO), i.e. exactly the part with NO replacement risk, while every production site and src/stream/stream.rs where the trait is defined are absent; the public ecosystem Stream impls have NO TEST (poll_next never invoked); and the downstream consumer fixture proves only the OWNED trait so it would not detect a removal breaking them. Also: registry claims features [default, test-internals] but futures-lite is unconditional with no gate; and the manifest comment says 'used by web handler adapter shims' which covers 2 of 6 sites. PROOF: 13/13 PASS on vmi1149989. BLOCKED: clippy per asupersync-yjwqba. No source under src/ changed.

title: ADR: preserve complete Kafka producer, transaction, consumer-group, security, and interop capability
description:
DECISION ONLY. Kafka is a substantial public integration, not a removable feature discovered to have few downstream users. Freeze all current producer and consumer APIs, configuration and behavior: metadata and broker routing; RecordBatch and headers; acks, retries, ordering and idempotence; transactions, epochs and sequence recovery; fetch, isolation and backpressure; group discovery, join, sync, cooperative or eager rebalance, heartbeat and leave; offset fetch, commit, seek and restart; compression; TLS and every configured SASL mechanism; cancellation, timeout, shutdown and stable errors.

The no-loss decision is: keep the kafka feature and rdkafka until a native safe Rust client proves all affected capability rows against real brokers and downstream consumers. No-consumer inventory does not authorize removal. The ADR sets supported broker/protocol versions, public API evolution, native-client boundaries, security policy, resource limits, diagnostics, migration/coexistence, shadow or differential mode and rollback. If a full native campaign is not justified, KEEP is the terminal optimal result.
acceptance_criteria: Every Kafka public API and operational capability has an ID, baseline and supported broker/security matrix. The ADR prohibits removing the kafka feature as a substitute for dependency replacement. It defines unit/protocol/property/fuzz, real multi-version broker E2E with detailed redacted logs, downstream consumer fixtures, performance/resource gates and rollback. Native cutover is conditional on SAME or BETTER rows; otherwise rdkafka remains.

comments.text:
DEP-ADR-009 RESOLVED (SapphireHill 2026-07-24). KEEP_UNTIL_PARITY / KEEP_INCUMBENT for CAP-KAFKA.

Headline: the public API is ALREADY completely rdkafka-free. Every producer/consumer/transaction/config/security/error type is first-party; the upstream error is imported under an alias and mapped into a hand-rolled taxonomy (no From impl); the context type that would leak an associated type is private. rdkafka is a swappable backend behind a facade we own.

Plan supersede: §5 rdkafka row + §9.3 said REMOVE the feature after a downstream inventory. Registry says KEEP_UNTIL_PARITY, no-claim boundary 'a wire codec or simple producer is not a Kafka client'. Registry governs. The gating inventory has never been run. Removal would also delete the owned fail-closed lane: modules are NOT feature-gated, so types compile on every build and a no-feature production call returns a typed FeatureDisabled error + diagnostic.

Two frozen capability gaps that bound what parity means: NO send_offsets_to_transaction (no read-process-write EOS; registry's 'transactional atomicity' covers producer side only), and NO admin surface at all (0 hits for AdminClient/NewTopic/create_topic).

Compression is softer than the enum: default-features=false and no compression shim crates resolve, so codec availability is decided by bundled librdkafka's ./configure autodetection ON THE BUILD HOST, not by any Cargo feature. Native build is configure+make, NOT cmake (lockfile-verified: no cmake crate resolves).

8 gaps frozen (KFK-GAP-01..08). Contract: 13/13 green.

title: NKey N7.1: opaque transcript signing provider for downstream consumers
description:
Current asupersync HEAD f9e3e7f04d390e12dbeeb206ede959f42a860ddb has the crypto primitive and downstream migration work separately owned, but no additive foundation-owned generic signing seam. `IdentityKeyStore::active_key_pair` still returns external `nkeys::KeyPair` (`src/security/keys/mod.rs`), and ATP's `CapabilitySigner`/`CapabilityVerifier` directly use nkeys behind a capability-specific transcript (`src/atp/policy/verification.rs`). A downstream that must authenticate a different canonical transcript therefore either imports nkeys, abuses the ATP-specific surface, or duplicates crypto policy.

Implement the smallest additive bridge after N5.1: reuse its audited owned Ed25519 operations rather than introducing another primitive. Expose opaque asupersync-owned public verification-key/signature/profile types plus IdentityKeyStore signing and public-key verification over exact caller-supplied domain-separated bytes. Bind key generation/fingerprint and rotation state explicitly; fail closed on unknown profiles, malformed inputs, revoked/retired generations, and key/domain/message substitution. Keep secret material non-serializable and redacted.

This child belongs under N7 because its product is a stable downstream API and migration proof. Preserve the current v0.4.3 `active_key_pair` behavior additively; do not remove or rename it in this tranche. The existing ATP capability authority remains transcript-specific and may only be routed through the shared primitive if behavior, serialized signatures, and errors remain compatible.

Immediate consumer: FrankenGraphDB bead `fgdb-asupersync-signing-provider-dj4j` needs to sign and verify its canonical identity transcript without a direct nkeys dependency. That consumer does not transfer ownership of key wrapping, HSM/threshold policy, durable graph-object key lifecycle, or database recovery to this task.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The public seam uses only asupersync-owned stable profile/version, public verification-key, fingerprint, and signature types; downstream source and public signatures do not name or require nkeys. 2. IdentityKeyStore signs exact caller-supplied canonical/domain-separated bytes without returning an external key type, and verification works from an asupersync-owned public key with typed unknown-profile, malformed-key/signature, wrong-key/domain/message, revoked/retired-generation, and signing failures. 3. Independent vectors and positive round trips cover empty, boundary, and large transcripts; planted negatives cover altered message/domain/signature/key, rotation overlap, retirement/revocation, and all unsupported profile values. 4. Debug, Display, errors, fixtures, and retained artifacts expose no seed/private bytes; signature/public-key encodings and rotation semantics are versioned and canonical. 5. Existing ATP capability signing and the v0.4.3 active_key_pair surface remain behavior-compatible; any internal routing through the shared authority is proved by exact regression tests. 6. A real FrankenGraphDB downstream compile/run fixture signs and verifies its canonical identity transcript without adding nkeys, while API-map and migration documentation show no capability loss. No claim is made for HSM/threshold signing, KMS policy, or FrankenGraphDB durable key lifecycle.

title: Kafka K15: performance, graph, no-loss signoff and conditional rdkafka/librdkafka cutover
description: Aggregate the explicit K2.5, K3.5, K4.7, K5.5, K6.5, K7.5, K8.6, K9, K10.5, K11.4, K12.5, K13.6 and K14.5 terminal evidence through the K14.5 chain, plus Phase-1 capability/verification gates. Benchmark throughput, p50/p95/p999, CPU, allocations/RSS, connections/partitions, compile time and binary size on named available Apple Silicon and high-core-count AMD/Intel hosts across representative producer, transaction and consumer workloads. Compute production/default/sparse dependency and native-code deltas. Remove rdkafka/librdkafka only if every capability is SAME/BETTER, security/resource/performance and downstream gates are accepted, oracle retirement is complete and rollback is proven; otherwise KEEP.
acceptance_criteria: Row-level signoff links raw unit/model/property/fuzz, real broker/downstream E2E, security, graph/native, benchmark, oracle and rollback evidence. Hardware results include distributions, workload/config, warmup, host/topology/toolchain/revisions; missing cells are no-claims. Feature/API/config/protocol/compression/security/platform behavior remains intact. Manifest/lock/ledger cutover is serialized last, followed by sparse/default/all-target and canonical E2E proof with validated detailed logs/replay. UNKNOWN or regression yields KEEP/DEFER, which is successful.

title: [fresh-eyes] raptorq/decision_contract: contract-error fallback returns CONTINUE not FALLBACK + reason not registered
description:
src/raptorq/decision_contract.rs:240-254 — When evaluate() returns Err (e.g. ActionIndexOutOfRange), the early-return GovernanceTelemetry sets:

  chosen_action: action_label(action::CONTINUE),                  // line 246 — CONTINUE = 0 = 'Continue the currently selected optimized path' (most aggressive)
  deterministic_fallback_triggered: true,                          // line 249
  deterministic_fallback_reason: "contract_action_out_of_range",  // line 250

Two defects:

(1) FAIL-OPEN ON CONTRACT ERROR: action::CONTINUE (=0) is the most-aggressive 'continue optimized path' action. The conservative action defined in the same module is action::FALLBACK (=3). Comment at line 234-239 claims it falls back to a 'BALANCED action' — but no such constant exists; the action set is {CONTINUE=0, CANARY_HOLD=1, MIXED_GUARDRAIL=2, FALLBACK=3}. Downstream safety gates that key on chosen_action == "fallback" when deterministic_fallback_triggered=true would NOT engage on contract evaluation error, contradicting fail-closed defaults.

(2) CANONICAL-REASON INVARIANT BROKEN: The string "contract_action_out_of_range" is NOT in G7_RUNTIME_FALLBACK_REASONS (lines 34-39 — only POLICY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, UNKNOWN_LOW_CONFIDENCE, REGRESSION_LOW_CONFIDENCE, UNCLASSIFIED). is_runtime_fallback_reason("contract_action_out_of_range") returns false (line 427). Test surfaces / golden snapshots / replay validators that filter by canonical reasons silently drop these decisions; observability gap for legitimate runtime fallback events. Test at line 1512 references G7_RUNTIME_FALLBACK_REASONS as the source of truth.

Fix:
  Line 246: chosen_action: action_label(action::FALLBACK)
  Line 250: deterministic_fallback_reason: FALLBACK_REASON_UNCLASSIFIED  (or add new const FALLBACK_REASON_CONTRACT_ERROR and register in G7_RUNTIME_FALLBACK_REASONS)
  Lines 234-239: replace 'BALANCED action' comment with accurate description ('conservative FALLBACK action').

Add regression test pinning: when evaluate returns Err, telemetry.chosen_action == 'fallback' AND is_runtime_fallback_reason(telemetry.deterministic_fallback_reason).

Comment updated (BALANCED action doesn't exist; conservative action is FALLBACK=3). Regression test dezwpc_contract_error_fallback_uses_canonical_action_and_reason pins action_label(FALLBACK)=='fallback' AND is_runtime_fallback_reason(FALLBACK_REASON_UNCLASSIFIED)==true AND the previously-buggy unregistered string remains rejected. 37 lib tests pass; cargo clippy --lib -D warnings clean. title: [deadlock-audit] CrashController emits evidence while holding controller state lock
description:
File: src/channel/crash.rs:269-283, 292-320
Supporting context: src/evidence_sink.rs:30-35, 90-101

Finding:
CrashController::crash() and CrashController::restart() hold self.state while calling emit_crash_evidence(), which immediately calls EvidenceSink::emit().

Concurrency story:
EvidenceSink is an arbitrary synchronous trait object. The in-tree JsonlSink implementation takes its own mutex and flushes to disk on every emit; a custom sink can also synchronously inspect or mutate crash/controller state. Calling that trait hook while self.state is locked creates a callback-under-lock reentrancy hazard: if the sink path re-enters crash()/restart() or blocks on any code waiting for the controller mutex, the thread deadlocks. Even without reentrancy, the controller critical section now includes unbounded I/O latency.

Why this matters:
Crash/restart is supposed to be a fast control-plane state transition. Holding the controller lock across sink I/O makes that state machine vulnerable to priority inversion and deadlock from instrumentation.

Expected fix shape:
Capture the evidence payload inputs (action/count/timestamp) into locals, release self.state, then emit evidence afterward. Add a regression test with a sink that re-enters controller methods or blocks on another mutex.
close_reason: Already fixed in 15da98895: CrashController drops state lock before evidence emission and includes probe regression coverage
