title: [durable-rch][submit] Implement detached proof submission lifecycle
description:
## Goal
Implement the durable submission lifecycle that turns a manifest proof lane into a detached RCH job record. Submitting a lane should allocate a stable proof-submission id, persist command/source expectations before execution, and survive the submitting agent disconnecting.

## Requirements
- Define lifecycle states such as queued, running, terminal_pass, terminal_fail, terminal_canceled, terminal_stale, and terminal_infra_error.
- Preserve RCH remote-required semantics; local fallback must be recorded as a refusal, not proof.
- Persist enough state for another agent to resume observation without knowing the original terminal session.
- Include lease/ownership rules so duplicate submissions for the same lane+HEAD are either coalesced safely or rejected with a structured reason.
- Never mutate source files or tracker state from the runner except for explicit receipt artifacts chosen by the implementation bead.

## Validation
Add deterministic unit tests for state transitions, duplicate submission policy, detach/reconnect behavior, and fail-closed local-fallback classification. Closeout must include the focused RCH proof command used.

Persist identity, command, source, rch_provenance, outcome, and claim_boundaries before detach where possible, and fail closed if the manifest lane, required command prefix, main branch, remote-required and no-local-fallback policy, or duplicate lane plus HEAD lease cannot be proven. title: [durable-rch][capture] Persist terminal output and stale/cancel classification
description:
## Goal
Capture a durable terminal receipt from each detached proof submission, including enough output and metadata to distinguish pass, compile/test failure, timeout, client disconnect, operator cancellation, RCH stale-progress detection, worker infrastructure failure, and local-fallback refusal.

## Requirements
- Store bounded first-blocker output and output digests without committing giant logs.
- Preserve worker id, remote location, timing, exit code, cancellation metadata, detector stale fields, and command envelope.
- Classify client-disconnect separately from proof failure and separately from operator cancellation.
- Make partial receipts explicit; a partial receipt can explain what happened but cannot satisfy a green proof claim.
- Include redaction rules for coordination or environment values that should not be copied into committed artifacts.

## Validation
Add golden fixtures for pass, cargo failure, stale-progress cancellation, heartbeat-stale infra failure, client disconnect before terminal status, local fallback, and oversized-output redaction. Tests must assert exact refusal reasons and first-blocker extraction.

First-blocker extraction should populate outcome.first_blocker_lines and outcome.output_digest while bounding log size. Redaction tests should prove command/env output cannot leak secrets, but must preserve command_fingerprint, env_fingerprint, worker_id, detector_progress_stale, detector_heartbeat_stale, cancellation_reason, and staleness_reason. Partial or client-disconnected receipts may explain state but must set citable false and refusal reasons.

title: [durable-rch][cli] Add submit/status/query/cancel UX for proof jobs
description:
## Goal
Expose an agent-friendly command surface for durable proof jobs. Operators should be able to submit a manifest lane, get a stable id, query status, fetch the terminal receipt, and request cancellation without relying on the original attached terminal session.

## Requirements
- Commands must produce deterministic JSON suitable for agents and concise human output suitable for closeouts.
- Status output must show lifecycle state, source HEAD, manifest lane, worker/progress metadata, and whether the receipt is citable.
- Query output must include machine-readable refusal reasons when the receipt cannot back a claim.
- Cancellation must be explicit and recorded as cancellation evidence; it must not be confused with a failing proof.
- UX must include examples for the exact RCH remote-required proof pattern used in AGENTS.md.

## Validation
Add CLI contract tests/goldens for submit, status while running, terminal pass, terminal fail, stale/canceled, unknown id, and unsupported broad claim. Include detailed logs around refusal reasons so agents can act without reading implementation code.

## Goal

title: [smallvec-spill] transport/router.rs DispatchResult SmallVec<[_;4]> spills on broadcasts to 5+ endpoints — silent perf regression
description:
src/transport/router.rs:1442,1445,1749-1750,1799-1800,1852-1853 — DispatchResult tracks succeeded/failed endpoints via SmallVec<[EndpointId; 4]> and SmallVec<[(EndpointId, DispatchError); 4]>. The inline capacity 4 is below typical cluster fan-out; broadcast/multicast/quorum to 5+ endpoints silently spills to the heap.

Why this is a perf regression: SmallVec's value-add is avoiding heap allocation in the common case. With capacity 4 and a typical k8s service of 10-50 pods, EVERY broadcast spills, defeating the optimization. The intent of using SmallVec here was 'usually inline, occasionally heap'; the actual behaviour is 'always heap, with a useless 4-slot inline buffer wasting 32+ bytes of stack per DispatchResult'.

Concrete cost:
  - Every spill is a small Vec heap allocation (24-byte header + N×24-byte entries for the failure tuple type).
  - A high-fan-out service emitting 1k broadcasts/sec to 50 endpoints = 50k entries × 1k = 50M allocations/sec for failure tracking alone.
  - Tail-latency p99 spike when allocator slowpath fires.

This is MEDIUM not HIGH because it's a perf-only regression, not a correctness bug, and the 'always heap' behaviour is at least bounded (linear in fan-out, no memory leak).

Fix direction:
  1. Increase the SmallVec inline capacity to 16 or 32 — typical cluster fan-out fits inside.
  2. Or: replace SmallVec with Vec entirely and accept the heap allocation as the standard case (removes the misleading optimization signal).
  3. Or: add a const generic to DispatchResult that lets callers tune the inline capacity per use-site.
  4. Microbench broadcast to 1, 4, 16, 64 endpoints and verify the p99 alloc count matches expectation.

Severity MEDIUM (perf regression, not correctness).

Source: /multi-pass-bug-hunting on src/transport/* deepest pass (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Fixed: DispatchResult SmallVec inline capacity 4 → 16 (commit c26ee7fb5)

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
AUDIT at origin 21f947faf (SapphireHill, source-read). Status of the 5 sub-defects:
1. Single admission slot / 96 s head-of-line DoS: FIXED by 153ef77ac (2026-09-22). pending_authenticated_accept is a VecDeque, queue_accept_output round-robins, and managed_accept_round_robin_skips_silent_and_credit_blocked_peers plus managed_accept_concurrent_capacity_and_cid_ownership_include_unread_receipts are green (q7lib/p7test).
2. Coalesced 1-RTT tail dropped: FIXED by 302e1d2da (retained in early; tests green).
3. Flight retransmits reuse packet numbers: STILL PRESENT. PendingAuthenticatedAccept::retransmit (managed_endpoint.rs ~155) re-queues last_flight.iter().cloned(), the byte-identical encrypted packets. RFC 9000 section 12.3 forbids packet-number reuse, and a client that already got the flight discards the duplicates, so a lost client ACK is never re-elicited. The fix needs the driver to re-emit the CRYPTO frames under fresh packet numbers (302e1d2da did this for the final ACK only).
4. Send-error classification: STILL PRESENT, two ways. (a) managed_endpoint.rs ~1999-2031 treats InvalidInput as a DESTINATION error, but endpoint.rs ~575-600 also raises InvalidInput for LOCAL faults ('packet size N exceeds endpoint limit', 'empty managed send batch'). One oversized packet we produce retires every connection to that peer address, e.g. all clients behind one NAT. (b) Every unlisted kind returns Err(UdpEndpoint) and ENDS THE WHOLE MANAGED LOOP. ENOBUFS (std has no specific kind for it) is transient kernel backpressure under UDP load, so one burst kills every connection on the endpoint.
5. sent_packets keeps ACK-only entries unbounded: PARTIALLY fixed by the GH#71 change. Loss detection forgets ACK-only entries behind the largest acknowledged packet, but a pure receiver that only emits ACK-only packets never gets anything acknowledged, so its deque grows without bound for the life of a long download, and each later ACK walks it twice. Needs a cap on non-in-flight entries, or a periodic ack-eliciting PING (RFC 9000 section 13.2.4).
Also listed in the first comment and still unaudited: streams.rs fragment accounting; connection.rs PATH_RESPONSE validation; legacy plaintext anti-amplification credit.
Proposed split: 3, 4a/4b and 5 as separate beads. 4b (ENOBUFS ends the loop) has the highest impact.

title: Capability registry source_owners wrong on >=4 rows; root cause = api_surface selectors match module-name words (encoding::/decoding:: -> CAP-SERDE-GENERIC)
description: artifacts/dependency_capability_registry_v1.json records source_owners for CAP-CONFIG-TOML-JSON as ["src/config.rs", "src/bin/asupersync.rs"]. Verified 2026-07-24 against the live tree: src/config.rs makes ZERO 'toml::' calls (its parse_config hand-splits lines on '=' with [section] headers, lowercases section names and strips '#'/'//' comments — an INI-style parser accepting a narrower, different grammar with different error semantics), and src/bin/asupersync.rs contains zero 'toml::' calls at all. The actual toml-crate owners are src/runtime/env_config.rs (the only runtime-config parse site: parse_toml_str, parse_toml_file, apply_toml_config, RuntimeTomlConfig/SchedulerToml/BlockingToml), src/runtime/builder.rs (RuntimeBuilder::from_toml, from_toml_str), src/cli/atp_config.rs (AtpInstallConfig and AtpConfigManager read AND write TOML), src/bin/atpd.rs (AtpdConfig), and src/bin/dependency_marginal_ledger.rs. IMPACT: any baseline, inventory or cutover work that trusts these rows will inventory the wrong files and miss the entire runtime and CLI TOML surface, including the write-back round-trip that is operator-visible. The api_surface_snapshot selector 'config-reexports' has the same defect: it maps name_prefix 'config::' to CAP-CONFIG-TOML-JSON, i.e. to the INI parser rather than to the TOML surface. Found while resolving DEP-ADR-004 (asupersync-dep-p3-api-adrs-h3jspm.4) and recorded there as CFG-GAP-01; the ADR explicitly does not certify these registry rows. FIX: correct source_owners and the api-surface selector; note the registry contract test asserts only that each source_owners path EXISTS, not that it implements the capability, so consider strengthening that check.
close_reason: 17 source_owners rows corrected against per-crate evidence; dependency_owners de-invented (base32/crc16/tls); encoding::/decoding:: selector root cause fixed; 3 enforcement tests added (resolution, attribution, stale-exemption ratchet); registry contract 25/25 and all downstream lanes green. Follow-up asupersync-pc5lbe filed for the codec API-map gap.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: SECOND INSTANCE OF THE SAME DEFECT CLASS, found 2026-07-24 while resolving DEP-ADR-002 (asupersync-dep-p3-api-adrs-h3jspm.2). CAP-PROTOBUF-GENERIC.source_owners = ["src/grpc/mod.rs", "src/encoding.rs"]. src/encoding.rs is the RaptorQ FEC encoding pipeline (EncodingPipeline, EncodedSymbol, EncodingStats, repair-symbol generation) and contains ZERO occurrences of prost or protobuf, verified by grep against the live tree. Worse, the file that actually owns the capability -- src/grpc/protobuf.rs, home of the generic pub struct ProstCodec<T,U> and ProtobufError -- is NOT named in the row at all. So the row simultaneously names an unrelated file and omits the real one. Recorded as PB-GAP-01 in DEP-ADR-002. Combined with the CAP-CONFIG-TOML-JSON defect already described here, this is now 2 of the spot-checked capability rows with wrong source_owners, which suggests the field was populated by inference rather than from the source. Recommend auditing all 50 rows. The structural fix remains the same: the registry contract asserts only that each source_owners path EXISTS, never that it implements the capability; a check such as 'at least one source_owners file must reference one of the row's dependency_owners' would have caught both instances cheaply.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED + TWO MORE ROWS, 2026-07-24 while resolving DEP-ADR-001. The defect is now 4 confirmed rows, and it is mechanical rather than random. CAP-SERDE-GENERIC.source_owners = [src/encoding.rs, src/decoding.rs]: both are RaptorQ erasure-coding pipelines with ZERO serde/serde_json/rmp_serde/bincode tokens, and the real owner src/types/typed_symbol.rs (SerdeCodec, SerializationFormat, TypedSymbol, TypeRegistry) is not named. CAP-PERSISTED-TRACE-SNAPSHOT.source_owners names src/trace/mod.rs, a pure pub-mod/pub-use facade with zero serialization code; the real owners are src/trace/{file,replay,crashpack,event,compat,streaming,integrity}.rs, and neither src/lab/snapshot_restore.rs nor src/distributed/snapshot.rs (the only production bincode user outside typed_symbol.rs) is named anywhere. CAP-TRACE-LZ4.source_owners has the identical facade error: it names src/trace/mod.rs while every trace-side lz4 call is in src/trace/file.rs. ROOT CAUSE: api_surface_snapshot.selectors contains exactly two selectors mapping to CAP-SERDE-GENERIC -- 'encoding-reexports' with name_prefix 'encoding::' and 'decoding-reexports' with name_prefix 'decoding::'. Someone pattern-matched the WORDS encoding and decoding to serialization, while the 'types::' prefix, where the codec actually lives, is mapped to CAP-PUBLIC-API-TOPOLOGY. That is why one unrelated FEC module is currently credited with two serialization capabilities. Second-order damage: artifacts/api_surface_map_v1.json contains ZERO codec symbols (no SerdeCodec, SerializationFormat, Serializer, Deserializer, TypedSymbol, TypedEncoder, TypedDecoder or TypeRegistry), so the entire public generic codec surface is invisible to the API drift-detection contract; the encoding::/decoding:: entries it does carry are all RaptorQ types. Also stale in the same family: artifacts/dependency_safety_taxonomy_v1.json still asserts that the SerdeCodec ADR names the removal of arbitrary Serialize and the Bincode/MessagePack variants, which now contradicts DEP-ADR-001 and the registry's own KEEP_UNTIL_PARITY disposition. RECOMMENDED FIXES: (1) audit all 50 source_owners rows against source, treating any entry ending in mod.rs as suspect; (2) correct the two api_surface_snapshot selectors; (3) add the codec symbols to api_surface_map_v1.json; (4) amend the safety taxonomy's removal framing; (5) strengthen the registry contract so a source_owners file must reference at least one of the row's dependency_owners -- that single check would have caught all four rows.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: SCOPE WIDENED AGAIN 2026-07-24 (DEP-ADR-005): the defect is NOT confined to auto-generated rows. All four CAP-CLI-* rows are wrong, and these were the HAND-CURATED ones -- the registry doc explicitly says CLI coverage is 'deliberately fail-closed while CLI A1 is pending' with all parser sources pinned by sha256 and line count. Four of the eight source_owners entries across those rows do not own the code they are credited with: (1) src/cli/mod.rs -- grep -c clap = 0, a pure module-declaration and re-export file with no parser, option, help text or exit path; named as co-owner of CAP-CLI-ASUPERSYNC. (2) src/cli/signal.rs -- grep -c clap = 0, and decisively atpd does NOT use it at all: src/bin/atpd.rs implements its own install_signal_listener() against signal_hook::consts::signal and raw libc::kill, while SignalHandler/CancellationToken in src/cli/signal.rs have zero references from any binary; named as co-owner of CAP-CLI-ATPD. (3) Cargo.toml -- the manifest, not source; named as co-owner of CAP-CLI-OFFLINE-TUNER. (4) src/cli/atp_command_tree.rs -- clap-dense so a naive grep passes, but it is imported by NO [[bin]]: consumers are only src/cli/atp_config.rs, src/cli/atp_workflows.rs and the src/cli/mod.rs re-export, so its 22 commands (config, ci, dataset, fuzz, release, archive, ...) are unreachable and untypable; named as co-owner of CAP-CLI-ATP. Meanwhile src/cli/args.rs (CommonArgs, COMMON_ARGS_HELP -- the ONLY frozen help text in the repo -- and parse_color_choice) and src/cli/output.rs (the entire ColorChoice/OutputFormat precedence contract) are source_owners of NOTHING. ADDITIONAL INCONSISTENCIES IN THE SAME BLOCK: the hash-pinned snapshot list and the source_owners lists disagree (args.rs is pinned but owns nothing; mod.rs and signal.rs own but are not pinned); the two hidden atp commands are recorded WITHOUT their real '__' prefix so the recorded names are not what a user types; the environment_variables list pins exactly 10 while the CLI reads at least 9 more (CI, SHELL, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, APPDATA, USERPROFILE, HOMEDRIVE, HOMEPATH, ASUPERSYNC_ATP_WORKFLOW_ROOT, RUST_LOG via env_logger::Env::default) and the count assertion only passes because it checks names against the 7 hash-pinned sources, which exclude output.rs/first_run.rs/completion.rs where several of those reads live; CAP-CLI-OFFLINE-TUNER claims feature benchmark-adapters which is not in the binary's required-features; CAP-CLI-ATP claims tls-native-roots while atp-cli pulls tls + dep:rustls-native-certs directly; and docs/dependency_capability_registry.md says 14 binaries while the artifact and its own test say 15. RECOMMENDATION UNCHANGED but now higher priority: audit all 50 rows against source. The proposed structural check (a source_owners file must reference at least one of the row's dependency_owners) would have caught mod.rs, signal.rs and Cargo.toml here; catching atp_command_tree.rs additionally needs a reachability check from [[bin]] roots.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: WIDENED AGAIN 2026-07-24 (DEP-ADR-007, DEP-ADR-011). Running total: wrong or materially incomplete source_owners on rows for CAP-CONFIG-TOML-JSON, CAP-PROTOBUF-GENERIC, CAP-SERDE-GENERIC, CAP-PERSISTED-TRACE-SNAPSHOT, CAP-TRACE-LZ4, all four CAP-CLI-*, CAP-FUTURES-STREAMS, CAP-HTTP-COMPRESSION, CAP-NKEY-AUTH and CAP-TIME-UTC-RFC3339. NEW THIS ROUND. (1) CAP-TIME-UTC-RFC3339 names src/time/mod.rs and src/bin/asupersync.rs. EVERY file under src/time/ has ZERO chrono and ZERO time-crate references -- it is asupersync's own async timer module (TimerWheel, VirtualClock, Sleep, Interval) and the registry appears to have matched on the WORD 'time', exactly like the encoding::/decoding:: selector defect. The row names NONE of the four files that actually own chrono: src/cli/atp_command_tree.rs (10 public serde-derived DateTime<Utc> fields), src/cli/atp_workflows.rs (calendar arithmetic + the three persisted JSON index stores), src/atp/benchmark/mod.rs and src/atp/benchmark/reports.rs. The row's own exposure field claims public-api and persisted-format, and the entire justification for BOTH lives in files it does not list. (2) CAP-NKEY-AUTH is different in kind -- its named owner src/messaging/nats.rs IS genuine, so this one is wrong by OMISSION rather than by phantom: five production files with real nkey code are missing, including src/security/keys/mod.rs which hosts the ONLY public nkeys leak (pub fn active_key_pair -> Result<nkeys::KeyPair, KeyStoreError>), plus src/runtime/config.rs, src/atp/identity/mod.rs, src/atp/policy/verification.rs and src/agent_swarm/control_plane.rs. Effect: the row makes the capability look NATS-shaped when it spans four independent subsystems, which is exactly the error plan 9.5 then inherited. (3) SEPARATE DEFECT CLASS in the same row: CAP-NKEY-AUTH.dependency_owners lists 'base32' and 'crc16' AS IF THEY WERE CRATES. The same list names ed25519-dalek as an owner although it is NOT a direct dependency, only transitive through nkeys. So dependency_owners needs auditing too, not just source_owners; an SBOM or marginal-cost calculation built from that field would reference crates that are not in the graph. RECOMMENDATION unchanged and now urgent: audit all 50 rows' source_owners AND dependency_owners against source and against Cargo.lock. The proposed structural check (a source_owners file must reference at least one of the row's dependency_owners) would have caught the time row instantly, and a second check (every dependency_owners entry must resolve to a package in Cargo.lock) would have caught base32/crc16.

comments.text:
Registry defect batch 4 of 4 — final 3 source_owners findings from the Phase-3 ADR sweep (SapphireHill 2026-07-24). Running total: 18 wrong/incomplete rows across 14 capabilities.

16. CAP-REGEX-PRIVACY.source_owners = [src/observability/mod.rs, Cargo.toml]. That file has ZERO occurrences of 'regex' — not even a comment; it only declares the gated otel module. The real owner src/observability/otel.rs (14 hits, the entire engine surface incl. the public regex::Error leak) is absent. Same facade failure mode as time/futures/cli.

17. CAP-KAFKA.source_owners = [src/messaging/kafka.rs, Cargo.toml]. Different failure mode from the others and worth distinguishing: both entries are GENUINE. The row is wrong by OMISSION — src/messaging/kafka_consumer.rs carries 16 rdkafka refs and its own distinct import set (BaseConsumer/CommitMode/Consumer, Offset, TopicPartitionList) that does not overlap kafka.rs's. A baseline from this row would cover the producer half and miss consumer groups, rebalancing, commits, seek and isolation entirely.

18. CAP-SQLITE.source_owners = [src/database/sqlite.rs, Cargo.toml] — CORRECT. Recording the negative result explicitly so the sample is not read as 'every row is broken'. rusqlite is correctly in dependency_owners, not source_owners.

So of 12 capabilities carrying ADRs, exactly one source_owners row was fully correct. The prefix-matching root cause I flagged earlier explains the rest: selectors map module-name WORDS (encoding::/decoding::/time::/regex-in-observability) rather than actual imports.

Both cheap structural checks I proposed still hold and would have caught 16 and 17:
(a) a source_owners file must reference at least one of the row's dependency_owners (catches #16: zero 'regex' in observability/mod.rs);
(b) every file importing a dependency_owner must appear in source_owners (catches #17: kafka_consumer.rs imports rdkafka but is unlisted).
Check (b) is the omission-direction dual of (a) and is the one this batch shows is needed — a row can be 100% genuine and still be half the surface.

comments.text:
MECHANICAL AUDIT OF ALL 50 ROWS — the hand-audit undercounted (SapphireHill 2026-07-25). Implemented both structural checks I proposed and ran them across the whole registry.

CHECK A (a source_owners file must reference one of the row's REAL crate dependency_owners; sentinels like workspace-owned/std:: excluded via Cargo.lock resolution): 16 TRUE DEFECTS of 47 checkable rows — 34%. Eleven are NEW, never found by hand:

  1. CAP-PUBLIC-API-TOPOLOGY   src/lib.rs                      (serde, thiserror)
  2. CAP-STRUCTURED-CONCURRENCY src/runtime/mod.rs, src/cx/mod.rs (parking_lot, crossbeam-queue, slab, smallvec, pin-project)
  3. CAP-HASH-MAPS            src/io/mod.rs   -> REAL: runtime/reactor/epoll.rs, runtime/scheduler/local_queue.rs (hashbrown, exactly 2 files)
  4. CAP-HOST-BENCH-METADATA  src/bin/offline_tuner.rs -> REAL: atp/benchmark/mod.rs (the ONLY file using num_cpus or whoami, 1 each); sysinfo: atp/logging/failure_bundle.rs, runtime/resource_monitor.rs, atp/daemon_control.rs
  5. CAP-TOKEN-SLAB           src/io/mod.rs, src/runtime/mod.rs -> REAL: service/rate_limit.rs, sync/waiter.rs, sync/semaphore.rs, time/wheel.rs (all 4 slab users)
  6. CAP-HEX-CODEC           src/encoding.rs (0 hex) -> hex is used in 50 files; top bin/atp.rs
  7. CAP-SIGNALS             src/signal/mod.rs (facade), src/cli/signal.rs -> REAL signal_hook users are exactly 3: bin/atpd.rs, signal/signal.rs, signal/kind.rs
  8. CAP-XATTR               src/fs/mod.rs, src/net/atp/mod.rs -> REAL: net/atp/transport_common/metadata.rs is the ONLY file in the tree using the xattr crate
  9. CAP-SYNC-LOCKS          src/sync/mod.rs, src/runtime/mod.rs -> parking_lot spans 172 files
 10. CAP-CONCURRENT-QUEUES   src/runtime/mod.rs, src/channel/mod.rs -> REAL: runtime/scheduler/global_queue.rs, blocking_pool.rs, epoch_tracking.rs, epoch_gc.rs
 11. CAP-QUIC-HTTP3-ATP      src/net/quic/mod.rs, src/net/atp/mod.rs (both facades)
 plus the 5 already known: CAP-SERDE-GENERIC, CAP-OTLP-ECOSYSTEM, CAP-REGEX-PRIVACY, CAP-HTTP-COMPRESSION, CAP-TRACE-LZ4.

SHARPEST NEW ONE — CAP-HTTP-COMPRESSION names src/web/compress.rs. That file EXISTS (33KB), which is why the current path_exists assertion passes, but it contains ZERO flate2/brotli/miniz_oxide tokens. The real owner is src/http/compress.rs (30 flate2 + 6 brotli). There are two same-named files and the registry names the wrong one. A path_exists check can never catch this class; check A catches it instantly.

CHECK C (every dependency_owner resolves to a Cargo.lock package): 16 non-resolving entries. Most are DELIBERATE sentinels and should be legitimised by declaring them — frankensqlite-reverse-dependency, regex-shaped-mock, workspace-owned, workspace-owned-e2e, service-images-and-binaries, tokio-test-quarantine, asupersync-published-api, librdkafka (bundled C), platform-intrinsics, repr-align, crossbeam-utils-cache-padded, std::*. But these are genuine errors: base32 and crc16 (CAP-NKEY-AUTH — do not exist, as reported), cargo and cargo-metadata (external tools, not deps), std (should be std::), tls (a FEATURE, not a crate).

PROPOSED FIX SHAPE: add an explicit allowed_non_crate_dependency_owners vocabulary to the registry, then enforce both checks in tests/dependency_capability_registry_contract.rs. That makes the sentinels pass by declaration while base32/crc16/tls/cargo fail closed, and it stops any new row from regressing. The 16 source_owners rows then get corrected against the derived owners above.

CAVEAT ON METHOD, so nobody over-trusts the derived lists: naive top-by-count is WRONG for multi-crate rows, because a ubiquitous crate swamps the distinguishing one — CAP-SIGNALS and CAP-XATTR both surface net/tcp/stream.rs purely because libc is in their dep lists and libc is everywhere. Every list above is derived per DISTINGUISHING crate (xattr, signal_hook, hashbrown, slab, lz4_flex, brotli, num_cpus, whoami), not per union. The genuinely cross-cutting rows (PUBLIC-API-TOPOLOGY, STRUCTURED-CONCURRENCY, SYNC-LOCKS at 172 files, SERDE-GENERIC, HEX-CODEC at 50 files, QUIC-HTTP3-ATP) cannot be reduced to a short honest file list at all and need a different kind of evidence pointer, not a longer array.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FIXED AND ENFORCED (SapphireHill 2026-07-25). 17 source_owners rows corrected, both structural checks implemented, root cause fixed. tests/dependency_capability_registry_contract.rs 25/25 green.

The check found MORE than my audit script did. Mine matched a bare word; the shipped check requires 'crate::' or 'use crate', which additionally caught three rows my looser regex let through: CAP-TOWER-COMPAT (src/service/mod.rs -> real owner src/service/service.rs, the ONLY tower file), CAP-POLLING-SOCKET (src/io/mod.rs + src/net/mod.rs -> the three reactors + net/tcp/socket.rs, stream.rs), and CAP-PROTOBUF-GENERIC (which I had documented by hand but my own script missed).

17 ROWS CORRECTED. Highlights: CAP-XATTR -> net/atp/transport_common/metadata.rs (the only file in the tree using the xattr crate). CAP-SIGNALS -> signal/signal.rs, signal/kind.rs, bin/atpd.rs (the only 3 signal_hook users; the old row named a facade plus cli/signal.rs, which has zero consumers). CAP-HOST-BENCH-METADATA -> atp/benchmark/mod.rs (the only file using num_cpus or whoami) + the 3 sysinfo users; the old row named bin/offline_tuner.rs, which uses none of them. CAP-HTTP-COMPRESSION -> src/http/compress.rs, not src/web/compress.rs. CAP-SERDE-GENERIC -> types/typed_symbol.rs + the trace serialization files + distributed/snapshot.rs. CAP-PROTOBUF-GENERIC -> grpc/protobuf.rs, grpc/codec.rs.

DEPENDENCY_OWNERS FIXED: CAP-NKEY-AUTH base32/crc16 removed (neither exists) -> nkeys, ed25519-dalek, ed25519, data-encoding, sha2. CAP-DATABASE-WIRE 'tls' removed: it is a Cargo FEATURE and was already correctly listed in that row's features array, so it was a pure category error. Verified rustls has ZERO occurrences under src/database/.

ROOT CAUSE FIXED: api_surface_snapshot selectors encoding-reexports and decoding-reexports now map to CAP-SIMD-RAPTORQ instead of CAP-SERDE-GENERIC. encoding:: re-exports EncodedSymbol/EncodingError/EncodingPipeline/EncodingStats, which are RaptorQ FEC types.

NEW FINDING while fixing that: I could NOT re-point the codec at the types:: selector, because SerdeCodec, SerializationFormat, TypedSymbol and TypeRegistry are NOT root-exported at all — 0 occurrences in src/lib.rs and 0 in artifacts/api_surface_map_v1.json. So the generic codec surface is reachable only as asupersync::types::typed_symbol::* and is invisible to API drift detection. That is the second-order damage ADR-001 predicted, now confirmed. It needs its own bead: adding those symbols to the API surface map is a public-API-map change, not a registry correction.

ENFORCEMENT (3 new tests, so the class cannot recur):
- every_dependency_owner_resolves_to_a_package_or_a_declared_non_crate_owner — every entry must resolve in Cargo.lock or appear in the new allowed_non_crate_dependency_owners vocabulary (20 declared sentinels, each with a reason: workspace-owned, librdkafka as bundled C, cargo/cargo-metadata as subprocess tools verified in dependency_marginal_ledger.rs, frankensqlite-reverse-dependency, regex-shaped-mock, std::*). base32/crc16/tls/cargo now fail closed.
- every_source_owner_row_attributes_to_its_dependency — the check itself.
- no_attribution_exemption_is_stale — an exemption that stops being needed must be removed, so the exemption list cannot become a hiding place.

5 DECLARED EXEMPTIONS, each with a written reason, for rows where no short file list would be true: CAP-PUBLIC-API-TOPOLOGY (serde/thiserror are derive-level across the whole API; its evidence is api_surface_map_v1.json), CAP-STRUCTURED-CONCURRENCY, CAP-HEX-CODEC (hex in 50 files), CAP-SYNC-LOCKS (parking_lot in 172 files; the intended boundary is the owned wrapper in plan 9.2), CAP-QUIC-HTTP3-ATP.

Also re-pinned the capability-registry sha256 in artifacts/dependency_phase1_aggregate_signoff_v1.json, which correctly caught the drift. Corrections only: no capability, disposition, evidence state or cutover state changed. Downstream lanes re-verified green: ADR registry 13/13, phase-3 signoff 14/14, phase-1 aggregate 8/8.

title: [database-deepest-4th] mysql/postgres: begin_with_isolation does not verify server applied the requested isolation level
description:
src/database/mysql.rs:2799-2814 begin_with_isolation: 'let set_sql = format!("SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL {level}"); match self.execute_unchecked(cx, &set_sql).await { Outcome::Ok(_) => {} ... } ... Outcome::Ok(MySqlTransaction { conn: self, finished: false, isolation_level: Some(level), read_only })'.

The OK response from the SET means the server parsed the command, NOT that the requested isolation level is in effect. Several MySQL/MariaDB configurations silently downgrade or ignore isolation requests:
  - MariaDB with binlog_format != ROW silently downgrades SERIALIZABLE on writes
  - Galera cluster ignores SERIALIZABLE / REPEATABLE_READ in some modes
  - MySQL replication replicas may pin to source isolation
  - innodb_isolation_level overrides session SET in some patches

After SET succeeds, the code unconditionally constructs MySqlTransaction { isolation_level: Some(level), ... } — the caller now BELIEVES they are at SERIALIZABLE while the server may be at READ_COMMITTED. Loss of write-conflict detection; lost-update + non-repeatable-read anomalies become possible.

Concrete repro:
  T0: caller invokes conn.begin_with_isolation(cx, IsolationLevel::Serializable, false).await
  T1: client sends 'SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE'
  T2: server returns OK (silently ignored)
  T3: client sends 'START TRANSACTION READ WRITE'
  T4: server returns OK
  T5: tx.isolation_level() returns Some(Serializable) — but the actual server transaction runs at READ_COMMITTED.

Why-not-mitigated:
  - prior 4th-pass fix yl4gu1 addressed tx-discard, NOT isolation verification
  - prior fix m6c35i addressed auth downgrade, not isolation downgrade
  - cvkoe9 prepared-statement LRU is unrelated
  - No SELECT @@tx_isolation (or @@transaction_isolation on MySQL 5.7.20+) follow-up read
  - No test in tests/database_e2e.rs or tests/conformance/ exercises begin_with_isolation against a server that silently downgrades

Same vulnerability shape exists in postgres.rs around line 3445 in PgConnection::begin_with_isolation, though Postgres is single-statement (BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL X) and far less likely to silently downgrade — Postgres servers reject unknown isolation tokens at parse time. MySQL is the higher-severity target.

Suggested fix: After execute_unchecked(SET TRANSACTION...) returns Ok AND before returning MySqlTransaction, issue 'SELECT @@SESSION.transaction_isolation' (MySQL 5.7.20+) or 'SELECT @@SESSION.tx_isolation' (older); parse the returned value; if it does not match the requested IsolationLevel, return Err(MySqlError::IsolationDowngraded { requested: level, actual: server_value }) and roll back the still-empty transaction. Same pattern for Postgres via 'SHOW transaction_isolation' (defensive even though Postgres is robust).
close_reason: begin_with_isolation now verifies server-applied isolation level on both MySQL and Postgres paths. Workflow: (1) issue SET / BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL X; (2) query @@SESSION.transaction_isolation (mysql) or SHOW transaction_isolation (postgres); (3) parse via new IsolationLevel::from_server_string helper (tolerates hyphen + space + lowercase forms, case-insensitive); (4) compare to requested level; (5) on mismatch, ROLLBACK and return MySqlError::IsolationLevelMismatch / PgError::IsolationLevelMismatch with {requested, observed} fields. 4 new unit tests cover from_server_string parsing across both backends + IsolationLevelMismatch Display surfacing requested/observed/bead trace. title: Lab scheduler RNG (LabConfig::rng) first draw is ~0 for every seed below 2^32; scrambling it would remap every lab schedule and golden - owner decision
description:
Found with asupersync-6g0qlk. LabConfig::rng() (src/lab/config.rs:435) is DetRng::new(self.seed): unscrambled xorshift64. Its first draw is near 0 for every seed below about 2^32: 2.5e-9 for seed 42, at most 1.5e-8 for seeds 0..255. Every small-seed run therefore makes the same first draw-based scheduling choice, a loss of exploration diversity at the first decision only. Later draws are well mixed.

Not fixed with 6g0qlk on purpose. Scrambling this seed would remap every lab schedule. That changes every pinned trace certificate, schedule hash and golden that depends on a seed (lab_scenario_runner_golden, demo checksums, replay artifacts recorded by older builds).

Options: (A) leave as is and document; (B) scramble behind a new opt-in; (C) scramble by default, with a planned golden refresh and a release note. Owner decision.
close_reason: Documented Option A: LabConfig::rng() preserves schedule stability, trace certificates, and golden hashes; ChaosRng applies SplitMix64 when unbiased small-seed exploration is required

title: [DX-CORE] Spawn mailbox: decouple spawn admission from the RuntimeState lock
description:
WHY (root architectural fix for the whole epic): Every spawn today must hold the global RuntimeState ContendedMutex while create_task runs (src/runtime/builder.rs:3986-4013 lock -> state.create_task -> store_spawned_task), and the public Scope::spawn signature leaks this by demanding `&mut RuntimeState` from the caller (src/cx/scope.rs:381,629,810). This single coupling causes: (a) the 56-line spawn-10-tasks on-ramp, (b) spawn throughput serialization under load, (c) the inability to offer Cx::spawn()/tokio-like ergonomics, (d) gen_server and web frameworks carrying RuntimeState internally as a workaround (gen_server.rs:1767).

WHAT: introduce a lock-free (or sharded-lock) SPAWN MAILBOX: spawn callers allocate a TaskId + JoinHandle optimistically and enqueue a SpawnRequest {region, budget, future, cx-derivation info} onto a per-worker or global MPSC injector WITHOUT touching RuntimeState. The scheduler performs ADMISSION (region liveness check, task-record insertion, region.add_task, obligation hookup) at dispatch time under the normal state lock it already holds. Region-closed-before-admission resolves the JoinHandle with Outcome::Cancelled(RegionClosed) — exactly the semantics of spawning into a closing region today, just observed later. This preserves every invariant: a task is never RUNNING without being region-owned; quiescence accounting includes mailbox entries (region close must drain its pending spawn requests — count them in the region's live-children accounting at enqueue time via an atomic per-region pending-spawn counter so close-waits-for-quiescence still holds).
design:
FILES: src/runtime/builder.rs (spawn paths ~3546-4058), src/runtime/state.rs (create_task), src/runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs (dispatch admission point), src/record/region.rs (pending-spawn counter in region accounting), src/cx/scope.rs (new internal path), new src/runtime/spawn_mailbox.rs.
SKETCH:
1. SpawnRequest struct: pre-allocated TaskId (from a sharded id allocator or reservation range per worker), erased future, region id, budget, name, completion slot (the JoinHandle's Arc).
2. Region gains AtomicU32 pending_spawns; enqueue increments, admission decrements. Region close treats pending_spawns>0 as live children (drain by admitting-then-cancelling or cancelling in place — choose admit-then-cancel so the cancellation PROTOCOL still runs and finalizers/obligations behave identically).
3. Admission failure modes are explicit: RegionClosed -> handle resolves Cancelled; QuotaExceeded -> handle resolves Err(SpawnError::quota) (see budget/spawnerror ergonomics bead).
4. Determinism: in lab mode the mailbox MUST preserve deterministic admission order (FIFO per seed; document the ordering rule and cover with replay tests). LabRuntime can keep using the direct synchronous path if simpler — but the PUBLIC semantics must be identical in both modes.
5. Keep the existing synchronous spawn path available internally for the lab kernel; mailbox is the production scheduler path.
acceptance_criteria:
1. New spawn path requires no caller-held RuntimeState borrow; existing Scope::spawn(state,...) keeps working during migration (removed in the Scope-v2 bead, not here).
2. Invariant proofs: lab tests demonstrating (a) region close with N un-admitted spawn requests still reaches quiescence with all N futures resolved Cancelled and zero task/obligation leaks (oracle-checked); (b) admission order deterministic across same-seed replays (fingerprint-identical traces).
3. Concurrency: loom or lab-explorer coverage of the enqueue/close race (spawn racing region-close must never lose a request silently).
4. Perf: spawn-throughput microbench (multi-thread spawners) added to benches/; must show >= baseline (target: measurable improvement under 8-thread contention; no-win documented if not).
5. Unit tests: happy path, region-closed, quota-exceeded, mailbox-full behavior (mailbox must be effectively unbounded or backpressure must be explicit and documented — silent drop forbidden).
6. Structured logging: spawn admission emits trace events (TaskSpawnEnqueued/TaskAdmitted) with task/region ids so e2e scripts can assert the full path; events visible in lab trace.
7. cargo check/clippy/fmt gates green; flamegraph artifact committed (scheduler-adjacent change, per Phase 6 gate).
notes: RISKS: quiescence accounting subtlety (pending_spawns counter must be incremented BEFORE the request becomes visible to the scheduler, and the close path must observe a consistent snapshot — document the ordering with an atomics proof note per Phase 6 proof-note gate). FALLBACK: config flag spawn_admission=direct|mailbox, default direct until the e2e + bench evidence is committed, then flip default in a separate commit for clean bisection. RELATION: unblocks Scope-v2 + Cx::spawn (child dep), feeds ShardedState completion in [SCHED-PERF]. This is the highest-leverage single change in the whole plan.

title: [DX-CORE] Macro diagnostics hardening — every macro misuse produces a teaching error
description:
WHY: recon evidence: spawn! inside a scope! block that lacks `state:` fails with an opaque 'cannot find value __state' (asupersync-macros/src/spawn.rs:17-18 hardcodes the hygiene-broken identifier), and spawn!'s positional argument parsing is ambiguous between name-string and scope expression (spawn.rs:81-124). Agents iterate on compiler output — every opaque macro error costs a full edit-compile loop.

WHAT: a diagnostics pass over the entire macro family (scope!, spawn!, join!, join_all!, race!, select!, the new attribute macros): (1) detect the known misuse patterns at expansion time and emit syn::Error with a fix-it style message ('spawn! requires a scope created by scope!(cx, state: <expr>, {..}) — add the state: parameter'); (2) resolve spawn!'s positional ambiguity by REDESIGNING the arg grammar to be keyword-explicit where ambiguity exists (no-compat policy permits: spawn!(name: "x", future) form); (3) ensure every macro's error spans point at the user's tokens, not macro internals; (4) after the v2 spawn migration most state-threading errors disappear — this bead covers what remains.

Error spans verified to highlight user tokens (trybuild output inspection). 3. spawn! grammar redesign documented in macro-dsl.md with before/after. 4. Zero regressions in existing macro expansion tests. 5. Error-message catalog module has a unit test preventing accidental wording drift (golden).

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
SapphireHill 2026-07-26: CLAIMED + DESIGN RECONNAISSANCE. No code written yet; recording the API findings first because they change the shape of the suite and they were not obvious from the bead text.

TREE STATE VERIFIED (not taken from prior comments): tests/api_v2_integration.rs does NOT exist -- this is greenfield. tests/common/ has coverage.rs, e2e_harness.rs, e2e_macros.rs but no mod.rs, so the "tests/common/mod.rs helpers" in the design section would be new. All four blockers (u1z5hn.1/.2/.5/.6) are genuinely CLOSED.

FINDING 1 -- THE REGION DIMENSION CANNOT USE THE Cx-ONLY HARNESS. There is no region-creating method on Cx: `grep 'pub async fn' src/cx/cx.rs` yields race/spawn families only, and the sole region entry point is `Scope::region(&mut state, &cx, policy, body)` (src/cx/scope.rs:557), which is state-threaded. So `run_async_under_lab(seed, |cx| ...)` -- the harness tests/join_set_cancel_drain_lab_proof.rs uses -- CANNOT create the child/grandchild cells. Those cells need a `RuntimeState` in hand. The runnable pattern is the one scope.rs's own inline tests use (src/cx/scope.rs, `region_closes_empty_child`):
    let mut state = RuntimeState::new();
    let cx = Cx::for_testing();
    let parent = state.create_root_region(Budget::INFINITE);
    let scope = Scope::<FailFast>::new(parent, Budget::INFINITE);
    block_on(scope.region(&mut state, &cx, FailFast, |child, state| async move { ... }))
Constructors are reachable from an integration test under --features test-internals: Cx::for_testing() (src/cx/cx.rs:4657) and Scope::new / new_with_capability_budget carry #[cfg_attr(feature = "test-internals", visibility::make(pub))] (src/cx/scope.rs:237,245). futures-lite is a normal [dependencies] entry (Cargo.toml:461), so `futures_lite::future::block_on` is linkable from tests/.

FINDING 2 -- THE THREE TIMING CELLS MAP ONTO RegionState, WHICH MAKES THEM ASSERTABLE. RegionState (src/record/region.rs:76) is Open -> Closing -> Draining -> Finalizing -> terminal, and the Closing doc comment says in as many words "No more spawns allowed". So the timing dimension is not vague:
  before close = RegionState::Open       -> spawn MUST succeed and the task MUST be owned by that region
  during close = Closing/Draining/Finalizing -> spawn MUST be rejected, SpawnError::RegionClosed(region)
  after close  = reclaimed               -> SpawnError::RegionClosed or RegionNotFound (the arena reclaims the record, per region_closes_empty_child asserting state.region(child_id).is_none())
Both variants exist on SpawnError (src/runtime/state.rs:1031-1033), so every rejection cell can assert an exact variant rather than just "is_err".

FINDING 3 -- THE OPEN DESIGN QUESTION, and the reason I am not guessing. Putting a region into Closing/Draining/Finalizing *deterministically and observably* is the crux of 6 of the 18 cells, and I did not find a public transition entry point: RuntimeState exposes region_was_closed / region_close_outcome / can_region_complete_close (state.rs:2667,2674,5973) but no request_close/begin_close. The realistic options are (a) drive a real close and catch the intermediate state from inside the region body or a finalizer, (b) use a test-internals transition helper if one exists on RegionRecord, or (c) assert the invariant at the admission seam instead of reconstructing the state. Choosing wrongly here produces a suite that looks authoritative while actually proving something weaker than "spawn cannot race region close", which is the whole point of the bead.

SCOPE HONESTY: AC1 alone (18 cells x oracle assertions) is the bulk. AC2 wants >=256 proptest cases with seed+repro in failure output, AC3 wants the suite wired into the standard lanes, AC4 wants a symbol-coverage checklist over every new public API symbol in the epic, AC5 wants zero flakes across 5 consecutive full runs. This is a multi-session deliverable, not a single sitting, and I would rather leave this reconnaissance for whoever continues than half-build a P0 safety proof for the spawn path.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
SapphireHill 2026-07-26: CORRECTION TO MY OWN PRIOR COMMENT — the design fork is resolved, no external decision needed.

My earlier note said "no public transition entry point" for reaching Closing/Draining/Finalizing deterministically, and that this blocked 6 of the 18 lifecycle cells. THAT WAS WRONG. My search was scoped to Cx and Scope; the transitions live on RegionRecord:

  src/record/region.rs:1088  pub fn begin_close(&self, reason: Option<CancelReason>) -> bool
  src/record/region.rs:1236  pub fn set_state(&self, state: RegionState)

Both are `pub`. A test that already holds a RuntimeState (which the region cells need anyway, per the earlier finding about Scope::region being state-threaded) can reach every phase of the enum.

HOW THE SUITE SHOULD USE THEM — this distinction is the whole point of the bead, so it is not a free choice:

- Use `begin_close(reason)` for the "spawn during close" cells. It is the REAL protocol transition — it is what the runtime itself drives, so a spawn rejected after it is genuine evidence that spawn cannot race region close.
- Use `set_state(...)` ONLY for phases not otherwise reachable in isolation (Draining/Finalizing with no children to wait on). It is a blunt setter that bypasses the protocol.

If every timing cell were built on `set_state`, the suite would assert against a hand-placed enum value rather than an actual close race. It would look authoritative while proving something strictly weaker than AC1 asks for. Prefer begin_close; reach for set_state only where reachability forces it, and say so in a comment at that cell.

Corroborating in-tree precedent that these are the intended levers:
  src/subsystem_mutation_testing.rs:5551  runtime_state.force_region_state(&region.id(), RegionState::Closing)
  src/lab/runtime.rs:5723                 region.set_state(RegionState::Closing)

title: [DX-CORE] Scope/Cx spawn API v2 — spawn without &mut RuntimeState; Cx::spawn for capability-holders
description:
WHY: With the spawn mailbox in place (dependency), the public API can finally drop the `&mut RuntimeState` parameter that recon identified as pain point #1. Target surface:
  scope.spawn(cx, |cx| async move { ... }) -> TaskHandle<T>       // region-scoped, structured
  cx.spawn(|cx| async move { ... }) -> Result<TaskHandle<T>, SpawnError>  // spawns into the Cx's CURRENT region (capability-gated by HasSpawn)
  scope.spawn_local(...), scope.spawn_blocking(...) same treatment.
Both routes keep: factory-receives-its-own-Cx (capability discipline), region ownership (no orphans), explicit Outcome semantics. The old state-threading signatures are REMOVED, not deprecated — AGENTS.md forbids compat shims and we have no users to break (per backwards-compatibility policy).

WHAT: rework src/cx/scope.rs spawn family to route through the spawn mailbox using a lightweight runtime handle held inside Cx (Cx already carries io/timer driver handles per task_context — add a SpawnHandle the same way; src/cx/scope.rs:1606-1632 shows the existing handle-plumbing pattern to follow). Add Cx::spawn gated on cap::HasSpawn. store_spawned_task ceremony disappears from user code entirely (absorbed by mailbox admission). Migrate ALL internal call sites (gen_server.rs, actor.rs, supervision.rs, web/, lab harnesses, examples — inventory the full call-site list with rg at migration start; expect on the order of a hundred sites across ~40 files) via parallel subagents with file reservations; no scripted rewrites per AGENTS.md.

[REVISED 2026-06-10: removed an unsupported '~112 call sites' figure from the first draft — the count must come from the migration-start inventory, not from planning estimates.]

title: [DX-CORE] JoinSet / TaskGroup — dynamic fan-out with structured collection
description:
WHY: recon gap #2 vs tokio: no dynamic-arity join. Fan-out N tasks and collect results is THE most common server pattern (per-request parallel calls, batch jobs), and today it requires hand-rolled Vec<TaskHandle> + sequential join loops. tokio::task::JoinSet is the ecosystem-expected name.

WHAT: asupersync::JoinSet<T> with the asupersync twist — it is region-aware and cancel-correct:
  let mut set = JoinSet::new(&scope);              // or JoinSet::in_cx(&cx)
  set.spawn(cx, |cx| async move { ... });           // any number, dynamically
  while let Some(out) = set.join_next(cx).await {}  // results as they complete, Outcome-typed
  set.join_all(cx).await -> Vec<Outcome<T,E>>       // ordered collection
  set.cancel_all(cx).await                          // protocol-cancellation of all members, DRAINED (not dropped)
  Drop of a non-empty JoinSet = cancellation request to members (region still guarantees no orphans — document that drop is request, region close is the quiescence backstop).
Aggregation honors the severity lattice (join_all returns the worst-severity summary alongside individual outcomes via a JoinSummary helper).
design: FILES: new src/combinator/join_set.rs (or src/cx/join_set.rs — decide by where Scope lives; combinator/ preferred for discoverability next to join.rs), re-export in prelude. Internals: members spawned through the v2 spawn path into the OWNING scope's region (no hidden child region by default — JoinSet is a collection helper, not a structure boundary; offer JoinSet::in_child_region(scope,...) for isolation when wanted, which DOES create a region so cancel_all=region cancel). join_next uses a shared completion queue (mpsc of (index, Outcome)) fed by a small wrapper future around each member — zero polling of non-ready members. Fairness: completion order = actual completion order (deterministic under lab).
acceptance_criteria:
1. API: new/in_cx/in_child_region, spawn, spawn_local, join_next, join_all, cancel_all, len/is_empty, abort-on-drop semantics documented + tested.
2. Cancel-correctness proof: cancel_all drives the full request->drain->finalize protocol on every member and join_next afterwards yields Cancelled outcomes — lab test with oracle checks, zero leaks.
3. Loser-drain equivalence test: JoinSet + cancel_all behaves identically to Scope::race loser handling for the cancelled subset.
4. Determinism: same-seed lab runs produce identical join_next orderings (replay fingerprint test).
5. Stress: 10_000-member fan-out completes without unbounded memory (completion queue bounded by member count); bench committed.
6. Doctests: fan-out-collect in <=15 lines on the type-level docs; example file examples/spawn_fanout.rs uses JoinSet as the blessed pattern.
7. Structured logging: members carry parent-set id in trace events for forensics.
notes: DEPENDS on scope-spawn-v2. DESIGN DECISION recorded: default JoinSet shares the caller's region (cheap, no extra quiescence point) vs in_child_region for isolation — both offered, default documented with reasoning (matches tokio mental model while keeping structure explicit). RELATION: prelude exports it; e2e bead exercises it under chaos.

Deviations recorded: no in_child_region constructor (design decision), no TaskGroup type (deferred to asupersync-ufdab2)

comments.text:
SapphireHill 2026-07-25: resumed my own month-dormant P0 claim (last touched 06-22). Landed the AC2/AC3/AC5 proof surface; found a real bug that blocks AC4.

STATE OF THE ACs on re-read:
- AC1 API: DONE (new/in_cx/spawn/spawn_local/join_next/try_join_next/join_all/cancel_all/cancel_all_with_reason/len/is_empty/summary + 17 inline tests).
- AC6 doctests/example: DONE (examples/spawn_fanout.rs, module docs).
- AC7 structured logging: ALREADY DONE and I nearly rebuilt it -- trace_member_spawn emits join_set_id/member_index/region/spawn_kind/active_members, with two inline tests asserting it. Marking it satisfied.
- AC2, AC3, AC5: DONE THIS SESSION in tests/join_set_cancel_drain_lab_proof.rs (5 passing).
- AC4 determinism: BLOCKED on asupersync-tncxj9 (new P1 bug, below). Test is committed #[ignore]d and is the acceptance test for that fix.

NEW P1 BUG asupersync-tncxj9 -- JoinSet::join_next is NOT wake-correct. Minimal repro: three members that complete IMMEDIATELY, drained via join_next under run_async_under_lab, never finishes (quiescent=false, steps_total=100000). The SAME set drained via join_all under the SAME harness returns cleanly with quiescent=true. Root cause: join_next builds a FRESH handle.join(cx) future inside poll_fn on every poll, polls it once, and drops it on Pending; JoinFuture wraps a oneshot recv whose waiter deregisters on drop, so poll_fn returns Pending with no waker registered anywhere. defuse_drop_abort() handles abort-on-drop but not waiter deregistration. It only looks fine on the live runtime because unrelated scheduler activity re-polls the task -- a consumer with no other wake source can hang the same way. join_all/cancel_all are unaffected because drain_all awaits each join future to completion.

I did NOT attempt the fix: it wants a poll-based method on TaskHandle (poll_join taking &mut self and &mut Context) so the waker registers against the handle's long-lived receiver, and that is a core runtime API change I would rather not make at the tail of a long session. Full analysis and three fix options are on tncxj9.

METHOD NOTE, because it cost me two rounds: my first cut of the parked member was an infinite loop that only awaited yield_now, and all five lab tests hit the step limit. That was MY bug, not cancel_all's -- cancellation is a protocol, and a body that only yields never observes the request. The member now calls cx.checkpoint() each iteration. Worth stating because a reviewer seeing "cancel_all hangs" would reasonably suspect cancel_all first; the isolating evidence is that join_all/cancel_all pass under the identical harness while join_next fails with instantly-completing members.

AC3 is guarded against vacuity: a companion test asserts that DEFAULT cancel_all does NOT claim race-loss attribution, so the equivalence test is proving something about the explicit-reason path rather than passing trivially.

Leaving in_progress: AC4 remains open behind tncxj9.

title: [DX-CORE] Concurrent join!, N-ary race!/select! with drain semantics — fix the macro lies
description:
WHY: recon found two correctness-adjacent embarrassments documented in the macros themselves: (1) join! awaits its branches SEQUENTIALLY (asupersync-macros/src/join.rs:94-104 'futures are awaited sequentially') — a concurrency macro that is not concurrent silently destroys parallelism for every user; (2) race! cancels losers by DROP, not by the cancellation protocol (race.rs:1-7), violating the project's own loser-drain invariant headline unless users know to reach for Scope::race instead. Both are Phase-0 leftovers that now actively mislead.

WHAT:
  join!(cx; a, b, c)        — truly concurrent polling of all branches (expand to a JoinAll-style combinator over the branches, not sequential awaits), returns tuple of Outcomes.
  race!(cx; a, b, c)        — N-ary, expands to Scope::race-equivalent machinery: losers get protocol-cancelled AND drained before the macro returns. The old drop-semantics variant is REMOVED (no compat shims).
  select! — biased/unbiased selection over heterogeneous branches with optional `else` arm; N-ary (lifts the Race2/Race3/Race4 fixed-arity ceiling found at src/combinator/race.rs:441-565); same drain guarantee.
All three get rustdoc that states the drain guarantee explicitly — it is the differentiator vs tokio::select!.
design: FILES: asupersync-macros/src/{join.rs,race.rs,+select.rs}, src/combinator/race.rs (N-ary support: either const-generic RaceN or a heterogeneous list via recursive nesting generated by the macro — generated nesting keeps the combinator library simple while the macro hides arity), src/combinator/join.rs. Drain mechanics reuse Scope::race internals; macro requires cx in scope (first arg, explicit — no ambient magic). Compile-fail tests for: missing cx, empty branch list, non-future branch.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Concurrency proof: lab test where join!(cx; sleep(10), sleep(10), sleep(10)) completes in ~10 virtual-ms not ~30 — the sequential regression test that would have caught the original bug.
2. Drain proof: race! losers show full request->drain->finalize transitions in trace + LoserDrainOracle green; test with a loser holding an obligation (must resolve, not leak).
3. N-ary: tests at arity 2,3,5,8; select! with else-arm and biased mode tested.
4. Old drop-semantics race! removed; grep-clean; all internal users migrated.
5. trybuild compile-fail suite with asserted messages (>=5 cases).
6. Determinism: same-seed winner selection stable across replays (document the tie-break rule in rustdoc).
7. docs/macro-dsl.md updated; doctests on each macro.
notes: DEPENDS on scope-spawn-v2 (macros expand to v2 internals). RISK: select! over heterogeneous types is the hardest macro in the family — bound scope to the documented branch forms; punt streams-in-select to a follow-up noted here rather than blocking. RELATION: README 'Coming from tokio' table updated in docs-refresh bead.
close_reason: done: all three macro lies fixed and proven — join! sequential->concurrent (AC1), race! drop->drain (AC2), select! added (N-ary heterogeneous drain-correct). AC3 arity 2/3/5/8 + select else/biased; AC5 trybuild 5-case suite; AC6 determinism + documented tie-break; AC7 macro-dsl.md + ignore-fenced examples (runtime-required, per codebase convention). AC4 race! macro migrated to race_drained + fallback doc-lie fixed; sole residual old-form race!(a,b) is in feature-gated real_cancel_e2e_tests.rs (dead under current macro, flagged for owner). Commits 4e2f0a582/95dee6a51/fefd409fe/a84e8aa98.

comments.text: SapphireHill 2026-06-15: race macro lie #2 (drop-not-drain) FIXED and shipped green to main. Source 8a880a504 + test fix e6395d100 (committed by a concurrent twin pane working this same P0 mid-session) + my docs 60e97a6a3. New impl Cx<cap::All> { race_drained / race_drained_named / race_drained_timeout / race_drained_timeout_named } spawns each branch as a region task and resolves via the already-proven Scope::race_all, so every loser is protocol-cancelled AND drained (awaited to termination) before the macro returns. race macro now expands to race_drained* (was inline drop-only Cx::race*). Zero internal race-macro users so no migration; Cx::race* kept as the documented drop-on-cancel escape hatch for non-static inline races. PROOFS (re-gated green on rch vs clean HEAD): asupersync-macros race token tests 7/7 assert every expansion routes through race_drained and no drop-only race* call survives (AC4 grep-clean guard); tests/race_macro_loser_drain.rs 3/3 proves AC2 drain BEHAVIOR — a park-until-cancelled loser runs its POST-cancellation resolution (the signal a dropped future never reaches at its suspend point) before race_drained returns + N-ary 4-way all-losers-drained + single-branch wiring. KEY FINDING: race_drained drains COOPERATIVE losers (observe cancel via Cx::current().checkpoint() inside the spawned task, or cancel-aware primitives like sleep/IO), NOT force-drop of arbitrary pending futures — a std::future::pending loser HANGS the race (task did not complete); branches get no cx param so they self-observe via Cx::current(). title: [DX-CORE] Channel completeness pack — unbounded mpsc, send sugar, bulk acquire, recv ergonomics
description:
[REVISED 2026-06-10 after source verification — original recon premise was wrong: most items already exist.]

WHY: the channel/sync convenience surface is mostly IMPLEMENTED but unevenly verified, documented, and discoverable. Verified existing: mpsc::unbounded_channel + UnboundedSender/UnboundedReceiver (mpsc.rs:394,891), Semaphore::acquire_many/try_acquire_many with an all-or-nothing test (semaphore.rs:367,449,1328), Receiver::recv_many (mpsc.rs:1176,1493), mpsc one-call send sugar (mpsc.rs:439), partial send-discipline docs (channel/mod.rs:37). What remains is the GAP-CLOSURE + assurance work.

WHAT (verification-first discipline — every item gets a verdict: exists-and-covered / exists-needs-tests / genuinely missing -> implement):
1. Sugar parity audit: does every channel type (broadcast, oneshot, watch) offer the one-call cancel-correct send form with identical obligation semantics to mpsc's send(cx, v)? Implement the missing ones; produce the parity table for module docs.
2. Decision-tree docs: expand channel/mod.rs into the full 'choosing your send discipline' guide (reserve+send for holds across awaits / send sugar / try_send load-shed / unbounded ownership-of-memory-pressure warning) — recon-requested, only partially present.
3. Coverage pass on the EXISTING surfaces: unbounded no-loss-under-cancel metamorphic tests mirroring the bounded suite (verify they exist; add if not), recv_many throughput bench, acquire_many contention test (exists at semaphore.rs:1328 — verify scope), doctests on every public convenience API.
4. Confirm src/real_channel_mpsc_combinator_select_integration_e2e_tests.rs compiles + runs green (the file that triggered the original wrong claim).
5. Telemetry parity: unbounded channels expose the same snapshot surface as bounded.

Sugar parity table complete across all 5 channel types; missing forms implemented with leak-oracle tests. 2. Decision-tree docs expanded in channel/mod.rs (4 disciplines + unbounded warning). 3. title: [DX-CORE] StreamExt completeness — for_each_concurrent, try_buffered, partition, fold_into, telemetry parity
description:
WHY: src/stream/ has 30+ combinators but recon found the high-traffic missing ones: for_each_concurrent (THE pattern for 'handle each item with bounded parallelism' — currently requires hand-rolling buffered+closures), try_buffered, partition, fold-into-collection, plus zero telemetry while mpsc has rich snapshots.

WHAT:
1. StreamExt::for_each_concurrent(limit, cx, f) — bounded-concurrency apply; cancel-correct: in-flight items drain on cancellation (uses JoinSet internally once available — that is why this bead depends on it).
2. try_for_each_concurrent — first Err/Cancelled short-circuits, remaining in-flight DRAINED before return (drain-on-error is the asupersync differentiator; document it).
3. partition(predicate) -> (impl Stream, impl Stream) over an internal two-lane buffer with explicit backpressure contract (document head-of-line rules).
4. fold_into<C: Default+Extend> terminal collector; collect_into for reuse of allocations.
5. Telemetry: StreamTelemetry snapshot (items in flight, buffered depth, waker churn) on buffered/buffer_unordered/for_each_concurrent, matching the mpsc telemetry idiom (channel/mpsc.rs:300-338).
design: FILES: src/stream/mod.rs (StreamExt additions), new src/stream/for_each_concurrent.rs, src/stream/partition.rs, extend src/stream/fold.rs; telemetry helper shared in src/stream/telemetry.rs. Concurrency limiter is a Semaphore (uses acquire_many bead only if batching). Determinism: completion interleaving deterministic under lab (tie-break documented). Budget integration: each in-flight item polls within the stream's cooperative budget (stream combinators already use 64-1024 budgets — keep the established pattern, see existing combinator docs).
acceptance_criteria: 1. for_each_concurrent: lab test proving bounded concurrency (max in-flight == limit, observed via telemetry), drain-on-cancel (no abandoned in-flight work; oracle green). 2. try_ variant: short-circuit + drain proven with an obligation-holding in-flight item. 3. partition: both halves consumable concurrently; backpressure contract tested (slow consumer on one half). 4. fold_into: type-level test with Vec/HashMap/String. 5. Telemetry snapshots deterministic + documented. 6. Doctests on every new combinator; stream module doc index updated. 7. Bench: for_each_concurrent vs manual buffered baseline committed.
notes: DEPENDS on JoinSet (internal building block for the concurrent variants). RELATION: [SERVER] middleware/multipart streaming consumes these; telemetry idiom shared with [INTROSPECT].
close_reason: All 7 ACs complete: for_each_concurrent/try_ (bounded concurrency + drain on error, cancel, and obligation-hold), partition, collect_into, StreamTelemetrySnapshot on the three buffering combinators, bench committed. AC6 executing-doctests delegated to zxqaqs.4. Landed ec9c674a2.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SapphireHill 2026-07-26: FIRST INCREMENT LANDED. Bead stays IN_PROGRESS — 3 of 7 ACs are complete, 3 partial, 1 not started. Precise status below so the next session does not have to re-derive it.

WHAT LANDED

  src/stream/try_buffered.rs        NEW  TryBuffered + 8 tests
  src/stream/for_each_concurrent.rs NEW  for_each_concurrent, try_for_each_concurrent
  src/stream/partition.rs           NEW  Partition + partition() + 9 tests
  src/stream/collect.rs             +3 tests for collect_into
  src/stream/mod.rs                 StreamExt::{try_buffered, collect_into, partition}, re-exports, doc index
  tests/stream_for_each_concurrent_lab_proof.rs  NEW  6 lab tests

EVIDENCE (all remote, RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1, --base HEAD --clean-overlay with only my files overlaid):
  clippy --lib --features test-internals --keep-going -- -D warnings  ->  exit 0, ZERO diagnostics (pedantic+nursery are on)
  cargo test --lib --features test-internals stream::                 ->  855 passed / 0 failed
  cargo test --test stream_for_each_concurrent_lab_proof              ->  6 passed / 0 failed
  rustfmt --edition 2024 --check                                      ->  exit 0

AC-BY-AC, HONESTLY

AC1 for_each_concurrent — SUBSTANTIALLY DONE, one gap.
  DONE: bounded concurrency proven in `for_each_concurrent_never_exceeds_the_limit`. The high-water mark is recorded BY THE ITEMS THEMSELVES (fetch_max on a shared counter inside each item body), not read off the implementation, and the test asserts both peak <= limit and peak > 1 so the bound cannot pass vacuously. Oracle green: report.quiescent && invariant_violations.is_empty().
  DONE: drain-on-ERROR, see AC2.
  NOT DONE: drain when the CALLER is cancelled from outside. The code path exists and is the first thing the drive loop checks (`cx.is_cancel_requested()` -> break -> cancel_all_with_reason), but no test drives it, because cancelling the root task mid-run needs a harness I did not build (spawn the call as a child task, cancel the handle, then assert). That is the single most valuable next test.
  DEVIATION: the AC says in-flight is observed "via telemetry". There is no StreamTelemetry yet (AC5), so the proof uses item-side instrumentation instead. Same claim, different instrument — but it means AC1 and AC5 are not both discharged by one test.

AC2 try_for_each_concurrent — SUBSTANTIALLY DONE, one gap.
  DONE: `try_for_each_concurrent_drains_in_flight_items_before_returning`. One item fails immediately; three park cooperatively on `cx.checkpoint()` and can only terminate via cancellation. After the call RETURNS, the test asserts all three observed cancellation. Asserting after the return is the whole point: it distinguishes "the combinator drained them" from "region close cleaned up afterwards", and a test that only checked quiescence would pass on region teardown alone and prove nothing.
  DONE: the reported failure is the ORIGINAL Err, not the Cancelled that the combinator's own drain produced. `finish()` encodes that rule explicitly, with one deliberate exception: a member that PANICS during drain wins, because a panic is never an expected response to a cancellation we requested.
  NOT DONE: the AC asks for the in-flight item to be OBLIGATION-HOLDING. My parked items hold no permit/lease, so the stronger claim ("a drained item resolves its obligations") is untested. Needs an item that reserves an mpsc permit and is cancelled mid-hold.

AC3 partition — DONE.
  9 tests: routing, per-lane ordering, stall at peer capacity, resume after peer drains, RE-stall when the peer buffer refills, dropped-peer exemption, end-of-source on both halves, zero-capacity panic, plus a conformance module (peer buffer never exceeds capacity; routing yields at the cooperative budget with a self-wake).
  Worth reading before changing it: the head-of-line coupling is DELIBERATE and documented, including the wakeup rule that makes "both halves must be consumed" a real requirement rather than advice. My first version of the resume test asserted the even half would drain to completion after the peer freed one slot; it does not, and should not — it re-stalls as soon as routing refills the peer buffer. The implementation was right and the test was wrong. The test now asserts the re-stall explicitly.
  NOT PROVEN: consumption from two concurrent TASKS. The halves are Send-capable (Arc<Mutex<..>>) but every test polls from one thread, so "consumable concurrently" is proven only in the interleaved-poll sense.

AC4 fold_into / collect_into — DONE, with a deliberate API deviation.
  `collect_into(collection)` is implemented and tested three ways: appends after seeded contents, REUSES the caller's allocation (asserted via capacity identity, which is what actually distinguishes it from `collect`), and accepts Vec / HashMap / String per the AC's type-level requirement.
  `fold_into` is NOT added, deliberately. The AC describes it as a "terminal collector over C: Default + Extend" — which is exactly what the existing `StreamExt::collect` already is (mod.rs, `fn collect<C>() where C: Default + Extend<Self::Item>`). Adding a second name for it would be a pure alias, and AGENTS.md forbids compatibility shims and wrapper functions for the same thing. The genuinely missing capability in that AC was allocation reuse, and that is what `collect_into` provides. Reopen this if `fold_into` was meant to be something else (e.g. fold-with-closure-into-collection); the name in the bead is ambiguous and I chose the reading that adds capability rather than vocabulary.

AC5 telemetry — NOT STARTED.
  Design note so it is not re-derived: mirror `SyncTelemetrySnapshot` (src/sync/mod.rs:31-59), not the mpsc one — it is the shared-shape precedent, `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]`, all-scalar fields, one `telemetry_snapshot(&self, id: u64)` accessor per type. Natural fit for Buffered / BufferUnordered / TryBuffered, which all own a persistent in_flight queue and a waker epoch that is a ready-made waker-churn counter.
  REAL OBSTACLE: `for_each_concurrent` is an async fn with no persistent object to snapshot, so the AC's request for telemetry on it needs an API DECISION first — a caller-supplied observer callback, or returning a handle instead of a plain future. That is a design choice, not a coding task, and it should be made deliberately rather than defaulted into.

AC6 doctests + module doc index — PARTIAL.
  DONE: module doc index updated, including a new "## Splitting" section and a "## Bounded Concurrency" section that states when NOT to use these (prefer buffer_unordered when the work is pure and holds no obligation).
  PARTIAL: usage examples were added on every new public item, but as ```ignore blocks, matching the existing convention in this module — iter.rs and stream.rs use ```ignore, and NO combinator in src/stream/ (buffered, collect, merge, forward, ...) has an executing doctest at all. Making these run is a module-wide convention change and a runtime-in-doctests decision; it should be its own piece of work rather than smuggled in here. Flagging it because an ```ignore block is documentation, not a doctest, and I do not want this AC read as discharged.

AC7 bench (for_each_concurrent vs manual buffered baseline) — NOT STARTED.
  Requires a new [[bench]] entry in the workspace Cargo.toml, which is a high-contention shared file; deliberately not touched mid-session.

DESIGN DECISIONS WORTH KNOWING

1. WHY JoinSet AND NOT INLINE FUTURES. BufferUnordered holds plain futures polled inline; when it is dropped they are dropped where they stand, unpolled, with no cancellation signal. That is fine for pure computation and wrong for work holding obligations. for_each_concurrent owns REGION TASKS instead, so in-flight items participate in region-close quiescence, receive cancellation as the request->drain->finalize protocol, and have their terminal Outcome observed. The cost is real and is documented on the module: items and item futures must be Send + 'static and the factory must be Clone. buffer_unordered remains the right choice when none of that is needed.

2. WHY FREE FUNCTIONS, NOT StreamExt METHODS. The bead spells these `StreamExt::for_each_concurrent(limit, cx, f)`. I implemented them as free functions instead. Every one of the ~33 existing StreamExt methods is Cx-free and returns a named combinator struct; these need a `&Cx` and are driven by an async state machine that would have to duplicate JoinSet's join loop to become a named poll-based type. `forward(cx, stream, sender)` in src/stream/forward.rs already establishes the free-function shape for exactly this case — a Cx-taking stream operation. Adding StreamExt methods later as thin `-> impl Future` delegates is still open if discoverability matters more than uniformity.

3. WHY THE FACTORY TAKES `Cx`. Signature is `FnMut(Cx, S::Item) -> Fut`, not `FnMut(S::Item) -> Fut`. Each item runs as a task with its own child Cx, and handing it to the body is what lets the item checkpoint, spawn, or hold obligations under the correct capability context. Dropping the Cx parameter would have been more ergonomic and would have made the items capability-blind, which is the opposite of the project's no-ambient-authority rule.

4. SPAWN FAILURE IS REPORTED AS Panicked. `JoinSet::spawn` can fail with SpawnError (no spawn gateway on this Cx). There is no `E` to describe that, and reporting Ok would be a lie. It surfaces as `Outcome::panicked(..)` so it dominates the severity lattice and can never be mistaken for a per-item failure or for success.

NEXT SESSION, IN PRIORITY ORDER
  1. AC1 gap: caller-cancellation drain test (spawn the call as a child, cancel the handle, assert in-flight items observed cancellation before the join returns).
  2. AC2 gap: obligation-holding in-flight item.
  3. AC5: decide the for_each_concurrent telemetry API, then implement StreamTelemetrySnapshot on the three buffering combinators.
  4. AC7: bench.
  5. AC6: decide whether src/stream/ adopts executing doctests at all.

comments.text:
SapphireHill 2026-07-26: AC1 GAP CLOSED — and closing it found a DEADLOCK in the code I had just landed. Fix is 2e0d5993e.

Updates my previous comment, which listed "drain when the CALLER is cancelled" as the single most valuable next test. I wrote that test. It failed, for a real reason.

THE DEADLOCK (introduced by 41177ea56, ~40 minutes earlier, now fixed):

The drive loop parked in `JoinSet::join_next`, which is documented as UNINTERRUPTIBLE — it waits for a member's terminal outcome so no-orphan accounting always holds. That is the correct default for a caller who will eventually be satisfied. For this combinator it is a deadlock, because both the cancellation check and the drain live AFTER the wait:

  caller is cancelled
    -> loop is parked in join_next, so it never reaches is_cancel_requested()
    -> so it never reaches cancel_all_with_reason()
    -> so the members are never cancelled
    -> so a member that only terminates BECAUSE it was cancelled never terminates
    -> so join_next never returns.

Measured rather than argued: the lab run burned its full 100_000-step budget and returned `quiescent=false, steps_total=100000`. After the fix the same test passes in 0.01s.

Note what the shape of this bug was. My loop DID check `is_cancel_requested()` — at the top of every iteration — and I had reasoned that was sufficient. It is not, because the check being present says nothing about whether it is REACHABLE. That is the same class as br-asupersync-c6ppu4's thesis (a red gate and a skipped gate look identical from outside) and evb4i9's (a gate that exists in the workflow but never executes). Here: a cancellation check that exists in the loop but is never reached.

THE FIX: wait cooperatively instead of parking. Poll `try_join_next()`, re-check `is_cancel_requested()`, `yield_now().await`. The cancellation check is now reachable on every scheduler turn, so the drain always runs.

I looked for a cheaper primitive first and there is not one: `Cx` exposes only the synchronous `is_cancel_requested()`, with no cancellation-await future to race `join_next` against (checked src/cx/cx.rs and src/cancel/). A yield-loop is the idiomatic cooperative wait in this runtime — it is exactly the shape of `parks_until_cancelled` in the test, and of the cooperative parking used elsewhere.

TRADEOFF, stated in the code rather than hidden: cooperative polling costs one wakeup per scheduler turn while waiting, where parking costs none. That is the price of being cancellable, and it is the right trade for a combinator whose entire reason to exist is drain-on-cancel. Callers who do not need that should use `buffer_unordered`, which the module docs already say. If the wakeup cost ever shows up in a profile, the real fix is a cancellation-await future on `Cx`, not reverting this.

THE NEW TEST IS DELIBERATELY ADVERSARIAL, so a regression cannot pass by accident: every item parks forever and can only terminate through cancellation, and the driver is cancelled while all four are in flight. If cancellation could not reach the items, the run comes back non-quiescent rather than merely slower — the failure is loud, not a timing wobble.
