assertions separate RESOLVED from LEAKED: no message delivered (permits aborted, not committed),

title: [DX-CORE] Budget & SpawnError ergonomics — request-timeout helpers, admission diagnostics
description:

WHAT:

title: HTTP/2 server send audit: trailers overtake flow-blocked DATA (DATA after END_STREAM; gRPC unary replies > 64 KiB); RST budget kills busy legitimate connections; blocked push DATA pinned forever; produced bodies starve the reader
description:
Read-only audit of the HTTP/2 server send path at origin/main 2780d3454 (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-04; read from origin). SapphireHill re-read F1 at origin.

## HIGH
F1. Connection::next_frame (src/http/h2/connection.rs ~2303-2311) sets aside DATA that has no send credit and keeps scanning; a later Headers op for the same stream (the trailers) passes stream_can_emit_queued_frames (which only checks error_code) and goes out with END_STREAM, then the DATA follows on a closed stream (RFC 9113 5.1: STREAM_CLOSED connection error for a conformant client). An empty DATA with END_STREAM queued behind blocked DATA jumps ahead the same way. Buffered responses queue head + body + trailers at once (listener.rs ~2050-2065, ~4159, pushes ~2134-2156), and native gRPC unary always adds a grpc-status trailer, so any gRPC reply larger than the client's initial window (64 KiB for grpc-go) is affected. Fix: once a stream has DATA set aside, its later HEADERS, DATA and PUSH_PROMISE stay queued behind it.

## MEDIUM
F2. Peer RST_STREAM and peer-caused stream errors share one 100-per-30 s budget, counting resets of finished streams; the listener never exposes Connection::rst_stream_rate_limit, and tripping it GOAWAYs and closes at once, cancelling every in-flight handler. A gRPC channel with >3.3 cancellations/s, or a browser cancelling 100 requests in 30 s, loses the connection. Fix (additive): Http2ListenerConfig option; count only resets of running streams or a reset/opened ratio; graceful GOAWAY.
F3. Pushed responses have no in-flight guard: a promised stream that never gets window credit keeps its body in pending_ops for the connection's life and blocks idle timeout and close (flow_control.rs next_deadline only tracks response_guards/produced_bodies).

## LOW
F4. next_driver_event polls produced bodies before framed.poll_next, so a fast producer with large client windows delays reading RST_STREAM/PING/SETTINGS/WINDOW_UPDATE/new HEADERS until credit runs out.

## Checked and sound
WINDOW_UPDATE overflow (connection and stream), SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE decrease (negative windows), DATA bounded by both windows and MAX_FRAME_SIZE, window re-check every loop, MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS (refused streams HPACK-decoded), client RST cleanup, GOAWAY ratchet, PING/SETTINGS ack caps, produced-response ordering, HPACK encode at emit time.
close_reason: Full verification complete. All items in scope landed and verified: F1 (blocked DATA queuing preserves trailer ordering in c8e217172), F3 (pushed responses bound by flow control deadlines in db2ec7e21), F4 (listener driver round-robins produced bodies with transport to prevent frame reader starvation in 9e749a583). F2 remains documented as owner policy decision on default RST rate limit behavior. All 602 http::h2 tests pass cleanly.

title: [Distributed] Implement Region Symbol Encoding/Distribution
[security] types/cancel.rs: derive(Deserialize) on CancelReason recurses through unbounded cause chain BEFORE max_chain_depth applies — stack-overflow / OOM DoS via crafted snapshot
description:
src/types/cancel.rs:426-444 — `CancelReason` carries `pub cause: Option<Box<Self>>` and uses `#[derive(Deserialize)]`. The derived implementation recurses through the entire cause chain BEFORE any application-layer truncation (`with_cause_limited`, `truncate_chain`, `chain_depth`) ever runs.

An attacker-controlled snapshot or trace artifact (distributed/snapshot.rs decoder, MessagePack frame on a fabric channel, JSON body in a debug endpoint) carrying

  { cause: { cause: { cause: { ... 50_000 levels deep ... } } } }

will cause the serde Deserialize impl to recurse 50K times. Either the program stack overflows (panic-DoS that kills the entire process) or memory-allocates 50K * sizeof(CancelReason) heap entries.

The `CancelAttributionConfig::max_chain_depth` (default 16) and `max_chain_memory` (default 4 KiB) bounds are applied AFTER deserialization completes — by which time the deep recursion has already happened.

Fix direction:
  1. Custom `impl Deserialize for CancelReason` that consults a depth-limited deserializer wrapper. serde provides `deserializer.deserialize_struct` with a Visitor that can count nesting; once nesting exceeds CONFIG_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH bail with InvalidData.
  2. Alternative: deserialize into a flat representation (pre-broken-up CancelReason without recursive cause) and only build the cause chain in `with_cause_limited`. Any input deeper than the limit is rejected at deserialize time.
  3. Pair with the existing distributed/snapshot.rs:319 metadata-len bounds-check pattern (asupersync-poshr8) — the same defence-in-depth axis.

Source: /multi-pass-bug-hunting src/types/* + src/record/* (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Routed CancelReason::cause through #[serde(deserialize_with = deserialize_bounded_cause)]. Custom deserializer uses thread-local Cell<usize> + RAII CauseDepthGuard to bound depth at 64 (4x headroom over runtime cap of 16; below serde_json's 128 default so this gate fires first; bare on MessagePack/bincode/postcard which have no built-in recursion limit). Returns serde::de::Error::custom on exceed. 3 new unit tests: 96-deep JSON rejected with dyao05 trace, 8-deep round-trips cleanly, thread-local counter resets between sequential deserialize calls. Commit 19f09cd1f.

title: HTTP/2 HPACK audit (r9): "unlimited" header list size lets one HEADERS block allocate ~1 GiB; malformed fields are connection errors; PUSH_PROMISE paths skip HPACK decode (table desync)
description:
Read-only audit of src/http/h2/hpack.rs and its feeders (connection.rs, listener.rs, settings.rs, frame.rs, stream.rs) at origin/main 66d50abcc (SapphireHill audit agent round 9, 10-05). Report: /data/tmp/rc_20260923/audit_r9_hpack.md. Defaults are safe; no panic is reachable from peer input. Split Cookie fields (the report's M2) are joined at the web router under a1q12q (F3); direct h2 listener users still receive one field per cookie, which RFC 9113 allows for non-HTTP/1 consumers.

Re-checked at origin 3d43b3fe9 (10-06): M3 holds; process_push_promise still returns on the GOAWAY, stream-state and concurrency paths before decoding the header block. dx72q4 (15b777f27) has changed connection.rs since, so line numbers here are 66d50abcc's.

## HIGH (opt-in configuration; owner decision)
H1. With max_header_list_size "unlimited" (u32::MAX: settings.rs ~212-216; gRPC maps the documented max_metadata_size(0) to it, grpc/server.rs ~1329-1333), one HEADERS block can allocate about 1 GiB: insert one ~4 KB dynamic entry, then send ~259k single bytes 0xBE (index 62); each decodes to a fresh 4 KB header (hpack.rs ~953-957, ~1015-1030, ~575-580 allocate before any budget check; the only decoded-size check, ~922-930, runs after). The 256 KiB cap (2e1zb) limits only the encoded block. Fix: a hard decoded ceiling (e.g. 1 MiB, or a few MiB) checked BEFORE to_header(), and optionally a field-count cap per block. This changes what "unlimited" and max_metadata_size(0) mean: both docs need a sentence.

## MEDIUM
M1. Malformed fields (uppercase or non-token names, NUL/CR/LF, non-UTF-8 values, an over-size list) return COMPRESSION_ERROR mid-block (hpack.rs ~1001-1010, ~1231-1264, ~1305-1307, ~1640, ~926-928, ~1286-1288), and the listener answers with GOAWAY (listener.rs ~3745-3772). RFC 9113 makes these stream errors (or 431). Behind a pooling proxy one client resets every other client's streams. Fix: decode the whole block (table stays in sync), return a malformed/oversize flag via a new decode_block(), map it to a stream error. Changes HpackDecoder's error behaviour. Partly tracked: 6hvls9 LOW 4 (non-UTF-8 only).
M3. Several PUSH_PROMISE paths return a stream error without decoding the header block (connection.rs ~1977-1983, ~1994-2008, ~2010-2019, ~2022-2023, ~1500, ~1774-1780), so the client's dynamic table desyncs and later responses decode to wrong header values silently. The HEADERS side was fixed in d19781b4e. Affects clients with push enabled: Settings::default() enables it (the in-tree clients use Settings::client(), push off), so external users of the public Connection are exposed. Fix: decode the block, then reset the promised stream, as the HEADERS path does.

## LOW
next_frame drops queued CONTINUATION frames if the stream is reset after its HEADERS went out (connection.rs ~2294); no required size update after we shrink the table; table-size limit applied before ACK; an advertised table size above 1 MiB not clamped; the encoder indexes authorization/cookie/set-cookie (should be never-indexed); the encoder accepts a peer-chosen table up to 1 MiB; get_indexed_name copies the value it discards; huffman_encoded_size overflows u32 for values over ~143 MB; leading/trailing whitespace in values (e427ys); extended CONNECT accepted without negotiation; six tests that cannot fail (test_dynamic_table_eviction, test_integer_decode_checked_mul_overflow, hpack_rfc7541_appendix_c_conformance, ...).

Judged SOUND: see the report (Huffman decode with EOS/padding, integer overflow, literal bounds before allocation, index checks, eviction accounting, size-update sequencing, CONTINUATION sequencing and caps, SETTINGS atomicity).

title: [mock-code-finder] Close placeholder/mock gap audit with real implementation seams
description:
Background: A comprehensive mock-code-finder pass after a full AGENTS.md, README.md, Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, and architecture-root read found that the production src ratchet is mostly healthy, but several conformance and audit surfaces still contain simulated, placeholder, or stale behavior. The goal of this epic is to convert every material gap into real implementation seams, executable conformance, truthful tests, and a final ratchet so future agents do not need the original audit transcript.

Architecture context: asupersync is a Rust 2024 async runtime built around explicit Cx capabilities, region-owned structured concurrency, request-drain-finalize cancellation, obligation accounting, cancel-correct channels and sync, and deterministic LabRuntime testing. The gaps below matter because fake conformance and stale audit prose undermine the project goal: specs should be checked against live production code, not fixture-only or mock-only harnesses.

Audit evidence to preserve in this epic: scripts/scan_stubs.sh passed 19/19 and found no production todo!, unimplemented!, or not-implemented panic under the existing ratchet. scripts/check_no_mock_policy.py failed with many lexical hits, most of them intentional test doubles or stale audit modules. Manual tracing identified real gaps in PostgreSQL COPY FROM, RFC6330 RaptorQ conformance registration and fixture-only tests, HTTP/2 conformance modules that bypass live Connection::process_frame, OpenTelemetry conformance binaries that simulate or return placeholder data, missing W3C baggage HTTP header integration, scheduler shutdown API audit mismatch, and an ignored RwLock upgrade audit test. Several other audit files are stale because production code already fixed them.

Scope: create and sequence focused beads that replace placeholder behavior with real seams, update tests and conformance runners, clean stale audit prose only after source truth is confirmed, and add a final mock-code-finder signoff ratchet. This epic intentionally does not authorize branches, worktrees, file deletion, broad rewrites, or code changes without file reservations.
design:
Dependency shape: common policy and signoff beads depend on all subsystem repairs; subsystem repairs are split by ownership boundary so agents can reserve disjoint files. PostgreSQL COPY FROM, RaptorQ RFC6330, HTTP/2 conformance, OpenTelemetry conformance, W3C baggage, scheduler shutdown, and RwLock audit cleanup are independent lanes. A stale-audit normalization bead depends on the source-truth repairs so cleanup never hides a real gap. A final signoff bead depends on every lane and owns the ratchet proof.

Execution rules for every child: read live source before changing, reserve exact files with Agent Mail before editing, keep work on main only, use rch for Rust validation, do not run broad full-workspace cargo builds, do not delete files, and record first unrelated compile blockers instead of widening scope. Each child must leave enough comments and acceptance detail for a future worker to execute without reading this planning session.
acceptance_criteria: Epic closes only when every child bead has either shipped real implementation and tests or produced an explicit blocker bead with exact file paths, live source evidence, and reason it cannot be completed safely. Final signoff must rerun scripts/scan_stubs.sh, scripts/check_no_mock_policy.py or its repaired successor, targeted rg or ast-grep scans for todo!/unimplemented!/not implemented/placeholder/mock, and the relevant rch-backed cargo tests for changed crates. The final comment must include exact commands, pass/fail status, remaining intentional allowlist entries, stale-audit modules removed or normalized, dependency graph health, and confirmation that no child relies on simulated behavior while claiming conformance.

title: Native HTTP/2 client (36b3d01b0) review follow-ups: download-window test no longer reaches WINDOW_UPDATE, leading/trailing-whitespace field values accepted (RFC 9113 8.2.1), MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS=0 treated as protocol error
description:
## Context
A fresh-eyes review (SapphireHill, 2026-10-01, read-only) of 36b3d01b0 (bounded native HTTP/2 client with duplex flow control), on current main including 5cba7fc2a and e5b320b2d.

No high-severity defects. The following are correct:
- send and receive flow control, including SETTINGS deltas making windows negative, overflow checks, and refills at 1/2 and 1/4 of the window with padding counted;
- bounded buffering;
- CONTINUATION interleaving, plus count and byte caps;
- response pseudo-header rules, connection-specific and uppercase fields, and HPACK table-size updates;
- GOAWAY (smallest last-stream-id; above it REFUSED_STREAM and GoAway), RST_STREAM, 1xx, trailers and content-length;
- drop and cancel, since each request owns its connection.

## Low findings
1. Test gap (low-medium, high confidence). tests/http2_client_native.rs ~60-101, "...uploads_and_downloads_beyond_both_initial_windows", no longer exercises the download direction. Since 5cba7fc2a the client advertises receive windows equal to the response limit, clamped to [65,535, 16 MiB] (client.rs ~749-760), so the 262,263-byte echo never uses them up. The receive-side WINDOW_UPDATE path is now untested end to end. It matters only when max_response_body is above 16 MiB. Add a test with a limit and a body above 16 MiB, or rename the test.
2. Field values with leading or trailing SP/HTAB are accepted. The request side is client.rs ~431-433. The response side is client.rs ~629-634 and connection.rs ~2553-2581, through h1 validate_header_field (h1/codec.rs ~646), which rejects only CR, LF, NUL, control bytes and DEL. RFC 9113 §8.2.1 calls such fields malformed. Strict peers (nghttp2-based servers: Apache mod_http2, Envoy) reset the stream with PROTOCOL_ERROR after I/O, though the builder's docs promise that invalid bytes fail before a socket opens. Note: the response-side check in connection.rs is shared with the H2 server's request validation, so tightening it changes server behavior. Decide whether to apply it to both or to the client only.
3. SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS = 0 fails the request at once with Http2ClientError::Protocol("max concurrent streams exceeded") (client.rs ~830, through stream.rs ~1590-1603). RFC 9113 §6.5.2 says zero is legal, SHOULD NOT be treated as special, and is expected only briefly. The client should wait within its deadline for a SETTINGS that raises the limit, or at least not report a legal setting as a peer protocol violation.

## Not defects (by design or a SHOULD)
- No GOAWAY or RST_STREAM on a single-use connection's error, drop or early completion.
- A non-NO_ERROR GOAWAY at or below the last stream id fails the request immediately.
- Strict rejection of content-length on 204 and 1xx, and of duplicate content-length.

title: [AUDIT] Deep correctness audit: obligation/no_aliasing_proof.rs
notes:
AUDIT COMPLETE: obligation/no_aliasing_proof.rs (1,994 lines) — SOUND

Machine-checkable formal proof that SendPermit obligations maintain no-aliasing invariant (at most one task holds any permit at any program point).

## Structures reviewed:
- GhostPermitMap: HashMap<ObligationId, GhostEntry> (active) + HashMap<ObligationId, ConsumedEntry> (consumed)
- GhostEntry: holder, kind, region, reserved_at
- ConsumedEntry: resolution (Committed/Aborted/Leaked), resolved_at, last_holder
- ProofStep: lemma, obligation, time, verified, description
- Lemma enum: 5 lemmas (AllocationFreshness, TransferExclusivity, ReleaseConsumption, ConcurrentIndependence, DropSafety)
- Counterexample: ViolationKind, obligation, time, description
- ViolationKind: 8 variants (DoubleOwnership, DuplicateAllocation, UseAfterRelease, TransferAliasing, KindDisagreement, RegionDisagreement, WrongKind, SelfTransfer)
- NoAliasingProver: ghost state + proof accumulator, sendpermit_only mode vs all_kinds
- TransferEvent: synthetic event for testing delegation paths

## Proof verification logic:
- check_allocation (Lemma 1): freshness (not active, not consumed) → insert → post: holder_count==1
- check_release (Lemma 3): preconditions (not consumed, active, kind/region agree) → remove+consume → post: holder_count==0
- check_drop (Lemma 5): like release but Leaked status, doesn't early-return on kind/region mismatch (correct for leak semantics)
- apply_transfer (Lemma 2): active, holder==from → update holder → post: holder_count==1
- check_frame_preservation (Lemma 4): all other active permits undisturbed (trivially true by HashMap invariant)
- check_final_invariant: all remaining active have exactly 1 holder

## Notes:
- ViolationKind::SelfTransfer and WrongKind defined but never produced (dead code, no correctness impact)
- Frame check (check_frame_preservation) is ceremonial (hardcoded count=1), acknowledged by comment
- check_drop intentionally consumes even on kind/region mismatch (counterexamples still recorded, is_verified() correct)

## Concurrency: NONE (pure &mut self verification)
## Unsafe: NONE
## Bugs found: 0
## Findings: 0
## Tests: ~30 (all 5 lemmas, mutation tests, realistic scenarios, edge cases)

title: [ALIEN] Phase 6: Canonical Concurrency + Certified Optimization + RFC-Grade FEC
description:
## Intent

Make Asupersync *qualitatively* better than conventional async runtimes by completing a set of mathematically-principled upgrades that compound:

- deterministic, semantics-aware schedule canonicalization (beyond Foata)
- topology-guided schedule exploration (coverage guided by invariants of the execution space)
- potential-function (Lyapunov) scheduling for fast cancellation/quiescence convergence
- RFC-6330-grade RaptorQ (systematic FEC) with proof-carrying decoding traces
- certified plan/DAG rewrites (e-graph-like optimizer + machine-checkable certificates)

These are explicitly aligned with Asupersync non-negotiables:
- structured concurrency (region ownership)
- cancellation is a protocol: request -> drain -> finalize
- losers are drained
- no obligation leaks
- no ambient authority (effects via Cx)
- deterministic lab runtime and trace replay

## Why this matters

Asupersync already has the key foundations:
- trace event model + resource-footprint independence relation
- Foata normal form canonicalization + trace fingerprints
- DPOR race detection + schedule explorer scaffolding
- static obligation analyses (abstract interpretation + VASS/WSTS projections)
- Lyapunov-governor prototype (potential function)
- plan IR for lawful combinator rewrites

Phase 6 upgrades turn those foundations into an "alien artifact" system:
- **Explainable**: every decision has a ledger (why this schedule, why this rewrite, why this task ran)
- **Provable where possible**: certificates and checkers, not vibes
- **Operationally excellent**: performance work is profile-driven and behavior-preserving

## Global constraints

- Deterministic: no wall-clock dependence in core algorithms.
- No new async runtime/executor introduced into core.
- Avoid allocations on hot paths; any heavy analysis belongs in lab / tooling paths.
- Prefer in-place revisions; avoid file proliferation unless truly new functionality.

## Deliverables (sub-epics)

1. Geodesic schedule normalization (canonical low-entropy replay)
2. Persistent-homology schedule prioritization (topological novelty -> coverage)
3. Lyapunov governor integrated into the real scheduler (cancel convergence)
4. Full RaptorQ (RFC 6330-class) + proof-carrying decode traces
5. Certified rewrite engine for plan IR (e-graph-like + proof verifier)
6. Extreme optimization harness (baselines, profiles, golden traces)

## Success metrics (project-level)

- Replays are canonicalized into low-entropy schedules that are stable across equivalent traces.
- Schedule exploration finds "black swan" concurrency failures with fewer runs than naive seed sweep (deterministic benchmark).
- Cancellation/quiescence convergence improves measurably under load without compromising determinism.
- RaptorQ is systematic, deterministic, and explainable (proof artifacts) with strong correctness tests.
- Plan rewrites are accompanied by certificates verified by a small checker.

title: process/fs/time/signal: cancelled fs::File write or seek credited to the next call; Command::status ignores configured stdio; with_time_getter timeouts use the runtime clock; is_available() disables Ctrl+C
description:
Read-only audit of the user-facing src/time (sleep/timeout/interval), src/process.rs, src/fs and src/signal at origin/main 731a0f5b1 (2026-10-03, SapphireHill subagent). It did not cover the timer wheel or scheduler internals. Items below are from reading the code; "confirmed" means re-read by SapphireHill.

1. (high) A cancelled fs::File write or seek is credited to the next write or seek (src/fs/file.rs ~828-835 poll_write PendingIo::Write, ~927-933 poll_seek).
   - poll_write returns Pending until the pool syscall finishes and treats the next call as a retry of the same bytes.
   - timeout(write_all(b"AAAA")) fires while the write is queued; a later write_all(b"BBBBBBBB") gets Ok(4) from the old write. The file ends AAAABBBB: four bytes of B are silently lost. A longer old chunk fails the next write with "invalid write count".
   - An abandoned seek(Start(100)) makes a later seek(Start(0)) return Ok(100) and leave the cursor at 100. This reaches BufReader<File>.
   - sync_all, sync_data, set_len and metadata (~495-518) do not wait for in-flight trait operations, so an fsync can run before an abandoned write lands.
   - tokio returns Ready(n) at once for a buffered write, so a pending operation always belongs to an earlier call, and its sync_all calls complete_inflight() first.
   - Suggested fix: record the submitted chunk (or a request id) in PendingIo::Write/Seek. If the next call does not match, settle the old operation as foreign and resubmit. Call settle_trait_pending() in the sync and set_len paths.
   - Suggested test: abandon_queued_io from tests/fs_file_poll_offload_e2e.rs with blocking_threads(1,1). Abandon write_all(b"AAAA"), then write_all(b"BBBBBBBB"); expect AAAABBBBBBBB.
2. (medium-high) TimeoutFuture::with_time_getter and Sleep::with_time_getter use the runtime timer's clock against a deadline from the custom clock (src/time/timeout_future.rs ~285-293, src/time/sleep.rs ~801-805, ~874-932).
   - In a runtime task, a timeout with deadline 10 s on a clock reading 0 returns Elapsed on its first poll once the process has been up 10 s. A Sleep fires early; with the custom clock ahead it fires late or never.
   - The docs promise this API is for "synthetic clocks that should not rely on wall-clock progression". GracefulBuilder::time_getter inherits the bug.
3. (medium) signal::is_available() registers a SIGINT handler that is never removed, so a program that only checks availability can no longer be stopped with Ctrl+C (src/signal/ctrl_c.rs ~86-96).
   - bi2462.113 listed this trigger; its fix changed only Signal::new.
   - On Windows, SignalDispatcher::start (signal.rs ~318-341) still registers all three signals on any signal() call.
   - The ctrl_c doc's "no Ctrl+C event is lost" (~50) is false: a SIGINT between two ctrl_c() calls is swallowed.
4. (medium, CONFIRMED, fix in progress) Command::status() and status_async() force Inherit on all three streams, ignoring .stdin(Stdio::Null)/.stdout(Stdio::Null) (src/process.rs ~2307-2321).
   - Regression from 824551061, which meant to stop output()/status() from overwriting the stored configuration.
   - A command told to read null stdin (ssh, git credential prompts) reads the parent's terminal and blocks.
5. (medium) With a process-group signal target, cancelling wait_async can leave group members running (src/process.rs ~2492-2534, ~2771-2780).
   - cancel_drain_child returns once the leader is reaped after SIGTERM and never sends SIGKILL to the group. After that, kill(), signal() and kill_on_drop all report "child already waited".
   - Example: sh -c '(trap "" TERM; exec sleep 30) & wait' with NewProcessGroup leaves sleep running.
6. (medium, io-uring feature only) create_dir, remove_dir, rename, remove_file and symlink create a ring and block inline on submit_and_wait, with no fallback (src/fs/dir.rs ~23-63, src/fs/path_ops.rs ~268-311, ~375-395, ~714-780). They fail where the kernel lacks those ring ops (rename on 5.10) or io_uring is blocked.
7. (low-medium, owner decision) fs::write, copy, rename, remove_file and write_atomic reject any path containing ".." (src/fs/path_ops.rs ~164-210). This was deliberate (slxtqw) but is undocumented, and std and tokio accept such paths. Absolute paths pass, and read() is not checked.
8. (low) A second wait() or try_wait() after a successful reap returns InvalidInput "child already waited"; std and tokio return the cached status (src/process.rs ~2414-2433, ~2790-2805). The fix needs a new Child field, so it must keep the unsafe-ledger line locators in process.rs.
9. (low, not reproduced) ChildStdin/ChildStdout/ChildStderr declare inner before registration, so drop closes the fd before deregistering it (src/process.rs ~3211-3214, ~3371-3375, ~3471-3475). net::TcpStream declares registration first. The epoll reactor tracks fd identity and cleans up after EBADF, so no failure was shown.

The auditor found these sound:
- sleep reset and re-arm, horizon and driver moves, Duration::MAX and Time::MAX saturation;
- timeout preferring a ready inner future;
- interval Burst, Delay and Skip;
- the process reaper waits only on its own pids;
- kill_on_drop;
- wait_with_output drains both pipes;
- read_dir keeps its state across cancellation;
- read-ahead rewind;
- atomic-write temp cleanup;
- each signal stream has its own delivery cursor.

title: [testing-quality] runtime/scheduler/priority_inversion_metamorphic.rs: 'metamorphic' tests verify a mock oracle, not the real PriorityInversionOracle
description:
src/runtime/scheduler/priority_inversion_metamorphic.rs: run_inversion_detection (line 184-280) is documented at line 189 as 'Create a mock oracle for testing (in a real implementation, this would integrate with the actual PriorityInversionOracle)'. The body is a hand-rolled simulation that:
- Computes severity via calculate_inversion_severity (line 283) which is a pure function of (priority_a - priority_b).
- Returns max_ready_gap = 5 if any inversion detected, else 0 (line 268) — pure function of detected_inversions.is_empty().
- Returns certificate_invalidations = detected_inversions.len() (line 271).

The metamorphic relation 'uniform priority shift invariance' holds tautologically because the mock's severity is computed from (high - low), which is shift-invariant by construction. The test therefore passes regardless of whether the real PriorityInversionOracle has the invariance property.

Concrete repro: introduce a real-oracle bug that breaks shift invariance and the test would still pass — because the test never touches the real oracle. The verify_uniform_priority_shift_invariance contract is meaningless.

Suggested fix: route ShiftTestTask scenarios through the actual PriorityInversionOracle (use PriorityInversionOracle::record_inversion / detect / etc.) and compare its outputs across the original-vs-shifted runs. The mock should be deleted or moved to docstring example.

title: Obligation mailbox audit: a panic while draining a batch drops the rest of it (regions never close); every obligation post wakes a worker; unified completion takes the state lock twice
description:
Read-only audit of src/runtime/obligation_mailbox.rs at origin/main 47117810a (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-05).

## HIGH
H1. A panic while draining a batch silently drops every post left in that batch (apply_obligation_posts_with_task_table ~943-948).
- What happens: up to `max` posts are popped into a local Vec before any is applied. If applying one of them unwinds, the rest of the Vec is dropped with it.
- Likely triggers:
  - The default leak policy is ObligationLeakResponse::Panic (config.rs ~2231). Applying a Leak post then reaches panic_any (state.rs ~5392), and any token dropped unresolved produces such a post.
  - A panicking MetricsProvider callback.
- Consequences:
  - A dropped checked Reserve never creates its record. Its credit's unapplied barrier is never released, so the region can never close, and its later Commit is refused.
  - pending_admissions stays above zero forever, so every task_completed sweeps the global backlog.
  - A dropped legacy Commit or Abort leaves its record pending, so a later completion audit reports a false leak.
- Reachable from every batched drain:
  - three_lane.rs ~6222 (64 per dispatch);
  - drain_obligation_posts_before_completion;
  - worker.rs;
  - the lab.
- d8e81f2cd fixed only the block_on caller.
- FIXED in stack P (P8): posts are popped and applied one at a time, so a post behind an unwinding one stays queued, and an AppliedReceipt guard counts each dequeued post once, also on unwind.

## MEDIUM
M1. Every post wakes a worker (~517-523, ~627, ~871-918).
- The notifier is coordinator.wake_one(). It always unparks a parker and calls io.wake() (an eventfd write).
- Sender::reserve + send and Semaphore::acquire post twice per operation, so up to 2 idle workers wake per message, and each then takes the global RuntimeState lock to drain.
- Fix: notify only on the mailbox's empty → non-empty transition, and have the drainer re-notify when its 64-post cap leaves a remainder.
- Test: a counting notify closure; register and commit 64 tokens without draining; notify count ≤ 1 (128 today).

M2. Unified (non-sharded) task completion takes the global state lock twice and revokes twice (three_lane.rs ~8588, ~8752-8759, ~8643-8646; state.rs ~7644). Fix: revoke + drain_obligation_posts_before_completion inside the one acquisition. This is three_lane.rs: handed to e0155ea8.

## LOW
- L1. The legacy pending-post credit gates nothing; obligation_mailbox.rs ~22-26, ~538-542, ~640-642 and region.rs ~851-857 say it does. See the region audit bead.
- L2. apply_obligation_post_from_dispatch_table is not #[track_caller], so every mailbox-minted obligation's acquired_at, backtrace and reserved_at point at the drainer, not at the user's call. Leak reports name state.rs.
- L3. The drain rate is fixed at 64 per dispatch, but one poll can post an unbounded number; the backlog is swept by an unrelated task's completion under the global lock.
- L4. Notify-panic hygiene on the legacy register/Drop paths (not reachable with the production wake_one).
- L5. The Reserve arm at ~1004-1006 is unreachable.

title: runtime/current_thread: post-root drain is unbounded for a spawn_local trampoline (lane never empty at the budget check)
description: three_lane.rs run_loop_until (~L4932): the loop breaks only when should_stop() && local_spawn_lane_is_empty(). A local task that re-spawns its successor with spawn_local on every poll keeps the lane non-empty at every check: next_task admits it, runs it, it enqueues the next request, and block_on never returns after its root completed, contradicting the documented bound (POST_ROOT_DRAIN_TURNS). A cx.spawn chain IS bounded (mailbox, not the lane). Fix: once the turn budget is spent, stop admitting from the lane and keep leftover requests for the next drive on this thread (same mechanism as stranded wakes). Regression test: spawn_local trampoline; block_on(async { spawn_local(trampoline); 42 }) must return.

title: NATS supervised client: -ERR reconnect storm (auth refusal, permissions violation treated as fatal), cut-off command leaves connection unusable, cancelled request leaks inbox SUB, dead commands still executed
description:
NATS supervised-client review (read-only subagent review, SapphireHill, 2026-09-28, origin b8195384a; src/messaging/nats.rs). Findings verified against the source:

1 (HIGH) Reconnect hot loop and fatal non-fatal errors. run_nats_supervisor turned EVERY server -ERR seen in drain_supervisor_frames into a transport failure: it shut down the socket and reconnected. try_reconnect restarted each recovery at attempt 0 with no delay, and CONNECT is not confirmed (non-verbose), so the handshake "succeeds" before the server answers.
   (a) A server that refuses the client after CONNECT (for example -ERR 'Authorization Violation', or Maximum Connections Exceeded) was reconnected immediately and forever, with no delay and no count toward max_reconnect_attempts. That is a TCP connect storm against the server.
   (b) -ERR 'Permissions Violation for Subscription to ...' is NON-fatal (the server keeps the connection), but the client tore the connection down. It then replayed the same denied SUB on reconnect, got the same -ERR, and looped hot. Any message buffered behind the -ERR was dropped with the read buffer.
2 (HIGH) A command cut off mid-exchange left the supervised connection unusable but still open. publish, subscribe, unsubscribe and ping mark connected=false before writing and restore it only on completion; this happens on caller cancellation (nats_io honours cancel) or a write error. The supervisor kept reading the socket.
   - Every later subscribe, unsubscribe, ping or request returned NotConnected until the server dropped the connection, which takes minutes for a stale-connection check. Only publish reconnected inline.
   - send_server_pong writes PONG even when connected=false, so a server PING could append PONG to a torn PUB payload. The server would then deliver a PUB whose payload ends in PONG bytes.
3 (MEDIUM) Cancelled request leaks its inbox subscription. When request()/request_with_headers() are cancelled while waiting for the reply, cleanup_request_subscription calls unsubscribe with the cancelled Cx. unsubscribe checkpoints first and returns Cancelled before sending UNSUB, so the server keeps the _INBOX SUB for the life of the connection, and it is replayed on every reconnect. Needs a masked or supervisor-owned cleanup UNSUB.
4 (MEDIUM) The supervisor executes commands whose caller already gave up. A command whose reply receiver has been dropped (the caller was cancelled while it was queued) is still executed. Examples: a PUB that the caller already saw fail with Cancelled, or a SUB whose Subscription no longer exists. Should skip commands whose reply side is closed, or race the reply-closed signal.

Fix plan: 1 and 2 in one landing (supervisor-only changes: anchored -ERR classification, reconnect streak carried across recoveries, replace the connection after a command leaves it unusable). 3 and 4 stay open on this bead.
close_reason: Fixed by dbec8d9d0+e70db24f5. Landed on main=master (tip e5b320b2d); receipts (fix lane green on the exact candidate, old-code control red, check and clippy on the chain tip) are in the commit message.

title: Borrow checker violation in masque.rs establish_tunnel method
description:
In src/atp/adapter/masque.rs line 197-201, tunnel.overhead_ratio is accessed after the tunnel struct has been moved into the HashMap. This causes a borrow checker error that prevents compilation.

Root cause: After checking tunnel.overhead_ratio on line 197, the tunnel is moved into self.tunnels.insert() on line 201, but then accessed again on line 200 via the same variable.

Fix: Check the overhead_ratio before creating the tunnel struct, or clone the value, or restructure to avoid the move.

title: Lock-order detector false positive: ContendedMutex held on one thread counts as held on another thread sharing the Cx (ASUP-E205 kills an H3 streaming test worker)
description:

## Stack (RUST_BACKTRACE=1, probe 438f97e1a, vmi1152480)
    asupersync::sync::lock_ordering::emit_lock_order_violation
    asupersync::sync::lock_ordering::check_acquire_with_module
    <ContendedMutex<TaskTable>>::lock
    ThreeLaneWorker::with_task_table::<CancellationEffects<Option<CheckpointCancelAck>>, ThreeLaneWorker::execute::{closure#11}>
    ThreeLaneWorker::execute
    ThreeLaneWorker::run_loop_until / run_loop

## Root cause: a detector false positive, not a real inversion
- src/sync/lock_ordering.rs keys held-lock state by `current_owner()`, which is `Task(cx.inner)` whenever a Cx is current and the thread otherwise. This came from a9tx66 (ef4e2566b), so Send (async) guards can migrate with their task.
- The name-tracked path (`record_acquire*`/`record_release*`) is used only by ContendedMutex. Its guard wraps std::sync::MutexGuard and never leaves its thread, yet it was keyed by the current Cx too.
- One Cx is legitimately current on several threads at once: ambient or owner binding of borrowed futures (e.g. net/quic_native/managed_endpoint.rs ~2351/2954/4323, symbol_service native/chunked.rs, cancel/mod.rs, hedge, http2 client). Worker A can hold the sharded `tasks`+`obligations` ContendedMutexes under owner Task(X). Worker B, still in `execute`'s post-poll store-back with X's Cx installed (three_lane.rs `_cx_guard` spans the Pending-path `with_task_table`), then locks `tasks` and sees Obligations "held". It panics, although no thread holds obligations then tasks.
- A second route: a ContendedMutex acquired and released under different current Cx scopes on one thread releases under the wrong owner and leaves a stale entry.
- Release builds do not run the checker, so this is a debug-build and CI reliability defect: it kills a worker's task in debug runs. There is no production deadlock.

## Fix candidate (SapphireHill, bf182e71e, stacked on the pending landing series)
- Name-tracked locks (ContendedMutex) are owned by the thread.
- Movable guard tokens stay task-owned, so the a9tx66 migration test still holds.
- `current_held_snapshot` is this thread's locks plus the current task's movable guards.
- `clear_held_locks` clears both.

Regression test `sync::lock_ordering::tests::a_thread_bound_lock_is_not_held_by_another_thread_sharing_the_cx`:
- Two threads share one Cx. One holds ContendedMutex "obligations"; the other acquires "tasks". Expected: no panic, and the other thread sees no held ranks.
- A real same-thread inversion still panics.

Control bb2eb0796 (the test on the old tracker) must fail. Probe 6dba034a2 runs the H3 streaming suite 60 times on the fix.

## Acceptance
- Old-red control receipt.
- `--lib sync::` green.
- 60 consecutive full-target runs of quic_h3_listener_streaming on the fix, where C2 failed within 15.
- clippy and check green.

title: ATP RQ: authenticate control transcript and bind symbol tags to sessions
description:
Current posture: RQ requires either a nonempty shared key or the explicit unauthenticated lab override, and keyed mode HMAC-authenticates UDP symbol envelopes. The reliable TCP control stream remains unauthenticated: sender/receiver identity, handshake, manifest, NeedMore, and completion frames are not cryptographically bound. Symbol tags are also not bound to a fresh session challenge, so captured valid symbols can be replayed across sessions.

Security impact: an active MITM can substitute the manifest/control transcript or replay signed symbols even though random forged UDP payloads fail HMAC and final bytes are checked against the received manifest. Integrity versus an unauthenticated manifest is not sender authenticity.

Fix: authenticate and transcript-bind the control channel, derive per-session symbol authentication from a fresh challenge/transfer identity, reject replay and cross-session tags, and preserve the explicit trusted-lab escape hatch. Acceptance requires real loopback MITM/tamper/replay tests for handshake, manifest, NeedMore, completion, and symbols. QUIC remains the production choice on untrusted networks until this closes.
notes: CobaltForge partial option-a implementation staged in working tree for src/net/atp/transport_rq/mod.rs + tests/atp_rq_loopback_e2e.rs: RqConfig now fails closed unless symbol_auth_context is provided or trusted unauthenticated mode is explicit; UDP RaptorQ datagrams carry per-symbol auth tags when enabled; handshake rejects auth-mode mismatch; receiver uses DecodingPipeline::with_auth when configured. Local non-cargo gates passed: rustfmt --edition 2024 --check on changed files and git diff --check on changed files. Single scoped RCH lane was run exactly once with shared target: RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/rch_target_asupersync_atp_rq CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 RUSTFLAGS='-D warnings -C debuginfo=0' cargo test -p asupersync --lib --features test-internals net::atp::transport_rq::tests::signed_datagram_roundtrips -- --nocapture. It failed before reaching the transport test due unrelated peer-owned dirty src/runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs private_interfaces error: LocalReadyQueueInner is more private than ScopedLocalReady::new. No retry/local cargo fallback per RCH discipline. Remaining beyond this partial: transport_tcp/control-channel/manifest authentication still not implemented, so do not claim full Byzantine injection prevention yet.

title: ATP-A3: Add packet protection and TLS provider boundary for native QUIC
description: Create the internal provider boundary that lets native QUIC perform Initial, Handshake, 0-RTT where supported, and 1-RTT packet protection without depending on an external QUIC implementation.
design: Do not hand-roll low-level cryptographic primitives in transfer code. Define traits and state transitions that connect existing TLS/security surfaces to QUIC packet protection, key derivation, header protection, key update, and transcript evidence.

title: Resilience combinator audit: stale half-open probes refill the cleared sliding window so a recovery re-opens the breaker; rate limiter sub-ms period never refills; RateLimiter::reset not atomic
description:
Read-only audit of src/combinator/{circuit_breaker,bulkhead,rate_limit,retry}.rs and src/time/interval.rs at 104817b1f (origin + SapphireHill stacks N/P), SapphireHill audit agent round 5, 10-05. The MEDIUM was confirmed by re-reading the code.

## MEDIUM
M1. Stale half-open probes write into the cleared sliding window, so a successful recovery re-opens the breaker (circuit_breaker.rs window_records_outcomes ~779).
- window_records_outcomes returns true for every Permit::Probe, even when the probe's half-open episode has already re-opened. The Normal-permit version of this bug was fixed; probes were left out.
- Trigger (reachable through CircuitBreakerMiddleware under concurrent requests): half_open_max_probes 4, success_threshold 1, sliding window minimum_calls 4 and rate 0.5.
  - 4 failures open the breaker.
  - 4 probes are admitted. P1 fails and re-opens the breaker; P2..P4 fail while it is open. The window becomes [F,F,F].
  - The next recovery probe succeeds and closes the breaker, recording S. The window [F,F,F,S] has a 0.75 failure rate, so the breaker re-opens immediately.
- Impact: a healthy dependency is held off for an extra open_duration, times_opened is inflated, and a spurious Closed->Open callback fires.
- FIX (SapphireHill, Q2): a probe's outcome is recorded only while its own half-open episode is current, or when its success just closed the breaker.

## LOW
- L2. rate_limit.rs ~368: the period is truncated to whole milliseconds. A sub-millisecond period never refills (retry_after = Duration::MAX), the SlidingWindowRateLimiter never expires entries, and a 1.9 ms period allows 1.9x the rate. Fix: nanosecond arithmetic, or reject period < 1 ms.
- L3. RateLimiter::reset (~893-909) is not atomic across the bucket and the queue. A concurrent process_queue grants from the fresh bucket, and then clear() drops those entries without a refund. Bulkhead::reset had the same race and was fixed by holding the queue lock.
- L4. SlidingWindowRateLimiter::compute_window_cost re-sums the whole window on every call: O(rate) per acquire.
- L5. retry.rs ~237: with initial_delay 0, the delay jumps to max_delay once powi overflows (attempt > ~1025).
- L6. RateLimitedRetryPolicy and RetryTokenBucket are not wired into retry(); the docs say they prevent retry storms.

## Adjacent (web/middleware.rs ~735)
RateLimitMiddleware commits its permit only after the handler finishes. A handler future dropped mid-flight (client disconnect, timeout, deadline cancel, panic) gets its tokens back although the downstream work ran, so a client that abandons requests on purpose is not rate limited. This is related to a1q12q LOW 5 (refund on panic, test-pinned): an owner decision.

Judged SOUND: interval.rs (missed-tick behaviours, Time::MAX guard), bulkhead.rs (permit accounting on every path, FIFO, reset), the Retry future (cancel checks, drain, Cx clock and RNG), sleep.rs (as a dependency).

Receipts are in each commit message: clippy -D warnings, the native cancellation contract and the touched modules, on the landed tree or on one that differs from it only in files these commits do not touch, and a control for every behaviour fix, with the fix reverted and its tests kept. title: [mock-code-finder][raptorq] Add RFC6330 conformance coverage report that distinguishes live, fixture-only, skipped, and blocker states
description:
Background: Once the CLI registers tests and the core tests call live implementation seams, future agents need a truthful coverage report that says which RFC6330 clauses are live-checked, fixture-only, skipped, expected-fail, or blocked. The current output can look polished while hiding that no tests were registered or that a test only validates fixtures.

Goal: make the RaptorQ RFC6330 conformance report self-auditing. It should not allow fixture-only tests to count as full production conformance, and CI/operator summaries must expose skipped or blocked clauses.

Reasoning: asupersync is spec-first. A conformance report must represent evidence quality, not just pass counts.
acceptance_criteria: Report schema includes clause ID, requirement level, implementation evidence kind, test status, blocker ID if blocked, fixture reference, production seam path, and exact command that produced the result. CLI summaries must count live-checked separately from fixture-only and skipped. CI mode must expose the same distinction in JSONL. Unit/golden tests must pin at least one live pass, fixture-only warning, skipped case, expected failure, and blocker case. title: [SECURITY] EarlyDataReplayProtection is a PHANTOM control: 0-RTT replay strategy is never enforced on the request path (validate_request_for_early_data has ZERO production callers; the doc-prescribed gate tls_stream.received_early_data() does not exist) — residual gap of CLOSED ycuuwy
description:
Phase-C phantom/unwired-control hunt (SapphireHill 2026-06-14). asupersync-ycuuwy (P1, CLOSED 2026-05-26, 'TLS 1.3 0-RTT replay vulnerability requires application-layer validation') added the EarlyDataReplayProtection control surface but its per-request ENFORCEMENT is unreachable, so the control is phantom: an operator who enables 0-RTT and selects a replay strategy gets a FALSE sense of replay protection.

WHAT ycuuwy DELIVERED (verified present + working):
- enum EarlyDataReplayProtection { None(default), SafeMethodsOnly, IdempotencyKeys, NonceValidation, UnprotectedForTesting } (src/tls/acceptor.rs:350).
- BUILD-TIME gate (FAIL-CLOSED, works): TlsAcceptorBuilder::build() refuses to enable 0-RTT (early_data_max_bytes>0) when protection==None (acceptor.rs:992-1001). early_data_max_bytes default 0 = 0-RTT off by default (acceptor.rs:588). So operators must explicitly opt in AND pick a strategy.
- helper EarlyDataReplayProtection::validate_request_for_early_data(method, has_idempotency_key, has_valid_nonce) (acceptor.rs:174-207) that returns Err for unsafe methods / missing key / missing nonce.

THE PHANTOM GAP (verified by ref-trace):
1. validate_request_for_early_data() has ZERO production callers. rg over src/: every call site (acceptor.rs:2543-2755) is inside #[cfg(test)]; the only non-test reference is a doc example (acceptor.rs:165). The HTTP server request pipeline (h1/h2/h3) never invokes it.
2. The doc (acceptor.rs:161-172) prescribes the intended use: 'In your HTTP handler: if tls_stream.received_early_data() { acceptor.early_data_replay_protection().validate_request_for_early_data(...) }'. But received_early_data() DOES NOT EXIST: rg 'received_early_data' src/ returns exactly one hit — that doc line (acceptor.rs:165). The TlsStream (src/tls/stream.rs) exposes sni_hostname() and alpn_protocol() accessors but NO early-data accessor (no received_early_data/is_early_data/early_data flag). So neither the library nor any application can determine whether a given request arrived as 0-RTT early data.
3. Meanwhile 0-RTT IS actually enabled at the rustls layer when the operator opts in: build() writes config.max_early_data_size = self.early_data_max_bytes (acceptor.rs:1187). So early data is accepted on the wire, but the chosen replay strategy (SafeMethodsOnly/IdempotencyKeys/NonceValidation) is never consulted for any request.

EFFECT: a deployment that enables 0-RTT with enable_early_data_with_protection(n) + with_early_data_replay_protection(SafeMethodsOnly) believes state-changing early-data requests (POST/PUT/DELETE) will be rejected with 425 Too Early. They are NOT — a captured 0-RTT POST replayed within the ticket window is processed normally (duplicate state change / financial / data-integrity impact, exactly the threat ycuuwy described). This is WORSE than no control because it manufactures false confidence. CLASS: same phantom-control family as asupersync-securityconfig-unwired-phantom-controls-x7ad3b and the unaddressed-item pattern of f4mdcr/b1fojq.

SEVERITY: filed P2 because 0-RTT is OFF by default and must be explicitly enabled (real-world exposure gated on operator opt-in); escalate to P1 for any deployment that actually enables 0-RTT, since there the replay protection is entirely absent despite being configured.

FIX OPTIONS (maintainer's call):
  (a) WIRE THE SIGNAL + ENFORCE: surface an early-data flag from the rustls ServerConnection handshake (rustls exposes whether early data was accepted) through TlsStream as received_early_data()/is_early_data(), thread it into the h1/h2 request context, and have the server pipeline AUTOMATICALLY call validate_request_for_early_data() (mapping Err -> 425 Too Early) for early-data requests using the acceptor's configured strategy. This is the real fix; spans src/tls/stream.rs + src/tls/acceptor.rs + the h1/h2 server request path (NOTE: src/http/h2/connection.rs + stream.rs are peer-dirty for mfqfst right now — coordinate or stage after).
  (b) FAIL CLOSED UNTIL WIRED: until (a) lands, do NOT actually enable 0-RTT on the wire for the non-test strategies — i.e. only set config.max_early_data_size when protection==UnprotectedForTesting (explicit test acknowledgment), and for SafeMethodsOnly/IdempotencyKeys/NonceValidation either keep max_early_data_size=0 (0-RTT effectively disabled) with a loud WARN that enforcement is not yet wired, or make build() return an error stating per-request enforcement is unavailable. This removes the false-confidence vector at the cost of 0-RTT not actually functioning until (a).
  (c) at minimum, fix the doc example (received_early_data() is not a real API) and document that EarlyDataReplayProtection is currently NOT enforced by the server pipeline.

Recommend (a) bundled with the in-flight h2 listener work (mfqfst), or (b) as the immediate fail-closed stopgap. Verified by SapphireHill via ref-trace; no code changed in this bead. Related: ycuuwy (closed parent), y0gm5q (explicit max_early_data_size write), x7ad3b (config-layer phantom-control twin).
close_reason: Fixed fail-closed in 67723b12e. build() now REJECTS 0-RTT for SafeMethodsOnly/IdempotencyKeys/NonceValidation (per-request enforcement unwired = phantom), consistent with the existing ycuuwy None-gate; only EarlyDataReplayProtection::UnprotectedForTesting (explicit no-protection ack) or 0-RTT-disabled builds. So replayable 0-RTT early data is never accepted on the wire for the un-enforced strategies => replayed 0-RTT is rejected. Also re-exported EarlyDataReplayProtection (was in a private module, unnameable externally -> the pub with_early_data_replay_protection param type was unusable) and fixed the misleading validate_request_for_early_data doc (prescribed non-existent received_early_data()). Tests: NEW tests/early_data_replay_failclosed.rs 6/6 PASS via rch (3 strategies + None fail closed; UnprotectedForTesting only build path; default no-0-RTT builds); 3 in-lib acceptor tests updated to fail-closed posture. Gates: rustfmt OK; integration 6/6 green (lib compiled clean, only peer three_lane.rs warning); clippy -D warnings peer-blocked by uncommitted three_lane refactor, my lib changes add zero rustc warnings. FOLLOW-UP (real fix, option a): wire received_early_data() through TlsStream + h1/h2/h3 -> auto 425 Too Early using the configured strategy; spans the peer-dirty mfqfst h2 pipeline. Pushed main+master.

title: Durable journal reopen can see Locked after the owner is dropped: flock shared with a concurrently forked child (5 lib tests flaked at once)
description:
## Observed (2026-09-30, hz4)
In one full default lib run (LTlib at 792232cec), 5 durable-journal tests failed with Err(Locked) when reopening a journal right after dropping its owner:
- distributed::membership::durable::tests::real_file_locks_and_restores_revocation_after_all_owners_are_dropped (tests.rs:220)
- distributed::symbol_service::durable::tests::actual_file_reopens_with_exact_batches_and_exclusive_lock (tests.rs:305)
- distributed::symbol_service::durable::tests::actual_file_torn_tail_is_preserved_and_committed_data_is_readable (tests.rs:332)
- distributed::membership::durable::runtime::tests::projection_callback_panic_closes_owner_but_returns_journal_for_recovery (runtime/tests.rs:146)
- distributed::membership::durable::runtime::tests::durable_decision_aborts_real_checked_obligation_before_reopen (runtime/tests.rs:67)

All five failed within about 13 s of each other. The same tree passed them alone (LTdur, 37/0) and in a second full run (LTlib3, 23913/0). The base 274346785 full run was also 23913/0. The code has not changed since 09-19, and none of these tests goes through LabRuntimeTarget. The fix under test (rug2tz) changes only that loop.

## Likely cause (hypothesis, not yet proven)
Both journals lock with std File::try_lock (flock). An flock belongs to the open file description, and it is released only when every descriptor sharing that description is closed. The lib test binary runs about 24k tests on parallel threads, and about 135 lib sites spawn child processes (process::*, parent_death, ATP, ...). A child forked while a journal file is open shares its description until exec closes the O_CLOEXEC descriptor. If a test drops its journal and reopens it inside that fork-to-exec window, the lock still appears held. A burst of spawns under load makes this likely enough to hit several durable tests at once.

## Why it matters beyond the flake
A production process that reopens a journal (restart or recovery in the same process) while another thread spawns a child can get a transient Locked, too. The durable open paths have no documented retry for this case.

## Work
1. Prove the mechanism. For example: a test that holds a locked journal, forks a child that sleeps before exec (pre_exec sleep), drops the journal and reopens; expect Locked until the child execs. Then repeat with the child exec'ing immediately.
2. Decide the remedy:
   - (a) the test helpers retry a Locked reopen for a bounded time;
   - (b) the open API documents the transient case and offers a bounded open_with_retry;
   - (c) switch to OFD locks (fcntl F_OFD_SETLK), which are shared across fork in the same way, so this is no fix. Document why.
   Do not weaken the tests' assertion that a second concurrent owner is refused.

title: HttpClient never asks for or decodes compressed responses: add opt-in gzip/Brotli response decompression (compression feature)
description:
HttpClient never uses the crate's gzip/Brotli decompressors: it sends no Accept-Encoding and returns encoded bodies as received (discovery finding #5 of 2026-10-07, origin 921d94484: Gzip/Deflate/BrotliDecompressor in http/compress.rs are used only in tests; h1/http_client.rs has no Accept-Encoding and never decodes Content-Encoding). This is a parity gap with reqwest's gzip/brotli options.

Plan (additive, `compression` feature, off by default): HttpClientBuilder::response_decompression(bool), plus HttpClientConfig::with_response_decompression and response_decompression().
- A buffered request whose own and default headers name no Accept-Encoding sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip, br`.
- Its final response is decoded (codings in reverse order) within max_body_size (16 MiB default), and Content-Encoding and Content-Length are removed.
- Decode failure or exceeding the limit gives ClientError::Io.
- A caller-chosen Accept-Encoding, streaming requests and other codings are returned as received.
- deflate is excluded (raw vs zlib framing; see the deflate bead).

Acceptance, as end-to-end tests against a canned TCP server:
- gzip and br are decoded, and the request carried the header;
- a caller-set Accept-Encoding gets the body as sent;
- a default client sends no Accept-Encoding;
- a body decoding past max_body_size fails with Io.
A control that disables the header, the decode and the caller-choice check must turn the corresponding tests red.

title: [security-audit-for-saas] grpc/streaming flow-control — verify cap, back-pressure, no infinite buffer
description:
Security/performance audit bead for grpc streaming flow control under misbehaving clients.

Problem:
- Server streaming and bidi streaming must apply bounded buffering and back-pressure when clients stop reading, send oversized messages, or ignore flow-control expectations.
- If buffers can grow without a cap, a single client can consume unbounded memory or delay cancellation/drain paths.

Required design:
1. Identify the production streaming send/receive queue and flow-control budget seam.
2. Prove bounded memory under slow-reader, non-reader, burst-writer, and cancellation scenarios.
3. Preserve correct message ordering and terminal status/trailer delivery for well-behaved clients.
4. Map cap/back-pressure violations to deterministic gRPC status or cancellation outcomes.
5. Emit counters or test-observable diagnostics for queue depth, budget usage, blocked sends, dropped/rejected messages if applicable, and cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover normal streaming, slow reader back-pressure, non-reader timeout/cancellation, configured buffer cap, oversized inbound frame, many small frames, server cancellation while blocked on send, client half-close while buffered messages remain, trailer/status ordering, and no leaked stream obligations. Integration/e2e script coverage must log stream ID, client behavior profile, configured flow-control cap, queue depth over time, bytes buffered, send/receive poll states, back-pressure events, cancellation/drain events, status/trailers, and final bounded-memory/no-leak verdict. Validation must include rch rustfmt plus targeted rch cargo test/check for grpc streaming and flow-control surfaces.

title: web::Response uses HashMap so multiple Set-Cookie values silently overwrite
description: src/web/response.rs:136 — pub headers: HashMap<String, String>. Set-Cookie is RFC 9110's canonical multi-valued response header (each cookie ships as its own header line), but a HashMap can only hold one value per key. Calling Response::set_header("set-cookie", X) (or the .header() builder) twice overwrites the first cookie. Real exploit path: src/web/session.rs:845 and 849 — SessionMiddleware sets the session cookie AFTER the inner handler runs via resp.set_header("set-cookie", ...). Any cookie the inner handler set (e.g., a CSRF cookie, remember-me cookie, post-login flash cookie) is silently dropped. The application thinks both cookies shipped; only the session cookie does. Affects Set-Cookie security primitives in any composed middleware stack. Fix: store Set-Cookie entries in a separate Vec<String> on Response, route set_header("set-cookie", ...) into that vec (append, not overwrite), expose append_set_cookie() as the explicit API, and have wire-format writers emit each entry as its own Set-Cookie header line. Severity HIGH — silent cookie loss in middleware composition is a security primitive failure.
close_reason: Landed in bebd96dc9. Response now stores Set-Cookie in a separate Vec<String> set_cookies; append_set_cookie is the explicit append-only API; set_header(set-cookie, _) routes through it; has_header/header_value/remove_header/ensure_header all special-case set-cookie. SessionMiddleware uses append_set_cookie. CR/LF/NUL still stripped. Regression test middleware_preserves_inner_handler_set_cookie wraps a CsrfEmittingHandler in SessionLayer and asserts BOTH cookies (csrf_token, session_id) appear in resp.set_cookies — pre-fix only one would survive. Plus 3 unit tests in response.rs (overwrite, CRLF strip, drain). cargo check --lib passes. Test verification on full lib build blocked by other agents broken WIP (proptest-using metamorphic_tests, mpsc_message_preservation_metamorphic) — manually reviewed.

title: [ambient-time] lab/config.rs: LabConfig::from_time derives seed from SystemTime::now without a replay-determinism warning — invites accidental flaky CI tests
description:
src/lab/config.rs:193-201 — LabConfig::from_time:

```
/// Creates a lab configuration from the current time (for quick testing).
#[must_use]
pub fn from_time() -> Self {
    use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};
    let seed = SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map_or(42, |d| d.as_nanos().min(u128::from(u64::MAX)) as u64);
    Self::new(seed)
}
```

The doc comment says 'for quick testing' but does NOT warn that the resulting LabRuntime is NOT replay-deterministic — every call produces a different seed. A user who reads the docs sees 'quick testing' and reaches for from_time in CI, getting:

  (a) Flaky CI failures on any test that asserts a deterministic outcome (oracle violations, trace fingerprints, certificate hashes). The flake reproduces only on the seed that triggered it — and that seed is gone forever because next CI run uses a fresh wall-clock.
  (b) Crashpack hash instability: every from_time-built LabRuntime produces a different fingerprint, defeating crashpack deduplication.
  (c) Lab/replay determinism boundary leak: the asupersync core invariant 'lab replay is byte-identical given the same seed' assumes the seed is durable; from_time silently violates that assumption every call.

The asupersync 'no ambient authority' invariant explicitly forbids this shape — every effect (including PRNG seeding) must flow through Cx or be explicit to the caller. from_time hides the wall-clock dependency behind a #[must_use] constructor that looks ergonomically equivalent to LabConfig::new(N).

Fix direction:
  1. Either deprecate with #[deprecated(note = "use LabConfig::new(seed) — from_time uses wall_clock and is non-replayable")] so any CI usage flags via -D warnings.
  2. Or document the non-determinism explicitly in the doc comment AND emit a one-time WARN log on first invocation per process.
  3. Or rename to from_wall_clock_seed_NON_REPLAYABLE so the foot-gun is impossible to ignore.
  4. Or remove entirely — LabConfig::new(rand::random()) (with explicit caller-side randomness) is just as easy and makes the wall-clock dependency visible.

Source: /reality-check on src/lab/* (2026-04-26).
close_reason: from_time deprecated; from_time_unstable alias added for explicit non-replayable use; HEAD has changes

title: [mock-ambient-time] transport/mock.rs SimTransportConfig defaults time_getter to wall_clock_now — tests inherit non-deterministic time
description:
src/transport/mock.rs:21-22,65 — SimTransportConfig defaults its time_getter to a closure that calls crate::time::wall_now(). Tests that don't explicitly override time_getter capture wall-clock readings into the simulator's internal state.

Threat model: this is a test-fixture ambient-time leak. Consequences:
  (a) Test flakiness when wall-clock progress between operations affects ordering / coarsening.
  (b) Replay tools that diff test runs see different time_getter outputs across executions.
  (c) Latency assertions (e.g., 'less than 50ms') become non-deterministic — they pass on fast machines and fail on slow ones.
  (d) The lab-runtime invariant 'tests are replayable' is violated for any test using SimTransportConfig::default() without overriding time_getter.

Why MEDIUM: this is a test-fixture concern, not a production correctness issue. But it propagates into the project's testing posture: tests build trust in the runtime; tests with ambient time can't be trusted to surface regressions deterministically.

Fix direction:
  1. Default time_getter to a closure that returns Time::ZERO and require tests to explicitly opt into wall-clock.
  2. Add a SimTransportConfig::deterministic(virtual_clock) constructor that wires the getter to virtual time.
  3. Update existing test setups (search for SimTransportConfig::default()) to pass an explicit cx-aware time-getter.
  4. Add a clippy-like lint or build-time check: if any test imports SimTransportConfig::default(), warn.

Severity MEDIUM (test-only impact, but high-value because it undermines the deterministic-replay framework).

Source: /multi-pass-bug-hunting on src/transport/* deepest pass (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Fixed: SimTransportConfig default time_getter is now deterministic_zero_time; with_wall_clock_time() opt-in added (commit dd6e3b705)

title: [alien-graveyard] Replace scheduler EXP3 cancel-streak tuner with discounted UCB
description:
Observed:
- `src/runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs:269-379` implements `AdaptiveCancelStreakPolicy` as a deterministic EXP3 controller over the fixed cancel-streak arm set `[4, 8, 16, 32, 64]`.
- `src/runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs:357-379` applies the classic EXP3 importance-weighted update `reward_hat = reward / p`, exponentiates it, then samples the next arm from the probability simplex.
- `src/runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs:1202-1203` and `2675-2696` show this policy is on the hot adaptive path for every worker epoch.
- The reward here is already bounded in `[0, 1]` (`reward_against()` at `src/runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs:233-265`) and comes from a directly observed scheduler epoch, not an adversarial loss oracle.

Paper / algorithm:
- Replace EXP3 with **discounted UCB** (Auer/Cesa-Bianchi/Fischer 2002 for UCB1; Garivier/Moulines, *On Upper-Confidence Bound Policies for Non-Stationary Bandit Problems*, arXiv:0805.3415, for discounted/sliding-window UCB under changing reward regimes).
- Why discounted UCB instead of Thompson here: same fixed 5-arm action space, bounded rewards, deterministic replay requirements, and a workload that shifts between cancel-flood and mixed-lane epochs. UCB keeps exploration explicit without the current `reward / p` variance spike or RNG-driven simplex sampling.

Why this is a better fit:
- EXP3 is robust to adversarial rewards, but it pays for that robustness with higher-variance importance weighting. In this file that shows up as `reward / p` amplification plus exponent/clamp logic even though the scheduler observes a stable bounded reward each epoch.
- The scheduler workload is not fully stationary, so plain UCB1 is not enough; discounted/sliding-window UCB is the right middle ground: faster convergence than EXP3 in stable phases, but still able to forget stale evidence after mode shifts.

Invariants preserved:
- Keep the existing candidate limit set `[4, 8, 16, 32, 64]`; only the arm-selection policy changes.
- Preserve the fairness certificate and hard bound semantics: `cancel_streak_limit` remains chosen from the same finite set, so `observed_max_cancel_streak <= effective_limit` stays the governing invariant.
- Preserve per-worker independence, fallback-cancel semantics, and current Lyapunov/deadline/fairness reward definition.
- Preserve deterministic replay/golden coverage: arm choice should remain deterministic for a fixed seed/workload, and ideally become easier to reason about because updates are confidence-index based instead of probability-simplex sampled.

Expected gain:
- Lower adaptive-limit oscillation and faster convergence on steady cancel-flood traces.
- Less numerical fragility in the hot path by deleting the `reward / p` importance-weight blow-up, exponentiation, and simplex renormalization.
- Better replay stability and interpretability of why one arm was chosen (empirical mean + confidence bonus) when auditing fairness drift.

Acceptance sketch:
1. Introduce a discounted-UCB policy alongside the current EXP3 implementation behind a narrow internal strategy enum so replay/golden tests can compare both.
2. Reuse existing adaptive replay helpers/goldens in `three_lane.rs` to assert no fairness invariant regression and to compare convergence/oscillation under steady and regime-shifted traces.
3. Add a focused benchmark or deterministic replay metric proving fewer arm switches / lower non-cancel stall variance at equal or better fairness-certificate outcomes.

title: quic_native managed loop: one ENOBUFS ends every connection, and a local oversized packet retires every connection to its peer address (send-error misclassification)
description:
## Defect (split from dvdvyi, sub-defect 4; source-audited at 21f947faf)
The managed QUIC loop (managed_endpoint.rs ~1994-2034, EndpointEvent::Sent(Err)) classifies send errors in two buckets only:
- ConnectionRefused / ConnectionReset / AddrNotAvailable / InvalidInput / HostUnreachable / NetworkUnreachable / PermissionDenied: treated as the DESTINATION's fault, retiring every connection and accept to that peer address.
- Everything else: `return Err(ManagedEndpointError::UdpEndpoint(..))`, which ENDS THE WHOLE LOOP and every connection on the endpoint.

Two consequences:
(a) Transient kernel backpressure (ENOBUFS has no specific std kind, and ENOMEM maps to OutOfMemory) kills every connection. Under UDP load on Linux, ENOBUFS is routine.
(b) endpoint.rs ~575-600 raises InvalidInput for LOCAL faults: "packet size N exceeds endpoint limit" and "empty managed send batch". One oversized packet that we build retires every connection to that peer address, e.g. all clients behind one NAT.

## Fix design
Classify into four classes:
- destination: retire the peer, as today, minus InvalidInput.
- transient backpressure (ENOBUFS by raw errno, OutOfMemory, WouldBlock): keep pending_outgoing intact and schedule a retry after a short bounded backoff via the endpoint's timer. Never spin. Count retries in metrics.
- local packet fault: drop only the offending packet, trace it, and fail that connection if the router can attribute it. Use a distinct error from endpoint.rs instead of overloading InvalidInput.
- fatal (EBADF, ENOTSOCK...): end the loop, as today.

## Tests
A test-only send-error injection seam on the managed UDP endpoint:
(1) one ENOBUFS then success: every packet is delivered, the loop survives, retry metric = 1, no busy loop (bounded polls);
(2) an oversized local packet: only it is dropped, and another connection to the same peer address still delivers;
(3) the existing native_loop_sends_healthy_peer_after_bad_destination_and_receives_during_load stays green.
Old-red: (1) and (2) fail on the current classification.
close_reason: Landed fa3eee4ff (main=master bc737135a). Send errors now fall into four classes: resource shortage (ENOBUFS/ENOMEM/EMFILE/ENFILE/OutOfMemory/WouldBlock) backs off 2 to 64 ms through the bound timer; destination errors retire the peer only when the OS reported them; oversized local datagrams fail only their own connection or admission; everything else still ends the loop. A committed prefix with a stringified error retries the tail. Old red: control ada9bf7d3 failed both new native tests. New green: 185/0 module run (2b2f595dc). Tip gates on 492ec0a75: tls clippy -D warnings 0 diagnostics and the default all-targets check 0/0.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Implementation (SapphireHill), E1 6047a2591 stacked on R1 6ef0404c0; gates queued (lib tests with tls, old-red control 41f7b4623, tls clippy, default check).

One design correction from the source: the existing test native_loop_sends_healthy_peer_after_bad_destination_and_receives_during_load plants 127.0.0.1:0, which Linux rejects with EINVAL. So an OS-level InvalidInput really is a destination fault, and removing InvalidInput from the destination class would regress it. The anchor is the error's origin instead: the destination class now requires raw_os_error().is_some(). An error the endpoint synthesizes (its size check, the empty-batch guard) can never retire a peer. This fails closed: an unknown synthesized error still ends the loop, as before.

Classes in the managed loop (managed_endpoint.rs, EndpointEvent::Sent(Err)):
1. Interrupted: cancellation (unchanged).
2. Resource shortage (send_error_is_resource_shortage): WouldBlock, OutOfMemory, raw ENOBUFS/ENOMEM/EMFILE/ENFILE (WSAENOBUFS/WSAEMFILE on Windows), mirroring tcp::listener::is_accept_resource_exhaustion. The queue stays intact and sends park until send_backoff_until. That deadline is folded into refresh_timer, so the loop's one bound timer wakes it, and receives, timers and the application keep running. The delay is 2ms doubling to a 64ms cap (the HTTP/remote listeners' constants). A successful send resets the streak.
3. Destination (send_error_blames_destination): the old kind list, now only for OS-reported errors. Retires the peer as before.
4. Anything else: ends the loop, as before.

Oversized local packets: drop_oversized_outgoing runs before every poll. A datagram above the socket's own max_packet_size is removed and fails only the connection that built it (remove_connection, or fail_authenticated_accept_at for an admission). Other connections to the same peer address keep sending. The endpoint's size check is now unreachable from the loop.

Partial batch: a committed prefix with a stringified error (a later sendmmsg chunk failed) no longer ends the loop. The unsent tail is retried, and that retry reports the concrete error kind to the classification above, which is the contract the portable path already documents. Each such turn commits at least one packet, so it cannot spin.

Metrics: EndpointMetrics is a public struct with all-public fields, so no new field (a v0.4.3 break for struct literals). The existing send_errors counts each failure; the streak is private.

Test seam: QuicUdpEndpoint gets a cfg(test) queue, inject_send_errors, which poll_send_batch returns before the socket and counts in send_errors like a real failure. Its config() accessor loses its tls gate because the loop reads the size limit in every build.

Tests (managed_endpoint.rs):
- native_loop_backs_off_from_send_buffer_shortage_and_delivers_every_packet (unix): 5 injected shortages (ENOBUFS x4, OutOfMemory x1) then 8 packets. All arrive in order; send_errors=5, packets_sent=8; at least 40ms elapsed (a capped backoff, not an immediate retry); at most 64 loop polls (it parks rather than yield-spins); streak and deadline cleared afterwards.
- native_loop_drops_only_an_oversized_datagram_and_keeps_its_peer: max_packet_size 4, two connections to one peer, the first queues 5 bytes. Only the second's datagram arrives, 1 connection stays active, the first is ConnectionNotFound, and the second can still be taken.
- send_errors_blame_a_destination_only_when_the_os_reported_them: raw EINVAL blames the destination, a synthesized InvalidInput does not; ENOBUFS is a shortage; EBADF is neither.
Old-red control 41f7b4623: the same tests, with the loop's classification, oversized drop and partial-batch handling reverted to origin's.
