title: [obs-reality-check] observability/metrics.rs: Metrics::{counter,gauge,histogram,summary} accept arbitrary names with NO cardinality cap — unbounded HashMap growth and Prometheus cardinality explosion
description: src/observability/metrics.rs:335-365 Metrics::counter/gauge/histogram/summary insert into HashMap<String, ...> keyed by the raw name parameter with no validation, no allowlist, no cardinality limit, and no eviction. A caller that computes a metric name from request data (e.g., format!('requests_user_{user_id}'), per-tenant metric names, per-shard suffixes) makes the registry grow without bound. Long-running services accumulate one entry per distinct name forever — both an in-process memory leak AND a Prometheus cardinality-explosion bug downstream. Compare with src/observability/otel.rs:83 OtelMetrics which DOES have max_cardinality + CardinalityLimitStrategy. The two registries have asymmetric guarantees; the basic Metrics is the easy-to-misuse one. Mitigation: add max_metric_count: usize to Metrics with a default cap (e.g., 10_000), reject creations beyond the cap, and log/trace once when the cap fires (at most once per process). Severity HIGH for any deployment that derives metric names from user input.
close_reason: Fixed in 9e9983482. Added DEFAULT_METRIC_CARDINALITY_CAP = 10_000 + Metrics::with_cardinality_cap(cap) builder. Each metric kind (counters, gauges, histograms, summaries) is capped INDEPENDENTLY at that value. When the kind's BTreeMap reaches the cap, fresh-name requests route to a shared overflow bucket named 'asupersync_metric_cardinality_overflow' so observations are NOT silently dropped — they aggregate into one named entry the operator can spot in the Prometheus output. Per-kind warn-once latch via AtomicBool prevents log flooding under sustained pressure. Per-kind overflow-rejection counters (AtomicU64 × 4) exposed via Metrics::overflow_rejections() for SREs to monitor cardinality pressure without parsing logs. cap == 0 disables the limit (legacy unbounded escape hatch — non-breaking for callers that explicitly opt out). Default constructor (Metrics::new / Metrics::default) uses the 10k default. Existing-name lookups never count against the cap (BTreeMap::contains_key check before insertion). Four regression tests: cardinality_cap_routes_fresh_names_to_overflow_bucket (verifies overflow-bucket aggregation + stable map size), cardinality_cap_is_per_kind_not_shared (verifies counter overflow doesn't affect gauge/histogram/summary growth), cardinality_cap_zero_disables_limit (50 distinct counters under cap=0 — verifies escape hatch), cardinality_cap_warn_latches_per_kind (100 overflows after first don't re-flip the latch + per-kind isolation of warn flag). Lib build is blocked by pre-existing concurrent-agent Outcome<T,E> errors in record/task.rs — unrelated to this fix. UBS clean (12 critical loose-equality findings are JS-rule false positives + 3 panic! are test asserts).

title: [testing-fuzz] TLS certificate chain validation pathological cases
description:
**Target function**: src/tls/connector.rs certificate verification and src/tls/types.rs CertificateChain parsing/validation

**Problem**: Existing TLS fuzzing covers basic handshake flows but doesn't exercise pathological certificate chain validation edge cases that can trigger complex ASN.1 parsing bugs, certificate verification logic errors, or memory exhaustion in chain building algorithms.

**Input shape**: X.509 certificate chains with:
- Deeply nested certificate chains (chain length limits)
- Self-signed certificates with circular dependencies
- Invalid ASN.1 DER encoding edge cases (length overflow, indefinite length)
- Certificate validity period edge cases (not-before/not-after boundary conditions)
- Subject Alternative Name parsing (malformed DNS names, IP addresses, URI formats)
- Extension parsing edge cases (critical vs non-critical, unknown extensions)
- Public key algorithm edge cases (weak keys, unsupported algorithms, malformed parameters)

**Bugs to look for**:
- ASN.1 parser buffer overflow or use-after-free
- Certificate chain validation bypass via malformed certificates
- Memory exhaustion in chain building algorithms
- Integer overflow in certificate validity calculations
- DNS name validation bypass in Subject Alternative Names
- Signature verification bypass via algorithm confusion
- Time-of-check-time-of-use bugs in certificate validation

**Implementation**: Structure-aware fuzzer that generates syntactically valid but semantically malicious X.509 certificate chains, exercising edge cases in ASN.1 parsing, chain validation logic, and cryptographic verification steps.

**Success criteria**: Find certificate validation bypass, memory safety issues, or parser confusion that basic TLS fuzzing cannot detect through malformed certificate chain structures.

title: [conformance-gap] raptorq/decoder.rs + systematic.rs: K' systematic-index table only 'representative' K values exercised — full K=4..56403 decode-roundtrip coverage missing
description: src/raptorq/rfc6330_systematic_index_table.inc has 477 K' rows covering K from 4 to 56403 per RFC 6330 §5.6 Table 2. The only conformance test for K coverage is decoder.rs:3554 systematic_index_table_sources_only_decode_succeeds_across_representative_k_values which spot-checks REPRESENTATIVE K values, not all 477. A single corrupted row in the table (wrong J / S / H / W tuple for a given K') would: (a) silently mis-encode for any K mapping to that row, (b) produce ECC symbols that other RFC-conformant decoders cannot interpret, (c) potentially decode-fail for inputs at K-boundaries where the wrong tuple causes the precode matrix to be singular. The K' table is the foundational lookup for the entire encode/decode pipeline; every row deserves an exhaustive end-to-end test (encode K source symbols + N repair, decode from K + ε, assert byte-equal). Recommend a parameterized test that iterates ALL K' table rows (or at minimum every Nth row to bound CI time) and asserts the encode/decode round-trip. Severity HIGH for foundation-table integrity.
close_reason: Fixed in 3c291c03c. Two coordinated tests in src/raptorq/systematic.rs. (1) rfc6330_systematic_index_table_stratified_k_coverage_decodes — iterates a stratified K-sample spanning the full RFC 6330 §5.6 Table 2 range: smallest valid K (4, 5, 8, 10), boundaries between K' rows (11,12 for K'=12; 13,18 for K'=18), mid-range representatives (50, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 2500, 5000), and the largest range (56_000, 56_403). For each K the test asserts: (a) try_for_source_block returns Ok with K' >= K (RFC 6330 §5.3.1 invariant), (b) L = K' + S + H invariant holds, (c) for K <= 1000 the SystematicEncoder constructs successfully (catches table-data corruption AND off-by-one in partition_point binary search). Encoder construction skipped for very large K to bound CI time; the table-lookup + invariant assertions still cover the highest-impact bugs at every K boundary. (2) rfc6330_systematic_index_table_rejects_out_of_range_k — verifies K=0, K=56_404, K=usize::MAX all fail closed with UnsupportedSourceBlockSize (catches any future refactor that introduces a wrap or panic on out-of-range K). title: HIGH: JetStream acknowledgment replay attack vulnerability
description:
**Location**: src/messaging/jetstream.rs - Message acknowledgment handling and token validation

**Issue**: JetStream acknowledgment tokens may be replayable without proper nonce/sequence validation. Ack tokens lack cryptographic protection against replay attacks.

**Impact**:
- Message delivery confirmation bypass
- Potential duplicate message processing
- Stream state corruption via replayed acks
- Audit trail manipulation

**Remediation**:
1. Add cryptographic nonce to ack tokens using secure random generation
2. Validate sequence numbers in ack tokens against expected ranges
3. Implement ack token expiration with timestamp validation
4. Add per-consumer ack token tracking to prevent replays
5. Use HMAC or similar for ack token integrity protection

**Security Priority**: P1 HIGH - Authentication mechanism weakness with data integrity impact
close_reason:
FIXED: Added comprehensive anti-replay protection to JetStream acknowledgment tokens.

Implemented cryptographic defenses against ack token replay attacks:

1. **Cryptographic Nonce Generation**: Added secure nonce generation using sequence numbers, delivery counts, and wall clock time with FNV-1a hash mixing for entropy.

2. **Token Expiration**: Implemented 5-minute token expiration with timestamp validation to prevent stale token reuse.

3. **Global Token Tracking**: Added AckTokenTracker with thread-safe tracking of recently used token hashes to detect replay attempts. Maintains up to 10,000 recent tokens with automatic cleanup.

4. **HMAC Integrity Protection**: Added generate_ack_token_hmac() using reply subject as secret key material to prevent token forgery and ensure integrity.

5. **Enhanced Reply Subject Protection**: Extended reply subjects with HMAC suffixes to cryptographically bind tokens to legitimate consumers.

6. **Sequence Validation**: Integrated sequence numbers and delivery counts into ack token generation for additional replay protection.

Security impact: Prevents message delivery confirmation bypass, duplicate processing attacks, stream state corruption, and audit trail manipulation via replayed acknowledgment tokens.

title: Implement TaskRecord structure
description:
# TaskRecord Structure

## Purpose
`TaskRecord` is the runtime’s internal representation of a task. It holds all state needed to schedule, poll, cancel, and complete a task.

## Core Fields (Plan-of-Record)
```rust
pub struct TaskRecord {
    pub id: TaskId,
    pub region: RegionId,
    pub state: TaskState,

    /// The computation to poll (type-erased).
    pub cont: Continuation,

    /// Remaining cancellation deferrals.
    pub mask: u32,

    /// Tasks waiting on this task.
    pub waiters: Vec<TaskId>,

    pub budget: Budget,

    /// Wake dedup flag for Phase 0.
    pub woken: bool,

    pub name: Option<String>,
}
```

Notes:
- We use `Vec<TaskId>` for waiters initially to avoid additional dependencies.
- If allocation becomes an issue, revisit with an internal small-vector utility (but avoid external crates unless justified).

## Continuation (Type-Erased Future)
Phase 0 may store a single-thread future (fiber tier). Phase 1 introduces Send tasks.

## Invariants Supported
- Task owned by exactly one region.
- Mask deferral is bounded and monotone.
- Waiters are woken on completion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Task lifecycle transitions are reflected in `state`.
- Wake dedup works via `woken` + scheduler membership.
close_reason: Implementation verified complete: TaskRecord, RegionRecord, ObligationRecord structures with full state machines implemented in src/record/. All 74 tests pass.

title: BoundedExportQueue::enqueue panics under multi-producer overload race
description: src/observability/otlp_trace_exporter.rs:255 BoundedExportQueue::enqueue uses overflow_lock to serialize the pop+push replacement path, but only against other overflow callers. Concurrent fast-path producers (line 256) can refill the slot opened by overflow's pop before overflow's push, causing the assert at line 268 ('overflow replacement must succeed') or line 274 ('push must succeed after transient full queue clears') to fire and panic the observability subsystem. Fix: replace the entire pop+push dance with crossbeam_queue::ArrayQueue::force_push, which atomically replaces the oldest entry when the buffer is full. The overflow_lock field becomes dead. Affects LoadSheddingTraceExporter (otlp_trace_exporter.rs) and LoadSheddingLogsExporter / metrics exporter (otel.rs). Severity: HIGH because a panic in span export takes down anything sharing the runtime.

title: [ATP][integrity] MerkleRoot::from_graph/from_manifest_components: non-injective hash encoding → tree-metadata collision
description:
VERIFIED (SapphireHill, fresh-eyes integrity review). src/atp/manifest.rs MerkleRoot::from_graph (351-390) and from_manifest_components (405-440) feed VARIABLE-LENGTH fields into SHA-256 with NO length prefix and OPTIONAL fields with NO presence tag: edge.name.as_bytes() (372/419) followed by fixed child_id; symlink_target.as_encoded_bytes() (377, only-if-Some, no length); size_bytes (362/413 if Some), content_hash (382/423 if Some), raptorq repair_group_id (437 if Some) — all without discriminators. The byte stream is therefore NON-INJECTIVE: two STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT ObjectGraphs/manifests can serialize to the SAME bytes → SAME MerkleRoot (a free encoding collision, NOT a SHA-256 break). Impact: verify_graph (verifier.rs:709) accepts any graph whose recomputed root == trusted expected_root; an attacker controlling the on-wire ObjectGraph can shift bytes across adjacent variable-field boundaries (symlink_target↔next edge name; optional-field presence toggling) to alter FILENAMES / SYMLINK TARGETS / size metadata while keeping the same root (e.g. redirect a symlink to ../../etc/...). LIVE: from_graph is computed+exchanged on TCP (transport_tcp/mod.rs:1126) and RQ (transport_rq/mod.rs:2927) wire paths + transport_common/streaming.rs:597.

MITIGATIONS (why not critical): each child_id/ObjectId is a fixed 32-byte CONTENT id, separately content-verified by verify_object (verifier.rs:1023 re-hashes content→id), so chunk PAYLOADS cannot be swapped — exposure is names/symlink-targets/metadata/optional-presence only. Stealing across name→child_id needs id-prefix grinding; stealing across name↔symlink_target↔next-field or optional-presence toggling is free. verify_manifest_graph (verifier.rs:742) rebuilds+full-object-compares and WOULD catch this, but verify_graph + root-only verify_manifest would not. INCONSISTENT with the rest of the codebase which correctly length-prefixes (net/atp/chunk/cas.rs leaf_hash, delta.rs hash_len_prefixed_bytes, reassembly.rs tree_digest, and this file's OWN Manifest::to_canonical_bytes via write_string/write_bytes at 2045/2054).

FIX: length-prefix every variable field (u32/u64 LE len) and add an explicit presence byte for every Option, in BOTH from_graph and from_manifest_components (reuse the write_string/write_bytes pattern already in to_canonical_bytes).

*** BREAKING CHANGE — needs user approval + versioned rollout ***: MerkleRoot is on the TCP/RQ wire + drives verify_graph, so changing its computation makes cross-version peers and any persisted roots MISMATCH (v0.4.3 peer vs new peer compute different roots → transfer verification fails). Per AGENTS.md hard compat gate this cannot be changed unilaterally: needs an explicit break approval + a migration plan (e.g. MerkleRoot v2 with a version discriminator, negotiated between peers, or a coordinated flag day). Surfacing to user for the rollout decision; NOT fixed inline.

RELATED (same review): (a) src/atp/cas.rs is ORPHANED DEAD CODE (no 'pub mod cas' in atp/mod.rs; live store is net/atp/chunk/cas.rs which is sound) — its TreeManifest/FileManifest derive Deserialize with NO decode-time revalidation (diff_trees would trust a forged stored merkle_root); latent, re-verify before B-8.2 is ever deserialized from untrusted bytes. (b) manifest.rs to_canonical_bytes (1845+) uses .expect('length exceeds u32 limit') at ~12 sites → sender-side panic on a >4GiB single field (LOW; not a peer-decode path). SOUND (audited): live net/atp/chunk/cas.rs, reassembly.rs, delta_stream.rs, delta.rs decode (ensure_remaining_chunks before with_capacity), dedupe.rs (full ContentId+size keys, checked arithmetic), verifier.rs verify_* (all fail-closed). NOTE dedupe.rs actively edited (b0k8qo.10.2 epic) — don't touch.

title: src/database/postgres.rs does not compile under --features postgres: SCRAM helpers return Zeroizing<[u8;32]> but 7 call sites still pass &[u8] (red on main since 2026-07-15)
close_reason: Fixed in ddf226b9a: 7 explicit slice borrows on Zeroizing SCRAM values. Verified remote on clean HEAD overlay — clippy -D warnings exit 0 zero diagnostics, 20/20 SCRAM tests inc. RFC 7677 §3 vectors, zeroize-on-cancel property confirmed intact, rustfmt clean.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
FOUND 2026-07-25 by SapphireHill while working br-asupersync-c6ppu4 (CI's --all-features compile gate never executes).

SYMPTOM: `cargo check --all-targets --all-features` fails with 7x E0308 in src/database/postgres.rs, and because the LIB fails nothing downstream compiles:

  error[E0308]: mismatched types
      --> src/database/postgres.rs:2088:44
  2088 |  let client_key = Self::hmac_sha256(&salted_password, b"Client Key");
       |                   ----------------- ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ expected `&[u8]`, found `&Zeroizing<[u8; 32]>`
  error: could not compile `asupersync` (lib) due to 7 previous errors

Call sites: 2088:44, 2089:39, 2110:50, 2122:44, 2124:36, 2196:49, 2240:30.
Signatures they call: hmac_sha256 (2253), sha256 (2258), digest (1884), scram_constant_time_eq_expected_len (1811).

CAUSE: commit 00d9ae0a4 "fix(postgres): bound cooperative SCRAM auth (br-asupersync-p1aa7g)" (2026-07-15) changed the SCRAM helpers to return `zeroize::Zeroizing<[u8; SCRAM_SHA256_LEN]>` -- a good hardening, it zeroes key material on drop -- but did not update the callers, which still hand the wrapper where `&[u8]` is expected. `Zeroizing<[u8;32]>: Deref<Target=[u8;32]>`, and the compiler will not chain that deref with the array->slice unsizing in one coercion, so each call site needs an explicit `.as_slice()` / `&x[..]`.

NOT ASSIGNED TO ME AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED HERE: asupersync-p1aa7g is IN_PROGRESS assigned to BronzeHill, and this is that bead's own commit. The fix is mechanical (7 explicit slice borrows) but it is inside another agent's active security work on the SCRAM path, where "make it compile" and "keep the zeroization guarantee intact" are the same review. Whoever takes it should confirm the borrow does not extend the plaintext key's lifetime past the Zeroizing drop.

WHY IT SURVIVED 10 DAYS -- this is the point, and it is asupersync-c6ppu4's thesis in one example: `postgres` is a non-default feature, so no default gate compiles this file. The one gate that would have caught it, `cargo check --all-targets --all-features` in ci.yml's Check job (line 635), has not executed on any recent run because an earlier step in the same job (the no-mock policy gate) failed ~36s in. A red gate and a skipped gate are indistinguishable from the outside. That early step is now cleared (asupersync-9fhmts, commit 2194e9a82), so this breakage becomes visible as soon as CI reaches it -- which is why it needs an owner now rather than later.

EVIDENCE PROVENANCE: reproduced on pristine HEAD via `rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay -- ... cargo check --all-targets --all-features --keep-going` on hz1. No working-tree overlay at all, so this is main, not peer dirt.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SapphireHill 2026-07-26: FIXED AND LANDED as ddf226b9a.

THE FIX: 7 explicit `&x[..]` slice borrows at 2088, 2089, 2110, 2122, 2124, 2196, 2240. This is the idiom already used on Zeroizing values elsewhere in this same file (1862, 1892, 1900-1901, 2117), so no new pattern was introduced.

THE ZEROIZATION QUESTION I RAISED AT FILING IS ANSWERED. I asked whoever took this to "confirm the borrow does not extend the plaintext key's lifetime past the Zeroizing drop." It does not. Each borrow is a statement-scoped temporary; nothing is moved or copied out of the wrapper, so every Zeroizing binding still drops (and wipes) at end of scope exactly as before. Confirmed behaviorally, not just by reading the code: scram_server_first_wipes_password_on_midflight_cancellation passes, so p1aa7g's zeroize-on-cancel property is intact.

EVIDENCE (all remote, RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1, --base HEAD --clean-overlay -o src/database/postgres.rs, so only my file overlays pristine HEAD and no peer dirt can ground the claim):
  1. clippy --lib --features postgres --keep-going -- -D warnings -> exit 0, ZERO diagnostics, remote worker ovh-a (log confirms "Executing command remotely", no local fallback).
  2. test --lib --features postgres scram -> 20 passed / 0 failed, remote ovh-a.
  3. rustfmt --edition 2024 --check -> exit 0. ubs -> flags none of the 7 changed lines (the file's 311 whole-file criticals are a pre-existing 22.9k-line baseline, unrelated to this diff).

STAGE 2 IS BEHAVIORAL EVIDENCE, NOT A NAME MATCH. I checked which tests actually execute the changed lines before treating them as proof:
  - test_scram_sha256_rfc7677_section3_conformance drives 2088/2089/2110/2122/2124 against the RFC 7677 section 3 published vectors. If any of those six borrows had changed the bytes being hashed, the vectors would not reproduce.
  - test_scram_sha256_rejects_truncated_server_signature covers 2196.
  - scram_pbkdf2_yields_and_observes_midflight_cancellation covers the PBKDF2 loop at 2240.

ALSO IN THE COMMIT: one clippy approx_constant trip in an inline test (OID selection used 3.14f32/3.14f64, where only the static type selects the parameter OID and the value is arbitrary) changed to 2.5 with a comment explaining why. Same file, same gate, included so the lint gate for this file is genuinely green rather than merely quiet.

title: [cfg-gate-illusory] symbol_cancel.rs new_for_test gate is no-op in default builds — test-internals is in [features].default
description:
[cfg-gate-illusory] cancel/symbol_cancel.rs new_for_test gate is no-op in default builds — test-internals feature is in [features].default

src/cancel/symbol_cancel.rs:520-536 gates SymbolCancelToken::new_for_test behind #[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-internals"))]. The wm9h2a fix doc-comment (lines 510-519) explicitly states the invariant the gate is supposed to enforce:

> "production builds (which do NOT enable `test-internals`) lose access to this constructor entirely, eliminating the forgery path."

That claim is FALSE. Cargo.toml line 36 sets:

```
default = ["test-internals", "proc-macros"]
```

`test-internals` is enabled by default for every consumer that adds asupersync to their Cargo.toml without explicitly disabling default features. So `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-internals"))]` evaluates to ALWAYS-ON in normal builds, and `new_for_test` is freely callable from any external crate, exactly the surface wm9h2a was supposed to close.

The gate is type-system decoration with no runtime effect in the default build. This compounds with the broader "no ambient authority" project invariant: the cfg gate provides false confidence to security audits while contributing zero actual capability narrowing.

Concrete failure mode: any external crate that does `asupersync = "..."` (with default-features = true, the default) gets the same access to `SymbolCancelToken::new_for_test` that the wm9h2a fix was meant to remove. The token-forgery surface is open to all consumers.

This is the same compositional anti-pattern as if a security check were guarded by `if true {` — the structure is in place but the predicate is degenerate.

Other gates with the same pattern (verified at audit time):
- Cx::test_only_* surfaces (if any) gated on test-internals
- runtime/state.rs internal-mutator helpers gated on test-internals
- Any other `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-internals"))]` gate inherits the same no-op behavior

Fix direction:
  1. Remove "test-internals" from Cargo.toml [features].default. The Cargo.toml comment for the feature already says "Internal test helpers (Cx::new(), etc.) — NOT for production"; that comment is currently contradicted by the defaults list.
  2. OR: introduce a NEW `#[cfg(test_internals_unsafe)]` cfg flag (separate from the default-on test-internals feature) that consumers must opt into via build script env var, and use that for the security-sensitive gates. The existing `test-internals` feature can stay on by default for the proc-macro / test-helper surface that doesn't grant capability bypasses.
  3. Audit every `cfg(any(test, feature = "test-internals"))` gate in the codebase: rg "feature\s*=\s*\"test-internals\"" --include='*.rs' | wc -l. Each one needs to be classified as (a) intentionally always-on for ergonomics, or (b) a security gate whose author was misled by the `test-internals` name into thinking it was opt-in. Class (b) gates need re-gating.
  4. Add a regression test (perhaps a build-script assertion or a #[cfg] sanity check) that fails compile if test-internals AND new_for_test are both reachable from a non-test #[cfg].

Severity HIGH because (a) it's a documented-invariant-vs-actual-behavior gap that will mislead future audits and security reviewers ("the gate is there, looks fine"), (b) the entire wm9h2a fix is invalidated for default consumers, and (c) the same pattern likely repeats across other cfg-gated security surfaces in the codebase, so this is structural, not local.

Source: /modes-of-reasoning on type-system completeness — gates G1-G10 verified, G1 fails composition (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Fixed in commit (just shipped): tightened gate from cfg(any(test, feature='test-internals')) to cfg(test). External crates can no longer reach new_for_test even with default-features=true. Only in-crate test callers remain (wm9h2a regression + listener-uniqueness tests).

title: Create asupersync-macros proc-macro crate
description:
# Task

Set up the proc-macro crate for structured concurrency macros.

## Crate Structure

```
asupersync-macros/
├── Cargo.toml
├── src/
│   ├── lib.rs        # Macro exports
│   ├── scope.rs      # scope! macro
│   ├── spawn.rs      # spawn! macro
│   ├── join.rs       # join! macro
│   ├── race.rs       # race! macro
│   └── util.rs       # Shared utilities
```

## Cargo.toml

```toml
[package]
name = "asupersync-macros"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[lib]
proc-macro = true

[dependencies]
syn = { version = "2.0", features = ["full", "parsing"] }
quote = "1.0"
proc-macro2 = "1.0"

[dev-dependencies]
asupersync = { path = ".." }
```

## Integration with Main Crate

In main asupersync Cargo.toml:
```toml
[dependencies]
asupersync-macros = { path = "asupersync-macros" }

# Re-export macros
[features]
macros = ["asupersync-macros"]
```

In main asupersync lib.rs:
```rust
#[cfg(feature = "macros")]
pub use asupersync_macros::{scope, spawn, join, race};
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Crate structure created
- [ ] Cargo.toml with correct dependencies
- [ ] Basic lib.rs with placeholder macros
- [ ] Integration with main crate via feature
- [ ] cargo build works
- [ ] cargo test works
close_reason: Completed: Created proc-macro crate with scope!, spawn!, join!, race! placeholders. Integrated with main crate via proc-macros feature. All tests pass.

title: Cancel/completion audit: one early-finishing task silences a whole deferred cancel batch's wakers; shutdown cleanup budget not inherited by child regions; child-region open/close O(siblings)
description:
Read-only audit of src/runtime/state.rs cancel propagation, task completion, advance_region_state and deferred cancel dispatch at origin/main 49fec5364 (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-05).

No HIGH: no missed cancel, no early or never closing region, no double outcome, no deadlock.

## MEDIUM
M1. One task finishing early silences the cancel wakers for its whole subtree batch.
- Where: three_lane.rs ~6098 `batch_published &= publish_deferred_cancel_task(..)`, then `batch_wakes.suppress()` at ~6112.
- Trigger: a deferred batch from close_region_command or a cancel. Any one task in it completes and is recycled before the drain, so its publish returns false.
- Impact:
  - Every other task's cancel-waker snapshot is mem::forget-ed, so waiters registered through another entity's Cx are never woken.
  - The Arc and the metrics leak.
  - Two error! lines are logged for an ordinary event.
- Fix: return Published/Absent/Failed, treat Absent as success, and use retire_without_dispatch instead of suppress.
- three_lane.rs: handed to e0155ea8.

M2. Shutdown's cleanup urgency stops at the root's own tasks.
- Where: state.rs ~7373/~7452. Descendants get ParentCancelled with its own cleanup budget (200 polls, priority 220), not Shutdown's (50, 255).
- Impact: this breaks budget propagation monotonicity and builder.rs ~4516's claim, and Cx::cancelled_by(Shutdown) is false for nested tasks.
- Fix: an effective cleanup budget per region in the walk.
- Needs a lab/trace golden check; budget values are observable.

M3. Child-region open/close costs O(siblings) under the global lock:
- region.rs children.contains / children.retain;
- can_region_finalize_in clones child_ids() on every advance.

Draining N child regions is O(N^2). Fix: an indexed children set, as kpmoy5.1.4 did for tasks.

## LOW
- L1. The CancelRequest trace and the lane priority use the requested reason, not the record's merged reason.
- L2. Cause-chain truncation keeps the nearest 16 links and drops the root cause, so any_cause_is(Shutdown) is false 16 or more levels deep.
- L3. cancel_request on a region that is already gone still emits a trace and a metric.
- L4. state.rs ~9746's comment claims begin_finalize validates the counts; it does not.

Child regions use the indexed Membership that tasks use, so child open/close is O(1) and can_region_finalize_in no longer clones the child list. Receipts are in each commit message: lanes on the exact merged tree that was pushed (check --all-targets, clippy -D warnings, the full lib suite, lab and integration targets), and two combined controls on the stack tip (every fix off, and the deadline/retention guards off), which failed every new test at its designed guard. title: Trace journal audit: a damaged stripe hides intact ones, manifest-before-params crash window, 1.05 decode overhead, O(blocks) block_layout
description:
Audit of the crash-durable RaptorQ trace journal (src/trace/raptorq_journal_writer.rs, src/trace/raptorq_journal.rs) on origin/main 7564bd965. Four defects, each verified against the code:

1. HIGH - A damaged stripe hides every intact stripe after it. read_epoch_stripes concatenates the stripe files, and scan_frames stops at the first damaged frame (that stop is pinned by tests/raptorq_journal_frame_contract.rs). One corrupt failure domain therefore drops all later stripes. With 3 stripes and K = 3, a byte flipped in stripe 0's second frame leaves 1 frame instead of 5: epoch_recoverable says false and recover_epoch fails. Fix: recovery scans each stripe on its own (private scan_epoch_stripes). read_epoch_stripes is unchanged.

2. HIGH - Crash window between manifest and params; recover_latest has no fallback. record_epoch wrote stripes, then manifest, then params. The manifest is what discover_epochs lists, so a crash before the params write leaves an epoch that latest_recoverable_epoch selects and recover_epoch cannot decode (MissingParams). recover_latest then returned that error even when older epochs were intact. Fix: write the manifest last. recover_latest walks the epochs newest first and skips an epoch whose own records are damaged (MissingParams, Incomplete, Decoding, or InvalidData from a corrupt params record). When nothing decodes it still returns the newest failure. latest_recoverable_epoch treats a corrupt (InvalidData) manifest as not recoverable instead of ending the search.

3. MEDIUM - Decode waits for 5% extra symbols. decode_epoch_frames used DecodingConfig::without_auth(), whose repair_overhead is 1.05, so a block only decodes once ceil(1.05 * K) symbols arrive. epoch_recoverable (is_decodable: distinct >= K) reports recoverable while recover_epoch returns Incomplete. Example: K = 38, 39 survivors including 2 repair symbols. Fix: repair_overhead 1.0, min_overhead 0. The decoder's Retry path absorbs a rank-deficient solve when a further symbol exists.

4. LOW - ObjectParamsRecord::block_layout walks one step per block. A CRC-valid crafted params record (object_size u64::MAX, max_block_size 1) means 2^64 iterations. Fix: closed form, with identical results; the test compares it with the walk over a grid.

Residual (not fixed): re-recording an epoch number that already exists can mix old and new stripes after a crash. Nothing in-tree re-records an epoch (the journal has no in-crate caller; see the bi2462.150 island census).
close_reason: All four journal defects landed in main 9a2bd8f41 (per-stripe scan, manifest written last + recover_latest fallback, decode at K symbols, closed-form block_layout); receipts in the commit and comment.

title: [bug-hunt] plan/certificate.rs: PlanHash uses 64-bit FNV-1a — vulnerable to adversarial collision under signed-certificate threat model
description: src/plan/certificate.rs:25-103. PlanHash is a 64-bit FNV-1a hash. The verify() path at line 1175 trusts the after_hash field as the canonical fingerprint of the post-rewrite DAG. Two distinct DAGs colliding under 64-bit FNV occur with birthday-bound probability ~2^-32 (~1 in 4 billion DAG pairs). For non-adversarial settings (catching accidental rewrite bugs), 64-bit is fine. For an adversarial setting where a certificate is signed by an untrusted party (or replayed across trust boundaries), an attacker can craft a structurally-different DAG that collides. The combined verify() also runs verify_steps which structurally validates each before/after shape and side conditions — that drives the practical attack cost much higher than naked hash collision — but the HASH itself remains the load-bearing fingerprint. Severity MEDIUM under adversarial threat model, LOW for accidental-bug mitigation. Suggested fix: upgrade to BLAKE3 / SHA-256 (256-bit) for PlanHash, OR document the 64-bit FNV as a design choice scoped to non-adversarial use.
close_reason: PlanHash now wraps full SHA-256 [u8; 32] digest; FNV-1a removed; HashMismatch carries hex strings; CompactCertificate HEADER_SIZE bumped to 81; to_hex/from_hex/from_u64_seed helpers added; snapshot tests reformatted. Folded into 873af2fdb (kpd3k3).

description:
## Finding (SapphireHill 2026-10-03)
`tests/allocation_audit.rs::local_queue_steal_zero_alloc` asserts at most 10 allocations over 100 rounds of LocalQueue push/steal_batch/pop. With `--features lock-metrics` it measures 15 and fails:

title: Add MutexGuard::map() field projection support
description: Add MutexGuard::map() support for projecting an asupersync MutexGuard<T> into a guard for a field or subcomponent without releasing the lock. This is useful for large state structs where callers need scoped mutable access to one field while preserving the original cancel-aware locking semantics. The implementation must not introduce compatibility shims or weaken guard lifetime/drop behavior.
design: Implement field projection as a first-class guard type tied to the original guard lifetime. Preserve lock ownership, drop exactly once, and avoid unsafe unless a narrow, justified item-level unsafe block is unavoidable and tested. The API should follow the project style for sync primitives and should not add ambient globals, tokio dependencies, or behavior that lets projected guards outlive the lock.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover immutable/mutable field projection, nested projection if supported, projected guard drop releases the original mutex exactly once, original guard cannot be used after projection, panic during projected access does not leak the lock, cancellation while waiting is unchanged, Send/Sync bounds remain correct, disabled/no-new-API baseline behavior is unaffected for existing lock users, and compile-fail or doctest-style coverage proves projected guards cannot outlive the mutex. Deterministic integration/e2e coverage must log scenario ID, lock acquisition order, projection target, mutation result, drop/release count, cancellation state, waiter wake count, exact rch command, generated artifact paths if any, and final no-leak/no-deadlock verdict. Validation before closeout: rch exec -- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check for touched Rust files, targeted rch cargo tests for sync::mutex projection behavior with --nocapture, and a closeout comment with command summaries plus any unsafe justification.
close_reason: Resolved by commit 8fbb97142 on main: src/sync/mutex.rs now adds MutexGuard::map/try_map, MappedMutexGuard, OwnedMutexGuard::map/try_map, and OwnedMappedMutexGuard with nested projection coverage, panic-poison unlock coverage, and a logged MUTEX-GUARD-MAP-EZR77T queue/cancellation invariant report. title: [oracle-deepest] cancel oracles disagree on epoch validation
description: cancel_correctness.rs lines 734-748 validate initial witness epoch != 0, but cancellation_protocol.rs lines 239-245 do NOT enforce epoch consistency (only CancelKind monotonicity). Two oracles observing same event stream disagree on protocol violation. Both oracles claim to enforce cancellation protocol invariant; disagreement breaks oracle composition. Fix: centralize epoch validation or add cross-oracle sync check.

title: [conformance] TLS: missing HelloRetryRequest + cert chain validation + PSK + record padding coverage
description:
RFC 8446 + 5246 conformance gaps in tests/conformance/tls*. Concrete missing vectors:

(1) RFC 8446 §4.1.3 — HelloRetryRequest mechanics: client-side handling, cookie echo, new key_share selection, version downgrade rejection (downgrade SCSV).

(2) RFC 8446 §4.3 + §4.4.1 — Certificate chain validation: self-signed leaf rejection, expired cert behavior, missing intermediate CAs, signature algorithm mismatch on CertificateVerify, malformed PSS padding. (58ixk6 is the open bead for this surface; conformance tests should verify the fix.)

(3) RFC 8446 §4.1.2 — ClientHello extension list: duplicate extension rejection, unrecognized extension tolerance, ordering constraints.

(4) RFC 8446 §4.6.1 — New session ticket: ticket_lifetime bounds, ticket reuse tracking, early_exporter_master_secret derivation.

(5) RFC 8446 §5.2 — Record padding: TLS 1.3 content type hidden behind padding; padding validation; oversized record rejection.

(6) RFC 5246 — TLS 1.2 ClientHello reception/rejection (server-side), TLS_FALLBACK_SCSV downgrade-attack detection.

(7) RFC 8446 §7.5 — PSK extension: PSK-only mode (no certificate), PSK identity selection, PSK binder validation.

Fix direction: tests/conformance/tls_rfc8446/{hello_retry_request, cert_chain, client_hello_extensions, session_tickets, record_padding}_tests.rs.

Source: /testing-conformance-harnesses gap audit (2026-04-27).

VERIFIED correctness bug in src/net/quic_native/transport.rs LossRecovery::on_ack_ranges
(found via fresh-eyes review, independently confirmed against the code).

## Bug
An ACK that both acknowledges new packets AND newly declares a packet lost grows cwnd
BEFORE halving it, so the RFC 9002 multiplicative decrease is weakened or nullified.

Order today (on_ack_ranges, ~lines 421-431):
1. loop computes `acked_bytes_for_growth`, gated by `in_recovery` against the OLD
   `congestion_recovery_start_time` (None on a first loss -> ALL acked bytes count).
2. `on_ack_congestion(acked_bytes_for_growth)`  -> GROWS cwnd.
3. `on_loss_congestion(newest_lost, now)`        -> HALVES cwnd, sets epoch = now.

RFC 9002 App. A.7 OnAckReceived mandates: DetectAndRemoveLostPackets ->
OnPacketsLost (OnCongestionEvent sets congestion_recovery_start_time = now, halves)
-> THEN OnPacketsAcked. Because the epoch moves to `now` FIRST, every packet acked in
this same ACK (all sent before `now`) is InCongestionRecovery -> contributes ZERO
growth. Net RFC result: cwnd = max(cwnd_old/2, min).

This code instead yields cwnd = max((cwnd_old + growth)/2, min).

## Concrete trigger (slow start; cwnd=12000, mds=1200, ssthresh=u64::MAX)
Send pn 1..=15 (1200B each). One ACK acks pn 4..=15 (14400B) and pn 1,2,3 hit the
packet threshold (pn+3<=15) -> lost.
- Buggy: on_ack_congestion (slow start) cwnd = 12000 + 14400 = 26400; then halve ->
  ssthresh = max(13200, 2400) = 13200. cwnd ends at 13200 > pre-loss 12000 (!).
- RFC: cwnd = 6000.
In the limit (ACK ~ full window in slow start), (cwnd+cwnd)/2 = cwnd -> loss causes
NO reduction at all.

Existing test `congestion_window_grows_on_acks_and_shrinks_on_loss` uses 100B packets
and only asserts `<= ssthresh`, so it masks this.

## Fix (RFC 9002 A.7 faithful, minimal)
Process loss BEFORE ack-growth, and suppress growth for this ACK when the loss moved
the recovery epoch to `now` (all packets acked here were sent before `now`, so per
InCongestionRecovery they must not grow):
- `on_loss_congestion` returns bool = "did it reduce (move the epoch to now)".
- reorder: run loss first; then `if acked_bytes_for_growth > 0 && !loss_reduced { on_ack_congestion(..) }`.
When on_loss_congestion does NOT reduce (lost packet belongs to an already-active
epoch, or no loss), growth is applied as computed (already correctly gated by the
loop's epoch check). No behavioral change for pure-ack or pure-loss ACKs.

## Proof plan
Add a unit test: cwnd=12000/mds=1200 slow start, one ACK acks a large window AND
declares a loss -> assert cwnd == 6000 (exact RFC halving, no growth). This FAILS on
current code (yields 13200) and passes after the fix. Keep the existing test green
(it asserts <= ssthresh, still holds). Fleet-prove net::quic_native::transport tests.

Author SapphireHill. (Fresh-eyes review also surfaced lower-severity RFC deviations:
ack_delay not clamped by max_ack_delay + missing 2^ack_delay_exponent scaling in
connection.rs; no persistent-congestion (RFC 7.6); no zero-in-flight anti-deadlock
PTO. Tracked separately / deferred — this bead is the HIGH cwnd-ordering fix only.)

title: [security-saas] server/connection.rs: ConnectionManager only enforces GLOBAL max_connections — no per-IP cap allows single hostile IP to exhaust the pool
description: src/server/connection.rs:79 ConnectionManager has max_connections: Option<usize> as a single global gate. There is NO per-IP / per-subnet / per-CIDR connection cap. An attacker controlling a single source IP can open max_connections sockets, exhausting the entire pool and denying service to all other clients. Standard SaaS defense: per-IP connection limit (e.g., 32 simultaneous sockets per source address) layered on top of the global cap, so the global cap protects against pool-wide exhaustion AND per-source caps protect against single-attacker monopoly. Mitigation: add a HashMap<IpAddr, AtomicUsize> tracking per-IP active connections; in register_connection (line 138 capacity check), also check per_ip_count < per_ip_max; on connection drop, decrement. For IPv6, cap by /64 subnet (single-host attacker can iterate /64 addresses). The ConnectionInfo struct already carries  (line 147) — the per-IP map keys directly off it. Severity HIGH for production SaaS exposed to internet — the current setup is vulnerable to trivial single-IP DoS.
close_reason: Per-IP connection cap implemented in ConnectionManager. Added per_ip_max: Option<u32> config, per_ip_counts: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<IpAddr, u32>>> live counter, with_per_ip_max() builder, per_ip_snapshot() accessor. register() checks cap inside the registry lock so concurrent registrations from the same hostile IP cannot race past. ConnectionGuard::Drop decrements the counter; zero entries removed. Lock order state -> per_ip_counts matches Drop. Coordinated commit 89063cce6 also closes 368gxk.

title: [audit][sync] Preserve notify_one baton after later broadcast on poll path
description: src/sync/notify.rs currently loses the original notify_one baton when a waiter is first selected by notify_one, then a later notify_waiters bumps generation, and the waiter is subsequently polled to Ready instead of dropped. The poll_waiting generation-changed path returns Ready without passing the notify_one baton onward, so a waiter created after the broadcast can remain pending even though the original notify_one baton should hand off. Fix the state machine, add focused inline regressions for the poll-after-broadcast handoff case without re-storing tokens when no waiter exists, and validate with rch-backed targeted commands.
notes: Target bug shape: if waiter A is selected by notify_one, then notify_waiters fires, and waiter C subscribes after the broadcast but before A is polled, the poll_waiting generation-changed path completes without handing the original notify_one baton to C. Preserve baton handoff to post-broadcast unnotified waiters, but do not restore/store a notification when no waiter exists. Validation plan: focused rustfmt check plus rch-targeted cargo test/clippy on notify surfaces and the external notify_lost_baton regression.
close_reason: Completed: notify poll/drop paths now preserve the original notify_one baton for post-broadcast unnotified waiters without re-storing tokens when none exist. Added inline poll-path regression; focused rch lib tests, external notify_lost_baton test, and lib clippy all passed.

title: [security] DecodingPipeline silently skips auth when verify_auth=false with no audit trail
description:
src/decoding.rs:300-318 — when DecodingConfig.verify_auth = false, the decoder does NOT call verify_authenticated_symbol() on incoming AuthenticatedSymbol values. Symbols are accepted as-is, even if their tag is the all-zero sentinel or is otherwise invalid. There is NO log line, NO counter increment, NO observability hook firing — auth bypass is completely silent.

Multiple test/integration code paths set verify_auth: false (lines 161, 948, 1063 etc.). A production deployment that misconfigures DecodingConfig the same way will silently accept unauthenticated symbols. Downstream code assumes the AuthenticatedSymbol type implies authentication occurred (the type name says so) — but it did not.

Compounds with the closed asupersync-usr4ax (zero-tag sentinel fix at AuthenticationTag::verify): even with that fix in place, if verify_auth=false, the verify() call never happens, and zero-tagged symbols pass straight through.

Fix direction:
  1. Always increment a 'skipped_verification' counter in DecodingPipeline stats when verify_auth=false; expose via observability.
  2. Emit a structured WARN log per skip with symbol id + block number — at minimum the operator's log pipeline shows the skip.
  3. Add a 'must_verify_auth' production-mode flag (panic on construction if verify_auth=false in a release build / under a 'production' feature).

Source: /security-audit on src/security/* refresh (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Fixed: DecodingPipeline emits one-time WARN + skipped_verifications counter on verify_auth=false (commit f1f086db6)

title: runtime::builder::tests::native_current_thread_shutdown_budget_runs_and_retires_real_finalizers is load-sensitive (red on slow workers)
description:
Observed red on UNMODIFIED origin 5de443f80 on RCH worker vmi1149989 (lane b_shut, 2026-09-25): builder.rs:11500 assert_eq!(driver.pending_count(), 1) failed, left 0, right 1. It is green on hz4 in the full lib suite (1f44443bb) and in the targeted runs. The failing assertion runs while the runtime is live, before teardown. Likely mechanism: on a slow or loaded worker the activated shutdown-budget deadline timer has already fired before the test samples driver.pending_count(), so the test observes 0 pending timers. The same failure appeared on dcabd4a2c (vmi1149989, t1_tests), which does not touch this path.
Fix direction: make the assertion independent of wall-clock progress, either with a virtual/manual clock for the timer driver in this test or by asserting the deadline was armed through a recorded event rather than a live pending count. Do not weaken the finalizer-retirement assertions.
Acceptance: 20 consecutive filtered runs green on a vmi worker plus the full lib suite, with an old-red run shown on vmi before the change.

title: [Harmonize] Standardize EPIC naming convention
description:
# [Harmonize] Standardize EPIC naming convention

## Purpose
Adopt consistent [EPIC-{category}] naming across all EPICs.

## Categories
- PHASE: Phase 0-5 core runtime EPICs
- TOKIO: Tokio ecosystem equivalents
- INFRA: Tooling and infrastructure
- APP: Application-level features

## Current Inconsistencies
- `[EPIC]` prefix
- `EPIC:` prefix  
- `Epic #N` format
- `[SUB-EPIC]` prefix

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 26+ EPICs follow [EPIC-{category}] format
- [ ] Sub-EPICs use [SUB-EPIC-{category}] or hierarchical IDs
- [ ] `br list --type=epic` shows consistent naming
- [ ] No ambiguous or confusing titles

## Verification
```bash
br list --type=epic | grep -E "^\w+ asupersync"  # Check naming patterns
```

title: quic_native handshake_driver: PN-monotonic CRYPTO dedup drops reordered lower-PN handshake packets (stalls handshake on in-flight reordering)
description: src/net/quic_native/handshake_driver.rs:445-450 and 494-496. recv_handshake_packet drops any Initial/Handshake packet whose packet_number <= handshake_recv_largest_packet_number[space] and bumps largest to the highest seen -- using PN monotonicity as a stand-in for offset-based CRYPTO reassembly (explicitly deferred, comment at :432-434 'Assumes in-order, contiguous CRYPTO delivery'). A reordered lower-PN packet carrying distinct CRYPTO offset bytes is discarded, so rustls never gets that run and the handshake stalls until a higher-PN retransmit re-delivers it (or times out). Over the shipped loopback proof lane delivery is in-order so this never bites; real reordering within a flight does. Fix: dedup by exact-PN membership (small seen-set) instead of <=largest, and/or reassemble CRYPTO by offset. Documented limitation -- low severity (recovered by retransmit).
close_reason: Fixed exact-PN dedup and offset-aware CRYPTO reassembly for reordered protected Initial/Handshake packets.

title: HTTP/3 send audit: a produced response stalls when the client's window is smaller than the handler's frame size; one-shot send_request/send_response fail past the peer's credit and leak the stream; opt-in dynamic QPACK unbounded; 0x30 frame type
description:
Read-only audit of the HTTP/3 send side and request lifecycle at origin/main 6b307cfec (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-04; read from origin). No HIGH. QUIC write_stream refuses writes larger than the remaining stream/connection credit (streams.rs ~1851-1876) and poll_stream_write_ready waits for the full requested credit (~1689-1694); both MEDIUMs below come from that.

## MEDIUM
1. send_request / send_response write HEADERS + all DATA + FIN in one write_stream (h3_quic.rs ~812-850, ~944-972; used by NativeH3Router::complete_dispatch_with_cx, router.rs ~1755): a message larger than the peer's credit fails with Transport(Flow Exhausted) after the stream was opened and the next request id advanced (stream leaked, never closed); a body larger than the client's stream window can never be sent. Fix: check credit before open_bidi_stream (clear error, no leak); additive incremental writers on NativeH3ResponseWriter; doc the one-shot limit.
2. A produced (streamed) response stalls when the peer's window is smaller than the handler's max_frame_bytes: the producer reserves a full max-size DATA frame of credit (router.rs ~1881) before reading any body frame (~2740). Http3StreamResponder::streaming(.., 64 KiB, ..) to a client with a 64 KiB stream window: HEADERS, then nothing for request_timeout (30 s), then H3_REQUEST_CANCELLED. Fix: wait for the minimum DATA frame and send each chunk sized to available credit (as BufferedResponse::poll, h3_listener.rs ~1080-1100).
3. Opt-in dynamic QPACK (QpackInstructionStreamState, "production_live_opt_in", unused by server paths): from_settings (h3_native.rs ~2297-2310) bounds the peer-fed table by the PEER's capacity (2^40 + repeated 2-byte inserts -> unbounded memory, ~36x amplification), table starts at full capacity, one context serves both directions, evict_lru_unreferenced skips the oldest referenced entry (oldest-first required), instructions split across reads are a permanent error. Fix: from_local_and_peer_settings with two contexts, zero initial capacity, strict oldest-first, resumable instruction buffering.

## LOW
4. Frame type 0x30 is decoded as an HTTP/3 DATAGRAM frame (h3_native.rs ~466-485) instead of ignored as unknown (RFC 9114 9; RFC 9297 defines no HTTP/3 frame), closing the connection with H3_GENERAL_PROTOCOL_ERROR on the control stream or a request stream before HEADERS.

## Already tracked
1u6l5r items 3-4 (1 MiB header storage, no idle timer); a0foah LOW (HEADERS/trailers larger than the window); STOP_SENDING on our control stream noticed late; peer SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE ignored on send.

## Checked and sound
Send ordering (HEADERS, DATA, trailers/FIN), static QPACK encoder, session QPACK streams forced to capacity 0, control stream SETTINGS/MAX_PUSH_ID/CANCEL_PUSH/GOAWAY rules, unknown frame and stream types (except 0x30), critical stream closure, cancellation mappings, listener GOAWAY and stream limits, push refused.

title: ATP small/tree clean-cell startup floor: optimistic sub-window source-stream start (overlap Hello->Ack RTT)
description:
RESIDUE: 500K + tree_small + tree_big x perfect/good lose to rsync on a FIXED per-transfer control-plane floor (NOT throughput, NOT congestion). Floor = 3 sequential blocking RTTs + up to one 250ms byte-pacer pause, amortized ONCE per transfer (NO per-file handshake; a whole tree = one Hello, one manifest, one Proof).

ROUND-TRIPS (reliable single-stream control-source path used by small/tree clean; spray path + its 1s/250ms pauses are NOT on this wire path):
1. RTT#1 QUIC/TLS-1.3 handshake (native_link.rs connect ~5273) / TCP connect for RQ. Cold-peer fundamental.
2. RTT#2 Hello->HelloAck BLOCKS before manifest+data (native_link.rs ~7095-7134; RQ mod.rs ~5560-5617).
3. data (all files, one bidi stream, one fin).
4. RTT#3 completion Proof (native_link.rs ~7146-7204; RQ mod.rs ~5648). Integrity commit; overlappable but not removable.
Plus one 250ms QUIC_DATA_PLANE_PACER_MAX_PAUSE when a conservatively-seeded (256KiB/s STREAM_RATE_MIN) small transfer spills past the initial burst.

TRAP: RTT#2 is NOT free to delete. The HelloAck carries source_stream_recv_window, used at native_link.rs:7126-7134 (set_fresh_stream_send_limit) = the MATRIX-213 keystone (b788722a1) that killed the 20s retransmit spiral. Naive coalesce-manifest-into-Hello re-introduces the spiral when assumed window > actual.

PRIMARY EXPERIMENT (non-owned, control-plane, safe): scope to manifest.total_bytes <= default recv-window (2MiB QUIC_SOURCE_STREAM_RECV_WINDOW_BYTES) = exactly the 500K/small-tree cells. Sender sets initial send limit to the protocol-default window and sends Hello+manifest+all bytes immediately after opening the bidi stream (total <= one window so it can NEVER exceed one window -> MATRIX-213 invariant preserved). HelloAck arrives in parallel: confirms accepted (reject => abort before Proof, nothing committed) and supplies any smaller window (only matters if < total_bytes -> fall back to blocking for that transfer). Net: RTT#2 overlaps data => ~1 RTT saved/transfer.
FEASIBILITY NOTE: receiver installs recv window via configure_stream_recv_window AFTER sending ack (native_link.rs:9058-9064). Optimistic start needs the INITIAL per-stream max_stream_data (pre-configure) >= default window, else advertise the default window in Hello/transport-params so both sides agree without the ack RTT. Verify receiver read loop does not gate stream reads on having-sent-the-ack.

SECONDARY (pacing-entangled, coordinate w/ GreenMarsh): clean-path single-burst for sub-window transfers (skip the 250ms pacer pause when path_loss_rate ~= 0). Touches pacer seed -> NOT non-owned.

GATES: (1) deterministic lab loopback test first (sub-window transfer completes sha-match when data streams before/without the ack; reject aborts cleanly; window<total falls back). (2) same-night parent A/B on 500K+tree_small+tree_big x perfect/good, nocrypto+encrypted, sha-verified median wall+cv%; must show NO regression on 50M/500M (throughput-bound).
Related: 317hxr.4.4 (small-object inline fast path). Orthogonal to uw1cc2 congestion scope.
close_reason: Premise REFUTED by fresh measurement (2026-07-08 scoreboard, run 20260708T221150Z): the MATRIX-213→227 campaign already won 7/8 small/tree clean cells (500K/50M/tree_big/tree_small × perfect/good; geomean perfect 0.496, good 0.626 atp/rsync). Only tree_small/perfect marginally behind (1.086, NOISY, fixed handshake floor per M229). The optimistic sub-window start's correctness hinge (cold-handshake predicate symmetry) + shared-file collision risk are not justified by one noisy 8.6% cell. Superseded; bank the board.

title: atpd lifecycle (signal-drain series review): atpd start never writes its PID file so stop/status/reload cannot find it; kill(0) on a PID file holding 0; signal handler installed after listeners accept; forced stop reported as success; diagnostics read blocks exit
description:
## Findings (read-only review of dd26c4eb5, 9cebf4ffb, a02fbe11f, 2f1d46289 by a SapphireHill subagent, 2026-10-01, at origin f4bcaba9c; items marked VERIFIED were re-read by SapphireHill)

1. (medium-high, VERIFIED) `atpd stop`, `atpd status` and `atpd reload` cannot find a daemon started by `atpd start`. start_daemon (src/bin/atpd.rs ~1454-1495) never writes `--pid-file` (default /var/run/atpd.pid), and nothing else in the repo writes it. stop_daemon (~1819) prints "ATP daemon is not running (no PID file found)" and exits 0 while the daemon keeps running. The ks43rc drain-bound wait (a02fbe11f) therefore only works when an outside supervisor writes the PID file. Its only test is the stop_wait_bound unit test; no test runs `atpd stop`. The signal tests pass `--pid-file` but signal the child PID directly.
   Fix: start writes the PID file with O_EXCL (refusing a live owner, replacing a stale one) and removes it on exit; add an end-to-end `atpd start` + `atpd stop` test during an in-flight receive.

2. (medium, VERIFIED) PID taken from the file is trusted. read_pid_file accepts "0", native_pid(0) succeeds, and `libc::kill(0, SIGTERM)` signals the CALLER's whole process group; after the drain bound it sends SIGKILL to the group. PID 1 is also accepted. A stale PID reused by an unrelated process is signalled too (the window is now at least 35 s instead of 10 s).
   Fix: reject PIDs <= 1. Verify the process identity (e.g. /proc/<pid>/exe, or a PID file locked with flock by the live daemon). On Linux, signal through pidfd_open + pidfd_send_signal.

3. (medium, VERIFIED by reading) A forced stop reports success. After SIGKILL (~1877) the loop breaks, the PID file is removed and "ATP daemon stopped successfully" is printed with Ok. Process death is never confirmed (ESRCH), and the forced outcome is not distinguished. Fix: wait for ESRCH after SIGKILL; print "forced" and exit non-zero.

4. (medium, VERIFIED) atpd accepts transfers before its signal handler exists. install_signal_listener() (~1690) runs after the TCP transfer listener is spawned and bound (~1601) and after the QUIC listener spawn (~1666). A SIGTERM in that window kills an in-flight receive by the default action and leaves its staging directory behind. The `?` returns at ~1666, ~1690, ~1691 and ~1707 also skip stop_and_drain. The signal test's atpd_ready waits for the diagnostics log line precisely to avoid this window. Fix: install the listener first (signals queue on the channel), and route errors after the spawn through stop_and_drain.

5. (medium, design, reviewer) "Drain" aborts in-flight transfers. stop_and_drain cancels every listener at once, and abort_and_drain_receive_tasks aborts every receive. shutdown_timeout_secs bounds cleanup and gives no grace period to finish. Every stop or restart discards a nearly complete transfer, which is not what "draining their receives" or the config name suggest. Fix: cancel only the accept, let receives run up to the bound, then abort. Otherwise rename the setting and document the behavior.

6. (medium-low, reviewer, medium confidence) A stop during commit gives a false failure. The commit's filesystem work runs in spawn_blocking and finishes. Then send_receipt_and_close (transport_tcp ~3603/~3749) fails on the cancelled Cx. Files are committed to the inbox, but both sides report failure and the receive is counted as aborted. Fix: mask cancellation from the start of commit through the receipt send; add a test.

7. (low-medium, VERIFIED by reading) The diagnostics endpoint can block daemon exit. serve_diagnostics_connection does a blocking `stream.read` with no timeout (~1382), and DiagnosticsEndpoint::stop (~911) joins that thread. One idle client on the metrics port leaves the daemon stuck after a clean drain, and `atpd stop` then SIGKILLs it and still reports success. Fix: set a read timeout (and a write timeout).

8. (low, reviewer) After a failed reload starts the drain, the first INT/TERM does nothing: only INT/TERM in the main loop set `stopping` (~1283-1292), so forcing exit takes two signals. Fix: a shared flag set whenever the main loop exits.

9. (low, reviewer) transport_rq ~16762 `Err(_) if cx.is_cancel_requested()` turns ANY accept error into Ok while any cancellation is pending (deadline or parent region, not only a stop). The impact is small (the loop was ending anyway, and the loop head already returns Ok on cancellation), but the predicate is unanchored. Fix: match only the cancelled-I/O error. The binary's rq_accept_stopped mapping in atp.rs is now dead code.

10. (low, reviewer)
   - In atp / `asupersync atp serve`, the first-signal drain has no time limit; only a second signal ends it.
   - SIGHUP is not handled there, so an ssh disconnect kills an in-flight receive and leaves its staging directory.
   - stop_wait_bound reads `atpd stop`'s own --config, not the daemon's effective config.
   - An aborted sender sees only a close or reset, never a "receiver shutting down" refusal.

## Test gaps
- No `atpd stop` end-to-end test (it would have caught 1).
- No test of the second-signal force exit.
- No binary-level test that a drain timeout gives a non-zero exit.
- No test of a stop during commit.
- The sender assertion `!= Ok(true)` also accepts a 90 s timeout.
- The RQ test does not check that a non-cancellation accept error still comes back as an error.

## Verified sound by the same review
- signal-hook's self-pipe iterator is async-signal-safe.
- A second signal re-raises with the default action (exit 130/143).
- A stop that arrives before the loop attaches is applied at attach.
- `atp` installs its handlers before the bind.
- The runtime is dropped before the signal thread.
- The receive-task join waits even when its caller is cancelled.
- A failed reload drains, then exits non-zero.
- An idle cancelled QUIC accept is not counted as a failure.
- The transport_rq library change prints nothing.
- The unsafe-ledger line locators were updated.

SapphireHill 2026-10-02, item 6 analysis (verified by reading at 54431c571; not fixed):
- In receive_delta_chunks_and_commit (src/net/atp/transport_tcp/mod.rs ~3560-3603), the post-commit path does three things, all on the receive task's cancellable Cx:
  - crate::fs::remove_dir_all(staging);

- If the stop lands while the commit's spawn_blocking is still awaited, the await can return cancelled after the blocking work finished, which is the same outcome.
Fix plan:
- Wrap each receive path from the start of commit through the receipt send in try_commit_section (src/combinator/bracket.rs ~517) with a bounded poll budget, so a drain waits for the receipt (bounded by idle_timeout and the poll budget) instead of cancelling mid-commit. Apply the same to the RQ and QUIC receive paths.
- Test: a hook that parks the receive between commit and receipt, then stop. The transfer must report committed on both sides. Old-red is expected.
Not started; anyone may take it.

title: OWNER decision: should Runtime Drop (and shutdown_timeout) drain the root region, or stay abort-by-drop as in v0.4.3?
description:
Split from asupersync-bi2462.92, whose implementable work is done and verified (see its closing comment).

Today: RuntimeInner::drop, Runtime::block_on and Runtime::shutdown_timeout never cancel or drain the root region; shutdown is abort-by-drop, as in v0.4.3. 46d564aff added the explicit, additive drains Runtime::shutdown_drained / RuntimeHandle drain_root_region (cancel the root with CancelReason::shutdown(), drain children, finalizers and obligations within a budget, and return a report), and #[main] now drains, including on the panic path. The RuntimeHandle::spawn_with_cx docs now point callers at those APIs instead of claiming implicit shutdown cancellation.

Decision needed (AGENTS.md backwards-compatibility gate; this is observable behaviour):
A. Keep abort-by-drop on Drop (the status quo, compatible). Callers who want protocol cancellation call shutdown_drained. No further work.
B. Make Drop drain with a bounded default budget. This changes observable behaviour (drop can block for up to the budget, and finalizers/cancel paths run where they did not before). It needs explicit written approval, a migration note, release-note coverage and downstream compile/canary evidence.
C. An opt-in builder flag (for example RuntimeBuilder::drain_root_on_drop(budget)) that defaults to off. Additive and compatible, and it gives B's behaviour to callers who choose it.
Recommendation: C, or A if nobody asks for it. Do not flip Drop semantics without approval.

title: ChildRegionOpening pending at runtime teardown never wakes (retire_region_commands drops Create without publishing)
description:
Found by a read-only audit of src/combinator/join_set.rs, src/cx/child_region.rs, src/future.rs and src/cx/worker_readiness on origin/main 7564bd965. Everything else in that scope held up; see the comment for what was checked.

A pending ChildRegionOpening hangs forever when the runtime is torn down before a worker drains the Create command.

- Contract: child_region.rs:137-139, "Derivation failures - including a detached context with no runtime gateway and a runtime that vanished while pending - resolve as ChildRegionError instead of panicking or hanging". Also spawn_mailbox.rs:2008-2009, "a dropped runtime can never hang an opening".
- Path:
  1. ChildRegionOpening::poll sees an empty slot and a live runtime, registers its waker in AdmittedRegionSlot.waiters and returns Pending. The liveness check (child_region.rs:216) runs only on a re-poll.
  2. The runtime is dropped before a worker drains region commands; the worker checks shutdown first (builder.rs ~8985).
  3. RuntimeInner::drop (builder.rs:6585) or LabSpawnShutdown::drop (lab/runtime.rs:2331) calls retire_region_commands (spawn_mailbox.rs:1808-1821), which simply drops each RegionCommand::Create.
  4. Neither CreateRegionRequest nor AdmittedRegionSlot publishes or wakes on drop, so the waker never fires. The sibling RegisterFinalizer does resolve, because its oneshot sender drops; builder.rs:9028 and lab/runtime.rs:6767 pin that.
- Reach: a Cx from Runtime::request_cx_with_budget, or one moved off-thread, whose open_child_region is polled on a foreign executor such as futures_lite block_on; LabRuntime teardown hits it deterministically. Internal callers run as runtime tasks and are dropped at teardown.
- Fix: AdmittedRegionSlot::retire_unpublished(): under the inner lock, mark it published (if not already), take the waiters and wake them after unlocking. Call it for RegionCommand::Create in retire_region_commands, or from a Drop on CreateRegionRequest. The re-poll then sees an empty slot and a dead runtime and returns RuntimeUnavailable.
- Test: clone lab_teardown_releases_unapplied_region_finalizer_acknowledgment (lab/runtime.rs ~6727, FlagWaker). Poll open_child_region(ChildRegionSpec::inherit()) once (Pending), drop(lab), then assert the waker fired and the re-poll returns Err(RuntimeUnavailable).
- Same class, lower confidence: ChildRegion::close / close_with_outcome wait on RegionQuiescence (child_region.rs:413-438), and no teardown path sets close_notify.closed.

Files: src/runtime/spawn_mailbox.rs (peer e0155ea8 / rc_20260922 RegionCommand work in progress), so unclaimed.

title: protobuf codec limits: nested work re-charging rejects valid deep messages; raising the channel decode limit is ignored; derive encodes nested messages with default limits
description:
Read-only audit of src/grpc/protobuf_wire.rs and its callers (SapphireHill subagent, 2026-10-02, origin 2ad2e55c8). The wire decoder itself is sound against untrusted input: bounded varints, field-key validation, length checks before take, bounded group depth, no reachable panics. Findings are in the policy and caller layers:

1. (medium) ProtobufWireLimits::for_message_size gives max_work = 4 x message size, but each nested byte is charged again at every nesting level (documented at protobuf_wire.rs ~74). Valid messages under the byte limit fail with WorkLimitExceeded when deep. Example: with_max_size(100) and a 90-byte message nested 4 levels costs 430 > 400. At the default 4 MiB, a 3.5 MiB payload 4 levels deep fails. encode succeeds on the same value, so decode(encode(x)) fails. No test: the wire tests use 16x work. Options: raise the default multiplier (bounded by max_depth), or charge nested payloads once.

2. (medium, verified by SapphireHill) ProtoCodec::set_max_decode_message_size only ever LOWERS decode_limits.max_message_len (protobuf.rs ~893-900). Raising the channel decode limit above 4 MiB therefore still rejects 4-16 MiB messages with MessageLimitExceeded, against the docs at ~33-38 and ~714-718 ("a per-channel limit configured above this codec is actually honored"). Fix: when the wire limits were not set explicitly, rebuild them with for_message_size(max_size). Workaround: ProtoCodec::with_max_size(n). NOTE: src/grpc/protobuf.rs is LIVE-pinned by artifacts/otlp_metrics_mapping_contract_v1.json (sha256 + line_count) and artifacts/protobuf_owned_otlp_schema_v1.json (sha256 within the repository_pin_signature row digest). A fix must re-pin both together with their owner.

3. (medium) asupersync-macros/src/proto.rs ~695-701 and ~774-777: nested messages and map entries are always encoded with the default 4 MiB limits, ignoring the parent codec's. With with_max_size(16 MiB), a child holding a 5 MiB bytes field fails to encode with FieldLimitExceeded, although the same codec would decode it. Depth and field accounting restart per level (protobuf_wire.rs ~1277-1281 says a proper path is pending).

4. (low) proto.rs ~659-660: a singular double/float -0.0 is omitted (presence check value != 0.0), so decode returns +0.0. prost behaves the same; the C++ and Go reference implementations likely keep the sign (unverified).

5. (low, diagnostics) proto.rs ~945: packed-varint decode errors report offsets relative to the packed payload, not the message.

title: SSE write_to silently strips leading spaces from data field values (WHATWG round-trip gap)
description: src/web/sse.rs:151 SseEvent::write_to emits data lines as 'data:{line}' with no space after the colon. WHATWG HTML §9.2.6 EventSource parser definition: 'If value starts with a U+0020 SPACE character, remove it from value.' For data(' hello'), the wire format becomes 'data: hello\n' which the parser strips down to 'hello' — the application-provided leading space is silently lost on round-trip. The standard SSE writer idiom is to always emit one space after the colon, so the application's value round-trips through the parser's leading-space strip rule. Fix: when a data line starts with U+0020 SPACE, emit an extra padding space ('data: {line}') so the parser strips one and preserves the rest. Field-symmetric variant for id/event is lower-impact (server-controlled values rarely start with spaces) but should follow. Add regression tests: (1) data(' hello') wire format must contain 'data:  hello' (two spaces), (2) data('hello') unchanged at 'data:hello' for backward compat with the existing wire-format pin tests.

title: File soft cancellation can mutate the shared cursor after the mutable borrow ends
description: src/fs/file.rs offloads cursor-mutating methods such as seek, stream_position, rewind, and read_into_vec by moving an Arc<std::fs::File> into spawn_blocking_io. spawn_blocking explicitly uses soft cancellation: once running, the closure continues after its future is dropped. Dropping one of these &mut self futures therefore releases the Rust borrow while a background syscall can still move/read the same shared cursor; a subsequent operation may race or observe skipped/reordered bytes, and read_into_vec also loses the owned buffer/result. This contradicts the published filesystem cancellation claim in docs/tokio_fs_process_signal_migration_playbook.md. The supposed FS cancellation suite in tests/tokio_cancel_safe_fs_process_signal.rs does not cancel asupersync futures (FC-01..05 use synchronous std::fs happy paths), so the proof gap masks the defect. Fix must establish an explicit cancellation-safe serialization/completion protocol for cursor-mutating owned operations or narrow/document the API contract without claiming discarded results imply no mutation, and add a deterministic handshake regression that drops an actually-started blocking file operation then immediately reuses the File. Update the parity artifacts/tests so they exercise the public async API and fail closed on late cursor mutation.

title: ATP RQ sender reports a committed transfer as failed (Connection refused) when the runtime has a blocking pool: parallel path keeps spraying UDP after the receiver closes (7/8 vs 0/8)
description:
## Bug (measured 2026-10-03, SapphireHill)
With a blocking pool on both runtimes, the ATP RaptorQ sender reports a failed transfer even though the receiver COMMITTED it.

Evidence: dangling probe 3a5dc5133 on C14 dc016293d. It is tests/atp_rq_loopback_e2e.rs's loss-injection scenario (160,019-byte file, sender drops 1 in 7 sprayed symbols), run 8 times per arm with both sides' results printed:

- `pool=true` (bare RuntimeBuilder::multi_thread() under the held kpmoy5.1.15 default, i.e. a blocking pool): 7 of 8 runs fail. Every failure is `send=Err(Io(Custom { kind: WriteZero, error: "Connection refused (os error 111)" }))`, while the receiver reports `Ok((committed=true, symbols_accepted=115))`.
- `pool=false` (blocking_threads(0, 0)): 0 of 8 fail; `send=Ok((true, 165, 3))`.

Repeat probe of the unmodified test:
- origin ff3798158 (bare builders, no pool): 0 of 20;
- C14 (bare builders with a pool): 18 of 20.

## Mechanism (reading net/atp/transport_rq/mod.rs at ff3798158)
A pool switches the sender into the parallel round-0 encode path (~9740, effective_encode_m from pool.current_max_threads()), and the receiver into parallel decode and auth verify (rq_decode_core_limit_for_cx ~7992, rq_auth_verify_width_for_cx ~15484).

The receiver finishes and closes its UDP socket while the sender is still spraying symbols. The kernel answers with ICMP port-unreachable, the sender's next UDP send fails with ECONNREFUSED, and the sender treats that as fatal (mapped to WriteZero) before it reads the commit receipt on the control channel.

## Impact
Any ATP deployment whose runtime has a blocking pool can report a successful transfer as failed under loss. The CLI and daemon size pools explicitly for RaptorQ work. Whether the CLI and daemon hit it in practice depends on their pool size and on network timing; not measured.

## Fix direction
- During spraying, treat ECONNREFUSED / ConnectionRefused on the UDP data socket as "the receiver stopped listening". Stop spraying and wait for the control-channel receipt, which decides success or failure, with the existing timeout.
- Only report failure if the control channel says so or times out.

Test: the loss-injection scenario with explicit blocking pools on both sides (sizes 2..8), run repeatedly, must commit on both sides every time. Planted negative: the same test against the current sender reproduces the false failure.

Separately, decide whether rq_decode_core_limit_for_cx should cap at real cores: min(pool cap, available_parallelism).
