title: [reality-check-wave2][http3] Implement full QPACK instruction streams and blocked-stream scheduling
description:
Implement full QPACK instruction-stream parity and blocked-stream scheduling for the native HTTP/3 lane.

Background and evidence:
The current HTTP/3 implementation is no longer merely static-only: src/http/h3_native.rs has H3QpackMode::DynamicTableAllowed, QpackContext, dynamic field-section helpers, Huffman string support, QPACK settings parsing, and recognition of H3UniStreamType::QpackEncoder / H3UniStreamType::QpackDecoder. The support matrix still draws a hard boundary: artifacts/http3_qpack_support_matrix_v1.json says full QPACK encoder/decoder instruction-stream parity and blocked-stream scheduling are not advertised. docs/integration.md says QPACK streams are recognized and duplicate streams fail closed, but instruction-stream processing and blocked-stream scheduling are not shipped. src/http/h3_native.rs currently errors with the stable message "qpack streams carry instructions, not h3 frames" when mapping QPACK streams as H3 frames.

Scope:
- Implement RFC 9204 encoder and decoder instruction-stream state machines for Set Dynamic Table Capacity, Insert With Name Reference, Insert Without Name Reference, Duplicate, Header Acknowledgement, Stream Cancellation, and Insert Count Increment.
- Integrate instruction streams with existing QpackDynamicTable and QpackContext rather than creating a parallel table implementation.
- Implement Required Insert Count blocking, unblocking, and SETTINGS_QPACK_BLOCKED_STREAMS enforcement with explicit connection-level and stream-level error mapping.
- Preserve default StaticOnly policy: dynamic table capacity and blocked streams must still fail closed unless H3QpackMode::DynamicTableAllowed is selected.
- Keep HTTP/3 frame parsing distinct from QPACK instruction streams; the current "qpack streams carry instructions" guard should become an instruction-stream dispatch boundary, not disappear into frame parsing.
- Update artifacts/http3_qpack_support_matrix_v1.json and docs only after source and tests prove the new support class.

Unit tests required:
- Instruction encode/decode round trips for every encoder and decoder instruction type, including boundary prefix-integer lengths and malformed/truncated instructions.
- Dynamic table state transitions for insert, duplicate, capacity shrink, eviction, reference protection, and insert count increment.
- Blocked-stream scheduler tests for zero blocked-stream capacity, max capacity, out-of-order acknowledgements, cancellation while blocked, and required-insert-count overflow.
- StaticOnly regression tests proving dynamic instructions/settings still fail closed under the default policy.

E2E/script proof required:
Add or extend a deterministic HTTP/3/QPACK proof runner that logs bead_id, scenario_id, qpack_mode, encoder_stream_id, decoder_stream_id, required_insert_count, known_received_count, blocked_stream_count, settings_blocked_streams, expected_event, actual_event, support_class, verdict, and first_failure. Include at least one multi-stream scenario where one stream blocks on Required Insert Count and later unblocks after Insert Count Increment.

Validation:
All Rust validation must run through rch exec. Minimum expected lanes: rustfmt for touched Rust files, targeted cargo test for h3_native/QPACK unit tests with --features test-internals,http3, an integration/conformance command for the new proof runner, and scoped clippy if the touched test frontier permits it.

Non-goals:
Do not pull in h3/quinn as a runtime dependency for the core crate. Do not weaken the default StaticOnly policy to make tests pass. Do not broaden README claims until the instruction-stream and blocked-stream behavior is actually implemented and proven.
close_reason: Verified parent QPACK implementation bead after landed source/docs/proof gates. asupersync-1xxmyo closed with commit 19b994835 for instruction-stream APIs and deterministic proof runner; asupersync-bdw1hb closed with commit de7d82df8 for support matrix/docs promotion gate. Live source exposes QpackInstructionStreamState, encoder/decoder instruction handling for Set Dynamic Table Capacity, Insert With Name Reference, Insert Without Name Reference, Duplicate, Header Acknowledgement, Stream Cancellation, and Insert Count Increment, plus bounded Required Insert Count blocked-stream scheduling. README/docs/artifacts preserve StaticOnly as default and explicitly avoid h3/quinn drop-in parity, full QUIC deployment parity, or default dynamic QPACK overclaim. Proofs verified on current main: matrix/runner/doc diff checks passed, rch rustfmt passed, rch http3_qpack_support_matrix_contract passed 5/5, scripts/http3_qpack_proof_runner.sh wrote fresh run_report git_sha=6d74b9784 validation_passed=true test_status=0 scenario_count=8 missing_scenarios=[] drifts=[], and no QPACK evidence paths changed from that proof SHA to closeout HEAD.

title: [SUB-EPIC] macOS Reactor (kqueue)
description:
# Sub-Epic: macOS Reactor (kqueue)

## Purpose

Implement a production-quality kqueue-based reactor for macOS and BSD systems. Important for developer experience since many developers use Macs.

## Background

### What is kqueue?

kqueue (kernel event queue) is the BSD/macOS event notification mechanism. Similar to epoll in goals, but different API and semantics.

Key syscalls:
- `kqueue()` - Create kqueue instance
- `kevent()` - Register interest and wait for events (combined operation)

### kqueue vs epoll

| Feature | epoll (Linux) | kqueue (BSD/macOS) |
|---------|---------------|-------------------|
| Level/Edge | Both, flag | Edge by default |
| Add/Wait | Separate calls | Combined in kevent() |
| Multiple events | No | Yes (one call) |
| Timer support | timerfd | Built-in |
| Signal support | signalfd | Built-in |

### Edge-Triggered Behavior

kqueue is edge-triggered by default:
- EV_CLEAR flag re-arms after delivery (like edge-triggered)
- Without EV_CLEAR, event is disabled after delivery (one-shot)

We'll use EV_CLEAR for persistent monitoring.

## Design

```rust
pub struct KqueueReactor {
    /// The kqueue file descriptor
    kq_fd: RawFd,
    /// Token slab and state
    inner: Mutex<KqueueInner>,
}

struct KqueueInner {
    wakers: TokenSlab,
    /// Track registered fds to prevent double-registration
    registrations: HashSet<(RawFd, i16)>, // (fd, filter)
}
```

## Key Differences from Epoll Implementation

1. **Combined register + wait**: kevent() does both
2. **Filters**: EVFILT_READ, EVFILT_WRITE (not flags)
3. **User data**: udata field for token (like epoll_event.data)
4. **Wakeup**: Use pipe or EVFILT_USER (macOS 10.6+)

## Platform Requirements

- macOS 10.6+ (for EVFILT_USER)
- Or FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD, DragonFlyBSD

## Deliverables

1. KqueueReactor implementing Reactor trait
2. EVFILT_USER wakeup mechanism (or pipe fallback)
3. EV_CLEAR for persistent monitoring
4. Unit tests with real sockets
5. Cross-platform test coverage with Linux

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Feature parity with EpollReactor
- [ ] Works on macOS Ventura+
- [ ] Cross-thread wakeup reliable
- [ ] All epoll tests have kqueue equivalents
close_reason: All dependencies complete: wx8h (Core Reactor Abstraction), cysj (register/deregister/poll/wake), and s24w (core KqueueReactor structure) are now CLOSED. The kqueue.rs implementation using the polling crate provides a production-quality kqueue-based reactor for macOS/BSD.

title: io_uring reactor register returns raw EBADF for an invalid fd; Reactor::register documents InvalidInput
description:
Reactor::register documents `io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput` for an invalid source fd (src/runtime/reactor/mod.rs ~991). IoUringReactor returns the raw EBADF from fcntl for both -1 and RawFd::MAX (io_uring.rs ~848-849 validate_safe_fd, called at ~1608). title: WebSocket audit: close()/send(Close) on the unsplit client/server ignore cancellation and close_timeout once CloseSent (can hang forever on a non-reading peer); a dropped close loses its Close frame
description:
Read-only audit of src/net/websocket/** at ac4d94ee7 (origin + SapphireHill stacks N/P), SapphireHill audit agent round 7, 10-05. The HIGH was confirmed by re-reading client.rs write_path_cancelled (~1007) and close() (~830) against split.rs's fixed write_path_cancelled (~232).

## HIGH
H1. close() / send(Message::Close) on the unsplit client and server can hang forever, ignoring both close_timeout and cancellation.
- Cause: initiate() moves the state to CloseSent before the Close frame is written. The writes then compute is_open = false, and write_path_cancelled(op_cx, false) is always false, so even an EXPLICIT op_cx is ignored. The cancel waker is refreshed only while open.
- close() bounds only the response read: the Close write, the server's Pong replies inside its close loop and the final shutdown() are unbounded.
- split.rs already fixed this class ("An explicitly supplied operation context remains authoritative even after a Close frame changes the handshake state to CloseSent"); client.rs and server.rs were not updated.
- Trigger: the peer stops reading (send buffer full), then ws.close(&cx, ..). The task never finishes even after cx is cancelled, so region close hangs. This contradicts close.rs ("Bounded timeout prevents hanging on unresponsive peers").
- FIX (SapphireHill, after N lands; client.rs/server.rs are in stack N): mirror split.rs (explicit op_cx authoritative, refresh the cancel waker for it), and bound the initiate/Pong/shutdown steps by close_timeout.

## MEDIUM
M2. A locally initiated Close frame is lost when the closing future is dropped before the frame's first byte is written.
- The state becomes CloseSent, but the frame sits in a local buffer across awaits (pre-flush, first poll_write, the split write permit).
- A retried close()/send(Close)/flush_close then only flushes write_buf, which does not hold the Close, and returns Ok without sending one.
- Trigger: the caller's timeout or select, or the crate's own recv-cancel timeout(close_timeout, initiate_close(..)).
- Fix: encode the Close into the retained write_buf synchronously in initiate_close_with_cx, then flush.

## LOW
- L3. The split writer can put a data frame after our Close echo (send checks is_open only before waiting for the permit).
- L4. recv can stay stuck on OutboundBufferFull until the heartbeat times out (the heartbeat Ping budget check runs before the write_buf flush).
- L5. The server misses its TCP shutdown in two paths (a close started via send(Close) and answered in recv; a recv cancelled mid-echo).
- Policy note: close codes 1016-2999 are accepted on receive (test-pinned); Autobahn 7.9.6-9 expect 1002. Owner.
- Already on 5aioka and still present: close_on_drop is never read; a failing connection never sends a Close; buffered Pongs are ignored by the heartbeat; EOF mid-message returns Ok(None); a deflate offer that cannot be honoured fails instead of being declined; split has no close_timeout.

Judged SOUND: frame.rs (lengths, masking rules, control frame limits, RSV bits, close payload validation, poisoning), MessageAssembler, data-frame send cancellation, handshake.rs, compression.rs (bounded inflation), heartbeat.rs (apart from the known item), close.rs parsing/encoding.

Tests close_on_a_stalled_peer_ends_when_cancelled (client and server; never-waking IO, cross-thread cancel). comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
FOUND 2026-07-26 by SapphireHill while clearing br-asupersync-u05hk9's unused-`cx` lint in this same file. The lint was the thread; this is what was on the end of it.

THE DEFECT: `unicode_normalization_injection_audit` Test Case 1 asserts two strings differ. They are byte-identical, so `assert_ne!` panics unconditionally and the test CANNOT pass.

  let regular_apostrophe = "user'@example.com"; // U+0027
  let unicode_apostrophe = "user'@example.com"; // U+2019 (right single quotation mark)
  assert_ne!(regular_apostrophe, unicode_apostrophe, "Unicode strings should be different");

VERIFIED BY BYTE INSPECTION, not by reading: hexdump of both literal lines shows `20 22 75 73 65 72 27 40` — 0x27 (ASCII apostrophe) in BOTH. Decoded via python3: both are `"user'@example.com"`, comparison IDENTICAL = True. The U+2019 the comment promises was never present; `git show a76823b63` confirms the file was authored with ASCII in both slots.

SAME FLATTENING AT TWO MORE SITES:
  - lines ~333/334: `user_input` vs `unicode_variant`, both ASCII.
  - `test_strings` (~374/375): `"user'quote", // U+0027` and `"user'quote", // U+2019` are the same string, so slots 2 and 3 of the byte-preservation loop test the same input twice.
Test cases 2 and 4 escaped correctly (`"cafe\u{0301}"`, `"test\u{200B}@domain.com"`) and still have teeth, as does the Cyrillic `а` (U+0430) at ~line 205 and `é` at ~372.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE ONE ASSERT: CI runs `cargo test --test '*' --all-features`. If that lane were green, this test would be red. It is not red, therefore the `--features sqlite` lane has NEVER RUN GREEN. That is independent, mechanical proof of the same skipped-gate thesis as br-asupersync-c6ppu4 — and it is exactly why an unused variable was able to sit at line 351 for the file's entire life without anyone noticing.

FIX — use explicit escapes so an editor or a normalizing tool cannot silently flatten them again:
  let unicode_apostrophe = "user\u{2019}@example.com";
  let unicode_variant    = "\u{2019}; DROP TABLE users; --";
  and in `test_strings`: "user\u{2019}quote"

DO NOT just delete the assert to make it pass. The assertion is correct in intent; the data is wrong. And expect the test to have MORE to say once the literals are real — a homoglyph-based injection audit whose homoglyphs are ASCII has been asserting nothing about homoglyphs at all.

NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY: I have not run this test with corrected literals, so I do not know whether the underlying SQLite behavior it audits is actually sound. Fixing the literals may surface a genuine second finding. That is the point.

RELATED: br-asupersync-u05hk9 (the lint that led here; its unused-`cx` fix is landing separately and does NOT fix this), br-asupersync-c6ppu4.

title: Implement Tower feature flag and optional dependency
description:
## Overview

Make Tower integration optional via feature flag to avoid mandatory dependencies.

## Requirements

### Feature Flag
```toml
# Cargo.toml
[features]
default = []
tower = ["dep:tower", "dep:tower-service"]

[dependencies]
tower = { version = "0.4", optional = true }
tower-service = { version = "0.3", optional = true }
```

### Conditional Compilation
```rust
// src/tower/mod.rs
#![cfg(feature = "tower")]

mod adapter;
mod service;

pub use adapter::{AsupersyncAdapter, TowerAdapter};
pub use service::AsupersyncService;
```

### Re-exports
```rust
// src/lib.rs
#[cfg(feature = "tower")]
pub mod tower;
```

### Documentation
Document feature in:
- README.md
- lib.rs module docs
- Cargo.toml metadata

## Acceptance Criteria
1. "tower" feature flag
2. Compiles without tower feature
3. tower module only present with feature
4. Feature documented in README
5. CI tests both with and without feature

## Test Requirements
- Test compilation without feature
- Test compilation with feature
- Test feature detection at runtime

title: perf: Framed/FramedWrite flush allocates+memcpys the drained prefix per write pass (split_to used purely to discard)
description: src/codec/framed.rs and src/codec/framed_write.rs poll_flush call  purely to discard the n bytes already written to the transport. This crate's BytesMut::split_to (src/bytes/bytes_mut.rs:304) does Vec::with_capacity(at)+extend_from_slice (alloc + memcpy of  bytes) then bumps self.start and compact_front_if_empty — so every write pass performs an up-to-8KB heap alloc + copy that is immediately dropped, up to ~32x per poll_flush. title: FramedRead re-enters ordinary decode between repeated EOF frames
description: src/codec/framed_read.rs calls decoder.decode unconditionally at the top of every poll, then calls decode_eof when eof is set. If decode_eof legitimately emits several final frames across polls, the second and later polls interpose ordinary decode after EOF-finalization has begun. A stateful decoder that allows pre-EOF decode but forbids it after its first decode_eof therefore yields final frame 0 and then panics or reorders instead of yielding 1..N. Full-duplex Framed already guards ordinary decode with if !eof after EOF is known, so this intervening-call defect is FramedRead-only. Minimum fix: mirror that guard and regress a decoder emitting four EOF frames. Full Tokio parity additionally needs readable/read-first state in both FramedRead and Framed: both currently call decode on an initially empty buffer before polling an immediate-EOF reader, whereas the reference routes a zero-byte read directly to repeated decode_eof and its multi_frames_on_eof decoder makes ordinary decode unreachable. Document repeated decode_eof semantics in Decoder, port the exact immediate-EOF multi-frame case, and retain pre-buffered normal decode behavior. Existing lifecycle fuzz can emit only one EOF remainder and no bead covers multiple final frames. Independently confirmed by two source reviews on 2026-07-15.

title: Framed writers have no backpressure boundary or readiness protocol
description: FramedWrite and Framed expose only synchronous unconditional send, which encodes directly into an internal BytesMut. with_capacity is allocation capacity, not a high-water mark. Downstream IO is polled only later by poll_flush, so a permanently Pending writer plus repeated send calls grows memory with total input and offers callers no readiness/capacity boundary. This violates docs/tokio_functional_parity_contract.md D5-BP-01 and can amplify real batches such as the H2 listener loop that drains every next_frame into Framed before one flush. Tokio-util has a configurable backpressure_boundary and Sink poll_ready that flushes at the boundary. Add an explicit boundary to both local types and make the normal send protocol readiness-aware (poll_ready/start_send or async send); do not retain unconditional send as the only standard path. Define soft-bound behavior for one oversized frame. Regress with an always-Pending writer: accept only to the boundary, then readiness stays Pending without further growth; after writes resume, readiness resumes. Mirror the test on Framed and cover one oversized frame. Closed asupersync-eiy5nx requested a backpressure fuzzer but its tracker-only commits added no target or production boundary; no open duplicate exists. Independently confirmed by two source reviews on 2026-07-15.

title: [cancel-bug-hunt] cancel/symbol_cancel.rs: cancel() listeners only see FIRST reason, strengthened reason never re-notifies
description: src/cancel/symbol_cancel.rs:210-286 SymbolCancelToken::cancel(). On the FIRST call (CAS wins), listeners are drained via mem::take and notified with the first reason. On a SUBSEQUENT call (CAS loses), the stored reason is strengthened via reason.strengthen(new) — which can escalate severity (e.g., Timeout → ParentCancelled → Shutdown). But the original listeners are GONE (drained on first call) and cannot be re-notified with the stronger reason. Cancel-protocol violation: monotone-severity propagation is observable in stored state but invisible to subscribers. A listener that scheduled soft cleanup based on Timeout will not learn that the cancellation has escalated to Shutdown and continue down the soft path. Mitigation options: (1) keep a separate 'escalation listeners' channel that fires on strengthen events; (2) replace the drain-once-and-discard model with a retain-and-re-notify model gated on reason change; (3) document the limitation and require callers to query reason() proactively after each cancellation event. Severity HIGH for systems whose cleanup behavior depends on cancel kind.
close_reason: listeners retained across cancels with notified_severity bookkeeping; cancel() re-fires listeners whose last severity is below the new strengthened severity (38ea89a6e)

title: [conformance] WebSocket: missing control-frame size limit + RSV bits + reserved opcodes + Sec-WebSocket-Accept coverage
description:
RFC 6455 conformance gaps in tests/conformance/websocket_rfc6455/*. Concrete missing vectors:

(1) RFC 6455 §5.2 — Control frame payload size limit MUST be ≤ 125 bytes. PING/PONG/CLOSE with 126+-byte payload must fail connection. No systematic test.

(2) RFC 6455 §5.1 — RSV bits (3 reserved bits): non-zero RSV on a frame without negotiated extension MUST fail connection per §7.2.2.

(3) RFC 6455 §5.5.1 — Reserved opcodes (0x3-0x7 data, 0xB-0xF control): peer MUST fail connection on receipt.

(4) RFC 6455 §4.4 — Sec-WebSocket-Accept value: client must verify SHA-1(client-key + GUID) base64 matches the server's response header; mismatch = handshake failure.

(5) RFC 6455 §4.1 — Handshake header case-insensitivity: Upgrade/Connection/Sec-WebSocket-* must accept any case mix per HTTP, but not all parsers handle this correctly.

(6) RFC 6455 §7.1.4 — Closing handshake status code validation: 1000-4999 ranges, status-code-before-reason byte order, non-UTF-8 reason rejection.

(7) RFC 6455 §5.5.2 — PING auto-response semantics: unrequested PONG arrival, out-of-order PONG matching, PING in closing state.

Fix direction: tests/conformance/websocket_rfc6455/{control_frame_size, rsv_bits, reserved_opcodes, accept_header_validation, close_status_codes}_tests.rs.

Source: /testing-conformance-harnesses gap audit (2026-04-27).

title: Soft-cancelled filesystem mutations can commit after cancellation
description: Most async filesystem mutators delegate directly to spawn_blocking_io, whose documented soft-cancellation model allows an already-running closure to finish after the returned future is dropped. Consequently File::create/OpenOptions with truncate, fs::write, copy, set_permissions, rename, remove_file, create/remove_dir, links, and write_atomic can mutate or destroy external state after the caller has observed cancellation; File::create or fs::write can truncate existing data even though no success result is delivered. This contradicts docs/tokio_fs_process_signal_migration_playbook.md section 2.5 claiming all file operations are cancel-safe and that dropped futures discard partial results without corruption, plus T37C-02 claiming File::create is cancel-safe. Several src/fs/dir.rs comments also call one-shot operations cancel-safe merely because each syscall is atomic, conflating atomicity with cancellation safety. Existing FC-01..05 tests do not poll then drop any asupersync future. Inventory every public fs mutator, publish accurate per-operation cancellation boundaries, remove false broad proof claims, and provide a two-phase/staged API where complete-or-nothing-after-cancel is promised (especially replacement writes). Add deterministic start/cancel/late-completion regressions through an injectable blocking seam so post-cancel external effects cannot be mislabeled as proved safe.

title: OTLP span processor uses mutex-protected queue under high-frequency load
description:
**PERFORMANCE BOTTLENECK DETECTED**: BatchSpanProcessor work-queue uses mutex contention

**AUDIT FINDING**: BoundedExportQueue (LoadSheddingTraceExporter) uses Mutex<VecDeque<T>> 
for span batch queuing, creating lock contention under high-frequency span creation.

**EVIDENCE**:
- File: src/observability/otlp_trace_exporter.rs:83
- Line 83: `queue: Mutex<VecDeque<T>>`
- Line 101: `let mut queue = self.queue.lock();` (enqueue)
- Line 115: `self.queue.lock().pop_front()` (dequeue)
- Line 120: `self.queue.lock().len()` (metrics)

**PERFORMANCE IMPACT**:
- High-frequency span creation (100K+ spans/sec) causes mutex contention
- Every span batch export acquires exclusive lock
- Potential serialization bottleneck limiting throughput
- Thread parking/unparking overhead under contention

**FLOW ANALYSIS**:
1. Span creation → SpanBatch
2. LoadSheddingTraceExporter.export() → export_queue.enqueue() 
3. enqueue() acquires mutex → serializes all span exports

**RECOMMENDATION**: Replace with lock-free queue implementation
- Consider crossbeam-queue or similar lock-free data structure
- SPSC (Single Producer Single Consumer) if export is single-threaded
- MPSC (Multi Producer Single Consumer) for multi-threaded span creation
- Atomic operations for queue management
- Benchmark improvement under 100K+ spans/sec load

title: [memory-ordering] sync/notify.rs try_consume_stored_notification CAS uses Acquire-Acquire instead of AcqRel-Acquire — release pairing missing on consume
description:
src/sync/notify.rs:359-363 — Notified::try_consume_stored_notification uses compare_exchange_weak with Ordering::Acquire on BOTH success and failure when decrementing stored_notifications. The success path needs Ordering::Release (or AcqRel) because it consumes a notification stored by notify_one() at line 215 with Ordering::Release.

Why this is a memory-ordering bug:
  - notify_one stores a notification by incrementing stored_notifications with Release ordering (line 215). The Release synchronizes-with any subsequent Acquire load that observes the new value.
  - try_consume_stored_notification decrements with Acquire on success (line 362). Acquire on the consume side pairs with Release on the produce side — that part is correct for OBSERVING the produced value.
  - BUT: the consumer is not just observing, it is ITSELF producing a happens-before edge for whatever runs after it. After the CAS succeeds, the consumer proceeds to use whatever resource was guarded by the notification. Other threads observing this consumption (e.g., a subsequent notify_one finding the counter back at zero and re-storing) need Release-ordering visibility into the consumer's preceding operations.
  - Acquire-on-success-Acquire-on-failure means the consumer's prior writes are NOT released to other threads at the CAS point. A subsequent producer that sees the lower stored_notifications value via Acquire load may miss the consumer's preceding work.

The common safe ordering for a CAS that BOTH consumes and signals is AcqRel on success and Acquire on failure.

Concrete failure mode: under heavy notify/consume contention, a consumer reads the notification, performs work, and another producer observes the counter via a relaxed-ish path. The producer's downstream operations may execute out of order relative to the consumer's prior work, causing TOCTOU-style races on resources guarded by the notification.

Fix direction:
  1. Change the CAS at line 362 from compare_exchange_weak(_, _, Ordering::Acquire, Ordering::Acquire) to compare_exchange_weak(_, _, Ordering::AcqRel, Ordering::Acquire).
  2. Add a regression test (Loom-based, using the loom-tests feature) that exercises concurrent notify_one + try_consume to verify no observation reorderings.
  3. Audit other consume-style CAS sites in sync/* for the same pattern.

Severity HIGH because (a) memory-ordering bugs are silent until very-specific load patterns trigger them, then they manifest as data races that are catastrophic to debug, and (b) Notify is a widely-used primitive in this codebase, so the bug is reachable from many code paths.

Source: /reality-check on src/sync/* deepest pass (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Notify try_consume_stored_notification CAS now uses AcqRel on success (Relaxed on failure). Pairs the consume-side release with subsequent acquire-side observers, closing the missing happens-before edge for post-notification work. Changes landed in commit 1df2e407e.

title: Runtime table audit: resolved obligation records are never reclaimed (one record per mpsc send kept forever), holder buckets and the finalization fence grow without bound; region-heap reclaim runs user Drop under the state lock
description:
Read-only audit of src/runtime/{task_table,region_table,obligation_table,region_heap}.rs at origin/main 47117810a (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-05). Each finding was re-checked against the code.

## HIGH
H1. ObligationTable::remove (obligation_table.rs ~400) has no production caller.
- commit (~508), abort (~559) and mark_leaked (~610) only change a record's state.
- Region close only adds the region to finalized_regions (state.rs ~9912).
- Every mpsc reserve/send therefore leaves one ObligationRecord in the arena for the life of the runtime: mpsc.rs ~1107 → Cx::try_register_obligation → obligation mailbox → create_obligation_in → ObligationTable::create. So do oneshot, broadcast, permits and leases.
- A record carries a description, a SourceLocation and, in debug builds, a Backtrace: about 150-200 B each.
- Every full scan (collect_obligation_leaks, counts, for_region, audits) becomes O(all obligations ever created).

H2. The by_holder buckets (~313-327, ~650-658) keep one (TaskId, ids) entry per task generation that ever used an arena slot.
- Entries leave only via remove.
- Every task completion calls ids_for_holder twice (collect_obligation_leaks_for_holder, sorted_pending_ids_for_holder).
- Each call is a linear scan of the bucket under the state lock, even for tasks with no obligation, so throughput degrades steadily.

H3. finalized_regions (~137, ~974) gains one entry per region ever closed and never shrinks. A server with a region per request grows it per request.

## MEDIUM
M1. debug_assert_pending_counters_match (~241-268) scans every record on every create/commit/abort/leak/remove and on pending_count(). Debug and lab runs become O(N^2) (the bzict6 class; TaskTable samples its check).

M2. RegionHeap::reclaim_all (region_heap.rs ~455-474) drops each payload in place mid-loop, after len=0. It is called from RegionRecord::complete_close under inner.write() and the RuntimeState lock, before the close receipt is stored and the close waiters are woken.
- A panicking Drop leaves the region Closed but never removed: the parent never closes, waiters are never woken, and a later dealloc underflows len.
- A re-entrant Drop deadlocks.
- Fix: take every payload out first, publish the close, then drop the payloads after the state lock is released, under catch_unwind.

## LOW
L1. region_heap.rs ~55-57 claims another heap rejects a stale HeapIndex. Every heap starts at generation 0, so heap B accepts A's {0,0,T}. RRef is still safe because rref_get checks the region id. Fix the doc or add a per-heap nonce.
L2. lyapunov.rs ~315-319 calls the task counters O(1), but TaskTable::count_in_phase scans the arena: 3 calls per snapshot, under the state and task-table locks.
L3. RegionTable::remove (~204-207) repeats the parent's remove_child (Vec::retain) that state.rs ~9946 already did, and add_child does Vec::contains. N sibling regions cost O(N^2).

## Status
H1, H2, H3 and M1 are fixed in SapphireHill's stack P (P2 9cbe9a591, not pushed yet):
- bounded retention of resolved records (4096), reclaimed through remove(), which also drops the holder-index entry; leaked and pending records are never reclaimed;
- a 4096-region fence;
- a sampled debug check.

M2 and the LOWs are open.
close_reason: LANDED in main ce8b3a049: L1 doc and L2 O(1) task phase tracking. Clarified region_heap generation vs cross-region RRef check (L1). Implemented TaskPhaseTracker and upgraded TaskPhaseCell to maintain atomic live and per-phase counts across direct mutations and recycling; TaskTable::count_in_phase is O(1) with sampled debug assertions. All audit findings (H1-H3, M1-M2, L1-L3) are now fully landed.

title: [EPIC-INFRA] Deterministic Replay Debugging
description:
## Overview

Deterministic Replay Debugging enables recording execution traces and replaying them exactly to debug issues. This is a unique capability enabled by asupersync's deterministic Lab runtime.

## Strategic Value

**Problem Solved**: Async bugs are notoriously hard to reproduce. Race conditions, timing-dependent failures, and heisenbugs often disappear when debugging is enabled.

**Why This Approach**: Because asupersync has a deterministic Lab runtime with controllable scheduling, we can record every scheduling decision, timer event, and I/O result, then replay them exactly. This transforms "unreproducible" bugs into deterministic test cases.

**Differentiation**: No other Rust async runtime offers this. Traditional runtimes use OS schedulers and real I/O, making exact replay impossible. Our Lab runtime's determinism makes this feasible.

## Architecture

### Recording Phase
- Instrument Lab runtime to emit trace events
- Capture: scheduling decisions, timer ticks, I/O results, RNG seeds
- Store in compact binary format (bincode or MessagePack)
- Include minimal metadata for versioning

### Replay Phase
- Load trace file, verify compatibility
- Create Lab runtime in replay mode
- Feed recorded decisions instead of making new ones
- Assert execution matches recorded state

### Debugging Integration
- Provide "step" and "continue" commands in replay
- Show region tree state at each step
- Highlight divergence if replay doesn't match

## Acceptance Criteria

1. RecordingTrace captures all non-determinism sources
2. Replay mode reproduces exact execution order
3. Trace file format is versioned and forward-compatible
4. Documentation includes debugging workflow examples
5. At least 3 complex test scenarios demonstrate value

## Dependencies

- Builds on existing trace module infrastructure
- May benefit from tracing integration (Epic #2)

## Priority Rationale

Ranked #6 because while powerful, it requires significant infrastructure and the target users (debugging complex issues) are a subset of all users.
close_reason: All dependency tasks closed (trace events, compression, compat, streaming replay, CLI, tests, docs). Epic complete.

# Task

Write comprehensive documentation and examples for the cancellation injection

   ```rust
   #[test]

               my_async_function(cx).await
   ```

3. **Injection Strategies**: When to use each

   - RandomSample: Large tests, fuzzing

4. **Understanding Failures**: How to read and fix failures

title: Child-region audit: close() awaited outside the runtime hangs at teardown; opening can lose its teardown wake; close_within reports an already-closed region as TimedOut; LiveTasks doc overclaims
description:
Read-only audit (subagent, origin e0a861347) of the owned child-region API: src/cx/child_region.rs and its region commands in spawn_mailbox.rs, three_lane.rs and lab/runtime.rs. Filed by SapphireHill 2026-10-04.

1. MEDIUM: close() and close_with_outcome() awaited OUTSIDE the owning runtime hang forever if the runtime is torn down while the region is still closing.
   - RegionQuiescence checked only RegionCloseState::closed.
   - retire_region_commands drops an unapplied Close (`_ => {}`), and teardown wakes nothing.
   - Same shape as werypv (monitors and links).
2. LOW: ChildRegionOpening::poll checked liveness BEFORE registering its waker. A teardown landing between the two finds no waiter, so an off-runtime opener stays pending.
3. LOW: close_within can report TimedOut, with no stragglers, for a region that already closed. TimeoutFuture checks its deadline before polling the inner future, so bound 0 or a late poll reads as elapsed; the lab says Quiescent.
4. LOW, doc: RegionLiveTasksQuery claims its list is "exactly the region's live tasks". With an external task table, a task turns terminal before its unlink is applied, so it can appear once.

Fix (candidate CRA2 9653c5133):
- close paths wait through ChildRegion::quiescence(), which registers the close state with the mailbox teardown list (impl TeardownWake for Mutex<RegionCloseState>). RegionQuiescence returns Result and fails closed with RuntimeUnavailable after the liveness guard is gone; it registers first, then checks.
- The opening registers before it checks liveness.
- close_within re-checks closed on Elapsed.
- The doc fix is line-neutral.

Tests:
- teardown_wakes_a_close_awaited_outside_the_runtime (lab);
- close_within_reports_an_already_closed_region_as_quiescent (native).
close_reason: Landed in 6e0f40280 (main=master ca1bc7485) with tests and a red control

title: [perf] runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs: next_task acquires self.local.lock() multiple times per dispatch
description: src/runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs:2772 Worker::next_task takes self.local.lock() (parking_lot::Mutex<PriorityScheduler>) at line 2828 (Phase 2: cancel/timed lanes), drops it, then re-acquires at line 2895 (Phase 3 peek for inversion check), drops it, and re-acquires at line 2917 (Phase 3b ready lane). For workers handling many short-lived tasks this is 2-3 acquire/release cycles per dispatch on the same hot mutex. Under N-worker contention the parking_lot mutex itself contends across cores. Mitigation: batch Phase 2 + Phase 3b into a single critical section (acquire once, check cancel/timed/ready in priority order, return on first hit), eliding the intermediate drops. The Phase 3 peek for inversion-check could use a lock-free snapshot OR be folded into the same critical section. Severity HIGH for high-worker-count deployments (16+ cores).

A downstream compatibility run of Asupersync main (0.6.0) by three consumers, for the next-release campaign (asupersync-yqlhh7, gate 5: downstream canaries). Run on 2026-10-09; local only, nothing published. It is evidence for the campaign, not a release receipt: the candidate was main at 419c0c093ab6, not an exact release SHA.

## Setup

- Asupersync main 419c0c093ab6 (0.6.0).
- fastapi_rust f317c0887b6b (= v0.5.0) and FrankenSQLite 022be25e5, each with an uncommitted one-line bump `asupersync = { version = "0.6.0", default-features = false }` plus `[patch.crates-io] asupersync = { path = ... }`.
- INATD (proprietary consumer) at 0e9dfd7 with asupersync, fastapi-core, fastapi-http, fsqlite and fsqlite-types path-patched. Cargo.lock resolves exactly one asupersync identity (0.6.0).

## Results

| Consumer / suite | Host | Result on 0.6.0 | Baseline on 0.5.0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| fastapi_rust `cargo test -p fastapi-core -p fastapi-http --no-fail-fast` | trj (x86_64 Linux) | 2,019 passed, 0 failed, 155 ignored | identical |
| FrankenSQLite `cargo test -p fsqlite --no-fail-fast` | trj | 1,042 passed, 1 failed, 33 ignored | 1,043 / 0 / 33 |
| INATD workspace `cargo test --workspace` | trj, macOS aarch64 | builds on both; trj 335 passed, 3 failed; macOS 340 passed, 4 failed; none caused by 0.6 (below) | all pass |
| TLS: rustls-graviola on `tls-core`, 27 cases incl. live handshakes | trj | 27 held, 0 failed | n/a (tls-core is 0.6-only) |
| Asupersync `cargo test --lib --no-fail-fast` | trj (load 40-110) | run 1: 24,966 passed, 2 failed; run 2: 24,967 passed, 1 failed (24 ignored) | n/a |

Asupersync lib failures, each passing in isolation (5/5, 5/5, 3/3), so load-sensitive rather than stable regressions:
- run 1: `cx::fiber::tests::a_panic_cancels_a_sibling_that_reads_its_context_later`, `cx::fiber::tests::a_panicking_fiber_cancels_its_siblings`;
- run 2: `sync::pool::tests::checked_pool_notifier_wake_retirement_and_resource_panics_preserve_primary`.

INATD failures, none caused by Asupersync 0.6:
- `int05_fp_closure` (2 tests, both hosts): INATD's dependency audit refuses path-sourced packages, so the rehearsal's own path patches fail it. A release re-pin uses crates.io packages.
- `sql_subset::the_store_query_forms_are_measured` (both hosts): a FrankenSQLite main change (STRICT primary-key NULL handling), filed there as bd-9y1gr.
- macOS only, `kernels_stay_inside_their_pool`: a thread-count race at load ~220 from other work; it passed 5/5 on re-run with the same tree.

## Downstream effect of the on-demand blocking pool default (8c7a87e96, kpmoy5.1.15)

Two consumers changed behavior only because a bare `RuntimeBuilder` now has a blocking pool:

1. **FrankenSQLite (observable on-disk change).** Its WAL-FEC repair pipeline starts whenever the runtime has a blocking pool. A read-only session on a fully backfilled WAL then creates `-wal-fec` and `-wal-fec.lock`, so its GH #294 artifact-stability test fails 5/5 on 0.6 and passes on 0.5 at the same commit. On 0.5 the same behavior reproduces with an explicit pool. Filed in FrankenSQLite as bd-xsxdz (bdf3afc11), with a reproduction and a proposed fix.
2. **INATD (thread budget).** Its store's owner runtime used `RuntimeBuilder::current_thread()` with no blocking configuration, relying on 0.5's "no pool". On 0.6 it would gain up to 512 threads its budget does not count. Fixed downstream by stating `blocking_threads(0, 0)` explicitly (INATD 0c0de9c).

kpmoy5.1.15 says this default is a documented-behavior change that needs owner approval. These two observations are relevant to that decision and to the release notes: consumers that relied on "no pool by default" should be told to state `blocking_threads(0, 0)`.

## Not covered

No exact release candidate, no Windows run, no `default-features = true` consumer, and no package (`cargo package`) check. Those remain the campaign's gates.

title: [formal-semantics] Tighten RECORD-COMPLETE wording in spec
description: Spec §3.7.1 RECORD-COMPLETE: 'k ∈ dom(D) ⇒ D'[k].outcome = Some(outcome)'. Implementation in src/remote.rs IdempotencyStore is stricter: it rejects completions on records that have already expired (checked in IdempotencyStore::check, src/remote.rs:1444). The impl is safer (fail-closed under TTL races) but technically violates the literal spec. Update spec to require '(k ∈ dom(D)) ∧ (now < D[k].expires_at)' to match impl, or add explicit caveat that completion of expired records is undefined.
close_reason: Spec §3.7.1 RECORD-COMPLETE tightened to require non-expired record; adds expiry-guard rationale and lazy-eviction operational note

title: H1 server and HTTP/3 router discard committed produced-body frames (incl. masked trailers) once the producer Cx is cancelled
description:
## Follow-up to the bi2462.105 root cause (SapphireHill, 2026-09-28)
OutgoingBody::poll_frame receives with the PRODUCER's request Cx: mpsc::Receiver::poll_recv checks cx.checkpoint() before popping the queue (src/channel/mpsc.rs ~1646). Once the producer's context is cancelled, frames it already committed are unreadable. That includes terminal trailers sent under Cx::masked, which is how gRPC's send_terminal publishes grpc-status after cancellation. The transport sees Err(BodyCancelled) and the committed output is discarded.
For HTTP/2 this hung the stream forever: body_eof was set, and then ProducedDone reported Finished{Trailers} with no trailers ever delivered. It is fixed by the pub(crate) OutgoingBody::poll_committed_frame (drains committed frames before observing cancellation) used by the H2 listener's produced-body poll (see the .105 landing).
The same read pattern remains in:
- src/http/h1/server.rs ~2447: Pin::new(&mut response.body).poll_frame(task_cx) in the chunked produced-response writer.
- src/web/router.rs ~2705: Pin::new(body).poll_frame(task_cx) in the native HTTP/3 produced-response poll.
Work: for each, (1) write a test where a producer commits DATA and trailers, masks the terminal send, and has its request Cx cancelled before the transport drains; assert the committed frames and trailers reach the peer; old red expected. (2) Switch the read to poll_committed_frame if the test confirms the loss. Check how each transport's finalize treats BodyCancelled versus a delivered trailer, so a committed terminal status is not replaced by an abort.
close_reason: H1 (75280f91d) and H2 (b4eba5785) fixed with red controls; H3 resets with H3_REQUEST_CANCELLED on request-region cancel with or without the router change (FH3/CH3 identical), so no silent loss; parity is an owner semantics choice

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
H3 half resolved with no code change (SapphireHill, 2026-09-28). Closing: H1 landed 75280f91d, H2 landed b4eba5785.

Evidence: I built the proposed H3 harness in tests/quic_h3_live_udp.rs, the test authenticated_listener_delivers_committed_trailers_after_producer_cancellation. The producer sends DATA and masked trailers into a two-frame channel, then cancels its producer Cx and returns Ok(sender). I gated it twice:
- FH3 66d0555eb (router.rs switched to poll_committed_frame) -> FAILED: StreamReset { stream_id: 0, error_code: 0x10c, final_size: 5 }
- CH3 755bc43cd (the router read unchanged, as on origin) -> FAILED with the identical StreamReset 0x10c, final_size 5 (hz2, lane ch3_ctl)

So the router read is not what decides the outcome. On H3 the producer Cx is the request region's Cx. Cancelling it goes through the request-body failure path and resets the stream with H3_REQUEST_CANCELLED after the 5 committed DATA bytes. The peer gets an explicit abort, not a silently truncated success. The silent-loss sequence hypothesized in this bead (BodyCancelled -> Pending -> EOF without trailers) is not reachable, because the reset comes first. The H2 hang class is not present on H3.

Whether H3 should instead drain committed masked trailers before honoring a request-region cancellation is a transport-semantics choice: H2 finalizes them, H3 resets. That belongs to the H3 owner, not to a bug fix, so the router change stays unlanded. If the owner wants H2 parity, the ready-made test and router diff are in /data/tmp/rc_20260923/wh3/ (router.rs, quic_h3_live_udp.rs). The router diff alone is insufficient; the request-body failure path would have to stop resetting while a committed terminal frame is queued.

title: transport dedup check_and_record returns UNIQUE without recording past max_symbols_per_object — false completion
description: Found in deep review (SapphireHill 2026-06-29). src/transport/aggregator.rs:~1306. Once an object reaches max_symbols_per_object (default 10_000) distinct symbols, check_and_record returns true (=new/unique) for EVERY further symbol WITHOUT recording it. So the same symbol_id presented twice both return true. In collect_fungible_symbols_until (~2023) each true increments unique_symbols toward target_unique_symbols, so re-presented DUPLICATES count as distinct progress -> complete = unique_symbols>=target can be reached with duplicates, and the RaptorQ decoder is re-fed the same symbol as unique. TRIGGER: object whose distinct symbol count exceeds the per-object cap (large RaptorQ block w/ many repair symbols, or repeated retransmits across paths). FIX: when over the per-object limit, fail safe — return false (treat as duplicate) instead of blindly claiming uniqueness, or use a bounded ring/Bloom so membership is still tested past the cap; at minimum de-dupe by symbol_id in collect_fungible_symbols_until rather than trusting the verdict. NOT FIXED HERE: same ATP-active-lane caution as the SymbolReorderer bead.
close_reason: Fixed (SapphireHill, commit pending): SymbolDeduplicator::check_and_record over the per-object cap (max_symbols_per_object, default 10_000) returned true/unique WITHOUT recording, so a NEW symbol_id past the cap presented twice both returned true -> collect_fungible_symbols_until counted re-presented duplicates as fresh unique progress (false completion, decoder re-fed same symbol). Now fails closed: past the cap return false (duplicate) + bump duplicates_detected. The max_objects over-cap branch is unchanged (deliberately tested). 10_000 is far above realistic single-block K. Updated dedup_enforces_max_symbols_per_object (4th symbol now duplicate; re-presented stays duplicate; unique_symbols==3, duplicates_detected==2). clippy --all-targets -D warnings exit 0; transport::aggregator 78 tests green.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: CORRECTION (SapphireHill, e200fd30e): the original fix (39e4b62e7) was WRONG and a severe regression — making check_and_record fail-closed past max_symbols_per_object would DISCARD symbols on the live MultipathAggregator::process path (it drops non-unique symbols), and the per-object cap (10000) is across ALL blocks (SymbolId=object+sbn+esi), so any object >~10MB (e.g. 50MiB QUIC = ~51k symbols) would starve the RaptorQ decoder past block ~20 -> transfer breaks. Caught in fresh-eyes re-review (confirmed independently by an adversarial review subagent). FIX: reverted check_and_record to the load-bearing pass-through (return unique, don't record past cap); fixed the ACTUAL false-completion bug where it lives — collect_fungible_symbols_until now de-dupes by symbol id LOCALLY (counted: HashSet<SymbolId>) so a re-presented past-cap duplicate can't inflate unique_symbols. Restored dedup test; added fungible_collection_does_not_count_over_cap_duplicates_as_progress. Note: collect_fungible is only used by a test today (QUIC uses process), so the real-world harm was the regression, not the original bug.

title: [swarm-perf] Add tail-risk-aware admission control for overload periods
description:
Background:
- The current runtime exposes governor/resource-monitor signals, but admission and overload responses are still mostly threshold/toggle oriented.
- Alien-artifact guidance for this repo points toward queueing theory + CVaR / expected-loss control using observables we already have: queue depth, wake-to-run latency, cancellation retry count, and degradation state.
- Massive agent swarms need graceful degradation that protects p99 without collapsing useful throughput.

Candidate surfaces:
- src/runtime/resource_monitor.rs
- src/runtime/config.rs
- src/runtime/builder.rs
- src/observability/* relevant runtime metrics

Required design:
1. Define the evidence vector used for overload decisions (queueing delay, backlog, retry pressure, memory pressure).
2. Add a bounded expected-loss / CVaR-inspired admission mode with explicit conservative fallback.
3. Record a compact decision ledger for why work was admitted, deferred, or shed.
4. Expose tuning as configuration rather than hard-coded magic thresholds.

Proof / validation:
- Synthetic overload tests that vary backlog, memory pressure, and retry storms.
- Demonstrate that safe-mode behavior is deterministic and explainable when confidence is low.
- Performance gates comparing p99 tail protection against fixed-threshold admission.

Success criteria:
- Tail latency or overload stability improves on synthetic swarm scenarios, with audit-friendly decision traces and an instant conservative fallback.
design: Tail-risk admission must be a bounded, explainable overload controller layered on the shared scheduler-evidence vocabulary from asupersync-99if94 and the controller-composition contract from asupersync-b4guhs. Separate evidence capture, expected-loss scoring, decision selection, fixed-threshold fallback, and report rendering so each can be tested independently. The controller must emit explicit admit/defer/shed decisions with reason codes, confidence, missing-evidence fields, evidence snapshots, fallback state, and comparison data against the conservative fixed-threshold profile. Configuration must own all thresholds and weights; no hidden magic constants may enter the runtime path. The full bead remains blocked until the shared telemetry schema and controller-interference proof land, but test/proof artifacts for the already-landed ledger slice may be safely adopted under a narrow cleanup commit if their owner releases the current file reservations.

Those blockers are logically correct: tail-risk admission consumes shared evidence and composes with other adaptive overload controllers.
- Existing dirty files that appear to implement the smoke proof are src/runtime/resource_monitor.rs, scripts/run_tail_risk_admission_smoke.sh, and artifacts/tail_risk_admission_smoke_contract_v1.json. title: Cache staleness in region state transitions
description: Region state transitions may result in stale cache entries being used after region state changes. The state machine relies on eventual consistency but lacks explicit cache invalidation on critical transitions, potentially leading to quiescence violations.
close_reason: Fixed cache staleness in region state transitions: Added explicit cache invalidation on protocol violations to prevent quiescence violations. Cache is now invalidated when region finalize, drain, or close transitions detect protocol violations, ensuring authoritative scans are used when system state consistency is questionable.

title: [admission-after-close] record/region.rs add_child/add_task_internal optimistic state check has narrow window allowing admission after close begins
description:
src/record/region.rs:520-530 (add_child) and 562-574 (add_task_internal) — both functions perform an optimistic AtomicRegionState load OUTSIDE the lock and a double-check under the mutex.

The optimistic fast path is intentionally a hint, and the locked double-check is the source of truth — so the basic correctness is preserved. But:
  - The state machine transitions Open -> Closing -> Draining -> Finalizing -> Closed run partly under the mutex and partly via Atomic-only updates depending on path.
  - A child or task admission that passes the locked double-check at line 528/571 succeeds, but the region's task_count is about to be frozen in can_region_complete_close().
  - The window between admission-success and state-freeze is narrow but non-zero.
  - Per AGENTS.md: 'once close begins, cleanup must stay within the existing region tree' — that contract is technically violated for one task.

The added child/task IS tracked in the region's count, so the count is correct; close will wait on it; safety is preserved. But the FINE-GRAINED ordering invariant is violated: state observers see 'region is Closing/Draining' AND 'a new task was added after close began'. Lab oracles that assert 'no admissions after close-begin' flag this.

Concrete failure modes:
  (a) Lab oracle 'closing-region-rejects-new-tasks' fires during high-contention scenarios.
  (b) Replay tools that fold per-region timelines see a 'task added after close-begin' event that the spec-level model considers impossible.
  (c) Future refactor that removes the locked double-check (assuming the optimistic check is sufficient) introduces real correctness bugs.

Fix direction:
  1. Replace the optimistic+double-check pattern with a single lock-protected check (drop the optimistic fast-path).
  2. Or: add a generation counter to the state field; the double-check validates the generation hasn't advanced between fast-path read and locked check.
  3. Or: explicitly document that 'admission-after-close-begin' is permitted within the post-fast-path window and update the oracle to allow it.

Severity LOW because safety is preserved (the admitted work is tracked and waited on), and the violation is observable only at the spec/oracle layer rather than in runtime behavior.

Source: /reality-check on src/runtime/scheduler/* + src/runtime/state.rs deepest 10th-pass (2026-04-26).
close_reason: begin_close now performs the Open -> Closing atomic state transition while still holding the inner write lock; admit() paths that take the same lock can no longer observe Open while begin_close concurrently flips state. Closes the spec-level admission-after-close-begin race that the lab-oracle invariant treats as impossible. Test: admission_after_begin_close_is_rejected. Commit 9a11de19f.

title: [swarm-perf] Add contention-adaptive combiner path for injection hot spots
description:
Background:
- Alien graveyard §14.2 (Flat Combining) and §14.7/FAA notes are a direct fit for heavy producer contention where parallel CAS traffic collapses throughput.
- Asupersync still has injection/control-plane paths that can see swarm-wide bursts (global injector, cancel injection, possibly wake fan-in).
- The goal is not a blanket rewrite; it is a budgeted fallback path that wins only after contention crosses a measured threshold.

Candidate surfaces:
- src/runtime/scheduler/global_injector.rs
- src/runtime/scheduler/priority.rs
- src/runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs
- benches/scheduler_benchmark.rs

Required design:
1. Identify one concrete enqueue/inject path with high CAS or mutex contention under N-producer load.
2. Add a combiner or batch-drain mode that activates only past a measured contention threshold.
3. Preserve the existing fast path for low-contention cases.
4. Emit metrics for retries/CAS failures/batch sizes so the mode is explainable and reversible.

Proof / validation:
- Contention microbench at 1, 8, 32, and 64 producer threads.
- Deterministic invariant coverage for ordering, no task loss, and no double-enqueue.
- Safe-mode fallback to the current implementation if the combiner underperforms.

Success criteria:
- Demonstrable throughput or p99 enqueue-latency win at high contention without hurting low-contention behavior.
design: Activate the combiner path only after measured contention crosses a threshold; preserve the straight-line low-contention fast path and expose mode-enter, mode-exit, batch size, and retry counters so the policy is explainable. The bead should focus on one concrete hot path rather than spreading heuristics across multiple queues.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover no-loss, no-double-enqueue, combiner handoff correctness, and fallback-to-baseline behavior; an N-producer scenario or e2e script logs retries, CAS failures, mode switches, batch sizes, and enqueue tail latency at 1, 8, 32, and 64 producers; benchmark artifacts must show the combiner never regresses the low-contention case beyond the agreed tolerance.

title: [validation-harness] raptorq/gf256_tests/validation_tests.rs: test_field_completeness coverage gap — inverses uniqueness ≠ permutation of 1..=255
description:
src/raptorq/gf256_tests/validation_tests.rs:217-239 — test_field_completeness() walks i in 1..=255, computes inv_val = gf_i.inv().raw(), and inserts into a HashSet asserting no duplicate + final len 255. That proves 'inverses are 255 unique u8 values', but does NOT prove 'inverses are exactly the set {1..=255}'.

Counterexample shape: a buggy inv() that returns 0 for one input and a unique non-zero for every other 254 inputs would still pass — 255 unique u8 values, no duplicates, set size 255. The set's CONTENTS are not validated, only its CARDINALITY.

In a finite field GF(256), the inverse map MUST be a permutation of {1..=255} → {1..=255} (zero has no inverse). A buggy implementation that violates this property (e.g. returns 0 from inv) is exactly the class of bug the validation harness should catch.

Fix direction: after the loop, assert
  let expected: HashSet<u8> = (1..=255u8).collect();
  assert_eq!(inverses_seen, expected, ...);
This catches any inv() that produces 0 OR any value outside 1..=255 OR fails to cover the full image.

Severity P3: latent coverage gap; no active bug today.

Source: deepest audit on src/raptorq/gf256_tests/* (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Fixed: test_field_completeness now asserts image == {1..=255} (commit 81a442f2c)

title: [correctness] record/region.rs: apply_distributed_snapshot REPLACES children + tasks lists instead of merging — partition-heal exchanges silently drop tasks, breaking CRDT commutativity / associativity
description:
src/record/region.rs:1110-1126 — `apply_distributed_snapshot()` unconditionally REPLACES `inner.children` and `inner.tasks` with the snapshot's lists (single Vec-assignment, no merge):

  inner.children = children;
  inner.tasks = tasks;

If two replicas hold disjoint task lists (replica A has tasks {1, 2}; replica B has tasks {3, 4}) and a snapshot from B is applied to A, A's tasks become {3, 4} — the {1, 2} that A legitimately owned are LOST. Symmetrically applying A's snapshot to B drops B's tasks. The merge is non-commutative and non-associative — applying snapshots A then B yields {3, 4}, applying B then A yields {1, 2}, applying both yields whichever was second.

Distributed CRDT contract requires: merge(merge(A, B), C) == merge(A, merge(B, C)) AND merge(A, B) == merge(B, A). This implementation breaks both — it is "last-writer-wins" at the collection level, when CRDT correctness requires set-union (or some other conflict-resolution that is provably commutative and associative).

Concrete trigger: a network partition heals and two replicas exchange snapshots. Partition started with task_count=10 spread across both. After exchange (one direction completed first): one replica has only the partition-other-side's tasks, the other has only its own. Total task count drops to 5. Region close-quiescence check then incorrectly reports zero live tasks for the side whose tasks were overwritten — silent task loss.

Fix direction:
  1. Replace direct-assign with set-union: `inner.children.extend(children.into_iter().filter(|id| !inner.children.contains(id)))` (and similarly for tasks). Note: a true CRDT merge requires causal context (vclock per element); a simple union may also have stale-element issues. Preferred: lattice-based merge consulting per-element vclocks.
  2. Add a regression test that asserts `merge(A, B) == merge(B, A)` and `merge(merge(A, B), C) == merge(A, merge(B, C))` for a representative set of disjoint and overlapping snapshots.
  3. This is the record-layer counterpart of asupersync-yppplg (bridge.rs sequence-gap detection) and asupersync-poshr8 (snapshot.rs metadata bounds-check) — three legs of the same "distributed snapshot integrity" surface.

Source: /multi-pass-bug-hunting src/types/* + src/record/* (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Fixed in commit (just shipped): apply_distributed_snapshot now G-set unions children + tasks instead of REPLACE. Regression test apply_distributed_snapshot_is_commutative_and_associative covers commutativity, associativity, idempotence, and silent-loss.

title: [WASM][Boundary] Refresh browser-feasibility contract and eliminate support-matrix drift
description:
Refresh the authoritative browser-feasibility contract from the live tree before adding more implementation work. The Browser Edition now exists, but the codebase still contains boundary drift: docs promise some things as feasible that public package diagnostics still reject, some capability types exist without corresponding public product surfaces, and some future-phase notes risk being read as current support promises.

This epic exists to remove that ambiguity. Its job is to encode, in executable form, which surfaces are directly supported in browsers today, which are feasible and should be implemented next, which require guarded deployment assumptions, and which are impossible enough that they must remain bridge-only or unsupported.
design:
Use a four-bucket model for every relevant surface:
- direct-runtime supported
- direct-runtime feasible but not yet shipped
- guarded optional (requires explicit deployment/runtime prerequisites)
- impossible for direct browser runtime and therefore bridge-only or unsupported

This epic should not become an abstract documentation exercise. It must reconcile README/docs/package diagnostics/tests so future implementers cannot accidentally build on a false support story.
acceptance_criteria:
1. There is a single authoritative classification for each major browser-related surface and runtime context.
2. Current contradictions between docs, diagnostics, and tests are removed or explicitly tracked.
3. The classification is encoded into contract tests and support diagnostics so it can drift only through deliberate review.
notes:
Known contradictions to resolve include at least:
- docs/WASM.md says the Phase 1 runtime may run on the main thread or a single Web Worker, while package diagnostics currently require window/document and reject worker globals.
- docs/WASM.md names IndexedDB as part of the browser persistence story but still says IndexedDB support is not yet implemented.
- io/cap.rs models WebTransport and worker/message-channel concepts, but the shipped public package surface remains narrower.
- README.md still treats the Rust-authored wasm path as not documented, tested, or public.

Expanding support for a new direct-runtime surface requires deliberate updates rather than silent drift.\n3. title: [reality-check] README.md + AGENTS.md 'no tokio' invariant violated: tokio v1.52.1 transitively in dep graph via opentelemetry_sdk experimental_async_runtime → rt-tokio
description:
README.md and AGENTS.md both state asupersync is a "no tokio" project — AGENTS.md line 114: "This project IS the async runtime. Tokio and the entire tokio ecosystem are FORBIDDEN."

Reality (2026-04-27): `cargo tree -e features --workspace --invert tokio` shows tokio v1.52.1 is pulled into the build graph via:

  asupersync (default features)
    → opentelemetry_sdk
    → opentelemetry_sdk feature "experimental_async_runtime"
    → opentelemetry_sdk feature "rt-tokio"
    → tokio (default + time)

The pull-in is via the `metrics` feature (which is in `default = [test-internals, proc-macros]` per Cargo.toml line 36, but `metrics` is NOT in default). Need to verify which exact feature combination activates `experimental_async_runtime` on opentelemetry_sdk. Possibilities:
  (a) The opentelemetry_sdk dep itself enables `experimental_async_runtime` by default in our Cargo.toml configuration.
  (b) A transitive dep pulls it.

Either way, the README/AGENTS.md "no tokio" invariant is observably violated — any consumer running `cargo tree` sees tokio in their dep graph.

Mitigation:
  1. Set `opentelemetry_sdk = { version = "0.31", default-features = false, features = ["trace"] }` (or the minimal feature set asupersync actually uses) so `experimental_async_runtime` and `rt-tokio` are NOT activated.
  2. Verify the metrics path (asupersync feature "metrics") still works without tokio — if it transitively requires tokio, replace the metric exporter with a non-tokio backend or document the metrics feature as "tokio-coupled" (and list it explicitly as an exception in the README "no tokio" claim).
  3. Add a CI gate: `cargo tree -e features --workspace 2>&1 | grep -E '^[│├└─ ]+tokio v' | grep -v 'asupersync-tokio-compat'` must produce zero lines.
  4. Update README.md / AGENTS.md to either close the gap or document the carve-out.

Severity HIGH because (a) the invariant is a foundational project commitment frequently cited to differentiate asupersync, (b) any external user / auditor running `cargo tree` discovers the discrepancy immediately, (c) even though the runtime doesn't EXECUTE on tokio, having tokio in the dep graph means tokio's ~30 transitive crates are compiled as part of any asupersync consumer build — measurable cost.

Source: /reality-check-for-project (2026-04-27).

title: [EPIC-INFRA] Integration, API Surface and Comprehensive Testing
description:
# EPIC: Integration, API Surface & Comprehensive Testing

**Bead ID:** asupersync-9mq
**Type:** EPIC
**Priority:** P1
**Status:** OPEN
**Owner:** Dicklesworthstone

---

## Vision

The Integration EPIC brings together all RaptorQ-related modules into a cohesive, production-ready system with a unified API surface. While the other EPICs define individual capabilities (encoding, transport, distributed regions, etc.), this EPIC is the "glue" that makes them work together seamlessly and provides the ergonomic interface that developers will actually use.

The vision is to hide complexity without sacrificing power. A developer should be able to send an object over a distributed, erasure-coded channel with a single function call, while an advanced user can customize every aspect of encoding, routing, security, and observability. The API should feel as natural as using standard library async I/O, but provide distributed system guarantees that would otherwise require hundreds of lines of boilerplate.

This EPIC also establishes the testing and validation infrastructure that proves the system works correctly. End-to-end tests verify realistic scenarios including network failures, resource pressure, and cancellation. Performance benchmarks establish baselines and prevent regressions. Documentation makes the system accessible to new developers.

---

## Goals

- **Unified configuration** with a single facade that propagates settings to all subsystems
- **Builder patterns** for constructing pipelines with sensible defaults and full customization

## API Surface Preview

```rust
// Simple usage: send object reliably
let result = raptorq::send(
    data,
    destination,
    RaptorQConfig::production(),
).await?;

    .with_encoding(EncodingConfig {
        symbol_size: 1024,

    })
    .with_transport(my_custom_transport)
    .with_security(SecurityContext::new(key))
    .with_tracing(TracingConfig::sampled(0.01))
    .build()?;

let pipeline = system.point_to_point(destination);
pipeline.send(data).await?;

// Advanced: distributed region with erasure-coded state
let region = DistributedRegionBuilder::new()
    .with_replicas(["node1", "node2", "node3"])
    .with_quorum(2)
    .with_epoch_duration(Duration::from_secs(10))
    .build(&system)?;

region.spawn(|cx| async move {
    // Work inside distributed region
    // State automatically replicated
}).await?;
```

title: SECURITY: Add runtime-based seed for production DetHasher
description:
CRITICAL: det_hash.rs uses fixed seed 0x16f1_1fe8_9b0d_677c making hash collision DoS attacks trivial for attacker-controlled keys. Add production mode with runtime-entropy seed while preserving deterministic seed for lab runtime. 

Attack vector:
1. Attacker reads source code seed
2. Generates colliding keys to target same bucket
3. O(n²) HashMap operations cause CPU exhaustion DoS

Fix approach:
- Add DetHasher::for_production() with random seed from OS entropy
- Keep existing DetHasher::for_lab() with fixed seed
- Update documentation on when to use each
- Add tests for both modes

Files affected: src/util/det_hash.rs

Security impact: HIGH - enables trivial DoS attacks on any HashMap using DetHasher with user-controlled keys
close_reason: Hash collision DoS vulnerability fixed - added production-safe DetHasher with random seeding

title: [GAP] fs::File poll traits perform blocking syscalls on the executor thread
description:
WHY: `File::poll_read/poll_write/poll_seek` (src/fs/file.rs ~412-470) perform blocking syscalls on the executor thread while holding the cursor gate, so any `BufReader<File>`/`Lines` user silently stalls an async worker. README documents it ("poll-based File traits still use direct blocking I/O") but nothing tracks fixing it. (Reality check 2026-09-01.)

WHAT: route the poll-trait paths through the blocking pool (owned-buffer state machine, like the `spawn_blocking_io` owned ops already do) or the io_uring path on Linux; keep the public trait surface unchanged.

ACCEPTANCE: a test on a current-thread runtime performs a large `BufReader<File>` read while a second task must keep making progress (checkpoint counter advances during the read); docs/fs section updated.
close_reason: File poll traits offload to the blocking pool; tests/fs_file_poll_offload_e2e.rs 3/3 on hz3

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text: SapphireHill 2026-09-02: implemented. `fs::File`'s AsyncRead/AsyncWrite/AsyncSeek now run each bounded (128 KiB) syscall on the blocking pool and return Pending until it completes; a per-handle `PendingIo` state machine keeps read-ahead from an abandoned poll, rewinds before writes/relative seeks, and the owned cursor methods (`seek`, `read_into_vec`, ...) settle any in-flight trait op before running. Without a pool the path degrades to the pre-existing inline behaviour (documented). Evidence: tests/fs_file_poll_offload_e2e.rs 3/3 on rch: a peer task advances >= 100 times during one 48 MiB `read_exact` on a single-worker runtime with a pool (one hop per chunk) and <= 40 without one (only ReadExact's cooperative yield); chunked write + abandoned-poll read-ahead + owned relative seek + write-after-read-ahead round-trip byte-exact. Landed in 59383b93d/9f95d73ba/6ab0fee51 (swept by the auto-committer before my own commit); README fs paragraph updated. Remaining before close: full clippy/check gate on the final tree.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text: SapphireHill 2026-09-02 close (self-verified). Landed: src/fs/file.rs poll-based AsyncRead/AsyncWrite/AsyncSeek for `File` now offload to the blocking pool as a state machine (PendingIo: Read/ReadAhead/Write/Flush/Seek, 128 KiB chunks) instead of blocking the worker thread; owned-cursor operations (`with_cursor_inner`) settle any in-flight trait operation and rewind unconsumed read-ahead so mixing the two APIs stays coherent (commits 59383b93d, 9f95d73ba, 6ab0fee51 + this session). Evidence: tests/fs_file_poll_offload_e2e.rs 3/3 on hz3 (rch, remote-required): (1) a spawned counter task keeps progressing while a 64 MiB read runs through the poll traits (>=100 ticks) whereas the planted negative without a blocking pool yields at most the ReadExact cooperative cadence (<=40); (2) read-ahead is never lost or duplicated across a write; (3) relative seek after a partial trait read lands on the logical position. Findings recorded in the test: File::create opens write-only; current_thread runs block_on on the caller thread; ReadExact yields every 32 polls. No-claim: no io_uring path; large sequential throughput not benchmarked.

title: [GAP] hedge(), time::timeout and plan::execute races drop losers while docs claim drain
description:
WHY: README says "race/select-style winners drain losers through dedicated drain paths". True for `race!`, `select!`, `Scope::race*`, and `Scope::hedge`; false for the `hedge()` future (src/combinator/hedge.rs:19-21 header: loser dropped), `time::timeout` (src/time/timeout_future.rs ~278-296 drops the inner future) while src/combinator/timeout.rs:4-11 claims "cancelled AND drained", and `plan::execute` race nodes (~781 comment: drop). (Reality check 2026-09-01.)

WHAT: make `hedge()` and the plan-execute race nodes protocol-cancel and drain losers when a `Cx` with spawn authority is available (mirroring `Scope::hedge`), or change their docs to state drop-on-cancel explicitly; fix the src/combinator/timeout.rs header to describe what `time::timeout` actually does.

ACCEPTANCE: tests assert loser cleanup ran before `hedge()` returns; docs match behaviour; planted negative: a loser that ignores cancellation is reported, not silently dropped.
close_reason: Scope::timeout drain-correct combinator landed; tests/scope_timeout_e2e.rs 4/4 on hz3; hedge/plan race drop documented as remaining

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text: SapphireHill 2026-09-02 close (self-verified; no independent verifier available tonight, stated plainly). Landed: `Scope::timeout(cx, duration, op)` in src/cx/scope.rs (commit bef4724c6 + follow-ups) — spawns the operation as an ordinary region task, races its join against the deadline, and on expiry requests cancellation (CancelReason::timeout) and JOINS the task, so cleanup after a checkpoint completes before the caller gets `TimedResult::TimedOut`; a value the task returns after acknowledging cancellation is preserved as `Completed(..)`. docs: src/combinator/timeout.rs header (Scope::timeout drains; time::timeout drops) and README timeout row. Evidence: tests/scope_timeout_e2e.rs 4/4 on hz3 (rch, remote-required): in-time Ok; acknowledged Err preserved + cleanup-before-return (cleanup counter read after the call); late Ok preserved; cancellation-blind task -> TimedOut. Fix during verification: the acknowledged-Err assertion had matched the wrong enum (TimedError vs OutcomeError), corrected to `result.into_result()`. NOT done (kept open elsewhere/documented): hedge() and plan::execute race nodes still drop losers; noted in the combinator table. No-claim: does not change time::timeout semantics.

title: [GAP] Stock mpsc/oneshot/broadcast/semaphore permits are not runtime obligations (futurelock and leak oracles are blind to them)
description:
WHY: README says futurelock detection covers "channel permits, leases, IoOp records, and semaphore permit tokens" and that a reserved permit is a tracked obligation. In code, stock `mpsc`/`oneshot`/`broadcast` `SendPermit`s and `SemaphorePermit`s never register an `ObligationKind` record (grep: zero `ObligationKind` refs in src/channel/mpsc.rs, oneshot.rs, broadcast.rs, src/sync/semaphore.rs); only session-tracked permits (src/channel/session.rs) and `IoOp` do. So the lab futurelock/obligation-leak oracles are blind to the most common permits, and the onramp Level 3 example has to create the obligation by hand. (Reality check 2026-09-01.)

WHAT: register a runtime obligation when a permit is reserved through a `Cx` that carries runtime state, resolve it on send/abort/drop, without allocating on the fast path (obligation ids from the existing arena; a no-state `Cx` keeps today's untracked behaviour). Same for `Semaphore::acquire` permits. Keep public signatures unchanged.

ACCEPTANCE: LabRuntime test: reserve an mpsc permit inside a task, complete the task without sending, and the obligation-leak oracle reports the leak naming the permit kind; a semaphore permit held across a task that stops being polled triggers futurelock detection; the methodology baseline bench rows for mpsc reserve/send show no regression beyond the gate. Update README "Futurelock detection is narrower" paragraph to match.

NO-CLAIM: does not make Mutex/RwLock guards obligations.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Apply the 2026-09-04 governing scope correction above; preserve remaining features and require the named source-bound behavior/compatibility evidence.
notes: 2026-09-04 scope update: channels now register via the gateway (closed .13/.14); semaphore/Pool .15 is active. Remaining admission-before-publication defect is bi2462.28/.29, and .16 handles remote Lease ownership. Normal SendPermit drop aborts and must not be turned into a leak to satisfy old acceptance. Raw unresolved token/retained-holder misuse is the leak fixture; no-Cx try_reserve remains explicitly distinct. Parent closure requires correct admitted accounting, cross-task/region attribution, native/lab cancel/close proof and measured hot-path impact, not merely a token field or focused marker test.
close_reason: Lab + native (cancel and region close) proof landed f9937bc9c/54cb51d08 with reverted-boundary controls; README fixed; bench reserve/send rows within gate

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text: SapphireHill 2026-09-02 scoping (no code change). Facts from the tree: (1) runtime obligations exist only through `RuntimeState::create_obligation(kind, holder, region, description)` and are resolved with `commit_obligation`/`abort_obligation` on the same `&mut RuntimeState` (src/runtime/state.rs ~4882/5326/5498). (2) The only kind minted by non-test code is `IoOp` via `IoOp::submit(&mut RuntimeState, ..)` — and grep finds NO production caller of `IoOp::submit`; io_op.rs is exercised by its own tests and the lab oracle. (3) The "session-tracked" permits (src/channel/session.rs) and MySQL/PG transaction tokens use `ObligationToken<K>::reserve(description, region)` from src/obligation/graded.rs, which is a standalone typestate token (fields: description, region, armed) that never touches the runtime obligation table; so the lab futurelock/leak oracles are blind to those too, not only to the stock permits. (4) A `Cx` carries no handle to `RuntimeState`; `SendPermit::send`/`Drop` run in synchronous code with only `&Sender` and the `Cx` used at reserve time. Consequence: making stock mpsc/oneshot/broadcast/semaphore permits runtime obligations needs a new Cx->state seam (an obligation gateway analogous to the spawn gateway, with reserve/commit/abort commands that never take the state lock under the channel mutex) plus obligation ids threaded into the permit types. That is a kernel design change (lock order: channel mutex vs RuntimeState), not a wiring job; README's "futurelock covers channel permits ... and semaphore permit tokens" stays a documented gap until it lands. Suggested first slice when picked up: obligation gateway + stock mpsc SendPermit only, LabRuntime test with the leak oracle naming SendPermit, then semaphore.
