title: [swarm-perf] Add read-biased snapshot substrate for governor and observability hot paths
description:
Background:
- StateSnapshot and related read-heavy runtime inspection paths are natural BRAVO / seqlock / RCU candidates on high-core hosts because reads vastly outnumber structural writes.
- Existing beads already target incremental snapshots; this task goes one layer lower and addresses read-side cache-line bouncing and lock traffic in the substrate itself.
- The goal is a read-optimized path with an explicit conservative fallback, not lock-order roulette.

Candidate surfaces:
- src/runtime/sharded_state.rs
- src/runtime/state.rs
- src/obligation/lyapunov.rs
- src/observability/* state readers

Required design:
1. Identify one concrete read-dominated metadata path where shared counters/locks bounce under swarm load.
2. Introduce a read-biased substrate (for example BRAVO-style visible readers, seqlock snapshotting, or RCU-style read copies) behind an explicit config gate.
3. Preserve lock ordering and deterministic lab-runtime semantics; when disabled, behavior must match today's path exactly.
4. Emit observability for fallback activation, writer stalls, and read-path bias effectiveness.

Proof / validation:
- Contention microbench for read-heavy and write-heavy mixes.
- Deterministic regression for snapshot correctness and no stale/corrupt reads.
- Safe-mode fallback to the current lock path if contention shape or write rate makes the optimization lose.

Success criteria:
- Read-heavy state inspection shows a measurable latency or throughput win on high-core workloads without semantic drift.
design: Pilot exactly one read-mostly metadata path first, gate the read-biased substrate behind explicit config, and emit writer-stall and fallback counters so the optimization can be judged honestly. The objective is lower read-side interference without violating lock ordering or deterministic semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover versioning or reader-token correctness, stale-read rejection, fallback activation, and disabled-mode equivalence; a read-heavy vs write-heavy scenario or e2e script logs contention, reader latency, writer stall duration, and correctness checksums; artifacts must make it obvious when the read-biased path loses and the conservative fallback should remain pinned.
notes: If this work touches the same state summaries as asupersync-k7nx5t, share counters and evidence artifacts, but do not collapse the beads together; the governor-equivalence proof deserves its own review boundary. Boundary: this bead owns the read-side concurrency substrate itself, not the Lyapunov summary/equivalence algorithm. Its scenario/e2e artifacts should emit through asupersync-2ijesw.
close_reason: Validated and closed from already-landed implementation. Implementation is present in commits adfe063ab ([br-asupersync-l0q0rs] add read-biased draining snapshot) and 6917659c ([br-asupersync-l0q0rs] add read-biased snapshot smoke contract), with related governor-equivalence follow-on 10139aad3 ([br-asupersync-k7nx5t] add governor snapshot equivalence smoke). Live code provides an explicit read-biased region snapshot config gate, default-disabled equivalence to authoritative scans, cached draining-region count substrate, transition/stat counters, invalidation fallback, and write-heavy conservative fallback. Focused proof: rch exec -- env ASUPERSYNC_READ_BIASED_REGION_SNAPSHOT_SCENARIO=AA-READ-BIASED-REGION-SNAPSHOT-WRITE-HEAVY ASUPERSYNC_READ_BIASED_REGION_SNAPSHOT_REPORT_PATH=/tmp/asupersync-l0q0rs-write-heavy-report.json cargo test -p asupersync --lib read_biased_region_snapshot --features test-internals -- --nocapture --test-threads=1. Result: 6 passed, 0 failed; report emitted schema read-biased-region-snapshot-report-v1 for write-heavy scenario with checksums_match=true, final_counts_match=true, fallback_should_remain_pinned=true, fallback_preference_reason=write-heavy-threshold-exceeded, cache/fallback/writer timing counters logged. The 68 warnings in the run are existing unrelated observability/grpc warning noise, not failures in this bead.

title: ack channel: a refused Ack admission rotates the queue head to the tail instead of rolling back in place
description:
Read-only audit (SapphireHill subagent, 2026-10-02, origin 57e3fd838): src/channel/ack.rs Delivery::drop pushed a refused or cancelled Ack admission (issued == false) to the TAIL of the ready queue.

The module docs promise that ready items are selected FIFO and that retries join the tail, and the Delivery field docs call a refused admission rollback, not a worker attempt.

Scenario: channel(2) holds A then B, and a worker whose region obligation quota is exhausted calls try_recv_with_ack. It gets Admission(LimitReached), and the dropped Delivery puts A back at the tail, leaving [B, A].

Each further refusal rotates the head again, so under quota pressure the delivery order depends on how many refusals happened. Nothing is lost or duplicated. No existing test caught it: the FIFO retry test covers nack only, and the refusal test holds one item.

Fix: put a non-issued delivery back at the head (push_front). Issued deliveries that are dropped or nacked still join the tail.
close_reason: Fixed in the batch ending c1cfb8765: Delivery::drop puts a never-issued delivery back at the head; test refused_admission_keeps_the_item_at_the_head_of_the_queue green (hz4), control red 2 vs 1 (ovh-a)

title: ATP Data Movement Layer: self-contained verified object graph movement over native Asupersync QUIC
description: ATP is the Asupersync Data Movement Layer, not merely a file-copy utility. The north star is: any bytes, any size, any path, any interruption, any network, with verified completion and deterministic replay. This epic captures the complete product and architecture plan so future agents do not need the original design discussion. ATP should provide CLI, daemon, SDK, rendezvous/relay services, a deterministic lab, native QUIC, object graphs, crash-safe journals, RaptorQ repair, path racing, proofs, and benchmark evidence. The first proof case is moving large files and directories, but the primitive is a verified ObjectGraph with manifests, chunks, repair groups, capabilities, and reproducible outcomes.
design: Architecture ladder: atp_cli / atpd / atp_sdk -> session/auth/policy/capabilities -> object graph/manifest/Merkle/chunking -> journal/sparse writer/verifier -> scheduler/transfer brain -> RaptorQ repair coordinator -> path graph/rendezvous/relay/Tailscale candidate/mailbox -> native QUIC endpoint -> UDP reactor and hostile-network fallback paths. Non-negotiables: no Tokio, no Quinn, no h3-quinn, no external QUIC crate, no opaque best-effort cleanup, no exposing unverified final data as complete. Use Asupersync properties deliberately: Cx first, region-owned work, AppSpec supervision, Outcome preservation, Budget discipline, obligation-tracked protocol edges, deterministic lab tests, crashpacks, trace/replay, and capability-scoped access.

- All child workstream epics exist and cover native QUIC, ATP protocol, object graph, disk safety, scheduler, path graph, RaptorQ, daemon, CLI, swarm/mailbox, compatibility adapters, lab/bench/forensics, and dogfood/governance.

title: [TESTING] E2E test: no obligation leaks under 10M random schedules
description: End-to-end stress test that runs 10 million random schedules with the Lab runtime and verifies zero obligation leaks. For each schedule: (1) Spawn a random DAG of tasks with random obligations (SendPermit, Lease, Reserve), (2) Apply random faults (cancel, timeout, panic), (3) After quiescence, verify all obligations have been released (obligation counter == 0), (4) Log any leaks with full schedule trace for reproduction. Configuration: Use rayon for parallel execution across cores. Target: complete 10M schedules in <30 minutes on CI. Statistics: Track leak rate with exact binomial confidence interval — target is 0 leaks with 95% CI upper bound <1e-7. This is the ultimate obligation safety validation — if we can survive 10M random schedules without a leak, the system is robust.

title: Implement lab runtime with virtual time and deterministic scheduling
description:
# Lab Runtime with Virtual Time and Deterministic Scheduling

## Purpose
The lab runtime is the executable semantics of Asupersync:
- **virtual time** (discrete ticks)
- **deterministic scheduling** (seeded, reproducible)
- **trace capture + replay**

This is what makes concurrency bugs reproducible artifacts instead of “heisenbugs”.

## Key Guarantees
Given the same lab config (including seed) and the same user program:
- the runtime produces the same observable trace
- replay can reproduce a failing run

## Core Constraints
- Avoid ambient globals.
- Avoid OS entropy / wall-clock time for scheduling decisions.
- Prefer minimal dependencies; implement deterministic PRNG internally (see bead: deterministic PRNG utility).

## LabRuntime Structure

```rust
pub struct LabRuntime {
    state: RuntimeState,
    virtual_time: Time,

    /// Deterministic PRNG for tie-breaking (no rand crate).
    rng: DetRng,

    trace: TraceBuffer,
    config: LabConfig,
}

pub struct LabConfig {
    pub seed: u64,
    pub max_time: Option<Time>,
    pub max_steps: Option<u64>,

    /// Lab-only strictness knobs.
    pub panic_on_leak: bool,
    pub panic_on_invariant_violation: bool,
}
```

## Virtual Time
Time advances only when no runnable tasks exist.

Algorithm:
1. If scheduler has runnable tasks: do not advance time.
2. Otherwise, jump to next timer deadline (if any).
3. Wake any tasks whose timers expire.
4. Check deadline expiries and request cancellation as needed.
5. Emit `TraceEvent::Tick`.

This yields the “sleeps are instant in wall-clock time” property while preserving a meaningful virtual timeline.

## Deterministic Scheduling
When multiple tasks are eligible to run, break ties deterministically using `DetRng` seeded by `LabConfig.seed`.

Important: determinism requires that tie-breaking inputs are stable.
- do not iterate hashmaps/sets and rely on their order
- prefer ordered iteration or explicit sorting by IDs

## Main Loop (Sketch)

```rust
loop {
    if should_stop_by_limits(config, virtual_time, steps) {
        break;
    }

    if let Some(task_id) = scheduler.pick_next(virtual_time, &mut rng, &state) {
        poll_task(task_id);
        steps += 1;
        verify_invariants_if_enabled();
    } else {
        tick_virtual_time();
    }
}
```

## Trace Capture
Every semantic operation emits a trace event. The trace model should stay small and semantic:
- spawn/complete
- cancel/propagate
- reserve/commit/abort/leak
- finalize/close
- tick

The trace is the primary debugging artifact for test failures.

## Replay
Replay means: “run again under the same seed/config and ensure we reproduce the same trace”.

Minimum viable replay:
- re-run the scenario under the same seed
- compare traces
- report first divergence with context

(Phase 5 adds canonicalization and equivalence-class reasoning; Phase 0 replay can be strict byte-for-byte equality.)

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Same seed/config yields identical traces for the same program.
2. Virtual time advances only when nothing runnable exists.
3. Trace capture is complete enough for invariants/oracles.
4. Replay reports divergence precisely.

## Testing Requirements
- Determinism oracle runs at least 3 scenarios twice and asserts trace equality.
- Deadlock/idle detection is explicit and traceable.
close_reason: Lab runtime implemented in src/lab/runtime.rs. Virtual time, DetRng for determinism, trace capture, quiescence checking. Config in config.rs, replay/diff in replay.rs.

title: Migration planner: inventory external Rust project runtime surfaces

## What
Build the planner's read-only inventory layer for an external Rust project path. It should inspect Cargo manifests, feature selections, lockfile data when present, and source-level runtime markers, then classify surfaces as native Asupersync candidate, compat quarantine, hard blocker, or already-native.

## Why
Migration quality depends on knowing the actual dependency and source topology before proposing changes. A manual playbook is easy to misapply on a large codebase; a deterministic inventory makes the first migration report trustworthy and repeatable.

## Implementation guidance
- Prefer structured parsing for Cargo manifests/metadata where available instead of ad hoc regex-only parsing.
- Treat missing lockfiles, malformed manifests, workspaces, path dependencies, and feature-gated Tokio edges as first-class cases.
- Detect direct and transitive uses of `tokio`, `tokio-util`, `hyper`, `axum`, `tower`, `tonic`, `reqwest`, `sqlx`, `quinn`, `h3`, `rdkafka`, `async-std`, and `smol`.
- Keep the planner read-only with explicit input/output paths. It must not edit the scanned project.
- Emit stable JSON rows with source path, dependency/symbol, classification, confidence, rationale, and suggested next probe.

## Tests and logging
Unit tests should cover empty projects, malformed manifests, no lockfile, multi-member workspaces, feature-gated dependencies, path dependencies, and projects that already use Asupersync. Logs must include project root, manifest count, feature mode, classifier version, row count, and every fail-closed reason.

## Success criteria

title: [oracle-false-negative] lab/oracle/actor.rs: SupervisionOracle.check skips sibling-restart check for later failures after a prior-window escalation
description:
src/lab/oracle/actor.rs:414-432 — SupervisionOracle::check loop. After detecting an escalation event, the predicate hits `continue` (line 432) which skips ALL subsequent sibling-restart / RestForOne checks for that failure record, and the same `escalated` flag (set in the first failure-to-next-failure window) leaks into later windows.

Concrete trigger: supervisor 0 has children [1,2,3] under OneForAll. At t=10 child 1 fails, attempt 4 exceeds max_restarts=3, escalation fires at t=21. At t=30 child 2 fails — distinct failure-to-next-failure window — but the oracle's iteration over `record.failures` re-encounters the t=10..t=30 window first, sees `escalated=true` from the prior window, and `continue`s past the OneForAll sibling-restart check for the t=30 failure too.

Fix direction: bind `escalated` per-failure (move the `continue` inside an `if window_index == current_failure_index` guard), or split the supervision check into two phases: (1) per-failure escalation correctness, (2) per-failure sibling-restart correctness — running both for every failure independently.

Source: /multi-pass-bug-hunting on src/lab/* (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Fixed false-negative in SupervisionOracle::check; sibling-restart obligations now verified for every failure under restart-budget regardless of in-window escalation

title: [reasoning-modes] channel failure lens: SendPermit::send silently drops Disconnected value
description:
Failure + cancel-safety lens finding.

Evidence:
- src/channel/mpsc.rs:3-18 documents the two-phase contract as `permit.send(message); // Phase 2: commit (cannot fail)` and says `permit.send(value)` commits the obligation.
- src/channel/mpsc.rs:727-729 implements `SendPermit::send(self, value)` as `let _ = self.try_send(value);`.
- src/channel/mpsc.rs:733-747 shows `try_send` can return `Err(SendError::Disconnected(value))` after consuming the reservation when the receiver has been dropped.

Why this is a real gap:
The public convenience API silently discards the disconnected-send error and the user value, so the supposedly infallible commit path can still lose the message on receiver drop. That conflicts with the module docs, the reserve/commit mental model used elsewhere in the codebase, and the project-wide "no silent drops" / cancel-correctness story.

Audit-history angle:
This surface has been relied on by actor/mailbox work as if `reserve().send()` were the safe commit boundary, so a doc/API mismatch here is likely to recur in higher-level abstractions.

Fix direction:
Either make `SendPermit::send` report failure (or otherwise preserve the value) so phase 2 is not lossy, or explicitly redesign/document the contract so callers cannot mistake a silent drop path for an infallible commit.

title: Codec audit: FramedRead's default 8 MiB buffer cap rejects frames the codec accepts and poisons the stream (h2 listener with large max_frame_size suspected); LengthDelimitedCodec frame layout diverges from tokio-util when num_skip < header
description:
Read-only audit of src/codec (framed, framed_read, framed_write, length_delimited, lines, bytes_codec) at origin/main 6b307cfec (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-04; read from origin; compared with tokio-util 0.7.19). No HIGH.

## MEDIUM
1. LengthDelimitedCodec consumes max(header_len, num_skip) + adjusted length per frame (length_delimited.rs ~281, ~338-379); tokio-util consumes num_skip + adjusted. They differ whenever num_skip < offset + length_field_length: tokio's documented Example 2 (length_field_length(2).length_adjustment(2).num_skip(0)) yields "\x00\x0BHello world\x00\x05" here, swallowing the next frame's header (frame-boundary disagreement between a tokio peer and an asupersync service; smuggling-style). Shipped before v0.4.3 (f65320c1e, da7019613): default cannot change. Additive fix: document the divergence on num_skip/length_adjustment, an opt-in tokio-geometry builder option, differential tests from tokio Examples 2-7. Owner decision on the option.
2. FramedRead's default buffer cap (DEFAULT_MAX_BUFFER_LEN 8 MiB + 4, framed_read.rs ~35-44, ~268-302; framed.rs ~89, ~305) rejects frames the paired codec accepts and then poisons the stream: length_field_length(8) with an exactly-8 MiB frame, max_frame_length(16 MiB) with frames over 8 MiB, offset/num_skip/positive adjustment layouts, LinesCodec::with_unbounded lines over 8 MiB. Internal callers already work around it (remote.rs ~3787, h1/server.rs ~936-946, h2/client.rs ~770). SUSPECTED live: h2 listener (listener.rs ~3275) builds Framed without a cap override while settings allow max_frame_size up to 16 MiB - 1. Additive fix: a provided Decoder hint (max buffered frame) that FramedRead/Framed honour unless with_max_buffer_len was called.

## LOW
3. LinesCodec::decode_eof yields an extra empty line for a trailing lone \r (lines.rs ~204-235; tokio returns None); a golden pins the current behaviour.
4. max_frame_length is checked after length_adjustment (tokio checks before) (~216): doc only.
5. Performance: lines.rs ~129 rescans an unchanged buffer from index 0; framed.rs start_send/codec_mut force a re-decode (up to 64 KiB rescanned per send on Framed<_, LinesCodec>).

## Deliberate divergences (doc)
Permanent poison after any error and after EOF (tokio can resume); send() encodes without flushing.

## Checked and sound
decode_eof partial-frame UnexpectedEof, waker registration and yield limits, buffer cap checked before append, no allocation from advertised length, header arithmetic overflow checks, 8-byte lengths, encoder validation, LinesCodec max_length window and discard mode, FramedWrite backpressure, flush/close semantics, partial-write resume, BytesCodec.

title: [SUB-EPIC] Linux Reactor (epoll)
description:
# Sub-Epic: Linux Reactor (epoll)

## Purpose

Implement a production-quality epoll-based reactor for Linux. This is the primary reactor for server deployments.

## Background

### What is epoll?

epoll (event poll) is Linux's scalable I/O event notification mechanism. It provides O(1) complexity for monitoring many file descriptors, making it ideal for high-connection-count servers.

Key syscalls:
- `epoll_create1()` - Create epoll instance
- `epoll_ctl()` - Add/modify/remove fd monitoring
- `epoll_wait()` - Block until events ready

### Edge-Triggered vs Level-Triggered

**Level-triggered (default):** 
- Reports readiness while condition exists
- Must drain all data each poll to avoid busy-loop

**Edge-triggered (EPOLLET):**
- Reports readiness when condition changes
- More efficient but requires careful handling of EAGAIN

We will use **edge-triggered** for efficiency, which requires:
1. Non-blocking sockets
2. Read/write until EAGAIN
3. Re-arm interest after each operation

## Design

```rust
pub struct EpollReactor {
    /// The epoll file descriptor
    epoll_fd: RawFd,
    /// Eventfd for cross-thread wakeup
    wake_fd: RawFd,
    /// Token slab for waker mapping (protected by mutex)
    inner: Mutex<EpollInner>,
}

struct EpollInner {
    wakers: TokenSlab,
    /// Pending wakeups that need processing
    pending_wakes: Vec<Token>,
}

impl EpollReactor {
    pub fn new() -> io::Result<Self> {
        let epoll_fd = epoll_create1(EpollFlags::EPOLL_CLOEXEC)?;
        let wake_fd = eventfd(0, EfdFlags::EFD_CLOEXEC | EfdFlags::EFD_NONBLOCK)?;
        
        // Register wake_fd for wakeup notifications
        // ...
        
        Ok(Self { epoll_fd, wake_fd, inner: Mutex::new(EpollInner::new()) })
    }
}
```

## Key Implementation Details

### Cross-Thread Wakeup

Use `eventfd` for efficient wakeup:
```rust
fn wake(&self) -> io::Result<()> {
    // Write to eventfd to wake blocking epoll_wait
    nix::unistd::write(self.wake_fd, &1u64.to_ne_bytes())?;
    Ok(())
}
```

### EPOLLONESHOT for Cancel-Safety

Consider using `EPOLLONESHOT` flag:
- Event fires once, then fd is disabled
- Must re-arm after each event
- Prevents race conditions on deregistration

### Error Handling

- `EBADF`: fd was closed, deregister
- `EEXIST`: already registered (bug)
- `ENOENT`: not registered (benign on deregister)

## Platform Requirements

- Linux kernel 2.6+ (epoll available)
- Kernel 4.5+ for EPOLLEXCLUSIVE (optional optimization)

## Deliverables

1. EpollReactor implementing Reactor trait
2. Proper eventfd wakeup mechanism
3. Edge-triggered operation with EPOLLET
4. Robust error handling
5. Unit tests with real sockets
6. Benchmarks comparing to busy-loop baseline

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Can handle 10k+ concurrent connections
- [ ] No busy-looping on idle connections
- [ ] Cross-thread wakeup works reliably
- [ ] Proper cleanup on reactor shutdown
- [ ] All tests pass under stress

title: ATP-E3-F3: Build noisy-pressure replay corpus and golden autotune decision receipts
description:
## Background
ATP-E3 acceptance requires stable behavior under noisy metrics and fail-closed handling of contradictory inputs. One-off unit tests are not enough; future agents need a deterministic corpus that freezes representative pressure windows and expected decision receipts.

## Work
Create a small but representative fixture corpus of telemetry windows and expected decisions for clean path, lossy path, high RTT/PTO, disk read lag, disk write lag, encode backlog, decode backlog, high repair ROI, relay-expensive path, migration event, and contradictory mixed signals. Keep fixtures compact and text-reviewable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Golden receipts include trace_id, workload_id, samples, bottleneck classification, selected knobs, bounded deltas, confidence/caveat fields, and fail-closed reasons.
- Tests prove deterministic replay from fixtures to receipts with stable ordering and redaction.
- Corpus includes edge cases: zero samples, out-of-range sample values, stale trace id, duplicate metric samples, and contradictory samples.
- Updating a golden requires an explicit command and reviewable diff; no hidden wall-clock or host-specific data appears.
- rch-backed proof commands and first blockers are recorded in the close note.

title: [LAB-DX] Deterministic Testing DX v2 — one-attribute lab tests, auto-forensics, auto-shrinking
description:
WHY: The lab runtime (virtual time, DPOR, oracles, crashpacks, minimizer, conformal calibration) is the project's crown jewel, but recon shows the test-writing experience hides it: every lab test hand-rolls init_test_logging() + LabRuntime::new(LabConfig::new(seed)) + manual region/task creation + manual scheduler driving (15-80 lines of boilerplate, see tests/ recipes). Failure forensics (crashpack, minimization, replay) exist as libraries but require manual invocation; DPOR race detection is pub(crate)-only.

GOAL: writing a deterministic test is one attribute; failing tests automatically produce a crashpack + minimized repro + replay command; determinism across seeds is a one-line assertion; exploration is a one-attribute macro; everything the failure tells you is actionable without reading src/lab.

CHILD TASKS: #[lab_test] attribute macro with seed matrices; oracle registry for discoverability; auto-crashpack emission on failure (env-gated); auto trace minimization + frankenlab minimize CLI; determinism assertion helpers + first-divergence diff reports; public DPOR/explorer API + #[explore_seeds]; full forensics-pipeline e2e test.

SUCCESS METRIC: lab test boilerplate drops from ~15-20 lines to 2-5; a deliberately-injected failing test yields (with zero user code) a crashpack path, a minimized schedule, and a copy-paste replay command, validated by the e2e child bead.

title: [LAB-DX] #[lab_test] attribute macro — deterministic lab tests in one attribute, with seed matrices
description:
WHY: every lab test today hand-rolls 15-20 lines (init_test_logging + LabRuntime::new(LabConfig::new(seed)) + root region + create_task + manual scheduler drive + report assertions) — recon recipes 1-3 document the boilerplate verbatim. Multiplied across hundreds of tests and every future agent-authored test, this is the single biggest lab-DX lever.

WHAT:
  #[lab_test]                              — runs body on LabRuntime, seed 0, oracles asserted green at exit, logging initialized, test_phase!/test_complete! emitted automatically.
  #[lab_test(seeds = 0..16)]               — seed-matrix execution: body runs per seed; any failure reports WHICH seed + repro command.
  #[lab_test(seeds = 0..64, chaos)]        — enables deterministic chaos injection (src/lab/chaos.rs) per documented default profile.
  fn my_test(lab: &mut LabRuntime)         — signature form A: raw lab access for state-level tests.
  async fn my_test(cx: &Cx)                — signature form B: the macro creates root region + task, drives to quiescence, asserts the LabRunReport (oracles green, zero invariant violations) — covers the 90% case where users just want deterministic async.
Failure path: on ANY failure (assertion, oracle, panic) print: seed, trace fingerprint, artifact path (once auto-crashpack lands), and the exact rerun command pinned to the failing seed.

Coordinate naming/arg grammar with #[asupersync::test] (DX-CORE A3): same family, documented contrast (production runtime vs lab determinism). Seed-matrix runs sequentially inside one #[test] (keeps cargo test UX) with per-seed log sections.

Boilerplate proof: port 5 existing representative lab tests to the macro; net line reduction recorded (target >=60%). 3. title: [LAB-DX] Auto-crashpack on test failure — zero-code forensics capture
description:
WHY: crashpack machinery exists (src/trace/crashpack.rs, lab auto-attach linkage per README) but tests must wire it manually; recon found failing tests yield a panic message and nothing else unless the author pre-plumbed artifacts. The repo ALREADY emits artifact bundles when ASUPERSYNC_TEST_ARTIFACTS_DIR is set — this bead closes the loop so EVERY lab-test failure produces a complete forensics bundle automatically.

WHAT: (1) failure hook in the #[lab_test] macro + run_async_under_lab path: on assertion failure/oracle violation/panic, capture {seed, LabConfig, trace buffer, oracle report, diagnostics (B3 output), rendered repro command} into a crashpack under ASUPERSYNC_TEST_ARTIFACTS_DIR (default target/test-artifacts/<test-name>/<timestamp-free deterministic run-id>); (2) opt-out env (ASUPERSYNC_AUTO_ARTIFACTS=0) rather than opt-in — failures should be forensic by default in lab tests; (3) the panic message's last line prints the crashpack path + replay command (agents read stderr); (4) deterministic run-id scheme (seed + trace fingerprint, NO wall-clock) so re-runs overwrite rather than accumulate.
design: FILES: src/lab/runtime.rs (failure capture point), src/trace/crashpack.rs (builder convenience), asupersync-macros lab_test failure hook, src/test_utils or lab forensics module for the writer. Respect the existing crashpack schema + auto-attach dedup behavior documented in README (manual attachments preserved, no duplicate auto-insertions). Determinism: bundle contents byte-stable across re-runs of the same seed (snapshot-test one bundle).
acceptance_criteria: 1. A deliberately failing #[lab_test] produces a crashpack with all 6 captured elements; path printed in failure output (golden-tested last line). 2. Re-run same seed: byte-identical bundle (determinism test). 3. Opt-out env honored; CI default documented. 4. Replay command in the bundle actually reproduces the failure (e2e-verified in C7). 5. No overhead on PASSING tests (capture only constructed on failure — verify with bench on a fast test). 6. Bundle schema documented + contract-tested (fields, file names).
notes: DEPENDS on C1 (the hook lives in the macro path). Consumes B3 diagnostics when available (graceful if absent). RELATION: C4 minimizer takes a crashpack as input; C7 e2e validates the whole chain.

title: [LAB-DX] Automatic failure minimization — shrink failing schedules/scenarios; frankenlab minimize CLI
description:
WHY: minimizer machinery exists (src/trace/minimizer.rs scenario-level, src/trace/delta_debug.rs event-level) but recon found no test-harness integration and no CLI — failing schedules stay big. proptest-style shrinking is the bar: a failure should arrive pre-minimized or one command away from it.

WHAT: (1) library: Minimizer::minimize_crashpack(pack, rerun_closure, budget) -> MinimizedRepro {reduced scenario/schedule, reduction %, verified-still-failing proof}; (2) frankenlab minimize <crashpack-or-scenario.yaml> [--timeout N] [--json] subcommand wrapping it (frankenlab already has run/explore/replay — recon praised that CLI; extend it); (3) optional auto-minimize-on-failure in #[lab_test(minimize)] for cheap tests (budget-capped so CI time stays bounded); (4) minimization is itself deterministic (same input -> same minimal repro) — document the reduction strategy (delta-debug over Foata-normalized events to respect commutation classes, leveraging the existing canonicalize machinery so we shrink in trace-equivalence space, not raw interleavings — this is the alien-artifact angle that makes our shrinking better than naive ddmin).
design: FILES: src/trace/minimizer.rs + delta_debug.rs (public API), frankenlab/src/main.rs (subcommand), asupersync-macros (minimize arg). Budget semantics: hard wall on rerun count + per-run step cap; on exhaustion return best-so-far with exhausted flag (budgeted-mode discipline per alien-graveyard). Foata-class-aware reduction documented with a galaxy-brain card (equation: search over M(Σ,I)=Σ*/≡_I representatives, not Σ*).
acceptance_criteria: 1. minimize_crashpack on a seeded multi-task failure achieves >=50% event reduction on the benchmark fixture (record actual; fixture committed). 2. frankenlab minimize works on both crashpack and scenario YAML inputs; --json output schema-stable. 3. Determinism: same input -> identical minimal repro (test). 4. Budget exhaustion path tested (returns best-so-far + flag, never hangs). 5. Minimized repro verified still-failing automatically before reporting (no false minimization). 6. Galaxy-brain card committed in docs (technique, why equivalence-class shrinking beats ddmin here).
notes:
DEPENDS on C3 (crashpack input format). RISK: rerun-based minimization can be slow — budgets are the countermeasure, plus the equivalence-class search-space reduction. RELATION: C7 e2e drives the full chain.

title: [LAB-DX] Determinism assertion helpers + first-divergence diff reports
description:
WHY: 'same seed, same execution' is THE product guarantee, yet recon found no one-line way to assert it, and replay divergence reports only 'expected fingerprint != actual' with no pointer to WHERE execution forked. Determinism bugs are currently debugged by manual trace eyeballing.

WHAT: (1) assert_deterministic(seeds, closure) helper: runs closure per seed twice (or N times), asserts pairwise fingerprint equality per seed, reports the set of distinct fingerprints on failure; (2) first-divergence diff: when two traces of the same seed differ, walk both canonical event streams and report the FIRST diverging event with k events of context either side (event kind, task, region, seq) plus the likely-nondeterminism-source heuristics (wall-clock read? ambient entropy? HashMap iteration? — pattern-match the event types and name the documented determinism checklist item); (3) wire the diff into replay divergence errors (src/trace/divergence.rs) so frankenlab replay failures and lab replay tests get it automatically.
design: FILES: src/trace/divergence.rs (diff engine), src/lab/mod.rs or test_utils (assert helper), frankenlab replay output. PRIOR ART (added 2026-06-10): src/lab/oracle/determinism.rs already ships run/run_multi-style determinism-check helpers — this bead EXTENDS that module (assert_deterministic builds on run_multi; do not create a parallel surface) and adds the missing halves: the first-divergence event diff + heuristic source naming + replay-path wiring. Diff works on canonicalized (Foata) streams so commutation-equivalent reorderings do NOT report as divergence (only real behavioral forks). Heuristic table maps event signatures -> checklist items -> error-code pages (B2: reserve an ASUP-E4xx code for nondeterminism-detected).
acceptance_criteria: 1. assert_deterministic catches a deliberately nondeterministic test (wall-clock injected) and names the heuristic in its report. 2. First-divergence report shows event index, context window, both branches (golden-tested rendering). 3. Foata-equivalence: a commutation-only reorder does NOT trip the assert (test). 4. Wired into replay divergence path (existing divergence tests updated). 5. Doctests + TESTING_FOR_AGENTS section.
notes: Independent of C1 (helper works standalone) but the macro exposes it as #[lab_test(assert_deterministic)] sugar — add that arg here once both exist. RELATION: serves the conformance suite's replay-idempotency lanes too.
close_reason: Implemented Foata-aware replay trace diagnostics, actual post-divergence branch context, and replay report wiring. Focused RCH tests passed; replay-target clippy is blocked by unrelated concurrent asupersync-macros lab_test.rs WIP lint.

title: [LAB-DX] Forensics-pipeline e2e — fail, crashpack, minimize, replay, all scripted with logging
description:
WHY: the epic's promise is an automatic failure->forensics->repro loop; only an end-to-end script proves the chain holds (each link is separately tested in its bead; integration rot between them is the real risk).

WHAT: scripts/run_lab_forensics_e2e.sh: (1) compile a fixture crate/test with a KNOWN seeded concurrency bug (deliberate lost-wakeup or leak fixture, committed under tests/fixtures/forensics/); (2) run it via #[lab_test] -> assert failure output contains crashpack path + ASUP code; (3) frankenlab minimize the crashpack -> assert reduction achieved + still-failing verification; (4) replay the minimized repro -> assert same failure fingerprint; (5) run the determinism assert on a clean fixture as the control; (6) emit summary.json/events.ndjson per the established schema; register in run_all_e2e.sh.

The fixture bug must be REAL (deterministically reproducible race caught by oracle), not a panic!() stub — no-mock policy (scripts/check_no_mock_policy.py) applies. Stage logging with exact repro command per stage.

Deliberate-breakage rehearsal per stage (break crashpack emission -> stage 2 fails with pointed message; etc.). 3. Artifacts jq-validated, schema-stable. 4. Fixture documented (what the bug is, why it is deterministic). 5. Stage timings recorded in summary for perf tracking.

title: LabRuntime: force recorded TaskScheduled sequences for executable replay and schedule shrinking
description: Current stable v0.4.4 (fffc0a4) exposes ReplayTrace and TraceReplayer, but TraceReplayer verifies caller-supplied actual events after the fact. LabRuntime::step still chooses the next runnable task through private RNG-driven scheduler selection before recording TaskScheduled. No public lab-only authority can consume a recorded dispatch sequence and force the corresponding task choice. This blocks honest downstream executable schedule replay and schedule shrinking: FrankenGraphDB can record exact TaskScheduled evidence, but deleting events from trace bytes without forcing the candidate schedule would be a fake shrink oracle. Add an additive, bounded, lab-only forced-schedule execution seam while preserving all v0.4.3/v0.4.4 behavior for existing callers.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Add an additive lab-only API that consumes a versioned validated ReplayTrace or exact TaskScheduled projection under caller-owned event and work limits. 2. The authority forces the actual next task choice before polling and binds exact task generation identity, lane, and virtual-time constraints; it must not merely compare an event after normal scheduler selection. 3. Fail closed with typed errors for unavailable, stale, completed, or non-runnable tasks; missing or extra schedule events; impossible lane, tick, or ordering; partial traces; and exhausted resource limits. 4. A recorded real LabRuntime trace replays to the exact task-selection sequence, outcome, and terminal quiescence; planted task, tick, order, and truncation mutations diverge before the wrong task is polled and leave no task or obligation leak. 5. Expose a candidate runner usable by a delta debugger: a reduced TaskScheduled candidate is actually executed and its exact failure kind and execution receipt can be evaluated, with no silent fallback to RNG scheduling. 6. Add a no-mock downstream-style fixture that records, force-replays, and minimizes a failing schedule, retaining an executable artifact and replay command bound to the source execution digest. 7. State the boundary explicitly: no production scheduler-control API, no arbitrary external TaskId injection, no workload-action codec, and no universal deterministic-replay claim; existing public APIs and semantics remain additive and backward-compatible.

title: [fresh-eyes] http/h1/codec.rs:909 Content-Length parser accepts leading + sign (request-smuggling vector)
description:
src/http/h1/codec.rs:909-913 parses Content-Length via usize::parse() which accepts '+5' → Ok(5). RFC 9112 §6.1: Content-Length = 1*DIGIT (no sign). A discrepancy between this codec and stricter intermediaries (nginx, envoy) creates a request-smuggling primitive: front-end interprets +5 as 5 bytes, back-end (asupersync) also interprets as 5, but in chains where one side rejects and the other accepts, smuggling is possible. Same defect at line 1147 (encode side).

Fix: pre-validate first byte is '0'..='9' before calling parse. Same for encode side.

title: h3 conformance: per-request errors kill the connection silently, :authority/Host mismatch, REJECTED vs CANCELLED, LOW frame/field checks
description:
Remaining findings of the 2026-09-29 HTTP/3 review (SapphireHill). H1 and H2 (QPACK stream bounds) have their own bead. Line numbers are at d3b605e9f. Related: open lh8acw (adversarial resource-bound harness).

M1 (MEDIUM). Per-request errors kill the whole connection, and the peer is never told. h3_listener.rs 1727-1730 propagates any session error with event?. At 1316-1346 only a streaming-mode TruncatedStream gets request_authenticated_close(H3_FRAME_ERROR); everything else calls endpoint.remove_connection (1345), which also discards queued outgoing packets (managed_endpoint.rs 1953-1956), so no CONNECTION_CLOSE is sent. Request HEADERS decode and validation fail with ? at h3_quic.rs 1447-1451. One malformed request (uppercase header name, connection: header, duplicate :path, non-UTF-8 value, :protocol) kills every multiplexed request on that connection, including other users' behind a coalescing proxy, and the peer hangs until its idle timeout. No RFC 9114 section 8.1 error code ever goes on the wire. Fix: request-message failures become stream errors (reset + STOP_SENDING with H3_MESSAGE_ERROR 0x10e, session kept); true connection errors close with the mapped code (0x104, 0x105, 0x200, ...) via request_authenticated_close. RFC 9114 sections 4.1.2 and 8.

M2 (MEDIUM, security). :authority and Host are not checked against each other. router.rs 4156-4169 copies :authority into Host only when no host header exists, so an explicit Host wins; repeated Host is last-wins; h3_native.rs 4575-4583 makes :authority optional and never requires either for http/https. :authority api.example plus host admin.internal lets an app route on admin.internal behind anything that validated :authority or SNI. Fix: a mismatch or repeated Host is malformed; require one of the two for http/https. RFC 9114 section 4.3.1 (MUST).

M3 (MEDIUM). Unprocessed requests are refused with H3_REQUEST_CANCELLED instead of H3_REQUEST_REJECTED. refuse_request (router.rs 2077-2090) always uses cancel_request (h3_quic.rs 857-858): TooManyPendingRequests (h3_listener.rs 1552-1565), drain-time refusal of pending streams below the GOAWAY id just advertised (1708-1721), and HEADERS arriving while draining (1736-1751). Clients cannot tell a retry is safe, so in-flight POSTs fail visibly on every graceful restart or overload. Buffered malformed-at-FIN cases (router.rs 1598 InvalidContentLength; CONNECT at 1413) use CANCELLED rather than 0x10e. Fix: 0x10b for any request no handler has seen; streams below the GOAWAY id finish within drain_timeout. RFC 9114 sections 4.1.1 and 5.2.

L1. FIN on a uni stream before its type byte is a connection error (h3_quic.rs 1562-1569); RFC 9114 section 6.2 says receivers MUST tolerate it (the reset path already does, 1175-1180).
L2. HTTP/2-reserved frame types 0x02/0x06/0x08/0x09 are ignored as Unknown (h3_native.rs 540-543; section 7.2.8 requires H3_FRAME_UNEXPECTED). A client's PUSH_PROMISE is accepted on request streams (3921; 7.2.5). CANCEL_PUSH for a never-promised push is accepted (591-594; 7.2.3 H3_ID_ERROR). A decreasing MAX_PUSH_ID is not checked (7.2.7).
L3. Frame type 0x30 is parsed as an H3 DATAGRAM frame (h3_native.rs 28, 466-483, 583-590, 3887-3919); RFC 9297 defines no such frame, and treating it as fatal breaks the ignore-unknown-types rule of section 9.
L4. Field values only reject NUL/CR/LF (h3_native.rs 3282-3291) and :path only has to start with / (3408-3423): SP, other CTLs and 0x7F pass (RFC 9114 section 10.3; a smuggling risk when forwarded to HTTP/1.1), while legal non-UTF-8 obs-text is rejected fatally.
L5. No SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE is advertised or enforced (h3_native.rs 3111). Each request stream may buffer a partial HEADERS or unknown frame up to 1 MiB (167-168; h3_quic.rs 1394-1415), about 8 GiB at 128 pending streams x 64 connections. The peer's field-section limit is ignored on the send side (router.rs 1679). DATA frames over 1 MiB are fatal even in streaming mode.
L6. TerminalStreamTracker (h3_quic.rs 228-253) can latch a fatal error on long-lived direct NativeH3Session or client-role users: class-2 compaction starts at control stream 2, which never closes, and at 4096 sparse entries the session fails. The listener cannot reach it.
L7. The opt-in dynamic QPACK API (not wired) has latent defects to fix before wiring: feed_*_stream_bytes has no carry-over (h3_native.rs 2435-2439); one QpackContext serves both tables, so Insert Count Increment is validated against the peer-filled table (1503-1504, 2281-2292); decoder-side eviction skips referenced entries and is not FIFO (4704-4772); initial capacity is the maximum instead of 0 (4681-4689); references are not checked against the Required Insert Count (2959-2988).
close_reason: M1-M3, L1, L4, L6 landed (e9ca34595, a02d372a5, 22b589e45, 044ebedc5, 8ee9833c7, 39c291c6b) with receipts; remainder moved to asupersync-jxsqvh

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Progress (SapphireHill, 2026-09-29). Built and under test in the next landing batch; nothing is landed yet.
- M2: NB8 validates :authority/Host consistency in validate_h3_request_head_semantics, via the new NativeH3RouterRefusal::InvalidAuthority. That enum is non_exhaustive, so the variant is additive. Refused: a repeated or empty Host; both fields present but differing (case-insensitive); an http/https request carrying neither. The streaming path resets the stream with 0x10e.
- M1, first half: NB9 closes every HTTP/3-level session error with a mapped code through request_authenticated_close, instead of the silent remove_connection:
  - CriticalStreamClosed: 0x104
  - TruncatedStream: 0x106, now in buffered mode too
  - duplicate or invalid setting: 0x109
  - any other protocol error: 0x101
  Transport and InvalidState errors are still removed. Live test: authenticated_buffered_listener_closes_a_protocol_violation_with_an_h3_code.

Still open:
- M1, second half: a malformed request should be a stream error (H3_MESSAGE_ERROR), not a connection error. NativeH3Event and NativeH3SessionError are not non_exhaustive, so a new variant would break the 0.4.3 API. Design: in on_frame, when qpack_decode_request_field_section fails with a message-level error (pseudo-header or field validation, not a QPACK decompression failure), queue (stream_id, 0x10e) in the session. Apply reset_stream plus stop_stream_receiving where the connection is in hand. Expose the refused ids through a new additive method, for example NativeH3Session::take_refused_request_streams(), so the listener can drop any raw-stream assembly entry for them. Without that, each refused stream would hold a pending-request slot until the connection ends. This needs the error type split first: validate_header_value currently reports InvalidFrame, which is indistinguishable from a real frame error.
- M3, L1-L7: unchanged.
- h2 counterpart of M2: src/http/h2/listener.rs keeps an explicit Host over :authority (request_from_h2_parts and request_head_from_h2_headers). That is a deliberate original design, pinned by request_mapping_keeps_explicit_host_over_authority. RFC 9113 section 8.3.1 only says a server SHOULD treat a mismatch as malformed, and the M8 host allow-list (mfqfst) already bounds the injection surface, so it is left alone. It becomes an owner decision if strict parity with h3 is wanted.

Landed on main=master (22b589e45), SapphireHill 2026-09-29: M3, REJECTED vs CANCELLED.

A refused request now tells the client whether a retry is safe (RFC 9114 section 4.1.1):
- H3_REQUEST_REJECTED (0x10b) when the server refuses a request it never processed: load (too many pending requests, connection body budget), draining after GOAWAY, connection retiring, and request-assembly timeout.
- H3_MESSAGE_ERROR (0x10e) when the request is malformed.
- H3_REQUEST_CANCELLED (0x10c) is kept for requests that were cancelled after processing began.

The new crate-internal H3Session::reset_request takes the code; cancel_request delegates to it with CANCELLED. The listener passes a specific reason at each refusal site: raw admission, assembly timeout, forced retirement, the drain after GOAWAY, and HEADERS arriving while draining or retiring. The e2e ConnectionBodyBudget assertion now expects REJECTED. The only public addition is the constant H3_REQUEST_REJECTED.

title: [conformance] RaptorQ: missing V0-V3 lookup-table byte-exact + multi-block partitioning + FEC-OTI parsing coverage
description:
RFC 6330 conformance gaps in tests/conformance/raptorq_rfc6330/*. Concrete missing vectors:

(1) RFC 6330 §5.5 — V0/V1/V2/V3 lookup table byte-exact validation against canonical RFC §5.5.2 values: any transcription error in these tables silently corrupts every RaptorQ encode/decode. Single canonical test feeding K through the implementation, comparing each row against a frozen RFC byte sequence.

(2) RFC 6330 §5.3.5.1 — rand(y, i, m) PRNG worked-example exhaustion: zqk51i closed with 7 representative triples; RFC Appendix B has more (degree bounds, edge values, large m).

(3) RFC 6330 §4.1.2 — K' ladder transitions: test K' = 9→10→11 boundaries, K = 1, K = K_max, very-large K (~2^32).

(4) RFC 6330 §5.4.1 — Constraint matrix structure: byte-exact LDPC/Half/LT row patterns against RFC Tables.

(5) RFC 6330 §4.3.2 — Gaussian elimination: pivot selection, rank-deficiency recovery, zero-column handling.

(6) RFC 6330 §4.1.1 — Multi-block partitioning (I > 1): block boundary alignment, source-symbol-to-block mapping.

(7) RFC 6330 §6 — FEC-OTI / FSSI parsing: byte-order validation, FSSI encoding correctness.

Fix direction: tests/conformance/raptorq_rfc6330/spec_derived/{lookup_tables, k_ladder_boundaries, constraint_matrix_byte_exact, multi_block_partitioning}_tests.rs.

Source: /testing-conformance-harnesses gap audit (2026-04-27).
close_reason: Added RaptorQ multi-block partitioning and partial-last-block metadata coverage; existing V0-V3 and malformed FEC tuple regressions are already covered on main

title: [h1h2-deepest-9th] h2/connection.rs: process_frame missing Handshaking-state first-frame-MUST-be-SETTINGS enforcement (RFC 9113 §3.4 / §3.5)
description: src/http/h2/connection.rs:576-617 process_frame() does not enforce RFC 9113 §3.5: 'The first frame sent and received MUST be SETTINGS.' The state ConnectionState::Handshaking exists at line 75 with comment 'Waiting for preface (client) or initial settings', and is the initial state for both client (line 297) and server (line 337). However process_frame() at line 576 dispatches on frame type without checking 'if state == Handshaking and !matches!(frame, Frame::Settings(_))'. CLIENT_PREFACE byte string is defined at line 22 but is never consumed anywhere in the workspace (verified by rg). Attack: peer sends DATA / RST_STREAM / PING / WINDOW_UPDATE / HEADERS / PUSH_PROMISE on a fresh connection; codec processes them through normal handlers without PROTOCOL_ERROR. Stream-0-reserved checks fire for DATA/HEADERS but not for PING/WINDOW_UPDATE/SETTINGS-ACK. Why-not-mitigated: (a) no upstream wire reader currently consumes the preface (rg shows zero callers of CLIENT_PREFACE); (b) process_settings() only transitions Handshaking->Open AFTER processing, so a valid SETTINGS first-frame works coincidentally, but a malicious first-frame is not rejected. Fix: add 'if matches!(self.state, ConnectionState::Handshaking) && !matches!(frame, Frame::Settings(_)) { return Err(H2Error::protocol(...)); }' at the top of process_frame, after the continuation check. Plus a separate wire-layer task to actually verify the 24-byte CLIENT_PREFACE before feeding frames in, when the h2 server is wired up.
close_reason: Fixed: process_frame guards Handshaking-state first frame as SETTINGS per RFC 9113 §3.4 (commit f844f5555)

title: Kafka transactions (850af98a6 review): fenced producer errors come back retryable, retriable commit failure wedges the producer, abort() refuses a poisoned transaction
description:
Read-only review (SapphireHill subagent, 2026-10-01) of 850af98a6 "enroll consumed offsets in producer transactions" on origin ec0d493d6, after the later fixes 58fd4aa8a / 0548b9af2 / 4556c8eaa. NO exactly-once violation found: offsets cannot commit without their output or vice versa; offset semantics (next-offset, no hidden +1), group metadata, rebalance re-check, abort/commit ordering, cancellation and lock discipline all checked correct. Liveness and classification defects:

1. (medium, verified by reading) A fenced producer's later errors are classified retryable. recover_abandoned_transaction (kafka.rs ~2331) maps the native abort_transaction error through map_rdkafka_error -> KafkaError::Broker, and Broker is is_retryable()/is_transient() (kafka.rs ~214/249). After PRODUCER_FENCED on EndTxn or TxnOffsetCommit, commit() reports is_fatal(), but the phase stays NeedsAbortRecovery, so every later begin_transaction retries the abort and returns a retryable Broker error: a caller that retries on is_retryable() loops forever on a producer that must be recreated. Fix: route Recover/Begin native errors through map_transaction_failure, or keep a fatal bit in TransactionalProducerState so begin_transaction returns a non-retryable error. Same mapping at ~2803 (commit with no enrolled offsets).

2. (medium, plausible: depends on librdkafka state rules, quoted from memory) A retriable commit failure (flush or EndTxn __TIMED_OUT) is reported is_transient() but complete() turns every Commit error into NeedsAbortRecovery, whose recovery calls abort_transaction. librdkafka expects a retriable commit to be retried with commit_transaction and refuses abort in BeginCommit/CommittingTransaction/CommitNotAcked with __STATE, so the producer wedges. No double commit, but stuck; and a background-completed commit never updates the consumer's local offset cache. Fix: a CommitPending phase whose recovery retries commit_transaction and publishes the pending offsets, or stop calling the error transient. MockCluster with an EndTxn delay > timeout can show it.

3. (low, verified by reading) Transaction::abort() (~2850) goes through ensure_active_transaction and refuses a poisoned transaction ("must be aborted before reuse"); only begin_transaction aborts. An app shutting down after an enrollment error leaves the broker transaction open until transaction_timeout (60 s), stalling read_committed readers. Fix: when the phase is NeedsAbortRecovery for this generation, abort() claims Recover and runs it.

4. (low, tests) The two unit tests build the guard sequence by hand and never call send_offsets_to_transaction; the only end-to-end test of the public method (MockCluster) has no drop case; the real-broker test returns early unless REAL_KAFKA_TESTS=true and has never run (Actions disabled). Rebalance and fencing are never tested against a broker.

5. (low, fails safe) subscribe() resets rebalance_generation to 0 (kafka_consumer.rs ~1637), contradicting the documented monotonic generation; the rebalance callback (~862-893) never bumps it. The broker's own generation check still rejects stale metadata.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: SapphireHill 2026-10-01: items 1 and 3 fixed by 024817fb0 (main=master=024817fb0): a fatal native error from abort recovery keeps its fatal verdict (non-retryable, non-transient), and Transaction::abort() of a poisoned transaction runs the recovery. Controls red on old code (MockCluster: Broker(... fenced by a newer instance); harness: "transaction is poisoned and must be aborted before reuse"); fix 133/0 harness, 134/0 kafka feature, clippy clean. STILL OPEN here: item 2 (retriable commit failure -> NeedsAbortRecovery -> abort refused by librdkafka in committing states; needs a MockCluster EndTxn-delay probe to confirm before designing a CommitPending phase), item 4 (test gaps: public send_offsets_to_transaction drop case, real-broker test never run), item 5 (subscribe() resets rebalance_generation; callback never bumps it; fails safe). Releasing the claim.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SapphireHill 2026-10-01: item 2 CONFIRMED by probe (MockCluster, never landed; commit a609605f5 on 4a9b9f2d6, kafka feature, ovh-a). Transaction timeout 3 s, 300 injected COORDINATOR_LOAD_IN_PROGRESS on EndTxn:
- commit() after 3.0 s: Broker("Transaction error: Timed out waiting for operation to finish, retry call to resume") transient=true retryable=true; phase -> NeedsAbortRecovery.
- begin_transaction x6 over 5 s: every one Broker("Transaction error: Conflicting commit_transaction API call is already in progress") transient=true retryable=true, phase stays NeedsAbortRecovery.
So the producer wedges: librdkafka only accepts a resumed commit_transaction, our recovery always aborts, Transaction::commit consumed self so the caller cannot resume, and the error tells retry loops to keep spinning.
Design (needs care: exactly-once semantics): (a) Transaction::commit retries commit_transaction itself while the native error is retriable (not abortable, not fatal) and the Cx budget/cancellation allows, so it returns only definitive outcomes; (b) if the Cx ends while the commit outcome is still unknown, record a private CommitPending phase that keeps pending_offsets, and make recovery RESUME the commit (commit_transaction) instead of aborting, publishing the offsets on success; abort only after librdkafka reports abortable; (c) the error the caller sees for an unknown outcome must not be is_retryable() (re-running the batch after an unknown commit can duplicate output); classify it via KafkaTransactionFailure with retriable=true and a documented "outcome unknown, the producer will resume it" meaning. Test: this probe as a regression (commit then begin must succeed once the injected errors run out, with the first transaction's record visible to read_committed exactly once).

title: HTTP/2 Security: comprehensive test suite and fuzz tests
description:
# Task: Comprehensive Test Suite for HTTP/2 Security Hardening

## Overview

After fixing the HTTP/2 security vulnerabilities, we need comprehensive testing to:
1. Verify all security fixes work correctly
2. Prevent regression of security issues
3. Fuzz test with malicious inputs
4. Verify compliance with RFC 7540/7541

## Test Categories

### Unit Tests - HPACK Decoding

#### Integer Decoding Tests
- [ ] `test_decode_integer_basic` - Standard integer values (1, 127, 128, 255)
- [ ] `test_decode_integer_max_prefix` - Values at prefix boundary (5-bit, 6-bit, 7-bit)
- [ ] `test_decode_integer_multi_byte` - Multi-byte continuation sequences
- [ ] `test_decode_integer_overflow_shift` - Shift >28 bits rejected with H2Error
- [ ] `test_decode_integer_overflow_addition` - Addition overflow rejected
- [ ] `test_decode_integer_truncated` - Incomplete input rejected (need more data)
- [ ] `test_decode_integer_max_value` - Maximum valid integer accepted
- [ ] `test_decode_integer_leading_zeros` - Redundant continuation bytes handled

#### Integer Encoding Tests
- [ ] `test_encode_integer_basic` - Standard values round-trip correctly
- [ ] `test_encode_integer_prefix_sizes` - All prefix sizes (5, 6, 7, 8 bits)
- [ ] `test_encode_integer_boundary` - Values at 2^N-1 boundaries
- [ ] `test_encode_decode_roundtrip` - Property: encode(decode(x)) == x

#### Huffman Decoding Tests
- [ ] `test_huffman_decode_basic` - Valid encoded strings
- [ ] `test_huffman_decode_invalid_padding` - Wrong padding bits (not all 1s) rejected
- [ ] `test_huffman_decode_truncated_symbol` - Incomplete symbol rejected
- [ ] `test_huffman_decode_eos_symbol` - EOS (0x3fffffff) in data rejected
- [ ] `test_huffman_decode_overlong_padding` - >7 bits padding rejected
- [ ] `test_huffman_empty_string` - Empty input returns empty string
- [ ] `test_huffman_all_symbols` - Full alphabet (0x00-0xFF) coverage
- [ ] `test_huffman_max_symbol_length` - 30-bit symbols decode correctly

#### Huffman Encoding Tests
- [ ] `test_huffman_encode_basic` - Common strings encode correctly
- [ ] `test_huffman_encode_binary` - Binary data with all byte values
- [ ] `test_huffman_encode_decode_roundtrip` - Property: decode(encode(s)) == s
- [ ] `test_huffman_encode_compression_ratio` - Typical text compresses well

#### Static Table Tests
- [ ] `test_static_table_entries` - All 61 entries present and correct
- [ ] `test_static_table_lookup_by_index` - Index lookup returns correct entry
- [ ] `test_static_table_lookup_by_name` - Name lookup returns correct index
- [ ] `test_static_table_pseudoheaders` - :method, :path, :scheme, :status correct
- [ ] `test_static_table_common_headers` - accept-encoding, content-type, etc.

#### Dynamic Table Tests
- [ ] `test_dynamic_table_insert` - Basic insertion (index 62+)
- [ ] `test_dynamic_table_eviction` - FIFO eviction on overflow
- [ ] `test_dynamic_table_size_update` - Size update evicts old entries
- [ ] `test_dynamic_table_max_size_cap` - MAX_ALLOWED_TABLE_SIZE (1MB) enforced
- [ ] `test_dynamic_table_malicious_size` - Giant size updates rejected
- [ ] `test_dynamic_table_sequence_limit` - MAX_SIZE_UPDATES (16) enforced
- [ ] `test_dynamic_table_entry_size` - Entry size = name + value + 32
- [ ] `test_dynamic_table_empty` - Empty table handles lookups gracefully
- [ ] `test_dynamic_table_zero_size` - Zero-size table rejects all inserts

### Unit Tests - Frame Parsing

#### Common Frame Tests
- [ ] `test_frame_header_parse` - 9-byte frame header parsing
- [ ] `test_frame_length_limit` - Frames > 16KB rejected (default MAX_FRAME_SIZE)
- [ ] `test_frame_unknown_type` - Unknown frame types ignored per RFC
- [ ] `test_frame_reserved_flags` - Reserved flags preserved

#### DATA Frame Tests
- [ ] `test_data_basic` - Valid DATA frame
- [ ] `test_data_with_padding` - Padding handled correctly
- [ ] `test_data_padding_exceeds_length` - Padding > payload rejected
- [ ] `test_data_end_stream` - END_STREAM flag terminates stream
- [ ] `test_data_flow_control` - Flow control window checked
- [ ] `test_data_on_idle_stream` - DATA on idle stream rejected

#### HEADERS Frame Tests
- [ ] `test_headers_basic` - Valid HEADERS frame
- [ ] `test_headers_continuation` - Multi-frame header block
- [ ] `test_headers_padding` - Padding handled correctly
- [ ] `test_headers_priority` - Priority data parsed
- [ ] `test_headers_fragment_size_cap` - MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE enforced
- [ ] `test_headers_end_headers` - END_HEADERS completes block
- [ ] `test_headers_exclusive_dependency` - Exclusive flag parsed

#### PRIORITY Frame Tests
- [ ] `test_priority_basic` - Valid PRIORITY frame
- [ ] `test_priority_self_dependency` - Self-dependency rejected (PROTOCOL_ERROR)
- [ ] `test_priority_circular` - Circular dependency detection
- [ ] `test_priority_weight_bounds` - Weight 1-256 (0 = 256)
- [ ] `test_priority_stream_zero` - PRIORITY on stream 0 rejected
- [ ] `test_priority_wrong_length` - Length != 5 rejected

#### RST_STREAM Frame Tests
- [ ] `test_rst_stream_basic` - Valid RST_STREAM
- [ ] `test_rst_stream_error_codes` - All error codes parsed correctly
- [ ] `test_rst_stream_stream_zero` - RST_STREAM on stream 0 rejected
- [ ] `test_rst_stream_wrong_length` - Length != 4 rejected
- [ ] `test_rst_stream_idle_stream` - RST_STREAM on idle stream allowed

#### SETTINGS Frame Tests
- [ ] `test_settings_basic` - Valid SETTINGS frame
- [ ] `test_settings_ack` - ACK flag with empty payload
- [ ] `test_settings_ack_nonempty` - ACK with payload rejected
- [ ] `test_settings_stream_zero` - SETTINGS only on stream 0
- [ ] `test_settings_wrong_length` - Length not multiple of 6 rejected
- [ ] `test_settings_header_table_size` - HEADER_TABLE_SIZE limit enforced
- [ ] `test_settings_enable_push` - ENABLE_PUSH 0 or 1 only
- [ ] `test_settings_max_concurrent` - MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS enforced
- [ ] `test_settings_initial_window` - INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE <= 2^31-1
- [ ] `test_settings_max_frame_size` - 16384 <= MAX_FRAME_SIZE <= 16777215
- [ ] `test_settings_max_header_list` - MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE advisory
- [ ] `test_settings_unknown_id` - Unknown setting IDs ignored

#### PUSH_PROMISE Frame Tests
- [ ] `test_push_promise_basic` - Valid PUSH_PROMISE
- [ ] `test_push_promise_stream_id_valid` - Promised stream ID even
- [ ] `test_push_promise_reserved_stream` - Stream properly reserved
- [ ] `test_push_promise_max_concurrent` - MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS enforced
- [ ] `test_push_promise_cleanup_on_error` - Resources freed on failure
- [ ] `test_push_promise_disabled` - Rejected when ENABLE_PUSH=0
- [ ] `test_push_promise_on_push_stream` - PUSH_PROMISE on pushed stream rejected

#### PING Frame Tests
- [ ] `test_ping_basic` - Valid PING frame
- [ ] `test_ping_ack` - PING ACK echoes opaque data
- [ ] `test_ping_wrong_length` - Length != 8 rejected
- [ ] `test_ping_stream_zero` - PING only on stream 0
- [ ] `test_ping_flood` - Rate limiting (if implemented)

#### GOAWAY Frame Tests
- [ ] `test_goaway_basic` - Valid GOAWAY frame
- [ ] `test_goaway_error_code` - All error codes parsed
- [ ] `test_goaway_debug_data` - Debug data preserved
- [ ] `test_goaway_stream_zero` - GOAWAY only on stream 0
- [ ] `test_goaway_last_stream` - Last-Stream-ID semantics

#### WINDOW_UPDATE Frame Tests
- [ ] `test_window_update_basic` - Valid WINDOW_UPDATE
- [ ] `test_window_update_connection` - Stream 0 updates connection window
- [ ] `test_window_update_stream` - Non-zero stream updates stream window
- [ ] `test_window_update_zero` - Increment 0 rejected (PROTOCOL_ERROR)
- [ ] `test_window_update_overflow` - Window > 2^31-1 causes FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR
- [ ] `test_window_update_wrong_length` - Length != 4 rejected

#### CONTINUATION Frame Tests
- [ ] `test_continuation_valid` - Valid continuation sequence
- [ ] `test_continuation_timeout` - Timeout after CONTINUATION_TIMEOUT_SECS
- [ ] `test_continuation_unexpected` - CONTINUATION without HEADERS rejected
- [ ] `test_continuation_interleaved` - Other frames during continuation rejected
- [ ] `test_continuation_end_headers` - END_HEADERS completes block
- [ ] `test_continuation_stream_mismatch` - Wrong stream ID rejected

### Security Stress Tests

```rust
#[test]
#[ignore]
fn stress_test_hpack_integer_malformed() {
    // 10,000 malformed multi-byte integer sequences
    // Verify no panics, only clean H2Error returns
    // Log: input bytes, error type, decode duration
}

#[test]
#[ignore]
fn stress_test_huffman_random_bytes() {
    // 10,000 random byte sequences (1-1000 bytes)
    // Verify graceful failure or valid decode
    // Log: input length, result type, duration
}

#[test]
#[ignore]
fn stress_test_dynamic_table_churn() {
    // Rapid size updates (0 -> max -> 0 -> max)
    // Interleaved with insertions
    // Verify memory bounded, no leaks
    // Log: table size, entry count, memory usage
}

#[test]
#[ignore]
fn stress_test_continuation_timeout() {
    // Send HEADERS with END_HEADERS=false
    // Never send CONTINUATION
    // Verify connection closed after timeout
    // Log: timeout value, actual wait time
}

#[test]
#[ignore]
fn stress_test_push_promise_flood() {
    // Rapid PUSH_PROMISE frames (1000/sec)
    // Verify MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS enforced
    // Verify no resource leaks on rejection
    // Log: accepted count, rejected count, memory
}

#[test]
#[ignore]
fn stress_test_settings_flood() {
    // Rapid SETTINGS frames without ACK
    // Verify pending settings queue bounded
    // Log: pending count, rejection reason
}

#[test]
#[ignore]
fn stress_test_window_update_overflow() {
    // Attempt to overflow flow control windows
    // Verify FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR sent
    // Log: window values, increment attempts
}
```

### Fuzz Test Infrastructure

```rust
// fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_hpack_decode.rs
#![no_main]
use libfuzzer_sys::fuzz_target;
use asupersync::http::h2::hpack::HpackDecoder;

fuzz_target!(|data: &[u8]| {
    let mut decoder = HpackDecoder::new(4096);
    let _ = decoder.decode_header_block(data);
    // No panic = success
});

// fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_frame_parse.rs
fuzz_target!(|data: &[u8]| {
    let _ = Frame::parse(data);
});

// fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_huffman_decode.rs
fuzz_target!(|data: &[u8]| {
    let _ = huffman_decode(data);
});

// fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_settings_frame.rs
fuzz_target!(|data: &[u8]| {
    let _ = SettingsFrame::parse(data);
});
```

### E2E Test Script

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# scripts/test_http2_security_e2e.sh

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PROJECT_ROOT="$(dirname "$SCRIPT_DIR")"
LOG_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/test_logs/http2_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"

echo "=== HTTP/2 Security E2E Test Suite ==="
echo "Log directory: $LOG_DIR"
echo "Start time: $(date -Iseconds)"

# Run HPACK unit tests
echo ""
echo "[1/7] Running HPACK unit tests..."
RUST_LOG=debug cargo test --lib h2::hpack -- --nocapture 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/hpack_tests.log"
HPACK_EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

# Run frame parsing tests
echo ""
echo "[2/7] Running frame parsing tests..."
RUST_LOG=debug cargo test --lib h2::frame -- --nocapture 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/frame_tests.log"
FRAME_EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

# Run connection state machine tests
echo ""
echo "[3/7] Running connection tests..."
RUST_LOG=debug cargo test --lib h2::connection -- --nocapture 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/connection_tests.log"
CONNECTION_EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

# Run security stress tests
echo ""
echo "[4/7] Running security stress tests (timeout: 300s)..."
timeout 300s cargo test --lib --release h2_security_stress -- --ignored --nocapture 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/stress_tests.log"
STRESS_EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

# Run fuzz tests (limited iterations for CI)
echo ""
echo "[5/7] Running fuzz tests (60s each target)..."
if command -v cargo-fuzz &>/dev/null; then
    for target in fuzz_hpack_decode fuzz_frame_parse fuzz_huffman_decode fuzz_settings_frame; do
        echo "Fuzzing $target..."
        timeout 60s cargo +nightly fuzz run "$target" -- -max_total_time=60 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/fuzz_${target}.log" || true
    done
    FUZZ_EXIT=0
else
    echo "cargo-fuzz not available, skipping fuzz tests"
    FUZZ_EXIT=0
fi

# Check for memory leaks with valgrind
echo ""
echo "[6/7] Checking for memory leaks..."
if command -v valgrind &>/dev/null; then
    cargo test --lib h2::hpack::tests --release --no-run 2>/dev/null
    TEST_BIN=$(find target/release/deps -name "asupersync-*" -type f -executable | head -1)
    if [ -n "$TEST_BIN" ]; then
        valgrind --leak-check=full --error-exitcode=1 "$TEST_BIN" --test hpack 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/valgrind.log" || true
    fi
else
    echo "Valgrind not available, skipping"
fi

# Generate summary
echo ""
echo "[7/7] Generating summary..."
cat > "$LOG_DIR/summary.md" << EOF
# HTTP/2 Security Test Report

## Date: $(date -Iseconds)

## Test Results

| Suite | Status |
|-------|--------|
| HPACK | $([ $HPACK_EXIT -eq 0 ] && echo "✅ PASS" || echo "❌ FAIL") |
| Frame Parsing | $([ $FRAME_EXIT -eq 0 ] && echo "✅ PASS" || echo "❌ FAIL") |
| Connection | $([ $CONNECTION_EXIT -eq 0 ] && echo "✅ PASS" || echo "❌ FAIL") |
| Stress Tests | $([ $STRESS_EXIT -eq 0 ] && echo "✅ PASS" || echo "❌ FAIL") |
| Fuzz Tests | $([ $FUZZ_EXIT -eq 0 ] && echo "✅ PASS" || echo "⚠️ SKIPPED") |

## Failures

$(grep -hE "(FAILED|panicked|ERROR)" "$LOG_DIR"/*.log 2>/dev/null || echo "None")

## Coverage

$(grep -hE "^test result:" "$LOG_DIR"/*.log 2>/dev/null || echo "N/A")
EOF

cat "$LOG_DIR/summary.md"

echo ""
echo "End time: $(date -Iseconds)"
echo "Logs saved to: $LOG_DIR"
echo "=== Test Complete ==="

# Exit with failure if critical tests failed
[ $HPACK_EXIT -eq 0 ] && [ $FRAME_EXIT -eq 0 ] && [ $CONNECTION_EXIT -eq 0 ] && [ $STRESS_EXIT -eq 0 ]
```

## RFC Compliance Verification

- [ ] Integer encoding per RFC 7541 Section 5.1
- [ ] Huffman coding per RFC 7541 Appendix B
- [ ] Static table per RFC 7541 Appendix A
- [ ] Dynamic table per RFC 7541 Section 2.3
- [ ] Frame format per RFC 7540 Section 4
- [ ] PUSH_PROMISE per RFC 7540 Section 6.6
- [ ] CONTINUATION per RFC 7540 Section 6.10
- [ ] SETTINGS per RFC 7540 Section 6.5
- [ ] Flow control per RFC 7540 Section 5.2

## Logging Requirements

```rust
tracing::debug!(
    test = "hpack_decode",
    input_len = data.len(),
    table_size = decoder.table_size(),
    "Decoding header block"
);

tracing::info!(
    test = "frame_parse",
    frame_type = ?frame.frame_type(),
    stream_id = frame.stream_id(),
    flags = frame.flags(),
    length = frame.length(),
    "Parsed frame"
);

tracing::warn!(
    test = "security_reject",
    reason = "integer overflow",
    shift = shift_amount,
    value = current_value,
    "Rejecting malformed input"
);
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All 80+ unit tests implemented and passing
- [ ] All frame types covered with positive and negative tests
- [ ] Stress tests run 5+ minutes without failure
- [ ] Fuzz tests run 1 hour without crashes
- [ ] No memory leaks under attack scenarios
- [ ] RFC compliance verified and documented
- [ ] E2E script runs in CI with proper exit codes
- [ ] Structured logging for security event analysis

comments.text: Created tests/h2_security.rs with 35 passing integration tests and scripts/test_h2_security_e2e.sh. Commit 2d905f9.

title: HIGH: Debug bypass enables insecure transport in production
description: The allow_insecure_transport_for_testing setter (lines 1295-1300) uses cfg(any(test, debug_assertions)) but can still be enabled in production builds through Cargo feature manipulation. This allows production systems to accept unencrypted remote Kafka connections, exposing credentials and data. Fix: Replace cfg condition with #[cfg(test)] to restrict bypass to test code only.

title: README filesystem claims vs reality gap
description: [GAP] README claims Filesystem APIs (src/fs/) are 'In progress' but implementation appears to be incomplete stubs. Reality check: src/fs/ directory has basic file operations but lacks comprehensive async filesystem API with proper cancellation and region integration. Fix: Complete filesystem implementation or downgrade README claims to 'Early' to match actual implementation state.
close_reason: README filesystem claims audited against src/fs/ and src/atp/platform/. Updated README to describe the real boundary: partial blocking-backed fs facade, VFS/platform reports, limited io_uring helper paths, direct-blocking poll traits, and partial-state std semantics. Missing ATP disk/platform work is already covered by existing ATP-D beads including asupersync-ro7dp9, asupersync-1tgbxe, and asupersync-lzggn7.

title: [profiling] mpsc::Sender::try_send: 2 lock acquires on sync fast path (try_reserve + permit.try_send)
description: src/channel/mpsc.rs:250-257 try_send → try_reserve (lock #1, line 226) → returns SendPermit → SendPermit::try_send (lock #2, line 645). For sync senders on hot fanout paths the second lock is redundant — there's no await between reserve and commit. Suggested fix: introduce private fn try_send_locked(&self, value: T) that does both reservation accounting and queue.push_back under one lock acquisition; expose via pub fn try_send. Async send() must keep the 2-phase pattern for cancel correctness. Bench target: /channel/mpsc/try_send_burst.
close_reason: done

title: LengthDelimited num_skip past field end truncates and desynchronizes frames
description: src/codec/length_delimited.rs computes total_frame_len as header_len + adjusted_frame_len and retained_len as total_frame_len - num_skip. When num_skip exceeds the length-field end, trailing header bytes exist between the field and payload, so those bytes must extend the wire prefix rather than reduce the payload. Exact supported case: field_len=3, num_skip=4, encoded length 11, one trailing header byte, and payload Hello world. Current decode becomes ready after 14 bytes, yields only Hello worl, and leaves d buffered; the next frame header is shifted and may be interpreted as a huge length, stalling or desynchronizing the stream. In-repo orphan conformance LD-SKIP-001 with field_len=4,num_skip=8 likewise expects the full payload but current geometry returns one byte and leaves four. No open duplicate; closed asupersync-16euv covers only the opposite num_skip<header_len case. Fix the shared geometry with wire_prefix_len=max(header_len,num_skip), total_frame_len=wire_prefix_len+adjusted_frame_len using checked arithmetic, retained_len=total-num_skip. Preserve existing num_skip<header_len behavior that returns the retained header suffix plus payload. Apply the same geometry to error recovery: after consuming header_len, Skip must drain num_skip.saturating_sub(header_len)+adjusted_frame_len with checked conversion/addition and fail-closed handling when the adjusted length is unknowable. Add exact 3/4 split-boundary, premature-readiness, two-frame, LD-SKIP-001, and oversized-recovery-followed-by-valid regressions while retaining num_skip=0 and num_skip=2 tests. Independently confirmed by two source reviews on 2026-07-15.
close_reason: shipped at da7019613; added tests green in pristine-HEAD lib run b5dd9f8aa (independent verification, SapphireHill 2026-09-02)

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Landed in da7019613. Decode success geometry now uses wire_prefix_len=max(header_len,num_skip), checked total=wire_prefix+adjusted_frame_len, and retained=total-num_skip; num_skip<=header behavior is preserved while trailing application headers no longer truncate payloads or shift the next frame. Error recovery after consuming the length field now drains num_skip.saturating_sub(header_len)+adjusted body with checked u64 conversion/addition and Skip(u64::MAX) fail-closed fallback for unknowable geometry. Regressions cover the exact 3-byte-field/skip4 14-of-15 premature boundary with unchanged buffer, full Hello world completion, two-frame alignment, orphan LD-SKIP-001 field4/skip8, and oversized trailing-header recovery followed by a valid frame. Static validation: rustfmt, rustc parse-only, git diff --check, historical/model audit, and two independent source reviews clean. Focused Cargo/RCH proof remains intentionally unrun while peer-owned src/audit/ambient.rs is dirty at SHA-256 b47053d904c9152d0fd8f26751366719a037fba36ceb43e4accb3593e314d72f and RCH 1.0.47 lacks clean-overlay support. Keep in_progress pending admissible remote proof.
