title: Gate transport/mock module behind test-internals feature
description:
## What

The transport simulator module (src/transport/mock.rs, ~830 lines) is unconditionally
compiled and publicly exported in production builds. It should be gated behind
#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-internals"))].

### Current state (src/transport/mod.rs)

```rust
pub mod mock;                    // Line 8: unconditional
// ...
pub use mock::{                  // Lines 23-26: unconditional re-export
    NodeId, SimChannelSink, SimChannelStream, SimLink, SimNetwork,
    SimSymbolSink, SimSymbolStream, SimTransportConfig, sim_channel,
};
```

### Target state

```rust
#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-internals"))]
pub mod mock;

#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-internals"))]
pub use mock::{
    NodeId, SimChannelSink, SimChannelStream, SimLink, SimNetwork,
    SimSymbolSink, SimSymbolStream, SimTransportConfig, sim_channel,
};
```

## Why

- mock.rs is documented as "Deterministic transport simulator for testing" (line 1)
- All actual usages are in test/benchmark code (verified by audit)
- Exposing test-only simulation types in production API surface:
  - Increases binary size unnecessarily
  - Creates risk of accidental production usage of SimNetwork
  - Pollutes the public API documentation
- The test-internals feature already exists and is enabled by default,
  so this change is zero-cost for development/testing while cleaning
  the production API surface

## How

1. Add cfg gate to mod declaration and re-exports in src/transport/mod.rs
2. Check if any non-test code imports from transport::mock:
   `rg 'transport::mock|SimNetwork|SimTransportConfig|SimLink|sim_channel' src/ --glob '!src/transport/'`
3. Check benches/: `rg 'SimNetwork|sim_channel' benches/`
   - If benches use it, they'll need #[cfg(feature = "test-internals")] too,
     but since test-internals is in default features this should be fine
4. Run cargo check --all-targets
5. Run cargo check --all-targets --no-default-features to verify the gate works
6. Run cargo test --lib transport to verify tests still pass

## Acceptance criteria

- mock module only compiled when test or test-internals feature active
- cargo check --all-targets passes (default features include test-internals)
- cargo check --no-default-features --all-targets passes (mock excluded)
- All transport tests pass
- No production code references SimNetwork/SimTransportConfig

## Considerations

- The test-internals feature is in the default feature set, so this is a
  non-breaking change for anyone using default features
- Benchmarks that reference SimNetwork will need the test-internals feature,
  which they already get by default
- If external consumers depend on mock types, they can enable test-internals

title: HttpClient cannot use net::dns::Resolver: every hostname connect is an uncached system lookup with no DNS timeout; the resolver has no consumer
description:
net::dns::Resolver (TTL cache, lookup timeout, retries, configurable nameservers, cache_stats) has no consumer in the crate. The pooled HTTP/1 client (HttpClient) resolves every hostname it dials with a fresh system lookup: connect_io and the SOCKS5 proxy dial call net::happy_eyeballs::connect_resolved("host:port"), which runs ToSocketAddrs on a blocking thread through net::lookup_all. Found by e8's wiring survey (TODO 03:41Z 10-09); taken by d0.

Effects:
- No DNS cache: a client that opens a new connection per request (Connection: close servers, pool limits, idle reaping) pays one getaddrinfo per connect.
- No DNS timeout of its own: a system lookup in a DNS outage can hold a connect for the resolver library's retry schedule (tens of seconds); only request_timeout or the budget bounds it.
- No way to point the client at specific nameservers (split-horizon DNS, tests with a local nameserver) without a system-wide change.
reqwest exposes this as ClientBuilder::dns_resolver; hyper's HttpConnector takes a resolver.

Plan (additive, opt-in, default unchanged):
- HttpClientBuilder::dns_resolver(Resolver) stores the resolver in a new private HttpClientConfig field (None by default). Resolver clones share one cache, so the caller can keep a clone and read cache_stats().
- connect_io (request target and HTTP proxy) and connect_via_socks5 (SOCKS5 proxy) resolve a hostname through the resolver when one is set, then race the addresses with the same Happy Eyeballs helper as today. Literal IP hosts are dialed directly, as now.
- A DnsError becomes ClientError::ConnectError with a matching io::ErrorKind (Timeout -> TimedOut, Cancelled -> Interrupted, InvalidHost -> InvalidInput, NoRecords -> NotFound, others -> Other).

Test: tests/http_client_dns_resolver.rs runs a local UDP nameserver that answers one made-up name, and an HTTP server that closes every connection. A client with dns_resolver reaches the made-up name twice; the nameserver sees one lookup (A and AAAA) and the shared cache_stats shows the second connect hit the cache. Control: connect_io ignoring the resolver must fail the test (the system resolver cannot resolve the made-up name).

Out of scope here: the HTTP/2 client (Http2Request::send) and the WebSocket client have no builder hook of this shape; they can take the same helper later.
close_reason: Wired net::dns::Resolver into HttpClientConfig, HttpClientBuilder, and HttpClient. Added dial_tcp_with_resolver to connect_io and connect_via_socks5, supporting cached lookups with Happy Eyeballs racing. Verified via integration test http_client_custom_dns_resolver_resolves_and_caches.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: SapphireHill d0, 2026-10-09, note after a review of ceac580d9: the opt-in HttpClientBuilder::dns_resolver path called resolver.lookup_ip without consulting the ambient I/O gate. A task without the IO capability could therefore send DNS queries before the TCP connect refused it. The cause was in net::dns::Resolver itself (no require_ambient_io), and c28671083 fixed it there (asupersync-t2i0o9). The client path is now refused with [ASUP-E009] before any query is sent. I staged a duplicate of this bead (dns_resolver, connect_addrs) and dropped it unlanded once ceac580d9 landed.

title: Define complete TraceEvent enumeration with versioning
description:
## Overview

Define the complete enumeration of all trace events that must be recorded for deterministic replay.

## Requirements

### Event Categories
```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
```

title: [OBLIGATION-SAFETY] Obligation Leak Detection System
description:
GOAL: Implement real-time tracking and detection of obligation leaks (uncommitted permits/acks/leases) to maintain the 'no obligation leaks' invariant.

BACKGROUND: Asupersync's obligation system ensures that all effects are properly committed or aborted. Permits, acknowledgments, and leases must be explicitly handled to prevent resource leaks. However, complex control flow and cancellation scenarios can lead to forgotten obligations.

RATIONALE: Obligation leaks can accumulate silently over time, leading to resource exhaustion or incorrect system behavior. Real-time detection prevents these leaks from going unnoticed and provides immediate feedback to developers about obligation handling bugs.

IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH:
- Instrument all obligation creation points (permits, acks, leases)
- Track obligation lifecycle through commit/abort paths
- Detect uncommitted obligations at region close boundaries
- Provide stack trace attribution for leaked obligations
- Integration with region lifecycle monitoring
- Optional runtime enforcement modes (warn vs panic)

KEY FEATURES:
- Comprehensive obligation lifecycle tracking
- Precise attribution of leak sources with stack traces
- Integration with structured concurrency boundaries
- Configurable enforcement levels for different environments  
- Detailed diagnostics for debugging obligation handling
- Performance monitoring to ensure minimal overhead

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS:
- Zero-cost tracking in release builds when disabled
- Minimal overhead in debug builds
- Thread-safe obligation tracking
- Integration with existing obligation infrastructure
- Structured logging of all detected leaks

SUCCESS METRICS:
- Detects all obligation leak patterns
- Zero false positives in correct code
- Clear attribution for debugging leaks
- Measurable prevention of resource accumulation bugs
close_reason: Enhanced obligation leak detection system implemented: added stack trace attribution, region boundary detection, feature flag for zero-cost compilation, enhanced diagnostics with leak severity classification, and comprehensive leak attribution methods. Core tracking infrastructure enhanced with backward compatibility.

title: [swarm-perf] Add bounded-load distributed routing for hot-node avoidance
description:
Background:
- Pure weighted or successor-based routing is easy to overload during skew, node failure, or hot-region concentration.
- Alien graveyard bounded-load consistent hashing is a direct fit for swarm routing because it caps worst-case node overload while keeping minimal-disruption placement.
- This matters once asupersync is coordinating or hosting many agent lanes across multiple nodes or shards.

Candidate surfaces:
- src/distributed/* routing surfaces
- src/transport/router.rs
- any existing weighted or ring-based placement logic

Required design:
1. Identify the current placement/routing seam where hot-node amplification occurs or would occur.
2. Add a bounded-load variant with explicit epsilon/capacity tuning and fallback to current routing.
3. Expose per-node actual_load/capacity telemetry and rebalance reasons.
4. Preserve deterministic tests with fixed topology and load vectors.

Proof / validation:
- Synthetic skew/failure scenarios comparing peak node utilization and request tails against current routing.
- Regression proving minimal disruption on node add/remove events.
- Config gate that keeps legacy routing intact until the bounded-load path is proven.

Success criteria:
- Peak node overload is bounded more tightly under skew or failure without requiring blunt overprovisioning.
design: Use an explicit bounded-load routing model with capacity vectors and deterministic load inputs, not ambient cluster heuristics. Preserve the current routing path as a selectable fallback and log rebalance reasons so operators can see why hot-node avoidance happened.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover placement invariants, minimal-disruption behavior on node add/remove, and capacity-bound enforcement under skewed demand; a deterministic skew/failure scenario or e2e script logs per-node offered load, accepted load, rebalance reasons, and request-tail behavior; artifacts must make the overload cap and routing churn visible enough for operators to tune epsilon/capacity safely.
notes: Keep this bead separate from scheduler locality work; it is about multi-node placement guarantees and operator-visible routing evidence, not per-socket task stealing. Its scenario/e2e artifacts should emit through asupersync-2ijesw so skew/failure results line up with the rest of the swarm-perf evidence pack.
close_reason: Implemented opt-in BoundedLoadHash routing for hot-node avoidance. Added BoundedLoadConfig with epsilon/min-capacity/weight capacity tuning, BoundedLoadDecision telemetry with selected primary, per-endpoint actual_load/capacity, and rebalance reasons, plus RoutingEntry/transport exports. Existing HashBased behavior remains unchanged as the fallback/config gate. Tests cover primary-within-capacity placement, over-capacity primary rebalance, all-over-capacity fallback to HRW primary, select_n uniqueness/under-capacity fill, survivor stickiness under endpoint removal, and a deterministic skew scenario that logs an operator JSON artifact with config, primary, selected endpoint, per-node load/capacity, and rebalance reason. Validation: rch rustfmt --edition 2024 --check src/transport/router.rs src/transport/mod.rs passed; rch cargo test -p asupersync --lib bounded_load_hash --features test-internals -- --nocapture --test-threads=1 printed 6 passed / 0 failed and the skew artifact. description: Native ATP over native QUIC remains the foundation. Compatibility adapters are valuable for browsers, enterprise egress, and hostile networks, but they must not drive the core architecture.

title: Channel audit: watch changed() can return Closed before a final value; BroadcastStream::get_mut lets a stale waiter token evict another receiver's waker
description:
Read-only audit of src/channel/broadcast.rs and src/channel/watch.rs at origin/main 47117810a (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-05).

No HIGH. Sound:
- broadcast: ring indices and lag accounting, lost-wakeup protection, close detection, permit obligations, panicking clones.
- watch: register-then-recheck on sends, waiter dedup, and cancel safety of changed().

## MEDIUM
M1. watch: changed() can return Closed while a final value is still unseen (watch.rs ~789-810).
- After registering, poll_changed re-reads the version, then checks is_sender_dropped() and returns Err(Closed) without reading the version again.
- A sender that sends and drops in that window loses its final value from the changed() loop. `while rx.changed(cx).await.is_ok()` exits without the last config or shutdown value, and WatchStream ends early the same way.
- The earlier branch (~749-756) gets this right, and the sender_dropped test documents "final update before Closed".
- FIXED in stack P (P5): the final check re-reads the version and reports Ok before Closed. A test-only hook interleaves the send and drop deterministically.

M2. The BroadcastStream waiter token is not tied to its channel, so swapping the stream's receiver evicts another receiver's waker (stream/broadcast_stream.rs ~42 get_mut, Drop ~121; broadcast.rs ~799-805, ~978-1001).
- After a parked poll on channel A, `*stream.get_mut() = tx_b.subscribe()` followed by a drop or re-poll uses A's arena token against B's waker arena. It removes or replaces the waker of a receiver parked on B, which then hangs.
- FIXED in stack P (P6): get_mut clears the registration before handing out the receiver. The edit is line-neutral above the unsafe-ledger line locators 56/66/67.

## LOW
- L1. broadcast::channel(capacity) allocates its whole capacity eagerly. channel(usize::MAX) panics with "capacity overflow", and a huge capacity aborts on allocation failure. The docs only mention 0.
- L2. Values stay in the ring after every receiver has read them, and Sender::len()/is_empty() count them. A `while !tx.is_empty()` drain loop never ends, and payload Drop side effects are delayed. This diverges from tokio.
- L3. The waker arena keeps its peak size, and every send scans all of it under the channel mutex. A debug_assert in arena.rs fires after 2^32 park/drain cycles on one slot.
close_reason: done

title: QUIC/H3 resource-bounded protocol state: stateful adversarial harness asserting a per-connection potential bound (split from bi2462.107 acceptance upgrade)
description:
## Why
Split from bi2462.107's 2026-09-22 acceptance upgrade. The three .107 defects are fixed with old-red receipts: N6 stateless Retry and displacement 2d7843fdd, N10 bounded PATH_CHALLENGE 080279c43, N11 unadvertised DATAGRAM 3c86c5cdd. That upgrade also asked for a stateful adversarial harness proving that protocol state stays resource-bounded under any frame sequence. It was never built; this task tracks it.

## Work
Define a per-connection potential phi = buffered stream bytes + queued control frames (PATH_RESPONSE, DATAGRAM, ACK) + live handlers + pending handshakes, with a configured bound. Drive a managed endpoint and an H3 listener with adversarial sequences: rapid reset (RST after HEADERS), PING and PATH_CHALLENGE floods, window-update games, partial prefaces, spoofed Initials with and without tokens, un-negotiated DATAGRAM, 1-byte STREAM frames in both orders (4gdidf). Assert phi <= bound after every step, and that graceful and forced shutdown finish within their deadlines.

## Acceptance
Each sequence runs against the pre-fix commit of the defect it targets (old-red: at least one sequence per fixed defect fails there) and passes on main. Also a live NativeH3Listener flood at its default max_pending_handshakes (16): legitimate clients connect while spoofed Initials arrive at line rate.

title: [reality-check-wave2][http3][qpack] Decoder feedback and acknowledgement accounting
description:
Parent: asupersync-fjkixh
Depends on: asupersync-pcsitc

Goal:
Implement the RFC 9204 decoder-stream feedback state machine so header acknowledgements, stream cancellations, and insert-count increments are tracked deterministically and can later drive blocked-stream release.

Current reality to preserve:
- src/http/h3_native.rs currently has dynamic field-section Required Insert Count and Base handling, but it does not track peer Known Received Count, outstanding blocked references, stream acknowledgements, or cancellation feedback.
- QPACK stream type recognition exists, but decoder stream bytes are not processed as instructions.

Implementation requirements:
- Add a QPACK decoder-feedback state structure owned by the HTTP/3/QPACK context or connection state as appropriate.
- Apply Header Acknowledgement to mark a stream acknowledged exactly once, reject unknown or duplicate acknowledgements with stable errors, and release any reference protection associated with that stream.
- Apply Stream Cancellation to mark a stream cancelled, release protected dynamic references, and make repeated cancellation idempotent only if the implementation deliberately documents that behavior.
- Apply Insert Count Increment to advance Known Received Count monotonically, reject zero increments if RFC-invalid, reject overflow, and expose the new count for blocked-stream scheduling.
- Keep encoder-instruction mutation separate from decoder-feedback accounting while sharing typed instruction definitions from asupersync-pcsitc.
- Preserve fail-closed behavior under StaticOnly and before the connection has accepted compatible QPACK settings.

Unit tests required:
- Header acknowledgement tests for happy path, unknown stream, duplicate ack, ack after cancellation, and reference release.
- Stream cancellation tests for happy path, unknown stream, cancellation after ack, repeated cancellation policy, and reference release.
- Insert Count Increment tests for one-step, multi-step, max-boundary, zero, overflow, and monotonicity.
- StaticOnly regression tests proving decoder feedback cannot silently enable dynamic decoding.
- Tests asserting exact fields needed later by the proof runner: known_received_count, acknowledged stream ids, cancelled stream ids, outstanding reference counts, and first error.

Acceptance:
- Decoder feedback state is deterministic, inspectable, and test-covered.
- It is ready to feed the blocked-stream scheduler without docs or registry promotion.
- All validation runs through rch exec.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic QPACK decoder-feedback state in src/http/h3_native.rs. Added Header Acknowledgement, Stream Cancellation, and Insert Count Increment application with inspectable known_received_count, acknowledged/cancelled stream sets, outstanding reference counts, and first_error. Added unit coverage for ack happy path/reference release/unknown/duplicate/after-cancel, cancellation happy path/reference release/unknown/duplicate/after-ack, increment one-step/multi-step/max-boundary/zero/overflow, StaticOnly fail-closed behavior, and duplicate/terminal/unknown stream reference tracking. Proof: timeout 1200 rch exec -- env CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 RUSTFLAGS='-C debuginfo=0' cargo test -p asupersync --lib qpack_decoder_feedback --features test-internals -- --nocapture => 6 passed; timeout 600 rch exec -- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check src/http/h3_native.rs => pass; git diff --check -- src/http/h3_native.rs .beads/issues.jsonl => pass; bv --robot-alerts => zero alerts.

Background: reservation-aware fallback ranking now reports reservation_snapshot.source from AgentMailChecker.last_check. If a fallback snapshot has no declared touched files, no per-file check runs, so the output can report source=disabled even when a reservation snapshot was supplied and enabled.

Goal: make rank-fallback output report reservation snapshot availability from the configured snapshot rather than the last per-file check state, while preserving per-candidate overlap details.

Acceptance criteria: add fixture-backed coverage for a fileless fallback bead plus a reservation snapshot; output reservation_snapshot.enabled must be true and source must identify the fixture source; ranked candidates should stay eligible with empty overlap arrays.

Validation: python syntax compile; git diff --check for touched files; rch cargo fmt --check; rch cargo test -p asupersync --test proof_runner_contract rank_fallback -- --nocapture; rch cargo clippy -p asupersync --test proof_runner_contract -- -D warnings.
close_reason: Implemented fileless reservation snapshot metadata fix in proof_runner. AgentMailChecker now reports top-level snapshot_status from configured reservation snapshot instead of the last per-file check state, so --rank-fallback-beads --reservation-snapshot reports source snapshot and enabled true even when candidates declare no touched_files. Added fixture-backed contract coverage for a fileless disk-safe fallback candidate with empty touched_files/overlaps and zero reservation demotion/hard-block counts. Validation: python3 -m py_compile scripts/proof_runner.py; git diff --check -- scripts/proof_runner.py tests/proof_runner_contract.rs .beads/issues.jsonl; rch cargo fmt --check; rch cargo test -p asupersync --test proof_runner_contract rank_fallback -- --nocapture passed 3/3; rch cargo clippy -p asupersync --test proof_runner_contract -- -D warnings passed. title: Harden three-lane cancel-mask transition observations

Background: GentleCitadel announced an active non-overlapping `/testing-fuzzing` fallback slice in Agent Mail thread `testing-fuzzing-rwlock-upgrade-race-poll-observer` and reserved `fuzz/fuzz_targets/rwlock_upgrade_race.rs` as reservation `12158`. This tracker bead records that in-flight work so it is not only represented in mail/file reservations.

Problem: `fuzz/fuzz_targets/rwlock_upgrade_race.rs` has paths where `TrackedReader::poll()` results can be ignored, which means `Poll::Ready(Err(_))` can be discarded instead of becoming a fuzz-visible failure. The concurrent-upgrade loop can also count the same successful reader repeatedly across repeated poll passes unless it deduplicates successful reader IDs.

Scope: File-local `/testing-fuzzing` hardening in `fuzz/fuzz_targets/rwlock_upgrade_race.rs`. Replace ignored reader poll outcomes with explicit observation, and ensure repeated poll loops count each successful upgrade reader once. Do not edit `.beads/*`, `fuzz/Cargo.toml`, H1 targets, three-lane targets, progress-certificate targets, pool targets, oneshot targets, or the pre-existing crash artifact unless separately reserved and justified.

Validation expectations: target rustfmt/diff/stale scans, `python3 scripts/fuzz_oracle_debt_scanner.py --repo-root . --root fuzz/fuzz_targets/rwlock_upgrade_race.rs --output json`, and bin-scoped `rch exec -- cargo check/clippy/run --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml --bin rwlock_upgrade_race` using a unique target dir if disk permits. If disk/tmpfs pressure blocks proof, record the exact blocker and avoid deleting generated artifacts without explicit user permission.

Current status: in progress by GentleCitadel based on reservation `12158` and Agent Mail start message `6634`; local disk/tmpfs pressure remains a known validation risk.
close_reason: Tracker reconciliation for GentleCitadel shipped commit 60d9d3abd. Closed based on Agent Mail closeout 6652: rwlock_upgrade_race now observes TrackedReader::poll outcomes, deduplicates successful reader IDs, uses shared UpgradeTracker, and passed rustfmt, git diff --check, oracle-debt scanner, and rch check/clippy/smoke with remote exit 0; local target artifact sync hit ENOSPC after proof.

title: [proof-lane] Classify rch remote-pass artifact retrieval failures
description:
Background: Recent shared-main proof lanes can reach a successful remote compile/test result and then fail during local artifact retrieval because /tmp or / is out of space. Agents currently have to explain this by hand, and closeouts can look ambiguous even though the remote command itself passed.

Goal: Add an explicit proof-lane classifier for rch logs that separates remote command status from artifact retrieval status. A run that prints the cargo/test success line and remote exit=0 should be recorded as remote_command=pass, while ENOSPC during retrieval should be recorded as artifact_retrieval=blocked and local_disk=critical, not as a compile failure.

Scope: Find the existing proof receipt / closeout verifier / session handoff tooling that parses rch evidence. Extend it in place with a small classifier and fixture coverage for: clean remote pass with artifact retrieval success, remote pass followed by rsync ENOSPC retrieval failure, remote compile/test failure, and local rch fallback marker.

Success criteria: The receipt output preserves separate fields for remote command result, artifact retrieval result, local disk pressure signal, and the exact blocker line. Existing green/broken proof semantics remain intact. No deletion or cleanup automation is introduced.

Validation: Add deterministic fixture/golden tests for the classifier, run the narrow script/test command, and if Rust code is touched run the relevant rch cargo test with a unique CARGO_TARGET_DIR. If disk is still critical, stop after non-Cargo fixture proof and report the exact rch blocker.

title: [swarm] Add disk-pressure preflight to fallback work discovery
description:
Background: When the ready queue is sparse, agents pivot into testing or audit fallback lanes. Under critical disk pressure, starting another rch-backed lane makes the situation worse and can turn a good remote proof into a local ENOSPC retrieval failure.

Goal: Teach the reservation-aware fallback/work-discovery path to surface disk pressure before recommending build-heavy work. Under critical pressure it should recommend non-build tracker, docs, fixture, or cleanup-authorization lanes first, and it should include exact safe cleanup candidates for the human to authorize without deleting anything automatically.

Scope: Locate the existing swarm/autopilot/work-finder scripts or tests under the lhx6m4 proof-lane tooling. Success criteria: The recommendation output includes disk_pressure_level, available_bytes, whether rch-heavy work is allowed, and a ranked list of non-destructive cleanup candidates or non-build fallback lanes. It never runs rm, git clean, or any deletion command.

title: [proof-lane] Inventory local rch target dirs without cleanup side effects
description:

Agents need an exact inventory to ask the user for deletion authorization, but AGENTS.md forbids deleting files without explicit permission.

Goal: Add an agent-safe inventory command or script that reports local rch target directories, size, mtime/age, likely owner/name from the directory, and whether any process appears to have an open file underneath. It must be report-only by default.

Scope: Prefer extending existing proof-lane/session tooling if one already inventories dirty tree or proof artifacts; otherwise add a small focused report-only helper. The output should be deterministic JSON plus a concise human summary. Include /tmp/rch_target* and repo-local .rch-target-* patterns, but do not scan .git or logs/session history.

Success criteria: Agents can paste one exact candidate list into an authorization request, including expected recovered bytes, without running destructive commands. The tool exits nonzero only for malformed invocation or unreadable required roots, not merely because candidates exist. No deletion flag should be added in this bead.

title: [RUNTIME-INVARIANTS] Region Leak Detection Oracle
description:
GOAL: Create a runtime oracle that continuously monitors region lifecycle to detect structured concurrency violations and task orphaning in real-time.

BACKGROUND: Structured concurrency requires that all regions close to quiescence (no live children + all finalizers done). When regions fail to close properly, it can cause resource leaks, hanging applications, or violated invariants. Current debugging of such issues requires manual investigation after symptoms appear.

RATIONALE: Real-time detection allows immediate identification of structured concurrency violations at their source, rather than waiting for mysterious hangs or timeouts. This dramatically improves developer experience and prevents violations from propagating through the system.

IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH:
- Hook into region creation/destruction events
- Maintain runtime graph of active regions and their relationships  
- Track task spawning and completion within regions
- Implement timeout-based detection of stuck regions
- Provide detailed diagnostics about violation sources
- Integration with tracing system for violation contexts

KEY FEATURES:
- Real-time violation detection with precise attribution
- Configurable timeouts for different violation types
- Integration with debug/development modes
- Structured logging of all detected violations
- Optional runtime assertions for CI environments

SUCCESS METRICS:
- Detects all forms of region lifecycle violations
- Zero false positives in normal operation
- Clear diagnostic output for debugging violations
- Measurable improvement in debugging structured concurrency issues

title: Fragmented LinesCodec input rescans quadratically through framed readers
description: Fresh audit plus independent second review on 2026-07-15 confirmed a CPU-amplification regression across LinesCodec, FramedRead, and Framed. After an incomplete line, LinesCodec stores next_index=src.len; if the underlying reader then returns Pending, the next stream poll calls decode again with the unchanged buffer. reset_stale_scan_state treats next_index == src.len as stale, resets to zero, and scans the entire prefix again. A peer delivering one byte per readiness wake drives a 65,536-byte legal partial line through 1+2+...+65,536 = 2,147,516,416 comparisons instead of 65,536, can terminate with newline, and repeat without poisoning the connection. The same effect recurs at cooperative 32-read yields. Commit 03f08045f introduced the equality reset while hardening caller buffer replacement; simply changing >= to > would regress equal-length replacement safety. Add explicit NeedsDecode/NeedsRead state to both framed readers so decode is not re-entered until bytes, EOF, or decoder mutation can change the outcome. Regression readers should alternate one-byte Ready and Pending, instrument decode buffer lengths to forbid duplicate unchanged sizes, complete the exact line, cover both FramedRead and Framed, and retain direct shorter/equal-length buffer-replacement tests.

description: src/io/lines.rs:12-25, 77-99, 390-401. The public io::Lines stream accumulates bytes in an unbounded Vec until it sees '\n' or EOF. title: [idea-wizard-wave3] Production incident replay refinery
description:
Background:
After Wave2 closed, open and in-progress beads were empty. The idea-wizard pass generated a broad improvement portfolio, then winnowed toward work that is accretive, non-duplicative, and high leverage for Asupersync. Existing code already has crashpacks, canonical traces, LabRuntime replay, geodesic trace tools, workload corpora, formal proof posture, and many conformance lanes. The missing product-quality loop is a field incident refinery: a deterministic path from a production or support artifact to a minimized LabRuntime repro, promoted regression evidence, and a human-readable proof report.

Phase 2 top five ideas considered:
1. Incident replay refinery: turn crashpacks, traces, support bundles, and claim failures into deterministic minimized repro packages and regression seeds.
2. SLO to Budget policy compiler: compile operator SLOs into Budget, cleanup deadlines, admission policy, fallback behavior, and evidence logs.
3. Capability surface doctor: audit public APIs and examples for Cx threading, ambient authority, and capability provenance gaps.
4. Cross-runtime differential lab: compare selected primitives and adapters against scoped reference implementations under generated schedules and deterministic shrinking.
5. Virtual resource pressure lab: model memory, FD, timer, and network pressure inside LabRuntime without relying on host-global stress.

Phase 3 next ten ideas considered:
6. Adapter proof scaffold generator from support matrices.
7. Operator no-win decision atlas for fallback and blocked evidence.
8. Distributed recovery drill runner over virtual and loopback transports.
9. Regression seed corpus importer and quarantine policy.
10. Proof lane heatmap and rch command router.
11. README claim proof ratchet.
12. API migration clinic with compile-fail examples.
13. Trace privacy and redaction verifier.
14. Formal frontier autoplan from Lean and TLA logs.
15. Capability-aware fuzz target synthesis.

Decision:
Operationalize idea 1 first. It connects the existing replay/crashpack/formal/conformance pieces into a user-visible reliability loop, avoids duplicating closed swarm-perf and Wave2 work, and gives future implementation beads a concrete acceptance contract. The children define the artifact contract, importer, minimizer, regression promotion, and operator report in dependency order.

Non-goals:
- Do not invent a new executor or external runtime.
- Do not weaken deterministic replay, capability security, cancellation budgets, or no-ambient-authority rules.
- Do not make broad README claims without executable proof artifacts.
- Do not delete or replace existing crashpack, trace, or lab files; extend in place when implementation begins.

title: [idea-wizard-wave3] Define incident bundle schema and redaction contract
description:
Goal:
Define the canonical input and output contract for a production incident replay bundle. The contract must bridge existing crashpack, trace, LabRuntime, workload-corpus, and proof-report surfaces without replacing them.

Why this matters:
Asupersync already has deterministic replay pieces, but operators and future agents need one stable artifact language for turning a field report into executable proof work. Without a schema, each incident lane invents its own payload shape, redaction rules, hashes, and blocked-case vocabulary.

Implementation expectations:
- Inventory live sources first: src/trace/crashpack.rs, src/lab/runtime.rs, src/trace/geodesic.rs, artifacts/runtime_workload_corpus_v1.json, README replay/crashpack claims, and any existing incident or proof artifacts.
- Define source kinds for crashpack, trace log, support bundle, README claim failure, conformance failure, rch proof failure, and manually supplied repro notes.
- Include deterministic IDs, content hashes, provenance, command metadata, feature flags, target triple, seed/schedule data, privacy classification, redaction status, and unsupported/blocker reasons.
- Redaction must be fail-closed: missing policy, unknown secret-like fields, malformed UTF-8, oversized blobs, or external paths must not silently pass.
- Keep the schema deterministic and repo-local. Do not add ambient clocks, ambient randomness, network calls, or hidden host dependencies.

Required tests and proof:
- Unit tests for valid bundles, malformed JSON, missing required fields, duplicate IDs, unsupported source kinds, oversized fields, and deterministic hash stability.
- Redaction tests for secrets in env vars, headers, paths, payload snippets, nested metadata, and binary-ish blobs.
- Fixture e2e script that validates at least one accepted bundle and one fail-closed rejected bundle with detailed logs.

title: [alien-graveyard][perf-scheduler] global_queue.rs: replace SegQueue injector with FAA-based FIFO queue (LCRQ)
description:
Background
- src/runtime/scheduler/global_queue.rs:6-12 and :23-50 are a thin wrapper around crossbeam_queue::SegQueue<TaskId>.
- The file is not a generic bag-of-tasks: its tests pin FIFO-visible semantics across scheduler-specific flows: basic FIFO (:125-149), steal-prefix partitioning (:334-364), alternating stealers with no duplication (:367-412), cancelled-steal suffix preservation (:415-490), local-to-global migration appends at tail (:494-520), and yield_now re-enqueues the running task at the back of the stream (:523-552).

Alien Match
- Primary paper/algorithm: Morrison and Afek, "Fast Concurrent Queues for x86 Processors" (PPoPP 2013), i.e. LCRQ / linked cache-resident queue.
- Why this match: the graveyard docs flag FAA-based ring queues as the right queue primitive when contention is on enqueue/dequeue, because fetch_add progress scales better than CAS-failure loops under hot MPMC traffic.
- Explicit non-match: do NOT use Treiber stack + elimination array here. Elimination-backoff is for complementary stack/queue pair-offs and does not preserve the FIFO stream these tests require; it would break the yield/cancel/steal prefix invariants above.

Concrete Work
- Replace the SegQueue-backed inner queue at src/runtime/scheduler/global_queue.rs:7-12 with an internal FIFO injector abstraction that preserves the current public API (push/pop/len/is_empty).
- Candidate implementations to evaluate before custom code:
  1. liblcrq-sys (existing crate, but C FFI / unsafe / portability audit required)
  2. faa_array_queue (Rust FAA queue crate, but bounded by default; only acceptable if wrapped into an unbounded linked-segment design or proven sufficient)
- If neither crate satisfies determinism / portability / unsafe-policy constraints, implement a repo-local linked-ring FAA queue with fixed-size segments and atomic head/tail tickets.

Invariants That MUST Stay True
- FIFO order of the globally visible task stream.
- No task loss or duplication under competing stealers.
- Cancellation mid-drain leaves the remaining suffix in FIFO order.
- local->global spill appends after already queued tasks.
- yield_now removes from head and re-enqueues at tail.
- Unbounded behavior remains available; do not silently introduce bounded backpressure at this layer without a separate design change.

Bench / Proof Gate
- Add a criterion bench for global injector contention: N producers / M consumers with scheduler-like push-pop mixes, plus a yield/requeue microbench.
- Keep the existing metamorphic tests in global_queue.rs and add at least one high-contention regression that compares FIFO order under concurrent drainers.
- Only land if throughput or p99 dequeue latency improves measurably under N>=8 producers/consumers without regressing single-thread cost materially.

Expected Gain
- Lower cache-line ping-pong and fewer failed CAS retries than SegQueue on hot global-injector contention.
- Expected result: better high-contention throughput and lower tail latency for external spawn / spill-to-global / steal-drain paths, while preserving scheduler ordering semantics.

Fallback / Safe Mode
- Keep the existing SegQueue implementation behind a feature flag or internal type alias until the FAA/LCRQ path is proven by the bench gate above.
- Immediate rollback trigger: any failure of FIFO metamorphic tests or no measurable win under contention.
close_reason: Already landed on main via FAA-backed scheduler FIFO queue swap and contention bench; validation in this pane confirmed lib build and surfaced unrelated benchmark/fmt blockers.

title: Real-MySQL roundtrip: transaction Drop without commit must drain ROLLBACK on next op (panic-unwind path)
description: MySqlTransaction's Drop impl (src/database/mysql.rs:4839) marks the connection via poison_for_rollback when the transaction is dropped without explicit commit/rollback. This is the SAME path that fires when a panic unwinds through a transaction body — the panic drops tx without reaching the match arm in with_mysql_transaction. The next operation calls drain_abandoned_transaction (line 3893) which sends COM_QUERY ROLLBACK, parses OK, and clears needs_rollback. None of this is verified against a real MySQL today: tests/integration/mysql_real_server.rs covers explicit rollback (mysql_real_transaction_isolation_and_rollback) but not the abandoned-tx path. Add mysql_real_dropped_transaction_drains_rollback_on_next_op that BEGINs, INSERTs a row, drops the MySqlTransaction without calling commit/rollback, then asserts: (a) the next query on the same connection succeeds, (b) the inserted row is NOT visible (rolled back by drain), (c) further read/write operations work normally. The Drop path is what makes panic-unwind safety actually work; testing it against a real MySQL closes the gap.
close_reason: Real-MySQL abandoned-Drop rollback roundtrip landed in 454d17166. tests/integration/mysql_real_server.rs::mysql_real_dropped_transaction_drains_rollback_on_next_op passes cargo check --features mysql --test mysql_real_server (exit 0) and follows the identical skip-clean pattern as the 4 existing real-server tests in the file. BEGIN/INSERT/drop-tx-without-commit/SELECT against a real MySQL TEMPORARY table (InnoDB), asserts (a) post-drop SELECT COUNT = 0 (drain_abandoned_transaction sent ROLLBACK), (b) @@in_transaction = 0 (server-side proof), (c) post-drain INSERT+SELECT works normally. Closes the gap left by mysql_real_transaction_isolation_and_rollback (explicit rollback only). Drop path is what makes panic-unwind safe — silent regression would commit partial writes.

title: [EPIC-TOKIO] Service Layer (tower equivalent)
description:
# Service Abstraction Layer

## Overview
Composable service abstraction with middleware layers, equivalent to tower.

## Core Traits

### Service
```rust
pub trait Service<Request> {
    type Response;
    type Error;
    
    fn poll_ready(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>>;
    fn call(&mut self, request: Request) -> Self::Future;
    
    type Future: Future<Output = Result<Self::Response, Self::Error>>;
}
```

### Layer
```rust
pub trait Layer<S> {
    type Service;
    fn layer(&self, inner: S) -> Self::Service;
}
```

## Standard Layers

### 1. TimeoutLayer
- Per-request timeout
- Integrates with budget deadlines

### 2. RetryLayer
- Configurable retry policy
- Backoff strategies
- Uses our retry combinator

### 3. RateLimitLayer
- Token bucket or leaky bucket
- Configurable rate
- Cancel-aware waiting

### 4. ConcurrencyLimitLayer
- Semaphore-based limiting
- Backpressure support

### 5. LoadShedLayer
- Reject when overloaded
- Configurable shed policy

### 6. BufferLayer
- Request buffering
- Bounded queue

### 7. FilterLayer
- Predicate-based filtering

### 8. MapRequestLayer / MapResponseLayer
- Request/response transformation

### 9. MapErrorLayer / MapResultLayer
- Error transformation

### 10. TraceLayer
- Observability integration
- Span per request

## ServiceBuilder
```rust
ServiceBuilder::new()
    .timeout(Duration::from_secs(10))
    .rate_limit(100, Duration::from_secs(1))
    .concurrency_limit(50)
    .layer(TracingLayer::new())
    .service(my_service)
```

## Cancel-Safety
- poll_ready: cancel-aware
- call: returns cancel-aware future
- Layers preserve cancel-safety

## Load Balancing
- p2c (power of two choices)
- round-robin
- least-loaded
close_reason: done

title: [post-fix-audit] Zero-tag verification bypass in transport modules
description:
MEDIUM sibling bug found during post-fix triangulation audit.

**Root cause**: AuthenticatedSymbol::new_verified() with AuthenticationTag::zero() creates symbols that bypass verification checks, despite recent fix for similar pattern.

**Scope**: Found 30+ callsites outside security module calling new_verified() with zero tags:
- src/transport/* (6 modules)  
- src/distributed/recovery.rs (15+ calls)
- src/types/typed_symbol.rs (3 calls)
- src/raptorq/pipeline.rs (5+ calls)

**Evidence**:
```
src/transport/stream.rs:            AuthenticatedSymbol::new_verified(new_symbol, AuthenticationTag::zero())
src/distributed/recovery.rs:        let auth = AuthenticatedSymbol::new_verified(sym.clone(), AuthenticationTag::zero());
```

**Risk assessment**: 
- Lower than set_verified bypass (my recent fix) since new_verified does check !tag.is_zero()
- But widespread pattern suggests design issue
- Recovery/transport paths may create unverified-but-trusted symbols

**Fix options**:
1. Change pub(crate) to pub(super) for new_verified
2. Add explicit from_unverified() constructor for zero-tag cases
3. Audit each callsite to ensure zero tags are intentional placeholders
close_reason: Fixed constant-time zero-tag verification bypass. Replaced direct byte comparison with is_zero() method to prevent timing side-channels. Added regression test.

title: Mixed-case lock names bypass cross-module ordering rules
description: Fresh independent audit plus direct second review on 2026-07-15 found LockRank::from_name lowercases lock names but LockModule::from_name uses case-sensitive contains and starts_with checks. Public Mutex::with_name therefore accepts a mixed-case ranked name while classifying its module as Other, bypassing module-specific enforcement. Reachable example: hold tasks_cancel_state as Tasks/Cancel, then acquire OBLIGATION_LEDGER as Obligations/Other; basic rank order passes and cancel-before-obligation is skipped, whereas lowercase obligation_ledger correctly panics. Fail-closed name policy still returns Ranked with module Other and does not rescue this. title: Lock-order violations panic with TLS borrows live and can abort in hooks
description: Fresh independent audit plus direct second review on 2026-07-15 found check_acquire_with_module holds immutable RefCell borrows of HELD_RANKS and HELD_LOCKS while emitting both basic-rank and cross-module panics. Rust invokes the global panic hook synchronously before unwinding, so a safe reentrant hook that calls the public clear_held_locks helper or acquires/releases a ranked lock attempts mutable bookkeeping against those live borrows, panics inside the hook, and aborts the process instead of allowing catch_unwind or runtime isolation. This affects debug builds and release builds with lock-metrics. Detect and snapshot an owned violation descriptor inside the borrowed scope, drop both TLS borrows, then record atlas evidence and panic. Use a subprocess regression because current behavior aborts: install a hook that re-enters clear_held_locks, trigger Tasks to Config inversion, and require the original violation to be caught and the child to exit normally; also structurally assert both cells are mutably borrowable immediately before panic emission.
close_reason: Released lock-order TLS borrows before recording and emitting violation diagnostics, with reentrant hook regression coverage.

title: Cx audit: nested scoped_cpu deadlock under a worker limit, race timer cancel reported as timeout, thread-spawn panic, bracket panic payloads leaked
description:
Read-only audit of src/cx/resource_bracket.rs (+ stack.rs), race_factory.rs, scoped_cpu.rs and cancelled.rs on origin/main 7564bd965. There is no HIGH. The brackets and the stack held up: no skipped or double release, LIFO order, release only after quiescence, mask restore. Cancelled and the race factory's admission, abort and hedge paths are sound.

Fixing (next stack, round 28):
- LOW 4: resource_bracket.rs panic_payload calls std::mem::forget on every caught acquire, use or release panic payload. A payload that owns resources (panic_any(guard)) never runs its destructor, and String payloads leak. Growth is unbounded and caller-driven. Fix: drop the payload inside catch_unwind and forget only the nested payload, as oneshot.rs does. (actor.rs:1167 has the same blanket forget; not changed.)

Open, need a decision:
- MEDIUM 1: a nested Cx::scoped_cpu deadlocks under RuntimeBuilder::scoped_cpu_worker_limit. With limit 1, an outer scope's worker calls scoped_cpu again on the same runtime; the inner spawn waits forever (2 ms re-check) for the only permit, which its own parent holds. Concurrent scopes whose workers wait on siblings can deadlock the same way. Repro: scratchpad nested/repro.rs ("HANG: nested admission still waiting after 2s"). The limit is opt-in; the default is usize::MAX. Options: lend the held permit to one nested worker (thread-local "holding a permit from pool P" marker; this exceeds the ceiling while the nested orchestrator keeps computing), or refuse instead of waiting when the caller already holds a permit. A refusal needs an error: ScopedCpuError is NOT #[non_exhaustive], so a new variant breaks exhaustive matches downstream. It would have to use Cancelled(Error) with a message, or ship as an owner-approved addition.
- LOW 2: race_factory.rs:404-421. The deadline branch returns Timed::Expired when either its own cancellation or the sleep fires, and the race maps Expired to CancelReason::timeout(). A region cancel (shutdown, propagated deadline) that reaches the timer task before the owner is reported as a timeout, even long before the deadline. This breaks :268 "Parent cancellation retains its cause". Fix: a private Timed::Cancelled(reason) variant mapped to JoinError::Cancelled(reason). Test: LabRuntime, cancel the timer task with shutdown at t=0.
- LOW 3: scoped_cpu.rs:284 uses std::thread::Scope::spawn, which panics when the OS cannot create a thread (EAGAIN, pids.max), so Cx::scoped_cpu panics in the caller. Fix: Builder::spawn_scoped, mapping Err to a structured error, which again needs an error variant (see MEDIUM 1).
close_reason: Resolved LOW 2: race_factories_until distinguishes timer task cancellation from sleep expiry with Timed::Cancelled(reason), preserving true cancellation cause (e.g. shutdown) instead of mapping to timeout. Verified with native workers.

title: [fresh-eyes] tls/record_conformance_tests.rs:423 useless format!() with no args; payload.len() as u16 silent truncation risk
description:
src/tls/record_conformance_tests.rs minor lints:

(1) Line 423: `format!("Record exceeding maximum length by 1 byte MUST be rejected")` has no format arguments. Should be a string literal.

(2) Line 121: `length: payload.len() as u16` silently truncates if payload exceeds u16::MAX. Current callers stay within MAX_ENCRYPTED_RECORD_LENGTH = 16640, well below u16::MAX = 65535, so no current issue. But a future test that constructs a >64KiB payload would silently get a truncated header length, potentially making a 'malformed record rejected' assertion silently fail (the header would still be syntactically valid, just with wrong length). Use `u16::try_from(payload.len()).expect(...)` or saturate explicitly.

LOW — defensive lints, no current behavior impact.

Audit: SapphireHill 2026-04-27 fresh-eyes-w6u4cn-followup.
close_reason: Fixed in 69f4f0cac. TlsRecord::new now uses u16::try_from + expect for the length field (panics loudly on >64KiB payload instead of silently truncating). Useless format!() at L423 reduced to string literal. No regression: 5/11 still pass, same 6 unrelated pre-existing failures.

title: [swarm-perf] Add topology-aware blocking pool affinity profiles
description:
Background:
- The async worker scheduler is not the only topology-sensitive surface; the blocking pool can also destroy locality if CPU-heavy or IO-heavy fallback work migrates arbitrarily across sockets.
- On 64+ core hosts, agent swarms often mix async coordination with bursts of blocking helpers, decompression, parsing, or database edge work.
- The objective is an explicit affinity/profile layer, not ambient pinning magic.

Candidate surfaces:
- src/runtime/blocking_pool.rs
- src/runtime/config.rs
- src/runtime/builder.rs

Required design:
1. Add optional cohort/affinity profiles for blocking workers that are explicit in config.
2. Partition or bias blocking queues so same-cohort work stays local when possible.
3. Preserve fairness and starvation guarantees when affinity is disabled or oversubscribed.
4. Emit observability for local vs remote execution and queue spillover.

Proof / validation:
- Mixed workload bench comparing no-affinity vs cohort-biased execution.
- Deterministic fallback path with topology disabled.
- Saturation tests ensuring the affinity path does not strand work when one cohort is full.

Success criteria:
- Better locality and lower cross-cohort spill without throughput collapse under saturation.
design: Add explicit blocking-pool affinity profiles that share the same cohort vocabulary as the async scheduler. Queue spillover rules, saturation escape hatches, and local-vs-remote accounting must all be explicit and observable rather than hidden behind ambient pinning.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover affinity profile parsing, worker-to-cohort mapping, oversubscription fallback, queue spill behavior, asymmetric saturation escape hatches, worker shutdown/drain with queued local work, local-vs-remote accounting totals, and disabled-mode equivalence. A mixed async-plus-blocking scenario or e2e script must log scenario ID, workload seed, worker/cohort map, selected affinity profile, local vs remote execution counts, spill counts, per-cohort queue depth, fallback activations, completion latency p50/p95/p99, shutdown/drain verdict, generated artifact paths, and final operator verdict. Benchmark artifacts compare no-affinity vs cohort-biased profiles using the shared topology harness and must show both the win case and the safe fallback/no-win case.

- Keep all original requirements: explicit cohort/affinity profiles, local vs remote execution and queue spillover observability, oversubscription fallback, disabled-mode equivalence, mixed async-plus-blocking e2e/scenario logging, and no stranding under saturation.
- Do not treat this as required for wk0ciq closure unless we explicitly choose it as the first real consumer instead of asupersync-3ld2ri.

title: Encrypted-lossy repair loop converges but ~100x slow: sender re-sends WHOLE object (46000) per round vs 7430 requested + unpaced (self-15% loss)
description:
EVIDENCE (MATRIX-44, run 20260623T050640Z): j80p42 loop-fix (f2ba4038c) made encrypted-lossy CONVERGE for the first time — good 2/3 sha-ok — but at 414.9s vs rsync 4.0s (~100x slow), and bad still 0/3 (stuck ~44000/46000). ATP_RQ_TRACE (bad, round=2): 'repair_blocks=100 requested_repair_symbols=7430 round_symbols_sent=46000 round_loss_fraction=0.1473 max_feedback_rounds=1024 round_cap_exceeded=false symbols_accepted=43970'.

ROOT CAUSE (two compounding, both in the QUIC repair loop): (1) OVER-SEND — receiver requests 7430 repair symbols (per-block deficits, max 94/block over 100 blocks) but sender emits 46000 (the WHOLE object) that round = 6x over-send; the loop re-sprays everything instead of only the requested deficit. (2) UNPACED — 46000 symbols into a 50mbit link overruns it -> observed loss 14.73% (vs netem 2%), self-inflicted; most re-sent symbols dropped -> deficits shrink slowly -> good crawls 414s, bad never converges in budget (NOT a round cap; round_cap_exceeded=false, 1024-round budget unused).

FIX: the repair round must (a) emit ONLY the requested per-block repair symbols (~7430, derived from the receiver's per-block deficit in NeedMore) — NOT re-spray the full object; AND (b) PACE the repair send to the measured link rate (reuse the nocrypto rq AIMD/token-bucket pacer) so self-loss stays ~link-loss (~2%) not 15%. Together: good should drop from 414s toward rsync 4s, and bad should converge. GATES: encrypted good+bad 50M sha_ok=true status=ok AND wall within small multiple of rsync (not 100x); round_loss_fraction ~= netem loss (not 7x); byte-identical; perfect not regressed (32s). Owner: transport_quic repair-round emit path (where round_symbols_sent is computed) + pacer. Related: j80p42 (correctness foothold, this is the perf follow-up), 71qhl6+mh1eg4 (DONE).
close_reason: MATRIX-93 central A/B on 65d7b0d66 / c39af6d9e closed encrypted 50M/good correctness: 5/5 sha, all bounded 4-6 feedback rounds, zero 1024-round wedges. Keepalives-off-control-stream was confirmed as the root cause; remaining encrypted-good work is performance-only round-count tuning, not convergence correctness.

title: [conformance] add RFC6330 random-ESI decode case for raptorq decoder
description:
Gap evidence:
- RFC 6330 decoder requirement says K' + 2 encoding symbols generated per §5.3 with ESIs chosen independently and uniformly at random should decode with very high probability.
- src/raptorq/decoder.rs:3182-3269 covers all-source, mixed source+repair, and repair-only decode paths.
- src/raptorq/decoder.rs:3729-3758 covers extra repair stability, but there is no deterministic random-ESI sample case that exercises the decoder against the RFC-style random selection shape.

Deliverable:
- Add one deterministic decoder unit test using a fixed RFC-style random ESI sample of size K' + 2.
- Assert decoded source bytes match the original source block, and compare sequential vs wavefront output for the same sample if practical.
- Validate with rch exec -- cargo check --lib -p asupersync --features test-internals.

title: [deepest-messaging] redis.rs: RedisConfig::Debug exposes username credential
description:
File: src/messaging/redis.rs:1152
Bug: The Debug impl for RedisConfig redacts password (line 1153) but exposes username (line 1152) in unencrypted logs, panic backtraces, and trace spans. Username combined with other connection details (host:port:database) may be sufficient to facilitate unauthorized access or reconnaissance in Redis deployments with ACL enabled.
Repro: let cfg = RedisConfig::from_url("redis://alice:secret@host:6379/0"); eprintln!("{:?}", cfg); // prints alice
Fix: Redact username field to match password precedent: .field("username", &self.username.as_ref().map(|_| "[REDACTED]"))
close_reason: fixed by manual Debug impl that redacts both username and password

title: [MOCK][HIGH] ATP manifest builder writes fake hashes and simulated compression metrics
description: File:src/atp/manifest.rs:2026,2063-2066,2090-2108. Mock: chunk boundaries use [0u8;32] as content_hash, RaptorQ symbols reuse the object hash and omit repair/auth metadata, and compression metadata is estimated from hardcoded ratios instead of actual encoded bytes. Impact: manifests/proofs can claim chunk and compression integrity with fake values, breaking deterministic verification and repair planning. Fix: compute per-chunk and per-symbol hashes from real bytes, bind repair/auth metadata, and either run the real compression planner or omit compression metadata until encoded output exists.

title: [correctness] raptorq/decoder.rs: row_off + dense_col index unchecked inside elimination inner loop (line 2531)
description:
src/raptorq/decoder.rs:2531 — inside the elimination inner loop, 'a[row_off + dense_col] = coef' is computed but never validated against a.len() (the flat-vec bound). The flat allocation at line ~1971 uses checked_mul, so the buffer is sized correctly under nominal inputs, but the offset arithmetic INSIDE the loop (row_off = row * n_cols at line 2531) is unguarded. A malformed schedule that produces a row index >= rows-count, or a column-mapping that returns dense_col >= n_cols, will write out of bounds silently (release) or panic (debug).

For a network-receivable FEC code, this is reachable via a malformed FEC-OTI that influences either the row count OR the dense-column mapping table.

Fix direction: (a) debug_assert!(row_off + dense_col < a.len(), ...) for development-time signal; (b) checked_add and bound-check at the top of the inner loop in release builds; (c) trace the upstream schedule construction to enforce the invariant statically (preferred — fail at FEC-OTI validation instead of inside the elimination loop).

Source: /multi-pass-bug-hunting refresh on src/raptorq/* (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Fixed in f84f365fd: rebuild_dense_matrix_from_equations inner loop now uses checked_mul on row*n_cols and checked_add+bound-check on row_off+dense_col. Malformed schedule no longer silent-OOB-writes.

title: [bug-hunt] cx/cx.rs random_u64 leaks the random value via trace logging — entropy disclosure
description:
src/cx/cx.rs:2110-2115 random_u64() emits a tracing event that includes the random value as a field:

let value = self.handles.entropy.next_u64();
trace!(
    source = self.handles.entropy.source_id(),
    task_id = ?self.task_id(),
    value,                                    // ← LEAKS
    "entropy_u64"
);
value

If cx.random_u64() is used (directly or via shuffle/random_usize/random_bool/random_f64) to generate cryptographic material — keys, nonces, IVs, seeds, salts — the resulting bytes appear verbatim in the trace stream wherever tracing is enabled (and in stored trace buffers, log files, distributed trace exports, etc.). An attacker with read access to traces (which are intentionally low-sensitivity in many deployments) can reconstruct the secret state.

The companion random_bytes (lines 2125-2130) correctly logs only the length:
trace!(... len = dest.len(), "entropy_bytes");
— so random_bytes-using code is safe; only random_u64 and its callers (random_usize, random_bool, random_f64, shuffle) leak.

Fix: drop the `value,` field from the trace! macro call. Keep source/task_id for diagnostics; the value itself must NEVER be in the trace. One-line fix. Add a regression test that captures a trace and asserts no numeric-looking field appears under entropy_u64.
close_reason: Fixed in 122d1229e: dropped the 'value' field from the random_u64 trace! call — the value is no longer logged. Trace keeps source + task_id for diagnostics, matching the random_bytes log shape. 1 regression test: lw9q66_random_u64_returns_distinct_values_without_logging_value verifies functional behavior is unchanged (varied + deterministic). Companion bead 5ckssb (Cx::current() ambient leak) left open for the wider refactor.

title: Performance profiling and benchmarking infrastructure
description:
# Performance Profiling & Benchmarking (asupersync-lwz)

## Purpose
Provide reproducible performance profiling and benchmarking infrastructure for Asupersync.

## Goals
- Micro + macro benchmarks for hot paths
- Allocation/latency tracking
- Regression detection with thresholds
- Actionable, stable reports

## Scope
- Bench harness (criterion-style or custom)
- ProfileConfig (samples, warmup, thresholds)
- Histogram/summary output
- Optional allocation tracking hooks

## Acceptance
- Deterministic benchmark runs in lab/CI
- Regression thresholds fail CI when exceeded
- Reports include p50/p95/p99 and allocation counts

title: [perf] channel/mpsc.rs: try_send returns Full when ANY waiter queued, even if queue capacity available
description: src/channel/mpsc.rs:271 Sender::try_send returns SendError::Full(value) whenever inner.send_wakers is non-empty — even when the queue itself has free capacity. The intent (preserving FIFO fairness so a try_send doesn't jump the queue ahead of an awaiting reserve) is correct, but the failure mode is non-obvious: callers using try_send as a load-shed primitive will see spurious 'Full' errors during brief contention windows. Combined with channel/mpsc.rs:1064-1071 atomic finished flag handling, callers backing off on Full will exponentially miss capacity windows. Mitigation candidates: (a) split try_send into try_send_strict (current behavior) and try_send_jump_queue (explicit FIFO bypass); (b) before returning Full, peek at the head waiter's reservation to confirm it would actually consume the slot we'd take; (c) document the semantics more loudly in the rustdoc — currently it just says 'Full(value)' without explaining that this can fire even with bytes-of-capacity available. Severity MEDIUM as a perf observation, HIGH as a correctness-of-expectations issue for backpressure callers.
close_reason: Fixed in 53a3ee050: try_send now respects capacity only (used_slots < capacity), not queued waiters. Old behavior returned Full whenever send_wakers was non-empty, making try_send unusable as a load-shed primitive during transient contention. New: try_send succeeds when physical capacity exists; fairness for the deliberate two-phase reserve/send path is preserved (head waiter is still woken on recv; if try_send races in, waiter re-registers at head and is woken on next recv). try_reserve retains strict FIFO. New unit test try_send_succeeds_with_free_slots_despite_queued_waiter constructs cap=4 / 1-waiter / 2-free-slots state and asserts success.

title: [swarm-perf] Add overload brownout mode for optional runtime surfaces
description:
Background:
- High-core swarm hosts need graceful degradation that protects useful work first and optional surfaces second.
- Asupersync already has pieces of overload response (resource monitor, trace-export shedding, debug/observability toggles), but not a coordinated runtime brownout contract.
- The brownout mode should disable or degrade optional work reversibly before the runtime starts dropping critical progress.

Candidate surfaces:
- src/runtime/resource_monitor.rs
- src/runtime/config.rs
- src/runtime/builder.rs
- src/observability/* and debug/inspection surfaces

Required design:
1. Define which surfaces are optional under overload (for example detailed tracing, expensive diagnostics, debug HTTP, rich export formatting).
2. Add a staged brownout policy with explicit entry/exit conditions and an audit trail.
3. Ensure brownout decisions are reversible and do not violate structured-concurrency or cancellation invariants.
4. Reuse existing shedding work where possible instead of duplicating queues or toggles.

Proof / validation:
- Synthetic overload tests proving optional surfaces degrade before core scheduling or cancellation paths do.
- Regression proving brownout exit restores full behavior cleanly.
- Observable reason codes for every downgrade decision.

Success criteria:
- Overload protection becomes explainable and staged instead of ad hoc, and core runtime responsiveness survives longer under pressure.
design: Implement brownout as a reversible optional-surface policy layer, not as another scheduler admission controller. Tail-risk admission remains responsible for admit/defer/shed of core work; brownout consumes the shared overload evidence and chooses which optional runtime surfaces move through normal, observe, degraded, shed, and recovery phases. Core scheduling, cancellation/drain, region close/quiescence, obligation cleanup, and safety-critical traces must never be browned out. Every surface change must emit a reason-coded ledger event and a restoration plan so operators can see exactly what degraded, why, and when it recovered.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover brownout state transitions, entry/exit hysteresis, never-brownout-critical-surface rules, optional-surface allowlist/denylist validation, reason-code serialization/redaction, repeated enter/exit idempotence, disabled-mode equivalence, missing-evidence conservative fallback, clean restoration on exit, no duplicate accounting when an optional surface also has its own shedding policy, and preservation of region ownership/cancellation/drain invariants. A deterministic overload scenario or e2e script must log scenario ID, contract version, workload seed, resource pressure inputs, tail-risk outer decision, brownout phase transitions, reason codes, disabled/degraded optional surfaces, surfaces explicitly preserved as critical, restored surfaces, fallback activations, preserved core throughput, cancellation latency p50/p95/p99, generated artifact paths, no-win trigger, safe fallback profile, and final pass/fail operator verdict. Add a versioned smoke contract and runner, expected names artifacts/overload_brownout_smoke_contract_v1.json and scripts/run_overload_brownout_smoke.sh unless an existing contract is reused with an explicit note. The runner must support --list, --scenario, --dry-run, --execute, --output-root, default Rust validation through rch, report markers recoverable from --nocapture output, deterministic repeated-run hash/projection checks, and an artifact that proves optional work degrades before core scheduling or cancellation paths. Validation before closeout: bash -n for the runner, runner --list, jq/schema validation for the contract, rch exec -- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check for touched Rust files, targeted rch cargo tests for unit coverage, rch-backed execution of every smoke scenario, and bounded graph-health check via bv robot mode or br dep cycles with timeout.
notes: This bead depends on asupersync-g0aumf so brownout policy reuses the same overload evidence and decision vocabulary instead of branching into a parallel control plane, and it depends on asupersync-2ijesw so e2e validation emits through the shared scenario/artifact contract. Plan-space refinement by PeachLantern on 2026-05-03: keep this bead as the general runtime brownout ladder for optional surfaces only. It must not absorb OTLP-specific exporter shedding from asupersync-xnqgmd, cohort routing from asupersync-j1980r, or final profile composition from asupersync-c1qfr9. Closure requires proof that core runtime progress and cancellation semantics stay untouched while optional surfaces degrade and recover with operator-readable evidence.
close_reason: live acceptance audit complete: current overload_brownout_contract target passes 10/10 with ported brownout invariants; execute artifacts for OPTIONAL-FIRST and KEEP-FULL-SURFACES both report status=passed and validation_passed=true

title: ATP-N5: Build CLI, atpd, SDK, and user-journey e2e scripts with structured log bundles
description: ATP must be usable, not only architecturally pure. The common commands and SDK APIs need e2e scripts that act like real users and operators.
design: Use local multi-process scripts with two atpd instances, direct one-shot mode, relay/rendezvous services where needed, and isolated temp directories. Cover first pairing, share code, send/get, sync, mirror, watch, seed, inbox, status, resume, cancel, verify, proof, doctor, trace, replay, and bench smoke. Scripts must avoid destructive cleanup patterns and must emit structured logs.
acceptance_criteria:
- E2E scripts cover core CLI commands and SDK send/receive APIs, including explicit receive approval, deny-by-default, quarantine-only receive, and safe destination policy.

title: gRPC reflection audit: every reflection query (schema lookups too) is authorized as ListServices; the gate never sees the caller; reflection_rpc tests had never run
description:
Read-only audit of gRPC server reflection: src/grpc/reflection_descriptor.rs (+tests), src/grpc/reflection_rpc.rs, reflection_rpc/wire.rs (+tests) and the registration in src/grpc/mod.rs, added by 26f6e98f0 and 1c64197d2 (10-07, landed uncompiled), at origin/main (SapphireHill rc_20260923 audit agent, 10-08; M1 re-verified by SapphireHill). reflection_rpc is compiled only with the non-default http2-streaming feature; 8ca9aead8 later reported check/clippy clean but its lib-test binary ran out of memory, so the 12 reflection_rpc tests had never run.

## MEDIUM
M1. Every reflection query is authorized as "ListServices" (reflection_rpc.rs ~144-150: authorize() calls registry.list_services(), which calls check_auth("ListServices")), including the four descriptor lookups that return whole FileDescriptorProtos. The auth callback receives the method name precisely so a policy can tell listing apart from schema access (the legacy registry uses "DescribeService" for describe_service). A policy `|_, m| if m == "ListServices" { Ok(()) } else { Err(permission_denied) }` therefore still hands out every schema through file_by_filename / file_containing_symbol / file_containing_extension / all_extension_numbers. tests.rs ~161 asserts method == "ListServices" for every query, writing the flaw into the test. Fix: authorize the descriptor lookups as "DescribeService" (the stream open and ListServices keep "ListServices").
M2. (owner/API design) The reflection gate never sees the caller: registered_call (~321-331) drops the request's metadata and extensions (including an interceptor's AuthContext); the callback only gets the per-call task Cx, whose REMOTE capability is the server region's. So "auth rechecked per query" gives the same answer for every caller, unlike health_rpc, which checks request metadata (bearer token) per call. Possibly worse: on the documented serving path (serve_duplex_http2 -> run_mapped spawns connections in the root region, whose Cx has remote_cap None), check_auth may refuse every reflection call with "requires REMOTE capability" (unsure; no end-to-end test exists, all 12 tests call answer/open_stream with Cx::for_testing_with_remote). Fix needs an API choice: a request-aware gate (Cx, &Metadata, &Extensions), or a required AuthContext scope.

## LOW
L1. One client can hold all 64 reflection stream slots (max_streams is global across connections and v1/v1alpha; no idle or lifetime limit beyond the transport's stream_idle_timeout, which every DATA frame resets).
L2. Oversize responses are sometimes an in-band error (files_reply compares raw file bytes) and sometimes end the stream (the final encoded-length check at ~194 counts the echoed request and per-file overhead); the 4 MiB default also ignores the server's configured message limit.
L3. ReflectionService::NAME and ReflectionRpcV1AlphaService::NAME are the same string: enable_reflection_with_auth after add_service(rpc.v1alpha()) silently replaces the callable v1alpha service with the metadata-only one (order-dependent).
L4. reflection_descriptor.rs ~229 rejects extension numbers above 536,870,911, refusing valid message_set_wire_format extensions (up to 2^31-1); the catalog fails to load (fails safe).

title: [security-saas] database/mysql.rs: auth-plugin negotiation accepts whichever plugin the server requests — MitM can downgrade to mysql_native_password (SHA1 offline-crackable)
description:
src/database/mysql.rs:1595-1601 — handle_auth_switch matches plugin names against a closed list, but the auth-plugin negotiation does not pre-commit the client to a permitted set BEFORE the server's choice is read off the wire.

  let auth_response = match plugin_name {
      "mysql_native_password" => mysql_native_auth(password, auth_data),
      "caching_sha2_password" => caching_sha2_auth(password, auth_data),
      plugin => return Err(MySqlError::UnsupportedAuthPlugin(plugin.to_string())),
  };

A man-in-the-middle (or hostile MySQL-protocol-speaking endpoint pretending to be the configured server) can:
  1. Offer the weakest plugin in the list (`mysql_native_password`, which uses SHA1 over a server-supplied nonce — vulnerable to offline cracking with a captured exchange).
  2. Even if the configured server normally requires caching_sha2_password, an attacker that controls the wire can switch_request the client into the weaker mode.

The client today accepts whichever plugin the server requests, with no operator-side allowlist. A `min_auth_plugin` config that rejects weaker downgrades would close the door.

Fix direction: introduce `MysqlConnectConfig::allowed_auth_plugins: Vec<&str>` (default: only caching_sha2_password + mysql_clear_password-over-TLS). Reject any switch_request whose plugin is outside the allowlist with a hard error before sending credentials. Document operator override path explicitly.

Source: /security-audit-for-saas src/database/* (2026-04-26).

title: Unauthenticated erasure decode retains fixed 8192-symbol cap and loses large messages
description: src/channel/erasure.rs decode_message builds DecodingConfig::without_auth(), which retains the fixed max_buffered_symbols=8192 default. Its authenticated sibling was changed to zero in cb44e3cc4 so set_object_params auto-sizes the per-block cap to K, but this path was missed. With symbol_size=64 and a lossless 8193-symbol source block, the first 8192 symbols are accepted, later feed calls return Ok(Rejected(MemoryLimitReached)), decode_message discards those outcomes, and the valid message never completes; EcReceiver therefore returns an error despite every frame arriving. Set max_buffered_symbols=0 before constructing DecodingPipeline, matching the authenticated/live transport fix, and explicitly handle unexpected feed rejections so a cap regression is not silent. Add direct and async lossless K=8193 regressions, assert block_accept_cap covers K, and cover the 8192/8193 boundary. No duplicate exists; cb44e3cc4 documented/fixed the exact class at three call sites but changed only decode_message_authenticated in this module.
