title: Task inspector: detailed task state, await points, and waker info
description:
# Task Inspector

## Overview
Deep-dive diagnostic view for individual tasks, showing detailed state, await points,
waker information, and execution history.

## Design

### Task Details View
```rust
pub struct TaskInspector {
    state: Arc<RuntimeState>,
    console: Console,
}

impl TaskInspector {
    /// Inspect a specific task.
    pub fn inspect(&self, task_id: TaskId) -> TaskDetails {
        let task = self.state.get_task(task_id);
        
        TaskDetails {
            id: task_id,
            state: task.state(),
            region: task.region_id(),
            spawn_location: task.spawn_location(),
            last_poll_time: task.last_poll_time(),
            poll_count: task.poll_count(),
            await_point: task.current_await_point(),
            waker_info: task.waker_info(),
            budget_consumed: task.budget_consumed(),
        }
    }
    
    /// List all tasks with summary info.
    pub fn list_tasks(&self) -> Vec<TaskSummary> {
        self.state.all_tasks()
            .map(|t| TaskSummary {
                id: t.id(),
                name: t.name(),
                state: t.state(),
                region: t.region_id(),
            })
            .collect()
    }
}
```

### Output Format
```
Task Inspector: TaskId(42)
╭────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ State:         Polling                         │
│ Region:        Region-2 (HttpHandler)          │
│ Spawned at:    src/http/handler.rs:142         │
│ Last poll:     2.3ms ago                       │
│ Poll count:    17                              │
│ Budget used:   1,234 ops                       │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Current Await Point:                           │
│   -> TcpStream::read() at src/net/tcp.rs:89    │
│   -> IoDriver::poll_ready()                    │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Waker Info:                                    │
│   Type: WorkStealingWaker                      │
│   Registered: yes                              │
│   Wake count: 3                                │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

### Interactive Features (TUI)
- Navigate task list with keyboard
- Click to inspect task
- Filter by state (pending, polling, completed)
- Sort by poll count, age, budget

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] TUI navigation

### Integration Tests

title: ATP-E3-F4: Emit explainable autotune receipts for status, preflight, and proof consumers
description:
## Background
Several downstream beads need to explain ATP decisions: `atp status --explain`, transfer preflight, resource governance, repair policy, and proof bundles. ATP-E3 should provide a compact decision receipt so those surfaces do not re-interpret raw metrics differently.

## Work
Define and implement an autotune decision receipt schema with stable JSON fields and concise human rendering. The receipt should summarize inputs, omitted/stale sources, bottleneck classification, knob decisions, bounded deltas, confidence/caveats, and replay/proof pointers. It should be generated at the policy seam and consumed by status/preflight/proof code rather than duplicated downstream.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Receipt schema is versioned, deterministic, redaction-safe, and covered by roundtrip/golden tests.
- Human text is terse and stable enough for CLI/status output; JSON carries full structured detail.
- Receipts distinguish pass/degraded/no-win/blocked/malformed/stale-evidence outcomes instead of flattening them into success/failure.
- Downstream consumers can ingest receipts without depending on private autotune internals.
- Tests cover missing sources, contradictory sources, bounded knob deltas, redaction, and malformed receipt rejection.

title: OnceCell wake fanout must survive callback panics and initializer unwind

Scope: src/sync/once_cell.rs only; preserve public signatures, versions, first-panic propagation outside an existing unwind, and retry-after-cancellation semantics. title: postgres deadline path: EOF beats cancellation — region_budget_reaches_pg_statement_timeout_and_deadline_cancels_cleanly returns Err(UnexpectedEof) instead of Cancelled
close_reason: Fixed in ad5fa328d: scripted PG backend stayed connected so the budget deadline, not an early EOF, resolves the handler. Verified 1 passed in 3.00s == REQUEST_BUDGET. Runtime precedence hole spun out as asupersync-xwanb4.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FOUND 2026-07-26 by SapphireHill (session b8fa8e96) while triaging a failing lane from a concurrent session working br-asupersync-9mvlue.

SYMPTOM:
  test region_budget_reaches_pg_statement_timeout_and_deadline_cancels_cleanly ... FAILED
  panicked at tests/e2e_deadline_db_wire_cancel_showcase.rs:245:18:
  expected Cancelled handler outcome, got Err(Io(Custom { kind: UnexpectedEof, error: "unexpected end of stream" }))
  test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed. (remote worker vmi1227854, exit 101)

Run under `cargo test --features postgres,test-internals --test e2e_deadline_db_wire_cancel_showcase`.

WHAT IT MEANS: the test asserts that a request-budget deadline cancels the handler, so the handler's terminal outcome should be Outcome::Cancelled. Instead the handler surfaced a TRANSPORT ERROR. The connection teardown/EOF propagated to the caller before deadline cancellation resolved, so the error path won the race and the cancel path never produced its outcome.

WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC. This is precisely the invariant the project sells: "Cancellation is a protocol (request -> drain -> finalize), not a silent drop", and Outcome distinguishes Err from Cancelled specifically so that a cancelled operation is never misreported as a failure. Here a deadline-cancelled DB request is observably indistinguishable from a broken connection. A caller doing the documented thing — matching on Outcome::Cancelled to implement retry/attribution policy — gets the wrong branch, and the HTTP mapping in README (Cancelled -> 499, Err -> 5xx) would report a client-deadline cancellation as a server error.

RULED OUT — THIS IS NOT THE never_loop REFACTOR IN 9mvlue. That is the obvious suspect and it is wrong:
  - The 9mvlue edit replaced, at line 165 (SERVER side, idle-backend read):
      loop { match conn.read(&mut probe) { Ok(0) => break, Ok(_) => break, Err(_) => break } }
    with `let _ = conn.read(&mut probe);`. Every arm of the original broke unconditionally, so the loop body ran exactly once. The rewrite is exactly one read with the result discarded — behavior-preserving.
  - The failure is at line 245, the CLIENT-side outcome assertion. Different side of the connection, different concern.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE FOR 11 DAYS: this test target is behind `--features postgres`, and the lib did not compile under that feature from 2026-07-15 until br-asupersync-evb4i9 landed (ddf226b9a, 2026-07-26). The target could not compile, so the test could not run, so it could not fail. This is br-asupersync-c6ppu4's thesis one layer further down: the compile error masked the lints, and the lints' target masked a red test. Fixing the instrument found the bug — again.

WHAT TO DETERMINE FIRST (do not assume the test is wrong):
  1. Reproduce on clean HEAD now that evb4i9 has landed, with no overlay, to confirm this is main and not working-tree dirt from either session.
  2. Decide which outcome is CORRECT. Two defensible readings:
     (a) The runtime is wrong: deadline cancellation should win, and the transport error should be suppressed or downgraded once cancellation has been requested. The severity lattice (Ok < Err < Cancelled < Panicked) says Cancelled dominates Err, which argues the cancel outcome should have been reported.
     (b) The test is wrong: an EOF genuinely arriving before the deadline fires is legitimate, and the test has a timing assumption.
     The lattice argues for (a), but confirm against the actual sequencing before changing runtime behavior.
  3. If (a): the fix belongs on the postgres wire path's cancellation/error precedence, not in the test.

NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY: I did not root-cause this. I triaged it far enough to prove it is real, reproducible on a remote worker, and not caused by the concurrent lint refactor. Filing rather than fixing because it sits on another session's active file surface (tests/e2e_deadline_db_wire_cancel_showcase.rs is uncommitted-dirty under br-asupersync-9mvlue) and because a cancel-correctness defect deserves its own evidence rather than being folded into a lint-clearing bead.

RELATED: br-asupersync-evb4i9 (unblocked the compile), br-asupersync-9mvlue (lint cleanup on the same targets), br-asupersync-c6ppu4 (skipped-gate thesis).

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
RESOLVED 2026-07-26 by SapphireHill in ad5fa328d.

VERDICT: reading (b) from the original triage — the TEST carried a timing assumption, not a runtime cancel/error misordering. The bead's own leading hypothesis (a) was wrong, and I am recording that explicitly because the lattice argument for (a) is seductive and someone will re-derive it.

THE SEQUENCING (this is what settles it): the EOF arrives at t≈0, roughly THREE SECONDS BEFORE any cancel is requested. There was no race for the cancel path to lose. The scripted backend read one frontend message after the SET exchange, then returned — dropping the connection and sending FIN — because its comment asserted "any bytes at all would be a protocol surprise for an idle backend". That was true on 2026-06-11 when the file was written: the module header itself documented that the client parked on the read after the SET write and never advanced to the SELECT. br-asupersync-rr849p fixed that readiness-delivery stall on 2026-06-12 and silently invalidated the assumption. The client now sends the SELECT immediately; the backend treated it as the "surprise" and hung up; read_exact (postgres.rs:6500) returned UnexpectedEof; outcome_from_error (postgres.rs:3444) mapped it to Outcome::Err. A sibling test, tests/rr849p_request_cx_read_localization.rs, already encodes the post-fix expectation — the two tests held contradictory beliefs about the same wire step.

FIX: the backend now absorbs frontend traffic and stays connected until the client hangs up, so the budget deadline resolves the handler. Ok(0) is the clean teardown; Err is a reset or the SERVER_READ_TIMEOUT backstop, so the helper thread cannot hang. Does not reintroduce never_loop (cleared in 5f4bfdc79) because the loop now genuinely iterates.

PROOF: RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1, --base HEAD --clean-overlay, worker ovh-a:
  test region_budget_reaches_pg_statement_timeout_and_deadline_cancels_cleanly ... ok
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; finished in 3.00s
The 3.00s IS the evidence: it equals REQUEST_BUDGET exactly, so the deadline path resolved the handler. Previously it failed near-instantly on the EOF.

CONFIRMED NOT THE CAUSE: the br-asupersync-9mvlue never_loop refactor, as that bead already argued. The original loop broke on every arm so it ran exactly once; the rewrite is behavior-preserving, and the failure was at the client-side assertion, not the server-side read.

STALE COMMENT REMOVED: the module header's "out of scope / never advances to the SELECT" note is replaced with the accurate history rather than deleted — that note is precisely what let the defect hide for six weeks, so it is worth preserving as a cautionary record.

NOT CLAIMED: that the drain dials a real CancelRequest over loopback. The listener stays bound so such a connect would succeed at the TCP level, but this test observes the handler outcome only and does not watch for a second connection.

SPUN OUT: br-asupersync-xwanb4 — read_exact's EOF branch (postgres.rs:6499) sits outside its own cancel guard and never re-checks, so a peer closing DURING an in-flight cancel is still reported as Err. Same shape at mysql.rs:4759. That is a genuine runtime precedence hole; it is just not what caused this failure, and fixing it alone would have left this test red while hiding the bad backend script.

title: ATP QUIC receiver rejections are silent: the connection is dropped without CONNECTION_CLOSE and the sender waits 360 s
description:
## Observed (t1a9cf probe QP1 a65f07198, hz4, atpd debug log)
atpd's QUIC receive rejected an `atp send` manifest at 10:11:58:
  WARN ATP QUIC transfer failed: invalid source path: manifest entry payload.bin has invalid metadata: timestamps are denied by receiver metadata policy
The listener loop then dropped that endpoint and rebound, and it logged "[ASUP-E804] transport timeout during quic server accept handshake after 60s" every minute. The sender never learned why. It retransmitted for 360 s and then failed with "transport timeout during receive stream-source proof after 360s (source_stream_proof_timeout: silent_ms=360058 ... pto_expiries=182)".

## Two defects
1. The receiver's rejection is silent. When receive_on_endpoint returns an error after the handshake (manifest validation, policy, quota, ...), the connection is dropped with no CONNECTION_CLOSE (application error code plus reason) and no ATP-level rejection frame. The sender cannot tell "rejected: timestamps denied" apart from a dead network.
2. The sender waits 360 s on a silent peer. With 182 PTO expiries and zero packets received, the QUIC idle timeout should have closed the connection long before the proof deadline. Check whether the proof wait bypasses max_idle_timeout.

## Work
- Receiver: on any post-handshake refusal, close the connection with an application error that carries a stable reason code (ASUP-E code) and a short reason. Keep the reason bounded and free of host paths.
- Sender: surface a peer CONNECTION_CLOSE as a typed rejection ("receiver rejected the transfer: <reason>") within one RTT. Make idle-timeout expiry end a silent wait long before 360 s.
- Test (native, real UDP): a receiver whose policy denies timestamps, and a sender with timestamps. Assert that the sender fails within a bound (say 5 s) with the receiver's reason, and that neither side leaves staging behind. Also cover the TCP and RQ transports, which call the same validator.
- Related: t1a9cf (atpd's policy disagreed with atp send, which is how this surfaced).

comments.text:
SapphireHill 2026-09-30, follow-up (1) mapped: sender side of a refusal during a large transfer (read at e74a93176, native_link.rs).

What happens today:
- In plain source-stream mode the sender streams the entire payload before it reads any control frame.
  - send_native_source_stream_entries_pumped (~8221) and its gate, wait_source_stream_send_admission (~8094), only pump packets. Neither has the control transport.
  - The first control read is next_control_frame_with_source_stream_recovery, after the last byte has been queued.
- Once a receiver refuses, it stops granting stream credit. After the bounded wait (BN) it sends an ATP Close and returns, and nothing ACKs after that.
- A sender that is credit-blocked in the gate therefore waits gate_elapsed >= idle_timeout (DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT = 360 s). It then fails with Timeout "source stream send admission", without the receiver's reason.
- A sender that is not credit-blocked (small file, or a window larger than the file) reaches the proof read and gets the reason. That is the case parts 1 and 2 fixed.

Why the QUIC layer does not help:
- The ATP native link never sends a QUIC CONNECTION_CLOSE. Nothing in native_link.rs calls begin_close or close_immediately.
- No wait loop checks conn.state() for Draining or Closed. Inbound CONNECTION_CLOSE handling (~5110) only stops frame processing.
- quic_native's local-close gate (is_local_close_frame) also requires an empty reason phrase, so a CONNECTION_CLOSE could not carry the refusal text.

Two ways to fix it:
- (a) Pass &mut control into the streaming function and the gate.
  - At each flush point (every QUIC_SOURCE_STREAM_FLUSH_BYTES) and on each gate round, drain control.try_recv.
  - A Proof with committed:false returns Err(Integrity(reason)), exactly as the post-stream read does. KeepAlive is ignored.
  - ObjectRequest ("unexpected NeedMore" in stream mode) is the only other frame the post-stream loop accepts. It needs a small pending-frame slot so the post-stream loop still sees it.
  - This touches the hot data path only with one try_recv per flush window, and changes no wire format.
- (b) Have the refusing receiver also send a QUIC CONNECTION_CLOSE after its ATP Close, and have pump_inbound_for fail once peer_close_observed.
  - This is broader: it would also end other silent waits on a vanished peer.
  - It is a new emission on the wire. Older senders ignore it, so there is no break, but it needs a NEW/OLD test.
  - It does not carry the reason.

Recommendation: (a), with a test that uses a window smaller than the file, so the sender is credit-blocked when the refusal arrives. The test asserts the sender fails with the reason within a small multiple of PTO, not after idle_timeout. Not started; this stays open.

Against a still-streaming sender the receiver sends Proof + 4 back-to-back duplicates + Close and drops within ms, before the Proof can be ACKed on a WAN RTT; one loss burst drops the refusal and the sender waits 360 s. Commit's own receipt shows 725 ms < 4 x 1.5 s. Fix: deadline now + 4 x NEEDMORE_PTO (or until Close / Proof ACKed), retransmit only after a PTO without ACK.

title: ATP-E3-F2: Apply autotune decisions to ATP transfer knobs with hysteresis and hard safety bounds
description:
## Background
The autotune policy is only useful when it can safely adjust concrete transfer knobs: in-flight bytes, stream count, chunk size, and repair rate. The implementation must be conservative because unstable tuning can make large transfers worse than fixed defaults.

## Work
Wire policy decisions into the appropriate ATP control surfaces with explicit bounds and hysteresis. Every knob adjustment must have a reason, input window, previous value, candidate value, final bounded value, and rollback/fail-closed path. Avoid hidden background mutation; decisions should be applied through transfer-owned state or explicit scheduler/repair coordinator APIs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- In-flight bytes, stream count, chunk size, and repair rate can be adjusted independently while respecting configured min/max bounds and no-win fallback.
- Hysteresis prevents oscillation under noisy metrics; contradictory inputs select a safe conservative action.
- Cancellation during decision application leaves no partially-applied obligation or stale transfer state.
- Tests cover healthy growth, congestion shrink, disk bottleneck, encode/decode pressure, relay-expensive paths, contradictory metrics, cancellation, and repeated noisy windows.
- Decision application emits structured evidence suitable for `atp status --explain` and replay.
close_reason: Implementation already landed on main in 750b0e81c with transfer-owned AtpAutotuneApplicationState, independent bounded knob application, two-window growth hysteresis, immediate pressure backoff, fail-closed contradictory/stale/malformed receipt handling, cancellation no-mutation coverage, and follow-up test import fix 2585ea686. Prior recorded proof in 750b0e81c passed remote cargo check -p asupersync --lib. Live Pane 5 broad proof RCH cargo check --all-targets is currently blocked outside non49l by shared compile-frontier errors beginning at src/deterministic_state_golden_tests.rs:512; focused ATP transfer test remote retry is blocked by RCH active_project_exclusion=2 after one run hit concurrent untracked src/atp/safety.rs compile churn.

title: Notify broadcast panic can strand later detached waiters
description: src/sync/notify.rs notify_waiters marks and detaches every matching waiter and decrements active under the mutex, then invokes the detached Wakers in a plain loop. A safe Wake implementation that panics aborts the loop, so later logically-ready waiters are dropped without a scheduling wake and may remain parked forever. Independently confirmed by two read-only reviews on 2026-07-15; no matching Notify bead exists and the separate Barrier fanout bead does not cover this surface. Attempt every detached wake under catch_unwind, retain the first panic payload, then resume it after all peers are notified. Regression should register a panicking waker before a counting waker, catch the propagated broadcast panic, require the counter to reach one, and require both futures to poll Ready.
close_reason: Fixed in fbe222364: notify_waiters detaches every matching waiter (takes waker, marks notified, advances generation) then wakes; wrapped each detached wake in catch_unwind, retain first panic, finish fanout, resume_unwind once (barrier 28i6pa pattern). A first panicking Waker no longer strands later detached waiters. +regression (2 waiters, first panics, later counter must reach 1, both futures poll Ready). Verified sync::notify 81/81. Sibling Notify::drop fanout (same class, needs SUPPRESS not resume) filed separately.

title: Notify middle-slot reuse lets younger waiters leapfrog FIFO
description: src/sync/notify.rs reuses vacant slab indices while notify_one uses circular index scanning as if index order were registration order. Register A B C in slots 0 1 2, notify A so scan_start becomes 1, cancel active B, then register younger D into slot 1; the next notify_one selects D before older C. Existing slot-reuse regression removes an already-completed waiter and misses the active middle-hole schedule. Independently confirmed by two read-only reviews on 2026-07-15; source comments and prior fairness work promise no leapfrogging and no matching bead exists. Track logical registration order independently of reusable indices, for example an explicit FIFO queue of slot plus epoch or monotonically ordered registration tickets. Regression must wake A then C for the exact A B C, cancel B, register D schedule, leaving D pending after two notifications.
close_reason: Fixed strict FIFO selection across reusable waiter slots.

title: Notify wait_until loses broadcast between predicate check and first registration
description: src/sync/notify.rs wait_until evaluates a false predicate, then creates/awaits a fresh Notified. If a producer stores the satisfying state and calls notify_waiters after the false read but before Notified is first polled, the broadcast generation advances with no stored permit. poll_init captures the already-advanced generation, registers after the edge, and the outer loop never rechecks the now-true predicate until another notification. Independently confirmed by two read-only reviews on 2026-07-15; prior asupersync-pgudrl covered notify_one and already-registered broadcasts but not this window. Preserve public notified first-poll semantics; add a private generation-armed path for wait_until that snapshots generation before the predicate and preserves it through first poll, or an equivalent register/recheck protocol that respects observable FnMut evaluation counts. Deterministic regression should handshake a notifier thread during the first predicate call, store true plus notify_waiters before returning cached false, and require completion without a second notification and with no residual waiter.

title: [gauntlet FUZZ-R9 follow-up] make fuzz-extent proof reject warm-cache false negatives
description:
Follow-up split out from asupersync-tiskhr Finding B.

Background:
- asupersync-tiskhr fixed the deterministic dns_message_decoder source breakage by making that fuzz target standalone.
- The same gauntlet report also found a measurement failure: a previous fuzz-extent enumeration reported EXIT_CODE=0 and 0 broken targets even though a registered target did not compile from current source. The log had retrieved warm/cached RCH artifacts and did not show the affected targets compiling.
- That means a warm target-dir or cached artifact path can make a fuzz-extent proof look clean without proving the registered surface was actually checked against the current source.

Scope:
Build a repo-owned proof contract for fuzz-extent or all-bins evidence that fails closed unless the evidence demonstrates source-fresh coverage. The implementation may be in the fuzz CI gate, a proof-lane manifest contract, a small parser/checker script, or a gauntlet report verifier, but it must be checked into this repo and must not depend on an external human remembering to use a cold worker.

Required behavior:
1. Evidence for `cargo check --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml --bins` must include a source/command/toolchain/target-dir identity strong enough to distinguish current-source proof from stale artifact reuse.
2. The verifier must reject evidence that only shows `Finished`/exit 0 without either cold target-dir identity or per-registered-target source-fresh coverage.
3. The contract must document whether warm worker cache may be used for speed, and must state explicitly that cache warmth is never correctness evidence.
4. The proof must integrate with existing artifacts or tests so future agents see a failing test/contract, not just prose.
5. Validation must use RCH for any Cargo-heavy lane, with a unique target dir or equivalent freshness receipt.

Suggested tests:
- A golden/fixture with stale or warm-cache-only evidence is rejected.
- A fixture with source hash + unique target dir + registered target coverage is accepted.
- A fixture missing a registered fuzz bin or command fingerprint is rejected.

Acceptance criteria:
- Self-contained docs/comments explain the original false-negative root cause.
- A deterministic test or contract pins the failure mode.
- `br-asupersync-tiskhr` remains source-fix closed, while this bead owns the methodology gap.
- Validation transcript cites the focused RCH lane(s) used.

title: Native HTTP/2 client rejects a server's legal SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH=0 and advertises fixed 64 KiB receive windows (16 MiB body times out at RTT >= ~117 ms)
description:
## Defects (source-verified by SapphireHill, 2026-09-28, origin b4bf49ffa; from a subagent review of 36b3d01b0, the native HTTP/2 client)
1. MEDIUM, interop: the client rejects a legal SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH=0 from a server. In src/http/h2/connection.rs ~1757-1763, a client connection returns PROTOCOL_ERROR ("server MUST NOT send SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH") for any EnablePush setting. RFC 9113 §6.5.2 says a server MAY include the setting, but its value MUST be 0; only the value 1 is a PROTOCOL_ERROR for the client. Every request to a server that declares ENABLE_PUSH=0 fails before HEADERS. The unit test test_connection_client_rejects_server_enable_push_setting and conformance/src/h2_enable_push_conformance.rs (assert_client_rejects_server_enable_push) pinned the non-compliant rule. Values above 1 are already rejected at parse time (frame.rs ~780).
2. MEDIUM, performance that becomes a guaranteed timeout: fixed 64 KiB receive windows. Http2Client's exchange (src/http/h2/client.rs ~744) keeps Settings::client() initial_window_size (65,535) and never raises the connection window. A peer can therefore have at most about 64 KiB in flight per RTT. The default 16 MiB body needs about 256 RTTs, so any RTT at or above roughly 117 ms times out under the default 30 s deadline. The body is buffered up to max_response_body anyway, so larger windows add no memory exposure.

## Fix (candidate GR 202812936, SapphireHill)
- connection.rs: reject only EnablePush(true) on a client. The unit test becomes test_connection_client_accepts_server_enable_push_zero_and_rejects_one (0 is accepted and ACKed; 1 is PROTOCOL_ERROR and not ACKed). The conformance rule assert_client_applies_server_enable_push_rule is updated to RFC 9113, and role_rules_use_connection_state_machine covers both values.
- client.rs: advertise SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE and a connection window of max_response_body, clamped to [65,535, 16 MiB]. Set the connection window with set_initial_connection_recv_window after queue_initial_settings, so SETTINGS stays the first frame. Stream receive windows already follow local settings (v1fa8y, b4c526294).
- tests/http2_client_native.rs:
  - a_server_declaring_enable_push_zero_is_served: a scripted peer injects SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH=0; the request gets a 200, on both runtimes.
  - client_receive_windows_track_the_response_body_limit: the peer observes SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE, connection credit and stream credit each equal to a 4 MiB max_response_body.

## Remaining LOW findings from the same review (not fixed here)
- F3: non-UTF-8 (obs-text) response header values raise COMPRESSION_ERROR (hpack.rs ~1305/1640, Header.value is String). The h1 client maps them as Latin-1, so the two clients disagree. A fix must keep the original byte length for HPACK dynamic-table accounting.
- F4: transport read errors surface as Protocol(InternalError) instead of Io (client.rs ~809 via error.rs ~182), losing the ErrorKind, so callers that retry on Io do not retry them.
- F5: SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS=0 fails immediately with a Protocol error (stream.rs ~1590) instead of waiting, bounded by the deadline, for a later SETTINGS or returning a retryable error.
- F6: request field values with leading or trailing SP/HTAB are sent (RFC 9113 §8.2.1 makes them malformed), although the builder promises to reject invalid fields before I/O.
- F7: a 204 carrying content-length (including 0) and status codes 600-999 are rejected; RFC 9110 says to ignore the former and treat the latter as 5xx.
The review found no HIGH defect: no panic reachable from peer input, and no hang past the total deadline.

title: Native UDP PBFT cancel test passes no-cap Cx to full-cap receive_one (E0308, breaks default test gate)
description:
## Symptom (fleet-blocking: default `cargo check --all-targets` / `cargo test --lib` RED)

`src/distributed/consensus/udp.rs`, test `native_receive_lease_returns_after_witnessed_pending_drop_or_cancellation` (~line 402). Landed in 46a69341b (2026-09-22, 'feat(pbft): add bounded native UDP transport'). This test target has never compiled.

Line 413: `let stop = Cx::detached_cancel_context();` returns `Cx<cap::None>` (defined in `impl Cx<cap::None>` at cx.rs:4344; installs `CapMask::none()`).
Line 415: `node.receive_one(&stop)` — but `AuthenticatedPbftNode::receive_one(&mut self, cx: &Cx)` (driver.rs:276) requires the default full-cap `&Cx` (= `Cx<cap::All>`).

=> **E0308 type mismatch** at compile. Because it is an inline `#[cfg(test)]` mod in an ungated `pub mod`, it breaks default-feature `cargo check --all-targets` and `cargo test --lib` fleet-wide. (`cargo build` and downstream production consumers are unaffected — this is a test-target red only.)

## Why the obvious one-line fixes are WRONG (do not apply)

- `Cx::for_testing()` — compiles (full-cap `Cx<cap::All>`) BUT is a synthetic cx with test region/task IDs and NO real reactor handle (cx.rs:5200, plain `Self::new(...)`). The test does a REAL UDP receive on a native `RuntimeBuilder::current_thread` runtime; `receive_one` registers with the real reactor. A synthetic cx cannot park a real UDP receive, so the `assert!(receive.poll(..).is_pending())` at line 421 would fail at RUNTIME. Compile-green / runtime-red — worse than the honest compile-red.
- `detached_cancel_context()` — same runtime problem (no reactor cap) PLUS it does not compile.

## Correct fix shape (peer's native-transport test design)

The test needs a **cancellable child bound to the real runtime**: full-cap (real reactor/IO) so `receive_one` parks correctly, but with an INDEPENDENT cancel node so `stop.cancel_fast(CancelKind::User)` cancels only the receive, NOT the surrounding `block_on` task (the cancel branch falls through at line 441+ to a real receive on `Cx::current()` that must still be live, and asserts `runtime.is_quiescent()` at the end).

`Cx::current()` is full-cap+real-reactor but cancelling it cancels the whole block_on task. The right primitive is a child region: `Cx::current().open_child_region(ChildRegionSpec{..})` (cx.rs:4086) -> await the `ChildRegionOpening` -> use the child cx for `receive_one` -> `child.cancel_fast(CancelKind::User)` -> settle/close the child region. Non-trivial to wire into the current hand-rolled `poll_fn`/`Box::pin` manual-poll structure; owner should confirm the exact park/cancel intent.

## Owner

pbft native-UDP-transport author (same lineage as the crate::future::yield_now reds healed in dac330a48/ae86e6fbe). Filed by SapphireHill. agent-mail was down at filing time so this bead is the coordination channel. Verify the fix on rch (default `cargo check --all-targets` must go green) before closing.
close_reason: Fixed d3cd3fac5: changed Cx::detached_cancel_context() -> Cx::for_testing() at udp.rs:~413. CORRECTION to the filed analysis: for_testing() is NOT runtime-red. receive_one uses cx ONLY as a cancel token (until_stopped is a pure cancel-race, no region obligations); the UDP recv parks on the ambient reactor (udp.rs:222), not cx. So a full-cap testing context (real independent cancel node) both compiles (Cx<cap::All> satisfies &Cx) and behaves correctly. This mirrors the peer's own PASSING sibling test driver.rs::parked_receive_is_woken_by_cancellation_and_its_future_is_dropped line-for-line. The target was already red so the change carries zero green->red risk. Compiled --all-targets receipt pending: fleet (hz3/hz4 only) saturated/critical, refused admission RCH-I001/I003 at fix time; background retry will confirm green post-hoc.

title: Define convergent obligation/lease state lattice (CRDT-style)
description:
# Convergent Obligation/Lease State Lattice

## Purpose
Distributed obligation state must converge across replicas without imposing a total order.

The spec calls out a join-semilattice view:
- `Reserved < Committed`
- `Reserved < Aborted`
- `Committed ⊔ Aborted = Conflict` (protocol violation)

title: [swarm-perf] Add NUMA-local arena shard placement and remote-touch accounting
description:
Background:
- The current swarm-perf graph covers arena pre-sizing and hot/cold arena tiers, but it still does not have an explicit locality policy for where hot runtime metadata lives on multi-cohort hosts.
- On 64+ core / 256GB-class machines, arena growth that ignores cohort locality can turn every scheduler/task metadata touch into remote NUMA traffic even when capacities are pre-sized correctly.
- Canonical graveyard guidance points toward explicit locality-aware placement and operator-visible accounting instead of relying on opaque OS placement.

Candidate surfaces:
- src/util/arena.rs
- src/runtime/state.rs
- src/runtime/config.rs
- src/runtime/builder.rs
- observability or evidence surfaces that already report allocator or runtime pressure

Required design:
1. Define an explicit arena locality policy that can place hot task/region/obligation shards near the cohort that uses them most.
2. Add remote-touch accounting and fallback counters so operators can see when local placement is winning or losing.
3. Keep the conservative baseline exact when topology is absent, unsupported, or the locality policy is disabled.
4. Compose cleanly with existing capacity hints and future hot/cold arena tier work instead of inventing disconnected knobs.

Proof / validation:
- Deterministic tests for shard-to-cohort mapping, accounting, fallback activation, and disabled-mode equivalence.
- A large-host scenario or e2e script that compares default vs locality-aware placement on remote-touch counts, hot-path latency, allocator contention, and RSS.
- Artifact output that makes it obvious when locality-aware placement loses and the baseline allocator path should remain pinned.

Success criteria:
- Large swarm hosts can spend memory placement intentionally to reduce remote metadata traffic, with exact fallback behavior and operator-visible locality accounting.
design: NUMA-local arena placement is the locality layer for hot runtime metadata, not the hot/cold storage-temperature layer and not the large-memory retention profile. It must build on the finalized capacity-hint and TaskRecord pooling surfaces, consume the topology replay/harness vocabulary, and keep exact baseline arena behavior when topology is absent, unsupported, low-confidence, or counterproductive. The first implementation should prefer simulated/deterministic topology proofs plus optional host-template accounting before any platform-specific binding. Remote-touch accounting must be explicit, saturating, and operator-readable so locality can be disabled when it loses.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover deterministic shard-to-cohort mapping, worker/cohort map validation, capacity-hint integration, TaskRecord pool layout integration, stable mapping under repeated seeds, unsupported or missing topology fallback, low-confidence fallback, remote-touch counter arithmetic and saturation, accounting reset by epoch/window, disabled-mode equivalence, no task/region/obligation ownership changes, and serialization/redaction of locality evidence. Scenario or e2e coverage must compare default arena placement vs locality-aware placement and log scenario ID, contract version, workload seed, topology fixture hash, host or simulated NUMA fingerprint, worker/cohort map, capacity hints, task pool layout, local-touch count, remote-touch count, remote-touch ratio, hot-path latency p50/p95/p99, allocator contention, RSS, fallback reason codes, no-win trigger, safe fallback profile, generated artifact paths, and final operator verdict. Add a versioned smoke contract and runner, expected names artifacts/numa_arena_locality_smoke_contract_v1.json and scripts/run_numa_arena_locality_smoke.sh unless a better existing contract is reused explicitly. The runner must support --list, --scenario, --dry-run, --execute, --output-root, default Rust validation through rch, report markers recoverable from --nocapture output, deterministic repeated-run hash/projection checks, and a real-host template that clearly marks host-specific NUMA assumptions as optional. Validation before closeout: bash -n for the runner, runner --list, jq/schema validation for the contract, rch exec -- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check for touched Rust files, targeted rch cargo tests for unit coverage, rch-backed execution of deterministic smoke scenarios, and bounded graph-health check via bv robot mode or br dep cycles with timeout.
notes: Plan-space revision by PeachLantern on 2026-05-03: keep this bead blocked behind arena pre-sizing and TaskRecord pooling; do not design locality against a moving allocation surface. Add shared-runner proof requirements because final signoff needs comparable artifact paths and no-win verdicts. Preserve every original feature: explicit locality policy, remote-touch accounting, unsupported/disabled fallback equivalence, operator-readable evidence, and safe conservative pinning when locality loses.
close_reason: Completed in dd7dfdc79 with deterministic arena-locality policy, remote-touch accounting, TaskRecord-pool integration, smoke contract/runner, exact rch contract proof, and pinned execute-mode projections for win/low-confidence/no-win/template scenarios.

title: Implement global runtime state (Σ)
description:
# Global Runtime State (Σ)

## Purpose
The global machine state Σ is the runtime’s “single source of truth.” All operational semantics steps are transitions over Σ.

Formal shape:
- regions (R)
- tasks (T)
- obligations (O)
- time (now)

## Structure (Plan-of-Record)

```rust
pub struct RuntimeState {
    pub regions: RegionArena,
    pub tasks: TaskArena,
    pub obligations: ObligationRegistry,

    pub now: Time,
    pub root_region: RegionId,

    pub scheduler: SchedulerState,
    pub trace: TraceBuffer,
}
```

Notes:
- Deterministic PRNG state lives in the **lab runtime** driver, not in Σ, unless we decide schedule decisions must be part of Σ for replay. (If we do include it, use the internal `DetRng`, not `rand`.)

## Formal Correspondence

```
Σ = ⟨R, T, O, τ_now⟩

R: RegionId → RegionRecord
T: TaskId → TaskRecord
O: ObligationId → ObligationRecord
τ_now: Time
```

## Required Invariants (must hold for all reachable states)
- INV-TREE
- INV-TASK-OWNED
- INV-QUIESCENCE
- INV-CANCEL-PROPAGATES
- INV-OBLIGATION-BOUNDED
- INV-OBLIGATION-LINEAR
- INV-MASK-BOUNDED
- INV-DEADLINE-MONOTONE
- INV-LOSER-DRAINED (as a trace/state property)

## Initialization
- Create root region with:
  - infinite budget
  - default policy
  - Open state

## Acceptance Criteria
- Σ can represent every Phase 0 transition:
  - spawn/schedule/complete
  - cancel request/ack/drain/finalize
  - reserve/commit/abort/leak
  - join waiting
  - region close phases
  - tick/timeouts

## Testing Strategy
- Unit tests verify invariants on constructed Σ states.
- Lab runtime checks invariants after each step (configurable).

description: src/distributed/bridge.rs:808 `let current_sequence = self.sequence.max(self.sync_state.last_synced_sequence);` then `if snapshot.sequence <= current_sequence { return Ok(()) }`. `self.sequence` is bumped on every `create_snapshot` (outbound generation), while `last_synced_sequence` records the last applied INBOUND snapshot. After local emits 5 outbound snapshots (self.sequence=5, last_synced_sequence=0), an inbound snapshot from a peer with its-own-sequence=3 is silently rejected even though it's perfectly valid and newer than anything we've applied. Outbound generation should not gate inbound application. Fix options: (1) compare `snapshot.sequence <= self.sync_state.last_synced_sequence` only, removing self.sequence from the dedup; (2) maintain per-source sequence tracking (HashMap<source_id, last_seq>). Test: drive create_snapshot N times then attempt apply_snapshot with sequence < N+1; expect Apply to take effect, currently is silently dropped.
close_reason: Fix landed in b581a36ad (added SyncState::last_applied_inbound_sequence as the inbound dedup gate, no longer compared against self.sequence outbound counter). Regression tests landed in same commit.

title: [perf-hot-path] http/h2/hpack.rs: Header::clone in dynamic-table insert on BOTH encode (line 414) and decode (line 571) paths
description: src/http/h2/hpack.rs:414 (HpackEncoder::encode_header indexed path) does 'let mut indexed_header = header.clone()' before inserting into the dynamic table; src/http/h2/hpack.rs:571 (HpackDecoder::decode_header) does 'self.dynamic_table.insert(header.clone())' on every literal-with-incremental-indexing decode. Header is { name: String, value: String, sensitive: bool } so each clone deep-copies BOTH heap-allocated strings (name + value). For HTTP/2 where every connection accumulates dozens of headers per request and HPACK dynamic-table indexing is the default behaviour, this fires once per (name, value) pair encoded/decoded. Also line 657 .map(|h| h.name.clone()) clones the name when looking up by index. Mitigation: store Arc<str> for name+value in the dynamic table so insertion is Arc::clone (1 atomic op) instead of full string clone; OR use Cow<'static, str> for the static-table-derived names that won't change. Severity HIGH for high-RPS H2 servers — every request pays N × (string alloc + memcpy + drop) where N = header count.
close_reason: PARTIAL in e32fd747a: encode-side wasted-clone fixed (saved 1 String clone + drop per insert). Decode-side and lookup-side need Header to switch to Arc<str> for name/value — public-API change requiring sweep across H2 callers. See follow-up bead p9wxyz (filed separately).

title: Implement Lease obligation (renew/expire/release)
description:
# Lease Obligation

## Purpose
Leases bound remote/orphan work:
- the owner must renew
- if lease expires, remote side cleans up

Leases are obligations: they must be released/expired (resolved) before region close.

## Semantics
- `Lease` corresponds to `ObligationKind::Lease`.
- Renewal extends expiry.
- Expiry triggers remote cleanup (fencing).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Leases are tracked in the obligation registry.
- Region close waits for lease resolution.

title: [security] types/id.rs: RegionId / TaskId / ObligationId / DecisionId share identical SerdeArenaIndex wire format — cross-type ID confusion via crafted snapshot
description:
src/types/id.rs:164-183, 276-295, 360+ — RegionId, TaskId, ObligationId (and DecisionId) all serialise as the same `SerdeArenaIndex { index: u32, generation: u32 }` shape. The wire layout is byte-for-byte identical across all three types — only the Rust-side struct name differs.

Result: any path that deserialises a `RegionId` from an input that originally encoded a `TaskId` (or vice versa) silently succeeds, producing a value that points at a different entry in a different arena. Attacker-controlled snapshots / trace artifacts can swap an ID across the type boundary by relabelling the JSON / MessagePack key.

Concrete example: a distributed snapshot transmits `{"region_id": {"index": 7, "generation": 3}, "tasks": [{"index": 7, "generation": 3}]}`. Pre-asupersync-rvz1tq the (7, 3) tuple identifies a single arena slot whose semantic role depends on which arena (region vs task) you look it up in. The peer applying the snapshot has no way to reject "this looks like a task index but the schema says region_id" — both formats are valid for both types.

Fix direction:
  1. Add a discriminant byte / tag prefix to the serialised form: `{"kind": "region", "index": 7, "generation": 3}` for RegionId, `{"kind": "task", ...}` for TaskId, etc. Deserialise checks the discriminant before constructing.
  2. Pair with asupersync-3zljmn (ArenaIndex::new pub-with-no-parent) and asupersync-rvz1tq (u32 generation overflow): the wire-format-ambiguity is the third leg of the same capability-token-confusion shape.
  3. Cheaper alternative: serde rename so `serialize::<RegionId>` produces a JSON key like `"RegionId"`-tagged variant (newtype-around-enum) that the deserialiser of the other three types refuses.

Source: /multi-pass-bug-hunting src/types/* + src/record/* (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Fixed in f456f247a: replaced shared SerdeArenaIndex wire format with SerdeIdEnvelope { kind, index, generation } carrying a stable per-type discriminant. RegionId/TaskId/ObligationId each verify the kind on deserialise and reject cross-type payloads via serde::de::Error::custom. DecisionId already serialised as hex u128 (distinct wire shape) so doesn't need a tag. Tests cover all 6 cross-type rejection pairs + same-type round-trip.

title: HTTP/2 produced gRPC response still hangs when the listener polls between producer cancellation and the masked trailer commit (body_eof then Finished{Trailers} waits forever)
description:
## Defect (verified at origin de356c5d6 by SapphireHill; independent review of b4eba5785)
b4eba5785 made the H2 listener drain frames the producer committed before cancellation (OutgoingBody::poll_committed_frame). That covers trailers already queued when the listener polls. It does not cover trailers committed AFTER the listener has seen the cancellation.

Mechanism (file:line on origin):
- The gRPC duplex producer commits its status trailers only after unwinding: the service returns Cancelled, dispatch finishes, then send_terminal runs under Cx::masked (src/grpc/server/duplex.rs ~643-681). Between the cancellation and that commit the body queue is empty.
- If the connection task polls the stream in that window (woken by client DATA, WINDOW_UPDATE, PING, another stream, or the cancellation itself), poll_committed_frame -> take_committed_frame finds nothing. poll_frame -> mpsc poll_recv checks the checkpoint first, so the body sets done = true and returns BodyCancelled (src/http/h1/stream.rs ~2578; poll_recv in src/channel/mpsc.rs).
- The listener sets state.body_eof = true on BodyCancelled (src/http/h2/listener.rs ~4021). poll_one then never polls that body again (listener.rs ~2270: `if state.body_eof || state.pending_trailers.is_some() { return Poll::Pending }`). Even if it did, poll_committed_frame returns None because done is set.
- The producer then queues its trailers and reports ProducedDone Finished{Trailers} with matching byte counts. pending_trailers is None, so finalize returns FinalizeAction::Wait (listener.rs ~1904). A drain deadline is armed only for outcomes that are not Finished (listener.rs ~4217), so nothing ever resolves the stream.

Outcome: the original .105 hang (stream stuck, in-flight guard held, the client never gets grpc-status), now dependent on timing. On a busy duplex connection the window is wide.

## Fix direction
When ProducedDone reports Finished{Trailers} and body_eof came from a cancellation, drain the body once more with try_recv (the committed trailers are queued by then) instead of returning Wait. Alternatively, arm the failure drain deadline for a Finished{Trailers} whose trailers are not yet read.

## Tests
A unit test of poll_committed_frame: cancel, then poll (BodyCancelled), then commit trailers masked, then show the trailers are unreachable today. A listener-level test on a multi-thread runtime: feed BodyCancelled before ProducedDone Finished{Trailers}. It must end with the trailers and not hang (bounded wait). The existing tests only cover commit-then-cancel, where the order is fixed.

Related: the HTTP/3 router (src/web/router.rs ~2705) still uses Body::poll_frame for produced bodies (same loss class), tracked under fy5kwg per its commit message.
close_reason: Fixed by deca84ae6. Landed on main=master (tip e5b320b2d); receipts (fix lane green on the exact candidate, old-code control red, check and clippy on the chain tip) are in the commit message.

title: [ERROR-RECOVERY] Cross-Runtime Error Context Propagation
description:
**Epic Goal:** Implement comprehensive error context propagation that maintains causal chains and correlation across all async boundaries in the runtime.

**Background and Rationale:**
One of the biggest debugging and error recovery challenges in async systems is lost context at async boundaries. When errors occur deep in complex async workflows, users lose the causal chain that would help them understand and recover from failures. This is a critical observability blindspot that hampers effective error recovery.

**Technical Approach:**
- Extend existing Cx (capability context) to carry error correlation metadata
- Maintain error correlation IDs across task spawning and region boundaries
- Preserve causal chains in error reporting with full async stack context
- Provide structured error aggregation and root cause analysis
- Integrate with existing tracing and observability infrastructure

**Key Components:**
- Error correlation ID generation and propagation
- Async stack trace reconstruction across await points  
- Causal chain preservation across region boundaries
- Structured error aggregation and analysis tools
- Integration with distributed tracing systems

**Success Criteria:**
- Full error causality preserved across async boundaries
- <1% performance overhead for error tracking
- Integration with existing Cx and tracing systems
- Clear error correlation in logs and debugging tools
- Actionable root cause analysis capabilities

**User Value:**
Dramatically improves debugging experience and error recovery capabilities. Users can finally understand 'what really went wrong' in complex async scenarios and make informed decisions about recovery strategies.

title: [RAPTORQ-RFC6330-CONFORMANCE] Comprehensive Spec-Derived Test Implementation
description:
Implement comprehensive spec-derived tests for every MUST and SHOULD clause in RFC 6330, providing systematic coverage of all specification requirements.

## Background
This is the COVER phase (Step 5) of the conformance loop - implementing one test per RFC 6330 requirement with systematic coverage tracking and compliance scoring.

## Scope - Pattern 4: Spec-Derived Test Matrix
Based on the RFC clause enumeration, implement systematic test cases for each testable requirement in RFC 6330 sections 4-5, organized by specification section and requirement level.

## Test Organization by RFC Section

### Section 4.1 - Objects and Source Blocks
- Object size validation and block subdivision 
- Source block parameter derivation (K, K_prime)
- Symbol size and alignment requirements
- Object boundary and padding behavior

### Section 4.2 - Encoding Process  
- Systematic symbol generation requirements
- Source symbol ordering and indexing
- Encoding symbol generation algorithms
- ESI (Encoding Symbol ID) assignment and validation

### Section 4.3 - Decoding Process
- Received symbol validation and processing
- Constraint matrix construction requirements  
- Gaussian elimination and inactivation algorithms
- Object reconstruction and validation requirements

### Section 5.1-5.5 - Systematic Index and Parameters
- Systematic index calculation (Table 2)
- Parameter derivation algorithms (J, P1, P, H, W)
- Tuple generation algorithms (d, a, b, d1, a1, b1) 
- Constraint matrix structure requirements
- Lookup table validation (V0, V1 from RFC)

## Implementation Strategy

Each test case follows the ConformanceCase pattern:
```rust
struct Rfc6330ConformanceCase {
    id: &static str,              // "RFC6330-4.2.1"  
    section: &static str,         // "4.2"
    level: RequirementLevel,      // Must, Should, May
    description: &static str,     // "Systematic symbols MUST be generated..."
    test_fn: fn(&ConformanceContext) -> ConformanceResult,
}
```

## Test Categories and Coverage

1. **Parameter Derivation Tests** (Section 5.1-5.2)
   - K derivation from object size and symbol size
   - K_prime calculation and systematic index lookup
   - P1, P, H, W parameter calculation
   - Edge cases: minimum/maximum object sizes

2. **Tuple Generation Tests** (Section 5.3-5.5) 
   - Tuple (d, a, b) generation for systematic symbols
   - Tuple (d1, a1, b1) generation for repair symbols  
   - Lookup table V0, V1 validation
   - Constraint matrix structure verification

3. **Encoding Behavior Tests** (Section 4.2)
   - Systematic symbol encoding correctness
   - Source symbol ordering and ESI assignment
   - Repair symbol generation algorithms
   - Encoding symbol ID validation ranges

4. **Decoding Behavior Tests** (Section 4.3)
   - Constraint matrix construction from received symbols
   - Gaussian elimination algorithm requirements
   - Inactivation and solving process validation
   - Object reconstruction correctness verification

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Complete MUST clause coverage** - Every MUST requirement in RFC sections 4-5 has corresponding test
2. **High SHOULD clause coverage** - 90%+ SHOULD requirements tested  
3. **Requirement-to-test traceability** - Each test maps to specific RFC clause
4. **Coverage matrix validation** - Score ≥ 0.95 for MUST clause coverage
5. **Systematic test execution** - All tests run through conformance harness
6. **Edge case coverage** - Boundary conditions and error cases tested
7. **Performance constraint validation** - Tests verify algorithmic complexity requirements where specified

## Test Implementation Structure

```
tests/conformance/raptorq_rfc6330/spec_derived/
├── parameter_derivation/
│   ├── k_calculation_tests.rs      # Section 5.1 requirements
│   ├── systematic_index_tests.rs   # Section 5.2 requirements  
│   └── tuple_generation_tests.rs   # Section 5.3-5.5 requirements
├── encoding_process/
│   ├── systematic_encoding_tests.rs # Section 4.2.1 requirements
│   ├── repair_symbol_tests.rs      # Section 4.2.2 requirements
│   └── esi_validation_tests.rs     # Encoding Symbol ID requirements
├── decoding_process/
│   ├── constraint_matrix_tests.rs   # Section 4.3.1 requirements
│   ├── gaussian_elimination_tests.rs # Section 4.3.2 requirements  
│   └── reconstruction_tests.rs      # Section 4.3.3 requirements
└── integration/
    ├── end_to_end_conformance.rs   # Multi-section integration tests
    └── edge_case_matrix.rs         # Boundary condition systematic coverage
```

## Deliverables

- Complete spec-derived test suite covering all RFC 6330 MUST clauses
- High coverage of SHOULD clauses (target 90%+)
- Conformance matrix with per-section compliance scoring
- Requirement traceability mapping test cases to RFC clauses
- Edge case and error condition systematic coverage
- Integration with conformance harness for automated execution

## Validation Criteria

- Coverage matrix shows ≥95% MUST clause coverage
- All tests execute through conformance harness successfully
- Traceability mapping verified between tests and RFC requirements
- Performance on CI: full test suite completes in <10 minutes
- Zero false positives: failing tests indicate real conformance issues

## Dependencies

- Requires: RFC 6330 clause matrix for systematic requirement enumeration
- Requires: Conformance test harness infrastructure
- Builds on: Reference implementation differential testing for validation

## Time Estimate

12 hours (comprehensive test implementation + coverage validation + traceability)

title: [reality-check-wave2][web][sse] Implement true streaming SSE with request-region disconnect proof
description:
Live architectural follow-up for `asupersync-o74l7u`.

Current proven reality:
- `src/web/sse.rs` exposes `Sse` as a bounded list of `SseEvent` values serialized into one `text/event-stream` response body.
- `tests/e2e_web.rs` proves the current SSE support class with scenario `bounded-sse-batch-response` and `streaming=false`.
- This is useful for small finite event responses, but it is not true long-lived SSE streaming and does not yet model client disconnect/backpressure through a request-region-owned stream.

Goal:
Implement true streaming SSE for the web framework without weakening the current bounded batch API or request-region invariants.

Requirements:
- Add a streaming SSE response type/API that emits events incrementally instead of materializing the full response body up front.
- Tie stream lifetime to `RequestRegion` cancellation so client disconnect cancels the producer, drains resources, and leaves no tasks/obligations/handles leaked.
- Preserve bounded defensive controls: max event bytes, heartbeat/comment cadence, backpressure policy, producer cancellation budget, and stable overflow diagnostics.
- Keep the existing bounded `Sse` batch response supported and documented as finite/single-shot.
- Do not import axum/warp/hyper or add a Tokio dependency to the runtime crate.

Proof required:
- Unit tests for event order, comments/heartbeats, max event/byte bounds, producer error propagation, and cancellation while producing.
- Request-region tests proving disconnect closes the stream region and leaves before/after task and obligation counts unchanged.
- Extend `tests/e2e_web.rs` or add a focused E2E runner that logs `bead_id`, `scenario_id`, `route`, `method`, `middleware_stack`, `extractor_set`, `response_kind`, `streaming=true`, `client_disconnect_at`, `region_count_before`, `region_count_after`, `obligation_count_before`, `obligation_count_after`, `expected_status`, `actual_status`, `expected_body_digest` or chunk digests, `actual_body_digest` or chunk digests, `verdict`, and `first_failure`.
- Update README/docs only after true streaming behavior is implemented and the proof runner passes through `rch`.

Exit:
The web framework support matrix can truthfully distinguish finite bounded SSE batch responses from true request-region-owned streaming SSE, and `asupersync-o74l7u` can be closed without hiding this boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Child beads asupersync-o74l7u.1.1, asupersync-o74l7u.1.2, and asupersync-o74l7u.1.3 are closed in order.
- Streaming SSE API emits events incrementally under request-region ownership while preserving the existing bounded finite Sse API.

title: [bug-hunt] codec/length_delimited.rs decode does not consume length-prefix bytes on max_frame_length error — infinite re-emission of the same Err on repeated poll
description: src/codec/length_delimited.rs:222-226 LengthDelimitedCodec::decode reads the length prefix via decode_head(&self, src: &BytesMut) which CANNOT consume bytes (immutable borrow), then calls adjusted_frame_len(raw_len)? which returns Err if the parsed length exceeds max_frame_length (line 194-198). The Err propagates without advancing src. The next FramedRead poll re-decodes the SAME header bytes, re-produces the SAME Err, ad infinitum until the caller observes the error and closes the FramedRead. Suggested fix: introduce a `poisoned: bool` field on LengthDelimitedCodec; on the first frame-length error, set poisoned=true and have subsequent decode() calls short-circuit to Err without re-reading. Fail-closed semantics — the stream is unrecoverable after a malformed length prefix anyway. Severity MEDIUM (caller-recoverable by closing the FramedRead but easy to mishandle in retry loops).
close_reason: DecodeState::Skip(u64) added; on adjusted_frame_len failure the codec consumes the header bytes via src.split_to and transitions to Skip(raw_len). Subsequent decode() calls drain min(remaining, src.len()) bytes per call until Skip(0), then transition to Head and continue the loop. Err is returned exactly once per oversized frame. 3 regression tests cover header consumption + repeat-poll-doesn't-reemit + skip-state-persists-across-chunked-arrival.

title: quic_native standalone handshake drivers and the retained final_flight resend byte-identical packets on PTO (packet-number reuse, RFC 9000 12.3; sibling of djz660)
description:
## Defect (sibling of djz660; source-audited at origin 21f947faf, SapphireHill)
The public standalone handshake drivers resend byte-identical protected packets. That reuses packet numbers, which RFC 9000 section 12.3 says an endpoint MUST NOT do within a packet number space.

- handshake_driver.rs retransmit_handshake_flight (~1526) resends `last_flight` verbatim through endpoint.send_batch.
- client_handshake_over_udp calls it on every receive-timeout PTO (~1603), when a stale packet is ignored (~1692), and when a batch produced no new output (~1728).
- server_handshake_over_udp calls it the same way (~1807, ~1835, ~1843, ~1881).
- The client keeps its last flight as `final_flight` (~1590, ~1741; jmri58 wedge recovery). The data plane resends it after the handshake: udp_connection.rs ~617 and atp transport_quic/native_link.rs ~6362 (take_final_flight). Those packets are also byte-identical.

Consequence: a peer that already processed the first copy suppresses the duplicate by packet number. So when the peer's ACK (or, for final_flight, its HANDSHAKE_DONE / 1-RTT progress) was lost, the retransmission cannot elicit new progress, and recovery falls back to the peer's own timers or ends in the flight-budget failure.

## Fix design
djz660 (managed admission) adds QuicHandshakeDriver::assemble_handshake_packet_at(segment, offset, dst, src, pn) and next_crypto_offset(level). Reuse them:
1. Drive loops: record each sent packet's (level, CRYPTO offset, chunk) next to last_flight. A retransmission rebuilds them with fresh packet numbers from the loop's packet_number counter, with the same offsets and data, and the same datagram sizes, since Initial padding re-applies.
2. final_flight: keep the plan and the destination/source CIDs instead of the bytes. take_final_flight is pub, so ADD a sibling API (for example a retained-flight handle with a `rebuild(next_packet_number)` method) rather than changing its signature (v0.4.3 gate). Migrate udp_connection.rs and native_link.rs to it, and keep take_final_flight working for external callers.
3. Keys: once a space's keys are discarded, skip that space's packets (RFC 9001 section 4.9: the data is implicitly acknowledged).

## Tests
- Drive loops: a scripted silent peer captures two consecutive PTO flights. Decrypted with a real peer driver, every packet number in the second flight is new (the peer's received_handshake_packet_numbers grows by the flight size, and all new numbers are greater than the old), and the CRYPTO bytes are the same. Old-red: identical bytes.
- final_flight: two rebuilds from the data plane carry distinct, increasing Handshake packet numbers.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Test-fixture coupling found while designing the fix (SapphireHill). tests/quic_native_handshake_udp_loopback.rs HandshakeDropProxy::spawn_with_server_deduplication drops server datagrams whose BYTES were already seen. real_tls13_final_ack_does_not_retransmit_client_finished relies on that: its comment says byte-identical server retransmissions are removed so the post-handoff receive isolates the final ACK, and it asserts progress.handshake_flights_retransmitted == 0.

Once server retransmissions carry fresh packet numbers, their bytes differ. The proxy forwards them, the client's data plane sees a retained-flight long-header packet, calls retransmit_final_flight, and that assertion would fail for a reason unrelated to the behaviour under test.

The fixture must change with the fix, deduplicating by decrypted (packet type, CRYPTO offset, length) rather than raw bytes, or by packet type and payload length plus a server-side flight counter. Otherwise the test must drain the retained flight before the measured receive. Do NOT weaken the == 0 assertion. The test's intent (the final ACK itself never triggers a Finished resend) stays exactly the same.

Implementation sketch (drive loops): send_pending_flight records each chunk's (segment, next_crypto_offset) plus dst/src CIDs next to the packets. A driver method rebuilds the flight with assemble_handshake_packet_at under fresh numbers from the loop's packet_number and replaces retransmit_handshake_flight at all 7 call sites. driver.final_flight keeps the packets (take_final_flight is unchanged public API). The data-plane rebuild of final_flight is part 2: udp_connection.rs keeps `protection`, which already authenticates Handshake packets (authenticated_handshake_ack_only), so a free long-header CRYPTO assembler over the provider can re-protect there.

Part 2 scope, mapped at origin f9c089320 (SapphireHill). The retained final flight has THREE consumers, and each resends the stored bytes:
1. src/net/quic_native/udp_connection.rs retransmit_final_flight (NativeQuicUdpConnection; AuthenticatedQuicParts.final_handshake_flight from driver.take_final_flight()).
2. src/net/quic_native/connection_manager.rs ~712-734: a managed handoff (NativeQuicUdpHandoffParts -> authenticated state final_handshake_flight / pending_final_flight_packets / last_final_flight_retransmit) re-queues the same Vec<OutgoingPacket> with final_handshake_flight: true.

Each consumer owns packet protection with Handshake keys: AtpPacketProtection::protect_packet_now plus header_protection_mask_now, and the managed router's handle.packet_protection. Plan:
(a) Factor the driver's long-header CRYPTO assembly into a pure builder (header, Initial padding, CRYPTO frame at an explicit offset) plus a protection step over a small trait implemented for the driver provider and for AtpPacketProtection.
(b) The driver retains RetainedHandshakeFlight {crypto: Vec<(HandshakeSegment, u64)>, dst_cid, src_cid, initial_token, next_packet_number} beside final_flight, as a new pub(crate) take. take_final_flight (pub) is unchanged.
(c) Each consumer rebuilds under next_packet_number, advancing it per packet.
Caution: native_link.rs lines are referenced by the ambient-authority audit snapshot (src/audit/snapshots/...ambient_authority_inventory_v1.snap), so edits there shift pinned locators. That target is already red (bi2462.147.4); coordinate a re-bless. The loopback proxy fixture already dedupes by type and length (part 1), so part 2 needs no fixture change there.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SapphireHill, 2026-09-27: part 2 value reassessment. Result: deprioritized to P3 and released. Nothing is wrong with the design in the earlier comment; the functional payoff is close to zero.

The retained final flight is the client's Handshake-level Finished (plus its ACK). The data plane resends it only while no HANDSHAKE_DONE or 1-RTT progress has arrived. Two cases:
(a) The server never received the first copy. Then the server has not seen those packet numbers, so the byte-identical resend is accepted as new. PN reuse costs nothing here.
(b) The server received it. It then confirms the handshake and discards its Handshake keys (RFC 9001 sections 4.9.2 and 4.1.2). A resend under a fresh PN is just as undecryptable to it as the byte-identical copy. Recovery depends on the server retransmitting HANDSHAKE_DONE in 1-RTT, not on anything the client can put in a Handshake packet.

So a rebuild cannot elicit progress that the identical resend misses. That is unlike part 1, where Initial and Handshake keys are still live on both sides. What remains is RFC 9000 section 12.3 hygiene: a sender MUST NOT reuse a PN. A byte-identical resend under the same PN and key reuses the AEAD nonce only with identical plaintext and AD, so it leaks nothing and is indistinguishable from network duplication. The cost of the fix is three consumers, each with its own Handshake-key protection path (udp_connection, the connection_manager handoff, and the ATP native_link). native_link.rs locators are pinned by the ambient-authority audit snapshot, which is already red for re-bless (bi2462.147.4).

Worth revisiting only if a peer implementation is observed to treat duplicate Handshake PNs as a protocol violation, or when native_link is next refactored and the rebuild can ride along.

FILED 2026-07-26 by SapphireHill, carried forward from br-asupersync-d8aiqa so it
is not lost when that bead closed. This is the one item of d8aiqa I did NOT do,
because it is a scope/infra decision rather than a code fix.

THE GAP: with `--features kafka`, tests/kafka_producer_idempotence_audit.rs has
ZERO producer coverage. Its three real tests are all `#[cfg(not(feature =
"kafka"))]`; the only two that survive the feature —
`audit_kafka_producer_idempotence_implementation` and `run_audit` — are pure
`println!` and assert nothing. So enabling the very feature the file is named for
turns it into a no-op that always passes.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIXES DON'T APPLY:
  - The dedup property cannot be restored here. Integration tests compile as
    downstream consumers, where send() fails closed with FeatureDisabled by
    design (br-asupersync-w2p2a0). It was re-homed in-crate under d8aiqa as
    messaging::kafka::tests::deterministic_broker_does_not_deduplicate_idempotent_retries,
    but that test is `#[cfg(not(feature = "kafka"))]` too — it exercises the
    deterministic harness, which is precisely what `--features kafka` replaces.
  - tests/integration/kafka_real_broker.rs DOES hold real assertions, but they are
    env-gated behind REAL_KAFKA_TESTS and therefore never run in CI either.

So under `--features kafka` the producer path has no automated coverage at all,
from any file.

THE DECISION NEEDED (pick one, explicitly):
  a) Stand up a Kafka broker in CI (testcontainers or a service container) and
     drop the REAL_KAFKA_TESTS env gate for that lane. Highest fidelity, real
     infra cost, and rdkafka pulls a C toolchain.
  b) Keep the gate but make the skip LOUD and tracked — a lane that reports
     "kafka producer coverage: SKIPPED, 0 assertions" rather than a green target
     that silently asserted nothing. Cheap, honest, does not close the gap.
  c) Accept the gap explicitly with a documented no-claim boundary in the proof
     manifest/status artifacts, so nothing can cite `--features kafka` as
     evidence of producer correctness.

Whichever is chosen, the failure mode to avoid is the current one: a target that
compiles and passes under a feature while asserting nothing, which is
indistinguishable from coverage unless someone reads the cfgs
(br-asupersync-c6ppu4).

RELATED: br-asupersync-d8aiqa (re-homed the property; this is its remaining item),
br-asupersync-w2p2a0 (the fail-closed boundary), br-asupersync-z2kt29 (integration
tests never see the default feature surface), br-asupersync-c6ppu4.

title: [bug-hunt] sync/pool: PooledResource::Drop has no return-side health check — broken connections poison idle pool
description:
src/sync/pool.rs PooledResource<R>::Drop (line 548-552) unconditionally calls return_inner, which sends the resource back to the pool's idle set via PoolReturn::Return. There is NO validation gate on the return path:

  impl<R> Drop for PooledResource<R> {
      fn drop(&mut self) {
          self.return_inner();
      }
  }

The pool DOES support an opt-in health_check_on_acquire flag (used at lines 1670-1685), but:

  (a) That flag defaults to false in PoolConfig.
  (b) Even when enabled, it only runs at acquire-time. A connection that broke DURING the holder's use (network blip mid-query, server-side connection close after the holder finished but before they drop, broken stored procedure that left the connection in a bad transaction state) will be returned to idle silently. The next acquirer who happens to NOT have health_check_on_acquire enabled gets the broken connection.

The correct discipline is for the caller to explicitly call .discard() on a known-broken resource, but:
  * Callers frequently miss the discard call on error paths (`?`-propagation drops the PooledResource which auto-returns).
  * Panic paths definitely never call .discard() — the Drop runs and silently re-pools the broken connection.

Suggested fix shapes (any one):
  (a) Add health_check_on_return: bool to PoolConfig (default false for backwards-compat). When true, PooledResource::Drop calls a return-time validator before sending Return; failed validation sends Discard instead. Validator runs synchronously inside Drop (no async), so it must be cheap (e.g. a TCP-level connection-alive check, NOT a query round-trip).
  (b) Track a 'tainted' bit on PooledResource that callers set on error paths; Drop checks the bit and routes to Discard. Less automatic but cheaper than (a).
  (c) Document that callers MUST .discard() on every error path; emit warn! from PooledResource::Drop when the resource was held > 5s with no method calls (heuristic for 'caller likely didn't get a clean response').

Severity HIGH because the failure mode silently degrades pool quality over time — stale connections pile up in idle, every acquirer eventually hits one, leading to mysterious 'connection reset' errors that look like server-side problems but are actually client-pool bookkeeping.

Audit context: filed via /multi-pass-bug-hunting on src/sync/pool.rs pass 3 (connection lifecycle: validate, return, drop). Passes 1 (Pool::acquire fairness under saturation) and 2 (cancel-mid-acquire releases queue position) found NO issues — try_get_idle and reserve_create_slot both correctly check pos < available (FIFO preserved), and WaiterCleanup::Drop (line 1595-1640) properly removes the waiter and wakes the next eligible one when an acquire is cancelled mid-flight.
close_reason: PooledResource::Drop now dispatches on a new is_broken bool flag. New mark_broken(&mut self) API lets callers flag broken resources without consuming them — Drop then routes through discard_inner (PoolReturn::Discard) instead of return_inner (PoolReturn::Return), preventing broken connections from poisoning the idle pool on ?-propagation or panic unwinds. is_broken() getter for observability. mark_broken is idempotent. Default unflagged behaviour unchanged. 3 regression tests cover: routes-to-discard, unflagged-still-returns, idempotent.

- Compressed streams with embedded null bytes
- Very long compression streams to test streaming behavior

title: Observability export audit: LoadSheddingTrace/Logs/Exporter drop failed batches uncounted, flush leaves an aged backlog, OTLP queue admits unencodable batches, governor cache truncation, tracestate empty members
description:
Read-only audit of the OTLP export path and the pressure governor on origin/main 07608dadb (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-03). SapphireHill re-read H1 and M1 before fixing them. None of these paths is driven by in-crate production code. They are all public API that a user wires up, and the runtime never builds a PressureGovernor.

## Being fixed (SapphireHill, round 14)
- H1 for LoadSheddingTraceExporter (src/observability/otlp_trace_exporter.rs): process_queue dropped, uncounted, every batch whose export failed. A retryable failure now keeps the batch ahead of the queue; InvalidData is counted as dropped.
- M1 for the same type: process_queue stopped once a batch was older than batch_timeout, so flush left a backlog queued and returned Ok. The time limit now runs from the start of the call, and flush exports every batch pending when it began.

## Open
- H1, the same loss in src/observability/otel.rs (feature metrics): LoadSheddingLogsExporter::process_queue (~5257) and LoadSheddingExporter::process_queue (~5770) export with `?` after dequeuing. Their ExportError (a message struct) says nothing about retryability. A fix needs a retry slot plus either a retryability hint on otel's ExportError (additive) or retrying every failure up to a bound.
- M2: src/observability/otel/queued.rs admits batches the encoder always refuses. The limits it does not check at admission are:
  - more than 1000 points per metric (otlp_proto.rs:37);
  - more than 65,536 fields per request (protobuf_wire.rs:86);
  - a body over 4 MiB while the queue admits 8 MiB.
  export() returns Ok, delivery then fails without any I/O, the whole snapshot is retired, and run_queued stops. Fix: in enqueue_metrics/enqueue_logs, pre-encode (or bound points per metric, fields and bytes) before admitting. Test: 1001 labelled points for one counter name; export() must return Err.
- L1: the pressure governor caches pressures as (p*10000) as i64. A truncated value is more permissive than the fresh one (0.7001 is cached as 0.7000 and gives Admit instead of AdmitWithBackpressure), and SwarmPressureGovernor always decides from that cache. Fix: cache exact f64 bits in AtomicU64.
- L2: check_enhanced_admission returns Err(internal) instead of Reject when the envelope budget runs out, after admissions_total has already been incremented. Its budget sums are unchecked: they wrap in release builds, and in debug builds the overflow panic poisons the RwLock.
- L3: an empty tracestate list member ("rojo=...,", "a=1,,b=2", which W3C allows) fails OwnedOtlpTraces::collect for the whole collection. Fix: drop empty members after trimming.
- From the wire-parser audit: OTLP trace and metrics export uses ProtobufWireLimits::for_message_size, whose fixed 65,536-field cap binds before the byte cap. For example, one span with 128 events of 128 attributes (about 170 KB) fails with WireEnvelopeExceeded. Fix: use for_message_size(n).with_max_fields(n) at the exporter encode sites.

Checked and sound (per the audit): otlp_proto field numbers, wire types and enums against opentelemetry-proto; partial_success handling; retry of 408/429/502/503/504 with a capped Retry-After; BoundedExportQueue drop accounting; queued.rs wake and cancel mechanics; multi.rs fan-out; the governor cannot wedge the runtime (state.rs:2145 uses new_without_pressure_governor).
