title: [reality-check-wave2][fs] Complete filesystem API parity and cancellation semantics
description:
Complete filesystem API parity and cancellation semantics for the in-progress fs lane.

Background and evidence:
README.md marks Filesystem APIs as in progress/early/mixed. src/fs contains real modules for file, open_options, metadata, read_dir, path_ops, buf_reader, buf_writer, lines, vfs, uring, and test helpers. The current implementation often routes through spawn_blocking_io or optional io_uring, with Vfs abstractions for real filesystem and deterministic tests. Users need a coherent fs support class with cancellation, cleanup, error mapping, and virtualized proof rather than a directory full of partial APIs.

Scope:
- Inventory the tokio::fs parity surface the project intends to support: File, OpenOptions, read/write/seek/sync/truncate, metadata/symlink_metadata, read_dir, create_dir/remove/rename/copy, read_to_string/write, buffered readers/writers/lines, Vfs, and io_uring where feature-enabled.
- Implement missing parity or explicitly mark unsupported operations with stable diagnostics and owner beads.
- Prove cancellation cleanup: pending blocking operations, pending io_uring completions, directory iterators, buffers, and Vfs operations must not leak tasks, file handles, obligations, or temp fixtures.
- Preserve platform-specific boundaries and no-file-deletion rules. Test-owned temp cleanup must be bounded and explicit.

Unit tests required:
- Happy path, empty input, invalid path, permission/error mapping, symlink behavior, large file/chunk boundaries, read_dir ordering/disposition, and buffer line edge cases.
- Cancellation tests for open/read/write/sync/read_dir/buf operations and io_uring stale completion handling where available.
- Vfs tests proving UnixVfs and any virtual/lab Vfs have equivalent semantics for supported operations.

E2E/script proof required:
Add a filesystem parity script or integration runner that logs bead_id, scenario_id, api, backend, platform, feature_flags, temp_root, operation, bytes_expected, bytes_actual, metadata_expected, metadata_actual, cancellation_point, cleanup_status, unsupported_reason, verdict, and first_failure.

Validation:
Use rch exec for rustfmt, focused fs tests, feature-gated io_uring tests where supported, and scoped clippy. Record exact unsupported platform skips.

Non-goals:
Do not delete arbitrary filesystem paths. Do not promise full cross-platform parity where the platform cannot support it. Do not add Tokio/fs dependencies to the runtime crate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Filesystem parity inventory names every supported tokio::fs-equivalent operation and every explicit unsupported/platform-scoped operation.
- Unit tests cover happy path, empty input, invalid paths, permission/error mapping, symlink behavior, chunk boundaries, read_dir ordering/disposition, buffered lines, Vfs equivalence, and cancellation for supported APIs.
- io_uring boundary child asupersync-3jh6i2 is closed, including stale-completion safety and deterministic pass/skip artifacts for io_uring feature/platform support.
- E2E/script proof logs the required fs parity schema fields, including backend, platform, feature_flags, temp_root, operation, cleanup_status, unsupported_reason, verdict, and first_failure.
- Tests never delete arbitrary filesystem paths; cleanup is test-owned, bounded, explicit, and audited.
- Validation uses rch exec for focused fs tests, feature-gated io_uring lanes where available, rustfmt/check/clippy as appropriate, and records unsupported platform skips exactly.

title: ★Authenticated source-first fast path (the DEFAULT path uses HMAC auth)
description: ★CRITICAL correctness+perf gap. The source-first fast path (try_complete_from_source_symbols — direct memcpy of systematic source symbols, the win that AVOIDS O(K²) inactivation decode on clean links) must work on the DEFAULT path, which uses per-symbol HMAC-SHA256 auth. Isomorphic + byte-identical. Profile clean-link DEFAULT-AUTH transfer before/after (expect large win if fast path was being bypassed under auth). Record ledger.

title: [mock-code-finder] Add one-command aggregate proof runner and evidence dashboard
description:
Background: Each subsystem lane now has its own proof/e2e script, and the final signoff bead requires those scripts. That still leaves a usability gap: future maintainers should not need to remember six commands, artifact locations, policy scans, and how to merge JSONL evidence by hand.

Goal: add a single mock-code-finder proof runner that executes or orchestrates all domain proof scripts and no-mock/stub policy checks, validates their JSONL against the shared logging contract, and emits one user-readable summary plus one machine-readable aggregate artifact.

Required behavior: support a default local mode, an rch-backed mode for Rust validation commands, a CI mode with deterministic paths, and a dry-run/list mode that shows exactly which child proofs and policy scans will run. The runner must preserve each child script's detailed artifacts rather than flattening away important evidence. It must fail nonzero when any required proof fails, when a script emits malformed JSONL, when a required subsystem emits zero scenarios, when evidence_quality is missing, or when a blocked/unsupported result lacks blocker/context details.

Required aggregate report fields: run_id, git_sha_or_tree_state, started_at/finished_at, invoked_by_bead, child_bead_id, subsystem, command, scenario_count, pass/fail/blocked/unsupported/expected_fail/fixture_only counts, first_failure_line, artifact paths, policy scan counts, and final verdict. The human summary should be concise enough for a release/signoff comment but detailed enough to identify the failing subsystem without opening raw logs.

Testing requirements: unit tests for JSONL parsing, schema validation, count aggregation, nonzero/zero-scenario handling, malformed child output, blocked evidence with and without blocker IDs, redaction checks, and command selection/dry-run behavior. E2E tests should run against small fixture child scripts that simulate pass, fail, blocked, unsupported, and malformed outputs with verbose logs so the runner's behavior is deterministic and debuggable.

User value: this turns the mock-code-finder closure from a set of expert-only commands into one reproducible proof entry point that operators and future agents can trust.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- The runner has default, CI, rch-backed, and dry-run/list modes.
- It invokes or orchestrates every domain proof script plus the no-mock/stub policy checks without hiding child artifacts.
- It validates all emitted JSONL against asupersync-qlvtin and fails nonzero on malformed output, zero scenarios, missing evidence_quality, missing blocker context for blocked/unsupported cases, or any required child failure.
- It emits one machine-readable aggregate artifact and one concise human summary with per-subsystem counts, artifact paths, first failure, policy scan counts, and final verdict.
- Unit tests cover parser, aggregator, redaction, malformed child output, zero-scenario output, blocked/unsupported context, dry-run command selection, and nonzero exit behavior.
- E2E fixture scripts simulate pass, fail, blocked, unsupported, expected_fail, fixture_only, and malformed child runs with detailed deterministic logs.
notes: Third plan-space review 2026-05-05: this remains the right bottleneck after domain proof scripts and policy cleanup because it converts expert-only evidence into a user-operable proof entry point. Do not implement it as a thin shell wrapper that hides child failures. The aggregate runner must preserve child artifacts, validate every child JSONL record with asupersync-qlvtin, enforce zero-scenario/malformed/missing-quality/missing-blocker failures, and emit both machine and human summaries. Unit tests should cover parser, aggregator, child command matrix, redaction, malformed output, zero scenarios, blocked/unsupported context, nonzero child exit, and dry-run/list selection. Fixture e2e scripts must simulate pass, fail, blocked, unsupported, expected_fail, fixture_only, and malformed child runs with detailed logs. The final user value is one command that tells a maintainer what is live, degraded, unsupported, or blocked without reading the original audit plan.
close_reason: Added aggregate mock-code-finder proof runner with local/rch/ci/list/dry-run/self-test modes, qlvtin JSONL validation, child artifact preservation, aggregate JSON/human summaries, and deterministic fixture tests for pass/fail/degraded/malformed cases.

title: [security-distributed] RegionSnapshot replay gate lacks origin/epoch provenance
description:
Attack vector:
- `src/distributed/bridge.rs:854-898` accepts inbound snapshots using only `snapshot.sequence` vs `last_applied_inbound_sequence`.
- `src/distributed/snapshot.rs:104-126` defines `RegionSnapshot` with `region_id`, `timestamp`, and monotonic `sequence`, but no origin replica identity, steward epoch, lease/generation, or vector-clock provenance.
- A fresh or restarted peer with watermark 0 can therefore accept a captured `sequence == 1` snapshot for the same `region_id` from an old authority branch, and any peer that loses its local watermark can be steered onto a stale-but-in-order snapshot stream with no provenance mismatch signal.

Why this matters:
- The current gap check fixes out-of-order jumps, but not stale-branch replay. A scalar per-region counter is only safe if the branch authority is also authenticated and monotonic across restarts. That is not represented in the snapshot itself.

Fix direction:
- Add authenticated origin/steward identity plus epoch or causal/version-vector metadata to `RegionSnapshot` (or its signed envelope).
- Track accepted inbound high-water marks per `(origin, epoch)` instead of one global scalar.
- Reject snapshots whose provenance does not dominate or match the currently accepted branch; force explicit resync on branch mismatch.

Relevant lines:
- `src/distributed/bridge.rs:854-898`
- `src/distributed/snapshot.rs:104-126`
close_reason: Added origin/epoch snapshot provenance, replay gate, and stale-epoch regression

title: [http-deepest-10th] h2/stream.rs:409-435 recv_headers trailer scenario does not reject pseudo-headers — RFC 9113 §8.1 violation
description:
src/http/h2/stream.rs:409-435 (recv_headers) — the server-side check for malformed trailers validates that trailers MUST have END_STREAM, but does NOT validate that trailers MUST NOT contain pseudo-headers. RFC 7540 §8.1.2.1 / RFC 9113 §8.1: "Trailers MUST NOT include pseudo-header fields."

Sibling of the connection.rs:884-927 finding. Same root cause — the trailer detection path knows it's a trailer (because headers_complete was already set on the stream) but the pseudo-header validator is invoked without that context, so it cannot reject pseudo-headers that should be forbidden in trailers.

Repro:
  T0 — server sends response HEADERS, stream goes HalfClosedLocal.
  T1 — peer sends HEADERS with END_STREAM, containing `:status 200` (a pseudo-header masquerading as a trailer).
  T2 — recv_headers passes the END_STREAM check (line 411-434) and the state-machine transition (line 455-456).
  T3 — pseudo-header `:status 200` is delivered to the application as a "trailer", confusing intermediaries that might re-canonicalise the response.

Impact: cache poisoning via :status mismatch (one status code in headers, another in trailers — caches that prefer the later instance get the wrong status); smuggling via :method on the request side; HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 downgrade gateways that fold trailers into headers may re-emit a malformed frame downstream.

Fix direction:
  1. In recv_headers, after detecting trailer scenario (headers_complete already true, END_STREAM set), scan the decoded headers list for any name starting with ':' and reject the stream with PROTOCOL_ERROR.
  2. Or: thread the trailer flag into validate_h2_pseudo_headers per the sibling bead, and have ONE validator handle both sides.
  3. Regression test: server-side recv_headers with a trailer carrying `:status 200`; assert PROTOCOL_ERROR returned.

Severity MEDIUM — same reasoning as the connection.rs sibling. Both should be fixed in the same commit so the validation is uniform across decode and recv paths.

Source: /multi-pass-bug-hunting on src/http/* DEEPEST 10th-pass (2026-04-26).

title: [conformance] gRPC: missing message framing + max-message-size + status-mapping + gRPC-Web frame format coverage
description:
gRPC-over-HTTP/2 + gRPC-Web conformance gaps in tests/conformance/grpc*. Concrete missing vectors:

(1) gRPC §5.1 — Message framing prefix [compression-flag:1 | unused:7] + 4-byte length + payload. Test matrix for compression flag set/unset with various algorithms (gzip, deflate, none) accepting/rejecting per server's grpc-encoding response.

(2) gRPC §5.1 — Max-message-size enforcement: grpc-max-send-message-length / grpc-max-receive-message-length header semantics; 4 MiB default; oversized rejection with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED.

(3) gRPC §6.0 — Status code matrix: error → status mapping (client deadline → DEADLINE_EXCEEDED=4; cancel → CANCELLED=1; etc.). Currently grpc_status.rs covers code values; no error-condition-to-code mapping tests.

(4) gRPC-Web §2 — Framed request body: 4-byte big-endian length prefix + frame format. No test vectors for framing.

(5) gRPC-Web §3 — Trailers-only response with grpc-status in HEADERS (1xx rejection); 0eyf7t/of0l5f are h2 trailer pseudo-header beads but cover a different concern.

(6) gRPC §7 — Custom metadata: -bin suffix binary encoding, ASCII restriction on non-bin headers, metadata size limits.

Fix direction: tests/conformance/grpc_message_framing.rs + grpc_max_message_size.rs + grpc_status_mapping.rs + grpc_web_frame_format.rs.

title: [bug-hunt] database/mysql: cancel-mid-query has no KILL QUERY path — server keeps executing cancelled queries
description:
Severity: MEDIUM (server-side resource leak, locks held indefinitely; no protocol corruption).

src/database/mysql.rs has no analogue to the PG `CancelRequest`
path that br-asupersync-gvkj1r just landed for postgres. The
existing cancel-handling pattern is:

    if cx.checkpoint().is_err() {
        return Outcome::Cancelled(...);
    }
    self.inner.closed = true;
    self.write_all(...).await?;

On cancel mid-query the connection is marked closed and the TCP
socket is shut down (via `PgConnectionInner::Drop` at line 1099-1102
or one of the explicit close paths). The MySQL server, however, has
no way to learn the client gave up — it continues executing the
SELECT / UPDATE / etc. until it hits an interrupt point of its own
volition or until it tries to write the next packet and notices
`EPIPE`. For long-running queries (analytics, missing-index scans,
optimizer mistakes) this can be many seconds of held locks and
wasted CPU per cancelled query.

MySQL's wire protocol does NOT have a one-frame analogue to PG's
`CancelRequest`. The standard cancellation mechanism is to open a
SECOND fully-authenticated session and send:

    COM_QUERY  "KILL QUERY <connection_id>"

then close. `<connection_id>` is the in-flight backend's session ID,
which is already saved on the connection at `inner.connection_id`
(set at line 1205 from the HandshakeV10 packet — see `parse_handshake`
around line 1242).

Fix shape:
  1. Save the connect options (host, port, user, password, ssl_mode,
     bounded connect_timeout) on `MySqlConnectionInner` at connect
     time, mirroring the `CancelTarget` struct introduced for
     postgres in br-asupersync-gvkj1r.
  2. Add `fire_kill_query(&self)` that spawns a detached
     std::thread, performs a fresh TCP+TLS+auth handshake, sends
     `COM_QUERY "KILL QUERY <connection_id>"`, reads the OK packet,
     sends COM_QUIT, closes. Bound by a hard 1–2s timeout cap so an
     unreachable / overloaded server can't stall the cancel path.
  3. Hook `fire_kill_query` BEFORE the `stream.shutdown` on the
     cancel branch of every query / execute path (or via a shared
     `cancel_in_flight` helper that does not currently exist in this
     file — adding one would also reduce duplication in the cancel
     code across the existing query/execute/prepare methods).
  4. Best-effort: errors deliberately swallowed, the original cancel
     path completes with `Outcome::Cancelled` regardless.

Note: this is heavier than the PG fix because MySQL needs a full
re-handshake before sending KILL QUERY, vs PG's stateless 16-byte
CancelRequest. The cost is acceptable on the cancel path (cold,
rare, bounded) but should not be made implicit on every cancel —
worth gating behind a config flag or a connection-level option.
close_reason: Implementation landed in 61967135c. (1) thread_id capture from HandshakeV10 was already present (connect_with_options:1205, pub fn connection_id:2420). (2) New pub async fn cancel_in_flight_query(&self, cx) opens a fresh MySqlConnection via stored MySqlConnectOptions, sends 'KILL QUERY <thread_id>' as COM_QUERY via execute(), drops the killer socket. MySqlConnection gains Option<MySqlConnectOptions> field populated by connect_with_options; all 10 test fixtures updated to set options: None,. Caller must pass a non-cancelled cx (Cx::for_request_with_budget or reaper region) — documented. Cargo check + lib-test build pass.

title: Implement deterministic PRNG utility (no deps)
description:
# Deterministic PRNG Utility (No Dependencies)

## Purpose
The lab runtime and some combinators require deterministic tie-breaking and deterministic jitter. We must not introduce ambient randomness or rely on external heavy RNG crates unless justified.

This task introduces a tiny internal PRNG used *only* when determinism is required:
- lab scheduler tie-breaking among runnable tasks
- deterministic jitter/backoff (retry, hedge) in lab mode
- any future schedule exploration tooling

## Constraints
- No `rand` crate in core unless explicitly justified.
- Must be reproducible across platforms and Rust versions.
- Must be fast and simple.

## Plan-of-Record Design
### Algorithm
Use a small, well-known PRNG suitable for deterministic testing:
- `SplitMix64` as a seed expander and/or direct generator
- optionally layer `xoroshiro`-class generator if needed later

SplitMix64 is attractive because:
- trivial to implement
- good statistical properties for non-crypto use
- deterministic by construction

### API
```rust
pub struct DetRng {
    state: u64,
}

impl DetRng {
    pub fn new(seed: u64) -> Self;
    pub fn next_u64(&mut self) -> u64;

    /// Deterministic range selection.
    /// Must be unbiased (use rejection sampling) unless we explicitly accept modulo bias.
    pub fn gen_index(&mut self, len: usize) -> usize;

    /// Deterministic u32 convenience.
    pub fn next_u32(&mut self) -> u32;
}
```

### Unbiased `gen_index`
- Implement rejection sampling to avoid modulo bias for small domains.
- Document performance tradeoff and why it’s acceptable in lab scheduling.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Same seed yields identical sequences across runs.
- `gen_index(len)` never panics for `len > 0` and is deterministic.
- Unit tests cover:
  - golden vectors for a few seeds
  - determinism
  - range correctness

## Testing
- Unit test: generate first N outputs for a fixed seed and compare against hard-coded expected values.
- Property test: `gen_index(len) < len` for many seeds/lengths.
close_reason: Implemented in src/ (tests + clippy clean)

title: Implement TraceReplayer for Lab runtime
description:
## Overview

Implement the TraceReplayer that feeds recorded decisions back into the Lab runtime to achieve exact execution replay.

## Background

This is the core replay mechanism. Instead of making scheduling decisions, the Lab runtime in replay mode reads the next decision from the trace and executes it.

## Design Requirements

### Exact Replay
- Every scheduling decision must match recorded
- Time advances must match exactly
- I/O results must be replayed, not simulated fresh

### Divergence Detection
- If execution diverges from trace, detect and report
- Divergence means bug or trace corruption
- Provide helpful error message with divergence point

### Stepping Support
- Support "step to next event" for debugging
- Support "continue to breakpoint" (e.g., specific tick or task)
- Support "run to completion"

## Implementation

```rust
pub struct TraceReplayer {
    reader: TraceReader,
    current_index: usize,
    mode: ReplayMode,
}

pub enum ReplayMode {
    Run,                    // Run to completion
    Step,                   // Stop after each event
    RunTo(Breakpoint),      // Run to specific point
}

pub enum Breakpoint {
    Tick(u64),
    Task(TaskId),
    Event(usize),           // Event index
}

impl TraceReplayer {
    pub fn new(reader: TraceReader) -> Self;
    pub fn next_event(&mut self) -> Option<&TraceEvent>;
    pub fn verify_matches(&self, actual: &TraceEvent) -> Result<(), DivergenceError>;
}

pub struct DivergenceError {
    pub index: usize,
    pub expected: TraceEvent,
    pub actual: TraceEvent,
    pub context: String,
}
```

## Lab Runtime Integration

```rust
impl LabRuntime {
    pub fn replay(trace: TraceReader) -> ReplayRuntime;
}

pub struct ReplayRuntime {
    lab: LabRuntime,
    replayer: TraceReplayer,
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Replayer correctly feeds decisions to Lab runtime
- [ ] Divergence is detected with helpful error
- [ ] Step mode allows event-by-event execution
- [ ] Complex scenario replays exactly
- [ ] Performance is similar to normal Lab execution

title: FlowControlMonitor public deadlock detector has no channel-owner input
description: The public FlowControlMonitor cannot detect any deadlock: its DFS needs channel_to_task edges, but add_channel_owner/remove_channel_owner are private dead-code methods and record_event never populates them. The unit test masks the complete feature failure by mutating detector internals directly. A public-event-only cycle such as BackpressureApplied(C1,consumer=T2), BackpressureApplied(C2,consumer=T1), ProducerBlocked(T1,C1), ProducerBlocked(T2,C2) reports no PotentialDeadlock. Wire backpressure consumer ownership into an owner set/refcount lifecycle and add explicit public owner acquired/released events for other controls if needed; derive graph edges from canonical live records; remove the cycle on release. Apply deadlock_detection_threshold_s to cycle age—the current detector reports immediately despite the named threshold—and deduplicate reports per live cycle episode. Add public-API-only two-task/two-channel detection, below-threshold, threshold-crossing, owner-release, and multi-owner tests; remove the private-internals-only oracle. No production call sites currently use this monitor, so severity is P2 despite the advertised feature being entirely inert. No duplicate/fix in history; b083bd588 introduced the unreachable graph. Independently confirmed by two source reviews on 2026-07-15.

- src/lab/** (deterministic test runtime)
- src/runtime/** (scheduler, state management, panic isolation) 
- src/sync/** (lock ordering system, mutex, rwlock implementations)
- src/channel/** (MPSC, broadcast, watch channels)

**Key findings:**

1. **SOPHISTICATED DEADLOCK PREVENTION SYSTEM ALREADY IN PLACE:**
   - E→D→B→A→C lock hierarchy (Config→Instrumentation→Regions→Tasks→Obligations) 
   - src/sync/lock_ordering.rs enforces ordering with runtime panic on violations
   - ContendedMutex and RwLock implementations track lock rank and validate ordering
   - Cross-module validation rules (Cancel-before-obligation, Cx-before-cancel, etc.)

2. **ACTUAL VULNERABILITY FOUND & FIXED:**
   - **br-asupersync-r9f0xn**: std::sync::Mutex usage in async contexts (FIXED)
   - Replaced with parking_lot::Mutex in src/runtime/panic_isolation.rs
   - Other instances were in test code and deemed safe

3. **CORRECT PATTERNS OBSERVED:**
   - Address-based lock ordering in src/runtime/scheduler/local_queue.rs prevents AB-BA
   - Cancel-during-acquire handling in src/sync/rwlock.rs with proper state cleanup
   - Test coverage for lock ordering violations with expected panics

4. **NO SERIOUS DEADLOCK HAZARDS FOUND:**
   - No mutex held across .await points in production code
   - No AB-BA deadlock patterns in production code
   - No self-deadlock patterns (non-recursive mutex re-entry)
   - No reader-upgrade deadlocks in production (only in tests)

**Audit quality:** COMPREHENSIVE - Used systematic static patterns from deadlock-finder-and-fixer skill, searched for all 9 deadlock classes.

**Recommendation:** asupersync has exemplary deadlock prevention. The existing lock ordering system should be maintained and used as a reference implementation.
close_reason: Completed: Static deadlock audit using deadlock-finder-and-fixer skill. Found sophisticated existing prevention system, fixed one std::sync::Mutex hazard. asupersync is deadlock-resistant.

title: Swarm-scale pressure admission and proof-lane hardening program
description:
Context:
Asupersync is now being operated by large multi-agent swarms on large machines. The runtime already has pressure atlases, proof-lane manifests, RCH fallback contracts, admission decision scripts, chaos DSL contracts, and operator runbooks. The next step is to compose those surfaces into a user-facing pressure/admission/proof-lane hardening program instead of leaving operators to infer safety from scattered artifacts.

Problem:
A reported stale exact cargo filter ran for hours and consumed extreme memory on another machine. Current main no longer contains that exact test, and the remote proof ran zero tests. That is valuable diagnosis, but zero-test proof lanes must not become reassuring evidence. Separately, release prep is blocked by peer-owned dirty source files, which shows that operators need better preflight visibility into dirty-tree ownership, file reservations, proof-lane freshness, memory/time envelopes, and pressure-control decisions.

Goal:
Make swarm-scale operation safer and more ergonomic without weakening runtime invariants. The program should preserve no-local-fallback validation through RCH, fail closed on stale proof evidence, provide deterministic operator reports, and make pressure/admission decisions inspectable with comprehensive unit tests and e2e scripts that emit detailed diagnostic logs.

Non-goals:
Do not implement a new executor. Do not add Tokio to the runtime crate. Do not make local Cargo fallback acceptable for heavy validation. Do not replace existing pressure or proof artifacts; compose and harden them. Do not remove current features or narrow the existing validation surface.

Success shape:
Future agents can run one or a small set of documented proof/admission commands and get an evidence-backed answer: which lanes are admissible, which are stale or blocked, who owns conflicting dirty files, what memory/time envelope applies, which tests actually ran, and which exact unit/e2e checks prove the guard behavior.
close_reason: Swarm-scale pressure admission and proof-lane hardening program complete. All listed blocker dependencies are closed, and the final third-wave child asupersync-ol11aa.9 is closed and pushed. The completed program now includes topology-aware admission, stale proof evidence debt reporting, brownout/no-win lab scenarios, runtime pressure integration, dirty-tree/reservation correlation, proof-lane memory/time envelopes, zero-test fail-closed handling, operator runbooks, profiling receipts, no-mock e2e guardrails, reservation-aware fallback work finding, crashpack receipts, second-wave certification, and third-wave swarm operations guardrails. Top-level closeout is tracker-only; validation is covered by the child close reasons and pushed commits.

title: Add deterministic large-host topology corpus for swarm pressure planning
description:
Context:
The current swarm pressure/admission program has strong aggregate evidence for large hosts, RCH lanes, dirty-tree ownership, and proof freshness. The remaining blind spot is machine topology. A 64-core/256GB host can behave very differently depending on socket count, NUMA memory locality, cache hierarchy, SMT, cgroup limits, and competing RCH slots. Operators should not have to infer these differences from raw worker names or ad hoc host notes.

Goal:
Introduce a deterministic topology corpus that models the large-host shapes we care about without probing the live machine at test time. The corpus should make topology an explicit input to admission, scheduling, and proof-lane planning work instead of treating CPU and memory as flat scalar totals.

Implementation shape:
- Add a versioned JSON artifact describing representative host profiles: single-socket high-core, dual-socket NUMA, constrained cgroup, memory-pressure degraded, and remote-worker queue contention.
- Include CPU cores, SMT threads, NUMA nodes, memory per node, cache-sharing groups, expected RCH slot shape, and known non-claims.
- Add a helper or report generator that emits stable JSON/Markdown summaries from the corpus without running Cargo or profilers.
- Add contract tests that validate schema fields, deterministic ordering, topology non-claims, and that every profile declares a safe fallback when topology data is missing.
- Document how this corpus feeds future topology-aware scheduler/resource placement, proof-lane admission, and large-host capacity decisions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Profiles cover at least 64c/256GB and 2-socket NUMA scenarios plus degraded/cgroup-limited variants.
- Tests prove the artifact does not claim fresh benchmark evidence or live host measurement.
- E2E/report script emits detailed deterministic logs and a stable receipt for each profile.
- All heavy validation commands are documented as RCH remote-required lanes.
- No runtime stdout/stderr or ambient host probing is introduced into core code.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic large-host topology corpus with read-only helper, E2E receipts, docs, negative fixture, and RCH-verified contract coverage.

title: Teach proof admission to account for topology-aware worker and lane placement
description:
Context:
The admission planner already considers dirty trees, RCH remote-required policy, pressure envelopes, worker warmth, and memory/time limits. It does not yet reason about topology-sensitive contention: two lanes can look admissible by aggregate CPU/memory while fighting for the same NUMA node, cache domain, disk, or worker slot class.

Goal:
Extend the proof/admission decision layer so it can consume the large-host topology corpus and produce topology-aware recommendations: admit, queue, split, or route lanes based on topology fit rather than scalar capacity alone.

Implementation shape:
- Consume the deterministic topology corpus as an optional input to the existing proof-lane admission decision/report path.
- Add stable reason codes for topology fit, topology missing, same-domain contention, split-lane recommended, and remote worker preferred.
- Preserve the current fail-closed behavior: missing or stale topology evidence must not become a green proof signal.
- Update fixtures for high-core admit, same-socket contention, low-memory NUMA node, stale topology input, and unrelated dirty-tree blockers.
- Emit operator-facing JSON/Markdown that distinguishes topology scheduling advice from correctness validation evidence.

Acceptance criteria:
- Contract tests cover admit/queue/split decisions with and without topology input.
- Dirty-tree and stale-proof blockers still override topology warmth or placement advice.
- The planner never treats topology warmth as correctness evidence.
- Report output includes exact input artifact IDs, non-coverage, and recommended RCH command envelopes.
- The implementation remains deterministic and does not introduce local Cargo fallback.
close_reason: Implemented topology-aware proof admission receipts with corpus-backed advisory placement, fixtures, docs, and E2E smoke.

comments.author: PinkStream
comments.text: Phase 6 refinement: include a bounded E2E runner/fixture in this bead, not just unit contracts. The E2E should feed topology-aware admission inputs through the planner and emit deterministic JSON/Markdown logs for admit, queue, split, stale-topology, and dirty-tree-override cases. The receipt must say topology placement advice is operator guidance, not correctness proof evidence.

title: Bridge SLO policy brownout decisions into runtime pressure seams
description:
Context:
The repository has a rich SLO policy model with admission, brownout, no-win, and proof report vocabulary. It is valuable as an artifact-level contract, but the next useful step is to connect it to actual runtime pressure seams without creating ambient global policy or weakening structured concurrency.

Goal:
Design and implement a narrow runtime bridge that lets explicit `Cx`-scoped capabilities ask a compiled SLO policy whether optional work should run, brown out, or fail closed under pressure. The bridge must preserve no ambient authority, deterministic lab testing, and cancellation/quiescence invariants.

Implementation shape:
- Add a typed runtime policy/admission object that is passed explicitly through `Cx` or a capability-bearing context, not a global singleton.
- Define request/decision records for required work, optional work, cleanup/finalizer work, and proof/reporting work.
- Ensure brownout decisions never drop obligations silently; optional work must either not start or be cancelled/drained with an explicit receipt.
- Add lab-runtime tests for admit, brownout, no-win, cancellation during brownout, and region close quiescence.
- Document how the bridge relates to existing SLO policy artifacts and what it explicitly does not prove.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests cover monotonic latency objectives, optional work ordering, no-win fallback, and explicit capability flow.
- Lab tests assert no task leaks, no obligation leaks, loser drain, and region close implies quiescence under brownout.
- The bridge does not introduce stdout/stderr in core runtime code.
- No Tokio or other executor dependency is added to the runtime crate.
- RCH validation lanes are listed for focused tests, all-target check, clippy, and fmt.
close_reason: Implemented explicit Cx-scoped SLO runtime bridge with required/optional/cleanup-finalizer/proof-reporting decisions, lab smoke quiescence, cancellation/no-win receipts, docs, and RCH validation.

comments.author: PinkStream
comments.text: Phase 6 refinement: include an E2E/lab smoke surface in addition to unit tests. It should drive explicit Cx-scoped policy decisions through required work, optional work, cleanup/finalizer work, and proof/reporting work, then log admitted/browned-out/no-win decisions plus final quiescence. Non-claim: this bridge is not a global policy engine and not a fresh performance benchmark.

title: Build brownout and no-win lab E2E scenarios for structured-concurrency pressure
description:
Context:
A runtime SLO bridge is only useful if it is exercised under realistic pressure transitions. Operators need deterministic evidence that brownout and no-win decisions preserve structured concurrency rather than creating orphan work, obligation leaks, or misleading success reports.

Goal:
Create a no-mock lab E2E suite that drives pressure transitions across required work, optional work, finalizers, proof/reporting work, and cancellation races. The suite should produce stable logs/receipts that explain exactly what was admitted, browned out, rejected, cancelled, drained, and finalized.

Implementation shape:
- Build bounded lab scenarios for healthy admit, optional-work brownout, no-win rejection, cancellation mid-brownout, and recovery after pressure clears.
- Include structured receipt rows with task counts, region IDs, obligation state, cancellation/drain counts, final quiescence, and operator interpretation.
- Keep all scenarios deterministic; avoid wall-clock sleeps and unbounded memory/CPU loops.
- Add an E2E shell runner that emits JSON/Markdown plus detailed deterministic logs under `target/`.
- Tie each scenario to the SLO bridge and topology/admission artifacts without claiming fresh performance benchmark results.

Acceptance criteria:
- Contract tests validate receipt schema and non-claims.
- E2E runner output is stable across repeated runs with the same fixtures.
- Tests assert no task leaks, no obligation leaks, loser drain, and region close quiescence.
- Failure fixtures show missing drain/finalizer evidence causes a red receipt.
- Heavy validation uses RCH remote-required cargo lanes.
close_reason: Brownout/no-win lab E2E receipts added with drain/finalizer/quiescence evidence; focused and full SLO contract RCH lanes plus check/clippy/fmt passed.

title: Build stale proof evidence debt graph and supersession report
description:
Context:
The project now has many proof artifacts: manifests, status snapshots, proof reuse receipts, freshness checks, worker health receipts, admission reports, and closeout messages. Individual guards exist, but operators still need one deterministic graph that explains which evidence is current, stale, superseded, blocked, zero-test, or merely advisory.

Goal:
Create a proof evidence debt graph that consumes the existing artifact and receipt surfaces and produces a ranked report of proof debt. It should tell future agents what must be rerun, what can be cited narrowly, what is superseded, and what must never be cited as correctness evidence.

Implementation shape:
- Add a helper that reads approved repo-local proof artifacts/fixtures and emits a deterministic graph of lanes, artifacts, touched surfaces, HEADs, blockers, and supersession edges.
- Add reason codes for stale-head, dirty-overlap, zero-tests, local-fallback, missing-envelope, superseded-by-newer-artifact, advisory-only, and blocked-by-peer-reservation.
- Include JSON and Markdown reports with ranked operator actions and exact RCH command envelopes.
- Add fixtures for clean current evidence, stale but reusable narrow evidence, superseded evidence, zero-test evidence, and dirty-tree overlap.
- Keep the helper read-only; it must not run Cargo, mutate Git, or rewrite artifacts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Contract tests prove the graph preserves non-claims and never upgrades advisory evidence to correctness evidence.
- Reports cite exact artifact IDs, lane IDs, touched surfaces, and recommended rerun commands.
- The graph handles missing optional artifacts fail-closed with actionable blockers.
- Documentation explains how to use the report before release prep or large swarm closeout.
- Validation commands are RCH remote-required where Cargo is involved.
close_reason: Implemented proof evidence debt graph helper, contract fixture, docs, README pointer, and Rust contract; validated focused RCH contract, all-targets check, clippy, and fmt.

comments.author: PinkStream
comments.text: Phase 6 refinement: add a bounded E2E report runner for the proof debt graph. It should consume fixture roots with mixed current/stale/superseded/zero-test evidence and emit stable JSON/Markdown logs. Non-claim: the graph ranks proof debt and rerun needs; it does not certify workspace health or replace broad RCH gates.

title: Generate minimal crashpack repro receipts from failed RCH proof lanes
description:
Context:
When a broad RCH proof lane fails, agents often spend time re-reading long logs and guessing the smallest useful rerun. The repo has proof runners, freshness receipts, worker health receipts, and some crashpack/repro tooling, but failed proof lanes should produce a standard minimal-repro receipt directly tied to the failing lane.

Goal:
Build a deterministic helper and contract suite that converts failed RCH proof-lane receipts/logs into a minimal repro plan: smallest cargo target/filter, source surface, suspected ownership, required environment, blocked/non-blocked classification, and next rerun command.

Implementation shape:
- Consume saved proof-runner/RCH log fixtures rather than invoking cargo directly.
- Parse first hard compiler/test failure, timeout, ENOSPC, SSH failure, retrieval failure, zero-test mismatch, and local-fallback refusal cases.
- Emit JSON/Markdown receipts with minimal command, why it is minimal, what evidence it does and does not prove, and which peers/reservations may own the blocker.
- Add fixtures for compile error, test assertion, timeout after first failure, worker disk pressure, retrieval timeout after pass, and zero-test proof.
- Integrate with existing proof evidence debt/freshness vocabulary where possible instead of inventing parallel status terms.

Acceptance criteria:
- Contract tests validate every classification and the first-hard-error extraction.
- The helper is read-only and deterministic; it does not run Cargo or touch Git.
- Recommended rerun commands preserve `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1`, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, and no-local-fallback semantics.
- Reports include actionable next steps without overstating workspace health.
- Docs explain how this fits release-prep and shared-main blocker triage.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic proof-lane failure repro receipt helper, contract artifact, docs, README wiring, and RCH validation; also fixed clippy blockers surfaced by all-target validation.

comments.author: PinkStream
comments.text: Phase 6 refinement: add an E2E fixture runner that converts representative failed RCH/proof-runner logs into minimal repro receipts and deterministic Markdown. Cover compile error, test failure, timeout, ENOSPC, retrieval timeout after pass, zero-test, and local-fallback refusal. The helper remains read-only and must not run Cargo itself.

title: Add reservation-aware fallback work finder for blocked or epic-only ready queues
description:
Context:
In shared-main swarm sessions, the ready queue can legitimately contain only an epic or a bead that is blocked by active peer ownership. Agents need a deterministic way to keep moving without entering communication purgatory or touching files reserved by another lane.

Goal:
Create a reservation-aware fallback work finder that inspects `br` ready/open state, Agent Mail reservations/messages, dirty-tree ownership receipts, and approved planning/test-only surfaces. It should recommend safe next actions: wait, coordinate, run a planning bead, pick a docs/test-only task, reopen a truly stale in-progress bead, or stop with a precise blocker.

Implementation shape:
- Add a read-only helper with fixture-based inputs for ready queue, open epics, stale/in-progress issues, dirty-tree status, and Agent Mail reservation summaries.
- Classify cases: claimable ready task, epic-only ready queue, blocked-by-active-reservation, stale in-progress candidate, tracker-only dirt, source peer dirt, no useful bead, and planning fallback recommended.
- Emit JSON/Markdown with recommended action, forbidden actions, exact files to avoid, and whether a new bead should be created.
- Add contract tests and E2E fixture runner with detailed deterministic logs.
- Document how the helper complements `bv --robot-*`, `br --no-auto-import`, and Agent Mail reservations.

Acceptance criteria:
- The helper never recommends editing peer-owned dirty paths or creating branches/worktrees.
- It distinguishes blocked source lanes from safe tracker/planning lanes.
- It produces explicit blockers when no action is safe.
- Tests cover stale in-progress reopening only when inactivity and ownership evidence justify it.
- All Cargo validation for the contract suite is documented as RCH remote-required.
close_reason: Implemented reservation-aware fallback work finder helper, contract fixture, docs, README pointer, and RCH validation; also removed a stale unknown Clippy allow surfaced by all-target validation.

comments.author: PinkStream
comments.text: Phase 6 refinement: spell out non-claims and forbidden recommendations. The fallback work finder does not prove source correctness, does not authorize editing peer-reserved paths, does not create branches/worktrees, and does not override Agent Mail reservations. It only recommends safe next actions or explicit blockers from read-only tracker/mail/git fixtures.

title: Publish second-wave swarm control-loop certification bundle
description:
Context:
The first swarm-scale program has many useful proof/admission artifacts, but second-wave control surfaces will only be credible if they converge into one certification bundle. Operators need a single answer for whether topology-aware placement, SLO brownout seams, stale-proof debt, crashpack repros, and fallback work finding have all been proven and how their guarantees compose.

Goal:
Create a certification bundle that signs off the second-wave swarm control loop as an operator workflow. The bundle should aggregate the relevant artifacts, tests, E2E receipts, RCH command evidence, non-claims, and open blockers without pretending to be a release tag or broad workspace health proof.

Implementation shape:
- Define a versioned certification artifact that references the second-wave child beads and their proof receipts.
- Add a contract test that fails if required child evidence is missing, stale, local-fallback-only, zero-test, or advisory-only.
- Emit a Markdown operator summary with green/yellow/red sections and exact rerun commands.
- Include final non-coverage: not a performance benchmark, not a release publish proof, not a substitute for broad check/clippy/test gates, and not evidence for unrelated source surfaces.
- Add a bounded E2E script that assembles the bundle from fixtures and emits detailed logs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Certification cannot pass until topology corpus, topology-aware admission, SLO brownout bridge/e2e, stale-proof debt graph, failed-proof repro receipts, and fallback work finder are represented by current receipts.
- Tests reject stale HEADs, missing RCH remote-required envelopes, local fallback, and zero-test evidence.
- Operator docs explain exactly how to refresh the bundle before release prep or large swarm operation.
- The bundle is deterministic and does not run unbounded CPU/memory work.
close_reason: Implemented second-wave swarm control-loop certification bundle with deterministic helper, artifact, E2E runner, docs, contract tests, and remote-required validation.

title: [idea-wizard][ol11aa] Third-wave swarm operations guardrails
description:
Context:
This bead records the end-to-end idea-wizard pass run on 2026-06-06 after the second-wave asupersync-ol11aa subtasks were closed. Current evidence: br ready exposes only the ol11aa feature parent while bv --robot-next reports no single actionable item; the live tree also contains peer tracker dirt, long RCH proof lanes, and a recently-repaired stale in_progress population.

Phase 2, 30 -> 5 best ideas:
1. Stale in-progress bead reaper with dry-run evidence and inactivity policy.
2. br/bv ready-queue divergence detector so graph drift cannot hide actionable work or produce empty top-pick reports.
3. Reservation lease watchdog for long RCH proof lanes so file reservations do not expire while a valid remote gate is still running.
4. Machine-readable closeout evidence receipt tying bead state, mail thread, reservations, proof commands, remote worker evidence, pushed refs, and remaining peer dirt into one deterministic artifact.
5. No-mock e2e harness that exercises these operator guardrails with detailed logs and fail-closed assertions.

Phase 3, next best 10 retained for follow-up design space:
6. RCH quiet-phase progress and timeout forecast receipts.
7. Peer-dirt safe tracker staging preflight for shared-main commits.
8. Goal-completion audit checklist generator for long persistent objectives.
9. Agent Mail closeout linter for ack/reservation/thread hygiene.
10. Proof-lane cost estimator from historical RCH receipts.
11. Runtime pressure report digest for quick human review.
12. Worker topology drift detector for admission plans.
13. Release mirror verification receipt for main:master sync.
14. Crashpack minimization queue for repeated proof failures.
15. Cross-agent ownership heatmap for high-conflict files.

Overlap review:
Existing closed ol11aa subtasks already cover topology-aware admission, stale proof evidence debt, crashpacks, reservation-aware fallback work finding, runbooks, profiling receipts, no-mock e2e, and pressure telemetry. This third wave deliberately avoids replacing those surfaces. It focuses on operational guardrails exposed by the current session: stale work reaping, br/bv drift, reservation expiry during long RCH jobs, deterministic closeout receipts, and a combined e2e proof.

Success shape:
The child beads form a self-contained graph that can be implemented incrementally. Each child must include deterministic unit or contract tests, and the combined e2e bead must emit enough logs for future agents to diagnose why a stale bead was or was not reopened, why br/bv disagreed, whether reservations were renewed or reported, and whether a closeout receipt proves the claim being made.
close_reason: Third-wave swarm operations guardrails complete. All child beads asupersync-ol11aa.9.1 through .9.7 are closed and pushed: stale in-progress reaper, br/bv graph drift detector, reservation lease watchdog, closeout receipt helper, RCH quiet-phase receipt, combined no-mock e2e guardrail suite, and operator runbook/signoff checklist. Parent closeout is tracker-only; validation is covered by the child bead close reasons and pushed commits, including remote RCH all-targets check/clippy for .9.6 and .9.7.

title: [ol11aa.9] Add stale in-progress bead reaper with dry-run evidence
description:
Build a deterministic helper and contract surface for finding clearly stale in_progress beads assigned to inactive agents, showing evidence, and reopening them only when policy says it is safe.

Motivation:
During the 2026-06-06 ol11aa continuation, 27 February in_progress rows were clearly abandoned and had to be reopened manually. That should become a repeatable, fail-closed operator workflow instead of an ad hoc JSONL repair.

Required behavior:
- Accept an inactivity threshold, current timestamp, active-agent snapshot, and bead rows as explicit inputs.
- Produce a dry-run report listing candidate ids, assignee, last update age, active-agent evidence, and the exact mutation that would be applied.
- Refuse to reopen beads with recent updates, live assignees, missing timestamps, malformed rows, or ambiguous ownership.
- Apply reopen only when explicitly requested; default must be report-only.
- Preserve append-only / no-peer-dirt assumptions around .beads/issues.jsonl and document how to stage the result without absorbing unrelated tracker dirt.

Tests required:
Unit or contract tests for stale candidate selection, live-agent exclusion, malformed row refusal, dry-run output stability, and apply-mode mutation. Include a no-mock e2e script or fixture with detailed logs showing candidate evidence and final status changes.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic stale in-progress bead reaper helper, contract artifact, operator docs, and Rust contract test; validated py_compile, JSON/Markdown helper output, jq, rustfmt, diff check, focused RCH contract test, all-target check, fmt check, and all-target clippy.

title: [ol11aa.9] Detect br/bv ready-queue divergence and graph freshness drift
description:
Build a deterministic report and contract tests for disagreement between br ready and bv robot outputs.

Motivation:
On 2026-06-06, br --no-auto-import ready --json showed asupersync-ol11aa as the only ready feature parent, while bv --robot-next returned no actionable item and bv --robot-triage showed no top picks. Future agents should get a clear explanation instead of guessing whether work exists, the graph is stale, or the ready item is an epic-only parent.

Required behavior:
- Compare br ready, br list status counts, bv --robot-next, bv --robot-triage quick_ref, and bv graph health using structured inputs.
- Classify cases: consistent actionable, epic-only ready, stale graph snapshot, DB/JSONL freshness mismatch, dependency-blocked despite br-ready, and tracker command failure.
- Emit a compact JSON report plus human-readable markdown summary with next action guidance.
- Fail closed for missing command provenance or mismatched data hashes.
- Link the report to proof-lane admission so zero-top-pick states are not treated as no-work states without explanation.

Tests required:
Golden fixtures for the live br-ready/bv-empty pattern, normal consistent ready output, stale data hash mismatch, and broken JSON output. Include detailed logs in any e2e wrapper so an agent can cite the report in Agent Mail closeout.
close_reason: Implemented read-only tracker graph drift report helper, contract artifact, operator docs, and Rust contract test; validated py_compile, script JSON/Markdown output, jq, diff check, focused RCH contract test, all-target check, fmt check, and all-target clippy.

title: [ol11aa.9] Add reservation lease watchdog for long RCH proof lanes
description:
Add an operator guardrail that detects when a long-running RCH proof lane may outlive its Agent Mail file reservations and either renews them through the MCP API or emits a fail-closed warning that closeout evidence is incomplete.

Motivation:
Required all-target check/clippy lanes can run for many minutes on cold workers. If reservations expire while an agent is still validating, peers may reasonably assume the files are free and collide with the lane. The guardrail should make reservation lifetime explicit in proof/admission workflows.

Required behavior:
- Accept active reservation records, proof-lane manifest envelope, current time, expected remaining duration, and command provenance as inputs.
- Classify reservation state as sufficient, renew-needed, expired, missing, or conflicting.
- Provide a dry-run mode and a renew mode that calls Agent Mail only when explicitly requested.
- Never hide a missing or failed renewal; closeout receipts must show whether reservation coverage existed for the entire proof interval.
- Keep the implementation outside the runtime crate and preserve no-Tokio/default-runtime guarantees.

Tests required:
Deterministic fixtures for sufficient TTL, near-expiry renewal, expired reservations, missing reservations, and renewal failure. Include an e2e-style script with detailed logs for a simulated long RCH lane.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic reservation lease watchdog helper, fixture, docs, and RCH-validated contract proof.

title: [ol11aa.9] Emit machine-readable swarm lane closeout receipts
description:
Define and implement a deterministic closeout receipt schema for swarm proof/admission lanes. The receipt should let a future agent or release coordinator verify what actually happened without reading a chat transcript.

Required receipt fields:
- bead id, title, pre/post status, assignee, and close reason.
- Agent Mail identity, thread id, messages sent, ack-required messages handled, and active-agent snapshot.
- File reservations held, renewed, released, and any gaps during validation.
- Proof commands with exact argv/env, RCH remote-required status, worker identity, command exit, tests-run counts where applicable, target dir class, and artifact digest/source fingerprint when available.
- Git evidence: starting HEAD, committed HEAD, origin/main ahead-behind check, push result, and main:master mirror verification.
- Remaining dirty-tree files classified as owned, peer-owned, or intentionally unstaged.

Fail-closed rules:
Missing remote-worker evidence, failed proof commands cited as green, zero-test exact filters, expired reservations, or unverified pushed refs must make the receipt non-admissible.

Tests required:
Golden JSON/Markdown receipts for a successful lane, a failed RCH lane, an expired-reservation lane, and a peer-dirt shared-main lane. Include schema validation and deterministic ordering checks.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic swarm lane closeout receipt helper, contract artifact, operator docs, and Rust contract test; validated py_compile, jq, JSON/Markdown helper output, rustfmt, diff check, focused RCH contract test, all-target check, fmt check, and all-target clippy.

title: [ol11aa.9] Add RCH quiet-phase progress and timeout forecast receipts
description:
Add deterministic parsing and reporting for long quiet phases in RCH proof lanes so agents can distinguish a valid cold-worker compile from a hung or under-provisioned lane.

Motivation:
Several asupersync proof lanes spend many minutes with no stdout after reaching workspace crates or while retrieving artifacts. Agents currently have to infer whether to wait, poll, or restart. This should become explicit evidence in proof closeout and operator reports.

Required behavior:
- Parse RCH log milestones: worker selected, sync start/end, remote command start, crate phase, workspace crate phase, remote command finish, artifact retrieval, and final remote summary.
- Estimate quiet-phase class using lane envelope from artifacts/proof_lane_manifest_v1.json when available.
- Emit warnings for missing remote-required evidence, elapsed time beyond envelope, artifact retrieval stalls, or local fallback.
- Never treat quiet progress as success; it is only liveness/progress evidence until exit code and proof semantics are verified.

Tests required:
Golden parsers for successful cold clippy, failed cargo test, artifact retrieval stall, and local-fallback refusal logs. Include unit tests for timeout forecast boundaries and deterministic report rendering.

title: [ol11aa.9] Build no-mock e2e suite for swarm guardrail workflows

title: [fuzz] fuzz/fuzz_targets/auth_aead.rs: stale AuthKey::from_bytes call sites — bit-rot post q3terg API change, 6 sites won't compile
description:
fuzz/fuzz_targets/auth_aead.rs uses 'let key = AuthKey::from_bytes(input.key_bytes)' as a direct value at 6 sites (lines 68, 102, 187, 192, 237, 281), but the q3terg fix changed AuthKey::from_bytes to return Result<Self, AuthKeyError> for entropy validation (src/security/key.rs:173). The fuzz target is registered in fuzz/Cargo.toml ([[bin]] name='auth_aead') so cargo +nightly fuzz build auth_aead now fails with E0308 mismatched types — verified via 'rch exec -- cargo +nightly fuzz build --fuzz-dir fuzz auth_aead'.

Fix options:
  (1) Use AuthKey::from_bytes(...).expect('fuzz fixture key passes entropy check') and bias arbitrary input to ensure entropy bounds (>= 8 distinct bytes, hamming in [8, 248]). Most fuzz inputs from libfuzzer's mutation engine pass these bounds in practice (uniformly-random 32-byte buffers have ~30 distinct values and hamming ~128).
  (2) Use AuthKey::from_bytes_unchecked(...) which is pub(crate) — would require either re-exporting it under a #[cfg(fuzzing)] feature gate, OR moving the harness inside src/ where pub(crate) is reachable.
  (3) On Err, libfuzzer_sys::Corpus::Reject the input — keep the entropy-validation contract intact, only fuzz on inputs that pass the gate. This is the cleanest option: 'let key = match AuthKey::from_bytes(input.key_bytes) { Ok(k) => k, Err(_) => return libfuzzer_sys::Corpus::Reject };' (return type change required).

The other 5 affected fuzz targets that may have the same issue per grep: authenticated_mac_verification.rs, fuzz_security_mac_verifier.rs, raptorq_aead_envelope.rs, raptorq_symbol_authentication.rs, security_authenticated_hmac.rs, security_tag_boundary.rs, security_tag_verifier.rs, symbol_auth.rs — verify each via 'rch exec -- cargo +nightly fuzz build --fuzz-dir fuzz <name>' and apply the same fix shape.
close_reason: fixed: 4 fuzz targets handle Result-returning AuthKey::from_bytes via early-return-on-Err. Corpus::Reject equivalent.

title: [security-saas-refresh] web/response.rs: Redirect Location accepts protocol-relative URLs (//attacker.com) — bypasses naive same-origin checks AND triggers protocol-confusion redirects
description: src/web/response.rs:417 Redirect::into_response only strips CR/LF from the Location value but does NOT validate that the URL is well-formed or same-origin (already filed as bead 0hj233). A SPECIFIC sub-vector worth a separate bead: PROTOCOL-RELATIVE URLs that start with '//' (e.g., '//attacker.com/phish'). Browsers interpret these as 'use the current page's protocol, but switch to the new host' — they bypass naive same-origin checks that just verify the URL starts with '/' (a common but wrong heuristic). Concretely: a developer writes their own Redirect-safety wrapper as 'if uri.starts_with('/') { allow }', forgetting that '//attacker.com' ALSO starts with '/'. Combined with the general open-redirect issue (bead 0hj233), this is the SECOND foot-gun pattern callers hit when they roll their own validation. The library should provide a Redirect::to_relative_path constructor that explicitly validates: (a) starts with '/', (b) does NOT start with '//', (c) does NOT contain '\\' (Windows path-traversal vector some parsers normalize), (d) does NOT contain '://' anywhere (catches 'foo:javascript:...' style injection in some parsers). Severity HIGH because the '//' protocol-relative attack is the SPECIFIC pattern that defeats most hand-rolled defenses.
close_reason: Hardened Redirect strict-mode validator against protocol-relative bypasses. Added byte-level prefilter rejecting any byte outside 0x21-0x7E (rejects leading whitespace/tab/CRLF/NUL before starts_with(//) check). Added /%2f and /%5c percent-encoded second-character rejection. external_unchecked* escape hatches unchanged. 8 unit tests including all bypass shapes. title: OnceCell successful waits can inflate cancellation telemetry
description: WaitInit and CancelAwareWaitInit can read a pre-transition state, lose the waiter-mutex race to transition_out_of_initializing (which stores terminal state and drains), then register a stale waker after the drain because register_waker does not validate state under the mutex. Make registration predicate-aware while holding waiters (WaitInit only INITIALIZING, CancelAware only not INITIALIZED), return whether it registered, and preserve the double-check. Add deterministic hooked interleavings for both future types proving Ready, empty queue, no retained waker, and unchanged cancellation_count. title: OnceCell telemetry snapshot can combine incompatible states

title: OnceCell completion retains and duplicates waiter spill allocation
description: transition_out_of_initializing uses guard.waiters.drain(..).map(...).collect(). Move the whole waiter SmallVec out with mem::take under the mutex, then unlock and wake InitWaiter entries directly, eliminating the second allocation and releasing spill capacity after fanout. title: sync: OnceCell::set blocks the OS thread on an in-flight async initializer, deadlocking a current-thread runtime
description: src/sync/once_cell.rs:215-240 set() on Err(INITIALIZING) calls wait_for_init_blocking() (:507-522), a Condvar::wait loop. If the current initializer is an async task (get_or_init suspended at an .await in f()) on the same OS thread as the set caller (always on a current-thread runtime), the condvar wait blocks the only thread that could resume the initializer: permanent deadlock. Name gives no hint it blocks; tokio returns an error instead. InitGuard reset path is sound; the hazard is the blocking wait meeting a same-thread async initializer. FIX: make set() return an error/retry on INITIALIZING instead of blocking, or document the deadlock explicitly. Found by fresh-eyes channels/sync review 2026-07-14 (CONFIRMED path).

title: Oneshot clones and destroys stored Wakers under its mutex
description: src/channel/oneshot.rs moved wake calls outside the parking_lot mutex, but still clones, replaces, and clears Wakers while holding OneShotInner. OneShotInner::clear_waker assigns None under lock; receive terminal/cancel/drop/try_recv paths call it under lock; both receive futures replace inner.waker under lock; Sender::poll_closed and Receiver::poll_closed clone/replace their Wakers under lock. On terminal receive, value.take happens before clear_waker, so a panicking Waker destructor unwinds and drops the already-removed payload instead of returning it. title: [ALIEN][TRACE] Geodesic Schedule Normalization (Canonical Low-Entropy Replay)
description:
## Goal

Compute a *canonical representative schedule* for a Mazurkiewicz trace equivalence class that is *better than Foata flattening* for human debugging and replay.

- Input: a trace `e_0..e_{n-1}` plus an independence relation `I(e_i, e_j)`.
- Output: a deterministic linear extension (total order) of the induced partial order that minimizes a chosen cost (default: task-switch count) under deterministic tie-breaking.

This is a Phase-6 upgrade: Foata normal form gives canonical equivalence-class IDs, but does not optimize for "visual entropy" / context switches.

## Key definitions (self-contained)

- **Independence relation** `I`: symmetric, irreflexive; independent events may be swapped without observable change.
- **Dependency DAG / poset**: build edges `i -> j` for each `i < j` such that `NOT I(e_i, e_j)`.
- **Linear extension**: any total order consistent with the DAG.
- **Switch cost**: number of times the "active task" changes between adjacent events. We define a deterministic event-to-lane mapping (usually TaskId; global events use a pseudo-task key).

## Determinism + correctness constraints

- Must preserve all dependency edges (soundness).
- Must be deterministic across runs given identical trace + config.
- Must never use wall-clock time.
- Must not change the equivalence class semantics: output is a reordering *only of independent events*.

## Deliverables

- Trace -> poset builder (reusable for other tooling).
- Exact solver for bounded traces (A*/IDA* with admissible heuristic).
- Deterministic heuristic for large traces (fallback when exact is too expensive).
- "Galaxy-brain" optional debug ledger: show cost breakdown and why choice X was made.
- Tests: linear-extension validity + equivalence-class invariants + cost improvements on known patterns.

Geodesic normalization is fully implemented with 39 unit tests, 14 E2E tests, 6 benchmark groups.

title: [bug-hunt] grpc/web: WebFrameCodec silently ignores reserved flag bits 0x02..0x40
description:
src/grpc/web.rs WebFrameCodec::decode (line 247-272): the flag byte is checked only for bit 7 (TRAILER_FLAG = 0x80) and bit 0 (compression). Bits 0x02..0x40 are reserved per gRPC-Web spec for future protocol extensions but are silently ignored — no error, no log.

A future protocol version that uses (e.g.) bit 0x02 for some new framing semantic would be silently misinterpreted by this decoder as a regular data frame. Strict implementations should reject unknown reserved bits with a protocol error (or at minimum tracing::warn) so operator visibility into unexpected wire formats exists.

Suggested fix: define RESERVED_FLAG_MASK = 0x7E and reject if (flag & RESERVED_FLAG_MASK) != 0 with GrpcError::protocol("reserved gRPC-Web flag bits set: 0x{flag:02x}"). Severity LOW because real-world peers don't set those bits today, but tightening the parser is cheap defense-in-depth.
close_reason: RESERVED_FLAG_MASK = 0x7E added; WebFrameCodec::decode rejects any frame with bits 1..=6 set via GrpcError::Protocol BEFORE consuming the buffer. 5 regression tests cover legal-flag pass, every reserved bit reject, full mask reject, reserved + legal-bit overlap reject, and buffer-not-consumed-on-reject. Companion to br-nbryje.

title: [codec-bytes-bug-hunt] length_delimited.rs: integer overflow in reserve() call at encode()
description:
src/codec/length_delimited.rs:391

The encode() function computes header_len via saturating_add (safe), but then passes header_len + frame_len to dst.reserve() WITHOUT checking for integer overflow. 

Attack: set codec.length_field_offset = usize::MAX, encode any frame. header_len saturates to usize::MAX. Then header_len + frame_len wraps around to small value, causing reserve(small_value) instead of OOM or error. Could lead to memory corruption if caller expects frame to fit.

Fix: Replace line 391 with checked_add() that returns an Err if header_len + frame_len overflows.
close_reason: Fixed in e76c2e0f5: replaced saturating_add+unchecked-add pair in encode() reserve budget with checked_add on both header_len (offset + length_field_length) and total (header + frame). Both overflow paths return InvalidData; attacker-controlled length_field_offset near usize::MAX is rejected explicitly. Tests cover header overflow, total overflow, zero-length, and max_frame_length boundary.

title: [SCHEDULER-RELIABILITY] Scheduler Fairness and Starvation Detection
description:
GOAL: Create monitoring and testing framework for the three-lane scheduler to detect fairness violations and starvation patterns.

BACKGROUND: The three-lane scheduler (priority, normal, cooperative) must provide fair access to CPU time while respecting priority relationships. Starvation bugs can cause high-priority work to block low-priority work indefinitely, or priority inversion where low-priority work prevents high-priority work from running.

RATIONALE: Scheduler fairness is critical for predictable performance. Starvation bugs are often subtle and only manifest under specific load patterns. Automated detection and prevention is essential for a production-ready runtime.

IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH:
- Runtime metrics collection for task scheduling patterns
- Automated detection of starvation scenarios (tasks waiting too long)
- Priority inversion detection (high-priority blocked by low-priority)
- Load pattern generation for systematic fairness testing
- Integration with existing scheduler infrastructure
- Configurable thresholds for different violation types

KEY DETECTION CAPABILITIES:
- Task starvation detection with configurable timeouts
- Priority inversion identification and attribution
- Scheduling latency anomaly detection  
- Fairness metric calculation and monitoring
- Integration with structured logging for analysis
- Optional enforcement modes (metrics vs assertions)

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS:
- Minimal scheduler overhead for metrics collection
- Integration with three-lane scheduler implementation
- Deterministic testing support via lab-runtime
- Thread-safe metrics aggregation
- Statistical analysis of scheduling patterns

DELIVERABLES:

- Comprehensive test suite for starvation detection
- CI integration to prevent fairness regressions
- Documentation of expected fairness properties

SUCCESS METRICS:
- Detects all known starvation patterns
- Zero false positive fairness violations
- Measurable improvement in scheduling predictability
- Clear diagnostics for debugging scheduler issues

title: [RUNTIME-EPOCH] Runtime Epoch Consistency Tracker
description:
GOAL: Monitor runtime epoch boundaries to ensure state transitions happen atomically without tearing or inconsistency across modules, detecting when different parts of the runtime get out of sync.

BACKGROUND: Asupersync's runtime operates in epochs to maintain consistency across scheduler, regions, tasks, and obligations. Epoch transitions must be atomic across all modules. Epoch tears can cause subtle bugs where different modules see inconsistent runtime state.

RATIONALE: Epoch consistency is fundamental for deterministic behavior and state machine correctness. Inconsistent epoch views can lead to race conditions, lost events, incorrect scheduling decisions, and non-deterministic behavior in lab testing.

IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH:
- Instrument epoch transition points across all runtime modules (scheduler, regions, tasks, obligations)
- Maintain epoch consistency tracking state with module-level epoch counters
- Detect when modules fall out of sync during epoch transitions
- Provide detailed diagnostics about which modules are lagging or inconsistent
- Integration with structured logging for epoch transition analysis
- Support for both synchronous and asynchronous epoch transition verification

KEY DETECTION CAPABILITIES:
- Module epoch synchronization violations (modules operating on different epochs)
- Slow epoch transitions that cause temporary inconsistency windows
- Missing epoch transition notifications between modules
- State updates using stale epoch information
- Epoch rollback scenarios and their consistency implications
- Cross-module state synchronization failures during epoch boundaries
- Epoch advancement order violations (modules advancing out of order)

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS:
- Low-overhead epoch tracking suitable for production use (<1% overhead)
- Thread-safe epoch state management across all runtime threads
- Integration with existing runtime module interfaces in src/runtime/
- Deterministic epoch transition verification in lab runtime
- Structured logging of epoch transition timing and violations
- Configurable epoch consistency checking levels (strict vs relaxed)
- Memory-efficient epoch state tracking with bounded memory usage

SPECIFIC MODULES TO MONITOR:
- Scheduler (three-lane scheduler epoch transitions)
- Region table (region creation/destruction epochs)
- Task table (task lifecycle epochs)
- Obligation table (permit/ack/lease epochs)
- Timer wheel (timer epoch advancement)
- I/O reactor (reactor epoch synchronization)
- Cancel protocol (cancellation epoch consistency)

COMPREHENSIVE UNIT TESTS:
- Test epoch synchronization across all module pairs
- Test detection of each type of epoch inconsistency

title: [reality-check-wave2][examples] Publish capability-first user examples and smoke recipes
description:
Publish capability-first user examples and smoke recipes for every wave2 promoted surface so users can actually adopt the runtime, not merely inspect internal proof artifacts.

Background and evidence:
The wave2 beads focus correctly on implementation, unit tests, E2E proof, support matrices, and signoff. That still leaves a user-experience gap: a capability can be technically shipped and honestly documented while remaining hard for Rust, Browser Edition, service, or operator users to try safely. README tables and support matrices answer what is supported; examples and smoke recipes answer how a user should start and how an agent should verify the example still works.

Scope:
- Add or update minimal but realistic examples for the promoted wave2 capabilities: HTTP/3/QPACK dynamic behavior, RemoteRuntime production-backed lifecycle, Browser Edition Rust API, service-worker/shared-worker decisions or supported broker paths, browser-native MessageChannel/BroadcastChannel/WHATWG streams, web middleware/streaming, filesystem parity/cancellation, Redis/NATS/Kafka broker-backed flows, repaired conformance suites, formal evidence lookup, and massive-swarm profile diagnostics.

- Add smoke recipes that agents can run after implementation to prove examples compile/run without relying on closed bead status.
- Link examples to docs/support classes only after the technical proof and evidence registry confirm the capability is shipped or explicitly deferred.

- Static contract tests ensuring each wave2 capability has either a runnable example, a platform/broker-gated smoke recipe, or an explicit owner bead for why no public example is possible yet.

title: ATP-B1: Define ATP binary frame codec, varints, versioning, and canonical transcript
description: Define the ATP binary framing layer carried over native QUIC streams. Frames should be compact, length-bounded, versioned, fuzzable, and canonical enough for transcript hashes and deterministic replay.
design: Frame types include ClientHello, ServerHello, TransferOffer, TransferAccept, Chunk, AckRange, RepairGroup, RepairSymbol, Commit, Abort, Cancel, PathProbe, ProofRecord, and extension frames. The codec must reject unknown critical frames and preserve safe optional extensions.

- Transcript hash is stable across platforms and binds version, feature negotiation, capability-relevant fields, ReceivePlan-relevant fields where applicable, and idempotency keys.
- Unit/property tests cover every frame family, varint boundaries, canonical encoding, transcript updates, extension preservation/rejection, redaction, and failure taxonomy.
- Fuzz/e2e harnesses cover split frames, truncation, oversized payloads, reordered frames, duplicate frames, extension handling, resume transcript replay, and minimized failure artifacts.
- Logs/proof artifacts include frame family, schema version, transcript digest, parse/validation error class, redacted field summary, and replay/minimization pointer.
notes: Can proceed before native QUIC completion by using in-memory streams.
