title: no-mock scanner is per-FILE and prose-blind: 6 of 7 recent violations were false positives, and clearing them blessed 6 whole files (incl. a 22k-line transport) for the defect class the gate exists to catch
description:
FOUND 2026-07-26 by SapphireHill while closing br-asupersync-9fhmts.

THE GATE'S PRECISION IS THE PROBLEM, NOT ITS STRICTNESS. Of the 7 production_stub violations that had been blocking ci.yml's Check job (and, separately, keeping tests/no_mock_policy_contract.rs red), exactly ONE was real unfinished work (src/bin/atp.rs, the bond-pull ssh -L tunnel leg, now under an expiring waiver). The other 6 were the scanner matching PROSE or TEST CODE:

  - src/bin/dependency_verification_matrix.rs  -- the literal string "no-mock dependency-sovereignty scenario" inside a JSON rule the binary EMITS. The scanner matched its own policy vocabulary.
  - src/net/atp/sdk/bonded.rs                  -- a module doc CONTRASTING itself with another type ("...whose in-process driver is still a fail-closed stub").
  - src/net/atp/transport_quic/native_link.rs  -- a comment explaining a landed fix ("one junk UDP packet ... fake-expires a 360s idle timeout").
  - src/net/atp/transport_rq/mod.rs            -- a call to sha256_hex_placeholder() inside that file's #[cfg(test)] module.
  - src/net/udp.rs                             -- a comment describing the non-Windows no-op platform shim as a "stub".
  - src/grpc/server.rs                         -- Status::unimplemented(...), the canonical gRPC status for an unsupported request encoding; simply missing from the canonical_grpc_status_code classification it already belonged to.

An 86% false-positive rate is not a strict gate, it is a broken one -- and a broken gate is dangerous rather than merely annoying, because the cheapest way to make it green is to declare the false positives approved.

WHAT CLEARING THEM COST, WHICH IS THE ACTUAL DEBT THIS BEAD TRACKS. Coverage in scripts/check_no_mock_policy.py is resolved PER PATH, not per hit: coverage_for_path(path, category, ...) matches an allowlist pattern against the file path alone. So one justified line blesses the ENTIRE FILE for that category, permanently. Clearing these 6 therefore turned off production_stub detection for, among others:

  - src/net/atp/transport_rq/mod.rs           (~22,900 lines, the ATP RaptorQ transport)
  - src/net/atp/transport_quic/native_link.rs (~4,600+ lines, the native QUIC link)
  - src/grpc/server.rs

Those are precisely the files where a real stub would matter most. A future `// TODO: implement symbol auth` in transport_rq is now invisible to this gate. The 5 allowlist entries added under 9fhmts name this bead as their replacement_issue for exactly that reason.

TWO FIXES, INDEPENDENT AND BOTH WORTH DOING:

(1) cfg(test) awareness. AGENTS.md mandates inline `#[cfg(test)]` unit tests in every module ("Every module includes inline #[cfg(test)] unit tests alongside the implementation"), and the policy already classifies tests/** wholesale as intentional_test_double with 254 covered paths and zero violations. So the policy's own position is that test doubles are legitimate -- yet a test double written in the project's own mandated style, inside src/, is classified production_stub. That is a category error that penalizes the mandated test layout. Hits inside a #[cfg(test)]-gated module in src/ should not be production_stub. Implementation must be fail-CLOSED: if the test region's extent cannot be determined unambiguously (string/char/comment-aware brace matching that does not terminate), treat the hit as production code and let it violate.

(2) Text-narrowed allowlist entries. Add an OPTIONAL field to allowlist entries (e.g. `justified_text`: a list of regexes). When present, the entry covers the path only if EVERY flagged hit in that file matches one of the patterns; any unmatched hit falls through to violation. Backwards compatible -- entries without the field behave exactly as today. This is what lets src/net/udp.rs be allowlisted for the one sentence about the platform shim while a newly added `// TODO: implement` in the same file still fails the gate. It is also drift-resistant in a way line numbers are not: the justification travels with the text.

DO NOT "FIX" THIS BY SUPPRESSING COMMENTS. Suppressing all //-comment hits would make the gate green and gut it: `// TODO: implement this` is a comment and is the single most important thing the gate should catch. The distinction the scanner needs is prose-describing-other-code vs. prose-describing-this-code, which is not mechanically decidable -- hence the explicit per-entry justification in (2) rather than a blanket rule.

VERIFICATION for whoever picks this up: scripts/check_no_mock_policy.py ships two self-tests that must stay green, and they already cover the fail-closed direction:
  python3 scripts/check_no_mock_policy.py --policy .github/no_mock_policy.json --self-test-policy-fixtures
  python3 scripts/check_no_mock_policy.py --self-test-negative-fixture
Add fixtures for both new behaviors: a #[cfg(test)] hit that is NOT a violation, a same-file non-test hit that IS, a justified_text entry that covers its sentence, and an unjustified hit in the same file that still violates. Then re-run the gate and tests/no_mock_policy_contract.rs and confirm the 5 broad entries can be narrowed or dropped.

NOT PROPOSED: relaxing the term list, or making the gate advisory. The gate caught a real unfinished code path (the ssh -L tunnel leg) on this very run; the goal is to keep that signal while removing the noise that currently forces whole-file blindness.
close_reason:
FIXED both halves; buy-back proven end-to-end, not just asserted.

(1) #[cfg(test)] AWARENESS. scripts/check_no_mock_policy.py now lexes Rust before classifying. A fail-closed mask marks line/block(nestable)/raw-string/byte-string/char-literal positions so brace matching and attribute detection never trip over a brace inside a doc comment or a formatted string. Test-only regions are recognised for #[cfg(test)] and #[cfg(all(test, ...))] -- and deliberately NOT for #[cfg(any(test, ...))], which still holds in a non-test build. Every ambiguity resolves to production: unreadable file, unlexable source, an inner #![cfg(test)] anywhere but file scope, or an extent the cross-check does not confirm.

Braced extents are cross-checked against rustfmt layout (closing brace opens its own line at the attribute's indent column). That is a second independent witness for the extent the lexer computed, so a lexer that silently drifted past the real close cannot quietly widen a test region over production code -- the direction that would actually hide a stub.

Two extent rules were wrong on first pass and both were real Rust, found by running the whole tree rather than a fixture: (a) 'use crate::foo::{A, B};' opens braces that are part of a path, not a body, so item extent must key on a ';' at brace-depth 0; (b) '#![cfg(all(test, ...))]' is an inner attribute gating the whole file, not a following item -- that alone accounts for the 8 src/real_*_e2e_tests.rs files. A third bug was mine: a parent block's closing brace drove depth negative before the body-confirmation check could fire. Unresolved files went 10 -> 2 -> 0 across those fixes; the whole tree now resolves unambiguously, and tests/no_mock_policy_contract.rs asserts test_gated_undetermined_paths == 0 so a file that ever falls into the fallback is visible rather than silently over-reported.

Effect: 259 hits across 90 paths are now correctly excluded as test-gated. Verified by audit, not by the count moving -- I checked every detected region's head against an independent oracle. The one class that looked wrong (src/grpc/streaming.rs marking 'pub struct ResponseStream' / 'RequestSink' as test-gated) is correct: those are genuinely #[cfg(test)]-gated in-file drivers, documented as such under br-asupersync-iuoayq.

(2) TEXT-NARROWED ENTRIES. Allowlist entries and groups take an optional justified_text list of regexes. The entry covers the path only if EVERY flagged line matches one; a single unmatched line makes the entry not apply, so the hit falls through to the next entry, then waivers, then violation. Absent field = old whole-file behavior, so this is backwards compatible. Malformed values are a load-time error rather than a silently ignored field, because a typo that disabled narrowing would restore whole-file coverage without saying so.

WHAT THIS BOUGHT BACK, MEASURED. src/net/atp/transport_rq/mod.rs needed no entry at all -- all 5 of its scanner hits are cfg(test)-gated, so its entry was removed. Its own revisit_condition had said to revisit 'if the scanner gains cfg(test)-aware classification'; it has. The other 4 are narrowed to the exact sentence each justifies. Proof for all 5: copy the real file into an isolated tree, confirm the gate passes, append a literal unfinished-work marker, confirm it flips to fail with coverage=violation. All 5 flip. Under the old whole-file entries every one of those markers would have been absorbed silently -- including in the 22.9k-line ATP RaptorQ transport and the 13.1k-line native QUIC link.

I did NOT suppress comment hits. The bead warned against it and the warning holds: '// TODO: implement this' is a comment and is the single most important thing this gate catches. The injected marker in the proof above is exactly that shape, and it fails the gate in all 5 files.

FIXTURES (both suites green, run remotely): a cfg(test) hit that does not violate; a production hit in the SAME file that still does, with category production_stub; an unterminated block comment that fails closed; any(test,...) rejected as a test gate while all(test,...) is accepted; a justified_text entry covering its own sentence; an unjustified hit in the same file still violating; an invalid regex rejected at load.

VERIFICATION. rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay -o <my 3 files> -- cargo test --test no_mock_policy_contract: 4 passed, 1 failed. The failure is no_mock_policy_evidence_runner_emits_valid_jsonl_and_logs dying on 'fatal: not a git repository' status 128 -- that is asupersync-bq3c9g, pre-existing and unrelated, and its baseline on pristine HEAD with --no-overlay fails identically. Clippy on the target is clean; rustfmt clean; both python self-test suites exit 0; the gate itself exits 0 with 0 violations.

An earlier plain 'rch exec --' run reported the exact pre-9fhmts violation set -- the worker cache was stale, not my tree. Worth recording: a bare rch lane in this shared tree cannot ground a gate claim; --base HEAD --clean-overlay -o <my files> can.

REPORT/CONTRACT CHANGES. New report fields scanned_hits, test_gated_hits/paths, test_gated_undetermined_paths, a test_gated row list, and the offending path names, so exclusions are auditable rather than silent. remaining_allowlist_entries fell 254 -> 199 because ~55 files stopped needing an entry at all; the Rust bound moved 250 -> 150 with that reason recorded inline, and violating_paths == 0 remains what actually proves coverage.

NOT DONE, filed as asupersync-3j4ib0 (P3): the 2026-05-05 groups still carry ~55 whole-file production_stub patterns. Nothing is hidden today -- that blindness is prospective, same as this bead's was.

comments.text:
SapphireHill 2026-07-26: INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION of all 7 sites, plus the measured blast radius. I had a second reader go through each site with full surrounding context before I let the allowlist entries land, because writing "approved" against somebody else's file on the strength of my own first read is exactly the move that turns a real signal off.

VERDICTS (7/7 agree with the 9fhmts triage):
  REAL_STUB      src/bin/atp.rs:2695 -- confirmed. bond_pull_ssh_tunnel_plan() (line 2499) only BUILDS a BondPullSshTunnel { forward_arg: "-L 127.0.0.1:{port}:{host}:{port}", donor_dial: "127.0.0.1:{port}" }; nothing consumes forward_arg beyond an eprintln!. No ssh child is ever spawned. When choice.transport == BondTransport::Ssh the code warns on stderr and then uses `let dial = spec.choice.dial;` -- the direct/tailnet endpoint. So `--transport ssh`, whose entire purpose is a donor behind NAT with UDP blocked, attempts a direct UDP dial that cannot work. Loudly disclosed, not silent, but unimplemented. The expiring waiver (2026-10-31, owner z01bbr.8.3) is the right instrument.
  FALSE_POSITIVE the other six, each for the reason recorded in its entry.

MEASURED BLAST RADIUS -- this is the part I could not have asserted without checking, and it is better than I feared:
  - src/bin/atp.rs, src/bin/dependency_verification_matrix.rs, src/net/atp/sdk/bonded.rs, src/net/atp/transport_quic/native_link.rs, src/net/udp.rs: the flagged line is the ONLY occurrence of any of the six terms in the whole file (atp.rs 12,090 lines; native_link.rs 13,088; udp.rs 4,347).
  - src/net/atp/transport_rq/mod.rs: 6 occurrences, ALL inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`. Boundaries pinned exactly: attribute at 15215, `mod tests {` at 15216, closing brace at 23867 (= last line of file; the only column-0 `}` after 15215, and no column-0 item follows 15216). Allowlisting this file currently blesses nothing outside the test module.
  - src/grpc/server.rs: 4 occurrences, all `Status::unimplemented(...)` -- 1317 (unknown grpc-encoding from peer), 1322 (known algorithm the server excludes), 1331 and 1373 (compression feature not compiled in). All four are canonical protocol behavior. No mock/fake/stub/placeholder/todo anywhere in its 7,145 lines. Note this path was fixed by CLASSIFICATION (canonical_grpc_status_code), not by a production_stub allowlist entry -- the effect on future detection is the same, but the reason it was flagged was miscategorisation.

SO: the debt these entries create is PROSPECTIVE, not present. Nothing real is hidden today. What is now hidden is the NEXT `// TODO: implement ...` written into any of those files -- including the 22.9k-line ATP RaptorQ transport and the 13.1k-line native QUIC link. That is what fix (2), text-narrowed entries, buys back, and it is why I filed this rather than treating 9fhmts as a clean close.

ONE MORE DATA POINT FOR (1), cfg(test) awareness: sha256_hex_placeholder() at src/net/atp/transport_rq/mod.rs:6483 returns "0".repeat(64) -- a literal 64-zero hex sentinel, not a real digest. That LOOKS like the worst case the gate exists to catch, and it is in fact a deliberate fixed-width wire sentinel for "digest not yet known", enforced fail-closed: ManifestDigestMode::Manifest errors outright on a missing digest (line 5764), and with require_source_stream_trailer the receiver errors if any entry lacks a real trailer digest (lines 6551-6564). It is used only in SourceStream mode where the digest is genuinely not yet computable. A cfg(test)-aware scanner would never have surfaced the test call site at all, and the production sentinel at 6483 does not match `\bplaceholder\b` (underscore is a word character), so it was never the thing being flagged.

title: Missing canonical HTTP/2 RST_STREAM → gRPC Status mapping (gRPC HTTP/2 spec)
description: The gRPC-over-HTTP/2 spec (https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/doc/PROTOCOL-HTTP2.md) defines a 14-row mapping from HTTP/2 RST_STREAM error codes to gRPC Status codes. The only mapping in asupersync is a 3-line test helper grpc_go_rst_stream_status in src/grpc/streaming.rs:914 that handles Cancel→CANCELLED, RefusedStream→UNAVAILABLE, and default→INTERNAL. Two spec-mandated mappings are MISSING: ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM(11) → RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED(8) and INADEQUATE_SECURITY(12) → PERMISSION_DENIED(7). Add a canonical Status::from_h2_rst_stream_code(ErrorCode) -> Status helper in src/grpc/status.rs covering the full table, and add a test asserting all 14 codes map per the gRPC spec.

title: spawn_blocking_drained: cancelled captures are destroyed outside pool busy accounting (pool starves new work) or inline on the executor when cancelled before the first poll
description:
## Defects (source-verified by SapphireHill, 2026-09-28, origin b8195384a; from a subagent review of ecda43b5b, spawn_blocking_drained)

F1, MEDIUM: a cancelled queued job destroys its captures after the pool counts the worker idle.
- blocking_worker_loop (src/runtime/blocking_pool.rs ~1487-1495) handles a cancelled task by decrementing busy_threads and calling signal_done, then drops the task (its work closure and captures) at `continue`.
- The drained controller sets the pool cancel flag on every observed cancellation, so this is the normal queued-cancel path, and its captures may block when dropped (the ParkedDrop fixture).
- While a destructor runs, maybe_spawn_thread_on_inner computes idle = active - busy and sees an idle worker, so new work gets no new thread even below max_threads. If the destructor waits on that new work, the pool deadlocks and the owning region never closes.
- is_done() and busy_threads() also report the job done and the worker idle meanwhile.
- queued_cancellation_waits_for_capture_destruction_even_after_handle_drop never checks the counters while the destructor is parked.

F2, MEDIUM: cancellation before the controller's first poll destroys captures on the async executor thread.
- drive_drained_blocking (src/runtime/spawn_blocking.rs ~314-318) calls drop(envelope) inline when the first checkpoint fails.
- Every other path destroys captures on the pool: skipped, declined and abandoned.
- A blocking capture Drop then runs on a runtime worker. On a current-thread runtime it blocks the only executor thread, including inside shutdown_drained.
- The same early return skips the panic check, so a panicking capture Drop yields an Ok task outcome (F3, LOW).

Pool rejection (shutdown) and stranded jobs after a failed thread spawn still drop inline (blocking_pool.rs ~878-896, ~1414-1416). That is noted, not fixed.

SUSPECTED: an unwind-unguarded EvidenceSink panic inside the controller's checkpoint could retire the task while its claimed closure still runs. DrainedBlockingHandle::drop also aborts unconditionally, even after a successful join.

## Fix (candidate B8, SapphireHill)
- The worker's skip branch destroys the task's work inside catch_unwind before decrementing busy_threads and signalling done, as the executed path does.
- A controller cancelled before its first poll still submits the envelope with the claim gate closed. A pool worker skips or declines the closure and destroys the captures, and the common wait then reports a capture panic.
Tests (tests/drained_blocking_native.rs):
- queued_cancellation_... asserts busy_threads() == 1 while the skipped captures' destructor is parked (0 before the fix).
- success_panic_prestart_abort_... asserts that a capture of a closure aborted before its first poll is destroyed on a "-blocking-" pool thread (the block_on thread before the fix).

## Goal

End-to-end validation for the certified rewrite engine:
- build a Plan IR fixture (or load from corpus)
- run the rewrite engine (e-graph search + deterministic extractor)
- produce an optimized plan + certificate
- verify certificate with the small checker
- execute original and optimized under the lab runtime with identical seeds

- Per-fixture report (JSON) with:
  - fixture id + seed
  - rewrite applied count + cost delta
  - certificate hash + size
  - verifier result
  - trace fingerprints for original and optimized
  - (optional) galaxy-brain ledger excerpt (bounded)

## Logging constraints

- No stdout/stderr in core. The harness may print a deterministic summary.
- Use trace events for rewrite decisions and equivalence-oracle outcomes.

## Acceptance criteria

- Deterministic: identical outputs (optimized plan + certificate + report) across repeated runs.
- For each fixture, either:

title: [security] security/key.rs AuthKey::from_bytes accepts weak repeating patterns without entropy validation
description:
src/security/key.rs:82-84 — pub const fn from_bytes(bytes: [u8; AUTH_KEY_SIZE]) -> Self { Self { bytes } } accepts ANY 32-byte buffer as a key, including all-zero, all-one, [42u8; 32] (used in the test at line 268), or any repeating low-entropy pattern.

HMAC-SHA256 security depends on the key having sufficient entropy. A key with zero entropy produces deterministic, predictable HMAC outputs. An attacker who learns that a deployment uses such a weak key (because of misconfig, a leaked default, or because from_bytes accepted whatever bytes some upstream code generated) can forge authentication tags for any symbol.

Threat: developer mints AuthKey::from_bytes([0u8; 32]) for test, ships, the constant remains in production binary; or a wrapping crate uses a weak deterministic seed that lands in from_bytes.

Fix direction: (a) add a min-entropy check (Hamming-weight >= 8 bits, or distinct-byte count >= K) inside from_bytes that rejects pathological inputs at construction; OR (b) downgrade from_bytes to pub(crate), forcing public callers through AuthKey::from_seed (deterministic but at least mixes the seed) or AuthKey::from_rng (true randomness).

Source: /security-audit on src/security/* refresh (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Fixed in commit 6d0333c45: AuthKey::from_bytes now Result with MIN_DISTINCT_BYTES (8) + Hamming-weight [8,248] validators. from_bytes_unchecked pub(crate) for HMAC-chain. 6 macaroon callers + 1 cryptographic_boundary_test migrated. 4 regression tests.

title: [EPIC] Cancel-Aware Synchronization Primitives (tokio-sync equivalent)
description:
# Cancel-Aware Synchronization Primitives

## Overview
Synchronization primitives that integrate with cancellation protocol and support two-phase patterns where needed.

## Components

### 1. Mutex
- lock() returns LockGuard (obligation)
- try_lock() for non-blocking
- Cancel-aware: waiting for lock respects cancellation
- Unlock is automatic via Drop

### 2. RwLock
- read() returns ReadGuard
- write() returns WriteGuard
- Upgradable read locks
- Cancel-aware waiting

### 3. Semaphore
- Two-phase: acquire_permit() returns Permit obligation
- Permit must be released or explicitly dropped
- Bounded and unbounded variants
- OwnedPermit for 'static lifetime

### 4. Barrier
- wait() blocks until N waiters
- Returns BarrierWaitResult (is_leader)
- Cancel-aware: if cancelled, barrier may never complete

### 5. Notify
- notify_one(), notify_waiters()
- notified() returns future
- Cancel-aware waiting

### 6. OnceCell
- get_or_init() with async initializer
- get_or_try_init() for fallible init
- Cancel-aware: racing initializers handled correctly

### 7. Watch Channel
- Single-producer, multi-consumer
- Receivers get latest value
- Cancel-aware subscription

## Invariants
- No deadlocks in well-formed programs
- Cancel-safe acquisition
- Obligations properly tracked
- Deterministic behavior in lab runtime

## Testing
- Concurrent access patterns
- Cancellation during wait
- Deadlock detection (debug builds)
- Deterministic scheduling in lab
close_reason: All child tasks complete: Mutex, RwLock, Semaphore, Barrier, Notify, OnceCell implemented with tests. Watch Channel deferred to separate task if needed.

title: [security-audit] tls/acceptor.rs: TlsAcceptorBuilder lacks min/max protocol version setters (asymmetric defense vs connector)
description: src/tls/acceptor.rs::TlsAcceptorBuilder has no min_protocol_version() / max_protocol_version() setters — build() unconditionally calls .with_safe_default_protocol_versions(). TlsConnectorBuilder DOES expose these setters (connector.rs:462-471). This asymmetry means a SaaS server cannot pin to TLS 1.3 only (eliminating downgrade-attack surface and TLS-1.2 cipher suite negotiation pitfalls), even when policy requires it. Today rustls 0.23's safe defaults exclude TLS 1.0/1.1, but there is no guarantee future rustls versions won't relax that — and operators have no programmatic way to enforce 'TLS 1.3 only' on the server side. Fix: mirror connector's min_protocol_version/max_protocol_version setters on the acceptor builder with the same SupportedProtocolVersion filtering pattern. Severity MEDIUM (forward defense + policy enforcement gap).
close_reason: TlsAcceptorBuilder now exposes min_protocol_version() and max_protocol_version() setters that mirror TlsConnectorBuilder's API one-for-one (signature, semantics, error shape). build() filters rustls::ALL_VERSIONS to the requested range when either bound is set; falls back to with_safe_default_protocol_versions() when both are None (preserves existing behaviour for unconfigured callers — rustls 0.23 safe defaults already exclude TLS 1.0/1.1, so no observable change for callers who don't opt in). Range validation rejects min>max with the same Configuration error string the connector emits. Three regression tests added: (1) test_min_protocol_version_inverted_range_rejected_at_build pins the range-validation error path; (2) test_min_protocol_tls13_pin_builds_and_handshakes_with_matching_client positive control — TLS-1.3-only acceptor handshakes successfully with a TLS-1.3-only connector via VirtualTcpStream; (3) test_acceptor_pinned_above_client_max_rejects_handshake negative control — acceptor pinned to TLS 1.3 floor + connector capped at TLS 1.2 ceiling => handshake fails (this is the analogue of the bead's 'min=1.2 rejects TLS 1.0' requirement; rustls 0.23 doesn't support TLS 1.0 at all, so we exercise the same defense surface against the lowest version rustls actually negotiates). title: [replay-determinism] trace/distributed/collector.rs: SymbolTraceCollector uses std HashMap<DistTraceId, TraceRecord> — non-deterministic eviction on tied timestamps + hash-DoS via attacker-controlled DistTraceIds
description:
src/trace/distributed/collector.rs:66, 78, 280-313 — SymbolTraceCollector stores in-flight distributed traces in a standard `HashMap<DistTraceId, TraceRecord>` with the default randomly-seeded hasher:

  pub struct SymbolTraceCollector {
      traces: RwLock<HashMap<DistTraceId, TraceRecord>>,
      ...
  }

The map's keyspace is **attacker-influenced**: DistTraceId values arrive from remote peers via the distributed bridge. Two security/correctness consequences:

  (a) **Hash-DoS.** Standard HashMap uses a randomly-seeded SipHash-1-3 hasher; that mitigates collision attacks IF the seed is per-process and unknown to the attacker. But `SymbolTraceCollector::record_span` accepts spans without rate-limiting, and a peer that submits 10K trace IDs that collide on the local hasher (via known SipHash collision techniques) will degrade lookup to O(N) for every subsequent operation. The default `max_traces=10_000` (line 79) does not protect against this — it caps cardinality but not collision density. Compare to the dichotomy noted in br-asupersync-yrwie0 for HeaderName HashMaps: attacker-controlled keys must use a randomized hasher OR a deterministic-but-domain-separated KDF.

  (b) **Replay non-determinism in eviction.** `evict_oldest` (line 280) sorts candidate IDs by `last_updated` timestamp, but timestamps may be tied (same-nanosecond bursts during cancel cascades). When `sort_by_key` produces a tied prefix, `iter().filter(...).map(...).collect::<Vec<_>>()` picks WHICH ties land first based on the underlying HashMap iteration order — which is randomized per process. Two replays of the same trace stream evict different traces, which propagates into oracle reports and causes apparent non-determinism in the lab.

Concrete trigger:
  - Spin up a SymbolTraceCollector with max_traces=4. Insert 5 traces with last_updated=t for the same t. Run evict_oldest. Repeat in a fresh process. The set of evicted IDs differs between runs.

Fix direction:
  1. Replace HashMap with `util::DetHashMap` (deterministic hasher, used elsewhere in trace/geodesic.rs) for replay determinism.
  2. Add a stable secondary sort key (e.g., `(last_updated, DistTraceId)`) so tied timestamps still produce a total order independent of hash insertion order.
  3. Cap collision density: track per-bucket length and reject inserts when buckets grow > 16 (signals an attempted hash-DoS).
  4. Or: switch to `BTreeMap<(Time, DistTraceId), TraceRecord>` so ordering is intrinsic to the structure.

Source: /multi-pass-bug-hunting on src/trace/* (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Fixed in 2721086f3: SymbolTraceCollector now stores in-flight traces in BTreeMap<DistTraceId, TraceRecord> instead of std HashMap. Eliminates hash-DoS (no hashing of attacker-influenced keys) and gives deterministic iteration order on tied timestamps. DistTraceId already derives Ord. Test deterministic_iteration_order_under_insertion_permutation guards against a regression to HashMap.

title: Build deterministic swarm pressure preflight report
description:
Context:
Asupersync already has pressure and proof artifacts such as admission-aware runtime pressure atlases, runtime pressure control evidence, proof-lane admission schemas, RCH fallback contracts, proof freshness receipts, chaos scenario contracts, and proof-status snapshots. These are powerful but scattered.

Problem:
Operators running massive agent swarms need one deterministic preflight report that answers whether the repo is ready to dispatch proof lanes or release gates, which pressure controls apply, which proof evidence is stale, and which dirty files are peer-owned. Without this, humans have to infer system safety from many separate JSON files, shell outputs, and mail threads.

Scope:
Create a deterministic preflight report surface that composes existing artifacts rather than replacing them. It should summarize pressure/admission status, proof-lane envelope health, exact-filter stale evidence, dirty-tree ownership, and release-blocking conditions. It can be a script, contract artifact, or test-backed report depending on the existing local pattern discovered during implementation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Report schema and golden fixtures cover green, blocked, stale-exact-filter, missing-envelope, peer-owned dirty tree, and mixed pressure states.
- Unit tests validate parser/normalizer behavior for every source artifact used by the report.
- E2E script emits detailed logs showing artifact paths, hashes or versions, parsed decisions, blocker aggregation, and final operator-facing summary.
- The report must distinguish proof of current-source diagnosis from proof of behavioral correctness.
- The report must preserve all existing proof/status surfaces and explicitly link to them by lane ID or artifact path.
- RCH-backed validation is documented for any Rust contract tests or cargo checks; no local heavy validation is accepted.

title: Instrument obligation lifecycle with tracing
description:
# Task

Add tracing instrumentation for the obligation (two-phase commit) system.

## Background

Obligations are the mechanism for cancel-safe resource management:
- SendPermit: Channel send slots
- Ack: Message processing confirmation  
- Lease: Borrowed resources (RPC slots, etc.)
- IoOp: In-flight I/O operations

The lifecycle is: Reserved → (Committed | Aborted | Leaked)

Leaked obligations indicate bugs - a task completed while holding an uncommitted obligation.

## What to Instrument

1. **Reserve**: Obligation created
   - Fields: obligation_id, kind, holder_task, owning_region
   
2. **Commit**: Obligation fulfilled
   - Fields: obligation_id, duration_held
   
3. **Abort**: Obligation explicitly cancelled
   - Fields: obligation_id, abort_reason (cancel, error, explicit)
   
4. **Leak detection**: Obligation not resolved when task completes
   - Level: ERROR
   - Fields: obligation_id, kind, holder_task, held_duration
   - This is a BUG indicator

## Integration with Cancellation

When a task is cancelled:
1. Cancel requested → obligations should start aborting
2. If task completes with Reserved obligations → LEAK ERROR

Tracing should make this flow visible:

```
obligation[id=55, kind=SendPermit, state=Reserved]
  task_cancel_requested[task=100]
    obligation[id=55, transition=Reserved→Aborted, reason=task_cancelled]
```

vs the bug case:

```
obligation[id=55, kind=SendPermit, state=Reserved]
  task_completed[task=100, outcome=Ok]
    obligation_leaked[id=55, kind=SendPermit] // ERROR!
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Reserve emits span with full context
- [ ] Commit/Abort emit events with duration
- [ ] Leak detection emits ERROR level event
- [ ] Cancellation→abort flow is traceable
- [ ] Integration tests verify obligation tracing
close_reason: done

title: kafka_record_batch_v2 conformance header claims to check our producer batching; production wraps librdkafka (fix with the provenance-matrix re-pin)
description:
## Finding (from bi2462.144's census, SapphireHill 10-01)
tests/conformance/kafka_record_batch_v2/mod.rs says the suite "ensures our producer batching and wire format handling conforms to the Kafka protocol specification".
- asupersync's Kafka client wraps rdkafka (src/messaging/kafka.rs:9, :35, :47) and has no RecordBatch v2 codec of its own.
- The module tests its own reference model (format.rs; crc32fast, not Kafka's CRC32C).
- The Kafka provenance matrix already classifies it correctly as KAFKA-K0-4-FIXTURE-PROFILE-005-RECORD-BATCH-LOCAL-MODEL, and docs/kafka_broker_fixture_provenance_matrix.md says "deterministic local evidence, not a versioned external oracle".

## Why it is not fixed yet
artifacts/kafka_broker_fixture_provenance_matrix_v1.json pins mod.rs (KAFKA-K0-4-PIN-015-RECORD-BATCH-MODULE: sha256 8c3a54c2..., 3785 bytes, 107 records), and that pin is currently fresh. A header edit therefore needs the matrix owner (sarszu.*) to re-pin in the same change, or that contract turns red.

## Work
Replace the module header's claim with a scope note in the style of postgres_logical_replication.rs (3316a7f8c): "asupersync's Kafka client wraps librdkafka and implements no RecordBatch codec; these tests check this module's own reference model and are not evidence about asupersync code". Re-pin PIN-015 in the same commit, with the provenance contract green.

title: [replay-determinism] lab/oracle/priority_inversion.rs: Instant::now() for inversion-duration thresholds breaks replay
description:
src/lab/oracle/priority_inversion.rs:220, 241, 256, 296, 381, 462, 579 — PriorityInversionOracle uses std::time::Instant::now() to time inversion windows and compare them against config.min_inversion_duration. The comment at lines 11-24 explicitly acknowledges this and claims it doesn't affect 'byte-stability of the violation that did fire' — but it DOES affect WHEN the violation fires, which is observable in trace events.

Same defect shape as the sibling region_leak.rs bead (Instant::now in oracle timing). In lab replay mode, virtual time advances deterministically, but this oracle's wall-clock measurements break across-run consistency.

Threat: regression test that snapshots oracle.violations() and asserts equality across re-runs of the same scenario with the same seed will flake. Cross-host CI shards (different wall-clock granularity) flake hardest.

Fix direction:
  1. Identical to the region_leak fix: route every Instant::now() through a Time parameter sourced from LabRuntime.
  2. The 'last_stats_report' / inversion-start timestamps become Time-typed.
  3. Coordinate with the region_leak fix — they share the same 'oracle takes virtual time' API contract.

Source: /multi-pass-bug-hunting deepest pass on src/lab/* (2026-04-26).

title: [replay-determinism] lab/oracle/region_leak.rs: HashMap iteration in regions/tasks tables — fragile across runs
description:
src/lab/oracle/region_leak.rs:307 — RegionLeakOracle stores 'regions: HashMap<RegionId, RegionState>' and 'tasks: HashMap<TaskId, TaskState>' with std::collections::HashMap (RandomState seed). Today the violations VecDeque preserves insertion order so the public surface is mostly safe, BUT check_for_violations (line 540) loops over both maps via .iter() — and any future refactor that surfaces the iteration order (e.g. a debug-print, a state snapshot, an eviction-by-min_by_key) will be silently non-deterministic.

This is the same fragility the closed asupersync-q6vujm (trace/distributed/collector.rs) and asupersync-ks0t6j (FairnessMonitor BTreeMap) and asupersync-jg4yyx/zhtjy9 (DetHashMap) fixes targeted. The lab oracle is even more sensitive because it's the SOURCE OF TRUTH for replay determinism.

Fix direction: replace both HashMaps with crate::util::DetHashMap (project-fixed SipHash seed) OR with std::collections::BTreeMap (deterministic by key). DetHashMap preserves O(1) lookup; BTreeMap is O(log N) but iteration is naturally sorted by RegionId/TaskId. For an oracle that already iterates linearly per tick, BTreeMap is the simpler fix — matches the priority_inversion.rs pattern (line 215-224 already uses BTreeMap).

Source: /multi-pass-bug-hunting deepest pass on src/lab/* (2026-04-26).

title: [reality-check] runtime/scheduler/worker: poll_start uses Instant::now() instead of Cx::time() — replay-determinism leak
description:
src/runtime/scheduler/worker.rs:383 calls `Instant::now()` to capture poll start time, then at line 637 uses `poll_start.elapsed()` to feed `self.metrics.scheduler_tick(1, poll_start.elapsed())`.

This is the only production-code ambient-authority leak across all 10 audited scheduler files (priority.rs, intrusive.rs, intrusive_heap.rs, three_lane.rs, worker.rs, local_queue.rs, global_queue.rs, global_injector.rs, decision_contract.rs, stealing.rs). The other Instant::now() / std::thread::sleep references (worker.rs lines 909, 961, 983, 1009, 1293; three_lane.rs lines 4934, 6044, 6232) are inside #[cfg(test)] modules and don't affect production determinism.

Impact: the wall-clock elapsed time is fed into observability metrics. If those metrics ever feed back into scheduler decisions (e.g., adaptive worker count tuning, EMA-based load balancing, lyapunov governor pressure), production scheduling could diverge from a lab-runtime replay using virtual time. Today the metric is read-only-for-observers, so the impact is contained to dashboards and trace files — but it violates the I7 ambient-authority invariant and creates a footgun for future refactors.

Suggested fix:
```rust
let poll_start = self.cx.as_ref()
    .and_then(|c| c.timer_driver())
    .map(|t| t.now())
    .unwrap_or_else(crate::time::wall_now);
```
Or pass a Time parameter through the scheduler entry point, mirroring how lab/runtime.rs threads virtual time through. This matches the pattern in src/tls/mod.rs::timeout_now() (Cx-aware time fallback).

Verified: grep -nE 'Instant::now|SystemTime::now|std::env::|std::process::' across all 10 scheduler files confirms only worker.rs:383 is in production code. /reality-check-for-project audit batch 2026-04-26.

DO NOT FIX in this batch per audit-only protocol — bead is for tracking only.
close_reason: Fixed in ad20709bf: replaced poll_start Instant::now() with self.timer_driver.as_ref().map_or_else(crate::time::wall_now, TimerDriverHandle::now). Both call sites (poll_start at line 383 + elapsed at line 637) now sample the worker's installed TimerDriverHandle when present (lab runtime's deterministic virtual time), falling back to wall_now() when no driver is attached. Both return Time so the elapsed computation is type-uniform via Time::duration_since → u64 nanos → Duration. Perf cost: one Option deref + branch on the hot path (timer_driver is a single pointer-sized field hot in cache); TimerDriverHandle::now is #[inline]; no atomic reads/locks/allocations. Test code (worker.rs:909, 961, 983, 1009, 1293) preserved per the audit's production-only scope. Lib check passes.

title: Graceful Degradation Framework
description:
EPIC: Resource-Aware Graceful Degradation for Structured Concurrency

## Background & Problem
Systems experience resource pressure and load spikes, but most runtimes fail catastrophically:
- Out-of-memory crashes instead of graceful resource management  
- No differentiation between critical and non-critical work
- Lack of automatic backpressure and load shedding
- Hard to predict system behavior under resource constraints

Structured concurrency provides unique opportunities for intelligent degradation through region priorities and hierarchical resource management.

## Solution: Priority-Based Resource Management
Implement automatic degradation based on resource pressure and work priority:
1. Region priority classification (critical/normal/background)
2. Resource monitoring (memory, file handles, CPU) with thresholds  
3. Automatic work shedding starting with lowest priority regions
4. Backpressure propagation through structured concurrency hierarchy
5. Recovery mechanisms when resources become available

## Degradation Strategies
- Memory pressure: Cancel background regions, throttle new allocations
- CPU pressure: Reduce time quantum for non-critical tasks
- IO pressure: Shed non-critical IO operations, prioritize critical channels
- Handle pressure: Close non-essential connections, defer cleanup

## Business Value
- Systems remain responsive under extreme load instead of crashing
- Graceful degradation enables handling unexpected traffic spikes  
- Reduces operational complexity (fewer midnight pages for OOMs)
- Enables running closer to resource limits safely

## Success Metrics
- System remains responsive up to 95% resource utilization
- Critical work continues execution during resource pressure
- Recovery time <1s when resources become available  
- Zero data corruption during degradation events
close_reason: Graceful Degradation Framework fully integrated — region priority, degradation stats, system pressure handling

title: SWIM: unauthenticated gossip adopts+re-floods fabricated node ids -> unbounded members map + cluster poisoning
description: Found in deep review (SapphireHill 2026-06-29). src/distributed/membership/swim.rs apply_rumor(~725)->adopt(~682). For any node not already in members, supersede is unconditionally true, so adopt() inserts a new Member and gossip.queue() buffers it for re-dissemination. No cap on member_count, no proof the subject exists. A peer/spoofed UDP source (SWIM has no source auth) sending gossip naming thousands of fabricated node ids makes the receiver grow members + GossipBuffer without bound AND amplify by re-flooding fake Alive rumors cluster-wide. Wire codec bounds rumors per-packet but nothing bounds cumulative distinct-node count. Module docs mark auth out-of-scope, but the codec+state machine ARE wired to a real UDP transport (udp.rs) so it is a deployable DoS. FIX (short term): bound members by a configured max_members (fail-closed reject new adoptions past cap); do not gossip.queue a newly-learned Alive about a node never corroborated via direct ping/ack. (long term) the documented authenticated-channel follow-up.
close_reason: Fixed (SapphireHill, commit pending): SWIM unauthenticated-gossip unbounded members + amplification. SwimConfig.max_members (default 65536, validated >=1 via new SwimConfigError::ZeroMaxMembers). adopt() now returns bool and fail-closed-rejects a brand-new member once members.len()>=max_members (updates to existing members unaffected); the 3 new-member callers (add_peer, apply_rumor, observe_sender) only gossip.queue when adoption succeeded, so a fabricated rumor past the cap is neither tracked nor re-flooded. Tests: members_capped_at_max_members_fail_closed + config default/validation. clippy clean; tests green.

title: Design resource monitoring and degradation triggers
description:
Design resource monitoring system and degradation trigger mechanisms.

## Resource Monitoring Requirements
- Memory usage tracking (heap, stack, arena allocators)
- File descriptor usage monitoring with OS limits  
- CPU usage and scheduler queue depth monitoring
- Network connection and socket usage tracking
- Custom resource types (database connections, etc.)

## Trigger System Design  
- Configurable thresholds (warning/critical levels)
- Hysteresis to prevent oscillation during degradation
- Integration with existing runtime resource management
- Efficient monitoring with <0.5% overhead

## Degradation Decision Engine
- Region priority classification system  
- Work shedding algorithms (which regions to cancel first)
- Resource reclamation strategies per resource type
- Recovery policies when pressure decreases

## Integration Points
- Runtime region creation checks resource availability
- Scheduler integration for CPU pressure handling
- Memory allocator integration for allocation pressure
- IO driver integration for handle pressure management

## Configuration Interface
- TOML configuration for thresholds and policies
- Runtime configuration updates without restart
- Per-application custom resource type registration
- Monitoring endpoint for current resource usage

title: Add Mutex::lock_until(deadline) timeout API
description: Audit found no native timeout API on Mutex. Currently callers must use combinator pattern: timeout(duration, mutex.lock(cx)).await which doesn't handle queue fairness properly - all waiters share same deadline rather than per-waiter deadlines. Need Mutex::lock_until(deadline) that honors deadline even with blocking queue ahead. See timeout pattern in time::timeout, combinator::timeout for reference.
design: Add deadline-aware mutex acquisition to the existing fair waiter queue instead of wrapping lock() in an outer timeout. Each waiter should carry its own deadline and be removed/expired deterministically without stealing another waiter slot or breaking fairness. The design must use asupersync time/Cx seams and preserve existing lock()/try_lock() semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover immediate lock before deadline, timeout while queued, multiple waiters with different deadlines, earlier waiter timeout allowing later waiter progress, deadline exactly equal to current time, already-expired deadline, guard drop waking the next non-expired waiter, cancellation while queued, no stale waiter nodes, fairness preservation against non-deadline lock waiters, and disabled/existing API equivalence. Deterministic LabRuntime/e2e coverage must log scenario ID, virtual start tick, deadline tick per waiter, queue order before/after expiry, acquisition result, timeout result, wake count, cancellation count, stale-waiter count, exact rch command, artifact paths if any, and final no-leak/fairness verdict. Validation before closeout: rch exec -- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check for touched Rust files, targeted rch cargo tests for sync::mutex deadline behavior with --nocapture, and a closeout comment documenting deadline semantics and edge cases.

title: UDP GSO: ATP-RQ send windows exceed one datagram (EMSGSIZE) and the first refusal disables GSO for the socket's lifetime
description:
ATP-RQ's UDP GSO send path has never carried a full send window. Found by a read-only audit of src/net/udp.rs and src/net/atp/udp/mod.rs (2026-10-02, SapphireHill); confirmed in the source.

1. Super-packets over one datagram (src/net/udp.rs, UdpSendBatchPlan::for_packets and ::for_connected_payloads)
   - The planner sets segments_per_packet = datagrams.min(max_gso_segments), with no byte limit.
   - An ATP-RQ window is RQ_SEND_BATCH_PER_SOCKET = UDP_MAX_GSO_SEGMENTS = 64 datagrams of 1,424 bytes (or 1,456 authenticated): 91,136 or 93,184 bytes in one GSO send.
   - The kernel refuses any UDP send over one IP datagram with EMSGSIZE, GSO included (__ip_append_data: payload at most 65,535 - 20 - 8 = 65,507 bytes for IPv4).
   - The first full window therefore fails at zero progress. The batch falls back to plain sendmmsg, and gso_demoted latches, so GSO stays off for the socket's lifetime.
   - Unit tests pinned the impossible plan (64 x 1,456 bytes as one super-packet; 4 x 65,000 bytes as one). The real-socket tests send only 4 datagrams.
   - benches/udp_send_batch_bench.rs asserts gso_send_used for exactly 64 x 1,456 bytes on Linux, but it was only ever compiled with cargo check, never run (wfrvuq comments).

2. Any refused first GSO send latches the demotion
   - The fallback arm latched gso_demoted for every zero-progress error, including errors unrelated to GSO. Examples: ECONNREFUSED left on a connected socket by an ICMP port-unreachable (an RQ sender that starts before its receiver binds), EACCES, EHOSTUNREACH.

Fix:
- Cap each super-packet at 65,507 bytes. A window of 64 full-size RQ datagrams then goes out as 44 + 20 segments in one sendmmsg call. A segment size where two cannot fit one datagram is planned without GSO.
- Latch the demotion only for errors showing GSO cannot work on the socket: EINVAL, EIO, EMSGSIZE, EOPNOTSUPP, ENOPROTOOPT.
- Correct the docs on ATP_UDP_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE and RQ_SEND_BATCH_PER_SOCKET, which said one batch fills one super-packet.

Related: asupersync-rq-e6b-gso-sendmmsg-native-send-wfrvuq (BronzeTiger, stale since 2026-06-24) built the GSO path; this bead fixes a defect in it. The ATP ledger's MATRIX-232 GSO note is about QUIC jumbo packets (gso_size above the MTU), a different cause.
close_reason: Fixed in a2d3ac04b: GSO super-packets within one datagram; GSO demoted only on GSO-specific errors; bench fixed; old code red on a real kernel and in the bench

1. region_factory_panic_after_spawn_cleans_up_orphan_task_records
   - "post-panic tasks_iter count must match pre-call count

2. metamorphic_nested_scope_cancellation_closes_descendants_without_spawn_leaks
   - "grandchild cancellation join should succeed: Ready(Err(Cancelled(...)))"

3. spawn_abort_cancels_task
   - "Task failed unexpectedly: task was cancelled: user: abort"
   - Expected Ok("cancelled") via tx.send delivery; got
     JoinError::Cancelled instead.

4. conformance_task_cancellation_propagation
   - Similar to #3.

Other 38 cx::scope tests pass.

Likely cause (uncertain): the factory pattern in
Scope::create_task_record at src/cx/scope.rs:1492 was changed in
056c70724 (br-asupersync-rel9qh, May 7 14:00) from
`*record = TaskRecord::new_with_time(...)` to field-by-field mutation
inside `insert_pooled_task_with`. That change is also the production
half of br-asupersync-j1e7zy. Companion change in
RuntimeState::create_task_infrastructure (state.rs:1682, 834f84c21)
is on a DIFFERENT call path — not used by Scope::spawn — so it cannot
directly affect these tests; remains green for the
runtime::task_table::tests path (25/25 pass including the j1e7zy
regression test for wake_state Arc reuse).

Note: BOTH paths leave non-identity TaskRecord fields at their
defaults (recycled-record `Recyclable::reset` clears state=Created,
phase=Created, etc.; miss-path `TaskRecord::new` initializes the same
defaults), so the field-mutation pattern is semantically equivalent
to the full-replacement pattern at the field-value level. The
difference is at the Arc-identity level: `wake_state` is reused from
the recycled record (allocated by reset()) instead of being dropped
and recreated. That should be safe — but if any test or production
path keys off Arc identity of `wake_state` across a recycle+reinsert
cycle (e.g. holds a Weak<TaskWakeState> from before recycle, or
compares Arc::ptr_eq() against pre-recycle reference), the new
pattern would surface a behavior delta.

Acceptance:

   change OR are pre-existing on main from before May 7.
   Verification step: run `cargo test --lib cx::scope::tests::` at
   commit 056c70724 (rel9qh, scope.rs has my factory) AND at commit
   767a1d07a (180d5m, scope.rs uses original *record assignment) and
   compare.
2. If failures are pre-existing, this bead becomes a tracking issue
   for the underlying cancellation/cleanup regression unrelated to
   j1e7zy.
3. If failures are caused by the rel9qh factory change, decide
   whether to (a) revert scope.rs to *record = TaskRecord::new_with_time(...)
   (loses one wake_state Arc allocation but restores tests), or
   (b) find what relies on wake_state Arc identity and fix it
   (preferable).

Fixed by matching Created|CancelRequested. Root cause 2: three async-spawn wrappers used tx.send(&cx_for_send, ...) where cx_for_send is the task's OWN cancellable Cx — when a task observed cancellation and returned a cancellation-aware payload, the post-completion delivery failed with SendError::Cancelled and TaskHandle::join saw the channel close instead. title: [AUDIT] Deep correctness audit: http/h2/connection.rs
notes:
VERDICT: SOUND — 0 bugs found

## Module: src/http/h2/connection.rs (2,752 lines: 1,106 production + 1,646 tests)

### Concurrency Analysis
ZERO concurrency primitives. Entirely single-threaded Connection struct with &mut self methods. Designed to be driven by an external event loop. No atomics, no locks, no wakers.

### Architecture
- **FrameCodec**: Encoder/Decoder for HTTP/2 binary framing. Partial header buffering. Unknown extension frame types correctly skipped (RFC 9113 compliant). max_frame_size validation.
- **ConnectionState**: Handshaking → Open → Closing → Closed state machine.
- **Connection**: local/remote Settings, StreamStore, HPACK encoder/decoder, send/recv windows (i32), pending_ops VecDeque, continuation tracking.

### Key Correctness Properties Verified

1. **Flow control**: Connection-level recv_window auto-replenish at 50% watermark. Stream-level auto WINDOW_UPDATE. WINDOW_UPDATE overflow check via i64 arithmetic before i32 assignment. Zero-increment correctly returns ProtocolError — stream error for stream-level (RFC 9113 §6.9.1), connection error for stream 0.

2. **CONTINUATION handling**: continuation_stream_id tracks expected stream. Only CONTINUATION frames accepted while awaiting. Timeout mechanism (configurable ms). Clears on END_HEADERS. Tests confirm SETTINGS and PING during continuation are rejected.

3. **PUSH_PROMISE security**: Validates (a) server-side only, (b) push enabled in settings, (c) odd stream ID (client-initiated), (d) associated stream not closed, (e) max concurrent streams check, (f) monotonic stream ID via reserve_remote_stream.

4. **Data sending flow control**: Respects min(connection_window, stream_window, max_frame_size). Remainder re-queued to front of pending_ops. end_stream flag set only on final piece when body fully sent.

5. **CONTINUATION frame ordering**: Header data split into max_frame_size chunks. CONTINUATION frames pushed to front of pending_ops in reverse order for correct emission sequence (RFC 9113 §6.10). Test confirms no interleaving with other pending ops between HEADERS and final CONTINUATION.

6. **GOAWAY semantics**: Sent-once guard prevents duplicate GOAWAY. Transitions to Closing state. Resets streams above last_stream_id. last_stream_id correctly reflects highest processed stream. Connection-level WINDOW_UPDATE still accepted in Closing state.

7. **Data after RST**: DATA on closed/reset stream correctly returns StreamClosed error.

### Tests
26+ tests covering: settings negotiation, flow control, CONTINUATION timeout and ordering, PUSH_PROMISE validation, GOAWAY semantics, zero-increment WINDOW_UPDATE (both stream and connection), data after RST, interleaving prevention.

### No unsafe blocks.
### No lock ordering concerns (single-threaded).

title: HTTP/3 QPACK: a field value with obs-text octets fails the field section (and closes the connection) instead of decoding as Latin-1 like HTTP/1 and HTTP/2
description:
HTTP/3's QPACK decoder (src/http/h3_native.rs, qpack_decode_string, used for every field value) requires UTF-8. RFC 9110 §5.5 allows obs-text (octets 0x80-0xFF) in field values, and HTTP/1 and (after 6hvls9 LOW 4) HTTP/2 read such a value as Latin-1.

Effect: a peer whose response or request carries one obs-text octet in a header value (a legacy app's Content-Disposition filename, a Set-Cookie value relayed by a proxy) fails the whole field section. h3_quic.rs treats a QPACK decode failure as a connection error, so every other stream on that connection dies with it. The production adapter is static-only (h3_quic.rs advertises a zero table capacity), so field sections are the whole production surface.

Fix: decode field values in field sections (literal with static or dynamic name reference, literal name, post-base name reference) with a Latin-1 fallback when they are not UTF-8, as HPACK does. Header names, pseudo-header values and values whose name cannot be resolved stay UTF-8 only. Values inserted through the encoder stream stay UTF-8 only: the public QpackEncoderInstruction carries Strings, so the dynamic table could not count a Latin-1 value's octets (RFC 9204 §3.2.1). That path is reachable only with the opt-in dynamic mode.

Tests: obs-text values on each line form (raw and Huffman-coded) decode as Latin-1; a UTF-8 value is unchanged; pseudo-header values with obs-text are still refused; a response head built from a section with an obs-text value keeps the header. Control: field values decoded strictly again, tests kept.

Depends on HP (6hvls9 LOW 4) for hpack's octet-level Huffman decoder (made pub(crate)).

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
Evidence (SapphireHill fresh-eyes review of the wasm microtask-pump merge, 2026-09-10, hz4 lane_spawnlocal LIBUNITS.log):

1. `runtime::builder::tests::browser_host_services_pump_contract_and_local_future_resolution` (added by fff4532f9 / fe4b4edcc) has never passed anywhere: it builds `RuntimeBuilder::new().browser_host_services(...)` and the builder's default `worker_threads` is 4, host-independent (src/runtime/config.rs), while `BrowserHostServices::spawn_workers` requires exactly one worker. Build fails with "runtime init: BrowserHostServices requires single-worker topology, got 4 workers". The merge was landed without running the lib tests behind it (the same merge left the lib clippy-red, 15ed4ebb5).

2. With `.worker_threads(1)` pinned (landed with the Runtime::spawn_local guard commit), the test reaches step 7 and fails there: `runtime.spawn_local(pending)` parks a `LocalSpawnRequest` on the test thread's thread-local lane, `drop(runtime)` runs, and `assert!(cancelled_handle.is_finished())` is false. `RuntimeInner::drop` cancels only the Send mailbox requests (`gateway_mailbox.dequeue*`); nothing drains the thread-local `!Send` lane, so the parked request keeps its three JoinProducers alive and `LocalJoinHandle::is_finished` (terminal || strong_count == 1) stays false. The expectation "dropping the runtime cancels never-admitted local requests" has no implementation. Attributing lane entries to a runtime is the open design question: `LocalSpawnRequest` carries only a root RegionId (RegionId(0:0) for every runtime) and the pump thread has no lane owner outside a pump step.

Fix shape: either give `LocalSpawnRequest` a runtime identity (e.g. the mailbox Weak it was enqueued for) so `RuntimeInner::drop` can drain and fail its own entries on the dropping thread, or drop step 7 from the test and document that a parked local request outlives a dropped pump runtime until the thread's lane is drained. Until then the test stays red on main at step 7.

title: [cardinality-dos] observability/otel.rs: CardinalityTracker does NOT cap distinct metric names — unbounded memory growth via attacker-controlled metric strings
description:
src/observability/otel.rs:242-256 — CardinalityTracker::check_and_record(metric: &str, labels: &[KeyValue], max_cardinality: usize) caps the number of label combinations PER metric, but does NOT cap the number of distinct metric strings. The internal `seen: RwLock<HashMap<String, HashSet<u64>>>` grows one entry per unique metric name; a code path that derives the metric name from request attributes (`format!("user_request_{user_id}")`, request URL path, content type, etc.) can register an unbounded number of metric names.

Each new entry adds a HashMap row + a fresh HashSet. Sustained attacker pressure (one metric name per request) causes per-process memory to grow without bound — the tracker becomes a DoS surface even though label cardinality is locally bounded.

Threat model: any HTTP handler that funnels untrusted input into a metric name (a common Prometheus pattern) becomes a memory-exhaustion vector. The existing per-metric label cap was the right idea but applied to the wrong axis; the global axis is missing.

Fix direction:
  1. Add `max_metrics: usize` to CardinalityTrackerConfig.
  2. In check_and_record, before `seen.entry(metric.to_string()).or_default()`, check `if !seen.contains_key(metric) && seen.len() >= max_metrics { drop or fall through to "other" bucket }`.
  3. Emit a one-time WARN log when the global cap is hit (mirrors the closed asupersync-f4mdcr DecodingPipeline auth-skip pattern).
  4. Consider an LRU eviction when the cap is hit so periodic high-cardinality bursts can shift names rather than accumulate.

Severity HIGH because this is a SaaS-grade memory-DoS that today depends only on the observability tracker being reachable from a request handler — a very common shape.

Source: /multi-pass-bug-hunting deepest 8th-pass on src/observability/* (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Added MetricsConfig::max_metrics (default 4096) + with_max_metrics builder. CardinalityTracker::check_and_record refuses new metric names when cap hit; existing names still accept new label combinations. 3 regression tests added. Changes landed in commit 1df2e407e.

title: symbol_cancel: CleanupCoordinator::cleanup no-pending else-branch drops/strands a concurrently-registered symbol
description: Found by bug-hunt (SapphireHill 2026-06-29, same class as the d679m7 premature-quiescence race). src/cancel/symbol_cancel.rs cleanup() no-pending else-branch (~1798-1824) is NOT atomic vs register_pending (~1567-1594). The else-branch does, WITHOUT holding pending.write(): read cleanup_buffer count (~1801) -> cleanup_buffer.write().remove(object) (~1815) -> completed.write().insert(object) (~1822). register_pending holds pending.write() for its WHOLE body, checks completed then cleanup_buffer under it, then inserts into pending. TWO losses: (1) a symbol buffered (register_pending) in the window between the count-read and the buffer-remove is dropped wholesale when remove() drops the entire buffer entry; (2) a register_pending running between buffer-remove and completed-insert sees completed empty + buffer absent, inserts into pending, then the else-branch marks completed -> symbol stranded forever (handler already dropped; future register_pending short-circuits on completed; stats() reports it pending indefinitely). The CORRECT paths prove it: the success path inserts completed BEFORE removing the buffer (~1740-1741); clear_pending holds pending.write() ACROSS the completed insert (~1676-1677). FIX: mirror them — hold self.pending.write() across the else-branch's terminal (re-check empty -> buffer-remove -> completed-insert), preserving the register_pending pending->cleanup_buffer lock order to avoid deadlock; or at minimum insert completed before removing the buffer. Caveat: CleanupCoordinator is pub (cancel::CleanupCoordinator) but only CONSUMED BY TESTS today (not wired into the live ATP/QUIC receive path), so latent public-API race, not a live production hang yet.
close_reason: Fixed (SapphireHill, commit pending): CleanupCoordinator::cleanup no-pending else-branch was not atomic vs register_pending. Reworked it to hold pending -> completed -> cleanup_buffer (the same lock order/discipline as restore_*) across the empty-buffer check, buffer removal, and completed insert. register_pending holds pending.write() for its whole body, so serializing on pending blocks it during the critical section: a concurrently-registered symbol can no longer be dropped with the removed buffer entry nor stranded in pending just before completion. The >0 restore path runs OUTSIDE the guard (restore_* re-acquires the chain). Verified no lock inversion (restore_*/register_pending all use pending<completed<cleanup_buffer; reset releases state before wait_queue... n/a here). Test cleanup_no_pending_branch_never_strands_concurrent_register (strand invariant: completed => pending_symbols==0). clippy --all-targets -D warnings exit 0; 233 module tests green.

title: IO replay audit (r18): ReplayIo reports a faithful replay as Diverged when a poll was still pending as the capture window closed (design decision); ordered/group replay LOWs (Overlap under concurrent clock/entropy, misattributed divergence, refused constructors drop the live stream)
description:
Read-only audit r18-d0 (SapphireHill d0, 2026-10-09) of the public IO record/replay modules at origin c395fecc3. No HIGH. Every item fails closed: none can make a divergent replay pass. Full reports, with code excerpts, scenarios, fix sketches and regression-test sketches:
- /data/tmp/rc_20260922/audit_r18_B1_io_replay.md (src/io/replay.rs, replay/codec.rs)
- /data/tmp/rc_20260922/audit_r18_B2_io_replay_session.md (src/io/replay_session.rs and replay_session/**)
- /data/tmp/rc_20260922/audit_r18_B3_io_replay_group.md (src/io/replay_group*.rs and replay_group_session/**)

## MEDIUM (design decision needed)
M1. ReplayIo can report a faithful replay as Diverged (replay.rs ~614-656, verify_complete ~592-602).
- The capture leaves out a poll that was still Pending when the window closed. The docs say so: "Only completed polls are recorded".
- In replay, that poll's next attempt meets the end of the tape. It gets a sticky Exhausted, and verify_complete() returns Diverged.
- With a duplex consumer (split halves, join!) the window's last operation wakes the parked poll straight into that failure. Whether the verdict is Ok or Diverged then depends on scheduling: join! vs select!, or which task runs first.
- A sequential consumer (write().await, then read().await) cancelled at its pending read is a false red every time.
- The auditor's fix covers only the concurrent case: an operation already parked at window close stays Pending. It would leave the sequential case red.
- The underlying trade-off: a beyond-window poll as Exhausted catches a consumer that does more IO than was recorded, at the cost of these false reds. Recording pending polls removes both, but it is a tape format change. The single-stream ordered session already has a recorded-pending mode (new_with_pending_io).
- The group replay makes the same choice on purpose and pins it in tests. That is r18 B3 L2: a trailing read or a speculative read before a due write diverges.
- Options:
  - (a) document it, and give IoReplayError a classifier for beyond-window polls, e.g. "exhausted at index == operations", so a determinism oracle can tell this apart from a real mismatch;
  - (b) an opt-in recorded-pending capture for RecordingIo and the group;
  - (c) the auditor's parked-at-close rule (partial).

## LOW
- B1 L1: V1 tape export and import always fail with IoTapeError::Format on wasm32-unknown-unknown and wasi, because std::env::consts::OS is "" there (codec.rs ~189-193, ~322-336).
- B1 L3: the error-kind ids on the wire are positions in the KINDS array (codec.rs ~14-54). No fixed test vector pins them, so reordering the array would silently remap saved tapes.
- B1 L2 and B2 L5: write fingerprints are unkeyed SHA-256 of the plaintext with exact lengths, so short guessable writes can be recovered by trying candidates. Buffer growth also leaves unwiped copies; that part is the kkw7vk class. The docs' "SHA-256, not plaintext" and "zeroized on drop" overstate both.
- B2 L1 (gate.rs ~419-422): in the default ordered mode, a consumer that reads the clock or entropy before its I/O on every poll hangs with no error. negative_control_completed_effect_order_alone_loses_the_pending_wakeup pins this as known, but the docs promise the I/O "is woken on progress".
- B2 L2 (gate.rs ~352-358): an I/O poll that arrives while another thread is inside an entropy or clock call fails the whole session as Overlap. That I/O could have waited. Multi-threaded executors fail faithful replays at random.
- B2 L3 (poll/io.rs ~51-53, poll.rs ~208-209): poll-level replay reports an earlier entropy or clock divergence as an I/O mismatch.
- B2 L4 (replay_session.rs ~89-101, ordered.rs ~110-156): when the constructors refuse with max_streams == 0, they drop the caller's live I/O object, for example an open TCP or TLS stream.
- B2 L6 (poll/codec.rs ~97-112): the polled decoder accepts any digest on Read, Flush and Shutdown steps, although the encoder writes only one fixed value there. The ordered decoder validates the equivalent field.
- B3 L1 (replay_group.rs ~351-353, ~531): IoGroupReplayError::Exhausted says "polled after group exhaustion" even when only the polled stream is exhausted.
- B3 L3 (gate.rs ~239-245, replay_group_session.rs ~396-422): every committed effect scans all streams linearly, and the capture's finish/covers checks are quadratic.
- B3 L4 (replay_group_session.rs ~206-209): register calls the provider's is_write_vectored() outside the capture guard, unlike connect_with. A provider that uses the session's clock or entropy there records a tape that can never replay.

title: [security] codec/length_delimited.rs: decode path uses saturating_add on header_len while encode uses checked_add — asymmetric overflow allows usize::MAX state on 32-bit targets
description:
src/codec/length_delimited.rs:236 (decode path) computes `header_len` via `saturating_add`:

  let header_len = self
      .builder
      .length_field_offset
      .saturating_add(self.builder.length_field_length);

Compare with the encode path at line 397, which uses `checked_add` and propagates an error on overflow. The asymmetry is the bug: an attacker who can influence the codec's builder configuration (or a 32-bit target where realistic offsets approach usize::MAX) can saturate `header_len` to `usize::MAX` while the subsequent `total_frame_len = header_len.checked_add(frame_len)` then sees a wrapped value that may pass the `max_frame_length` check.

Concrete trigger on a 32-bit target: `length_field_offset = usize::MAX - 3`, `length_field_length = 4`. `saturating_add` clamps to `usize::MAX`. Subsequent `checked_add(frame_len)` with `frame_len = 0` returns `Some(usize::MAX)`. The state machine ends up in `Data(usize::MAX)` and either spins waiting for bytes that will never arrive or attempts a `usize::MAX` allocation.

Fix direction:
  1. Replace `saturating_add` at line 236 with `checked_add(...).ok_or_else(|| make_overflow_io_error())?`. Match the encode path's pattern verbatim — symmetry is the fix.
  2. Add a builder-time validation that `length_field_offset + length_field_length <= max_frame_length` so the operator can never construct a codec where the header is bigger than any decodable frame.
  3. Add a regression test that constructs a builder with `length_field_offset = usize::MAX - 3` and asserts that `decode_head` returns Err rather than entering the wrapped-state branch.

Source: /multi-pass-bug-hunting src/codec/* (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Fixed: LengthDelimitedCodec decode uses checked_add on header_len, symmetric with encode (commit ee7a273ba)

title: BrowserStorage persists bytes outside typed-array subviews
description: packages/browser/src/index.ts normalizeBrowserStorageValue delegates to normalizeWebTransportPayload, which deliberately preserves Uint8Array and ArrayBufferView subviews. BrowserStorage.set then passes that view directly to IndexedDB store.put. Structured cloning preserves the view's byteOffset/byteLength together with a clone of its entire backing ArrayBuffer. Concrete reproduction: a 1-byte Uint8Array at byteOffset 524288 over a 1048576-byte buffer is stored and read back with byteLength 1, byteOffset 524288, and buffer.byteLength 1048576; sentinel bytes outside the authorized 1-byte view remain recoverable through result.buffer. This creates a durable confidentiality leak when the caller's backing allocation contains adjacent secrets, and enables up to backing-buffer-size storage/memory amplification while BrowserArtifactStore accounts only logical view bytes. LocalStorage serializes only visible bytes and is not affected. Impact is live in the public BrowserStorage IndexedDB backend. Fix direction: introduce a storage-specific byte canonicalizer instead of changing the WebTransport no-copy normalizer. Keep a full-span Uint8Array fast path, but copy any subview or non-full-span ArrayBufferView into a right-sized owned Uint8Array before store.put. Canonicalize IndexedDB reads too so legacy or foreign subview records expose and retain only logical bytes. Regressions: store a tiny subview over a large buffer containing sentinels on both sides; assert the stored/read byteOffset is zero, buffer.byteLength equals byteLength, sentinels are absent, and artifact quota accounting matches physical retained bytes. Include ArrayBuffer, DataView, full-span, empty, and real IndexedDB structured-clone cases.

The target argument is an arbitrary string hashed into the fake transfer id — no peer resolution exists. (2) src/bin/atpd.rs: the daemon loads config/identity, starts an AppSpec service graph, but NEVER binds network.bind_addr (default 0.0.0.0:8472); the only real socket is the diagnostics HTTP endpoint (default 127.0.0.1:8473) serving a JSON health snapshot. title: [mock-code-finder] Define shared verification logging contract and proof artifact layout
description:
Background: The mock-code-finder repair program spans protocol conformance, database behavior, observability propagation, scheduler shutdown, sync invariants, and policy ratchets. Without a shared proof/logging contract, each implementation can pass locally while leaving inconsistent evidence for final signoff.

Goal: define the common contract every domain e2e/proof script must follow. This is plan-space infrastructure: it should be decided before implementations so future workers can build scripts that produce comparable, grep-friendly, machine-readable evidence.

Required log fields: bead_id, scenario_id, subsystem, support_class, source_files_inspected, command, rch_command_if_used, cargo_features, test_filter, env_keys_required with secret values redacted, deterministic_seed_or_fixture_id, input_artifact, output_artifact, expected_behavior, actual_behavior, verdict, first_failure_line, duration_ms, git_sha_or_tree_state, blocker_bead_id if blocked, and evidence_quality such as live, fixture_only, unsupported, expected_fail, or blocked.

Design considerations: scripts should emit JSONL for machines plus concise human summaries; failures must exit nonzero; logs must avoid secrets; artifact paths must be stable under artifacts/mock-code-finder or a similarly scoped directory; outputs must be deterministic enough for CI and future archaeology; no script should claim production conformance from a local fake model.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- A documented JSONL schema exists for every proof/e2e script, with required fields and allowed verdict/evidence_quality/support_class values.
- A validator or self-test exists and is usable by child proof scripts and the aggregate runner.
- Golden/fixture records cover pass, fail, blocked, unsupported, expected_fail, fixture_only, malformed JSON, missing required fields, zero-scenario child output, and redacted secret/env values.
- Unit tests verify schema parsing, validation failures, redaction checks, deterministic artifact path construction, and stable human-summary rendering.
- E2E fixture scripts demonstrate that the validator fails nonzero on malformed or dishonest evidence and preserves detailed logs for debugging.
- The contract explicitly forbids claiming production conformance from local fake models, fixture-only data, or audit-only structs.
close_reason: Shared mock-code-finder verification contract and validator are present; validator self-test passed; rch cargo test -p asupersync --test mock_code_finder_verification_contract mock_code_finder passed 3 qlvtin contract tests. Local rch wrapper was terminated after remote test success because artifact retrieval hung.

title: Real-SQLite roundtrip: transaction body cancelled mid-flight must fully rollback and leave file consistent
description: with_sqlite_transaction (src/database/transaction.rs:442) calls tx.rollback on the Outcome::Cancelled arm, and SqliteTransaction::Drop (src/database/sqlite.rs:1801) calls poison_for_rollback for the unwind path. Both rely on the underlying rusqlite ROLLBACK propagating to the on-disk WAL before any other connection can observe the partial write. Existing unit tests use :memory: and don't exercise the on-disk WAL fsync path. Add tests/sqlite_real_disk_cancel_rollback.rs that opens a tempdir-backed SQLite file, runs with_sqlite_transaction with a body that INSERTs a row then sleeps on a Cx that gets cancelled from a sidecar thread, asserts (a) outcome is Outcome::Cancelled, (b) the row is NOT visible on a fresh connection to the same file (rollback hit disk), (c) PRAGMA integrity_check returns 'ok' (no torn writes).
close_reason: Real-SQLite cancel-rollback durability test landed in 0e30027c2 (the other agent's commit swept up the file I authored from working tree). tests/sqlite_real_disk_cancel_rollback.rs::sqlite_real_disk_cancel_during_tx_body_rolls_back_and_leaves_file_consistent: tempdir-backed SQLite file with journal_mode=WAL, with_sqlite_transaction body INSERTs a row then awaits a 5s sleep on a Cx that gets cancelled by a sidecar std::thread after 150ms; asserts (a) Outcome::Cancelled with CancelKind::User, (b) elapsed < 3s (proves cancel landed mid-body), (c) fresh SqliteConnection on same path sees 0 rows (rollback hit disk before another reader could observe), (d) PRAGMA integrity_check returns 'ok' (no torn pages, no orphaned WAL frames). Compiles under cargo check --features sqlite --test sqlite_real_disk_cancel_rollback. Each assertion failure message points at the relevant src/database/transaction.rs:442 / src/database/sqlite.rs:1801 line for review.
