title: README describes adaptive cancel-streak controller as opt-in EXP3/Hedge {4,8,16,32}; shipped is default-on discounted UCB1 {4,8,16,32,64}
description:
Discovered during the 2026-08-13 asupersync-mega-skill refresh + adversarial verification pass (SapphireHill). README describes the adaptive cancel-streak scheduler controller as a deterministic EXP3/Hedge policy in at least five places, but the shipped controller at HEAD 91c7da69f is discounted UCB1, with a different arm set and a different default posture. README even prints EXP3 weight-update equations as if they were the shipped mechanism.

DOC CLAIMS (all README.md):
- :55 capability table — "Deterministic EXP3/Hedge policy tunes cancel streak limits with regret-bounded updates"
- :375-386 — section "Regret-Bounded Adaptive Cancel Preemption (Deterministic EXP3/Hedge)": "Workers CAN run a deterministic EXP3/Hedge-style policy over ... {4, 8, 16, 32}", followed by the EXP3 p_t(a)/w_{t+1}(a) formulas
- :794 scheduler bullet — "workers run an EXP3/Hedge-style policy over candidate cancel-streak limits"
- :1320 math table row — "EXP3/Hedge no-regret online learning"
- :1334 alien-artifact status table — "EXP3/Hedge scheduler control | Implemented runtime scheduling control surface"

SHIPPED IMPLEMENTATION (src/runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs):
- :520-522 "Discounted UCB1 policy for adaptive cancel-streak limits" (AdaptiveCancelStreakPolicy); select_arm_ucb at :582
- :172 ADAPTIVE_STREAK_ARMS: [usize; 5] = [4, 8, 16, 32, 64] — five arms including 64 (README says {4, 8, 16, 32})
- :173 ADAPTIVE_UCB_DISCOUNT = 0.95; default arm index 2 == 16 (:544)
- reward in [0,1] blends normalized Lyapunov drop + deadline penalty + fairness penalty + fallback penalty (:511-516), plus an anytime-valid e-process over epoch rewards (:532, :644-645, :3396)
- DEFAULT-ON: src/runtime/config.rs:2234-2235 — enable_adaptive_cancel_streak: true, adaptive_cancel_streak_epoch_steps: 128. README's "Workers can run" phrasing reads as opt-in.

IMPORTANT NUANCE: a seeded EXP3 controller genuinely exists in ATP transport adaptation (src/net/atp/transport_rq/adaptive.rs:6 — "seeded EXP3 controller ... opt-in"), so a blanket s/EXP3/UCB1/ across the repo would be wrong. The scheduler sections must be re-attributed while the ATP transport description keeps EXP3.

FIX: update the five README locations to describe the shipped discounted-UCB1 controller (arms {4, 8, 16, 32, 64}, discount 0.95, fixed epoch-boundary updates, blended reward, e-process monitor, enabled by default), or — if EXP3/Hedge remains the intended design direction — state explicitly that the shipped selector is discounted UCB1 and EXP3/Hedge is design lineage. Keep the regret language honest: discounted UCB1 carries a nonstationary stochastic-bandit guarantee, not EXP3's adversarial no-regret bound — do not carry the adversarial-regret claim over unexamined.

ACCEPTANCE:
- README scheduler bullet, capability table, alien-artifact table, and math table rows match three_lane.rs (algorithm family, arm set, default-on status).
- ATP transport EXP3 attribution preserved (src/net/atp/transport_rq/adaptive.rs).

title: README/AGENTS proc-macro contract section is false at HEAD (race! drains, join! concurrent, select!+entry attrs missing)
description:
Discovered during the 2026-08-13 asupersync-mega-skill refresh + adversarial verification pass (SapphireHill). README's "Proc Macros" current-contract section makes three claims that are false or incomplete at HEAD 91c7da69f, and the section actively misleads on cancellation semantics — the exact topic this project treats as contract-grade.

FALSE/INCOMPLETE CLAIMS (README.md ~lines 1203-1208):

1. README:1207 — "`race!` expands to `Cx::race*`; losers are cancelled by drop, not drained. Use `Scope::race` when loser-drain semantics matter."
   At HEAD, `race!` expands ONLY to the drain-correct `Cx::race_drained` / `race_drained_named` / `race_drained_timeout(_named)` family (asupersync-macros/src/race.rs:163-174); every loser is protocol-cancelled AND drained before return, and race.rs:248-249 carries an explicit regression guard that the old drop-only expansion "must never reappear". The macro rustdoc (asupersync-macros/src/lib.rs:266-310) and docs/macro-dsl.md both state drain-correctness. The remaining drop-only boundaries the rewrite should state instead: the `timeout:` elapsed path abandons the whole race by drop (src/cx/cx.rs:3938-3943), and direct `Cx::race*` calls are drop-on-cancel.

2. README:1206 — "`join!` and `join_all!` are supported today, but they still await branches sequentially."
   At HEAD both poll all branches concurrently in one `poll_fn` (asupersync-macros/src/join.rs:3-5,19-21: "three 10ms sleeps complete in ~10ms, not ~30ms"), replacing the earlier sequential placeholder (join.rs:31-36), with regression tests forbidding fallback to the sequential chain (join.rs:376,386).

3. README:1203 — "Supported root macros in `proc-macros` builds are `scope!`, `spawn!`, `join!`, `join_all!`, and `race!`."
   Omits `select!` (N-ary heterogeneous drain-correct select, asupersync-macros/src/select.rs; exported at src/lib.rs:451) and the `#[main]` / `#[test]` / `#[lab_test]` entry attributes. AGENTS.md:272 ("# scope!, spawn!, join!, race! macros") and AGENTS.md:838 carry the same stale list.

WHY IT MATTERS: an agent following README will avoid `race!`/`select!` whenever loser drain matters and hand-roll drain logic (or drop to `Scope::race` unnecessarily), producing worse code and contradicting the drain guarantees the macro crate now tests. This drift already propagated: the in-repo agent skill copied the stale drop-only claim verbatim twice before being caught by source-level verification (fixed in skill commit 0817fd6fa). Cancellation-semantics documentation drift is exactly the class the backwards-compat/escaped-defect policy treats as serious.

FIX:
- Rewrite the README "Current contract" bullets to match the macro crate rustdoc: `race!`/blocking `select!` drain-correct via `Cx::race_drained*`/`Scope::race_all`; `select!` `else` form polls each branch exactly once in source order and never drains; `race!` `timeout:` elapsed abandons by drop; branches must be `Send + 'static` with spawn authority; `join!`/`join_all!` poll concurrently in one `poll_fn`; supported list includes `select!` and the entry attributes.
- Update AGENTS.md:272 and AGENTS.md:838 macro lists to match.
- STRUCTURAL GUARD (required — this drift survived the race!-rework landing unnoticed): pin the corrected macro-contract sentences in a checked lane, either by extending tests/readme_claim_freshness_contract.rs or by adding doc-consistency assertions alongside the macro trybuild suite, so a future docs-vs-expansion divergence fails a test instead of persisting.

title: [ERASURE-CHANNEL reliability] EcReceiver.pending reassembly buffer is UNBOUNDED — add max_pending cap + FIFO eviction before wiring a lossy transport
close_reason: Fixed: EcReceiver reassembly buffer now bounded (DEFAULT_MAX_PENDING_MESSAGES=1024 + max_pending field + pending_order VecDeque FIFO eviction in ingest_unit; try_complete keeps index in sync). comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE (first-principles): src/channel/erasure.rs EcReceiver. recv() inserts a MessageReassembler into pending: HashMap<u64,(MessageHeader,MessageReassembler)> on each Header (line 518) and only removes it when is_ready() (try_complete line 553). An incomplete message — loss exceeds the N-K repair margin, or the sender is cancelled mid-send leaving <K symbols, or a message_id is abandoned — NEVER becomes ready and is NEVER evicted. No cap/TTL/LRU. INVARIANT VIOLATED: a fountain-coded reassembler must bound in-flight partial state; this one doesn't. IMPACT: with the module's INTENDED lossy/untrusted transport (the whole point of K-of-N coding), incomplete messages are intrinsic -> pending grows unbounded -> OOM/DoS (bounded only by max_message_size PER message, not by COUNT). CURRENTLY LATENT: no live EcReceiver callers (unwired) and the present transport is loss-free in-memory (erasure.rs:412), so every message completes today. FIX: add max_pending_messages to ErasureChannelConfig (default ~256, mirroring max_message_size); track insertion order (VecDeque<message_id>); on a NEW header when pending.len()>=cap, evict the oldest still-incomplete entry (lazy: pop_front skipping ids already completed/removed) before inserting; add a regression test (sender emits headers + <K symbols for many ids -> pending stays bounded). title: Redis PubSub control loops buffer invalid acknowledgements and can hang
description: RedisPubSub subscribe/psubscribe/unsubscribe/punsubscribe control loops buffer every non-matching PubSubEvent while waiting for acknowledgements. With exclusive &mut self, only interleaved Message events are legitimate; a wrong Subscription kind or unsolicited Pong is a protocol violation, but today it is queued and the loop waits indefinitely for another frame. The parsed remaining count is also ignored, including negative or state-divergent counts. Reject wrong control kinds promptly, validate nonnegative/coherent remaining counts against tracked channel+pattern state, preserve legitimate interleaved messages, and add deterministic fail-closed/poison regressions for wrong kind/target/count.

title: Redis PubSub PING accepts wrong payload as success
description: RedisPubSub::parse_event classifies every top-level non-null BulkString as Pong, and RedisPubSub::ping accepts Pong(_) without validating the requested payload. Consequently PING expected succeeds on an unrelated or wrong bulk reply, and argument-less PING accepts any bulk payload. Move RESP3 scalar PONG handling into the PING control context, require +PONG for no-argument RESP3 PING (while preserving RESP2 [pong, empty] fallback), and require byte-exact bulk/array echo for PING payload including empty/non-UTF8 bytes. Wrong shape or mismatch must return RedisError::Protocol and poison the ambiguous control connection. Add deterministic correct/mismatch/no-argument regressions.

title: REFUTED perf hypothesis: do NOT replace h1 windows(2).position CRLF scan with memmem::find (memmem is 4.7x SLOWER here)
description: Hypothesis: the h1 chunked/response CRLF scans (windows(2).position(|w| w==b'\r\n') at stream.rs, client.rs) are slow scalar scans that should use memchr::memmem::find like the request-header path. MEASURED via the project's own http1/crlf_scan bench (protocol_benchmark): find/legacy_scalar (windows(2).position) = 8.78 ns vs find/memmem = 41.27 ns — memmem is 4.7x SLOWER. Reason: memmem has SIMD-searcher/prefilter setup overhead that dominates for a 2-byte needle matched near the buffer front, which is exactly the codec case (the \r\n ends the current chunk-size/trailer line at the front). The 'legacy_scalar' bench name is misleading: the scalar scan is CORRECT and faster here; the bench exists to JUSTIFY it. I applied memmem, measured, and REVERTED (git-clean). Do not re-attempt. Lesson: measure before committing — the plausible SIMD swap was a pessimization. Refuted by profiling 2026-07-14.

title: [fs/file] seek/read/write methods need mutable access to Arc<File> content
description:
Compilation error in src/fs/file.rs due to borrowing issues. Methods like seek(), stream_position(), rewind(), read(), write(), flush() try to call mutable operations on &std::fs::File when they need &mut std::fs::File. The file is wrapped in Arc<std::fs::File> which provides only immutable access.

Root cause: Recent refactor consolidated blocking wrappers but didn't handle the mutability requirements properly.

Solution: Use either:
1. Unsafe pointer manipulation (since file operations are atomic at OS level)  
2. Convert to async patterns using with_inner() method
3. Use interior mutability (Mutex<File> or similar)

Compiler errors:
- src/fs/file.rs:150: cannot borrow inner as mutable (seek)
- src/fs/file.rs:157: cannot borrow inner as mutable (stream_position)  
- src/fs/file.rs:164: cannot borrow inner as mutable (rewind)
- src/fs/file.rs:179: cannot borrow inner as mutable (read)
- src/fs/file.rs:192: cannot borrow inner as mutable (write)
- src/fs/file.rs:198: cannot borrow inner as mutable (flush)
- src/fs/file.rs:214: cannot borrow inner as mutable (AsyncSeek::poll_seek)
close_reason: Fixed compilation errors in fs/file.rs by resolving Arc<File> mutability issues. Used Arc::try_unwrap when possible and unsafe pointer manipulation for shared access patterns. Also fixed several clippy warnings in observability module.

title: Remote service audit: peer budget raises its own priority and its absolute deadline is read on the wrong clock; finished handler cached as Cancelled; idle peers' idempotency memory never freed; no per-IP slot limit
description:
Read-only audit of src/remote.rs (remote computation service: mutual-TLS, one length-prefixed JSON request with hello/computation/input/lease/idempotency key/optional budget; V3 sends Accepted then handles Cancel/RenewLease until one Terminal event; V2/V3 outcomes cached per peer by idempotency key) at origin/main 4ef260a14 (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-04). No HIGH. Known items of asupersync-bi2462.77 (per-peer admission before decode, protected control lane, legacy-path accounting, static peer labels) were excluded.

## MEDIUM
1. The peer's wire budget raises its own scheduling priority and is read against the wrong clock. The wire budget is copied as-is (3288) and the V3 path opens the child region with it (4903-4908); combining with the parent budget takes the HIGHER priority (types/budget.rs 565), so priority 255 from a peer outranks all local ready-lane work, although RemoteCap documents remote_budget as a ceiling ("tighter than region budget"). deadline_nanos is an absolute Time from the ORIGIN process's clock (time/driver.rs 67-71), so on a server up longer than the client it lands in the past and the handler is cancelled at its first checkpoint (client sees LeaseExpired). The V2 path ignores the request budget (5425-5427). Priority: a peer must not raise it. Deadline: needs a relative encoding (wire-format change; owner decision) or dropping.
2. A handler that already finished can be reported and cached as Cancelled: the V3 race checks lease expiry before task.poll_join (5016-5023); expire/cancel/disconnect paths (5043, 5150, 5396; helper 5562-5575) return Cancelled(reason) without polling the task. V2 has the same order (5465-5471). distributed/remote_owned.rs 376-385 polls the join result after close.
3. Idempotency memory is not released for idle peers: records keep the full input bytes plus the outcome (1607-1612, 1625-1627); expired records are evicted only when the same peer is admitted again (3518-3522, 3570). Defaults (4096 records x ~32 KiB input + 64 KiB outcome) let one peer pin ~380 MiB for the life of the process once it goes quiet, contrary to 1561-1563 (TTL bounds memory).
4. Unauthenticated clients can occupy every connection slot: only a listener-wide cap (9357, 9466); ConnectionManager::new leaves the per-IP limit unset (server/connection.rs 148) and with_per_ip_max (174) is never called. A client stalling in the TLS handshake holds a slot up to the handshake/initial-frame timeout (9489-9504).

## LOW
1. No write deadline when sending frames (3826-3840; used 4582, 5305): a peer that stops reading holds its slot until drain or force-close.
2. Renewal echoes the unclamped requested lease (5205-5209) though the server enforces at most 24 h (5202), contrary to 4102-4106.
3. Admission errors leak configuration before authentication: a peer with a CA-valid but unpinned certificate learns which NodeIds are granted and a granted one's SPKI pin list (2593-2597, 2553-2557, 4514-4518; tls/error.rs 174-182). The bootstrap check (8849-8899) accepts the same pin under two node ids.
4. In-flight idempotency records can be stranded when one connection's context is cancelled while the listener keeps running (9655-9683): the key stays OperationInFlight and uses the peer's record cap.
5. MembershipLeaseManager never prunes released or expired leases of live nodes (1501-1507, 1538).

## Checked and sound
Pre-auth frame length cap with bounded buffer (3773-3788), strict JSON (deny_unknown_fields), no decompression, cancel-reason cause depth 64 (2958-3153), first-frame timeout; dispatch needs a verified client leaf matching a pin, constant-time compare, report-only pin sets refused (2488, 2553-2564); origin rebuilt from the authenticated hello (3279), cache keyed by the authenticated peer; V3 commands only reach the connection's own task, renewal ids strictly increasing (5118-5204); no panics from peer input; V3 disconnect/flush failure/decode error cancel and drain the child then commit; client driver guard always publishes a terminal result; dropped RemoteHandle requests cancellation.

title: Retry jitter boundary math can panic or exceed the configured cap
description: ExponentialBackoff::calculate_delay computes Full jitter with entropy % (max_delay + 1); a public max_delay_ms == u64::MAX overflows in debug and wraps to % 0 in release, panicking synchronously inside RetryFuture::poll. Decorrelated jitter also returns uncapped base_delay whenever the computed upper bound is <= base_delay, so base > max (including base 30001 with the default max 30000) violates the configured delay cap; SmartRetry inherits it. Add an unbiased inclusive sampler with an explicit full-u64 case, make inverted/degenerate Decorrelated intervals return the capped upper bound, and add deterministic MAX/zero/base-above-cap tests plus metamorphic coverage that removes the current max>=base assumption.

title: perf(runtime/reactor/epoll): reduce two-lock + HashMap overhead on poll hot path
description:
Static /profiling-software-performance hand-off for /extreme-software-optimization. No live bench this session (reactor is hard to isolate without a driver); hotspot ranking is static-evidence-only with code citations at src/runtime/reactor/epoll.rs. File an issue here for scoring (Impact × Confidence / Effort ≥ 2.0) before any code change.

SCENARIO FINGERPRINT (proposed for when a bench harness lands):
- N registered fds in {64, 512, 4096}; K ready events per tick in {1, 16, 128}
- Workload: EpollReactor::poll called 1M times with pre-registered fds and a driver generating ready events
- Metric: per-poll p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU%, contention (if another worker registers concurrently)

RANKED HOTSPOT TABLE (static evidence):

| Rank | Location | Metric | Expected Cost | Category | Evidence |
|------|----------|--------|---------------|----------|----------|
| 1 | poll() double-lock acquisition | wait_ns/poll | 2 parking_lot::Mutex lock/unlock per poll call (poll_events + state). ~40-80ns baseline uncontended; O(worker_count) under contention | lock | epoll.rs:491 (poll_events.lock), :507 (state.lock) |
| 2 | translate_poll_event under state lock | p95 latency | For each of N ready events, HashMap<Token, RegistrationInfo>::get with default SipHash; loop held under state lock | CPU+lock | epoll.rs:269, 512-516 |
| 3 | registration_count() each call takes state lock | wait_ns | Reports tokens.len() but acquires full Mutex; schedulers that poll this per-tick pay lock cost for a counter read | lock | epoll.rs:528-530 |
| 4 | PollEvents::with_capacity on hysteresis-triggered resize | alloc/poll | Vec reallocation when current<target or current>=4*target; rare but visible in p99 tail | alloc | epoll.rs:276-278 (predicate), 499-500 (allocation) |
| 5 | Debug::fmt takes state lock | correctness/debug | state.lock() inside Debug::fmt would deadlock if a thread Debug-prints while holding the lock; benign under AGENTS.md lock ordering but adds Mutex in tracing paths | lock | epoll.rs:533-540 |

HYPOTHESIS LEDGER:
- two-lock overhead: supports — both locks are parking_lot::Mutex<T>; uncontended ~20-40ns each, contended scales with worker count
- HashMap hot-path: supports — SipHash at ~30-50ns per lookup, called N times per poll with state lock held
- resize thrashing: rejects — should_resize_poll_events at :276-278 has 4×-hysteresis, thrash needs oscillating capacity requests across polls
- registration_count contention: unknown — needs callgraph audit; if schedulers call per-tick, this is a straightforward atomic-counter win

CANDIDATE LEVERS (for extreme-software-optimization scoring):
1. Thread-local PollEvents per reactor worker — eliminates the poll_events Mutex entirely. High impact if reactor is per-worker, zero if single-reactor; confirm architecture first.
2. registration_count -> AtomicUsize incremented on register, decremented on deregister — removes one Mutex acquisition every time schedulers read the count.
3. Switch tokens: HashMap<Token, RegistrationInfo> to FxHashMap or ahash — integer keys benefit most; per-event ~30-50ns → ~5-10ns.
4. Snapshot the interest lookups before the loop — walk poll_events once to collect Tokens, take state.lock() briefly, collect (token, interest) into a local Vec, drop the lock, then build Events outside. Shrinks critical section from O(N) to roughly a single hash-bulk-lookup.
5. Split state Mutex into two: one for token-hot-path reads (RwLock favoring readers) and one for register/modify mutations.

Audit commits: 12509448 (sharded_state deadlock-audit CLEAN) → 5f91f5d4 (buffered backpressure laws) → 9b199562 (grpc-timeout conformance). No code changes in this bead.

title: Instrument task lifecycle with tracing spans
description:
# Task

Add tracing instrumentation to task lifecycle in runtime/scheduler.

## What to Instrument

1. **Task spawn**: When `scope.spawn()` is called
   - Fields: task_id, owning_region, name (if provided), initial_state
   
2. **Task poll**: Each time the task is polled
   - Fields: task_id, poll_number, budget_remaining
   - Keep as trace-level to avoid overhead
   
3. **Task wake**: When waker is invoked
   - Fields: task_id, wake_source (timer, io, explicit)
   
4. **Task state transitions**: Created → Running → CancelRequested → Cancelling → Finalizing → Completed
   - Fields: task_id, from_state, to_state, outcome (on completion)

5. **Task completion**: Final outcome
   - Fields: task_id, outcome_kind (Ok/Err/Cancelled/Panicked), duration, poll_count

## Implementation Notes

- Task span should be child of region span
- Use span.in_scope() for poll instrumentation
- Wake events use follows_from to link to waker source
- Completion closes the task span

## Causality Links

```
Region[1] ──creates──> Task[100]
Task[100] ──woken_by──> Timer[5] 
Task[100] ──woken_by──> IoEvent[fd=3]
Task[100] ──cancelled_by──> Region[1].close()
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Spawn creates task span as child of region
- [ ] Poll events recorded at trace level
- [ ] Wake events include source
- [ ] State transitions recorded
- [ ] Completion includes outcome and metrics
- [ ] Causality links correctly established
close_reason:
Instrumented task lifecycle with tracing spans:

1. **Task spawn** (scope.rs): Already had debug_span + debug! with task_id, region_id, initial_state, budget fields. Fixed StoredTask::new() -> StoredTask::new_with_id() so poll tracing actually fires with task IDs (was silently inactive before).

2. **Task poll** (stored_task.rs): trace-level events now include task_id, poll_number, budget_remaining. Added set_polls_remaining() for executor to supply budget context.

3. **Task wake** (waker.rs): Added WakeSource enum (Timer, Io{fd}, Explicit, Unknown). New waker_for_source() method enables source attribution. Wake trace now includes wake_source field. 4 new tests for source variants + equality.

4. **Task state transitions** (record/task.rs): Already fully instrumented at every transition (Created->Running, ->CancelRequested, ->Cancelling, ->Finalizing, ->Completed) with trace!/debug! including old_state, new_state, cancel_kind, budgets.

5. **Task completion** (record/task.rs): Enhanced complete() and finalize_done() to include duration_us and poll_count metrics. Added total_polls counter and created_instant (wall-clock Instant) fields to TaskRecord.

6. **Causality links**: WakeSource enables linking wake events to their source (timer, io fd, explicit). follows_from() available via tracing_compat NoopSpan for when tracing-integration feature is enabled.

title: atp CLI legacy delta receive/commit/state server never runs (receive delta gate always off; spawn_delta_state_server has no caller) and carries latent HIGH defects if revived: root replacement deletes receiver-only files, no fsync before deleting the old copy, torn state wedges receives, unauthenticated state disclosure; decide: remove/compile-gate or fix
description:
Read-only audit of the atp CLI's delta receive/commit/state-server path in src/bin/atp.rs (path helpers ~4100-4310, apply_delta_packages, refresh/export/serve_delta_state_connection ~6035-6440, commit_delta_tree_files/safe_delta_path ~6844-7000) at origin/main 1edbeeb61 (SapphireHill rc_20260923 audit agent, 10-09; reachability re-verified by SapphireHill: selected_cli_metadata_policy() sets preserve_timestamps: true, so cli_content_delta_enabled() is always false, pinned by the test at atp.rs:9750; spawn_delta_state_server has no caller).

OWNER DECISION: this receive/commit/serve path never runs in a production build. Every finding is latent, several HIGH if the gate flips (the next change to selected_cli_metadata_policy would turn F2-F4 and F8 on for every receive). Options: (a) remove or #[cfg(test)]-gate the legacy receive/commit/serve code (keep __delta-state-export, which is live and local), or (b) fix F1-F8 before any gate change. Not claimed.

I reviewed origin/main at `1edbeeb61`. None of the in-scope paths that write files or answer the network run in a production build. Every finding below is a latent defect that becomes live if a gate is switched on.

# ATP CLI delta receive / commit / state-server audit

## Reachability

- **Receive-side delta is always off.** `delta_enabled = cli_content_delta_enabled(args.no_delta)` (atp.rs:8964) is always false:
  - `selected_cli_metadata_policy()` (891-896) sets `preserve_timestamps: true`.
  - `cli_delta_policy_is_content_only` (4287) requires it to be false.
  - The test at 9750 pins it: `assert!(!cli_content_delta_enabled(false))`.
  - So `handle_post_receive_delta` (5701) returns at 5702-5704. `apply_delta_packages`, `apply_delta_package`, `commit_delta_tree_files`, `write_delta_files_under` and `refresh_delta_state` never execute.
- **The state server is dead code.** `spawn_delta_state_server` (6219, `#[allow(dead_code)]`) has zero callers in the repo, so `serve_delta_state_connection` and `write_all_tcp_before_deadline` never run.
- **The sender never builds a package or fetches remote state.** Both sit behind `allow_unauthenticated_delta_sidecar`, which is rejected at 3190, 3702 and 8919.
- **A network sender cannot plant a package even if the gate flips.** The library receivers reject `.asupersync-atp-delta-package-*` and `.asupersync-atp-delta-v1` names (safety.rs:1100-1107, called from transport_rq:5352, transport_quic:9536, streaming:279). Only a local process that can write to dest could plant one.
- **Live in-scope code, local only:**
  - `validate_user_transfer_namespace` runs on every `atp send` (1850).
  - `export_delta_state` runs via the hidden `__delta-state-export` command (188, 13782).

## Findings

**F1. A commit replaces the whole top-level root, deleting receiver-only files with no safety checks.**
- Severity: LOW today. HIGH if a package can reach dest.
- Location: `commit_delta_tree_files` 6844-6933.
- Mechanism:
  - `final_target = dest/<first component>` (6851-6852).
  - If it differs from the object, the existing tree is renamed to `state/backups` (6887-6892) and the staged tree renamed in (6898).
  - The backup is then deleted with `remove_dir_all` (6901-6905).
- Trigger: dest/tree holds `payload.bin` and `local.txt`, where `local.txt` was added after the last state refresh or came from another sender. A package whose object is only `tree/payload.bin` is applied.
- Wrong outcomes:
  - `local.txt` is permanently deleted.
  - Edits made to `payload.bin` after the state export are silently overwritten. Nothing checks that the current tree still matches the base the package was diffed against.
  - Every file is recreated with umask defaults, so a 0600 file becomes 0644.
- Contrast: the library commits file by file. Its mirror deletion is opt-in and has a max-delete-fraction guard (transport_common/mirror.rs:1-25).
- Why tests miss it: `delta_commit_retry_removes_staging_and_backup_artifacts` (10128) only uses files present on both sides, and it asserts `backups/` is empty, which pins the deletion.
- Fix shape:
  - Before replacing, require the current root's snapshot sha to equal the receiver-state base.
  - Either commit per file, or keep backups unless mirror mode is explicitly enabled.
- Failing test: create `tree/local.txt` before calling commit, then assert it still exists.

**F2. Nothing is fsynced before the old copy is deleted.**
- Severity: latent MEDIUM.
- The only `sync_all` in the file is a test fixture (13531).
- Order of operations: `write_delta_files_under` writes files without syncing (6935-6947), the staged tree is renamed in (6898), the backup is deleted (6903), the receipt is written (5788-5795) and the package is removed (5797).
- Wrong outcome: after a crash, the new files can be empty (ext4 delayed allocation; `auto_da_alloc` does not cover renaming a directory) while the old copy is already gone.
- Fix shape: fsync the files, the staging directories, the rename and the dest directory, and only then delete the backup and write the receipt.

**F3. A torn state file wedges the receiver permanently.**
- Severity: latent MEDIUM.
- `refresh_delta_state` rewrites chunk files (6070-6073) and `state.json` (6078-6087) in place with `File::create`, which truncates.
- After a crash mid-write, a short chunk file triggers a fatal "existing delta state chunk does not match" (6061-6067) on every later refresh.
- `finish_delta_refresh` turns that fatal error into Err even when nothing was applied (5714-5722). Every later `recv --once` then exits non-zero after a successful transfer, until someone cleans up by hand.
- A torn `state.json` makes `apply_delta_package` fail. The `?` at 5705 then skips the refresh as well.
- Fix shape:
  - Write each state file to a temp file, fsync it, then rename it into place.
  - Treat a content-addressed chunk that does not match as a cache miss and rewrite it.
- Failing test: truncate one `<id>.chunk` file, call `refresh_delta_state`, and expect Ok.

**F4. One bad entry in dest blocks every package and every refresh.**
- Severity: latent LOW/MEDIUM.
- `apply_delta_packages` returns Err in all of these cases:
  - any top-level entry with a non-UTF-8 name, even an unrelated user file (5742-5744; this check runs before the reserved-name filter);
  - a reserved name in non-canonical case;
  - a reserved package path that is a file;
  - an `.applied` entry that is a directory (5781-5785);
  - any package that fails to apply (5787).
- A failing package is never removed. A name like `…-package-0` sorts first, so it blocks every later package and the refresh on every receive.
- An unapplied package that already contains an `.applied` file is deleted without being applied and without a log line (5776-5778). The receipt is not tied to the object sha.
- Fix shape:
  - Skip non-reserved non-UTF-8 names (as `collect_delta_dest_tree_files` already does).
  - Move failed packages into a quarantine directory and continue.
  - Tie the receipt to the object sha.
- Failing test: create `dest/"\xff"` plus one valid package and expect `applied == 1`.

**F5. Paths are checked and then used by name, and the state directory's ownership is never verified.**
- Severity: latent MEDIUM; needs a local attacker.
- The guards (4100-4150) check with `symlink_metadata`. The operations then use plain path calls that follow symlinks:
  - `File::create` (4182) follows a symlink in the final component and truncates the target;
  - `create_dir_all` (4169) follows symlinks in intermediate components;
  - `rename` (4253).
- The re-check in `write_delta_file` (4191) runs after the truncation has already happened.
- `create_delta_dir_all` accepts an existing `.asupersync-atp-delta-v1` directory owned by someone else (4167-4171).
- Trigger: dest is a shared inbox (mode 1777 or group-writable). Another user pre-creates the state directory. Because they own it, they can swap the receiver's `staging-*` directory for a symlink between `require_delta_directory` and `File::create`. The receiver then writes the delta content as the receiving user, outside dest.
  - That user also receives the victim's previous tree when it is moved into `state/backups` (6887-6892).
- Fix shape:
  - Create the state directory with `create_dir` and mode 0700.
  - Verify its owner is the current user and that group/other cannot write it.
  - Do all I/O relative to directory handles (openat with `O_NOFOLLOW|O_EXCL`, e.g. cap-std or rustix).
  - Use `create_new` for staging files.

**F6. The symlink guard checks system directories above dest.**
- Severity: LOW, functional.
- `delta_link_or_reparse_prefix` (4101-4106) checks every ancestor of the absolute path, with no trusted starting point.
- Any dest under a symlinked prefix is refused: `/tmp` and `/var` on macOS, a symlinked home directory, a symlinked data volume.
- From reading the code (not run), the test at 10128 should fail on macOS, because tempfile directories live under `/var/folders`.
- Fix shape: canonicalize dest once and check only the components below it.

**F7. The dead state server would be HIGH if revived.**
- Severity: LOW today.
- It has no authentication. A peer that sends nothing for 50 ms (6325-6334) receives the whole state: manifest chunk ids and sizes, the object sha and byte counts for every root under dest. That lets a peer confirm whether a known file is present.
- Connections are handled one at a time inside the accept loop (6246). One client holds it for 2 s, so a client that keeps reconnecting starves the real sender.
- Each connection may buffer a request of up to 64 MiB + 8 KiB.
- On macOS and Windows, accepted sockets inherit non-blocking mode from the listener (6232). The read timeouts then do nothing, and signature requests race the first read and can be answered with the plain state.
- Fix shape: delete it, or gate it behind `#[cfg(test)]`.

**F8. The state refresh has no memory or disk limits.**
- Severity: latent MEDIUM.
- After every receive, the refresh reads all of dest into memory, about 3× the 4 GiB default limit (5296-5345).
- It writes a second full copy of dest into `state/chunks` (6042-6074), including roots that ATP never touched.
- Chunks are never garbage-collected, so disk use grows with every version.

## Checked and sound

- **Path validation** (`validate_delta_rel_path` / `validate_portable_relative_path` / `validate_distinct_delta_paths` / `safe_delta_path`) rejects:
  - empty paths, a leading `/` or `\`, `.`, `..` and empty components;
  - NUL and control characters, `\` and `:` (which covers drive letters and alternate data streams);
  - trailing dots or spaces, and Win32 device names even with an extension;
  - reserved names in any case.

  Collision checks use NFC plus uppercase keys, including prefix collisions. A file-versus-directory clash (`a` and `a/b`) gets past the set check but fails safely when created (4174-4181 or the `create_dir_all` error).
- The commit root name is validated. A symlinked final target or a symlinked package root is refused.
- The staging root is created with `create_dir`, so it fails on a planted symlink. A failed commit restores the backup.
- `remove_delta_path_if_exists` is only called on package directories with the exact prefix, on state staging and backup directories, and on the sender guard, which enforces the prefix itself. Std `remove_dir_all` does not follow symlinks.
- **Size and deadline bounds:**
  - File reads check the metadata length first and stop at max+1.
  - Exact-size reads have hard caps; `state.json` is capped at 64 MiB.
  - Tree decode bounds its counts by the remaining bytes before reserving memory, and uses `try_reserve`.
  - The state server's request read and response write both honour an absolute deadline.
- `export_delta_state` is local, bounded and passes the symlink-prefix guard.
- `validate_user_transfer_namespace` does not descend into symlinks, and path-length limits bound its depth. It skips non-UTF-8 names, but the library receivers reject the reserved names anyway.
- I found no panics reachable from on-disk or peer data in these regions.

## Test gaps

- No integration test exercises the CLI package path. tests/atp_cli_* either use `--no-delta` or test the library's delta. Only isolated helpers have unit tests, and the gate stays pinned off.
- Missing cases:
  - files present only on the receiver under the replaced root;
  - local edits made after the state export;
  - a torn state chunk;
  - a non-UTF-8 sibling in dest;
  - a failing or poisoned package;
  - a state directory pre-created by another user;
  - a dest under a symlinked prefix;
  - the state server on a non-Linux accept.
- Recommendation: the gate is always false and the state server has no callers, so remove or compile-gate the legacy receive, commit and serve path. As it stands, the next change to `selected_cli_metadata_policy` would turn on F2-F4 and F8 for every receive with no warning, plus F1 and F5 for any local process that can write to dest.

title: [h2-protocol] http/h2/connection.rs: connection-specific headers (Connection, Upgrade, Keep-Alive, Transfer-Encoding) bypass HTTP/2 validation
description:
src/http/h2/connection.rs validate_h2_pseudo_headers() (lines ~1616-1751) checks pseudo-headers (:method, :path, :scheme, :authority, :status) but does NOT reject the connection-specific headers that RFC 9113 §8.2.2 explicitly forbids in HTTP/2:

  - Connection
  - Upgrade
  - Keep-Alive
  - Proxy-Connection
  - Transfer-Encoding (forbidden in HTTP/2; chunked is implicit)
  - TE (allowed only with the value 'trailers')

Per RFC 9113 §8.2.2: 'HTTP/2 implementations MUST NOT forward Connection or Keep-Alive header fields, [etc].' The current implementation accepts these headers silently and forwards them downstream — a request with Connection: close lands at an HTTP/1 backend and causes unexpected connection termination, OR an Upgrade: h2c header from a peer is propagated to a worker that mis-parses it.

Threat model: an attacker that controls a peer (browser, proxy, malicious client) sends an HTTP/2 request with Connection: close (or any of the above). The h2 stack accepts. If the gateway then proxies to an HTTP/1 backend, the connection-specific header passes through and the backend's connection-management state machine is poisoned. With Transfer-Encoding: chunked + h2 length-delimited bodies, request-smuggling primitives become reachable.

Fix direction: extend validate_h2_pseudo_headers (around line 1692) to iterate the ordinary-headers list and reject — with PROTOCOL_ERROR + GOAWAY — any header whose name (case-insensitive) is one of:
  Connection, Upgrade, Keep-Alive, Proxy-Connection, Transfer-Encoding, Proxy-Authenticate, Proxy-Authorization
And reject TE unless its value is exactly 'trailers'.

Source: /multi-pass-bug-hunting deep on src/http/h2/connection.rs+hpack.rs+frame.rs (2026-04-26). Subagent surveyed all 12 candidate findings; this is the only one not already covered by closed beads or correctly implemented.
close_reason: Fixed in b6ac6d908: validate_h2_pseudo_headers now rejects the 5 RFC 9113 §8.2.2 connection-specific header names (Connection, Keep-Alive, Proxy-Connection, Transfer-Encoding, Upgrade) and enforces te:trailers-only. Both decode_headers and decode_push_promise already route the validator's error through ProtocolError, satisfying the spec's PROTOCOL_ERROR requirement. 3 tests cover all 5 forbidden + te value enforcement + ASCII-printable regression.

title: B-8 ★rsync-KILLER: FastCDC content-defined delta / incremental re-sync
description:
THE highest-ceiling unaddressed lever for 'crush rsync EVERYWHERE'. rsync's defining advantage is the ONE scenario atp has zero answer for: INCREMENTAL re-sync — when the destination already holds an older/similar copy, rsync's rolling-checksum delta sends only changed bytes (often ~0), while atp re-sends the WHOLE object every time. On repeated backups/mirrors (rsync's most common real use) atp loses by orders of magnitude. Closing this makes atp beat rsync on the axis rsync was designed for.

GOAL: when the receiver already has a prior version of a file/tree, transfer only the changed content (target: bytes-on-wire proportional to the DELTA, not the file size), staying byte-identical + fail-closed.

APPROACH (dream big; FastCDC + RaptorQ): (1) FastCDC content-defined chunking (gear-hash rolling boundaries, ~avg 8-16KB chunks, shift-resistant — beats fixed-block on insert/delete) on BOTH sender object + receiver's existing copy; (2) receiver sends its chunk fingerprint set (or the sender requests it); (3) sender transmits only chunks the receiver lacks, as RaptorQ symbols (keeps loss-resilience); (4) receiver reassembles existing+new chunks -> verify whole-object sha + merkle (fail-closed). Composes with E-15 packing + the source-first fast path.

PROFILE-FIRST (do NOT implement blind — the mmap lesson): assess what already exists before designing — planner.rs has partial-resume-chunk logic (br-asupersync-arq-quic-epic-b0k8qo.10.1, 'keep partial resume chunks unskipped'); the journal subsystem; any existing chunk/rolling-hash code. Build on it, don't duplicate. Then microbench FastCDC chunking throughput (must not bottleneck) + the fingerprint-exchange round-trip cost.

DECOMPOSE (code-first sub-beads once designed): FastCDC chunker (+ unit tests vs known vectors) -> chunk-fingerprint manifest exchange protocol -> sender changed-chunk selection -> receiver reassembly + whole-object verify -> CLI surface. EVIDENCE (orchestrator central Phase-2, NOT per-bead): a NEW benchmark dimension = re-sync a file after a small edit (e.g. 100MB, 1% changed) atp-delta vs rsync; measure bytes-on-wire + wall + RSS, byte-identical sha; record in ledger as a new F-POS scorecard row. KEEP only if it beats rsync's delta; ledger-loss w/ retry-cond otherwise.

This is bigger than one bead — it's a mini-epic. Treat THIS as the design/profile-first parent; spawn implementation sub-beads after the profile + design pass. Mine /alien-graveyard + /extreme-software-optimization for the chunker + dedup-index ideas (FastCDC, gear hash, content-defined boundaries, similar-file detection).

title: [bug-hunt][P2] channel/fault.rs: cancel-mid-reorder leaks already-buffered values when auto_flush is interrupted
description: src/channel/fault.rs:243-260. The reorder-buffer path: if buffer.len()+1 >= reorder_buffer_size, the function calls auto_flush_including_current(cx, value).await? — a partial flush that may push some values to the underlying inner.send and then fail (cancel mid-flush). The propagated SendError carries only the CURRENT value, but values that were already drained from the buffer and partially sent through inner.send are silently lost or duplicated depending on which await point cancelled. Pass-3 (cancel mid-reserve) variant for the auto-flush path. Suggested investigation: trace auto_flush_including_current to confirm whether it preserves buffer integrity under cancellation, and document the behaviour.
close_reason: Implementation landed in 669c20e3b. On close inspection the AutoFlushGuard::Drop pattern (lines 318-330) and take_current_value() helper (lines 297-315) DO already preserve the linear-obligation contract — the user's CURRENT message is extracted from current/pending BEFORE Drop runs, then either delivered or returned via SendError::Cancelled(value); buffered values are restored to the reorder_buffer for retry. The genuine gap was OBSERVABILITY: the cancel-induced restoration was silent. Fix: new stat_reorder_cancel_residue: AtomicU64 in FaultSender, wired into AutoFlushGuard::Drop (atomically bumped by restored.len() on every early return), surfaced via FaultChannelStats.reorder_cancel_residue field + Display 'cancel_residue: N'. Now SREs can see how often auto_flush is being interrupted before completion via a monotone counter, and a steadily-growing value signals that the operator should call FaultSender::flush() explicitly from a non-cancelled context. Cargo check passes; UBS scan on src/channel/fault.rs reports 0 critical/0 warning attributable to the change.

title: Implement internal Arena<T> utilities for runtime records
description:
# Internal Arena<T> Utilities

## Purpose
Phase 0 needs stable, compact IDs and fast lookup for runtime records:
- regions
- tasks
- obligations

We want the benefits of a slab/arena without bringing in external crates unless necessary.

## Design Requirements
- Deterministic behavior (no hash-randomized iteration relied on for semantics)
- O(1) insert/get/get_mut by ID
- Clear policy about ID reuse (reuse allowed only after safe removal; documented)
- Ergonomic newtype IDs (e.g., `TaskId(u32)`) with explicit conversion

## Plan-of-Record Design
### Arena storage
Use a `Vec<Option<T>>` plus a free list:
- `slots: Vec<Option<T>>`
- `free: Vec<u32>`

Insert:
- if `free` non-empty, pop index and fill
- else push new slot

Remove:
- set slot to None
- push index to free list

### ID types
- `RegionId`, `TaskId`, `ObligationId` are newtypes around `u32`.
- Reserve `0` as root region if desired (explicit constant).

### Safety / invariants
- All public APIs that accept an ID must validate existence (in debug/lab) or be carefully audited.
- Removal rules must be documented:
  - Phase 0 may keep records forever (no removal) to simplify.
  - If we do remove, it must only happen after quiescence/closure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `Arena<T>` supports:
  - `insert -> Id`
  - `get/get_mut`
  - `contains`
  - `iter` for debugging
- Unit tests validate:
  - no accidental reuse while still live
  - removed IDs become invalid
  - insertion after removals reuses indices (if we choose reuse)

## Notes
We should avoid depending on iteration order of arenas for semantics. If order matters for determinism, we must explicitly sort by IDs or use ordered structures.

title: ATP-D: Implement crash-safe disk, journal, sparse writer, resume, and verifier layer
description: ATP is only trustworthy if partial transfers survive crashes and cancellation without corrupting user-visible data. This workstream owns sparse writes, preallocation, append-only journals, bitmaps, verification, atomic final commit, and platform-specific filesystem semantics.
design: The receiver must never expose unverified final output as complete. Cancellation must leave either a valid resume state or a clearly quarantined partial state. Platform behavior is part of the product: Linux, macOS, and Windows differ in sparse files, preallocation, fsync, atomic rename, path normalization, and writeback behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- Append-only journal and bitmap recover accurately after process kill, power-loss-style fault injection, partial writes, torn records, duplicate records, and compaction interruption.
- Sparse writer supports verified chunk writes, preallocation policy, fsync policy, temp/final/quarantine state, overwrite protection, and final atomic rename/commit.
- Platform doctor reports sparse files, preallocation, atomic rename, fsync policy, path constraints, case sensitivity, symlink semantics, and degradation decisions.
- Unit/property tests cover journal encode/decode, bitmap ranges, chunk verification, writer state machine, rollback, cancellation during journal write/sparse write/verifier/repair decode/final rename, and no obligation leaks.
- E2e crash-resume scripts kill sender/receiver/daemon at every disk phase and emit structured logs, journal digests, recovered bitmap, final proof bundle, and replay/minimization artifact.
- Region close leaves no live disk workers, held permits, leaked obligations, unverified final files, or ambiguous temp files.
notes: This workstream is security and trust critical. Prefer slower correct commit semantics before optimizing disk throughput.

title: ATP-RQ single-block convergence over real network: decodes in-process but not cross-machine
description: transport_rq: a single-block (K=512) 512KB transfer DECODES correctly in-process (coding_roundtrip_k512_single_block passes) but FAILS to converge cross-machine (Hetzner hz1 -> Contabo vmi1156319, 93ms RTT). Traced empirically: round 0 sends 589 symbols (512 source + 77 repair), receiver accepts all 589 (ZERO loss on round 0), yet block stays pending; feedback rounds accumulate to 2637+ distinct accepted symbols, still no decode; fails closed after 17 rounds ('did not converge'). Since the SAME symbol set decodes in-process, the bug is in the NETWORK/PROTOCOL feed path, candidates: (a) feed_symbol reconstructs Symbol from (object_id, sbn, esi, kind, payload) — verify the reconstructed symbol is byte-identical to the encoder's (esp. kind/ESI for the systematic-padding symbols K..K'); (b) the pump_until_control race: ObjectComplete (TCP) may be processed before all of a round's UDP symbols are fed, so is_complete is checked on a partial set — add a grace-drain window after ObjectComplete, or move to a two-task receiver that continuously drains UDP independent of the control round; (c) source symbols partially lost but masked in the accept count. Repro: build release atp (feature atp-cli), atp recv <dst> --listen 0.0.0.0:PORT --transport rq --once on receiver, atp send 512k.bin HOST:PORT --transport rq on sender; ATP_RQ_TRACE=1 on both shows symbols_accepted growing without decode. The transport FAILS CLOSED (no corruption/hang/fake success). Two-task receiver also fixes the busy-spin + decode-blocks-recv buffer overflow on large blocks.
close_reason: Cross-machine close criterion met: RaptorQ UDP spray plane converged on the exact traced pair (hz1->vmi1156319, 94.5ms RTT, release build, authenticated): 432 symbols round 0, all K=375 source accepted, committed sha_ok/merkle_ok byte-identical — vs June's fail-closed 17-round stall on the same shape

title: Review r21 B2: root ATP receiver accepts peer uid/gid + setuid bits by default (owner decision); Kafka SASL codes 33/34 became retryable (d03028d1a); ATP cancel substrings override typed kinds; xattr filter behavior change undocumented
description:
Read-only review round r21-d0 B2 (SapphireHill) of 50140dd85 (ATP xattr namespace filter) and d03028d1a (typed Kafka error codes and ATP cancel kinds), at origin/main 0423a5a05. Full report: /data/tmp/rc_20260922/audit_r21_B2_xattr_typed_codes.md. Each item was re-read in the code; nothing was run unless noted.

## HIGH H1 (pre-existing; the goal 50140dd85 states is not met): a root ATP receiver accepts the peer's uid/gid and setuid bits by default
- metadata.rs ~577, 597-599, 2888, 2902, with object.rs ~254-265 and bin/atp.rs ~903-915.
- The default receive policy restores the sender's uid/gid and its setuid/setgid mode bits, and chown runs before chmod.
- A root `atp recv` / `atp serve` given {uid:0, gid:0, mode:0o4755} writes a setuid-root executable. No opt-in is needed.
- 50140dd85 filters privileged xattr namespaces to stop a peer escalating privileges, but this path stays open.
- Changing the default changes documented behavior (v0.4.3 gate), so this is an OWNER DECISION. Options:
  - strip setuid/setgid unless ownership preservation is explicitly requested and the peer is trusted;
  - default to not preserving ownership when running as root (rsync daemons run as nobody or with fake super);
  - document it loudly.

## MEDIUM
- M1 (50140dd85): metadata.rs ~2771-2870 changed what --preserve-xattrs / preserve_extended_attributes do without saying so. On Linux only user.* is restored now, so root mirrors silently lose ACLs (system.posix_acl_*), SELinux labels and file capabilities (security.*), visible only in trace logs. There is no opt-out and no CHANGELOG entry.
- M2 (d03028d1a), CLAIMED by SapphireHill, fix KS: kafka.rs map_error_code. UnsupportedSASLMechanism (33) and IllegalSASLState (34) used to match the "SASL" display substring and be non-retryable Authentication. They now fall to retryable Broker, reachable through any coded RdKafkaError (MetadataFetch, Transaction(native), ...). Exactly 4 librdkafka descriptions match the old predicate: -169, 33, 34, 58.
- M3 (d03028d1a): outcome.rs ~1162-1176, parse_atp_cancel_reason. The ATP message contains() checks still run before the typed CancelKind and apply to every kind. For example, CancelReason::shutdown().with_message("... repair decode ...") becomes RepairDecodeAbandoned, not Shutdown. to_base_reason encodes PathRaceLost, RepairDecodeAbandoned and DaemonRestart as CancelKind::User with fixed messages, and ResourceBudgetExhausted as Timeout with a fixed message. So the checks belong only under those kinds, ideally as exact matches. Only the diagnostic TransferTranscript::cancellation_source is affected; there is no in-tree production caller.

## LOW
- L1: metadata.rs ~2777-2782. On non-Linux Unix the xattr filter is a denylist, so unknown namespaces pass (Hurd gnu.translator / gnu.author). Android takes the denylist, which happens to be equivalent today.
- L2: bin/atp.rs ~655-656. The bond-recv help says to prefer --rq-auth-key-stdin, but BondRecvArgs has no such flag, so following the help fails with "unexpected argument".
- L3: CHANGELOG.md ~149-151. The next_progress note is filed under v0.6.0, but it shipped in v0.4.11 (1a673bd16).
- L4: metadata.rs ~4311-4346. The xattr test pins only the deny side; a filter that rejected everything would pass.
- L5: kafka.rs ~458-459, 539-556. Error text now carries only the code name; the operation and librdkafka's reason are gone. Non-delivery topic errors report InvalidTopic("unknown"). Transactional error text and class changed with no CHANGELOG entry.
- L6: outcome.rs ~1193, 1203, 835. A generic RaceLost maps to PathRaceLost. ParentCancel does not round-trip: to_base_reason emits linked_exit, which the table maps to None.
- L7: tests. Only 1 of the 4 Kafka assertions behaves differently from the old code, and Transaction(native) is untested. The outcome test does not pin message-less kinds, RaceLost, LinkedExit or the round trip.

Found sound:
- On Linux the xattr filter is a user.*-only allowlist (fail-closed). The only production xattr::set (metadata.rs ~2871) is reached from every TCP, RQ, QUIC, FIFO, staged-file and directory receive path.
- The unsafe ledger matches the code: 8 locators, no new unsafe.
- The new xattr test fails without the filter.
- No public signature changed in either commit.

title: [SPORK] OTP-Grade Layer for Asupersync (Beats Elixir Naturally)
description:
Goal: build **Spork**, an OTP-grade ergonomics layer on top of asupersync that feels as natural as Elixir/Erlang for building long-lived concurrent systems, but is **strictly stronger** on determinism, cancellation-correctness, and auditable reasoning.

Why this exists:
- OTP is an operational model, not an actor library. The win is the *defaults*: supervision, naming, linking/monitoring, backpressure conventions, and coherent shutdown.
- asupersync already has most of the hard primitives: region ownership + quiescence, two-phase cancel-safe effects, supervision policies, lab determinism + DPOR tooling.
- What is missing is a compiled, opinionated surface that makes the right thing the easy thing.

Non-negotiable invariants (Spork must preserve):
- Region close => quiescence (no live children, finalizers done).
- Cancellation is a protocol: request -> drain -> finalize.
- Losers are drained (no abandoned tasks after races).
- No obligation leaks (permits/acks/leases committed or aborted).
- No ambient authority: Spork features are capabilities hanging off `Cx`/regions.

Alien-artifact bar:
- Explainability: supervisors/registries produce evidence ledgers for decisions.
- Formal hooks: traces are canonicalizable and replayable; failures emit minimal repro artifacts.
- Deterministic testing: lab runs + DPOR exploration are first-class for Spork apps.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
# Context: "Beat Elixir Naturally" (OTP++)

This epic is the answer to:

- Jose Valim (Elixir author) arguing Elixir is a top-tier language for AI agents because the *operational model* is friendly: immutability, docs, stability, and tooling.
- Darin's pushback: "don't try to replicate OTP" and "there are already 20 actor libs in Rust".

The synthesis here is:

1. **Darin is right** if we interpret the goal as "make yet another Rust actor library".
2. **Jeff is right** if we interpret the goal as "ship an OTP-grade *operational model*".

Spork is explicitly the latter: an OTP-class toolkit compiled onto asupersync's kernel primitives.

# The Core Claim

Spork can be *more natural than OTP* while being strictly stronger, because asupersync already has primitives OTP doesn't:

- **Structured concurrency** (region ownership) rather than unowned processes.
- **Close = quiescence** as an invariant, not a social convention.
- **Cancellation as a protocol** (request -> drain -> finalize), not ad-hoc `exit/2`.
- **Two-phase effects / obligations** so reply-or-abort is enforced (no silent drops).
- **Deterministic lab runtime** so failures are replayable and schedule-explorable.
- **Crash artifacts + trace canonicalization** so bugs become files, not mysteries.
- Optional: **formal semantics hooks** (Lean/TLA scaffolding) so we can state and check real claims.

In other words: OTP gives amazing defaults. Spork aims to give *even better* defaults because our substrate can enforce them.

# What "More Natural Than OTP" Means

"Natural" is not syntax; it's that the correct architecture is the path of least resistance:

- You start a service under a supervisor, and it is *owned*.
- You name it without globals, and names cannot go stale.
- You call/cast it, and cancellation cannot silently drop protocol obligations.
- When something fails, you get:
  - a canonicalized trace fingerprint
  - a seed + minimal divergent prefix
  - a crashpack manifest
  - an evidence ledger
  - a single command to replay

If we deliver that, Spork is better-than-Elixir for AI agents even if the language is Rust.

# Key Architecture Decision: "Compile OTP to Regions"

OTP runtime model:
- process tree + supervisors + links/monitors + name registry

Spork runtime model:
- **region tree** is the source of truth
- supervisors are *compiled* into region ownership + policy application
- links/monitors are explicit cancellation/failure propagation edges with deterministic ordering
- registry is a `Cx` capability: lease obligations prevent stale names

This is why we don't need yet another actor library: the meaning lives in the composition of region + obligation + lab determinism.

# Proposed User-Facing Surface (Sketch)

A minimal high-level surface (not final API):

- `spork::app::{App, AppHandle, AppSpec}`
- `spork::supervisor::{SupervisorSpec, Strategy, ChildSpec}`
- `spork::gen_server::{GenServer, ServerHandle}`
- `spork::registry::{Registry, NameLease}` (capability)
- `spork::monitor::{monitor, link, trap_exit}`

Pseudo-usage:

```rust
cx.region(|root| async move {
  let app = MyApp::spec()
    .with_registry(root.registry())
    .with_supervisor(|sup| {
      sup.one_for_one()
        .child("chat", ChatServer::spec())
        .child("presence", Presence::spec());
    });

  let handle = app.start(root).await?;
  // ...
  handle.stop(root).await?; // closes region => quiescence
}).await;
```

# Acceptance: How We'll Know We Won

- Conformance: an OTP mental-model suite passes for GenServer/Supervisor/Registry/Link-Monitor.
- Determinism: every failing Spork app test emits a crashpack with replay.
- Correctness: no obligation leaks, no task leaks, losers drained.
- Ergonomics: "happy path" app code is smaller than Rust actor libs, because policies are defaults.

# Dependencies: Big Rocks

This epic is intentionally decomposed into sub-epics:

- Spec + ordering contracts (`bd-11z9a`)
- GenServer (`bd-1zok9`)
- Supervisors (`bd-2n7yw`)
- Registry (`bd-3rpp8`)
- Link/Monitor (`bd-pr46z`)
- Lab harness + DPOR (`bd-1vk6c`)
- Crash artifacts (`bd-qbcnu`)
- Observability (`bd-iu07v`)
- Performance kernel (`bd-2u7ns`)
- Formal hooks (`bd-3ccru`)

The new epics added in this pass extend the missing "OTP Application" layer and the explicit AI/agent-first ergonomics layer.

title: [RUNTIME][P1] timeout()/timeout_at()-wrapped reactor read stalls until deadline (general; not D1-specific)
description: Found while building the AC1 showcase for eeexl1.1 (tests/e2e_deadline_db_wire_cancel_showcase.rs). Under RuntimeBuilder::new().worker_threads(1), a PgConnection query run INSIDE ServerRequestRegion::run_with_protocol_drain successfully writes the budget-derived 'SET statement_timeout = 3000' to the wire (confirmed via scripted-server DIAG), but then PARKS on the read of the SET response and is not re-woken until the 3s request-budget timer fires. Because the query never advances past apply_statement_timeout's SET-response read, it never sends the actual SELECT, so the drain-phase CancelRequest dial (which keys off the in-flight main query) never happens in this composed flow. Connect's own write-then-read handshake works under the same runtime/cx, so the regression is specific to the post-connect read under the request cx / AmbientCxScope inside run_with_protocol_drain. FIRST INVESTIGATION STEP: localize by running a plain query_unchecked(&task_cx, 'SELECT 1') under the same runtime WITHOUT the request region — if that round-trips but the region-wrapped one hangs, the bug is in the request-cx I/O wiring or AmbientCxScope poll/waker interaction (build_request_cx_from_inner DOES pass guard.io_driver_handle(), so suspect reactor-turn/readiness-delivery under single worker, or a waker-registration race when the ambient cx is re-installed per poll). This is potentially D1-premise-breaking (an HTTP-request-region-wrapped DB query that can't read responses), so prioritize confirming severity. The wire-cancel FRAME itself is independently proven by src/database/postgres.rs cancel_in_flight_sends_cancel_request_before_resolving (D1.2); the region/drain/disconnect oracle behavior by src/web/request_region.rs server_hop lab cells (D1.1). DIAG transcript: accepted primary; read startup 26B; wrote handshake; first message Q 'SET statement_timeout = 3000'; wrote SET response, waiting for handler query; [SELECT never arrives; client tears down at 3s budget].
notes:
SHARPENED ROOT-CAUSE ANALYSIS (2026-06-12, do not patch speculatively — needs reactor instrumentation):
- Registrations for these reads are PollMode::Oneshot (LEVEL-triggered oneshot, NOT edge): src/runtime/reactor/epoll.rs:261-263 (plain Interest::READABLE -> Oneshot). So a simple lost-EDGE is ruled out — a level-oneshot arm on an already-readable fd should fire on the next epoll_wait.
- Worker loop (three_lane.rs run_loop ~4286): each idle iteration calls drive_io_phase (~4189) which computes io_timeout = next_deadline (timer/local/global) or IDLE_IO_POLL_MAX_TIMEOUT (=250ms, line 182), then io.try_turn_with(io_timeout) = epoll_wait(io_timeout).
- THE SMOKING GUN: the no-timer region read completes in ~90ms (< 250ms), i.e. within ONE epoll_wait(250ms) cycle; the finite-budget/timeout case stalls the FULL timer deadline. Since 90ms < 250ms, recovery in the no-timer case is NOT necessarily the fd event firing — it is consistent with the periodic 250ms idle re-poll cadence masking a LOST fd-readiness event: each loop re-attempts next_task -> re-polls the task -> re-attempts the read -> reads the already-buffered response. With a pending timer the single epoll_wait(timer_deadline) does not re-loop until the deadline, exposing the lost wakeup.
- IMPLICATION: the fd readiness event appears to NOT be delivered (or not to wake the right waker) for these reads; the 250ms idle poll normally hides up-to-250ms read latency. A long timer deadline removes that masking. Confirm by instrumenting drive_io_phase / the reactor turn to log whether the fd event actually fires vs whether recovery is timeout-driven.
- SUSPECTS to instrument: (a) does Sleep/timer registration (src/time/sleep.rs + timer driver) race or interfere with the fd registration's wake delivery? (b) rearm() in src/runtime/io_driver.rs (cached_waker will_wake guard line 808-821 + wake_polling_reactor line 795 + modify_interest line 805) — does modify_interest actually re-arm a oneshot registration that already fired, and is the cached waker the one epoll wakes? (c) is the read's waker the worker-unpark waker, and does the reactor turn actually call it on fd events?
- CANDIDATE MITIGATION (defensible but has a power tradeoff; let the reactor owner decide): cap io_timeout in drive_io_phase at IDLE_IO_POLL_MAX_TIMEOUT even when a further-out timer deadline exists, so a single epoll_wait never blocks longer than the idle re-poll cadence. This restores the proven no-timer behavior (latency <= 250ms) and preserves timer firing (the loop checks the timer driver each iteration). Downside: wakes every 250ms whenever any timer is pending (idle power regression). This is a MASK, not the root fix — prefer fixing the lost fd-event delivery.
- NOT FIXING in this session: hot-path scheduler/reactor concurrency; needs loom + perf bench + interactive instrumentation that a background loop cannot run. Repro is committed #[ignore]d at tests/rr849p_request_cx_read_localization.rs (un-ignore as the regression guard when fixed).

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text: MECHANISM CONFIRMED + FIX IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-12). Monitor timeline during the 4s stall: timer_next_ms=Some(0) timer_pending=2 FROZEN from +551ms to +4509ms — the 1ms fallback-rewake timer sat DUE and UNPROCESSED in the wheel the whole time. Full mechanism: (1) workers only process wheel timers in next_task() PHASE 0 (outer loop); the inner backoff loop re-checks queues on every park-wake but never pumps the wheel, so a due wheel timer cannot fire from a worker stuck there (including the DeadlineDue 1ns-park cycle, which spins without firing); (2) the block_on main thread is the only park-by-wheel-deadline pump, and it races: computing its park duration between a fallback timer firing and the re-polled task registering the next one, it sees only the far 4s Sleep and parks 4s; (3) phase A survives because with no far timer the main thread takes the None-deadline -> 1ms BLOCK_ON_RUNTIME_RECHECK_INTERVAL branch. title: Obligation ledger audit: ObligationLedger never prunes resolved records (FabricConsumer grows per delivery, panics at u32 index overflow); ledger ids collide across consumers on one cell
description:
Read-only audit of the src/obligation modules with production importers (ledger.rs and graded.rs), at origin/main 8ce1b742a (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-05).
- Skipped, because no production code imports them: guarded.rs, leak_check.rs (tests only), saga.rs (tests and choreography only), recovery.rs.
- ledger.rs importers: the messaging-fabric modules (consumer, fabric, service and session obligation; a non-default feature), and runtime/obligation_table.rs (counts and audit-record types only).

## HIGH
H1. ObligationLedger never prunes resolved records, and FabricConsumer creates one per delivery (ledger.rs ~738; consumer.rs ~1650, ~2349-2385).
- Ack, nack, redeliver and dead-letter only change the record's state.
- Memory grows with every delivery. finalize_region's scan becomes O(every delivery ever made). After u32::MAX - 1 acquisitions, acquire panics with "index overflow... reset required" inside the consumer's handler.
- Fix: bounded retention as in fu6cr0 (remove resolved records, keep Reserved and Leaked), plus a safe index wrap.

## MEDIUM
M1. The ASUP-E103 panic in ObligationToken::reserve fires after NameRegistry has changed its state. This is the same root cause as the registry audit's M1; see that bead.

M2. Ledger obligation ids are unique only within one ledger, and consumer attempt certificates are bound only by that id.
- Two consumers on one SubjectCell get identical ids. B.acknowledge_delivery(&a_delivery.attempt) commits B's pending window, and B's message is lost. nack and dead-letter misfire the same way.
- Fix: a per-consumer nonce in AttemptCertificate, checked on use.

## LOW
- L1. ledger try_commit/try_abort delegate to commit/abort, which panic on NotPending, NotFound and TokenMismatch, so the "fallible" API panics in the drain-then-late-commit race.
- L2. The docs promise reported leaks, but in production nothing calls check_leaks. ServiceObligation has no Drop, so a dropped handle stays Reserved forever. The reserve doc's "region must be valid and active" is only an as_u64() != 0 check.
- Out of scope and unverified: service.rs's saga kernel compensates only the failing step, never earlier completed ones.

title: [db-bug-hunt] database/postgres.rs: begin() lacks isolation level / read-only configuration — applications cannot request SERIALIZABLE atomically with BEGIN
description: src/database/postgres.rs:3082 PgConnection::begin only sends literal 'BEGIN' via simple-query — no API for isolation level, no API for READ ONLY / READ WRITE. Per Postgres protocol, the syntax is 'BEGIN [READ ONLY|READ WRITE] [ISOLATION LEVEL {SERIALIZABLE|REPEATABLE READ|READ COMMITTED|READ UNCOMMITTED}]' — these MUST be set in the same statement as BEGIN to apply to the started transaction. Applications relying on SERIALIZABLE for correctness (financial, inventory, anything with update-update or read-modify-write hazards) cannot request it through the typed PgTransaction guard. Workaround is execute('SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE') AFTER begin — this DOES work because the SET TRANSACTION command applies to the current transaction, but: (a) it's a separate round-trip (latency cost), (b) the typed PgTransaction wrapper carries no record of the isolation level (debuggability gap), (c) bypassing the typed wrapper is itself a footgun (someone forgets the SET, gets default READ COMMITTED silently). MySQL (src/database/mysql.rs ~begin()) has the same gap. Mitigation: add fn begin_with_isolation(cx, IsolationLevel) -> Outcome<PgTransaction>; encode the level into the PgTransaction struct for introspection. Severity HIGH for correctness-sensitive workloads.
close_reason: Fixed in 8eae20001: added IsolationLevel enum + begin_with_isolation(cx, level, read_only) on PgConnection and MySqlConnection. Postgres emits single atomic BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL X READ {ONLY|WRITE}; MySQL emits SET TRANSACTION + START TRANSACTION pair (per spec). PgTransaction/MySqlTransaction now carry isolation_level/read_only fields with const accessors.

title: [runtime-state] runtime/reactor/token.rs: SlabToken generation wraps after 256 register/deregister cycles on 32-bit targets — ABA collision delivers stale tokens to fresh wakers
description:
src/runtime/reactor/token.rs:121 — SlabToken::MAX_GENERATION = 0xFF on 32-bit targets:

  #[cfg(target_pointer_width = "32")]
  pub const MAX_GENERATION: u32 = 0xFF;

The 32-bit packing splits a usize into 24 bits of index + 8 bits of generation. A long-lived runtime that performs more than 256 deregister/register cycles on the SAME slot index will see the generation wrap from 0xFF back to 0x00 — the same generation a stale outstanding token may have been issued under.

Concrete failure mode (32-bit target, e.g., wasm32-unknown-unknown or a 32-bit embedded host):
  1. Slot index 5 is registered for fd_A → SlabToken { index: 5, generation: 0 } encoded into the OS reactor.
  2. fd_A closes; deregister evicts the slab slot.
  3. fd_B through fd_257 cycle through index 5 with generations 1..255, then back to 0.
  4. fd_A's late OS event (e.g., delivered after socket close due to kernel buffering) arrives at the reactor with the original (5, 0) token.
  5. The dispatch loop in io_driver.rs:379 looks up wakers.get((5, 0)) — and finds the CURRENT occupant of slot 5 (also at generation 0).
  6. The CURRENT task's waker fires, the CURRENT task wakes up, polls its non-existent event, and either spurious-wakes (best case) or processes a corrupt readiness signal as if it were its own (worst case).

Concrete failure mode (severity bound): this can also be triggered by an attacker who can control the rate at which a SOCKET connects and disconnects to the asupersync runtime — 256 connect/disconnect cycles at, say, 1 cycle/ms = 256ms to wrap on a single slot. Sustained at 1k connections/sec, the entire generation namespace cycles in under a second.

64-bit targets are not affected (MAX_GENERATION = u32::MAX, ~136 years of cycles at 1B/sec).

Fix direction:
  1. Refuse slot reuse when the generation would wrap. The slab keeps the slot in a 'poisoned' state and skips it on next allocate. Bounded waste is one slot per 256 cycles, ~0.4% of address space; acceptable.
  2. Or: switch the 32-bit packing to (16 bits index + 16 bits generation) — 65k slots max, but 65k generations before wrap. Most workloads fit in 65k concurrent registrations and 65k generations is ~18 hours at 1 cycle/sec.
  3. Or: introduce a separate u64 generation counter on a side-table for 32-bit targets (Vec<u64> indexed by index). The token encodes (index, generation_u8) but the slab verifies against the side-table's u64 on lookup. Catches 32-bit ABA across all 2^64 generations.
  4. Add a regression test on a forced-32-bit-encoding path: register/deregister 257 times on the same index, attempt to deliver a stale token from cycle 0, assert the waker dispatch FAILS rather than wakes the cycle-256 task.

Severity P2 because (a) most production targets are 64-bit (correctness gap is theoretical there), (b) wasm32 is the practical concern and is currently a preview surface, and (c) the existing #[cfg(target_pointer_width = "32")] path is exercised by the wasm-browser-* builds.

Source: /multi-pass-bug-hunting on src/runtime/io_op.rs + timer.rs + io_driver.rs (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Fixed in HEAD (ee7a273ba): SlabToken 32-bit packing widened from 24+8 (256 generation cycles, ABA-vulnerable) to 16+16 (65,536 cycles). MAX_GENERATION on 32-bit moves from 0xFF to 0xFFFF; new MAX_INDEX const exposes the index ceiling. 64-bit packing unchanged (32+32 lossless). Tests: max_generation_supports_at_least_2_to_16_cycles, pack_unpack_preserves_high_generation_values, high_bit_generation_does_not_collide_with_low.

title: Lab conformance loop advances virtual time past a pending spawn admission (timeouts fire before spawned work is polled)
description:
## Defect (found by the lab/native differential harness, bi2462.148)
LabRuntimeTarget::block_on (src/conformance/mod.rs) jumps virtual time to the next timer deadline whenever the scheduler is empty. A task spawned through the spawn gateway sits in the lab's spawn mailbox until step_for_test admits it, and during that time the scheduler is empty. So when a task spawns work and then immediately parks on a timer, the loop advances virtual time to the deadline before the spawned task has been admitted or polled. The seed then decides whether the timer's owner or the new task runs first.

Observed: the harness scenario scope_timeout_with_a_real_deadline wraps a parked operation in Scope::timeout(50 ms).
- Lab reported TimedOut (the operation was cancelled before its first poll) in 4 of 6 seeds.
- The native runtime polled the operation first in 6 of 6 runs: Completed(Ok(0)) after the cancellation was acknowledged.
The production runtime reaches the TimedOut outcome only if a worker stalls past the deadline. The lab over-produced it, and it did so for every timeout/sleep race run through LabRuntimeTarget (conformance suites, many lib tests).

LabRuntime::run_with_auto_advance already has the right rule: when the scheduler is empty it steps instead of advancing while has_pending_dispatch_commands() (spawn mailbox or deferred cancel dispatches) is true. The conformance loop lacked that check.

## Fix
- Advance only when the scheduler is empty AND no dispatch command is pending.
- LabRuntime::has_pending_dispatch_commands becomes pub(crate); there is no public API change.

## Proof
- Regression test tests/kernel_semantics_differential.rs::lab_time_does_not_advance_past_a_pending_spawn, over 32 seeds: a child spawned just before the root sleeps must observe unchanged virtual time at its first poll. It is red without the fix and green with it.
- The differential scenario then shows the lab producing Completed(Ok(0)) like native.
- Also run: every integration target that drives LabRuntimeTarget or reads these files, the full default lib suite, the sqlite/tls lib modules that use LabRuntimeTarget, and the exact-tree check.
close_reason: Fixed in d4c7fdea6: LabRuntimeTarget::block_on no longer advances virtual time while a spawn awaits admission (same rule as run_with_auto_advance). Old red LTold 7fcf7c9ef (regression test fails, lab Scope::timeout timed_out 4/6 seeds); new green LTnew 16 targets 286/0 (lab completed 6/6 = native), LTbase identical, full lib LTlib3 23913/0 = base, sqlite/tls lib 354/0, exact check green.
