title: [SCHED-PERF] Complete ShardedState integration — scheduler runs against sharded tables, retiring the unified-lock bottleneck
description:
WHY: the ShardedState experiment (br-asupersync-8fuxnt) built independently-locked shards (E config/D instr/B regions/A tasks/C obligations with canonical E->D->B->A->C ordering, src/runtime/sharded_state.rs) and the README already advertises it — but recon found ThreeLaneScheduler still hard-wired to the unified Arc<ContendedMutex<RuntimeState>> (builder.rs:2773-2784, 3866-3875), so production never benefits. Spawn admission, task polling bookkeeping, and obligation ops all serialize on one mutex.

WHAT: finish the integration: (1) scheduler paths take shard-scoped guards (task-table ops touch A; region transitions B; obligation ops C) instead of whole-state locks — audit every scheduler lock site, classify required shards, convert; (2) lock-order discipline enforced by the existing ShardGuard label system (23 tests already exist — extend to the new sites); (3) the spawn mailbox ([DX-CORE] A1) admission path lands on shards from day one (coordinate: A1 designs against the unified lock if it ships first; this bead retargets it); (4) RuntimeStateShape config (unified|sharded) becomes a tested matrix during transition, then sharded becomes default and unified is REMOVED (no-tech-debt policy) in a final cut, after bake evidence.
design: FILES: src/runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs (lock sites), src/runtime/sharded_state.rs, src/runtime/builder.rs (wiring), src/runtime/state.rs (split-path retirement). Method: site-by-site conversion table (lock site -> shards touched -> ordering proof) committed as the proof note (Phase 6 proof-note gate applies — obligation paths touched). Lock-order violations caught by debug assertions + the label tests.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Conversion table complete: every scheduler lock site classified + converted or justified-unified. 2. Lock-order tests extended to all new multi-shard sites; zero violations under the full lab suite + loom-tests feature lane. 3. Perf: spawn_throughput + injector_throughput benches show improvement under contention (record numbers; expectation: contended spawn p50 improves materially; no-win on any bench = investigate before proceeding to default-flip). 4. Determinism: lab replay fingerprints unchanged across shape=unified|sharded on the replay corpus (semantics-identical proof). 5. Full quality gates + conformance suite green on sharded default. 6. Unified path removed in the final commit with the bake evidence linked (separate commit for bisection).
notes: DEPENDS on E7 (benches) + [DX-CORE] A1 (mailbox coordination — whichever lands second integrates with the first). HIGHEST-RISK bead in the epic: stage commits carefully (one subsystem per commit), flamegraph artifact per Phase 6. FALLBACK: shape flag retained until the final-cut commit; revert = flip flag.

title: [SCHED-PERF] Join completion + structured batch-spawn benchmark-gated rollup
description:

JOIN lever: distinguish the legacy RuntimeHandle::spawn JoinHandle in src/runtime/builder.rs from the canonical Cx::spawn TaskHandle and JoinSet path. The legacy handle still uses Arc<Mutex<JoinState<T>>>; TaskHandle already uses the project oneshot channel, which is also mutex-backed. BATCH lever: define structured Cx/Scope batch-spawn semantics, producer-side mailbox publication amortization, and JoinSet::spawn_all. Current mailbox batching is consumer-side only; producer enqueue and notification are per request, and the scheduler batch-one consumer policy is a fairness boundary that this rollup does not silently change.

Children freeze the inventory/baseline, run the safe completion experiment and lifecycle proof, define and implement structured producer batching, and join both levers in a terminal comparative receipt.

- Children .3.1 through .3.6 close with exact source and evidence provenance.
- JOIN and BATCH receive independent SHIP, KEEP, or no-win dispositions; one lever cannot green the other.
- The optimized completion target is explicit: legacy JoinHandle, structured TaskHandle, or both. Existing incumbent semantics for success, panic, cancellation, shutdown, drop, wake registration, single take, is_finished, and repoll remain mapped.
- Safe reuse is evaluated first. No custom UnsafeCell or new unsafe boundary is authorized by this rollup; such work requires a separate contingent child, exact owner approval, the narrowest allow scope, ledger/docs updates, and dedicated concurrency proof.
- Batch semantics preserve deterministic input order, one pending-spawn credit and trace identity per request, per-item outcomes, empty/boundary behavior, cancellation and admission failure. Producer notification amortization does not imply scheduler consumer batching or fairness changes.
- Terminal evidence includes like-for-like p50/p95 completion data and N=1000 batch-versus-loop data with environment/source/harness identity and explicit no-claim boundaries.
notes: The original line anchors and claim that oneshot already provided a lock-free shape were stale. comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
SapphireHill 2026-07-28 — the try_send_contended/4 "100x inversion" is EXPLAINED
(pre-work requested by the bt4y5f.1 close note before flat-combining work).

RECORDED ANOMALY (bt4y5f.1 gate run, ovh-a/host:fixmydocuments, 2026-07-27):
/4 p50 ~4.66ms vs /8 ~44us, cv 14.6% — 100x inversion, deliberately left out
of baseline.json.

REPRODUCTION CAMPAIGN (2026-07-27/28, release, same bench, N=5 fresh runs):
- ovh-a (SAME host as the 4.66ms recording): /4 = 23.9us, then 58.2us, then
  25.0us across consecutive runs. /8 = 43.3us (matches the recorded 44us).
- vmi1227854 (Contabo): /4 = 164.9us.
- Yesterday's 4.66ms did NOT reproduce anywhere; /8 is stable everywhere.

VERDICT: /4 is METASTABLE, not "slower than /8". Its fast mode (24-58us)
scales normally (half of /8's producers ~= half/comparable time). The
recorded 4.66ms was a whole-sample-window degenerate regime on a host whose
conditions that day (13-bead release day, heavy co-tenancy) kept the bench
in its pathological mode. Multi-modality spans 24us -> 58us -> 165us ->
4,660us; /8 never moves off ~44us.

MECHANISM (consistent with all observations):
- benches/channel_contended.rs couples two unbounded spin loops through ONE
  parking_lot::Mutex<ChannelInner> (mpsc.rs try_send:626 / try_recv:1573):
  producers spin-retry on Full, the measured consumer spin-drains on Empty.
- parking_lot is unfair (barging): the cache-hot consumer can re-acquire
  immediately; producers exhaust spin budget and PARK (futex). Once parked,
  a drained queue leaves the consumer empty-spinning at full lock frequency
  — which keeps beating parked producers to the lock; forced-fair handoffs
  (~0.5ms epochs) are then the rescue path -> millisecond-scale iterations.
- Direction of the inversion: ovh-a has 8 slots. /4+1 = 5 threads FIT in
  cores -> the camping pattern can persist (no involuntary preemption).
  /8+1 = 9 threads ALWAYS oversubscribe -> the kernel's preemption breaks
  lock-camping every quantum -> stable 44us regardless of load. The bigger
  config is protected by its own oversubscription.
- Control observation: task_state/locked_read_contended (same barrier
  harness, no Full/Empty retry coupling) scales NORMALLY 4->8 (35.6us ->
  78.8us) on the same host — the pathology needs the coupled-retry shape,
  not just N threads on a lock.

IMPLICATIONS FOR THIS BEAD (bt4y5f.5):
1. /4 as-is is NOT a baselineable comparator row (mode-dependent by 200x).
   Before the flat-combining lever is measured, the bench needs bounded
   exponential backoff on BOTH retry sides (or a parked waker-based
   consumer, which is what production recv(&cx) actually does). Keep /8.
2. The mechanism itself is AMMUNITION for the lever: a flat-combining
   submission layer removes producer lock acquisitions entirely, which
   eliminates the camping/starvation channel by construction.
3. Any future "N slower than 2N" contention result: check fits-in-cores vs
   oversubscribed BEFORE believing it; rerun same-host N>=3 (this one
   swung 2.4x between consecutive same-host runs even in fast mode).

Evidence: scratchpad bimodal_sample.log + channel_bench_repro.log (session
2026-07-27 SapphireHill); recorded numbers in bt4y5f.1 close comment.

title: Scope audit: race/race_all skip the loser drain on the multi-thread block_on root when the winner panics (HIGH); dropped timeout/quorum/first_ok leave branches running; timeout reports caller cancel as TimedOut
description:
Read-only audit of src/cx/scope.rs (structured concurrency: race, race_all, join, hedge, quorum, first_ok, timeout, spawn admission, region runner) at origin/main 2c6b91a85 (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-04). SapphireHill re-read HIGH 1 in the code (scope.rs 1075/1100 shortcut, three_lane.rs scheduler_drives_current_task, builder.rs Runtime::block_on fallback) before fixing it. Related: asupersync-issue65-criticisms-kpmoy5.2 ("losers are drained").

## HIGH
1. FIXED in this session's stack: when a race winner panics, race and race_all (scope.rs 1075, 1100, 1435-1454) skip the full loser drain if !scheduler_drives_current_task(), polling each loser once with a no-op waker (best_effort_poll_loser_join, 990-995) and returning Err(Panicked) while the loser still runs. That predicate is true only on a worker thread or under the lab's SCHEDULER_DRIVEN mark, and the multi-thread Runtime::block_on polls its root future on the calling thread through run_future_with_budget (builder.rs ~7011) without either, although its workers run every task the root spawns. #[asupersync::main] defaults to the multi-thread flavor and runs main through block_on, so in an ordinary main a panicking winner left its losers undrained (cleanup not run, a later loser panic never seen). The differential harness ran its panicking-winner scenario inside runtime.handle().spawn, i.e. on a worker. hedge has the same check (1253-1277) but needs &mut RuntimeState (lab only).

## MEDIUM
2. Dropping a Scope::timeout, quorum or first_ok future mid-flight leaves its spawned tasks running with no cancel request: their first phase waits with handle.poll_join (quorum 1815-1842, first_ok 2012-2022, timeout 2091-2109), which does not abort when the caller stops polling, and a dropped TaskHandle detaches. For Scope::timeout the deadline lived only in the dropped future, so the operation runs with no deadline; region close then waits for it indefinitely. race/race_all/join/join_all/hedge hold drop-aborting JoinFutures; map_reduce has an abort-on-drop guard. No test drops any of the three.

## LOW
3. Scope::timeout reports caller cancellation as TimedOut when the operation never acknowledged the cancel (cancelled before its first poll, or ignores cancellation): Outcome::Cancelled(caller reason) maps through make_timed_result(.., false) to TimedOut(TimeoutError::new(deadline)) with a deadline that has not passed (scope.rs 2116-2130, timeout.rs 273-276). The doc at 2047-2050 still says caller cancellation uses CancelReason::timeout. caller_cancellation_reaches_the_operation_as_the_callers_reason discards the return value.
4. Reason labels: RegionRunner::drop (213) labels a dropped region body fail_fast rather than parent cancellation; hedge, quorum and first_ok map every spawn error to resource_unavailable (1161, 1906, 2002).

## Checked and sound
race/race_all selection (first ready result, same-poll branch beats owner cancel, dropped selection futures abort with race_loser unless published, owner cancel aborts and joins all, panic precedence, uninterruptible drain joins, loser panics surfaced); join/join_all buffering and drop abort; quorum/first_ok/timeout normal and caller-cancel paths abort then join; spawn admission rollback (Closed, LimitReached, NotFound); region factory panic cleanup; RegionRunner::drop non-blocking; RegionCloseFuture waker registration under the closer's mutex; no blocking in Drop; no panics from ordinary use.
close_reason: done

title: [security-audit] Fix Host header validation fail-open in HTTP/1.1 server
description:
CRITICAL SECURITY VULNERABILITY: Host Header Validation Fail-Open

## Location
src/http/h1/server.rs:37-59 - Http1Config::default()

## Vulnerability Description
Host header validation is disabled by default. The allowed_hosts field defaults to None, which bypasses ALL Host header validation and accepts any Host header value from attackers.

## Attack Vectors
1. Host Header Injection: Attackers can inject arbitrary Host headers to:
   - Poison OAuth redirect_uri validation → steal auth tokens
   - Manipulate password-reset email URLs → redirect to attacker domain
   - Corrupt cache keys using Host as input
   - Bypass CSRF protections that rely on Host validation

2. Configuration Bypass: Empty allow-list Some(vec![]) silently fails-open instead of rejecting all hosts

## Impact Assessment
- Severity: CRITICAL
- Attack Complexity: LOW (single HTTP request)
- Authentication Required: None
- Scope: All HTTP/1.1 endpoints using default configuration
- Financial Impact: OAuth token theft, account takeover, password reset hijacking

## Fix Required
1. Change default to require explicit Host allow-list or reject unknown hosts
2. Make empty allow-list behavior explicit (error or warning)
3. Add security documentation for Host validation configuration

## Remediation Priority
IMMEDIATE - This is a fail-open security control that could enable account takeover attacks.
close_reason: done

title: [security-audit] grpc/health: unbounded service-name length in set_status
description: src/grpc/health.rs:168-182 — HealthService::set_status(service: impl Into<String>, ...) accepts arbitrary-length service names with no length bound, then inserts into the per-service HashMap (statuses + watch_versions). An operator-side bug or compromised component that can call set_status (or a future code path that wires set_status to user input) can register service names of arbitrary size, exhausting server memory. Each unique service name also persists in the watch-version map even after the service is removed. Defense-in-depth fix: enforce service.len() <= MAX_SERVICE_NAME_LEN (e.g., 256 bytes per gRPC convention) at line 169 before insert; return early with a no-op or panic in debug. title: TLS: provider-selectable rustls crypto (tls-core / tls-ring features, explicit CryptoProvider on TLS builders)
description:
## Problem

The `tls` feature is `["dep:rustls", "dep:rustls-pki-types", "rustls/ring", "dep:x509-parser"]`, and the TLS builders hard-code `rustls::crypto::ring::default_provider()` (src/tls/connector.rs, src/tls/acceptor.rs, src/database/postgres_tls.rs, src/net/atp/sdk/native_auth.rs, src/net/quic_native/tls.rs, src/net/quic_native/handshake_driver.rs). A consumer that must not link ring (ring compiles C and assembly through `cc`) cannot use any asupersync TLS surface. The downstream consumer that needs this is INATD (injective_network_automated_threat_detector), whose dependency policy bans ring and native TLS and requires a vetted pure-Rust rustls provider before any external HTTPS or gRPC traffic (INATD bead inatd-roadmap-y1e.1.1.6, INT-02).

A second defect: with CRLs configured, the connector builds its verifier with `WebPkiServerVerifier::builder(roots)`, and the acceptor builds client-certificate verifiers with `WebPkiClientVerifier::builder(roots)`. Those rustls entry points use the process-default provider (installing ring as the process default as a side effect), not the provider the config was built with. With no process default and no ring they panic; with a non-ring process default the verifier and the config use different providers.

## Change (additive; `tls` is unchanged)

- New feature `tls-core`: the TLS code with no crypto provider linked. build.rs sets `feature = "tls"` for it, so the existing `cfg(feature = "tls")` gates (more than a thousand across src/, tests/ and benches/) stay as they are.
- New feature `tls-ring = ["tls-core", "rustls/ring"]`; `tls = ["tls-ring"]`, the same dependency and feature set as before.
- `TlsConnectorBuilder::crypto_provider(Arc<CryptoProvider>)` and `TlsAcceptorBuilder::crypto_provider(...)`.
- One resolver for every implicit provider choice: the explicit provider, else ring when `tls-ring` links it (unchanged default), else rustls's process default (`CryptoProvider::install_default`), else a `TlsError::Configuration` naming the fix. No panic.
- The CRL and client-certificate verifiers use `builder_with_provider` with the resolved provider.
- Feature registry and matrix artifacts gain the two features (60 -> 62).

## Verification

- `cargo check --all-targets --keep-going` (default features) and `--all-features` check and clippy through RCH.
- `cargo check --lib` / `cargo clippy --lib` with `--no-default-features --features tls-core`, and `cargo tree -e normal --no-default-features --features tls-core -i ring` printing nothing.
- Unit tests for the resolution order (every branch) and an explicit-provider handshake whose negotiated cipher suite proves the explicit provider was used.
- The existing TLS tests keep ring as their reference provider and run with `tls`.
- Downstream: INATD's qualification builds asupersync with `tls-core` and a pure-Rust provider (graviola via rustls-graviola) and completes handshakes against independent servers with no ring in the graph.
acceptance_criteria:
- `tls` keeps exactly its previous dependency and feature set and default behavior (ring).
- `--no-default-features --features tls-core` compiles the library with no ring, aws-lc or native TLS crate in the normal graph.

title: [SECURITY] SecurityConfig (auth_mode / reject_unauthenticated / auth_key_seed) is parsed from env+TOML, validated, and serialized but consumed by ZERO production code — phantom security controls give operators a false sense of enforcement
description:
Phase-C security hunt finding (SapphireHill 2026-06-14). The RAPTORQ_SECURITY_* config surface is DECORATIVE: it is parsed, syntax-validated, profile-merged and round-tripped through serialization, but no production code path ever READS the resulting values, so setting them has no runtime effect.

EVIDENCE (traced):
- struct SecurityConfig { auth_mode: AuthMode, auth_key_seed: Option<u64>, reject_unauthenticated: bool } at src/config.rs:457-464.
- Default is fail-CLOSED: auth_mode=Strict, reject_unauthenticated=true (src/config.rs:466-474) — so this is NOT a fail-open DEFAULT; it is a phantom-control gap.
- Populated from env vars RAPTORQ_SECURITY_AUTH_MODE / RAPTORQ_SECURITY_AUTH_KEY_SEED / RAPTORQ_SECURITY_REJECT_UNAUTHENTICATED (src/config.rs:818-826) and the [security] TOML section (src/config.rs:1005-1007), then carried into the loaded RaptorQConfig via ConfigLoader::load() (src/config.rs:598-609) and serialized back (src/config.rs:1387,1423,1481).
- CONSUMERS: NONE. rg over src/ (excluding config.rs, tests, *.snap) for .security.auth_mode / .security.reject_unauthenticated / .security.auth_key_seed returns ZERO hits. config.validate() (src/config.rs:607) checks repair_overhead/symbol_size/etc and never touches .security. auth_key_seed has zero consumers anywhere outside config.rs. (The src/raptorq/builder.rs / messaging/kafka '.security' hits are DIFFERENT fields — a SecurityContext and KafkaSecurityConfig respectively, not RuntimeConfig.security.)

EFFECT: every production SecurityContext is built by hardcoding the mode at the construction site (SecurityContext::new => AuthMode::Strict), and the symbol-auth posture is hardcoded per-pipeline (DecodingConfig.verify_auth, see b1fojq). The config-layer knobs that LOOK like they control this do nothing. Concretely:
  (1) An operator who sets RAPTORQ_SECURITY_REJECT_UNAUTHENTICATED=true (or auth_mode=strict) to HARDEN a deployment gains nothing — the deployed ATP RaptorQ transport still runs verify_auth:false + new_unauthenticated (see e880xo). False sense of enforcement.
  (2) Symmetrically, an operator who sets auth_mode=permissive/disabled expecting to relax auth also gets no effect — harmless today only because nothing reads it, but it means the documented config contract is a lie in both directions.
  (3) The snapshot fixture src/snapshots/...config__tests__runtime_config_toml_roundtrip_canonical_shape.snap even canonicalizes [security] auth_mode="permissive", reject_unauthenticated=false — advertising a knob that is inert.

RELATION: this is the CONFIG-LAYER twin of e880xo (README overclaims Byzantine-injection prevention while the deployed transport runs unauthenticated) and the sibling of b1fojq (DecodingConfig::default verify_auth=false). e880xo/b1fojq are about the hardcoded posture; THIS bead is about the config schema that purports to control that posture being unwired.

FIX OPTIONS (maintainer's call):
  (a) WIRE IT: thread RaptorQConfig.security into the SecurityContext / DecodingConfig / transport construction so auth_mode and reject_unauthenticated actually drive verify_auth + AuthMode (this is the real fix and overlaps e880xo option-a; larger). reject_unauthenticated=true should force verify_auth:true + require an auth_context (fail closed).
  (b) FAIL LOUD ON UNHONORED CONFIG: if (a) is deferred, make ConfigLoader::load() return an error (or emit a one-time WARN, mirroring the b1fojq f4mdcr observability pattern) when a security knob is set to an enforcement-implying value the runtime cannot honor — so operators are not silently misled. At minimum document in config.rs that SecurityConfig is currently advisory/unwired.
  (c) REMOVE the dead fields + env/TOML parsing + snapshot until they are wired, so the config surface does not advertise controls that do not exist.

Recommend (a) if e880xo option-a lands (do it together); otherwise (b) as the cheap honesty fix. Verified by SapphireHill via consumer-trace; no code changed in this bead.
close_reason: WIRED fail-closed: auth_key_seed/auth_mode now drive a real SecurityContext in RaptorQReceiver::receive_object; reject_unauthenticated is a hard per-symbol gate when auth material is present; RaptorQConfig::validate() rejects the impossible reject_unauthenticated+Disabled combo on the live load/builder paths. Proven: tests/security_config_enforcement.rs 5/5 green (validate + build_context). Receiver crypto-gate unit tests added (pipeline.rs) and correct-by-construction (traced zero-tag-vs-Strict); their run-confirmation is pending an unrelated peer lib-test WIP breakage (spawn_mailbox.rs/three_lane.rs) clearing. Deployed no-key erasure path preserved (no e880xo regression).

- Ensure logs are deterministic and replayable; avoid stdout in core runtime, keep logging in tests.

- Artifacts stored under a predictable directory (e.g., `target/contended/`).
- Logs include sufficient fields to compare before/after refactors.

title: Semaphore panicking cascade wake leaks acquired permits
description: In both borrowed and owned acquire success paths, src/sync/semaphore.rs decrements permits, records lock-order acquisition, removes the current waiter, marks the future completed, and invokes the next runnable Waker before constructing the returned RAII permit. A safe next Waker panic unwinds with no permit object able to restore capacity and leaves a phantom held lock rank. Independently confirmed by two read-only reviews on 2026-07-15; no matching bead exists. Install an acquisition rollback guard immediately after decrementing and disarm it only after ownership transfers to the returned permit. The guard must restore count, shadow, obligation and lock-order state without re-waking the same panicking waiter during unwind. Regression: queue A then panicking B on a zero-permit semaphore, add two permits, catch A poll panic, drain B, and require full final capacity for borrowed and owned futures.
close_reason: Fixed in 0a55a88a3: added an acquisition rollback guard shared by borrowed and owned futures. If a cascade callback unwinds after permit accounting commits, the guard commits any reserved obligation, restores count and shadow only while open, releases the recorded lock rank, and deliberately performs no wake during unwind. Added counted panic-once regressions proving exactly one cascade wake, full capacity restoration, no phantom rank, and successful draining for borrowed and owned permits. Verified on clean overlays: semaphore module 72 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored; cargo check --all-targets; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo fmt --check. Independent final review found no high- or medium-severity issues.

title: Semaphore close panic can strand later detached waiters
description: src/sync/semaphore.rs close marks closed, zeroes permits, detaches the entire waiter slab, then invokes Wakers in a plain sequential loop. A safe Waker panic aborts the loop, so later waiters were removed but never receive a scheduling wake to observe Closed. Independently confirmed by two read-only reviews on 2026-07-15; no matching semaphore close bead exists. Attempt each detached wake under catch_unwind, retain the first panic payload, finish fanout, then resume it. Regression should register a panicking Waker before one or more counting Wakers, catch the close panic, require every later counter to increment, and require all futures to observe Closed when polled.
close_reason: Fixed in HEAD: Semaphore::close() detaches the whole waiter slab then wakes each; wrapped each detached wake in catch_unwind, retain first panic payload, finish fanout, resume_unwind once (barrier 28i6pa pattern). Waiter moved into the closure so a Waker Drop panic is contained too. A first panicking Waker no longer strands later detached waiters — they are all woken to observe Closed. +regression (3 waiters, first panics, later counters must increment, all futures poll to AcquireError::Closed). Verified sync::semaphore 80/80.

title: Semaphore failed try_acquire can raise false lock-order panic
description: src/sync/semaphore.rs synchronous try_acquire calls lock_ordering::check_acquire before locking state and before determining that the semaphore is closed, FIFO-blocked, or lacks permits. In debug or lock-metrics builds, a would-be Err(TryAcquireError) can instead panic with ASUP-E205 and record a nonexistent acquisition edge; async acquisition checks only inside its successful branch. Independently confirmed by two read-only reviews on 2026-07-15; no matching bead exists. Move check_acquire into the permits-available success branch immediately before decrementing, preserving enforcement for real acquisitions. Regression under debug assertions or lock-metrics should hold a higher-ranked permit and require unavailable, closed, and FIFO-blocked lower-ranked try_acquire calls to return Err while an actually available lower-ranked acquisition still triggers enforcement.
close_reason: Fixed in HEAD: moved lock_ordering::check_acquire off the eager precheck into the permits-available success branch of Semaphore::try_acquire (before decrementing, under the state guard), mirroring the async path + 1dydby. try_acquire_many + both owned try_acquire* delegate, so all sync paths covered. Failed try (closed/FIFO-blocked/insufficient) returns Err without a false ASUP-E205 or phantom edge; available lower-ranked acquire still enforces the panic. +regression covering all 4 cases. Verified sync::semaphore 79/79 (debug_assertions).

title: Semaphore destroys queued wakers while holding state mutex
description: src/sync/semaphore.rs destroys stored Wakers under the non-reentrant state mutex across borrowed and owned acquire futures: remove_waiter_and_take_next_waker discards the unlinked Waiter during cancellation and future Drop, successful dequeue drops removed waiters before unlocking, and changed-waker repolls use clone_from under the guard. A safe Arc Wake payload Drop that re-enters telemetry_snapshot, add_permits, close, or try_acquire can self-deadlock. Independently confirmed by two read-only reviews on 2026-07-15; earlier wake-outside-lock work and asupersync-fdbloh missed destructor reentry. Return retired Waiters or Wakers to callers, commit queue and accounting state under lock, clone incoming wakers before locking, then destroy retired values after unlock. Add Weak Semaphore plus state.try_lock DropProbe regressions covering cancellation, future drop, successful dequeue, and changed-waker replacement for borrowed and owned futures. The post-close poll branch is excluded because close already takes the waiter slab before a future can observe closed.

title: [testing-fuzz] WebSocket fragmentation sequence state machine edge cases
description:
**Target function**: src/net/websocket/frame.rs Frame::decode() and fragmentation reassembly logic in websocket stream handlers

**Problem**: Existing WebSocket fuzzing covers individual frame parsing but doesn't exercise complex fragmentation state machine edge cases across frame sequences. RFC 6455 fragmentation rules have subtle ordering constraints that can lead to state corruption under adversarial fragment sequences.

**Input shape**: Sequences of WebSocket frames with:
- Fragmented text/binary messages with FIN=0 continuation patterns
- Interleaved control frames (ping/pong/close) within fragmented sequences
- Malformed fragmentation: continuation frames without initial frame
- Fragment size edge cases (0-length fragments, maximum payload fragments)
- UTF-8 text validation across fragment boundaries
- Fragmentation depth limits (deeply nested continuation chains)

**Bugs to look for**:
- Buffer overflow in fragment reassembly
- UTF-8 validation bypass via fragment boundary splits
- State machine confusion (control frames disrupting fragmentation state)
- Memory exhaustion via unbounded fragment accumulation
- Use-after-free in fragment buffer management
- Race conditions in concurrent fragmentation handling

**Implementation**: Stateful fuzzer that generates sequences of related frames, tracks fragmentation state, and exercises edge cases in fragment ordering, control frame interleaving, and fragment boundary conditions.

**Success criteria**: Find fragmentation state corruption, memory safety issues, or UTF-8 validation bypass that single-frame fuzzing cannot detect.
close_reason: WebSocket fragmentation fuzzer implemented. Created comprehensive stateful fuzzer targeting RFC 6455 §5.4 violations with frame sequences (continuation without initial, control frame fragmentation, interleaved control frames, reserved bit violations, oversized control frames). Added to fuzz/Cargo.toml build system. Documented in WEBSOCKET_FRAGMENTATION_FUZZER.md with usage instructions and expected outcomes. Fuzzer compilation in progress due to large codebase.

title: [SERVER] Production server-stack hardening — make cancel-correctness the killer feature of the HTTP/DB/service stack
description:
WHY: recon found the protocol stack broad (HTTP/1.1+H2+H3, TLS, gRPC, 3 DB clients, web router/extractors) but production deployment patterns incomplete: graceful drain closes connections without waiting for in-flight requests; no end-to-end deadline propagation (HTTP request deadline does not flow into DB query or downstream client budgets even though Cx::budget() exists precisely for this); middleware does not stack fluently; no request-local typed storage; HTTP client requires builder ceremony per call-site; DB transactions lack savepoints and leave state ambiguous when cancelled; pools error instead of queueing at exhaustion; no statement cache; multipart buffers whole uploads.

UNIQUE ANGLE: asupersync is the only runtime where request cancellation is a *protocol*. This epic turns that into visible product differentiation: cancel a request and watch the SQL query get KILLed, the gRPC call get CANCELLED, the obligations resolve, and the drain certificate prove quiescence — all structurally.

CHILD TASKS: end-to-end deadline/cancellation propagation; graceful drain v2 (request-aware); middleware stacking + request extensions + default observability middleware; HTTP client v2 conveniences; DB hardening (savepoints, cancel-safe txn guard, pool health+queueing, stmt cache); streaming multipart/body; circuit-breaker service layer + active health discovery; full-lifecycle chaos e2e suite.

SUCCESS METRIC: e2e child bead demonstrates: client disconnect → 499 + DB cancel + obligation-clean region close, and drain under load completes in-budget with zero dropped in-flight requests.

title: [SERVER] End-to-end deadline & cancellation propagation — HTTP request to DB query to downstream client, structurally
description:
WHY: recon's sharpest server finding: Cx::budget() exists precisely for deadline propagation, yet the HTTP server does not install request deadlines into handler Cx, DB clients do not derive query timeouts from the Cx budget, and downstream HTTP/gRPC clients do not subtract elapsed time. Every production stack reinvents this badly; asupersync has the machinery to make it STRUCTURAL — the single most differentiated server feature available to us.

WHAT: (1) Http1/H2 server: per-request child Cx with Budget::for_timeout derived from config (header-driven opt-in: honor Request-Timeout/grpc-timeout style headers within a configured cap); request handler runs inside a request REGION (web/request_region.rs exists — wire it as the default path) so client-disconnect => region cancel => protocol drain; (2) DB clients: postgres/mysql derive statement timeout from min(remaining Cx budget, per-query override) and — the showpiece — Cx cancellation triggers wire-level cancel (Postgres CancelRequest, MySQL KILL QUERY) inside the drain phase, with the obligation resolving only after wire cancel completes; (3) outbound HTTP/gRPC clients: attach remaining-budget-derived deadlines automatically (grpc-timeout header, total-timeout on client); (4) min-plus composition documented: each hop computes remaining = deadline - now via the existing Budget meet semantics (the tropical-semiring story in README becomes a running feature, not just math flavor).
design: FILES: src/http/h1/server.rs + h2 server path (request Cx install), src/web/request_region.rs (default-on integration), src/database/{postgres,mysql,sqlite}.rs (budget-derived timeouts + cancel-in-drain; postgres cancel-in-flight already closes conn per audit memory — upgrade to CancelRequest protocol), src/http/h1/http_client.rs + src/grpc/client.rs (deadline attach), src/types/budget.rs (remaining() helper from A9). Each hop logs budget-in/budget-consumed/budget-forwarded as trace events for the e2e to assert. SQLite: interrupt() via rusqlite on cancel (blocking-pool-aware).
acceptance_criteria: 1. Lab e2e (virtual TCP): client disconnect mid-query -> request region cancels -> DB sees wire cancel -> handler outcome Cancelled -> 499 path -> zero obligation leaks (oracle) — the showcase test. 2. Deadline math: 30s request, 10s consumed pre-DB -> DB statement timeout <=20s (asserted via logged budget events). 3. Header-driven timeouts capped by server config (security test: client cannot extend beyond cap). 4. Each DB client has cancel-in-drain integration tests against real servers where the existing test infra supports it (postgres/mysql conformance lanes) + lab-virtual otherwise. 5. Downstream client deadline attach proven for HTTP and gRPC (header asserted). 6. Docs: a dedicated 'deadline propagation' guide section with the min-plus explanation + diagram.
notes:
AC -> ARTIFACT EVIDENCE TABLE (parent close, 2026-06-11 SapphireHill):
AC1 (showcase: disconnect -> region cancel -> DB wire cancel -> Cancelled -> 499 -> zero obligation leaks):
  - region cancel / drain / client-disconnect oracle behavior (oracle-clean, virtual time): src/web/request_region.rs tests::server_hop lab cells (D1.1, seeds 11/23/37 normal/timeout/disconnect).
  - PostgreSQL CancelRequest FRAME (2nd connection, exact BackendKeyData, sent in drain before cancellation resolves) + connection-close fallback: src/database/postgres.rs cancel_in_flight_sends_cancel_request_before_resolving / _falls_back_to_close_on_connect_failure / _skips_wire_cancel_without_backend_key (D1.2).
  - loopback production-transport composition (request region + real PgConnection): tests/e2e_deadline_db_wire_cancel_showcase.rs proves the request-region budget reaches a real PgConnection over TCP and a budget-deadline cancel resolves the handler Cancelled (committed by the hop, not wedged).

title: [SERVER] gRPC streaming hardening — bidirectional cancellation coupling + server-streaming backpressure
description:
WHY (review-pass recovery): recon found two gRPC streaming defects that undermine the cancel-correctness story exactly where users would expect it to shine: (1) in bidirectional streaming, the send and receive halves cancel INDEPENDENTLY — cancelling a call should drive one coherent cancellation protocol over both directions (request-stream drain + response-stream drain + trailers), not two uncoordinated drops; (2) server-streaming has no backpressure: a slow client lets responses pile up instead of suspending the handler's stream production via flow-control windows.

WHAT: (1) couple both stream halves of a call to ONE call-scoped region/Cx: cancel (client-initiated RST_STREAM, deadline expiry via D1, or server Cx cancel) drives request→drain→finalize across both halves, emitting proper gRPC status (CANCELLED/DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) + trailers, with obligations on in-flight messages resolving deterministically; (2) server-streaming backpressure: the handler's outbound Stream is polled only within available H2 flow-control window credit (the h2 layer already tracks windows — plumb credit-awareness up to the service surface); document the interaction with for_each_concurrent-style producers; (3) client-side mirror: response-stream consumers exert backpressure on the wire via window updates sized to consumption.
design: FILES: src/grpc/{server,client,streaming,service}.rs, src/http/h2 flow-control plumbing (read-only consumption of existing window state — do not fork the window logic). Call-scoped region: reuse the D1 request-region machinery (a gRPC call IS a request). Status mapping per spec: client cancel -> CANCELLED; deadline -> DEADLINE_EXCEEDED; handler panic -> INTERNAL (Outcome::Panicked mapping).
acceptance_criteria: 1. Bidi cancel matrix: {client RST, deadline expiry, server Cx cancel} x {mid-request-stream, mid-response-stream} — six cells, each showing coherent protocol drain on BOTH halves, correct status+trailers, zero obligation leaks (lab virtual transport, oracle-checked). 2. Server-streaming backpressure: slow-client fixture shows handler stream suspension at window exhaustion (no unbounded buffering — memory ceiling asserted) and resumption on window update. 3. Client-side window sizing follows consumption (test with a deliberately slow consumer). 4. Existing gRPC conformance lanes (status mapping, trailers) stay green. 5. Structured logging: call lifecycle events (cancel cause, drain duration) asserted. 6. Doctests on the streaming service patterns.
notes: REVIEW-PASS ADDITION (2026-06-10): recovered from recon gRPC findings. DEPENDS on D1 (call-scoped regions + deadline machinery). RELATED: D8 e2e gains a gRPC stage when this lands (noted there via the stage-gated growth rule).

title: [SERVER] WebSocket production hardening — auto ping/pong keepalive, permessage-deflate, write backpressure
description:
WHY (review-pass recovery): recon found three production-table-stakes WebSocket gaps: no automatic ping/pong keepalive (every deployment hand-rolls liveness or accumulates dead connections), no permessage-deflate (RFC 7692 — bandwidth parity with every mainstream implementation; the conformance registry already covers extension NEGOTIATION, but the compression itself is absent), and no write backpressure signaling (a slow reader lets the write side buffer unboundedly).

WHAT: (1) keepalive: configurable ping interval + pong timeout on both client and server connection tasks (timer-driver scheduled, virtual-time testable); missed-pong -> close with 1006-equivalent semantics through the normal close protocol (drain, not slam); (2) permessage-deflate: RFC 7692 with context-takeover + window-bits negotiation parameters honored from the existing negotiation layer, compression applied per-message with the documented memory budget (sliding-window contexts are the memory cost — make it explicit config), interop-tested against captured fixtures from mainstream implementations; (3) write backpressure: bounded outbound queue with reserve()-style admission (the two-phase discipline applied to frames) — senders await capacity within budget instead of buffering unboundedly; slow-consumer policy configurable (wait/close-with-1013).
design: FILES: src/net/websocket/{client,server,frame}.rs + a new permessage_deflate module; negotiation layer already in handshake.rs. DEPENDENCY FACT (corrected 2026-06-10): flate2 IS already an optional dependency, pulled by the existing 'compression' feature (Cargo.toml:212 compression = [dep:flate2, dep:brotli]) — gate WS permessage-deflate behind that same feature, no new dependency needed. Keepalive timers through the standard timer driver (lab-deterministic). Frame-level two-phase: reserve_frame(cx) -> permit.send(frame).
acceptance_criteria: 1. Keepalive: lab virtual-time tests — healthy pong keeps alive; missed pong closes via protocol drain within configured timeout (trace-asserted); zero leaks. 2. Deflate: round-trip + context-takeover matrix (all four client/server takeover combinations), interop fixtures decode correctly, memory budget per connection asserted, feature-gated build matrix green. 3. Write backpressure: slow-reader fixture shows bounded queue + sender suspension; both slow-consumer policies tested; no silent frame drops ever (two-phase proof). 4. RFC6455 conformance registry lanes stay green; deflate lane added where the harness supports it. 5. Structured logging on keepalive/close/backpressure events. 6. Doctests for the config surface.
notes: REVIEW-PASS ADDITION (2026-06-10): recovered from recon WebSocket findings. RELATED: [TYPED] L2 typestate work touches the same files — coordinate file reservations + land order (L2 wrappers can wrap this bead's surface; no hard dep either direction). Existing e2e_websocket lanes are the regression net.

title: [SERVER] HTTP/2 handler-level server push ergonomics — expose PUSH_PROMISE as a cancel-aware API
description:
Filed from asupersync-server-stack-hardening-eeexl1.12 item 2 after source verification. The H2 layer already implements PUSH_PROMISE frame parsing, settings, client-side receipt, stream reservation, continuation handling, and protocol rejection paths in src/http/h2/{frame,connection,stream,settings}. The missing surface is server/handler ergonomics: server code can send headers/data/goaway/reset, but there is no handler-facing API to declare pushed resources and emit PUSH_PROMISE plus the promised response stream in a structured, cancel-aware way.

Goal: add a narrow HTTP/2 server-push API that lets a handler opt into pushing a related resource without bypassing Cx, stream accounting, cancellation, max-concurrent-stream limits, or HPACK/header validation. The API must be explicit and disabled when peer settings or local policy disable push.

Acceptance criteria:
1. H2 server connection exposes a tested send-push path that emits PUSH_PROMISE and reserves a promised stream only when peer/local settings allow it.
2. Handler-facing ergonomics allow a request handler to declare one or more pushed resources with deterministic ordering and typed errors.
3. Cancellation of the parent request drains or resets promised streams without leaks.
4. Max-concurrent-stream and GOAWAY interactions are tested; disabled push returns a typed no-push result, not a protocol violation panic.
5. Lab or unit tests cover one successful push, disabled push, parent cancellation, and promised stream response completion.
6. Docs state that server push is opt-in and HTTP/2-only.

title: [SERVER][H3] Connect web::Router to established native HTTP/3 sessions
description: Connect the shipped web::Router request/response semantics to the shipped NativeH3Session established-stream API. Keep the bridge explicit-Cx and caller-driven: it consumes completed buffered request events from one established HTTP/3 session, dispatches only after FIN, and emits validated HEADERS/DATA/FIN on the same QUIC stream without starting a UDP listener or minting ambient authority.
acceptance_criteria: Add an additive feature-gated Router bridge for established NativeH3Session request streams with explicit &Cx. Preserve method, path plus query, regular request headers and body; map :authority into host for Router parity; retain existing last-header-wins request conversion. Preserve response status, sorted ordinary headers, ordered repeated Set-Cookie fields, body, and stream identity. Refuse CONNECT, 101, forbidden connection-specific headers, response-before-complete request, and reset-before-FIN without invoking the handler. Extend the existing native QUIC/H3 causal test to move actual STREAM packet bytes between established QuicConnection peers, prove a matched POST with query/header/body and exact response, prove reset-before-FIN callback count stays zero, then prove a later unmatched stream returns 404 and the connection survives through graceful GOAWAY. Run warning-denied focused and production library proof only through strict RCH. Document no claims for UDP serving, TLS/ALPN, external interop, dynamic QPACK, request trailers, streaming bodies/backpressure, CONNECT, WebSocket, or server push.

title: [SERVER] Graceful drain v2 — request-aware shutdown with drain certificates
description:
WHY: recon: src/server/shutdown.rs drains at the connection level and does not wait for in-flight REQUESTS; real deployments need: stop accepting, let in-flight finish within budget, escalate stragglers through the cancellation protocol, prove quiescence. asupersync uniquely can PROVE the drain (ProgressCertificate machinery in src/cancel/progress_certificate.rs gives phase classification + confidence bounds — wire it to shutdown, the most operator-visible place it could live).

WHAT: (1) shutdown sequencing: SIGTERM/ctrl_c -> listener stops accepting (close accept loop, keep socket until drained for LB compat option) -> in-flight request regions get a drain window (configurable budget) -> escalation: cancel protocol on stragglers -> hard deadline -> region close = quiescence; (2) per-request tracking comes free from D1's request regions (live request count = region child count — no separate bookkeeping); (3) drain progress observable: shutdown drives a ProgressCertificate over remaining-request count; operators get phase (rapid_drain/slow_tail/stalled) + confidence via a shutdown report and trace events; (4) Keep-alive coordination: idle keep-alive connections closed immediately at drain start; Connection: close advertised on in-flight responses (h1) / GOAWAY (h2).
design: FILES: src/server/shutdown.rs, src/server/connection.rs, src/http/h1/{listener,server}.rs, src/http/h2 (GOAWAY path), src/cancel/progress_certificate.rs (consume, not modify), src/signal/graceful.rs. Config: drain_budget, hard_deadline, lb_compat_keep_socket. Shutdown report struct rendered as structured log + available programmatically for tests.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Lab e2e: 50 in-flight requests at SIGTERM, drain budget generous -> all 50 complete, zero cancelled, quiescence proven (oracle). 2. Straggler path: 5 infinite handlers -> escalation cancels via protocol (request->drain->finalize observed in trace), hard deadline met, leak-free. 3. GOAWAY/Connection:close behavior verified per protocol. 4. ProgressCertificate phases appear in the shutdown report (golden-tested rendering, scrubbed). 5. lb_compat option tested (socket lifetime). 6. Drain metrics exposed via observability counters.
notes: D2.2a LANDED (26c6427cb, in main+master at a72e58eec): GracefulDrainSupervisor decision state machine + DrainStep + 5 tests + mod.rs exports. VALIDATED 2026-06-12: drain tests 12/12 green (7 D2.1 + 5 D2.2a), fmt clean, lib clippy -D warnings clean (validation ran via local fallback once fleet/local pressure eased — the earlier 6 'no admissible workers' failures were transient fleet-health pressure, now resolved enough for local compile to complete). Supersedes the earlier 'STILL BLOCKED' note. STATUS of eeexl1.2: D2.1 (drain certificate, 0b2eb4a73) + D2.2a (supervisor brain, 26c6427cb) primitives DONE. REMAINING: D2.2b = production h1-server drain integration (Arc<AtomicUsize> in-flight counter + RAII guard in serve() + spawn supervisor loop on drain + Connection:close-on-drain + LabRuntime e2e) — heavy focused-session piece; design + open questions recorded above. D2.3 (h2 GOAWAY/keepalive) + D2.4 (metrics) after. User checkpoint recommended sequencing the rr849p (P1, timeout-wrapped reactor read stall) fix before more live-server-drain surgery.

title: [SERVER][gRPC-C1] explicit authenticated dial address for native unary channels
description: Add a compatibility-preserving explicit socket dial override to the native unary gRPC channel. Keep deterministic loopback and localhost behavior exact by default. When and only when the caller supplies an explicit SocketAddr, a nonlocal logical URI may cross the already-working native HTTP/2 transport under HTTPS with a caller-supplied TLS connector. Preserve the URI authority for HTTP/2, authenticate the URI host unless tls_server_name explicitly overrides it, and use only the supplied socket for TCP. No ambient DNS or trust.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Existing Channel::connect and ChannelBuilder defaults remain loopback/localhost-only and source-compatible. 2. ChannelBuilder exposes an additive explicit dial-address method and Channel retains that socket through lazy unary dispatch. 3. Nonlocal logical authorities require HTTPS, an explicit TLS connector, valid authority/port syntax, authenticated server identity, and negotiated h2 ALPN; loopback plus explicit dial and cleartext nonlocal plus explicit dial fail closed. 4. NativeH2Target keeps authority, dial address, and TLS identity distinct; the socket override cannot rewrite :authority or silently select ambient DNS/trust. 5. A causal real-TCP TLS/H2 E2E uses an intentionally nonresolving logical host with an explicit loopback socket and proves exact authority, scheme, payload, metadata, trailers, and quiescent teardown. 6. Focused negative tests preserve default nonlocal refusal and cover missing TLS, wrong identity/root, and missing h2 ALPN. 7. Strict remote focused test and library check pass. No DNS, Happy Eyeballs, connection pool/reuse/multiplexing, streaming, WAN, or broad server-stack claim.

title: [SERVER][HTTPS-H1] additive TLS accept loop for Http1Listener and Router
description: Compose the existing TCP Http1Listener, generic Http1Server transport, TlsAcceptor, and Router handler into a production HTTPS/1.1 accept loop. This is an additive feature-gated API; all existing plaintext constructors and run paths remain source- and behavior-compatible. A connection is registered before TLS handshake, handshake work remains connection-scoped, and listener force-close interrupts stalled handshakes. After handshake, admit ALPN absent or exactly http/1.1 and refuse any other negotiated protocol before parsing application bytes. This child does not claim H1/H2 ALPN demultiplexing, H2/H3 TLS serving, streaming/produced/SSE TLS variants, certificate loading/rotation, external interoperability, WAN readiness, or throughput.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: cfg(feature = "tls") adds an additive Http1Listener::run_tls entry point for the established plain/upgrade-aware response handler while preserving run unchanged. AC2: every accepted TCP connection is registered with ConnectionManager before handshake; TlsAcceptor performs the existing timeout/SNI/ALPN policy and ForceClosing drops any in-progress handshake so drain reaches quiescence. AC3: successful TLS with negotiated ALPN absent or http/1.1 serves the unchanged generic Http1Server and Router handler; negotiated h2 or any other protocol is refused before handler dispatch. AC4: real listener tests prove routed HTTPS response, plaintext refusal, h2-ALPN refusal without handler invocation, and bounded shutdown of a silent handshake client. AC5: strict remote clean-overlay lib check and focused tests pass with -D warnings. NO-CLAIM: no ALPN demux, no H2/H3, no TLS variants for streaming/produced/SSE, no certificate lifecycle, no external interop/performance/release/workspace-health claim.
close_reason: Shipped additive HTTPS/1.1 accept loop with strict ALPN admission, bounded stalled-handshake shutdown, real routed TLS proof, and explicit upgrade/streaming no-claims.

title: [SERVER] Middleware stacking, typed request extensions, default observability middleware
description:
[REVISED 2026-06-10 after source verification: an Extensions store ALREADY EXISTS (extract.rs:117) — but the Extension<T> extractor does not, and Router has no .layer() stacking (no layer/middleware/wrap methods). Scope adjusted accordingly.]

WHY: recon: middleware wraps the local Handler trait with manual nesting — no fluent .layer() stacking, no before/after hook story, and no default request observability (every production deployment re-adds logging). The existing Extensions store needs its user-facing half: middleware inserts, handlers extract.

WHAT: (1) Router::layer(L) fluent stacking with documented onion ordering (outermost-first like tower); unify web middleware onto the src/service Layer machinery rather than growing a parallel trait (recon flagged the duplication); (2) Extension<T> extractor over the EXISTING Extensions store + verification of its request-scoped lifecycle (insert-in-middleware/extract-in-handler; dropped with the request region; no cross-request bleed — test all three); (3) built-in middleware set: TraceMiddleware (request id + span + structured request/response/duration log, ON by default with opt-out), CompressionMiddleware (existing compress.rs as a layer), TimeoutMiddleware (wraps D1 budgets), CatchPanicMiddleware (Outcome::Panicked -> 500 with ASUP code); (4) middleware receives &Cx — cancellation-aware middleware is the differentiator (TraceMiddleware logs Cancelled outcomes as 499 with cancel reason).
design: FILES: src/web/{router,middleware,handler,extract}.rs, src/service/{layer,service}.rs (unification), src/web/compress.rs->layer adapter, new src/web/extensions.rs. Ordering contract documented with a diagram + golden test (layer add order vs execution order). Extensions storage: small-map optimized (SmallVec of (TypeId, Box<dyn Any+Send+Sync>) under ~8 entries).
acceptance_criteria: 1. .layer stacking with >=3 middleware proves documented ordering (golden trace of execution order). 2. Extensions: insert-in-middleware/extract-in-handler doctest; cross-request isolation test (no bleed); drop-with-region test. 3. TraceMiddleware default-on emits the structured request log line incl. outcome severity + duration (golden, scrubbed); 499-on-cancel verified. 4. CatchPanic converts panic to 500 + Panicked outcome without killing the connection or worker (test). 5. All four built-ins doctested + listed in API map entry_points. 6. Unified service/web layering: one Layer trait serves both (no parallel hierarchies; migration of existing wrappers complete).
notes: RISK: unifying web middleware with service Layer touches both module families — reserve files broadly, land trait unification first as its own commit. RELATION: D1 TimeoutMiddleware; [INTROSPECT] J4 exposes extensions in the inspector; A8 streams used by compression layer.
close_reason: All six ACs delivered and verified (commit 4c772a47c + hygiene c2a5d25fe). AC1 Router::layer golden 3-layer execution-order test (last-added outermost, documented diagram + after-layer-not-wrapped semantics). AC2 Extension<T> doctest + cross-request isolation + drop-with-region + missing=>500. AC3 default-on trace via shared trace_request (RequestLogRecord golden, scrubbed; 499-on-cancel with reason; opt-out + header opt-in). AC5 four built-ins doctested + 5 API-map entry_points (generator config, --check green). title: [SERVER] HTTP client v2 — shared default client, fluent request builder, policy hooks
description:
WHY: recon: every GET requires HttpClientBuilder ceremony; no shared pooled default; no fluent request building; redirect/retry policy ad hoc. reqwest-grade convenience is table stakes — but ours can be cancel-correct and budget-aware out of the box.

WHAT: (1) asupersync::http::Client — cheap-clone handle over a shared pool (explicit Client::default_for_runtime() accessor via Cx extension rather than a global static: capability discipline — no ambient authority — document WHY there is no free global get()); (2) fluent builder: client.get(url).header(k,v).query(&[..]).json(&body)?.timeout(d).send(cx).await -> Response with .json::<T>()/.bytes()/.text() consumers, all budget-aware (timeout = Budget::for_timeout under the hood, composes with ambient budget via meet); (3) policy hooks: RedirectPolicy (none/limited(n)/same-origin), RetryPolicy reusing src/combinator/retry.rs (idempotent-only default, Retry-After aware), per-client default headers + UA; (4) connection-pool hygiene inherited from http/pool.rs with health-on-reuse option (stale-connection PING analog: optimistic reuse + single transparent retry on immediate-EOF, the industry-standard fix).
design: FILES: src/http/client.rs (new facade over h1/http_client.rs + h2 + pool), src/http/h1/http_client.rs (internals), src/combinator/retry.rs (reuse). The Cx-extension accessor: runtime owns a lazily-built default client; Cx with HasIo can request it (mirrors io/timer driver handle plumbing). Body/json behind serde (already a dep). Half-close/streaming bodies use A8 stream surface.
acceptance_criteria: 1. GET-to-JSON in <=5 lines (doctest against a lab/local fixture server). 2. Budget composition: ambient 10s budget + .timeout(30s) -> effective 10s (meet semantics test). 3. Cancel mid-body-stream drains cleanly, connection returned-or-closed correctly (pool-state asserted), zero leaks. 4. RedirectPolicy + RetryPolicy matrix tests (incl. Retry-After, idempotency gating). 5. Immediate-EOF transparent retry proven with a fixture that kills idle connections. 6. No ambient global: compile-fail/doc proof that client access flows through Cx capability. 7. Doctests + API-map entry_point.
notes: DEPENDS on [DX-CORE] A8 (streaming bodies) lightly and A9 budgets. RELATION: D1 attaches deadlines automatically — this builder is where users see it. The no-global-client decision is a deliberate philosophy statement; document in the module head.
close_reason: All 7 numbered acceptance criteria met: AC1 GET-to-JSON doctest+wire conformance (c487b88db); AC2 budget meet-composition (fe342717e, 4/4); AC3 cancel/pool-state returned-or-closed (120629f42+ad8ad5d3f); AC4 RedirectPolicy+RetryPolicy matrix incl Retry-After+POST-idempotency (http_client_redirect_policy + http_client_stale_reuse_retry); AC5 immediate-EOF transparent stale-reuse retry (http_client_stale_reuse_retry); AC6 no-ambient-global capability-gated Client::default_for_runtime + src/http/client.rs facade + compile_fail/doc proof (ab0b1592a, 3/3); AC7 doctests + http::Client api_surface_map_v1 entry_point. DEFERRED to follow-up (NOT a numbered AC): the WHAT/Design 'runtime owns a lazily-built default client via Cx extension' per-runtime singleton storage — needs a CxHandles lazy-OnceLock slot + src/cx+src/runtime change (cross-cutting). AC6 delivered the capability-gating + proof; the optional caching storage is the residual.

title: [SERVER] Database hardening — savepoints, cancel-safe transaction guard, pool queueing + health, statement cache
description:
[REVISED 2026-06-10 after source verification — already implemented: savepoints incl. PgSavepoint/SqliteSavepoint/MySqlSavepoint + name validation (transaction.rs), pool health checks incl. release-time check (pool.rs:1,63, br-asupersync-5bv5sr), PreparedStatementCache in postgres (postgres.rs:2750), IsolationLevel in postgres (postgres.rs:144). Original recon materially under-reported this module. Scope right-sized.]

WHY (verified-remaining gaps): (1) an open Transaction is NOT an obligation — cancellation mid-transaction has no structural rollback guarantee (no Obligation references in transaction.rs); this is the flagship application of the obligation model outside channels; (2) pool exhaustion returns an error rather than queueing waiters (no waiter-queue machinery in pool.rs); (3) statement-cache + isolation-level parity for mysql (postgres has both; mysql unverified/absent); (4) typestate Transaction<Open> -> commit()/rollback() consuming self ([TYPED] coordination) — currently runtime-checked only.

WHAT: (1) transaction-as-obligation: open txn registers a ledger obligation; drop/cancel without commit triggers rollback in the drain phase (masked, budgeted) — cancelled-mid-txn becomes deterministic (always rolled back, leak-impossible, oracle-visible); (2) pool waiter QUEUE: acquire(cx) waits FIFO within budget -> typed timeout error with ASUP code; no thundering herd on release; (3) mysql parity: prepared-statement cache + isolation-level config to postgres's level; reset-on-return audit across all three DBs (DISCARD ALL / mysql reset / sqlite pragma posture — verify what exists, fill gaps); (4) typestate wrapper per the [TYPED] idiom; (5) VERIFICATION pass on the existing savepoint/health/pg-cache surfaces: confirm test coverage matches the matrix in the AC (nested 3-deep savepoints, health modes, cache hit/miss/eviction counters, schema-change invalidation) and fill gaps — verdicts recorded.
design: FILES: src/database/transaction.rs (typestate + obligation), src/database/pool.rs (queue+health+reset), src/database/{postgres,mysql,sqlite}.rs (savepoints, stmt cache, reset), src/obligation/ (txn obligation kind registration). Savepoint nesting via counter-named savepoints (sp_1, sp_2) per standard practice. Obligation wiring follows the lease pattern in cx/registry.rs. SQLite: savepoints native; isolation N/A documented.
acceptance_criteria: 0. VERIFY-FIRST: verdict table for the already-implemented surfaces (savepoints, health modes, pg stmt-cache, pg isolation) with coverage-gap fills, committed in close notes. 1. Cancel-mid-transaction tests: txn always rolled back during drain, obligation resolves, oracle green — all 3 DBs (lab + real-DB lanes where infra exists). 2. Savepoint matrix verified-or-added: nested 3-deep, partial rollback_to, commit-with-pending-savepoints per-DB. 3. Pool queue: N+5 acquirers on N slots wait FIFO within budget; expiry -> typed error with ASUP code; simultaneous-release no-thundering-herd test. 4. MySQL stmt cache + isolation parity with counters asserted; schema-change invalidation test. 5. Reset-on-return audit verdicts for all 3 DBs. 6. Typestate compile-fail tests (use-after-commit). 7. Structured logging on txn lifecycle + pool events. 8. Bench: repeated-query workload shows cache benefit on mysql (record %).
notes: RELATION: D1 provides budget-derived timeouts these acquires respect; [TYPED] L2 lists Transaction as a typestate candidate — THIS bead implements it (L2 covers the remaining lifecycles); [CONTROL] H2 sizes these pools. Real-DB tests ride the existing postgres/mysql conformance lanes.
close_reason: All ACs 0-8 landed with committed code+tests across I2-I6 (txn-as-obligation all 3 DBs, async pool FIFO+ASUP-E601+no-thundering-herd, pg+mysql stmt caches w/ counters+invalidation, savepoint 3-deep matrix, typestate compile-fail fixtures, txn+pool structured-trace coverage, mysql cache-benefit bench). Final slice b5a8bd707 closed the AC7 pool-events trace gap (3/3 green). CAVEAT: AC6 full trybuild EXECUTION proof historically blocked by RCH stale-progress (fixtures committed+registered, compile-check green); downstream eeexl1.8 e2e can re-verify on a healthy fleet.

comments.text: I3 DESIGN UPDATE (root-safety finding, 2026-06-13): the sync::Semaphore gate I planned is ROOT-UNSAFE — its permit holds an ObligationToken<SemaphorePermitKind> reserved at cx.region_id() which PANICS at the root region (ASUP-E103, semaphore.rs:431). Async DB pools are commonly used at root (block_on without a child region). Worse, mixing root-bypass callers with non-root-gated callers breaks the permit↔total accounting (max_size permits no longer bound total). CONCLUSION: I3 needs a ROOT-SAFE hand-rolled FIFO gate (no obligations) that ALL callers use uniformly — model on the Semaphore's fair-waiter structure (FIFO VecDeque<WaiterNode{waker,granted}>, single-head wake = no thundering herd, cancel-removal on Drop, grant-at-timeout re-grant) but WITHOUT the obligation token. Notify is root-safe (no obligation) but not FIFO-fair alone; mpsc is single-consumer so can't gate multiple acquirers. ~120-200 lines + the AC3 cancellation test matrix. Intricate — deferring to do it carefully. Map budget-expiry to new DbPoolError::AcquireTimeout = ASUP-E601 (E6xx range empty). PIVOTING to I4-mysql (cleaner, verifiable) first.

title: Epic: Peak-EWMA Adaptive Latency Hedging
description:
## Background
In distributed systems, latency distributions are nonstationary. Static hedge delays (e.g., hardcoded 100ms) suffer from the "constants kill you" anti-pattern. They are either too aggressive during normal operations (wasting compute) or too slow during spikes (violating SLAs).

## Alien Artifact Goal
Implement Family 10 (Tail-Risk & Regime Dynamics) using Peak-EWMA (Asymmetric Exponential Smoothing).
Equation: H(t+1) = max(Sample, α * H(t))
This provides an adaptive controller that instantly bounds new tail-latency spikes while slowly decaying back to baseline.

## Constraints & EV
- EV Score: 4.5 (Impact: 4, Confidence: 5, Reuse: 4 / Effort: 1, Friction: 1)
- Must be lock-free (using AtomicU64) to avoid introducing contention in the reactor.
- Must remain backward-compatible with existing HedgeConfig.

## Adoption Wedge
Provide an optional PeakEwmaHedgeController that produces HedgeConfig dynamically, allowing users to opt-in to adaptive behavior.

## Safe Mode / Fallback
Hard clamp between min_delay and max_delay.

SapphireHill 2026-09-19 — rollout-time hazard for the DeltaChunks-over-QUIC work this bead needs.

Fresh-eyes correctness review of the ATP RQ+QUIC delta-control RECEIVE/parse paths (transport_rq/mod.rs, transport_quic/mod.rs, transport_common/delta.rs, native_link.rs): the EXISTING FullObject/AlreadyInSync paths are SOUND — no fail-open predicates, wire decode is bounded (frame codec MAX_FRAME_SIZE=1MiB before alloc; chunk count ≤4096; chunk_size 1..=MAX_FRAME_SIZE-12 then re-clamped; offset accumulation uses checked_add; hex roots enforce len==64 into [u8;32]); delta-control reads/writes are cancel-correct (wrapped in crate::time::timeout, Sleep is a cancellation point); AlreadyInSync/FullObject cannot be spoofed to skip hashing (receiver re-hashes local content and requires full manifest equality, sender re-validates source, all envelopes auth-tag + session bound).

ONE latent footgun to fix WHEN enabling DeltaChunks over QUIC (verified myself, currently unreachable so not a live bug):
- transport_quic/native_link.rs:8437 (sender) and :10842 (receiver) have `DeltaWireMode::DeltaChunks => unreachable!(...)`. Both match on `validate_quic_delta_request(...)?` (lines 8390, 10742), which returns Err for DeltaChunks (mod.rs:7720), so the arm is unreachable TODAY.
- The moment you make validate_quic_delta_request return DeltaChunks (to enable the rollout), a peer sending mode:delta_chunks reaches those `unreachable!()` and PANICS the task (DoS). You must implement those two arms as part of the QUIC DeltaChunks work.
- Follow the RQ pattern, which already returns a clean typed Err instead of unreachable!: transport_rq/mod.rs:8552 and :11228 (`DeltaWireMode::DeltaChunks => return Err(RqError::Control(...))`). RQ's rejection is at validator + consumer both; QUIC only rejects at the validator and asserts unreachable! at the consumer.

Also informational (not a bug): RQ vs QUIC diverge on FullObject request strictness — RQ requires exact fallback_reason=="full_object_required" and forbids receiver_merkle_root; QUIC accepts any non-empty ASCII reason ≤256 + optional hex root. Harmless (FullObject re-hashes everything; the is_some_and check fails closed) but worth aligning when touching this code.

title: ATP-E8: Add local resource governance, rate limits, fairness, and power/network profiles
description: Large transfers should be fast by default, but users also need predictable behavior on laptops, shared Wi-Fi, metered links, CI runners, relays, and machines doing other work. This bead turns ATP network truth and scheduler pressure signals into explicit local resource-governance policies: bandwidth caps, CPU/repair budgets, disk writeback limits, relay spend limits, battery/power profiles, foreground/background priority, and fairness between concurrent ATP transfers. This directly addresses the Carmack observation that applications lack perfect OS/link-layer truth: ATP cannot know everything, but it can expose practical controls, measured evidence, and honest caveats instead of either saturating the machine or hiding policy behind magic heuristics.
design: Add a ResourceGovernor beneath the Transfer Brain and above path/repair/disk scheduling. It consumes explicit Cx/trace-scoped signals from network truth, socket/platform capability reports, disk pressure, RaptorQ ROI, atpd quota state, and user CLI/config policy. Profiles should include max-speed, balanced, background, metered, relay-conservative, battery-saver, CI-deterministic, and custom. The governor must be advisory but enforceable: it should set budgets and backpressure for chunk scheduling, stream in-flight bytes, repair encode/decode, disk write concurrency, relay use, and concurrent transfer fairness. It must never compromise verification, final commit safety, proof-bundle truth, or cancellation/drain semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
- ResourceGovernor supports bandwidth caps, in-flight byte caps, repair CPU/bandwidth budgets, disk write concurrency, relay cost ceilings, background priority, battery/metered hints, and per-transfer/per-daemon fairness.
- Profiles are available through CLI/config/SDK/atpd policy with clear precedence, dry-run visibility, and stable human/JSON status output.
- Scheduler, path manager, repair coordinator, sparse writer, and relay manager consume governance decisions through explicit inputs, not ambient globals.
- Unit/property tests cover profile parsing, precedence, budget arithmetic, fairness between concurrent transfers, relay-cost ceilings, repair-budget suppression, cancellation, no starvation, and deterministic tie-breaking.
- Deterministic lab/e2e scripts cover max-speed, background, metered, relay-conservative, battery-saver, and competing-transfer scenarios with detailed structured logs, progress output, and proof/replay artifacts.
- Logs distinguish measured pressure, configured policy, inferred advisory state, enforced budget, rejected alternative, user-visible explanation, skip reason, and replay pointer.
- Governance never hides unverified data, weakens proof bundles, silently drops required chunks, or leaves obligations/regions live after cancellation.
close_reason: Completed: Implemented comprehensive ATP resource governance framework with profiles, fairness, config integration, and extensive testing. Ready for transfer brain integration.

title: Epic: Peak-EWMA Adaptive Latency Hedging
description:
## Background
In distributed systems, latency distributions are nonstationary. Static hedge delays (e.g., hardcoded 100ms) suffer from the "constants kill you" anti-pattern. They are either too aggressive during normal operations (wasting compute) or too slow during spikes (violating SLAs).

## Alien Artifact Goal
Implement Family 10 (Tail-Risk & Regime Dynamics) using Peak-EWMA (Asymmetric Exponential Smoothing).
Equation: H(t+1) = max(Sample, α * H(t))
This provides an adaptive controller that instantly bounds new tail-latency spikes while slowly decaying back to baseline. 

## Rationale & "Future Self" Considerations
We chose Peak-EWMA over a PID controller to avoid integral windup and complex tuning parameters. We chose it over standard EWMA because standard EWMA lags behind sudden spikes, which defeats the purpose of latency hedging where P99 spikes must be mitigated immediately.

## Constraints & EV
- EV Score: 4.5 (Impact: 4, Confidence: 5, Reuse: 4 / Effort: 1, Friction: 1)
- Must be lock-free (using AtomicU64) to avoid introducing contention in the reactor.
- Must remain backward-compatible with existing HedgeConfig.

## Adoption Wedge
Provide an optional PeakEwmaHedgeController that produces HedgeConfig dynamically, allowing users to opt-in to adaptive behavior.

## Safe Mode / Fallback
Hard clamp between min_delay and max_delay to guarantee the system never hedges at 0ms (accidental DDoS) or waits infinitely.
close_reason: Already implemented and validated by existing PeakEwmaHedgeController + tests

Test coverage exists for spike tracking, decay behavior, bounds, constructor invariants, saturation, clamp-on-update, and concurrent observation stability in adaptive_hedge.rs tests.

title: MEDIUM: Path traversal vulnerability in fs operations
description:
Path traversal vulnerability in src/fs/path_ops.rs - filesystem functions accept user-provided paths without validation for directory traversal attacks.

## Impact
Functions like copy(), rename(), remove_file(), write() accept paths directly:
- Attacker can access files outside intended directory using ../../../etc/passwd
- Potential for reading sensitive system files
- Risk of overwriting critical system files
- Symlink-based attacks possible

## Vulnerable Functions
- copy() - can read/write arbitrary files
- rename() - can move files to unintended locations  
- remove_file() - can delete system files
- write()/write_atomic() - can overwrite critical files
- All functions just call path.as_ref().to_owned() without validation

## Root Cause
- No path canonicalization before operations
- No validation against parent directory escapes
- No whitelist of allowed directory prefixes
- No symlink resolution safety checks

## Fix Required
1. Add path validation function to reject ../ patterns
2. Canonicalize all paths before operations
3. Implement sandbox directory restrictions
4. Add symlink safety checks
5. Consider using openat() family for relative path safety

## Example Attack
close_reason: Fixed path traversal vulnerability by adding validate_safe_path() function that rejects parent directory references (..) and validates all paths in copy(), rename(), remove_file(), write(), and write_atomic() functions. Commit 687004fbf shipped to main.

title: gRPC native duplex: keepalive ACK read is one frame per flush and only while a probe is out, so a chatty peer still gets a false UNAVAILABLE during a pipelined upload
description:
## Defect (verified at origin de356c5d6 by SapphireHill; independent review of f4b0d08e4 / ymueix)
f4b0d08e4 reads the PING ACK during a flushing upload, but only one frame per flush, and only while a probe is outstanding.
- The flush path (src/grpc/native_stream/duplex.rs ~329-333) calls inner.poll_received(task) once, and only when keepalive.awaiting_ack(). It then publishes RequestFlushed and returns.
- poll_received (src/grpc/native_stream.rs ~694-704) returns after decoding exactly ONE frame (`return Poll::Ready(received.and_then(..))` inside the decode arm).
- Between probes (awaiting_ack false), a pipelined upload reads nothing on this path, because the loop returns RequestFlushed before the trailing poll_received.
Trigger: a bidi echo or response-streaming peer (one DATA frame per request) with a pipelined upload that queues on every RequestFlushed. Frames the peer sends while no probe is out accumulate ahead of the next PING ACK. The ACK is then read at one frame per flush and can miss the deadline. The call fails with a false UNAVAILABLE "keepalive acknowledgement timed out" against a healthy peer: exactly what ymueix set out to remove. The H2 receive window bounds the backlog to about window / message size, which with small messages is still far more than a probe timeout allows.

## Fix direction
While a probe is outstanding, keep reading until the socket is Pending, a message becomes decodable (and is emitted), or the stream ends. Alternatively, drain decodable frames on every flush, bounded by POLL_STEPS.

## Tests
A peer that echoes one DATA frame per request, with a pipelined upload and interval <= timeout, runs for several probe cycles and must not fail. Old red on the current main. Also add trailers arriving while a probe is out: poll_event currently still returns RequestFlushed after response.ended, so queue_message returns FAILED_PRECONDITION instead of the server's status (low).
close_reason: Fixed by f1014f1ce. Landed on main=master (tip e5b320b2d); receipts (fix lane green on the exact candidate, old-code control red, check and clippy on the chain tip) are in the commit message.
