title: ATP-H7: Implement receive-side safety preflight, destination policy, consent, and quarantine
description: ATP should be safe to leave running. A peer should not be able to fill a disk, overwrite important files, sneak path traversal or symlink effects into a destination, materialize executables unexpectedly, or force a receiver into ambiguous partial state. This bead makes receive-side safety a first-class product feature rather than scattered checks across atpd, grants, object graphs, disk writing, and CLI prompts. The default receiver posture should be conservative: explicit grants, visible object graph summary, free-space and quota preflight, destination policy, quarantine before final commit, and auditable consent or policy-based auto-accept.
design: Add a receive-side safety layer between session/grant acceptance, preflight planning, object graph interpretation, and disk/journal commit. It should produce a ReceivePlan that states: sender identity, manifest root, object graph summary, destination root, free-space/quota estimate, destructive actions, executable/symlink/device/special-file policy, metadata policy, quarantine path, commit policy, consent source, and rollback/resume behavior. Interactive CLI may prompt; atpd must also support non-interactive policies such as deny-by-default, allow-listed peers, auto-accept under quota, mailbox-only, and quarantine-only. The layer must be deterministic, logged, and replayable; it must never depend on ambient process cwd or hidden OS state without platform capability evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
- ReceivePlan covers sender identity, grant/capability scope, manifest root, object graph summary, destination root, expected bytes, free-space/quota result, overwrite/delete/rename actions, symlink/executable/special-file policy, metadata policy, quarantine path, final commit policy, consent source, and rollback/resume behavior.
- Default receive policy is deny or quarantine unless an explicit grant, CLI confirmation, or atpd allow rule authorizes destination, object class, size/quota, destructive actions, and metadata effects.
- Path traversal, absolute paths, platform-reserved names, case collisions, symlink escapes, hard-link/device/special-file surprises, executable-bit surprises, overwrite attempts, disk-full risk, and quota exhaustion fail closed before final commit.
- Unit/property tests cover ReceivePlan construction, policy precedence, path normalization, case-insensitive conflicts, symlink escape, overwrite refusal, quota/free-space arithmetic, consent token replay, cancellation, quarantine recovery, and stable human/JSON output.
- E2e scripts cover interactive receive approval, non-interactive atpd allow rule, denied transfer, quarantine-only receive, explicit overwrite, disk-full simulation, symlink attack, mailbox receive, relay receive, daemon restart/resume, detailed logs, proof bundle, and replay artifact.
- Logs/proof artifacts include sender peer id, grant id, destination policy id, ReceivePlan digest, user/daemon consent source, rejected action reason, quarantine/final path state, rollback decision, Cx trace id, and replay pointer.
- The feature integrates with CLI dry-run/status/doctor so users can understand what will happen before accepting large or potentially destructive transfers.
close_reason: Completed: ATP receive-side safety preflight with CLI integration, E2e scenarios, and comprehensive test coverage

title: [pending-leak] cx/registry.rs: NamePermit::abort() enables pending-entry leak
description:
File: src/cx/registry.rs:342
Bug: NamePermit::abort() is public and permits callers to abort the obligation token without removing the pending registry entry. If a caller calls permit.abort() and forgets to call registry.cancel_permit(&permit), the pending entry for the name remains in self.pending forever, blocking future registrations and reservations of that name. The documentation (line 865-866) states 'The caller must also call NamePermit::abort on the permit itself to resolve the obligation' but does not warn about the pending entry remaining if cancel_permit is skipped.

Attack: Task A calls registry.reserve(name) → gets permit. Task A calls permit.abort(). Task A forgets cancel_permit(). Pending entry leaks. Task B cannot reserve/register the name anymore, causing DoS.

Fix: Either make NamePermit::abort() private and add a registry.abort_permit() method that handles both obligation abort and pending entry removal, OR emit a warning in the docstring.
close_reason: Fixed: NamePermit::abort is pub(crate); public surface is NameRegistry::abort_permit (atomic cancel + resolve) (commit 543ae4dfa)

title: spawn_local must reject foreign-runtime Cx on another runtime worker
description: Cx::spawn_local currently gates only on current_worker_id(). A Cx retained from runtime A can therefore be called while polling on runtime B worker; the request is parked on B thread-local lane, while its gateway, pending credit, cancellation path, region id, and parent capability state belong to A. Worker IDs and region IDs are runtime-local and can collide, so B may admit and run the task under the wrong runtime instead of failing closed. Evidence: src/cx/cx.rs spawn_local_via_lane checks only current_worker_id and enqueue_local_spawn is process-thread TLS; src/runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs drains that TLS into the current worker state. Fix must be backward-compatible and fail closed before reservation/enqueue unless the current worker runtime owns the Cx gateway. Add a native two-runtime regression using public RuntimeBuilder/RuntimeHandle/Cx APIs; prove the foreign-runtime call is rejected, no future is polled, no pending reservation leaks, and same-runtime spawn_local still works. Preserve v0.4.3 API.
acceptance_criteria: Native two-runtime old-red/new-green regression proves a runtime-A Cx used on a runtime-B worker is rejected before local admission; the foreign future is never polled; both runtimes shut down cleanly without pending spawn/task leaks; existing same-runtime spawn_local behavior remains green; focused RCH lane and UBS on changed files pass.
notes: Confirmed and repaired three runtime-ownership defects without public API change: (1) Cx::spawn_local accepted a retained runtime-A Cx while polling runtime B; (2) nested runtime-B block_on on runtime-A worker could publish into A local-spawn TLS; (3) raw scheduler fast/local-ready/cancel TLS paths accepted colliding foreign-runtime TaskIds. Repairs bind local-spawn TLS to the runtime-unique SpawnMailbox Arc and gate scheduler TLS queues by backing-state Arc identity. Permanent native/public and scheduler tests cover both runtime crossings, non-polling/no-leak behavior, and owner fail-closed cleanup. Exact old-red evidence: nested spawn-local RCH exit 101; scheduler fast/local-ready base old run 2 failures; cancel-lane base 062ad0ae305ba33e4fe6d8861dd0b0fd5e545882 on vmi1227854 job 29981392402120709 ran 1 and failed because foreign runtime TLS was accepted. Exact current evidence: spawn-local integration 14/14 and unit 6/6 green; scheduler fast/local-ready 2/2 green; cancel-lane base c2c896520591c6ebe17c9d635b43bf36ad010a67 on ovh-a job 29981392402120710 ran 1 and passed with expected diagnostic plus retryable wake-state assertion. Focused Clippy with -D warnings passed on vmi1264463 job 29981392402120708. cargo fmt --all -- --check and git diff --check passed. Bounded adjacent review found no additional confirmed owner-routing defect; captured local waker already carries exact owner queues. title: Runtime spawn-vs-drop race: raced Cx::spawn during runtime drop returns Ok but hangs TaskHandle forever
description:
Audit of commit e035e2128 (fail cx spawn after runtime drop). The sequential drop-then-spawn case now fails closed correctly, but a CONCURRENT spawn racing runtime drop is still unsafe.

Root cause (src/runtime/spawn_mailbox.rs:845-852 enqueue_and_notify + builder.rs:3821 _spawn_liveness + builder.rs:4213-4232 Drop for RuntimeInner): the liveness token Arc<()> is a plain field, so it drops only AFTER Drop::drop has already run scheduler.shutdown() and joined all workers. ThreeLaneScheduler::shutdown just sets a flag + wakes workers; run_loop exits with NO final mailbox drain, and RuntimeInner::drop never drains spawn_mailbox. So any Cx::spawn that passes the is_runtime_available() check during the whole drop window enqueues into a mailbox no consumer will ever drain. With a retained Cx the chain stays alive forever: the returned Ok(TaskHandle) never resolves (permanent join hang) and the PendingSpawnCounter reservation is held indefinitely. The e035e2128 regression test only covers sequential ordering.

Proposed fix: (1) store the token as Option<Arc<()>> and drop it FIRST in RuntimeInner::drop; (2) producer holds the upgraded Arc ACROSS the enqueue (liveness_guard() -> Option<Arc<()>> instead of a boolean probe); (3) after joining workers, spin until Weak::strong_count()==0 then drain the mailbox, calling resolve_failed(SpawnError::RuntimeUnavailable) on every leftover. Invariant becomes 'upgrade succeeded => a final drain observes my request'. Also align spawn_local_via_lane (cx.rs:3693) which has NO liveness check at all. (Deferred: Drop-order change is subtle; do under focused session with loom/stress coverage.)

=== VERIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (SnowyFortress 2026-06-14, code-confirmed; correctness reasoned, NOT yet loom/stress-verified) ===
Confirmed against current code. Exact changes:

1) src/runtime/spawn_mailbox.rs enqueue_and_notify (now ~845): replace the boolean is_runtime_available() probe with a HELD guard:
   let Some(_liveness_guard) = self.runtime_liveness.upgrade() else { request.into_parts().resolve_failed(SpawnError::RuntimeUnavailable); return Err(SpawnError::RuntimeUnavailable); };
   ...existing clock + self.mailbox.enqueue(request, now) + (self.notify)(); Ok(())...
   _liveness_guard (Arc<()>) MUST stay in scope across enqueue+notify so the request is visible before the strong ref drops.

2) src/runtime/builder.rs:3825 field: _spawn_liveness: Option<Arc<()>>; construction (~4036): Some(spawn_liveness).

3) src/runtime/builder.rs Drop for RuntimeInner (~4217): BEFORE scheduler.shutdown(), take the token, downgrade to a Weak, drop the strong ref (so racing upgrades fail closed):
   let liveness_weak = self._spawn_liveness.take().map(|t| { let w = Arc::downgrade(&t); drop(t); w });
   ...existing shutdown + blocking_pool + join workers (scope the worker_threads lock)...
   then: if let (Some(w), Some(mb)) = (liveness_weak, self.spawn_mailbox.as_ref()) { while w.strong_count() > 0 { std::thread::yield_now(); } while let Some(req) = mb.dequeue() { req.into_parts().resolve_failed(SpawnError::RuntimeUnavailable); } }

4) src/cx/cx.rs spawn_local_via_lane (~3693): add the missing is_runtime_available()/liveness guard (currently NONE). NOTE: cx.rs is frequently peer-active — coordinate.

CORRECTNESS: Arc::upgrade is atomic and never resurrects a 0-count Arc, so (a) a producer that upgraded before the token drop holds a strong ref => Drop's strong_count spin waits for its enqueue to become visible, then drains+fails it; (b) a producer that upgrades after the drop fails closed. No hang, reservation released via resolve_failed.

REMAINING (focused-session): write a stress test (retained Cx; one thread spawning in a tight loop while main drops the runtime; assert every TaskHandle resolves to RuntimeUnavailable within a timeout — a hang = bug) and ideally loom coverage of the upgrade-vs-drop interleavings, then verify the runtime suite is green before commit. Do NOT land on the core teardown path without that verification.

title: net: owned TcpStream/UnixStream split halves keep stale direction-waker, causing union-interest rearm busy-loop under backpressure
description: src/net/tcp/split.rs:296-309 registration_interest, :378-404 (wakers only ever set), :506-529 clear only on half-drop; identical in src/net/unix/split.rs:201-209,383+. read_waker/write_waker are set on first Pending per direction and never cleared until drop; the shared registration re-arms with the union of has-a-waker directions. Bidirectional-proxy backpressure: task A owns read half (read once => read_waker Some forever), task B owns write half; peer keeps sending => socket level-readable; B's write WouldBlock => rearm(READABLE|WRITABLE) => epoll Oneshot is level-triggered so the readable event fires immediately => wakes A (spurious) and B => B re-polls, WouldBlock, rearm => hot loop (poller + 2 tasks) until reader drains. Single-owner TcpStream::register_interest (stream.rs:607) was already narrowed to only the caller's interest for exactly this class; split re-introduced it. FIX: clear the direction waker when its event is delivered / before returning Ready from that direction, or track currently-waiting not ever-waited. Found by fresh-eyes reactor/net review 2026-07-14 (CONFIRMED).

title: sqlite: hard-dropped begin() future leaks an untracked open transaction (silent data loss + write-lock starvation)
description: src/database/sqlite.rs:1974-2009 begin()/begin_immediate() set NeedsRollback only in the Outcome::Cancelled arm. A HARD drop (timeout(d, conn.begin(cx)) expiring, or a select!/race! loser — the class 87d2bd9ac fixed for pool.rs) drops the future at .await before any arm runs, so transaction_state stays Autocommit. BlockingTaskHandle has no Drop-cancel (blocking_pool.rs:439) so the queued BEGIN still executes and opens a real txn. drain_orphaned_transaction is gated on NeedsRollback and never fires. Every later execute() returns Ok but runs inside the leaked txn; on close/rollback those writes are silently discarded, and meanwhile the conn holds the write lock (SQLITE_BUSY for peers). FIX: cross-check is_autocommit() on the next op regardless of mirror state, or give BlockingTaskHandle a drop-cancel. Found by fresh-eyes db review 2026-07-14 (CONFIRMED, residual hole in c73ceba22).

comments.author: BronzeHill
comments.text:
Implemented the managed SQLite hard-drop fix in src/database/sqlite.rs (SHA-256 9320cf78c92059ded603f3a0a01fa0f4a3a2b63603ad311fda7c1cfcef42c091; +745/-101; rustfmt and git diff --check clean).

Root cause: begin* poisoning lived after the await, so a hard-dropped future could leave its blocking worker free to open a physical transaction while the mirror stayed Autocommit. The fix coordinates async ownership and the worker through a shared BEGIN lifecycle plus a per-connection transaction generation. Abandoned BEGIN workers either roll back while serialized on the connection or poison the mirror for next-operation cleanup. Managed COMMIT/ROLLBACK effects validate their captured generation, so stale jobs cannot finish a replacement transaction. Terminal effects advance the generation; exhaustion fails closed before issuing BEGIN SQL.

Regression coverage: hard drops for BEGIN/IMMEDIATE/EXCLUSIVE with cleanup overtaking; hard drop after worker completion with a lagging COMMIT; real two-worker stale COMMIT and ROLLBACK overtaken by cleanup plus a replacement transaction; generation exhaustion without SQL. The private-worker barrier test is unwind-safe via an exactly-once release guard.

title: SQLite/pool audit (r10): a dropped begin_immediate keeps the write lock; dropped one-shot queries keep running; a panicking disconnect leaks pool capacity; LOWs
description:
Read-only audit of src/database/sqlite.rs, src/database/pool.rs and src/database/transaction.rs at origin/main b94da3ea9, re-checked unchanged at d6208c454 (SapphireHill audit agent round 10, 10-07). Report: /data/tmp/rc_20260923/audit_r10_sqlite_pool.md. No HIGH. Mixed-clock lead refuted: cx.now() and wall_now() share the process clock in production.

## MEDIUM
M1. A begin_immediate / begin_exclusive future dropped after its worker ran BEGIN only marks the connection for rollback (sqlite.rs ~197-204, ~508-512): the RESERVED/EXCLUSIVE lock stays held until that connection's next operation, so every other writer gets SQLITE_BUSY. timeout() triggers it naturally (a deadline that passes after BEGIN completed returns Elapsed without collecting the transaction). Fix: schedule the same rollback a dropped transaction gets. The existing test hard_dropped_begin_after_worker_completion_survives_lagging_commit must be updated with the fix (it would become racy).
M2. A one-shot query/execute dropped (lost timeout() or select!) neither interrupts nor cancels its blocking job (sqlite.rs ~2778-2968): a runaway statement keeps the connection and a pool thread until it finishes. Row streams already interrupt on drop.
M3. (OWNER, overlaps gq84an/pj1q40 held by CopperOak) All SQLite connections share one 4-thread blocking pool and each job holds a thread while waiting for its connection: one busy connection or a lock convoy stalls every SQLite operation in the process and surfaces as spurious SQLITE_BUSY. Changing the pinned "a queued cancel waits for its job" behaviour is a decision.
M4. (91hka0 item 12, never landed) When the manager's disconnect panics, the pool catches the panic but still counts the connection (pool.rs ~574-590, ~1435-1439, ~1531-1533, ~1618-1626, ~3263-3282), also leaking the per-client quota; after enough panics the pool reports Full / AcquireTimeout forever.

## LOW
L1. A begin() cancelled before its BEGIN was even submitted still marks the connection for rollback (sqlite.rs ~201); the next operation rolls back a raw transaction the caller opened with execute_unchecked("BEGIN").
L2. (91hka0 item 12) Sync get_with_retry_for_client sleeps 100 ms before its first attempt on every call (pool.rs ~1260-1310).
L3. In the async pool a waiter handed a stale or invalid idle connection loses its FIFO place and its acquire deadline restarts on each re-wait (pool.rs ~2294, ~2417-2551), so an acquire can exceed connection_timeout.
L4. When commit is refused (cancelled Cx) or fails, the three transaction helpers return while the rollback is only scheduled or deferred (transaction.rs ~279, ~522, ~571, ~806): the commit-path leftover of 91hka0 item 10.
L5. (OWNER) The legacy is_busy/is_locked checks match substrings of the error message (sqlite.rs ~1213-1229).
L6. (OWNER, new API) A pool of SQLite connections cannot detect an open transaction on return.
L7. (OWNER, new API) AsyncDbPool has no evict_stale or warm_up, and its unhealthy-drop path does not count discards.

Overlaps: 91hka0 (closed; item 12 never landed), x043bj, s8spmh, gq84an/pj1q40 (CopperOak, in progress; M3).

title: BrowserStorage aliases ill-formed UTF-16 keys and namespaces
description: BrowserStorage encodes namespaces and keys with TextEncoder after only trim/empty validation. The Encoding Standard converts every lone UTF-16 surrogate to U+FFFD, so distinct JavaScript strings such as U+D800, U+D801, U+DC00, and literal U+FFFD all map to bytes EF BF BD and base64url 77-9. Both IndexedDB and localStorage therefore permit cross-alias reads, overwrites, deletes, listing, and bulk namespace clearing within the same backend. Example: set namespace tenant-U+D800 and key k, then get or clear through namespace tenant-U+FFFD; likewise a key written with U+D800 is readable/deletable through U+FFFD. Current canonical IndexedDB decoding does not catch this because U+FFFD has valid canonical UTF-8. No cross-origin or remote-input path is claimed, but namespace isolation and data integrity are violated. Fix fail closed before any backend I/O: add an ES2020-compatible UTF-16 well-formedness checker, call it from namespace/key normalization and as an encoder backstop, reject unmatched high/low surrogates with TypeError, accept valid surrogate pairs and literal U+FFFD, and do not attempt ambiguous v1 migration. Extend the existing dedicated-worker IndexedDB fixture to prove lone-surrogate keys cannot overwrite a U+FFFD sentinel, lone-surrogate namespace clear cannot delete the U+FFFD namespace, raw key count is unchanged, and a valid emoji pair round-trips. Pin source and fixture/checker markers in the existing Rust contract. Add localStorage coverage if an existing no-package-manager harness can exercise the shared validation path.

title: [security] AuthenticatedSymbol::new_verified reachable via TypedEncoder zero-tag placeholders — downstream skip-verify accepts forged
description:
src/types/typed_symbol.rs:630, 925, 1204 — three encode paths still construct AuthenticatedSymbol::new_verified(symbol, AuthenticationTag::zero()) as a placeholder waiting for 'a larger refactor — wire a key into TypedEncoder via a Cx-rooted capability'. The closed asupersync-usr4ax (commit 42c0052fc) added a fail-closed check in AuthenticationTag::verify() so a verify() call against a zero-tagged AuthenticatedSymbol returns false. But three problems remain:

  1. AuthenticatedSymbol::new_verified bypasses the verify path entirely — the resulting symbol has verified=true at the type level, NOT because verification succeeded.
  2. Any downstream consumer that trusts the verified=true flag without re-running verify() will accept the zero-tag symbol as authenticated.
  3. The fix interacts badly with the OPEN bead asupersync-f4mdcr (DecodingPipeline silently skips auth when verify_auth=false): such a pipeline never re-verifies, so it accepts the placeholder unchecked.

Fix direction: (a) make AuthenticatedSymbol::new_verified fully private (remove pub(crate); confine to the authenticated.rs test module); (b) require ALL production code to call AuthenticatedSymbol::compute(key, symbol) — a constructor that derives the key from a Cx-rooted capability and computes a real tag; (c) update typed_symbol.rs encode paths at lines 630/925/1204 to take a Cx parameter and call compute() instead of new_verified+zero(). This is the 'larger refactor' the existing comments anticipate.

title: StreamingSse H1 accounting commits before body-channel send

title: SSE: heartbeat_chunk lacks the closed guard (cancels a finished request Cx) and counts keep-alives against max_total_bytes
description: src/web/sse.rs:546-550 heartbeat_chunk has no self.closed guard (next_chunk at :519 does). After the source completes (finish() sets closed=true), a heartbeat still serializes and writes to the finished body channel => HttpError::BodyChannelClosed => send_h1_bytes(:613) calls cancel_for_disconnect => sets cancel_requested on a cleanly-COMPLETED request Cx (indistinguishable from a real disconnect), poisoning connection-reuse/audit/obligation/disconnect-metric decisions and over-counting bytes. FIX: guard heartbeat_chunk on self.closed (mirror next_chunk) and stop the driver emitting heartbeats after next_chunk returned None. Separately (#6): server-authored keep-alive heartbeats are charged against max_total_bytes (default 16MiB), so a 1s heartbeat with no events tears down a healthy long-lived StreamingSse after ~2.7 days with TotalBytesExceeded — exclude heartbeat bytes from the attacker-payload cap. Found by fresh-eyes http review 2026-07-14 (CONFIRMED).
close_reason: Fixed 3913ddd89 (#5, the serious bug): send_h1_heartbeat + heartbeat_chunk now guard on self.closed so a post-completion heartbeat never writes to the finished body channel and wrongly cancels a completed request Cx. #6 (heartbeat vs max_total_bytes cap) split to asupersync-sse-heartbeat-total-bytes-cap-75hkpo (needs a two-counter design to preserve the total_bytes reporting contract). rch web::sse tests green.

title: SSE: server keep-alive heartbeats count against max_total_bytes, tearing down healthy long-lived streams (~2.7d)
description: src/web/sse.rs heartbeat_chunk -> serialize_event charges max_total_bytes (default 16MiB), so a 1s keep-alive with no events hits TotalBytesExceeded after ~1.29M ticks (~2.7 days) and tears down a healthy StreamingSse. The cap is meant to bound client-visible EVENT volume, not server-authored transport keep-alives. Clean fix = two counters: keep bytes_emitted as the reported transport total (events + heartbeats, for Sent.total_bytes), add event_bytes for the cap check (events only). serialize_event increments both + caps on event_bytes; heartbeats increment bytes_emitted only via serialize_event_uncharged (already extracted). The naive 'uncharged heartbeat' fix broke streaming_sse_h1_transport_sends_heartbeat_comment which asserts heartbeat total_bytes==heartbeat_len, so the two-counter split is required. Split off from sse-heartbeat-guards-d2iwxs (whose #5 closed-guard fix landed). SapphireHill 2026-07-14.
close_reason: shipped at 491e229a3; added tests green in pristine-HEAD lib run b5dd9f8aa (independent verification, SapphireHill 2026-09-02)

title: [ALIEN][PLAN] Semantics spec: trace-equivalence + side-condition schema
description:
## Purpose

Define what it means for two Plan IR programs to be "the same" in Asupersync, and define the schema that makes rewrite rules checkable.

This is the foundation for:
- e-graph search (we can only merge nodes if we know the equivalence notion)
- certificates + verifier (what exactly is being certified?)
- lab equivalence oracle (how we test equivalence deterministically)

## Equivalence notion (independence-aware, not schedule-identical)

We target observational equivalence up to the runtime's trace semantics.

Two plans P and Q are equivalent if, under the same deterministic lab configuration (seed, policies, budgets):
- they produce the same terminal Outcome (including CancelReason / severity lattice position)
- they satisfy the same safety invariants (no obligation leaks, region close => quiescence, losers drained)
- their executions are equivalent up to allowed commutations of independent events (Mazurkiewicz / trace-monoid equivalence)

We do NOT require identical step-by-step schedules.

Operationally, the lab equivalence oracle will compare:
- canonicalized trace fingerprints (Foata / independence-normalized)
- plus explicit observable state projections (obligation ledger summaries, region tree quiescence)

## Allowed law families (rewrite preconditions)

Every rewrite rule must declare which laws it relies on, in machine-checkable form.

- algebraic laws for combinators (examples):
  - monoid: associativity of join, identity elements
  - semiring-like: distributivity or absorption, if applicable

- concurrency / trace laws:
  - commutation only when independence is proven
  - loser-drain laws for race

- cancellation protocol laws:
  - request -> drain -> finalize (idempotent)
  - masking rules (where cancellation can/cannot be observed)

- obligation laws:
  - linearity: permits/acks/leases must be resolved
  - no implicit drops

- budget laws:
  - meet/propagation laws for Budget semiring
  - deadline safety: rewrites must not weaken deadlines or increase required poll quota beyond declared bound

## Side-condition schema (what the analysis must prove)

Each rewrite step must carry a side-condition object that can be checked by a small verifier:
- independence conditions for commutations
- obligation-flow safety conditions (no new leak paths)
- cancellation safety conditions (loser drain preserved, cancel responsiveness not worsened beyond bound)
- budget monotonicity conditions
- determinism conditions (no iteration-order dependence introduced)

## Certificate/verifier contract (ties into bd-2jck)

A certificate is a sequence of rewrite steps plus their side conditions, with stable hashing.

The verifier must:
- validate each step matches a known rule schema
- validate all referenced side conditions (via analysis summaries or explicit witnesses)
- validate deterministic hashing / ordering constraints

## Acceptance criteria

- Provides an unambiguous equivalence target for tests and certificates.
- Enumerates law families and side-condition schema explicitly.
- Defines what data the verifier needs and what the lab oracle must compare.
close_reason: Added trace-equivalence + side-condition schema to formal semantics docs

title: [STABLE] Stable-Rust compatibility track — audit and gate nightly features so the crate builds on stable
description:
WHY: recon identified the nightly toolchain pin as an absolute adoption blocker for a large class of users and CI environments. The known hard dependency is the Try-trait impl on Outcome (#![feature(try_trait_v2)], try_trait_v2_residual) which has no stabilization timeline; portable_simd is already opt-in via simd-intrinsics. Edition 2024 itself is stable. What has never been done is a precise audit of exactly which nightly features the default feature set actually requires, and a gating plan that preserves ergonomics on nightly while admitting stable users.

CHILD TASKS: (1) nightly-feature audit — enumerate every #![feature(...)] and nightly-only dependency in the default + common feature graphs, classify each as gateable / replaceable / hard-blocker, and produce a decision record; (2) implement the gating — `nightly` cargo feature carrying the Try impl and any other sugar, stable-compatible alternatives documented (Outcome::branch()-free combinators, into_result()), plus a stable CI lane (cargo +stable check/clippy/test on the supported feature subset) wired into the proof-lane manifest so the claim "builds on stable" becomes a checked artifact, not prose.

DISCIPLINE: zero ergonomics regression for nightly users; stable lane failures block merges only for the audited subset; README/AGENTS feature tables updated truthfully (no blanket "works on stable" claim until the lane is green).

SUCCESS METRIC: `cargo +stable check -p asupersync --no-default-features --features <audited-stable-set>` passes in CI with a committed proof-lane row.

title: [STABLE] Nightly-feature audit — enumerate, classify, and decide every nightly dependency
description:
WHY: 'requires nightly' is a hard adoption wall (CI policies, enterprise toolchains, MSRV-conscious users) — recon ranked it the #1 unfixable-looking blocker, but nobody has actually MEASURED how unfixable it is. Known: try_trait_v2/try_trait_v2_residual power Outcome's ? operator (no stabilization timeline); portable_simd is opt-in already; Edition 2024 is stable. Unknown: the full feature inventory across the workspace + feature graphs.

WHAT: a decision-record audit: (1) enumerate every #![feature(...)] in every workspace crate + any nightly-only dependency behavior, mapped to the feature flags that activate it (default vs optional); (2) classify each: GATEABLE (nightly-only sugar with a stable fallback path), REPLACEABLE (stable alternative exists at acceptable cost), HARD (no stable path — quantify what breaks without it); (3) for Outcome/Try specifically: design the stable story — methods like .ok_or_propagate()?, into_result()?, or a custom macro propagate!(outcome) — measure the real ergonomic cost on representative code (port 3 modules' worth of ? usage to each candidate, count tokens/readability); (4) deliverable: docs/design/stable_rust_decision_record.md with the inventory table + per-item decision + the K2 implementation plan.
design: Method: rg '#!\[feature' across workspace + cargo build probes with stable toolchain per feature-set to find indirect nightly needs. The Outcome-? ergonomics study is the heart: stable users will live with the chosen pattern — choose with evidence, not taste. Include MSRV implications + what the rust-toolchain.toml pin would become (stable-pinned + nightly lane, or keep nightly default + stable CI lane).
acceptance_criteria: 1. Complete inventory table (feature -> crates -> activating cargo-features -> classification -> decision). 2. Outcome-? study with the 3-module port comparison committed (token counts + subjective notes). 3. Decision record reviewed against the no-tech-debt policy (no permanent dual-API sprawl — the chosen stable pattern must be THE pattern, nightly Try impl is sugar on top). 4. K2 implementation plan section (exact gates, CI lane spec). 5. provider_audit_log.md updated if README claims change.
notes: Pure investigation; blocks K2. Time-boxed: if the inventory reveals >3 HARD blockers beyond Try, the epic pivots to documenting-the-wall honestly instead of gating (record that branch in the decision).
close_reason: Completed K1 stable Rust decision record: source-level nightly inventory, Outcome propagation study, no-tech-debt decision, K2 proof-lane plan, and provider-log disposition committed in docs/design/stable_rust_decision_record.md.

title: [STABLE] Implement nightly gating + stable CI lane — 'builds on stable' becomes a checked artifact
description:
WHY: executes K1's decision record. The goal state: `cargo +stable build` works for the audited feature set, nightly users keep full ergonomics, and the claim is enforced by CI + proof-lane manifest rather than prose.

WHAT (shaped by K1, expected form): (1) a `nightly` cargo feature (default-on initially to avoid disrupting the fleet; flip later with evidence) carrying #![cfg_attr(feature="nightly", feature(try_trait_v2,...))] + the Try impl + any other classified-GATEABLE items; (2) the stable-path Outcome ergonomics per K1's chosen pattern applied across the codebase where ? was used on Outcome in stable-relevant paths; (3) stable CI lane: cargo +stable check/clippy/test on the audited feature subset, wired as a proof-lane manifest row (artifacts/proof_lane_manifest_v1.json) so the guarantee has the same governance as the no-tokio proof; (4) README/AGENTS toolchain sections updated truthfully (what works on stable, what needs nightly, exactly).

Migration of ?-on-Outcome call sites by parallel subagents (no scripts). The lane runs on the rch fleet with a stable toolchain install (verify fleet support first — infra note).
acceptance_criteria: 1. cargo +stable check -p asupersync (audited feature set) green in the new lane; lane registered in proof_lane_manifest with envelope metadata + contract tests green. 2. Nightly default unchanged for the fleet (zero disruption proof: full existing gates green). 3. ?-ergonomics: nightly code keeps ?; stable pattern applied consistently (grep-audit committed). 4. Outcome unit tests run under BOTH toolchains in CI (semantics identical). 5. README feature-table + toolchain docs updated; provider_audit_log row. 6. Proof-status snapshot row added (claim -> lane mapping). 7. Local runner (review-pass addition): scripts/run_stable_lane_e2e.sh executes the stable-toolchain check/clippy/test sequence with per-stage structured logging + summary.json, registered in run_all_e2e.sh, so the stable claim is verifiable locally, not only in CI.

title: StreamReader fuses after an error item and drops later chunks
description: src/io/stream_adapters.rs sets StreamReader.done=true when returning either an immediate stream Err item or a deferred pending_error. Only Poll::Ready(None) terminates a Stream; an Err item can be followed by more data. Retrying after [Err(Interrupted), Ok(x), None] therefore returns false EOF and discards x. Likewise [Ok(a), Err(e), Ok(b), None] returns a, then the deferred error, then false EOF and discards b. Remove both error-path done assignments and set done only on Ready(None). Add deterministic regressions for immediate error then data, buffered data then deferred error then more data, and fused EOF after true None. The local Tokio parity contract promises equivalent StreamReader error deferral and continuation semantics.

title: broadcast/watch wake fan-outs are not panic-safe; watch send_modify wakes under send_lock
description:
Found by the 2026-09-29 sync/channel review (SapphireHill), items 1 and 3.

1. MEDIUM. The broadcast and watch wake fan-outs are not panic-safe, so receivers can hang forever.
- broadcast send_impl, unchecked path (src/channel/broadcast.rs, about line 768 at d3b605e9f): the wakers are drained out of the arena under the lock. Then drop(popped) runs the evicted message's T::drop BEFORE the wake loop. A panicking T::drop drops the drained wakers during the unwind without waking them, and those receivers are no longer in the arena, so no later send or sender drop can reach them.
- The same class, where one panicking wake() strands the rest: broadcast Sender::drop, watch wake_all_waiters and watch Sender::drop. In watch the unprocessed entries also keep queued = true.
- The checked broadcast path already uses CheckedSendNotifications, which wakes each waker behind its own catch_unwind and resumes the first panic afterwards. The same class was fixed in notify (cnl0jn, b3td9n), rwlock (dkubr0), semaphore (dl9wc3) and mutex (l4sgpj).

3. LOW. watch send_modify woke the waiters and dropped the old value while still holding send_lock, because _write_serialize was declared first and so dropped last. An inline-polling waker, or a T::Drop that sends on the same channel, deadlocks on the non-reentrant mutex. send() already avoids this.

Fix (NB5): the unchecked send and broadcast Sender::drop own their wakers in a CheckedSendNotifications, taken before the evicted message is dropped. watch gains a wake_waiters helper that clears every queued flag first, then wakes and drops each waiter behind its own unwind boundary and resumes the first panic; wake_all_waiters and Sender::drop use it. send_modify scopes send_lock to the clone, closure and writeback.

Tests (lib, feature test-internals): unchecked_send_wakes_parked_receivers_when_the_evicted_message_drop_panics, last_sender_drop_wakes_every_parked_receiver_despite_a_panicking_waker (broadcast), sender_drop_wakes_every_parked_receiver_despite_a_panicking_waker (watch). The control restores the old loops behind std::hint::black_box and must fail all three.
close_reason: Fixed by a22082353 (items 1 and 3). Landed on main=master (tip 865c617f6); receipts (fix lane green on the exact candidate, old-code control red, check and clippy on the chain tip) are in the commit message.

title: Supervision audit: a supervisor past its own budget deadline restarts children into a dead region and escalates as a restart limit; Transient sibling failure lost under OneForAll; LOWs
description:
Read-only audit of src/supervision.rs (topology/planning, RestartHistory and RestartTracker, the managed controller from bind_managed with OneForOne/OneForAll/RestForOne and Permanent/Transient/Temporary children, the legacy per-actor Supervisor, MonitorTable, DynamicChildTable) at origin/main 4ef260a14 (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-04). SapphireHill re-read MEDIUM 1 in the code before fixing it. No HIGH.

## MEDIUM
1. FIXED in this session's stack: a supervisor whose own budget deadline (SupervisorBuilder::with_budget, ~2957) has passed restarts Permanent children into a region where they die at their first checkpoint: restart admission is checked against the controller's budget (~3012), not the supervisor's; the new generation's region (~2490) and spawn do not refuse a past deadline. Outcome: Stop wastes N restarts; Escalate reports RestartLimit and FailFast-cancels the caller's region (~3033, ~2933); ResetCounter restarts until the parent is cancelled. AppSpec gives each generation a fresh deadline (app.rs ~243), so that path is unaffected.

## LOW-MEDIUM
2. Under OneForAll or RestForOne on the multi-worker native runtime, a Transient sibling's own failure can be lost: S publishes Err while its shutdown flag is still false (~2612); the controller's batch for another child cancels S's region (~2216) before S's completion is recorded, the Cx::spawn contract (cx.rs ~4505-4512) reports an unacknowledged cancellation, so task_outcome becomes Cancelled; the restart filter (~3105) sees shutdown_requested_before_completion == false and Transient::eligible requires task_outcome.is_ok(): S stays stopped and the report says Ok. Fix: when the terminal was published before the shutdown flag, judge eligibility on the published outcome, ignoring a Cancelled task_outcome whose reason is the controller's own generation drain.

## LOW
3. The legacy Supervisor appends one EvidenceEntry and one EvidenceRecord per actor crash and never drains them (~6374-6377; actor.rs ~1537, ~1583): with the default 3 restarts per 60 s an actor crashing once a minute is never stopped and memory grows linearly with crashes. Fix: ring buffer or opt-out.
4. Docs: docs/spork_deterministic_ordering.md 314-319 (SUP-STOP) says each child's stop completes before the next begins, but the controller cancels all affected children first then drains in reverse (~3085, ~3159), deliberately (managed_cancel_all_precedes_cleanup_that_waits_for_sibling_cancellation); the spec doc is stale. The CompiledSupervisor::spawn rustdoc (~1622-1624) still says CompiledSupervisor trees are never restarted, but bind_managed restarts them (README 1880, 2637).

## Checked and sound
Start-order reordering at bind time (RestForOne suffix correct), reverse cancels and forward restarts with dependency checks; restart-window arithmetic (inclusive cutoff, saturating, sliding prune, max_restarts 0, backoff exponent cap 30); escalation fires once and drains before publishing; stale generation terminals rejected; one batch counts once; cancel/abort mid-restart (checks before backoff, before every start, inside start; finish drains; drop backstop); spawn rejections compensated (no lost wakeup); failure classification (Ok/Err/Cancelled/Panicked) per mode; legacy boot failure handling; MonitorTable and DynamicChildTable indexes.

title: Stream combinator audit: concurrent for_each blind to failure/cancel while waiting on the source; try_buffered lost wake >1024; usize::MAX limit panics
description:
Read-only audit of src/stream/try_buffered.rs, partition.rs, for_each_concurrent.rs and src/channel/ack.rs (+ ack/receipt.rs) on origin/main 7564bd965. partition, ack and receipt held up (partition also passed a 20,000-schedule randomized simulation).

1. HIGH (fixing, round 25): for_each_concurrent and try_for_each_concurrent wait for the next item with stream.next().await, which polls only the source. While parked there, a member's failure and caller cancellation go unseen until another item arrives, which may be never with a quiet channel source. The drain does not happen, and an item arriving later is admitted after the failure. This breaks the docs at for_each_concurrent.rs:126-127, 199-200 and 239-240. Fix: a poll_fn that reaps finished members and checks cancellation before polling the source, and self-wakes while members are in flight.
2. MEDIUM: try_buffered (and Buffered / BufferUnordered, which share the scheme) can lose a wakeup with more than 1024 futures in flight. The epoch scheme treats "polled under the current waker" as "still registered", but a wake consumes the registration. Reproduced with 2048 gate futures: the front entry is woken, the next poll scans a window that excludes it, and the stream returns a bare Pending with nothing registered. This breaks try_buffered.rs:25-27. Fix: per-entry wakers plus a ready set, like join_set.rs ReadyMembers/MemberWake.
3. LOW: try_buffered pulls more items from the source after the terminating Err is already known at the front (admission runs before take_ready_front), then drops them unpolled. With limit 3 and source [Ok1, Err, Ok3, Ok4], Ok4 is consumed from the source. Fix: skip admission when the front holds Some(Err).
4. LOW: try_buffered(usize::MAX) panics ("capacity overflow"), and huge limits abort, because of VecDeque::with_capacity(limit). Only a zero limit is documented as a panic. Buffered and BufferUnordered preallocate the same way. Fix: with_capacity(limit.min(admission budget)).
close_reason: all audit items landed

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SapphireHill, 10-03. Status:
- HIGH (for_each_concurrent blind while waiting on the source) is fixed in my next stack, round 25.
- LOW 3 (try_buffered admits after a ready front Err) and LOW 4 (usize::MAX limit panics, also in Buffered and BufferUnordered) are fixed in round 26.
- The MEDIUM (lost wakeup with more than 1024 in flight, in try_buffered, Buffered and BufferUnordered) is NOT fixed yet.

Why the cheap fixes don't work for the MEDIUM:
- A blanket self-wake when len > budget turns an all-pending oversized buffer into a permanent busy poll; all_pending_buffer_does_not_busy_poll pins that.
- Starting a new epoch on every external poll strands an entry that woke during an in-progress sweep.

The correct fix is per-entry wakers: each entry gets a child waker that records its id in a shared ready set and then wakes the parent, as join_set.rs does with ReadyMembers/MemberWake. Each poll first polls the woken entries (outside the round-robin budget window), then continues the window scan for entries never polled. Entry ids must stay stable across removals: Buffered removes only at the front, BufferUnordered removes anywhere. Scope: all three combinators. Test: the audit's 2048-gate sequence (fire a gate outside the scanned window, then the front gate; the final poll must be Ready or must have requested a wake).

title: Cross-entity ops with lock ordering (cancel/obligation/region close)
description:
Goal: refactor multi-entity operations to use canonical lock ordering and narrow critical sections without changing semantics.

Scope:
- Cancellation propagation across tasks/regions.
- Obligation reserve/commit/abort paths.
- Region close/drain paths that touch tasks + obligations.

Acceptance Criteria:
- All multi-shard operations follow lock order spec; no lock inversion.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
## bd-2wfti Analysis: Cross-Entity Ops with Lock Ordering

### Current State

RuntimeState is behind a single `ContendedMutex<RuntimeState>` (the "big lock"):
- `src/runtime/builder.rs:942` - `state: Arc<ContendedMutex<RuntimeState>>`
- `src/runtime/scheduler/worker.rs:35` - same pattern
- `src/runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs:295` - same pattern
- `src/runtime/scheduler/local_queue.rs:29` - same pattern

ShardedState + ShardGuard infrastructure exists in `sharded_state.rs` but `ShardGuard::*` is only used in its own tests. No production callsite uses ShardGuard yet.

### Cross-Entity Operations to Refactor

All operations currently take `&mut self` (RuntimeState). Need to refactor to work with individual table references from ShardGuard.

| Method | Lines | Tables | Target Guard |
|--------|-------|--------|-------------|
| commit_obligation | 1162-1203 | B→A→C | for_obligation_resolve |
| abort_obligation | 1210-1259 | B→A→C | for_obligation_resolve |
| mark_obligation_leaked | 1265-1327 | B→A→C | for_obligation_resolve |
| create_obligation | 1094-1156 | B→C | for_obligation |
| create_task_infrastructure | 789-885 | B→A | for_spawn |
| create_task | 909-936 | B→A | for_spawn |
| cancel_request | 1495-1700+ | B→A→C | for_cancel |
| task_completed | 1770-1849 | B→A→C | for_task_completed |
| advance_region_state | 2089-2185 | B→A→C | inherited |
| snapshot | 696-739 | B→A→C | all |

### Refactoring Strategy

**Phase 1: Extract cross-entity logic into free functions**
- Each cross-entity method becomes a free function taking `(&mut RegionTable, &mut TaskTable, &mut ObligationTable, ...)` or a subset
- RuntimeState methods become thin wrappers calling these functions
- This preserves backward compatibility while enabling ShardGuard usage

**Phase 2: Create ShardedState dispatch methods**
- Add methods on ShardedState that acquire ShardGuard and call the free functions
- e.g., `ShardedState::commit_obligation()` acquires `for_obligation_resolve`, unwraps guards, calls `cross_entity::commit_obligation(&mut regions, &mut tasks, &mut obligations, ...)`

**Phase 3: Migrate callsites**
- Update worker.rs, three_lane.rs, local_queue.rs, builder.rs to use ShardedState instead of ContendedMutex<RuntimeState>
- This is the actual contention reduction payoff

### Key Complication: Tracing + Metrics

Many cross-entity methods emit trace events and update metrics. These are Shard D (lock-free). The free functions need access to:
- `TraceBufferHandle` (for trace events)
- `Arc<dyn MetricsProvider>` (for counters)
- Various config fields (ObligationLeakResponse, etc.)

**Solution**: Pass a `&ShardedState` reference alongside the table references, or create a `CrossEntityContext` struct.

### Regression Tests Needed (per acceptance criteria)

1. **Cancel propagation**: Spawn task in child region, cancel parent, verify task cancelled + region closed + obligations aborted
2. **Obligation commit during region drain**: Create obligation, begin region close, commit obligation, verify region advances to finalizing
3. **Task completion with orphan obligations**: Spawn task with pending obligations, complete task without committing, verify obligations auto-aborted
4. **Cascading region close**: Create 3-level region tree, close leaf, verify parent chain advances
5. **Concurrent cancel + obligation resolve**: Use deterministic seed for interleaving

All tests should use deterministic seeds and structured logs per acceptance criteria.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
FILED 2026-07-26 by SapphireHill while closing br-asupersync-xwanb4 (e9705807e).

THE GAP: xwanb4 fixed the cancel-precedence hole in postgres/mysql read_exact
and landed 11 deterministic tests, but NONE of them drives the actual race the
bead was about: cancellation landing inside a single poll, after the
top-of-poll cancel guard and before the `n == 0` EOF check.

WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY COVERED, and why the obvious test is a trap: the guard is
the first thing in the poll_fn closure. If a test pre-sets the cancel and then
calls read_exact, the GUARD fires and returns Cancelled -- the test goes green
without ever executing the EOF branch it claims to cover. That is a false green
of exactly the kind br-asupersync-c6ppu4 is about: a check that exists is not a
check that runs. Any test written for this must prove it reached the branch.

WHAT xwanb4 DID INSTEAD: extracted `eof_or_cancelled` (postgres.rs, mysql.rs)
and `stream_io_error` (mysql.rs) so the *decision* is unit-testable in both
directions, positive and negative, with deliberate-failure controls proving each
test has teeth. That covers the classification logic completely. It does not
cover the interleaving that puts the classification in that state.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEEDED: a deterministic injection point that flips
cancellation between the guard and the length check within one poll. Candidates
already in the tree:
  - src/lab/chaos.rs has pre-poll / post-poll injection points and is seed-bound
    and deterministic (see src/lab/config.rs, src/lab/runtime.rs).
  - LabRuntime + a virtual/scripted stream that returns Ready(Ok(())) with zero
    bytes filled on a chosen step.
A wall-clock loopback test is the wrong vehicle -- it would be flaky and would
silently degrade into "the guard caught it" most runs, which is the false green
above.

ACCEPTANCE: the test must FAIL against the pre-xwanb4 code (revert
`eof_or_cancelled` to return Io unconditionally) and pass after, and must assert
it actually took the EOF path rather than the guard path.

RELATED: br-asupersync-xwanb4 (the fix), br-asupersync-c6ppu4, br-asupersync-nmqrmi.

title: [tls-trust-bypass] tls/connector.rs: is_ca_certificate gate only applied in env-cert path — direct add_pem_file with leaf cert is a complete trust bypass
description:
src/tls/connector.rs:967-979 (and src/tls/types.rs load_pem_file) — the `is_ca_certificate()` predicate (which checks BasicConstraints CA:TRUE) is invoked only inside `load_env_certs()` when `enable_env_cert_loading()` is called. Other code paths that add a cert to the RootCertStore (direct `add_pem_file()`, `add_root_certificate()`, or any caller-provided RootCertStore) BYPASS the gate entirely.

Threat: a misconfigured operator who attempts to add their server's own leaf cert to the trust store as a 'self-signed root' (a common dev misstep that occasionally ships to prod) will succeed silently. Any subsequent connection that presents a cert signed by THAT leaf is then accepted as trusted — a complete trust bypass.

Concrete attack:
  (a) Operator copies their server's leaf cert into the env-var path that is read by load_env_certs(); the gate rejects it (good).
  (b) Operator copies the same cert into a different path that is loaded via `add_pem_file()` directly; the gate is silent (BAD).
  (c) Any future connection presenting a cert signed by that leaf is accepted by the connector — trust is rooted at a non-CA cert.

The defence-in-depth principle is that EVERY ingress to the root store should enforce the CA gate, not just the env-var path. Currently the gate is decoration on a single sub-path.

Fix direction:
  1. Move the is_ca_certificate gate INTO the wrapper around RootCertStore so all add_* paths enforce it.
  2. Or: replace direct rustls RootCertStore exposure with a project-controlled VerifiedRootStore that wraps each add() call with the CA check.
  3. Provide an explicit `add_pinned_leaf()` method for the (rare) case where a pinned non-CA cert is intentional, accompanied by a documented warning.
  4. Regression test: try to add a leaf cert via add_pem_file directly; assert the call returns Err.

Severity HIGH because (a) reachable from the public TlsConnector builder, (b) the failure mode is silent (no error, no warning) and produces a complete trust bypass, and (c) the gate's existence in load_env_certs creates a misleading impression that the project enforces CA-only roots universally — defence-in-depth principle violated.

Source: /security-audit-for-saas on src/tls/* deepest refresh (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Added with_strict_ca_validation() builder; gates add_root_certificate / add_root_certificates with is_ca_certificate. enable_env_cert_loading() flips it as a side effect (so env-cert opt-in implies strict gate everywhere). insecure_add_root_certificate() provides explicit bypass for sandbox/test pinning. Tests: add_root_certificate_strict_ca_rejects_self_signed_leaf, enable_env_cert_loading_implies_strict_ca_validation. Commit 1960e018a.

title: Remote/symbol-service audit: 1-byte chunks make chunked symbol uploads copy quadratically under the global staging lock; LOWs (wake-all admission, single durable gate, zero-tail journal)
description:
Read-only audit of src/distributed/remote_owned (outgoing and incoming remote-call admission) and src/distributed/symbol_service (signed symbol batch put/get, chunked upload, durable journal, recovery/continuation) at origin/main 2c6b91a85 (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-04). SapphireHill re-read MEDIUM 1 in the code before fixing it. No HIGH; no panic reachable from peer input.

## MEDIUM
1. FIXED in this session's stack: one authenticated peer could stall every chunked symbol upload with 1-byte chunks (service/chunked.rs 151, 189, 198, 219). Each CHUNK grew the staging Vec by exactly the new bytes (try_reserve_exact(bytes.len())), so each append could reallocate and copy everything staged so far, about T^2/2 bytes for a T-byte upload, all under the one global staging lock that every peer's BEGIN/CHUNK/COMMIT/READ takes (COMMIT also verifies under it). The buffer is Zeroizing, but every reallocation freed the old copy unzeroed. Fix: allocate the declared total (already charged to the staging quota at BEGIN) once on the first append.

## LOW
2. Every admission release, claim or ticket drop calls notify_waiters(), waking all W waiters; each takes the executor lock and scans the queue with selected() (admission.rs 122, queue.rs 204, 259-262, 392): O(W^2) per release, bounded by the configured queue limits.
3. The durable symbol service has one compare-and-swap gate for all peers with no queue (service/durable.rs 30, 118); one peer with several connections can hold it almost continuously, so others mostly get "busy". Fix: route it through RemoteServiceAdmission keyed by invocation.peer_node().
4. A journal whose tail holds 40 or more bytes of zeros or garbage (a filesystem exposing unwritten extents after a crash) fails the header check with Authentication and the whole open fails (durable.rs 308-317, 343), leaving committed data unreadable. A trailing zero run could be treated as ReadOnlyTail (deleting a suffix is already undetectable).

## Relation to asupersync-bi2462.77
RemoteExecutor and RemoteServiceAdmission deliver the invocation-level budget (per-peer active/waiting counts and bytes, cancellation-aware reserve with exact release, FIFO per class). Still missing for bi2462.77: per-peer frame/byte admission before decoding in the remote.rs session loop; a protected lifecycle-control lane; shared accounting for the legacy run_remote/spawn_remote/send_message paths; admission on the symbol services (they register directly); identity-generation cleanup for peer labels.

## Checked and sound
Admission charge release exactly once (spawn failure, early return, length mismatch, cancel-after-claim, unwinding); Notify generation counter (no lost wakeup); ticket drop/cancel/deadline/close; FIFO and bounded priority bypass; inbound peer identity from the session; batch/request/receipt/progress/range/manifest/journal/continuation parsers bound lengths and arithmetic before indexing or allocating; durable store poisons on write/fsync failure, signed chained records, quotas re-checked on replay; continuation snapshots signed over their metadata with the expected identity from the caller; client-side recovery bound to the trusted digest with per-fetch deadlines.

title: Sync/channel audit: Semaphore::try_acquire notifies under its lock with no rollback; Notify differs from tokio (unpolled notified misses broadcasts, permits accumulate); oneshot reserve, Mutex revoked-grant, watch doc
description:
Read-only audit of src/sync and src/channel on origin/main 101f469e5 (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-03). Not yet verified by a second read or fixed.

I found no high-severity bugs at origin/main (`101f469e5`). There are 2 MEDIUM and 3 LOW findings that no open bead covers, plus 2 known items from bead `c11v6v` that are still in the code. This was a read-only audit: I built nothing and ran nothing, so each scenario below comes from reading the code end to end, not from a test run. Paths are under `/data/projects/asupersync/src/`.

### 1. MEDIUM: `Semaphore::try_acquire` calls the runtime notifier while holding the semaphore mutex, with nothing to roll back
- **Where:** `sync/semaphore.rs:566-616`. It subtracts the permits at 582. Still holding the state lock, the `SemaphorePermit` literal at 605-607 registers a runtime obligation. That call path ends in `WorkerCoordinator::wake_one` (`runtime/obligation_mailbox.rs:517-523`, `runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs:972-981`), which unparks a worker, calls the reactor's `io.wake()`, and runs the wake notifier that users can install. The lock is only released at 615.
- **Effects:**
  - Inside a runtime task, every successful `try_acquire` (and `OwnedSemaphorePermit::try_acquire`/`try_acquire_arc`) makes futex and eventfd wake calls inside the critical section.
  - If the notifier touches the same semaphore (`try_acquire`, `add_permits`, `close`, `telemetry_snapshot`), it deadlocks on the non-reentrant lock.
  - If the notifier panics, the `count` permits are lost for good, because no permit object exists to give them back. The lock-order token taken at 590 is also never released.
- **Contract broken:** the module's own rule to arm rollback before any notifier runs. The async path (unlock at 940, register at 948) and `try_acquire_checked` (514-540) both follow it; `try_acquire` doesn't.
- **Fix:** copy `try_acquire_checked`: create an `AcquisitionRollbackGuard` with `notify_on_rollback = true`, subtract and `arm()` under the lock, release the lock, then mint both obligations and call `into_borrowed_permit()`.
- **Test sketch:** build a gateway with `ObligationGateway::new(Arc::new(ObligationMailbox::new()), notifier, Arc::downgrade(&liveness))`. The notifier records `sem.state.try_lock().is_none()` into a flag, then panics. Install it with `Cx::set_current(Some(Cx::for_testing().with_obligation_gateway(Some(gw), None)))`. `catch_unwind(|| sem.try_acquire(1))` should be `Err`; then assert the flag is false and `available_permits() == 1`. Today the flag is true and permits are 0. The `try_lock` probe proves the lock is held without actually re-entering, so the test fails instead of hanging.
- **Beads:** not tracked. `122k6j` (closed) covered only waker drops; `bi2462.15` (closed) added this registration.

### 2. MEDIUM (docs vs tokio): `Notify` behaves differently from `tokio::sync::Notify`, but the README presents it as a direct replacement
- **(a) Unpolled futures miss broadcasts.** A `notified()` future records the broadcast generation on its first poll, not when it is created (`sync/notify.rs:340-348, 704-714`). Tokio enrolls the future at creation. Take the common tokio pattern: `let n = notify.notified(); if ready.load() { return } n.await;`. If the producer sets `ready` and calls `notify_waiters()` between the load and the first poll, the waiter blocks forever, because broadcasts store no permit. There is no `Notified::enable()` to opt in early.
- **(b) Stored permits pile up.** `notify_one` with no waiter increments an unbounded counter (440, 537); tokio stores at most one permit.
- **Contract:** `README.md:113` maps the tokio type with no caveat, and `docs/tokio_functional_parity_contracts.md:86` says "stores permit". Both behaviours are deliberate and pinned by tests (`notify_tests.rs:1922` and the accumulation test around line 2604).
- **Fix:** additive. Add `Notified::enable()` that arms the generation and registers, the way `notified_at_generation` already does internally. Document both differences on `notified`/`notify_one` and in the README.
- **Test sketch:** call `enable()` on a pinned `notified()`, then `notify_waiters()`, then `poll_once` should be `Ready`.
- **Beads:** not tracked. `veh9r8` (closed) fixed only `wait_until` and kept the first-poll behaviour on purpose.

### 3. LOW: oneshot `Sender::reserve` marks a permit outstanding before any permit exists
- **Where:** `channel/oneshot.rs:513-524`. It sets `sender_consumed` and `permit_outstanding`, then calls `try_register_obligation` inside the `SendPermit` literal.
- **Scenario:** if that call panics (gateway notifier), no `SendPermit` exists to drop. `Sender::drop` sees the sender as consumed and does nothing. `is_closed()` then stays false forever, and a pending `recv` is never woken and never returns `Closed`.
- **Contract:** the module docs ("drop → recv() → Err") and `recv`'s "Err(Closed) if the sender was dropped". mpsc `Reserve` (1038-1046) and `reserve_checked` both create the owner first.
- **Fix:** build the permit with `obligation: None`, then assign the obligation.
- **Test sketch:** use the planted-panic gateway pattern from `oneshot_tests.rs:153`. Poll `rx.recv` once with a counting waker that never wakes itself (Pending). `catch_unwind(|| tx.reserve(&cx))` should be `Err`. Assert one wake and that the next poll is `Ready(Err(Closed))`. Today: no wake, Pending forever.
- **Beads:** not tracked (`l0y8xq` covers the send-side wake panic).

### 4. LOW: Mutex waiter whose grant was revoked queues itself again on a free mutex
- **Where:** `sync/mutex.rs:388-399` revokes the grant when the grantee's waker panics (the `l4sgpj` fix) but leaves that future's `waiter_id` set. On its next poll, the fast path at 583 is skipped (it requires `waiter_id.is_none()`), `replace_waker` fails, and line 622 pushes it back to the front and returns Pending while the mutex is unlocked with no grant.
- **Scenario:** nothing will wake that waiter. Until another `lock()` barges in, `try_lock` (244) returns `Locked` on an unlocked mutex.
- **Fix:** in the `Err` branch, if the mutex is unlocked and nothing is granted, acquire immediately.
- **Test sketch:** hold a guard; poll `lock()` with a waker whose `wake` panics once; `catch_unwind(|| drop(guard))`. Poll again with a counting waker and expect `Ready(Ok)`. Today it is Pending, and `try_lock` returns `Err(Locked)` while `!is_locked()`.
- **Beads:** not tracked; follows on from `l4sgpj` (closed).

### 5. LOW (docs): `watch` send with zero receivers
`channel/watch.rs:488-510` returns `Ok` when there are no receivers. That is deliberate (watch.rs:72-74), but contract C03.7 in `docs/tokio_functional_parity_contracts.md:73` requires an error and lists watch in its scope. The fix is to exempt watch in the doc.

### Known (bead `c11v6v`) and still present
- **Item 8 (RwLock writer handoff, fairness only, no hang):** `rwlock.rs:506-520, 625-638` hand the lock to the head writer without checking which waiter arrived first.
- **Item 9 (unchecked semaphore acquire):** `semaphore.rs:887` and `953-955` keep `notify_on_rollback = false`. An unwind after `arm()` restores capacity without waking a successor that could now run.
- **Probably landed:** `c11v6v` items 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7, and `6zm9xr` (`session.rs:260-269`). Worth checking and closing those beads.

### Checked and found sound
- **Mutex:** grant handoff on unlock, cancel, timeout and poison; `try_lock` respects queued waiters.
- **Waiter IDs:** waiter-queue IDs are monotonic `u64`; mpsc tokens and broadcast/watch arena indices carry generations. No ID-reuse (ABA) problems found.
- **Semaphore (async paths):** strict FIFO, waking the next runnable waiter when the front leaves, close wakes everyone, rollback guard.
- **RwLock:** waiter counts for granted-but-unpolled writers, the forced reader turn, downgrade, poison wake-up, cancelling a granted waiter.
- **Notify:** recheck under the lock, slab epochs, passing on a cancelled `notify_one`.
- **Barrier:** cancel racing a trip; removal by waiter id.
- **OnceCell:** reset and wake when an initializer is cancelled, panics or errors.
- **Pool:** eligibility arithmetic, wakes on return/discard/cancel, return-dispatcher handoff.
- **mpsc:** atomic reserve and commit; `try_send` and `try_reserve` don't jump the queue; wake-up chain and handoff on cancel; last-sender and receiver-drop wake ordering; `recv` and `recv_many` are cancel-safe.
- **oneshot:** a ready value wins over cancellation; waiter identity tracking.
- **broadcast:** lag accounting, eviction during an in-flight clone, last-receiver vs subscribe race.
- **watch:** version is bumped before waiters are taken, so register-then-recheck can't miss a send; sender-drop ordering; subscribe under the read lock.
- **session and ack:** obligations are owned before notification, and waiters register before checking queue state.

I did not audit the fault-injection modules (`partition`, `crash`, `fault`, `clock_skew`, `erasure`, `flow_control_monitor`) or the `lock_ordering` internals in depth.
close_reason: All sync/channel audit items verified and resolved: (1) Semaphore::try_acquire registers obligations unlocked with armed rollback, landed in cf7b52635; (2) Notify::notified vs tokio documented in README.md and tokio_functional_parity_contracts.md, Notified::enable landed; (3) oneshot Sender::reserve creates permit before obligation registration; (4) Mutex waiter whose grant was revoked re-acquires unqueued without phantom lock; (5) watch send with zero receivers exempted in C03.7 contract doc. All 684 sync and 778 channel tests pass cleanly.

title: Sync audit: write guard taken during unwinding poisons RwLock for good; read-mode hand-offs skip the writer-preference bound; Interval fires forever at Time::MAX (all LOW)
description:
Read-only audit of src/sync/contended_mutex.rs (never audited), src/time/interval.rs (never audited) and src/sync/rwlock.rs (last audited 2026-06-03) at origin/main 4ef260a14 (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-04). Verdicts: contended_mutex.rs SOUND; interval.rs SOUND apart from I-1; rwlock.rs hand-off state machine SOUND, two LOWs. Nothing was run; the reproducers are from the code.

## LOW
R-1. A write guard acquired while the thread is already unwinding poisons the lock permanently (rwlock.rs Drop for RwLockWriteGuard ~1086 and OwnedRwLockWriteGuard ~1263 poison whenever std::thread::panicking(), without checking whether the thread was already panicking at acquire; std checks this). The docs (~206-210) promise poisoning only "if a panic occurs while holding a write guard"; there is no clear_poison and into_inner/get_mut refuse a poisoned lock. Trigger: a Drop-based cleanup handle that does try_write() while an unrelated panic unwinds. Fix: store panicking_at_acquire in both write-guard types at every grant site (315, 951, 977, 1522, 1548) and poison only if !panicking_at_acquire && panicking(). NOTE: rwlock.rs is pinned by the unsafe-boundary ledger at lines 70, 222-223, 1021-1029, 1056-1073, 1176-1290 (live); the new fields and grant-site lines must be offset line-neutrally between pins.
R-2. Read-mode hand-offs skip the forced-reader-turn check and arrival order, breaking the documented (p+1)*N bound: release_reader (~506-519) and abandon_read_waiter (~625-639) always pop the head writer, downgrade (~1130-1134, ~1306-1310) never looks at consecutive_writers_served. With N+2 writers queued then reader R, granting each writer and dropping g.downgrade() keeps R pending past N+1 hand-offs. Related: the forced turn (~558-587) runs before the arrival-order check (admits R1 alone, then W17 ahead of the older R2), and ~666-678 re-admits readers only when writer_waiters == 0 (W2 ahead of an older R1 after W1 is cancelled). Nothing hangs; readers still get FIFO admission. Fix: one decision function for release_reader, abandon_read_waiter's granted branch, downgrade and read-mode writer cancellation (counter first, then arrival order via take_eligible_reader_waiters, then the writer).
I-1. Once an Interval's deadline saturates at Time::MAX it fires forever (interval.rs ~383, 387, 399 via poll_tick ~257-265 and tick ~289-299): every poll_tick(Time::MAX) returns Some(Time::MAX), so a drain-all-due-ticks loop never ends; Duration::MAX periods and reset_after(_, Duration::MAX) end the same way. Fix: mark the interval exhausted when it saturates.

## Note
Under --features lock-metrics, ContendedMutex::new and RwLock::with_name panic on names outside the lock-name policy (lock_ordering.rs 500-528): intentional fail-closed, but the constructors do not document the panic.

## Checked and sound
RwLock: grant under the state lock before the wake ("dequeued means granted"), cancel/drop at every stage passes a grant on, single writer_waiters decrement, no queue-jumping fast paths, poison wakes all waiters, wakes outside the lock and panic-isolated, atomic downgrade, ManuallyDrop + ptr::read in the owned downgrade, waiter-id wraparound. ContendedMutex: std poisoning, guard released before metrics, lock-order check before blocking acquire, coherent metrics, !Send guard. Interval: Burst/Delay/Skip match docs, Skip arithmetic guarded, zero period rejected, first tick at start, reset semantics documented, no drift.

title: [reality-check-wave2][wasm] Promote service-worker direct runtime lane
description:
Promote Browser Edition service-worker direct runtime from fail-closed boundary to shipped capability, or produce a precise blocker bead if the browser security model prevents promotion.

Background and evidence:
README.md says Browser Edition is implemented for browser main-thread and dedicated-worker consumers, while service-worker direct runtime is deferred. docs/integration.md classifies service workers as deferred and unsupported for direct runtime but notes bounded broker scaffolding. packages/browser/src/index.ts exposes service_worker_not_yet_shipped and service_worker_direct_runtime_not_shipped reason codes, broker support helpers, and durable handoff scaffolding. src/runtime/builder.rs has tests pinning service-worker direct runtime as fail-closed while preserving broker diagnostics.

Scope:
- Decide and implement the promotion path for direct BrowserRuntime creation inside service-worker hosts without silently remapping to browser main-thread or dedicated-worker lanes.
- If promotion is feasible, wire explicit service-worker host detection, capability negotiation, durable lifecycle state, cache/fetch/event constraints, region ownership, cancellation, drain/finalize, and replay/trace evidence.
- If full direct runtime is not feasible, create a narrower live blocker bead with exact browser/security limitation evidence and strengthen the broker/handoff contract so users receive an optimal supported path; do not leave vague deferral language.
- Preserve existing broker helpers and fail-closed diagnostics until the shipped replacement proves equivalent or better behavior.

Unit tests required:
- RuntimeBuilder service-worker probe tests for promoted, unsupported, degraded, and policy-disabled states.
- JS/TS package tests for reason-code migration, lane selection, broker compatibility, durable handoff decoding, and no silent remapping to unrelated lanes.
- Rust wasm boundary tests for Cx/region/cancel behavior in service-worker-compatible profiles.

E2E/script proof required:
Add a browser-run fixture that exercises service-worker install/activate/fetch/message events with direct runtime creation or the final supported broker path. The proof must log bead_id, scenario_id, host_context, service_worker_scope, lifecycle_event, selected_lane, direct_runtime_supported, fallback_target, region_count_before, region_count_after, cancel_event_count, durable_state_key, expected_reason, actual_reason, verdict, and first_failure.

Validation:
Use rch exec for Rust wasm profile checks and Rust contract tests. JS/TS/browser commands should be deterministic and logged; if they are CPU-heavy, route through the repo-approved remote/offload pattern where available.

Non-goals:
Do not fake service-worker support by running on the window thread. Do not break the current broker APIs for applications that already use the bounded handoff path. Do not broaden docs until the browser fixture proves the shipped behavior.

title: L3 commit-write rename-not-copy: stage large-object fragments contiguously → same-fs rename at commit (flip 5G clean)
description:
## Goal
Flip 5G/perfect clean (atp currently LOSES nocrypto 51.0 vs rsync 47.86, ~TIE auth) by eliminating the commit-write fragment-concatenation copy. This is the DIRECT continuation of the L1 clean-large flip (MATRIX-190, landed 81c44d28e) which won 500M but did NOT scale to 5G (MATRIX-191).

## Proven root cause (ledger MATRIX-191, run 20260701T055332Z)
The 3-lever hash-pipeline (inc-hash faa93d808 + L2 463a4cfae + L1 81c44d28e) fully overlapped hashing with streaming — recv.time shows verify_hash_micros=0 even at 5G. But that EXPOSED the next serial post-stream tail: commit_write_micros=5461583 (rep1)/2541857 (rep2) = 2.5-5.5s at 5G (was 240927=0.24s at 500M, hidden under the old 1.43s hash). total_micros ≈ commit_write; everything else is microseconds. commit_write 5.46s > the 3.1s gap → fixing it flips 5G (atp ~45.5s < rsync 47.86).

## Code
A large single file is committed via CommitWrite::Fragments → write_large_object_fragments (src/net/atp/transport_rq/mod.rs:9666, called at :10022): it CREATEs out_path and RE-READS every staged RaptorQ block/shard file (each staged separately at staging_dir.join(entry_index), :7648) and WRITEs them concatenated → a full-size (5GB) read+write copy at ~940 MB/s NVMe = the 2.5-5.5s. LargeObjectFragment already carries logical_offset + logical_size + len (:2530); fragments are verified strictly contiguous (:4287).

## Fix (rename-not-copy / stage-contiguous)
1. STAGE each logical file's blocks into ONE contiguous staging file located in the SAME directory as the eventual out_path (so the final rename is same-fs, metadata-only). Write each decoded block at its logical_offset (pwrite / seek+write), not to per-block files. Pre-create/allocate the file to logical_size.
2. VERIFY sha/merkle on that single contiguous staging file (the L1/L2/inc-hash running digests already compute this incrementally — reuse; fall back to a single-file streaming hash if needed). Fail-closed: mismatch → NO rename, Integrity error, unlink staging.
3. COMMIT = crate::fs::rename(staging, out_path) — replaces write_large_object_fragments' concat copy for the single-file case. Metadata-only when same-fs (the staging dir must be under dest, not a cross-device tmp).

## Constraints / correctness
- Byte-identical end-to-end (sha-ok is the gate). Fail-closed preserved (verify BEFORE rename; a sha/merkle mismatch writes nothing into place).
- Keep the lossy/datagram path working (blocks may arrive/decode out of order → pwrite-at-offset handles that; the contiguous file is only complete once all fragments' byte ranges are filled).
- Directory transfers + multi-file + small-file packed-member path (CommitWrite::Members) UNCHANGED — this is only the large-single-file Fragments path.
- Same-fs guarantee: ensure the fragment staging dir (.atp-rq-fragment-staging, :17233) is created UNDER the destination root so rename() is same-device; if the receiver dest and staging can be cross-device, fall back to the existing concat copy (no regression).

## Tests (mandatory — needs cargo test RUNS, not just check)
- e2e: a large multi-fragment single-file transfer commits sha-ok with commit = rename (assert no full-size copy: e.g. staging inode == committed inode, or commit_write_micros ~0 for a large file).
- fail-closed: a tampered fragment byte → Integrity error, NO file at out_path, staging cleaned.
- out-of-order fragment arrival still reconstructs byte-identical.
- lossy/datagram path unchanged + still fail-closed.
- directory + small-file packed-member paths regression (unchanged).

## Gate
SapphireHill central netns A/B: 5G/perfect nocrypto+auth < rsync (47.86/50.04) sha-ok 2/2 = the 5G flip; 500M/perfect no-regress (still <rsync); 50M/bad no-regress. recv.time commit_write_micros should drop ~0 for large clean. Then MATRIX-192.

## Lineage
Continues br-asupersync-2eb4k2 (L1, CLOSED). Ledger MATRIX-190 (500M win) + MATRIX-191 (5G finding + this lever). Spec mirror: /data/tmp/l3_commit_rename_spec.txt
close_reason: L3 landed bae50415d; 5G clean beats tuned rsync nocrypto+auth (46.17/46.24 vs 46.71/46.94), 500M no-regress, sha_ok 2/2, commit_write 5.46s->202us, MATRIX-192

title: Size-gate the receiver decode fanout: 500M/bad 4.6x win (704->151.6s) but 50M/bad regressed 57->89s (over-parallelizes small)
description: EVIDENCE (MATRIX-49): LANE-A parallel decode (2f69e377f 'keep 500M decode fanout wide' + 2ec9e5674 decode-width cap) is a MAJOR win at 500M/bad: 704s->151.6s (4.6x faster, now 1.54x of rsync 98.4s, atp 41MB RSS vs rsync 750MB = 18x less mem), sha-ok byte-identical. BUT it REGRESSED 50M/bad: 57s->88.9s (walls 61-91 high-variance) — chosen_fanout=8 over-parallelizes the smaller object; pool-dispatch+coordination overhead dominates when per-block decode is already cheap. FIX: make the decode fanout SIZE-GATED — only parallelize when object/block-count is large enough that per-block decode dominates dispatch overhead (e.g. K or block_count above a threshold tuned so 500M parallelizes, 50M stays sequential). Keep small objects on the sequential decode path (50M/bad back to 57s). GATES: 500M/bad holds ~151.6s (4.6x win preserved), 50M/bad back to ~57s (no regression), all sha-ok byte-identical, 500M/good+perfect not regressed. I bench-verify centrally. Owner: transport_rq receiver decode-fanout selection (where chosen_fanout is computed). This converts LANE-A from a 500M-win-with-50M-regression into a clean across-sizes win.
close_reason: Size-gate verified MATRIX-50: 500M/bad 4.4x win preserved (704->161.3s, fanout=8 held); 50M/bad recovered 89->61.2s (~57 baseline). 50M fanout still mixed 1/8 = minor follow-up, regression resolved.
