title: service middleware: Steer loses wakeups with two waiters on one backend (hang); Retry retries after cancellation; RateLimit refill timer spins when cancelled; ConcurrencyLimit tied to first poller's Cx; discovery panic deadlock
description:
Read-only audit of src/service (tower-style middleware) at origin/main (2026-10-03, SapphireHill subagent). Findings were confirmed by reading the code paths. The with_time_getter clock mismatch in Timeout and Hedge is e66q35 item 2 and is excluded here.

1. (high, CONFIRMED, fix in progress) Steer loses wakeups when several requests wait on one backend (src/service/steer.rs ~186-209, call ~248-254).
   - Each SteerFuture polls poll_ready on the shared Arc<Mutex<S>> with its own waker.
   - RateLimit (rate_limit.rs ~520-537) and the semaphore behind ConcurrencyLimit (semaphore.rs ~1479-1488) keep only the latest waker.
   - SteerFuture wakes nobody when it dispatches, fails or is dropped. Over ConcurrencyLimit(1) with the permit held, request A waits, then request B waits and replaces A's waker. The release wakes only B, and A hangs forever.
   - Buffer already handles this with inner_wakers.
2. (medium-high) Retry keeps retrying after cancellation, with no backoff (retry.rs ~526-569, ~890-908).
   - RetryDelay polls Sleep through Future::poll, which is Ready at once in a cancelled task, so the backoff counts as elapsed.
   - ExponentialBackoff(3, 1000 ms) over a call that fails fast makes 3 more calls in one poll after a cancel.
   - hedge.rs ~632-642 does the right thing: a cancelled task starts no backup.
3. (medium) The RateLimit refill timer (rate_limit.rs ~586-613):
   - (a) spins at 100% CPU in a cancelled task: the cancel-aware Sleep is Ready at once, then dropped and rebuilt;
   - (b) is built with Sleep::new(next_deadline), which ignores the layer's time_getter (a different clock domain).
4. (medium) ConcurrencyLimit ties its acquire future to the first poller's Cx (concurrency_limit.rs ~216-237).
   - Shared through Buffer, Steer or LoadBalancer, a cancelled first poller makes every later poller fail with LimitExceeded, an error the docs say "should not happen".
5. (medium) A resolver panic deadlocks DnsServiceDiscovery permanently (discover.rs ~862-935).
   - in_flight_generation stays Some, so every later poll_discover waits on resolve_done forever.
6. (medium, docs/parity, OWNER) ServiceBuilder applies layers in the reverse of tower's order: the last-added layer is outermost (builder.rs ~36-41).
   - The order is deliberate (eeexl1.3, layer.rs ~329 test), but the rustdoc never says so.
   - The parity docs (docs/tokio_web_grpc_parity_map.md ~182, docs/tokio_compatibility_limitation_matrix.md ~157) call the builder complete or equivalent.
   - The tower idiom .load_shed().concurrency_limit(10) never sheds.
7. (low-medium) Buffer has no channel or worker, despite its docs (buffer.rs ~9-11 vs ~368/408).
   - The slot is freed only when the response completes, so capacity caps in-flight requests rather than queued ones. Buffer(1) serializes all traffic.
8. (low-medium) CircuitBreaker records a dropped response future as a failure (circuit_breaker.rs ~630-637).
   - That contradicts the combinator's own guard and the Disposition docs ("cancellation ignored").
   - Hedge(CircuitBreaker(svc)) records one failure per hedged request on a healthy backend.

The auditor found these sound:
- Timeout's deadline taken at call();
- ConcurrencyLimit permit release paths;
- RateLimit reservation bookkeeping;
- Hedge slots and cancel path;
- LoadShed, Filter, Reconnect epochs, Oneshot, Ready;
- Buffer waker lists;
- LoadBalancer P2C/SWRR and load-metric decrements;
- backoff overflow handling;
- DNS discovery generation ordering.
close_reason: Completed: Item 1 in 6b9f855cd (Steer ReadinessWaiters), Item 2 in retry.rs (cancelled task starts no further attempt), Item 3 in rate_limit.rs (poll_deadline without cancel-aware busy spin), Item 4 in concurrency_limit.rs (restart on first poller cancellation), Item 5 in discover.rs (ReleaseInFlightOnUnwind), Item 6 in builder.rs and parity docs (reversed layer order), Item 7 in buffer.rs (slot-bounded coordinator doc), and fixed LoadShed inner readiness release timing in 8ef1cd867.

title: Add Mutex::try_lock_owned() convenience method
description: Add Mutex::try_lock_owned() as a convenience API for acquiring an owned mutex guard without awaiting, returning immediately with either an owned guard or a would-block result. This should serve sync-adjacent integration code while preserving asupersync cancellation-aware locking semantics and without changing existing lock()/try_lock() behavior.
design: Implement the owned guard path on top of the current mutex state machine rather than adding a parallel lock implementation. The API must preserve fairness/accounting, must not bypass waiter queues incorrectly, and must make ownership/lifetime semantics explicit. Prefer Result/Option types consistent with existing try_lock APIs and keep diagnostics redacted and deterministic.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover successful try_lock_owned on an unlocked mutex, would-block on a locked mutex, guard drop releases the lock, owned guard can move across allowed ownership boundaries only when trait bounds permit, existing try_lock/lock semantics unchanged, waiter fairness unaffected after a failed try_lock_owned, cancellation state unaffected, panic/drop cleanup, and no lock leak under repeated acquire/drop churn. Deterministic integration/e2e coverage must log scenario ID, acquisition attempt index, lock state before/after, would-block count, owned guard drop count, waiter wake count, cancellation/leak counters, exact rch command, artifact paths if any, and final pass/fail verdict. Validation before closeout: rch exec -- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check for touched Rust files, targeted rch cargo tests for sync::mutex owned-guard behavior with --nocapture, and a closeout comment documenting trait-bound decisions and any rejected API shapes.

title: [conformance-final] RaptorQ proof-of-decoding correctness vectors
description:
Add comprehensive conformance harness for src/raptorq/proof.rs DecodeProof artifact verification.

**Gap Analysis**: tests/conformance/ lacks proof-of-decoding correctness vectors that freeze the deterministic behavior of RaptorQ decode proofs under various failure and success scenarios.

**Concrete Vectors Needed**:

1. **Successful decode proof vector**:
   - Input: Complete symbol set (K=8, symbols 0-7 received)
   - Expected: DecodeProof with outcome=Success, all peeling/elimination steps recorded
   - Freeze: Exact pivot sequence, inactivation count, final matrix rank

2. **Insufficient symbols proof vector**:  
   - Input: Incomplete symbol set (K=8, only symbols 0-5 received)
   - Expected: DecodeProof with outcome=InsufficientSymbols, partial peeling trace
   - Freeze: Exact stopping point, missing symbol IDs, rank deficiency

3. **Corrupted symbols proof vector**:
   - Input: Symbol set with 1-2 deliberately corrupted symbols 
   - Expected: DecodeProof with outcome=MatrixSingular or elimination failure
   - Freeze: Point of failure detection, corrupted symbol fingerprint

4. **Bounded artifact vector**:
   - Input: Large decode attempt (MAX_PIVOT_EVENTS exceeded)
   - Expected: DecodeProof with truncated trace, bounded collections
   - Freeze: Exact truncation behavior, artifact size limits

**Implementation**: tests/conformance/raptorq_proof_correctness.rs with deterministic test vectors that validate DecodeProof.replay_and_verify() produces identical artifacts on replay.

**Quality Gate**: Each vector must specify concrete byte-level inputs and expected DecodeProof serialization to freeze the proof system behavior against regressions.

title: [TYPED] Compile-fail proof suite expansion — the negative-space test lane for every type-level guarantee
description:
WHY: type-level guarantees are only real if the ILLEGAL programs provably fail to compile — and stay failing as the compiler/crate evolve. The repo has scattered trybuild coverage (session_types, macros); this bead consolidates it into a first-class lane with the same governance as runtime tests.

WHAT: (1) a unified compile-fail lane: tests/compile_fail/ organized by guarantee family (capability narrowing, session protocols, typestate surfaces, macro misuse, Send/spawn bounds), each case a minimal program + expected-error snapshot; (2) coverage audit: enumerate every type-level guarantee claimed in docs/README (capability gating, two-phase linearity where type-enforced, typestate surfaces from L2, macro contracts) and ensure each has >=1 compile-fail witness — the claim-to-witness table committed + contract-tested against the docs claims; (3) error-message quality gate: expected outputs reviewed for actionability (the compile error IS agent-facing UX — coordinate phrasing standards with [AGENT-DX] B2); (4) toolchain-drift policy: trybuild snapshot churn on toolchain bumps handled by a documented refresh procedure (not ad-hoc).
design: FILES: tests/compile_fail/ tree + a runner test, docs/claim-to-witness table (could live in the test dir README), refresh procedure in TESTING.md. Inventory method: grep docs for guarantee language ('cannot', 'unrepresentable', 'compile-time') -> table rows.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Claim-to-witness table complete (every documented type-level guarantee has a witness or a filed gap-bead). 2. Lane green; >=30 cases across the families (count recorded). 3. Error-message review pass done (actionability notes per case). 4. Toolchain-refresh procedure documented + rehearsed once. 5. Lane wired into standard test runs + TESTING_FOR_AGENTS.
notes: DEPENDS on L1, L2 (their surfaces feed cases) + A10/[DX-CORE] macro cases (consolidates them). This lane is where 'incorrect code is unrepresentable' stops being marketing.

title: QUIC streams audit: out-of-order fragments bounded only per stream (memory DoS), O(S^2) MAX_STREAM_DATA re-send per packet, no transport-error CONNECTION_CLOSE, blocked frames for unopened streams fail, and LOWs
description:
Read-only audit of QUIC streams and flow control (src/net/quic_native/streams.rs and the stream/flow-control frame handling in connection.rs) at origin/main c06414315 (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-03). SapphireHill re-read F1 before fixing it. Handshake, TLS, key update, loss recovery and congestion control were out of scope.

## HIGH
F1. FIXED in this session's stack: out-of-order receive fragments were bounded per stream only (4096), so a peer could keep that many one-byte holes on every stream it may open: about 1M holes, roughly 350 MB of tree and buffer metadata per connection for about 2 MiB of flow-control credit.

## MEDIUM
F2. Every received ack-eliciting packet re-queues MAX_STREAM_DATA for every bounded-window stream, finished ones included, at O(S^2) cost: queue_ack_frame (connection.rs 3479-3489) calls queue_max_stream_data_frame (1248-1263), whose VecDeque::retain scans the whole control queue, for every stream from bounded_recv_window_advertisements (streams.rs 1790-1796), which has no state filter. The HTTP/3 listener gives every accepted stream a bounded window, so S is 256 by default and up to 4224. A peer that opens/finishes S streams and then sends PINGs costs S^2 work per packet and S useless frames per flush. RFC 9000 3.2: no MAX_STREAM_DATA needed in Size Known. Fix: re-attach only for streams with no final size, reset or stop; replace the retain with a per-stream pending index. Pin: bounded_recv_window_advertises_via_reads_and_reattaches_on_acks (connection.rs 4252) stays valid for a live stream.
F3. Stream-layer protocol violations never produce a CONNECTION_CLOSE with the RFC code (FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR, FINAL_SIZE_ERROR, STREAM_LIMIT_ERROR, STREAM_STATE_ERROR, FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR). NativeQuicConnectionError has no transport-code mapping; the managed endpoint logs and continues with the packet partially applied and unacknowledged (managed_endpoint.rs 2633-2637); the UDP driver returns Err and closes with the application code (udp_connection.rs 737-750, 1180-1194).
F4. STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or MAX_STREAM_DATA for a peer stream not yet created fails with UnknownStream instead of opening it (connection.rs 2566-2577, 2655-2673; RFC 9000 3.2). If the first STREAM packet is lost and a later packet carrying STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED arrives first, the UDP driver fails the connection and the managed endpoint drops the packet every time it is retransmitted. Fix: accept_remote_stream (with limit checks) first.
F6. (liveness) Streams without a configured receive window never get more than the initial window: MAX_STREAM_DATA is only generated for streams with recv_window_bytes set (streams.rs 1757-1782); STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED is ignored otherwise (1566-1570). HTTP/3 and ATP opt in; a direct endpoint_api user stalls after initial_max_stream_data bytes. Fix: default to consumption-clocked replenishment.

## LOW
F5. No direction checks for RESET_STREAM on a send-only stream (the app gets a reset event for a stream it can only write), MAX_STREAM_DATA on a receive-only stream, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED on a send-only stream (RFC 19.4, 19.10, 19.13: STREAM_STATE_ERROR).
F7. QuicStreamIo::poll_write is all-or-nothing (streams.rs 2626-2647): a write larger than the remaining credit returns Pending forever if the peer grants credit only after receiving data. Fix: write min(len, capacity).
F8. reset_send accepts a final size larger than what was sent (streams.rs 997-1003); require final_size == send_offset.
F9. STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED is queued without dedup and also when the connection limit is the binding one (should be DATA_BLOCKED, 19.12); stream frames are accepted in any packet-number space (12.4); STREAMS_BLOCKED above 2^60 is not rejected (19.14).

## Suspected
ATP's zero-copy frame slices keep a whole datagram alive per 1-byte fragment (native_link.rs 5261-5262), which made F1 worse for ATP streams; requeue_sent_stream_frame and release_retransmittable_refs scan linearly per lost/acked frame; quic_frames.rs 799-803 casts a STREAM length with `as usize` (32-bit truncation).

## Checked and sound
Duplicate/overlapping data (first copy wins, never delivered twice); final-size rules; receive flow control on the highest offset; limit frames only increase, MAX_STREAMS above 2^60 rejected, remote stream limit enforced; stream-id direction checks for STREAM and STOP_SENDING; STOP_SENDING answered with RESET_STREAM; send credit charged at queue time, identical retransmissions; checked offset arithmetic; wakeups re-checked after registration; per-stream state bounded while MAX_STREAMS is never raised.
close_reason: All actionable items landed and verified: F1 (connection/stream fragment limits), F2 (MAX_STREAM_DATA re-queue state filter), F3 (RFC 9000 transport error codes), RC1 (peer violation close), F4 (accept_remote_stream for blocked/max frames), F5 (direction checks), F7 (poll_write bounded write), F8 (reset_send final_size check), F9 (packet space & blocked frame dedup), length cast try_from, and zero-copy datagram retention bounds. F6 documented as owner decision. All 467 net::quic_native tests passing.

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
SapphireHill e0155ea8, 2026-10-06: F3, F5 and part of F9 LANDED in 52fe5536f.
- F3: a peer frame that breaks a stream, flow-control or frame-encoding rule now closes the connection with the RFC 9000 transport code. Before, the error returned with the connection still open and nothing sent.
  - The connection starts draining before the error returns and records the offending frame type. Its local CONNECTION_CLOSE is the transport variant (0x1c) naming that frame type; an application close stays 0x1d.
  - Codes: FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR, STREAM_LIMIT_ERROR, STREAM_STATE_ERROR, FINAL_SIZE_ERROR, FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR (which includes an unknown frame type and an undecodable payload).
  - The UDP driver flushes the close before it returns the error.
  - The router marks the route's close as requested, and the managed endpoint's next deferred-output turn sends it.
  - Errors with no peer cause, and errors the mapping does not name, keep today's behaviour.
- F5: RESET_STREAM and STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED on a send-only stream, and MAX_STREAM_DATA on a receive-only stream, are STREAM_STATE_ERROR.
- F9 (part): STREAMS_BLOCKED above 2^60 is FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR.
- Tests:
  - peer_stream_violations_close_with_the_transport_error_code: eight cases, plus an unknown frame type;
  - a_local_close_stays_the_application_variant;
  - udp_peer_flow_control_violation_sends_a_transport_close: real sockets; the peer receives FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR;
  - authenticated_peer_flow_control_violation_sends_a_transport_close: the router sends ConnectionClose{0x03, frame type 0x0c}.
- received_max_streams_rejects_unencodable_grants_before_mutation now reads the unchanged credit from the stream table, because the rejected grant closes the connection.
- Control: red at every designed guard (CTL5 b5189f3b9, vmi1152480). All eight violation cases stay Established with no close code; the three F5 frames and STREAMS_BLOCKED above 2^60 are accepted with Ok(()); the UDP and router tests see Established instead of Draining; MAX_STREAMS gets close code None instead of 0x07. a_local_close_stays_the_application_variant passes by design (it is a regression pin with no guard).
Still open:
- F6: liveness with no configured receive window. H3 and ATP replenish credit explicitly, and endpoint_api exposes configure_stream_recv_window and advertise_connection_recv_limit; a default would change on-wire behaviour, so it is an owner call.
- F9 rest: STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED dedup on the write path, DATA_BLOCKED when the connection limit binds, and packet-space checks for stream frames. The last matters only for the legacy plaintext path, since authenticated routes never hand Initial/Handshake payloads to frame processing.
- A frame in the wrong packet space, HANDSHAKE_DONE at a server, and DATAGRAM limit violations still return InvalidState without a close (PROTOCOL_VIOLATION is not mapped).
Pushed in main = master 6add7aa05 (the stack replayed on 544243c87). Receipts are in each commit message: clippy (default and features) and release checks clean; full lib 24490/4, where the 4 failures are main's own (three mpsc tests from d7c139d62 and the grpc owner_cancellation race); 22 QUIC/H3/ATP integration targets green except main's quic_h3_live_udp buffered-deadline attribution red, which fails the same on bare 1db301788 and on 0ded69da2.

SapphireHill e0155ea8, 2026-10-06: a limitation of the F3 landing (52fe5536f), found in a fresh-eyes review.
- The router's requested-close state (LocalCloseOutput::Requested) exists only in builds with tls and either http3 or test.
- In those builds, a route whose connection a peer violation closed sends its transport CONNECTION_CLOSE on the next deferred-output turn of the managed endpoint.
- In a build with tls but without http3, the route drains silently until its drain deadline and sends no close. A plaintext route never sends one, because it has no packet protection.
- The UDP driver (NativeQuicUdpConnection) sends the close in every build.
- If a tls-only managed endpoint needs the close, the fix is to make Requested and its drain_deferred_output branch unconditional on http3.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SapphireHill d0, 2026-10-07: a read-only fresh-eyes review of ff1cbbacd (small payloads copied), verified on origin, found a MEDIUM gap.
The "within 4x" bound does not hold, because the copy threshold is applied to the whole frame BEFORE overlap trimming:
- connection.rs ~2490 and ~3673 compare the frame's len against the datagram.
- QuicStream::insert_recv_bytes (streams.rs ~1085) then keeps only the bytes not yet buffered, as zero-copy sub-slices (insert_recv_gap, ~1112, ~1125).
- RecvRun::compact_if_fragmented (~419) joins a run only once pieces * 64 > len.
Attack (authenticated peer):
1. Buffer an out-of-order run [S, E) of length L.
2. Repeatedly send a STREAM frame in a 64 KiB datagram covering [E-K+1, E+1) with K >= 16 KiB. The frame passes the 4x test, so it is not copied.
3. The receiver keeps a 1-byte slice that pins the whole 64 KiB datagram.
Up to about L/64 such pieces fit before compaction joins them, so pinned memory is about 1024 x L, not 4 x L. For example, a 2 MiB window allows about 2 GiB.
Fix: apply the threshold to each trimmed slice in insert_recv_gap (copy when slice.len() * 4 < backing datagram len), or charge the backing size in RECV_PIECE_OVERHEAD.
Also LOW (6a49ba73a): the two new length tests pass with the old `as usize` code on 64-bit hosts and no lane builds 32-bit, so the regression is not pinned. The fix itself is complete.

title: Native runtime leaks memory: loser-drain and finalizer oracle histories grow without bound (every race and region close appends forever)
description:
Found while working bi2462.89 (SapphireHill, 2026-09-26, source-verified at dc7515a9a).

RuntimeState keeps two histories "for post-run oracle hydration", and both were append-only in every runtime, including native production ones:
- loser_drain_history (LoserDrainHistoryRecorder, src/runtime/state.rs ~446). Every Scope::race / race_all appends RaceStarted (with its participant Vec), one TaskCompleted per participant and RaceCompleted. That covers race!, select!, Cx::race_drained* and the factory form race_drained_with, which also ends in scope.race_all. RuntimeState::new always creates the recorder (~2082), and every Scope spawn wires it into the child Cx (scope.rs ~1541), so this runs on native runtimes, under a global mutex.
- finalizer_history (Vec<FinalizerHistoryEvent>). Every successful region close appends RegionClosed (~9521), and every finalizer appends Registered and Ran.
Nothing ever trimmed either one, and RuntimeState::snapshot() cloned both whole on every snapshot. A server that opens a region or runs a race!/select! per request (the README's tokio::select! replacement) grows by roughly 250-500 B per race plus ~40 B per region close for the life of the process.
Only the lab oracles replay these histories (lab/oracle hydrate_temporal_from_state, lab snapshot_restore, which caps a restorable history at 1,000,000 events).

Fix: native runtimes (RuntimeBuilder::initialize_runtime_state) bound both histories. Every in-flight race and every open region's events are kept whole, and only the most recent N completed races / closed regions are retained (N = 1024, pruned in batches when the tail exceeds 2N). Lab and default RuntimeState construction stay unbounded for oracle replay.
close_reason: Fixed by fdb0b56d4 (landed 458ef9164); control red 2112/2112, fix keeps 1087

FOUND 2026-07-26 by SapphireHill (session b8fa8e96) during the `--all-features` sweep mandated by AGENTS.md after landing br-asupersync-evb4i9.

THE SWEEP: `cargo check --all-targets --all-features --keep-going`, run RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 with `--base HEAD --clean-overlay -o src/database/postgres.rs` so only the evb4i9 fix overlaid pristine HEAD. But `check` is not `clippy`. The sweep emitted 5 warnings that CI's lint-build job WOULD deny, because it runs `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --keep-going -- -D warnings`:

  tests/sqlite_unicode_injection_audit.rs:351:9      unused variable: `cx`
  tests/kafka_producer_idempotence_audit.rs:13:36    unused imports: `KafkaProducer` and `ProducerConfig`
  tests/kafka_producer_idempotence_audit.rs:14:5     unused import: `asupersync::test_utils::run_test_with_cx`
  tests/messaging_kafka_rebalance_lifecycle.rs:26:44 unused import: `RebalanceResult`
  (plus one `unused variable: client_config`)

WHY THESE ARE NOT TRIVIAL. Individually they are one-line deletions. Collectively they mean the `--all-features` clippy gate is RED on main right now, which matters because that gate was just restored to reachability: it had been short-circuited in CI's Check job by an earlier failing step (cleared under br-asupersync-9fhmts), and the lib itself did not compile under `--features postgres` until evb4i9 landed. So this is the first moment the gate can actually run — and it will fail on these.

SCOPE: sqlite- and kafka-gated test targets only. Deliberately NOT folded into br-asupersync-9mvlue, whose scope is the postgres-gated clippy surface and whose no-claim boundary explicitly excludes the kafka/mysql/quic/io-uring graphs.

CARE REQUIRED — DO NOT BLIND-DELETE. An unused import in a test can mean the assertion that used it was dropped, in which case deleting the import hides missing coverage rather than fixing anything:
  - `RebalanceResult` unused in a REBALANCE LIFECYCLE test is suspicious on its face — check whether a rebalance-outcome assertion was removed or never written.
  - `KafkaProducer`/`ProducerConfig` unused in a PRODUCER IDEMPOTENCE test, together with an unused `run_test_with_cx`, suggests the test body may be a stub that never constructs a producer.
  - an unused `cx` in an injection-audit test may mean the audit runs without the capability context it was supposed to exercise.
For each site, establish whether the symbol is genuinely surplus or is the fingerprint of an amputated assertion, and say which in the commit message. If a test turns out to be hollow, that is a bigger finding than the lint and should be filed separately rather than silently made to compile quietly.

title: [ambient-id] types/id.rs: RegionId::new_ephemeral / TaskId::new_ephemeral mint identifiers from process-global static counters — bypasses runtime registration and breaks deterministic replay
description:
src/types/id.rs:13-14 — two process-global atomic counters are used by the public `new_ephemeral` constructors:

  static EPHEMERAL_REGION_COUNTER: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(1);
  static EPHEMERAL_TASK_COUNTER: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(1);

Public surface (id.rs:80-86 and the analogous TaskId::new_ephemeral):
  pub fn new_ephemeral() -> Self {
      let index = EPHEMERAL_REGION_COUNTER.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
      Self(ArenaIndex::new(index, 1))
  }

The asupersync core invariant 'every task/fiber/actor is owned by exactly one region — no orphan tasks' depends on RegionId being minted by the runtime's region table (where the parent pointer, lifecycle state, and budget are tracked atomically with the ID). new_ephemeral mints an unbounded supply of IDs that are NEVER registered with any region table — they are pure ambient identifiers detached from runtime ownership.

Concrete failure modes:
  (a) **Replay non-determinism.** The counter starts at 1 at process boot and advances based on global call ordering. Two replays of the same recorded trace produce different RegionId values because other code in the process consumed counter slots between runs. Lab-replay byte-identity invariant is silently violated.

  (b) **Bypassed registration.** A nextjs-bootstrap request handler, a wasm-browser preview, or a CLI utility can mint a 'fresh' RegionId, attach a Cx to it, and pass it to runtime APIs (record_trace_event, supervision oracles, leak detector). Those APIs then operate on a region that has no entry in state.regions — producing oracle violations or panics in regions().get().

  (c) **Ambient authority surface.** new_ephemeral has no `&Cx` parameter. Anyone in the codebase can mint identifiers without holding any capability. This is the textbook violation of 'effects require explicit capabilities flowing through Cx'.

The doc comment explicitly notes the intent: 'production request handling that needs unique identifiers without full runtime region registration' — but that intent contradicts the structured-concurrency contract the rest of the runtime depends on.

Fix direction:
  1. Move new_ephemeral behind a capability-scoped issuer: `Cx::ephemeral_region_id() -> RegionId` that draws from a per-Cx counter (deterministic + replayable).
  2. Or: deprecate new_ephemeral entirely and require all RegionId/TaskId values to come from the runtime's create_root_region / create_task path.
  3. Audit all callers of `new_ephemeral` in production code paths and rewrite them to take a Cx.
  4. Add a regression test that asserts: `Cx::current()` is required to mint any identifier reachable from oracles.

Source: /reality-check-for-project on src/types/* (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Fixed in 9aecc9f1e: RegionId::new_ephemeral and TaskId::new_ephemeral are now gated to cfg(any(test, feature='test-internals')) + #[doc(hidden)]. Runtime-internal bootstrap (app.rs::build_app_root_cx) uses new pub(crate) next_bootstrap_region_id / next_bootstrap_task_id helpers; the counter stays crate-internal. Production code must use runtime-arena IDs.

title: Missing narrow structure-aware fuzzer for PriorityFrame::parse (RFC 9113 §6.3)
description: fuzz/fuzz_targets has wide coverage of PriorityFrame BEHAVIOUR (h2_priority_*.rs files exercise dependency cycles, max weight, idle streams, etc.) but no narrow STRUCTURE-AWARE fuzzer for PriorityFrame::parse alone. Existing h2_frame_*.rs fuzzers either parse the full Frame enum or test high-level scenarios. PriorityFrame::parse has tight RFC 9113 §6.3 invariants worth pinning at the parser boundary: exact 5-byte payload (else stream FRAME_SIZE_ERROR), reserved high bit of dependency word stored as exclusive flag (high bit must be CLEARED in dependency field), self-dependency (stream depends on itself) rejected as stream PROTOCOL_ERROR, stream_id == 0 rejected as connection PROTOCOL_ERROR. Add fuzz/fuzz_targets/h2_priority_frame_parse_roundtrip.rs as a structure-aware Arbitrary-driven target: arbitrary FrameHeader + 5-byte payload + arbitrary additional-bytes-out-of-band, encode+parse round-trip for valid inputs, parse-only for malformed, asserting per-invariant error categories.

Asserts RFC 9113 §6.3 invariants at the parser boundary: stream_id==0 → connection PROTOCOL_ERROR, payload!=5 bytes → stream FRAME_SIZE_ERROR, exclusive bit must NOT leak into returned dependency field, self-dependency → stream PROTOCOL_ERROR. On well-formed inputs runs encode→FrameHeader::parse→PriorityFrame::parse round-trip and asserts the (stream_id, exclusive, dependency, weight) tuple is a fixed point. close_reason: Landed 5c1975ec4: delta chunk builders fill whole chunks via read_full_chunk; RED e2e (peer closed mid-transfer) on old code, GREEN rq loopback 14/0/1, lib delta units 115/0, contract+CDC 17/0, clippy + fmt clean

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
Found (SapphireHill, 2026-09-10T07:00Z) by the sizeku delta re-sync gate (scripts/atp_bench/resync_bench.sh, rq transport, run /data/tmp/atp_resync_bench/20260910T064934Z_sizeku): all six atp re-sync cells (5M and 100M x 1pct/append/insert) aborted in ~0.1 s. Receiver: "atp failed: frame error: malformed RQ delta chunk at position 0"; sender: "peer closed control connection mid-transfer". The rsync lane of every cell passed, and the atp INITIAL (full) syncs passed, so only the delta negotiation is broken.

Root cause: the delta chunk manifest builders read a file in `chunk_size` buffers and treated ONE AsyncReadExt::read as one chunk (transport_rq build_rq_delta_manifest_for_file with RQ_DELTA_CHUNK_SIZE = 1 MiB - 12; the same loop shape in transport_tcp at the sender manifest builder and the receiver CAS chunker, and in transport_quic's delta manifest builder). Since 59383b93d / 81a7353e8 (2026-09-02, "offload poll-based AsyncRead/AsyncWrite/AsyncSeek file traits to blocking pool"; in v0.4.11, not in v0.4.10) crate::fs::File's poll_read submits at most POLL_IO_CHUNK_BYTES = 128 KiB per hop, so a 1 MiB read returns 131072 bytes and chunk 0 is advertised as 131072 bytes. The receiver's validate_rq_delta_manifest requires every non-final chunk to equal delta.chunk_size (a4c838345, wajozf) and rejects position 0. Every file larger than 128 KiB is affected; the existing loopback delta tests use 79 KiB payloads, which fit one read, so nothing in the suite noticed. The whole-object paths are unaffected: the QUIC/native-link source streaming loops and the TCP/RQ full transfers consume whatever each read returns.

Fix (working tree): transport_common::delta::read_full_chunk fills the buffer until full or EOF; the four chunk builders read through it (rq 1 site, tcp 2 sites, quic 1 site). The validator is unchanged: fixed-size chunks remain the wire contract. Tests: unit read_full_chunk_fills_the_buffer_across_short_reads (a reader capped at 128 KiB per poll; 300 000 bytes -> chunks 262144 + 37856 + EOF) and the public-API reproducer authenticated_delta_fallback_survives_files_larger_than_one_file_read in tests/atp_rq_loopback_e2e.rs (1 300 000-byte payload, delta enabled on both sides, destination differs -> full fallback must commit; old code fails at the manifest). RED = HEAD + the e2e file only; GREEN = all five files: rq loopback e2e target, lib -- delta filter, the delta public-contract and CDC test targets, strict clippy, fmt. Escaped-defect notes: found by the in-repo bench, not a downstream report; the 0.4.11 regression means every `atp` delta re-sync of a file > 128 KiB fails on 0.4.11, which should go in the release notes and, if 0.4.12 is cut, its headline.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SapphireHill, diagnosis from the failing runs. The failures have independent causes; raising one timeout would not fix them:
1. symbol_durable_process.rs:134 "worker readiness: Timeout". The replica subprocess must print READY within 10 s. Its startup creates a journal (file sync_all plus directory sync_all in journal_path) and binds TLS. On a worker with slow fsync (hz3 p99 around 5 s, measured 09-2x), that plausibly exceeds 10 s.
2. continuation.rs:230, ConnectionRefused (os 111) on the FIRST run_scoped connect to the Sink. The Sink binds its listener before returning, so a refused connect means the Sink worker thread had already exited and dropped the listener. Candidates: an accept error other than WouldBlock (for example EMFILE under parallel tests, which returns Err at once), or its 45 s deadline. It needs an eprintln of the worker's exit reason to tell which.
3. continuation.rs:318 "actual Pending effect read: Timeout" (8 s), plus the revocation-owner panic at :293, which is its consequence. The workload's first Pending effect did not reach the sink within 8 s.
Next step: log each harness exit reason (Sink worker result, subprocess stderr on readiness timeout, elapsed times), then reproduce with several copies of the suite in parallel on one worker. Only after that, widen the bounds that are pure liveness guards (readiness, effect read). The lease and shutdown bounds carry semantics.

CONTRAST: nocrypto rq tier converges + WINS on identical netem (500M/broken 565s WIN, 50M/broken 58s WIN, MATRIX-209/212) because its repair/feedback loop rides the reliable TCP control channel with honest arrival-based loss accounting + calibrated round-0 FEC + targeted sparse retransmits (MATRIX-207 stack). The QUIC tier's converging cells all ride the reliable source stream; at >=5M/broken the loss target pushes it to the datagram/FEC path whose repair loop (round markers + NeedMore over lossy 1-RTT datagrams + per-block repair) still wedges/crawls — the MATRIX-170 wedge class was fixed for the e2e proxy but real netem cells still fail. FIX DIRECTION (from the rq playbook): port the MATRIX-207 stack to the QUIC datagram path — arrival-evidence loss accounting, right-sized round-0 FEC (alpha 0.02), targeted sparse source retransmits, PTO-robust round markers (partially done), receiver-driven repair requests independent of markers; and/or extend source-stream eligibility upward with the bounded window now that recovery is window-capped. The 363s uniform failure signature = ATP idle-timeout class, worth one ATP_QUIC_TRACE forensic run on 5M/broken to pin the wedge point.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-07-06, SapphireHill) — NOT the datagram/FEC repair loop. All failing cells ride the reliable SOURCE STREAM (stream eligibility was raised to 8GiB/0.30-loss on 2026-06-29, 596a37b15, before the gate39 sweep; the CLI maps atp-quic-tls13 to TransportAuthenticated at src/bin/atp.rs:834 so the stream gate passes at 10% loss). Forensic ATP_QUIC_TRACE on 5M/broken: RECEIVER DIED AT 5.02s wall (/usr/bin/time) with 'transport timeout during receive QUIC source stream after 360s' — udp_packets_received=245, one_rtt_packets_ingested=244, unprotect_packets_dropped=1, while stream data was still arriving. Sender then retransmitted into the void for 359s to its own real 360s idle timeout = the uniform ~363s cell signature. MECHANISM: pump_inbound_for_with_drain_budget (native_link.rs) counts only *successfully processed* 1-RTT packets; a batch whose packets ALL fail unprotect/decode (netem-mangled/stale/dup — InboundPacketDecode::Dropped) yields processed=0, then the received_len<receive_limit fast-exit returns Ok(0) after ONE socket read — and callers (read_native_source_stream_chunk et al) escalate 0 to a fatal idle-timeout. One junk UDP packet arriving alone kills the session: deterministic within seconds at 10% loss (all ≥5M/broken cells), probabilistic at 500K (2/5), rare-per-packet but certain over ~500K packets at 500M/bad (0/3@900s). FIX (landed in working tree): zero-progress deadline in the pump — a dropped-only batch re-arms the wait with the REMAINING allowance instead of returning 0; Ok(0) now genuinely means the full timeout elapsed. Regression test: real_udp_quic_transfer_survives_solo_undecryptable_junk_packets (tests/atp_quic_real_udp_transfer_e2e.rs) sprays 1-RTT-shaped junk at the receiver through a 4MiB loopback transfer. title: [mock-code-finder] Final gap closure signoff and ratchet proof
description:

It should run only after subsystem beads have either shipped real implementation/conformance fixes or produced explicit blocker beads. Its purpose is to prove that no fake, stale, or placeholder code remains in surfaces claiming production behavior or conformance.

title: MPSC audit (r12): Sender::closed() can miss a racing close on weak-memory targets; Receiver::drop skips waking parked reservers when its own waker's destructor panics
description:
Read-only audit of src/channel/mpsc.rs and src/channel/mpsc_closed.rs (focus on 8231eec0e, "wake idle producers when MPSC receivers close") at origin/main c5cf7f175 (SapphireHill rc_20260923 audit agent, 10-08). No HIGH or MEDIUM. Close paths, Notify generation guard, Reserve vs close, permit/obligation accounting and waiter-queue integrity checked and sound.

## LOW
L1. Sender::closed() can miss a racing close on weak-memory targets (mpsc_closed.rs ~40-47 and WakeClosed::drop ~68-70). The Notify is created lazily by the first waiter; the closer signals only if notify.get() sees it. Waiter: is_closed() false, get_or_init, wait_until reads the generation, predicate is_closed() (Acquire) false, parks. Closer: stores receiver_dropped (Release), unlocks, notify.get() (Acquire) sees INCOMPLETE and returns. Both reads seeing the old value is a store-buffering outcome the C++/Rust model allows without SeqCst; x86 and ARMv8 cannot produce it in practice, POWER and RISC-V can. The waiter then stays parked although the channel is closed. Fix: after get_or_init in closed(), take and release the channel mutex once (the closer sets the flag under it), or SeqCst fences on both sides. No deterministic test; a Miri many-seeds loop might show it.
L2. Receiver::drop (mpsc.rs ~2124-2147, older than 8231eec0e, from aaf84e11b) drops the receiver's own waker before wake_detached(wakers). A receiver waker whose destructor panics unwinds past the fan-out, so every parked reserve drained from the queue is never woken (and during an existing unwind the process aborts, the 9siwk7 class). close_receiver chains recv_waker into wake_detached and is not affected. Fix: retire recv_waker under catch_unwind, run wake_detached, then resume the panic. Deterministic test: channel(1), try_reserve to fill, park a reserve with a counting waker, poll_recv with a waker that panics on drop holding the last reference, catch_unwind(drop(rx)), assert the reserve was woken and then reports Disconnected.
close_reason: done

- L2: Retired recv_waker under catch_unwind in Receiver::drop so a panicking waker destructor cannot prevent parked sender/reserver wakeups or trigger double-unwind process aborts.

title: Missing TE.TE different-values smuggling test (Transfer-Encoding: chunked + Transfer-Encoding: identity)
description: src/http/h1/codec.rs reject_duplicate_transfer_encoding (line 1825) tests TWO IDENTICAL 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' headers, which is the easy case. The HIGH-RISK smuggling primitive is DIFFERENT values across duplicate Transfer-Encoding header lines — e.g., 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' + 'Transfer-Encoding: identity'. Front-end and back-end proxies disagree on which header wins (first vs last vs first-non-identity), and the gap creates a CL.TE/TE.TE smuggle. Asupersync's transfer_and_content_length() rejects ANY second TE line with DuplicateTransferEncoding so the smuggle is blocked, but no test pins this for the different-values case. Add tests/h1_te_te_smuggling_audit.rs covering: (a) chunked + identity (different values, smuggling-relevant), (b) chunked, identity in a single header (RFC §6.1: chunked must be the FINAL coding — asupersync rejects all multi-coding via require_transfer_encoding_chunked), (c) Transfer-Encoding then transfer-encoding (case-insensitive header name MUST also be rejected as duplicate), (d) Transfer-Encoding split with CR-LF in value (header injection) — must be rejected at validation.
close_reason: Landed in 2162ba46b. tests/h1_te_te_smuggling_audit.rs adds 7 cases per RFC 9112 §6.1/§5.1/§7.1 + RFC 9110 §5.1/§5.5: chunked+identity TE.TE, identity+chunked, chunked,identity in one line, case-insensitive duplicate, header-value CRLF injection smuggling TE, whitespace-before-colon TE, plus a positive control (mixed-case Chunked must still parse as chunked). cargo check --test h1_te_te_smuggling_audit passes (compile clean in isolation). title: Design TraceEvent schema for recording
description:
## Overview

Design the TraceEvent enum that captures all sources of non-determinism in the Lab runtime.

## Background

For deterministic replay, we need to capture every decision point that could vary between runs. The existing trace module provides some infrastructure, but we need a comprehensive schema that covers all non-determinism.

## Sources of Non-Determinism to Capture

### Scheduling Decisions
- Which task was chosen when multiple are ready
- Task spawn ordering
- Task completion notification ordering

### Time Events
- Virtual time advances
- Timer creation and expiration
- Deadline checks

### I/O Simulation
- Simulated I/O results (success, error, bytes)
- I/O ordering when multiple pending

### RNG
- Deterministic RNG seed
- Each RNG call result (for verification)

### External Inputs
- Any future injection points
- Test oracle responses

## Deliverables

1. `TraceEvent` enum with variants for each category
2. `TraceMetadata` struct with version, timestamp, runtime config
3. Serialization derive macros (serde)
4. Size estimation (traces should be compact)

## Implementation Notes

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum TraceEvent {
    // Scheduling
    TaskScheduled { task_id: TaskId, at_tick: u64 },
    TaskYielded { task_id: TaskId },
    TaskCompleted { task_id: TaskId, outcome: Outcome<()> },
    
    // Time
    TimeAdvanced { from: u64, to: u64 },
    TimerCreated { id: u64, deadline: u64 },
    TimerFired { id: u64 },
    
    // I/O (simulated)
    IoResult { token: u64, result: SimulatedIoResult },
    
    // RNG
    RngSeed { seed: u64 },
    RngValue { value: u64 },
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All non-determinism sources identified and covered
- [ ] Events are compact (estimate < 64 bytes typical)
- [ ] Format is versioned for forward compatibility
- [ ] Unit tests for serialization round-trip

title: [http][client][SECURITY] default_headers Authorization/Cookie leak to cross-origin redirect target
description: VERIFIED (SapphireHill, fresh-eyes HTTP client security review). src/http/h1/http_client.rs build_request (1913) re-applies the client-wide self.config.default_headers on EVERY request including redirect targets, filtered only for name==host and names already in extra_headers (1948-1955) — with NO origin check. strip_sensitive_headers_on_redirect (3009) correctly strips Authorization/Cookie/Proxy-Authorization on cross-origin redirect but is applied ONLY to the per-request extra_headers (1458 buffered, 1562 streaming), NOT to default_headers. default_header() (748) accepts any name incl. Authorization. Default policy Limited(10) follows cross-origin redirects. ATTACK: HttpClient built with .default_header("Authorization", "Bearer <token>") (normal one-API-one-token setup); request to https://good/ returns 302 Location: https://attacker/ (or downgrade to http://good/); execute_with_redirects strips extra_headers but build_request re-injects the default Authorization -> bearer token sent to attacker. Same for a default Cookie / Proxy-Authorization. Violates the invariant the code documents for itself at 3004-3008. HIGH: credential exfiltration; only triggers when the credential is a client-wide DEFAULT (per-request creds ARE correctly stripped). FIX: strip sensitive default_headers when the redirect target is cross-origin vs the ORIGINAL origin (consecutive-hop comparison has a hole: a same-origin hop within a foreign origin re-injects the default). Thread the original origin (Option<&ParsedUrl>, None=initial) through execute_with_redirects(+streaming) -> execute_single(+streaming/retry/proxy variants, ~5 build_request callers) -> build_request; in build_request add sensitive names to the default_headers exclusion when Some(origin) && !same_origin(origin, parsed) (reuse same_origin @2988). TEST REQUIRED: a NEW test — client with default Authorization, server 302 to a different host AND an https->http downgrade, assert the redirect-target request carries NO Authorization/Cookie/Proxy-Authorization (and that a same-origin redirect DOES carry them). Quiet file (last touched 2026-09-12, clean tree). EVERYTHING ELSE DEFENDED (verified): per-request auth/cookie stripping (3009 via same_origin scheme+host+port), cookie-jar host-exact scope + Secure-over-http filter, redirect bound (10) TooManyRedirects, 301/302/303->GET vs 307/308 method/body, scheme validation (only http/https, file: treated as path), TLS verification preserved+non-disableable across redirect (new host = new SNI + pool key). LOW: no SSRF guard by design (follows Location to loopback/link-local — flag only if user-supplied URLs); cookie Path attribute ignored (same-host, non-cross-origin).
close_reason: Fixed + fully verified. Threaded origin: Option<&ParsedUrl> through execute_with_redirects(+streaming) -> execute_single/retry/streaming/proxy -> build_request_with_origin with original-origin pinning; strips client-wide default Authorization/Cookie/Proxy-Authorization on a cross-origin (different host OR https->http downgrade) redirect target while keeping the host-scoped cookie-jar fallback. Commits 434055b2d/ea15dd411/af8d3d430. EVIDENCE: (1) non-test 'cargo check -p asupersync' under RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings GREEN on hz3 (exit 0) - compile + dead_code(#[cfg(test)] wrapper) clean; (2) regression test build_request_with_origin_strips_default_credentials_cross_origin RAN GREEN on native lib-test (vmi1149989): 'test result: ok. 1 passed' - initial+same-origin retain creds, different-host+downgrade strip all three, non-sensitive default forwarded; (3) independent static review by CopperOak (mail 6542) confirming all 4 redirect paths + cookie fallback. CopperOak review fixes applied (cfg(test) wrapper, eq_ignore_ascii_case). Behavioral run was delayed by unrelated fleet infra + CopperOak's red lib-test (their 1639b0f66 fixed it).

title: [conformance-gap] raptorq/rfc6330.rs: deg() degree-distribution conformance only spot-checks 4 boundary values — no statistical test against RFC 6330 §5.3.5.2 f[] table histogram
description: src/raptorq/rfc6330.rs:201 fn deg(v) implements the RFC 6330 §5.3.5.2 degree generator. Tests at lines 603-620 only spot-check 4 boundary thresholds: deg(0)=1, deg(5242)=1, deg(5243)=2, deg(1048575)=30. There is NO statistical-distribution conformance test that samples N random v values (e.g., 100_000) and asserts the resulting degree histogram matches the RFC 6330 §5.3.5.2 f[] cumulative table within statistical tolerance (chi-squared or Kolmogorov-Smirnov). A subtle off-by-one in any of the 30 f[] thresholds (or a wrong cumulative range) would silently bias the degree distribution — the receiver would still decode correctly for most inputs but the failure-rate analysis vs RFC's claimed bound would be invalid AND the wire format would diverge from any other RFC-conformant implementation. Mitigation: add a test that draws 100_000 samples from deg(rand_v) and asserts the per-degree count distribution is within 5σ of the RFC's expected counts (where σ is the binomial standard deviation for that bin's expected probability). Severity HIGH for cross-implementation interoperability and decode-failure-rate calibration.
close_reason: Fixed in 3c291c03c. Added deg_distribution_matches_rfc_thresholds_within_5_sigma at src/raptorq/rfc6330.rs. Test draws N=200_000 samples from a deterministic LCG (Numerical Recipes ranqd1 constants, seed 0xCAFEF00DDEADBEEF for reproducible failures), maps each to [0, 2^20) matching the Rand[X, 0, 2^20] domain, calls deg(v), and accumulates a 31-element histogram. For each degree 1..=30, computes expected count = N * (threshold[d] - threshold[d-1]) / 2^20 and asserts |observed - expected| < 5σ where σ = sqrt(expected) (binomial standard deviation). Also asserts histogram total == N (catches off-by-one if any sample falls outside ALL thresholds) and histogram[0] == 0 (catches deg() returning 0 which is invalid per RFC 6330 §5.3.5.2). The 5σ bound gives a flake rate < 1 in 3.5M while still catching distribution drift > 0.5% in any single bin. Threshold values hardcoded from RFC 6330 DEGREE_TABLE so any future edit to that table without a parallel test edit triggers a clear assertion failure with bin/expected/observed/sigma in the message. Lib build still has unrelated pre-existing concurrent-agent 'method contains is never used' error. UBS clean (1 critical loose-equality finding is JS-rule false positive).

title: [cardinality-leak] observability/cancellation_tracer.rs entity_traces HashMap unbounded by user-controllable entity_id
description:
src/observability/cancellation_tracer.rs:352 — start_trace() inserts into:

  entity_traces: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, Vec<CancellationTraceId>>>>

keyed by root_entity (a user-controllable string passed in by the caller). The HashMap is never culled when the corresponding traces complete. completed_traces VecDeque IS bounded by max_traces (line 474), but entity_traces is not.

Threat: an attacker (or a noisy production caller) that uses high-cardinality entity IDs (per-request UUIDs, per-user identifiers, etc.) accumulates one HashMap entry per unique value forever. The Vec<CancellationTraceId> values associated with each key may become stale (referring to traces evicted from completed_traces), but the keys themselves never go away. Heap memory grows unbounded.

Concrete failure modes:
  (a) Production runtime memory bloat over uptime; eventually OOM in the observability subsystem.
  (b) On forced shutdown / debug dump, the HashMap serializes to a huge artifact that may exceed log-rotation limits.
  (c) Lookup operations () become measurably slower as the table grows beyond cache-friendly sizes.

Fix direction:
  1. Apply a cardinality cap MAX_ENTITY_TRACES (e.g., 1024 active entities) and evict entries when the bound is hit. LRU on last-trace-completion time is a natural choice.
  2. Or: cull entity_traces entries whenever a trace is evicted from completed_traces — keeping the two structures size-coupled.
  3. Or: store the entity-trace inverse index as a tombstoned reverse lookup that is rebuilt periodically rather than maintained incrementally.

Severity HIGH because (a) reachable from public start_trace() API, (b) an attacker who can influence entity IDs (e.g., by issuing requests with controlled headers) can induce unbounded memory growth, and (c) the same cardinality-bound pattern was already filed and fixed for otel CardinalityTracker (br-bs92bg) — this is the same anti-pattern in a sibling structure.

Source: /multi-pass-bug-hunting on src/observability/* deepest pass (2026-04-26).

Existing regression test uae0hk_entity_traces_cap_with_overflow_bucket at line 1508 covers the cap behavior. Closing as already-applied.

title: OWNER decision: give the HTTP/2 listener a default stream_idle_timeout (today None: one idle open stream disables the connection idle timeout)
description:
Split from asupersync-hw83se (its last open item) and noted in asupersync-bi2462.102 as 'known and still present'.

Http2ListenerConfig::stream_idle_timeout defaults to None (src/http/h2/listener.rs, config default ~4373; setter ~4487: 'None disables it'). With None, a request stream that stays open without progress keeps the connection alive past the connection idle timeout, which is a slow-client and slowloris lever. .102 added preface and write-progress deadlines and a per-response DATA-credit deadline, but none of them covers an idle request stream.

Decision needed (v0.4.3 compatibility gate: a new default is observable behaviour):
A. Keep None and document the risk and the recommended setting in the listener docs (compatible).
B. Default to a bounded value (e.g. 60 s; existing streaming handlers that legitimately idle longer must opt out with None). Needs release-note coverage and a downstream check.
C. Keep None in Http2ListenerConfig::default() and add an explicitly hardened preset (e.g. Http2ListenerConfig::hardened()) that sets it. Additive and compatible.
Recommendation: C, or A plus C.

title: io_uring reactor ignores Interest::EDGE_TRIGGERED: every completion disarms until modify, so a new edge after a drain is lost (epoll delivers it)
description:
IoUringReactor accepts Interest::EDGE_TRIGGERED but ignores it. Every poll completion disarms the registration until the caller calls modify (src/runtime/reactor/io_uring.rs ~1883-1903 for the interest mapping, ~1975-1977 for the disarm). So after an edge is delivered and the socket drained, a NEW edge produces no event unless the caller re-arms. EpollReactor maps the flag to real EPOLLET (epoll.rs ~252-257) and delivers the next edge without modify.

The Reactor trait (mod.rs ~930-933) documents non-edge registrations as oneshot and re-armed by modify, which implies edge registrations are not oneshot. A caller that relies on the documented edge mode loses wakeups on io_uring.

Found by the production-backed reactor conformance suite (bi2462.144), contract `edge_triggered_redelivers_after_drain`. It runs epoll and io_uring and compares them. That row is ExpectedGap with this bead id until fixed. Options: implement edge mode with multishot poll (IORING_POLL_ADD_MULTI) or an automatic re-arm after each completion, or refuse EDGE_TRIGGERED on io_uring with a typed error and document it.
close_reason: Fixed by ac01e7857 (main=master): EDGE_TRIGGERED (without ONESHOT) is one multishot PollAdd with EPOLLET; F_MORE handling with fd-checked re-arm; AsyncCancel for multishot on modify/deregister; Linux 5.13+ probe. Receipts: lib uring 47/0 on a live kernel (vmi1149989, 10 new edge tests), conformance io_uring edge row + io_uring_vs_epoll differential Pass (ovh-a); old-red strict rows on unfixed io_uring FAILED 'delivered it as oneshot'; clippy io-uring and default clean; no io_uring.rs ledger drift.

title: [EPIC-INFRA] Symbol Broadcast Cancellation
description:
# EPIC: Symbol Broadcast Cancellation

**Bead ID:** asupersync-ucq
**Type:** EPIC
**Priority:** P1
**Status:** OPEN
**Owner:** Dicklesworthstone

---

## Vision

Symbol Broadcast Cancellation implements asupersync's cancel-correctness guarantee for distributed symbol operations. When an encoding, transmission, or decoding operation is cancelled, the cancellation must propagate correctly to all participants, cleanup must occur on both sender and receiver sides, and peers must be notified that an object transfer is being abandoned.

The fundamental principle is that cancellation is a protocol, not silent data loss. When you cancel a symbol stream, you're not just stopping your local work - you're communicating intent to the distributed system. Receivers need to know they can discard partial symbol sets. Senders need to stop generating and transmitting symbols. Resource managers need to release memory and network resources.

This EPIC defines how cancellation tokens are embedded in symbol metadata for cross-process propagation, how cancellation broadcasts efficiently reach all participants, and how cleanup coordination ensures no orphaned resources remain. The result is a system where cancellation is as well-defined and reliable as successful completion.

---

## Goals

- **Embed cancellation tokens in symbol metadata** for cross-process propagation
- **Implement broadcast semantics** for efficiently cancelling all participants in a symbol stream
- **Coordinate cleanup** on both sender and receiver sides
- **Bound cleanup time** ensuring cancellation completes within budget
- **Integrate with existing cancellation** (`Cx` context, structured concurrency)
- **Provide observable cancellation state** for monitoring and debugging

---

## Non-Goals

- **Reliable cancellation delivery**: Best-effort broadcast is acceptable for lossy networks
- **Consensus-based cancellation**: This is advisory, not authoritative
- **Transaction rollback**: Cancellation stops work; it doesn't undo completed work
- **Persistent cancellation state**: Cancellation is transient runtime state
- **Automatic retry after cancellation**: Retry is application-level decision

---

## Child Beads

| ID | Title | Status | Priority | Description |
|----|-------|--------|----------|-------------|
| asupersync-uls | Implement Symbol Broadcast Cancellation Protocol | OPEN | P1 | Core cancellation tokens, broadcast, cleanup coordination |

---

## Phases

### Phase 1: Cancellation Token Design
**Duration:** 0.5 sprint
**Deliverables:**
- `CancelToken` that can be embedded in symbol metadata
- `CancelReason` enum categorizing why cancellation occurred
- `CancelTokenSource` for creating and triggering tokens
- Integration with `CancelKind` from existing runtime

**Exit Criteria:**
- Tokens can be created, cloned, and embedded
- Triggering a token propagates to all clones
- Tokens serialize/deserialize for network transmission

### Phase 2: Broadcast Protocol
**Duration:** 1 sprint
**Deliverables:**
- `CancelBroadcaster` for propagating cancellation to all stream participants
- Symbol-embedded cancellation via metadata
- Out-of-band cancellation channel
- Best-effort delivery semantics

**Exit Criteria:**
- Cancellation reaches all registered participants
- Broadcast completes within bounded time
- Network failures don't prevent local cleanup

### Phase 3: Cleanup Coordination
**Duration:** 1 sprint
**Deliverables:**
- `SymbolStreamCanceller` orchestrating sender-side cleanup
- `ReceiveCancellationHandler` orchestrating receiver-side cleanup
- Partial symbol set cleanup
- Resource release protocol

**Exit Criteria:**
- All resources released on cancellation
- No orphaned partial state
- Cleanup completes within budget

---

## Success Criteria

1. **Propagation Correctness**: Cancellation signal reaches all participants that received any symbol
2. **Bounded Cleanup**: Cleanup completes within 2x the cancellation budget
3. **Resource Release**: No memory or network resources leak after cancellation
4. **Observability**: Cancellation state is queryable for debugging
5. **Idempotency**: Multiple cancel calls are safe and have same effect
6. **Integration**: Works seamlessly with `cx.cancelled()` and structured concurrency
7. **Best-Effort Tolerance**: System remains correct even if some cancellation broadcasts are lost

---

## Dependencies

### Depends On
- **asupersync-0vx** (Foundation Layer) - Symbol types for metadata embedding
- **asupersync-7gm** (Transport Layer) - Transport for cancellation broadcast
- `src/cx/cancel.rs` - Existing `CancelToken` infrastructure
- `src/types/id.rs` - `CancelKind`, `CancelReason` types

### Blocks
- **asupersync-9mq** (Integration) - Cancellation in unified API

---

## Acceptance Criteria Checklist

### Symbol Broadcast Cancellation Protocol (asupersync-uls)

#### Cancellation Token Types
- [ ] `CancelToken` with unique ID and triggered state
- [ ] `CancelTokenSource` for creating tokens and triggering cancellation
- [ ] `CancelReason` enum: Timeout, UserRequest, ResourceExhausted, UpstreamFailure, EpochExpiry
- [ ] `is_triggered()` check without blocking
- [ ] `triggered_reason()` returns reason if triggered
- [ ] `wait_triggered()` async wait for cancellation
- [ ] Cloning shares underlying state (like Arc)
- [ ] Serialization for network embedding

#### Cancellation Metadata
- [ ] `CancelMetadata` struct embedded in symbol headers
- [ ] Token ID and triggered state in metadata
- [ ] Reason code for debugging
- [ ] Source task/region for tracing
- [ ] Compact serialization (<32 bytes overhead)

#### Broadcast Mechanism
- [ ] `CancelBroadcaster` tracks participants per object/stream
- [ ] `register_participant(object_id, endpoint)` for tracking
- [ ] `broadcast_cancel(object_id, reason)` sends to all participants
- [ ] Best-effort delivery: fire-and-forget semantics
- [ ] Bounded broadcast time via timeout
- [ ] Out-of-band cancel channel separate from symbol stream

#### Sender-Side Cleanup
- [ ] `SymbolStreamCanceller` for encoding pipeline
- [ ] Stop generating new symbols immediately
- [ ] Abort in-flight symbol transmissions
- [ ] Release encoding resources (memory pools)
- [ ] Broadcast cancellation to registered receivers
- [ ] Report cancellation stats (symbols sent, symbols aborted)

#### Receiver-Side Cleanup
- [ ] `ReceiveCancellationHandler` for decoding pipeline
- [ ] Listen for cancellation on symbol stream and out-of-band channel
- [ ] Discard partial symbol sets for cancelled objects
- [ ] Release decoding resources (buffers, partial state)
- [ ] Acknowledge cancellation receipt (optional, best-effort)
- [ ] Report cancellation stats (symbols received, symbols discarded)

#### Integration with Cx
- [ ] `cx.with_cancel_token(token)` for propagating token through context
- [ ] Token automatically embedded in symbols sent from context
- [ ] `cx.check_cancelled()` checks both Cx cancellation and token
- [ ] Structured concurrency: child task cancellation propagates

#### Testing
- [ ] Unit tests for token creation and triggering
- [ ] Unit tests for broadcast to multiple participants
- [ ] Integration tests for end-to-end cancellation
- [ ] Tests for partial symbol set cleanup
- [ ] Tests for concurrent cancellation race conditions

---

## Cancellation Flow

```
SENDER                          NETWORK                         RECEIVER
  │                                                                 │
  │  ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ │
  │  Normal operation: symbols flowing                              │
  │  ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ │
  │                                                                 │
  │                                                                 │
  │ ┌─────────────────────┐                                        │
  │ │ Cancel triggered    │                                        │
  │ │ (timeout/user/etc)  │                                        │
  │ └─────────────────────┘                                        │
  │           │                                                     │
  │           ▼                                                     │
  │ ┌─────────────────────┐      ┌─────────────────────┐           │
  │ │ Stop encoding       │      │ Broadcast cancel    │───────────│───┐
  │ │ new symbols         │      │ to all receivers    │           │   │
  │ └─────────────────────┘      └─────────────────────┘           │   │
  │           │                                                     │   │
  │           │                                                     │   │
  │           ▼                                                     │   ▼
  │ ┌─────────────────────┐                              ┌─────────────────────┐
  │ │ Abort in-flight     │                              │ Cancel received     │
  │ │ transmissions       │                              │ or detected         │
  │ └─────────────────────┘                              └─────────────────────┘
  │           │                                                     │
  │           ▼                                                     ▼
  │ ┌─────────────────────┐                              ┌─────────────────────┐
  │ │ Release encoding    │                              │ Discard partial     │
  │ │ resources           │                              │ symbol set          │
  │ └─────────────────────┘                              └─────────────────────┘
  │           │                                                     │
  │           ▼                                                     ▼
  │ ┌─────────────────────┐                              ┌─────────────────────┐
  │ │ Report cancellation │                              │ Release decoding    │
  │ │ stats               │                              │ resources           │
  │ └─────────────────────┘                              └─────────────────────┘
  │                                                                 │
  │  ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ │
  │  Cancellation complete: no orphaned resources                   │
  │  ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ │
```

---

## Cancellation Detection Strategies

### Strategy 1: Metadata-Embedded Token
```rust
// Sender embeds token in every symbol
let symbol = Symbol::new(data)
    .with_cancel_token(token.clone());

// Receiver checks token on each symbol
for symbol in stream {
    if symbol.cancel_token().is_triggered() {
        cleanup_partial_state();
        break;
    }
    process(symbol);
}
```

### Strategy 2: Out-of-Band Channel
```rust
// Sender broadcasts on dedicated cancel channel
cancel_broadcaster.broadcast(object_id, CancelReason::Timeout);

// Receiver listens on cancel channel in parallel
select! {
    symbol = stream.next() => process(symbol),
    _ = cancel_channel.recv() => cleanup_and_exit(),
}
```

### Strategy 3: Heartbeat-Based Detection
```rust
// Receiver detects cancellation via missing heartbeats
let last_symbol_time = Instant::now();
if last_symbol_time.elapsed() > HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT {
    // Sender likely cancelled, initiate cleanup
    assume_cancelled_and_cleanup();
}
```

---

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|------------|--------|------------|
| Cancellation broadcast lost | High | Medium | Multiple strategies, receiver timeout-based detection |
| Cleanup takes too long | Medium | Medium | Bounded cleanup with timeout, incremental resource release |
| Race between cancel and completion | Medium | Low | Clear semantics: cancel wins if not already complete |
| Token overhead in symbols | Low | Low | Compact encoding, optional embedding |
| Cascading cancellation storm | Low | High | Rate limiting, cancellation coalescing |

title: HIGH: JetStream consumer pull batch size DoS vector
description:
**Location**: src/messaging/jetstream.rs - Pull consumer batch size handling and MAX_PULL_BATCH validation

**Issue**: Current MAX_PULL_BATCH protection may be insufficient against memory exhaustion attacks. Pull consumer requests with oversized batch parameters can cause service DoS.

**Impact**:
- Service availability DoS via memory exhaustion
- Resource starvation affecting other consumers
- Potential cascade failure of JetStream cluster
- Performance degradation under malicious load

**Remediation**:
1. Add per-consumer rate limiting for pull requests
2. Implement dynamic batch size clamping based on available memory
3. Add consumer-level memory usage tracking and limits
4. Implement exponential backoff for oversized requests
5. Consider adaptive batch sizing based on system load
6. Add monitoring/alerting for abnormal pull patterns

**Security Priority**: P1 HIGH - Availability DoS vector with service impact
close_reason:
FIXED: Implemented comprehensive DoS protection against JetStream consumer pull batch size attacks.

Added multi-layered defense against memory exhaustion and service degradation attacks:

1. **Per-Consumer Rate Limiting**: Added PullRateLimiter to enforce 50ms minimum interval between pull requests per consumer, with exponential backoff (1.5x multiplier, max 5s delay) for rapid requests. Prevents individual consumers from overwhelming the system.

2. **Dynamic Batch Size Clamping**: Enhanced validate_and_clamp_pull_batch_size() to reduce requested batch sizes by up to 50% under rate limiting pressure or memory constraints. Maintains minimum viable batch size (16 messages) while protecting against oversized allocations.

3. **Global Rate Limiting**: Implemented GlobalPullRateTracker with system-wide limit of 1000 pull requests/second. Uses circular buffer to track recent requests and prevents cascade failure across all consumers.

4. **Memory Pressure Monitoring**: Added memory usage estimation (2KB per message) with progressive batch size reduction above 256MB threshold. Rejects requests that would exceed 512MB system memory usage to prevent OOM conditions.

5. **Adaptive Resource Management**: Integration with existing max_ack_pending flow control provides coordinated protection. Rate limiting state influences batch clamping and automatic recovery when request patterns normalize.

6. **Comprehensive Testing**: Added full test suite covering rate limiting enforcement, exponential backoff, global limits, memory pressure detection, and end-to-end DoS protection validation.

Security Impact: Prevents service availability DoS via memory exhaustion, resource starvation affecting legitimate consumers, potential JetStream cluster cascade failures, and performance degradation under malicious load patterns.

Implementation maintains backward compatibility while providing transparent protection against both accidental and malicious oversized batch requests.

title: Decide whether a TaskGroup surface is wanted on top of JoinSet, or close as WONT-DO
description:
RAISED 2026-07-25 by SapphireHill while closing asupersync-dx-core-api-v2-u1z5hn.5, which is titled "JoinSet / TaskGroup". All seven of that bead's acceptance criteria are met and JoinSet shipped, but no separate `TaskGroup` type shipped. Rather than silently narrow the title's scope at close time, the question is recorded here.

THE QUESTION: does the public surface want a `TaskGroup` in addition to `JoinSet`, and if so what distinguishes it?

ARGUMENT FOR "NO" (current default, and why the bead was closed without it): JoinSet already IS the dynamic task-group primitive -- region-owned members, completion-order join_next, spawn-order join_all, drained cancel_all, severity-lattice summary, abort-on-drop request. A `TaskGroup` that is a rename or type alias over the same semantics is exactly the kind of compatibility shim AGENTS.md forbids ("Never create compatibility shims", "no tech debt"), and it would give agents two names for one concept to choose between -- a DX regression, not a DX win, for a project whose docs are read by coding agents.

ARGUMENT FOR "YES": a TaskGroup could carry genuinely different semantics rather than being an alias. Candidates worth evaluating before dismissing:
  - a group that OWNS a child region by construction (so cancel_all == region cancel and group exit == a quiescence boundary), which is what JoinSet deliberately does NOT do -- JoinSet shares the caller's region and documents Scope::region + JoinSet::new(&child_scope) as the isolation path. A type whose whole point is "this IS a structure boundary" is a real distinction, not a rename.
  - scoped/borrowed (non-'static) members, if the borrow story can be made sound.
  - a nursery-style API where the group value cannot outlive the scope at all.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: pick one of (a) close as WONT-DO and edit the JoinSet docs to say explicitly that JoinSet is the task-group primitive and no TaskGroup is planned, so future agents stop looking for it; or (b) specify the owns-a-child-region variant as its own bead with its own ACs. Do not add an alias.

Owner call, not an agent call: this is a public-API naming/surface decision.
close_reason: WONT-DO, decided by the project owner 2026-07-25: no separate TaskGroup type. JoinSet is the task-group primitive. Rationale as filed -- a TaskGroup that renamed or aliased JoinSet would be exactly the compatibility shim AGENTS.md forbids, and would leave agents choosing between two names for one concept, which is a DX regression for a codebase whose docs are read by coding agents. The one genuinely distinct design (a group that OWNS a child region by construction, so cancel_all == region cancel and group exit == a quiescence boundary) is explicitly NOT deferred-with-an-alias: it is documented as the composition scope.region(..) + JoinSet::new(&child), which already gives those exact semantics without a second type. title: [fresh-eyes] grpc/status.rs: with_details no size cap + transport-message substring match for deadline mapping
description:
Two LOW defense-in-depth findings in src/grpc/status.rs:

(1) Lines 137-144 — Status::with_details accepts arbitrarily large Bytes with no cap:
   Per recent themes (gRPC metadata size cap fix br-asupersync-7u4r72), Status objects round-tripped to/from wire could carry attacker-controlled detail blobs to OOM downstream serializers. Wire codec is the canonical place for caps but a defensive MAX_STATUS_DETAILS_LEN (e.g. 64KB matching gRPC default per RFC) and MAX_STATUS_MESSAGE_LEN (~8KB) check or truncation here would be defense in depth.
   Fix: add const MAX_STATUS_DETAILS_LEN: usize = 65_536; const MAX_STATUS_MESSAGE_LEN: usize = 8_192; in with_details, truncate or reject.

(2) Lines 349-355 — transport_message_implies_deadline does substring match on free-form attacker-influenced text:
   Status-code mapping is keyed on .to_ascii_lowercase().contains() of free-form transport error text. A peer-controlled error string (DNS error text, upstream proxy error message, OS errno text containing 'timeout') routes to DeadlineExceeded instead of Unavailable, changing client retry semantics. gRPC clients commonly treat DeadlineExceeded as terminal vs. Unavailable as retryable. Not a security boundary, but contract-correctness is fragile.
   Fix: thread a typed TransportErrorKind { Timeout, ConnectFailed, ResetByPeer, ... } from the codec layer into GrpcError::Transport(kind, msg); have the Status mapping switch on the typed kind, not text inspection.

Audit: SapphireHill 2026-04-26 fresh-eyes-7d-diff via subagent a3fe06ca; verified live at status.rs:137-144 (no caps) and 349-355 (substring match).

title: [reality-check-wave2] Promote truthful boundaries into shipped user capabilities
description:
Reality-check wave2 epic: promote truthful support boundaries into shipped, user-valuable capabilities.

Background and evidence:
The 2026-05-04 reality-check program correctly made the README and support matrices honest, but several important surfaces were closed as truthful boundaries rather than completed product capabilities. That was the right first-wave move, because users should never be misled by aspirational docs. This wave2 program is the next move: turn the biggest explicitly deferred or partial support classes into implemented, tested, operator-grade capabilities.

Source evidence to preserve:
- README.md states HTTP/3 is partial: default static-only QPACK plus opt-in dynamic field-section context, with no full QPACK instruction-stream parity or blocked-stream scheduler claim.
- artifacts/http3_qpack_support_matrix_v1.json explicitly says full QPACK encoder/decoder instruction-stream parity and blocked-stream scheduling are not advertised as shipped production parity.
- src/remote.rs is a real transport-agnostic RemoteRuntime contract, and README/docs state production network execution remains adapter responsibility rather than a shipped backend.
- docs/WASM.md, README.md, packages/browser/src/index.ts, and src/runtime/builder.rs state Browser Edition is shipped for browser main-thread and dedicated-worker consumers, while service-worker and shared-worker direct runtime are fail-closed/deferred.
- docs/integration.md says public browser messaging-surface APIs are direct-runtime feasible but not promoted public contracts yet.
- README.md marks web framework, filesystem APIs, and messaging clients as in progress/early/mixed, even though substrate code exists.
- artifacts/conformance_registry_contract_v1.json still lists dormant inline followups for h1 suites, sqlite_prepared_statements, actor_mailbox_protocol, dns_cache, grpc_deadline, grpc_health, trace_event, udp_socket, unix_listener, and web_session_cookies.
- formal proof posture is meaningful but deliberately bounded to checked core invariants; adapter/protocol/runtime refinement remains lane-specific rather than blanket proof.
- The project owner explicitly wants capabilities that are compelling for massive agent swarms on 64+ CPU / 256GiB+ RAM hosts, including world-class responsiveness and resource utilization.

Program shape:
This epic intentionally creates implementation beads rather than another doc-only downgrade. Each child bead must include comprehensive unit tests plus E2E or script-level proof with detailed deterministic logging. Every child must use Agent Mail file reservations before editing, keep work on main only, run Rust build/test/clippy through rch exec, and preserve the no-file-deletion and no-Tokio-runtime-core rules.

Unit tests required:
The epic is not an implementation unit, but it is still testable. It is closable only after child beads add or update unit/contract tests for every promoted surface and after the final signoff artifact schema test proves every wave2 child has source evidence, unit evidence, and E2E/script evidence. The final signoff test must fail if any wave2 child lacks a proof command, artifact path, support-class transition, residual-risk disposition, or explicit unsupported reason.

E2E/script proof required:
The epic requires the final wave2 signoff script to emit bead_id, wave_id, child_bead_count, closed_child_count, promoted_count, deferred_count, proof_command_count, e2e_artifact_count, docs_drift_count, bv_cycle_count, br_ready_count, residual_risk_count, artifact_path, verdict, and first_failure. That script is the E2E proof for the program as a whole and must inspect actual artifacts/commands rather than closed tracker status alone.

Validation:
Before closing this epic, run the final signoff bead validation through rch exec for Rust contract tests, run bv --robot-plan, bv --robot-alerts, bv --robot-suggest, and attempt br dep cycles. If br dep cycles remains degraded on the large graph, record the exact timeout/degraded output and rely on bv advanced_insights.cycle_break only as a documented fallback, not as silent proof.

Non-goals:
