title: [perf-hot-path] bytes/bytes.rs: Bytes uses Arc<Vec<u8>> instead of inline raw pointer + atomic refcount — extra indirection per deref + extra allocation layer vs tokio-bytes
description: src/bytes/bytes.rs:35-53 Bytes wraps BytesInner::Shared(Arc<Vec<u8>>) — a double indirection. Per deref: bytes.deref() → Arc<Vec<u8>>::deref() → &Vec<u8> → Vec::deref() → &[u8]. That's two pointer chases vs tokio-bytes' single chase (data ptr inline in the Bytes struct, refcount via inline AtomicUsize). For per-frame body access in HTTP/2 / gRPC / framed-codec hot paths, this compounds: every read of a Bytes payload pays the indirection cost. Construction also adds an allocation layer: every Bytes from heap data wraps both the Vec<u8> AND the Arc — tokio-bytes uses a single allocation for both. Mitigation: refactor to (data_ptr: *const u8, len: usize, refcount: Option<NonNull<AtomicUsize>>) shape with a vtable for backing storage flavors (static / shared / owned). This is a substantial unsafe-code change but the well-known correct pattern; tokio-bytes is the reference implementation. Severity HIGH because Bytes is the foundational type touched by every codec / HTTP / gRPC / messaging path; the indirection compounds across the entire networking stack.
close_reason: DEFERRED-ARCHITECTURAL: Bytes Arc<Vec<u8>> → inline raw pointer + atomic refcount is a major architectural rewrite (matches tokio-bytes internal layout) that would touch the entire bytes/buf API surface. Repeatedly surfaced across many ticks and consistently flagged as too large for incremental fixes. Requires explicit human review + dedicated branch session (not orchestrator scope). Closing to clean triage; can be reopened when prioritized for a focused refactor sprint.

title: BrowserStorage emits false and duplicate terminal telemetry
description: src/io/browser_storage.rs documents StorageEventOutcome::Allowed as a request that passed policy and was applied, but authorize_and_record appends Allowed immediately after authority/availability checks, before quota validation, host calls, or local accounting. Observable sequences are contradictory: post-authority quota and host failures append Allowed then Denied; sync calls against async-only backends do the same; all five async methods authorize first and then call the sync method when no async backend is registered, so fallback success appends Allowed twice and fallback failure appends Allowed, Allowed, Denied. A real async host future polled to Pending and then dropped leaves a sole Allowed event even though the generic host contract cannot say whether the effect was absent, committed, or indeterminate. Existing tests inspect only events().last() and miss cardinality. Impact is integrity of public security/operations telemetry, not a direct authority bypass; no production consumer outside this module/tests was found. Fix direction: make authorization success silent; emit exactly one Allowed only after successful host/local completion; keep exactly one Denied on returned errors with reason codes; route async fallback before outer authorization or through already-authorized private cores; document that dropped pending futures produce no terminal event and host errors do not prove absence of partial effects. Add exact event-delta regressions for sync/async success, quota rejection, host failure, async-only mismatch, fallback success/failure, never-polled futures, and poll-to-Pending drop. Coordinate with asupersync-3v9vre so post-read quota checks do not reintroduce Allowed then Denied.
close_reason: Shipped fix verified by exact current-head focused RCH lane (19/19 green).

title: Task panics never reach MetricsProvider::record_panic on the native runtimes (only the never-built legacy worker called it)
description:
MetricsProvider::record_panic never fires on the real runtimes.

Found by e8's 10-09 unwired-machinery survey (handed to c7 at 03:36Z in rc_20260922/TODO.md).
- Its only caller is PanicIsolator in the legacy scheduler::Worker, which RuntimeBuilder never constructs.
- The three-lane worker's task-poll panic arm (src/runtime/scheduler/three_lane.rs, the Err(payload) branch near payload_to_string) completes the task as Panicked without telling the provider.
- The current-thread runtime dispatches spawned tasks through the same ThreeLaneWorker.
- So a custom RuntimeBuilder::metrics provider that counts panics by location reads 0 on both runtime shapes. The trait docs (observability/metrics.rs ~1078-1088) say production providers should override record_panic to count panics.

Fix (additive, no API change):
- SchedulerTicks (three_lane.rs), which already resolves the provider once per worker loop for scheduler_tick, keeps it for panics whatever wants_scheduler_ticks says.
- The panic arm calls record_panic("task_execution") after the execution guard is released. "task_execution" is the PanicIsolator tag. The call is contained in catch_unwind with the payload forgotten, like the tick callback.
- A root-future panic in Runtime::block_on is resumed to the caller, not isolated, so it is not reported.

Test: runtime::state::tests::task_panics_reach_the_metrics_provider. On current_thread and 2-worker runtimes, a finished task and a panicking task join, and the provider records exactly ["task_execution"]. Control: the call removed, so nothing is recorded.
close_reason: Fixed in d834b4305 / rebased: routed task execution panics (both unhandled unwinds and structured caught panics via CatchUnwind) to MetricsProvider::record_panic("task_execution") in ThreeLaneWorker. Decoupled timing from panic recording in SchedulerTicks so providers retain the record_panic callback regardless of wants_scheduler_ticks. Added regression test task_panics_reach_the_metrics_provider verifying current_thread and 2-worker configurations.

title: Implement reservation-aware fallback work finder
description:
Background: Empty br/bv queues do not mean there is no useful work. Agents need a bounded fallback selector that respects active Agent Mail reservations, dirty files, and approved fallback lanes such as testing-fuzzing or mock-code-finder.

Goal: Implement a reservation-aware work finder that reports safe candidate slices without touching files owned by active peers.

Implementation approach: Combine br/bv ready state, Agent Mail reservation metadata or local archive artifacts, git dirty/staged status, and a small registry of approved fallback lanes. Output should be deterministic and easy for a human to inspect before claiming work.

Non-goals: Do not auto-edit code, auto-claim beads, or override another agent reservation.

title: [OBSERVABILITY] Real-Time Performance Budget Monitor
description:
**Epic Goal:** Implement real-time monitoring and alerting system for performance budgets across all runtime components.

**Background and Rationale:**
Performance budgets are critical for production systems but are currently only enforced at CI time. Users need real-time visibility into budget compliance and immediate alerts when budgets are violated. This addresses the observability blindspot of 'are we actually meeting our performance commitments in production?'

**Technical Approach:**
- Integrate with existing SystemPressure and monitoring infrastructure
- Provide real-time dashboards showing budget vs actual performance
- Implement configurable alerting thresholds and escalation paths
- Generate optimization recommendations based on budget violations
- Support per-component and composite budget tracking

**Key Components:**
- Budget definition and configuration system
- Real-time measurement collection with <0.5% overhead
- Alert generation and routing system  
- Performance trend analysis and prediction
- Integration with external monitoring systems (Prometheus, etc.)

**Success Criteria:**
- Sub-second detection of budget violations
- <0.5% overhead in normal operation
- Clear actionable alerts with optimization guidance
- Historical trending and analysis capabilities
- Integration with existing observability stack

**User Value:**
Transforms performance budgets from static CI checks to dynamic production guarantees. Enables proactive performance management and builds user confidence in system reliability.

title: HTTP/1 plain request path mints each request Cx from the runtime root, not the connection Cx: handler-spawned work escapes the listener's region (seen under Http1Listener::run_in)
description:
## Finding (SapphireHill 2026-10-04, while building Http1Listener::run_in for kpmoy5.4.5)
The plain HTTP/1 server path (src/http/h1/server.rs ~1151) mints each request's context with `ServerRequestRegion::mint`, which calls `Runtime::current_request_cx_with_budget` (builder.rs ~4238 -> build_request_cx_from_inner). That gives a ROOT-region request Cx, whatever region the connection task belongs to.

Observed: under `Http1Listener::run_in(&child_cx)`, the connection task runs in the child region, but a handler's `Cx::current().region_id()` is RegionId(0:0) (root). Seen in lane LShl2int, when the first version of the run_in test asserted the handler's region.

Consequences:
- Work a handler spawns through its request Cx lands in the root region. A service region's close neither waits for nor cancels it; this is the kpmoy5.2.3 escape again, one layer down.
- The streaming path already does the structured thing: `ServerRequestRegion::mint_from_connection(.., connection_cx)` (server.rs ~1522) derives the request Cx from the connection Cx.

## Work
Mint the plain-path request Cx from the connection Cx when one exists (`mint_from_connection`, as the streaming path does), and keep the runtime-minted fallback for no-runtime/legacy callers. Check before changing:
- the request-region budget and cancel bridging (`run_with_protocol_drain(.., conn_cx, ..)`);
- the request-region e2e and README "request-region E2E proof" claims;
- that root-run listeners behave identically (their connection Cx is root anyway).
Test: under run_in, a handler's Cx region equals the listener's region, and a task the handler spawns is a straggler of a bounded close of that region. Old-red: today's root region.
close_reason: Landed 46ac25c70: plain HTTP/1 request Cx derives from the connection Cx (handler work belongs to the listener's region), and connection-derived request Cxs carry the spawn route (cx.spawn no longer RuntimeUnavailable); e2e straggler test green, both controls red at their guards, lib 2623/0, clippy clean.

SapphireHill 2026-10-04: LANDED main=master 46ac25c70 (fast-forward on 2780d3454).

Fix:
- src/http/h1/server.rs: the plain path mints the request Cx with mint_from_connection when it runs inside a task (it used to mint at the root).
- src/web/request_region.rs: child_cx_from_connection now lends the connection's spawn gateway and pending-spawn counter, when the connection has a gateway, plus its logical clock and loser-drain history.

title: [security-audit] http/h2/connection.rs: decode_headers returns HPACK-decoded headers without RFC 9113 §8.3.1 pseudo-header validation
description:
src/http/h2/connection.rs:851-885 (Connection::decode_headers) decodes HPACK-compressed headers via self.hpack_decoder.decode(&mut src)? at line 879 and immediately returns the raw header list via ReceivedFrame::Headers at line 881-885 with NO validation of HTTP/2 pseudo-header rules per RFC 9113 §8.3.1.

Asymmetry confirmed against the HTTP/3 implementation:
  * src/http/h3_native.rs:670 calls validate_request_pseudo_headers(&pseudo)?
  * src/http/h3_native.rs:692 calls validate_request_pseudo_headers_with_settings(...)
  * Plus dedicated helpers: validate_method_token (line 1418), validate_scheme_syntax (line 1452), validate_authority_form (line 1474)

HTTP/2 has NO equivalent — grep across src/http/h2/ for 'validate.*pseudo|PROTOCOL_ERROR.*pseudo' returns zero matches. The decode_headers callers (lines 772 and 834) just propagate the headers up the stack.

RFC 9113 §8.3.1 specifies multiple MUST requirements that go unchecked:
  * Request pseudo-headers MUST be one of :method, :scheme, :path, :authority (no others; no duplicates)
  * Pseudo-headers MUST appear before regular headers — a regular header followed by a pseudo-header is a stream/connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR
  * :method, :scheme, :path are REQUIRED on requests; :authority is recommended
  * Connection-specific headers (Connection, Keep-Alive, Proxy-*, Transfer-Encoding, Upgrade) MUST NOT appear in HTTP/2

Concrete attack scenarios a malicious peer can exploit:

  1. Duplicate :method in a HEADERS frame:
     [HPACK: :method=GET, :method=POST, :path=/, :scheme=https, :authority=victim]
     → application sees both methods and may dispatch on either depending on its own iteration order. Smuggling vector if a downstream proxy parses one method and the asupersync application parses the other.

  2. Missing :path:
     [HPACK: :method=GET, :scheme=https, :authority=victim]
     → application receives a request with no path. Behavior depends on application code; some panic, some default to '/', some leak partial state.

  3. Pseudo-header after regular header:
     [HPACK: user-agent=foo, :method=GET, :path=/, :scheme=https]
     → MUST be rejected per RFC 9113 §8.3 but currently passes through. Smuggling vector when downstream consumers re-serialize.

  4. Invalid :method token (e.g., :method=GET\r\nX-Injected: bad):
     → CRLF in header value should already be rejected by HPACK, but :method-specific validation (RFC 7230 token grammar) is missing.

  5. Connection-specific headers like Transfer-Encoding sneaking in via h2 (RFC 9113 §8.2.2 forbids them).

Severity HIGH. The asymmetry with h3_native demonstrates the project's own bar for pseudo-header validation; h2 falling below that bar is a regression-class gap, not a missing-feature gap.

Suggested fix: extract the helper(s) from h3_native.rs (validate_request_pseudo_headers, validate_method_token, validate_scheme_syntax, validate_authority_form) into a shared module (e.g., src/http/pseudo_header.rs) and call from both h3_native and h2/connection.rs. title: H1/H2 listeners treat fd exhaustion (EMFILE/ENFILE/ENOBUFS/ENOMEM) as a fatal accept error and exit the accept loop permanently; H2 comment wrongly claims EMFILE is backed off
description:
The HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 listeners classify accept errors by io::ErrorKind, and the transient set (WouldBlock, TimedOut, ConnectionRefused, ConnectionAborted, ConnectionReset, Interrupted) contains no file-descriptor-exhaustion error. On Linux EMFILE, ENFILE and ENOBUFS decode to ErrorKind::Uncategorized and ENOMEM to ErrorKind::OutOfMemory, so the first accept() that fails because the process is out of descriptors takes the non-transient arm, run_with returns Err, the listening socket is dropped, and the server never accepts again. The H2 comment at the transient arm explicitly claims EMFILE is backed off, so this is a wrong belief encoded in code, not a considered policy.

Evidence (7fc9e53a4):
- src/http/h1/listener.rs 1291-1301 is_transient_accept_error; 822-832: transient errors back off (2 ms doubling per 16-streak, 64 ms cap), everything else is `Err(e) => return Err(e)`. src/http/h2/listener.rs 263-273 and 3855-3869 are the same by design ("h1 parity"); the comment at 3856-3858 reads "so a persistent accept failure (e.g. EMFILE) does not busy-spin the accept loop", but EMFILE never reaches that arm.
- Rust std maps EMFILE/ENFILE/ENOBUFS to no named kind (Uncategorized) and ENOMEM to OutOfMemory (library/std/src/sys/pal/unix/mod.rs decode_error_kind); none of these are in the list. There is no ErrorKind for too-many-open-files.
- src/net/tcp/listener.rs 183-223: poll_accept forwards any non-WouldBlock error from the OS accept unchanged.
- Tests h1 1384-1418 (transient_error_detection) only cover the listed kinds and assert AddrInUse and PermissionDenied are fatal; no fd-exhaustion case exists in either listener.
- On the early return, ConnectionTasks (1237-1266) is dropped without join_all, begin_drain never runs, and self.tcp_listener is dropped, so new clients get connection refused while the accepted connections finish on their own; the caller of Http1Listener::run / Http2Listener::run sees an io::Error and must restart the process to accept again.

How it is reached: Http1ListenerConfig::max_connections defaults to 10_000 (listener.rs 276) while a typical RLIMIT_NOFILE soft limit is 1024, so about a thousand concurrent keep-alive connections (legitimate load, or one client holding idle connections inside the 60 s idle window) exhaust descriptors before the listener's own cap applies; the next accept returns EMFILE and the listener exits. tokio's accept documentation and hyper's server loop both treat EMFILE/ENFILE/ENOBUFS/ENOMEM as retry-with-backoff for this reason.

Suggested repair (both listeners, shared helper): classify by raw_os_error as well as kind. Minimal: add raw EMFILE, ENFILE, ENOBUFS, ENOMEM (libc constants; WSAEMFILE/WSAENOBUFS on Windows) plus ErrorKind::OutOfMemory to the transient set, keep the existing backoff, and fix the H2 comment. Safer: invert the policy so only a known-permanent set is fatal (EBADF, ENOTSOCK, EINVAL, EOPNOTSUPP, i.e. the listener itself is unusable) and every other accept error backs off with the capped exponential delay and a rate-limited error log; a misclassified transient error then costs a 64 ms retry instead of a permanent outage. Add a classifier test that constructs io::Error::from_raw_os_error(libc::EMFILE) and asserts it is transient, and a loop-level test with a fake accept source that yields EMFILE twice then a connection, asserting the listener keeps running and records two transient errors.

Impact: availability. A P2 in my view: reachable by ordinary overload with default configuration, and the failure is permanent until restart.

Found during the read-only fresh-eyes pass (asupersync-cqzuzt) while source is frozen; no edits made.

title: UDP review (r20): recv_error discards the only record of an ICMP error on set_recverr sockets and waits forever; Windows drops oversized datagrams silently
description:
Read-only review (SapphireHill e8 round r20, 10-10) of the API lane's fb479e039, d65f34661 and d14f1333b at origin fbb67e5f6; full report /data/tmp/rc_20260923/audit_r20/B5_udp_bytes.md (kernel facts behind U1 probed on Linux 7.0).

MEDIUM:
- U1 (d65f34661). UdpSocket::recv_error on a set_recverr socket now reads and DISCARDS a nonzero SO_ERROR when the error queue is empty (txtime.rs ~600-616), assuming it duplicates a queued report. But dequeuing a report already clears SO_ERROR, so the branch runs exactly when SO_ERROR is the only record: (a) receive buffer full (the kernel drops the queued report but sets SO_ERROR), (b) the error arrived before set_recverr(true), (c) a try_clone'd handle whose cached flag says on after another handle turned the shared kernel option off. The error is lost and recv_error waits forever (v0.4.3/previous behaviour: returned Err(code)). The rustdoc still says the pending error is returned. Fix: return the code (option A), or re-read the queue once and return Err(code) if still empty (option B).
- U2 (fb479e039, Windows). WSAEMSGSIZE datagrams (oversized; Winsock consumes them) are skipped silently in recv_batch_from (udp.rs ~3624-3640, ~3690): no truncation flag, no report.error, no counter; the skip loop does not yield. Bead p95fe4 asked for a truncated read. No Windows lane verified it.
LOW:
- U3. AtpUdpSocket lab poll_recv_from ignores the endpoint generation (atp/udp/mod.rs ~919-955): a stale handle can take a rebound endpoint's datagram and replace its waker.
- U4. AtpUdpSocket::send_packets loses partial-send accounting on the per-chunk cancel checkpoint and on the mid-batch oversize check (retry duplicates).
- U5 (compat). AtpUdpSocket::bind now refuses max_send_batch above the new cap, which v0.4.3 accepted and sent fine (sends chunk at 1024 anyway).
- U6. The new tests mostly do not prove the changes (Take/Chain zero-copy not asserted; empty-chunk tests would hang, not fail; d65 test only checks the getter).
- U7. Chain::copy_to_bytes allocates three times when a copy crosses the boundary (was one).

title: [idea-wizard][swarm-scale] Build pressure-lab and resource-governed scheduler roadmap
description:
Idea-wizard Phase 2/3 result after the project reached zero ready open beads: the strongest accretive direction is a self-contained swarm-scale performance and safety program for Asupersync users running massive agent workloads on 64+ cores and 256GB+ RAM.

Rationale: Asupersync already has structured concurrency, explicit Cx capabilities, deterministic lab/runtime proofs, scheduler benchmarks, resource governance pieces, and many closed audit/testing beads. The next leverage point is not a speculative micro-optimization; it is an integrated pressure lab plus resource-aware scheduler feedback loop that can prove responsiveness, quiescence, memory discipline, deadlock resistance, and benchmark stability under large synthetic and no-mock agent swarms.

Phase 2 generated 30 candidate ideas and winnowed the top five: deterministic swarm pressure lab; NUMA/cohort-aware scheduler placement; region-level resource budget/admission control; p95/p99/CV evidence ledger for swarm runs; and deadlock/lost-wakeup radar tied to LabRuntime. Phase 3 added complementary ideas: no-mock e2e script, trace summarizer, scheduler autopilot, regression gates, failure minimizer, RCH-aware proof lanes, pressure scenario corpus, and operator-readable reports. This epic converts those into granular implementation beads.

Acceptance criteria for closing this epic:
- Every child bead is closed with focused RCH-backed cargo proof where it compiles/tests/benches Rust.
- The final system includes deterministic unit/lab tests, no-mock e2e scripts with detailed logs, and Criterion or release-perf evidence for high-contention scheduler/resource cases.
- The design preserves asupersync invariants: structured concurrency, region close equals quiescence, cancellation request/drain/finalize, loser drain, no obligation leaks, and no ambient authority.
- The plan remains main-only, no branches/worktrees, with exact Agent Mail reservations before edits.
- No new runtime/executor dependency is introduced and no default production tokio edge is added.

title: [idea-wizard][swarm-ops] Build adaptive swarm operations cockpit and scenario DSL
description:
## Background
Idea-wizard continuation after the ready queue was saturated behind active swarm trace and Kafka/conformance work. Phase 2 generated 30 candidate improvements for making Asupersync compelling for massive agent swarms on 64+ cores and 256GB+ RAM, then winnowed to the strongest new program that does not duplicate the existing pressure-lab, trace-summarizer, e2e, and autopilot beads.

## Phase 2 winnow: top 5 new ideas
1. A workload scenario DSL that lets operators describe swarms, cancellation storms, memory pressure, channel fanout, and admission failure modes once, then run them through LabRuntime and no-mock live runners.
2. An RCH-aware proof-lane planner that turns a touched surface plus scenario manifest into bounded remote validation commands with cache/provenance evidence and no local Cargo fallback.
3. A memory-residency and brownout policy model that translates region pressure into explicit admission, shedding, spill, and no-win receipts without violating cancellation or obligation cleanup.
4. A contention heatmap ledger that joins lock metrics, scheduler lanes, region ids, and trace summaries into actionable p95/p99 wait and hold evidence.
5. A failure minimizer that takes pressure-lab crashpacks and shrinks them to deterministic replay seeds, scenario deltas, and owner-bead suggestions.

## Phase 3 next 10 ideas folded into this epic
Operator cockpit reports, workload profile presets, CI/release certification adapters, compare-against-baseline panels, dependency-aware proof batching, redaction-safe artifact bundles, SLO policy integration, scenario corpus governance, runbook-quality diagnostics, and self-checking no-mock e2e scripts.

## Non-goals
Do not introduce another runtime or executor. Do not replace the current swarm pressure lab, trace summarizer, no-mock e2e script, or scheduler autopilot beads; this epic layers a higher-level operations and planning surface over them. Do not claim production proof from synthetic-only results.

## Acceptance criteria
- Child beads define a scenario DSL, proof planner, memory/brownout policy model, contention ledger, failure minimizer, operator report contract, no-mock e2e proof script, and final certification bundle.
- Every implementation child records focused RCH validation and avoids local Cargo fallback.
- Every report/artifact has stable JSON plus deterministic text suitable for agent handoff.
- Tests cover empty/malformed scenarios, saturated swarms, cancellation storms, memory pressure, missing trace fields, stale baselines, and redaction.
- The program preserves structured concurrency, region-close quiescence, cancellation request/drain/finalize, loser drain, no obligation leaks, and no ambient authority.

title: [idea-wizard][swarm-ops][scenario-dsl] Define workload scenario schema and replay corpus
description:
## Background
Operators need one durable way to describe massive agent-swarm workloads instead of hand-written scripts per proof lane. This child bead builds the first scenario schema and corpus for region counts, task counts, channel fanout, cancellation rate, obligation rate, memory pressure, admission failure, and timeout behavior.

## Scope
- Define a stable JSON schema for swarm workload scenarios with explicit seed, scale, runtime knobs, failure-mode knobs, and artifact expectations.

- Connect the schema to LabRuntime-oriented replay planning without requiring the no-mock live runner to exist first.
- Reject placeholder/mock markers and malformed scale knobs fail-closed.

## Why this matters
A scenario DSL is the hinge between pressure-lab work, no-mock e2e scripts, trace summaries, performance ledgers, and future scheduler feedback. Without it, each proof lane invents its own inputs and cannot be compared reliably.

## Risks
Overfitting the schema to one test runner would make later live/e2e evidence awkward. Keep runner-specific details in provenance fields and keep semantic workload fields stable.

## Acceptance criteria
- Schema contract tests cover empty, malformed, minimal, and saturated scenarios.
- Fixture corpus includes at least six named scenarios with deterministic seeds and scale knobs.
- Documentation inside the bead closeout explains how future no-mock and LabRuntime runners consume the same scenario shape.
- RCH validation covers the schema/fixture contract.
- No new runtime dependency or Tokio edge is introduced.

title: [idea-wizard][swarm-ops][rch] Build proof-lane planner with remote-only provenance
description:
## Background
Large swarm features need repeatable proof lanes that do not overload the local machine and do not accidentally pass through local Cargo fallback. This bead creates a planner that maps touched surfaces and scenario manifests to RCH-only commands plus provenance records.

## Scope
- Define a proof-lane plan schema covering command, target dir, feature set, expected artifacts, timeouts, remote-worker provenance, and fallback policy.
- Encode remote-required semantics explicitly: local fallback is an invalid result unless the user explicitly authorizes it.
- Batch compatible lanes so agents can choose focused checks first and broader checks later without losing evidence.
- Include stale-cache and stale-HEAD detection so proof records cannot be reused silently after code or fixture changes.

## Why this matters
The project already has many proof commands, but agents still spend time rediscovering which RCH lane proves which claim. A planner makes validation faster, safer, and more operator-readable under many-agent contention.

## Risks
The planner must not pretend to prove broad release health from a narrow check. Every lane needs explicit covers/does_not_cover fields.

## Acceptance criteria
- Contract tests reject missing RCH provenance, local fallback markers, stale commit SHAs, missing target dirs, and commands without explicit feature scope.
- At least one scenario-DSL fixture maps to a focused LabRuntime/summarizer proof lane.
- Closeout records a real RCH validation command for the planner contract.
- The output is stable JSON plus concise deterministic text for Agent Mail handoffs.

title: [idea-wizard][swarm-ops][memory] Add memory residency and brownout policy model
description:
## Background
The existing resource-governance work established admission-control foundations. Massive agent swarms also need explicit memory-residency policy: what stays hot, what can spill, what optional work browns out, and when the runtime emits a no-win receipt rather than pretending it can keep up.

## Scope
- Define a region/workload memory pressure model with residency tiers, soft/hard envelopes, brownout classes, spill eligibility, and no-win outcomes.
- Integrate with existing SLO/admission vocabulary rather than adding hidden globals.
- Preserve cancellation and obligation cleanup: shedding optional work must still drain losers and resolve permits/leases.
- Emit structured evidence for admitted, deferred, shed, spilled, browned-out, and no-win decisions.

## Why this matters
On 256GB+ machines, failure modes often come from unbounded memory growth and allocator churn, not just CPU scheduling. Users need predictable degradation and evidence, not late OOM behavior.

## Risks
A memory model based on approximate estimates can overclaim precision. Treat estimates as policy inputs with confidence and clamp behavior; never use them as proof of exact resident set size.

## Acceptance criteria
- Unit tests cover empty budget, exact limit, over limit, stale metrics, contradictory policy, and no-win fallback.
- Lab/metamorphic tests prove brownout does not disable cancellation drain, loser drain, obligation cleanup, or region quiescence.
- Structured reports include before/after envelopes, decision class, fallback reason, affected region/task ids, and proof lane metadata.
- RCH validation covers the policy model and at least one scheduler/governance seam.

title: [idea-wizard][swarm-ops][contention] Add lock and scheduler contention heatmap ledger
description:
## Background
Asupersync already has lock metrics, scheduler telemetry, trace summaries, and performance ledgers, but operators still need a single artifact that answers: where did the swarm spend time waiting, which region or lane caused it, and which owner bead should investigate?

## Scope
- Define a contention heatmap report schema joining ContendedMutex wait/hold metrics, scheduler lane counters, region/task ids, trace summary ids, and p50/p95/p99 wait classes.
- Include deterministic text output that ranks top hot locks, regions, lanes, and queue-pressure windows.
- Treat missing lock-metrics or trace fields as incomplete, not pass.
- Add source references and suggested owner bead fields so the report is actionable.

## Why this matters
For 64+ core workloads, the important question is often not whether the runtime is correct, but why p99 latency or throughput changed. A heatmap ledger gives agents and operators a fast route from symptom to file/module.

## Risks
Raw lock metrics can be noisy. The report should aggregate by stable ids and keep provenance, not overfit to one run.

title: [idea-wizard][swarm-ops][minimizer] Add deterministic swarm failure minimizer
description:
## Background
Large swarm runs can fail with huge traces and expensive reproduction cost. This bead adds a minimizer that turns pressure-lab or no-mock crashpacks into a smaller deterministic scenario seed, scale delta, and replay command while preserving the first invariant violation.

## Scope
- Define minimization inputs: scenario manifest, trace summary, failure bundle, invariant verdict, and proof-lane provenance.
- Implement a deterministic reduction strategy over scale knobs, failure-mode knobs, and schedule seeds, with explicit stop reasons.
- Preserve redaction and artifact integrity; minimized bundles must not drop the causal evidence needed for owner routing.
- Emit suggested owner bead/module when the minimized failure maps to a known hazard class.

## Why this matters
A compelling massive-swarm runtime needs failures that future agents can reproduce quickly. Shrinking a 100k-task failure into a 500-task replay is often the difference between fixing and ignoring it.

## Risks
Minimization can accidentally remove the bug. Require invariant-preserving checks at each reduction step and keep the original bundle pointer.

## Acceptance criteria
- Tests cover already-minimal failures, non-reproducible failures, cancellation storm minimization, deadlock/lost-wakeup suspect minimization, obligation leak suspect minimization, and redaction preservation.
- Output includes original artifact pointer, minimized scenario, replay command, invariant class, first failure, and owner suggestion.
- RCH validation runs focused minimizer contract tests.
- The minimizer never marks a failure minimized unless the invariant violation still reproduces.

title: [idea-wizard][swarm-ops][cert] Publish final swarm-ops certification bundle
description:
## Background
The final child bead for this epic publishes the evidence bundle that lets future agents and operators verify the entire swarm-ops program without reading the original idea-wizard notes.

## Scope
- Aggregate child proof commands, artifact paths, scenario corpus ids, report schemas, and known limitations into one stable certification artifact.
- Include covers/does_not_cover sections so synthetic, LabRuntime, no-mock, benchmark, and release evidence are not conflated.
- Verify current HEAD, RCH provenance, and child bead closure state.
- Send final Agent Mail handoff with artifact pointers and remaining caveats.

## Why this matters
The objective is not just to add features; it is to make massive-swarm operation credible and reproducible. A final certification bundle prevents the plan from becoming tribal knowledge.

## Risks
Certification can overstate support. The bundle must fail closed on missing child evidence or stale artifact SHAs.

## Acceptance criteria
- All implementation/test/report child beads are closed or explicitly classified deferred with owner bead and reason.
- Bundle contract rejects missing proof command, missing RCH provenance, stale commit SHA, stale scenario corpus, and broad claims without a matching proof lane.
- `bv --robot-insights` or equivalent graph check records no cycles in this subgraph.
- Final closeout message lists commands, artifacts, and support boundaries.

title: [tls-sni-required] tls/acceptor.rs: no require_sni() option — SNI-less connections accepted by default in multi-tenant servers
description:
src/tls/acceptor.rs and src/tls/stream.rs:157-162 — the server can extract the SNI hostname from ClientHello via `sni_hostname()` and the application can READ it, but there is NO mechanism on the acceptor to REQUIRE that SNI be present, nor to validate it against an allow-list, before the handshake completes. A client that omits the SNI extension produces `sni_hostname() = None` and the connection proceeds.

Threat: in multi-tenant SaaS servers (the asupersync target use case) SNI is the disambiguation mechanism for which tenant's certificate / configuration to apply. A connection with no SNI gets the server's default cert (usually the first configured), which:
  (a) Reveals the existence of the default tenant to a probing attacker.
  (b) Lets the attacker bypass per-tenant rate-limits / WAF rules that key on SNI.
  (c) Confuses logging / audit trails (the connection is logged under no tenant, or the default tenant).
  (d) Lets a sophisticated attacker reach the default tenant's services even when tenant-routing was supposed to confine them.

Fix direction:
  1. Add a `require_sni()` builder method to TlsAcceptorBuilder that fails the handshake (TLS alert level fatal) when SNI is absent.
  2. Add an `allowed_sni_names(Vec<String>)` method that further constrains acceptable SNI values.
  3. Default the acceptor to require SNI when more than one cert is configured (multi-tenant config implicit).
  4. Document the security tradeoff between SNI-less compatibility and multi-tenant isolation.
  5. Regression test: build an acceptor with require_sni(); drive a ClientHello without SNI; assert handshake fails.

Severity HIGH because (a) the asupersync project explicitly targets SaaS workloads (per docs) where SNI-based tenant isolation is foundational, (b) there is no warning to operators that SNI-less connections silently bypass tenant confinement, and (c) the fix is small and aligns with established TLS-server hardening practice (RFC 6066 §3 recommends servers may require SNI for multi-tenant configurations).

Source: /security-audit-for-saas on src/tls/* deepest refresh (2026-04-26).

title: [RaptorQ] Fuzz decoder K..K' boundary recovery edge cases
description:
CRITICAL GAP IDENTIFIED: K..K' boundary recovery edge cases in RaptorQ decoder

**UNDEREXPOSED SURFACE**: RFC 6330 systematic encoding boundary conditions
- K = actual source symbols required for decoding  
- K' = padded symbol count to satisfy RFC 6330 matrix constraints
- Gap K..K' contains zero-padded rows in encoding matrix
- Decoder must correctly handle missing/incomplete symbols in boundary region

**EXISTING COVERAGE GAP**: 
- raptorq_decoder.rs mentions "padded K..K' synthesis" only in integration tests
- No focused testing of boundary edge cases and encoder/decoder mismatches
- Missing coverage of zero-padding artifacts and matrix inversion failures

**VULNERABILITY SCENARIOS**:
1. **Encoder/Decoder Mismatch**: Encoder built without padding, decoder expects padded symbols
2. **Boundary Missing Symbols**: Missing symbols exactly at K boundary causes matrix singularity
3. **Gap Region Confusion**: Missing symbols in K..K' gap leads to incorrect padding assumptions  
4. **Straddling Corruption**: Symbols missing across K boundary trigger edge case bugs
5. **Repair Symbol References**: Repair symbols referencing zero-padded positions K..K'
6. **Matrix Zero Rows**: Zero-padded matrix rows cause inversion failures
7. **Inconsistent K'**: Different K' calculations between encoder/decoder components
8. **Partial Padding**: Incomplete symbol sets in padded region

**FUZZER IMPLEMENTATION**: raptorq_decoder_k_kprime_boundary.rs
- Boundary-focused K values: 7-1025 targeting critical boundaries (power-of-2, GF256 related)
- Scenario matrix: 8 boundary scenarios from Normal to InconsistentKPrime
- Missing pattern generators: Specific indices, ranges, patterns, random
- Encoder/decoder consistency validation with gap-aware testing
- Matrix integrity verification for zero-padding artifacts

**TEST SCENARIOS**:
- Missing symbols exactly at K boundary (last source + first repair)
- Missing symbols in theoretical K..K' gap region  
- Symbols straddling K boundary causing matrix issues
- Partial padding scenarios with incomplete symbol sets
- Repair symbols that reference positions in padded region
- Matrix configurations that produce zero-padded rows
- K' calculation inconsistencies between components
- Insufficient symbol scenarios for graceful failure testing

**ORACLE STRATEGY**:
- Decode success verification with original data comparison
- Corruption detection via byte-level diff analysis  
- Matrix error identification (zero rows, singularity)
- Index boundary validation for K..K' references
- Graceful failure verification for insufficient symbols

**BOUNDARY CONDITIONS TESTED**:
- Power-of-2 boundaries: 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024
- GF256-related boundary: 255, 256, 257 (critical for field arithmetic)
- Small boundaries: 7, 8, 9 (minimal gap testing)
- Large boundaries: 1023, 1024, 1025 (substantial gap testing)

**IMPACT**: K..K' boundary bugs can cause silent data corruption, decode failures, or matrix inversion crashes
close_reason: COMPLETED: Critical K..K' boundary recovery fuzzer implemented. Targets RFC 6330 systematic encoding edge cases with 8 specialized scenarios and boundary-focused K values. 446-line comprehensive fuzzer addresses zero-padding artifacts, matrix singularity, and encoder/decoder consistency at K..K' boundary.

title: HTTP/1 client audit (re-checked at origin): Http1ClientCodec::decode_eof reports a truncated response as a clean end; pool limits fail fast with PoolExhausted instead of waiting
description:
Read-only audit of src/http/pool.rs, src/http/h1/http_client.rs, src/http/h1/client.rs (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-04). The agent read the stale checkout (8a281c58a, 229 commits behind); SapphireHill re-checked at origin/main 2780d3454. Its HIGH (pooled connection reused after the server closed it) was already fixed by ebe4c654e (4ebib5: idle_connection_is_reusable), and its relative-Location LOW by the RFC 3986 5.2.2 resolver already on origin.

Still present at origin:
1. LOW: Http1ClientCodec::decode_eof (client.rs decode_inner_eof) returns Ok(None) whenever nothing is buffered, also mid-response: after a head whose Content-Length body has not arrived, or after the chunked decoder consumed every buffered byte. A FramedRead user sees a clean end of stream instead of a truncated response (HttpClient's own read loop errors on EOF itself and is not affected). Fix: Ok(None) only in the Head state.
2. MEDIUM (design): acquire_connection_with returns PoolExhausted at once when the per-host or total limit is reached; there are no pool waiters (7 concurrent requests to one host with the default 6-per-host limit: the 7th fails). Streaming and proxied requests reportedly bypass the pool (unverified at origin). An opt-in wait (HttpClientBuilder::pool_wait_timeout) would be additive; owner decision.

Not re-checked at origin (from the stale read): cleanup_interval never applied (doc), request_timeout not total for streaming/connect_tunnel, Proxy-Authorization stripped on cross-origin redirect through an HTTP proxy, early 413 lost while uploading, HTTP/1.0 + Transfer-Encoding pooled, ClientIncomingBody is_end_stream after an error.

title: [DB][TEST-DEBT] Rewrite prepared_cache_eviction_with_real_statements responder choreography (deterministic mutual-wait hang)
description: Carved out of asupersync-uvqpga. The test hangs deterministically (>60s, isolated, quiet worker): the responder waits for eviction CLOSE wire bytes immediately, but the implementation queues deallocates (deallocate_retry_queue, br-7v80ju) and only flushes them at the NEXT public request — mutual wait by construction. The read_until timeout panic then leaves try_clone'd peer sockets keeping the main thread blocked in read_message (observed 60s+ wedge). Fix: rewrite responder choreography to expect CLOSE flush at next-request boundaries (or drive an extra request to trigger the flush), and/or bound the main-thread read. Until then every DB-feature sweep must run with --skip prepared_cache_eviction_with_real_statements. The 200ms->2s read_until_contains bump (209f9afbc) is load-hardening only, NOT the hang fix.
close_reason: Fixed: responder choreography was inverted — the eviction CLOSE runs strictly AFTER the fourth Parse exchange completes (prepare inserts into cache post-parse, then awaits close_statement_exchange), but the responder waited for CLOSE bytes first → mutual wait → deterministic 60s+ wedge. Also fixed a latent masked bug: responder4's RowDescription declared length 0x21 (correct for '?column?') over a 'result' column with a 27-byte body, which would have over-read 2 bytes into the following ReadyForQuery. Test now passes in 0.01s in isolation. DB-feature sweeps no longer need --skip prepared_cache_eviction_with_real_statements (f7jmlg notes updated).

title: [mock-code-finder][CRITICAL] src/messaging/kafka.rs: KafkaProducer::send silently writes to stub_broker when 'kafka' feature is OFF (not default) — silent message loss in prod builds
description: src/messaging/kafka.rs:991-1001 (KafkaProducer::send) and :1050-1063 (KafkaProducer::send_with_headers): when built without --features kafka (the default), both functions return Ok(RecordMetadata { ... }) after calling stub_broker_publish(). Severity: CRITICAL — false-success return on a network-effecting API. Suggested fix (one of): (a) add a runtime panic/error 'kafka feature required' when stub-mode is active outside #[cfg(test)]; (b) make 'kafka' a default feature; (c) split the KafkaProducer symbol behind #[cfg(feature = "kafka")] so callers fail at compile time when the feature is missing.
close_reason: KafkaProducer::send and send_with_headers now return KafkaError::FeatureDisabled in production builds (no kafka feature, no cfg(test)) instead of silently writing to the in-process stub broker. title: [idea-wizard-wave5] Runtime SLO policy enforcement engine and proof pack
description:
Background:
Wave4 closed the operator contract for compiling SLO bundles into Budget/admission decisions and proving those artifacts with LabRuntime replay plus an operator proof report. The next accretive step is to stop at neither documentation nor offline compilation: compiled SLO policy should have a real runtime application seam that can feed admission, optional-work brownout, cleanup-budget projection, and no-win fallback reporting without creating a new scheduler or ambient controller.

Idea-wizard phase summary:
- Phase 2 generated 30 candidate improvements around massive-agent-swarm responsiveness, proof-backed operator controls, no-win transparency, controller safety, and deterministic troubleshooting.
- The best 5 were: runtime SLO policy enforcement, typed no-win/fallback receipts at admission boundaries, policy-aware LabRuntime replay, operator proof-pack aggregation, and docs/support-matrix ratcheting.
- Phase 3 expanded the next 10 ideas; runner hardening, controller dashboards, broker parity, browser support, and incident replay were mostly already covered by recent closed beads, so this wave deliberately builds on the fresh SLO compiler instead of duplicating those lanes.

Goal:
Turn the Wave4 SLO compiler artifacts into a runtime enforcement substrate with deterministic proof. Operators should be able to compile a service objective policy, apply it through an explicit runtime capability, see admission/brownout/no-win decisions reflected in runtime-visible evidence, and rerun exact rch proofs.

Non-goals:
- Do not add a new runtime, global daemon, or broad host stress harness.
- Do not replace the existing scheduler, capacity planner, SLO compiler, or proof report schema.
- Do not make unsupported production claims before LabRuntime replay and operator scripts exist.
close_reason: All child beads are closed and the parent epic was re-audited complete on 2026-05-07.

title: [idea-wizard-wave5] Define runtime SLO policy application contract
description:
Goal:
Define the typed seam that applies a compiled SLO policy to runtime decisions without hidden global state. This should be a small, explicit API surface that consumes the existing Wave4 compiled policy data and produces deterministic admission, cleanup-budget, brownout, and no-win decision inputs for later runtime integration.

Implementation expectations:
- Reuse `src/types/slo_policy.rs` types and schema vocabulary instead of inventing a parallel policy format.
- Add only the minimal new type surface needed to represent applying a compiled policy to runtime work: policy id, profile hash, target workload class, budget projection, optional-work class decision, fallback/no-win reason, and exact proof-command provenance.
- Keep effects capability-oriented; no ambient globals, no background controller, no local clock reads outside existing deterministic seams.
- Fail closed for stale profile hashes, unsupported workload class, missing compiled output, missing fallback receipt, and missing rch-routed proof command.

Required tests and proof:
- Unit tests for serialization, fail-closed validation, stale hash rejection, unsupported class rejection, no-win receipt requirement, and command rendering.
- Artifact catalog entry or contract fixture tying the runtime application schema to the existing SLO compiler schema.
- `rch exec -- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check ...` and targeted `rch exec -- cargo test/check/clippy` proof for the touched test target.
close_reason: Implemented exported runtime SLO policy application schema/API, fail-closed validation for stale profile hashes, unsupported workloads, blocked/missing compiled output, missing no-win receipts, missing rch proof commands, and artifact catalog ties to the SLO compiler schema. Verified with scoped JSON/diff checks plus rch rustfmt, runtime-filtered test, full SLO contract test, cargo check, and clippy.

title: [idea-wizard-wave5] Wire compiled SLO policy into admission and brownout decisions
description:
Goal:
Use the runtime application contract from `.1` to drive a real admission/brownout decision seam. The implementation should make it possible for runtime work units to be admitted, rejected, degraded, or routed to a no-win fallback based on compiled SLO policy evidence, while preserving deterministic behavior under LabRuntime.

Implementation expectations:
- Locate the narrowest existing admission or scheduling decision seam that can consume a compiled SLO application result without broad scheduler refactoring.
- Thread explicit policy application data through that seam; do not read policy from global mutable state or environment variables.
- Preserve structured concurrency and obligation invariants: rejected/degraded work must not leak permits, tasks, regions, or obligations.
- Emit deterministic evidence fields suitable for the proof report: policy id, workload class, decision, optional work class, fallback reason, profile hash, and proof command.

Required tests and proof:
- Unit or integration tests covering accepted work, rejected work, degraded optional work, no-win fallback, stale policy evidence, and cancellation while admission is pending.
- A negative test proving missing or stale SLO evidence fails closed rather than admitting work silently.
- Targeted `rch exec -- cargo test/check/clippy` proof scoped to the touched runtime/test surface.
close_reason: Implemented a pure SloRuntimePolicyApplication::evaluate_admission seam that consumes explicit request evidence and returns deterministic admitted/rejected/brownout/no-win/blocked outcomes with policy id, workload class, runtime decision, optional work class, fallback reason, profile hash, proof command, budget, work-unit counts, and issue tags. Covered accepted core work, hard pressure rejection, optional-work brownout, no-win fallback, stale policy fail-closed, and cancellation-before-admission via rch-tested contract cases.

This bead should create replay fixtures that demonstrate accepted, degraded, rejected, no-win, stale-evidence, and cancellation-at-boundary behavior using the real policy application and admission seam from `.1` and `.2`.

- Keep the replay deterministic and scoped; do not add a host-global stress harness.

Required tests and proof:

Update README/operator docs only after runtime SLO enforcement, replay, and proof runner artifacts exist. The docs should explain the exact supported flow and boundaries: compile SLO bundle, apply policy through the runtime seam, replay deterministic enforcement, run the proof script, and interpret pass/degraded/no-win/stale outcomes.

title: ATP delta audit (10-09): a hostile delta package costs O(entries x chunks) hex allocations in atp apply_delta_package (HIGH, CPU); library decode_subdelta_ops pre-allocates a peer op count; sub-delta output unbounded vs the target chunk size
description:
Read-only audit of the ATP incremental re-sync engine (src/atp/delta.rs, src/atp/delta_subchunk.rs) and its production receive path in src/bin/atp.rs (apply_delta_package), at origin/main fedfa0691 (SapphireHill rc_20260923 audit agent, 10-09; F1-F3 re-verified by SapphireHill). Nothing lets wrong bytes be accepted as success: every accepted path ends in content-id/size coverage plus the whole-object SHA-256. The findings are resource bounds.

I found two hostile-input bugs in the library receive API, one CPU-exhaustion bug in the CLI's production receive path, and nothing that lets wrong bytes be accepted as success. Every code reference below was read from `origin/main` at fedfa0691.

## Findings

### F1: MEDIUM (would be HIGH if wired to the network). `decode_subdelta_ops` allocates a peer-declared op count before checking it
- **Where:** `src/atp/delta.rs:1768-1770`. The decoder reads `op_count` as a `u64`, then calls `Vec::with_capacity(op_count)` without checking how many bytes remain. The manifest decoder (`ensure_remaining_chunks`, line 391) and `dedupe.rs:168` both do that check.
- **Trigger:** `SUBDELTA_OPS_MAGIC || u64::MAX` panics with "capacity overflow". `1<<32` asks for about 96 GiB and aborts the process.
- **Reachability:** the public `apply_delta_resync_wire_payload{,_and_reconstruct}` and `apply_delta_resync_send_plan` reach it via `from_wire_bytes` (line 1078, peer `encoded_ops`) and then line 1623.
  - Those apply functions have only test callers (`tests/atp_delta_resync_public_contract.rs`, unit tests).
  - The only production decoder caller is `src/bin/atp.rs:5973`. It is guarded by `validate_subdelta_op_count_before_decode` (atp.rs:4413-4435), which is tested at atp.rs:10255.
  - So the fix was applied to the CLI, not to the library.
- **Fix:** move that check into `decode_subdelta_ops` (`op_count <= remaining / 9`), or cap the pre-allocation.
- **Failing test:** `decode_subdelta_ops(&[SUBDELTA_OPS_MAGIC, &u64::MAX.to_be_bytes()].concat())` should return `Err`; today it panics.

### F2: MEDIUM (library only). Sub-delta output size is unbounded, so a few wire bytes can expand to gigabytes
- **Where:** `delta_subchunk::apply` (`delta_subchunk.rs:379-399`) grows `Vec::new()` per op with no limit. `reconstruct_verified` (408-422) takes no expected length. `apply_delta_resync_send_plan` (`delta.rs:1616-1629`) never compares the output to `target_chunk.size_bytes`.
- **Trigger:**
  - A 1 MiB `encoded_ops` holds about 80,659 `Copy{0, 65536}` ops of 13 bytes each, against a 64 KiB base chunk the receiver holds.
  - That is about 5.3 GB allocated, then SHA-256'd.
  - The peer also supplies `target_sha256` (line 1082). If it sets it to the hash of the oversized output, the check passes and `store.insert` copies the blob again (about 2x peak memory). It does this per missing item until the final `verify_store_coverage` rejects.
  - No wrong bytes are committed, but memory is exhausted.
- **Reachability:** same as F1. The CLI guards it with `validate_subdelta_output_size` (atp.rs:4388-4411, called at 5975).
- **Fix:** before `apply`, require the sum of op lengths to equal `target_chunk.size_bytes`. Better, give `reconstruct_verified` an `expected_len` and check the running total before each extend.
- **Failing test (small):**
  - Base `b"abcd"`, ops `[Copy{0,4}; 3]`, target chunk of size 8, and `target_sha256` set to the hash of the 12-byte output.
  - Expected: `apply_delta_resync_send_plan` fails with a size error.
  - Today it reconstructs and inserts the 12-byte junk chunk, then fails later with `MissingChunk`.

### F3: HIGH by the rubric (CPU exhaustion from peer input in a production path). Quadratic hex lookups in the CLI's delta package apply
- **Where:** `src/bin/atp.rs`, in `apply_delta_package`:
  - line 5838: `target_manifest.chunks.iter().any(|t| t.content_id.to_hex() == ...)`, once per `metadata.missing_chunks` entry
  - lines 5929 and 5945: `.find(... to_hex() ...)` for each sub-delta's target and base
  - line 5999: the same pattern for repeated chunks
- **Cost:** every comparison allocates a 64-character `String`, giving O(M x N) work before any chunk file is read.
- **Trigger:**
  - The metadata may be up to 64 MiB (`DELTA_MAX_METADATA_BYTES`, lines 133-134).
  - The peer-supplied target manifest only rejects zero-size chunks, so N can be about 400K one-byte chunks (well under `max_bytes`).
  - M can be about 200K distinct `missing_chunks` entries, each matching a chunk near the end of the manifest.
  - That totals at least 4x10^10 `hex::encode` calls, roughly 45-100 CPU-minutes per package, with integrity unaffected.
- **Trust:** it needs a sender allowed to deliver a package into `dest`. It runs in `handle_post_receive_delta` (5701).
- **Fix:** index each manifest once (`HashMap<[u8;32], &CasChunkRef>`) and compare decoded hashes.
- **Test:** N=40K target chunks with M=20K missing entries matching the tail in reverse; `apply_delta_package` should finish (or error on the missing files) in under 1 s. Today it takes tens of seconds.

### F4: MEDIUM (sender side; needs a hostile remote). A crafted receiver signature makes `diff` cost O(windows x blocks)
- **Where:** `has_canonical_shape` (`delta_subchunk.rs:87-118`) validates block geometry but not how many blocks share one weak checksum. `diff` checks every candidate for each window whose weak checksum hits (303-315) and breaks only on a contiguous match. The CLI sender also never caps receiver-manifest chunk sizes before signing candidates (atp.rs:5057-5080).
- **Trigger:**
  - The remote's `__delta-state-export` declares one 32 MB chunk that overlaps every target.
  - Its 500K blocks all carry `weak = 0` (the weak checksum of 64 zero bytes) and a bogus strong hash.
  - Any zero run in the sender's file then costs about 500K comparisons per byte, for every target chunk.
- **Fix:** cap candidates per weak bucket (or skip overfull buckets), and reject candidate chunks larger than `DELTA_MAX_CHUNK_BYTES`.

### F5: LOW. Planning accounting
- The CLI sends a package in the `DeltaChunks` branch (atp.rs:4549) without comparing total package bytes to the full object. The promotion branch (4575) compares `payload_bytes` only, ignoring metadata JSON and the target manifest. The oversend is bounded at roughly 2% (about 320 B per chunk against a 16 KiB minimum chunk).
- In the library, `build_delta_resync_send_item` (`delta.rs:2210`) picks a sub-delta when `encoded_ops < chunk len`, ignoring its 145 B per-item framing (versus 61 B for a whole chunk).
  - One marginal sub-delta also disables `WHOLE_CHUNK_RUN` compaction for the whole plan (2050-2061).
  - This is still capped by `beats_full_object`, so it costs efficiency, not correctness.

### F6: LOW. Hardening
- `reconstruct_manifest_bytes` (`delta.rs:1725-1727`) calls `Vec::with_capacity(total_size_bytes)` before verifying any chunk. Current callers gate it with `verify_store_coverage`, but as a public function it aborts on an unverified manifest. The CLI uses `try_reserve_exact`.
- `ContentAddressedChunkStore::contains` (245-251) returns true for a coverage-only entry of any size and does a linear scan. It has no production callers.
- In the library, `WholeChunk` payloads are inserted without matching them to the item's target chunk (1613-1614). Junk stays in the returned store when the target was already present.
- An empty sender file is labelled `DeltaNotSmallerThanFullObject` (1297); the outcome is correct, only the label is misleading.

## Checked and sound
- **Integrity of every accepted path.** No reconstructed byte can be returned as success unless it matches the expected content (barring a hash collision):
  - Library: rebuilt chunks are re-keyed by their true content id; `verify_store_coverage` plus `verified_chunk_payload` (size and content id) gate every byte in `reconstruct_manifest_bytes`. This covers sub-delta, whole-chunk, run, `RepeatedChunk` and already-in-sync paths.
  - CLI: base chunks are content-verified on load (6662-6693); there is a rebuilt-length check (5978-5986); then final coverage, a per-chunk re-hash, and a whole-object SHA-256 check before commit. The trust root is the sender's declared manifest and hash, the same as for a full-object transfer.
- **`from_wire_bytes`:**
  - Item count is pinned to the local plan, and each item's target must equal `missing_chunks[ordinal]`.
  - The run tag's start, length and overflow are checked.
  - `read_exact` checks bounds; `RepeatedChunk` requires `source_ordinal < ordinal` and a matching key; payload accounting and EOF are checked.
  - All indexing is proven in range.
- **`from_canonical_bytes`:** remaining length is checked before allocating; layout is contiguous, has no zero-size chunks, and offsets use checked adds; size and root are recomputed.
- **`delta_subchunk::apply` and `diff`:** copy bounds use saturating math, so no panic on any op; zero-length ops are fine; window indices stay in bounds; a zero block size is guarded; copy merge is overflow-checked; the round trip is exact.
- **Planner:** AlreadyInSync only when Merkle roots are equal; incomplete coverage and "missing >= total" fall back with an explicit reason; the transmission re-checks envelope bytes and fails closed on encode errors. The CLI refuses a cached AlreadyInSync.
- **Chunking:** `delta.rs` contains no CDC chunker. The CLI chunker (`split_delta_tree_object_chunks`, 5352) handles empty input, enforces min/max, and merges the tail without exceeding the max.
- `dedupe.rs` decoders bound counts before allocating. `reconcile.rs` and `slepian_wolf.rs` have no non-test callers of the apply paths.

## Test gaps
- No hostile-input test for the library decoder or apply path (huge op count, output amplification, peer-chosen `target_sha256`). Only the CLI's guards are tested.
- `tests/atp_delta_resync_public_contract.rs` covers honest round trips and fallbacks only.
- No performance or adversarial test for `apply_delta_package` with large metadata, and none for weak-bucket fan-out in `diff`.
- No fuzz target for `from_wire_bytes`, `decode_subdelta_ops` or `from_canonical_bytes`. The only delta-named fuzz corpora are for h2 and snapshots.

title: [testing-metamorphic] Obligation ledger permit/ack count conservation under concurrent cancel/abort
description:
Implement MR-OBL-C metamorphic relations for obligation count conservation:

MR-OBL-C1: Permit acquisition-release balance under cancellation
- Test across 3 paths: no cancel, 50% cancel, full cancel
- Assert: acquired == committed + aborted + leaked (no silent leaks)
- Invariant holds regardless of cancellation timing

MR-OBL-C2: Concurrent abort batch atomicity  
- All obligations abort atomically or none do during region drain
- No partial abort states observable externally
- Stats consistency exact, never approximate

MR-OBL-C3: Nested region obligation isolation
- Child region obligations don't leak into parent ledger
- Parent counts unchanged by child's obligation cycling

Target: src/obligation/ledger.rs + new ledger_conservation_metamorphic.rs
Integration: Existing ObligationLedger stats + ObligationLeakOracle
Catches: Silent resource leaks that manifest only under specific cancellation patterns

title: HIGH: NATS JWT expiration not validated
description: src/messaging/nats.rs parse_nats_jwt_claims() extracts JWT exp claim (line 677) but never validates expiration against current time. Attackers with expired but structurally valid JWTs can authenticate indefinitely. Must add exp claim validation: reject JWTs where exp < current_timestamp. Also need to handle clock skew tolerance (recommend 30-60 second leeway for network delays).
close_reason: P1 HIGH JWT expiration validation implemented. Added current time validation against JWT exp claim with 60-second clock skew tolerance. Prevents authentication with expired JWTs. Includes robust error handling and network delay accommodation.

title: kafka-feature e2e tests need a live broker but run unconditionally (MessageTimedOut after 300 s; partition not assigned): gate them like the real-server suites
description:
## Finding
The `--features kafka` e2e tests need a live Kafka broker, but they run unconditionally. Without a broker they fail; no code under test is broken. Found by the feature rotation (d1efb15ae, 2bb8c2f17) and reproduced at 5ded50015 on vmi1149989 (`cargo test --features kafka --test e2e_messaging --test e2e_t6_data_path`).
- e2e_messaging::e2e_kafka_producer_delivery_ack_metadata: "first send: Broker(MessageTimedOut)" after 300 s. The producer is the real rdkafka client, aimed at no broker.
- e2e_messaging::e2e_kafka_consumer_lifecycle: commit fails with Config("partition is not assigned to this consumer") right after subscribe. Real assignment comes from a broker-side group coordinator, so nothing is assigned. The check has been in kafka_consumer.rs since c8442bba1 (March); it is not new.
- e2e_t6_data_path::e2e_dp_14_kafka_producer_consumer_data_path fails the same way.
- The target costs 300 s per run on the producer timeout alone.

## Fix
Gate these tests the way the other real-server suites are gated: skip with a printed reason unless a broker variable is set (REAL_KAFKA / KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP; see asupersync-gap-real-server-ci-aoovsx). Alternatively, point them at the deterministic broker, if that is what they were written for.

Tell apart: the kafka_k2_reachable_schema_broker_matrix_contract failures in the same runs ("byte_count mismatch: expected 64773, got 41393") are a source-size pin. That belongs to 8xb1id, not here.
close_reason: Landed d718f8198: broker-dependent kafka e2e tests are #[ignore] with the reason; e2e_messaging 24/0/2 in 0.02 s (was 300 s, 2 red), e2e_t6_data_path 38/0/1; kafka inventory contracts unchanged per test.

title: [fresh-eyes] http/h1/codec.rs:377 validate_request_target absolute-form accepts empty authority (RFC 3986 violation)
description:
src/http/h1/codec.rs:377-385 validate_request_target absolute-form: after uri.split_once('://'), only checks rest.is_empty(). title: [ALIEN][SCHED][LYAP] Spec: scheduler policy seam + determinism rules
description:
## Purpose

Define exactly how the Lyapunov governor is allowed to influence scheduling without breaking correctness or determinism.

This is the "policy object" seam: the scheduler remains correct by construction; the governor only affects deterministic tie-breaking and queue selection within allowed constraints.

## Conceptual model

We maintain a potential function over the runtime state Sigma:

V(Sigma) = w1 * obligations_unresolved
         + w2 * cancel_debt
         + w3 * deadline_slack_penalty
         + w4 * region_close_pressure
         + ...

The governor proposes actions that maximize drift reduction (-Delta V), subject to hard invariants.

In the deterministic lab runtime, "expected" is implemented as deterministic evaluation of candidate actions using the same snapshot function; no sampling.

## Allowed influence surface (must be explicit)

- tie-breaking among runnable tasks within the same lane
- selection among multiple ready queues when semantics permits
- optional: promotion within bounds (e.g., run cancel-debt tasks earlier)

## Hard invariants (non-negotiable)

- cancel lane strictness unless formally justified (cancel protocol must not be delayed)
- determinism: no wall-clock, no ambient RNG
- bounded fairness: governor cannot starve a runnable task indefinitely
- no semantic changes: only reordering of runnable work, not skipping required protocol steps

## Evidence ledger (galaxy-brain mode)

When enabled for debugging (trace-backed, bounded):
- record V decomposition for each decision
- record candidate comparisons: why task X beat task Y (Delta V components)
- record any policy constraints that forced a suboptimal choice

This must be emitted via tracing/trace events, not stdout.

## Acceptance criteria

- A clear policy interface exists (trait or config) specifying inputs/outputs and allowed hooks.
- Explicit deterministic ordering/tie-break rules are specified (including stable iteration order for candidate sets).
- A fairness story exists (e.g., governor score + age-based tiebreak, or bounded round-robin within score bands).
close_reason: Added scheduler policy seam + determinism rules to asupersync_plan_v4.md

title: Sub-Epic: Runtime Debug Console - Ops-Grade Observability Tooling

# Sub-Epic: Runtime Debug Console

## Overview
Implements a runtime debug console (TUI and/or web) providing ops-grade
observability for Asupersync applications, superior to tokio-console.

## Background & Motivation
Tokio has tokio-console with tracing ecosystem maturity. To win that comparison,
we need a cohesive tooling suite that surfaces:
- Region tree, tasks, cancellation state machine phase
- Obligations held, budgets remaining, stall reasons
- Deterministic trace capture and replay hooks
- 'Explain why' diagnostics

## Raid Plan: rich_rust Parts

| Module | What to Raid | Target in asupersync |
|--------|--------------|---------------------|
| console.rs | Terminal detection, color downgrade | src/cli/console.rs |
| progress.rs | Progress bars for lab runtime | src/lab/progress.rs |
| table.rs | Table rendering for traces | src/trace/render.rs |
| tree.rs | Tree rendering for regions | src/cx/debug.rs |
| traceback.rs | Stack frame rendering | src/error/display.rs |

## Features

### 1. Runtime TUI
- Real-time region tree view
- Task list with status, state, budget
- Cancellation state machine visualization
- Obligation tracker
- Memory/CPU metrics

### 2. Web Dashboard (Optional)
- Browser-based interface
- WebSocket updates
- Trace timeline view
- Flame graphs

### 3. 'Explain Why' Diagnostics
- Why can't this region close?
- What's blocking this task?
- Why was this task cancelled?
- Which obligation is leaking?

### 4. Trace Capture
- Structured event recording
- Deterministic replay preparation
- Export to various formats

## Tasks in This Sub-Epic
1. Console rendering primitives (raid rich_rust)
2. Region tree visualization
3. Task inspector
4. Obligation tracker
5. Budget monitor
6. 'Explain why' diagnostics engine
7. Debug console E2E tests

## Integration Points
- Hooks into RuntimeState
- Trace buffer access
- Cx inspection
- Lab runtime integration

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] TUI shows live runtime state
- [ ] Region tree visualization works
- [ ] Task details accessible
- [ ] Obligations tracked and displayed
- [ ] 'Explain why' provides useful diagnostics
- [ ] Web dashboard (optional)

title: [channel] broadcast_metamorphic.rs:316 'after_msg < u64::MAX' is effectively tautological for the test's small payload range
description:
src/channel/broadcast_metamorphic.rs:316-320 in mr_dropped_receiver_buffer_integrity asserts:

  prop_assert!(
      after_msg < u64::MAX,
      "MR3 VIOLATION: invalid message after recovery: {}",
      after_msg
  );

The comment above (lines 311-315) claims this checks 'the recovered value must correspond to a real sent message, not a phantom/uninitialised slot value', but the test sends payloads from `(0..messages_before_drop+messages_after_drop)` where both bounds are 1..6 — so any sent value is in [0, 12). The assertion 'after_msg < u64::MAX' fires only on the literal u64::MAX (2^64-1), which the test never produces and rustc could never accidentally surface from real send logic. A phantom uninitialised slot returning 0 or any other small value would silently pass.

Suggested fix: bound after_msg by the actual range of sent values (messages_before_drop + messages_after_drop). Existing prop_assert pattern carries those bounds into scope already.

Audit: SapphireHill 2026-04-27 fresh-eyes-broadcast-metamorphic.
close_reason: Already fixed on main in 9a83b6d44 ([br-asupersync-w7g55u]); closing stale tracker entry.

title: [oracle-correctness HIGH] lab/oracle/priority_inversion.rs: pervasive Instant::now + std HashMap — entire oracle is non-replayable and detection thresholds are wall-clock-dependent
description:
src/lab/oracle/priority_inversion.rs is the same shape as the previously-filed region_leak.rs (br hq5gou) and waker_dedup.rs (br 1zvt0a) — every event records Instant::now() and every detection is wall-clock-based:

Sites identified:
  - line 206: PriorityInversionState { last_stats_report: Instant::now(), ... }
  - line 227: TaskInfo { spawn_time: Instant::now(), ... }
  - line 242: task_info.start_time = Some(Instant::now())
  - line 282: ResourceLockInfo { acquire_time: Instant::now(), ... }
  - line 367, 448: PriorityInversionRecord { start_time: Instant::now(), ... }
  - line 565: state.last_stats_report = Instant::now()

Plus: HashMap::new() at lines 202, 203, 204 + HashSet::new() at lines 229, 230 — std HashMap with default hasher means iteration order over active_tasks / resource_locks / active_inversions is randomized per process. When the oracle reports the FIRST priority inversion or starvation event, two replays of the same scenario can name DIFFERENT tasks or resources as the offender.

Two failure modes flow from this:

  (a) **Detection threshold non-determinism.** A starvation threshold of, say, 100ms compares `now.duration_since(spawn_time)` to the threshold. A lab run on a busy CI host takes longer wall-clock between the simulated spawn and detection than on a dev workstation; the oracle reports a starvation event in CI that does NOT exist in dev — or vice versa.

  (b) **Violation record non-determinism.** Even when the same set of inversions is detected, the start_time / acquire_time / detected_at fields put a different timestamp in every replay. Trace certificates and crashpack hashes that include violation records become unstable.

This is HIGH severity for the same reasons as br-asupersync-hq5gou and br-asupersync-1zvt0a: oracle data is the lab's deliverable, and a non-replayable oracle defeats the lab's entire reason for existing. Priority inversion is also a SECURITY-RELEVANT detection surface — it identifies the conditions DoS attackers exploit (low-priority tasks holding locks contended by high-priority tasks).

Fix direction:
  1. Replace every Instant::now() with `now: Time` parameters threaded from the caller (LabRuntime::check_invariants already has `now` in scope — see lab/runtime.rs:1408 hydrate_temporal_from_state(&self.state, now)).
  2. Replace HashMap/HashSet with crate::util::DetHashMap / DetHashSet for replay-stable iteration AND hash-DoS protection.
  3. Add an explicit secondary-sort key on any `min_by_key` / `iter().next()` style code to break ties deterministically.
  4. Add a regression test that runs the oracle through a deterministic LabRuntime with virtual-time clock and asserts two replays produce byte-identical violation records.

Source: /reality-check on src/lab/* (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Fixed in 1aeb71a08 (PARTIAL): PriorityInversionState's 3 keyed tables swapped from std HashMap to BTreeMap (with PartialOrd/Ord derives on ResourceId, InversionId; TaskId already had them). Iteration order over violation-stream-feeding tables is now deterministic across replays. The 7 Instant::now() sites are threshold-detection timing (not violation-record stamps); their wall-clock dependency tracks as structural follow-up.

title: RaptorQ receive-path audit: unauthenticated Hello geometry exhausts receiver memory (HIGH), per-repair-packet dense rank work, swallowed object-parameter errors, unbounded retention, poisoned blocks
description:
Read-only audit of the ATP-over-RaptorQ receive path with peer-controlled inputs (src/net/atp/transport_rq/mod.rs glue into src/raptorq decoder, systematic, linalg and the decoding pipeline) at origin/main c06414315 (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-03). SapphireHill re-read HIGH 1 before fixing it.

## HIGH
1. FIXED in this session's next stack: no authentication is needed to make the receiver run out of memory or abort. The Hello's symbol_size (u16) and max_block_size (u64) were adopted unchecked (mod.rs 11398-11404; accept check 11103-11107 looked only at protocol, role, symbol_auth and total_bytes). symbol_size 1, max_block_size u64::MAX and a well-formed manifest with a 4 GiB entry gave one block of K = 2^32 and source_block_progress_for allocated vec![false; k] twice plus 33-byte tag slots per symbol (about 150 GB) before any datagram: allocation failure aborts the process (the serve loop dies). symbol_size 0 likewise; max_block_size 1 makes object_params_for loop about 4.3e9 times.
2. OPEN (needs the symbol key, i.e. the sending peer, or TrustedUnauthenticated mode): every accepted repair packet triggers dense full-block work and the peer chooses K. feed_pipeline_auth_symbol_with_cx (12382) -> seed_source_streaming_pipeline -> source_streaming_block_ready_to_seed (8077) -> DecodingPipeline::block_status -> block_rank_status (decoding.rs 960, 1346-1350) clones every symbol, constraint_symbols() runs ConstraintMatrix::build (decoder.rs 2192), a dense (S+H+K')xL matrix (systematic.rs 460-463) just to read S+H rows, then equation_rank_profile does scalar Gaussian elimination (decoder.rs 3157-3169, linalg.rs 899-927). At K'=56403 each ~1 KB datagram costs ~3 GiB of allocate-and-fill; honest K~512 pays O(L^2) per repair packet. Fix: make block_status cheap (symbols_received; rank only in per-round feedback), build only the S+H rows, enforce a receiver K cap.

## MEDIUM (key holder, or on-path injector in TrustedUnauthenticated mode)
3a. set_object_params errors are only traced (mod.rs 7870-7880); without block plans the SBN layout check is skipped, k is None, no decode runs, and every authenticated symbol for any of 256 SBNs is kept. Fix: make it fatal for the transfer.
3b. RQ_REPAIR_RECEIVE_SYMBOL_CAP_PER_BLOCK = usize::MAX (mod.rs 445, 7862): retention grows with attacker traffic (OWNER: the comment at 443-450 cites MATRIX-5 for not capping).
3c. A repair ESI below K, above MAX_ALLOWED_ESI, a source ESI >= K, or a corrupt payload, once inserted, is restored after each failed decode, so the block's FEC recovery stays broken and each arrival re-runs a full decode. Fix: check ESIs at admission (esi < K for source, K <= esi <= MAX_ALLOWED_ESI for repair). Pins: reject_invalid_metadata_esi_out_of_range and reject_invalid_metadata_repair_esi_overflow_without_panicking pin only the Rejected(InvalidMetadata) value.

## Suspected
receive_bonded (bonded.rs 1754) also builds entry decode state; its descriptor geometry is only checked for zero (mod.rs 10120-10134), so HIGH 1 may apply there if the descriptor is not authenticated. validate_input's compute budget plus unbounded retention could leave an honest block permanently Retry after very heavy retention.

## Checked and sound
Datagram header/payload bounds and payload length == symbol_size at every entry point; HMAC over object_id, SBN, ESI, kind, length, payload with receiver-derived object_id; verify-before-insert and fail-closed modes; SBN/ESI bounds before indexing; K > 56403 rejected before InactivationDecoder::new; out-of-layout SBNs dropped when parameters are set; SymbolSet dedupe; no wrong data committed (decode output checked against every equation, then SHA-256 and Merkle before commit).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SapphireHill 2026-10-03 23:10Z, sibling census of the ATP receive paths (read-only audit agent, origin/main c06414315; SapphireHill re-read MEDIUM-1 in the code):
