title: Redis pooled APIs return connections with MULTI/WATCH/SELECT/SUBSCRIBE state to the pool; later borrowers inherit it (GET reads as missing, wrong database)
description:
## Defect (source-verified by SapphireHill, 2026-09-28, origin b4bf49ffa; found by a subagent review of 713e6b1d8; predates it)
The pooled Redis APIs return a connection to the shared pool after any command, including commands that change connection-scoped state. Later borrowers, including RedisClient::session(), inherit that state:
- RedisClient::cmd_bytes (src/messaging/redis.rs ~3323-3336) calls conn.return_to_pool() on Ok and on a server error reply, whatever the command was.
- Pipeline::exec (~4046) re-pools after draining, whatever was queued.
- Transaction::exec (~4170) re-pools after EXEC, even if a queued SELECT, CLIENT or SUBSCRIBE took effect at EXEC.
The session API has a reserved-command guard (validate_session_command); the pooled paths had none.

Scenarios:
- MULTI leak: client.cmd(cx, ["MULTI"]) returns +OK and the connection goes back to the pool in MULTI state. A later client.get(cx, "k") on it receives +QUEUED, which as_bytes() maps to Ok(None): an existing key reads as missing, and the GET is queued into someone else's transaction.
- SELECT leak: client.cmd(cx, ["SELECT", "5"]), or a SELECT queued inside a legacy MULTI, leaves the pooled connection on db 5. A later borrower's commands, including a session's WATCH/EXEC, run against the wrong database and report success.
- WATCH leak: a raw WATCH makes the next borrower's EXEC abort spuriously (legacy Transaction error, or a session WatchConflict on a key it never watched).
- SUBSCRIBE leak (RESP2): a SUBSCRIBE queued inside a legacy MULTI puts the pooled connection in subscriber mode.
RedisClient::watch documents WATCH as unsupported on the pooled client, but cmd(["WATCH", ..]) bypassed that.

## Fix (candidate GR 202812936, SapphireHill)
- cmd_bytes refuses commands that open connection-scoped protocol state (MULTI, WATCH, the SUBSCRIBE family, MONITOR, SYNC/PSYNC, QUIT, CLIENT REPLY) with RedisError::Protocol, before acquiring a connection. These cannot be used through a pooled one-shot call; the typed transaction(), session() and pubsub() APIs exist for them.
- Other state-changing commands (SELECT, AUTH, HELLO, RESET, READONLY/READWRITE, ASKING, any CLIENT subcommand except the inspecting ones) still run and return their reply. Their connection is closed instead of re-pooled. The same rule applies after a Pipeline or legacy Transaction that queued one. MULTI...EXEC inside a Pipeline stays legal; that connection is closed afterwards.
- Tests (src/messaging/redis_tests.rs): pooled_cmd_refuses_protocol_state_openers_before_acquiring_a_connection (a panicking pool factory proves no connection is acquired), and pooled_state_changes_close_their_connection_instead_of_reusing_it (scripted server; the SELECT connection must reach EOF and the next PING must arrive on a new connection, for cmd, Pipeline and Transaction).

## Related LOW (not fixed here)
RedisSessionTransaction::exec after a queue error returns "transaction requires DISCARD after a queue error", but consumes the transaction and closes the session, so DISCARD can no longer be sent (redis.rs ~3918-3921). The same applies to -EXECABORT and complete error replies to WATCH/UNWATCH/MULTI. The doc line "Complete Redis error replies leave this session usable" does not hold for those. Fail-closed, with no data risk. Fix: send DISCARD on that path, or correct the message and doc. redis_session_native_terminal_failures_discard_and_allow_replacement currently pins the closing behaviour.
close_reason: Fixed by 6ee7dbe7b. Landed on main=master (tip e5b320b2d); receipts (fix lane green on the exact candidate, old-code control red, check and clippy on the chain tip) are in the commit message.

title: [METHODOLOGY] Capture baseline p50/p95/p99 for all primary operations
description:
Run comprehensive benchmarks for all primary Asupersync operations and capture baseline performance metrics. This is the foundation for all future optimization work -- without baselines, we cannot measure improvement or detect regressions.

BACKGROUND (section 0.11 Tail-Latency Decomposition): The Alien CS Graveyard methodology requires statistical benchmarking with p50/p95/p99 percentiles and bootstrap confidence intervals. Tail-latency decomposition identifies which subsystem contributes most to high-percentile latency. For Asupersync, the tail terms that usually dominate are: queueing (scheduler queue depth), synchronization (lock contention), and retries (cancellation retry count).

OPERATIONS TO BENCHMARK: (1) Task spawn -- measure time from spawn call to first poll. (2) Task cancellation -- measure time from cancel signal to all obligations released. (3) Channel send/recv -- measure one-way latency for both bounded and unbounded channels. (4) Cx capability check -- measure has<T>() and get<T>() latency. (5) Budget check -- measure budget remaining check and propagation latency. (6) RaptorQ encode/decode -- measure encoding and decoding throughput at various block sizes. (7) DPOR exploration -- measure exploration rate (states/second) for a standard test program.

RUST IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE: (1) Use criterion.rs with sample_size(100) and measurement_time(Duration::from_secs(10)) for stable results. (2) Each benchmark produces: p50, p95, p99 latencies and 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. (3) Store results in artifacts/baseline.json with schema: { operation: string, p50_ns: u64, p95_ns: u64, p99_ns: u64, ci95_lower_ns: u64, ci95_upper_ns: u64, timestamp: string, git_sha: string }. (4) First mandatory counters for tail decomposition: scheduler_queue_depth (histogram), cancellation_retry_count (counter), wake_to_run_latency_us (histogram). Expose via metrics crate with prometheus exporter. (5) Use black_box() to prevent compiler optimization of benchmark targets. (6) Benchmark both cold (first run) and warm (steady state) performance.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: (1) Baselines captured for all 7 operations listed above. (2) Each baseline has valid confidence intervals (CI width < 20% of median). (3) Results are reproducible: running baseline twice produces overlapping CIs. (4) artifacts/baseline.json is committed to the repository with git SHA tag. (5) CI can compare new results against baseline and flag >5% regression. (6) Tail-latency counters (queue depth, retry count, wake-to-run) are operational and emitting.

LOGGING REQUIREMENTS: Each benchmark run logs: operation_name, sample_count, p50_ns, p95_ns, p99_ns, ci95_lower_ns, ci95_upper_ns, git_sha, timestamp, machine_info (cpu, os). Tail-latency counters are emitted as prometheus-style metrics: asupersync_scheduler_queue_depth_histogram, asupersync_cancellation_retry_count_total, asupersync_wake_to_run_latency_us_histogram. Summary report generated as Markdown for PR comments.

TESTING APPROACH: (1) Verify benchmark harness itself: a known-cost operation (sleep 1ms) should benchmark at ~1ms +/- 10%. (2) Verify baseline stability: run same benchmark 5 times, assert all p50 values are within 10% of each other. (3) Verify regression detection: artificially degrade an operation by 10%, assert CI pipeline flags it.

title: fs::uring test double-closes a transferred fd: closes a concurrent test fd; the io-uring lib test binary died with SIGBUS after 5790 tests
description:
## Evidence
LIBB, the first full lib run with the production feature set (includes
io-uring): RCH, clean overlay, hz3, bd6e69d01.
- Command: `cargo test --lib --features test-internals,metrics,...,io-uring,...`
- 5790 tests passed; then
  `fs::uring::tests::test_uring_from_raw_fd_closes_fd_when_position_probe_fails
  ... FAILED`.
- The test binary then died with `signal: 7, SIGBUS: access to undefined
  memory`. The remaining ~18,000 lib tests never ran.
Log: /data/tmp/rc_20260922/lanes/LIBB_bd6e69d01.log.

## Cause
The test hands a pipe's read end to IoUringFile::from_raw_fd, which is
expected to fail (ESPIPE) and close the fd through its OwnedFd. The test
then calls `libc::close(read_fd)` itself and asserts -1/EBADF. libtest runs
tests on parallel threads, so between the constructor's close and the
test's close another test can be handed the same fd number. The second
close then closes that test's live descriptor. The FAILED line shows the
second close did not return EBADF, so it hit a live fd. The SIGBUS
followed immediately.
The io_uring reactor tests already avoid this race on purpose: they use
dup2, and their comment explains why.

## Fix
Probe the pipe instead of the fd number. With no reader left, a write to
the pipe's write end fails with EPIPE; Rust ignores SIGPIPE. No second close
of `read_fd`. The unsafe boundary ledger locators for this test move with
the change.
close_reason: fixed 82541f730: EPIPE probe; control red; full prod lib run completes (26613 passed, no SIGBUS)

title: Every integration test silently compiles with test-internals+metrics+tracing-integration+fuzz via the conformance dev-dep cycle, so no integration test ever exercises the default feature surface

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
FOUND 2026-07-26 by SapphireHill while closing br-asupersync-d8aiqa, by trying to
verify a claim I had filed myself and discovering it was false.

THE MECHANISM:
  conformance/Cargo.toml:173
      asupersync = { version = "0.3.5", path = "..",
                     features = ["metrics", "test-internals", "tracing-integration", "fuzz"] }
  asupersync/Cargo.toml [dev-dependencies]
      conformance = { package = "asupersync-conformance", path = "conformance", default-features = false }

That is a cycle: asupersync dev-depends on conformance, conformance depends back
on asupersync with four features turned on. Cargo unifies features across the
dev-dependency graph, so building ANY asupersync test/bench target enables
`test-internals`, `metrics`, `tracing-integration`, and `fuzz` on the lib those
targets link against. `default-features = false` on the dev-dep does not prevent
this; it only declines conformance's own defaults.

EVIDENCE: `cargo check --test kafka_producer_idempotence_audit` on pristine HEAD
with DEFAULT features succeeds (RCH, --base HEAD --clean-overlay --no-overlay,
exit 0). That target uses `asupersync::test_utils` and
`asupersync::messaging::kafka::lock_deterministic_broker_for_tests`, and BOTH are
gated `feature = "test-internals"` for a downstream consumer (src/lib.rs:370,
src/messaging/kafka.rs:770). It compiles only because the feature is on.

WHY IT MATTERS — this is a coverage boundary, not a build convenience:
  1. No integration test in this repo ever exercises the DEFAULT feature surface.
     A downstream consumer running `asupersync` with default features links a
     materially different lib than every test in tests/ was compiled against.
     Anything that is `#[cfg(not(feature = "test-internals"))]` or otherwise
     default-only is untested by that whole directory.
  2. `fuzz` is included. AGENTS.md states the fuzz feature deliberately enables
     opentelemetry-proto's gen-tonic-messages path (tonic -> tokio) and that the
     no-tokio production guarantee explicitly EXCLUDES fuzz. So every integration
     test build has tokio in its graph. That does not violate the documented
     guarantee (which scopes to the default and metrics production graphs), but it
     does mean the tests/ directory cannot be cited as evidence for it.
  3. Fail-closed boundaries are the specific casualty. The whole point of
     br-asupersync-w2p2a0 was that downstream consumers must get FeatureDisabled
     rather than silently using the deterministic broker. The tests asserting that
     boundary are themselves compiled WITH test-internals, so they verify the
     opt-in flag path, not the genuinely-default path.

NOT A REGRESSION, AND DO NOT "FIX" IT BY BREAKING THE CYCLE BLINDLY: the
conformance crate legitimately needs those features. The useful work is to add a
lane that compiles/runs a representative slice of tests/ against the true default
surface, so the default-only cfg branches are covered by something. Removing the
dev-dep would be a large change with its own fallout.

HOW I GOT HERE, worth recording: I filed on br-asupersync-d8aiqa that this target
"does not compile on a plain cargo test without test-internals" and proposed a
`required-features` entry. I ran the check before editing Cargo.toml, and it
passed. Had I trusted my own note I would have added a required-features line that
fixed nothing and masked this.

RELATED: br-asupersync-d8aiqa, br-asupersync-w2p2a0, br-asupersync-c6ppu4
(a red gate and a skipped gate are indistinguishable), br-asupersync-47ppcq.

title: Add Sender::send_blocking() sync API for oneshot channel
description: Missing sync API for sending from non-async contexts. Current async-only send() requires Cx parameter and async context. It must never block an asupersync runtime worker indefinitely; use a documented timeout/try-send/immediate-return shape if the current scheduler cannot safely block. Preserve Cx-taking async send semantics and make sync limitations explicit in docs and errors.

Validation before closeout: rch exec -- rustfmt --edition 2024 --check for touched Rust files, targeted rch cargo tests for channel::oneshot send_blocking behavior with --nocapture, and a closeout comment explaining why the blocking policy cannot deadlock runtime workers.

The broken-count is a MOVING TARGET: round 6 fixed 3, round 7 reveals 3 new. title: [lost-wakeup-race] sync/notify.rs pass_baton_if_waiter_exists generation check is racy with concurrent waiter registration
description:
src/sync/notify.rs:300-316,507-512 — pass_baton_if_waiter_exists scans for an unnotified active waiter to hand off a notification token but does NOT mint a replacement stored notification if no waiter is found. There is a TOCTOU race between the generation check (line 511) and the actual scan (line 512): a new waiter can register with an older generation between the two operations, miss the baton, and hang.

Concrete sequence:
  T0 — broadcast B1 fires, increments generation
  T1 — caller checks 'is the original waiter still on generation older than B1' (line 511) — yes
  T2 — caller invokes pass_baton_if_waiter_exists (line 512)
  T2.5 — concurrent task registers a new waiter W2 with the old generation
  T3 — pass_baton_if_waiter_exists scans, finds W2 (matches the older generation), passes the baton
  Alternatively at T2.5, W2 registers AFTER the scan starts; pass_baton finds no waiter, drops the notification on the floor; W2 then waits forever for an event that already fired.

The current docstring justifies dropping the notification when no waiter is found ('a later broadcast already covered the original waiter set'), but the broadcast happened at the OLDER generation; a NEW waiter registered between check and scan has the same generation and SHOULD see the notification.

Fix direction:
  1. Move the generation check INSIDE pass_baton_if_waiter_exists, under the waiters lock, so the check and the scan are atomic relative to new waiter registration.
  2. Or: if no waiter is found AND a generation transition occurred during the scan, mint a stored notification fallback (single replacement) instead of dropping.
  3. Add a Loom regression test that drives the interleaving: register waiter W, broadcast B, register waiter W2 concurrently with the post-broadcast cleanup. Assert W2 either sees the notification or correctly waits for the next one.

Severity MEDIUM (the race window is narrow; reachable only when a Notified is dropped after a later broadcast and a new waiter registers in the same micro-interval).

Source: /reality-check on src/sync/* deepest pass (2026-04-26).
close_reason: fixed: pass_baton_if_waiter_exists now stores fallback notification, eliminating the lost-baton race when no post-broadcast waiter exists at scan time

title: [obs-reality-check] observability/mod.rs: replayable_system_time falls back to ambient SystemTime::now when no Cx — observability emitted from Drop / panic / background sweep silently leaks ambient wall-clock and breaks replay determinism
description: src/observability/mod.rs:148-154 replayable_system_time(): if Cx::current().is_none(), falls back to std::time::SystemTime::now() (ambient). The doc claims this is the canonical replacement for direct SystemTime::now() (per asupersync_plan_v4.md §I7 — no ambient authority for time queries) and downstream observability files dutifully call it. BUT the fallback path means: any observability emitted OUTSIDE a Cx scope grabs ambient wall-clock. Common cases: (a) Drop impls that emit a final tracing event (no Cx in destructor), (b) panic-recovery paths (Cx may be torn down), (c) background sweeps spawned outside the runtime, (d) observability fired from std::thread::spawn'd helpers, (e) lazy-static or once-cell emit paths. Each leak makes that observability record non-deterministic across replays — a record that should be byte-identical between two runs of the same lab scenario will diverge in its timestamp field. Mitigation: at minimum, add tracing::warn-once when the fallback fires (so operators see the leak); ideally, reject the call (return UNIX_EPOCH or skip the record) so the deterministic invariant is hard rather than soft. Severity HIGH for replay-determinism guarantees the project advertises.
close_reason: Fixed in c226018b8. New 3-tier resolution policy in src/observability/mod.rs::replayable_system_time: (1) Cx::current() → cx.now_for_observability() — fully deterministic / replayable (unchanged primary path); (2) GLOBAL_OBSERVABILITY_CLOCK static OnceLock<fn() -> SystemTime> installed via the new pub fn install_global_observability_clock — deterministic for lab/replay runs that wire a virtual clock at test setup; (3) ambient SystemTime::now fallback wrapped in AMBIENT_FALLBACK_WARNED AtomicBool latch so tracing::warn! fires AT MOST ONCE per process when ambient leak occurs — the warn line names the install function so SREs/operators can wire a clock and stop the leak. Also added try_replayable_system_time -> Option<SystemTime> as the strict variant: NEVER calls SystemTime::now, NEVER emits the warn, returns None when neither Cx nor global clock is available — for callers that prefer to skip the record over emitting non-replay-deterministic timestamps. OnceLock semantics: the global clock is a process-wide singleton, install at most once (subsequent installs return Err). Two regression tests: try_replayable_system_time_returns_none_without_source_in_isolated_thread (verifies strict-no-fallback behavior in fresh thread, skips assertion if a prior test in the process already installed the clock since OnceLock is process-wide) and install_global_observability_clock_is_once_only (verifies first install Ok / second Err and that try_ returns Some after install). Lib build is blocked by pre-existing concurrent-agent Outcome<T,E> errors in record/task.rs unrelated to this fix. UBS clean (0 critical / 0 warning on this file).

title: HTTP/1 client: idle connections to other hosts are never evicted (PoolExhausted for every new host), stale idle reuse without liveness check, uncapped Retry-After, HEAD-blind public codec (review F1-F13)
description:
HTTP/1 client stack review (read-only subagent review, SapphireHill, 2026-09-28, origin 154a3c6c9). Files: src/http/pool.rs, src/http/h1/http_client.rs, src/http/h1/client.rs. F1 was re-verified by reading pool.rs:397-430 and http_client.rs:2279-2299.

F1 (HIGH) Idle connections to other hosts are never evicted. Pool::can_create_connection counts every unexpired connection, idle ones included, against max_total_connections (default 100). HttpClient::acquire_connection returns PoolExhausted at once, with no eviction or wait. The only cleanup is idle-timeout expiry (90 s). Sequential GETs to 100 different hosts each leave one idle socket, so the request to host 101 fails, and so does every new host, until the oldest entry expires. With max_total_connections(1) the second host fails. Fix: when the total limit blocks, evict the least-recently-used idle connection of another key (pool metadata and idle socket).
F2 (MEDIUM) Idle connections are reused without a liveness check (http_client.rs ~2263), and the stale-connection retry (~1689) calls acquire_connection, which prefers idle connections again.
- A server keep-alive shorter than the 90 s idle timeout makes a POST fail on a socket the server already closed.
- After a server restart, several stale idle sockets fail GETs in a row.
- Late bytes (408 on idle close) are read as the next request's response.
Fix: on checkout, do a non-blocking read probe (discard on data, EOF or error), and have the retry force a fresh dial.
F3 (MEDIUM) Retry-After is uncapped (~2966-2992). With retry_idempotent_statuses, a 503 carrying Retry-After: 4000000000 parks the request for about 126 years without a deadline. HTTP-date values are ignored, so they give zero delay. Fix: clamp the delay, and return the response when the delay exceeds the remaining deadline.
F4 (MEDIUM) The public Http1ClientCodec does not record the request method, so a HEAD response with Content-Length desyncs a Framed connection (client.rs 252-369, 483-604). Fix: keep a queue of pending methods, as hyper does.
F5 (LOW-MEDIUM) An explicit or default Proxy-Authorization header is sent inside the HTTPS tunnel to the origin (~2006-2044), while CONNECT carries only URL credentials. Fix: strip it from tunnelled requests and put it on CONNECT.
F6 (LOW) Expect: 100-continue has no fallback timer (client.rs 744-848). It deadlocks against servers or proxies that ignore Expect unless a deadline is set.
F7 (LOW) Cancellation during I/O surfaces as HttpError(Io(Interrupted)), not ClientError::Cancelled, so is_cancelled() is false.
F8 (LOW) A redirect that converts to GET keeps Content-Length, Content-Type and Content-Encoding, so a user-set Content-Length makes the redirect fail with BadContentLength. A 303 on HEAD becomes GET.
F9 (LOW) The URL fragment is sent on the wire. The request target allows NUL, control bytes, DEL and non-ASCII, which the server's own parser rejects.
F10 (LOW) Scheme matching is case-sensitive: an HTTPS:// Location is treated as a relative path (fails safe), and HTTP:// URLs are rejected.
F11 (LOW) Any non-UTF-8 byte (valid obs-text) in a response head fails the whole response.
F12 (LOW, suspected) try_acquire's maybe_cleanup discards the removed ids, so an expired idle ClientIo can stay in idle_connections until the client drops (likely with idle_timeout(0)).
F13 (LOW, documented) request_streaming bounds only the response head, and bypasses the pool limits.

Sound: buffered responses are drained before reuse; framing rejects TE+CL, duplicate CL and non-chunked TE; the bodyless rules apply to HEAD/204/304; cancel mid-request releases the pool slot; deadlines cover every phase; stale retry is limited to idempotent methods; cross-origin redirects strip credentials; CR/LF injection is rejected. See the review for the full sound list.

Plan: F1 and F3 first (small, contained), then F2.
close_reason: F1-F11 landed with receipts; F12 unreachable from HttpClient (additive option documented), F13 documented contract

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
F12 analysis (SapphireHill, 2026-09-29, origin 162841cf7): HttpClient cannot reach it, so I made no change.

Pool::try_acquire calls maybe_cleanup, which periodically runs cleanup_expired and discards the removed ids. In HttpClient, however, acquire_connection first calls cleanup_expired_idle_connections(now). That runs cleanup_expired_entries and drops the matching ClientIo from idle_connections. The client then calls try_acquire, evict_idle_for and can_create_connection with the same `now`, so the discarding cleanup finds nothing left to expire. No expired socket is stranded.

The remaining exposure is external users of the public crate::http::pool::Pool who rely on try_acquire's built-in cleanup: they never learn which ids expired. An additive fix is available if wanted: queue the ids removed by maybe_cleanup and expose them through a new take_expired() method; or document "call cleanup_expired_entries before try_acquire".

title: [security-audit] grpc/interceptor.rs: InterceptorLayer chain has no typed auth-context propagation between interceptors
description: src/grpc/interceptor.rs:109-123 (InterceptorLayer::intercept_request). The chain iterates interceptors and propagates Err early on Status, but there is no shared typed AuthContext (user_id, scopes, request_id) passed between interceptors. An interceptor that authenticates the user has no way to share the parsed identity with downstream interceptors except by stuffing it into request.metadata_mut() — which leaks the auth context onto the WIRE (downstream services see it; outbound responses can re-export it). Severity MEDIUM (P2): not a vulnerability per se, but a structural gap that pushes users toward the leaky workaround (mutate metadata in-place). Suggested fix: thread an &mut CallContext (or similar typed map) through intercept_request signatures so AuthInterceptor can write user_id and downstream interceptors can read it without touching metadata.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 66e31c541: AuthContext type in grpc/interceptor.rs + Request<T>::extensions() typed map in grpc/streaming.rs. Documented the right pattern in interceptor.rs module header. No wire leakage.

title: [axiom-violation] web/session: Session::regenerate skipped on cancel
description: src/web/session.rs line 738 middleware call. I3 CANCELLATION PROTOCOL VIOLATION. The middleware invokes self.inner.call(req) at line 738, which is cancellable. If handler is cancelled mid-execution before returning, Session::regenerate() never fires, leaving REGENERATE_FLAG_KEY unset. Middleware then proceeds steps 5-7 using OLD session ID — session-fixation defense SKIPPED silently. Regenerate finalize is not idempotent under cancellation. Fix: scope handler to prevent cancel during regenerate, move regenerate to post-handler, or explicitly document unsafe-under-cancel and fail-closed.
close_reason: Duplicate of qokau8 — fix landed in same Session::regenerate cancel-tolerance commit

title: CRITICAL: Non-deterministic float serialization in manifest hashing
description: File: src/atp/manifest.rs:375,433,460. Commit: f1ebeca7a (and earlier). title: Broadcast executes message clone and rollback drop under channel mutex
description: src/channel/broadcast.rs clones T while holding the channel-wide inner mutex in Receiver::try_recv and poll_recv_with_waiter. A valid blocking Clone stalls all senders, receivers, subscriptions, and telemetry; a clone whose captured state re-enters Sender::len self-deadlocks. SendPermit::send also discards a just-pushed value with let _ = pop_back while locked when the last receiver disappears between liveness snapshots, so T::drop can re-enter and deadlock. Store retained payloads behind Arc<T>: clone only Arc under lock, clone T after unlock, and advance/revalidate the receiver cursor only after cloning succeeds so clone panic preserves delivery. Move rollback payload ownership into a local and destroy it after unlocking. Regress blocking/reentrant Clone, clone panic cursor preservation, eviction during out-of-lock clone, and forced zero-receiver rollback Drop re-entry. Closed asupersync-6mg6ja only moved stale subscribe-buffer destruction outside the lock. Independently confirmed by two source reviews on 2026-07-15.

title: [AUDIT] Deep correctness audit: src/http/h1/codec.rs

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Deep Audit: src/http/h1/codec.rs (1092 lines)

**Verdict: SOUND** — no bugs found.

### Analysis

HTTP/1.1 server-side codec implementing Decoder<Request> + Encoder<Response> with DecodeState machine (Head → Body{remaining} / Chunked{decoder}).

**Security hardening (excellent):**
- Anti-smuggling: rejects both TE+CL (AmbiguousBodyLength), rejects compound TE values (only bare 'chunked'), rejects duplicate CL/TE headers
- Header injection prevention: tchar set validation (RFC 7230), rejects \r\n in header names and values, reason phrase injection blocked
- DoS hardening: size limits on request line (8KB), headers (64KB configurable), body (16MB configurable), chunk size line (1KB), trailers, header count (128)

**Decoder path:**
- decode_head: request line length check before headers-end scan. UTF-8 validated. Header count bounded.
- body_kind: TE/CL anti-smuggling, HTTP/1.0 chunked rejection, CL parse validation
- Content-Length body: upfront BodyTooLarge check (line 569), exact remaining-bytes read
- ChunkedBodyDecoder: 4-phase state machine (SizeLine/Data/DataCrlf/Trailers). saturating_add for body size check. Chunk extensions stripped via ';' split. Trailer validation reuses parse_header_line. Trailer byte count correctly tracked (line 429-432).
- State transitions: mem::replace to Head after each complete request — no state leak

**Encoder path:**
- validate_header_field on all response headers and trailers
- TE+CL consistency rejection, TrailersNotAllowed without chunked
- CL mismatch detection (declared vs actual body length)
- Auto Content-Length insertion when absent
- Chunked: correct hex chunk-size + data + CRLF + terminal 0-chunk + trailers + terminal CRLF

**Design note (not a bug):** Line 412 trailer DoS check uses src.len() (entire remaining buffer) rather than just trailer data. With large pipelined requests following chunked trailers, this could cause false HeadersTooLarge rejection. In practice: unlikely at 64KB default, and lines 429-432 perform the correct per-trailer accounting. Defense-in-depth that errs conservative.

**Tests:** 35 tests covering GET/POST, chunked with extensions/trailers, sequential decoding, size limits, smuggling protection, encoding variants. Good coverage.

title: remote V3: LeaseRenewed echoes the requested lease, not the clamped lease the server enforces (R27c, split from bi2462.123)
description:
src/remote.rs (~:5170-5180, origin/main 5d4c02a33+): on a V3 renewal the server enforces `expires_at = now + remote_service_clamp_lease(lease)` (24 h cap, 2ab2f1fbf) but acknowledges with `LeaseRenewed { lease_secs: lease.as_secs(), lease_subsec_nanos: lease.subsec_nanos() }`, i.e. the UNclamped requested value. For requests above 24 h the acknowledgement overstates what is enforced. Impact is low: 086303195 made the native origin clamp its own renewal schedule (remote_service_clamp_lease at the origin), so this origin never relies on the echo. A third-party V3 client could, and would under-renew.
Fix: compute `let granted = remote_service_clamp_lease(lease)` once, use it for both `expires_at` and the echo (and for `last_renewal` so a replayed renewal echoes the same granted value). Leases <= 24 h are unchanged, so the V1-V3 wire goldens stay byte-identical.
Test: a V3 session renewal requesting 48 h is acknowledged with lease_secs == 86_400. Include a replay of the same renewal_id, which must echo the same granted value. Old-red at 5d4c02a33.

COMPATIBILITY HAZARD (found while scoping the fix; do NOT ship the server change alone): `RemoteServiceSession::renew_lease` (src/remote.rs ~:4115-4140) rejects any LeaseRenewed whose lease differs from the one it requested, with `RenewalLeaseMismatch`. Echoing the clamped value on its own would therefore break every deployed client that renews for more than 24 h. It would turn a cosmetic overstatement into a failed renewal and a torn-down session.
Safe order:
(1) the client accepts `actual <= requested` as the granted lease and schedules from `actual`; strictly larger stays a mismatch;
(2) release that client;
(3) only then, or behind V3 capability negotiation (a new protocol version per v4 §8.4.1), have the server echo the clamped grant.
Tests: an old client against the new server, and a new client against both old and new servers (the NEW/OLD matrix).

Tests: a scripted V3 peer (lib) and the mTLS silent peer granting 2 s against a 10 s request (1 and 2 workers). Controls A (client) and B (origin) both red. STILL OPEN: step 2, release this client; step 3, the server echoes the clamped grant only after that, or behind V3 capability negotiation.

title: Real-Kafka roundtrip: KafkaConsumer::close() does NOT commit pending positions — must be explicit (contract test)
description: src/messaging/kafka_consumer.rs:1383 close() does not call commit_offsets before unsubscribe. Worse: line 1399 it explicitly clears state.committed_offsets along with positions. If a consumer polls messages and updates positions but skips commit_offsets before close, the broker side has NO record of progress. The next consumer with the same group_id will re-read every message (or skip them, depending on AutoOffsetReset). For payment/billing pipelines this is duplicate processing on every graceful shutdown. The close() docstring is just 'Close the consumer.' with no mention of commit semantics. Add tests/integration/kafka_real_broker.rs::test_real_broker_close_without_commit_loses_positions that produces N messages, consumes them with consumer A (no commit), closes A, then verifies a fresh consumer B with the same group_id re-reads ALL N messages — proving the contract that close() is NOT a commit barrier. Run with REAL_KAFKA_TESTS=true cargo test --features kafka --test kafka_real_broker test_real_broker_close_without_commit.
close_reason: Real-Kafka close-without-commit contract test landed in 74e46c8a8. tests/integration/kafka_real_broker.rs::test_real_broker_close_without_commit_loses_positions pins the contract that KafkaConsumer::close() (src/messaging/kafka_consumer.rs:1383) does NOT auto-commit pending positions: producer writes 3 messages, consumer A polls all 3 without commit_offsets, calls close(); consumer B (same group_id, AutoOffsetReset::Earliest) re-reads all 3 — proves the broker still sees the pre-A baseline. Diagnostic assertion message tells future agents what to do if close() ever starts auto-committing. Skips cleanly without REAL_KAFKA_TESTS=true; compiles under cargo check --features kafka --test kafka_real_broker (zero errors after HashSet path fix).

title: Platform reactors E2E test suite: cross-platform I/O verification
description:
# Platform Reactors E2E Test Suite

## Overview
Comprehensive test suite verifying reactor implementations work correctly on
all supported platforms (Linux, macOS, Windows).

## Test Directory Structure
```
tests/e2e/reactor/
├── mod.rs                    # Test module root
├── common/
│   ├── mod.rs                # Shared test utilities
│   └── tcp_echo.rs           # TCP echo server helper
├── trait_contract/
│   ├── register.rs           # Registration tests
│   ├── poll.rs               # Polling tests
│   ├── wake.rs               # Wakeup tests
│   └── lifecycle.rs          # Cleanup tests
├── tcp/
│   ├── connect.rs            # TCP connect tests
│   ├── accept.rs             # TCP accept tests
│   └── throughput.rs         # Throughput benchmarks
├── stress/
│   ├── many_connections.rs   # High connection count
│   ├── rapid_register.rs     # Fast register/deregister
│   └── concurrent_poll.rs    # Multi-threaded polling
└── platform_specific/
    ├── io_uring.rs           # Linux io_uring specific
    ├── epoll.rs              # Linux epoll specific
    ├── kqueue.rs             # macOS specific
    └── iocp.rs               # Windows specific
```

## Test Categories

### 1. Trait Contract Tests
Verify all reactors implement the Reactor trait correctly:
- register() adds source to reactor
- reregister() modifies interest
- deregister() removes source
- poll() returns ready events
- wake() interrupts blocked poll()

### 2. TCP Integration Tests
Real TCP operations through reactor:
- Client connect (non-blocking)
- Server accept (listener)
- Read/write cycles
- Concurrent connections

### 3. Stress Tests
- 10K+ connections simultaneously
- Rapid register/deregister cycling
- Multi-threaded poll() calls
- Memory pressure scenarios

### 4. Platform-Specific Tests
Tests that only run on specific platforms:
- io_uring: sqpoll, registered buffers
- epoll: EPOLLET edge-triggered behavior
- kqueue: kevent batching
- IOCP: overlapped I/O completion

## CI Matrix

### GitHub Actions Configuration
```yaml
strategy:
  matrix:
    os: [ubuntu-latest, ubuntu-20.04, macos-latest, windows-latest]
    rust: [stable, nightly]
    include:
      - os: ubuntu-latest
        features: io-uring
      - os: ubuntu-20.04
        features: epoll-fallback  # Older kernel without io_uring
```

## Logging Requirements

### Log Fields
```rust
tracing::info!(
    reactor_type = %reactor_name,
    platform = %std::env::consts::OS,
    connection_count = count,
    poll_latency_us = latency.as_micros(),
    events_per_poll = events,
    "Reactor test metrics"
);
```

### Artifact Collection
- Per-test timing data
- Event histograms
- Memory usage snapshots
- Platform-specific diagnostics

## Test Scripts

### Run All Platform Tests
```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

export RUST_LOG="asupersync::reactor=debug,test=info"

echo "=== Platform Reactor Tests ==="
echo "Platform: $(uname -s)"
echo "Kernel: $(uname -r)"

# Detect available reactor
if [[ "$(uname -s)" == "Linux" ]]; then
    if [[ $(uname -r | cut -d. -f1) -ge 5 ]]; then
        echo "Reactor: io_uring (preferred)"
    else
        echo "Reactor: epoll (fallback)"
    fi
elif [[ "$(uname -s)" == "Darwin" ]]; then
    echo "Reactor: kqueue"
fi

cargo test -p asupersync --test e2e_reactor -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture 2>&1 | tee reactor_tests.log
```

## Dependencies
- Requires: All reactor implementations (bd-2m9k, bd-2q5d, bd-39vt, bd-1gx6)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All trait contract tests pass on all platforms
- [ ] TCP integration tests work
- [ ] Stress tests pass (10K+ connections)
- [ ] CI runs on Linux, macOS, Windows
- [ ] Structured logging with metrics
- [ ] Test scripts documented
- [ ] Platform-specific tests run only where applicable

title: examples/spawn_fanout.rs panics at runtime with 'spawn: RuntimeUnavailable' — the epic's headline fan-out on-ramp has never been executed by any gate
description:
WHAT: `examples/spawn_fanout.rs` — the DX-CORE epic's headline "15-line fan-out"
on-ramp program — PANICS at runtime:

    thread '...' panicked at examples/spawn_fanout.rs
    spawn: RuntimeUnavailable

The `.expect("spawn")` on `JoinSet::spawn` fails. `JoinSet::spawn` delegates to
`Cx::spawn_in(&self.scope, f)` (src/combinator/join_set.rs:141), and
`SpawnError::RuntimeUnavailable` is produced by
`SpawnGateway::enqueue_and_notify` when `liveness_guard()` cannot upgrade its
weak runtime-liveness handle (src/runtime/spawn_mailbox.rs:1412-1418). So under
`#[asupersync::main]`, the spawn gateway reachable from the body's `Cx` has no
live runtime behind it.

`examples/hello.rs` still runs fine (exit 0) because it only calls
`cx.checkpoint()` and never spawns.

HOW IT SURVIVED: nothing ever RAN the examples. `cargo check --all-targets`
compiles `examples/*.rs`, so the file has always been green in every routine
gate; execution was never gated. The failure surfaced on the first execution,
by the new `scripts/run_api_v2_e2e.sh` lane
(br-asupersync-dx-core-api-v2-u1z5hn.12).

EVIDENCE (remote, RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1, `--base HEAD --clean-overlay` with only
the on-ramp paths overlaid; worker hz2):
    stage run_example:spawn_fanout -> exit status 101 after 194831ms
    stderr: "spawn: RuntimeUnavailable"
    artifacts: target/e2e-results/api_v2/run_full7/{events.ndjson,rch_run_example_spawn_fanout.log}

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the program the epic advertises as the second step of the
on-ramp, and the README's fan-out story. A new user or agent copying it gets a
panic. It also means the `#[asupersync::main]` + `JoinSet` combination — the
exact pairing the epic promotes — has no executing coverage anywhere.

SCOPE NOTE: not fixed under u1z5hn.12, which owns the e2e harness that found it,
not the spawn API. The fix belongs with the entry-macro / spawn-gateway owner.
Whoever takes it should also check whether `#[asupersync::test]` has the same
gap: `tests/api_v2_integration.rs` (landed by u1z5hn.12) exercises `Cx::spawn`
and `JoinSet` under `#[asupersync::test]` and has not yet been executed on a
healthy worker, so it may be red for the same reason.

SUGGESTED FIRST CHECK: whether the `#[main]` expansion keeps a STRONG runtime
liveness handle alive for the duration of the body, or drops it once the root
future is handed to `block_on`.
close_reason: Fixed in fcd683ef6: block_on ambient Cx now carries spawn gateway + root-region pending-spawn counter; red/green executing evidence on bead

comments.author: SapphireHill
comments.text:
SapphireHill 2026-07-27: ROOT CAUSE FOUND — and it corrects my own filed hypothesis.

WRONG (my filing): "SpawnError::RuntimeUnavailable is produced by
SpawnGateway::enqueue_and_notify when liveness_guard() cannot upgrade".
The request never reaches enqueue_and_notify.

RIGHT: the ambient Cx that `Runtime::block_on` installs is built by
`build_request_cx_from_inner` (src/runtime/builder.rs:4503), which attaches
drivers/observability/entropy but NEVER attaches the spawn gateway or a
pending-spawn counter (both default to None in Cx::new_with_drivers,
src/cx/cx.rs:1030). `Cx::spawn` / `Cx::spawn_in` therefore fail at the
`let Some(gateway) = self.spawn_gateway_handle()` guard (src/cx/cx.rs:4015 /
4080) with RuntimeUnavailable — while the runtime's one worker thread
(current_thread == worker_threads(1)) sits idle and fully able to run tasks.

Every properly wired Cx path attaches BOTH handles: task creation
(state.rs:3130), scope child-cx boot path (scope.rs:1338), lab (cx.rs:4904).
The block_on request-Cx path is the one that forgot.

FIX (landing under this bead): wire `guard.spawn_gateway()` +
`guard.region(inner.root_region).map(RegionRecord::pending_spawn_handle)`
into build_request_cx_from_inner. Children spawned from the block_on body are
admitted through the mailbox into root_region as ordinary REGISTERED tasks
with region accounting; only the request-scoped parent stays unregistered.
This does NOT expose the request Cx publicly (deliberately consistent with
RusticBasin's fsqlite-actor-external-cx audit: their concern is external-owner
threads polling an unregistered Cx; block_on's own thread is the one place
that Cx is designed to be polled).

EVIDENCE PLAN (running):
1. RED control: tests/api_v2_integration at HEAD, --clean-overlay --no-overlay
   (first-ever execution of that stage): cx_spawn/join_set tests must FAIL
   with RuntimeUnavailable, proving the tests reach the broken branch.

3. cargo run --example spawn_fanout (the exact filed artifact): exit 0.
4. New inline unit test block_on_ambient_cx_spawns_through_the_gateway pins
   gateway+counter presence AND an executing spawn/join from block_on.
5. check/clippy --all-targets + fmt on the touched surface.

title: [mock-finder] runtime/panic_isolation.rs: MetricsProviderPanicExt::record_panic is a documented placeholder that silently drops panic metrics
description:
src/runtime/panic_isolation.rs lines 565-580: the blanket impl of MetricsProviderPanicExt for all MetricsProvider types provides a record_panic method whose entire body computes a _location_tag (note the underscore prefix — discarded) and then does nothing. The inline comment explicitly admits: 'Record panic metrics - implementation would depend on the metrics system. For now, we'll just use a placeholder since the actual MetricsProvider interface would need to be extended.' Followed by an empty 'Metrics recording would happen here' comment.

Caller impact: anywhere panic recovery wires panic_isolation into the MetricsProvider trait, panics in task execution, finalizer execution, region cleanup, obligation handling, and scheduler-internal panics are all silently invisible to whatever metrics backend the operator wired up (OpenTelemetry, Prometheus exporters, custom sinks). Operators believe they are observing panic-rate; in fact every panic is dropped on the floor by this stub.

Real implementation paths:
  1. Extend the MetricsProvider trait with a record_panic(&self, location: PanicLocationTag, count: u64) method (or, if extending the trait is undesirable, a separate PanicMetricsRecorder trait that production providers opt into).
  2. Have the blanket impl call into that trait method via downcasting / explicit registration so existing providers don't break.
  3. Wire each PanicLocation variant to a typed counter (panic_total{location=task_execution}, etc.) per the existing label conventions in observability/metrics.rs.

Tests should verify: (a) a custom MetricsProvider counts every panic recorded via record_panic, (b) each PanicLocation maps to a distinct counter / label-set, (c) calling record_panic from inside a panic handler does not itself panic.

Source: /mock-code-finder skill (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Fixed in 9d9fb7fd6: added fn record_panic(&self, location: &'static str) to MetricsProvider trait with default empty body (existing impls unchanged). Extension trait MetricsProviderPanicExt::record_panic now routes PanicLocation variants to canonical string tags and calls into the trait. Existing PanicIsolator call site uses UFCS to disambiguate. Production providers can now override record_panic to count panics by location. Test record_panic_routes_to_metrics_provider verifies all 5 PanicLocation variants route correctly.

title: [testing-metamorphic] barrier reset preserves next-generation rendezvous semantics
description:
Design one metamorphic relation for src/sync/barrier.rs: inserting a fully-completed barrier generation before a target rendezvous should not change the next generation's observable behavior except for the expected generation counter offset.

Baseline: run a single N-party rendezvous under LabRuntime with fixed staggered arrivals and capture one leader, full release set, zero residual arrived count, and zero residual waiters.
Transformed input: run an extra sacrificial generation first, then replay the same target rendezvous.

Expected relation: the target generation remains single-leader, releases all parties, drains waiters, and leaves arrived=0 regardless of the prior completed generation. Generation should advance by exactly +1 relative to baseline because of the inserted reset cycle.

title: [testing-e2e] src/grpc/client.rs loopback-only channel needs real HTTP/2 service lane
description:
Observed:
- src/grpc/mod.rs documents the current surface as "loopback-only client/server" with deterministic in-memory behavior.
- src/grpc/client.rs says Channel::connect is loopback-only and not a network HTTP/2 client.
- tests/grpc_e2e.rs and tests/grpc_production_features.rs exercise Channel::connect("http://loopback:...") and therefore never leave the in-memory seam.

Risk:
- This can hide bugs in real HTTP/2 transport integration: socket backpressure, HPACK/header framing, trailers over a real connection, TCP half-close, GOAWAY/RST_STREAM handling, keepalive/deadline behavior, and cross-stack interop.

Suggested real-service replacement strategy:
- Add a localhost-only integration/conformance lane that binds an actual TCP listener and serves a small asupersync gRPC service over real HTTP/2.
- Drive it with a real external client fixture (tonic/grpcurl in conformance is acceptable because tokio is already allowed there), or once available, a network-backed asupersync client.
- Cover unary, server-streaming, trailer/status propagation, deadline/cancel, and one connection-drain case (GOAWAY or clean half-close).
- Use structured JSONL test logging and the same localhost/prod-safety guards as the existing real NATS/MySQL/Postgres lanes.
close_reason: Added real HTTP/2 service lane for localhost testing. Modified Channel::connect to support localhost/127.0.0.1 addresses. Added comprehensive HTTP/2 E2E test suite with structured JSON logging covering unary, streaming, timeouts, metadata, and connection management. Tests follow testing-perfect-e2e methodology with localhost-only safety guards.

title: [proof-citation] reject failed proof artifacts before current-clean
description:
Child of asupersync-bagg00.

Background:
The proof artifact freshness helper checks HEAD, branch, touched surface, command provenance, Cargo routing, RCH local fallback, fuzz extent freshness, and dirty overlap, but it does not currently make artifact status part of the citeability decision. A current-head clean-surface artifact with status fail, failed, error, or a nonzero exit marker should never become current-clean.

Required behavior:
1. Status values that clearly mean failure must classify as non-citeable before the helper can return current-clean.
2. The classification and reason must be specific enough for operators to understand that the proof itself failed, not that the artifact is stale.
3. Existing status pass fixtures remain citeable when all other provenance is valid.
4. Add a deterministic fixture with current HEAD, main branch, touched_files, valid RCH command, but failed status, and a contract test that asserts safe_to_cite=false.

Validation:
Use local Python and format smoke checks for non-Cargo work and RCH for the proof_artifact_freshness_receipt_contract cargo test lane.

Acceptance criteria:
- Failed status fixture returns a failure-specific classification and safe_to_cite=false.
- Full proof_artifact_freshness_receipt_contract remains green through RCH.
- Closeout cites the exact RCH commands and commit.

title: [EPIC-INFRA] Symbolic Obligations
description:
# EPIC: Symbolic Obligations

**Bead ID:** asupersync-zfn
**Type:** EPIC
**Priority:** P1
**Status:** OPEN
**Owner:** Dicklesworthstone

---

## Vision

Symbolic Obligations bring linear type semantics to distributed symbol operations, ensuring that every symbol that must be delivered is tracked, every acknowledgment that must be sent is recorded, and any leaked obligation is detected and reported. This EPIC extends asupersync's existing obligation tracking system to the RaptorQ distributed layer.

The core insight is that symbol delivery is not just data transfer - it's a responsibility. When a task takes ownership of symbols to transmit, it acquires an obligation that must be resolved: either the symbols are successfully delivered (committed) or the transmission is explicitly abandoned (aborted). Silently dropping symbols without resolution is a programming error that the obligation system will detect and report.

This model directly supports asupersync's cancel-correctness guarantee: cancellation is a protocol, not silent data loss. When a symbol transmission is cancelled, the obligation is aborted cleanly, and cleanup handlers run to notify relevant parties. The two-phase pattern (reserve/commit) prevents data loss during cancellation by ensuring obligations are tracked before any work begins.

Symbolic obligations also enable partial fulfillment tracking. When transmitting an object that requires 100 symbols, the obligation tracks how many have been acknowledged. Progress is observable, and the system knows exactly when delivery is complete.

---

## Goals

- **Define SymbolicObligation type** that wraps core obligations with symbol-specific metadata
- **Track partial fulfillment** for multi-symbol object deliveries
- **Detect leaked obligations** when tasks complete without resolving their symbol responsibilities
- **Integrate with epoch windows** so obligations have bounded validity
- **Integrate with existing obligation system** preserving the two-phase (Reserved/Committed/Aborted) protocol
- **Provide RAII guards** for automatic obligation resolution on scope exit

---

## Non-Goals

- **Exactly-once delivery**: Delivery guarantees are a system property, not a type guarantee
- **Distributed obligation tracking**: This is local tracking; distributed coordination is separate
- **Persistent obligation storage**: Obligations are runtime state, persistence is external
- **Automatic retry**: Retry logic is application-level, not obligation-level
- **Transaction semantics**: ACID across multiple obligations is not addressed

---

## Child Beads

| ID | Title | Status | Priority | Description |
|----|-------|--------|----------|-------------|
| asupersync-fxd | Implement SymbolicObligation Type and Partial Fulfillment | OPEN | P1 | Core obligation type with progress tracking |
| asupersync-t3v | Integrate with Existing Obligation Tracking | OPEN | P1 | Bridge to ObligationRecord system |

---

## Phases

### Phase 1: SymbolicObligation Type
**Duration:** 1 sprint
**Deliverables:**
- `SymbolicObligation` type wrapping `ObligationRecord`
- `SymbolObligationKind` enum (Transmit, Ack, Decoding, EncodingSession, Lease)
- Epoch window validity checking
- Deadline expiry detection
- Commit/abort/mark_leaked methods

**Exit Criteria:**
- All obligation kinds can be created and resolved
- Epoch and deadline validity correctly enforced
- Double-resolution panics with clear message

### Phase 2: Tracking and Integration
**Duration:** 1 sprint
**Deliverables:**
- `SymbolicObligationTracker` for managing obligations within a region
- Indices by symbol ID and object ID for fast lookup
- `ObligationGuard` RAII wrapper for automatic resolution
- Integration with region close (leak detection)
- Epoch-based and deadline-based automatic abort

**Exit Criteria:**
- Tracker correctly maintains obligations
- Guards resolve obligations on drop
- Leaks detected during region close
- Automatic abort on epoch/deadline expiry

### Phase 3: Testing and Documentation
**Duration:** 0.5 sprint
**Deliverables:**
- Comprehensive unit tests (12+ scenarios)
- Integration with region lifecycle tests
- API documentation with usage examples

**Exit Criteria:**
- All acceptance criteria met
- Full test coverage
- Clear documentation

---

## Success Criteria

1. **Leak Detection**: 100% of unresolved obligations are detected during region close
2. **Type Safety**: Impossible to silently drop a symbolic obligation without resolution
3. **Partial Progress**: Object delivery progress is trackable at symbol granularity
4. **Epoch Enforcement**: Obligations outside their epoch window are automatically aborted
5. **Deadline Enforcement**: Obligations past their deadline are automatically aborted
6. **Double-Resolution Prevention**: Resolving an already-resolved obligation panics
7. **RAII Semantics**: ObligationGuard correctly resolves on drop

---

## Dependencies

### Depends On
- **asupersync-0vx** (Foundation Layer) - `SymbolId`, `ObjectId` types
- **asupersync-bsx** (Epoch Concurrency) - `EpochId`, `EpochWindow` types
- `src/record/obligation.rs` - Base `ObligationRecord` and `ObligationState`
- `src/types/id.rs` - `ObligationId`, `TaskId`, `RegionId`, `Time`

### Blocks
- **asupersync-9mq** (Integration) - Obligation tracking in unified API

---

## Acceptance Criteria Checklist

### SymbolicObligation Type and Partial Fulfillment (asupersync-fxd)
- [ ] `SymbolicObligation` wraps `ObligationRecord` with symbol metadata
- [ ] `SymbolObligationKind` enum with all five kinds:
  - [ ] `SymbolTransmit { symbol_id, destination }`
  - [ ] `SymbolAck { symbol_id, source }`
  - [ ] `DecodingInProgress { object_id, symbols_received, symbols_needed }`
  - [ ] `EncodingSession { object_id, symbols_encoded }`
  - [ ] `SymbolLease { object_id, lease_expires }`
- [ ] `EpochWindow` with start/end epochs and validity checking
- [ ] Factory methods: `transmit()`, `ack()`, `decoding()`, `lease()`
- [ ] `is_pending()` returns true until resolved
- [ ] `is_epoch_valid(current_epoch)` checks epoch window
- [ ] `is_expired(now)` checks deadline
- [ ] `commit()` for successful resolution
- [ ] `abort()` for clean cancellation
- [ ] `mark_leaked()` for runtime-detected leaks
- [ ] `update_decoding_progress()` for partial fulfillment
- [ ] Double resolution panics

### Integrate with Existing Obligation Tracking (asupersync-t3v)
- [ ] `SymbolicObligationTracker` managing obligations per region
- [ ] HashMap storage indexed by `ObligationId`
- [ ] Secondary index by `SymbolId` for fast symbol-based lookup
- [ ] Secondary index by `ObjectId` for decoding/encoding obligations
- [ ] `register()` adds obligation and returns ID
- [ ] `resolve(id, commit)` removes and sets final state
- [ ] `pending()` iterator over unresolved obligations
- [ ] `by_symbol(symbol_id)` returns obligations for a symbol
- [ ] `pending_count()` returns count
- [ ] `check_leaks()` marks all pending as leaked, returns list
- [ ] `abort_expired_epoch(current_epoch)` aborts out-of-window
- [ ] `abort_expired_deadlines(now)` aborts past-deadline
- [ ] `ObligationGuard<'a>` with `commit()` and `abort()` methods
- [ ] Guard resolves (abort) on drop if not explicitly resolved
- [ ] Logging for register, resolve, leak, abort events

---

## Obligation Lifecycle

```
     ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
     │                     RESERVED                                    │
     │                                                                 │
     │  SymbolicObligation created via factory method                 │
     │  Registered in SymbolicObligationTracker                       │
     │  Work begins (symbol transmission, decoding, etc.)             │
     │                                                                 │
     └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                │                    │                    │
                │ success            │ failure            │ dropped
                │                    │                    │
                ▼                    ▼                    ▼
     ┌─────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────┐
     │   COMMITTED     │  │    ABORTED      │  │     LEAKED      │
     │                 │  │                 │  │                 │
     │  Symbols        │  │  Operation      │  │  Task ended     │
     │  delivered      │  │  cancelled      │  │  without        │
     │  successfully   │  │  cleanly        │  │  resolution     │
     │                 │  │                 │  │  (BUG!)         │
     └─────────────────┘  └─────────────────┘  └─────────────────┘
```

---

## Integration Patterns

### Pattern 1: Symbol Transmission with Tracking
```rust
async fn send_symbol(
    cx: &Cx,
    tracker: &mut SymbolicObligationTracker,
    symbol: Symbol,
    destination: RegionId,
) -> Result<(), Error> {
    // Create and register obligation
    let ob = SymbolicObligation::transmit(
        generate_id(), cx.task_id(), cx.region_id(),
        symbol.id(), destination, Some(cx.deadline()), None,
    );
    let ob_id = tracker.register(ob);

    // Perform work
    match transport.send(symbol).await {
        Ok(()) => {
            tracker.resolve(ob_id, true); // Commit
            Ok(())
        }
        Err(e) => {
            tracker.resolve(ob_id, false); // Abort
            Err(e)
        }
    }
}
```

### Pattern 2: RAII Guard for Automatic Resolution
```rust
async fn with_lease<T>(
    tracker: &mut SymbolicObligationTracker,
    object_id: ObjectId,
    f: impl FnOnce() -> Result<T, Error>,
) -> Result<T, Error> {
    let ob = SymbolicObligation::lease(/* ... */);
    let ob_id = tracker.register(ob);
    let guard = ObligationGuard::new(tracker, ob_id);

    let result = f();

    if result.is_ok() {
        guard.commit(); // Explicit success
    }
    // If result is Err, guard drops and aborts automatically

    result
}
```

---

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|------------|--------|------------|
| Too many obligations cause memory pressure | Medium | Medium | Per-region limits, TTL-based cleanup |
| Leak detection floods logs in failure scenarios | Medium | Low | Rate limiting, aggregation |
| Epoch window misconfiguration causes false aborts | Low | Medium | Validation, sensible defaults |
| Guard drop order causes surprising behavior | Medium | Medium | Clear documentation, explicit API preference |
| Integration with existing obligations fragile | Low | High | Careful wrapping, exhaustive tests |

title: bug-hunt runtime io_uring drain_wake_fd race loses concurrent wakes
description: src/runtime/reactor/io_uring.rs IoUringReactor::poll() WAKE_USER_DATA handler at lines 575-582 resets wake_pending=false BEFORE drain_wake_fd(). Race: between store(false) and drain_wake_fd(), a concurrent wake() observes wake_pending=false, swaps to true, writes 1 to eventfd. Then drain_wake_fd() reads ALL pending bytes (including the concurrent write). After rearm_wake_poll(), eventfd=0 and wake_pending=true. Future wake() calls observe wake_pending=true via swap() and early-return without writing — silently lost. The new poll never fires. Poller blocks indefinitely until some unrelated I/O CQE arrives. Fix: re-publish missed wake by re-writing to eventfd after rearm if wake_pending is still set.
close_reason: Fixed in 9d1608941. After drain_wake_fd() and rearm_wake_poll(), reload wake_pending and re-write to eventfd if still true. Race scenario: thread X's wake() between poller's store(false) and drain_wake_fd() succeeds (sets pending=true, writes 1 to eventfd) but its write is then absorbed by drain. Without the fix, the new poll never fires (eventfd=0) and future wake() calls observe pending=true via swap and early-return — silent wake loss. With the fix, the poller observes pending=true after rearm and re-writes 1 to eventfd, so the new wake poll fires and clears the flag in the next cycle. Regression test test_wake_pending_recovery_after_drain_race verifies the invariant that successive wakes are always deliverable.

title: [OBLIGATION-INVARIANTS] Structured Concurrency Obligation Invariant Conformance
description:
Systematically test all structured concurrency obligation invariants to ensure no obligation leaks, proper region lifecycle management, and correct cancellation propagation throughout the obligation system.

## Background
Asupersync implements structured concurrency through an obligation system where every async operation must be properly scoped and cancelled. This bead establishes comprehensive conformance testing for obligation invariants that are critical to system correctness.

## Scope - Obligation System Invariants

### Core Obligation Invariants
1. **No Obligation Leaks** - Every created obligation must be properly resolved or cancelled
2. **Region Close = Quiescence** - Region closure must wait for all obligations to complete
3. **Cancel Propagation** - Cancel signals must propagate correctly through obligation hierarchies  
4. **Resource Cleanup** - Obligation cleanup must not leak resources (memory, wakers, handles)
5. **Temporal Safety** - Obligations cannot outlive their parent regions

### Obligation System Components
- **Region Management** - Region creation, nesting, and closure semantics
- **Obligation Tracking** - Obligation creation, resolution, and leak detection
- **Cancel Protocols** - Cancellation propagation and handling
- **Resource Management** - Cleanup of obligation-associated resources
- **Invariant Enforcement** - Runtime validation of obligation system invariants

## Conformance Test Architecture

### Invariant Validation Framework
```rust
pub trait ObligationInvariantTest {
    fn invariant_name(&self) -> &str;
    fn test_category(&self) -> InvariantTestCategory;  
    fn run_test(&self, ctx: &ObligationTestContext) -> InvariantTestResult;
    fn validate_invariant(&self, tracker: &ObligationTracker) -> bool;
}

pub enum InvariantTestCategory {
    NoLeakValidation,      // Test obligation leak detection
    RegionQuiescence,      // Test region closure behavior
    CancelPropagation,     // Test cancel signal propagation
    ResourceCleanup,       // Test resource cleanup correctness
    TemporalSafety,        // Test lifetime and scoping invariants
}
```

### Obligation Tracking Infrastructure
```rust
pub struct ObligationTracker {
    pub active_obligations: HashMap<ObligationId, ObligationMetadata>,
    pub region_hierarchy: RegionTree,
    pub resource_tracker: ResourceTracker,
    pub invariant_violations: Vec<InvariantViolation>,
}

pub struct ObligationTestContext {
    pub tracker: ObligationTracker,
    pub stress_config: StressTestConfig,
    pub timeout_config: TimeoutConfig,
    pub leak_detection: LeakDetectionConfig,
}
```

## Test Matrix Organization

| Invariant | Basic Tests | Stress Tests | Error Tests | Edge Cases |
|-----------|-------------|--------------|-------------|------------|
| No Obligation Leaks | ✅ Test | ✅ Test | ✅ Test | ✅ Test |

## Implementation Structure

## Critical Test Scenarios

### No Obligation Leaks Validation
```rust
#[test]
fn obligation_create_resolve_no_leak() {
    let tracker = ObligationTracker::new();
    let region = create_test_region(&tracker);
    
    // Create obligations
    let obligations = create_multiple_obligations(&region, 100);
    
    // Resolve all obligations  
    for obligation in obligations {
        obligation.resolve();
    }
    
    // Close region and validate no leaks
    region.close().await;
    assert!(tracker.no_active_obligations());
    assert!(tracker.no_resource_leaks());
}
```

### Region Quiescence Validation
```rust
#[test]  
fn region_close_waits_for_obligations() {
    let tracker = ObligationTracker::new();
    let region = create_test_region(&tracker);
    
    // Create long-running obligation
    let long_obligation = create_slow_obligation(&region, Duration::from_secs(2));
    
    // Start region close (should wait for obligation)
    let close_start = Instant::now();
    let close_future = region.close();
    
    // Close should not complete until obligation resolves
    assert!(close_future.now_or_never().is_none());
    
    // Complete obligation
    long_obligation.resolve();
    
    // Now close should complete
    close_future.await;
    assert!(close_start.elapsed() >= Duration::from_secs(2));
    assert!(tracker.region_is_quiescent(&region));
}
```

### Cancel Propagation Validation
```rust
#[test]
fn cancel_propagates_through_obligation_tree() {
    let tracker = ObligationTracker::new();
    let parent_region = create_test_region(&tracker);
    let child_region = create_nested_region(&parent_region);
    
    // Create obligations in nested regions
    let parent_obligation = create_obligation(&parent_region);
    let child_obligation = create_obligation(&child_region);
    
    // Cancel parent region
    parent_region.cancel();
    
    // Validate cancel propagates to children
    assert!(parent_obligation.is_cancelled());
    assert!(child_obligation.is_cancelled());
    assert!(child_region.is_cancelled());
    assert!(tracker.no_active_obligations());
}
```

title: Implement trace compression with LZ4
description:
## Overview

Implement optional LZ4 compression for trace files to reduce storage and I/O overhead.

## Requirements

### Compression Integration
```rust
pub struct TraceFileConfig {
    /// Enable compression (default: true for large traces).
    pub compression: CompressionMode,
    
    /// Chunk size for streaming compression (default: 64KB).
    pub chunk_size: usize,
}
```

```
  Flags: u16 (bit 0 = compressed)
```

title: [ambient-hash-leak] record/symbolic_obligation.rs SymbolicObligationRegistry::new uses HashMap::new() — RandomState breaks replay determinism
description:
src/record/symbolic_obligation.rs:721-722 — SymbolicObligationRegistry::new (pub fn at line 719) initializes two HashMap fields:

  by_id: Arc::new(RwLock::new(HashMap::new())),
  by_object: Arc::new(RwLock::new(HashMap::new())),

Same pattern as types/symbol_set.rs: HashMap::new() uses RandomState seeded from process entropy. Registry is shared across runtimes via Arc, so any traversal order leaks ambient hash state into observable outputs.

Why this is the asupersync 'no ambient authority' violation:
  - Obligation registries are central to the obligation/no-leak invariant.
  - Lab oracles (obligation_leak.rs, region_leak.rs) traverse this registry to assert no leaks at region close.
  - Order of traversal affects which obligation is reported first when multiple leaks exist — that's a user-observable diagnostic that must be replay-stable.

Concrete failure modes:
  (a) obligation_leak oracle reports symbolically-equivalent leak sets in different orders → diff tools show spurious churn.
  (b) Trace events emitted during traverse arrive in different orders across replays.
  (c) Cross-host distributed-region comparison (record/distributed_region.rs interacts with this registry) sees different sequencing.

Fix direction:
  1. Replace HashMap with DetHashMap (FNV-1a, fixed seed) — same fix as br-asupersync-bs92bg applied to otel CardinalityTracker.
  2. The other two fields (by_holder: Vec, by_region: Vec) are already deterministic; only by_id and by_object need updating.
  3. Add a regression test: build two registries with identical sequences of insert calls; assert their iteration orders match exactly. Currently it's a coin flip.

Severity HIGH because (a) reachable from public SymbolicObligationRegistry::new(), (b) the registry is in a primary-invariant path (no obligation leaks), and (c) the same pattern was already filed and fixed in observability (bs92bg), so this is a recurring class that needs systematic sweep.

Source: /reality-check on src/types/* + src/record/* (2026-04-26).
close_reason: Fixed: DetHashMap (commit 7a2c34b59)

title: [bug-hunt] cx/registry.rs commit_permit reuses pending entry's identity_nonce as active lease, violating documented invariant
description:
src/cx/registry.rs:818-845 commit_permit removes the pending entry, performs identity check, then promotes via `self.leases.insert(name, entry)` at line 842 — but the `entry` value carries the pending permit_id in its `identity_nonce` field. The NameEntry struct doc at line 497-499 states 'Identity nonce for pending entries. Active leases store 0.' — so this insertion violates the documented invariant by leaving identity_nonce != 0 in the active leases map.

Not directly exploitable today (no code path discriminates active vs pending by nonce==0 — that distinction is by which map the entry lives in), but:
(a) any future code that adds an active-vs-pending sanity check via 'nonce == 0' would silently fail on commit_permit-promoted entries
(b) breaks the doc/code contract, making the codebase harder to reason about
(c) leaks the permit_id into the active map, where it persists across cleanup cycles — a subtle information-theoretic concern

Fix: reset entry.identity_nonce = 0 before self.leases.insert(name, entry). One-line change. Add an assertion in tests that all active lease entries have identity_nonce == 0.
close_reason: Fixed in 9e32af079: commit_permit now resets entry.identity_nonce = 0 before inserting into self.leases, restoring the documented 'Active leases store 0' invariant. 2 regression tests verify (a) committed permit produces zero-nonce entry, (b) all register paths (register, Fail, Replace, waiter-grant) produce zero-nonce entries.

title: Migration planner: fixture-driven E2E readiness proof
description:
## What
Build a deterministic fixture-driven E2E proof for the planner. The proof should run the full pipeline against synthetic external Rust projects and verify that reports, proof commands, risk rows, and failure modes are coherent.

## Why
The planner will influence migration decisions before code changes happen. A mock-free-enough fixture proof catches false green reports, zero-match scans, stale proof commands, and missing residual-risk rows before users trust it.

## Implementation guidance
- Use repo-local fixtures only; do not require network access or mutate real external projects.
- Cover at least: clean native Asupersync project, Tokio HTTP service, mixed compat-boundary service, malformed workspace, feature-gated Tokio edge, and blocked ambient-authority service.
- Verify deterministic hashes for generated JSON/Markdown artifacts.
- Ensure heavy Rust validation, if any, is routed through RCH. Non-Cargo script linting can remain local.

## Tests and logging
The E2E runner must support `--list`, `--scenario`, `--dry-run`, `--execute`, and `--output-root`. Logs must include scenario id, fixture hash, pipeline stage, row counts, proof command count, final verdict, and generated artifact paths.

## Success criteria
One narrow command proves the planner end-to-end on representative fixtures and fails closed when the scanned project is malformed or produces zero actionable evidence.

title: Pipeline audit: a sink effect that finishes after cancellation is aborted instead of committed (consumed undercounts; a resume repeats the write); cancel/outcome type LOWs
description:
Read-only audit of src/combinator/pipeline.rs, src/types/cancel.rs and src/types/outcome.rs at origin/main 49fec5364 (SapphireHill audit agent, 10-05).

Sound:
- strengthen is monotone, idempotent and associative.
- Every CancelKind is covered.
- Cleanup budgets are finite.
- Outcome::join matches the documented lattice.
- Pipeline credit accounting, no backpressure deadlock, and TerminationTally are correct.

## HIGH
H1. A sink effect that completes after cancellation is never acknowledged, so its credit is aborted instead of committed (pipeline.rs ~408).
- What happens: the sink acknowledges with ack_sender.send_checked. That goes through Reserve, which checks cx.checkpoint() first, and the checkpoint keeps failing while a cancel is pending.
- Trigger: a pipeline cancelled while the sink is inside sink(..).await, via a parent abort, a region cancel, or drain aborting siblings after a stage failure.
- Impact:
  - The write completes, but the ack is refused, and drain aborts credit k.
  - summary.consumed leaves k out. A caller resuming from consumed repeats the write, and the ledger says Aborted for an effect that happened.
- FIXED in stack P (P10): the sink acks with try_send (no cancellation gate; the capacity is at least the outstanding credits). An impossible Full falls back to the checked send.

## LOW
- L1. strengthen breaks equal-severity ties on a placeholder timestamp (CancelReason::xxx() stamps 1 s and the test region). That contradicts docs/semantic_contract_invariants.md ("first-received kind wins"), and the task record and the Cx can end up with different kinds of the same severity class.
- L2. Cause chains longer than 64 serialize but fail to deserialize: link.rs uses unbounded with_cause, and CancelAttributionConfig::unlimited() is accepted.
- L3. pipeline error() depends on join order when two concrete stage errors meet a stronger outcome.
- L4. Docs:
  - cancel.rs says cleanup budgets are enforced, but they are advisory in production.
  - ASUPERSYNC_CLEANUP_BUDGET_OVERRIDE does not exist.
  - The pipeline! macro checks neither cancellation nor errors between stages, and PipelineConfig::check_cancellation / continue_on_error are never read.
- L5. CancelKind derives Ord in declaration order, not severity order. with_cause_limited keeps a stale cause/truncated flag on its depth-0 branches.
close_reason: Completed: HIGH H1 landed in db2ec7e21 (ecdd32e75) with tests verifying sink effect committed and counted as consumed on cancellation via try_send; verified all 45 pipeline tests, 43 cancel tests, and 43 outcome tests pass cleanly.

title: Browser Edition fetch bridge bypasses FetchAuthority
description:
The shipped browser fetch path never calls FetchAuthority::authorize. Public fetch_request enters asupersync-browser-core::fetch_request_impl, which normalizes only method and GET/HEAD body shape; WasmExportDispatcher::fetch_request checks only active scope and nonempty URL; spawn_browser_fetch then calls Window/Worker fetch directly. FetchAuthority::authorize has no production callsite. Consequently a runtime intended to deny all fetches or grant only https://api.example.com can issue POST https://evil.example/collect through RegionHandle::fetchRequest. CORS does not prevent an attacker-controlled endpoint from accepting the request, and unauthorized same-origin targets can receive default same-origin credentials.

Impact: live public Browser Edition code performs ambient network effects outside the explicit capability model.

Fix direction: store explicit FetchAuthority in the runtime/region capability capsule; resolve it from request.scope; convert method and URL to the canonical FetchRequest; authorize before handle allocation, pinning, or host invocation; fail closed when no fetch grant exists; canonicalize once with browser-equivalent URL semantics and pass the exact authorized serialization to the host. Do not add a permissive ambient default. Regressions: deny_all and unlisted origin call a host-fetch spy zero times and allocate no handle; listed origin calls once; child scope without inherited grant denies; parser corpus matches browser origin; wasm e2e replaces globalThis.fetch and proves denied requests have no network effect.
close_reason: Shipped 1e8cc62b6: explicit inherited default-deny fetch authority, pre-effect authorization, canonical browser URL/credential semantics, focused Rust contracts, and dedicated-worker host-fetch spy regression coverage.

Implementing a default-deny per-runtime/per-region FetchAuthority capsule, authorization before handle allocation/host invocation, browser URL canonicalization, explicit credential mode, focused dispatcher/canonicalization tests, and dedicated-worker host-fetch spy coverage.

title: HTTP deflate content-coding is raw RFC 1951, not the zlib format RFC 9110 requires (server middleware emits it; DeflateDecompressor rejects spec-conforming bodies)
description:
`Content-Encoding: deflate` is produced and consumed as raw RFC 1951 data, but RFC 9110 section 8.4.1.2 defines the deflate coding as the zlib format (RFC 1950: a 2-byte header, deflate data, an Adler-32 trailer).

Evidence (origin b00bb46da):
- In http/compress.rs, DeflateCompressor wraps flate2::write::DeflateEncoder and DeflateDecompressor wraps flate2::write::DeflateDecoder, both raw.
- ContentEncoding::Deflate's own doc says "deflate (RFC 1951 wrapped in zlib)".
- web::middleware::CompressionMiddleware can select ContentEncoding::Deflate (middleware.rs ~955). A client that sends only `Accept-Encoding: deflate` therefore receives raw deflate labelled deflate.

Impact:
- Spec-strict clients that inflate deflate as zlib (for example reqwest/async-compression's ZlibDecoder) fail on these responses. Browsers and curl tolerate both.
- Conversely, DeflateDecompressor fails on spec-conforming zlib `deflate` bodies from other servers. That is why the HttpClient decompression option (see its bead) neither asks for nor decodes deflate.

Fix: switch the compressor and decompressor to zlib (ZlibEncoder/ZlibDecoder), keeping the LimitedWriter bomb limits. The decompressor falls back to raw data when the 2-byte zlib header check fails, which is the widely used tolerant behavior. This changes the framing for direct users of DeflateCompressor/DeflateDecompressor, so record it in the release notes; the doc already promises zlib.

Tests:
- round-trip;
- decode of a flate2 ZlibEncoder body;
- decode of a raw body (fallback);
- a middleware response decodable by flate2::read::ZlibDecoder.
